children.text: Adhyāya 1:
children.translated_text: Adhyāya 1:

children.text: athāto dharmajijñāsā // MS_1,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s>. // MS_1,1.1 //

children.text:
loke yeṣv artheṣu prasiddhāni padāni, tāni, sati sambhave, tadarthāny eva sūtreṣv ity avagantavyam. nādhyāhārādibhir eṣāṃ parikalpanīyo 'rthaḥ, paribhāṣitavyo vā. evaṃ hi{*1/1*} vedavākyāny evaibhir vyākhyāyante. itarathā vedavākyāni vyākhyeyāni svapadārthāś ca vyākhyeyāḥ. tad yatnagauravaṃ{*1/2*} prasajyeta.
tatra loke 'yam athaśabdo vṛttād anantarasya prakriyārtho dṛṣṭaḥ. na ceha kiñcid vṛttam upalabhyate. bhavitavyaṃ tu tena, yasmin saty anantaraṃ dharmajijñāsāvakalpate. tathā hi prasiddhapadārthakaḥ sa kalpito bhavati. tat tu vedādhyayanam. tasmin hi sati sāvakalpate. naitad evam. anyasyāpi karmaṇo 'nantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā yuktā, prāg api ca vedādhyayanāt.
ucyate - tādṛśīṃ{*1/3*} tu dharmajijñāsām adhikṛtyāthaśabdaṃ prayuktavān ācāryaḥ, yā vedādhyayanam antareṇa na saṃbhavati. katham? vedavākyānām anekavidho vicāra iha vartiṣyate. api ca naiva vayam iha [2]{*1/4*} vedādhyayanāt pūrvaṃ dharmajijñāsāyāḥ pratiṣedhaṃ śiṣmaḥ{*1/5*}. na hy etad ekaṃ vākyaṃ purastāc ca vedādhyayanād dharmajijñāsāṃ pratiṣedhiṣyati{*1/6*}, parastāc cānantaryaṃ prakariṣyati. bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. anyā hi vacanavyaktir asya purastād vedādhyāyanād dharmajijñāsāṃ pratiṣedhataḥ, anyā ca parastād ānantaryam upadiśataḥ{*1/7*}. vedān adhītya ity{*1/8*} ekasyāṃ vidhīyate 'nūdyānantaryam, viparītam anyasyām. arthaikatvāc caikavākyatāṃ vakṣyati{*1/9*}. kiṃ tv{*1/10*} adhīte vede dvayam āpatati, gurukulāc ca samāvartitavyaṃ vedavākyāni ca vicārayitavyāni. tatra gurukulān mā samāvartiṣṭa; kathaṃ nu vedavākyāni vicārayed ity evamartho 'yam upadeśaḥ.
yady evam, na tarhi vedādhyayanaṃ pūrvaṃ dharmajijñāsāyāḥ{*1/11*}. evaṃ hi samāmananti - vedam adhītya snāyād iti{*1/12*}. iha ca vedam adhītya snāsyan dharmaṃ jijñāsamāna imam āmnāyam atikrāmet. na cāmnāyo nāmātikramitavyaḥ.
tad ucyate - atikramiṣyāma imam āmnāyam. anatikrāmanto vedam arthavantaṃ santam anarthakaṃ kalpayema{*1/13*}. dṛṣṭo hi tasyārthaḥ karmāvabodhanaṃ nāma. na ca tasyādhyayanamātrāt{*1/14*} tatrabhavanto yājñikāḥ phalaṃ samāmananti. yad api ca samāmanantīva, tatrāpi - dravyasaṃskārakarmasu parārthatvāt phalaśrutir arthavādaḥ syād ity{*1/15*} arthavādatāṃ vakṣyati. na cādhītavedasya snānānantaryam etad vidhīyate. na hy atrānataryasya vaktā kaścic chabdo 'sti. pūrvakālatāyāṃ hi{*1/16*} ktvā smaryate, nānantarye.
dṛṣṭārthatā cādhyayanasyānantarye vyāhanyeta. lakṣaṇayā tv eṣo 'rthaḥ syāt. na cedaṃ snānam adṛṣṭārthaṃ vidhīyate. kiṃ tu lakṣaṇayāsnānādiniyamasya paryavasānaṃ vedādhyayanasamakālam āhuḥ vedam adhītya snāyād, gurukulān mā samāvartiṣṭety adṛṣṭārthatāparihārāyaiva.
[3]{*1/17*} tasmād vedādhyayanam eva pūrvam abhinirvartyānanataraṃ dharmo jijñāsitavya ity athaśabdasya sāmarthyam. na brūmo 'nyasyāpi karmaṇo 'nantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā na kartavyā iti, kiṃ tu vedam adhītya tvaritena na snātavyam, anantaraṃ dharmo jijñāsitavya ity athaśabdasyārthaḥ.
ataḥśabdo vṛttasyāpadeśako hetvarthena{*1/18*}, yathā kṣemasubhikṣo 'yaṃ deśaḥ, ato 'ham asmin deśe prativasāmīti. evam adhīto vedo dharmajijñāsāyāṃ hetur jñātaḥ, anantaraṃ dharmo jijñāsitavyaḥ ity ataḥśabdasya sāmarthyam. dharmāya hi vedavākyāni vicārayitum anadhītavedo na śaknuyāt. ataḥ, etasmāt kāraṇāt, anantaraṃ dharmaṃ jijñāsitum icched ity ataḥśabdasyārthaḥ.
dharmāya jijñāsā dharmajijñāsā. sā hi tasya jñātum icchā. sa punaḥ{*1/19*} kathaṃ jijñāsitavyaḥ? ko dharmaḥ, kathaṃlakṣaṇaḥ, kāny asya sādhanāni, kāni sādhanābhāsāni, kiṃparaś ceti. tatra ko dharmaḥ, kathaṃlakṣaṇa ity ekenaiva sūtreṇa vyākhyātaṃ codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharma iti{*1/20*}. kāny asya sādhanāni, kāni sādhanābhāsāni, kiṃparaś ceti śeṣalakṣaṇena{*1/21*} vyākhyātam{*1/22*}. kva puruṣaparatvaṃ kva vā puruṣo guṇabhūta ity etāsāṃ pratijñānāṃ piṇḍasya etat sūtram athāto dharmajijñāseti.
dharmaḥ prasiddho vā syād aprasiddho vā. sa cet prasiddhaḥ, na jijñāsyaḥ{*1/23*}. athāprasiddhaḥ, natarām. tad etad{*1/24*} anarthakaṃ dharmajijñāsāprakaraṇam.
athavārthavat. dharmaṃ prati hi vipratipannā bahuvidaḥ. kecid anyaṃ dharmam āhuḥ, kecid anyam. so 'yam avicārya pravartamānaḥ kaṃcid evopādadāno vihanyetānarthaṃ carcchet. tasmād dharmo jijñāsitavyaḥ{*1/25*}. sa hi niḥśreyasena puruṣaṃ saṃyunaktīti pratijānīmahe.
tad abhidhīyate -
children.translated_text:
Words that are well-known in ordinary usage with respect to certain meanings should be understood, where possible, as having those very same meanings in the <s>sūtras</s>. Their meaning should not be constructed through ellipsis and other [devices], nor should it be defined [arbitrarily]. For thus the Vedic sentences are explained by these very [words]. Otherwise, both the Vedic sentences would need to be explained and the individual word-meanings would also need to be explained — and that would entail an excess of effort.
In this regard, the word 'atha' (now) is seen in ordinary usage as denoting the commencement of something that follows upon a preceding [activity]. But here nothing preceding is perceived. However, there must be some [preceding activity], upon the completion of which the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> becomes appropriate. For thus the word [atha] would be employed with its well-known meaning. That [preceding activity] is the study of the <s>Veda</s>. For when that has been completed, the [inquiry] becomes appropriate. [Objection:] This is not so. The inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> is appropriate after any other action too, and even before the study of the <s>Veda</s>.
[Reply:] It is said — the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher) has used the word 'atha' with reference to such an inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> as is not possible without the study of the <s>Veda</s>. How? Because a multi-faceted examination of Vedic sentences will take place here. Moreover, we do not here teach a prohibition of the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> before the study of the <s>Veda</s>. For this single sentence will neither prohibit the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> before the study of the <s>Veda</s> nor establish the immediate succession after it. For the sentence would be split thus: one semantic form would be that of prohibiting the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> before the study of the <s>Veda</s>, and another would be that of teaching the immediate succession after it. In one [interpretation], the immediate succession is enjoined with 'having studied the <s>Vedas</s>' being presupposed; in the other, the reverse. And [the principle] 'unity of sentence arises from unity of meaning' will be stated [later]. However, when the <s>Veda</s> has been studied, two [obligations] arise: one must return from the teacher's house, and one must examine the Vedic sentences. Of these, [the meaning is:] 'Do not return from the teacher's house; rather, immediately examine the Vedic sentences' — this is the purport of this teaching.
If so, then the study of the <s>Veda</s> is not [taught as] prior to the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s>. For thus they traditionally state: 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should take the ceremonial bath.' And here, one who, having studied the <s>Veda</s> and being about to take the bath, wishes to inquire into <s>Dharma</s>, would transgress this traditional rule. And a traditional rule is not to be transgressed.
To this it is said: We shall transgress this traditional rule. [For] by not transgressing it, we would render the <s>Veda</s>, which is meaningful, meaningless. For its purpose is clearly seen to be the comprehension of ritual action. And the revered ritualists do not traditionally state that from mere study [of the <s>Veda</s>] there accrues a fruit. And even what they seem to state in that regard — regarding rituals of consecrating substances, [the principle] 'since they serve another purpose, the statement of fruit is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage)' — [the text] will declare it to be <s>arthavāda</s>. Nor is this [verse] prescribing that the bath must immediately follow the study of the <s>Veda</s>. For there is no word here that denotes immediate succession. The absolutive [<s>ktvā</s>] is used to express mere temporal priority, not immediate succession.
Moreover, the purposefulness of study would be contradicted if immediate succession [were meant]. This meaning [of immediate succession] would [only] be by secondary signification. And this bath is not prescribed as having an unseen [transcendent] purpose. Rather, they say by secondary signification that the conclusion of the period of [Vedic] study-and-bath-observance is simultaneous with the completion of Vedic study — 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should take the bath; do not return from the teacher's house' — precisely for the purpose of avoiding [the conclusion that the bath has] an unseen purpose.
Therefore, having first completed the study of the <s>Veda</s> itself, immediately thereafter <s>Dharma</s> should be inquired into — this is the force of the word 'atha.' We do not say that the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> should not be undertaken after any other action too; rather, the meaning of the word 'atha' is: having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should not hastily take the bath; immediately thereafter, <s>Dharma</s> should be inquired into.
The word 'ataḥ' (therefore) indicates a [preceding] accomplishment, with the sense of a reason — just as [one says]: 'This region has peace and abundance; therefore I reside in this region.' Similarly, the study of the <s>Veda</s> is understood as the reason for the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s>; immediately thereafter, <s>Dharma</s> should be inquired into — this is the force of the word 'ataḥ.' For one who has not studied the <s>Veda</s> would be unable to examine Vedic sentences for the purpose of [understanding] <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore (ataḥ), for this reason, one would wish to inquire into <s>Dharma</s> immediately thereafter — this is the meaning of the word 'ataḥ.'
The inquiry for the sake of <s>Dharma</s> is <s>Dharma-jijñāsā</s>. For it is the desire to know it. Now, how is [<s>Dharma</s>] to be inquired into? What is <s>Dharma</s>? What are its characteristics? What are its means of establishment? What are the false means? And what is its ultimate purpose? Of these, 'What is <s>Dharma</s>? What are its characteristics?' is explained by a single <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Dharma</s> is that purpose which is characterized by a Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>).' 'What are its means, what are the false means, and what is its ultimate purpose?' is explained by the remaining [<s>sūtras</s>]. 'Where is the human being the principal [factor], and where is the human being subordinate?' — this <s>sūtra</s>, 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s>,' is the summary of all these propositions.
<s>Dharma</s> is either well-known or not well-known. If it is well-known, there is no need for inquiry. If it is not well-known, all the more [there is no point]. Thus this topic of the inquiry into <s>Dharma</s> would be purposeless.
Or rather, it is purposeful. For many learned persons have divergent views regarding <s>Dharma</s>. Some declare one thing to be <s>Dharma</s>, others declare another. One who proceeds without proper examination, adopting just any [view], would be thwarted and would pursue a wrong course. Therefore, <s>Dharma</s> must be inquired into. For we affirm that it connects a person with the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).
That is now stated —

children.text: codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ // MS_1,1.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is that purpose which is characterized by a Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>). // MS_1,1.2 //

children.text:
codaneti kriyāyāḥ pravartakaṃ vacanam āhuḥ. ācārya[4]{*1/26*}coditaḥ karomīti hi dṛśyate. lakṣyate yena, tal lakṣaṇam. dhūmo lakṣaṇam agner iti hi vadanti. tayā yo lakṣyate, so 'rthaḥ puruṣaṃ niḥśreyasena saṃyunaktīti pratijānīmahe. codanā hi bhūtaṃ bhavantaṃ bhaviṣyantaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vyavahitaṃ viprakṛṣṭam ity evaṃjātīyakam arthaṃ śaknoty avagamayitum, nānyat kiṃcanendriyam.
nanv atathābhūtam apy arthaṃ brūyāc codanā, yathā yatkiṃcana laukikaṃ vacanaṃ nadyās tīre phalāni santīti. tat tathyam api bhavati, vitatham api bhavatīti.
children.translated_text:
By <s>codanā</s> (injunction) they mean a verbal statement that impels one to action. For it is observed [in common usage]: 'Impelled by the teacher, I act.' That by which [something] is characterized is its characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). As they say: 'Smoke is the characteristic of fire.' That which is characterized by it [i.e., by <s>codanā</s>] is the <s>artha</s> (purpose/object). We affirm that it connects a person with the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). For a <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) is capable of making known an object of the following kinds: past, present, future, subtle, concealed, remote — no other sense-faculty [can do this].
[Objection:] But a <s>codanā</s> might state something that is not actually so, just as any ordinary worldly statement [might] — such as 'There are fruits on the bank of the river.' That can be true or it can be false.

children.text:
ucyate - vipratiṣiddham idam abhidhīyate{*1/27*} bravīti ca vitathaṃ ceti. bravītīti ucyate 'vabodhayati, budhyamānasya nimittaṃ bhavatīti. yasmiṃś ca nimittabhūte saty avabudhyate, so 'vabodhayati. yadi ca codanāyāṃ satyām agnihotrāt svargo bhavatīty avagamyate{*1/28*}, katham ucyate na tathā bhavatīti. atha na tathā bhavati{*1/29*}, katham avabudhyate. asantam artham avabudhyata iti vipratiṣiddham.
na ca svargakāmo yajetety{*1/30*} ato vacanāt saṃdigdham avagamyate bhavati vā svargo na vā bhavatīti. na ca niścitam avagamyamānam idaṃ mithyā syāt. yo hi janitvā pradhvaṃsate naitad evam iti, sa mithyāpratyayaḥ. na caiṣa kālāntare puruṣāntare 'vasthāntare deśāntare vā viparyeti. tasmād avitathaḥ. tasmād avitathaḥ.
yat tu laukikaṃ vacanam, tac cet pratyayitāt puruṣād indriyaviṣayaṃ vā, avitatham eva tat. athāpratyayitāt puruṣād anindriyaviṣayaṃ vā, tat{*1/31*} puruṣabuddhiprabhavam apramāṇam. aśakyaṃ hi tat puruṣeṇa jñātum ṛte vacanāt. aparasmāt pauruṣeyād vacanād avagatam iti cet, tad api tenaiva tulyam. naivaṃjātīyakeṣv artheṣu puruṣavacanaṃ prāmāṇyam upaiti, jātyandhānām iva vacanaṃ rūpaviśeṣeṣu.
nanv aviduṣām{*1/32*} upadeśo nāvakalpate. upadiṣṭavantaś ca manvādayaḥ. tasmāt puruṣāḥ{*1/33*} santo viditavantaś{*1/34*} ca. yathā cakṣuṣā rūpam upalabhyata iti darśanād evāvagatam.
ucyate - upadeśo{*1/35*} hi vyāmohād api bhavati. asati vyāmohe vedād api bhavati. api ca pauruṣeyād vacanād evam ayaṃ puruṣaḥ vedeti bhavati pratyayaḥ, na evam ayam artha iti. viplavate khalv api kaścit puruṣakṛtād vacanāt pratyayaḥ. na tu vedavacanasya mithyātve kiṃcana pramāṇam asti.
nanu sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati{*1/36*}. pauruṣeyaṃ vacanaṃ vitatham upalabhya vacanasāmānyād{*1/37*} vedavacanaṃ mithyety anumīyate{*1/38*}.
na, anyatvāt. na hy anyasya vitathabhāve{*1/39*} 'nyasya vaitathyaṃ bhavitum arhati{*1/40*}, anyatvād eva. na hi devadattasya śyāmatve yajñadattasyāpi śyāmatvaṃ bhavitum arhati. api ca puruṣavacanasādharmyād vedavacanaṃ vitatham{*1/41*} ity anumānam{*1/42*}. pratyakṣas tu vedavacane{*1/43*} pratyayaḥ. na cānumānaṃ pratyakṣavirodhi{*1/44*} pramāṇaṃ bhavati{*1/45*}. tasmāc codanālakṣaṇo 'rthaḥ{*1/46*} śreyaskaraḥ. evaṃ tarhi śreyaskaro jijñāsitavyaḥ. kiṃ dharmajijñāsayā? ucyate - ya eva śreyaskaraḥ, sa eva dharmaśabdenocyate. katham avagamyate{*1/47*}? yo hi yāgam anutiṣṭhati, taṃ dhārmika iti samācakṣate. yaś ca yasya kartā, sa tena vyapadiśyate{*1/48*}, yathā pācako lāvaka iti. tena yaḥ puruṣaṃ niḥśreyasena saṃyunakti, sa eva{*1/49*} dharmaśabdenocyate. na kevalaṃ loke, vede 'pi -
yajñena yajñam ayajanta devāḥ/
tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan//
children.translated_text:
It is replied: This is self-contradictory — 'it speaks and yet speaks falsely.' 'It speaks' means 'it makes known, it becomes the cause of understanding.' And that which, being the cause, brings about understanding — that 'makes known.' Now, if when the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is real, one understands that 'from the <s>Agnihotra</s> arises heaven,' how can one say 'it is not so'? And if it is not so, how does one understand? To say 'one understands a non-existent thing' — this is self-contradictory.
Moreover, from the statement 'let the one desiring heaven sacrifice' — from this injunction, what is understood is not doubtful, [as if one would think] 'heaven may or may not result.' Nor can that which is understood with certainty be false. For a false cognition is one that, having arisen, is subsequently sublated [by the judgment] 'this is not so.' But this [Vedic cognition] is never reversed at another time, in another person, in another condition, or in another place. Therefore it is not false. Therefore it is not false.
As for worldly speech: if it comes from a trustworthy person or concerns a sense-perceptible object, it too is unfailing. But if it comes from an untrustworthy person or concerns a non-sense-perceptible object, it is born of human intellect and is not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). For that [supersensible matter] cannot be known by a human being without [Vedic] speech. If one says 'it is known from another human utterance' — that [utterance] too is subject to the same [defect]. In matters of this kind, human speech does not attain the status of a valid means of knowledge, just as the speech of those born blind [has no authority] regarding distinctions of color.
But [an objector says:] surely instruction is not possible for the ignorant, and <s>Manu</s> and others have given instruction; therefore, being persons, they knew. Just as it is known from direct experience itself that form is perceived by the eye.
It is replied: Instruction can also arise from delusion. In the absence of delusion, it can also arise from the <s>Veda</s> itself. Moreover, from human speech the cognition arises that 'this person knows the <s>Veda</s>' — not that 'such is the nature of the thing.' For some cognition arising from man-made speech is indeed overturned. But there is no evidence whatsoever for the falsity of Vedic speech.
[Objection:] Perhaps there will be an inference from general similarity. Having observed that human speech is false, one infers by the general character of speech that Vedic speech too is false.
[Reply:] No, because of their difference. For the falsity of one does not entail the falsity of another, precisely because they are different — just as the dark complexion of <s>Devadatta</s> does not entail the dark complexion of <s>Yajñadatta</s>. Moreover, the inference that Vedic speech is false based on similarity with human speech is [only] an inference. But the cognition regarding Vedic speech is direct (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). And an inference contradicting direct experience is not a valid means of knowledge. Therefore, the object characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is conducive to the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>). If so, then that which is conducive to the highest good should be inquired into. What is the point of inquiring into <s>Dharma</s>? It is replied: That very thing which is conducive to the highest good is denoted by the word '<s>Dharma</s>.' How is this known? He who performs a sacrifice is called '<s>dhārmika</s>' (a righteous person). And one who is the agent of something is designated by that [action], as in 'cook' or 'harvester.' Therefore, that which unites a person with the highest good — that alone is denoted by the word '<s>Dharma</s>.' Not only in worldly usage, but in the <s>Veda</s> too: 'By sacrifice the gods sacrificed the sacrifice; those were the first <s>dharmas</s>.'

children.text:
ity{*1/50*} yajatiśabdavācyam{*1/51*} eva dharmaṃ{*1/52*} samānanti. ubhayam iha codanayā lakṣyate, artho 'narthaś ca. ko 'rthaḥ? yo niḥśreyasāya jyotiṣṭomādiḥ. ko 'narthaḥ? yaḥ pratyavāyāya śyeno vajra iṣur ity evamādiḥ. tatrānartho dharma ukto mā bhūd ity arthagrahaṇam{*1/53*}. kathaṃ punar asāv anarthaḥ? hiṃsā hi sā, sā ca{*1/54*} pratiṣiddhā{*1/55*}. kathaṃ punar asāv anarthaḥ kartavyatayopadiśyate{*1/56*}? ucyate - naiva śyenādayaḥ kartavyatayā vijñāyante. yo hi hiṃsitum icchet, tasyāyam abhyupāya iti hi teṣām upadeśaḥ. śyenenābhicaran yajeteti{*1/57*} hi samāmananti, nābhicaritavyam iti.
nanv aśaktam idaṃ sūtram imāv arthāv abhivaditum, codanā[6]{*1/58*}lakṣaṇo dharmo nendriyādilakṣaṇaḥ, arthaś ca dharmo nānartha iti. ekaṃ hīdaṃ vākyam. tad evaṃ sati bhidyeta.
ucyate - yatra vākyād evārtho{*1/59*} 'vagamyate, tatraivam. tat tu vaidikeṣu, na sūtreṣu. anyato 'vagate 'rthe sūtram evamartham{*1/60*} ity avagamyate, tena caikadeśaḥ sūtryata iti{*1/61*} sūtram. tatra bhinnayor eva vākyayor imāv ekadeśāv ity avagantavyam. athavā arthasya sataś codanālakṣaṇasya dharmatvam ucyata{*1/62*} ity ekārtham{*1/63*} eveti.
children.translated_text:
Thus they identify <s>Dharma</s> with what is denoted by the verb 'to sacrifice' (<s>yajati</s>). Both are indicated here by injunction (<s>codanā</s>) — the beneficial (<s>artha</s>) and the harmful (<s>anartha</s>). What is the beneficial? That which serves the highest good, such as the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like. What is the harmful? That which leads to downfall, such as the <s>Śyena</s>, <s>Vajra</s>, <s>Iṣu</s> (Arrow), and similar [rites]. The specification '<s>artha</s>' (beneficial object) is [added] lest the harmful be [mistakenly] called <s>Dharma</s>. But how is that harmful? For it involves <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence), which is prohibited. But how is that harmful thing taught as something to be done? It is replied: The <s>Śyena</s> and similar rites are not at all understood as obligatory duties. The instruction concerning them is: 'This is the means for one who wishes to harm.' For they prescribe: 'One who practices sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Śyena</s>' — not 'one should practice sorcery.'
[Objection:] But this <s>sūtra</s> is incapable of conveying both meanings — that <s>Dharma</s> is characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>), not by the senses and the like, and that <s>Dharma</s> is the beneficial, not the harmful. For this is a single sentence; if so, it would have to be split.
[Reply:] That [objection applies] where the meaning is understood from the sentence alone — that is the case with Vedic [passages], not with <s>sūtras</s>. When the meaning is understood from elsewhere, the <s>sūtra</s> is understood as having that meaning; and because a portion [of the meaning] is formulated [in compact form], it is called a <s>sūtra</s>. Therefore, these two portions should be understood as belonging to two distinct sentences. Alternatively, the <s>Dharma</s>-hood of the existent object characterized by injunction is being stated — thus it is a single meaning after all.

children.translated_text: The examination of its means [of knowledge] (<s>tasya nimittaparīṣṭiḥ</s>) || MS 1.1.3 ||

children.text:
uktam asmābhiś codanānimittaṃ dharmasya jñānam iti. tat pratijñāmātreṇoktam. idānīṃ tasya nimittaṃ parīkṣiṣyāmahe, kiṃ codanaivotānyad{*1/64*} apīti. tasmān na tāvan niścīyate codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharma iti.
tad ucyate -
children.translated_text:
We have stated that the knowledge of <s>Dharma</s> is caused by injunction (<s>codanā</s>). That was stated merely as a thesis. Now we shall examine its means — whether injunction alone [is the means] or whether there is something else as well. Therefore, the statement that the object characterized by injunction is <s>Dharma</s> is not yet established.
That is addressed [as follows] —

children.text: satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tat pratyakṣam animittam, vidyamānopalaṃbhanatvāt // MS_1,1.4 //
children.translated_text: When there is a connection (<s>saṃprayoga</s>) of the senses of a person with an existing [object], the cognition that arises — that is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>); it is not a means [of knowing <s>Dharma</s>], because it apprehends only what is [presently] existing. || MS 1.1.4 ||

children.text:
idaṃ parīkṣyate - pratyakṣaṃ tāvad animittam. kiṃ kāraṇam? evaṃlakṣaṇakaṃ hi tat - satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tat pratyakṣam. satīndriyārthasaṃbandhe yā puruṣasya buddhir jāyate, tat pratyakṣam. bhaviṣyaṃś caiṣo 'rtho na jñānakāle 'sti{*1/65*}. sataś caitad upalambhanam, nāsataḥ. ataḥ pratyakṣam animittam.
buddhir vā janma vā saṃnikarṣo veti naiṣāṃ kasyacid avadhāraṇārtham etat sūtram. satīndriyārthasaṃprayoge, nāsatīty etāvad avadhāryate. anekasminn avadhāryamāṇe bhidyeta vākyam. pratyakṣapūrvakatvāc cānumānopamānārthāpattīnām apy akāraṇatvam{*1/66*}. abhāvo 'pi nāsti, yataḥ -
children.translated_text:
This is being examined: Perception, to begin with, is not a means [of knowing <s>Dharma</s>]. What is the reason? For its definition is as follows: 'When there is a connection of the senses of a person with an existing [object], the cognition that arises — that is perception.' When there is contact between the senses and an existing object, the cognition that arises in a person — that is perception. And this object [i.e., the result of <s>Dharma</s>] is future and does not exist at the time of cognition. Moreover, this [perception] apprehends what exists, not what does not exist. Therefore, perception is not a means [of knowing <s>Dharma</s>].
[The <s>sūtra</s> says] 'cognition' or 'arising' or 'connection' — this <s>sūtra</s> is not intended to determine [the meaning of] any one of these [specifically]. What is determined is only this: 'when there is a connection of the senses with the object, not when there is none' — just this much is ascertained. If multiple things were being determined, the sentence would have to be split. And because inference (<s>anumāna</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), and postulation (<s>arthāpatti</s>) are based on prior perception, their incapacity [to know <s>Dharma</s>] is also [established]. Nor is absence [a means of knowing <s>Dharma</s>], because —

children.text: autpattikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya jñānam upadeśo 'vyatirekaś cārthe 'nupalabdhe, tat pramāṇaṃ bādarāyaṇasya, anapekṣatvāt // MS_1,1.5 //
children.translated_text: The relation of a word with its meaning is innate (<s>autpattika</s>); the knowledge of that [relation] is instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>); and there is no deviation [of word from meaning] regarding an object that is not [otherwise] apprehended — that is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) according to <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because [Vedic words] are independent [of any other source]. || MS 1.1.5 ||

children.text:
autpattika iti nityaṃ brūmaḥ. utpattir hi{*1/67*} bhāva ucyate lakṣaṇayā. aviyuktaḥ śabdārthayor bhāvaḥ saṃbandhena{*1/68*}, notpannayoḥ paścāt saṃbandhaḥ. autpattikaḥ śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasyāgnihotrādilakṣaṇasya dharmasya nimittaṃ pratyakṣādibhir anavagatasya{*1/69*}. katham? upadeśo hi bhavati. upadeśa iti viśiṣṭasya śabdasyoccāraṇam. avyatirekaś ca bhavati tasya{*1/70*} jñānasya. na hi tad utpannaṃ{*1/71*} jñānaṃ viparyeti. yac ca nāma jñānam utpannaṃ{*1/72*} na viparyeti, na tac chakyate vaktuṃ naitad evam iti, yathā vijñāyate{*1/73*}, na tathā bhavati, yathaitan na vijñāyate, tathaitad iti. anyad asya hṛdaye, anyad vāci syāt. evaṃ vadato viruddham idam avagamyata{*1/74*} asti nāsti ceti{*1/75*}. tasmāt tat pramāṇam, anapekṣatvāt. na hy evaṃ sati pratyayāntaram apekṣitavyaṃ puruṣāntaraṃ vā. svayaṃpratyayo{*1/76*} hi asau. bādarāyaṇasyedaṃ{*1/77*} mataṃ kīrtyate bādarāyaṇaṃ pūjayituṃ nātmīyaṃ mataṃ paryudasitum.
vṛttikāras tv anyathemaṃ granthaṃ varṇayāṃcakāra tasya nimittaparīṣṭir ity evamādim - na parīkṣitavyaṃ nimittam. pratyakṣādīni hi prasiddhāni pramāṇāni tadantargataṃ ca śāstram. atas tad api na parīkṣitavyam.
nanu{*1/78*} vyabhicārāt parīkṣitavyaṃ nimittam{*1/79*}. śuktikā hi rajatavat prakāśate yatas, tena pratyakṣaṃ vyabhicarati, tanmūlatvāc cānumānādīny api. tatrāparīkṣya pravartamāno 'rthād vihanyeta anarthaṃ cāpnuyāt kadācit.
naitad evam. yat pratyakṣam, [8]{*1/80*} na tad vyabhicarati. yad vyabhicarati, na tat pratyakṣam. kiṃ tarhi pratyakṣam?
tatsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma sat pratyakṣam{*1/81*}.
yadviṣayaṃ jñānam, tenaiva saṃprayoga indriyāṇāṃ puruṣasya buddhijanma sat pratyakṣam. yad anyaviṣayaṃ jñānam anyasaṃprayoge bhavati, na tat pratyakṣam. kathaṃ punar idam avagamyata idam tatsaṃprayoge{*1/82*}, idam anyasaṃprayoga{*1/83*} iti. yan nānyasaṃprayoge, tat tatsaṃprayoge. etadviparītam anyasaṃprayoga iti. kathaṃ jñāyate{*1/84*}, yadā hi śuktikāyām api rajataṃ manyamano rajatasaṃnikṛṣṭaṃ me cakṣur iti manyate? bādhakaṃ hi yatra jñānam utpadyate naitad evam, mithyā-jñānam idam iti, tad anyasaṃprayoge, viparītaṃ tatsaṃprayoga iti. prāg bādhakajñānotpatteḥ katham avagamyate, yadā na tatkāle saṃyagjñānasya mithyājñānasya ca kaścid viśeṣaḥ? yadā{*1/85*} kṣudādibhir{*1/86*} upahataṃ mano bhavati, indriyaṃ vā timirādibhiḥ, saukṣmyādibhir vā bāhyo viṣayaḥ, tato mithyājñānam, anupahateṣu saṃyagjñānam. indriyamanorthasaṃnikarṣo hi jñānasya{*1/87*} hetuḥ, asati tasmin ajñānāt{*1/88*}. tadantargato doṣo mithyājñānasya hetuḥ. duṣṭeṣu hi jñānaṃ mithyā bhavati. katham avagamyate? doṣāpagame saṃpratipattidarśanāt. kathaṃ duṣṭāduṣṭāvagama iti cet, prayatnenānvicchanto na ced doṣam upalabhemahi{*1/89*}, pramāṇābhāvād aduṣṭam iti manyemahi. tasmād yasya ca duṣṭaṃ karaṇaṃ yatra ca mithyeti pratyayaḥ, sa evāsamīcīnaḥ pratyayo nānya iti.
nanu sarva eva nirālambanaḥ svapnavat pratyayaḥ. pratyayasya hi nirālambanatā svabhāva upalakṣitaḥ{*1/90*} svapne. jāgrato 'pi stambha iti vā kuḍyam{*1/91*} iti vā pratyaya eva bhavati. tasmāt so 'pi nirālambanaḥ.
ucyate - stambha iti jāgrato buddhiḥ supariniścitā, kathaṃ viparyasiṣyati{*1/92*}? svapne 'py evam eva supariniścitāsīt prāk{*1/93*} prabodhanāt{*1/94*}. na tatra kaścid viśeṣa iti cet{*1/95*}, na, svapne viparyayadarśanād aviparya[9]{*1/96*}yāc cetarasmin. tatsāmānyād itaratrāpi bhaviṣyatīti cet. yadi pratyayatvāt svapnapratyayasya mithyābhāvaḥ, jāgratpratyayasyāpi bhavitum{*1/97*} arhati. atha pratītis tathābhāvasya hetuḥ{*1/98*}, na śakyate pratyayād ayaṃ{*1/99*} anya iti vaditum{*1/100*}. anyatas tu{*1/101*} svapnapratyayasya mithyābhāvo viparyayād avagataḥ. kuta iti cet. sanidrasya manaso daurbalyān nidrā mithyābhāvasya hetuḥ svapnādau svapnānte ca. suṣuptasya pratyayābhāva eva{*1/102*}. acetayan eva hi suṣupta ity ucyate. tasmāj jāgrataḥ pratyayo na{*1/103*} mithyeti. nanu jāgrato 'pi karaṇadoṣaḥ syāt? yadi syāt, avagamyeta. svapnadarśanakāle 'pi nāvagamyata iti cet. tan na{*1/104*}. prabuddho hy avagacchati - nidrākrāntaṃ me mana āsīd iti.
śūnyas tu. katham? arthajñānayor ākārabhedaṃ nopalabhāmahe. pratyakṣā ca no buddhiḥ. atas tadbhinnam artharūpaṃ nāma na kiṃcid astīti paśyāmaḥ.
syād{*1/105*} etad evam, yady arthākārā buddhiḥ syāt. nirākārā tu no buddhiḥ, ākāravān bāhyo 'rthaḥ.
sa hi{*1/106*} bahirdeśasaṃbaddhaḥ pratyakṣam upalabhyate. arthaviṣayā hi pratyakṣabuddhir na buddhyantaraviṣayā. kṣaṇikā hi sā na buddhyantarakālam avasthāsyata iti{*1/107*}. utpadyamānaivāsau jñāyate jñāpayati cārthāntaraṃ pradīpavad iti yady{*1/108*} ucyeta{*1/109*}, tan na. na hy ajñāte 'rthe kaścid buddhim upalabhate, jñāte tv anumānād avagacchati. tatra yaugapadyam anupapannam.
nanu utpannāyām eva buddhāv artho jñāta{*1/110*} ity ucyate nānutpannāyām. ataḥ pūrvaṃ buddhir utpadyate, paścāj jñāto 'rthaḥ. nanu utpannāyām eva buddhāv artho jñāta ity ucyate nānutpannāyām. ataḥ pūrvaṃ buddhir utpadyate, paścāj jñāto 'rthaḥ. satyam. pūrvaṃ buddhir utpadyate, na [10]{*1/111*} tu pūrvaṃ jñāyate. bhavati hi kadācid etat, yaj jñāto{*1/112*} 'rthaḥ so 'jñāta ity ucyate. na ca arthavyapadeśam antareṇa buddheḥ rūpopalambhanam{*1/113*}. tasmān nāvyapadeśyā{*1/114*} buddhir, avyapadeśyaṃ ca naḥ pratyakṣam{*1/115*}. tasmād apratyakṣā buddhiḥ.
api ca kāmam ekarūpatve buddher evābhāvaḥ, na tv{*1/116*} arthasya pratyakṣasya sataḥ{*1/117*}. na caikarūpyam. nirākārām{*1/118*} eva hi buddhim anumimīmahe, sākāraṃ cārthaṃ pratyakṣam evāvagacchāmaḥ. tasmād arthālambanaḥ pratyayaḥ.
api ca niyatanimittas tantuṣv evopādīyamāneṣu paṭapratyayaḥ. itarathā tantūpādāne{*1/119*} 'pi kadācid ghaṭabuddhir avikalendriyasya syāt. na caivam asti. tasmān{*1/120*} na nirālambanaḥ pratyayaḥ. ato na vyabhicarati pratyakṣam.
anumānaṃ jñātasaṃbandhasya ekadeśadarśanād ekadeśāntare 'saṃnikṛṣṭe 'rthe buddhiḥ. tat tu dvividhaṃ pratyakṣatodṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ ca. tatra{*1/121*} pratyakṣatodṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ yathā dhūmākṛtidarśanād agnyākṛtivijñānam. sāmānyatoḍṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ ca yathā devadattasya gatipūrvikaṃ deśāntaraprāptim upalabhyāditye 'pi{*1/122*} gatismaraṇam.
śāstraṃ śabdavijñānād asaṃnikṛṣṭe 'rthe vijñānam.
upamānam api sādṛśyam asaṃnikṛṣṭe 'rthe buddhim utpādayati, yathā gavayadarśanaṃ gosmaraṇasya.
arthāpattir api dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vārtho 'nyathā nopapadyata ity arthakalpanā, yathā jīvato devadattasya{*1/123*} gṛhābhāvadarśanena bahirbhāvasya adṛṣṭasya kalpanā.
abhāvo 'pi pramāṇābhāvo nāstīty asyārthasyāsaṃnikṛṣṭasya. tasmāt prasiddhatvān na parīkṣitavyaṃ nimittam.
nanu pratyakṣādīny anyāni bhavantu nāma pramāṇāni, śabdas tu na pramāṇam. kutaḥ -
animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt{*1/124*}.
animittam apramāṇaṃ śabdaḥ. yo hy upalambhanaviṣayo [11]{*1/125*} nopalabhyate, sa nāsti, yathā śaśasya viṣāṇam. upalambhanāni{*1/126*} cendriyāṇi paśvādīnām. na ca paśukāmeṣṭyanantaraṃ paśava upalabhyante. ato neṣṭiḥ paśuphalā. karmakāle ca karmaphalena{*1/127*} bhavitavyam. yatkālaṃ hi
mardanam, tatkālaṃ mardanasukham.
kālāntare phalaṃ dāsyatīti cet, na, na kālāntare phalam iṣṭer ity avagacchāmaḥ. kutaḥ? yadā tāvad asau vidyamānā āsīt, tadā phalaṃ na dattavatī. yadā phalam utpadyate, tadāsau nāsti. asatī ca kathaṃ dāsyati? api ca karmakāla eva phalaṃ śrūyate - yāgaḥ karaṇam iti vākyād{*1/128*} avagamyate, karaṇaṃ ced utpannam, kāryeṇa bhavitavyam iti{*1/129*}. pratyakṣaṃ ca phalakāraṇam anyad upalabhāmahe{*1/130*}. na ca dṛṣṭe kāraṇe saty adṛṣṭaṃ kalpayituṃ śakyate{*1/131*}, pramāṇābhāvāt. evaṃ dṛṣṭāpacārasya vedasya svargādy api phalaṃ na bhavatīti manyāmahe.
dṛṣṭaviruddham api bhavati kiṃcid vaidikaṃ{*1/132*} vacanam. pātracayanaṃ vidhāyāha - sa eṣa yajñāyudhī yajamāno 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokaṃ yātīti{*1/133*} pratyakṣaṃ śarīraṃ{*1/134*} vyapadiśati. na ca tat svargaṃ lokaṃ yāti. pratyakṣaṃ hi tad dahyate. na caiṣa yātīti vidhiśabdaḥ. evaṃjātīyakaṃ ca pramāṇaviruddhaṃ vacanam apramāṇam ambuni majjanty alābūni, grāvānaḥ plavanta iti{*1/135*} yathā. tatsāmānyād agnihotrādicodanāsv{*1/136*} apy anāśvāsaḥ. tasmān na codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ.
autpattikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya jñānam{*1/137*}.
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. apauruṣeyaḥ śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasyāgnihotrādilakṣaṇasyārthasya{*1/138*} jñānaṃ pratyakṣādibhir{*1/139*} anavagamyamānasya. tathā ca{*1/140*} codanālakṣaṇaḥ saṃyakpratyaya{*1/141*} iti. pauruṣeye hi sati saṃbandhe{*1/142*} yaḥ pratyayaḥ, tasya mithyābhāva āśaṅkyeta. parapratyayo [12]{*1/143*} hi tadā{*1/144*} syāt. atha śabde bruvati kathaṃ mithyeti? na hi tadānīm anyataḥ puruṣād avagamaḥ{*1/145*}. bravītīty{*1/146*} ucyata avabodhayati{*1/147*}, budhyamānasya nimittam bhavatīti{*1/148*}. śabde cen{*1/149*} nimittabhūte{*1/150*} svayam avabudhyate{*1/151*}, kathaṃ vipralabdhaṃ brūyān naitad evam iti. na cāsya codanā syād vā na veti sāṃśayikaṃ pratyayam utpādayati. na ca mithyaitad iti kālāntare deśāntare 'vasthāntare puruṣāntare vā punar avyapadeśyaḥ pratyayo{*1/152*} bhavati. yo 'py anyapratyayaviparyāsaṃ{*1/153*} dṛṣṭvātrāpi viparyasiṣyatīty ānumānikaḥ pratyaya utpadyate, so 'py anena pratyakṣeṇa pratyayena{*1/154*} virudhyamāno bādhyate. tasmāc codanālakṣaṇa eva dharmaḥ.
syād etad evam{*1/155*} - naiva śabdasyārthenāsti{*1/156*} saṃbandhaḥ, kuto 'sya pauruṣeyatā veti. katham? syāc ced arthena saṃbandhaḥ, kṣuramodakaśabdoccāraṇe mukhasya pāṭanapūraṇe syātām,

'<s>Autpattika</s>' (innate) means eternal — this is what we assert. For '<s>utpatti</s>' (origination) is used by secondary signification to mean 'existence' (<s>bhāva</s>). The existence of the relation between word and meaning is inseparable [from them]; the relation does not [arise] subsequently between [entities] that were [first] produced [independently]. The relation of a word with its meaning is innate (<s>autpattika</s>) — it is the means of knowing that <s>Dharma</s> characterized by the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, which is not apprehended through perception and other [ordinary means]. How? Because there is instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>). '<s>Upadeśa</s>' means the utterance of a specific word. And there is no deviation of that cognition [from the object]. For a cognition that has arisen does not become reversed. And that which is a cognition that, having arisen, is not reversed — one cannot say of it 'this is not so; what is known is not the case; what is not known is the case.' Otherwise, one's heart would be at variance with one's speech. Of one speaking thus, this contradictory [state] is understood: 'it exists and does not exist.' Therefore, it is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), because it is independent. For in this case, no other cognition need be resorted to, nor [the testimony of] another person. For it [the Vedic word] is self-certifying. This view of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> is mentioned in order to honor <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, not to set aside [the author's] own view.
The <s>Vṛttikāra</s> (commentator), however, has explained this passage differently, beginning with 'the examination of its means' — the means need not be examined. For perception and the like are well-known valid means of knowledge, and scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) is included among them. Therefore, that too need not be examined.
[Objection:] Surely the means must be examined because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). For a shell gleams like silver; from that, perception deviates; and since inference and the like are rooted in [perception], they too [deviate]. One who proceeds without examination would be thwarted by reality and might sometimes attain an undesirable result.
[Reply:] This is not so. What is perception does not deviate. What deviates is not perception. What then is perception?
'When there is contact (<s>saṃprayoga</s>) of a person's senses [with the object of that very cognition], the cognition that arises with regard to an existing [object] — that is perception.'
The cognition whose object is a certain thing — when there is contact of the person's senses with that very [object], the cognition that arises regarding an existing [object] — that is perception. A cognition whose object is one thing but which arises from contact with another — that is not perception. But how is it known which is 'contact with its own object' and which is 'contact with another object'? That which does not [arise from] contact with another is [from] contact with its own [object]. The reverse is contact with another. How is [the difference] known — for when one, regarding even a shell, thinks 'it is silver' and believes 'my eye is in contact with silver'? Where a sublating cognition arises — 'this is not so, this is a false cognition' — that is [from] contact with another; the reverse is contact with its own [object]. But prior to the arising of the sublating cognition, how is it known, when at that time there is no difference between a correct cognition and a false cognition? When the mind is impaired by hunger and the like, or the sense-organ by disorders such as <s>timira</s> (visual defect), or the external object is [imperceptible] due to subtlety and the like — then there is false cognition; when these are unimpaired, there is correct cognition. For the contact of sense-organ, mind, and object is the cause of cognition; in the absence of that, there is no cognition. A defect within that [contact] is the cause of false cognition. For when these [factors] are defective, the cognition is false. How is this known? Because when the defect is removed, concordant cognition is observed. If one asks: how is the defective-versus-non-defective [state] known? — if, searching with effort, we do not perceive a defect, we consider it non-defective due to the absence of evidence [of defect]. Therefore, only that person whose instrument [of cognition] is defective and in whose case there is the judgment 'this is false' — only that is an incorrect cognition, not any other.
[Buddhist objection:] But surely every cognition is without a real object (<s>nirālambana</s>), like a dream. For the objectlessness of cognition has been observed as its nature in dreams. Even for one who is awake, the cognition 'this is a pillar' or 'this is a wall' is just a cognition [without external reality]. Therefore, it too is without a real object.
[Reply:] It is said — The cognition of one who is awake, 'this is a pillar,' is well-ascertained; how will it be reversed? [Objection:] In a dream too, it was equally well-ascertained before awakening. There is no difference. [Reply:] No, because in dreams, reversal is observed, but not in the other [waking state]. [Objection:] By the general similarity [between them], it should be so in the other case too. [Reply:] If the falsity of dream-cognition is due to its being a cognition [in general], then the waking cognition too ought to be [false]. But if the experience is the cause of [the thing's] being-as-such, then one cannot say 'this [waking cognition] is different from that [dream].' However, the falsity of dream-cognition is understood from another source — namely, from [subsequent] reversal. From what [source]? From the weakness of the mind that is drowsy — sleep is the cause of the falsity in dreams, both at the beginning and end of the dream. In deep sleep, there is simply the absence of cognition. For one who is unconscious is said to be in deep sleep. Therefore, the cognition of one who is awake is not false. [Objection:] But might there not be a defect of the instrument even for one who is awake? [Reply:] If there were, it would be perceived. [Objection:] Even at the time of dream-experience, it is not perceived. [Reply:] That is not [a valid analogy]. For upon awakening, one knows: 'My mind was overpowered by sleep.'
[Buddhist (Vijñānavādin):] But [everything is] void. How? We do not perceive any difference in form between the object and the cognition. And our cognition is directly experienced. Therefore we see that there is no object-form different from it [the cognition].
[Reply:] This would be so if the cognition had the form of the object. But our cognition is formless; it is the external object that has form.
For that [object] is directly perceived as connected with an external location. Perceptual cognition has an object as its content, not another cognition. For that [cognition] is momentary and would not endure for the duration of another cognition. If one says 'it is known even as it arises and also illuminates another object, like a lamp' — that is not so. For no one perceives a cognition without having [first] known the object; rather, one understands [the cognition] afterwards, through inference, when the object is known. Therefore, simultaneity [of knowing the cognition and the object] is untenable.
[Buddhist:] But we say that the object is known precisely when the cognition has arisen, not when it has not yet arisen. Therefore, the cognition arises first, and the object is known afterwards. [Reply:] True, the cognition arises first; but it is not known first. For it sometimes happens that an object is called 'known' which is [simultaneously] called 'unknown.' And without reference to an object, the form of the cognition cannot be apprehended. Therefore, cognition is not independently describable, and what is independently indescribable is — in our view — not directly perceived. Therefore, cognition is not directly perceived [independently].
Moreover, even granted the uniformity of cognition, it would [at most] be the non-existence [of the cognition itself, not of the object] — but not of the object, which is directly perceived and existing. Nor is there uniformity [between cognition and object]. For we infer the cognition as formless, and we directly perceive the object as having form. Therefore, cognition has a [real] object as its basis.
Moreover, the cognition of cloth is produced from a specific cause — only when threads are employed. Otherwise, even from the employment of threads, a cognition of a pot would sometimes arise in a person with unimpaired senses. But this is not the case. Therefore, cognition is not without a [real] object. Hence, perception does not deviate.
Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is the cognition of an object that is not directly connected [with the senses], from the observation of one part of a relation whose [terms] are known. It is twofold: based on a relation observed through direct perception, and based on a relation observed through general principle. Of these, inference based on a directly perceived relation is, for example, the knowledge of the form of fire from seeing the form of smoke. Inference based on a generally observed relation is, for example, when one perceives that <s>Devadatta</s> has arrived at a different place through prior locomotion, and then remembers locomotion [as applying] to the sun as well.
Scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) is the cognition of an object not directly connected [with the senses], arising from the knowledge of words.
Analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) too — similarity produces cognition of an object not directly connected [with the senses], as when the sight of a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) evokes the memory of a cow.
Postulation (<s>arthāpatti</s>) too is the supposition of a meaning when a seen or heard fact cannot be explained otherwise — as when, from observing the absence from home of <s>Devadatta</s> who is alive, one postulates his being outside, which is unseen.
Non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) too is a means of knowledge — the absence of evidence [is the means of knowing] the meaning 'it does not exist,' which is not directly connected [with the senses]. Therefore, since these are well-known, the means need not be examined.
[Objection:] Granted that perception and the like are valid means of knowledge; but verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is not a valid means of knowledge. Why?
'Because it is without a cause, since what exists is [ordinarily] perceived.'
Verbal testimony is not a valid means of knowledge and is without a cause [for validity]. For that which is a possible object of perception but is not perceived — that does not exist, just as the horn of a hare [does not exist]. And the senses are the means of perception for animals and the like. And animals are not perceived after the <s>Paśukāmeṣṭi</s> sacrifice [which promises them as a result]. Therefore, the sacrifice does not have animals as its fruit. And the fruit of an action must [exist] at the time of the action. For at the time of pressing, there is pressing-pleasure.
[Objection:] If one says 'it will give the fruit at a later time' — [Reply:] No, we do not understand that the sacrifice gives its fruit at a later time. Why? When the sacrifice was still existing [being performed], it did not give the fruit. When the fruit arises, the sacrifice no longer exists. And how can what does not exist give [anything]? Moreover, the fruit is stated [in the Veda] as [arising] at the very time of the action — from the sentence 'the sacrifice is the instrument,' it is understood that if the instrument has been produced, the effect must follow. And we perceive through direct experience another [worldly] cause of the fruit. And when a seen cause exists, an unseen [cause] cannot be postulated, due to the absence of evidence. Thus we consider that even for the <s>Veda</s>, which has been observed to deviate [in some instances], there is no fruit such as heaven and the like.
Some Vedic statements are even contradicted by direct experience. After prescribing the laying of the fire-pans, [the <s>Veda</s>] says: 'This sacrificer, equipped with sacrificial implements, goes straight to the heavenly world' — it refers to the visible body. But that [body] does not go to heaven. For it is visibly burned. Nor is 'he goes' a prescriptive word [here]. And a statement contradicted by a valid means of knowledge is not itself a valid means of knowledge — just as [the statement] 'gourds sink in water, stones float.' By general similarity with such [statements], there is no confidence in the injunctions regarding the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like either. Therefore, the object characterized by injunction is not <s>Dharma</s>.
[The <s>sūtra</s> replies:] 'The relation of a word with its meaning is innate; its knowledge [is therefore valid].'
The word 'tu' (but) distinguishes [this] from the [opposing] position. The relation of a word with its meaning is not made by any person (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) — it is the knowledge of that object characterized by the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, which is not apprehended by perception and other [means]. And thus the cognition characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is correct. For if the relation [between word and meaning] were man-made, then the cognition [derived from it] might be suspected of falsity. For it would then be dependent on another [person's authority]. But when the word itself speaks, how can it be false? For at that time, there is no understanding from any other person. 'It speaks' means 'it makes known, it becomes the cause for one who is understanding.' If the word, being the cause, one understands by oneself — how could one say one has been deceived, that 'this is not so'? Nor does the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) produce a doubtful cognition — '[the result] may or may not [follow].' Nor is there ever — at any other time, in any other place, in any other condition, or in any other person — a non-describable cognition [that would say] 'this is false.' And even the inferential cognition that arises [in someone] who, having seen the reversal of other cognitions, [thinks] 'this [Vedic cognition] too will be reversed' — that [inference] too, being contradicted by this direct perceptual cognition, is sublated. Therefore, <s>Dharma</s> is precisely that which is characterized by injunction.
[Objection:] This might be so — but the word simply has no relation with any meaning at all; so the question of whether [that relation] is man-made does not even arise. How? If there were a relation with a meaning, then upon uttering the words 'razor' and 'sweetmeat,' there would be cutting of the mouth and filling [of the mouth] respectively.

yadi{*1/157*} saṃśleṣalakṣaṇaṃ saṃbandham{*1/158*} abhipretyocyate. kāryakāraṇanimittanaimittikāśrayāśrayibhāvayaunādayas{*1/159*} tu saṃbandhāḥ śabdasyānupapannā eveti.
ucyate - yo 'tra vyapadeśyaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, tam ekaṃ na vyapadiśati bhavān, pratyayyasya pratyāyakasya ca yaḥ saṃjñāsaṃjñilakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandhas tam{*1/160*} iti. āha - yadi pratyāyakaḥ śabdaḥ, prathamaśrutaḥ kiṃ na pratyāyayati? ucyate - sarvatra no darśanaṃ pramāṇam. pratyāyaketi hi pratyayaṃ dṛṣṭvāvagacchāmaḥ, na prathamaśruta iti prathamaśravaṇe pratyayam adṛṣṭvā. yāvatkṛtvaḥ śrutād arthāvagamaḥ. yathā cakṣur draṣṭr na bāhyena prakāśena vinā prakāśayatīty adraṣṭṛ na bhavati.
yadi [13]{*1/161*} prathamaśruto na pratyāyayati, kṛtakas tarhi śabdasyārthena saṃbandhaḥ. kutaḥ? svabhāvato hy asaṃbandhāv etau śabdārthau. mukhe hi śabdam upalabhāmahe, bhūmāv artham. śabdo 'yaṃ na tv arthaḥ, artho 'yaṃ na śabdeti ca vyapadiśanti. rūpabhedo 'pi bhavati. gaur itīmaṃ śabdam uccārayanti, sāsnādimantam artham avabudhyanta{*1/162*} iti. pṛthagbhūtayoś ca yaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, sa{*1/163*} kṛtako dṛṣṭaḥ, yathā rajjughaṭayor iti. atha gaur ity atra kaḥ śabdaḥ? gakāraukāravisarjanīyā iti bhagavān Upavarṣaḥ. śrotragrahaṇe hy arthe loke śabdaśabdaḥ prasiddhaḥ. te ca śrotragrahaṇāḥ.
yady evam, arthapratyayo nopapadyate. katham? ekaikākṣaravijñāne hy{*1/164*} artho nopalabhyate. na cākṣaravyatirikto 'nyaḥ kaścid asti samudāyo nāma, yato 'rthapratipattiḥ syāt. yadā hi{*1/165*} gakāraḥ, na tadaukārādivisarjanīyau. yadaukāravisarjanīyau, na tadā gakāraḥ. ato gakārādivyatirikto 'nyo gośabdo{*1/166*} 'sti, yato 'rthapratipattiḥ syāt. antarhite 'pi{*1/167*} śabde smaraṇād arthapratyaya iti cet{*1/168*}, na. smṛter api kṣaṇikatvād akṣarais tulyatā.
pūrvavarṇajanitasaṃskārasahito 'ntya varṇaḥ pratyāyaka{*1/169*} ity adoṣaḥ. nanv evam api{*1/170*} śabdād arthaṃ pratipadyāmaha iti laukikaṃ vacanam anupapannaṃ syāt{*1/171*}.
ucyate - yadi nopapadyate, anupapannaṃ nāma. na hi laukikaṃ vacanam anupapannam ity etāvatā pratyakṣādibhir anavagamyamāno{*1/172*} 'rthaḥ śakyo 'bhyupagantum{*1/173*}. laukikāni vacanāny upapannārthāny anupapannārthāni ca dṛśyante, yathā devadatta, gām abhyājety evamādīni daśa dāḍimāni ṣaḍ apūpā ity evamādīni ca.
nanu ca śāstrakārā apy evam āhuḥ pūrvāparībhūtaṃ bhāvam ākhyāte[14]{*1/174*}nācaṣṭe vrajati, pacatīty upakramaprabhṛty apavargaparyantam iti{*1/175*} yathā. na śāstrakāravacanam apy alam imam artham apramāṇakam upapādayitum.
api ca naivaitad{*1/176*} anupapannārtham. akṣarebhyaḥ saṃskāraḥ, saṃskārād arthapratipattir iti bhavanty{*1/177*} arthapratpattāv akṣarāṇi nimittam. gauṇa eṣa{*1/178*} śabda iti cet, na gauṇo 'kṣareṣu nimittabhāvaḥ, tadbhāve bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvāt. athāpi gauṇaḥ syāt, na gauṇaḥ śabdo mā bhūd ity etāvatā{*1/179*} pratyakṣādibhir anavagamyamāno 'rthaḥ śakyaḥ parikalpayitum. na hy agnir māṇavaka ity ukte 'gniśabdo gauṇo mā bhūd iti jvalana eva māṇavaka ity adhyavasīyate. na ca pratyakṣo gakārādibhyo 'nyo gośabda iti, bhedadarśanābhāvād abhedadarśanāc ca. gakārādīni hi pratyakṣāṇi. tasmād gaur iti gakārādivisarjanīyāntaṃ padam akṣarāṇy eva. na tebhyo{*1/180*} vyatiriktam anyat padaṃ nāma iti. nanu saṃskārakalpanāyām apy adṛṣṭakalpanā. ucyate - śābdakalpanāyāṃ sā ca śabdakalpanā ca. tasmād akṣarāṇy eva padam.
atha gaur ity asya śabdasya ko 'rthaḥ? sāsnādiviśiṣṭākṛtir iti brūmaḥ. nanv ākṛtiḥ sādhyāsti vā na veti? na pratyakṣā satī sādhyā bhavitum arhati. rucakaḥ, svastikaḥ, vardhamānaka iti hi pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate. vyamoha iti cet, na. nāsti pratyayaviparyāse vyamoha iti śakyate vaktum{*1/181*}.

āha - yadi vijñānād anyad asti vijñātṛ, vijñānam apāsya tan nidarśyatām - idam tad īdṛśam ceti. na ca tan nidarśyate. tasmān na tato 'nyad astīti.
atrocyate - svasaṃvedyaḥ sa bhavati. nāsāv anyena śakyate draṣṭum. katham asau nidarśyeteti{*1/294*}. yathā ca{*1/295*} kaścic cakṣuṣmān svayaṃ rūpaṃ paśyati na ca śaknoty anyasmai jātyandhāya tan nidarśayitum, na ca tan na śakyate nidarśayitum ity etāvatā nāstīty avagamyate, evam asau puruṣaḥ svayam ātmānam upalabhate na cānyasmai śaknoti darśayitum, anyasya draṣṭus taṃ puruṣaṃ prati darśanaśaktyabhāvāt. so 'py anyaḥ puruṣaḥ svayam ātmānam upalabhate, na parātmānam{*1/296*}. tena sarve svena svenātmanā ātmānam upalabhamānāḥ santy eva, yady api parapuruṣair nopalabhyanta{*1/297*} iti. athāsmin arthe brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati - śāntāyāṃ vāci kiṃjyotir evāyaṃ puruṣaḥ? ātmajyotiḥ, saṃrāḍ iti hovāceti{*1/298*}. pareṇa nopalabhyata ity atrāpi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati - agṛhyo na hi gṛhyateti{*1/299*}. pareṇa na gṛhyata ity etadabhiprāyam etat. kutaḥ? svayaṃjyotiṣṭvavacanāt. atrāpi{*1/300*} brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati - atrāyaṃ puruṣaḥ svayaṃjyotir bhavatīti{*1/301*}.
kena punar upāyenāyam (ayam){*1/302*} anyasmai kathyata iti? atrāpy{*1/303*} upāye [23]{*1/304*}brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati - sa eṣa neti nety ātmeti hovāceti{*1/305*}. asāv ayam{*1/306*} evaṃrūpa iti na śakyate nidarśayitum. yac ca paraḥ paśyati, tatpratiṣedhas tasyopadeśopāyaḥ. śarīraṃ paraḥ paśyati. tenātmopadiśyate. śarīraṃ nātmā. asti śarīrād anyaḥ{*1/307*} sa cātmeti śarīrapratiṣedhenātmopadiśyate{*1/308*}. tathā prāṇādayo nātmāna iti{*1/309*} tatpratiṣedhena tebhyo 'nya upadiśyate. tathā parasthāḥ sukhādayaḥ pareṇa liṅgair upalabhyante. te 'pi nātmāna iti tatpratiṣedhena tebhyo{*1/310*} 'nya upadiśyate.
yaḥ svayaṃ paśyati, na tato 'nyaḥ puruṣa ity etad api puruṣapravṛttyānumīyate, yadāsau puruṣaḥ pūrvedyuḥ sāmikṛtānām arthānāṃ pratisamādhāne śeṣānuṣṭhāne ca yatate, ataḥ{*1/311*} pravṛttyāvagamyate nūnam asāv anityān nityam avagacchatīti{*1/312*}.
upamānāc copadiśyate yādṛśaṃ bhavān svayam ātmānaṃ paśyati, anenopamānenāvagaccha - aham api tādṛṣam eva paśyāmīti, yathā kaścid ātmīyāṃ vedanāṃ parasmā ācakṣīta - dahyamānasyeva me bhavati, yātyamānasyeva me bhavati, rudhyamānasyeva{*1/313*} me bhavatīti. ataḥ svayam avagamyamānatvād asti tadvyatiriktaḥ puruṣa iti.
yad apy{*1/314*} ucyate - vijñānam apāsya tan nidarśyatām iti, yady upāyam eva niśedhasi, na śakyam upāyam antareṇopeyam upetum. ayam evābhyupāyo jñātavyānām arthānāṃ yo yathā jñāyate, sa tatheti. tad yathā - kaḥ śuklo nāma? yatra śuklatvam asti. kiṃ śuklatvaṃ nāma? yatra śuklaśabdapravṛttiḥ. kva tasya pravṛttiḥ? yac chuklaśabda uccarite pratīyate. tasmān na vijñānaṃ pratyākhyāya kasyacid rūpaṃ nidarśayituṃ śakyam.
na ca niyogataḥ pratyaye pratīte pratyayārthaḥ pratīto bhavati. apratīte 'pi hi pratyaye saty arthaḥ pratīyata eva. na hi vijñānaṃ pratyakṣam, vijñeyo 'rthaḥ pratyakṣa ity etat pūrvam evoktam. tad avaśyakarta[24]{*1/315*}vye 'pahnave kāmaṃ vijñānam apahnūyeta nārtha ity etad apy{*1/316*} uktam eva. tasmād asti sukhādibhyo 'nyo nityaḥ puruṣa iti.
atha yad uktaṃ vijñānaghana evaitebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tāny evānuvinaśyati, na pretya saṃjñāstīti, atrocyate - atraiva mā bhagavān mohāntam āpīpadad iti{*1/317*} paricodanottarakāle 'pahnutya mohāntābhiprāyam{*1/318*} asya vacanasya{*1/319*} varṇitavān na vā are 'haṃ{*1/320*} mohaṃ bravīmi, avināśī vā are 'yam ātmānucchittidharmā, mātrāsaṃsargas tv asya bhavatīti{*1/321*}. tasmān na vijñānamātram. tasmād vaiṣamyam.
yad uktam - na caiṣa yātīti vidhiśabda iti, mā bhūd vidhiśabdaḥ. svargakāmo yajeteti vacanāntareṇāvagatam anuvadiṣyate. tasmād avirodhaḥ.
