children.text: śāstradṛṣṭavirodhāc ca // MS_1,2.2 //
children.translated_text: And because of contradiction with what is observed through scripture and [direct] observation. // MS_1,2.2 //

children.text:
stenaṃ manaḥ. anṛtavādinī vāg ityevaṃjātīyakānāṃ dharmaṃ praty aprāmāṇyam, bhūtānuvādāt. vipariṇāmādibhir api kalpyamāne steyaṃ mṛṣodyaṃ ca kartavyam ity āpatati. tac cāśakyaṃ steyānṛtavādapratiṣedham abādhamānenānuṣṭhātum. na ca vikalpaḥ, vaiṣamyāt. ekaḥ kalpyo vidhiḥ, ekaḥ pratyakṣaḥ.
atha dṛṣṭavirodhaḥ. tasmād dhūma evāgner divā dadṛśe nārciḥ. tasmād arcir evāgner naktaṃ dadṛśe na dhūma iti{*1/405*}. asmāl lokād utkramyāgnir ādityaṃ gataḥ, rātrāv ādityastam ity etad upapādayitum idam, ubhayam api dṛṣṭaviruddham ucyate. tasmān naiṣāvadhāraṇā sidhyatīti. aparo dṛṣṭavirodhaḥ - na caitad vidmo vayaṃ [41]{*1/406*} brāhmaṇā vā smaḥ, abrāhmaṇā vety{*1/407*}{*1/408*} akriyārthatvād anarthakam. athāyam arthaḥ - naivaitaj jñāyate kiṃ vā brāhmaṇā vayam utābrāhmaṇā eveti, pratyakṣaviruddham apramāṇam. aparaḥ śāstradṛṣṭena virodhaḥ - ko hi tad veda, yad amuṣmiṃl loke 'sti vā, na veti{*1/409*}. yadi praśno 'yam, akriyārthatvād anarthakaḥ. athānavakḷptiḥ, śāstradṛṣṭena virodhaḥ. ataḥ pratyakṣaviruddham apramāṇam.
children.translated_text:
The mind is a thief; speech speaks falsehood — regarding sentences of this kind, there is no validity for <s>Dharma</s>, because they are mere restatements of [empirical] facts. Even if one were to construct [a meaning] through transformation and the like, it would follow that theft and lying should be practiced. And it is impossible to practice that without contradicting the prohibition of theft and falsehood. Nor is there an option [between them], because of their inequality — one [injunction] is constructed, the other is explicit.
Then there is the contradiction with observation: 'Therefore, only the smoke of fire was seen during the day, not the flame; therefore, only the flame of fire was seen at night, not the smoke.' To explain that fire, having departed from this world, has gone to the sun, and at night the sun has set — both of these are stated in contradiction with observation. Therefore this restriction does not hold.
Another contradiction with observation: 'We do not know whether we are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> or non-<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>' — since it does not serve any ritual action, it is purposeless. If the meaning is 'it is not at all known whether we are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> or non-<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>' — this contradicts perception and is not a valid means of knowledge.
Another contradiction with what is observed through scripture: 'For who knows whether there is [anything] in the other world or not?' If this is a question, it is purposeless since it does not serve any ritual action. If it is a denial [of the other world], it contradicts what is observed through scripture. Therefore, what contradicts perception is not a valid means of knowledge.

NOTES:
Tait.Br. 2.1.2.10, cf. ŚBh ad MS 1.2.12 | [Page refs: E2: 2,5; E4: 1,19; E5: 2,13; E6: 1,29] | Tait.Br. 2.1.2, Gop.Br. 5.21, Mait.S. 1.4.11 | [E2 omits 'smaḥ, abrāhmaṇā vā'] | Tait.S. 6.1.1; 6.2.2, cf. ŚBh ad MS 1.2.14

children.text: tathā phalābhāvāt // MS_1,2.3 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, because of the absence of a [visible] fruit. // MS_1,2.3 //

children.text: gargatrirātrabrāhmaṇaṃ prakṛtyocyate - śobhate 'sya mukhaṃ ya evaṃ veda iti{*1/410*} yadi bhūtānuvādaḥ, anarthakaḥ. athādhyayanaphalānuvādaḥ, tato 'sadanuvādaḥ. kālāntare phalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti cet. na hy atra pramāṇam asti. vidhiḥ syād iti cet. naiṣa vidhiparaḥ, dravyasaṃskārakarmasv iti{*1/411*} cintayiṣyaty etad upariṣṭāt, kiṃ phalaviddhir utārthavāda iti. iha tu kiṃ bhūtānuvādaḥ, kriyārtho veti{*1/412*}. āsya prajāyāṃ vājī jāyate ya evaṃ vedeti codāharaṇam.
children.translated_text: The <s>Garga-trirātra-brāhmaṇa</s> is cited as the basis: 'His face shines who knows thus' — if this is a mere restatement of fact, it is purposeless. If it is a statement of the fruit of study, then it is a statement of something untrue [since no such result is observed]. [Objection:] The fruit will come at a later time. [Reply:] There is no evidence for this. [Objection:] It may be an injunction. [Reply:] This [passage] is not injunctive in purport. [The principle] 'regarding rituals of consecrating substances' — this will be considered later: whether it is an injunction of fruit or an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage). Here, however, [the question is] whether it is a restatement of fact or serves a ritual purpose. And the example is cited: 'In his offspring a strong [son] is born who knows thus.'

children.text: anyānarthakyāt // MS_1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: Because of the purposelessness of the others. // MS_1,2.4 //

children.text: pūrṇāhutyā sarvān kāmān avāpnoti{*1/413*}. paśubandhayājī sarvāṃl lokān abhijayati. tarati mṛtyum, tarati brahmahatyāṃ yo 'śvamedhena yajate, ya u cainam evaṃ vedeti{*1/414*}. yadi bhūtānuvādamātram anarthakam. atha phalavidhiḥ, itareṣām ānarthakyam. na hi, akṛtvā pūrṇāhutim agnihotrādayaḥ kriyante. na [42]{*1/415*} cāniṣṭvāgnīṣomīyeṇa somena yajante. na cādhītyāśvamedhena yajante. tad yathā, pathi jāte 'rke madhūtsṛjya, tenaiva pathā madhvarthinaḥ parvataṃ na gaccheyuḥ, tādṛśaṃ hi tat. api cāhuḥ -
children.translated_text: By the <s>Pūrṇāhuti</s> (full oblation) one obtains all desires. The performer of the animal sacrifice conquers all worlds. One who sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) crosses over death, crosses over the sin of <s>Brahma</s>-killing — and so too one who knows thus. If this is merely a restatement of fact, it is purposeless. If it is an injunction of fruit, the other [rituals] become purposeless. For the <s>Agnihotra</s> and other [rituals] are performed only after performing the <s>Pūrṇāhuti</s>. Nor does one sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> without first performing the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal sacrifice]. Nor does one sacrifice with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> without first studying [the <s>Veda</s>]. It is as if, when honey is found in a tree along the path, those seeking honey would not go to the mountain by that very same path — for this is exactly like that. Moreover, they say:

children.text:
arke cen madhu vindeta, kim arthaṃ parvataṃ vrajet/
iṣṭasyārthasya saṃsiddhau ko vidvān yatnam ācaret// iti{*1/416*}.
children.translated_text: If one could find honey in a tree, why would one go to the mountain? When the desired goal has been achieved, what wise person would exert further effort?

NOTES:
Tait.Br. 3.8.10 | Cf. Tait.Br. 5.3.12.2 | [Page refs: E2: 2,8; E4: 1,32; E5: 2,16; E6: 1,29] | [Source unknown]

children.text: abhāgipratiṣedhāc ca // MS_1,2.5 //
children.translated_text: And because of the prohibition of what is not [ordinarily] excluded. // MS_1,2.5 //

children.text: na pṛthivyām agniś cetavyo nāntarikṣe na divīty{*1/417*} apratiṣedhabhāginam arthaṃ pratiṣedhanti. vijñāyata evaitat, antarikṣe, divi cāgnir na cīyata iti. pṛthivīcayanapratiṣedhārthaṃ ca yad vākyam, bhavec cayanapratiṣedhārtham eva tat. athāpramāṇam, naiṣa virodho bhavati. kathaṃ tat pramāṇam, yad vidhyantaram ākulayet, svayaṃ cākulaṃ syāt. na cetavyam, hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya cetavyam iti.
children.translated_text: The [passage] 'Fire should not be laid on the earth, nor in the atmosphere, nor in heaven' — they prohibit a meaning that is not [ordinarily] subject to prohibition. For it is well known that fire is not laid in the atmosphere or in heaven. And the sentence that [might serve] to prohibit the laying of fire on the earth could [at most] serve to prohibit the laying [of fire on earth] alone. If [the passage is considered] invalid as a means of knowledge, there is no contradiction. For how can that be a valid means of knowledge which would confuse another injunction and itself be confused? [The passage says:] 'It should not be laid' [and then] 'having placed gold, it should be laid.'

NOTES:
Tait.S. 5.2.7.1

Now, a supporter rises again for those portions of the <s>Veda</s> that have been challenged: '<s>Babara Prāvāhaṇi</s> desired...'

children.text: vidhinā tv ekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ // MS_1,2.7 //
children.translated_text: But because of [their] forming a single sentence with an injunction, they serve the purpose of praising the injunctions. // MS_1,2.7 //

children.text:
idaṃ samāmnāyate - vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ, vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā, vāyum eva svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati, sa evainaṃ bhūtiṃ gamayatīti{*1/421*}. vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatety ato yady api kriyā nāvagamyate, kriyāsaṃbaddhaṃ vā kiṃcit. tathāpi vidhyuddeśe[43]{*1/422*}naikavākyatvāt pramāṇam. bhūtikāma ity evam anto vidhyuddeśaḥ, tenaikavākyabhūto vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatetyevamādiḥ. katham ekavākyabhāvaḥ. padānāṃ sākāṅkṣatvād vidheḥ stuteś caikavākyatvaṃ bhavati. bhūtikāma ālabheta. (kasmāt?){*1/423*} yato vāyuḥ kṣepiṣṭheti. nāyam abhisaṃbandho vivakṣitaḥ, bhūtikāmenālabdhavyam iti. kathaṃ tarhi ālabheta? yatas tato bhūtir iti bhinnāv imāv arthau, ubhayābhidhāne vākyaṃ bhidyeta.
kim arthā stutir iti cet. kathaṃ roceta, nonuṣṭhīyeteti. nanu prāk stutivacanād anuṣṭhānaṃ bhūtikāmāntāt siddham, stutivacanam anarthakam. na hi, yadā stutipadāsaṃnidhānaṃ tadā pūrveṇaiva vidhiḥ. yadā stutipadasaṃbandhaḥ, na tadā bhūtikāmasyālambho vidhīyate. yathā paṭo bhavatīti paṭa utpadyata ity arthaḥ. nirākāṅkṣaṃ ca padadvayam. yadā ca tasminn eva rakta ity aparaṃ śrūyate, tadā rāgasaṃbandho bhavatīty arthaḥ, bhavati ca raktaṃ pratyākāṅkṣā. evaṃ yadā na stutipadāni, vidhiśabdenaiva tadā prarocanā, yadā stutivacanam, tadā stavanena. nanv evaṃ sati kiṃ stuti-vacanena, yasmin saty avidhāyakam, mā bhūt tat. tadabhāve 'pi pūrvavidhinaiva prarocayiṣyata iti. satyam, vināpi tena sidhyet prarocanam. asti tu tat, tasmin vidyamāne yo 'rtho vākyasya, so 'va-gamyate stutiprayojanaṃ{*1/424*} tayoḥ. tasminn avidyamāne vidhinā prarocanam iti.
nanu satsv api stutipadeṣu pūrvasya vidhisvarūpatvād vidhir abhipretaḥ syāt, na vivakṣyeta stutipada-saṃbandhaḥ. āha - stutipadāni hy anarthakāny abhaviṣyan sākāṅkṣāṇi. bhavantv anarthakānīti cet. na, gamyamāne 'rthe 'vivakṣitārthāni bhavitum arhanti. [44]{*1/425*} yo 'sau vidhyuddeśaḥ, sa śaknoti nirapekṣo 'rthaṃ vidhātum, śaknoti ca stutipadānāṃ vākyaśeṣībhavitum, pratyakṣaś ca vākyaśeṣabhāvaḥ. ato 'smād vidheḥ stutim avagacchāmaḥ.
nanu nirapekṣād api vidhim avagamiṣyām. bhavatv evam, naivaṃ sati kaścid virodhaḥ. kiṃ tv aśakyaḥ stutipadasaṃbandhe sati vidhyartho vivakṣitum. vākyaṃ hi saṃbandhasya vidhāyakam, dvau cet saṃbandhau vidadhyāt - bhūtikāma ālabheta; ālambhena caiṣa guṇo bhaviṣyatīti, bhidyeta tarhy evaṃ sati vākyam. atha yad uktam - na kriyā gamyate na tatsaṃbaddhaṃ vā kiṃcid iti{*1/426*}. stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ, stutiśabdāḥ stuvantaḥ kriyāṃ prarocayamāṇā anuṣṭhātṝṇām upakariṣyanti kriyāyāḥ. evam imāni sarvāṇy eva padāni kaṃcid arthaṃ stuvanti vidadhati. ataḥ pramāṇam evaṃjātīyakāni, vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devateti{*1/427*}.
children.translated_text:
This is taught in the <s>samāmnāya</s> (codified teaching): '<s>vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ</s>' — 'One who desires prosperity should sacrifice a white [animal] to <s>Vāyu</s>'; '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity; he approaches <s>Vāyu</s> with his own share; [<s>Vāyu</s>] indeed leads him to prosperity.' Even though from '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity' no action is understood, nor anything connected with action, nevertheless, because of its syntactic unity (<s>ekavākyatva</s>) with the injunctive passage, it is authoritative. The injunctive passage ends with 'one who desires prosperity'; thus '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity' and so on form a single sentence (<s>ekavākya</s>) with it. How is there syntactic unity? Because the words have mutual expectancy (<s>sākāṅkṣatva</s>), the injunction and the praise form a single sentence. 'One who desires prosperity should sacrifice' — (Why?) — 'because <s>Vāyu</s> is the swiftest.' This connection is not the intended one — that 'one who desires prosperity must sacrifice.' How then [should we understand] 'should sacrifice'? 'From whatever source comes prosperity' — these are two separate meanings, and if both were expressed [in one sentence], the sentence would be split.
If one asks: What is the purpose of praise? [The answer is:] So that [the performer] may be pleased and thereby carry out [the ritual]. But surely, prior to the laudatory statement, the performance is already established from the injunctive passage ending with 'one who desires prosperity' — so the laudatory statement is purposeless. This is not so. When there is no proximity of laudatory words, the injunction operates by itself. When there is connection with laudatory words, the sacrifice by one who desires prosperity is not [merely] being enjoined. Just as 'cloth comes into being' means 'cloth is produced' — and the two words are syntactically complete. But when 'dyed' is additionally heard in regard to that very [cloth], then the connection with dyeing becomes the meaning, and there is expectancy toward 'dyed.' Similarly, when there are no laudatory words, encouragement is through the injunctive word alone; when there is a laudatory statement, then through praise. If one objects: 'What then is the purpose of the laudatory statement — whose presence makes [the passage] non-injunctive? Let it not exist!' Even in its absence, the earlier injunction alone will provide encouragement. True — encouragement would be accomplished even without it. But it does exist; when it is present, the meaning of the sentence is understood — [namely,] that the purpose of praise is [to encourage]. When it is absent, encouragement is through the injunction.
But even when laudatory words are present, since the prior [passage] has the nature of an injunction, the injunction would be intended, and the connection with laudatory words would not be intended. He replies: The laudatory words would indeed be purposeless [were they] expectant [of completion]. 'Let them be purposeless!' — No, when the meaning is understood, they cannot be treated as having an unintended meaning. That injunctive passage is capable of conveying its meaning independently, and it is also capable of having the laudatory words as its syntactic complement (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>), and the complementary status is directly perceived. Therefore, from this injunction we understand [the passage to be] a praise.
But we could understand it as an injunction even from [the passage] taken independently. Let it be so — there is no contradiction in that case. However, when there is a connection with laudatory words, the injunctive meaning cannot be intended. For a sentence establishes a connection; if it were to establish two connections — 'one who desires prosperity should sacrifice' and 'by the sacrifice this quality will result' — then the sentence would be split. Now, as for what was said — 'no action is understood, nor anything connected with it' — [the laudatory words] serve the purpose of praise; the words of praise, by praising the action and encouraging the performers, will be useful to the action. Thus all these words either praise something or enjoin something. Therefore, passages of this kind are authoritative — such as '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity.'

children.translated_text: And the traditional [teaching] is the same. // MS 1.2.8 //

children.text: athocyeta - prāk stutipadebhyaḥ, nirākāṅkṣāṇi vidhāyakāni, vidhisvarūpatvāt, stutipadāni tu pramādapāṭha iti. tan na evam{*1/428*}, arthāvagamāt, tulyaṃ ca sāṃpradāyikam, saṃpradāyaḥ (prayojanaṃ){*1/429*} yeṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sarve te vidhipadānām arthavādapadānāṃ ca tulyāḥ. adhyāyānadhyāyate{*1/430*}, gurumukhāt pratipattiḥ, śiṣyopādhyāyatā ca sarvasminn evaṃjātīyake, avighnārthe tulyam ādriyante. smaraṇaṃ ca dṛḍham. ato na pramādapāṭha iti.
children.translated_text: If one were to say: 'Prior to the laudatory words, the injunctive [words] are syntactically complete, having the nature of injunction, and the laudatory words are [merely] erroneous recitation (<s>pramādapāṭha</s>)' — this is not so, because their meaning is understood. 'And the traditional [teaching] is the same' — the <s>saṃpradāya</s> (tradition), i.e., the purpose, of all these <s>dharmas</s> is the same for the words of injunction and the words of <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages). In the study and non-study [of texts], the reception from the teacher's mouth, and the teacher-student relationship — all these apply equally to passages of this kind; they are treated with equal care for the sake of uninterrupted [transmission]. And the memorization is firm. Therefore, [these are] not erroneous recitation.

children.text: api ca yaiṣānupapattir uktā śāstradṛṣṭavirodhād ityevamādyā{*1/432*}, sā so 'rodīd ityevamādiṣu na prāpnoti. kutaḥ? prayoge hi steyādīnām ucyamāne virodhaḥ syāt, śabdārthas tv aprayogabhūtaḥ, tasmād upapadyeta - stenaṃ manaḥ, anṛtavādinī vāg iti.
children.translated_text: Moreover, that impossibility which was stated — [namely,] 'because of contradiction with what is seen in the <s>śāstra</s>' and so forth — that does not apply to [passages like] 'he wept' and the like. Why? For the contradiction would arise if stealing and such things were being enjoined as [ritual] practice; but the meaning of the word is not part of [ritual] practice, and therefore it would be justified — [for instance,] 'the mind is a thief' and 'speech is a liar.'

yad uktam - vidheyasya prarocanārthā stutir iti{*1/433*}. tad iha katham avakalpyeta yatrānyad vidheyam, anyac ca stūyate. yathā - vetasaśākhayāvakābhiś cāgniṃ vikarṣatīti{*1/434*} vetasāvake vidhīyete, āpaś ca stūyante - āpo vai śāntā iti{*1/435*}. tad ucyate - guṇavādas tu. gauṇa eṣa vādo bhavati, yat saṃbandhini stotavye saṃbandhyantaraṃ stūyate. abhijano hy eṣa vetasāvakayoḥ. tatas te jāte. abhijanasaṃstavena cābhijātaḥ stuto bhavati. yathā - aśmakābhijano devadatto 'śmākeṣu stūyamāneṣu stutam{*1/436*} ātmānaṃ manyate. evam atrāpi draṣṭavyam.
atha so 'rodīd iti kasya vidheḥ śeṣaḥ. tasmād barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam ity{*1/437*} asya. kutaḥ? sākāṅkṣatvāt padānām. so 'rodīt, yad arodīt, tad rudrasya rudratvam ity{*1/438*} atra sa iti prakṛtāpekṣaḥ, tatpratyayāt. tasya yad aśrv aśīryateti tasyeti pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣa eva. upapattiś coparitanasya yo barhiṣi rajataṃ dadyāt purāsya saṃvatsarād gṛhe rodanaṃ bhavatīti{*1/439*}. asya hetutvenāyaṃ pratinirdiśyate - tasmād barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam iti. evaṃ sarvāṇi sākāṅkṣāṇi. kathaṃ vidher{*1/440*} upakurvantīti. [46]{*1/441*} guṇavādena. rodanaprabhavaṃ rajataṃ barhiṣi dadato rodanam āpadyate. tat pratiṣedhasya guṇaḥ, yad arodanam iti. kathaṃ punar arudaty arodīd iti bhavati? kathaṃ vānaśruprabhave rajate 'śruprabhavam iti vacanam? purāsya saṃvatsarād asati rodane, kathaṃ rodanaṃ bhavatīti? tad ucyate - guṇavādas tu. gauṇā ete śabdāḥ. rudra iti rodananimittasya śabdasya darśanād yad arodīd ity ucyate. varṇasārūpyān nindann anaśruprabhavam apy aśruprabhavam ity āha. nindann eva ca dhanatyāge dukhadarśanāt purāsya saṃvatsarād gṛhe rodanaṃ bhavatīty āha.
tathā - yaḥ prajākāmaḥ paśukāmo vā syāt, sa etaṃ prājāpatyaṃ tūpuram ālabheta iti{*1/442*}, ākāṅkṣitatvād asya vidheḥ śeṣo 'yam - sa ātmano vapām udakhidad iti{*1/443*}. kathaṃ guṇavādaḥ? itthaṃ nāma - nāsan paśavaḥ, yad ātmano vapām udakhidad iti. etac ca karmaṇaḥ sāmarthyaṃ yad agnau prahṛtamātrāyāṃ vapāyām ajas tūpura udagāt, itthaṃ bahavaḥ paśavo bhavantīti. kathaṃ punar anutkhinnāyāṃ vapāyāṃ prajāpatir ātmano vapām udakhidad ity āha. ucyate - asad vṛttāntānvākhyānaṃ stutyarthena praśaṃsāyā gamyamānatvāt. ihānvākhyāne vartamāne dvayaṃ niṣpadyate{*1/444*} - yac ca vṛttāntajñānam, yac ca kasmiṃścit prarocanā dveṣo vā. tatra vṛttāntānvākhyānaṃ na pravartakaṃ na nivartakaṃ ceti prayojanābhāvād anarthakam ity avivakṣitam. prarocanayā tu pravartate dveṣān nivartata iti tayor vivakṣā. vṛttāntānvākhyāne 'pi vidhīyamāne ādimatā doṣo vedasya prasajeta. kathaṃ punar idaṃ nirālambanam anvākhyāyata iti. ucyate - nityaḥ kaścid arthaḥ prajāpatiḥ syād vāyuḥ, ākāśaḥ, ādityo vā. sa ātmano vapām udakhidad iti vṛṣṭim, vāyum, raśmiṃ vā. tām agnau prāgṛhṇāt, vaidyute, ārcīse, laukike vā. tato 'ja ity annam, bījam, virud vā. tam ālabhya tam upayujya prajāḥ paśūn prāpnotīti gauṇāḥ śabdāḥ.
ādityaḥ prāyaṇīyaś carur āditya udapanīyaś carur ity{*1/445*} asya vidheḥ śeṣaḥ - devā vai devayajanam adhyavasāya diśo na prājānann iti, ākāṅkṣitatvāt. sarvavyāmohānām ādityaś carur nāśayitā, api diṅmohasyeti stutiḥ. katham asati diṅmohe diṅmohaśabda iti. ucyate - aprākṛtasya bahoḥ karmasamūhasyopasthitatvād gauṇo mohaśabdo 'vadhāraṇāvakāśadānādibhir jñāpayatīti gauṇatā.
children.translated_text:
It was said that praise serves to encourage what is enjoined. How then would this apply where one thing is enjoined and another is praised? For example: 'He draws forth the fire with a <s>vetasa</s>-branch and with <s>avakā</s>-grass' — here <s>vetasa</s> and <s>avakā</s> are enjoined, but water is praised — 'for water is peaceful.' To this it is said: 'But [it is] figurative speech.' This speech is figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>), in that when the related [thing] should be praised, something else that is related is praised instead. For water is the origin of <s>vetasa</s> and <s>avakā</s>; from that they are born. And by praising the lineage, the offspring is praised. Just as <s>Devadatta</s>, who is from the <s>Aśmaka</s> family, considers himself praised when the <s>Aśmakas</s> are praised — so too it should be understood here.
As for 'he wept' — of which injunction is this the complement? Of [the injunction] 'Therefore one should not give silver on the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass).' Why? Because of the mutual expectancy of the words. 'He wept; because he wept, that is the <s>rudra</s>-nature of <s>Rudra</s>' — here 'he' (<s>sa</s>) refers to something previously mentioned, due to the [anaphoric] pronoun. 'His tears that flowed' — 'his' also refers back to what was previously mentioned. And the justification of the subsequent [passage] is: 'Whoever gives silver on the <s>barhis</s>, weeping arises in his household before a year [passes].' This is indicated as the reason: 'Therefore one should not give silver on the <s>barhis</s>.' Thus all [the words] have mutual expectancy. How do they serve the injunction? Through figurative speech (<s>guṇavāda</s>). Silver, originating from tears — when given on the <s>barhis</s>, weeping results. That is the quality [invoked by] the prohibition — namely, 'non-weeping.' But how can one who has not wept be said to have wept? And how can silver not originating from tears be called 'originating from tears'? And when there was no weeping before the year, how can 'weeping arises' [be said]? To this it is said: 'But [it is] figurative speech.' These words are figurative. Because the word <s>rudra</s> is seen to derive from weeping (<s>rodana</s>), 'he wept' is said. From similarity of phonetic form (<s>varṇasārūpya</s>), censuring [the act], he calls even that which does not originate from tears 'originating from tears.' And censuring — because sorrow is perceived in the giving up of wealth — he says 'weeping arises in his household before a year.'
Similarly: 'One who desires offspring or cattle should sacrifice this <s>prājāpatya tūpura</s>-animal' — because of [the passage's] expectancy, the complement of this injunction is 'he cut out the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) from himself.' How is this figurative speech? Thus — 'There were no cattle; [but when <s>Prajāpati</s>] cut out the <s>vapā</s> from himself' — and this is the power of the ritual: when the <s>vapā</s> was merely cast into the fire, the <s>tūpura</s> goat emerged, thus many cattle come to be. But how can <s>Prajāpati</s>, whose <s>vapā</s> was not actually cut out, be said to have 'cut out the <s>vapā</s> from himself'? It is replied: The narration of an event that did not [actually] occur [serves] the purpose of praise, because commendation is understood [from it]. Here, in a narration, two things are accomplished — knowledge of the event and either encouragement or aversion toward something. Of these, the event-narration itself neither impels nor dissuades, so being purposeless, it is not the intended [meaning]. But through encouragement one is impelled, and through aversion one desists — so those are the intended [meanings]. If the event-narration were also taken as enjoined, the defect of [the <s>Veda</s>] having a beginning would follow. But how is this [narrated] without any [real] basis? It is replied: Some eternal entity — <s>Prajāpati</s>, or <s>Vāyu</s>, or space, or the sun — 'he cut out the <s>vapā</s> from himself' means rain, or wind, or a ray. 'He cast it into the fire' — into the lightning-fire, the flame-fire, or the ordinary fire. 'From that, a goat' means food, or seed, or a plant. By sacrificing it, by employing it, one obtains offspring and cattle — thus the words are figurative.
'The sun is the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening) oblation; the sun is the <s>udapanīya</s> (concluding) oblation' — this injunction's complement is 'The gods, having resolved upon the divine sacrifice, did not know the directions' — because of expectancy. The sun as the oblation destroys all confusions; it will destroy even directional confusion — thus the praise. How can the word 'directional confusion' be used when there is no [actual] directional confusion? It is replied: Because a large, non-ordinary collection of ritual acts is at hand, the word 'confusion' is figurative, indicating [the difficulty of] determining, giving scope [to various procedures], and the like — thus the figurativeness.

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ haste bhavati, atha gṛhṇātīti{*1/446*} sākāṅkṣatvād asya vidheḥ śeṣaḥ - stenaṃ mano 'nṛtavādinī vāg iti. nindāvacanaṃ hiraṇyastutyarthena yathā - kim ṛṣiṇā, devadatta eva bhojayitavyaḥ. kathaṃ punar astenaṃ mano ninditum api stenaśabdenocyate, vācaṃ cānanṛtavādinīm apy anṛtavādinīti brūyat. guṇavādas tu rūpāt. yathā - stenāḥ pracchannarūpāḥ, evaṃ ca mana iti gauṇaḥ śabdaḥ. prāyāc cānṛtavādinī vāg iti.
children.translated_text: Gold is in his hand, then he takes it — because this injunction is syntactically incomplete (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>), the remainder is: 'the mind is a thief, speech is a liar.' The censuring expression serves the purpose of praising gold — just as [one says]: 'What need for a <s>ṛṣi</s>? <s>Devadatta</s> alone is to be fed.' But how can the mind, which is not a thief, be censured using the word 'thief,' and speech, which is not false, be called 'false-speaking'? This is secondary usage (<s>gauṇa</s>) based on [perceived] form. Just as — thieves are of hidden nature, so too is the mind — hence the word is metaphorical (<s>gauṇa</s>). And speech is predominantly (<s>prāyāt</s>) a liar.

children.text: dṛṣṭavirodha{*1/448*} udāharaṇam - tasmād bhūma evāgner divā dadṛśe nārciḥ{*1/449*}. tasmād arcir evāgner naktaṃ dadṛśe, na dhūma iti agnir jyotir jyotir agniḥ svāheti sāyaṃ juhoti, sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ sūryaḥ svāheti{*1/450*} prātar iti miśraliṅgamantrayor vidhānasyākāṅkṣitatvāc cheṣaḥ. ubhayor devatayoḥ saṃnidhāne homa iti stuter upapattiḥ. dūrabhūyastvād dhūmasyāgneś cādarśane gauṇaḥ śabdaḥ.
children.translated_text: An example of conflict with observed fact (<s>dṛṣṭavirodha</s>) — 'Therefore, it is only the smoke of fire that is seen by day, not the flame. Therefore, it is only the flame of fire that is seen by night, not the smoke.' [The mantras:] 'Fire is light, light is fire, <s>svāhā</s>' — this is offered at the evening oblation, and 'The sun is light, light is the sun, <s>svāhā</s>' — [this] at the morning oblation. Since the ritual ordinance of these two mixed-characteristic <s>mantras</s> is syntactically incomplete, this is the remainder. The propriety of the praise lies in the offering being performed in the presence of both deities. Because smoke is preponderantly remote [from fire's visibility by day], the expression about fire's non-visibility is metaphorical (<s>gauṇa</s>).

children.text: dṛṣṭavirodha evodāharaṇam - na caitad vidma iti{*1/452*}. tat pravare pravriyamāṇe devāḥ pitara iti brūyād ity{*1/453*} ākāṅkṣitatvād asya vidheḥ śeṣaḥ. abrāhmaṇo 'pi brāhmaṇaḥ pravarānumantraṇena syād iti stutiḥ. durjñānatvād ajñānavacanaṃ gauṇam. stryaparādhena kartuś ca putradarśanena. apramatā rakṣata tantum enam ityādinā durjñānam.
children.translated_text: This too is an example of conflict with observed fact — 'We do not know this.' During the <s>pravara</s> (ancestry recitation) when the lineage is being recited, one should say 'gods and fathers' — because this injunction is syntactically incomplete, this is the remainder. Even a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would become a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through the <s>pravara</s> recitation — this is praise. The expression of ignorance is metaphorical because [the subject] is difficult to know. [This is] because of the fault of the woman (<s>strī</s>), and by seeing the son of the agent. The passage 'Protect this thread, being attentive' and so forth [shows that] it is difficult to know.

children.text: vidyāpraśaṃsā // MS_1,2.15 //
children.translated_text: Praise of knowledge. // MS 1.2.15 //

children.text: tathā phalābhāvād ity{*1/456*} atrodāhṛtam - śobhate 'sya mukham iti{*1/457*}. gargatrirātravidher ākāṅkṣitatvāc cheṣaḥ. [49]{*1/458*} vedānumantraṇasya cāsya prajāyāṃ vājī jāyata iti śeṣaḥ. mukhaśobhā vājimattvaṃ ca guṇavacanatvād gauṇaḥ śabdaḥ. śobhata iva śiṣyair udīkṣyamāṇam. kule saṃtatādhyayanaśravaṇān medhāvī jāyata iti sa pratigrahād annaṃ prāpnotīti.
children.translated_text: Similarly, what was illustrated under [the principle] 'because of the absence of fruit' — the example cited here is: 'His face is radiant.' Because the injunction of the <s>Garga</s>-trirātra rite is syntactically incomplete, this is the remainder. [Page 49] And this Vedic recitation has as its remainder: 'In his offspring, a vigorous one will be born.' The expressions about facial radiance and virility are metaphorical (<s>gauṇa</s>) because they are statements about qualities. 'Radiant' means as if gazed upon by students [with admiration]. Through continuous hearing of study in the family, an intelligent one is born — he obtains food from gifts.

NOTES:
[MS 1.2.3; E1, p. 41/8, Tā.Br. 20.16.6; Edition cross-references: E2: 2,30; E4: 1,120; E5: 2,33; E6: 1,34]

children.text: sarvatvam ādhikārikam // MS_1,2.16 //
children.translated_text: The [expression of] totality pertains to the topic at hand (<s>ādhikārika</s>). // MS 1.2.16 //

children.text: anyānarthakyavākya udāharaṇam - pūrṇāhutyā sarvān kāmān avāpnotīti{*1/459*}, pūrṇāhutiṃ juhotīty ākāṅkṣitatvād asya vidheḥ śeṣaḥ. ya u cainam evaṃ vedeti, tarati mṛtyum ity{*1/460*} asyākāṅkṣitvāc cheṣaḥ. phalavacanaṃ stutiḥ. sarvakāmaphalasya nimitte sarvakāmāv āptivacanaṃ gauṇam. asarveṣu sarvavacanam adhikṛtāpekṣam.
children.translated_text: An example regarding a sentence that would otherwise be purposeless — 'By the full oblation one obtains all desires' — because the injunction 'One offers the full oblation' is syntactically incomplete, this is the remainder. 'And whoever knows him thus — he transcends death' — because this [injunction] is syntactically incomplete, this is the remainder. The statement of fruit is praise. The expression of obtaining all desires, since all-desire-fulfillment requires a cause, is metaphorical. The expression 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) in reference to those who are not [actually] all depends on the context of the topic (<s>adhikṛta</s>).

children.text: phalasya karmaniṣpattes teṣāṃ lokavat parimāṇataḥ phalaviśeṣaḥ syāt // MS_1,2.17 //
children.translated_text: Since the result is accomplished by the ritual action, the distinction of result for those [cases] should be based on measure, as in the world. // MS 1.2.17 //

children.text: anvāruhya vacanam idaṃ{*1/461*} yady api vidhiḥ, tathāpy arthavattā parimāṇataḥ sārato vā phalaviśeṣāt.
children.translated_text: Following up on this statement — even though it is an injunction, nonetheless its meaningfulness [comes] from the distinction of result, either in terms of measure or in terms of quality.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{1/461: E1, S.49/6: pūrṇāhutyā sarvān kāmān avāpnotīti}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[E1, p. 49/6: 'By the full oblation one obtains all desires']

children.text: antyayor yathoktam // MS_1,2.18 //
children.translated_text: For the last two, as stated. // MS 1.2.18 //

children.text: abhāgipratiṣedhād ityādāv udāhṛtam - na pṛthivyām agniś cetavyo nāntarikṣe na divīti{*1/462*}, hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya cetavyam ity{*1/463*} ākāṅkṣitatvād asya vidheḥ śeṣaḥ. pṛthivyādīnāṃ nindā hiraṇyastutyarthā. asati prasaṅge pratiṣedho nityānuvādaḥ. yac cānityadarśanaṃ babaraḥ prāvāhaṇir akāmayata iti{*1/464*}. tatparihṛtam. arthavādākṣepeṇa punar utthitam idānīm arthavādaprāmāṇye tenaiva parihāreṇa parihariṣyata iti//
children.translated_text: What was cited under [the topic of] prohibition concerning those who are ineligible — 'Fire should not be piled up on the earth, nor in the atmosphere, nor in heaven' — because the injunction 'One should pile [the fire altar] upon gold' is syntactically incomplete, this is the remainder. The censure of earth and the rest serves the purpose of praising gold. When there is no occasion [for the act], the prohibition is merely a permanent re-statement (<s>nityānuvāda</s>). And as for the observation of non-eternality — '<s>Babara Prāvāhaṇi</s> desired' — that was refuted. Having been raised again through an objection based on <s>arthavāda</s>, it will now be refuted by the same refutation as before, [namely] that <s>arthavāda</s> is not authoritative. //
Page 50

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 5.2.7.1, cited in ŚBh on MS 1.2.5; Tait.S. 5.2.7.3; Cf. MS 1.2.6, Tait.S. 7.1.10.2; Edition cross-references: E2: 2,33; E4: 1,129; E5: 2,34; E6: 1,35]

children.text: vidhir vā syād apūrvatvāt, vādamātraṃ hy anarthakam // MS_1,2.19 //
children.translated_text: Or it may be an injunction, because of its novelty; for mere assertion is purposeless. // MS 1.2.19 //

children.text: iha ye vidhivan nigadā arthavādās te arthavādās te udāharaṇam - audumbaro yūpo bhavaty ūrg vā uduṃbara ūrk paśava ūrjair vāsmā ūrjaṃ paśūn nāpnoti ūrjo 'varuddhyā iti{*1/466*}. kim asya vidhiḥ kāryam utāsyāpi stutir iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? vidhir vā syād apūrvatvāt, vādamātraṃ hy anarthakam. vidhivan nigadeṣv evaṃjātīyakeṣu phalavidhiḥ syāt, phalaṃ hy avagamyate, tathā hy apūrvam arthaṃ vidhāsyati. itarathā stutivādamātram anarthakaṃ syāt. stutaś cāstutaś ca tāvān eva so 'rthaḥ. api ca ūrjo 'varuddhyā iti prayojanaṃ śrūyate. na ca - praśasto 'yam artha iti kaścic chabdo 'sti. lakṣaṇayā tu stutir gamyate. śrutiś ca lakṣaṇāyā jyāyasīti.
children.translated_text: Here, those statement-like recitations (<s>nigada</s>) that are like injunctions — the <s>arthavāda</s> examples — the example is: 'The sacrificial post is of <s>udumbara</s> wood — <s>ūrj</s> (nourishment) indeed is <s>udumbara</s>, <s>ūrk</s> (nourishment) are cattle, he obtains nourishment for himself, nourishment and cattle, for the securing of nourishment.' Should this be understood as an injunction of something to be done, or is this too praise? What then is the prima facie view? It may be an injunction, because of its novelty; for mere assertion is purposeless. In such injunction-like recitations, there should be an injunction of a fruit — for a fruit is understood, and thus it will enjoin something novel. Otherwise, it would be mere praise-assertion, which is purposeless. For whether praised or not, that thing remains exactly the same. Moreover, 'for the securing of nourishment' — a purpose is heard. And there is no word [that means] 'this thing is praiseworthy.' Rather, praise is understood only through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). And direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) is stronger than secondary signification.

NOTES:
[Cf. Tait.S. 2.1.1.6]

children.text: lokavad iti cet // MS_1,2.20 //
children.translated_text: If [you say it is] like the world. // MS 1.2.20 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi - stutir anarthikā, na ca śabdenāvagamyata iti. laukikāni vākyāni bhavanto vidāṃ kurvantu. tad yathā - iyaṃ gauḥ kretavyā devadattīyā, eṣā hi bahukṣīrā, stryapatyā, anaṣṭaprajā ceti. kretavyety apy ukte guṇābhidhānāt pravartantetarāṃ kretāraḥ. bahukṣīreti ca guṇābhidhānam avagamyate. tadvad vede 'pi bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — praise is purposeless and is not known from the word itself — then consider worldly sentences, gentlemen. For example: 'This cow of <s>Devadatta</s> should be purchased, for she gives much milk, has female offspring, and has not lost her young.' Even when [only] 'should be purchased' has been said, buyers are further motivated by the statement of qualities. And 'gives much milk' is understood as a statement of quality. Likewise it will be in the <s>Veda</s> as well.

children.text: na pūrvatvāt // MS_1,2.21 //
children.translated_text: Not so, because of priority. // MS 1.2.21 //

children.text: naitad evam. loke viditapūrvā arthā ucyante bahukṣīrādayaḥ. teṣāṃ vijñānam eva na prayojanam. ataḥ praśaṃsā gamyate. aviditavāde na śraddadhīran pūrvavacanād iva. viditatvād eva ca prarocayante. vaidikeṣu punar yadi vidhiśabdena na prarocayante na tarām arthavādena. jātāśaṅko hi vidhiśabde sa tadānīm. atha vidhiśabdena prarocitaḥ, kim arthavādaśabdena. api ca vede vyaktam asaṃvādaḥ. ūrjo 'varuddhyai ity aprasiddhaṃ vacanam. ūrgvā udumbara iti hetutvaṃ cāprasiddham. yasmād ūrg udumbaraḥ, tasmāt tanmayo yūpaḥ kartavya iti. ūrg udumbara ity anṛtavacanād anyad asyānṛtam iti parikalpyeta.
children.translated_text: This is not so. In the world, the qualities stated — such as giving much milk — are things already known from before. Their cognition [by the hearer] itself is not the purpose. Therefore, [the function of] praise is understood. If stated about unknown things, people would not believe, as if [spoken] from prior [authority]. And precisely because [the qualities are already] known, they [the buyers] are persuaded. But in the case of Vedic [passages], if they are not persuaded by the injunctive word, how much less so by <s>arthavāda</s>. For one who has doubts about the injunctive word at that point — how will <s>arthavāda</s> help? And if one is already persuaded by the injunctive word, what need for <s>arthavāda</s>? Moreover, in the <s>Veda</s> there is clearly a lack of correspondence [with fact]. 'For the securing of nourishment' — this expression is unfamiliar. '<s>Ūrg</s> (nourishment) is <s>udumbara</s>' — and the causal relation is also unfamiliar. [The claim that] because <s>udumbara</s> is nourishment, therefore a post made of it should be made — [and that] '<s>ūrg</s> is <s>udumbara</s>' is a false statement — from this falsehood, another falsehood about it would be constructed.

children.text: uktaṃ tu vākyaśeṣatvam // MS_1,2.22 //
children.translated_text: But it has been stated that [<s>arthavāda</s>] is syntactically connected [to an injunction]. // MS 1.2.22 //

children.text: uktam asmābhir vākyaśeṣatvam - vidhinā tv ekavākyatvād iti{*1/467*}. nanūktam - phalavacanam iha gamyate na stutir iti. yad iha phalavacanam, tad audumbarasya yūpasya. na ca, avihita audumbaro yūpo 'sti. tatra phalavacanam evānarthakam. stutivacanaḥ śabdo nāstīti cet. iha phalavacanena phalavattā pratīyate phalavāṃś ca praśasta iti, tatra phalavattāyām ānarthakyam iti yo dvitīyo 'rthaḥ praśaṃsā nāma sa gamyate. lakṣaṇeti cet, na, lakṣaṇāyām apy arthavattā bhavaty eva. lakṣaṇāpi hi laukikī. nanūktam asaṃvādo vede, na hy ūrg udumbara iti. guṇa vādena prarocanārthatāṃ brūmahe - gauṇatvāt saṃvādaḥ. kiṃ? sādṛśyam - yathānnaṃ prīteḥ sādhanam, evam idam api prītisādhanaśaktiyuktaṃ praśaṃsituṃ{*1/468*} praśaṃsāvācinā śabdenocyate{*1/469*}, śakyate hi tat pakvaphalasaṃbandhād ūrg iti vaktum.
children.translated_text: We have stated its syntactic connection — 'because of being one sentence with an injunction.' [Opponent:] But was it not said — 'a statement of fruit is understood here, not praise'? Whatever statement of fruit there is here pertains to the <s>udumbara</s> sacrificial post. But there is no <s>udumbara</s> post that has been enjoined [independently]. Therefore, the statement of fruit itself is purposeless. [Opponent:] 'There is no word for praise' — [we reply:] Here, through the statement of fruit, fruitfulness is understood, and what is fruitful is praiseworthy; therefore, since [fruitfulness] would be purposeless, the second meaning — namely, praise — is understood. [Opponent:] If through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — [we reply:] No, for even in secondary signification there is meaningfulness. Secondary signification too is used in the world. [Opponent:] But it was said there is no correspondence in the <s>Veda</s>, for '<s>ūrg</s> is <s>udumbara</s>' [is factually untrue]. [We reply:] We say that the persuasive function operates through metaphorical usage (<s>guṇavāda</s>) — the correspondence is because of the metaphorical nature. How so? Similarity — just as food is a means of satisfaction, so too this [<s>udumbara</s>], being endowed with the power to produce satisfaction, is spoken of with the word denoting praise; for it can be called '<s>ūrj</s>' (nourishment) because of its connection with ripe fruits.
Page 52

NOTES:
[Cf. MS 1.2.7; Textual variants across editions regarding <s>praśaṃsitum</s> and <s>prītisādhanaśabdenocyate</s>; Edition cross-references: E2: 2,40; E4: 1,151; E5: 2,40; E6: 1,36]

children.text: vidhiś cānarthakaḥ kvacit, tasmāt stutiḥ pratīyeta, tatsāmānyād itareṣu tathātvam // MS_1,2.23 //
children.translated_text: An injunction too is purposeless in some cases; therefore, praise should be understood, and because of similarity with those, the same applies in the other [cases]. // MS 1.2.23 //

children.text: apsuyonir vā aśvaḥ, apsujo vetasa iti{*1/471*} apsuyonir aśvaḥ kartavya iti vidher aśakyatvād ānarthakyam. tatrāvaśyaṃ stutiḥ kalpayitavyā, śamayitrībhir adbhir aśvasyāvakānāṃ ca saṃbandho yajamānasya kaṣṭaṃ śamayatīti. tatsāmānyād itareṣu tathātvam - tatheti yāvat, tāvat tathātvam iti. kiṃ tat sāmānyam. vidhyasaṃbhavaḥ stutisaṃbhavaś ca.
children.translated_text: ['The horse is water-born, the <s>vetasa</s> (reed) is water-born'] — 'a water-born horse should be made' — since an injunction would be impossible [to carry out], it is purposeless. Therefore, praise must necessarily be construed: by the calming waters, the connection of the horse and its afflictions — 'it calms the hardship of the sacrificer.' Because of similarity with those, the same applies in the other [cases] — 'same' means 'to that extent, that sameness.' What is that similarity? The impossibility of an injunction and the possibility of praise.

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 5.3.12]

children.text: prakaraṇe saṃbhavann apakarṣo na kalpyeta, vidhyānarthakyaṃ hi taṃ prati // MS_1,2.24 //
children.translated_text: When [praise] is possible within the context, a forced interpretation should not be construed; for the purposelessness of the injunction [points] toward that [praise]. // MS 1.2.24 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmaḥ stutir iti. kutaḥ? idaṃ samāmananti - yo vidagdhaḥ, sa nairṛtaḥ; yo 'śṛtaḥ, sa raudraḥ. yaḥ śṛtaḥ, sa daivataḥ. tasmād avidahatā śrapayitavyaḥ, sa daivatatvāyeti{*1/472*}. yadi stutir darśapūrṇamāsayor eva śṛtaḥ stāviṣyate. tathā saṃbhavann apakarṣo na kalpyeta. apakṛṣyate ity apakarṣaḥ. vidhipakṣe tu yatra nairṛtaḥ, tatra vidagdhatā nīyeta. tathā sati prakaraṇaṃ bādhitaṃ bhaved. darśapūrṇamāsakarma prati nairṛtābhāvād vidagdhānam anarthakaṃ syāt. tasmāt stutir eva.
children.translated_text: For this reason too we see that it is praise. Why? They teach thus — 'What is burnt is <s>Nairṛta</s> (belonging to <s>Nirṛti</s>); what is uncooked is <s>Raudra</s> (belonging to <s>Rudra</s>); what is cooked is divine. Therefore, [the offering] should be cooked without burning, for the sake of its divine nature.' If praise [applies], it will praise only the cooked [offering] of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites. Thus, a forced interpretation (<s>apakarṣa</s>) that is possible [within the context] should not be construed. 'Forced interpretation' means 'that which is dragged away [from its context].' But on the injunction hypothesis, where [the offering] is <s>Nairṛta</s>, burning would be required [there]. In that case, the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) would be overridden. Since there is no <s>Nairṛta</s> quality in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rite, the prohibition of burning would be purposeless. Therefore, it is praise alone.

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 2.6.3]

children.text: vidhau ca vākyabhedaḥ syāt // MS_1,2.25 //
children.translated_text: And on the injunction [hypothesis], there would be a splitting of the sentence. // MS 1.2.25 //

children.text: audumbaro yūpo bhavatīti vidhāv etasminn āśrīyamāṇe ūrjo 'varuddhyā ity{*1/473*} etasmiṃś ca vākyaṃ bhidyeta. ittham audumbaro yūpaḥ praśastaḥ, sa corjo 'viruddhyā iti. tasmād vidhivan nigadānām api stutir eva kāryam arthavādānām iti.
children.translated_text: 'The sacrificial post is of <s>udumbara</s> wood' — if this is treated as an injunction, and 'for the securing of nourishment' is [treated separately], then the sentence would be split. [Rather,] thus: the <s>udumbara</s> post is praiseworthy, and it is for the non-obstruction of nourishment. Therefore, even for those injunction-like recitations (<s>nigada</s>), [the function of] <s>arthavāda</s> is praise alone. //
Page 53

NOTES:
[Cf. Tait.S. 2.1.1.6; Edition cross-references: E2: 2,42; E4: 1,159; E5: 2,44; E6: 1,37]

children.text: hetur vā syād arthavattvopapattibhyām // MS_1,2.26 //
children.translated_text: Or it may be a reason, because of [its] purposefulness and logical fitness. // MS 1.2.26 //

children.text:
atha ye hetuvan nigadāḥ - sūrpeṇa{*1/475*} juhoti, tena hy annaṃ kriyata ityevamādayaḥ{*1/476*}. teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ stutis teṣāṃ kāryam uta hetur iti. kiṃ prāptam. hetuḥ syād annakaraṇaṃ homasya.
nanv aprasiddhe kāryakāraṇabhāve na hetūpadeśaḥ{*1/477*}. satyam evaṃ loke, vidhāyiṣyate tu vacanena vede. sūrpeṇa{*1/478*} home kartavye 'nnakaraṇaṃ hetur ity upadiśyate. kiṃ prayojanam. anyad api darvipīṭharādy{*1/479*} annakaraṇaṃ yat, tenāpi nāma kathaṃ homaḥ kriyeteti. kutaḥ. tasyāpy annakriyāyām arthavattā, śakyate ca tenāpy annaṃ kartum. etād dhi kriyata ity ucyate. na hi vartamānakālaḥ kaścid asti yasyāyaṃ pratinirdeśaḥ. hetau ca śrutiḥ śabdaḥ{*1/480*}, stutau lakṣaṇā. yadi ca darvipīṭharādi{*1/481*} na sākṣād annaṃ karotīti, nānnakaraṇam ity ucyate. vyarthe tasmin sūrpastutir{*1/482*} anarthikā syāt. sūrpam{*1/483*} api hi na sākṣād annaṃ karotīti, tena vinārthena sūrpasya{*1/484*} stutir nopapadyate.
children.translated_text:
Now, those <s>nigadas</s> (ritual recitations) that contain a reason — such as 'he offers with a winnowing basket (<s>sūrpa</s>), for by that food is made' and so forth. Regarding these there is a doubt: is their function praise (<s>stuti</s>) or reason (<s>hetu</s>)? What is the initial assumption? It should be a reason — [namely] that the making of food is the reason for the <s>homa</s> (oblation).
[Objection:] But when the cause-effect relation is not established, there can be no teaching of a reason. [Reply:] True, this is so in the world, but [in the <s>Veda</s>] it will be enjoined by the word. When a <s>homa</s> is to be performed with a winnowing basket, the making of food is taught as the reason. What is the purpose? So that even with something else that makes food — a ladle, a basin, etc. — the <s>homa</s> might likewise be performed. Why? Because that too has purposefulness in making food, and food can be made with that too. For 'food is made' is stated [in the present tense]. But there is no present-tense instance to which this statement refers. Moreover, for the reason-interpretation, the word bears its primary meaning (<s>śruti</s>); for the praise-interpretation, it bears a secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). And if a ladle, basin, etc. does not directly make food, it would not be called 'food-making.' Then, with that [ladle etc.] being purposeless, the praise of the winnowing basket would also be pointless. For the winnowing basket too does not directly make food, and therefore without that purpose, praise of the winnowing basket would be unjustified.

children.text:
NOTES:

*{1/479: E2,4: darvipiṭharādi; E5: darvīpīṭharādi; E6: darvīpiṭharādi}*

*{1/482: E2,4,5,6: śūrpastutir}*

children.text: stutis tu, śabdapūrvatvād acodanā ca tasya // MS_1,2.27 //
children.translated_text: But it is praise, because of [its] being preceded by the word, and because that [reason-statement] is not an injunction (<s>codanā</s>). // MS 1.2.27 //

children.text: na tv etad asti, śabdapūrvako 'yam arthaḥ/ annakaraṇaṃ hetur iti, śabdaś cānnakaraṇaṃ sūrpahome hetur ity āha. na ca darvipīṭharahome, tena śabdapūrvaṃ sūrpam, na ca darvipiṭharādeś{*1/485*} codanā.
children.translated_text: But this is not so — this meaning is preceded by the word. 'The making of food is the reason' — and the word says that the making of food is the reason in the <s>homa</s> with the winnowing basket, not in the <s>homa</s> with a ladle or basin. Therefore, the winnowing basket is preceded by the word, and there is no injunction (<s>codanā</s>) for the ladle, basin, and so forth.

children.text:
NOTES:

children.text: arthas tu vidhiśeṣatvāt, yathā loke // MS_1,2.29 //
children.translated_text: But it has a purpose, because of being a supplement to an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), as in the world. // MS 1.2.29 //

children.text: asmatpakṣe 'rtho 'sti. vākyaśeṣo hi sa vidhes tadā bhavati. saṃvādaś ca stutivacanatvena, yathā vayaṃ sūrpeṇānnaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ jānīmaḥ, tathā sūrpeṇānnaṃ kriyata ity eva gamyate. tadā cāvartamānaṃ stautuṃ{*1/487*} vartamānam ity upadiśati. tvatpakṣa eṣa doṣaḥ, yasya te hetuvidhiḥ. vidhau hi na paraḥ śabdārthaḥ pratīyate. na ca vartamānam upadiśan vedaḥ śakyam arthaṃ vidadhyāt. āsmatpakṣe tu eṣa paraśabdaḥ paratra vartate. yathā loke balavān devadatto yajñadattādīn prasahata iti. prakṛṣṭabale 'pi balavac chabdo vartamāno na siṃhaṃ śārdūlaṃ vāpekṣya prayujyate, ye devadattāt tu nikṛṣṭabalāḥ, tānapekṣya bhavati. evaṃ tena hy annaṃ kriyata iti prakṛṣṭānnakaraṇena saṃstavaḥ sūrpasya{*1/488*}, nikṛṣṭāny anyāny annākaraṇāny apekṣya bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: In our position, there is a purpose. For it [the statement] is then a supplement (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>) to the injunction. And there is agreement with its being a laudatory statement — just as we know that food is made with the winnowing basket, so too from 'food is made with the winnowing basket' this is understood. Then [the statement], while teaching something present as [if it were something] not present, praises it. This fault belongs to your position, where you hold the reason-interpretation. For in the case of an injunction, no further meaning beyond the word's meaning is apprehended. And the <s>Veda</s>, while teaching something present, could not enjoin a [new] purpose. But in our position, this secondary word refers elsewhere. Just as in the world, 'strong <s>Devadatta</s> overpowers <s>Yajñadatta</s> and others' — the word 'strong,' even when applied to one of great strength, is not used with reference to a lion or tiger, but is used with reference to those of lesser strength than <s>Devadatta</s>. Similarly, 'for by that food is made' — the praise of the winnowing basket through its superior food-making capacity will be with reference to other, inferior food-making [implements].
[TEXTUAL NOTES: E2,4,5,6 read <s>stotuṃ</s>; E2 has uncertain reading <s>śūrpapaya</s>.]

children.text: yadi ca hetur avatiṣṭheta nirdeśāt, sāmānyād iti ced avyavasthā vidhīnāṃ syāt // MS_1,2.30 //
children.translated_text: And if the reason were maintained, [then] from the statement [being general], because of generality — thus if objected — there would be instability of the injunctions. // MS 1.2.30 //

children.text: yady api ca bhaved annakaraṇaṃ hetur darvipiṭharaprakārāṇām, tathāpi sūrpa etāvatiṣṭheta. śabdād annakaraṇaṃ hetur iti vijñāyate. śadaś ca sūrpasyāha, na darvīpiṭharādīnām. tad dhi nirdiśyate, yasmāt sūrpeṇānnaṃ kriyate, tasmāt sūrpeṇa juhotīti. yathā yasmād balavad upadhmāto 'gniḥ, tena me gṛhaṃ dagdham iti, nānagnir api balavad upadhmāto dahatīti gamyate. atha matam - yena yenānnaṃ kriyate praṇāḍyā sūrpād anyenāpi, tena tenāpi homaḥ kriyata iti. avyavasthā vidhīnāṃ syāt, na kenacit praṇāḍyānnaṃ kriyate. tatra yāvad uktaṃ syāj juhotīti, tāvad evānnakaraṇena juhotīti. asmatpakṣe punaḥ sūrpaṃ stūyate - tena hy annaṃ kriyata iti vṛttāntānvākhyānaṃ na ca vṛttāntajñāpanāya, kiṃ tarhi prarocanāyaiva. tasmād dhetuvan nigadasyāpi stutir eva kāryam iti.
children.translated_text: Even if the making of food were the reason for [using implements] of the ladle-and-basin type, still the winnowing basket alone would be established [as the instrument]. From the word it is known that 'the making of food is the reason.' And the word speaks of the winnowing basket, not of ladles and basins. For what is specified is this: 'because food is made with the winnowing basket, therefore one offers with the winnowing basket.' Just as [in the example]: 'because the fire, strongly blown upon, [burned fiercely], my house was burned by it' — it is not understood from this that even a fire not strongly blown upon burns [a house]. Now, if one thinks 'with whatever food is made — whether a tube or something other than the winnowing basket — with that too the oblation should be performed' — there would be instability of the injunctions: no food is made with a tube. In that case, as much as was stated by 'he offers,' just that much would be [performed] by means of food-making. But in our position, the winnowing basket is praised — 'for by that food is made' is a narration of an [existing] fact, not for the purpose of informing about the fact, but rather for the purpose of commendation alone. Therefore, praise is the function even of a <s>nigada</s> containing a reason.

tadarthaśāstrāt // MS_1,2.31 //{*1/489*}
athedānīṃ kim vivakṣitavacanā mantrāḥ, utāvivakṣitavacanāḥ. kim arthaprakāśanena yāgasyopakurvanti, utoccāraṇamātreṇeti. yady uccāraṇamātreṇa, tadā na niyogato{*1/490*} barhir devasadanaṃ dāmīty{*1/491*} eṣa barhirlavane viniyujyeta. abhidhānena cet, prakaraṇena vijñātāṅgabhāvo{*1/492*} nānyatropakartuṃ śaknotīty antareṇāpi vacanam, barhirlavana eva viniyujyeteti. tad evam avagacchāmaḥ -uccāraṇamātreṇaivopakurvantīti. kutaḥ? tadarthaśāstrāt. yad abhidhānasamartho mantraḥ, tatraivainaṃ śāstraṃ nibadhnāti. uruprathā uru prathasveti{*1/493*} puroḍāśaṃ prathayatīti{*1/494*} vacanam idam anarthakam, yady arthābhidhānenopakurvanti. athoccāraṇamātreṇa, tato vaktavyo viniyogaḥ, uktaś ca. ato nārthābhidhānena. yathā sākṣaḥ puruṣaḥ pareṇa cen nīyate, nūnam akṣibhyāṃ na paśyatīti gamyate.
nanv arthavādārthaṃ bhaviṣyatīti cet. na hi, yena vidhīyate tasya vākyaśeṣo 'rthavāda ity uktam. na ca nirapekṣeṇa vihite 'rthavādena kiṃcid api prayojanaṃ kriyate. ato nārthavādārthaṃ vacanam.
tathābhyādānasamarthā mantrā{*1/495*} udāharaṇam. liṅgād evādāne prāptā vacanena vidhīyante, tāṃ caturbhir ādatta{*1/496*} iti. catuḥsaṃkhyārtham iti cet, na, samuccayaśabdābhāvāt. [56]{*1/497*} tathā, imām agṛbhṇan rasanāmṛtasyety{*1/498*} aśvābhidhānīm ādatta ity{*1/499*} udāharaṇam. rasanādāne{*1/500*} prāptasya{*1/501*} rasanādāna{*1/502*} eva śāstraṃ viniyojakam. tad vivakṣitārthatve na ghaṭeteti.
nanu gardabharasanāṃ{*1/503*} parisaṃkhyāsyati. na śaknoti parisaṃkhyātam{*1/504*}. parisaṃcakṣāṇo hi svārthaṃ ca{*1/505*} juhyāt, parārthaṃ ca kalpeta, prāptaṃ ca bādheta. tasmān na vivakṣitavacanā mantrāḥ. ato na pramāṇaṃ barhirdevasadanaṃ dāmīty asya rūpaṃ barhirlavane viniyogasya.
children.translated_text:
Because of a scripture [concerned with] its purpose. // MS 1.2.31 //
Now then — are <s>mantras</s> statements with intended meaning (<s>vivakṣitavacana</s>), or statements without intended meaning (<s>avivakṣitavacana</s>)? Do they assist the sacrifice by conveying meaning, or merely by their utterance? If merely by utterance, then the [<s>mantra</s>] 'O <s>Barhis</s> (sacrificial grass), seat of the gods, covering' would not necessarily be applied to the cutting of the sacrificial grass. But if by denotation — [then] the ancillary relationship understood through context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) could not serve elsewhere without [explicit] statement, and even without the statement it would be applied to the cutting of the grass alone. Thus we understand — they assist merely by utterance. Why? Because of a scripture [concerned with] its purpose. Where a <s>mantra</s> is capable of denoting a meaning, there alone does the scripture bind it. 'Spread wide, spread thyself wide' — the statement 'he spreads the sacrificial cake' — this statement would be purposeless if [<s>mantras</s>] assist by conveying meaning. But if merely by utterance, then the application must be stated, and it has been stated. Therefore, [they do] not [assist] by conveying meaning. Just as a man who has eyes — if he is being led by another, [one concludes] he surely does not see with his eyes.
[Objection:] It will serve the purpose of a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>). [Reply:] No, for it has been said that a laudatory passage is a supplement to what is enjoined. And no purpose whatsoever is served by a laudatory passage for something enjoined independently [without needing further justification]. Therefore, the statement is not for the purpose of a laudatory passage.
Similarly, <s>mantras</s> capable of taking [offerings] serve as an example. [<s>Mantras</s>] applicable by contextual indication to the taking [of offerings] are [instead] enjoined by a [specific] statement: 'He takes them with those four [<s>mantras</s>].' [Objection:] It is for the purpose of [specifying] the number four. [Reply:] No, because of the absence of a cumulative word (<s>samuccaya-śabda</s>). Similarly, 'This immortal rein I have grasped' — and 'he takes the horse-rein' — [this serves as] an example. For one to whom rein-taking is applicable, the scripture enjoining rein-taking itself is the assigner of application. This would not work under the intended-meaning interpretation.
[Objection:] It will exclude the donkey-rein [by specifying which rein]. [Reply:] It cannot exclude. For one who excludes would have to sacrifice his own purpose and accommodate another's purpose, and override what is established. Therefore, <s>mantras</s> are not statements with intended meaning. Hence the form of 'O <s>Barhis</s>, seat of the gods, covering' is not a valid authority for application to the cutting of the grass.

children.text: vākyaniyamāt // MS_1,2.32 //
children.translated_text: Because of the fixed [word-]order in sentences. // MS 1.2.32 //

children.text: niyatapadakramā hi mantrā bhavanti. agnimūrdhā diva iti{*1/506*}, na viparyayeṇa. yady arthapratāyanārthāḥ, viparyayeṇāpy arthaḥ pratīyata iti niyamo 'narthakaḥ syāt. athoccāraṇaviśeṣārthāḥ, viparyaye 'nyad uccāraṇam iti niyama āśrīyate. tena yatarasmin{*1/507*} pakṣe niyamo 'rthavān, sa nūnaṃ pakṣa iti. nanv arthavatsv api niyamo dṛśyate. yathā - indrāgnīti. yuktaṃ tatra tat, viparyaye 'rthapratyayābhāvāt.
children.translated_text: For <s>mantras</s> have a fixed word-order: '<s>Agni</s>, head of heaven' — and not in reverse order. If they were for the purpose of conveying meaning, the meaning would be understood even in reverse order, and so the fixed order would be purposeless. But if they are for the purpose of a specific utterance, a reversed [order] would be a different utterance, and so the fixed order is justified. Therefore, in whichever interpretation the fixed order has a purpose, that is surely the [correct] interpretation. [Objection:] But fixed order is seen even in meaningful [sentences] — as in '<s>Indrāgnī</s>' (Indra-and-Agni). [Reply:] That is justified there, because in reverse the meaning would not be apprehended.

children.text: buddhaśāstrāt // MS_1,2.33 //
children.translated_text: Because of [evidence from] a context where [the meaning is already] known (<s>buddhaśāstra</s>). // MS 1.2.33 //

children.text: buddhe khalv api pāṭhād arthe tadabhidhānasamartho mantro bhavati. agnīd agnīn vihared{*1/508*} iti{*1/509*}. sa buddhe kiṃ bodhayet. atha nūccāraṇaviśeṣārthāḥ{*1/510*}, buddhe 'py uccāraṇaviśeṣo 'vakalpyeteti. nanu punarvacanāt saṃskāraviśeṣo bhaviṣyati. evam asmatpakṣam evāśrito 'si. vacanam uccāraṇam. tad dhi śakyate kartuṃ nārthapratyāyanam. tat pratīte 'śakyam. yathā sopānatke pāde dvitīyām upānaham aśakyatvān nopādatte.
children.translated_text: Indeed, even when the meaning is [already] known from the recitation, a <s>mantra</s> capable of denoting that meaning exists. [For example:] 'The fire-priest (<s>Agnīdh</s>) should tend the fires.' That [meaning] being [already] known — what would it teach? But if [<s>mantras</s>] are for the purpose of a specific utterance, even when [the meaning is already] known, a specific utterance can be accomplished. [Objection:] But from a [repeated] statement, a special purificatory power (<s>saṃskāra</s>) will result. [Reply:] Thus you have resorted to our very position. Statement is utterance. That can indeed be performed, but conveying meaning [to one who already knows] cannot. When [the meaning] is [already] known, [conveying it again] is impossible — just as one who has a shoe on one foot does not put on a second shoe [on the same foot] because of the impossibility.

children.text: avidyamānavacanāt // MS_1,2.34 //
children.translated_text: Because of the statement of what does not [actually] exist. // MS 1.2.34 //

children.text: yajñe sādhanabhūtaḥ prakāśayitavyaḥ. na ca tādṛśo 'rtho{*1/512*} 'sti, yādṛśam abhidadhati{*1/513*}. yathā catvāri śṛṅgā{*1/514*} iti. na hi catuḥśṛṅgaṃ tripādaṃ dviśiraskaṃ saptahastaṃ kiṃcid yajñasādhanam asti. tad atrābhidhānārthaḥ kim abhidadhyāt. uccāraṇārthe tv avakalpyate. tathā mā mā hiṃsīr ity asatyām api hiṃsāyāṃ kim abhidadhyāt.
children.translated_text: What is to be illuminated is the means of the sacrifice. But no such object exists as [the <s>mantras</s>] describe. For example, 'Four horns [has it]' — for there is no sacrificial means having four horns, three feet, two heads, and seven hands. What then would [a <s>mantra</s>] intended for meaning-conveyance denote there? But for the purpose of utterance, it can be justified. Similarly, 'Do not harm me, do not harm me' — even when there is no actual harm, what would it denote [if its purpose were meaning-conveyance]?

children.text: acetane 'rthabandhanāt // MS_1,2.35 //
children.translated_text: Because of binding meaning to an insentient [entity]. // MS 1.2.35 //

children.text: acetane 'rthe khalv arthaṃ nibadhnanti - oṣadhe trāyasvainam{*1/515*} iti{*1/516*}. abhidhānenopakurvanta evaṃjātīyakā oṣadhiṃ paśutrāṇāya pratipādayeyuḥ. na cāsāv acetanā śakyā pratipādayitum. uccāraṇārthe tu naiṣa doṣo bhavati. tasmād uccāraṇārthāḥ. śṛṇota grāvāṇa iti{*1/517*} codāharaṇam.
children.translated_text: They bind meaning to an insentient object — 'O herb, protect him!' If [<s>mantras</s>] assist by conveying meaning, such [<s>mantras</s>] would direct the herb to protect the animal. But that [herb], being insentient, cannot be directed. For the purpose of utterance, however, this is no fault. Therefore, [<s>mantras</s>] are for the purpose of utterance. 'Listen, O pressing-stones' is given as another example.
[TEXTUAL NOTES: E4 has uncertain reading <s>trāyasvanaim</s>; source references Taittirīya-saṃhitā 1.2.1.1 and 1.3.13.1.]

children.text: arthavipratiṣedhāt // MS_1,2.36 //
children.translated_text: Because of the contradiction of meaning. // MS_1,2.36 //

children.text: arthavipratiṣedho 'pi bhavati. aditir dyaur aditir antarikṣam iti{*1/518*} saiva dyaus tad evāntarikṣam iti ko jātucid avadhārayet. anavadhārayaṃś ca kim abhidhānenopakuryāt. uccāraṇamātre tu naiṣa virodho bhavati. tasmād uccāraṇārthā mantrāḥ. eko rudro na dvitīyo 'vatasthe{*1/519*}. asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi, ye rudrā adhibhūmyām iti{*1/520*} codāharaṇam
children.translated_text: There is also a contradiction of meaning [in mantras if they are meant to convey meaning]. '<s>Aditi</s> is the sky, <s>Aditi</s> is the atmosphere' {*1/518*} — who could ever determine that the sky itself is the atmosphere? And being unable to determine this, what benefit would there be from the expression? But in [mere] utterance, there is no such contradiction. Therefore, mantras are for the purpose of utterance. 'One <s>Rudra</s> stands, without a second' {*1/519*}. 'Innumerable thousands — the <s>Rudras</s> who are upon the earth' {*1/520*} — this too is an example.

children.text: svādhyāyavad avacanāt // MS_1,2.37 //
children.translated_text: As in the case of Vedic recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>), because there is no [meaningful] statement. // MS_1,2.37 //

children.text: svādhyāyakāle pūrṇikāvahanti karoti. māṇavako 'vahanti mantram adhīte. nāsau tena mantreṇa tadabhidhānam abhyasyaty akṣarānupūrvyā avadhāraṇa eva yatate. yena ca nāma prayojanam, tad abhyasitavyam. ata uccāraṇābhyāsād uccāraṇena prayojanam ity avagacchāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: At the time of Vedic recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>), [the student] performs the <s>pūrṇikā-avahanti</s> [rite]. A student recites the <s>avahanti</s> mantra. He does not practice the expression of its meaning with that mantra — he merely strives for the correct sequence of syllables. And what has a purpose — that should be practiced. Therefore, from the practice of utterance, we understand that the purpose lies in the utterance [itself].

children.text: avijñeyāt // MS_1,2.38 //
children.translated_text: Because of [mantras being] incomprehensible. // MS_1,2.38 //

children.text: api ca keṣāñcin mantrāṇām aśakya evārtho veditum. yathā - amyak sā ta indra ṛṣṭir asma iti{*1/522*}. sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharītv iti{*1/523*}. indraḥ somasya kāṇuketi{*1/524*} ca. ete kiṃ pratyāyayeyuḥ. uccāraṇārthe tu na doṣaḥ. tasmād uccāraṇārthā mantrā iti.
children.translated_text: Moreover, the meaning of some mantras is simply impossible to know. For example: '<s>amyak sā ta indra ṛṣṭir asme</s>' {*1/522*}; '<s>sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharītu</s>' {*1/523*}; and '<s>indraḥ somasya kāṇuke</s>' {*1/524*}. What could these convey? But for the purpose of utterance, there is no defect. Therefore, mantras are for the purpose of utterance.

children.text: anityasaṃyogān mantrānarthakyam // MS_1,2.39 //
children.translated_text: Because of the impermanent connection [of mantras with specific objects], the mantras would be purposeless [if they were meant to convey meaning]. // MS_1,2.39 //

children.text: anityasaṃyogaḥ khalv api bhaven mantreṣv abhidhānārtheṣu. yathā - kiṃ te kṛṇvanti kīkaṭeṣu gāva iti{*1/525*}. kīkaṭā nāma janapadā. naicāśākhaṃ nāma nagaram. pramaṅgado{*1/526*} rājeti. yady abhidhānārthāḥ, prāk pramaṅgadān{*1/527*} nāyaṃ mantro 'nubhūtapūrva{*1/528*} iti gamyate. tad etais tadarthaśāstrādibhiḥ{*1/529*} kāraṇair mantrāṇām avivakṣitavacanatā.
children.translated_text: There would also be an impermanent connection if mantras were intended to convey meaning. For example: 'What do your cows do among the <s>Kīkaṭas</s>?' {*1/525*}. The <s>Kīkaṭas</s> are a people. <s>Naicāśākha</s> {*1/526*} is a city. <s>Pramaṅgada</s> {*1/527*} is a king. If [mantras] were meant to convey meaning, it would follow that this mantra was not experienced before [the time of] <s>Pramaṅgada</s> {*1/528*}. Therefore, by these reasons — the treatise on that purpose and the like {*1/529*} — the meaning of mantras is not intended to be expressed.

children.translated_text: Now, is that treatise indeed purposeless? No, for —

children.text: guṇārthena punaḥśrutiḥ // MS_1,2.41 //
children.translated_text: The repetition is for the purpose of a subsidiary [element]. // MS_1,2.41 //

children.text: yad uktam{*1/534*} - tāṃ caturbhir ādatta iti samuccayaśabdābhāvān na samuccayārtham iti. catuḥsaṃkhyāviśiṣṭam ādānaṃ kartavyam iti vākyād avagamyate. tad ekena mantreṇa gṛhṇan na yathāśrutaṃ{*1/535*} gṛhṇīyād iti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said {*1/534*} — 'he takes it with four [verses]' — [the objection was that] because of the absence of a word of accumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>), [the repetition] is not for the purpose of accumulation. [Reply:] From the sentence, it is understood that the taking is to be done with the specific number of four. Therefore, one who takes with a single mantra would not take as prescribed {*1/535*}.

children.text:
NOTES:

*{1/535: E2 om. gṛhṇan na yathāśrutaṃ}*

children.text: parisaṃkhyā // MS_1,2.42 //
children.translated_text: Enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>). // MS_1,2.42 //

children.text:
parisaṃcakṣāṇe ca{*1/536*} - imām agṛbhṇann ity aśvābhidhānīm ādatta iti trayo doṣāḥ prāduḥṣyur iti. naivaṃ saṃbandha ity ādatta iti. kathaṃ tarhi, ity aśvābhidhānīm iti. [60]{*1/537*} liṅgād raśanāmātre śabdāt tu viśeṣe 'śvābhidhānyām iti. sati ca vākye liṅgaṃ viniyojakam. tac cāsya prakaraṇāmnānānumitaṃ vākyaṃ nāsti. kataratat. etena mantreṇādānaṃ kuryād iti, yasmin sati raśanāmātre liṅgāt prāpnoti. aśvābhidhānyāṃ tu pratyakṣam eva vacanam. asmin sati tad ānumānikaṃ nāsti. tena gardabharaśanāyāṃ na prāptir eveti.
NOTES:
*{1/536: E1, S.56/4-6, Tait.S. 5.1.2.1}*
*{1/537: E2: 2,59; E4: 1,210; E5: 2,59; E6: 1,41}*
children.translated_text:
And when enumerating {*1/536*} — '<s>imām agṛbhṇāt</s>' (he seized this one) — [the objection was that] in taking [a halter described as] 'one that designates a horse,' three defects would arise. [Reply:] The connection is not thus — 'he takes [the halter].' How then? '[He takes] the one that designates a horse.' [60]{*1/537*} From the indicatory mark, [the mantra applies to] a halter in general; but from the [explicit] word, specifically to a horse-halter. And when there is a [Vedic] sentence, the indicatory mark serves as the means of assignment. And this [mantra] does not have a sentence inferred from context-recording. Which [sentence would that be]? 'He should perform the taking with this mantra' — in which case, from the indicatory mark, [the mantra] would apply to a halter in general. But for the horse-halter, there is a direct [Vedic] statement. When this [direct statement] exists, that inferred [sentence] does not exist. Therefore, there is simply no application to a donkey-halter.
NOTES:
*{1/536: E1, p. 56/4-6, <s>Tait.S.</s> 5.1.2.1}*
*{1/537: E2: 2,59; E4: 1,210; E5: 2,59; E6: 1,41}*

children.text: arthavādo vā // MS_1,2.43 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>). // MS_1,2.43 //

children.text:
uru prathā uru prathasveti puroḍāśaṃ prathayatīty{*1/538*} arthavādārthena punaḥśrutiḥ, yajñapatim eva tat prathayatīti. nanu nāyaṃ mantrasya vākyaśeṣaḥ, na ca prāptasya stutyā prayojanam.
satyam{*1/539*}, nāyaṃ mantrasya vidhiḥ, na saṃstavaḥ. prathanam eva tatra stūyate. mantraḥ punā rūpād eva prāpta ihānūdyate prathanaṃ stotum - itthaṃ prathanaṃ praśastam, yat kriyamāṇam evaṃrūpeṇa mantreṇa kriyate. kas tadā bhavati guṇaḥ. yajñapatim eva tat prajayā paśubhiḥ prathayati. kim etad evāsya phalaṃ bhavati. neti brūmaḥ. stutiḥ kathaṃ bhaviṣyatīty evam ucyate.
katham asati prathane prathayatīti śabdaḥ. mantrābhidhānāt - mantreṇa puroḍāśam adhvaryuḥ prathasveti brūte. yaś caivaṃ prathasveti brūte, sa prathayati, yathā - yaḥ kurv iti brūte, sa kārayati.
children.translated_text:
'Spread wide, spread wide' — [the objection was that] in '<s>puroḍāśaṃ prathayati</s>' (he spreads the sacrificial cake) {*1/538*}, the repetition is for the purpose of an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) — that [the mantra] 'spreads' the sacrificer himself [with prosperity]. [Objection:] But this is not the sentence-completion of the mantra, and there is no purpose in praising what is already obtained.
[Reply:] True {*1/539*}, this is neither an injunction of the mantra nor a eulogy. The spreading itself is praised there. The mantra, being already obtained by its very form, is here restated in order to praise the spreading — 'the spreading is praiseworthy, since when performed, it is performed with a mantra of such form.' What then is the subsidiary benefit? 'It spreads the sacrificer himself with offspring and cattle.' Is this the only result? We say no. How [otherwise] would it be a praise? — thus it is stated.
How can the word '<s>prathayati</s>' (he spreads) [be used] when there is no [actual] spreading? [Reply:] Because of the mantra-expression: with the mantra, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> says to the sacrificial cake '<s>prathasva</s>' (spread!). And he who says '<s>prathasva</s>' (spread!) [to something] thereby 'makes it spread' (<s>prathayati</s>) — just as he who says '<s>kuru</s>' (do!) thereby 'makes [another] do' (<s>kārayati</s>).

children.text:
NOTES:
*{1/538: Tait.S. 3.2.8.4, zitiert: ŚBh ad MS 1.2.31}*
*{1/539: E2 om. satyam}*
children.translated_text:
