*{1/539: E2 om. <s>satyam</s>}*

children.text: aviruddhaṃ param // MS_1,2.44 //
children.translated_text: The higher [interpretation, namely that mantras convey meaning,] is non-contradictory. // MS_1,2.44 //

children.text: yad uktam{*1/540*} - padaniyamasyārthavattvād{*1/541*} avivakṣitārthā mantrā iti. kāmam anarthako niyamaḥ, na dṛṣṭam apramāṇam. niyatoccāraṇam adṛṣṭāyeti cet, aviruddhā adṛṣṭakalpanāsmatpakṣe 'pi. evaṃ pratyāyamānam abhyudayakāri bhavatīti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said {*1/540*} — 'because the word-regulation is meaningful {*1/541*}, mantras do not intend to convey meaning' — [reply:] by all means let the regulation be purposeless; [but] something directly perceived cannot be invalidated. [Objection:] If [mantras have] regulated utterance for a transcendent purpose (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>)... [Reply:] The postulation of a transcendent [purpose] is equally non-contradictory in our position too. [And in addition,] what is conveyed [by the mantra] produces well-being (<s>abhyudaya</s>).

children.text: saṃpraiṣe karmagarhānupālambhaḥ saṃskāratvāt // MS_1,2.45 //
children.translated_text: In a directive (<s>saṃpraiṣa</s>), the reproach of action is not a censure, because [the directive] serves as a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>). // MS_1,2.45 //

children.text: atha yad uktam{*1/543*} - prokṣaṇīr āsādayeti buddhabodhanam aśakyam, ata uccāraṇād adṛṣṭam iti. tan na. kartavyam ity api vijñāte 'nuṣṭhānakāle smṛtyā prayojanam. upāyāntareṇāpi sā prāpnoti, ato 'nenopāyena kartavyeti niyamārtham āmnānam, saṃskāratvāt.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was said {*1/543*} — 'Set the sprinkling waters!' — awakening someone who is [already] aware is impossible; therefore, from the utterance [arises] a transcendent result. [Reply:] This is not so. Even when [the procedure] 'this must be done' is already known, at the time of performance, memory serves a purpose. That [memory] could be obtained by another means as well; therefore, the recording [of the directive] is for the purpose of restricting [the ritual to] this particular means — because [the directive] serves as a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>).

children.text:
NOTES:
*{1/543: ŚBh ad MS 1.2.33, Mādhy.S.1.28; Tait.S. 3.2.9}*
abhidhāne 'rthavādaḥ // MS_1,2.46 //
children.translated_text: When there is expression [of meaning], it is an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>). // MS_1,2.46 //

children.text:
catvāri śṛṅgā ity{*1/544*} asad abhidhāne gauṇaḥ śabdaḥ. gauṇī kalpanā pramāṇavattvāt. uccāraṇād adṛṣṭam apramāṇam. catasro hotrāḥ śṛṅgāṇīvāsya. trayo 'sya pādā iti savanābhiprāyam. dve śīrṣa iti patnīyajamānau. sapta hastāsa iti chandāṃsy abhipretya. tridhā baddha iti tribhir vedair baddhaḥ. vṛṣabhaḥ kāmān varṣatīti. roravīti śabdakarmā. maho devo martyān āviveśeti, manuṣyādhikārābhiprāyam. tad yathā - cakravākastanī haṃsadantāvalī kāśavastrā śaivālakeśī nadīti nadyāḥ stutiḥ.
yajñasamṛddhaye sādhanānāṃ cetanasādṛśyam upapādayitukāma āmantraṇaśabdena lakṣayati{*1/545*} - oṣadhe trāyasvainam iti{*1/546*}. śṛṇota grāvāṇa iti{*1/547*}, ataḥ paraṃ prātaranuvākānuvacanaṃ bhaviṣyati, yatrācetanāḥ santo grāvāṇo 'pi śṛṇuyuḥ, kiṃ punar vidvāṃso 'pi brāhmaṇā iti. itthaṃ cācetanā api grāvāṇa āmantryante.
children.translated_text:
'Four horns' {*1/544*} — when the expression is of something that does not exist [literally], the word is secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>). The secondary construal is [adopted] because it has the support of a valid means of knowledge. [The alternative, that] a transcendent result [arises] from utterance, is without [such] support. [The meaning is:] 'Four oblation-priests (<s>hotrā</s>) are like his horns. His three feet' — this refers to the three pressings (<s>savana</s>). 'Two heads' — [these are] the wife (<s>patnī</s>) and the sacrificer. 'Seven hands' — this refers to the metres (<s>chandas</s>). 'Bound threefold' — bound by the three <s>Vedas</s>. 'The bull rains [desired objects].' 'He bellows' — his function is connected with sound. 'The great god has entered mortals' — this refers to the domain of human [ritual] activity. Just as [one might praise] a river: 'Having the voice of a <s>cakravāka</s> bird, with rows of teeth like swans, clothed in <s>kāśa</s> grass, with hair of moss' — this is a praise of the river.
Desiring to establish a likeness of the ritual implements to sentient beings for the prosperity of the sacrifice, [the text] indicates [this] through the vocative form {*1/545*}: 'O herb, protect him!' {*1/546*}. 'Listen, O pressing-stones!' {*1/547*} — henceforth there will be the recitation of the dawn-litany (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>), at which even the insentient pressing-stones would listen — how much more so the learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>! Thus, even the insentient pressing-stones are addressed.

children.text: guṇād avipratiṣedhaḥ syāt // MS_1,2.47 //
children.translated_text: Because of [the use of] secondary meaning, there would be no contradiction. // MS_1,2.47 //

children.text: aditir dyaur iti{*1/548*} gauṇa eṣa śabdaḥ, ato na [62]{*1/549*}vipratiṣedhaḥ/ yathā - tvam eva mātā, tvam eva{*1/550*} piteti. tathaikarudradaivatya eko rudraḥ, śatarudradaivatye śataṃ rudrā ity avirodhaḥ.
children.translated_text: '<s>Aditi</s> is the sky' {*1/548*} — this word is secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>); therefore, there is no [62]{*1/549*} contradiction. Just as [one says]: 'You alone are [my] mother, you alone are [my] father' {*1/550*}. Similarly, in a hymn addressed to a single <s>Rudra</s>, '<s>Rudra</s>' is one; in a hymn addressed to a hundred <s>Rudras</s>, '<s>Rudras</s>' are a hundred — and there is no contradiction.

children.text: vidyāvacanam asaṃyogāt // MS_1,2.48 //
children.translated_text: The statement [about <s>svādhyāya</s>] pertains to [Vedic] study, because of the absence of connection [with sacrifice]. // MS_1,2.48 //

children.text: yat tu{*1/551*} - akarmakāle 'vahanti mantreṇa māṇavako na pūrṇikāvahantiṃ prakāśayitum iccatīti. ayajñasaṃyogāt, na yajñopakārāyaitat prakāśayitum icchati. nanu prakāśanānabhyāso 'kṣarābhyāsaś ca paricoditaḥ. ucyate - saukaryāt prakāśanānabhyāso durgrahatvāc cākṣarābhyāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: As for [the argument] {*1/551*} — that at a time when there is no ritual action, a student [reciting] the <s>avahanti</s> mantra does not wish to illuminate the <s>pūrṇikā-avahanti</s> [rite] — [we reply:] because of the absence of connection with sacrifice, he does not wish to illuminate it for the purpose of assisting a sacrifice. [Objection:] But is not the non-practice of meaning-illumination and the practice of syllable-[recitation] what has been pointed out? [Reply:] It is said: the non-practice of meaning-illumination is due to ease [of recitation without understanding], and the practice of syllable-[recitation] is due to the difficulty of grasping [the meaning].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{1/551: ŚBh ad MS 1.2.37}*

sataḥ param avijñānam // MS_1,2.49 //{*1/552*}
vidyamāno 'py arthaḥ pramādālasyādibhir nopalabhyate. nigamaniruktavyākaraṇavaśena dhātuto 'rthaḥ kalpayitavyaḥ. yathā - sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharītv ityevamādīny{*1/553*} aśvinor abhidhānāni dvivacanāntāni lakṣyante. anenāśvinoḥ kāmam aprā ity{*1/554*} āśvinaṃ sūktam avagamyate. devatābhidhānāni ca ghaṭante jarbharītyevamādīni. avayavaprasiddhyā ca laukikenārthena viśeṣyante. evaṃ sarvatra.
children.translated_text:
The supreme [reality] beyond what exists is unknowable. // MS 1,2.49 //
Even an existing object is not apprehended due to carelessness, laziness, and the like. The meaning should be determined from the root by means of the Vedic concordance (<s>Nigama</s>), etymology (<s>Nirukta</s>), and grammar (<s>Vyākaraṇa</s>). For example, [words like] 'sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharī' and similar designations of the <s>Aśvins</s> are observed to end in the dual number. From this, the <s>Āśvina</s> hymn 'aśvinoḥ kāmam aprā' is understood. And the designations of deities such as 'jarbharī' and the like are fitting. And through the well-known component meanings, they are specified by ordinary [etymological] meaning. Thus everywhere.

children.text:
uktaś cānityasaṃyogaḥ // MS_1,2.50 //{*1/555*}
paraṃ tu śrutisāmānyamātram ity{*1/556*} atreti{*1/557*}.
children.translated_text:
And the non-permanent connection has been stated. // MS 1,2.50 //
But it is merely a general similarity of scripture — thus here.

children.text: liṅgopadeśaś ca tadarthavat // MS_1,2.51 //
children.translated_text: And the indication through secondary marks (<s>liṅga</s>) is in accordance with the intended meaning. // MS 1,2.51 //

children.text: āgneyāgnīdhram upatiṣṭhata iti{*1/559*} vidhānād vivakṣitārthānām eva mantrāṇāṃ bhavati liṅgeṇopadeśaḥ. yadi te 'gniprayojanāḥ, tatas ta āgneyā nāgniśabdasaṃnidhānāt.
children.translated_text: From the injunction 'approach the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [fire-altar] with the <s>Āgneya</s> [formula]: upatiṣṭhata,' the indication through secondary marks occurs only for mantras whose meaning is intended. If they serve the purpose of fire (<s>Agni</s>), then they are called <s>Āgneya</s> — not merely because of the proximity of the word <s>Agni</s>.

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 3.1.6]
Modification (<s>ūha</s>). // MS 1,2.52 //

children.text: ūhadarśanaṃ ca vivakṣitārthānām eva bhavati. kim ūhadarśanam. na pitā vardhate, na māteti{*1/560*}. anye vardhanta iti gamyate. pratyakṣaṃ kaumārayauvanasthāvirair vardhante mātrādayaḥ. śabdo na vardhata iti brūte. kā punaḥ śabdasya vṛddhiḥ. yad dvivacanabahuvacanasaṃyogaḥ.
children.translated_text: The observation of modification (<s>ūha</s>) also occurs only for [mantras] whose meaning is intended. What is the observation of modification? 'The father does not grow, nor the mother.' [From this] it is understood that others grow. It is directly perceived that the mother and others grow through childhood, youth, and old age. The text says that the word does not grow. But what is the growth of a word? It is the connection with dual and plural [forms].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{1/560: Vgl. Tait.Br. 3.6.6.1}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[Cf. Tait.Br. 3.6.6.1]

children.text: vidhiśabdāś ca // MS_1,2.53 //
children.translated_text: And injunctive words [confirm this]. // MS 1,2.53 //

children.text: vidhiśabdāś ca vivakṣitārthān eva mantrān anuvadanti - śataṃ himāḥ śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvyāsam ity etad evāheti{*1/561*}.
children.translated_text: Injunctive words too refer back to mantras whose meaning is indeed intended — 'May I live a hundred winters, a hundred years' — this is exactly what it says.

children.text: dharmasya śabdamūlatvād aśabdam anapekṣaṃ syāt // MS_1,3.1 //
children.translated_text: Since <s>Dharma</s> has its root in [Vedic] words, that which is without [Vedic] words should be disregarded. // MS 1,3.1 //

children.text: evaṃ tāvat kṛtsnasya vedasya prāmāṇyam uktam. athedānīṃ yatra na vaidikaṃ śabdam upalabhemahi, atha ca smaranti - evam ayam artho 'nuṣṭhātavyaḥ, etasmai ca prayojanāyeti. kim asau tathaiva syān na veti. yathā - aṣṭakāḥ kartavyāḥ; gurur anugantavyaḥ; taḍāgaṃ khanitavyam; prabhā pravartayitavyā; śikhākarma kartavyam ityevamādayaḥ. tad ucyate - dharmasya śabdamūlatvād aśabdam anapekṣaṃ syād iti. śabdalakṣaṇo dharma ity uktam{*1/563*} - codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ iti. ato nirmūlatvān nāpekṣitavyam iti. nanu ye vidur ittham asau padārthaḥ kartavya iti, katham iva te vadiṣyanty akartavya evāyam iti. smaraṇānupapattyā, na{*1/564*} hy ananubhūto 'śruto vārthaḥ smaryate. na cāsyāvaidikasyālaukikasya ca smaraṇam upapadyate, pūrvavijñānakāraṇābhāvād iti. yā hi bandhyā smareta - idaṃ me dauhitrakṛtam iti, na me duhitāstīti matvā, na jātucid asau pratīyāt - samyag etaj jñānam iti. evam api yathaiva pāramparyeṇāvicchedād ayaṃ veda iti pramāṇam eṣāṃ smṛtiḥ, evam iyam api pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. naitad evam. pratyakṣeṇopalabdhatvād granthasya, nānupapannaṃ pūrvavijñānam. aṣṭakādiṣu tv adṛṣṭārtheṣu pūrvavijñānakāraṇābhāvād vyāmohasmṛtir eva gamyate. tad yathā kaścij jātyandho vadet - smarāmy aham asya rūpaviśeṣasyeti. kutas te pūrvavijñānam iti ca paryanuyukto jātyandham evāparaṃ vinirdiśeta. tasya [65]{*1/565*} kutaḥ? jātyandhāntarāt. evaṃ jātyandhaparamparāyām api satyāṃ naiva jātucit saṃpratīyur vidvāṃsaḥ samyagdarśanam etad iti. ato nādartavyam evaṃjātīyakam anapekṣaṃ syād iti.
children.translated_text:
Thus, the authoritativeness of the entire <s>Veda</s> has been established. Now, where we do not find a Vedic text, yet people remember: 'This matter should be practiced, and for this purpose' — should that be [accepted] as valid or not? For example: 'The <s>Aṣṭakā</s> rites should be performed; the teacher should be followed; a reservoir should be dug; a water-fountain should be set up; the <s>śikhā</s>-ceremony should be performed' — and similar [injunctions]. To this it is said: 'Since <s>Dharma</s> has its root in [Vedic] words, that which is without [Vedic] words should be disregarded.' It has been stated that <s>Dharma</s> is characterized by [Vedic] words — '<s>Dharma</s> is that purpose characterized by Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>).' Therefore, being without foundation, it should not be heeded.
[Objection:] But those who know say 'this thing should be done' — how could they say it should not be done? [Reply:] Because remembrance (<s>smṛti</s>) is untenable [in such cases] — for an object that has never been experienced or heard of is not remembered. And remembrance of something that is neither Vedic nor worldly is untenable, due to the absence of a cause for prior cognition. For if a barren woman were to remember 'this was done by my grandchild' — knowing that 'I have no daughter' — no one would ever trust that 'this is valid knowledge.'
[Objection:] But just as the <s>Veda</s> is authoritative through unbroken tradition, so too this remembrance will be authoritative. [Reply:] This is not so. Because the text [of the <s>Veda</s>] is apprehended through direct perception, prior cognition is not untenable [in its case]. But for the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> rites and the like, which have unseen purposes, remembrance is understood to be mere delusion, due to the absence of a cause for prior cognition. Just as a person born blind might say 'I remember this particular visual form' — and when asked 'What is your basis for prior cognition?' would point to another person born blind. And what is that [second person's] basis? Yet another person born blind. Thus, even though there is a succession of persons born blind, the learned would never accept that 'this is correct perception.' Therefore, what is of this kind should not be heeded — 'that which is without [Vedic words] should be disregarded.'

NOTES:
[Cf. MS 1.1.2] | [E2,4 omit 'na'] | [Edition page references: E2: 2,73; E4: 1,243; E5: 2,70; E6: 1,45]

children.text: api vā kartṛsāmānyāt pramāṇam anumānaṃ syāt // MS_1,3.2 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, because of the commonality of authorship, inference would be a valid means of knowledge [for <s>smṛti</s>]. // MS 1,3.2 //

children.text:
api veti pakṣo vyāvartyate. pramāṇaṃ smṛtiḥ, vijñānaṃ hi tat. kim ity anyathā bhaviṣyati. pūrvavijñānam asya nāsti, kāraṇābhāvād iti cet. asyā eva smṛter draḍhimnaḥ kāraṇam anumāsyāmahe. tat tu nānubhavanam, anupapattyā. na hi manuṣyā ihaiva janmany evaṃjātīyakam artham anubhavituṃ śaknuvanti. janmāntarānubhūtaṃ ca na smaryate. granthas tv anumīyeta, kartṛsāmānyāt smṛti-vaidikapadārthayoḥ. tenopapanno vedasaṃyogas traivarṇikānām.
nanu nopalabhanta evaṃjātīyakaṃ grantham. anupalabhamānā apy anumimīran, vismaraṇam apy upapadyata iti. tad upapannatvāt pūrvavijñānasya tarivarṇikānāṃ smaratām, vismaraṇasya copapannatvād granthānumānam upapadyata iti pramāṇaṃ smṛtiḥ.
aṣṭakāliṅgāś ca mantrā vede dṛśyante - yāñ janāḥ pratinandantītyevamādayaḥ{*1/566*}. tathā pratyupasthitaniyamānām ācārāṇāṃ dṛṣṭārthatvād eva prāmāṇyam - guror anugamāt prīto gurur adhyāpayiṣyati granthagranthibhedinaś ca nyāyān parituṣṭo vakṣyatīti. tathā ca darśayati - tasmāc chreyāṃsaṃ pūrvaṃ yantaṃ pāpīyān paścād anvetīti{*1/567*}. prapāstaḍāgāni ca paropakārāya, na dharmāyety evāvagamyate. tathā ca darśanam - dhanvann iva prapā [66]{*1/568*} asīti{*1/569*}. tathā - sthalayodakaṃ parigṛhṇantīti ca. gotracihnaṃ śikhākarma, darśanaṃ ca - yatra bāṇāḥ saṃpatanti kumārā viśikhā iveti{*1/570*}. tena ye dṛṣṭārthāḥ, te tata eva pramāṇam. ye tv adṛṣṭārthāḥ, teṣu vaidikaśabdānumānam iti.
children.translated_text:
The word 'api vā' (or alternatively) indicates a shift of position. <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition) is a valid means of knowledge, for it is indeed cognition. Why should it be otherwise? [Objection:] Its prior cognition does not exist, due to the absence of a cause. [Reply:] We shall infer a cause for the firmness of this very remembrance. But that [cause] is not [direct] experience, because [such experience] is untenable — for human beings in this very lifetime are unable to experience objects of this kind. And what was experienced in a previous birth is not remembered. But a [Vedic] text may be inferred, because of the commonality of authorship between <s>smṛti</s> and Vedic subjects — [both were composed by] the three upper castes (<s>traivarṇika</s>). Thus the connection with the <s>Veda</s> is established for those of the three castes.
[Objection:] But they do not find a text of this kind. [Reply:] Even without finding [it], they may infer [it], for forgetting is also tenable. Therefore, since prior cognition is tenable for the three-caste members who remember, and since forgetting is tenable, the inference of a [lost Vedic] text is tenable — hence <s>smṛti</s> is a valid means of knowledge.
Moreover, mantras indicating the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> rites are seen in the <s>Veda</s> — [such as] 'those which people welcome' and similar [passages]. Likewise, for customs whose purpose is self-evident and which are currently practiced, their validity [comes] precisely from the visible purpose — [for example,] from following the teacher, the pleased teacher will teach the texts and, being satisfied, will explain the methods that untangle difficult passages. And scripture shows this too: 'Therefore, the better one going ahead, the inferior one follows after.' And water-fountains and reservoirs are for the benefit of others, not for <s>Dharma</s> — this is exactly how it is understood. And scripture shows: 'Like a water-fountain in a desert, you are.' Also: 'They collect water on dry land.' The <s>śikhā</s>-ceremony is a clan-mark, and the scriptural evidence [is]: 'Where arrows fall, like boys without topknots.' Therefore, those [practices] whose purpose is visible have their validity from that [visible purpose] alone. But for those whose purpose is unseen, the inference of a Vedic text [is proposed].

NOTES:
[Pāra.GS 3.2.2, Āp.MP 2.20.27] | [E2: anveti] | [Edition page references: E2: 2,78; E4: 1,259; E5: 2,78; E6: 1,45] | [ṚV 10.4.1c] | [ṚV 6.75.17a]

children.text: virodhe tv anapekṣaṃ syāt, asati hy anumānam // MS_1,3.3 //
children.translated_text: But when there is a contradiction [with <s>śruti</s>], it should be disregarded; for inference [operates] only in the absence [of direct scriptural evidence]. // MS 1,3.3 //

children.text:
atha yatra śrutivirodhaḥ, tatra katham. yathaudumbaryāḥ sarvaveṣṭanam, audumbarīṃ spṛṣṭvodgāyed iti śrutyā viruddham. aṣṭācatvāriṃśad vaṛṣāṇi vedabrahmacaraṇam, jātaputraḥ kṛṣṇakeśo 'gnīn ādadhītety anena viruddham. krītarājako bhojyān na iti, tasmād agnīṣomīye saṃsthite yajamānasya gṛhe 'śitavyam ity anena viruddham. tat pramāṇam, kartṛsāmānyād ityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - aśakyatvād vyamoha ity avagamyate. katham aśakyatā. sparśavidhānān na sarvā śakyā veṣṭayitum udgāyatā spraṣṭuṃ ca. tām udgāyatā spraṣṭavyām avagacchantaḥ kenemaṃ saṃpratyayaṃ bādhemahi sarvaveṣṭanasmaraṇeneti brūmaḥ.
nanu nirmūlatvād vyāmohas tat smaraṇam iti vaidikaṃ vacanaṃ mūlaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. bhaved vaidikaṃ vacanaṃ mūlam, yadi sparśanaṃ vyāmohaḥ. avyāmohe tv aśakyatvād anupapannam. yathānubhavanam anupapannam iti na kalpyate, tathā vaidikam api vacanam. kathaṃ tarhi sarvaveṣṭanasmaraṇam. vyāmohaḥ. kathaṃ vyāmohakalpanā. śrautavijñānavirodhāt. atha kim arthaṃ nemau vidhī vikalpye[67]{*1/571*}te vrīhiyavavad bṛhadrathantaravad vā. nāsati vyāmohavijñāne vikalpo bhavati. yadi sarvaveṣṭanavijñānaṃ pramāṇam, sparśanaṃ vyāmohaḥ. yadi sparśanaṃ pramāṇam, smṛtir vyāmohaḥ. vikalpaṃ tu vadan sparśanasya pakṣe tāvat prāmāṇyam anumanyate. tasya ca mūlaṃ śrutiḥ. sā cet pramāṇam anumatā, na pākṣikī. pākṣikaṃ ca sarvaveṣṭanasmaraṇam, pakṣe tāvan na śaknoti śrutiṃ parikalpayitum, sparśavijñānena bādhitatvāt. tataś cāvyāmohe ca tasminn aśakyā śrutiḥ kalpayitum. na cāsāv avyāmohaḥ pakṣe, pakṣe vyāmoho bhaviṣyatīti. yad eva hi tasyaikasmin pakṣe mūlam, tad evetarasminn api. ekasmiṃś cet pakṣe na vyāmohaḥ, śrutiprāmāṇyatulyatvād itaratrāpy avyāmohaḥ. na cāsāv ekasmin pakṣe śrutiḥ, nibaddhākṣarā hi sā na pramādapāṭha iti śakyā gaditum. tena naitat pakṣe vijñānaṃ vyāmohāt pakṣāntaraṃ saṃkrāntam ity avagamyate. tatra duḥśrutasvapnādivijñānamūlatvaṃ ta sarvaveṣṭanasyeti virodhāt kalpyate. na hi tasya sati virodhe prāmāṇyam abhyupagantavyam iti kiṃcid asti pramāṇam. tasmād yathaivaikasmin pakṣe na śakyā śrutiḥ kalpayitum, evam aparasmin pakṣe, tulyakāraṇatvāt.
api cetaretarāśraye 'nyataḥ paricchedāt. keyam itaretarāśrayatā. pramāṇāyāṃ smṛtau sparśanaṃ vyāmohaḥ, sparśane pramāṇe smṛtir vyāmohaḥ, tad etad itaretrāśrayaṃ bhavati. tatra sparśanasya kḷptaṃ mūlaṃ kalpyaṃ smṛteḥ, so 'sāv anyataḥ paricchedaḥ. kalpyamūlatvāt smṛtiprāmāṇyam anavakḷptaṃ. tad aprāmāṇyāt sparśanaṃ na vyāmohaḥ. tad avyāmohāt smārtaśrutikalpanānupapannā pramāṇābhāvāt. nanv evaṃ sati vrīhisādhanatvavijñānasyāpy avyāmohād yavaśrutir nopapadyeta. satyaṃ nopapadyate, yady apratyakṣā syāt. pratyakṣā tv eṣā. na hi pratyakṣam anupapannaṃ nāmāsti. dvayos tu śrutyor bhāvāt. dve hy ete vākye. tatraikena kevalayavasādhanatā gamyate, [68]{*1/572*} ekena kevalavrīhisādhanatā. na ca vākyenāvagato 'rtho 'pahnūyate. tasmād vrīhiyavayor upapanno vikalpo bṛhadrathantarayoś ca. tasmād uktaṃ śrutiviruddhā smṛtir apramāṇam iti. ataś ca sarvaveṣṭanādi nādaraṇīyam.
children.translated_text:
Now, where there is a contradiction with <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture), what then? For example, the complete wrapping of the <s>Audumbarī</s> posts [prescribed by <s>smṛti</s>] contradicts the <s>śruti</s> 'one should sing the <s>Udgītha</s> while touching the <s>Audumbarī</s> [post].' [Similarly,] forty-eight years of Vedic studentship contradicts 'one whose hair is still black and who has begotten a son should establish the sacred fires.' [And] 'one who has bought <s>Soma</s> should not eat at [others' houses]' contradicts 'therefore, when the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice] is completed, one should eat at the sacrificer's house.'
Having arrived at [the conclusion that] <s>smṛti</s> is a valid means of knowledge because of the commonality of authorship, we now say: because [the prescribed action] is impossible, it is understood as delusion. How is it impossible? Because of the injunction of touching — one who sings the <s>Udgītha</s> cannot wrap the entire [post] and also touch it. Recognizing that one singing the <s>Udgītha</s> must touch [the post], by what evidence could we override this understanding with the remembrance of complete wrapping? — we say.
[Objection:] Since [the remembrance] is without foundation, it is delusion — but a Vedic text will be its foundation. [Reply:] A Vedic text could be the foundation if the touching were the delusion. But [touching] not being a delusion — since [complete wrapping] is impossible — [the inference of a Vedic text] is untenable. Just as an experience that is untenable is not postulated, so too a Vedic text [is not postulated when untenable]. Then how [to explain] the remembrance of complete wrapping? It is delusion. How is the supposition of delusion [justified]? Because it contradicts the knowledge derived from <s>śruti</s>.
Then why are these two injunctions not treated as alternatives — like rice and barley, or like the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> [sāmans]? An alternative is not possible without the knowledge [of complete wrapping] being a delusion. If the cognition of complete wrapping is valid, then touching is a delusion. If touching is valid, then the tradition is a delusion. But one who proposes an alternative thereby concedes, in one case at least, the validity of touching. And the basis for that is <s>śruti</s>. If that [<s>śruti</s>] is accepted as valid, it is not merely a contingent option. The remembrance of complete wrapping is contingent — in [at least] one contingency it cannot postulate a <s>śruti</s>, since it is overridden by the cognition of touching. Therefore, in that [contingency] where [complete wrapping] is not a delusion, [the proponent] is unable to postulate a <s>śruti</s> [for it]. And it is not the case that in one contingency it is not a delusion — [for] it would be a delusion in [at least one] contingency.
For whatever serves as the basis for one contingency serves as the basis for the other as well. If in one contingency it is not a delusion, then because of the equal validity of <s>śruti</s>, it would not be a delusion in the other contingency either. But in one contingency [touching] does have a <s>śruti</s> [as its basis], for <s>śruti</s> consists of fixed syllables and cannot be said to be a careless recitation. Therefore, the cognition [of complete wrapping] has not migrated from [the status of] delusion in one contingency to the other contingency — this is understood. Hence it is postulated, due to the contradiction, that the [remembrance of] complete wrapping has its root in mishearing, dreams, and similar [unreliable] cognitions. For there is no valid evidence that its authoritativeness should be accepted when there is a contradiction. Therefore, just as in one contingency a <s>śruti</s> [for complete wrapping] cannot be postulated, so too in the other contingency, because the grounds are equal.
Moreover, when there is mutual dependence, resolution comes from [settling] one side. What is this mutual dependence? If <s>smṛti</s> is valid, then touching is a delusion; if touching is valid, then <s>smṛti</s> is a delusion — this is mutual dependence. In this [situation], touching has an established basis [in <s>śruti</s>], while <s>smṛti</s>'s basis needs to be postulated — that is the resolution from one side. Since <s>smṛti</s>'s basis needs to be postulated, its validity is not established. Since its validity is not established, touching is not a delusion. Since touching is not a delusion, the postulation of a <s>smṛti</s>-based <s>śruti</s> is untenable, due to the absence of valid evidence.
[Objection:] But if so, then since the cognition of rice being the [exclusive] instrument is also not a delusion, the <s>śruti</s> [enjoining] barley would also be untenable. [Reply:] True, it would be untenable — if it were not directly perceived. But this [<s>śruti</s> for barley] is directly perceived. For what is directly perceived is never called untenable. But in the case of the two <s>śrutis</s> — for there are indeed two sentences: by one, exclusive barley-instrumentality is understood; by the other, exclusive rice-instrumentality. And a meaning understood from a sentence cannot be denied. Therefore, the alternative between rice and barley, and between <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>, is well-established. Therefore it is stated that <s>smṛti</s> contradicting <s>śruti</s> is not a valid means of knowledge. Hence the complete wrapping and the like should not be heeded.

children.text: hetudarśanāc ca // MS_1,3.4 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of a [worldly] reason [for the practice]. // MS 1,3.4 //

children.text:
lobhād vāsa āditsamānā audumbarīṃ kṛtsnāṃ veṣṭitavantaḥ kecit. tat smṛter bījam. bubhukṣamāṇāḥ kecit krītarājakasya bhojanam ācaritavantaḥ. apuṃstvaṃ pracchādayantaś cāṣṭācatvāriṃśad varṣāṇi vedabrahmacaryaṃ caritavantaḥ. tata eṣā smṛtir ity avagamyate.
adhikaraṇāntaraṃ vā. vaisarjanahomīyaṃ vāso 'dhvaryur gṛhṇātīti, yūpahastino dānam ācarantīti. tatkartṛsāmānyāt pramāṇam iti prāpte{*1/573*}. apramāṇaṃ smṛtiḥ. atrānyan mūlam. lobhād ācaritavantaḥ kecit, tata eṣā smṛtiḥ. upapannataraṃ caitad vaidikavacanakalpanāt.
children.translated_text:
Out of greed for garments, desiring to take them, some wrapped the entire <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood altar). That is the seed of the <s>smṛti</s> (tradition). Some, being hungry, practiced the eating of purchased food. And some, concealing their impotence, observed Vedic <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) for forty-eight years. From these, this <s>smṛti</s> is understood.
Or [consider] another topic. 'The <s>adhvaryu</s> takes the garment for the <s>vaisarjana</s>-oblation,' and 'those with the sacrificial post in hand practice giving.' When it is concluded that [this practice] is authoritative because of the commonality of the agent — [we reply:] <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) is not authoritative. Here there is another root [cause]: out of greed some practiced [this]; from that, this <s>smṛti</s> [arose]. And this [explanation] is more fitting than postulating a Vedic sentence [as source].

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {1/573: MS 1.3.2}]

children.text: śiṣṭākope 'viruddham iti cet // MS_1,3.5 //
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is non-contradictory because the learned do not object. // MS 1.3.5 //

children.text: ācāntena kartavyam; yajñopavītinā kartavyam; dakṣiṇācāreṇa kartavyam ityevaṃlakṣaṇāny udāharaṇāni. kim etāni śrutiviruddhāni na kartavyāni utāviruddhāni kāryāṇīti. [69]{*1/574*} iti{*1/575*} cet paśyasi, tair apy anuṣṭhīyamānair vaidīkaṃ kiṃcin na kupyati, tasmād aviruddhānīti.
children.translated_text: Examples of this type are: 'One should act having sipped water (<s>ācamana</s>)'; 'One should act wearing the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>)'; 'One should act in the right-handed manner (<s>dakṣiṇācāra</s>).' Are these, being contradicted by <s>śruti</s>, not to be performed, or being non-contradictory, to be performed? If you see it thus — even when these are practiced, nothing in the Vedic [ritual] is disturbed — therefore they are non-contradictory.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {1/574: Edition cross-references} {1/575: E2,4,6 omit <s>iti</s>}]

children.text: na śāstraparimāṇatvāt // MS_1,3.6 //
children.translated_text: No, because [the ritual] is delimited by <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative teaching). // MS 1.3.6 //

children.text: naitad evam. śāstraparicchinnaṃ hi kramaṃ bādheran. katham. vedaṃ kṛtvā vediṃ kurvītetīmāṃ śrutim uparundhyād antarā vedaṃ vediṃ cānuṣṭḥīyamānam ācamanādi. dakṣiṇena caikahastenānuṣṭhīyamāneṣu padārtheṣu kadācit pradhānaṃ svakālam atikrāmeta. ubhābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ anutiṣṭhan pradhānakālaṃ saṃbhāvayiṣyati.
children.translated_text: This is not so. For they would obstruct the sequence delimited by <s>śāstra</s>. How? The <s>śruti</s> [says] 'Having made the <s>veda</s> (altar-grass bundle), one should make the <s>vedi</s> (altar)' — <s>ācamana</s> and such [acts] performed between the <s>veda</s> and the <s>vedi</s> would obstruct this. And when items are being performed with the right hand alone, sometimes the principal [act] might miss its proper time. By performing with both hands, one will be able to meet the time of the principal [act].

children.text: api vā kāraṇāgrahaṇe prayuktāni pratīyeran // MS_1,3.7 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, [practices] employed when no [contradictory] reason is apprehended should be accepted. // MS 1.3.7 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. agṛhyamāṇakāraṇā evaṃjātīyakāḥ pramāṇam. nanu kramakālau virundhanti{*1/576*}. virudhnantu{*1/577*}. naiṣa doṣaḥ. ācamanaṃ padārthaḥ padārthānāṃ ca guṇaḥ kramaḥ. na ca guṇānurodhena padārtho na kartavyo bhavati. api ca prāptānāṃ padārthānām uttarakālaṃ krama āpatati. yadā padārthaḥ prāpnoti, tadā krama eva nāsti, kena saha virodho bhaviṣyatīti. tathā yadi dakṣiṇena nācaryate, kālo mā virodhīd iti, tatra kālānurodhena padārtho nānyathātvam abhyupagacchet. prayogāṅgaṃ hi kālaḥ padārthānām upakārakaḥ. ato na kālānurodhena vyathayitavyaḥ padārthaḥ. api ca śaucaṃ dakṣiṇācāratā yajñopavītitvaṃ caivaṃjātīyakā arthā vyavadhātāro na bhavanti. sarvapadārthānāṃ [70]{*1/578*} śeṣabhūtatvāt. tasmād ācamanādīnāṃ prāmāṇyam.
children.translated_text: The word 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) reverses the position. Practices of this kind whose [contradictory] reason is not apprehended are authoritative. But do they not contradict sequence and time? Let them contradict. This is no defect. <s>Ācamana</s> (sipping) is a subsidiary item, and sequence is a property of subsidiary items. And a subsidiary item should not be left undone merely because of [concern for] sequence. Moreover, sequence applies to items already obtained at a later time. When the item is [first] obtained, sequence does not yet exist — with what would there be a contradiction? Similarly, if the right-handed manner is not practiced, [one might say] 'lest it contradict the time' — but in that case, the subsidiary item should not be altered merely because of [concern for] time. For time is an ancillary of [ritual] performance, a helper of the items. Therefore, the item should not be disturbed because of [concern for] time. Moreover, purification (<s>śauca</s>), right-handed practice (<s>dakṣiṇācāratā</s>), and wearing the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavītitva</s>) — practices of this kind do not constitute interruptions. Because they are subordinate to all the [ritual] items. Therefore, <s>ācamana</s> and such practices are authoritative.

NOTES:

children.text: teṣv adarśanād virodhasya samā vipratipattiḥ syāt // MS_1,3.8 //
children.translated_text: Since no contradiction is seen in them, the conflicting opinion would be equal [on both sides]. // MS 1.3.8 //

children.text: yavamayaś caruḥ; vārāhī upānahau{*1/579*}; vaitase kaṭe prājāpatyān saṃcinotīti yavavarāhavetasaśabdān samāmananti. tatra kecid dīrghaśūkeṣu yavaśabdaṃ prayuñjante, kecit priyaṅguṣu. varāhaśabdaṃ kecit śūkare{*1/580*}, kecit kṛṣṇaśakunau. vetasaśabdaṃ kecid vañjulake, kecij jambvām. tatrobhayathā padārthāvagamād vikalpaḥ.
children.translated_text: 'An oblation made of barley (<s>yava</s>)'; 'sandals made of boar-[skin] (<s>vārāhī</s>)'; 'On a <s>vetasa</s> (reed) mat, he arranges the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [bricks]' — thus the words <s>yava</s>, <s>varāha</s>, and <s>vetasa</s> are taught. Among these, some use the word <s>yava</s> for long-awned [grain], others for millet (<s>priyaṅgu</s>). Some use <s>varāha</s> for a pig, others for a black bird. Some use <s>vetasa</s> for the <s>vañjula</s> (willow), others for the <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) tree. In these cases, since the referent is understood either way, there is an option (<s>vikalpa</s>).

NOTES:

children.text: śāstrasthā vā tannimittatvāt // MS_1,3.9 //
children.translated_text: Or [the meaning is determined by the usage of] those established in <s>śāstra</s>, because [the word's meaning] is caused by that. // MS 1.3.9 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. yavaśabdo yadi dīrghaśūkeṣu sādṛśyāt priyaṅguṣu bhaviṣyati. yadi priyaṅguṣu, sādṛśyād yaveṣu. kiṃ sādṛśyam. pūrvasaśye{*1/581*} kṣīṇe bhavanti dīrghaśūkāḥ priyaṅgavaś caitat tayoḥ sādṛśyam. kaḥ punar atra niścayaḥ. ya śāstrasthānāṃ sa śabdārthaḥ. ke śāstrasthāḥ. śiṣṭāḥ. teṣām avicchinnā smṛtiḥ śabdeṣu vedeṣu ca. tena śiṣṭā nimittaṃ śrutismṛtyavadhāraṇe. te hy evaṃ samāmananti yavamayeṣu karambhapātreṣu vihiteṣu vākyaśeṣam - yatrānyā oṣadhayo mlāyante, athaite modamānā ivottiṣṭhantīti{*1/582*} dīrghaśūkān yavān darśayati vedaḥ. vede darśanād avicchinnapāramparyo dīrghaśūkeṣu yavaśabda iti gamyate. tasmāt priyaṅguṣu gauṇaḥ. tasmād dīrghaśūkānāṃ puroḍāśaḥ kartavyaḥ. tasmād varāhaṃ gāvo 'nudhāvantīti{*1/583*} śūkare{*1/584*} varāhaśabdaṃ darśayati. apsujo vetasa iti{*1/585*} vañjule vetasaśabdam. [71]{*1/586*} śūkaraṃ{*1/587*} hi gāvo 'nudhāvanti. vañjulo 'psu jāyate. jambūvṛkṣa sthale girinadīṣu vā.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) reverses the position. If the word <s>yava</s> [is applied] to long-awned [grain], it would apply to millet through similarity. If [applied] to millet, [it would apply] to barley through similarity. What is the similarity? When the early crop has been consumed, both long-awned grain and millet grow — this is their similarity. But what is the definitive determination here? The meaning of the word is [determined by] those established in <s>śāstra</s> (the learned). Who are those established in <s>śāstra</s>? The learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>). Their memory (<s>smṛti</s>) regarding words and <s>Vedas</s> is unbroken. Therefore, the learned are the basis for determining [the meaning of] <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. For they teach thus: When oblations made of barley are enjoined in the form of <s>karambha</s>-vessels, the syntactic complement is — 'Where other plants wither, then these rise up as if rejoicing' — the <s>Veda</s> indicates long-awned grain as <s>yava</s>. Because it is seen in the <s>Veda</s>, the unbroken tradition applies the word <s>yava</s> to long-awned grain. Therefore, [the usage] for millet is secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>). Therefore, the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake offering) should be made of long-awned grain. Similarly, 'Cows follow the <s>varāha</s>' — [the <s>Veda</s>] indicates the word <s>varāha</s> for a pig. 'The <s>vetasa</s> is born in water' — [the <s>Veda</s> indicates] the word <s>vetasa</s> for the <s>vañjula</s> (willow). For cows indeed follow a pig. And the <s>vañjula</s> grows in water. The <s>jambū</s> tree [grows] on dry land or by mountain rivers.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {1/581: E2,5,6 read <s>pūrvasasye</s>; E4 reads <s>pūrvasasyeṣe</s>} {1/582: Source unknown} {1/583: <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 4.4.3.19} {1/584: E2,4,5 read <s>sūkare</s>} {1/585: Source unknown} {1/586: Edition cross-references} {1/587: E2,4,5 read <s>sūkaraṃ</s>}]

children.text: coditaṃ tu pratīyetāvirodhāt pramāṇena // MS_1,3.10 //
children.translated_text: But what is enjoined should be accepted, provided it is not contradicted by [another] valid means of knowledge. // MS 1.3.10 //

children.text: atha yāñ chabdān āryā na kasmiṃścid arthe ācaranti, mlecchās tu kasmiṃścit prayuñjate, yathā pikanemasatatāmarasādiśabdāḥ{*1/588*}. teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ nigamaniruktavyākaraṇavaśena dhātuto 'rthaḥ kalpayitavya uta yatra mlecchā ācaranti, sa śabdārtha iti. śiṣṭācārasya prāmāṇyam uktaṃ nāśiṣṭasmṛteḥ. tasmān nigamādivaśenārthakalpanā. nigamādīnāṃ caivam arthavattā bhaviṣyati. anabhiyogaś ca śabdārtheṣv aśiṣṭānām abhiyogaś cetareṣām. tasmād dhātuto 'rthaḥ kalpayitavya ityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - coditam aśiṣṭair api śiṣṭānavagataṃ pratīyeta, yat pramāṇenāviruddham, tad avagamyamānam, na nyāyyaṃ tyaktum. yat tu śiṣṭācāraḥ pramāṇam iti, tat pratyakṣānavagate 'rthe. yat tv abhiyuktāḥ śabdārtheṣu śiṣṭā iti. tatrocyate - abhiyuktatarāḥ pakṣiṇāṃ poṣaṇe bandhane ca mlecchāḥ. yat tu nigamaniruktavyākaraṇānām arthavatteti, tatraiṣām arthavattā bhaviṣyati, na yatra mlecchair apy avagataḥ śabdārthaḥ. api ca - nigamādibhir arthe kalpayamāne 'vyavasthitaḥ śabdārtho bhavet, tatrāniścayaḥ syāt. tasmāt pika iti kokilo grāhyaḥ, nemo 'rdham, tāmarasaṃ padmam, sata iti dārumayaṃ pātram parimaṇḍalaṃ śatachidram.
children.translated_text: Now, as for those words that the cultured (<s>ārya</s>) do not employ for any referent, but the <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians) use for some [referent] — such as the words <s>pika</s>, <s>nema</s>, <s>sata</s>, <s>tāmarasa</s>, and the like. Regarding these there is doubt: should the meaning be derived from the root according to the <s>Nigama</s> (Vedic lexicon), <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology), and <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar), or is the meaning that for which the <s>mlecchas</s> use them the word-meaning? The authority of the practice of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>) has been stated, not that of the tradition of the unlearned. Therefore, meaning should be derived from the root through <s>Nigama</s> and such [sources]. And thus the <s>Nigama</s> and such [texts] will have their meaningfulness. And the unlearned lack application to word-meanings, while the others have application [to them]. Therefore, the meaning should be derived from the root — when this is the prima facie conclusion, we say: What is enjoined, even by the unlearned, [but] not known to the learned, should be accepted if it is not contradicted by a [valid] means of knowledge. What is thus understood should not rightly be abandoned. As for [the principle] that the practice of the learned is authoritative — that applies when the meaning is not directly known. As for [the claim] that the learned are those who are experts in word-meanings — to this we say: The <s>mlecchas</s> are more expert in the rearing and keeping of birds. As for [the principle] that the <s>Nigama</s>, <s>Nirukta</s>, and <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> have meaningfulness — they will have their meaningfulness where the meaning of the word is not even known to the <s>mlecchas</s>. Moreover, if meaning were derived through <s>Nigama</s> and such [sources alone], word-meanings would become unsettled, and there would be no certainty. Therefore, <s>pika</s> means the cuckoo, <s>nema</s> means half, <s>tāmarasa</s> means lotus, and <s>sata</s> means a round wooden vessel with a hundred holes.

children.text: prayogaśāstram iti cet // MS_1,3.11 //
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is a manual of [ritual] practice (<s>prayogaśāstra</s>). // MS 1.3.11 //

children.text: iha kalpasūtrāṇy udāharaṇam - māśakam, hāstikam, kauṇḍinyakam ityevaṃlakṣaṇakāni kiṃ pramāṇam apramāṇaṃ veti saṃdigdhāni. kiṃ prāptam. prayogasya śāstraṃ pramāṇam evaṃjātīyakam iti brūmaḥ. satyavācām etāni vacanāni. katham avagamyate. vaidikair eṣāṃ saṃvādo bhavati. ya eva hi vede grahāḥ, ta eveha, yā eva vede iṣṭakāḥ{*1/590*}, tā eveha. tasmāt satyavāca ācāryāḥ. ācāryavacaḥ pramāṇam iti ca śrutiḥ. pratyakṣataḥ prāmāṇyam anavagatam iti yady ucyeta, pramāṇāntareṇa vacanenāvagatam iti na doṣaḥ. vedavākyaiś caiṣāṃ tulya ādaraḥ. tasmāt pramāṇam.
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>Kalpa-sūtras</s> are the example — those of the <s>Māśaka</s>, <s>Hāstika</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> types — whether they are authoritative or not is in doubt. What is the prima facie view? A <s>śāstra</s> that deals with [ritual] practice — such a work is authoritative, we say. These are the utterances of truthful speakers. How is this known? Because they agree with the Vedic [texts]. For the very same <s>graha</s>-cups that are in the <s>Veda</s> are also here, and the very same bricks (<s>iṣṭakā</s>) that are in the <s>Veda</s> are here too. Therefore, the teachers speak truth. And [there is] a <s>śruti</s>: 'The teacher's word is authoritative.' If it is said that their authority is not known by direct perception — [we reply:] it is known by another means of knowledge, namely verbal testimony (<s>vacana</s>) — so there is no defect. And the respect [given to them] is equal to that of Vedic sentences. Therefore, they are authoritative.

children.text: nāsanniyamāt // MS_1,3.12 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the absence of [proper] regulation. // MS 1.3.12 //

children.text: naitad evam, asanniyamāt. naitat samyaṅnibandhanam, svarābhāvāt.
children.translated_text: This is not so, because of the absence of [proper] regulation. This [work] is not properly composed, because of the absence of [Vedic] accents (<s>svara</s>).

children.text: avākyaśeṣā{*1/591*}c ca // MS_1,3.13 //
children.translated_text: And because of [its] not being a syntactic complement [of the <s>Veda</s>]. // MS 1.3.13 //

children.text: ṛtvijo vṛṇīte; vṛtā yajanti{*1/592*}; devayajanam adhyavasyantīti{*1/593*}. nātra vidhir gamyate vartamānakālapratyayanirdeśāt. na cātra vākyaśeṣaḥ stāvako 'sti. tasmād{*1/594*} apramāṇam. yaś cādara uktaḥ, sa nāntarīyakatvād vedavākyamiśrasamāmnānāt. yat tu śrutir iti naitat, arthavādatvāt{*1/595*}. katham arthavādaḥ. vidhyantaraṃ hy asti - āgneyo 'ṣṭākapāla iti. atrācāryo vedo 'bhipretaḥ, ācinoty asya buddhim iti. yad vācāryavacanaṃ [73]{*1/596*} pramāṇaṃ tadapekṣam. kataratat. yat pramāṇagamyam.
children.translated_text: 'He selects the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>)'; 'The selected ones sacrifice'; 'They resolve upon the divine sacrifice.' Here no injunction is understood, because of the use of present-tense verbal suffixes. And here there is no syntactic complement that is laudatory. Therefore, [it is] not authoritative. As for the respect that was mentioned — that is because [the <s>Kalpa-sūtras</s>] are necessarily mixed together with Vedic sentences in their teaching, [and the respect is] not [for them] independently. As for [the argument from] <s>śruti</s> ('the teacher's word is authoritative') — this is not [applicable], because it is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage). How is it an <s>arthavāda</s>? Because there is another injunction: 'The [sacrificial cake] of eight potsherds is for <s>Agni</s>.' Here, by 'teacher' (<s>ācārya</s>) the <s>Veda</s> is intended — 'for it builds up (<s>ācinoti</s>) his understanding.' And as for 'the teacher's word is authoritative' — that depends on [the teacher's teaching being] accessible to a [valid] means of knowledge. Which [teaching] is that? That which is known through a [valid] means of knowledge.

children.text: yac coktam - satyavācām etāni vacanānīti, tan na -
children.translated_text: And what was said — 'These are the utterances of truthful speakers' — that is not [so] —

children.text: sarvatra ca prayogāt saṃnidhānaśāstrāc ca // MS_1,3.14 //
children.translated_text: And because of [their] practice everywhere, and because of [the existence of] an authoritative text that is proximate. // MS 1.3.14 //

children.text: ācāryavacanaṃ hi bhavati pūrvapakṣe - sarvāsu tithiṣv amāvāsyeti{*1/597*}. saṃnihitaṃ ca śāstram - paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā yajeta, amāvāsyāyām amāvasyayā yajed iti{*1/598*}. tena śrutiviruddhavacanān na satyavācaḥ, tasmād apramāṇam.
children.translated_text: For the teacher's statement in the prima facie position is: 'On all lunar days, [one should offer] the new-moon [rite].' And there is a proximate authoritative text: 'On the full-moon day one should sacrifice with the full-moon [rite]; on the new-moon day one should sacrifice with the new-moon [rite].' Therefore, because of uttering statements contradicting <s>śruti</s>, they are not truthful speakers; therefore, [the <s>Kalpa-sūtras</s> are] not authoritative.

children.text: anumānavyavasthānāt tatsaṃyuktaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt // MS_1,3.15 //
children.translated_text: Because of the determination [of authority] through inference, what is connected with that should be authoritative. // MS 1.3.15 //

children.text: anumānāt smṛter ācārāṇāṃ ca prāmāṇyam iṣyate. yenaiva hetunā te pramāṇam, tenaiva vyavasthitāḥ{*1/599*} prāmāṇyam arhanti. tasmād holākādayaḥ{*1/600*} prācyair eva kartavyāḥ; āhnīnaibukādayo dākṣiṇātyair{*1/601*} eva; udvṛṣabhayajñādaya udīcyair eva. yathā śikhākalpo vyavatiṣṭhate kecit triśikhāḥ, kecit pañcaśikhā iti.
children.translated_text: The authority of <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) and <s>ācāra</s> (customary practices) is accepted on the basis of inference. By whatever reason they are authoritative, by that very [reason] they are established [only within that scope] and deserve authority [accordingly]. Therefore, [practices like] <s>Holāka</s> and the like should be performed only by the easterners (<s>prācya</s>); <s>Āhnīnaibuka</s> and the like by the southerners (<s>dākṣiṇātya</s>) alone; and <s>Udvṛṣabhayajña</s> and the like by the northerners (<s>udīcya</s>) alone. Just as the convention regarding the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>) is established — some have three topknots, some have five topknots.

children.text: api vā sarvadharmaḥ syāt, tannyāyatvād vidhānasya // MS_1,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, [the practice] should apply to all, because the reasoning of the injunction [is universal]. // MS 1.3.16 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. evaṃjātīyakaḥ sarvadharmaḥ syāt. kutaḥ. tannyāyatvād vidhānasya. vidhīyate 'neneti vidhānaṃ śabdaḥ. so 'numīyate smṛtyāḥ. na ca tasyākṛtivacanatā nyāyyā. na ca vyaktivacanatā, na sarveṣām anuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ yad ekaṃ [74]{*1/602*} sāmānyaṃ, tasya vācakaḥ kaścit śabdo 'sti, yo 'numīyeta. tasmāt sarvadharmatā vidher nyāyyā. kutaḥ. padārthāḥ kartavyā iti pramāṇam asti, vyavasthāyāṃ tu na kiñcit pramāṇam asti.
children.translated_text: The expression 'or' (<s>api vā</s>) indicates the exclusion of an alternative view. Every [type of] <s>Dharma</s> would be of this kind [i.e., applicable to all]. Why? Because the injunction has this as its logical character. That by which [something] is enjoined is the injunction (<s>vidhāna</s>), i.e., the word. That [word] is inferred from the <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition). And it is not reasonable that it denotes a generic form (<s>ākṛti</s>). Nor does it denote an individual (<s>vyakti</s>) — there is no single common [feature] shared by all performers that some word could denote and from which [the injunction] could be inferred. Therefore, it is reasonable that the injunction applies to all [types of] <s>Dharma</s>. Why? Because there is a valid means of knowledge [establishing] that the meanings of words are to be performed, but there is no valid means of knowledge for the restriction [to particular persons or groups].

children.text: atha yad uktam, yathā śikhākalpo vyavatiṣṭhata iti -
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'just as the <s>śikhā</s>-kalpa (topknot-rule) is restricted' —

NOTES:
[Page refs: E2: lacuna; E4: 1,486; E5: 2,113; E6: 1,50]

children.text: darśanād viniyogaḥ syāt // MS_1,3.17 //
children.translated_text: The specific application would be from observation. // MS_1,3.17 //

children.text: gotravyavasthayā śikhākalpavyavasthāyāṃ darśanaṃ spaṣṭam.
children.translated_text: The restriction of the <s>śikhā</s>-kalpa (topknot-rule) through the restriction by <s>gotra</s> (lineage) is clear from observation.

children.text: liṅgābhāvāc ca nityasya // MS_1,3.18 //
children.translated_text: And because of the absence of a distinguishing mark for what is permanent. // MS_1,3.18 //

children.text: idaṃ padebhyaḥ kebhyaścid uttaraṃ sūtram. kāni tāni padāni. atha kim arthaṃ na liṅgād vyavasthā. yathā - śuklo hotā iti. nāsti tan nityam eṣāṃ liṅgam, yad yathādarśanam anuvartate. ye 'pi śyāmā bṛhanto lohitākṣāḥ, te 'pi na sarva ārhnīnaibukādīn kurvate. anevaṃliṅgā api cānutiṣṭhanti. tasmān na vyavasthā. śuklo hoteti pratyakṣā śrutiḥ.
children.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> follows from certain words [in the preceding discussion]. Which words are those? Now, why should the restriction not be based on a distinguishing mark (<s>liṅga</s>)? For example — 'The <s>Hotṛ</s> (priest) is fair-complexioned.' There is no permanent mark of these [persons] that consistently corresponds to observation. Even those who are dark, tall, and red-eyed — they too do not all perform the <s>Āhnīnaibuka</s> and similar rites. And even those who do not have such marks also perform [these rites]. Therefore, there is no restriction [based on marks]. 'The <s>Hotṛ</s> is fair-complexioned' — this is a directly heard Vedic statement.

children.text: ākhyā hi deśasaṃyogāt // MS_1,3.19 //
children.translated_text: For the designation [comes] from connection with a place. // MS_1,3.19 //

children.text: atha kasmān na samākhyayā niyamaḥ. ye dākṣiṇātyā iti samākhyātāḥ, ta āhnīnaibukādīn kariṣyanti. ya udīcyā iti samākhyātāḥ, ta udvṛṣabhayajñādīn. ye prācyā iti, te holākādīn. yathā - rājā rājasūyeneti. naitad evam. deśasaṃyogād ākhyā bhavati. dākṣiṇadeśān nirgataḥ prākṣu vodakṣu vāvasthita āhnīnaibukādīn karoty eva. udīcyāś ca deśāntara udvṛṣabhayajñādīn{*1/603*}, prācyāś ca holākādīn. anyadeśaś ca deśāntaragato na niyogataḥ parapadārthān{*1/604*} karoti. tasmān na vyavasthā{*1/605*}. rājā rājasūyeneti tu niyatā jātiḥ.
children.translated_text: Now, why is there no restriction based on the designation? Those who are designated as 'southerners' (<s>Dākṣiṇātya</s>) would perform the <s>Āhnīnaibuka</s> and similar rites. Those designated as 'northerners' (<s>Udīcya</s>) would perform the <s>Udvṛṣabhayajña</s> and similar rites. Those who are 'easterners' (<s>Prācya</s>) would perform the <s>Holāka</s> and similar rites. Just as — 'A king [should sacrifice] with the <s>Rājasūya</s>.' This is not so. The designation arises from connection with a place. One who has come out from the southern region and settled in the eastern or northern [regions] still performs the <s>Āhnīnaibuka</s> and similar rites. And those from the north perform the <s>Udvṛṣabhayajña</s> and similar rites in another region, and those from the east perform the <s>Holāka</s> and similar rites [elsewhere]. And one who has gone to another region does not necessarily perform the ritual acts of the other [region]. Therefore, there is no restriction [based on designation]. But 'a king [should sacrifice] with the <s>Rājasūya</s>' — here the <s>jāti</s> (class) is fixed.
Page 75

*{1/604: E4 (Fn.): niyogataḥ padārthān}*
*{1/605: E4 (Fn.): tasmād avyavasthā}*

NOTES:
[Variant: E4 footnote reads 'udīcyāś codvṛṣabhayajñādīn'] | [Variant: E4 footnote reads 'niyogataḥ padārthān'] | [Variant: E4 footnote reads 'tasmād avyavasthā'] | [Page refs: E2: 2,180; E4: 1,497; E5: 2,116; E6: 1,51]

children.text: na syād deśāntareṣv iti cet // MS_1,3.20 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] it would not apply in other regions — // MS_1,3.20 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi - yadi deśasaṃyogād ākhyā bhavet, deśāntarasthasya na bhavet. bhavati ca deśānatarasthasya māthura ity asaṃbaddhasyāpi mathurayā. tasmān na deśasaṃyogād ākhyā.
children.translated_text: 'If you see [it] thus' — if the designation arose from connection with a place, one who is in another place would not have [that designation]. But one who is in another place does [still] have [the designation] — one is called '<s>Māthura</s>' (from <s>Mathurā</s>) even when unconnected with <s>Mathurā</s>. Therefore, the designation does not arise from connection with a place.

children.text: syād yogākhyā hi māthuravat // MS_1,3.21 //
children.translated_text: It would be a designation based on [prior] connection, like [the case of] a <s>Māthura</s>. // MS_1,3.21 //

children.text: deśasaṃyoganimittāyām apy ākhyāyāṃ deśān nirgatasya tadākhyā na viruddhā. yata eṣā yogākhyā yogamātrāpekṣā, na bhūtavartamānabhaviṣyatsaṃbandhāpekṣā. yato dṛśyate - mathurām abhiprasthito māthura iti, mathurāyāṃ vasan mathurāyā nirgataś ca. yasya tv ato 'nyatamaḥ saṃbandho nāsti, na sa māthuraḥ. tasmān na samākhyayā vyavasthā.
children.translated_text: Even when the designation arises from connection with a place, [the fact that] one who has left the place [retains] that designation is not contradictory. For this is a designation based on [prior] connection (<s>yoga</s>-ākhyā), depending merely on [some] connection — not dependent on whether the connection is past, present, or future. For it is observed — one who has set out for <s>Mathurā</s> is called '<s>Māthura</s>,' as is one residing in <s>Mathurā</s> and one who has left <s>Mathurā</s>. But one who has none of these connections is not [called] a <s>Māthura</s>. Therefore, there is no restriction based on designation.

children.text: karmadharmo vā pravaṇavat // MS_1,3.22 //
children.translated_text: Or [the place may be] a property of the ritual action, like [the case of] a slope. // MS_1,3.22 //

children.text: atha kasmān na karmāṅgaṃ deśaḥ. yaḥ kṛṣṇamṛtikāprāyaḥ, sa āhnīnaibukādīnām. yathā - prācīnapravaṇe vaiśvadevena yajeteti{*1/607*}.
children.translated_text: Now, why should the place not be a subsidiary element of the ritual action? A place that is predominantly of black soil would [be appropriate] for the <s>Āhnīnaibuka</s> and similar rites. Just as — 'One should sacrifice to the <s>Viśvedevas</s> on an eastward-sloping [ground].'

NOTES:
Mān.ŚS. 1.7.1.5

children.text: tulyaṃ tu kartṛdharmeṇa // MS_1,3.23 //
children.translated_text: But it is the same as with the property of the agent. // MS_1,3.23 //

children.text: yathā kartary avyavasthitaṃ liṅgaṃ śyāmādi{*1/608*} na padārthaiḥ saṃvādam upaiti, tadvad deśaliṅgam avyavasthitam{*1/609*}. kṛṣṇamṛtikāprāye 'py anye na kurvanti, tathānyaliṅge 'pi kurvanti. tasmān na deśato vyavasthā. prācīnapravaṇaṃ tu śrutyā niyataṃ vaiśvadevasya.
children.translated_text: Just as the distinguishing mark — such as being dark-complexioned — is not fixed in the agent and does not correspond to the ritual acts, so too the distinguishing mark of the place is not fixed. Even in a place predominantly of black soil, others do not perform [those rites], and even in places with different marks, [some] do perform [them]. Therefore, there is no restriction based on place. But the eastward slope is fixed for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> rite by direct Vedic statement.
Page 76

*{1/609: E4: deśaliṅgavyavasthitam}*

children.text: prayogotpattyaśāstratvāc chabdeṣu na vyavasthā syāt // MS_1,3.24 //
children.translated_text: There would be no restriction based on words, because [their variety] arises from effort in production and is not scriptural. // MS_1,3.24 //

children.text: gaur gāvī goṇī gopotalikā ityevamādayaḥ{*1/611*} śabdā udāharaṇam. gośabdo yathā sāsnādim iti pramāṇam, kiṃ tathā gāvyādayo 'py uta neti saṃdehaḥ. kim atraikaḥ śabdo 'vicchinnapāramparyo 'rthābhidhāyī, itare 'pabhraṃśāḥ, uta sarve 'nādayaḥ. sarva iti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ. pratyayāt. pratīyate hi gāvyādibhyaḥ sāsnādimān arthaḥ. tasmād ito varṣaśate 'py asyārthasya saṃbandha āsīd eva, tataḥ pareṇa, tataś ca paratareṇety anāditā. kartā cāsya saṃbandhasya nāstīti vyavasthitam eva. tasmāt sarve sādhavaḥ, sarvair bhāṣitavyam. sarve hi sādhayanty artham. yathā - hastaḥ, karaḥ, pāṇir iti. arthāya hy eta uccāryante, nādṛṣṭāya. na hy eṣām uccāraṇe śāstram asti. tasmān na vyavatiṣṭheta kaścid eka eva sādhur itare 'sādhava iti.
children.translated_text: <s>Gaur</s>, <s>gāvī</s>, <s>goṇī</s>, <s>gopotalikā</s> — such words are the examples. The word <s>go</s> (cow) [denotes] that which has a dewlap and the like — this is established. The question is: do <s>gāvī</s> and the like [denote the same] in the same way, or not? Here, is one word the [correct] one with unbroken tradition that denotes the meaning, while the others are corruptions (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>)? Or are all [words] beginningless? We say: all are [beginningless]. Why? Because of the cognition [they produce]. For from <s>gāvī</s> and the like, the meaning 'that which has a dewlap and the like' is cognized. Therefore, even a hundred years ago, this meaning had a relation [with these words], and [so also] before that, and further before that — thus [the relation] is beginningless. And it is established that there is no creator of this relation. Therefore, all are correct (<s>sādhu</s>); one may speak with all of them. For all of them convey the meaning — just as <s>hasta</s>, <s>kara</s>, <s>pāṇi</s> (all meaning 'hand'). For these are uttered for the sake of meaning, not for an unseen [transcendent] purpose. For there is no scriptural injunction regarding their utterance. Therefore, no one should maintain that only one is correct and the others are incorrect.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{1/611: Vgl. Mahābhāṣya, Einltg., E1 (4th ed., 1985), Bd.1, S.5/21-22}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
Cf. <s>Mahābhāṣya</s>, Introduction, E1 (4th ed., 1985), Vol. 1, p. 5/21-22

children.text: śabde prayatnaniṣpatter aparādhasya bhāgitvam // MS_1,3.25 //
children.translated_text: Because speech is produced through effort, it is subject to error. // MS_1,3.25 //

children.text: mahatā prayatnena śabdam uccaranti - vāyur nābher utthitaḥ, urasi vistīrṇaḥ, kaṇṭhe vivartitaḥ, mūrdhānam āhatya parāvṛttaḥ, vaktre vicaran vividhān śabdān abhivyanakti. tatrāparādhyetāpy uccārayitā, yathā - śuṣke patiṣyāmīti kardame patati, sakṛd upasprakṣyāmīti dvir upaspṛśati. tato 'parādhāt pravṛttā gāvyādayo bhaveyuḥ, na niyogato 'vicchinnapāramparyā eveti.
children.translated_text: With great effort one utters speech — the air, having risen from the navel, expanded in the chest, turned in the throat, and having struck the head and returned, moving about in the mouth, manifests various sounds. In this process, the utterer may also commit an error — just as one who intends 'I shall step on dry [ground]' steps in mud, or one who intends 'I shall touch [water] once' touches twice. From such error, <s>gāvī</s> and the like may have arisen — not necessarily as words with unbroken tradition.
Page 77

children.text: anyāyaś cānekaśabdatvam // MS_1,3.26 //
children.translated_text: And the multiplicity of words [for one meaning] is unreasonable. // MS_1,3.26 //

children.text: na caiṣa nyāyaḥ yat sadṛśāḥ śabdā ekam artham abhiniviśamānāḥ, sarve 'vichinnapāramparyā eveti. pratyayamātradarśanād abhyupagamyate, sādṛśyāt sādhuśabde 'py avagate pratyayo 'vakalpyate. tasmād amīṣām eko 'nādir anye 'pabhraṃśāḥ. hastaḥ, karaḥ, pāṇir ityevamādiṣu tv abhiyuktopadeśād anādir amīṣām arthena saṃbandha iti.
children.translated_text: And this is not reasonable — that similar words all referring to a single meaning should all have unbroken tradition. [This is merely] accepted on the basis of the mere observation of cognition [produced by them]; because of similarity, even when the correct word is known, the cognition [from the corrupt word] is attributed [to the correct word]. Therefore, of these, one is beginningless and the others are corruptions. But in the case of <s>hasta</s>, <s>kara</s>, <s>pāṇi</s> and the like — because of the instruction of the learned, the relation of these [words] with their meaning is beginningless.

children.text: tatra tattvam abhiyogaviśeṣāt syāt // MS_1,3.27 //
children.translated_text: The truth in that [matter] would [be determined] by the distinction of [the learned person's] expertise. // MS_1,3.27 //

children.text: kathaṃ punas tatra{*1/613*} tattvaṃ śakyaṃ vijñātum. śakyam ity āha. arthino hy abhiyuktā bhavanti. dṛśyate cābhiyuktānāṃ guṇayatām avismaraṇam upapannam. pratyakṣaṃ caitad guṇyamānaṃ na bhraśyata iti. tasmād yam abhiyuktā upadiśanti, eṣa eva sādhur ity avagantavyaḥ{*1/614*}.
children.translated_text: But how can the truth in that [matter] be known? It can be, he says. For those who seek [knowledge] are diligent. And it is observed that among the diligent who repeatedly practice, non-forgetfulness is well-established. And it is directly perceived that what is repeatedly practiced is not lost. Therefore, whatever the learned instruct — that alone should be understood as correct.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{1/613: E4 (Fn.): punar atra}*
*{1/614: E4 (Fn.): sādhur avagantavyaḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[Variant: E4 footnote reads 'punar atra'] | [Variant: E4 footnote reads 'sādhur avagantavyaḥ']

children.text: tadaśaktiś cānurūpatvāt // MS_1,3.28 //
children.translated_text: And [the cognition from corrupt words] is due to the inability [to utter the correct word], because of the resemblance [to the correct word]. // MS_1,3.28 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - artho 'vagamyate gāvyādibhyaḥ, ata eṣām apy anādiarthena saṃbandha iti. tadaśaktir eṣāṃ gamyate. gośabdam uccārayitukāmena kenacid aśaktyā gāvīty uccāritam. apareṇa jñātaṃ sāsnādimān asya vivakṣitaḥ, tad arthaṃ gaur ity uccārayitukāmo gāvīty uccārayati. [78]{*1/615*} tataḥ śikṣitvāpare 'pi sāsnādim iti vivakṣite gāvīty uccārayanti. tena gāvyādibhyaḥ sāsnādimān avagamyate. anurūpo hi gāvyādigośabdasya.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'meaning is cognized from <s>gāvī</s> and the like, therefore these too have a beginningless relation with meaning' — the inability [to utter the correct word] of these [speakers] is to be understood. Someone who wished to utter the word <s>go</s>, due to inability, uttered <s>gāvī</s>. Another person understood that [the speaker's] intended meaning was 'that which has a dewlap and the like'; [this person], wishing to utter <s>go</s> for that meaning, [also] utters <s>gāvī</s>. Then, having learned from [that person], others too, when intending 'that which has a dewlap and the like,' utter <s>gāvī</s>. Thus, from <s>gāvī</s> and the like, 'that which has a dewlap and the like' is cognized. For <s>gāvī</s> and the like resemble the word <s>go</s>.

children.text: ekadeśatvāc ca vibhaktivyatyaye syāt // MS_1,3.29 //
children.translated_text: And because of being a partial [form], cognition would arise even when case-endings are transposed. // MS_1,3.29 //

children.text: ata eva hi vibhaktivyatyaye 'pi pratyayo bhavati. aśmakair āgacchāmīty aśmakaśabdaikadeśa upalabdhe, aśmakebhya ity eva śabdaḥ smaryate. tato 'śmakebhya ity eṣo 'rtha upalabhyata iti. evaṃ gāvyādidarśanād gośabdasmaraṇam, tataḥ sāsnādimān avagamyate.
children.translated_text: For this very reason, cognition arises even when case-endings are transposed. When one says 'I come from the <s>Aśmakas</s>' [with a non-standard case-ending], a partial form of the word <s>Aśmaka</s> is apprehended, and the word '<s>Aśmakebhyaḥ</s>' (from the <s>Aśmakas</s>) is recalled. From that, the meaning 'from the <s>Aśmakas</s>' is apprehended. Similarly, from seeing <s>gāvī</s> and the like, the word <s>go</s> is recalled, and from that, 'that which has a dewlap and the like' is cognized.

children.text: prayogacodanābhāvād arthaikatvam avibhāgāt // MS_1,3.30 //
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of an injunction for [specific] usage, the meaning is one [for all variants], since there is no distinction. // MS_1,3.30 //

children.text:
atha gaur ityevamādayaḥ śabdāḥ kim ākṛteḥ pramāṇam uta vyakter iti saṃdehaḥ. ucyate. idaṃ tāvat parīkṣyatām - kiṃ ya eva laukikāḥ śabdāḥ, ta eva vaidikā utānya iti. yadā ta eva, tadāpi kiṃ ta evaiṣām arthāḥ, ye loke, utānya iti saṃśayaḥ. tatrānye laukikāḥ śabdāḥ, anye vaidikā anye caiṣām arthā iti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ. vyapadeśabhedād rūpabhedāc ca. ime laukikāḥ, ime vaidikā iti vyapadeśabhedaḥ. agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanad ity{*1/616*} anyad idaṃ rūpaṃ laukikād agniśabdāt. śabdānyatvāc ca na ta evārthāḥ. api ca samāmananti - uttānā vai devagavā vahantīti{*1/617*}. ye devānāṃ gāvaḥ, ta uttānā vahantīty ukte gamyata eva - ya uttānā vahanti, te gośabdenocyanta [79]{*1/618*}iti. tasmād anyo vaidikagośabdasyārthaḥ. tathā - devebhyo vanaspate havīṃṣi hiraṇyaparṇa pradivaste artham iti{*1/619*}, hiraṇyaparṇo vai devo{*1/620*} vanaspatir vede. etad vai daivyaṃ madhu, yad ghṛtam iti{*1/621*} veda ghṛte madhuśabdaḥ. tasmād amīṣām anye 'rthā iti prāpte brūmaḥ - ya eva laukikāḥ śabdāḥ, ta eva vaidikāḥ, ta evaiṣām arthā iti. kutaḥ. prayogacodanābhāvāt. evaṃ prayogacodanā saṃbhavati, yadi ta eva śabdāḥ, ta evārthāḥ. itarathā śabdānyatve 'rtho na pratīyeta. tasmād ekaśabdatvam iti. ucyate prayojanam idam, hetur vyapadiśyatām iti. tato hetur ucyate - avibhāgād iti. na teṣām eṣāṃ ca vibhāgam upalabhāmahe. ata evaikaśabdatvam. tāṃś ca tāṃś cārthān avagacchāmaḥ. ato nānyatvaṃ ca vadāmaḥ. yac coktam - ya uttānā vadanti, te devagāvāḥ; yad ghṛtam, tan madhu; yo hiraṇya-parṇaḥ, sa vanaspatir iti. nāsti vacanaṃ yad uttānānāṃ vahatāṃ gotvaṃ brūyāt. ye gāvaḥ, ta uttānā vahantīty evaṃ tat. yadi cānena vacanena gotvaṃ vidhīyate, uttānā vahantīty anuvādaḥ syāt. na cottānā vahantaḥ prasiddhāḥ kecit. te niyogato vidhātavyāḥ, teṣu vidhīyamāneṣu na śakyaṃ gotvaṃ vidhātum. bhidyate hi tathā vākyam. yadi cānye vaidikāḥ, tata uttānādīnām artho na gamyeta. tatra natarāṃ śakyetāvijñātalakṣaṇaṃ gotvaṃ vijñātum. na cottānavahanavacanam apy anarthakam, stutyarthenārthavad bhaviṣyatīti. evaṃ ghṛtasya madhutvam, hiraṇyaparṇatā ca vanaspateḥ. tasmāt ta eva śabdā arthāś ca.
yadi laukikās ta evārthāḥ, tadā saṃdehaḥ - kim ākṛtiḥ śabdārtho 'tha vyaktir iti. kā punar ākṛtiḥ, kā vyaktir iti. dravyaguṇakarmaṇāṃ sāmānyamātram ākṛtiḥ, asādhāraṇaviśeṣā [80]{*1/622*} vyaktiḥ. kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? gaur ity ukte sāmānyapratyayād, vyaktau ca kriyāsaṃbandhāt.
tad ucyate - vyaktiḥ śabdārtha iti. kutaḥ? prayogacodanābhāvāt. ālambhanaprokṣaṇaviśasanādīnāṃ prayogacodanā ākṛtyarthe na saṃbhaveyuḥ. yatroccāraṇānarthakyam, tatra vyaktyarthaḥ. ato 'nyatrākṛtivacana iti cet. uktam{*1/623*} - anyāyaś cānekārthatvam iti. kathaṃ sāmānyāvagatir iti cet. vyaktipadārthasyākṛtiś cihnabhūtā bhaviṣyati, ya evam ākṛtikaḥ, sa gaur iti. yathā yasya daṇḍo 'sti, sa daṇḍīti, na ca daṇḍavacano daṇḍiśabdaḥ. evam ihāpi.
children.translated_text:
Now, the question arises whether words such as 'cow' (<s>go</s>) and the like are evidence for the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>) or for the individual (<s>vyakti</s>). It is said: Let this first be examined — are the words used in the world the very same as the Vedic words, or are they different? If they are the same, then too the question arises — are their meanings the same as in worldly usage, or different? In this regard, we say: worldly words are different [from Vedic words], Vedic words are different, and their meanings too are different. Why? Because of the difference in designation and the difference in form. 'These are worldly, these are Vedic' — this is the difference in designation. '<s>Agni</s> who slays obstacles' — this form is different from the worldly word '<s>agni</s>' (fire). And because the words are different, the meanings are not the same either. Moreover, they teach: 'The cows of the gods carry [things] upwards.' When it is said that the cows belonging to the gods carry upwards, it is understood that those which carry upwards are denoted by the word '<s>go</s>' (cow). [Page 79] Therefore, the meaning of the Vedic word '<s>go</s>' is different. Similarly — 'O <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest), convey the oblations to the gods, O golden-leaved one, established since ancient times' — the golden-leaved divine <s>Vanaspati</s> is known in the <s>Veda</s>. 'This indeed is the divine honey, namely ghee' — in the <s>Veda</s> the word '<s>madhu</s>' (honey) [denotes] ghee. Therefore, the meanings of these [Vedic words] are different. To this prima facie view we say: The worldly words are the very same as the Vedic ones, and their meanings are the same. Why? Because of the absence of a rule for [separate] usage. A rule for usage is possible only if they are the same words with the same meanings. Otherwise, if the words were different, the meaning would not be understood. Therefore, they are the same words. It is said: State the purpose — this is [the demand]; now state the reason. Therefore, the reason is stated — 'because of non-differentiation.' We do not perceive any differentiation between those [Vedic words] and these [worldly words]. Hence they are the same words. And we understand these very same meanings. Therefore, we do not assert their difference either. As for what was said — 'those which carry upwards are the divine cows; ghee is honey; the golden-leaved is the <s>Vanaspati</s>' — there is no statement that would attribute cow-nature to those which carry upwards. Rather, [the meaning is:] those which are cows carry upwards — that is how it should be [understood]. And if by this statement cow-nature is being enjoined, then 'carrying upwards' would be a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>). But those which carry upwards are not well-known [entities]. They would necessarily have to be enjoined [as such], and when they are being enjoined, cow-nature cannot also be enjoined. For the sentence would be split in that case. And if Vedic [words] were different, then the meaning of 'upward-carrying' and the rest would not be understood. In that case, even less could one know the cow-nature of [entities] whose defining characteristics are unknown. Nor is the expression about upward-carrying purposeless — it will be meaningful as serving the purpose of praise. Similarly, the honey-nature of ghee, and the golden-leaved nature of <s>Vanaspati</s>. Therefore, the words and meanings are the same.
If the worldly meanings are the same, then the question arises — is the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>) the meaning of the word, or the individual (<s>vyakti</s>)? What then is the universal form, and what is the individual? The mere generality (<s>sāmānya</s>) of substance, quality, and action is the universal form; the distinctive particular (<s>asādhāraṇa viśeṣa</s>) [Page 80] is the individual. Whence the doubt? Because when 'cow' is uttered, a cognition of the universal arises, and because action is connected with the individual.
To this it is said: The individual is the meaning of the word. Why? Because of the absence of a rule for usage [with the universal]. The rules for usage of acts such as seizing, sprinkling, slaughtering, and the like would not be possible if the universal were the meaning. Where the utterance would be purposeless [without denoting an individual], there the word denotes the individual. [Objection:] In other cases, then, it denotes the universal. [Reply:] It was stated — 'And it is improper for [a word] to have multiple meanings.' [Objection:] How then is the cognition of the universal [explained]? [Reply:] The universal form will serve as the identifying mark (<s>cihna</s>) of the individual, which is the referent of the word — 'whatever has this universal form, that is a cow.' Just as one who has a staff is called a 'staff-bearer' (<s>daṇḍin</s>), but the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>' does not denote the staff. So too here.

children.text: dravyaśabdāt // MS_1,3.31 //
children.translated_text: Because of [the use of] substance-words. // MS 1.3.31 //

children.text: dravyāśrayasya śabdo dravyaśabdaḥ, na tatra dravyāśrayavacanaḥ śabdo bhavet, yady ākṛtiḥ śabdārtho bhavet. ṣaḍ deyā dvādaśa deyā{*1/624*} caturviṃśatir deyā iti. na hy ākṛtiḥ ṣaḍādibhiḥ saṃkhyābhir yujyate. tasmān nākṛtivacanaḥ.
children.translated_text: A 'substance-word' is a word whose locus is a substance (<s>dravya</s>). Such a word, which denotes a substance-possessing [entity], would not exist if the universal form were the meaning of the word. 'Six should be given, twelve should be given, twenty-four should be given' — for the universal form cannot be qualified by numbers such as six and so on. Therefore, [the word] does not denote the universal form.

children.translated_text: If a consecrated animal were to flee, one should seize another of the same color and same age. If the word denoted the universal form, the seizing of 'another' would be unjustified. For in another animal-substance as well, the universal form is the very same. Therefore, [the word] denotes the individual.
