tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. ākṛti śabdārthaḥ. kutaḥ? kriyārthatvāt. śyenacitaṃ cinvīta iti{*1/626*} vacanam ākṛtau saṃbhavati, yady ākṛtyarthaḥ śyenaśabdaḥ. vyaktivacane tu na cayanena śyenavyakti[81]{*1/627*}r utpādayituṃ śakyata ity aśakyārthavacanād anarthakaḥ. tasmād ākṛtivacanaḥ.
nanu śyenavyaktibhiś cayanam anuṣṭhāsyate. na sādhakatamaḥ śyenaśabdārthaḥ, īpsitatamo hy asau śyenaśabdena nirdiśyate. ataś cayanena śyeno nivartayitavyaḥ, sa ākṛtivacanatve 'vakalpyate.
nanūbhayatra kriyāyā asaṃbhava eva vyapadiśyate. nākṛtiḥ śabdārthaḥ. kutaḥ. kriyā na saṃbhaved ākṛtau śabdārthe, vrīhīn prokṣatīti{*1/628*}. tathā na vyaktiḥ śabdārthaḥ, kriyaiva na saṃbhaved vyakteḥ śabdārthatve{*1/629*}, śyenacitaṃ cinvīta iti. yad apy ucyate - vrīhīn prokṣatīti vyaktilakṣaṇārthākṛtir iti, śakyam anyatrāpi śyenacitaṃ cinvīta iti vaditum ākṛtilakṣaṇārthā vyaktir iti. kiṃ punar atra jyāyaḥ.
ākṛtiḥ śabdārtha iti. yadi vyaktiḥ śabdārtho bhavet, vyaktyantare na prayujyeta. atha vyaktyantare prayujyate, na tarhi vyaktiḥ śabdārthaḥ, sarvasāmānyaviśeṣavinirmuktā hi vyaktir ity. ucyate - naiṣa doṣaḥ. vyaktyantare sarvasāmānyaviśeṣavinirmukta eva pravartiṣyate. yadi vyaktyantare sarvasāmānyaviśeṣaviyukte pravartiṣyate, sāmānyam eva tarhi tat. nety ucyate - yo hy arthaḥ sāmānyasya viśeṣāṇāṃ cāśrayaḥ, sā vyaktiḥ. vyaktivacanaś ca śabdo na sāmānye, na viśeṣe vartate. teṣāṃ tv āśrayam evābhidadhāti, tena vyaktyantare vṛttir adoṣaḥ. na hi tat sāmānyam.
yadi vyaktyantareṣv api bhavati, sarvasāmānyaviśeṣaviyuktāyām aśvavyaktau gośabdaḥ kim iti na vartate. āha - yeṣv eva prayogo dṛṣṭaḥ, teṣu vartiṣyate, na sarvatra. na cāśvavyaktau gośabdasya prayogo dṛṣṭaḥ. tasmāt tatra na vartiṣyate. yadi yatra [82]{*1/630*} prayogo dṛṣṭaḥ, tatra vṛttiḥ, adyajātāyāṃ gavi prathamaprayogo na prāpnoti tatrādṛṣṭatvāt. sāmānyapratyayaś ca na prāpnoti, iyam api gaur iti, iyam api gaur iti; iyaṃ vā gaur iti, iyaṃ vā gaur iti syāt. bhavati tu sāmānyapratyayo 'dṛṣṭapūrvāyām api govyaktau. tasmān na prayogāpekṣo gośabdo vyaktivacana iti śakyata āśrayitum. evaṃ tarhi śakteḥ svabhāva eṣaḥ, yat kasyāṃcit vyaktau vartate, kasyāṃcin na. yathā - agnir uṣṇaḥ, udakaṃ śītam, evam etad bhaviṣyatīti. naivaṃ sidhyati. na hy etad gamyate kasyāṃcid vyaktau vartate, kasyāṃcin neti. satyam etat, gotvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. yatra gotvaṃ tasyāṃ vyaktāv iti. evaṃ tarhi viśiṣṭā vyaktiḥ pratīyeta. yadi ca viśiṣṭā, pūrvataraṃ viśeṣaṇam avagamyeta. na hy apratīte viśeṣaṇe viśiṣṭaṃ kecana pratyetum arhantīti. astu, viśeṣaṇatvenākṛtiṃ vakṣyati, viśeṣyatvena vyaktim. na hy ākṛtipadārthakasya vyaktir na padārthaḥ, vyaktipadārthakasya vā nākṛtiḥ. ubhayam ubhayasya padārthaḥ. kasyacit kiṃcit prādhānyena vivakṣitaṃ bhavati, tenātrākṛtir guṇabhāvena, vyaktiḥ pradhānabhāvena vivakṣyata iti.
naitad evam. ubhayor ucyamānayor guṇapradhānabhāvaḥ syāt. yadi cātrākṛtiḥ pratīyate śabdena, tadā vyaktir api padārtha iti na śakyate vaditum. kutaḥ. ākṛtir hi vyaktyā nityasaṃbaddhā, saṃbandhinyāṃ ca tasyām avagatāyāṃ saṃbandhyantaram avagamyate. tad etad ātmapratyakṣam, yac chabda uccarite vyaktiḥ pratīyata iti. kiṃ śabdād utākṛter iti vibhāgo na pratyakṣaḥ. so 'nvayavyatirekābhyām avagamyate. antareṇāpi śabdam, ya ākṛtim avabudhyeta, avabudhyetevāsau{*1/631*} vyaktim. yas tūccarite 'pi śabde mānasād apacārāt kadācid ākṛtiṃ nopalabheta, na jātucid asāv imāṃ vyaktim avagaccheta. nanu vyaktiviśiṣṭāyām ākṛtau vartate. [83] vyaktiviśiṣṭāyāṃ ced varteta, vyaktyantaraviśiṣṭā na pratīyeta. tasmāc chabda ākṛtipratyayasya nimittam. ākṛtipratyayo vyaktipratyayasyeti.
nanu guṇabhūtā pratīyata ity uktam. na guṇabhāvo 'smatpakṣasya bādhakaḥ. sarvathā tāvat pratīyate. arthād guṇabhāvaḥ pradhānabhāvo vā. svārthaṃ ced uccāryate, pradhānabhūtā. atha na svārtham, parārtham eva, tato guṇabhūtā. na tatra śabdavyāpāro 'sti.
nanu ca daṇḍīti, na tāvad daṇḍiśabdena daṇḍo 'bhidhīyate, atha ca daṇḍaviśiṣṭo 'vagamyate. evam ihāpi na tāvad ākṛtir abhidhīyate, atha cākṛtiviśiṣṭā vyaktir gamyeteti. naitat sādhu ucyate. satyaṃ daṇḍiśabdena daṇḍo nābhidhīyate. na tv apratīte daṇḍe daṇḍipratyayo 'sti. asti tu daṇḍiśabdaikadeśabhūto daṇḍaśabdaḥ, yena daṇḍaḥ pratyāyitaḥ. tasmāt sādhv etad, yat - pratīte viśeṣaṇe viśiṣṭaḥ pratīyata iti.
nanu{*1/632*} gośabdāvayavaḥ kaścid ākṛteḥ pratyāyakaḥ, anyo vyakteḥ, yata ucyate tata ākṛtir avagatā, na gośabda ākṛtivacana iti. na ca yathā daṇḍiśabdo na daṇḍe prayuktaḥ, evaṃ gośabdo nākṛtau. tadartham eva nidarśitaṃ kevalākṛtyabhidhānaḥ śyenaśabda iti. tad evam anvayavyatirekābhyām asati śyenavyaktisaṃbandhe śyenaśabdoccāraṇād ākṛtivacana iti gamyate. na tu vrīhyākṛtisaṃbandham antareṇa vrīhivyaktau śabdasya prayogo dṛṣṭaḥ. tasmād ākṛtivacanaḥ śabda ity etaj jyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text:
The word 'tu' (but) excludes the [opponent's] position. The universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>) is the meaning of the word. Why? Because of its purposiveness toward action. The statement 'one should construct a hawk-shaped [fire-altar]' is possible [only] with reference to the universal form, if the word '<s>śyena</s>' (hawk) has [its] universal form as its meaning. But if it denotes an individual (<s>vyakti</s>), then since an individual hawk cannot be produced by construction, the statement would be purposeless as conveying an impossible meaning. Therefore, [the word] denotes the universal form.
[Objection:] The construction will be carried out with [actual] individual hawks. [Reply:] The meaning of the word '<s>śyena</s>' is not [what is] most efficacious [in performing the rite], for what is most desired is what is denoted by the word '<s>śyena</s>.' Therefore, the hawk must be produced through construction, and this is possible [only] under the universal-form interpretation.
[Objection:] But in both cases the impossibility of action is being pointed out. The universal form is not the word-meaning. Why? Because action would not be possible if the universal form were the word-meaning — [for example,] 'he sprinkles the rice-grains.' Likewise, the individual is not the word-meaning, for action would be impossible if the individual were the word-meaning — [as in] 'one should construct a hawk-shaped [altar].' And as for saying 'he sprinkles the rice-grains' means [the word denotes] a universal form characterized by individuals — one could equally say in the other case, 'one should construct a hawk-shaped [altar]' [means the word denotes] individuals characterized by universal form. What then is the stronger [position]?
The universal form is the word-meaning. If the individual were the word-meaning, [the word] would not apply to another individual. But if it does apply to another individual, then the individual is not the word-meaning, for an individual is devoid of all universals and particulars. [Reply:] This is not a fault. [The word] will apply to another individual precisely [as one] devoid of all universals and particulars. [Objection:] If it applies to another individual devoid of all universals and particulars, then that is just the universal. [Reply:] No — for that which is the substratum (<s>āśraya</s>) of both universal and particular is the individual. And a word denoting the individual operates neither in the universal nor in the particular; it denotes only their substratum. Therefore, application to another individual is not a fault, for it is not [merely] the universal.
[Objection:] If it applies even to other individuals, why does the word 'go' (cow) not apply to a horse-individual, [which is equally] devoid of all universals and particulars? [Reply:] It will apply [only] where usage has been observed, not everywhere. And no usage of the word 'go' has been observed with respect to horse-individuals. Therefore it will not apply there. [Objection:] If application depends on where usage has been observed, then the first application to a newly-born cow would not be possible, since [the word] has not been observed [used of it]. And the cognition of the universal — 'this too is a cow,' 'this too is a cow'; or 'this is a cow,' 'this is a cow' — would not be possible. [Reply:] But the universal-cognition does arise even in regard to a cow-individual never seen before. Therefore, it cannot be maintained that the word 'go' denotes individuals on the basis of [observed] usage. [Objection:] Then this is a property of [the word's] power — it applies to some individuals and not to others, just as fire is hot and water is cold — it will be like that. [Reply:] This does not succeed. For it is not known [by what principle] it applies to some individuals and not others. [Objection:] True, cowness (<s>gotva</s>) will be the distinguishing mark — [the word applies to] that individual in which cowness [inheres]. [Reply:] Then a qualified individual would be apprehended. And if qualified, the qualifier must be apprehended first. For nobody can apprehend the qualified without first apprehending the qualifier. [Objection:] Let it be so — the universal form will be stated as the qualifier, and the individual as the qualificand. For it is not the case that for one whose word-meaning is universal form, the individual is not a word-meaning; nor for one whose word-meaning is the individual, is the universal form not. Both are the word-meaning of both. But for someone, something is intended as primary — and so here, the universal form is intended subordinately, and the individual primarily.
[Reply:] This is not so. When both are stated, the subordinate-primary relation would [need to be established]. And if the universal form is apprehended by the word here, then it cannot be said that the individual too is a word-meaning. Why? Because the universal form is permanently connected with the individual, and when a connected [entity] is apprehended, the correlate is [also] apprehended. This is self-evident: when a word is uttered, an individual is apprehended. But the distinction — whether [it is apprehended] from the word or from the universal form — is not self-evident. That is understood through co-presence and co-absence (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>). Even without the word, one who apprehends the universal form would apprehend the individual. But one who, even when the word is uttered, does not apprehend the universal form due to mental inattention, would never apprehend this individual. [Objection:] [The word] operates with respect to a universal form qualified by an individual. [Reply:] If it operated with respect to [a universal form] qualified by [a particular] individual, [it] would not be apprehended as qualified by another individual. Therefore, the word is the cause of the cognition of the universal form, and the cognition of the universal form [is the cause] of the cognition of the individual.
[Objection:] But it was said that [the universal form] is apprehended as subordinate. [Reply:] The subordinate status does not invalidate our position. It is apprehended in every way. Subordinate or primary status [depends] on the context. If [the universal form] is uttered for its own sake, it is primary. If not for its own sake but only for another's sake, then it is subordinate. There the word's operation is not [at issue].
[Objection:] Consider '<s>daṇḍin</s>' (staff-bearer) — the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>' does not denote the staff, yet one apprehends [the person] as qualified by the staff. Similarly here too, the universal form is not denoted, yet the individual qualified by the universal form would be apprehended. [Reply:] This is not well said. True, the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>' does not denote the staff. But without the staff being apprehended, there is no cognition of a staff-bearer. And there is the word '<s>daṇḍa</s>' (staff) as a component of the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>,' by which the staff is conveyed. Therefore, this is correct — that the qualified is apprehended [only] when the qualifier is apprehended.
[Objection:] Some component of the word 'go' conveys the universal form, another [conveys] the individual; therefore, from that the universal form is understood — but the word 'go' is not [itself] a universal-form-denoter. And it is not the case that, just as the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>' is not used for the staff [alone], the word 'go' is not [used] for the universal form. For this very purpose it was shown that the word '<s>śyena</s>' denotes the universal form alone. Thus, by co-presence and co-absence, in the absence of a connection with individual hawks, from the utterance of the word '<s>śyena</s>' it is understood that [it is] a universal-form-denoter. But usage of the word [for rice-grain individuals] is not observed apart from a connection with the rice-grain universal form. Therefore, [the position that] the word denotes the universal form — this is the stronger [view].

children.text: ākṛtyarthatvāc chabdasya, yasyā vyakter ākṛtyā saṃbandhaḥ, tatra prayogaḥ, prokṣaṇaṃ hi dravyasya kartavyatayā śrūyate. katamasya. yad yajati sādhanam. apūrvaprayuktatvāt tasya nākṛteḥ, aśakyatvāt. tatra vrīhiśabda ākṛtivacanaḥ prayujyate prokṣaṇāśrayaviśeṣaṇāya. sa hy ākṛtiṃ pratyāyayiṣyati, ākṛtiḥ pratītā satī prokṣaṇāśrayaṃ viśekṣyatīti. tenākṛtivacanaṃ na virudhyata iti. evaṃ ṣaḍ deyā gāvo dakṣiṇā iti dakṣiṇādravye saṃkhyāyāḥ prayoktavye gāva ity ākṛtivacano viśeṣakaḥ. tathā - anyam iti vinaṣṭasya pratinidher anyatvasaṃbandhaḥ. tatra paśuśabda ākṛtivacana ākṛtyā viśekṣyatīti. tasmād gaur aśva ityevamādayaḥ śabdā ākṛter abhidhāyakā iti siddham.
children.translated_text: Because the word has universal form as its purpose — [the word] is applied to that individual which has a connection with the universal form. For sprinkling is heard as something to be done to a substance. To which [substance]? That which is the means of the sacrifice. Because it is prompted by the unseen [transcendent purpose] (<s>apūrva</s>), [it pertains] not to the universal form, since that is impossible. There, the word '<s>vrīhi</s>' (rice), being a universal-form-denoter, is applied to qualify the substratum of the sprinkling. For it will convey the universal form, and the universal form, once apprehended, will qualify the substratum of the sprinkling. Therefore, the universal-form-denotation is not contradicted. Similarly, 'six cows should be given as the sacrificial fee' — when the number is to be applied to the fee-substance, 'cows' as a universal-form-denoter serves as the qualifier. Likewise, 'another' — the connection of otherness pertains to the substitute for something destroyed. There, the word '<s>paśu</s>' (animal), being a universal-form-denoter, will qualify through the universal form. Therefore, it is established that words such as 'go' (cow), 'aśva' (horse), and the like are denoters of the universal form.

children.text: uktaṃ samāmnāyaidam arthyaṃ tasmāt sarvaṃ tadarthaṃ syāt // MS_1,4.1 //
children.translated_text: It has been stated that the revealed tradition (<s>samāmnāya</s>) has this [ritual action] as its purpose; therefore, everything [in it] should serve that purpose. // MS 1.4.1 //

children.text:
udbhidā yajeta{*1/636*}; balabhidā yajeta{*1/637*}; abhijitā yajeta{*1/638*}; viśvajitā yajeteti{*1/639*} samāmananti{*1/640*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim udbhidādayo guṇavidhayaḥ, āhosvit karmanāmadheyānīti. kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? ubhayathāpi pratibhāto vākyāt - udbhidety eṣa śabdo yajetety anena saṃbadhyate. sa kiṃ vaiyadhikaraṇyena saṃbandham upaiti{*1/641*} - udbhidā dravyeṇa yāgam abhinirvartayed iti, uta sāmānādhikaraṇyena - udbhidā yāgena yajeteti. dvedhāpy etasmin pratibhāti vākye, saṃbhavati saṃśayaḥ.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? uktam asmābhiḥ samāmnāyasyaidam arthyam. kaścid asya bhāgo vidhiḥ, yo 'viditam arthaṃ vedayati, yathā - somena yajeteti. kaścid arthavādaḥ, yaḥ prarocayan vidhiṃ stauti, yathā - vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā iti{*1/642*}. kaścin mantraḥ, yo vihitam arthaṃ prayogakāle prakāśayati, yathā - barhir devasadanaṃ dāmītyevamādiḥ{*1/643*}. tasmād udbhidādayo 'mīṣāṃ prayojanānām anyatamāya prayojanāya bhaveyuḥ. tatra tāvan nārthavādaḥ, vākyaśeṣo hi sa bhavati vidhātavyasya. na ca mantraḥ, evaṃjātīyakasya prakāśayitavyasyābhāvāt. pāriśeṣyād guṇavidhiḥ - udbhidguṇatā yāgasya vidhīyate. kutaḥ. prasiddher anugrahāt, guṇavidher arthavattvāt pravṛttiviśeṣakaratvāc ca. na caiṣāṃ yāgārthatā loke 'vagamyate. na ca vedena paribhāṣyate. ato guṇavidhayaḥ. yadi guṇavidhiḥ, na tarhi karma vidhīyate. avihite ca karmaṇi tatra guṇavidhāna[86]{*1/644*}m anarthakam. neti brūmaḥ. prakṛtau jyotiṣṭome guṇavidhānam arthavad bhaviṣyati. yadi nāmadheyaṃ syād, yāvad eva yajeteti, tāvad eva udbhidā yajeteti, na pravṛttau kaścid guṇaviśeṣaḥ syāt. guṇavidhau ca guṇasaṃyogād abhyadhikam arthaṃ vidadhata udbhidādayaḥ śabdā arthavanto bhaviṣyanti. tasmād guṇavidhaya ity evaṃ prāptam.
children.translated_text:
'One should sacrifice with the <s>Udbhid</s>'; 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Balabhid</s>'; 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Abhijit</s>'; 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>' — thus they teach in the revealed tradition (<s>samāmananti</s>). There arises a doubt: are <s>Udbhid</s> and the like qualificatory injunctions (<s>guṇavidhi</s>), or are they names of sacrifices (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>)? Whence the doubt? Because the sentence yields both interpretations — the word '<s>udbhid</s>' is syntactically connected with 'one should sacrifice.' Does it enter into connection through co-referentiality (<s>vaiyadhikaraṇya</s>) — 'one should accomplish the sacrifice with the substance [called] <s>udbhid</s>' — or through co-ordinative predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) — 'one should sacrifice with the sacrifice [called] <s>udbhid</s>'? Since the sentence yields both interpretations, doubt arises.
What is the prima facie view? We have stated that the revealed tradition has this [ritual action] as its purpose. Some part of it is an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), which teaches an unknown purpose — such as 'one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>.' Some part is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), which praises the injunction by commending [it] — such as '<s>Vāyu</s> is the swiftest deity.' Some part is a <s>mantra</s>, which illuminates the enjoined purpose at the time of performance — such as 'O <s>Barhis</s>, seat of the gods, covering' and the like. Therefore, <s>Udbhid</s> and the like should serve one of these purposes. Among these, [the passage is] not a laudatory passage, for that is a supplement to what is to be enjoined, [and nothing has been enjoined here independently]. Nor is it a <s>mantra</s>, since there is nothing of this kind to be illuminated. By elimination, [it is] a qualificatory injunction — the <s>udbhid</s>-quality of the sacrifice is enjoined. Why? Because of the support of established usage, because of the purposefulness of a qualificatory injunction, and because it produces a specific mode of performance. And the sacrifice-nature of these [terms] is not known in the world. Nor is it defined by the <s>Veda</s> [as a name]. Therefore, [they are] qualificatory injunctions. If [they are] qualificatory injunctions, then the sacrifice [itself] is not being enjoined [by these words]. And when the sacrifice is not enjoined, the qualificatory injunction [for it] would be purposeless. [Reply:] Not so, we say. The qualificatory injunction will be purposeful with respect to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> as the primary [sacrifice]. If [they were] names, then to the extent that 'one should sacrifice' [says], to that same extent 'one should sacrifice with <s>Udbhid</s>' [would say] — there would be no qualificatory distinction in the performance. But under the qualificatory injunction [interpretation], [the words] <s>Udbhid</s> and the like, by enjoining additional meaning through the combination of a quality, will be purposeful. Therefore, [they are] qualificatory injunctions — thus is the prima facie view.

children.text: evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: Having arrived at this [prima facie view], we say —

children.text: api vā nāmadheyaṃ syād yad utpattāv apūrvam avidhāyakatvāt // MS_1,4.2 //
children.translated_text: Or it may be a name (<s>nāmadheya</s>), because what is novel at the time of origination does not enjoin. // MS 1.4.2 //

children.text:
api veti pakṣo viparivartate. nāmadheyaṃ syād iti pratijānīmahe evam avihitam arthaṃ vidhāsyati - jyotiṣṭomād yāgāntaram. śrutiś caivaṃ yāgam abhidhāsyati. itarathā śrutir udbhidādīn vakṣyantī udbhidādimato lakṣayet. udbhidvatā yāgena kuryād iti. yāgena kuryād iti yajetety asyārthaḥ. karaṇaṃ hi yāgaḥ, udbhidādy api tṛtīyānirdeśāt karaṇam, tatrodbhidā yāgeneti karmanāmadheyatvena sāmānādhikaraṇyasāmañjasyam. dravyavacanatve matvarthalakṣaṇayā sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ syāt. śrutilakṣaṇāviśaye ca śrutir jyāyasī. tasmāt karmanāmadheyam. nanu prasiddhaṃ dravyavacanatvam apahnūyeta, aprasiddhaṃ karmavacanatvaṃ pratijñāyeta. ucyate - tṛtīyānirdeśāt karmavacanatā. kutaḥ? karaṇavācino hi prātipādikāt tṛtīyā bhavati, karaṇaṃ ca yāgaḥ. tena yāgavacanam imam anumāsyāmahe.
naitad yuktam. yadi tṛtīyānirdeśe saty udbhidādibhyaḥ śabdebhyo yāge buddhir utpadyeta syād etad evam. na hi no buddhir utpadyate, tasmād ayuktam. tṛtīyāvacanam anyathā nopapadyata iti cet. kāmaṃ nopapādi{*1/645*}, na jātucid anavagamyamāne [87]{*1/646*} 'pi yāgavacano bhaviṣyati, tasmād guṇavidhayaḥ. lakṣaṇeti cet. varaṃ lakṣaṇā kalpitā, na yāgābhidhānam. laukikī hi lakṣaṇā, haṭho 'prasiddhakalpaneti. api ca - yadi nāmadheyaṃ vidhīyate, na yāgaḥ. atha yāgaḥ, na nāmadheyam. ubhayavidhāne vākyabheda iti. ucyate - na nāmadheyaṃ vidhāyiṣyate. anuvādā hy udbhidādayaḥ. kutaḥ prāptir iti cet. tato 'bhidhīyate - ucchabdasāmarthyād bhicchabdasāmarthyāc codbhicchabdaḥ kriyāvacanaḥ - udbhedanaṃ prakāśanaṃ paśūnām anena kriyata ity udbhid yāgaḥ. evam ābhimukhyena jayād abhijit, viśvajayād viśvajit. evaṃ sarvatra. ataḥ karmanāmadheyam. yat tv apravṛttiviśeṣakaro 'narthaka iti, nāmadheyam api guṇaphalopabandhenārthavat. tasmāt karmanāmadheyāny evaṃjātīyakānīti siddham.
children.translated_text:
The word 'or' (<s>api vā</s>) reverses the position. We maintain that it is a name. Thus, [the word] will enjoin an unenjoined meaning — a sacrifice different from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. And the scripture will denote such a sacrifice. Otherwise, the scripture, intending to speak of <s>Udbhid</s> and the like, would indicate [something] possessing <s>Udbhid</s> and so on — 'one should perform [the rite] with a sacrifice possessing <s>Udbhid</s>.' 'One should perform with a sacrifice' means 'one should sacrifice' — that is the meaning. For the sacrifice is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), and <s>Udbhid</s> and the like are also instruments, since they are indicated with the instrumental case ending. Thus, the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) in '<s>Udbhid</s>-sacrifice' is consistent with [<s>Udbhid</s>] being a name of the ritual action. If it denoted a substance, the co-referentiality would be through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) with possessive meaning (<s>matvarthā</s>). And in a matter where both direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) and secondary signification are possible, direct expression is stronger. Therefore, it is a name of the ritual action. [Objection:] But the well-known meaning as a substance-word would be denied, and the unfamiliar meaning as an action-word would be claimed. [Reply:] It is said — the action-word status is [established] from the instrumental case indication. How so? For the instrumental case suffix comes from a stem that denotes an instrument, and the sacrifice is the instrument. By this we shall infer that it denotes a sacrifice.
This is not correct. If, when the instrumental case indication exists, a cognition of sacrifice arose from words like <s>Udbhid</s> and the like, then this would be so. But no such cognition arises in us; therefore, it is incorrect. [Objection:] If you say the instrumental case usage cannot be explained otherwise — [Reply:] Granted it cannot be explained, [Page 87] but [the word] will never denote a sacrifice when none is apprehended; therefore, [the words are] subsidiary injunctions (<s>guṇavidhi</s>). [Objection:] If [you say it is] secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — [Reply:] Better to posit secondary signification than designation of a sacrifice. For secondary signification is worldly [i.e., well-attested], whereas forcing an unfamiliar construction is arbitrary. Moreover — if a name is being enjoined, then the sacrifice is not. If a sacrifice, then not a name. In enjoining both, there would be sentence-splitting. [Reply:] It is said — the name is not being enjoined. <s>Udbhid</s> and the like are re-statements (<s>anuvāda</s>). [Objection:] How is the [prior] establishment [of the name] known? [Reply:] To this it is said — by the semantic capacity of the prefix <s>ud</s> and the root <s>bhid</s>, the word <s>udbhid</s> denotes an action — '<s>udbhid</s>' means 'a sacrifice by which animals are manifested (<s>udbhedana</s>), brought to light.' Similarly, <s>Abhijit</s> from frontal conquest (<s>ābhimukhya-jaya</s>), <s>Viśvajit</s> from conquering all. And so in all cases. Therefore, it is a name of the ritual action. As for the [objection] that what does not cause a difference in practice is purposeless — even a name is meaningful through its connection with subsidiary qualities and results. Therefore, it is established that such [words] are names of ritual actions.

NOTES:
[E2,4,5,6: <s>mopapādi</s>; Edition cross-references: E2: 2,274; E4: 2,21; E5: 2,192; E6: 1,59]

children.text: yasmin guṇopadeśaḥ pradhānato 'bhisaṃbandhaḥ // MS_1,4.3 //
children.translated_text: When a subsidiary quality is taught, the connection is with the principal [ritual action]. // MS 1.4.3 //

'One who desires cattle should sacrifice with <s>Citrā</s>'; '<s>trivṛt</s> is the outer <s>Pavamāna</s>'; 'the <s>Ājya</s>-[<s>stotras</s>] are fifteen-versed'; 'the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>-[<s>stotras</s>] are seventeen-versed' — these are examples. The question is: are the words <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, <s>Ājya</s>, and <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> subsidiary injunctions or names of ritual actions? Because of familiarity, meaningfulness, and causing a difference in practice, they are subsidiary injunctions. These [words] are not well-known as [names of] ritual actions. Nor are they etymologically derived (<s>yaugika</s>). For these are class-words (<s>jātiśabda</s>), and '<s>citrā</s>' is a quality-word. In 'one sacrifices with <s>Citrā</s>,' the sacrifice is a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>), since it is already known — not an injunction of sacrifice. When a result is attributed to the subsidiary, the [verb] '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) is not intended [as an injunction]. Similarly with 'the <s>Ājyas</s> exist' and 'the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> exist.' Even in construing a subsidiary injunction, there is no [need for] secondary signification. Therefore, [the initial assumption is:] they are subsidiary injunctions. [Page 88]
To this prima facie view we say: When there is a doubt whether it is a subsidiary injunction or a name, and another subsidiary quality is taught, the connection of that [subsidiary quality] is with the principal ritual action — meaning it is a name of the ritual action. For if it were a subsidiary injunction, the sentence would be split. When a male animal has been established [as the norm] but a female animal [is prescribed], when cattle are the result, and <s>citra</s> (variegated) is the [subsidiary] quality — these cannot be enjoined by a single sentence. If the variegated quality is being enjoined [as a subsidiary], it would be enjoined in a female [animal], but that [quality] would not be enjoined in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> rite or in the rite for one desiring cattle, and that [rite] too would not [be enjoined] in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. Similarly, 'the <s>Ājya</s>-[<s>stotras</s>] are fifteen-versed' — the fifteen-verse count [applies] to the <s>Ājyas</s>. But the <s>Ājyas</s> among the <s>stotras</s> (chants) have not been enjoined, and there is no other injunctive sentence that would both enjoin the <s>Ājyas</s> in the <s>stotras</s> and the fifteen-verse count. Yet the connection between the fifteen-verse count and the <s>Ājyas</s> is understood. The connection of the <s>Ājyas</s> with the <s>stotras</s> is unknown, as is the connection with the fifteen-verse count. These two meanings cannot be enjoined by a single sentence. But if it is a name of the ritual action, this conflict does not arise. Only the numerical connection is then enjoined. Moreover, with the words 'the <s>Ājyas</s> are <s>stotras</s>,' the subsidiary quality would be enjoined only through secondary signification. Therefore, these are names of ritual actions — of those [actions] already enjoined by other sentences as 'one chants with the <s>Ājyas</s>,' 'one chants with the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>,' and so on. As for the [objection] that [these words] as names of ritual actions are unfamiliar — [this is answered] through etymological familiarity (<s>avayavaprasiddhi</s>): <s>Ājyas</s> from racing (<s>ājigamana</s>). How is racing [the derivation]? Through a statement in a laudatory passage: 'Because they raced, that is the <s>Ājya</s>-nature of the <s>Ājyas</s>.' <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> from [their association with] touch (<s>sparśa</s>). <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> from having <s>Pavamāna</s>-related <s>mantras</s> and from the connection with [being performed] outside. <s>Citrā</s> from the variety of substances — curds, honey, milk, ghee, parched grain, rice, water. Therefore, such [words] are names of ritual actions. [Objection:] Then why are <s>Ājyas</s> qualified by the number fifteen not enjoined in the <s>stotra</s>-rituals? [Reply:] Because there is no word that denotes [entities] thus qualified.
[Objection:] But this pair of words will serve as the denoter — '<s>pañcadaśāni ājyāni</s>' (fifteen-versed <s>Ājyas</s>) [Page 89] — of those [entities] thus qualified, and will enjoin them in those <s>stotras</s>. [Reply:] This pair of words too is not injunctive. One of them is injunctive, the other is the indicatory subject (<s>uddeśaka</s>). When both are injunctive, there would be no mutual connection between them. When [one is] non-injunctive, the connection with the <s>stotras</s> is not enjoined. And one and the same word cannot serve as the indicatory subject with respect to the qualifier and as the injunctive with respect to the <s>stotra</s>. Because of the difference in the mode of expression, this [objection] is therefore an unsuccessful resolution.

children.translated_text: And another scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) declares it similarly. // MS 1.4.4 //

children.text:
agnihotraṃ juhoti svargakāma iti{*1/660*}; āghāram āghārayatīti{*1/661*} ca samāmananti. tatra saṃśayaḥ -kim agnihotraśabda ādhāraśabdaś ca guṇavidhī, uta karmanāmadheya iti. guṇavidhī iti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ? gamyate hi agnaye hotram asminn iti. tathā kṣaraṇasamarthaṃ dravyaṃ ghṛtādi, āghāram āghārayatīti. prasiddhir evam anugrahīṣyate. guṇavidhiś ca darvihome, āghāraś copāṃśuyāje. tatraitayor arthavattā pravṛttiviśeṣakaratvaṃ ca. na ca guṇavidhipakṣe lakṣaṇā bhavati yathodbhidā yajeta iti. agnihotre samāsenāvagataṃ guṇavidhānam. āghāre 'pi āghāraṃ nirvartayatīti śrutyaiva guṇo vidhīyate. tasmād guṇavidhīty evaṃ prāpte.
brūmah - tatprakhyaṃ cānyaśāstram. yau guṇāv etābhyāṃ vidhīyeta ity āśaṅkyate, tāv anyata evāvagatau. yad agnaye ca prajāpataye ca sāyaṃ juhotīti{*1/662*} devatāvidhānam. caturgṛhītaṃ vā etad abhūt tasyādhāram ādhāryā ity{*1/663*} ādhāre ca dravyavidhiḥ. aviditavedanaṃ ca vidhir ity ucyate. viditaṃ cātrānyato guṇavidhānam. tasmān na guṇavidhī. karmanāmadheye tu saṃbhavataḥ. yasminn agnaye hotraṃ [90]{*1/664*} homo bhavati, tad agnihotram. dīrghadhārā kṣaraṇakriyā prasiddha evāghāraḥ. tasmāt karmanāmadheye. prasiddhyādayaś coktottarāḥ. prajāpatinivṛttyartham agnividhānaṃ bhaviṣyatīti cen. naitad evam. agniṃ hy eṣa vidhātuṃ śaknoti, na parjāpatiṃ pratiṣeddhuṃ. pratiṣidhyamānasya ca prajāpater vidhānam anarthakaṃ syāt, prajāpatir devateti gamyate. gamyamānaṃ ca na śakyaṃ mithyeti kalpayitum. ato 'yam asamādhiḥ. ucyate - āghāram āghārayatīti dravyaparā codanā. yais tu dravyaṃ cikīrṣyata iti{*1/665*}, dravyaṃ hy anayā kriyayā kṣāryate. kṣāritaṃ ca yāgaṃ sādhayati. tat kasya pradhānasya karmaṇo nāmadheyam iti. ucyate - etad evāghāraṇaṃ pradhānakarma. nanv asya dravyadevataṇ nāsti. astīti brūmaḥ. tasyāghāram āghāryety ājyaṃ dravyam; māntravarṇikī devatā - indra ūrdhvoddhara ity āghāram āghārayatīti{*1/666*} mantro hy abhidadhat karma, tatsādhanaṃ vā karmaṇi samavaiti. eṣa ca mantra indram abhidhātuṃ śaknoti. sa yadīndras tatsādhanaṃ bhavet, evam anena mantreṇāghāraḥ śakyate kartum. tasmād indro devatā, dravyadevatāsaṃyuktam āghāraṇam. tasmād yajatiḥ, tasya yajater nāmadheyam iti.
children.translated_text:
'One offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> desiring heaven'; and they teach 'he pours the <s>Āghāra</s>' — there is a doubt: are the words '<s>Agnihotra</s>' and '<s>Āghāra</s>' subsidiary injunctions or names of ritual actions? We say they are subsidiary injunctions. Why? Because it is understood — 'that in which the oblation (<s>hotra</s>) is [offered] to <s>Agni</s>' — that is [the meaning of <s>Agnihotra</s>]. Similarly, a substance capable of flowing, such as ghee — 'he pours the <s>Āghāra</s>.' Familiarity will thus be supported. And [they are] subsidiary injunctions — '<s>Agnihotra</s>' in the <s>darvi-homa</s> (ladle oblation), '<s>Āghāra</s>' in the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (silent offering). In those [cases], they have meaningfulness and the ability to cause a difference in practice. And in the subsidiary-injunction interpretation, there is no secondary signification, as there is in 'one sacrifices with <s>Udbhid</s>.' Thus, in summary, the subsidiary injunction [interpretation] is understood for <s>Agnihotra</s>. For <s>Āghāra</s> too — 'he accomplishes the <s>Āghāra</s>' — the subsidiary quality is enjoined by the direct expression itself. Therefore, [the initial assumption is:] they are subsidiary injunctions.
We say: And another scripture declares it similarly. The two subsidiary qualities that are suspected of being enjoined by these [words] — those are [already] known from elsewhere. 'He offers in the evening to <s>Agni</s> and to <s>Prajāpati</s>' — this is the injunction of the deity. 'Four scoops were taken, the <s>Āghāra</s> is to be poured from those' — and here is the injunction of the substance for the <s>Āghāra</s>. And it is said that an injunction is [something that teaches] what is not [previously] known. Here, however, the subsidiary injunction is [already] known from elsewhere. Therefore, they are not subsidiary injunctions. But they can be names of ritual actions. [Page 90] That in which the oblation (<s>hotra</s>) is the offering (<s>homa</s>) to <s>Agni</s> — that is the <s>Agnihotra</s>. A long stream, a well-known flowing action — that is the <s>Āghāra</s>. Therefore, [they are] names of ritual actions. The [objections based on] familiarity and so forth have [already] been answered. [Objection:] The injunction of <s>Agni</s> [as deity] may serve the purpose of excluding <s>Prajāpati</s>. [Reply:] This is not so. For [the injunction] is capable of enjoining <s>Agni</s>, but not of prohibiting <s>Prajāpati</s>. And when <s>Prajāpati</s> is being prohibited, its injunction would be purposeless — [since] '<s>Prajāpati</s> is the deity' is understood [from the other passage]. And what is understood cannot be construed as false. Therefore, this [objection] is an unsuccessful resolution. [Reply to another objection:] It is said — 'He pours the <s>Āghāra</s>' — this injunction pertains to the substance. [Objection:] But it is thought that the substance is what is intended — for the substance is poured by this action. And the poured [substance] accomplishes the sacrifice. Then of which principal ritual action is [<s>Āghāra</s>] the name? [Reply:] It is said — this very act of pouring (<s>āghāraṇa</s>) is the principal ritual action. [Objection:] But it has no substance and deity. [Reply:] We say it does. Its substance is ghee, [known from] 'the <s>Āghāra</s> is to be poured from those [four scoops]'; its deity is known from the <s>mantra</s>-words — 'O <s>Indra</s>, draw upward' — this is the <s>mantra</s> for pouring the <s>Āghāra</s>. For a <s>mantra</s>, by denoting the ritual action or its instrument, is connected with the ritual action. And this <s>mantra</s> is capable of denoting <s>Indra</s>. If <s>Indra</s> is the instrument of that [<s>Āghāra</s>], then with this <s>mantra</s> the <s>Āghāra</s> can be performed. Therefore, <s>Indra</s> is the deity; the pouring (<s>āghāraṇa</s>) is endowed with substance and deity. Therefore, [it involves the verb] '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), and [<s>Āghāra</s>] is its name.

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 1.5.9; Tait.S. 6.3.7.3, Tait.Br. 3.3.7; Cf. Mait.S. 1.8.7; Source not traced; Edition: E2: 2,286; E4: 2,66; E5: 2,214; E6: 1,61; MS 2.1.8; ŚPBr. 1.5.1.4, Tait.Br. 3.3.7.7, Mantra: Mādhy.S. 2.8, Tait.S. 1.1.12]

children.text: tadvyapadeśaṃ ca // MS_1,4.5 //
children.translated_text: And because of the designation of that [as such]. // MS 1.4.5 //

children.text: athaiṣa śyenenābhicaran yajeta{*1/667*}; athaiṣa saṃdaṃśenābhicaran yajeta{*1/668*}; athaiṣa gavābhicaran yajeteti{*1/669*} samāmnāyante. tatra guṇavidhiḥ karmanāmadheyam iti saṃdehaḥ. prasiddhyādibhiḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ, udbhidādīnām iva. te tūdbhidādayaḥ kriyānimittāḥ śaknuvanti yāgaṃ vaditum. ime punar jātinimittā na śaknuvanti, [91]{*1/670*} tena guṇavidhaya ity evaṃ prāptam. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tadvyapadeśaṃ ca. tena śyenādīnā prasiddhena yasya vyapadeśaḥ, tac ca karmanāmadheyam. śrutir hi nāmadheyatve, lakṣaṇā guṇavidhau. yat tu jātiśabdāḥ, ime na yāgam abhivadantīti. sādṛśyavyapadeśād abhivadiṣyanti. evaṃ hi vyapadeśo bhavati - yathā vai śyeno nipatyādatte, evam ayaṃ dviṣantaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ nipatyādatte, yam abhicaranti śyeneneti{*1/671*}. nipatyādatta ity anena sādṛśyena śyenaśabdo yāge, yathā siṃho devadatta iti. tasmāt karmanāmadheyam. saṃdaṃśe, saṃdaṃśena yathā durādānam ādatta iti. gavi yathā gāvo gopāyantīti. tasmāt saṃdaṃśaśabdo 'pi karmanāmadheyaṃ gośabdo 'pi.
children.translated_text: Now, the following are traditionally recited: 'One who practices sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Śyena</s> (hawk)'; 'One who practices sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Saṃdaṃśa</s> (tongs)'; 'One who practices sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Gava</s> (cow).' There, the doubt arises: is this an injunction of a subsidiary element (<s>guṇavidhi</s>), or is it the name of a ritual action (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>)? The prima facie view [favoring <s>guṇavidhi</s>] is [supported] by familiarity and so on, as in the case of <s>Udbhid</s> and the like. But those [words like] <s>Udbhid</s> and the like, being occasioned by the action, are capable of denoting the sacrifice. These [words] however, being occasioned by the <s>jāti</s> (species/class), are not capable [of denoting the sacrifice]. Therefore, it follows that they are injunctions of subsidiary elements. When this has been arrived at, we say — 'And because of the designation by that.' That which is designated by the well-known [animal] <s>Śyena</s> and the like — that is the name of the ritual action. For the direct sense (<s>śruti</s>) favors it being a name, while secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) [would be needed] for a subsidiary-element injunction. As for [the objection] that these species-words do not denote the sacrifice — they will denote it through designation based on similarity. For the designation occurs thus: 'Just as a hawk, swooping down, seizes [its prey], so this [sacrifice] swoops down and seizes the hostile rival — for one who practices sorcery with the <s>Śyena</s>.' By the similarity 'swooping down and seizing,' the word <s>Śyena</s> is [applied] to the sacrifice, just as [one says] '<s>Devadatta</s> is a lion.' Therefore, it is a name of the ritual action. In the case of <s>Saṃdaṃśa</s> — 'Just as with tongs one seizes what is difficult to seize.' In the case of <s>Gava</s> — 'Just as cows protect.' Therefore, the word <s>Saṃdaṃśa</s> too is a name of the ritual action, and so is the word <s>Gava</s>.

children.text: nāmadheye guṇaśruteḥ syād vidhānam iti cet // MS_1,4.6 //
children.translated_text: If [you say that] when there is a heard subsidiary element in the name, there should be an injunction — // MS_1,4.6 //

children.text: vājapeyena svārājyakāmo yajeteti{*1/672*} śrūyate. tatra kiṃ guṇavidhiḥ, karmanāmadheyam iti saṃdehaḥ. evaṃ cet saṃdehaḥ, dṛśyate guṇavidhiḥ. na saṃdehaḥ, śrūyate hi guṇaḥ. so 'vagamyamāno na śakyo nāstīti vaditum. tasmād guṇavidhiḥ.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'One desiring sovereignty should sacrifice with the <s>Vājapeya</s>.' There, the doubt arises: is this an injunction of a subsidiary element, or is it the name of a ritual action? If there is such a doubt, a subsidiary-element injunction is observed [as prima facie]. There is no doubt, for a subsidiary element is heard. That which is being cognized cannot be said to be non-existent. Therefore, it is an injunction of a subsidiary element.

NOTES:
Tait.Br. 1.3.6.9

children.text: tulyatvāt kriyayor na // MS_1,4.7 //
children.translated_text: Because of the equality of the two actions, it is not [a subsidiary-element injunction]. // MS_1,4.7 //

children.text: naitad evam, tulye hīme kriye syātām. yā ca vājypeyakriyā, yā ca darśapurṇamāsakriyā, ubhayatra dārśapaurṇamāsiko vidhyantaḥ syāt. tathā ca dīkṣāṇām upasadāṃ ca darśanaṃ nāvakalpyeta, saptadaśadīkṣo vājapeya iti, saptadaśopasatko vājapeya iti. atha vā tulyatvāt kriyayor neti. yadi na guṇavidhiḥ, tatas tulyaiṣā vājapeyakriyā jyotiṣṭomakriyayā. tatra{*1/673*} dīkṣāṇā[92]{*1/674*}m upasadāṃ ca darśanam upapannam. tasmāt karmanāmadheyam iti. liṅgaṃ tv etat, prāptiḥ punar uttarasūtreṇa.
children.translated_text: This is not so, for the two actions would be equal. The <s>Vājapeya</s> action and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> action — in both cases, the <s>Dārśapaurṇamāsika</s> [model] would be the injunctive content. And thus, the observation of [specific numbers of] consecrations (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and preparatory rites (<s>upasad</s>) would not be possible — 'the <s>Vājapeya</s> has seventeen consecrations,' 'the <s>Vājapeya</s> has seventeen preparatory rites.' Alternatively: 'Because of the equality of the two actions, it is not [a subsidiary-element injunction]' — if it is not a subsidiary-element injunction, then this <s>Vājapeya</s> action is equal to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> action. In that case, the observation of [specific numbers of] consecrations and preparatory rites is well-established. Therefore, it is a name of the ritual action. This, however, is an indicative sign (<s>liṅga</s>); the [definitive] establishment is by the next <s>sūtra</s>.

NOTES:
[Variant: E4 reads 'tadā ca'; E4 variant: 'tatthā'] | [Page refs: E2: 2,292; E4: 2,95; E5: 2,224; E6: 1,63]

children.text: ekaśabdye parārthavat // MS_1,4.8 //
children.translated_text: When there is a single word [for both], [it would function] like [a word] serving another's purpose. // MS_1,4.8 //

children.text: yadi guṇavidhiḥ syāt, svārthavat parārthavac cābhidhānaṃ vipratiṣidhyeta{*1/675*} yajetety asya śabdasya. yadi svārājyakāmo yajeteti svārājyakāmasya yāgaṃ vidhātuṃ svārtham ucyate, na tarhi vājapeyena guṇena saṃbaddhuṃ parārtham anūdyeta yāgena vājapeyaguṇakeneti. bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. nanu dve evaite vākye pratyakṣam upalabhāmahe - svārājyakāmo{*1/676*} yajetety{*1/677*} etad ekaṃ pratyakṣaṃ padadvayam. yajeta vājapeyenety etad api pratyakṣam eva. naitad evam. evaṃ sati catvāri padāny upalabhemahi, trīṇi caitāny upalabhyante. ucyate - yajetety etad ubhābhyāṃ saṃbhantsyate. kathaṃ sakṛd uccāritaṃ saṃbandham ubhābhyām eṣyatīti. rūpābhedāt. īdṛśam evāsya rūpaṃ svārājyakāmena saṃbadhyamānasyā, īdṛśam eva vājapeyena. atas tantreṇobhābhyāṃ saṃbhantsyata iti. naitad astīdṛśenaiva rūpeṇeti. yady ajñātaḥ, tato{*1/678*} vidhiḥ. yadi jñātaḥ, tato 'nuvādaḥ. na ca jñāto 'jñātaś ca yugapat saṃbhavatīti. āha - yad idam uktam, guṇavidhipakṣe 'nuvādo yajeteti. yady ayam anuvādaḥ, kenedānīṃ guṇo vidhīyate. vājapeyaśabdeneti mā vocaḥ. na hy ākhyātam antareṇa kṛtyaṃ vā, nāmaśabdārthasya vyāpāro{*1/679*} vidhīyate. yaś cātrākhyātaśabdo yajeteti, so 'nuvāda ity uktam. kenedānīṃ tasya vyāpāro vidhīyate. ataḥ svārājyakāmaṃ guṇaṃ ca prati yajeteti vidhiḥ. tasmād ubhābhyāṃ saṃbadhyata iti. yady ubhayatra vidhiḥ, vājapeyo na svārājyakāmasya yāgena saṃbadhyeta. dve hy ete tadā vākye, na svārājyakāmasya yāgena saha guṇavidher ekavākyatā.[93]{*1/680*} prakaraṇāt saṃbandhaḥ svārājyakāmasya yāgeneti cet, na, vākyena yāgamātre vidhānāt. astu yāgamātreṇa saṃbandha iti cet, na, svārājyakāmasya yāgena sahaikavākyatāyā gamyamānatvāt. tad evaṃ prakaraṇasya vākyasya ca bādho{*1/681*} yujyate, yadi karmanāmadheyam. guṇavidhipakṣe hi sarva ime vākyabhedādayo doṣāḥ prādurbhaveyuḥ. tasmāt karmanāmadheyaṃ vājapeyaśabda iti siddham.
children.translated_text: If it were a subsidiary-element injunction, there would be a contradiction between the word '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice) functioning for its own purpose and functioning for another's purpose. If 'one desiring sovereignty should sacrifice' is stated for its own purpose — to enjoin the sacrifice for one desiring sovereignty — then the sacrifice would not be restated for another's purpose, to be connected with the subsidiary element <s>Vājapeya</s>, as 'one sacrifices with the subsidiary element <s>Vājapeya</s>.' For the sentence would be split thus. [Objection:] But we directly perceive two sentences — 'one desiring sovereignty should sacrifice' — this is one directly perceived pair of words; 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Vājapeya</s>' — this too is directly perceived. [Reply:] This is not so. If that were the case, we would perceive four words, but we perceive [only] three. It is said: the word '<s>yajeta</s>' will be connected with both. How can what is uttered once achieve connection with both? Because of the non-difference in form. Its form is exactly the same whether connected with 'one desiring sovereignty' or with '<s>Vājapeya</s>.' Therefore, it will be connected with both through combination (<s>tantra</s>). [Objection:] It is not the case that the form is exactly the same. [Reply:] If [the form is] unknown, then it is an injunction. If known, then it is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>). And being both known and unknown simultaneously is impossible. He says: as to what was said — 'in the subsidiary-element view, <s>yajeta</s> is a restatement' — if this is a restatement, then by what is the subsidiary element enjoined? Do not say 'by the word <s>Vājapeya</s>.' For without a finite verb or a verbal derivative (<s>kṛtya</s>), the activity of a noun-word's meaning cannot be enjoined. And the finite verb here, <s>yajeta</s>, has been said to be a restatement. By what, then, is its activity enjoined? Therefore, '<s>yajeta</s>' is an injunction with respect to both — the one desiring sovereignty and the subsidiary element. Hence it is connected with both. [Objection:] If it is an injunction in both cases, the <s>Vājapeya</s> would not be connected with the sacrifice of the one desiring sovereignty, for these would then be two [separate] sentences, and there would be no unity of sentence between the subsidiary-element injunction and the sacrifice of the one desiring sovereignty. [Objection:] The connection with the sacrifice of the one desiring sovereignty would be from the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). [Reply:] No, because the sentence enjoins merely a sacrifice. [Objection:] Let the connection be with mere sacrifice. [Reply:] No, because the unity of sentence with the sacrifice of the one desiring sovereignty is understood. Thus, the overriding of both context and sentence is justified if it is a name of the ritual action. For in the subsidiary-element view, all these defects — splitting of the sentence and the rest — would arise. Therefore, the word <s>Vājapeya</s> is a name of the ritual action — this is established.

children.text:
yad āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavatītyevamādayaḥ{*1/682*} śrūyante. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim āgneyo 'gnīṣomīya ityevamādayo guṇavidhayaḥ, karmanāmadheyānīti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. guṇavidhau saty aneko guṇo vidhīyeta - agnipuroḍāśāṣṭākapālā iti. tasmān na guṇavidhaya iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tac ca karmaṃ guṇāś cāsya vidhīyeran. avibhaktā hi te karmaṇo vidhānārthe tad dhitānte śabde. tatra hy aṣṭākapālasyāgneyatā vidhīyate. sa eṣa evam āgneyo bhavati, yady agnaye saṃkalpya dīyate, tenāyam anena prakāreṇa yāgo vihito bhavati. sa evaṃ vidhīyamāno na śakyo 'gnim aṣṭākapālaṃ cāvidhāya vidhātum, saṃbandho hi vidhīyamāno na śakyate saṃbandhināv avidhāya vihita iti vaktum. tasmād guṇavidhayaḥ. aṣṭasu kapāleṣu saṃskriyamāṇo vrīhimayo yavamayo vā puroḍāśa eva bhavati. so 'nuvādaḥ. siddhaś cātrāṣṭākapāla ucyate kapāleṣu śrayayatīti{*1/683*} vaca[94]{*1/684*}nād nānyena śrapitaṃ gṛhṇanti. tenāsmin pakṣe na vākyabhedo bhavati. na ced anyena śiṣṭāḥ. yatra punar anyena vacanena śiṣṭā guṇā bhavanti, bhavati tatra nāmadheyam. yathā - agnihotraṃ juhotīti.
children.translated_text:
The following is heard: 'An offering cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) of eight potsherds for <s>Agni</s>, for <s>Acyuta</s> on the new-moon and full-moon days' and so on. There, the doubt arises: are '<s>Āgneya</s>' (for <s>Agni</s>), '<s>Agnīṣomīya</s>' (for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>), and the like, subsidiary-element injunctions or names of ritual actions? What is first arrived at? If they are subsidiary-element injunctions, multiple subsidiary elements would be enjoined — '<s>Agni</s>, <s>puroḍāśa</s>, eight potsherds.' Therefore, they are not subsidiary-element injunctions.
When this has been arrived at, we say: both the ritual action and its subsidiary elements should be enjoined. For those [elements] are undifferentiated from the injunctive purpose in that word ending with the <s>taddhita</s> suffix. For there, the <s>Āgneya</s>-nature of the eight-potsherd [offering] is enjoined. It becomes <s>Āgneya</s> (belonging to <s>Agni</s>) when it is dedicated and offered to <s>Agni</s> — thus the sacrifice is enjoined in this manner. When being enjoined thus, it cannot be enjoined without enjoining [both] <s>Agni</s> and the eight-potsherd [offering cake], for a relation being enjoined cannot be said to be enjoined without enjoining the relata. Therefore, they are subsidiary-element injunctions. A <s>puroḍāśa</s> (offering cake) — being a preparation of rice or barley on eight potsherds — is indeed a <s>puroḍāśa</s>. That is a restatement. And the eight-potsherd [offering] is stated here as an established [fact], because of the statement 'one cooks on the potsherds' — they do not accept what is cooked by another [means]. Therefore, in this view, there is no splitting of the sentence. 'Unless they have been taught by another [passage]' — but where the subsidiary elements have been taught by another statement, there it is a name [of the ritual action]. For example — 'One offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>.'

children.text: barhirājyor asaṃskāre śabdalābhād atacchabdaḥ // MS_1,4.10 //
children.translated_text: In the case of <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) and <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter), since [the words are used] without the ritual preparation, and because the word is obtained [even without preparation], the word is not [a preparation-word]. // MS_1,4.10 //

children.text:
barhirājyayoḥ puroḍāśe ca saṃdehaḥ - kim ete saṃskāraśabdā uta jātiśabdā{*1/685*} iti. saṃskāraśabdā iti brūmaḥ. saṃskṛteṣu tṛṇeṣu barhiḥśabdam upacaranti sarvatra, nāsaṃskṛteṣu. saṃskṛte ca ghṛte ājyaśabdam. tathā saṃskṛte piṣṭe puroḍāśaśabdam. nanv asaṃskṛte 'pi kasmiṃścid deśa upacaryate. yathā barhir ādāya gāvo gatā iti bhavanti vaktāraḥ. tathā - ājyaṃ krayam iti. puroḍāśena me mātā prahelakaṃ dadātīti. sādṛśyāt teṣu prayogaḥ. yathopaśaye yūpaśabdaḥ. kuta etat? yata ekadeśe hi śabdaprayogaḥ, tasmāt saṃskāraśabdā ity evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - barhirādiṣv asaṃskṛteṣv api śabdalābhān na saṃskāraśabdāḥ. nanūktaṃ sādṛśyād ekadeśe bhaviṣyanti. tan na, prasiddhe hi saṃskāraśabdatve, sādṛśyād iti śakyate vaktum. tac cāprasiddham. katham? barhirādiśabdair uddiśya saṃskārā vidhīyante. tena satsu śabdeṣu saṃskārair bhavitavyam, sati ca saṃskāre śabdalābha itītaretarāśrayaṃ bhavati. na cāvihitāḥ saṃskārā bhavanti, yān ālocya lokaḥ prayuñjīta. tasmān na lokāḥ saṃskṛteṣu barhirādīn prayuñjate. tata ekadeśe 'pi jāti[95]{*1/686*}nimittā dṛṣṭāḥ, sarvatra jātinimittā bhavitum arhanti. na cālaukikānāṃ satāṃ vedād eva pūrvottarapadasaṃbandham anapekṣya śakyate 'rtho 'dhyavasātum. pūrvottarapade anarthake mā bhūtām ity evaṃ sa parikalpyeta. aśakyas tv anavagamyamānaḥ parikalpayitum, arthavatī ca te pade pūrvottare laukikenāsaṃskṛtaprayogeṇa bhaviṣyataḥ. tasmāj jātiśabdā evaṃjātīyakāḥ. prayojanam - barhiṣā yūpāvaṭam avastṛṇātīti saṃskṛtair eva staritavyam, yadi pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, viparītaṃ siddhānte.
children.translated_text:
Regarding <s>barhis</s>, <s>ājya</s>, and <s>puroḍāśa</s>, the doubt arises: are these preparation-words (<s>saṃskāra-śabda</s>) or class-words (<s>jāti-śabda</s>)? We say: they are preparation-words. The word <s>barhis</s> is used everywhere for ritually prepared grass, not for unprepared grass. Similarly, the word <s>ājya</s> for prepared ghee. And the word <s>puroḍāśa</s> for prepared flour. [Objection:] But in some regions, [these words] are used even for unprepared [items]. For example, people say 'the cows went off carrying <s>barhis</s> (grass).' Similarly, '<s>ājya</s> (ghee) is for sale.' And 'my mother gives me a treat with <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake).' [Reply:] The usage in those cases is based on resemblance, just as the word <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post) is used for an <s>upaśaya</s> (pillar). How is this known? Because the usage of the word is limited to one context — therefore, they are preparation-words. This is the prima facie view.
When this has been arrived at, we say: since the words are obtained even for unprepared <s>barhis</s> and the rest, they are not preparation-words. [Objection:] Was it not said that the usage in [some] regions will be based on resemblance? [Reply:] No, for [the argument from] resemblance can be made only if the preparation-word status is established. But that is not established. How? Preparations are enjoined by designating [items] with the words <s>barhis</s> and the like. Therefore, the words must exist [first], then the preparations must follow; and if the preparations exist, the words are obtained — this leads to mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). And there are no un-enjoined preparations that people in the world would observe and then apply [these words]. Therefore, people in the world do not use <s>barhis</s> and the like for ritually prepared [items]. Since even in one context [the words] are seen to be based on the class (<s>jāti</s>), they should be based on class everywhere. And for [words] that are not worldly, when they exist [in the <s>Veda</s>], their meaning cannot be determined without considering the connection of prior and subsequent words [in the Vedic sentence]. [One might say:] Let [the meaning] be construed so that the prior and subsequent words would not be purposeless. But what cannot be understood cannot be construed, and those prior and subsequent words will be meaningful through the worldly usage for unprepared [items]. Therefore, words of this kind are class-words. The practical consequence: 'One covers the <s>yūpa</s>-pit with <s>barhis</s>' — [this means] one must cover with ritually prepared [grass] alone, if the first view [is correct]; the opposite in the established conclusion.

children.text: prokṣaṇīṣv arthasaṃyogāt // MS_1,4.11 //
children.translated_text: In the case of the sprinkling waters (<s>prokṣaṇī</s>), because of connection with the purpose. // MS_1,4.11 //

children.text: prokṣaṇīr āsādaya iti{*1/687*} śrūyate. tatra prokṣaṇīśabdaṃ prati saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ saṃskāranimitta uta jātinimitta uta yaugika iti. tatra saṃskāreṣu satsu darśanāt saṃskāraśabdatāyām avagamyamānāyām asaṃskṛte śabdalābhāj jātiśabdaḥ. asaṃskṛtāsv evāpsu prokṣaṇībhir udvejitāḥ sma iti kasmiṃścid deśe bhavanti vaktāraḥ. tena jātiśabda iti prāpte. yaugika ity ucyate. kutaḥ? arthasaṃyogāt. prokṣaṇya ity upasargadhātupratyayasamudāyasya jātinimittatā prayogād anumīyate. secanasaṃyogāt tūpasargadhātukaraṇapratyayasahito 'psu pravatata iti prasiddhir anugṛhītā bhaviṣyati. yadānyad api secanaṃ prokṣaṇaśabdenocyate tadā tatsaṃyogād evāpsu bhaviṣyatīti na samudāyārthaḥ kalpayituṃ śakyate. tasmād yaugikaḥ. prayojanaṃ ghṛtaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ bhavatīti, yadi saṃskāraśabdāḥ prokṣaṇīrāsādayeti praiṣaḥ. yadi jātiśabdaḥ, ghṛtam āsādayeti. yadi yaugikaḥ prokṣaṇam iti.
children.translated_text: 'Set in place the sprinkling waters (<s>prokṣaṇī</s>)' — this is heard. Regarding the word <s>prokṣaṇī</s>, there is a doubt: is it based on a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>), or on class (<s>jāti</s>), or is it etymologically derived (<s>yaugika</s>)? Among these, when the word is understood as a preparatory-rite term — since [the usage] is observed where preparatory rites exist — water that has not undergone the preparatory rite would not receive the designation; [hence] it would be a class-term. [But] even in unsanctified waters, in certain regions speakers say 'we were startled by the sprinkling waters (<s>prokṣaṇī</s>).' Therefore, having arrived at [the conclusion that] it is a class-term, we say: it is etymologically derived. Why? Because of connection with meaning. The combination of prefix, root, and suffix in '<s>prokṣaṇya</s>' — [the supposition] that it denotes a class is inferred from usage. But through connection with the act of sprinkling, the well-established understanding that [the combination of] prefix, root, instrument-suffix extends to waters will be supported. When sprinkling other [things] too is called by the word <s>prokṣaṇa</s>, then through that very connection with [sprinkling], it will apply to waters — hence no aggregate meaning needs to be postulated. Therefore, it is etymologically derived. The practical consequence: ghee would be [a valid] sprinkling [substance] — if [<s>prokṣaṇī</s>] were a preparatory-rite term, the injunction would be 'set in place the sprinkling waters.' If it were a class-term, [it would mean] 'set in place the ghee.' If etymologically derived, [it means] 'the sprinkling [agent].'

children.text: tathā nirmanthye // MS_1,4.12 //
children.translated_text: Likewise with [the fire] produced by churning (<s>nirmanthya</s>). // MS 1,4.12 //

children.text: nirmanthyeneṣṭakāḥ pacantīti. saṃskṛte darśanāt saṃskāraśabdo nirmanthya iti. asaṃskāre 'pi dṛśyate. nirmanthyamānayādainaṃ pakṣyāma iti. nirmanthanayogāt pūrvavad yaugika iti saṃsthitam. prayojanaṃ saṃskāranimitte saṃskṛteneṣṭakāḥ paktavyāḥ. jātiśabde yathopapannena. yaugike 'ciranirmathite yathā nāvanītena bhuṅkta ity aciranirdagdheneti gamyate.
children.translated_text: 'They bake the bricks with [fire] produced by churning (<s>nirmanthya</s>).' Since [the usage] is observed with sanctified [fire], <s>nirmanthya</s> would be a preparatory-rite term. But it is also seen without the preparatory rite: 'bring him with [fire being] churned, we shall bake [the bricks].' Because of the connection with the act of churning, it is established as etymologically derived, as before. The practical consequence: if it were a preparatory-rite term, the bricks would have to be baked with [fire that has been] sanctified. If a class-term, with whatever [fire] is available. If etymologically derived, with [fire] recently churned — just as 'one eats with fresh butter' is understood as 'with recently churned [butter].'

children.text: vaiśvadeve vikalpa iti cet // MS_1,4.13 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] there would be an alternative in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [rite] — // MS 1,4.13 //

children.text: cāturmāsyeṣu prathame parvaṇi vaiśvadeve saṃdehaḥ - vaiśvadevena yajeta iti{*1/689*}. kiṃ vaiśvadevaśabdo guṇavidhir uta karmanāmadheyam iti. yadi saṃdeho na saṃdehaḥ. vaiśvadeve vikalpaḥ. guṇavidhir vaiśvadevaśabdaḥ. gamyate hi guṇavidhānam. viśvedevā vidhīyanta āgneyādiṣu yāgeṣu. tatrāgnyādīnāṃ viśvair devair vikalpaḥ. evaṃ prasiddhir arthavatī bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly) rites, in the first <s>parvan</s> (division), there is a doubt regarding the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> — 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.' Is the word <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> a quality-injunction or a ritual name (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>)? If there is a doubt — no, there is no doubt. In the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, [there would be] an alternative. The word <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> is a quality-injunction. For a quality-injunction is understood — the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) are enjoined in the <s>Āgneya</s> and other sacrificial offerings. In those [offerings], <s>Agni</s> and other [deities] would be alternatives to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>. Thus the well-known [usage] will be meaningful.

children.text: na vā prakaraṇāt pratyakṣavidhānāc ca na hi prakaraṇaṃ dravyasya // MS_1,4.14 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the context and the explicit injunction; for the context [does not override] a substance [explicitly prescribed]. // MS 1,4.14 //

children.text: naitad evam. pratyakṣaśrutivihitā agnyādayas teṣāṃ yāgānām, viśvedevā vākyena prakaraṇāt tenaiva nānyeneti gamyate. na cāyaṃ viṣamaśiṣṭho vikalpo bhavitum arhati. na hi prakaraṇaṃ śrutasya dravyasya bādhane samartham. tasmāt karmanāmadheyam.
children.translated_text: This is not so. <s>Agni</s> and the other [deities] are enjoined for those sacrifices by explicit scripture (<s>pratyakṣaśruti</s>); the <s>Viśvedevas</s> [are understood] from the sentence and from context — by that [context] alone, not by anything else — this is understood. And this unequal alternative is not proper. For the context is not capable of overriding a substance that is [explicitly] heard [in scripture]. Therefore, it is a ritual name (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>).
