children.text: mithaś cānarthasaṃbandhaḥ // MS_1,4.15 //
children.translated_text: And [there would be] a mutual connection of purposelessness. // MS 1,4.15 //

children.text: athocyate vaiśvadeva ity anena śabdena pratyakṣam agnyādiguṇaviśiṣṭo yāgaguṇo lakṣyate. vaiśvadevī hi tatrāmikṣā samavaiti. yadi vaiśvadevaśabdena yāgaguṇo lakṣyate na tarhi viśvedevā vidhīyante kathaṃ sakṛd uccarito vaiśvadevaśabdo yāgaguṇaṃ lakṣayiṣyati viśvāṃś ca devān vidhāsyatīti nāyaṃ vaiśvadevaśabdasya viśvair devair mithaḥ saṃbandho ghaṭate. tasmāt karmanāmadheyam eva guṇavidhir iti.
children.translated_text: Now it is said: by the word <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, a quality (<s>guṇa</s>) of the sacrifice — specifically, [one] characterized by <s>Agni</s> and other deities — is directly indicated. For the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> curds (<s>āmikṣā</s>) are associated with it. If by the word <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> a quality of the sacrifice is indicated, then the <s>Viśvedevas</s> are not [separately] enjoined. How could the word <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, uttered only once, both indicate a quality of the sacrifice and also enjoin the <s>Viśvedevas</s>? This mutual connection of the word <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> with the <s>Viśvedevas</s> does not work. Therefore, it is indeed a ritual name (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>), not a quality-injunction.

children.text: parārthatvād guṇānām // MS_1,4.16 //
children.translated_text: Because qualities serve another [purpose]. // MS 1,4.16 //

children.text: parārthāś ca guṇāḥ. te na śaknuvanti pradhānam āvartayitum. tena sakṛd yāga kartavyo na guṇānurodhenāvartitum arhati. saṃpratipannadevatatvāc ca na virodhaḥ. tatraikasyāṃ pradhānāhutau triṃśadāhutayo hūyanta iti triṃśatsaṃkhyāsaṃpattir āhavanīyāhutīnāṃ nāvakalpate. tasmāt karmanāmadheyam iti siddham.
children.translated_text: Qualities serve another purpose. They cannot cause the principal [offering] to be repeated. Therefore, the sacrifice should be performed once — it should not be repeated on account of the qualities. And because the deity has been agreed upon, there is no contradiction. In that case, [the supposition] that in a single principal oblation, thirty oblations are offered — this fulfillment of the number thirty for the oblations in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] does not work. Therefore, it is established that it is a ritual name (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>).

children.text: pūrvavanto 'vidhānārthās tatsāmarthyaṃ samāmnāye // MS_1,4.17 //
children.translated_text: Those [passages] containing prior [elements] serve the purpose of injunction; this capacity [of theirs] is [understood] from the codified teaching (<s>samāmnāya</s>). // MS 1,4.17 //

children.text: vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet putre jāta iti{*1/691*} śrūyate. tatra yadaṣṭākapālo bhavati gāyatryaivainaṃ brahmavarcasena punātītyevamādayaḥ kapālavikalpāḥ śrūyante teṣu saṃdehaḥ kim aṣṭatvādayo guṇavidhaya utārthavādā iti. tatra guṇavidhaya ity evaṃ brūmaḥ - katham? ye hi pūrvavanto (viditapūrvam{*1/692*} artha[98]{*1/693*}m abhivadanti){*1/694*} te 'vidhānārthāḥ tad etad asya vākyasya samāmnāye sāmarthyaṃ yadavihitapūrvakābhidhānam. kiṃ tat, vidhānasāmarthyam. evam avihitam arthaṃ vidhāsyati. itarathārthavādāḥ santo 'narthakāḥ syuḥ. na ca dvadaśakapālasya śeṣabhāvam upagantum arhati. pratyakṣā hy aṣṭānāṃ kapālānāṃ stutiḥ parokṣā dvādaśānām. pratyakṣābhāve ca parokṣā syāt. tasmād guṇavidhayaḥ.
children.translated_text: 'One should offer a twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> when a son is born' — this is heard. There, [passages such as] 'when it has eight <s>kapālas</s>, it is by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] alone that it purifies him with the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>' and similar alternatives regarding the number of <s>kapālas</s> are heard. Regarding these there is a doubt: are the [numbers] eight and so on quality-injunctions, or laudatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>)? We say they are quality-injunctions. How? Those [passages] that contain prior [elements] (that refer to a meaning already known) serve the purpose of injunction — this is the capacity of this sentence in the codified teaching, namely the expression of what has not been previously enjoined. What is that? The capacity for injunction. Thus, it will enjoin what has not [yet] been enjoined. Otherwise, being laudatory passages, they would be purposeless. Nor is it proper for the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] to be subordinated [to the others]. For the praise of eight <s>kapālas</s> is explicit, while [the praise of] twelve is indirect. In the absence of the explicit, the indirect would apply. Therefore, they are quality-injunctions.

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 2.2.5.3, Vāj.S. 29.60] | [E4 footnote: vihitapūrvam] | [Edition page references: E2: 2,307; E4: 2,157; E5: 2,249; E6: 1,67] | [Bracketed in E1]

children.text: guṇasya tu vidhānārthe tadguṇāḥ prayoge syur anarthakā na hi taṃ pratyarthavatāsti // MS_1,4.18 //
children.translated_text: But if [they are] for the purpose of enjoining a quality, then those qualities would be purposeless in [actual] performance; for nothing meaningful exists with respect to that [quality-injunction]. // MS 1,4.18 //

children.text: naitad asti guṇavidhaya iti. guṇasya vidhānārthā ete santaḥ puroḍāśasya kapāleṣu saṃkhyā vidadhyuḥ. na śaknuvanti yāgaprayogasya vidhātum. dvādaśakapālatā hi yāgasya vākyena, aṣṭākapālādayaḥ prakareṇa. tena te yāge na bhaviṣyanti. api cāṣṭatvādayaḥ puroḍāśenaikavākyabhūtāḥ prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā, na yāgasya bhaviṣyanti. yāgāsaṃbandhe cānarthakāḥ puroḍāśasaṃbandhe phalābhāvāt. arthavādatvena tu vaiśvānarayāgasya stutir upapadyate. tasmād arthavādā iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — [that they are] quality-injunctions. If these serve the purpose of enjoining a quality, they would prescribe the number of <s>kapālas</s> for the sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>). They cannot prescribe for the performance of the sacrifice [itself]. For the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> nature of the sacrifice [is established] by the sentence, while eight-<s>kapāla</s> and the like [come] from the context. Therefore, they will not apply to the sacrifice. Moreover, [the numbers] eight and so on, forming a single sentence with the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, would override the context — they would not apply to the sacrifice. And being unconnected with the sacrifice, they are purposeless — because there is no fruit [from being] connected with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> [alone]. But as laudatory passages, the praise of the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> sacrifice is well-established. Therefore, they are laudatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>).

children.text: taccheṣo nopapadyate // MS_1,4.19 //
children.translated_text: The subordination to that [sacrifice] is not tenable. // MS 1,4.19 //

children.text: iti yad uktaṃ tat parihartavyam ity ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram.
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> [extends] up to the introduction [of the next topic], meaning: what was stated [in the previous sūtra] must be refuted.

children.text: avibhāgād vidhānārthe stutyarthenopapadyeran // MS_1,4.20 //
children.translated_text: Since they are undifferentiated [from the injunctive portion], they could serve the purpose of praise while serving the purpose of injunction. // MS 1,4.20 //

children.text: yadā tv aṣṭākapālādiprarocanārthā anarthakā ity avagataṃ tadā lakṣaṇayā dvādaśakapālasya stutir vaiśvānarayāgaprarocanārthā bhaviṣyati. santi hi dvādaśasaṃkhyāyām aṣṭatvādayaḥ saṃkhyāviśeṣā [99]{*1/695*} avibhaktāḥ. ato dvādaśakapālasya stutyarthatvenāvayavastutir upapadyate. yathā śobhanam asya cakrasya nemitumbāram, śobhanam asyāḥ senāyā hastyaśvarathapādātam iti. tasmād upapannā stutir iti.
children.translated_text: When it is understood that [the passages about] eight-<s>kapāla</s> and so on are purposeless as exhortations, then by figurative usage, they will serve as praise of the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake], for the purpose of commending the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> sacrifice. For within the number twelve, the specific numbers such as eight and so on are present in an undifferentiated way. Therefore, as praise of the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] serving the purpose of laudation, the praise of its constituent parts is well-established. Just as [one says] 'beautiful is the rim, hub, and spokes of this wheel' [and] 'beautiful are the elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry of this army.' Therefore, the praise is well-established.

NOTES:
[Edition page references: E2: 2,310; E4: 2,171; E5: 2,252; E6: 1,68]

children.text: kāraṇaṃ syād iti cet // MS_1,4.21 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] there would be a [separate] cause — // MS 1,4.21 //

children.text: iti ced bhavān paśyaty arthavādā iti, kāraṇam aṣṭatvādīnāṃ brahmavarcasādi kasmān na bhavati. brahmavarcasakāmasyāṣṭākapālaḥ. evam uttareṣu yathākāmam. kim evaṃ bhaviṣyati. puroḍāśasya guṇavidhāne 'py ānarthakyaṃ na bhaviṣyati na ca lakṣaṇayā dvādaśakapālasya stutiḥ kalpitā bhaviṣyati. tasmāt kāmebhyo vidhayo baviṣyanti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that they are laudatory passages — why should the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmavarcas</s>) and the like not be the cause for [the numbers] eight and so on? [That is,] for one desiring the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, [let there be] an eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake]. Similarly for the subsequent ones, according to desire. What would [the consequence] be? Even if they are quality-injunctions of the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, there would be no purposelessness, and the figurative praise of the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] would not need to be postulated. Therefore, there would be injunctions according to the desires.

children.text: ānarthakyād akāraṇaṃ kartur hi kāraṇāni guṇārtho hi vidhīyate // MS_1,4.22 //
children.translated_text: Because of purposelessness, [the desires] are not causes; for causes belong to the agent, since what is enjoined serves a quality. // MS 1,4.22 //

children.text: yadi kāmāya vidhayaḥ, bhinnāni vākyāni bhaveyuḥ. ekaṃ cedaṃ vākyam, vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśa-kapālaṃ nirvapet putre jāta ity edamapakrāntaṃ yad dvādaśakapālo bhavati jagatyaivāsmin paśūn dadhāti yasmiñ jāta etām iṣṭiṃ nirvapati pūta eva sa tejasv yan nāda indriyāvī paśumān bhavatīty{*1/696*} evam antam. tasya madhye 'ṣṭatvādayaḥ śrūyamāṇā yadi na saṃbadhyeraṃs tato vākyāntarāṇi bhaveyuḥ. [100]{*1/697*} kartur hi kāraṇāni pūtatvādīni bhaveyuḥ. sa eṣa guṇārtho 'tra vidhīyate vaiśvānarayāge pūta eva ityevamādiḥ. tena caite 'ṣṭatvādayaḥ sākṣād dhetutvena saṃbadhyante yasmād gāyatryaivainaṃ brahmavarcasena punāti tena pūta eva saḥ, yasmāt trivṛtaivāsmiṃs tejo dadhāti tena tejasvī. yasmād virājaivāsminn annādyaṃ dadhāti tenānnādaḥ. yasmāt triṣṭubhaivāsminn indriyaṃ dadhāti tenendriyāvī. yasmāj jagaty aivāsmin paśūna dadhāti tena paśumān iti. tataḥ kāmāya vidhayo 'saṃbhavanto yady arthavādā api na bhaveyur ānarthakyam evaiṣāṃ syāt. tasmād akāraṇaṃ brahmavarcastvād yo 'ṣṭatvādīnām. tasmād aṣṭatvādayo 'rthavādā iti.
children.translated_text: If [there were separate] injunctions for [each] desire, the sentences would be separate. But this is a single sentence — 'One should offer a twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> when a son is born' — beginning from this and extending to: 'when it has twelve <s>kapālas</s>, it is by the <s>Jagatī</s> [meter] alone that it establishes livestock in him; in whom, when born, one offers this <s>iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice), he is purified, resplendent, a consumer of food, possessed of vigor, and possessed of livestock' — thus ending. Within that [single sentence], [the numbers] eight and so on, being heard, if they were not connected [to the whole], would form separate sentences. The causes — purity and the like — would belong to the agent. What is enjoined here as serving a quality in the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> sacrifice is: 'he is indeed purified' and so on. Therefore, these [numbers] eight and so on are directly connected as reasons: 'because by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone it purifies him with the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, therefore he is purified; because by the <s>Trivṛt</s> alone it places radiance in him, therefore he is resplendent; because by the <s>Virāj</s> alone it places food in him, therefore he is a consumer of food; because by the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> alone it places vigor in him, therefore he is possessed of vigor; because by the <s>Jagatī</s> alone it places livestock in him, therefore he is possessed of livestock.' Therefore, since injunctions according to desire are impossible, even if they are not laudatory passages either, they would simply be purposeless. Therefore, the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> and the like are not causes for [the numbers] eight and so on. Therefore, [the numbers] eight and so on are laudatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>).

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 2.2.5.3] | [Edition page references: E2: 2,312; E4: 2,178; E5: 2,253; E6: 1,68]

children.text: tatsiddhiḥ // MS_1,4.23 //
children.translated_text: This is thereby established. // MS 1,4.23 //

children.text:
yajamānaḥ prastaraḥ{*1/698*}; yajamāna ekakapāla ityādi{*1/699*} samāmnāyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ yajamānaḥ prastara ity eṣa guṇavidhiḥ, kim arthavāda iti. tathā yajamāna ekakapāla iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. guṇavidhir iti. kim evaṃ bhaviṣyati evam apūrvam arthaṃ vidhāsyati. itarathārthavādo 'narthakaḥ syāt. arthavattvaṃ ca nyāyyam. tasmād vidhiḥ.
naitad evam, yadi vidhiḥ syāt, tataḥ prastarakārye{*1/700*} yajamāno niyamyeta. yajamānakārye vā prastaraḥ. prastare juhūm āsādayati, sarvā vā sruva{*1/701*} iti yajamāne juhūr āsādyeta. sarvā vā sruva{*1/702*} iti. tathāsati{*1/703*} na yājamānaṃ śakyate kartum, dīkṣaṇato brahmayajamānāv āsāte karmaṇa kriyamāṇasya iti{*1/704*}. na ca prastaro yājamānaṃ śaknoti kartum. tathā yadi yajamāna ekakapālakārye viniyujyeta sarvahutaḥ kriyeta. tatra sarvatantraparilopaḥ [101]{*1/705*} syāt. na caikakapālo yājamānaṃ śaknoti kartum. tasmān na vidhiḥ. vidhyantaraṃ cāsti prastaram uttaraṃ barhiṣaḥ sādayati, ekakapālaṃ sarvahataṃ karoti, iti. tasmād api na vidhiḥ. kiṃ hi arthavādaḥ. yajamāno jñāyata eva prastara ekakapāla iti ca.
kathaṃ punar anayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ jñāyate. na hi prastara ekakapālo vā yajamānaḥ. na ca yajamāna ekasmin kapāle saṃskṛtaḥ puroḍāśaḥ prathamo vā kaśam ṣṭir lūnaḥ. kathaṃ paraśabdaḥ paratra vartate, kim arthaṃ vā jñāyamānasva saṃkīrtanam iti. ucyate - jñāyamānaḥ saṃkīrtyate stotum. prastara uttaro barhiṣaḥ sādayitavyo yajamānatvāt. tathā yajamāna ekakapālaḥ sarvahutaḥ kartavyaḥ svarga āhavanīyas tatra pratiṣṭhāpito bhavatīti.
kathaṃ paratra vartate paraśabda iti. guṇavādas tu. guṇād eṣa vādaḥ. katham aguṇavacano guṇaṃ brūyāt. svārthābhidhānaneti brūmaḥ. sarva evaite gauṇāḥ śabdā na svārthaṃ hitvā guṇeṣu vartante. prasiddhahānir hi tathā syād aprasiddhakalpanā ca. na ca sarve guṇasamudāyavacanāḥ. guṇahīne 'pi darśanāt. aprasahyakāry api hi kadācid rogeṇopahataḥ siṃhyāḥ putraḥ siṃha eva. samudāyavācī ca nāvayave pravartitum arhati. sarvasiṃhavyāktiṣu yat sāmānyaṃ tad vacanaḥ śabda iti sthito nyāyaḥ pratyuddhriyeta. na cāsati siṃho parikalpanayā pravarteta. kalpanāyā aśakyatvāt. kathaṃ nu svārthābhidhānena pratyayavyavastheti cet. arthasaṃbandhāt. siṃha iti nirjñāyate prasahyakāritā tatra prāyeṇeti prasahyakārīti gamyate, arthaṃ pratyayasāmarthyāt. yo hi manyate prasahyakāriṇaṃ pratyāyayeyam iti sa yadi siṃhaśabdam uccārayati sidhyaty asyābhipretam. siṃhārthaḥ pratītaḥ prasahya[102]{*1/706*}kārīti saṃbandhād itaram arthaṃ pratyāyayati. evaṃ svārthābhidhānena tadguṇasaṃbandhaḥ pratīyate. iha tu yajamānaḥ prastaraḥ yajamāna ekakapāla iti kīdṛśo guṇa saṃbandhaḥ pratīyate. tatsiddhikara iti. sarvo hy ātmanah kāryasiddhiṃ karoti. anyo 'pi yas tasya kāryasiddhiṃ karoti sa tasminn uccarite hṛdayam āgacchati. yathā rājā pattigaṇaka iti. pattigaṇako rājñaḥ kāryaṃ sādhayati. sa rājaśabda uccarite pratīyate. evam ihāpi yajamānakāryaṃ prastaraikakapālau sādhayataḥ, tau yajamāne pratīte pratīyete. tasmāt tau yajamānaśabdena pratyāyete. kathaṃ? stutau syātāṃ barhiṣa uparisādane sarvahome ceti. tasmād evaṃjātīyakā arthavādā na vidhaya iti.
children.translated_text:
It is taught: 'The sacrificer is the <s>prastara</s> (grass bundle)'; 'The sacrificer is the single-potsherd [cake],' and so on. Here there is doubt: Is 'the sacrificer is the <s>prastara</s>' a qualifying injunction (<s>guṇavidhi</s>), or is it an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage)? Similarly, 'the sacrificer is the single-potsherd [cake].' What is the prima facie view? It is a qualifying injunction. What will result from this? It will thus enjoin an unprecedented meaning. Otherwise, as an <s>arthavāda</s>, it would be purposeless. And meaningfulness is the proper [inference]. Therefore, it is an injunction.
This is not so. If it were an injunction, then the sacrificer would be restricted to the function of the <s>prastara</s>, or the <s>prastara</s> to the function of the sacrificer. 'He places the <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) on the <s>prastara</s>, or all [ladles] on the <s>sruva</s> (spoon)' — [if so,] the <s>juhū</s> would have to be placed on the sacrificer, or all on the <s>sruva</s>. In that case, the sacrificer's [ritual] role could not be performed — 'From the consecration onward, the <s>brahman</s> and the sacrificer sit while the ritual is being performed.' Nor can the <s>prastara</s> perform the sacrificer's role. Similarly, if the sacrificer were employed in the function of the single-potsherd [cake], it would become a <s>sarvahuta</s> (completely offered oblation). In that case, there would be a loss of the entire ritual system. Nor can the single-potsherd [cake] perform the sacrificer's role. Therefore, it is not an injunction. And there is another injunction — 'He places the <s>prastara</s> on top of the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass)'; 'He makes the single-potsherd [cake] a <s>sarvahuta</s>.' For this reason too, it is not an injunction. What then? It is an <s>arthavāda</s>. The sacrificer is known [in connection with] the <s>prastara</s> and the single-potsherd [cake].
But how is the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of these two understood? For the <s>prastara</s> or the single-potsherd [cake] is not the sacrificer. Nor is the sacrificer a <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake) prepared on one potsherd, nor the first bunch of <s>kuśa</s>-grass that is cut. How does the word for one thing apply to another, and why is there a mention of what is [already] known? It is replied: What is [already] known is mentioned for the purpose of praise. The <s>prastara</s> should be placed on top of the <s>barhis</s> because of its being [like] the sacrificer. Similarly, the sacrificer's single-potsherd [cake] should be made a <s>sarvahuta</s> — 'heaven is the <s>āhavanīya</s> (fire), it is established therein.'
How does the word for one thing apply to another? 'But [it is] figurative speech.' This speech is based on a quality (<s>guṇa</s>). How can a word that does not denote a quality express a quality? Through the expression of its own meaning, we say. All these figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) words do not abandon their own meaning to apply to [mere] qualities. For that would entail the abandonment of the well-known and the postulation of the unknown. Nor are all [such words] expressions of the totality of qualities. For [the word is used] even when the quality is absent — even one who does not act with force, when afflicted by disease, if he is the son of a lioness, is still a lion. And a word denoting an aggregate should not apply to a [single] component. The established principle — that the word designates the universal that is common to all individual lions — would be overturned. And in the absence [of a lion], the word would not apply through mere postulation, because postulation is impossible [without basis]. If one asks: 'How then is the semantic determination [made] through the expression of one's own meaning?' — [we reply:] through connection with the meaning. [The word] 'lion' is understood [to mean] 'one who acts with force' — 'such is generally [the case]' — and so 'one who acts with force' is understood, through the power of the contextual understanding. For one who thinks 'I shall make him understand [that this person] acts with force' — if he utters the word 'lion,' his intention is accomplished. The meaning 'lion' is understood; through the connection [between lion and force], it conveys the other meaning. Thus, through the expression of its own meaning, the connection with its quality is understood. But here, 'the sacrificer is the <s>prastara</s>' and 'the sacrificer is the single-potsherd [cake]' — what kind of quality-connection is understood? [The connection is:] 'that which accomplishes its purpose.' For everyone accomplishes the fulfillment of his own purpose. And whoever else accomplishes his purpose — that [person] comes to mind when [the former] is mentioned. Just as [one says] 'the king is the infantry-commander' — the infantry-commander accomplishes the king's purpose. He is understood when the word 'king' is uttered. Similarly here, the <s>prastara</s> and the single-potsherd [cake] accomplish the sacrificer's purpose; when the sacrificer is understood, they are understood. Therefore, they are conveyed by the word 'sacrificer.' How? They serve the purpose of praise in the placing on top of the <s>barhis</s> and in the <s>sarvahuta</s> offering. Therefore, <s>arthavādas</s> of this kind are not injunctions.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {1/698: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.5} {1/699: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.6.3.4} {1/700-706: Various edition cross-references and variant readings}]
Birth-class (<s>jāti</s>). // MS 1.4.24 //

children.text: āgneyo vai brāhmaṇaḥ{*1/707*}; aindro rājanyaḥ{*1/708*}; vaiśyo vaiśvadeva ityevamādayaḥ{*1/709*} śrūyante. tatra guṇavidhayaḥ ārthavādā iti saṃdehaḥ. guṇavidhaya iti brūmaḥ. evam apūrvam arthaṃ vidhāsyanti, itarathārthavādāḥ santo 'narthakāḥ syuḥ. na vidhir vidhyantarasya bhāvāt. tasmāt saṃvādaḥ. tasya saṃkīrtanaṃ vidhistutyartham. anāgneyādiṣv āgneyādiśabdāḥ kena prakāreṇa. guṇavādena. ko guṇavādaḥ. agnisaṃbandhaḥ. katham? ekajātīyakatvāt. kim ekajātīyakatvam. prajāpatir akāmayata, prajāḥ sṛjeyam iti. sa mukhatas trivṛtaṃ nirabhimīta, tam agnir devatānvasṛjyata, gāyatrī chandaḥ, rathantaraṃ sāma, brāhmaṇo manuṣyāṇām ajaḥ paśūnām. tasmāt te mukhyāḥ, mukhato hy asṛjyanta. uraso [103]{*1/710*} bāhubhyāṃ pañcadaśaṃ nirmimīta, tam indro devatānasṛjyata, triṣṭup chandaḥ, bṛhat sāma, rājanyo manuṣyāṇām, aviḥ paśūnām. tasmāt te vīryavantaḥ, vīryād dhi asṛjyanta. ūrubhyāṃ madhyataḥ saptadaśaṃ niramimīta, taṃ viśvedevā devatā anvasṛjyanta, jagatī chandaḥ, vairūpaṃ sāma, vaiśyo manuṣyāṇām, gāvaḥ paśūnām{*1/711*}. evam ukte saty ekasminn evaṃjātīyake vijñāte 'nyo 'pi tajjātīyako hṛdayam āgacchati. tasmād arthavādaśabdāḥ{*1/712*}.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> belongs to <s>Agni</s>'; 'The <s>Kṣatriya</s> belongs to <s>Indra</s>'; 'The <s>Vaiśya</s> belongs to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>,' and so on. Here there is doubt whether these are qualifying injunctions or <s>arthavādas</s>. We say: they are qualifying injunctions. Thus they will enjoin an unprecedented meaning; otherwise, being <s>arthavādas</s>, they would be purposeless. [Reply:] They are not injunctions, because of the existence of another injunction. Therefore, [they express] agreement (<s>saṃvāda</s>). Their mention serves the purpose of praising an injunction. How do the words '<s>āgneya</s>' (belonging to <s>Agni</s>) and the like apply to those who do not [actually] belong to <s>Agni</s> and the like? Through figurative speech (<s>guṇavāda</s>). What is the figurative usage? The connection with <s>Agni</s>. How? Because of being of the same class (<s>ekajātīyaka</s>). What does 'being of the same class' mean? <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I create progeny.' From his mouth he fashioned the <s>trivṛt</s> (threefold <s>Stoma</s>); <s>Agni</s> as deity followed it; <s>Gāyatrī</s> as meter; <s>Rathantara</s> as <s>Sāman</s>; the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> among humans; the goat among animals. Therefore, they are foremost, for they were created from the mouth. From his chest and arms he fashioned the <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold <s>Stoma</s>); <s>Indra</s> as deity followed it; <s>Triṣṭubh</s> as meter; <s>Bṛhat</s> as <s>Sāman</s>; the <s>Kṣatriya</s> among humans; the sheep among animals. Therefore, they are powerful, for they were created from power. From his thighs and middle he fashioned the <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeenfold <s>Stoma</s>); the <s>Viśvedevas</s> as deities followed it; <s>Jagatī</s> as meter; <s>Vairūpa</s> as <s>Sāman</s>; the <s>Vaiśya</s> among humans; cattle among animals. When this is stated, when one of this kind is known, another of the same kind comes to mind. Therefore, [these are] <s>arthavāda</s>-words.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {1/707: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 2.7.3.1} {1/708: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.4.13} {1/709: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 2.7.2.2} {1/710: Edition cross-references} {1/711: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 7.1.1.4-5, cf. <s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.90} {1/712: E1,6 read <s>arthavādaśabdāḥ</s>; E2,4,5 read <s>arthavādāḥ</s>}]

children.text: sārūpyam // MS_1,4.25 //
children.translated_text: Formal similarity (<s>sārūpya</s>). // MS 1.4.25 //

children.text: yajamāno yūpaḥ; āditye yūpa ityādi{*1/713*} śrūyate. tatra guṇavidhiḥ, arthavādaḥ, iti saṃdehaḥ. arthavattvād guṇavidhi. aśakyatvād yūpakāryasādhane yajamānasya, yajamānakāryasādhane vā yūpasya vidhyantarabhāvāc ca na vidhiḥ. vidhistutyarthaṃ saṃvādaḥ. guṇavādāt sāmānādhikaraṇyam. ko guṇaḥ? sārūpyam. kiṃ sārūpyam? ūrdhvatā tejasvitā ca. tasmād evaṃjātīyakā arthavādāḥ.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'The sacrificer is the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>)'; 'The sun is in the sacrificial post,' and so on. Here there is doubt whether it is a qualifying injunction or an <s>arthavāda</s>. Because of meaningfulness, it would be a qualifying injunction. [Reply:] Because of the impossibility of the sacrificer accomplishing the function of the <s>yūpa</s>, or the <s>yūpa</s> accomplishing the function of the sacrificer, and because of the existence of another injunction, it is not an injunction. The agreement (<s>saṃvāda</s>) serves the purpose of praising the injunction. The co-referentiality is through figurative speech (<s>guṇavāda</s>). What is the quality? Formal similarity (<s>sārūpya</s>). What is the formal similarity? Uprightness and brilliance. Therefore, <s>arthavādas</s> of this kind [are praise].

NOTES:

children.text: praśaṃsā // MS_1,4.26 //
children.translated_text: Praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>). // MS 1.4.26 //

children.text: apaśavo vā anye go 'śvebhyaḥ, paśavo go 'śvāḥ{*1/714*}. ayajño vā eṣa yo 'sāmā{*1/715*}. asatraṃ vā etad yad achandomam iti{*1/716*} śrūyate. tatra vidhyartha vādasaṃdehe, arthavattvād vidhaya iti prāpte. abhidhīyate - yadi vidhayo bhaveyuḥ, go 'śvā eva paśavaḥ syuḥ, sāmavān eva yajñaḥ, chandomavad eva satram. anyeṣāṃ paśūnām, yajñānām, [104]{*1/717*} satrāṇāṃ cotpattir anarthikā syāt. vidhyantaraṃ ca nāvakalpeta. ataḥ stutyarthaṃ saṃvādaḥ. go 'śvān praśaṃsitum anyeṣāṃ paśūnāṃ nindā. sāmavataḥ praśaṃsitum asāmnāṃ nindā. chandomavanti praśaṃsitum acchandomakāni nidyante. yathā - yad aghṛtam, abhojanaṃ tat. yan malinam, avāsas tad iti.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'Those other than cows and horses are not [true] animals; cows and horses [alone] are animals'; 'That is indeed no sacrifice which is without a <s>Sāman</s>'; 'That is indeed no <s>sattra</s> (soma session) which is without a <s>chandoma</s> (metrical <s>Stoma</s>).' When the doubt arises whether these are injunctions or [laudatory] statements, and when the prima facie view is that they are injunctions because of meaningfulness — it is said: If they were injunctions, then only cows and horses would be animals; only a [rite] with a <s>Sāman</s> would be a sacrifice; only [a session] with a <s>chandoma</s> would be a <s>sattra</s>. The origination of other animals, sacrifices, and <s>sattras</s> would be purposeless. And no other injunction would be possible. Therefore, the agreement (<s>saṃvāda</s>) serves the purpose of praise. The censure of other animals serves to praise cows and horses. The censure of those without <s>Sāman</s> serves to praise those with <s>Sāman</s>. Those without <s>chandoma</s> are censured to praise those with <s>chandoma</s>. Just as [one says]: 'What is without ghee is not food; what is dirty is not clothing.'

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {1/714: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.2.9.4} {1/715: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 1.5.7.1} {1/716: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 7.3.8.1} {1/717: Edition cross-references}]
Preponderance (<s>bhūmā</s>). // MS 1.4.27 //

children.text: sṛṣṭīr upadadhātīti{*1/718*} śrūyate. tatra guṇavidhir arthavāda iti saṃdehe apūrvatvād vidhir iti prāpte. ucyate - yadi vidhiḥ, sṛṣṭimantrakā upadadhātīṣṭakā ity arthaḥ. tatra neṣṭakānāṃ viśeṣaḥ kaścid āśrīyate, evaṃrūpāḥ sṛṣṭimantrakā naivaṃrūpā iti. tatra sarvāsāṃ sṛṣṭiliṅgā mantrāḥ prāpnuyuḥ. anyeṣām asaṃyuktānāṃ mantrāṇām ānarthakyaṃ syāt. tasmād anuvādo mantrasamāmnānāt prāptānām upadhāne mantrāṇām. sṛṣṭīnāṃ saṃkīrtanaṃ{*1/719*} sarjanārthavādārtham. api ca vidhitve lakṣaṇā, ekayā stuvata ity{*1/720*} atra yā asṛṣṭayas tā lakṣayet. nanv anuvāde 'pi lakṣaṇā{*1/721*}. nānuvādapakṣe lakṣaṇāyāṃ doṣaḥ. kathaṃ tv asṛṣṭiṣu sṛṣṭiṣu ca sṛṣṭiśabda iti. bhūmnā. bahavas tatra sṛṣṭiliṅgā mantrāḥ, alpaśo viliṅgā iti.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'He places the <s>sṛṣṭi</s>-[bricks].' Here, when there is doubt whether it is a qualifying injunction or an <s>arthavāda</s>, and when it is prima facie concluded that it is an injunction because of its unprecedented nature, it is said: If it were an injunction, the meaning would be 'he places bricks accompanied by <s>sṛṣṭi</s>-mantras.' In that case, no distinction among the bricks would be relied upon — [such as] 'those of this form [are accompanied by] <s>sṛṣṭi</s>-mantras, not those of that form.' In that case, <s>sṛṣṭi</s>-indicative <s>mantras</s> would apply to all [bricks]. The other, non-connected <s>mantras</s> would be purposeless. Therefore, it is a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of the <s>mantras</s> already established for the placing through the teaching of <s>mantras</s>. The mention of <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) serves the purpose of <s>arthavāda</s> about creation. Moreover, if it were an injunction, there would be [the need for] identification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — 'praise with one [mantra]' — here, those which are not <s>sṛṣṭi</s>-[mantras] would have to be identified [as such]. But surely, even in the re-statement view, there is identification. [Reply:] In the re-statement view, there is no defect in identification. But how can the word <s>sṛṣṭi</s> apply to both non-creation [mantras] and creation [mantras]? Through preponderance (<s>bhūmā</s>). Many of those [mantras] have creation-indicative content; a few have different indicative content.

liṅgasamavāyaḥ // MS_1,4.28 //{*1/723*}
prāṇabhṛta upadadhāti{*1/724*}; ājyānīr upadadhātīti{*1/725*} vidhitve prāṇabhṛn mantrakāsūpadhīyamānāsu viliṅgānāṃ mantrāṇām ānarthakyam/ tasmād anuvādaḥ/ liṅgasamavāyāt paraśabdaḥ paratra vartate. yathā - chatriṇo gacchantīty, ekena chatriṇā sarve lakṣyante. na cāyaṃ prāṇabhṛc chaśabdaḥ sṛṣṭiśabdaś ca jahatsvārthaṃ mantragaṇaṃ lakṣayet. yad gaṇe ca sṛṣṭiprāṇabhṛc chabdau samavetau, tāv api parigṛhyete. yathā - chatriśabdena svārthalakṣaṇārthena so 'pi chatrī gṛhyata iti.
children.translated_text:
Co-occurrence of indicatory signs (<s>liṅgasamavāya</s>). // MS 1.4.28 //
It is heard: 'He places the <s>prāṇabhṛt</s> (life-sustaining) [bricks]'; 'He places the <s>ājyānī</s> (ghee-related) [bricks].' If [they were] injunctions, when [bricks] are being placed with <s>prāṇabhṛt</s>-mantras, the <s>mantras</s> with different indicatory content would be purposeless. Therefore, it is a re-statement. The word for one thing applies to another because of the co-occurrence of indicatory signs (<s>liṅgasamavāya</s>). Just as [one says] 'those with umbrellas are going' — by one who has an umbrella, all are designated. And this <s>prāṇabhṛt</s>-word and <s>sṛṣṭi</s>-word do not, abandoning their own meaning, designate the <s>mantra</s>-group. Rather, those in the group that have the co-occurrence of the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> and <s>prāṇabhṛt</s> words are also included. Just as — by the word 'umbrella-bearer,' which expresses its own meaning through secondary designation, that very umbrella-bearer is included.

children.text: saṃdigdheṣu vākyaśeṣāt // MS_1,4.29 //
children.translated_text: In doubtful cases, [the determination is] from the syntactic complement. // MS 1.4.29 //

children.text:
aktāḥ śarkarā upadadhāti{*1/726*}; tejo vai ghṛtam iti{*1/727*} śrūyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ ghṛtatailavasānām anyatamena dravyeṇāñjanīyāḥ śarkarā uta ghṛtenaiveti. kathaṃ saṃdehaḥ. añjanasāmānyena vākyasyopakramo ghṛtena viśeṣeṇa nigamanam. yathopakramaṃ nigamayitavyam ekasmin vākye. tatra yad vā sāmānyam ādau viśeṣopalakṣaṇārthaṃ vivakṣyate. yad vā nigamane viśeṣaḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇārthaḥ. tadārambhanigamanayoḥ kiṃ samañjasam iti saṃśayaḥ. evaṃ saṃdigdheṣūpakrame sāmānyavacane virodhābhāvān na viśeṣaḥ parikalpyaḥ. nigamane tūpajātaḥ sāmānyapratyaya iti virodhāl lakṣaṇārthaṃ ghṛtavacanam. yathā sṛṣṭiṣv asṛṣṭiṣu ca sṛṣṭiśabdaḥ, evaṃ ghṛtam aghṛtaṃ ca ghṛtam ity ucyate.
[106]{*1/728*} saṃdigdheṣv evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sāmānyavacanena viśeṣāpekṣiṇopakramo vākyasya viśeṣe nigamanavaśena. kutaḥ? na hi sāmānyaṃ vihitam. yena virodho nigamanasya. katham avihitam. saṃdigdheṣu vidhānaśabdābhāvāt. na hi vidhānaśabdo 'sti. aktāḥ śarkarā upadadhātīti vartamānakālanirdeśāt. nāpi sāmānyasya sākṣāt stutiḥ, pratyakṣaṃ tu ghṛtasya stavanam. śrutyā ghṛtasya stutiḥ, lakṣaṇayā sāmānyasya. śrutiś ca lakṣaṇāyā jyāyasī. tasmād ghṛtavidhānam. evam vāsaḥ paridhatte, etad vai sarvadevatyaṃ vāso yat kṣaumam iti tathā imāṃ spṛṣṭvodnāyet, imāṃ hy audumbarīṃ viśvābhūtāny upajīvanīti.
children.translated_text:
'He places down anointed pebbles' — 'splendor indeed is ghee' — thus it is heard. There arises a doubt: should the pebbles be anointed with any one of the substances ghee, oil, or fat, or with ghee alone? How does the doubt arise? The sentence begins with the general [term] 'anointing' and concludes with the specific [term] 'ghee.' In a single sentence, the conclusion should follow the beginning. There, either the general [term] at the beginning is intended to indicate the specific, or the specific at the conclusion is intended in the sense of the general. The doubt is: which is consistent — the beginning or the conclusion? Thus, when the beginning is doubtful and states the general, since there is no contradiction, no specific [meaning] should be imposed. But at the conclusion, where a cognition of the general has [already] arisen, because of contradiction, the mention of 'ghee' is used in a secondary sense (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). Just as the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' (creation/release) [is used] for both things released and things not released, so too both ghee and non-ghee are called 'ghee.'
When the doubt arises thus, we say: The beginning of the sentence, whose general statement requires a specific [determination], is [governed] by the specific, in accordance with the conclusion. Why? Because the general [anointing] has not been enjoined — hence there is no contradiction with the conclusion. How is it not enjoined? Because in the doubtful [cases] there is no injunctive word. For there is no injunctive word — 'he places down anointed pebbles' uses the present tense [descriptive, not injunctive]. Nor is there a direct praise of the general; but there is a manifest praising of ghee. By primary meaning (<s>śruti</s>), the praise is of ghee; by secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), of the general. And primary meaning is stronger than secondary signification. Therefore, [the injunction is for] ghee specifically. Similarly, 'he puts on a garment — this garment which is of linen is indeed sacred to all gods.' And likewise, 'having touched this [staff], he should raise it up — for this <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood staff), all beings depend upon it.'
[TEXTUAL NOTES: Source reference Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa 3.12.5.12 for both citations; edition page numbers — E2: 2,328; E4: 2,238; E5: 2,268; E6: 1,72.]

children.text: arthād vā kalpanaikadeśatvāt // MS_1,4.30 //
children.translated_text: Or [the determination may be made] from the purpose, because of being one part of the construal. // MS 1.4.30 //

children.text:
sruveṇāvadyati; svadhitināvadyati; hastenāvadyatīti{*1/729*} śrūyate tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ sruveṇāvadātavyaṃ sarvasya dravasya saṃhatasya māṃsasya ca tathā svadhitinā, hastena ca, uta sarveṣām arthato vyavasthā dravāṇāṃ sruveṇa, māṃsānāṃ svadhitinā, sahatānāṃ hasteneti. aviśeṣābhidhānād avyavastheti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - arthād vā kalpanā, sāmarthyāt kalpaneti. sruveṇāvadyed yathā śaknuyāt. tathā yasya śaknuyā. tasya ceti, ākhyātaśabdānām arthaṃ bruvatāṃ śaktiḥ sahakāriṇī, [107]{*1/730*} eva ced yathāśakti vyavasthā bhavitum arhati. tathā - añjalinā saktūn pradāvye juhotīti{*1/731*}. dvihastasaṃyogo 'ñjaliḥ, sa vyākośo 'rthāt kartavyaḥ. tathā hi śakyate homo nirvartayitum. tad yathā - kaṭe bhuṅkte kāṃsyapātryāṃ bhuṅkta ity{*1/732*} arthāt kalpyate - kaṭe samāsīnaḥ kāṃsyapātryāmodanaṃ nidhāya bhuṅkta iti.
children.translated_text:
'He cuts off with a ladle'; 'he cuts off with an axe'; 'he cuts off with the hand' — thus it is heard. There arises a doubt: should one cut off with the ladle all [types of offerings] — liquid, solid, and meat — and likewise with the axe and the hand? Or should there be a contextual determination: liquids with the ladle, meat with the axe, and solid [offerings] with the hand? Because of the absence of a specific statement, [the prima facie view is that] there is no determination.
When the doubt arises thus, we say: Or the construal [is made] from the purpose — that is, from capacity, the construal [follows]. 'He should cut off with a ladle' — as one is able. And likewise for whichever [substance] one is able [to cut with that instrument]. And [this follows] because the capacity of the instruments is a cooperating factor for the action-words that express the meaning. Therefore, if [the determination is made] according to capacity, a determination can indeed be made. Similarly — 'he offers <s>saktus</s> (barley meal) poured into cupped hands' — the cupped hands (<s>añjali</s>) is the joining of two hands; it must be opened in accordance with the purpose. For thus the <s>homa</s> can be accomplished. Just as — 'he eats on a mat, he eats from a bronze vessel' — it is understood from the context that 'seated on a mat, having placed food in a bronze vessel, he eats.'
