children.text: Adhyāya 2:
children.translated_text: <s>Adhyāya</s> 2:

children.text: bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdās tebhyaḥ kriyā pratīyetaiṣa hy artho vidhīyate // MS_2,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Action-words have 'bringing into being' (<s>bhāva</s>) as their meaning; from them, the ritual activity is understood; for this is the purpose that is enjoined. // MS 2.1.1 //

children.text:
prathame 'dhyāye pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ vṛttam, tatra vidhyarthavādamantrasmṛtayas tattvato nirṇītāḥ, guṇavidhir nāmadheyaṃ ca parīkṣitam, sandigdhānām arthānāṃ vākyaśeṣād arthādhyavasānam uktam. tan na prasmartavyam. anantaraṃ pradhānāpradhānāni{*2/1*} parīkṣiṣyante, bhinnāny abhinnāni ceti, eṣa evārtho varṇanīyo nānyaḥ, eṣa eva cādhyāyasaṃbandhaḥ. tad iha ṣaḍvidhaḥ karmabhedo vakṣyate - śabdāntaram, abhyāsaḥ, saṃkhyā, guṇaḥ, prakriyā, nāmadheyam iti vakṣyamānam anusaṃkīrtyate. pradarśitam ucyamānaṃ sukhaṃ grāhayiṣyata iti śrotuś ca buddhiḥ samādhīyate, tad etan nānākarmalakṣaṇam ity adhyāyam ācakṣate, etat tātparyeṇa, ato 'nyad upodghātaprasaktānuprasaktaṃ{*2/2*} ceti.
tatra prathamaṃ tāvad idaṃ cintyate - prathame 'dhyāya idam uktam - codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharma iti {*2/3*}, codanā ca kriyāyā abhidhāyakaṃ vākyam, vākye ca padānām arthāḥ, tatra kiṃ padena padena dharma ucyate{*2/4*}, uta sarvair eka eveti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? prati padaṃ dharma iti.
evaṃ prāpta ucyate - yadaikasmād apūrvam, tadānyat tadarthaṃ [109]{*2/5*} bhaviṣyati, evam alpīyasy adṛṣṭānumānaprasaṇgakalpanā bhaviṣyati. tasmād ekam apūrvam.
yadaikam, tadā sandehaḥ - kim, bhāvaśabdebhyaḥ, uta dravyaguṇaśabdebhya iti?. kaḥ punar bhāvaḥ? ke te punar bhāvaśabdā iti? yajati dadāti juhotītyevamādayaḥ. nanu yāgadānahomaśabdā ete, na bhāvaśabdāḥ. naitad evam. yāgādiśabdāś caite bhāvaśabdāś ca, yajyādyarthaś cāto 'vagamyate, bhāvayed iti ca. tathā yateta, yathā kiṃcid bhavatīti. tenaite bhāvaśabdāḥ, dravyaguṇaśabdebhyo dravyaguṇapratyayo na bhāvanāyāḥ. atas te na bhāvaśabdā iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? aviśeṣeṇeti.
tata ucyate - bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdāḥ, tebhyaḥ kriyā pratīyeta, yajetetyevamādibhyaḥ. kutaḥ? bhāvārthatvād eva. ya āhuḥ - kim api bhāvayed iti, te svargakāmapadasaṃbandhāt svargaṃ bhāvayed iti brūyuḥ. tasmāt tebhyaḥ kriyā pratīyeta, phalasya kriyā karaṇaṃ niṣpattir iti. te ca yāgadānahomasaṃbaddhāḥ svargasyotpattiṃ vadanti. kutaḥ? eṣa hy artho vidhīyate, yathā - yāgādinā svargakāmaḥ kena bhāvayet svargam? yāgādineti. yasya ca śabdasyārthena phalaṃ sādhyate, tenāpūrvaṃ kṛtvā, nānyatheti, tato 'pūrvaṃ gamyate, ato yaḥ tasya vācakaḥ śabdaḥ, tato 'pūrvaṃ pratīyata iti. tena bhāvaśabdā apūrvasya codakā iti brūmaḥ. na tu kaścic chabdaḥ sākṣād apūrvasya vācako 'sti. bhāvārthaiḥ kim api bhāvayitavyam, svargakāmasya ca kenāpi bhāvyateti, tayor naṣṭāśvadagdha-rathavat saṃprayogaḥ, yajetetyevamādayaḥ sākāṅkṣāḥ, yajeta kiṃ kena katham iti. svargakāma ity anena prayojanena nirākāṅkṣāḥ. naivaṃ dravyaguṇaśabdāḥ. tasmād bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdā apūrvaṃ codayantīti. atha kasmād ubhayaṃ [110]{*2/6*} sūtritam{*2/7*} - bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdā iti. ucyate - bhavanti kecit karmaśabdā na bhāvārthāḥ, yathā śyenaikatrikādayaḥ{*2/8*}. kecid bhāvārthā na karmaśabdāḥ, yathā bhavanaṃ bhāvo bhūtir iti. kiṃ punar ihodāharaṇam? śyenenābhicaran yajeta{*2/9*}, citrayā yajeta paśukāma iti{*2/10*}. kiṃ śyenenābhicarann uta yajetābhicarann iti? tathā citrayā paśukāmaḥ, uta paśukāmo yajeteti sthite etasminn adhikaraṇe guṇavidhiḥ, nāmadheyam iti vicāro bhaviṣyati. tathā darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeteti, darśaḥ kālaḥ, pūrṇamāsa iti ca, kiṃ tābhyāṃ svargakāmaḥ, uta svargakāmo yajeteti, darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iti ca śyeneneti ca citrayeti ca naite bhāvavacanāḥ. na ca eṣām arthinā kaścit saṃbandho 'sti, vivibhaktikatvāt. tasmān na dravyaguṇaśabdā apūrvasya vidhāyakā iti.
children.translated_text:
In the first <s>adhyāya</s>, the characterization of the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) was completed; therein, injunctions, laudatory passages, <s>mantras</s>, and tradition (<s>smṛti</s>) were truly determined; the qualificatory injunction and the sacrifice-name were examined; and the ascertainment of doubtful matters through syntactic connection (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>) was stated. That should not be forgotten. Next, the primary and subsidiary [elements] will be examined, as well as the different and non-different [sacrifices] — this alone is the topic to be discussed, no other, and this is the connection of the <s>adhyāya</s>. Here, a sixfold classification of ritual actions will be stated — a different word, repetition, number, quality, procedure, and name — what is to be stated is recapitulated. [For] what has been previewed will be easily grasped when stated [in detail], and the mind of the listener is thus composed. They call this [the chapter on] the defining characteristics of different ritual actions; this is its essential purport, and other matters are incidentally connected with the main theme.
Therein, first this is to be considered: In the first <s>adhyāya</s> it was stated — 'The purpose (<s>artha</s>) characterized by Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is <s>Dharma</s>' — and an injunction is a sentence that denotes an action; and in a sentence there are the meanings of words. The question is: does each word [individually] state <s>Dharma</s>, or do all [words together] state a single [<s>Dharma</s>]? What is the prima facie view? That each word [states a] <s>Dharma</s>.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, it is said: When the unseen result (<s>apūrva</s>) [arises] from a single [source], then other [words] will serve that purpose — thus there will be less recourse to inferring unseen [entities], like [the principle of] the lost horse and the burnt chariot. Therefore, the <s>apūrva</s> is one.
If one, then a doubt [arises]: is it [understood] from action-words (<s>bhāva-śabda</s>) or from substance-and-quality-words (<s>dravya-guṇa-śabda</s>)? What then is <s>bhāva</s> (being/becoming)? And which are the action-words? Words such as 'he sacrifices' (<s>yajati</s>), 'he gives' (<s>dadāti</s>), 'he offers' (<s>juhoti</s>), and the like. [Objection:] But these are words for sacrifice, gift, and oblation, not action-words. [Reply:] This is not so. These are both sacrifice-words and action-words; from them, the meaning of sacrifice and the like is understood, as well as 'one should bring into being.' Likewise, 'one should strive' [means] 'so that something comes into being.' Therefore, these are action-words. From substance-and-quality-words, the cognition of substance and quality [arises], not of 'bringing into being.' Therefore, those are not action-words. What is the prima facie view? That there is no distinction [between the two types].
Then it is said: Action-words have 'bringing into being' as their meaning; from them — from words such as 'he should sacrifice' and the like — the ritual activity is understood. Why? Precisely because of their having 'bringing into being' as their meaning. Those who say 'one should bring something into being' — they, because of the syntactic connection with the word 'one who desires heaven,' would say 'one should bring heaven into being.' Therefore, from them the ritual activity is understood — the ritual activity is the means, the instrument for the accomplishment of the fruit. And these, being connected with sacrifice, gift, and oblation, state the production of heaven. Why? Because this is the purpose that is enjoined — as in: 'By what should one who desires heaven bring heaven into being? By sacrifice and the like.' And the word whose meaning accomplishes the fruit — through that [word] alone the <s>apūrva</s> is produced, not otherwise — from that the <s>apūrva</s> is understood. Therefore, whatever word expresses that [meaning], from that the <s>apūrva</s> is understood. Hence we say: Action-words are the enjoiners of the <s>apūrva</s>. But there is no word that directly denotes the <s>apūrva</s>. 'Something must be brought into being' by action-words, and 'something must be accomplished' by one who desires heaven — the connection of these two is like that of the man whose horse is lost and whose chariot is burnt [each needing the other]. Words such as 'he should sacrifice' have syntactic expectancy — 'what should one sacrifice, with what, how?' The word 'one who desires heaven' [supplies] the purpose and removes the expectancy. Substance-and-quality-words are not like this. Therefore, action-words, having 'bringing into being' as their meaning, enjoin the <s>apūrva</s>. Now, why are both stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — 'action-words have bringing-into-being as their meaning'? It is said: Some action-words do not have 'bringing into being' as their meaning — such as <s>Śyena</s>, <s>Ekatrika</s>, and the like [which are sacrifice-names]. Some have 'bringing into being' as their meaning but are not action-words — such as <s>bhavana</s> (coming-into-being), <s>bhāva</s> (being), <s>bhūti</s> (prosperity). What then is the example here? 'One who practices sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Śyena</s>'; 'one who desires cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Citrā</s>.' [The question is:] Is it 'one who practices sorcery with the <s>Śyena</s>' or 'one who practices sorcery should sacrifice'? Similarly, 'with the <s>Citrā</s> one who desires cattle' or 'one who desires cattle should sacrifice'? — in this [topic], the discussion will arise as to whether [it is] a qualificatory injunction or a name. Likewise, 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-and-full-moon sacrifices)' — <s>Darśa</s> is a time [new moon], <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> likewise — [the question is:] is it 'with those two, one who desires heaven' or 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice'? And 'with <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>,' '<s>Śyena</s>,' and '<s>Citrā</s>' — these are not action-denoting words. And they have no connection with the desirer [of the fruit], because of being in an oblique case. Therefore, substance-and-quality-words are not enjoiners of the <s>apūrva</s>.

[TEXTUAL NOTES: E2 reads <s>pradhānāpradhānādi</s>; E2,4 read <s>upoddhātaprasaktānuprasakta</s>; cf. MS 1.1.2; E2,4,6 omit <s>ucyate</s>; edition page numbers across editions; E4 reads <s>sūcitaṃ</s>; <s>Jhā</s> conjectures <s>śyenacitrādayaḥ</s>; source references Ṣaḍviṃśa-brāhmaṇa 3.8.1 and Taittirīya-saṃhitā 2.4.6.1.]

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvo 'rtha iti cet // MS_2,1.2 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Because 'bringing into being' is the meaning of all [words]. // MS 2.1.2 //

children.text: evaṃ ced bhāvan paśyati, abhāvaśabdatvān na dravyaguṇaśabdā apūrvasya vidhāyakā iti, sarveṣāṃ bhāvo 'rthaḥ, svargakāmo darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ity etayoḥ saṃbandhaṃ yajeteti vakṣyati, śyenenābhicarann ity etayoś ca, tathā citrayā paśukāma iti. tasmād ete 'pi sākāṅkṣatvād bhāvavacanāḥ. sarveṣu bhāvavacaneṣu nāsti vinigamanāyāṃ hetuḥ, karmaśabdā evāpūrvasya vidhāyakāḥ, na dravyaguṇaśabdā iti.
children.translated_text: If you see [it] thus — that because of not being action-words, substance-and-quality-words are not enjoiners of the <s>apūrva</s> — [we reply:] 'bringing into being' is the meaning of all [words]. 'One who desires heaven [should sacrifice] with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — [the opponent] will say that these have a connection, and 'he should sacrifice' [completes it]; and likewise for 'one who practices sorcery with the <s>Śyena</s>,' and 'with the <s>Citrā</s>, one who desires cattle.' Therefore, these too, being [words] with syntactic expectancy, are action-denoting. When all are action-denoting, there is no reason for the determination that 'only action-words are enjoiners of the <s>apūrva</s>, not substance-and-quality-words.'

children.text: yeṣām utpattau sve prayoge rūpopalabdhis tāni nāmāni, tasmāt tebhyaḥ parākāṅkṣā bhūtatvāt sve prayoge // MS_2,1.3 //
children.translated_text: Those [words] at whose production [i.e., utterance], in their own application, a [persisting] form is perceived — those are nouns (<s>nāman</s>); therefore, from them there is an expectancy for something else, because [their referent] already exists in their own application. // MS 2.1.3 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ śabdānām uccāraṇotpattau sve 'rthe prayujyamānānāṃ rūpa[111]{*2/11*}m upalabhyate, yat sakṛd utpannaṃ kālāntaran tiṣṭhati, na kriyevotpannamātraṃ vinaśyatīty arthaḥ, tāni nāmāni, te dravyaguṇaśabdāḥ, īdṛśo dravyaguṇaśabdānām arthaḥ. te dravyaguṇaśabdā iti vaktavye tāni nāmānīti sūtritam, ato nāmānīti eṣāṃ paryāyaśabdaḥ. kathaṃ gamyate? yata eṣāṃ vibhaktayo nāmikya ucyante. katamāstāḥ? vṛkṣaḥ{*2/12*} vṛkṣau vṛkṣāḥ, śuklaḥ śuklau śuklā ityevamādayaḥ. tasmāt samyak sūtritam. yata eṣāṃ na kṣaṇiko 'rthaḥ, tataḥ tebhyaḥ parākāṅkṣā pradhānākāṅkṣā na vidyata - iti naiṣām utpattiḥ kartavyā, bhūtatvāt sve prayoge svaprayogakāle vidyamānatvād ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: Those words at whose utterance, when applied to their own meaning, a form is perceived — [a form] that, once arisen, persists for another time, unlike an action which perishes the moment it arises — those are nouns (<s>nāman</s>); they are substance-and-quality-words; such is the meaning of substance-and-quality-words. Instead of saying 'they are substance-and-quality-words,' [the <s>sūtra</s>] says 'those are nouns' — hence 'nouns' is their synonym. How is this known? Because the case-endings [used with them] are called 'nominal' (<s>nāmikī</s>). Which are those? '<s>Vṛkṣaḥ</s>' (tree), '<s>vṛkṣau</s>' (two trees), '<s>vṛkṣāḥ</s>' (trees); '<s>śuklaḥ</s>' (white), '<s>śuklau</s>' (two white ones), '<s>śuklāḥ</s>' (white ones) — and the like. Therefore, [the <s>sūtra</s>] is well formulated. Since their meaning is not momentary, from them there is an expectancy for something else — a primary expectancy [for an action] does not exist — hence their [referent's] production need not be brought about, because [the referent] already exists at the time of its own application — this is the meaning.
[TEXTUAL NOTES: Edition page numbers — E2: 2,355; E4: 2,328; E5: 2,314; E6: 1,75; E2 omits <s>vṛkṣaḥ</s>.]

children.text: yeṣāṃ tūtpattāv arthe sve prayogo na vidyate, tāny ākhyātāni. tasmāt tebhyaḥ pratīyetāśritatvāt prayogasya // MS_2,1.4 //
children.translated_text: But those [words] at whose production the referent does not exist in their own application — those are verbs (<s>ākhyāta</s>). Therefore, from them [the <s>apūrva</s>] is understood, because the application depends [on bringing the referent into being]. // MS 2.1.4 //

children.text:
yeṣāṃ tu śabdānām uccāraṇotpattau sve 'rthe prayogo na vidyate. prayogakāle yeṣām artho nopalabhyata ity arthaḥ, tany ākhyātānīti bhāvaśabdān paryāyaśabdenopadiśati. kathaṃ paryāyaśabdatā bhāvaśabdānām. yata eṣāṃ vibhaktaya ākhyātikya ity ucyante. katamāstāḥ? pacati pacataḥ pacantītyevamādyaḥ. tasmāt tebhyo 'pūrvaṃ pratīyeta. bhavyārthās te bhūtārthaiḥ samuccaritāḥ. bhūtasya bhavyārthatāyāṃ dṛṣṭārthatā, bhavyārthasya prayojanayata utpattir arthavatī, sā ca bhūtena kriyata iti dṛṣṭo 'rthaḥ. bhavyasya punar bhūtārthatāyāṃ na kiñcid dṛśyate, kalpyate cādṛṣṭam. tasmān na yāgo dravyārthaḥ.
kiṃ ca - āśritatvāt prayogasyaiteṣāṃ prayogaḥ puruṣeṇāśrito bhavati, puruṣasaṃbaddhā bhāvanocyate, puruṣaṃ hi vadati, bhāvayed iti, tena svargakāmo yajeteti puruṣo 'pi pratīyate[112]{*2/13*}, yāgo 'pi saṃbandho 'pi. svargakāmo dravyeṇeti dravye{*2/14*} pratīyate puruṣaś ca, na tu saṃbandhaḥ.
children.translated_text:
But those words whose usage in their own meaning is not found at the time of origination through utterance — meaning, those whose meaning is not apprehended at the time of usage — those are verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta</s>), and [<s>Śabara</s>] teaches <s>bhāva</s>-words (activity-words) using a synonym. How are <s>bhāva</s>-words synonymous [with <s>ākhyāta</s>]? Because their inflections are called '<s>ākhyātikī</s>' (verbal). Which are those? '<s>Pacati</s>' (he cooks), '<s>pacataḥ</s>' (they two cook), '<s>pacanti</s>' (they cook) — forms such as these. Therefore, from these [words] the transcendent result (<s>apūrva</s>) should be understood. They [the <s>bhāva</s>-words] having future purpose are uttered together with [words] having past purpose. When the past [purpose] serves a future purpose, there is a perceived purpose: the origination of the future purpose is meaningful, and that [origination] is accomplished by the past [action] — this is the perceived purpose. But when the future [purpose] serves a past purpose, nothing is perceived; rather, the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) is posited. Therefore, the sacrifice is not a substance-meaning.
Moreover — because performance depends [on a person]. The performance of these [<s>bhāva</s>-words] is dependent on a person; the productive power (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is said to be connected with a person, for it addresses a person — 'he should produce' (<s>bhāvayet</s>). Therefore, from 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice,' [Page 112] both the person, the sacrifice, and their connection are understood. [But] from 'one who desires heaven [should produce] by means of a substance,' the substance and the person are understood, but not the connection [between them].

children.text: nanu etad uktaṃ bhavati, arthinaś ca dravyasya ca saṃbandhaṃ yajeteti vakṣyati, dravyeṇa bhāvayed iti. ato dravyeṇārthasya bhāvanā gamyeta, ākāṅkṣā ceti. satyaṃ gamyate, dravyeṇa bhāvayed iti tu vākyena, yāgena bhāvayed iti tu śrutyā. yadā tu, yāgena bhāvāyed iti yāgasaṃbandho vidhīyate, na tadā dravyeṇa bhāvayed iti dravyasaṃbandhaḥ. na ca dravyasaṃbandhe vidhīyamāne yajetety anena saṃbandhaḥ. anūdyamāne tu saṃbhavati, na ca, yaugapādyena vidhyanuvādau saṃbhavataḥ. tasmāc chrutivākyayor virodhaḥ, virodhe ca śrutibalīyasī, tenārthinā na dravyasaṃbandhaḥ. tatra dravyam asati svargakāmasaṃbandhe svargārthaṃ bhaviṣyatīty anupapannam, eṣa vinigamanāyāṃ hetuḥ, yena bhāvaśabdā evāpūrvasya codakāḥ, na dravyaguṇaśabdā iti, yadā yāgena kuryād iti, tadā{*2/15*} yāgavacanam eva bhavati. darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iti lakṣaṇayā, darśe ca pūrṇamāse ca yāgo vihita iti.
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But it has been said that [the verb] '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice) will express the connection of the person seeking [results] and the substance — 'he should produce [the result] by means of the substance.' Therefore, from 'by means of the substance,' the productive power (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of the purpose would be understood, along with the syntactic expectation. [Reply:] True, it is understood — but 'he should produce by means of the substance' is [understood] from the sentence [as a whole], whereas 'he should produce by means of the sacrifice' is [understood] from the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>). And when the connection with the sacrifice is being enjoined [by the direct expression] 'he should produce by means of the sacrifice,' at that point the connection with the substance through 'he should produce by means of the substance' [does not apply]. And when the connection with the substance is being enjoined, [the verb] '<s>yajeta</s>' is not connected with that. While a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>) is possible [alongside an injunction], an injunction and a re-statement cannot occur simultaneously. Therefore, there is a conflict between the direct expression and the sentence. And in a conflict, the direct expression is stronger. Therefore, the connection of the person seeking [results] is not with the substance. In that case, [the claim] that the substance, in the absence of a connection with the heaven-desirer, will serve the purpose of heaven — that is unjustified. This is the reason for the determination [of the issue] — namely, that <s>bhāva</s>-words alone are the prompters of the transcendent result (<s>apūrva</s>), not substance-words or quality-words. Thus, when [we say] 'one should perform by means of the sacrifice,' that is indeed a sacrifice-denoting [expression]. '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsābhyām</s>' (by means of the new-moon and full-moon [rites]) is through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), [meaning] the sacrifice is enjoined at the new moon and the full moon.

children.text: kathaṃ punar idam avagamyate, asti tad apūrvam iti. ucyate -
children.translated_text: How then is this understood — that this transcendent result (<s>apūrva</s>) exists? It is said —

NOTES:
[Edition cross-references: E2: 2,357; E4: 2,332; E5: 2,316; E6: 1,76; E2,4,5,6 read <s>dravyaṃ</s>; E6 omits <s>tadā</s>]

children.text: codanā punar ārambhaḥ // MS_2,1.5 //
children.translated_text: The injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is [evidence for] a fresh undertaking. // MS 2.1.5 //

children.text:
codanety apūrvaṃ brūmaḥ, apūrvaṃ punar asti, yata ārambhaḥ śiṣyate - svargakāmo yajeteti, itarathā hi vidhānam anarthakaṃ syāt, bhaṅgitvād yāgasya, yady anyad anutpādya yāgo vinaśyet[113]{*2/16*}, phalam asati nimitte na syāt. tasmād utpādayatīti. yadi punaḥ phalavacanasāmarthyāt tad eva na viniśyatīti kalpyate. naivaṃ śakyam. na hi karmaṇo 'nyad rūpam upalabhāmahe, yad āśrayaṃ deśāntaraṃ prāpayati, tat{*2/17*} karmety ucyate, na tad ātmani samavetam, sarvagatatvād ātmanaḥ, sarvatra kāryopalambhaḥ sarvatra bhāve liṅgam, na tu{*2/18*} tad eva deśāntarād āgamanasya, na hy asaty āgamane kiṃcid viruddhaṃ dṛśyate. yatra samavetam āsīt, tad vinaṣṭaṃ dravyam, tasya vināśāt tad api vinaṣṭam ity avagamyate. āśrayo 'py avinaṣṭa iti cet. na, bhasmopalambhanāt. saty api basmany astīti cet. na vidyamānopalambhane 'py adarśanāt. phalakriyā liṅgam iti cet. evaṃ saty adarśane samādhir vaktavyaḥ. saukṣmādīnām anyatamad bhaviṣyatīti yadi cintyate, kalpitam evaṃ sati kiṃcid bhavatīti. tatrāpūrvaṃ vā kalpyeta tad veti. aviśeṣakalpanāyām asti hetuḥ, na viśiṣṭakalpanāyām. anāśritaṃ karma bhaviṣyatīti cet. tad api tādṛśam eva. svabhāvāntarakalpanena deśāntaraṃ na prāpayiṣyatīti. tādṛśam eva. tasmād bhaṅgī yajiḥ, tasya bhaṅgitvād apūrvam astīti.
kiṃ cintāyāḥ prayojanam? yadi dravyaguṇaśabdā apy apūrvaṃ codayanti, dravyaguṇāpacāre na pratinidhir upādātavyaḥ, yathā tarhi pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. yathā tarhi siddhāntaḥ, dravyaṃ guṇaṃ vā pratinidhāya prayogo 'nuṣṭhātavya iti
children.translated_text:
By 'injunction' (<s>codanā</s>) we mean the transcendent result (<s>apūrva</s>). The transcendent result must exist, because an undertaking (<s>ārambha</s>) is taught — 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice.' For otherwise, the injunction would be purposeless. Because of the perishable nature of the sacrifice — if the sacrifice were to perish without producing anything else, then, in the absence of a cause, there would be no result. Therefore, [the sacrifice] produces [something]. If, however, one posits by the force of the statement about a result that the [sacrifice] itself does not perish — that cannot be maintained. For we do not perceive any other form of the ritual action. [Page 113] That which conveys something from one place to another — that is called 'action' (<s>karman</s>). It does not inhere in the self (<s>ātman</s>), because the self is omnipresent — [if it did,] one would observe effects everywhere, and that everywhere-existence would be an indicatory sign [of it]. But that very [action] does not [demonstrate] the coming from another place. For in the absence of [such] coming, nothing contradictory is observed. [The action] inhered in the substance in which it was established, and that substance has perished; from its destruction, [the action] too is understood to have perished. [Objection:] But the substratum (<s>āśraya</s>) has not perished. [Reply:] No, because ashes are perceived [remaining]. [Objection:] Even when ashes exist, [it] exists. [Reply:] No, because even when [it supposedly] still exists, it is not perceived. [Objection:] The result-production is an indicatory sign [of its continued existence]. [Reply:] If so, then the non-perception needs to be accounted for. [Objection:] It will be [explained by] one of [the options:] subtlety and the like. [Reply:] If one thinks thus, then something is [merely] posited [without evidence]. In that case, one might equally posit the transcendent result (<s>apūrva</s>) or [the continued existence of the sacrifice itself]. When the postulation is equally unspecified, there is a reason [to prefer one], but not for a specific postulation. [Objection:] The action will exist without a substratum. [Reply:] That too is of the same [speculative] kind. [Objection:] By positing a different nature, [the action persists and] will reach another location. [Reply:] That too is of the same kind. Therefore, the sacrifice is perishable. Because of its perishability, the transcendent result exists.
What is the practical consequence of this inquiry? If substance-words and quality-words also prompt the transcendent result, then when the substance or quality is lacking, a substitute (<s>pratinidhi</s>) should not be employed — as per the first view. But according to the established conclusion, the performance should be carried out by substituting a [different] substance or quality.

NOTES:
[Edition cross-references: E2: 2,359; E4: 2,337; E5: 2,320; E6: 1,77; E2,4 read <s>yat</s>; E1,6; E2,4,5 read <s>nanu</s>]

children.text: tāni dvaidhaṃ guṇapradhānabhūtāni // MS_2,1.6 //
children.translated_text: Those [<s>bhāva</s>-words] are of two kinds — subsidiary and principal. // MS 2.1.6 //

children.text: avagatam etat, bhāvaśabdāḥ karmaṇo vācakā iti, bahuprakārāś ca bhāvaśabdāḥ, yajati, juhoti, dadātīti, eva[114]{*2/19*}ṃprakārāḥ, dogdhi, pinaṣṭi, vilāpayatītyevamādayaś ca. teṣu sandehaḥ - kiṃ sarve pradhānakarmaṇo vidhāyakāḥ, uta kecit saṃskārakarmaṇa iti. bhāvārthatvāviśeṣāt sarve pradhānakarmaṇo vācakā iti prāptam. tato brūmaḥ - tāni dvaidhaṃ bhavitum arhantīti dviprakārāṇi, kānicit pradhānakarmaṇo vācakāni, kānicit saṃskārakarmaṇaḥ. evam api sarvāṇy arthavanti, arthavattve sati sarvebhyaḥ na śakyam apūrvaṃ kalpayitum. ato na sarvāṇi pradhānakarmaṇo vācakāni.
children.translated_text: It has been understood that <s>bhāva</s>-words denote ritual actions. And <s>bhāva</s>-words are of many kinds — '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers), '<s>dadāti</s>' (he gives) — [Page 114] such forms, and also '<s>dogdhi</s>' (he milks), '<s>pinaṣṭi</s>' (he grinds), '<s>vilāpayati</s>' (he melts) — such forms and the like. Regarding these, there is a doubt: do all of them denote a principal ritual action, or do some denote a preparatory action (<s>saṃskāra-karman</s>)? Since there is no difference in their <s>bhāva</s>-nature, the prima facie view is that all denote the principal ritual action. To this we say: those [<s>bhāva</s>-words] ought to be of two kinds — that is, two types. Some denote the principal ritual action, some denote the preparatory action. Even so, all are meaningful. And when all are meaningful, the transcendent result cannot be postulated from all of them. Therefore, not all denote the principal ritual action.

NOTES:
[Edition cross-references: E2: 2,379; E4: 2,384; E5: 2,324; E6: 1,77]

children.text: yair dravyaṃ na cikīrṣyate, tāni pradhānabhūtāni, dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt // MS_2,1.7 //
children.translated_text: Those by which a substance is not intended to be produced are principal, because the substance is subsidiary. // MS 2.1.7 //

children.text: evaṃ saty alpīyasy aḍṛṣṭakalpanā nyāyyā, na tu{*2/20*} vinigamanāyāṃ hetur{*2/21*} avagacchāmaḥ, kuto{*2/22*} 'pūrvam, kuto neti. tad ucyate - yair bhāvakarmabhir na dravyaṃ saṃskartum iṣyate, utpādayituṃ vā, tāni pradhānabhūtāni pradhānakarmaṇo vācakāni, dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt. dravyaṃ hi guṇabhūtam, karmanirvṛtter īpsitatamatvāt.
children.translated_text: In that case, a lesser postulation of the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) is proper, but we do not understand the reason for the determination — whence the transcendent result, and whence not. To this it is said: those <s>bhāva</s>-actions by which no substance is intended to be prepared or produced — those are principal, those denote the principal ritual action, because the substance is subsidiary. For the substance is subsidiary, since the completion of the ritual action is what is most desired.

NOTES:
[E1,6; E2,4,5 read <s>nanu</s>; E1,6; E2,4,5 read <s>hetum</s>; E2 reads <s>kṛto</s>]

children.text: yais tu dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate guṇas tatra pratīyeta, tasya dravyapradhānatvāt // MS_2,1.8 //
children.translated_text: But those by which a substance is intended to be produced — [the action] should be understood as subsidiary there, because [the action] has the substance as its principal [purpose]. // MS 2.1.8 //

children.text: yais tu dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate, guṇas tatra pratīyeta karma. kutaḥ? tasya dravyapradhānatvāt. pratyakṣaṃ yajetetyevamādibhir dravyaṃ na cikīrṣyate, tasmāt [115]{*2/23*} tāni pradhānakarmaṇo vācakāni, dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt. pinaṣṭi - ityevamādibhir dravyaṃ saṃskriyate, tasmāt tāni guṇakarmavacanāni. eṣa eva vinigamanāyāṃ hetuḥ. prayojanaṃ tu pūrvasmin pakṣe praiyaṅgave 'pi carau vrīhaya utpādyā avadhātārthatvena. siddhānte notpādyāḥ.
children.translated_text: But those by which a substance is intended to be produced — the action there should be understood as subsidiary. Why? Because [the action] has the substance as its principal [purpose]. It is directly perceived that by [verbs] such as '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice) and the like, no substance is intended to be produced. Therefore, [Page 115] those denote the principal ritual action, because the substance is subsidiary. By [verbs] such as '<s>pinaṣṭi</s>' (he grinds) and the like, a substance is being prepared. Therefore, those denote subsidiary actions. This is the very reason for the determination. The practical consequence: according to the first view, even in the <s>priyaṅgu</s>-<s>caru</s> (priyaṅgu porridge), rice-grains would have to be produced [i.e., the grinding would generate a new substance serving as the offering material]. According to the established conclusion, they are not to be [separately] produced.

NOTES:
[Edition cross-references: E2: 2,381; E4: 2,389; E5: 2,329; E6: 1,78]

children.text: dharmamātre tu karma syād anirvṛtteḥ prayājavat // MS_2,1.9 //
children.translated_text: But in a case concerning <s>dharma</s> alone, [the action] should be the [principal] ritual action, because it does not accomplish [a substance], like the <s>Prayāja</s> rites. // MS 2.1.9 //

children.text:
srucaḥ{*2/24*} saṃmārṣṭi, agniṃ saṃmārṣṭi, paridhiṃ saṃmārṣṭi, puroṅāśaṃ paryagni karotīti{*2/25*} śrūyate.
tatra sandehaḥ - kiṃ paryagnikaraṇam, saṃārjanaṃ ca pradhānakarma, uta guṇakarmeti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. tata{*2/26*} ucyate - karmamātram evaṃjātīyakam aparyāptaṃ yat prayojanasya dṛṣṭasya, tad dharmamātram iti brūmaḥ, tatra pradhānakarmatvaṃ syāt. kasmāt? anirvṛtter upakārasya, na hy evaṃjātīyakaṃ dravyasyopakārakam, dravyaṃ tv evaṃjātīyakam abhinirvartayad{*2/27*} guṇabhūtam. tasya guṇabhūtatvād idaṃ pradhānabhūtam.
children.translated_text:
'He wipes the ladles,' 'he wipes the fire,' 'he wipes the enclosing stick,' 'he performs the <s>paryagnikaraṇa</s> (circumambulation of fire) around the offering cake' — thus it is heard.
Regarding these, there is a doubt: are <s>paryagnikaraṇa</s> and wiping principal ritual actions or subsidiary actions? What is the prima facie view? To this it is said: an action of this kind — one that is wholly insufficient for a directly perceived purpose — that we call '[pertaining to] <s>dharma</s> alone' (<s>dharmamātra</s>); there, it should be a principal ritual action. Why? Because it does not accomplish [anything for] the service [of a substance]. For an action of this kind does not serve a substance. But a substance — being produced by an action of this kind — would be subsidiary. Because that [substance] is subsidiary, this [action] is principal.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{2/24: E5: sucaḥ}*
*{2/25: Tait.S. 3.3.1}*
*{2/26: E2,4,6: tad}*
*{2/27: E2: abhinirvartayed}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[E5 reads <s>sucaḥ</s>; Tait.S. 3.3.1; E2,4,6 read <s>tad</s>; E2 reads <s>abhinirvartayed</s>]

children.text: tulyaśrutitvād vetaraiḥ sadharmaḥ syāt // MS_2,1.10 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of identical grammatical construction, it would have the same nature as the others. // MS 2.1.10 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. itarair guṇakarmabhiḥ sadharmaḥ syād evaṃjātīyakaḥ, yathā vrīhīn avahanti, tathā. kutaḥ? tulyaśrutitvāt, tulyā hi dvitīyā śrutir eṣāṃ dravyeṣu, yathā vrīhīn avahantīti{*2/28*}, evam agniṃ saṃmārṣṭi, puroṅāśaṃ paryagni karotīti. kiṃ guṇakarmaṇi dravye dvitīyā dṛṣṭeti yato dvitīyādarśanād ihāpi sāmānyato dṛṣṭena guṇakarmatā. neti brūmaḥ - dvitīyā vibhaktiḥ kartur īpsitatame smaryate, sā ceha dvitīyā vibhaktiḥ, tata eva tadīpsitatamam iti gamyate, tac ced īpsitatamam, karma guṇabhūtam. yady api pratyakṣādibhir guṇabhāvo na gamyate, [116]{*2/29*} pramāṇāntareṇa śabdena gamyate, tasmād guṇabhūtam evaṃjātīyakam iti.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) reverses the position. An action of this kind would have the same nature as the other subsidiary actions. Just as 'he husks the rice-grains' — likewise. Why? Because of identical grammatical construction (<s>tulyaśrutitvāt</s>). For the accusative case (<s>dvitīyā</s>) construction of these with respect to substances is identical. Just as in 'he husks the rice-grains' [there is an accusative], so too in 'he wipes the fire,' 'he performs <s>paryagnikaraṇa</s> around the offering cake.' [Objection:] Is it the case that the accusative is observed in subsidiary actions with respect to substances, and therefore from the observation of the accusative here too, the subsidiarity is [established] through general reasoning (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>)? [Reply:] We say no. The accusative case ending is remembered [by grammarians as applying] to what is most desired by the agent. And here there is an accusative case ending. From that itself it is understood that [the substance] is what is most desired. And if it is most desired, the action is subsidiary. Even though the subsidiary status is not apprehended through direct perception and the like, [Page 116] it is apprehended through another means of knowledge — namely, the word (<s>śabda</s>). Therefore, an action of this kind is subsidiary.

NOTES:
[Tait.Br. 3.2.5.6; Edition cross-references: E2: 2,384; E4: 2,398; E5: 2,332; E6: 1,79]

children.text: dravyopadeśa iti cet // MS_2,1.11 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Because of the teaching of a substance. // MS 2.1.11 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi - dvitīyādarśanāt pradhānabhūtam atra dravyam iti. naitad evam, guṇabhūte 'pi dvitīyā bhavati, tathā hi dṛśyate - saktūñ juhoti{*2/30*}, mārutaṃ juhoti, ekakapālaṃ juhotīti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — from the observation of the accusative, the substance is principal here — this is not so. The accusative occurs even when [the substance] is subsidiary. For thus it is observed: 'he offers the barley-flour,' 'he offers to <s>Māruta</s>,' 'he offers on a single potsherd.'

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 3.3.8.4]

children.text: na, tadarthatvāl lokavat tasya ca śeṣabhūtatvāt // MS_2,1.12 //
children.translated_text: No, because [the substance] serves [the sacrifice's] purpose, as in the world; and because that [substance] is in the position of a subordinate. // MS 2.1.12 //

children.text:
na guṇabhūte 'pi dvitīyā, evaṃ hy abhiyuktā upadiśanti - karmaṇi dvitīyā{*2/31*}, kartur īpsitatamaṃ karmeti{*2/32*}, na ca loke guṇabhūte kvacid dvitīyāṃ paśyāmaḥ. yad api ca taṇḍulān odanaṃ paceti, odanārthaṃ taṇḍulān saṃskurv itīpsitā eva taṇḍulāḥ. balvajān śikhaṇḍakān kurv iti, balvjā eva tenā-kāreṇa saṃbaddhā īpsitā iti tatrābhiprāyaḥ. laukikaś ca prayogaḥ śabdārthaparicchede hetur na vaidikaḥ. yat tu laukike{*2/33*} juhotīti prayoge dvitīyā, śakyate tatra vaktum īpsitatama eva sa prayoga iti, taṇḍulān adya juhudhi, taṇḍulān adya homena saṃbandhayeti loke bhavati hi bahuprakārā vivakṣā. anyāyaś cānekārthatvam, tena pradhānabhāvena siddhā satī dvitīyā guṇabhāvena kalpyeta. vede tu kathaṃ dvitīyānirdiṣṭe guṇabhāva iti. dvitīyānirdeśāt pradhānyam evāvagacchāmaḥ, evam avagate pradhānye balīyasā hetunā nāsti prādhānyam ity avagamyate. kutaḥ? na homasya kecit prakāreṇa saktvarthatāvakalpyate kutaḥ? saktūnāṃ [117]{*2/34*} niṣprayojanatvāt, na saktūnām anyat prayojanaṃ dṛśyate śrūyate{*2/35*} vā, yadi vā homas tadartho homo 'pi niṣprayojanaḥ, athārād upakārako homaḥ, tataḥ prayojanavān, jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇe pāṭhād gamyate prayojanavattā, nāprayojana iti śakyate vaktum, prayogavacanena hi sa ākāṅkṣyate. nanu saktūnām api prakaraṇapāṭhāt prayojanavattvaṃ bhaviṣyati. ko vā brūte - neti, prayojanavattaiva, prayojanavattvan tu homam abhinirvartayatām, nānyena prakāreṇa. nanu te 'pi prayogavacanenākāṅkṣyante. tad ucyate - na dravyaṃ tenākāṅkṣyate, itikartavyatāṃ hi sa ākāṅkṣati, homaś cetikartavyatā, na dravyam. nanu home kṛte saktubhyo 'dṛṣṭaṃ niṣpatsyate. nāsty atra pramāṇam. nanu dvitīyā vibhaktiḥ pramāṇam. na hi dvitīyā vibhaktir homasya saktvarthatāṃ jñāpayati. na saktavaḥ prayojanavanta iti bhaved dhomaḥ saktvarthaḥ, homasaṃbaddhāḥ saktavaḥ syur iti, bhavanti home kṛte saktavo homasaṃbaddhāḥ. na homasya saktvarthatā niṣprayojaneṣu saktuṣu ghaṭate, saktv-arthatāvacanaṃ tu na puruṣasyopakārakaṃ na kratoḥ, tadanarthakam eva syāt. yato na{*2/36*} tadvacanāc chakyam anyatarat{*2/37*} kalpayitum. sa eṣa dvitīyāntaḥ saktūnāṃ homasya ca saṃbandhaṃ karoti, saṃbandhe ca sati dravyāṇāṃ karmasaṃyoge guṇatvenābhisaṃbandha iti bhūtatvāt,
guṇabhāve ca tṛtīyā, tenocyate - tṛtīyāyāḥ sthāne dvitīyeti, tena tadarthatvād dhomārthatvāt saktūnāṃ na pradhānyaṃ dvitīyāsaṃyoge 'pi. evam saty arthavad vacanam, na cārthavattve saty ānārthakyam ity ucyate. tasya ca puroḍāśāder yāgādiṣu śeṣabhāvaḥ, tena prayojanavantaḥ, tatra saṃskāro nānarthakaḥ. na sa dṛṣṭopakārāyeti cet. adṛṣṭārtho bhaviṣyati, adṛṣṭo 'pi saṃskāro 'stīty avagamyate loke, yathā grāmāntarād āgatānāṃ puruṣānāṃ paryagnikareṇādṛṣṭa upakāraḥ kriyata ity ucyate. loke ca nānupapattiḥ.
[118]{*2/38*} prayojanaṃ ca varuṇapraghāseṣu śrūyate, śamīmayaḥ sruco bhavanti hiraṇmayo{*2/39*} veti, prakṛtau nānāvṛkṣasruksaṃmārgasādhyam apūrvam iti, nānāvṛkṣasruca utpādayitavyāḥ saṃmārgārthatvena yathā pūrvapakṣaḥ. yathā tarhi siddhāntaḥ, śamīmaya eva hi hiraṇmayo vā saṃmārṣṭavyāḥ. tathā yatra bāṇavantaḥ paridhayas tatrāpi pālāśā utpādayitavyāḥ pūrvapakṣe. siddhānte bāṇavanta eva saṃmārṣṭavyāḥ. avabhṛthe ca pūrvapakṣa utpādayitavyo 'gniḥ saṃmārgāya, siddhānte cāpaḥ saṃmārjanīyāḥ. tathā{*2/40*} ṣaṭtriṃśatsaṃvatsaretarasamayāḥ puroḍāśāḥ savanīyā{*2/41*} iti śrūyate. tatrāpi piṣṭamayaḥ puroḍāśa utpādayitavayaḥ paryagnikaraṇārthatvena pūrvapakṣe, siddhānte māṃsamayā eva paryagnikartavyā iti.
children.translated_text:
The accusative case (<s>dvitīyā</s>) is not used even for a subsidiary element. For the learned thus teach: 'The accusative is used in the object' (<s>karmaṇi dvitīyā</s>); 'The object is that which the agent most desires to attain' (<s>kartur īpsitatamam karma</s>). And in worldly usage, we never see the accusative used for a subsidiary element. Even in 'he cooks rice (<s>taṇḍulān</s>) into porridge (<s>odanam</s>),' the rice is the desired [object] since it is being prepared for the purpose of porridge. In 'he makes <s>balvaja</s>-grass into crests,' the <s>balvaja</s>-grass is desired as connected with that particular form — this is the intent. And worldly usage is the means for determining the meaning of words, not Vedic usage. As for the accusative in the worldly usage of '<s>juhoti</s>' (offers), one can say that that too is a usage for the most desired [object]: 'offer the rice-grains today, connect the rice-grains with the oblation today' — for in the world, there are multiple ways of expressing intention. And it is improper for [a case] to have multiple meanings; therefore, the accusative, being established in the sense of the principal [object], should not be construed as [denoting] a subsidiary element. But in the <s>Veda</s>, when something is indicated by the accusative, how can it be subsidiary? From the accusative indication, we understand principalness alone. When principalness has thus been understood, it is understood by a stronger reason that principalness does not exist. Why? The purpose-serving-<s>saktu</s>-nature of the oblation cannot be construed in any way. Why? Because the <s>saktus</s> (barley-meal) are purposeless — no other purpose of the <s>saktus</s> is seen or heard. If the oblation is for their sake, the oblation too is purposeless. But if the oblation is remotely beneficial, then it has a purpose. Its purposefulness is understood from its being recited in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context — one cannot say it is purposeless, for it is expected by the sentence prescribing the performance. [Objection:] The <s>saktus</s> too will have purposefulness from being recited in the context. [Reply:] Who says they do not? They do indeed have purposefulness — but their purposefulness consists in accomplishing the oblation, not in any other way. [Objection:] They too are expected by the sentence prescribing the performance. [Reply:] To this it is said: it is not the substance that is expected by that [sentence]; rather, it expects the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>), and the oblation is the procedure, not the substance. [Objection:] When the oblation is performed, an unseen [transcendent result] will arise from the <s>saktus</s>. [Reply:] There is no evidence for this. [Objection:] The accusative case-ending is the evidence. [Reply:] The accusative case-ending does not indicate the <s>saktu</s>-serving nature of the oblation. It is not that the <s>saktus</s> are purposeful and therefore the oblation serves the <s>saktus</s>; rather, [the accusative indicates that] the <s>saktus</s> shall be connected with the oblation — and when the oblation is performed, the <s>saktus</s> become connected with the oblation. The <s>saktu</s>-serving nature of the oblation does not work when the <s>saktus</s> are purposeless, and the statement of <s>saktu</s>-serving nature benefits neither the person nor the sacrifice — it would be purposeless. Since from that statement neither [purpose] can be construed, this accusative-ending [word for] <s>saktus</s> merely establishes the connection between the <s>saktus</s> and the oblation. And when a connection exists, since substances are connected to ritual actions as subsidiaries — because of being [already] existent —
and the instrumental case (<s>tṛtīyā</s>) is used for subsidiaries, therefore it is said: the accusative is in place of the instrumental. Hence, because of [being] for the purpose of the oblation, the <s>saktus</s> are not principal even though [indicated by] the accusative.
When this is the case, the statement is meaningful, and when meaningful, it is not said to be purposeless. And the subordination of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (offering cake) and the like to the sacrifice and the like [is established]. Therefore, they are purposeful; the ritual preparation there is not purposeless. [Objection:] It does not serve a visible purpose. [Reply:] It will serve an unseen purpose. It is understood that even unseen preparation exists in the world — just as it is said that for persons who have come from another village, circumambulation with fire (<s>paryagnikaraṇa</s>) produces an unseen benefit. And in the world, there is no impossibility.
Moreover, a purpose is heard in the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> rites: 'The ladles are of <s>śamī</s>-wood or of gold.' In the basic model, the production of ladles from various trees serves the purpose of wiping (<s>saṃmārga</s>) as a novel [ritual element] — thus, ladles from various trees must be produced for the purpose of wiping, according to the prima facie view. But according to the established conclusion: only <s>śamī</s>-wood or golden [ladles] should be wiped. Likewise, where there are <s>bāṇa</s>-wood enclosing sticks (<s>paridhis</s>), <s>palāśa</s> [sticks] must be produced according to the prima facie view; in the established conclusion, the <s>bāṇa</s>-wood ones themselves should be wiped. And in the concluding bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>), fire must be produced for wiping according to the prima facie view; in the established conclusion, the waters should be wiped. Similarly, it is heard: 'The offering cakes (<s>puroḍāśas</s>) of the pressing days (<s>savanīya</s>) are [prepared in] thirty-six seasonal [batches].' There too, a <s>puroḍāśa</s> of flour must be produced for the purpose of circumambulation with fire according to the prima facie view; in the established conclusion, the meat [offerings] themselves should be circumambulated with fire.

NOTES:
Pāṇ. 2.3.2 | Pāṇ. 1.4.49 | [Variant: E1,6; E2,4 read 'yā laukike'; E5 reads 'yā tu'] | [Page refs: E2: 2,387; E4: 2,402; E5: 3,335; E6: 1,79] | [E2 omits 'śrūyate'] | [Variant: E2,4 read 'na ca'] | [Variant: E2,4 read 'anyat'] | [Page refs: E2: 2,389; E4: 2,402; E5: 2,338; E6: 1,80] | [Variant: E2 reads 'hiraṇmayā'] | [Variant: E2,4 read 'yathā'] | [Variant: E2 reads 'savanīyāṃ']

children.text: stutaśastrayos tu saṃskāro yājyāvad devatābhidhānatvāt // MS_2,1.13 //
children.translated_text: In the case of hymns of praise (<s>stuta</s>) and recitations (<s>śastra</s>), the ritual preparation is like the invitatory verse (<s>yājyā</s>), because they serve to designate the deity. // MS_2,1.13 //

children.text: praugaṃ śaṃsati, niṣkevalyaṃ śaṃsati, ājyaiḥ stuvate, pṛṣṭaiḥ stuvate - iti guṇavacanaṃ stavanaṃ śaṃsanaṃ ca, yathā - indrasya tu vīryāṇi pravocam iti{*2/42*}, yad etad guṇavacanaṃ śrūyate, kim etad guṇabhūtaṃ devatāṃ prati, uta pradhānam iti. tatrocyate - stutaśastre saṃskārakarmaṇīti. kutaḥ? devatābhidhānatvāt, guṇavacane nirvartyamāne guṇinī devatā saṃkīrtyate, nānyathā tadguṇavacanaṃ bhavati, tatra pratyakṣaṃ devatābhidhānaṃ gamyate, devatāprakāśanena ca pratyakṣa [119]{*2/43*} upakāro yāgasiddhiḥ. tasmāt saṃskārakarmaṇī yājyāvat, yathā yājyām anāha, puro 'nuvākyām anvāheti stutivacanaṃ devatāprakāśanenārthavat, tadvad etad apīti.
children.translated_text: One recites the <s>prauga</s>, one recites the <s>niṣkevalya</s>, one praises with the <s>ājya</s> [hymns], one praises with the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [hymns] — thus the praise and recitation are statements of qualities. As [in]: 'I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>' — when this statement of qualities is heard, the question is: is this subsidiary with respect to the deity, or is it principal? To this it is said: the hymns of praise and recitations are preparatory ritual acts. Why? Because they serve to designate the deity. When the statement of qualities is being performed, the deity who is the possessor of the qualities is mentioned — not otherwise does that statement of qualities occur. There, the designation of the deity is directly understood. And the direct benefit through the manifestation of the deity is the accomplishment of the sacrifice. Therefore, they are preparatory ritual acts, like the invitatory verse (<s>yājyā</s>) — just as one first utters the invitatory verse and then the offering verse (<s>anuvākyā</s>), so too the statement of praise, being meaningful through the manifestation of the deity, is likewise.

children.text: arthena tv apakṛṣyeta devatānām acodanārthasya guṇabhūtatvāt // MS_2,1.14 //
children.translated_text: But [a hymn] might be transferred by its content, because of the subsidiarity of a non-injunctive [verse] to the deities. // MS_2,1.14 //

children.text: yadi saṃskārakarmaṇī eva{*2/44*} stotraśastre, arthenāpakṛṣyeta devatānām naś codanārthasya guṇabhūtatvāt, devatārthasya guṇabhūto mantra iti tatpradhānabhāve yatra pradhānaṃ tatra nīyeta, tatra kramasannidhī uparudhyeyātām. tasmād eṣa duṣṭaḥ pakṣaḥ - iti paryudasitavyaḥ. katamaḥ punar asau mantraḥ. abhi tvā śūrety{*2/45*} aindraḥ pragātho māhendrasya grahayajeḥ sannidhāv āmnāto yatrendras tatrāpakṛṣyeta.
children.translated_text: If the hymns of praise and recitations are merely preparatory ritual acts, they might be transferred by their content — because of the subsidiarity to the deities of [a verse] that does not serve the purpose of injunction. The <s>mantra</s> is subsidiary to the deity's content, and in the view that the deity is principal, [the verse] would be drawn to where the principal [deity] is — and there, the [prescribed] sequence and proximity would be disrupted. Therefore, this view is defective — it must be set aside. Which <s>mantra</s> is this? The one beginning 'We praise you, O hero' (<s>abhi tvā śūra</s>) — an <s>Aindra</s> (addressed to <s>Indra</s>) <s>pragātha</s> (verse pair) recited in the proximity of the <s>Māhendra</s> (great <s>Indra</s>) <s>graha</s>-offering — it would be transferred to wherever <s>Indra</s> [is the deity].

NOTES:
[Variant: E2 reads 'evaṃ'] | Mā.S. 27.35

children.text: vaśāvad vā guṇārthaṃ syāt // MS_2,1.15 //
children.translated_text: Or it would be for the purpose of a subsidiary element, like the case of the barren cow (<s>vaśā</s>). // MS_2,1.15 //

children.text: na paryudasiṣyāma imaṃ pakṣam, saṃskārakarmaṇī eva stotraśastre, devatābhidhānatvād eva, yad uktam{*2/46*} - pragāthasyotkarṣa iti, tan na, indraśabdena mahendro 'bhidhāyiṣyate, sa evendro mahattvena guṇena mahendra ity ucyate, pratyakṣaṃ hīndraśabdaṃ devatāvacanam upalabhāmahe, mahattvavacanaṃ ca mahacchabdam, yathā rājā mahārājaḥ, brāhmaṇo mahābrāhmaṇa iti, vaśāvat, yathā sā vā eṣā sarvadevatyā yad ajā vaśā, vāyavyām ālabhetety{*2/47*} ajāvaśāśabdena codite karmaṇi chāgaśabdena nigamā bhavanti, tadvat saguṇe codite nirguṇenābhidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati. tena na{*2/48*} bhaviṣyaty utkarṣa iti.
children.translated_text: We shall not set aside this view — that the hymns of praise and recitations are merely preparatory ritual acts, precisely because they serve to designate the deity. As to what was said — 'the <s>pragātha</s> addressed to <s>Indra</s> would be transferred [to the <s>Māhendra</s>]' — that is not so. The word '<s>Indra</s>' will designate <s>Mahendra</s> (great <s>Indra</s>) — for <s>Indra</s> himself, by the quality of greatness, is called <s>Mahendra</s>. For we directly perceive the word '<s>Indra</s>' as designating a deity, and the word '<s>mahat</s>' (great) as designating greatness — just as [one says] 'king, great king' or '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' Like the case of the barren cow (<s>vaśā</s>) — just as when the ritual action has been enjoined by the words <s>ajā-vaśā</s> ('she-goat [that is] a barren cow'), that very <s>ajā</s> ('she-goat, all-deities' sacrifice') is designated as <s>Vāyavya</s> ('for <s>Vāyu</s>') by the word <s>chāga</s> (goat) in the <s>nigama</s>-references — similarly, when [the sacrifice] is enjoined with the qualified [name], designation by the unqualified [name] will also apply. Therefore, there will be no transfer.

NOTES:
[Variant: E2,4,5,6 read 'yat tūktam'] | Tait.S. 3.4.3.2 | [Variant: E2 omits 'tena'; E4 reads 'te na']

children.text: na, śrūtisamavāyitvāt // MS_2,1.16 //
children.translated_text: No, because [the word <s>Indra</s>] is inherently connected with the Vedic text (<s>śruti</s>). // MS_2,1.16 //

children.text: naitad evam, indro 'sya grahasya devateti taddhitasaṃyogena vijñāyeta{*2/49*}, [120]{*2/50*} na cāsya mahattvam apekṣamāṇasya taddhitasaṃyoga upapadyate, taddhitasaṃyogāpekṣasya vā mahattvasaṃbandhāt samāsakalpanā. na ca taddhitārthe vṛttasya mahattvasaṃbandhaḥ, na ca samāsārthe vṛttasya taddhitasaṃbandhaḥ. na cāsminn eva prayoge samāsārthe vṛttir iṣyate, etasminn eva taddhitārthe. na cāyam indraśabdo 'vihitavat svārthaṃ taddhitārthena saṃbadhyeta, vihitavac ca parārthaṃ mahattvena saṃbaddham anūdyeta. vispaṣṭaś cāyam anyo 'rtho mahendro bhavati, mahān indro bhavatīti mahendraḥ, anyaś cendro haviṣo devatā bhavatīti sakṛd uccāraṇe ca nobhayaṃ śakyeta. tasmān nendro devatā mahattvaviśiṣṭaḥ, mahendraśabdāt tu taddhita utpannaḥ, tasmāt tadprātipadikam arthavad iti gamyate, na tv avayavasaṃbandhena. tasmād devatāntaram indrān mahendraḥ, tenaindrasya pragāthasyotkarṣaḥ prāpnoti, ataḥ paryudastitavyaḥ eṣa pakṣaḥ. yad apy ucyate - indrasya vṛtravadhottarakālaṃ mahendratvaṃ darśayati, mahān vāyam abhūd yo vṛtram avadhīd iti{*2/51*}, tathā vedasyādimattādoṣaḥ prasajyeta, ato 'nya indro mahendrāt.
children.translated_text: This is not so. It would be known through the <s>taddhita</s>-suffix connection that '<s>Indra</s> is the deity of this <s>graha</s>-offering.' But the <s>taddhita</s>-suffix connection is not possible for [a word] that requires greatness [as part of its meaning], and for [a word] that requires the <s>taddhita</s>-suffix connection, the construction of a compound with greatness [follows]. But [a word] functioning in the <s>taddhita</s>-derivative sense does not have a connection with greatness, and [a word] functioning in the compound sense does not have a <s>taddhita</s>-connection. And it is not the case that in this very usage, the compound sense is intended, and in that very [usage], the <s>taddhita</s> sense. Nor would this word '<s>Indra</s>' — like an un-enjoined [word] — be connected with its own meaning through the <s>taddhita</s> sense, and like an enjoined [word] — be restated as connected with another's meaning, namely greatness. And this other meaning is clearly distinct — '<s>Mahendra</s>' means '<s>Indra</s> who is great, therefore <s>Mahendra</s>' — and '<s>Indra</s>' [simply] as the deity of the oblation — both cannot be [achieved] in a single utterance. Therefore, <s>Indra</s> is not the deity qualified by greatness. But from the word <s>Mahendra</s>, the <s>taddhita</s> [suffix] is derived, and therefore its base (<s>prātipadika</s>) is understood as meaningful — not through the connection of its component parts. Therefore, <s>Mahendra</s> is a different deity from <s>Indra</s>. Hence the transfer of the <s>Aindra</s> <s>pragātha</s> is entailed — therefore, this view must be set aside. As for what is said — 'it shows that <s>Indra</s> became <s>Mahendra</s> after slaying <s>Vṛtra</s>: he became great because he slew <s>Vṛtra</s>' — then the fault of the <s>Veda</s> having a beginning would follow. Therefore, <s>Indra</s> is different from <s>Mahendra</s>.

NOTES:
[Variant: E1,6; E2,4,5 read 'vijñāyate'] | [Page refs: E2: 2,396; E4: 2,431; E5: 2,345; E6: 1,82] | Ai.Br. 3.21

children.text: vyapadeśabhedāc ca // MS_2,1.17 //
children.translated_text: And because of the difference in designation. // MS_2,1.17 //

children.text: vyapadeśabhedaś ca bhavati, bahu dugdhīndrāya devebhyo havir iti{*2/52*}, bahu dugdhi mahendrāya devebhyo havir iti{*2/53*}, ato 'pi devatāntaram, ekadevatātve mantravikalpaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: There is also a difference in designation: 'Much-milked, [prepare] the oblation for <s>Indra</s> and the gods' and 'Much-milked, [prepare] the oblation for <s>Mahendra</s> and the gods.' From this too, [<s>Mahendra</s>] is a different deity. If they were the same deity, there would be an option between the <s>mantras</s>.

NOTES:
Tai.Br. 3.2.38 | Mā.Sh.S. 1.1.3.29

children.text: guṇaś cānarthakaḥ syāt // MS_2,1.18 //
children.translated_text: And the quality would be purposeless. // MS_2,1.18 //

children.text: yadā vidhiśabdād avagatam etad bhavati - indro devateti, tadāsya guṇānvākhyāne kiṃ prayojanam, mahattvaṃ nāmendrasya guṇo bhavatīti devatābhidhānam. kathaṃ tasyai devatāyai dīyata iti. [121]{*2/54*} guṇe 'pi hi vihite sati tasyā eva devatāyai dīyate, avihite 'pi. tasmād guṇavidhānam anarthakam. athocyate - yo 'smin grahe indraḥ sa mahān iti. naivaṃ grahasaṃbandhasyāprasiddhatvād viśeṣaṇaṃ nātra kalpyate, guṇasaṃbandhasya cāprasiddhatvād guṇena viśeṣaṇam anavakḷptam. tasmād api devatāntaram.
children.translated_text: When it is understood from the injunctive word that '<s>Indra</s> is the deity,' then what is the purpose of the statement of the quality — namely, that greatness is a quality of <s>Indra</s> — for designating the deity? How is the offering given to that deity? For even when a quality is enjoined, the offering is given to that very deity; and even when not enjoined, [it is still given to the same deity]. Therefore, the injunction of a quality is purposeless. If it is said: 'The <s>Indra</s> who is [the deity] of this <s>graha</s>-offering is the great one' — [we reply:] This is not so. Since the connection of [<s>Indra</s>] with the <s>graha</s>-offering is not well-known, no qualifying determination can be construed here; and since the connection with the quality is not well-known, qualification by the quality is not established. Therefore, from this too, [<s>Mahendra</s>] is a different deity.

children.text: tathā yājyāpurorucoḥ // MS_2,1.19 //
children.translated_text: Likewise with the invitatory and offering verses (<s>yājyā</s> and <s>puroruc</s>). // MS_2,1.19 //

children.text: evaṃ sati yājyāpuronuvākyayor bhedena darśanam upapadyate, endra{*2/55*} sānasiṃ rayim ity{*2/56*} aindrayājyāpuronuvākyād vayam, mahān indro ya ojasā - iti{*2/57*} bhedena māhendraṃ darśayati, tadekatve vikalpyeta. tatra, pakṣe bādhaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: This being so, the observation of differentiation between the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) and <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) is well-established: 'O <s>Indra</s>, [give us] wealth from the abode' — from the <s>Aindra</s> (related to <s>Indra</s>) <s>yājyā</s>-<s>puronuvākyā</s> we [derive our view]; 'Great is <s>Indra</s>, who by might' — by this differentiation, [the text] shows the <s>Māhendra</s> (related to <s>Mahendra</s>) [rite]. If the two were identical, there would be an alternative. In that case, in one option there would be an override.

NOTES:
[E1,5; E2: indra, E4,6: aindra] | [Tait.S. 3.4.11.3] | [ṚV 5.8.9]

children.text: vaśāyām arthasamavāyāt // MS_2,1.20 //
children.translated_text: In the [case of the] barren cow (<s>vaśā</s>), because of the co-occurrence of meaning. // MS 2,1.20 //

children.text: yad uktam - ajāvaśāśabdena codite karmaṇi chāgaśabdena nigamā bhavantīti, tad yuktam, vaśāyām arthasamavāyitvaṃ vayaṃ pratyakṣam avagacchāmaḥ, chāgasya vapāyā medaso 'nubrūhīti{*2/58*} yaiva vaśā saiva chāgeti. tasmāt pragāthasyotkarṣaḥ saṃskārapakṣe, ataḥ pradhānakarmaṇī iti.
children.translated_text: What was said — that when a ritual action is enjoined by the words <s>ajā</s> (she-goat) and <s>vaśā</s> (barren cow), the citations (<s>nigama</s>) use the word <s>chāga</s> (goat) — that is proper, [for] in the [case of the] barren cow, we directly perceive the co-occurrence of meaning: 'Recite the <s>anuvākyā</s> for the fat and marrow of the goat' — the very barren cow is indeed the goat. Therefore, in the view that [<s>stotra</s> and <s>śastra</s>] are preparatory rites (<s>saṃskāra</s>), there is the superiority of the <s>pragātha</s> (a pair of verses); hence [they serve] the principal ritual actions.

children.text: yatreti vārthavattvāt syāt // MS_2,1.21 //
children.translated_text: Where [it applies], or [alternatively], it would be so because of meaningfulness. // MS 2,1.21 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati, saṃskārakarmaṇī eva stotraśastre, yac caitat, praghāthasyotkarṣa iti, utkṛṣyatāṃ yatrendras tatra praghāthaḥ, liṅgena hi kramasannidhī bādhitavyāv eva.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) excludes the [previous] position. The <s>stotra</s> (hymnal chanting) and <s>śastra</s> (recitation) are [related to] the preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) only. And as for this — [regarding] the superiority of the <s>pragātha</s> — let the <s>pragātha</s> be given preference wherever <s>Indra</s> [is the deity]. For the order and proximity [of the verses] must be overridden by the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>).

children.text: na tv āmnāteṣu // MS_2,1.22 //
children.translated_text: But not among those [mantras] that are codified [in the traditional teaching]. // MS 2,1.22 //

children.text: apareṣāṃ mantrāṇām utkṛṣṭānām anyatrārthavattā nāsti, teṣām ānarthakyaṃ syāt, yathā yām yāḥ śaṃsanti{*2/59*}, śipiviṣṭavatīṃ{*2/60*} pita[122]{*2/61*}devatyām{*2/62*} āgnimārute{*2/63*}, kuṣumbhakasūktam, akṣasūktam, mūṣikāsūktam ityevamādīnām.
children.translated_text: For the other mantras that have been given preference — there is no meaningfulness for them elsewhere; they would become purposeless. For example, [the mantras] 'those which they recite,' the one containing <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, the one having the Fathers as deities in the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [rite], the <s>Kuṣumbhaka-sūkta</s>, the <s>Akṣa-sūkta</s> (hymn of dice), the <s>Mūṣikā-sūkta</s> (hymn of mice), and similar ones.

children.text: dṛśyate // MS_2,1.23 //
children.translated_text: It is observed [that they have a purpose]. // MS 2,1.23 //

children.text: tad ucyate - sarveṣām arthavattāsti, maṇḍūkasūktasyāgnau, akṣasūktasya rājasūye, mūṣikāsūktasyaikādaśinyām, sarveṣāṃ vācastome, sarvā ṛcaḥ sarvāṇi yajūṃṣi sarvāṇi sāmāni vācastome, pāriplavam aśvamedhe{*2/64*} śaṃsatīti, tathā yasyāśvine śasyamāne sūryo nodiyād api sarvā dāśatayīr anubrūyād iti, tasmād asty arthavattotkṛṣṭānām. ataḥ saṃskārakarmaṇī stotraśastre iti.
children.translated_text: To this it is said: all have meaningfulness — the <s>Maṇḍūka-sūkta</s> (frog hymn) [has its use] in [the rite involving] fire, the <s>Akṣa-sūkta</s> in the <s>Rājasūya</s>, the <s>Mūṣikā-sūkta</s> on the <s>Ekādaśinī</s> (eleventh day), all [mantras have their use] in the <s>Vācastoma</s>: 'All <s>ṛcs</s>, all <s>yajus</s>-formulas, all <s>sāmans</s> [are recited] in the <s>Vācastoma</s>.' [Also,] 'one recites the <s>Pāriplava</s> [narratives] in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).' Similarly, 'at whose <s>Āśvina</s> [rite], when being recited, the sun does not rise — he should recite all the <s>Dāśatayī</s> [hymns].' Therefore, the mantras that have been given preference do have meaningfulness. Hence, the <s>stotra</s> and <s>śastra</s> serve the preparatory rite.

children.text: api vā śrutisaṃyogāt prakāraṇe stautiśaṃsatī kriyotpattiṃ vidadhyātām // MS_2,1.24 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the connection with scripture, the hymnal chanting (<s>stauti</s>) and recitation (<s>śaṃsati</s>) in the context [of the principal rite] would enjoin the origination of the [ritual] act. // MS 2,1.24 //

children.text:
api vā pradhānakarmaṇī stotraśastre syātām. kutaḥ? śrutisaṃyogāt, saptamī śrutisaṃyogo hi bhavati, kavatīṣu stuvate, śipiviṣṭavatīṣu stuvate - iti{*2/65*}, yadi stutiḥ, tataḥ kavatyakṣareṣv āhitā. yadi prakāśanam, tato devatāyām, tatra karaṇaṃ kavatyas{*2/66*} tṛtīyayāśroṣyam{*2/67*}, na saptamyā.
api ca - śrutisaṃyogo bhavati, praugaṃ śaṃsati, niṣkevalyaṃ śaṃsatīti. ataḥ stutir abhinirvartayitavyā tena mantreṇa, guṇavacanaḥ śabdaḥ stutinirvartanārtho 'dṛṣṭam{*2/68*} arthaṃ kariṣyati. tasmāt pradhānakarmaṇī.
[123]{*2/69*} api ca, śrutisaṃyogo bhavati ṣaṣṭhīvibhaktisaṃyogaḥ, yathendrasya tu vīryāṇi pravocam iti{*2/70*}. tena devatāśabdaḥ stutisaṃbandhārtha ity ucyate, devatābhidhānārthe prātipadikārthatvāt prathamā syāt. atha yat prathamāntam, tad devatārthaṃ bhavitum arhati, yathā - indro yāto vasitasya{*2/71*} rājeti{*2/72*}. nety ucyate, tad api vākyasaṃyogāt stutyartham eva. nanu vākyāl liṅgaṃ balīyaḥ. satyam, etad api liṅgam, yat stutivākyasya sākāṅkṣasya nirākāṅkṣīkaraṇasāmarthyam. tathāpy ubhayathā liṅge 'nugṛhyamāṇe kuto nirṇayaḥ? vākyaśeṣād eva na devatābhidhānārtha iti. devatābhidhānārtha ity etasmin pakṣe stutyarthaṃ sākāṅkṣavacanam anarthakam eva syāt. tasmād adṛṣṭārthatvāt stutivacanasya pradhānakarmaṇī stotraśastre.
api ca - stautiśaṃsatīti sākṣād guṇavacanau lakṣaṇayābhidhānārthau syātām, tasmāt kriyotpattim apūrvotpattiṃ vidadhyātām iti.
children.translated_text:
Or rather, the <s>stotra</s> and <s>śastra</s> would [serve] the principal ritual actions. Why? Because of the connection with scripture — the seventh [case-ending] is the scriptural connection: 'he chants in the <s>kavatī</s> [verses],' 'he chants in the <s>śipiviṣṭavatī</s> [verses].' If this is [a description of] praise (<s>stuti</s>), then the praise is established in the <s>kavatī</s> syllables. If it is a manifestation, then [it relates to] the deity — in that case, the <s>kavatī</s> [verses] would be the instrument, to be heard with the third [case-ending], not the seventh.
Moreover, there is a scriptural connection: 'he recites the <s>prauga</s> (introductory recitation),' 'he recites the <s>niṣkevalya</s> (independent recitation).' Therefore, the praise must be accomplished by that mantra; the word expressing a quality will serve the purpose of accomplishing the praise and will produce an unseen result. Hence, [they serve] the principal ritual actions.
Moreover, there is a scriptural connection in the sixth case-ending: as in 'I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>.' Therefore, the word denoting the deity is said to serve the purpose of connecting with the praise — for [if it were] for the purpose of denoting the deity, there would be a first case-ending, since the meaning of a nominal stem [is expressed by the first case]. And what ends in the first case should serve to denote the deity, as in '<s>Indra</s>, who has gone to [the dwelling of] <s>Vasita</s>, is king.' No, it is said — that too, because of the syntactic connection, serves the purpose of praise only. [Objection:] But the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is stronger than the sentence. [Reply:] True, but this too is an indicatory mark — namely, the capacity to complete the expectancy of the praise-sentence. Even so, when the indicatory mark is supported in both ways, how [is there] a resolution? From the remainder of the sentence alone — [the word] is not for the purpose of denoting the deity. In the position that [the word] serves to denote the deity, the praise-purpose [of the] expectancy-bearing expression would simply be purposeless. Therefore, because the praise-expression serves an unseen purpose, the <s>stotra</s> and <s>śastra</s> serve the principal ritual actions.
Moreover, 'hymnal chanting' (<s>stauti</s>) and 'recitation' (<s>śaṃsati</s>) directly express a quality; by figurative usage, they would serve to denote [the ritual]. Therefore, they would enjoin the origination of the [ritual] act — the origination of the unprecedented [result].

NOTES:

children.text: śabdena pṛthaktvam eva gamyate, dvādaśastotraśastro 'gniṣṭomaḥ, itarathā hi dvādaśatvaṃ na syāt. stotrāṇāṃ śastrāṇāṃ ca ekam eva śaṃsanaṃ stavanaṃ ca, atha bheda āśrīyate, tato na dvādaśatve 'vatiṣṭhate.

[If] the chanting and recitation of the <s>stotras</s> and <s>śastras</s> were one and the same, and then a differentiation were relied upon, the number twelve would not be maintained.

children.text: agniṣṭuti{*2/73*} śrūyate - āgneyā grahā bhavantīti, tatra punar ucyate - āgneyīṣu śaṃsantīti, tan na vidhātavyam eva yadi saṃskārakarma{*2/74*}. tasmād api pradhānakarmaṇī iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Agniṣṭuti</s> (praise of <s>Agni</s>), it is heard: 'The cups (<s>graha</s>) are <s>Āgneya</s> (related to <s>Agni</s>).' There, it is said again: 'They recite in the <s>Āgneyī</s> [verses].' That need not be enjoined at all if [the <s>stotra</s> and <s>śastra</s>] are preparatory rites. Therefore, [they serve] the principal ritual actions.

Or, if [it is] a statement about something unprecedented, then one is the <s>stotra</s> and another the <s>śastra</s>; otherwise, what is the <s>stotra</s> would be the very same <s>śastra</s>.

Therefore, the <s>stotra</s> and <s>śastra</s> serve the principal ritual actions. The purpose is tied to [specific] <s>sūtras</s> elsewhere: in the tenth chapter, since the <s>stuta</s> and <s>śastra</s> serve as principal ritual actions, [this principle] would apply when the deity of the cups (<s>graha</s>) differs.

children.text: vidhimantrayor aikārthyam aikaśabdyāt // MS_2,1.30 //
children.translated_text: The injunctive [passage] and the mantra have unity of purpose because of identity of expression. // MS 2,1.30 //

children.text: idaṃ samāmnāyate - na tā naśanti, na dabhāti, taskaro nāsām ā mitro{*2/81*} vyathir ā dadharṣati. devāṃś ca yābhiryajate, dadāti ca jyog ittābhiḥ sa ca te gopatiḥ saheti{*2/82*}. yajate dadātīty udāharaṇam, kiṃ yadvad brāhmaṇe bhāvaśabdo vidhāyakas tadvan mantre 'pi, uta mantre 'bhidhāyaka{*2/83*} iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam, vidhau matre cāmnāyamānasya bhāvaśabdasya eka evārthaḥ syāt, aika[125]{*2/84*}śabdyāt, sa evāyam ekaḥ śabdo brāhmaṇagato vidhāsyati, mantragato na śaknoti vidhātum ity anupapannam, tasmād vidhāyakaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is taught: 'They do not perish, no thief steals them, no hostile adversary dares [to take them]. He sacrifices to the gods with them, and gives — long may he be with those [cows], and he the lord of cattle.' 'He sacrifices, he gives' — this is the example. The question is: just as the verb-form (<s>bhāvaśabda</s>) in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage] is injunctive, is it likewise injunctive in the mantra too? Or is it descriptive (<s>abhidhāyaka</s>) in the mantra? What is the prima facie view? The verb-form that is taught in both the injunction and the mantra should have one and the same meaning, because of identity of expression. This very same single word, when occurring in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, will enjoin; [to say] that when occurring in the mantra it cannot enjoin — this is untenable. Therefore, it is injunctive.

children.text: api vā prayogasāmarthyān mantro 'bhidhānavācī syāt // MS_2,1.31 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the capacity [to function] in the ritual performance, the mantra would be descriptive (<s>abhidhānavācī</s>). // MS 2,1.31 //

children.text: api veti pakṣo vyāvartyate, evaṃjātīyako mantro 'bhidhānavacanaḥ syāt, prayogasāmarthyāt, prayoge kriyamāṇe 'sya sāmarthyaṃ vidyate, godānaṃ goyāgaṃ ca pratyāyayitum, na vidhātum. kutaḥ? vihitatvād godānasya dakṣiṇāvidhāne, goyāgasya tv anubandhyāyām. karmāntaraṃ bhaviṣyatīti cet. na, asakṛd apy ucyamāne tatpratyayād eva. stutyarthakalpanāyām apy ānarthakyam, parisamāptena sārthavādakena vākyena vihitatvād yāgasya. tasmān na mantragato bhāvaśabda evaṃjātīyako vidhāyaka iti.
children.translated_text: The word 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) excludes the [previous] position. A mantra of this kind would be descriptive, because of its capacity in the ritual performance — when the performance is being carried out, its capacity exists to make known the cow-gift (<s>godāna</s>) and the cow-sacrifice (<s>goyāga</s>), but not to enjoin [them]. Why? Because the cow-gift has [already] been enjoined in the injunction of the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), and the cow-sacrifice in [connection with] the subsidiary animal (<s>anubandhyā</s>). [Objection:] It will be a different ritual action. [Reply:] No, because even when [the mantra] is uttered repeatedly, the understanding is of that very same [already-enjoined act]. Even in the supposition that it serves the purpose of praise, there would be purposelessness, since the sacrifice has [already] been enjoined by the complete sentence with the <s>arthavāda</s>. Therefore, the verb-form occurring in a mantra of this kind is not injunctive.

children.text: taccodakeṣu mantrākhyā // MS_2,1.32 //
children.translated_text: In those [mantras] that are enjoined [along with their ritual actions], [they receive] the designation 'mantra.' // MS 2,1.32 //

children.text:
mantragato bhāvaśabdo vidhāyako neti parīkṣitam. ko 'yaṃ mantro nāmeti ucyate. ajñāte mantre tadgato bhāvaśabdaḥ kathaṃ vicārita iti, idam artho 'dhikaraṇaṃ pūrvaṃ draṣṭavyam. kathaṃ lakṣaṇo mantra iti, taccodakeṣu mantrākhyā, abhidhānasya codakeṣv evaṃjātīyakeṣv abhiyuktā upadiśanti, mantrān adhīmahe, mantrān adhyāpayāmaḥ, mantrā vartanta iti. prāyikam idaṃ lakṣaṇam, anabhidhāyakā api kecin mantrā ity ucyanta{*2/85*}, yathā vasantāya kapiñjalān ālabhata iti{*2/86*}, na śakyaṃ pṛṣṭhākoṭeṇa{*2/87*} tatra tatropadeṣṭum iti lakṣaṇam uktam - ṛṣayo 'pi padārthānāṃ nāntaṃ yānti [126]{*2/88*} pṛthakkaśaḥ{*2/89*}. lakṣaṇena tu siddhānām antaṃ yānti vipaścitaḥ. udāharaṇam - medho 'sītyevamādayo 'syantāḥ, iṣe tvety{*2/90*}evamādayas tvāntāḥ, āyurdā asīty{*2/91*} āśīḥ, agnirmūrddheti{*2/92*} stutiḥ, saṅkhā{*2/93*} eko mameti{*2/94*}, pralapitam akṣī te indrapiṅgale duler{*2/95*} iveti, parivedanam{*2/96*} ambe ambika iti{*2/97*}, praiṣa agnīd agnīn iti{*2/98*}, anveṣaṇaṃ ko 'si katamo 'sīti{*2/99*}, pṛṣṭhaṃ{*2/100*} pṛṣṭhāmi{*2/101*} tveti{*2/102*}, ākhyānam iyaṃ vedir iti{*2/103*}, anuṣaṅgo 'cchidreṇa pavitreṇeti{*2/104*}, prayogaḥ traisvaryaṃ cātusvaryaṃ{*2/105*} ca, sāmarthyam abhidhānam, tac caitad vṛttikāraṇenodāharaṇopadeśenākhyātam{*2/106*}. etad api prāyikam eva, asimadhyā api ca mantrā bhavanti, īḍyaś cāsi vandyaś ca vājin iti{*2/107*}, tvāmadhyāś ca tattvāyāmīti. āśīr brāhmaṇam api, so 'kāmayata prajāḥ sṛjeyeti, stutir api vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devateti{*2/108*}, pralāpo na caitad vidmo yadi brāhmaṇā vā smo 'brāhmaṇāḥ smo veti{*2/109*}, paridevanaṃ ye mām adhukṣanta te māṃ pratyamuñcanta iti, praiṣa amutaḥ somam āhareti, anveṣaṇam iha vā sa iha veti, praśnaḥ veda karṇavatīṃ sūrmim iti, prativacanaṃ vidmo veti, anuṣaṅgaḥ hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyaty atha jihvāyā atha vakṣasīti{*2/110*}, prayogaḥ traisvaryaṃ cātusvaryaṃ{*2/111*} ceti, sāmarthyaṃ sruveṇāvadyati draveṣv iti. lakṣaṇakarmaṇi prayojanaṃ prasiddhatvān na vaktavyam, laghīyasī pratipattir lakṣaṇena. ākṣepeṣv apavādeṣu prāptyāṃ lakṣaṇakarmaṇi. prayojanaṃ na vaktavyaṃ yaś ca kṛtvā pravartate. ākṣepeṣu pūrvādhikaraṇasya prayojanam, apavādeṣūtsargasya, prāptyām
uttaravivakṣā, kṛtvācintāyāṃ pūrvādhikaraṇasya prayojanam. asti vede mantraśabdo yasyāyam arthaḥ parīkṣitaḥ, ahe budhniya mantraṃ me gopāya yam ṛṣayas trayīvidā viduḥ, ṛcaḥ sāmāni yajūṃṣīti{*2/112*}
children.translated_text: It has been examined whether a <s>bhāva</s>-word (optative/potential verb) occurring in a <s>mantra</s> is injunctive or not. [Now] it is asked: What is this <s>mantra</s>? Since the <s>bhāva</s>-word occurring in an unknown <s>mantra</s> — how was it examined? — this topic should be considered first. What is the defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of a <s>mantra</s>? The designation '<s>mantra</s>' [belongs to those passages] that are prompting (<s>codaka</s>). The learned instruct that the designation [applies] to prompting passages of this kind: 'We study the <s>mantras</s>'; 'We teach the <s>mantras</s>'; 'The <s>mantras</s> are current.' This is only a general characteristic, for even some non-expressive [passages] are called <s>mantras</s> — such as 'One should sacrifice <s>kapiñjala</s>-birds to <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring).' Since it is not possible to instruct about each individual case, the defining characteristic is stated: 'Even <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) do not reach the end of individual items one by one. But the wise reach the end of those that are established by a defining characteristic.' Examples: [Mantras] ending in '<s>asi</s>' (you are) — such as '<s>medho 'si</s>' (you are the sacrificial animal); [mantras] ending in '<s>tvā</s>' — such as '<s>iṣe tvā</s>' (for nourishment, you); a blessing (<s>āśīḥ</s>) — '<s>āyurdā asi</s>' (you are a giver of life); praise (<s>stuti</s>) — '<s>agnir mūrddhā</s>' (<s>Agni</s> is the head); a count (<s>saṅkhyā</s>) — '<s>eko mama</s>' (one is mine); a raving (<s>pralapita</s>) — '<s>akṣī te indrapiṅgale</s>' (your two eyes, O <s>Indra</s>, are tawny, like a <s>ḍulī</s>); a lamentation (<s>parivedana</s>) — '<s>ambe ambike</s>' (O mother, O little mother); a command (<s>praiṣa</s>) — '<s>agnīd agnīn</s>' (O <s>Agnīdh</s>, [kindle] the fires); a search (<s>anveṣaṇa</s>) — '<s>ko 'si katamo 'si</s>' (Who are you? Which one are you?); a question (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>) — '<s>pṛṣṭhāmi tvā</s>' (I ask you); a narration (<s>ākhyāna</s>) — '<s>iyaṃ vediḥ</s>' (this is the altar); a tag-formula (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) — '<s>acchidreṇa pavitreṇa</s>' (with an unbroken filter); performance (<s>prayoga</s>) — the three-tone and four-tone [accents]; capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) — expression. And all this has been explained through the method of activity (<s>vṛttikāraṇa</s>) and through the teaching of examples. This too is only general, for there are also <s>mantras</s> with '<s>asi</s>' in the middle — '<s>īḍyaś cāsi vandyaś ca vājin</s>' (You are praiseworthy and adorable, O steed); and with '<s>tvā</s>' in the middle — '<s>tattvāyāmi</s>' (I extend to you). A blessing [occurs] in a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too — '<s>so 'kāmayata prajāḥ sṛjeyam</s>' (He desired: 'May I create progeny'); praise too — '<s>vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā</s>' (<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity); a raving — '<s>na caitad vidmo yadi brāhmaṇā vā smo 'brāhmaṇāḥ smo vā</s>' (We do not know whether we are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> or non-<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>); a lamentation — '<s>ye mām adhukṣanta te māṃ pratyamuñcanta</s>' (Those who milked me, let them release me); a command — '<s>amutaḥ somam āhara</s>' (Bring <s>Soma</s> from there); a search — '<s>iha vā sa iha vā</s>' (Is he here or here?); a question — '<s>veda karṇavatīṃ sūrmim</s>' (Does he know the eared vessel?); an answer — '<s>vidmo</s>' (We know); a tag-formula — '<s>hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyati, atha jihvāyā, atha vakṣasi</s>' (He cuts at the tip of the heart, then of the tongue, then at the chest); performance — three-tone and four-tone [accents]; capacity — meaning. The defining characteristic and its purpose need not be stated, as it is well-known — understanding is easier through a defining characteristic. In objections, in exceptions, in [determining] scope, and in the defining-characteristic activity — the purpose need not be stated, nor for one who acts after having done [the defining]. In objections, the purpose [comes] from the previous topic; in exceptions, from the general rule; in scope, from the desire [to state] the subsequent [rule]; in the 'having done' inquiry, the purpose [comes] from the previous topic. There is the word '<s>mantra</s>' in the <s>Veda</s> whose meaning has been examined: '<s>Ahe Budhnya</s>, protect my <s>mantra</s>, which the <s>ṛṣis</s> who know the threefold [Veda] know — the <s>ṛcs</s>, <s>sāmans</s>, and <s>yajus</s>-formulas.'
