children.text: śeṣe brāhmaṇaśabdaḥ // MS_2,1.33 //
children.translated_text: The designation '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' [applies to] the remainder. // MS 2.1.33 //

children.text: atha kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brāhmaṇam? mantrāś ca brāhmaṇaṃ ca vedaḥ, tatra mantralakṣaṇa ukte pariśeṣasiddhatvād brāhmaṇalakṣaṇam avacanīyam, mantralakṣaṇavacanenaiva siddham, yasyaital lakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati, tad brāhamaṇam iti pariśeṣasiddhaṃ brāhmaṇam. vṛttikāras tu śiṣyahitārthaṃ prapañcitavān itikaraṇabahulam, ity āhopanibaddham, ākhyāyikāsvarūpam, hetuḥ sūrpeṇa{*2/114*} juhoti tena hy annaṃ kriyata iti{*2/115*}, nirvacanam, tad dadhno dadhitvam{*2/116*}, nindā, upavītā vā etasyāgnayaḥ, praśaṃsā, vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devateti{*2/117*}, saṃśayaḥ, hotavyaṃ gārhapatye na hotavyam iti, vidhiḥ, yajamānasaṃmitaudambarī{*2/118*} bhavati{*2/119*}, parakṛtiḥ, māṣān eva{*2/120*} mahyaṃ{*2/121*} pacatīti{*2/122*}, purākalpaḥ, ulmukhair ha sma pūrve samājagmur iti, vyavadhāraṇakalpanā, yāvato 'śvān pratigṛhnīyād iti. hetur nirvacanaṃ nindā praśaṃsā saṃśayo vidhiḥ. parakriyā purākalpo vyavadhāraṇakalpanā. upamānaṃ daśaite tu vidhayo brāhmaṇasya tu. etad vai{*2/123*} sarvavedeṣu niyataṃ vidhilakṣaṇam. etad api prāyikam, itikaraṇabahulo mantro 'pi kaścit, iti veti me manaḥ{*2/124*}, ity{*2/125*} āhopanibaddhaś ca, bhagaṃ bhakṣīty{*2/126*} āha, ākhyāyikāsvarūpaṃ cogro ha bhujyam iti{*2/127*}, hetur idaṃ vo{*2/128*} vāmuśanti hi{*2/129*}{*2/130*}, nirvacanaṃ tasmād āpo nu sthanā{*2/131*} - iti{*2/132*}, nindā mogham annaṃ vindata apraceteti{*2/133*}, praśaṃsā - agnir mūrddheti{*2/134*}, saṃśayaḥ - adhaḥ khidāsīd{*2/135*} upari khidāsīd{*2/136*} iti{*2/137*}, vidhiḥ - pṛṇīyādinn ādhamānāyeti{*2/138*}{*2/139*}, parakṛtiḥ - sahasram ayutādadat{*2/140*}{*2/141*}, purākalpaḥ - yajñena yajñam ayajanta devā iti{*2/142*}.
children.translated_text: Now, what is the defining characteristic of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage]? <s>Mantras</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [together constitute] the <s>Veda</s>. Since the <s>mantra</s>-characteristic has been stated, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-characteristic need not be stated, as it is established by elimination — it is already established by the statement of the <s>mantra</s>-characteristic: whatever does not have that characteristic is <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Thus, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is established by elimination. But the commentator (<s>vṛttikāra</s>), for the benefit of students, has elaborated: [it is] abundant in <s>itikaraṇa</s> (narrative connectors like 'thus'); connected with '<s>iti āha</s>' (thus he said); having the form of a narrative (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>); [containing] a reason — '<s>sūrpeṇa juhoti tena hy annaṃ kriyate</s>' (He offers with a winnowing basket, for by that food is made); [containing] an etymology (<s>nirvacana</s>) — '<s>tad dadhno dadhitvam</s>' (That is the curd-nature of curds); [containing] censure (<s>nindā</s>) — 'The fires of this [sacrificer] are <s>upavīta</s> (improperly invested)'; [containing] praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>) — '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity'; [containing] doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) — 'Should one offer in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] or not?'; [containing] an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) — 'The <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood [post]) should be the measure of the sacrificer'; [containing] the act of another (<s>parakṛti</s>) — 'He cooks beans for me'; [containing] ancient lore (<s>purākalpa</s>) — 'The ancients used to come together with firebrands'; [containing] a stipulation (<s>vyavadhāraṇakalpanā</s>) — 'However many horses one should accept.' [Verse:] 'Reason, etymology, censure, praise, doubt, injunction, the act of another, ancient lore, and stipulation — with illustration, these are the ten modes of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' 'This is the fixed injunction-characteristic in all <s>Vedas</s>.' This too is only general, for some <s>mantras</s> also have abundant <s>itikaraṇa</s> — '<s>iti veti me manaḥ</s>' (Thus or not — [so goes] my mind); and [a <s>mantra</s>] connected with '<s>āha</s>' — '<s>bhagaṃ bhakṣīty āha</s>' (He says: 'Eat the <s>Bhaga</s> [share]'); and having narrative form — '<s>ugro ha bhujyam</s>' (The fierce one [drove away] <s>Bhujyu</s>); and a reason — '<s>idaṃ vo vāmuśanti hi</s>' (For they desire this desirable [thing] of yours); and an etymology — '<s>tasmād āpo nu sthanā</s>' (Therefore, [they are called] waters); and censure — '<s>mogham annaṃ vindate apracetaḥ</s>' (The thoughtless one finds food in vain); and praise — '<s>agnir mūrddhā</s>' (<s>Agni</s> is the head); and doubt — '<s>adhaḥ svidāsīd upari svidāsīd</s>' (Was it below? Was it above?); and an injunction — '<s>pṛṇīyād inn ādhamānāya</s>' (One should give to the destitute); and the act of another — '<s>sahasram ayutādadat</s>' (He gave a thousand, ten thousand); and ancient lore — '<s>yajñena yajñam ayajanta devāḥ</s>' (The gods worshipped the sacrifice with sacrifice).

children.text: anāmnāteṣv amantratvam āmnāteṣu hi vibhāgaḥ // MS_2,1.34 //
children.translated_text: For those not codified [in the mantra-collection], there is non-mantra status; for those codified, there is a division. // MS 2.1.34 //

children.text: ūhapravaranāmadheyeṣu saṃśayaḥ, mantrā uta neti. abhidhāyakatvān mantrā iti prāpte brūmaḥ - anāmnāteṣu mantratvaṃ na syād abhidhāyakeṣv api, nābhidhāyakatvaṃ mantratve hetuḥ, kiṃ tarhy abhiyuktaprayogaḥ, ye abhiyuktair mantrā iti nocyante, na te mantrāḥ, na caivamādāyo mantrasamāmnāye santi, tasmād amantrāḥ. prayojanam, mantre duṣṭe yat prāyaścittam amantreṣu tan na.
children.translated_text: Regarding <s>ūha</s> (adapted <s>mantras</s>), <s>pravara</s> (ancestry recitation), and <s>nāmadheya</s> (ritual names), there is doubt — are they <s>mantras</s> or not? When it is prima facie concluded that they are <s>mantras</s> because of their expressive nature, we say: For those not codified [in the <s>mantra</s>-collection], there should be no <s>mantra</s>-status even if they are expressive. Expressiveness is not the reason for <s>mantra</s>-status. Rather, [the reason is] the usage of the learned. Those which are not called <s>mantras</s> by the learned are not <s>mantras</s>. And such [passages] as these are not in the <s>mantra</s>-collection. Therefore, they are non-<s>mantras</s>. The practical consequence: the expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) prescribed for a defective <s>mantra</s> does not apply to non-<s>mantras</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ ṛg yatrārthavaśena pādavyavasthā // MS_2,1.35 //
children.translated_text: Among those, an <s>ṛc</s> is [a mantra] where the arrangement of metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>) is determined by meaning. // MS 2.1.35 //

children.text: ṛca ity asti vede, ahe budhniya mantraṃ me gopāya yam ṛṣayas trayīvidā{*2/144*} viduḥ ṛco{*2/145*} yajūṃṣi sāmānīti{*2/146*}. kathaṃlakṣaṇikā ṛcaḥ? teṣām ṛg yatrārthavaśena pādavyavasthā, yatra pādakṛtā vyavasthā sa mantra ṛg nāmā, yathā - agnim īla iti{*2/147*}, evaṃjātīyakeṣu mantreṣv abhiyuktā upadiśanti, ṛco 'dhīmahe, ṛco 'dhyāpayāmaḥ, ṛco vartanta iti. yady arthavaśenety ucyate, yatra vṛttavaśena tatra na prāpnoti, agniḥ pūrvebhir ṛṣibhir iti{*2/148*}, yato nārthavaśeneti vṛttādivaśavyāvṛttyartham, kiṃ tarhy anuvāda eṣa pradarśanārthaḥ. avaśyaṃ caitad evaṃ vijñeyam, vṛttādinirvṛttyarthe sati vākyaṃ bhidyeta. tasmād yatra pādakṛtā vyavasthā, sā ṛg iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>ṛc</s> exists in the <s>Veda</s> — '<s>Ahe Budhnya</s>, protect my <s>mantra</s>, which the <s>ṛṣis</s> who know the threefold [<s>Veda</s>] know — the <s>ṛcs</s>, <s>yajus</s>-formulas, and <s>sāmans</s>.' What is the defining characteristic of <s>ṛcs</s>? 'Among those, an <s>ṛc</s> is [a mantra] where the arrangement of metrical feet is determined by meaning.' A <s>mantra</s> in which the arrangement is made by metrical feet — that <s>mantra</s> is called an <s>ṛc</s>. For example: '<s>agnim īḻe</s>' (I praise <s>Agni</s>) and [mantras] of this kind. In <s>mantras</s> of this kind, the learned instruct: 'We study the <s>ṛcs</s>'; 'We teach the <s>ṛcs</s>'; 'The <s>ṛcs</s> are current.' If it says 'by meaning' (<s>arthavaśena</s>), then where [the arrangement is] by meter (<s>vṛtta</s>), it would not apply — [for example,] '<s>agniḥ pūrvebhir ṛṣibhiḥ</s>' (<s>Agni</s>, [praised] by former <s>ṛṣis</s>). Since the [arrangement] is not by meaning, the phrase 'by meaning' serves to exclude [arrangement] by meter and the like. Rather, this is a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>) for illustrative purposes. And this must necessarily be understood thus — if it were for the purpose of producing metrical feet and the like, the sentence would be split. Therefore, wherever the arrangement is made by metrical feet, that is an <s>ṛc</s>.
Page 129

children.text: gītiṣu sāmākhyā // MS_2,1.36 //
children.translated_text: In [mantras set to] melodies, the designation '<s>Sāman</s>' [applies]. // MS 2.1.36 //

children.text: atha sāmnaḥ kiṃ lakṣaṇam? viśiṣṭā kācid gītiḥ sāmety ucyate, pragīte hi mantravākye sāmaśabdam abhiyuktā upadiśanti, sāmāny adhīmahi, samāny adhyāpayāmaḥ, sāmāni vartanta iti, abhiyuktopadeśaś ca naḥ pramāṇam. yathā - amlaṃ{*2/150*} dadhi, madhuro guḍa iti gītiviśiṣṭe tāvan mantre gītiśabdaḥ, gītisaṃbandhān mantre saṃpratyaya ity avagantavyam.
children.translated_text: Now, what is the defining characteristic of a <s>Sāman</s>? A specific kind of melody (<s>gīti</s>) is called <s>Sāman</s>. For when a <s>mantra</s>-sentence is sung, the learned instruct [using] the word <s>Sāman</s>: 'We study the <s>Sāmans</s>'; 'We teach the <s>Sāmans</s>'; 'The <s>Sāmans</s> are current.' And the instruction of the learned is our authoritative source. Just as 'curds are sour, <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) is sweet' — the word '<s>gīti</s>' (melody) [applies to] a <s>mantra</s> that is distinguished by melody. It should be understood that the cognition [of a passage as <s>Sāman</s>] arises from the <s>mantra</s>'s connection with melody.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{2/150: E2: pratyakṣā amlaṃ, E4: yakṣā amlaṃ}*

children.text: śeṣe yajuḥśabdaḥ // MS_2,1.37 //
children.translated_text: The designation '<s>Yajus</s>' [applies to] the remainder. // MS 2.1.37 //

children.text: atha yajuṣaḥ kiṃ lakṣaṇam iti. yajuṣo lakṣaṇaṃ na vaktavyam, ṛglakṣaṇasāmalakṣaṇābhyām eva yajur vijñāsyate vaiparītyena, yā na gītir na ca pādabaddham, tat praśliṣṭapaṭhitaṃ yajur iti.
children.translated_text: Now, what is the defining characteristic of a <s>Yajus</s>? The defining characteristic of <s>Yajus</s> need not be stated. <s>Yajus</s> will be understood through the defining characteristics of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> by contrast — whatever is neither a melody nor composed in metrical feet, that which is recited in continuous prose, is <s>Yajus</s>.

children.text: atha nigado nāma kiṃ yajūṃṣy uta yajuṣo 'nya iti?
children.translated_text: Now, is a <s>nigada</s> (recitation formula) [a type of] <s>Yajus</s>, or is it something other than <s>Yajus</s>?

children.text: nigado vā caturthaṃ syād dharmaviśeṣāt // MS_2,1.38 //
children.translated_text: Or, the <s>nigada</s> would be a fourth [category], because of the distinction of its properties. // MS 2.1.38 //

children.text: nigadāḥ na yajūṃṣi. kutaḥ? dharmaviśeṣāt, uccaiḥ ṛcā kriyate, uccaiḥ sāmnā, upāṃśu yajuṣā, uccair nigadenety eṣa dharmaviśeṣaḥ, uccair nigadenety anūdyate, yadi yajuṣo nigadatvaṃ [130]{*2/151*} syāt, na ca tasyoccais tvaṃ dharmo dṛśyeta. dṛśyate tu. tasmāc caturthaṃ mantrajātaṃ nigado nāma.
children.translated_text: <s>Nigadas</s> are not <s>yajus</s>-mantras. Why? Because of a difference in ritual property (<s>dharma</s>). The <s>ṛc</s> is recited aloud, the <s>sāman</s> is chanted aloud, the <s>yajus</s> is [recited] in a low voice (<s>upāṃśu</s>), and the <s>nigada</s> is [recited] aloud — this is the difference in ritual property. 'One should recite the <s>nigada</s> aloud' is a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>); if the <s>nigada</s> were [a type of] <s>yajus</s>, the property of being recited aloud would not be observed [for it]. But it is observed. Therefore, <s>nigada</s> is a fourth class of <s>mantra</s>.
[TEXTUAL NOTES: Edition page numbers — E2: 2,428; E4: 2,513; E5: 2,379; E6: 1,89.]

children.text: vyapadeśāc ca // MS_2,1.39 //
children.translated_text: And because of the designation. // MS 2.1.39 //

children.text: vyapadeśo 'pi bhavati, yajūṃṣi vartante, na nigadāḥ. nigadā vartante, na yajuṃṣīti. tasmād api mantrāntaram.
children.translated_text: There is also a designation [distinguishing them]: 'The <s>yajus</s>-mantras are operative, not the <s>nigadas</s>'; 'The <s>nigadas</s> are operative, not the <s>yajus</s>-mantras.' Therefore, [the <s>nigada</s>] is a different [class of] <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: yajūṃṣi vā tadrūpatvāt // MS_2,1.40 //
children.translated_text: Or [<s>nigadas</s>] are [indeed] <s>yajus</s>-mantras, because of having the same form. // MS 2.1.40 //

children.text: yajūṃṣy eva vā nigadāḥ. kutaḥ? tadrūpatvāt, tad evaiṣāṃ rūpam, yad yajuṣāṃ praśliṣṭapāṭhaḥ, ṛksāmalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇatā ca.
children.translated_text: <s>Nigadas</s> are indeed <s>yajus</s>-mantras. Why? Because of having the same form — their form is the very same as that of the <s>yajus</s>: continuous recitation (<s>praśliṣṭapāṭha</s>) and being distinct from the defining characteristics of <s>ṛc</s> and <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: vacanād dharmaviśeṣaḥ // MS_2,1.41 //
children.translated_text: The difference in [ritual] property is because of the [specific] statement. // MS 2.1.41 //

children.text: vacanāt pratyāyanasāmarthyāt, asti hi puruṣāntarapratyāyanasāmarthyaṃ keṣāṃcid yajuṣām.
children.translated_text: Because of the statement — that is, because of the capacity to communicate to another person. For some <s>yajus</s>-mantras have the capacity to communicate to another person.

children.text: arthāc ca // MS_2,1.42 //
children.translated_text: And because of the purpose. // MS 2.1.42 //

children.text:
asti ca taiḥ puruṣāntaraiḥ pratyāyitaiḥ prayojanam, nopaṃśūccāryamāṇāḥ puruṣāntaraṃ pratyāyayeyuḥ. tasmād dharmaviśeṣo 'rthavān. yāni ca yajaṃṣy{*2/152*} uccair uccāryante te nigadāḥ. kutaḥ? niśabda{*2/153*}, prakarṣasya vaktā, yathā prakarṣeṇa raktaṃ nitarāṃ raktam ity ucyate. gadatir gadanārthaḥ pāṭhavacanaḥ. eṣa eva hi prakarṣo yad uccais tvāvacchinnatvaṃ.
nanu vācaniko guṇo yajuṣām upāṃśutvam. neti brūmaḥ - guṇo nāma sa bhavati, yaḥ svakāryaṃ kurvatām upakāre vartate, na ca parasaṃbodhanārthānāṃ yajuṣām upāṃśutvaṃ sāhāyye vartate, tad dhi svakarmakriyāvighātaṃ karoti, tena puruṣāntarasaṃbodhanārtham uccais tvaṃ guṇaḥ. itarārthaṃ tu vacanaṃ bhaviṣyati, itarāṇi yāni [131]{*2/154*} yajūṃṣi na parasaṃbodhanārthāni, teṣūpāṃśutvaṃ nivekṣyate.
children.translated_text:
And there is a purpose served by communicating to those other persons — [the <s>nigadas</s>] could not communicate to another person when recited in a low voice. Therefore, the difference in [ritual] property is purposeful. And those <s>yajus</s>-mantras that are recited aloud are the <s>nigadas</s>. Why? [The prefix] 'ni-' indicates emphasis, just as what is intensely red is called 'very red' (<s>nitarāṃ raktam</s>). The root '<s>gad</s>' means 'to speak,' [indicating] recitation and utterance. For this very emphasis is what is distinguished by loudness.
[Objection:] But the low-voice property of <s>yajus</s>-mantras is their verbal [i.e., scripturally stated] quality. [Reply:] We say no — a 'quality' is that which assists [something] in performing its own function. But the low-voice property does not assist <s>yajus</s>-mantras that are meant for communicating to another person; indeed, it obstructs the performance of their own function. Therefore, loudness is the [proper] quality for those [<s>yajus</s>-mantras] intended to communicate to another person. The [injunction for low voice] will be a statement about the others — those other <s>yajus</s>-mantras that are not intended to communicate to another person; for them, the low-voice [recitation] is to be applied.
[TEXTUAL NOTES: E2,4,5,6 read <s>yajūṃṣi</s> and <s>niśabdaḥ</s>; edition page numbers — E2: 2,430; E4: 2,517; E5: 2,380; E6: 1,89.]

children.text: guṇārtho vyapadeśaḥ // MS_2,1.43 //
children.translated_text: The designation is based on a quality. // MS 2.1.43 //

children.text: atha yad uktaṃ vyapadeśa iti, sa caikatve 'pi guṇato bhavati, yatheto brāhmaṇā bhojyantām, itaḥ parivrājakā iti. evam uccaistvena guṇena tāny eva yajūṃṣi vyapadiśyante, nigadā iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was said about the designation — even when [they are] one [type], a designation can be based on a quality, just as [one says] 'let the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> be fed here; let the wandering ascetics [go] there.' Similarly, those very same <s>yajus</s>-mantras are designated as '<s>nigadas</s>' because of the quality of loudness.

children.text: sarveṣām iti cet // MS_2,1.44 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If [this applied] to all [loud recitations]. // MS 2.1.44 //

children.text: yadi ya uccair gadyate sa nigadaḥ, ṛg api nigadaḥ prāpnoti.
children.translated_text: If whatever is recited aloud is a <s>nigada</s>, then the <s>ṛc</s> too would be a <s>nigada</s>.

children.text: na, ṛgvyapadeśāt // MS_2,1.45 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the designation '<s>ṛc</s>.' // MS 2.1.45 //

children.text: na ṛco nigadā{*2/155*} vyapadiśyante, ayājyā vai nigadā ṛcaiva yajantīti pṛthaktvanimittā hi vyapadeśā bhavanti. ucyate, vyapadeśo liṅgam, prāptir ucyatām iti. apādabaddhe gadatir vartate, apādabaddho hi gadya ity ucyate.
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛc</s>-verses are not designated as <s>nigadas</s> — 'the <s>nigadas</s> are not [used for] sacrifice; one sacrifices with <s>ṛc</s>-verses alone.' For designations arise from a distinguishing cause. It is said: the designation is the indicatory mark; let the [actual] applicability be stated. The root '<s>gad</s>' (to speak) applies to what is not bound in metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>), for what is not bound in feet is said to be 'spoken' (<s>gadya</s>).

children.text: arthaikatvād ekaṃ vākyaṃ sākāṅkṣaṃ ced vibhāge syāt // MS_2,1.46 //
children.translated_text: A sentence is one because of unity of purpose; if, when divided, [the parts] would have syntactic expectancy. // MS 2.1.46 //

children.text:
atha praśliṣṭapaṭhiteṣu yajuḥṣu katham avagamyeta iyad ekaṃ yajur iti? yāvatā padasamūhenejyate, tāvān padasamūhaḥ ekaṃ yajuḥ. kiyatā cejyate? yāvatā kriyāyā upakāraḥ prakāśyate, tāvad vaktavyatvād vākyam ity ucyate. tenābhidhīyate - [132]{*2/156*} arthaikatvād ekaṃ vākyam iti, etasmāc cet kāraṇād ekavākyatā bhavati. tasmād ekārthaḥ padasamūho vākyam, yadi ca vibhajyamānaṃ sākāṅkṣaṃ padaṃ bhavati. kim udāharaṇam? devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti{*2/157*}. nanu padaṃ padam atraikārtham. satyam, na tu tadvibhāge sākāṅkṣaṃ. na tarhy arthaikatvam upapadyate. bahutvāt padārthānām, padasamudāyasya ca pṛthagartho nāstīty uktam. bhedaḥ saṃsargo vā vākyārtha iti yady ucyate, tathāpy ekārthatā na syāt, bahupade bhedānāṃ saṃsargāṇāṃ ca bahutvāt. ekaprayojanatvād upapannam, yathā tāvad devasya tveti nirvāpaprakāśanam, tasya viśiṣṭasya vācaka etāvān padasamūhaḥ, tat vākyam. nanv atra devasya tvā savituḥ prasave nirvapāmīty ekaṃ vākyam, aśvinor bāhubhyāṃ nirvapāmīty aparam, evaṃ bahūni vākyāni. yadi nirvapāmīty anuṣaṅgaḥ, tato bahūni vākyāni, na tv evam anuṣaṅgo bhavati, yadi guṇabhūto nirvapāmīti, tadā pratipradhānaṃ bhidyeta. na ca nirvāpo devasya tvetyevamādīnām arthenocyate, sādhanaprādhānye hy adṛṣṭārthatā vacasya syāt. nirvāpe punaḥ pradhāne dṛṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ nirvāpaprakāśanam, tat sarvair viśeṣaṇair viśiṣṭam ucyate. tasmād avirodhaḥ. yathā ca padaṃ padena viśeṣyate tathoktaṃ tadbhūtānām iti{*2/158*}. tasmād ekaṃ vākyam.
atha kiṃ artham ubhayaṃ sūtritam, arthaikatvād iti ca vibhāge sākāṅkṣatvād{*2/159*} iti ca, ucyate, bhavati kiṃcid ekārtham, na tu vibhāge sākāṅkṣam, yathā bhago vāṃ vibhajatu, aryamā vāṃ vibhajatv ity ekārthāḥ sarve vibhāgam abhidadhati. nanu bhagaviśiṣṭād vibhāgād aryam aviśiṣṭo 'nyo vibhāgaḥ. nety ucyate, [133]{*2/160*} vibhāgasāmānyenāsya prayojanam, na viśeṣeṇa, sāmānye hi dṛṣṭo 'rtho bhavati, na viśeṣe, vibhāge tu na sākāṅkṣam. tasmād bhinnam idaṃ vākyaṃ vibhāge vikalpyate. tathā syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghṛtasya dhārayā susevaṃ{*2/161*} kalyayāmi{*2/162*}. tasmin sīdāmṛte pratitiṣṭha vrīhīṇāṃ medhaḥ sumanasyamāna iti{*2/163*} vibhāge sākāṅkṣam, dve tu prayojane kriyete, sadanakaraṇaṃ puroḍāśapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ ca. tasmād bhinne vākye, pūrvaṃ sadanakaraṇe viniyujyate, uttaraṃ{*2/164*} puroḍāśapratiṣṭhāpane. tasmāt samyak sūtritam, na sūtropālaṃbho bhavati.
children.translated_text:
Now, among <s>yajus</s>-mantras recited in continuous form, how is it determined that 'this much is one <s>yajus</s>'? Whatever group of words is used in the sacrifice — that group of words is one <s>yajus</s>. And how much is used? As much as is needed to illuminate the assistance to the ritual action — that much, being what needs to be stated, is called a 'sentence' (<s>vākya</s>). Therefore it is said: 'A sentence is one because of unity of purpose' — if from this cause there is sentence-unity. Therefore, a group of words with a single purpose is a sentence, provided that when divided, the [individual] words would have syntactic expectancy. What is the example? 'Of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, by the impulse.' [Objection:] But here each word has its own meaning. [Reply:] True, but when [the words are] divided, they do not have [syntactic] expectancy [that would be unfulfilled]. [Objection:] Then the unity of purpose is not established — because of the multiplicity of word-meanings. And it has been said that the aggregate of words has no meaning separate [from the word-meanings]. [Reply:] If it is said that the sentence-meaning is either the [mutual] exclusion or the combination [of word-meanings], even so there would be no unity [of purpose], since in a multi-word [sentence] there are many exclusions and combinations. [The unity] is established because of serving a single purpose. For example, 'of the god, you' illuminates the [ritual of] offering (<s>nirvāpa</s>) — the group of words that expresses that specific [meaning] is the sentence. [Objection:] But here, 'of the god, you, of <s>Savitṛ</s>, by the impulse, I offer' is one sentence, and 'of the two <s>Aśvins</s>, by the arms, I offer' is another — thus there are many sentences. [Reply:] If 'I offer' is carried over [to each clause], then there would be many sentences. But such carrying-over does not occur if 'I offer' is subordinate. In that case, [the sentence] would be divided for each primary [element]. And the offering is not expressed by [phrases] such as 'of the god, you' and the like [as their primary meaning]; for if the instrument were primary, the statement would serve an unseen [transcendent] purpose. But when the offering is primary, the visible function is the illumination of the offering — that is stated with all its qualifiers as qualified. Therefore, there is no contradiction. And just as one word is qualified by another word, so it has been stated in 'of those that are components thereof.' Therefore, [it is] one sentence.
Now, why are both stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — 'because of unity of purpose' and 'if, when divided, [there would be] syntactic expectancy'? It is said: Something may have unity of purpose but not syntactic expectancy when divided. For example, 'May <s>Bhaga</s> divide for you, may <s>Aryaman</s> divide for you' — all have a single purpose, namely division. [Objection:] But <s>Bhaga</s>-qualified division is different from <s>Aryaman</s>-qualified division. [Reply:] No, it is said — the purpose here is the general [notion of] division, not the specific [qualified versions]. For the visible purpose is in the general, not in the specific; and in [the case of] division, there is no syntactic expectancy [when the clauses are separated]. Therefore, this sentence, when divided, yields alternatives. Similarly, 'I make a comfortable seat for you; I sprinkle [it] well with a stream of ghee. Sit upon it, O immortal, take your stand; O glory of the rice-grains, being pleased' — when divided, there is syntactic expectancy, but two purposes are served: the making of the seat and the establishment of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake). Therefore, [when] the sentence is divided, the first part is applied to the making of the seat, the second to the establishment of the <s>puroḍāśa</s>. Therefore, [the <s>sūtra</s>] is well formulated; there is no fault in the <s>sūtra</s>.

[TEXTUAL NOTES: Edition page numbers — E2: 2,435; E4: 2,522; E5: 3,383; E6: 1,90; source Taittirīya-saṃhitā 1.1.4.2; cf. MS 1.1.25; E5,6 read <s>sākāṅkṣatvāt</s>; E2,4 read <s>sākāṅkṣam</s>; editions vary on <s>suśevaṃ</s>/<s>suṣevam</s> and <s>kalpayāmi</s>/<s>kalyayāmi</s>; source Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa 3.7.5.2-3; E2 reads <s>uttare</s>.]

children.text: sameṣu vākyabhedaḥ syāt // MS_2,1.47 //
children.translated_text: In [the case of clauses with] the same [purpose], there should be sentence-division. // MS 2.1.47 //

children.text:
īṣe tvā, ūrje tveti{*2/165*}, tathā - āyuryajñena kalpatām, prāṇo yajñena kalpatām iti{*2/166*}. atra sandehaḥ, kim evamādiṣu bhinnaṃ vākyam utaikam iti? ekam iti brūmaḥ, īṣe tvety evam ukte na kiṃcid dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam, tathā - ūrje tvety api ca, vacanasāmarthyād adṛṣṭam, tad ubhābhyām ekaṃ kalpayituṃ nyāyyam, evam alyīyasy adṛṣṭānumānakalpanā bhaviṣyati. tasmād ekaṃ vākyam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sameṣu vākyabhedaḥ syāt, sameṣu parasparānākāṅkṣeṣu vākyaṃ bhidyate, īṣe tvety anenaiko 'rthaḥ kriyate, ūrje tvety anenāparaḥ. nanu idānīm evoktaṃ nātra dṛṣṭo 'rtha iti. yady api pratyakṣādinā pramāṇena nopalabhyate, śrutyā tu gamyate, īṣe tveti chinati, ūrje tvety anumārṣṭīti{*2/167*}. tathā - āyuryajñena kalpatām, prāṇo yajñena kalpatām ity āyuḥkḷpter anyā prāṇakḷptiḥ. nanu sāmānyamātram idaṃ tan na viśeṣaṇabhedād bhedam arhatīti, yathā - agnaye juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmīti [134]{*2/168*} nirvāpa ekas tasya viśeṣāḥ savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ puṣṇo{*2/169*} hastābhyām iti, na teṣāṃ bhedān nirvāpasya bheda iṣyate, evam ihāpi kḷptir nāmaiko 'rthaḥ, nāsāv āyurādibhir viśeṣair bhinno bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate - iha kḷptīr vācayatīti bahvaḥ{*2/170*} kḷptayaḥ śrūyante, tāś ca vaktavyāḥ, tatraikām āyuḥkḷptim āyuḥyajñena kalpatām ity eṣa mantraḥ śaknoti vaditum, prāṇo yajñena kalpatām ity ayam api prāṇakḷptim aparām, evaṃ tu sarve kḷptiviśeṣavacanāḥ, tac ca dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam. tasmād anekārthatvāt tatrāpi vākyabheda iti. nanu sāmānyavacanād ekatvaṃ yathā vibhāge. naitad evam, vibhāge dṛṣṭārthaṃ sāmānyam iha na. api ca kḷptīr vācayatīti vihitam, āyuḥyajñena kalpatām iti cāyuḥkḷptyabhidhānam abhinivartyate pratyakṣam. prāṇo yajñena kalpatām iti ca prāṇakḷpteḥ. tasmād vākyabhedaḥ.
children.translated_text:
'For nourishment, you'; 'for vigor, you' — and likewise: 'May life be established through the sacrifice'; 'May breath be established through the sacrifice.' Here the doubt [arises]: in such cases, is the sentence divided or one? We say: one. 'For nourishment, you' — when stated thus, no visible purpose is served. Likewise 'for vigor, you.' From the power of the statement, [there is] an unseen [purpose]; it is proper to construe a single [unseen purpose] from both — thus there will be less recourse to inferring unseen [entities]. Therefore, [it is] one sentence.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: In [the case of clauses with] the same [purpose], there should be sentence-division — when [the clauses] are the same [in structure] and do not have syntactic expectancy for each other, the sentence is divided. 'For nourishment, you' — by this, one purpose is served; 'for vigor, you' — by this, another. [Objection:] But it was just said that no visible purpose [is served] here. [Reply:] Even if it is not apprehended by a means of valid knowledge such as perception, it is understood from scripture — 'for nourishment, you' [means] he cuts; 'for vigor, you' [means] he wipes. Similarly, 'May life be established through the sacrifice'; 'May breath be established through the sacrifice' — the establishment of life is different from the establishment of breath. [Objection:] But this is merely a generality that does not warrant division because of the differentiation of qualifiers. Just as 'I offer what is pleasing to <s>Agni</s>' — the offering is one, and its qualifiers 'by <s>Savitṛ's</s> impulse,' 'by the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>,' 'by the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>' — because of the differentiation of those [qualifiers], the division of the offering is not sought. So too here, [the] establishment is a single meaning, and it will not be divided by the qualifiers 'life' and the like. [Reply:] It is said: Here, 'he causes the establishments' — thus many establishments are heard, and they must be stated. Among those, this <s>mantra</s> can state one [establishment] — the establishment of life — through 'May life be established through the sacrifice'; and this [other <s>mantra</s>] can state another — the establishment of breath — through 'May breath be established through the sacrifice.' Thus all [<s>mantras</s>] state specific establishments, and that is a visible purpose. Therefore, because of multiplicity of meanings, sentence-division [applies] there too. [Objection:] But because of the general statement, [there should be] unity, as in [the case of] division [discussed earlier]. [Reply:] This is not so. In [the case of] division, the general [notion] has a visible purpose; here it does not. Moreover, 'he causes the establishments' is enjoined, and 'May life be established through the sacrifice' is a manifest statement about the establishment of life. And likewise about the establishment of breath by 'May breath be established through the sacrifice.' Therefore, [there is] sentence-division.

[TEXTUAL NOTES: Sources — Taittirīya-saṃhitā 1.1.3, Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā 1.1 and Taittirīya-saṃhitā 1.7.9.1; cf. Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa 1.1.6.6, 1.7.1.2, 4.3.1.7; edition page numbers; E2,4,6 read <s>pūṣṇo</s>; E2,4,5,6 read <s>bahvyaḥ</s>.]

children.text: anuṣaṅgo vākyasamāptiḥ sarveṣu tulyayogitvat // MS_2,1.48 //
children.translated_text: Carrying-over (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) [provides] sentence-completion for all [clauses], because of equal applicability. // MS 2.1.48 //

children.text:
yā te agne 'yāśayā tanūrvarṣiṣṭhā gahvareṣṭhā, ugraṃ vaco apāvadhīt tveṣaṃ vaco apāvadhīt svāhā, yā te agne rajāśayā, yā te agne harāśayety{*2/171*} atra sandehaḥ, tanūrvarṣiṣṭheti kiṃ sarveṣv anuṣaktavyam, āhosvil laukiko vākyaśeṣaḥ kartavya iti. kiṃ prāptam? yā te agne rajāśayety etasya tanūr-varṣiṣṭheti na vākyaśeṣaḥ, na hy ayam asmāt paraḥ prayujyate. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - anuṣaṅgo vākyasamāptiḥ syāt tanūrvarṣiṣṭheti, yathaiva hy ayaṃ yā te agne 'yāśayety etasyānantaram, evaṃ yā te agne rajāśayā, yā te agne harāśayety etayor api. harāśayety etasya vyavahita iti cet. tan na, samudāyasyāvyavadhānāt, avyavahito rajāśayeti samudāyaḥ [135]{*2/172*} samudāyena ca vākyaśeṣasya saṃbandhābhāvāt samudāyibhyāṃ saṃbandhaḥ, samudāyisaṃbandhe ca na gamyate viśeṣaḥ. tasmāt sarvatrānuṣaṅgaḥ.
api ca sākāṅkṣasya sannidhau paras tātpurastād vā paripūrṇasamarthaḥ śrūyamāṇo vākyaśeṣo bhavati. kiyāṃs tu kālaḥ sannidhir iti? ucyate - yāvati śaknoty ubhāv apy apekṣitum. kaś cāsau? ānantaryaṃ saṃbandhipadavyavāyo vā, tāvati hi śaknoty ubhāv apy apekṣitum, saṃbandhipadavyavāye hi saṃbandhād eva pūrvasaṃskāro nāpaiti. yatrāpy apareṇa sākāṅkṣena vyavāyas tatrāpy asti saṃbandhaḥ, dvayor api hi kāryaṃ vaktavyam iti, paraḥ pūrvam apekṣate, anapekṣamāne 'nyataraḥ pramādapāṭhaḥ syāt, śakyate cāsāv apekṣitum, tasmād yathaivāyam ekasya sannidhāv evam aparasya, dvayor apy asaṃbaddhaiḥ padair avyavahitatvāt, dvayor apy ākāṅkṣator{*2/173*} etāvac ca vākyaśeṣasaṃbandhe kāraṇam, nānantaryam, avyavadhāne vicchede 'pi bhavati saṃbandhaḥ. tasmād anuṣaṅgaḥ.
atheha kathaṃ bhavitavyam? yatra nirākāṅkṣāṇāṃ sannidhau paripūraṇasamarthaḥ śrūyate, yathā citpatis tvā punātu, vākypatis tvā punātu, devasya tvā{*2/174*} savitā punātv achidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhir iti{*2/175*}, atra hi punātv antāni paripūrṇāni na kiṃcid ākāṅkṣanti. nanv achidreṇety etad ākāṅkṣiṣyati{*2/176*}. satyam ākāṅkṣati, ākāṅkṣad apy etad ekam ākāṅkṣet, ekenaivaitan{*2/177*} nirākāṅkṣaṃ saṃpadyata iti, ekena hi nirākāṅkṣīkṛto netarāv ākāṅkṣiṣyati, an-arthakatvād ākāṅkṣati, ekena ca saṃbaddho nānarthako bhavati. tasmān netarāv ākāṅkṣatīti, itarāv api paripūrṇatvān na tam ākāṅkṣataḥ. nanv etasya vākyaśeṣasyaikam apy ākāṅkṣato na gamyate viśeṣaḥ, kena nirākāṅkṣīkriyate, kena vā neti. tenānavagamyamāne viśeṣe sarvaiḥ saha saṃbhantsyate. āha, naitad evam, yenāsya pratyakṣam ānantaryam upalabhāmahe tena saha saṃbhantsyata iti gamyate viśeṣaḥ, tasmāt tenānantareṇa saha saṃbha[136]{*2/178*}ntsyata iti nāsti sarvatrānuṣaṅga iti. āha - naitad evam, punātuśabdenāsya pratyakṣam ānantaryam upalabhāmahe, punātuśabdasyāpi citpatis tvetyevamādibhiḥ, ekaś cāsau punātuśabdaḥ punaḥ punar uccaritaḥ, tenāvagacchāmaḥ, yatra punātuśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ, tatra tenaikavākyatvād achidreṇety ayam api prayoktavyaḥ, tathā ca sati citpatis tvetyevamādayo vinā punātuśabdena, sākāṅkṣāḥ, te ca punātuśabdam ākāṅkṣanti, sa ca punātuśabdo 'chidreṇety anena viśiṣṭaḥ, tena punātuśabdena sānuṣaṅgeṇa niyogataḥ sarve nirākāṅkṣīkartavyāḥ. tasmāt sarveṣu tulyaprayogā iti vākyaparisamāptir anuṣajyate.
children.translated_text:
'O <s>Agni</s>, that form of yours which rests on the ground, which is body-dwelling and cavity-dwelling — the fierce word has struck it down, the sharp word has struck it down, <s>svāhā</s>; that form of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, which rests on dust; that of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, which rests on green [vegetation]' — here the doubt arises: should '<s>tanūrvarṣiṣṭhā</s>' (body-dwelling) be carried over (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) to all [the mantra-verses], or should ordinary sentence-completion be applied? What is the prima facie view? For 'O <s>Agni</s>, that which rests on dust,' '<s>tanūrvarṣiṣṭhā</s>' is not a sentence-complement, for it is not applied after that [clause]. When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: The sentence-completion should be carried over (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) — that is, '<s>tanūrvarṣiṣṭhā</s>' [applies to all]. For just as it immediately follows 'O <s>Agni</s>, that which rests on the ground,' so too it [applies to] 'O <s>Agni</s>, that which rests on dust' and 'O <s>Agni</s>, that which rests on green [vegetation].' [Objection:] But 'that which rests on green [vegetation]' is separated [from it]. [Reply:] Not so, because the aggregate is not separated. The aggregate — '[that which rests on] dust' — is unseparated, [Page 135] and since the sentence-complement has no connection with the aggregate [as a whole], the connection is with the members of the aggregate. And when connected with the members of the aggregate, no distinction is apprehended. Therefore, carry-over [applies] everywhere.
Moreover, when a syntactically incomplete [expression] is heard in proximity — whether after or before it — [an expression] capable of completing [it] is heard, that is a sentence-complement (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>). But how long is the 'proximity'? It is said: as long as one is able to regard both [as connected]. And what is that? Immediate succession, or the intervening of a related word — for to that extent one is able to regard both. For when a related word intervenes, the prior impression does not fade because of the very connection. Even where the intervention is by another syntactically incomplete [expression], there too there is a connection — for since the purpose of both must be stated, the latter regards the former. If it did not regard it, one of the two would be a careless recitation. And it is possible to regard it. Therefore, just as [the complement connects] with one in proximity, so with the other — because both are not separated by unrelated words, and because both are syntactically incomplete. And just this much is the reason for the connection of the sentence-complement — not immediate succession [alone]. Even when there is separation without a break, there is connection. Therefore, there is carry-over.
But here, how should it be [when the expressions are syntactically complete]? Where a [word] capable of completing [the sentence] is heard in the proximity of syntactically complete [expressions] — as in 'May the lord of the mind purify you, may the lord of speech purify you, may the divine <s>Savitṛ</s> purify you with an unfailing filter, with the rays of the sun that is wealth' — here, the [clauses] ending in 'may he purify' are complete and do not expect anything. [Objection:] But 'with an unfailing [filter]' is expected [by one of them]. [Reply:] True, it is expected. But even if expected, it would expect just one [clause]; being connected with one alone, [the expression] becomes syntactically complete. For once made complete by one [clause], it will not expect the other two, since that would be purposeless — it is expected [by one], and being connected with one, it is not purposeless. Therefore, it does not expect the other two — and the other two, being [already] complete, do not expect it either. [Objection:] But since no distinction is apprehended as to with which one of these clauses this sentence-complement [connects] — by what is it made complete, and by what not? [Reply:] In that case, when the distinction is not apprehended, it will connect with all of them. [Śabara] says: This is not so. We perceive its direct immediate succession with one [clause], and from that the distinction is apprehended that it will connect with that [immediately succeeding clause]. Therefore, it will connect with the immediately succeeding one, [Page 136] and there is no carry-over everywhere. [Śabara] says: This is not so. We perceive its direct immediate succession with the word 'may he purify' (<s>punātu</s>). And [the word] 'may he purify' itself [is in immediate succession] with 'the lord of the mind, you' and so forth. And that word 'may he purify' is one, uttered again and again. Therefore, we understand that wherever the word 'may he purify' is used, there, because of sentence-unity with it, this 'with an unfailing [filter]' too is to be used. And this being so, [the expressions] 'the lord of the mind, you' and so forth, without the word 'may he purify,' are syntactically incomplete. And they expect the word 'may he purify.' And that word 'may he purify' is qualified by 'with an unfailing [filter].' Therefore, by that word 'may he purify' — together with its carry-over — all [clauses] must necessarily be made syntactically complete. Therefore, since the application is equal in all, the sentence-completion is carried over.

NOTES:

children.text: vyavayān nānuṣajyeta // MS_2,1.49 //
children.translated_text: Because of separation, [the complement] should not be carried over. // MS 2.1.49 //

children.text: saṃ te vāryur{*2/179*} vātena gacchatām, saṃ jayatrair aṅgāni{*2/180*}, saṃ yajñapatir āśiṣā{*2/181*} iti. vāryur{*2/182*} vātena gacchatām ity eṣa saṃ yajatrair aṅgānīti bahuvacanāntana vyavahitatvāt saṃyajñapatir āśiṣety atra nānuṣajyata{*2/183*}, ekena sākāṅkṣeṇa vyaveto{*2/184*} gacchatām iti śeṣaḥ, tato bahuvacanāntena saṃ yajatrair aṅgānīty etena saṃbandham anupetya vyavetatvāt pareṇa na saṃbadhyate, gamyate hi tadā viśeṣaḥ, ekena vyaveta iti, gamyamāne viśeṣe na tatra bhāvo vākyaśeṣasyopapadyate. tasmād bahuvacanāntasya parasya ca tadvyapetasya laukiko vākyaśeṣaḥ kartavya iti.
children.translated_text: 'May your vitality go together with the wind, may [your] limbs [go together] with the victorious ones, may the lord of the sacrifice [go together] with blessing' — [in this passage:] 'May the vitality go together with the wind' — this [clause], because of being separated by the plural-ending [clause] 'may [your] limbs [go together] with the victorious ones,' does not carry over to 'may the lord of the sacrifice [go together] with blessing.' [The complement] 'may it go' is the sentence-completion of the first [clause], which is syntactically incomplete. Then, [after] the plural-ending [clause] 'may [your] limbs [go together] with the victorious ones' intervenes — because the connection [with the complement] has not been established across the [plural-ending] intervention — it does not connect with the subsequent [clause]. For then the distinction is apprehended — that it is separated by one [intervening clause]. When the distinction is apprehended, the sentence-complement's connection there is not justified. Therefore, for the plural-ending [clause] and the subsequent one that is separated from it, ordinary sentence-completion should be applied.
Page 137

children.text: śabdāntare karmabhedaḥ kṛtānubandhatvāt // MS_2,2.1 //
children.translated_text: When there is a different word, [there is] a difference of ritual action, because [each word] has already formed its own connection. // MS 2.2.1 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭomas tatra śrūyate - somena yajeta, dākṣiṇāni juhoti, hiraṇyamātreyāya dadātīti{*2/186*}; yajati - dadāti - juhotayas te kiṃ saṃhatya kāryaṃ kurvanti, uta viyutyeti saṃśayaḥ, sādhakāḥ saṃhatyāpi sādhayanto dṛśyante, viyutyāpi. saṃhatya tāvat, trayo grāvāṇa ekāmukhāṃ dhārayanto dṛśyante, nāgadantakās tu viyutyāpi, ekaikasmin hi śakyate śikyam avalambayitum. ato yajati, dadāti, juhotavyaḥ saṃhatya sādhayeyur viyutya veti jāyate saṃśayaḥ.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam, saṃhatyeti. kutaḥ? adṛṣṭārthānām upakārakalpanālpīyasī nyāyyeti. katham?
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; there it is heard: 'He sacrifices with <s>Soma</s>'; 'he offers the southern oblations'; 'he gives gold to the <s>Ātreya</s> [priest].' [The verbs] '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), '<s>dadāti</s>' (he gives), and '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers) — do they accomplish a purpose jointly, or separately? This is the doubt. Agents are seen to accomplish [a purpose] both jointly and separately. Jointly — as when three grinding stones, supporting a single hook, are seen [working together]. But separately too — as with elephant-tusk [pegs], for a rope-sling can be hung on each one individually. Therefore, the doubt arises: do '<s>yajati</s>,' '<s>dadāti</s>,' and '<s>juhoti</s>' accomplish [the purpose] jointly or separately?
What is the prima facie view? That they [work] jointly. Why? Because the postulation of auxiliary factors for the unseen [result] is lesser [and hence more proper] [when they are combined]. How so?

children.text:
adṛṣṭo yo 'śruto vārthaḥ, sa nāstīty avagamyate/
tasminn asati dṛṣṭaś cet śruto vā na virudhyate//
children.translated_text:
An unseen or unheard purpose is understood as non-existent;
when it is [thus] non-existent, if the seen or heard [result] is not contradicted [it remains non-existent];

children.text:
virudhyamāne kalpyaḥ syāj jāyate tena so 'rthavān/
viśeṣaś cen na gamyeta, tato naiko 'pi kalpyate//
children.translated_text:
When there is contradiction, [the unseen] should be posited, and thereby that [contradiction] becomes meaningful;
but if no distinction is apprehended, then not even one [unseen entity] is posited.

children.text:
gamyate ca viśeṣaḥ, bahubhya ekam apūrvam iti. tasmāt samudāyaś cikīrṣitaḥ, tato hy adṛṣṭe kalpyamāne, avayavānāṃ samudāyaṃ praty arthavattvād ekam apūrvaṃ samudāyāt kalpitaṃ bhaviṣyati. na ca, aśabdaḥ samudāyaḥ, avayavaśabdair eva samudāyasyoktatvāt. tasmāt samudāyaś cikīrṣitaḥ. atha vā yajetety etasya pūrvo bhāgo [138]{*2/187*} yajaty arthaṃ bravīti, uttaras tam eva{*2/188*} bhāvayed ity anuvadati, evaṃ juhotīti pūrvo bhāgo juhoty artham, uttaras tam evānuvadati. tenaikasyāṃ bhāvanāyāṃ trayo yajaty ādaya upāyā vidhīyante śrutyā. tasmād etair yāgadānahomair viśiṣṭāpūrvasya bhāvanā pratīyate, ata ucyate - saṃhatyaikam apūrvaṃ sādhayantīti. yad vā yajatiśabdena vihitaṃ dānaṃ dānahomaśabdenānūdyate guṇasambandhārtham, tasmād ekam apūrvam iti prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - pratiśabdam apūrvabheda iti, śabdāntare karmabhedaḥ kṛtānubandhatvāt, yajetety anena kevalasya yāgasya kartavyatocyate, na tu juhotiśabdābhihitasya dadātiśabdābhihitasya vā, śabdāntaratvāt. prayogavākyaśeṣabhāvena hi samudāyasya sattāsambandho gamyate, śrutyāvayavasya, yajeta - iti sannihitayor api vākyena dānahomayoḥ, śrutyā yāgasyaiva sattāsambandho gamyate, na dānahomayoḥ. śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī. tasmān na samudāyaḥ śabdaḥ, kalpyamāno hi prayogavacanenaikavākyatāṃ nītvā kalpyeta, śabdāntaraṃ ca yajater dadātiḥ. tatra yady api paro bhāgo bhāvanāvacanaḥ sarveṣu samānaḥ, tathāpy ekaikasya pūrvo 'vayavo 'nyaḥ, anyaś ca tena samudāyaḥ śabdāntaram anyasmāt samudāyāt, tatrārthāntaraṃ vyaktam, dadyād iti dānena sādhayed iti kevalam eva dānaṃ karaṇaṃ bhāvanāyāḥ pratīyate, na yāgahomau sahāyāv apekṣate. tathā juhotīti homasādhanāṃ bhāvanām āha, na dānayāgāv apekṣate. tatraitāvac chabdenāvagatam, dānena kevalena sidhyatīti juhotīty api homena kevalena sidhyatīti, na tu dānena kevalena sidhyatīti vijñānam nivartate. dadāti tarhi svena kārakagrāmeṇa kṛtānubandho na yāgaṃ homaṃ vānubandham apekṣate. tasmād bhinnāni vākyani, pratiśabdam apūrvabhedaḥ [139]{*2/189*} iti. na ca dānasya yajati juhotir vānuvādo yāgahomayor avivakṣāprasaṅgāt. na ca dānam itarayor anuvādaḥ, parasvatvārthatvād dadāteḥ, itarayoś ca tyāgārthatvāt. prayojanaṃ pūrvapakṣe samudāyād apūrvam, siddhānte tu yāgasya phalavattvād itarayor guṇabhāvaḥ.
children.translated_text:
And a distinction is apprehended — [namely,] one <s>apūrva</s> from many [actions]. Therefore, the aggregate is intended. For when the unseen is being posited, since the component [actions] are meaningful with respect to the aggregate, one <s>apūrva</s> posited from the aggregate will suffice. And the aggregate is not [something] un-denoted by words, because the aggregate is [already] denoted by the words of its components. Therefore, the aggregate is intended. Alternatively — the first part of '<s>yajeta</s>' [Page 138] expresses the meaning of sacrifice, and the latter part restates that very [meaning as] 'he should bring into being.' Similarly, the first part of '<s>juhoti</s>' expresses the meaning of oblation, and the latter part restates it. Therefore, in a single productive power (<s>bhāvanā</s>), three [actions] — sacrifice, gift, and oblation — are enjoined as means by the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>). Therefore, a productive power qualified by these — sacrifice, gift, and oblation — is understood for a single <s>apūrva</s>. Hence it is said: jointly they accomplish one <s>apūrva</s>. Or alternatively, the gift — enjoined by the word '<s>yajati</s>' — is restated by the words for giving and offering for the purpose of connecting [it with] subsidiary elements. Therefore, the <s>apūrva</s> is one — this is the prima facie view.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: there is a difference of <s>apūrva</s> for each word. When there is a different word, there is a difference of ritual action, because [each word] has already formed its own connection. '<s>Yajeta</s>' — by this, the obligation of sacrifice alone is expressed, not [the obligation] of what is denoted by the word '<s>juhoti</s>' or the word '<s>dadāti</s>,' because they are different words. It is through being a syntactic complement in a statement of procedure (<s>prayogavākya</s>) that the connection of the aggregate with existence is understood; [but] by the direct expression, [only] the connection of the component [is understood]. Even when both — gift and oblation — are proximate through the sentence, by the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) it is the connection of sacrifice alone with existence that is understood, not of gift and oblation. And the direct expression is stronger than the sentence. Therefore, the aggregate is not [denoted by] the word. For [the aggregate,] when being posited, would be posited by bringing [the procedure-sentence] into a single sentence [with the direct expression]. But a different word from '<s>yajati</s>' is '<s>dadāti</s>.' There, even though the latter part — the productive-power statement — is the same in all [verbs], still the first component of each is different. And therefore the aggregate is a different word from another aggregate. And therein the difference of meaning is clear — '<s>dadyāt</s>' (he should give): by giving alone, as the [sole] instrument of productive power, [the result] is understood — [giving] does not require sacrifice and oblation as auxiliaries. Similarly, '<s>juhoti</s>' expresses a productive power whose instrument is oblation alone — it does not require gift and sacrifice. Thus, this much is understood from the word: 'by giving alone it is accomplished'; and from '<s>juhoti</s>' too, 'by oblation alone it is accomplished.' But the understanding 'by giving alone it is accomplished' does not cease [when combined with others]. Gift, therefore, having formed its own connection with its own set of auxiliary factors, does not require sacrifice or oblation as auxiliaries. [Page 139] Therefore, the sentences are separate; the <s>apūrva</s> is different for each word. And the gift is not a restatement of sacrifice or oblation — for that would lead to the non-intention of sacrifice and oblation [i.e., they would be rendered meaningless]. Nor is the gift a restatement of the other two — because '<s>dadāti</s>' means transferring to another's ownership, while the other two mean relinquishing [to the deity]. The practical consequence: according to the prima facie view, the <s>apūrva</s> [comes] from the aggregate; according to the established conclusion, because the sacrifice alone has a stated result, the other two [gift and oblation] are subsidiary to it.

children.text: ekasyaivaṃ punaḥśrutir aviśeṣād anarthakaṃ hi syāt // MS_2,2.2 //
children.translated_text: If the same [word] is repeated, [it is] without distinction; for [a mere repetition] would be purposeless. // MS 2.2.2 //

children.text:
samidho yajati, tanūnapātaṃ yajatītyevamādiḥ{*2/190*} pañcakṛtvo 'bhyasto yajatiśabdaḥ kim ekam apūrvaṃ codayati, kiṃ pratyabhyāsam apūrvabheda iti. śabdāntare karmabheda uktaḥ, iha sa eva śabdaḥ punaḥ punar uccāryate. tasmād ekam evātrāpūrvam. nanv apūrvāntaram avidadhad anarthako bhavati. satyam evāprayojano bhavati, bahukṛtvo 'pi coccāryamāṇo nānyārtho bhavati, yat prathame uccāraṇe{*2/191*} gamyate, śatatame 'pi{*2/192*} tad eva gamyate. tasmāt pañcakṛtvo 'bhyasto yajatiśabda ekam apūrvaṃ codayati. na cābhyāso 'narthako bhaviṣyati, tanūnapādādīr devatā vidhāsyati, tasmād ekam apūrvam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ekasyaivaṃ punaḥśrutiḥ syāt, karmabhedaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ. tāvaty eva vidhīyamāne 'sati kasmiṃścid viśeṣe punaḥśrutir anarthakā bhavet. nanūktaṃ na śaknoty arthāntaraṃ vidhātum iti. ucyate - samidho yajatīty api prathamo 'nuvāda eva, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti yāgaḥ prāpta eva. tatra devatā na śakyā vidhātum, śrutiprāptā hi tatra devatā, iyaṃ vākyāt prakaraṇād vā, tayor vikalpo na nyāyyaḥ, sa eṣa devatāyāgasaṃbandho [140]{*2/193*} vidhīyamāno 'kriyamāṇe yāge na śakyaḥ kartum ity anarthakaḥ syāt. kriyamāṇe tu śakyate. tasmād abhyasitavyo yāgaḥ, pratyabhyāsaṃ cādṛṣṭabheda{*2/194*} iti, na ca yat samitsaṃbandhena kriyate, tat tanūnapātsaṃbandhena, bhinnatvāt tayoḥ, ato na vikalpaḥ. prayojanaṃ{*2/195*} pūrvapakṣe sakṛt prayoga iti, siddhānte punaḥ punaḥ prayoga iti.
children.translated_text:
The word <s>yajati</s> (he sacrifices), as in 'he sacrifices to <s>Samidh</s> (kindling wood),' 'he sacrifices to <s>Tanūnapāt</s>' and so on, is repeated five times. Does it enjoin a single unprecedented [result] (<s>apūrva</s>), or is there a difference of unprecedented [result] with each repetition? [In previous cases,] the differentiation of ritual actions was established by the use of different words; here, the very same word is uttered again and again. Therefore, there is only a single unprecedented [result] here. [Objection:] But if it does not enjoin a different unprecedented [result], it is purposeless. [Reply:] True, it is indeed purposeless — even when uttered a hundred times, it does not acquire a different meaning; what is understood at the first utterance is understood at the hundredth too. Therefore, the word <s>yajati</s>, repeated five times, enjoins a single unprecedented [result]. And the repetition will not be purposeless — it will enjoin the deities <s>Tanūnapāt</s> and the others. Therefore, [there is] a single unprecedented [result].
Having arrived at this [prima facie view], we say: The re-hearing of the same [word] would result in a differentiation of ritual actions — this is the meaning. If only that much were being enjoined [i.e., a single rite], the re-hearing in some particular [context] would be purposeless. [Objection:] But it was said that [the repeated word] cannot enjoin a different meaning. [Reply:] It is said: even 'he sacrifices to <s>Samidh</s>' — the first [occurrence] is itself merely a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>); for the sacrifice has already been obtained from [the injunction] 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> [rites].' There, the deity cannot be enjoined [by the repeated word], for the deity there is obtained from <s>śruti</s> — this one from the sentence, that one from the context — and an alternative between them is not proper. This connection between deity and sacrifice, which is being enjoined, would be purposeless if the sacrifice were not being performed — but when it is being performed, it can be [enjoined]. Therefore, the sacrifice must be repeated, and with each repetition there is a difference of unseen [result]; for what is done in connection with <s>Samidh</s> is not the same as what is done in connection with <s>Tanūnapāt</s>, since the two are different. Hence there is no alternative. The practical consequence: in the prima facie view, a single performance; in the established conclusion, repeated performance.

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 2.6.1.1-2] | [E2,4 variant: yat prathamaṃ uccāryamāṇe] | [E2,4 variant: śatakṛtvo 'pi] | [Edition page references: E2: 3,15; E4: 3,20; E5: 2,415; E6: 1,96] | [E2,4 variant: vāpūrva] | [E2,4 variant: pakṣoktaṃ]

children.text: prakaraṇaṃ tu paurṇamāsyāṃ rūpāvacanāt // MS_2,2.3 //
children.translated_text: But the context [indicates that it is] on the full-moon [day], because of the non-mention of form. // MS 2,2.3 //

children.text: evaṃ hi samāmananti - yad āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavati{*2/196*}; tāv abrūtām agnīṣomāv ājyasyaiva tāv upāṃśu{*2/197*} paurṇamāsyāṃ yajann iti; tābhyām etam agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ paurṇamāse prāyacchat{*2/198*}; aindraṃ dadhyamāvāsyāyām aindraṃ payo 'māvās-yāyām iti{*2/199*}. tathāghāram āghārayati{*2/200*}; ājyabhāgau yajati, sviṣṭakṛte samavadyati, patnīsaṃyājān yajati, samiṣṭayajur juhoti{*2/201*}. tathā ya evaṃ vidvān paurṇamāsīṃ yajate, ya evaṃ vidvān amāvāsyāṃ yajata iti{*2/202*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - sarvāṇy etāni samapradhānāni, utāgneyādīni payontāni pradhānāni, āghārādīny ārādupakārakāṇy aṅgāni? tathā, ya evaṃ vidvān ity evaṃ saṃyuktau prakṛtānāṃ karmaṇām anuvaditārau, atha vā ya evaṃ vidvān paurṇamāsīṃ yajate, ya evaṃ vidvān amāvāsyāṃ yajata ity apūrvayoḥ karmaṇor vidhātārau, tatretare guṇavidhaya iti. kiṃ{*2/203*} prāptam - śabdāntara-tvād abhyāsāc ca samapradhānānīti prāpte brūmaḥ{*2/204*} - prakaraṇaṃ tu paurṇamāsyām, prakṛtānām āgneyādīnām anuvaditārau paurṇamāsyamāvāsyāsaṃyuktau. kutaḥ? rūpāvacanāt, ya evaṃ vidvān paurṇamāsīsaṃjñakaṃ yāgaṃ yajata iti na sarve yāgā [141]{*2/205*} ucyante, yaḥ paurṇamāsīsaṃjñakaḥ sa vidhīyate, na caitad evam avagacchāmaḥ, kīdṛśam evaṃsaṃjñakasya yāgasya rūpam iti, te na{*2/206*} kiṃcit pratipadyemahi. ato brūmaḥ - yady apūrvasya vidhātārāv anarthakāv iti. atha nu prakṛtānām anuvaditārau, tataḥ sannihitāḥ paurṇamāsyamāvāsyāsaṃyuktā yāgā iti gamyate rūpam, tatrārthavattā vacanasya. kathaṃ punar ekavacanānto bahūnāṃ vācako bhaviṣyatīti yady ucyate. samudāyaśabdatayāvakalpiṣyate, rūpavanto hi pūrvaprakṛtā yāgāḥ, teṣāṃ ca pracayaśiṣṭaḥ samudāyo 'py asti tadapekṣo 'yam arūpaśabdaḥ, tasmād ekavacanāntatā na doṣaḥ, bhavati hi bahūnām ekavacanāntaḥ śabdaḥ samudāyāpekṣaḥ, yathā - yūthaṃ vanaṃ kulaṃ pariṣad iti. yadāgneyādīnāṃ samudāyavacanāvetau, tadā darśapaurṇamāsaśabdenaita evābhidhīyante. tata eṣāṃ phalasaṃbandhaḥ, phalavat sannidhes tv āghārādīny ārādupakārakāṇīti.
children.translated_text: For this is how they teach: 'The <s>Āgneya</s> (related to <s>Agni</s>) eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] is constant on both the new-moon and full-moon [days]'; 'The two said: <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, with ghee alone, the two offering in silence on the full-moon day'; 'He gave to them this eleven-<s>kapāla</s> <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [cake] at the full-moon'; '<s>Aindra</s> (related to <s>Indra</s>) curds on the new-moon day, <s>Aindra</s> milk on the new-moon day.' Similarly, 'he offers the <s>āghāra</s> (preliminary offering)'; 'he sacrifices the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions), he cuts at [the rite of] <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, he sacrifices the <s>Patnīsaṃyājas</s> (wives' offerings), he offers the <s>Samiṣṭayajus</s>.' Also, 'he who, knowing thus, sacrifices on the full-moon day; he who, knowing thus, sacrifices on the new-moon day.' There the doubt arises: are all these of equal principal status, or are the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others up to the milk-offering the principal ones, while the <s>āghāra</s> and the others are subsidiary elements (<s>aṅga</s>) that assist from a distance? Also, regarding 'he who, knowing thus' — are these two [sentences] re-statements (<s>anuvāda</s>) of the rituals already established in the context, or are they injunctions of two unprecedented ritual actions, [namely] 'he who, knowing thus, sacrifices on the full-moon day' and 'he who, knowing thus, sacrifices on the new-moon day,' in which case the others are quality-injunctions? What is the prima facie view? Because of the use of different words and because of repetition, they are of equal principal status — having arrived at this, we say: But the context [indicates that it is] on the full-moon [day]; the two [sentences] connected with full-moon and new-moon are re-statements of the previously established <s>Āgneya</s> and other [rites]. Why? Because of the non-mention of form — 'he who, knowing thus, sacrifices the sacrifice called full-moon' — not all sacrifices are being referred to; what is being enjoined is the sacrifice called 'full-moon.' And we do not understand thus — what is the form of a sacrifice of such a name — we would not understand anything. Therefore, we say: if [the two sentences] were injunctions of unprecedented [rites], they would be purposeless. But if they are re-statements of previously established [rites], then the form — namely, the sacrifices connected with the full-moon and new-moon [days] that are proximate — is understood, and the statement is meaningful. As for [the objection] 'how would a singular-ending [word] denote many [rites]?' — it will be construed as a collective term. For the previously established sacrifices have [specific] forms, and their aggregate too, taught by accumulation, exists. This formless word depends on that [aggregate]. Therefore, the singular ending is not a defect; for there are indeed singular-ending words for many [things] when depending on an aggregate, such as 'herd,' 'forest,' 'family,' 'assembly.' When these two are collective terms for the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [rites], then these very [rites] are denoted by the words <s>Darśapaurṇamāsa</s>. From that comes their connection with the fruit; and because of the proximity to [the sentence bearing] the fruit, the <s>āghāra</s> and the others are subsidiary elements that assist from a distance.

children.translated_text: This is not so — [that] the two [sentences] connected with full-moon and new-moon are collective terms. Rather, they are injunctions of two unprecedented ritual actions. If so, there will be no characterizing term. [Objection:] But there is no form [specified]. [Reply:] We shall understand the form from another sentence. 'On the full-moon day, there is an eight-<s>kapāla</s> <s>Āgneya</s> [cake]' — this is the form of the full-moon ritual: <s>Agni</s> is the deity, the sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) is the substance. Therefore, by the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others, a quality is being enjoined.

children.text:
karmacodanā vāgneyādayaḥ syuḥ. kutaḥ? guṇānāṃ yugapac chāsanāt, ekenaiva vākyenātrāneko guṇo vidhātum iṣyate bhavatā, na ca, śabdāntareṇa codite karmaṇy aneko guṇaḥ parasparasaṃbandhe cāsati śakyate vidhātum. katham? yadi tāvat paurṇamāsyām aṣṭākapālo bhavatīti saṃbandho vivakṣitaḥ, na tadāyam artho 'ṣṭākapālaḥ sat tayābhisaṃbadhyata iti, kas tarhy aṣṭākapālaḥ paurṇamāsyābhisaṃbandhyata iti? tatra tadā bhavatir vartate, tadānīm āgneya ity ayam asyāntikād apy upanipatito bhavati saṃbandhābhāvān nānena saṃbandham arhati, aṣṭākapāla āgneyo bhavatīti. athāgneyaḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ bhavatīti vivakṣyate. tadāgneyapuroṅāśayor asaṃbandha eva syāt. atha paurṇamāsyām aṣṭākapālasyāgneyatā vidhīyate. vaktavyam{*2/211*}, kena tasyām aṣṭākapālo vihita iti. atha tasyām āgneyasyāṣṭākapālatā. tathāpy eṣa doṣaḥ{*2/212*}. atha paurṇamāsīty ubhābhyāṃ saṃbadhyeta.
paraspareṇa dravyadevatayor asaṃbandha eva{*2/213*} syāt. atha dravyadevate paraspareṇa viśiṣṭe satyau paurṇamāsyā saṃbadhyeyātām ity ucyate. āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo yaḥ, sa paurṇamāsyāṃ bhavatīti, tasyāprasiddhatvād etad apy ayuktam. atha kenacid agnaye saṅkalpitaḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ vidhīyate. tathāpi devatāyā avidhānād rūpābhāva eva. athāgnir devatā bhaviṣyatīti kaścid brūyāt. sa [143]{*2/214*} vaktavyaḥ - mithaś cānarthasaṃbandha iti, na hy āgneyaśabdo 'nuvādo vidhiś ca bhavatīti. kalpayiṣyāmo devatām iti cet. na, asati vidhāne devatāyā abhāvāt. saṃbandhiśabdo 'yaṃ devateti sa evāgnir aṣṭākapālasya devatā, nājyasya. tasmād avaśyam āgneyāṣṭākapālasaṃbandho vidhātavyaḥ, sa eṣa yāgo bhavatīti, tena paurṇamāsīyāgasyāparo yāgaḥ saṃbandhī vidhīyate, na dravyaṃ devatā vā. na ca yāgasya yāgāntaraṃ rūpaṃ bhavati. ato rūpāvacanāt paurṇamāsyam āvāsyāsaṃyuktau nāpūrvayoḥ karmaṇor vidhātārau. yat tūktam - paurṇamāsyamāvāsyāśabdau lakṣaṇayā prakṛtān yāgānanuvadituṃ śaknuto nāñjasyeneti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, yadāñjasyena śabdārtho nāvakalpate, tadā lakṣaṇayāpi kalpyamānaḥ sādhur bhavati, yathā, agnau tiṣṭhati, avaṭe tiṣṭhati, agnisamīpe, avaṭasamīpe tiṣṭhatīti bhavati saṃvyavahāraḥ. lakṣaṇāpi hi laukikyeveti.
children.translated_text:
Or, the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others would be injunctions of ritual actions. Why? Because of the simultaneous teaching of the qualities by a single sentence — you wish to enjoin multiple qualities by a single sentence, but when a ritual action has been enjoined by a separate word, multiple qualities cannot be enjoined in the absence of mutual connection. How? If the intended connection is 'on the full-moon day, there is an eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake],' then the meaning is not 'what is [already] eight-<s>kapāla</s> is thereby connected [with the full-moon].' Rather, [the question is:] what eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] is connected with the full-moon? There, the verb 'is' (<s>bhavati</s>) functions [to denote existence]. Then '<s>Āgneya</s>' (related to <s>Agni</s>), though proximate, in the absence of a connection, should not be connected with it — [i.e., one cannot say] 'the eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] is <s>Āgneya</s>.' If it is intended that 'there is an <s>Āgneya</s> [cake] on the full-moon day,' then there would be no connection between <s>Āgneya</s> and the sacrificial cake at all. If the <s>Āgneya</s> nature of the eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] is being enjoined on the full-moon day, then one must state by what [authority] the eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] has been enjoined for that [day]. If the eight-<s>kapāla</s> nature of the <s>Āgneya</s> [cake is being enjoined] — the same defect [applies]. If [both] are to be connected with 'full-moon' —
There would be simply no connection between the substance and the deity with each other. If it is said that the substance and deity, being mutually specified, would then be connected with the full-moon — [that is,] 'that which is <s>Āgneya</s> and eight-<s>kapāla</s>, that exists on the full-moon' — since that [combination] is not well-known, this too is improper. If [it is said] that [a cake] intended for <s>Agni</s> by someone is [then] enjoined on the full-moon — even so, since the deity is not [separately] enjoined, there is simply no form [specified]. If someone were to say '<s>Agni</s> will be the deity' — to that one should reply: 'there would be a mutual connection of purposelessness,' for the word <s>Āgneya</s> cannot be both a re-statement and an injunction. [Objection:] We shall postulate the deity. [Reply:] No — in the absence of an injunction, the deity does not exist. This word '<s>devatā</s>' (deity) is a relational word; that very <s>Agni</s> is the deity of the eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake], not of the ghee. Therefore, the connection between <s>Āgneya</s> and eight-<s>kapāla</s> must necessarily be enjoined — 'this sacrifice exists' — and thereby another sacrifice is enjoined as connected with the full-moon sacrifice, not a substance or a deity. And a sacrifice does not have another sacrifice as its form. Therefore, because of the non-mention of form, the two [sentences] connected with full-moon and new-moon are not injunctions of unprecedented ritual actions.
As for what was said — 'the words full-moon and new-moon can denote the previously established sacrifices only by figurative usage, not directly' — this is not a defect. When the direct meaning of a word does not work, even a figuratively construed [meaning] is valid. Just as [one says] 'he stands in the fire' or 'he stands in the pit' — [meaning] 'he stands near the fire' or 'near the pit' — this is how the convention works. For figurative usage too is indeed part of ordinary [language].

children.text: jāmi vā etad yajñasya kriyate yad anvañcau puroḍāśāv upāṃśuyājam antarā yajatīti{*2/216*}, viṣṇur upāṃśu yaṣṭavyo 'jāmitvāya, prajāpatir upāṃśu yaṣṭavyo 'jāmitvāya, agnīṣomāv upāṃśu yaṣṭavyāv ajāmitvāya iti. tatra sandehaḥ - upāṃśuyājamantarā yajatīti kiṃ viṣṇvādiguṇakānāṃ prakṛtānāṃ yāgānāṃ samud-āyasya vācakaḥ, atha vāpūrvasya yāgasyeti. tata ucyate - paurṇamāsīvad upāṃśuyājo bhavitum arhati. kutaḥ - nāmasaṃbandhāt, nāmasaṃbaddho hi viśiṣṭo yāgaḥ śrūyate, upāṃśuyājasaṃjñakaḥ, na ca dravyadevate rūpam, prakṛtāś copāṃśuguṇakā yāgā vidyante. tasmāt samudāyaśabda iti. nanūpāṃśuguṇakaṃ yāgāntaram upāṃśutvena rūpeṇa rūpavad vidhīyate. na evaṃjātīyakaḥ śabda upāṃśuviśiṣṭaṃ yāgaṃ śaknoti vaktum, upāṃśuyāga iti hi tasya vaktā, cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyator{*2/217*} iti{*2/218*} kutvena bhavitavyam, avyutpannaḥ punar upāṃśuyājaśabdaḥ. tasmān na rūpavad yāgāntaram. athāpi nāmasaṃyuktaṃ yajatisāmānyam eva, tathāpy anupadiṣṭadevatādravyarūpaṃ na yāgāntaraṃ pratipadyemahi. nanv evaṃ sati prakṛtānām apy avācakaḥ prāpnoti. mā bhūd upāṃśuyājaśabdaḥ, yajatiśabdo bhaviṣyati, tathā saty upāṃśuyājaśabde 'py anuvādatvād anāñjasye 'pi na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: 'This creates kinship-monotony (<s>jāmi</s>) in the sacrifice — that one sacrifices two offering cakes (<s>puroḍāśas</s>) in succession with the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice in between.' '<s>Viṣṇu</s> should be worshipped silently (<s>upāṃśu</s>) for the sake of non-kinship (<s>ajāmitva</s>); <s>Prajāpati</s> should be worshipped silently for the sake of non-kinship; <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> should be worshipped silently for the sake of non-kinship.' There, the doubt arises: does 'he sacrifices with the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice in between' denote the aggregate of the basic (<s>prakṛta</s>) sacrifices qualified by <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the other [deities], or a novel sacrifice? To this it is said: the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice should be like the full-moon sacrifice. Why? Because of the connection with the name — for a specific sacrifice, connected with a name, is heard — one designated by the name '<s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>' — and the substance and deity are not its form; and the basic sacrifices qualified by the <s>upāṃśu</s> quality do exist. Therefore, it is a term for the aggregate. [Objection:] But a different sacrifice qualified by the <s>upāṃśu</s> quality is enjoined with the <s>upāṃśu</s> nature as its characteristic form. [Reply:] No — a word of this kind cannot denote a sacrifice distinguished by the <s>upāṃśu</s> [quality], for it would have to say '<s>upāṃśuyāga</s>' — and by the rule '<s>cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ</s>' [Pāṇ. 7.3.52], the <s>ku</s>-substitution should apply — but the word '<s>upāṃśuyāja</s>' is underived [from this rule]. Therefore, it is not a different sacrifice with a characteristic form. But even if [it is] merely the general sense of '<s>yajati</s>' (sacrificing) connected with the name, even so, we would not accept [that it denotes] a different sacrifice whose deity and substance are not taught. [Objection:] But in that case, [the word] would fail to denote even the basic [sacrifices]. [Reply:] Let it not be the word '<s>upāṃśuyāja</s>' — the word '<s>yajati</s>' will [serve]; in that case, even for the word '<s>upāṃśuyāja</s>' too, since it is a restatement, there is no fault in the indirectness.

children.text: codanā vāprakṛtatvāt // MS_2,2.10 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] an injunction, because [those sacrifices] are not basic (<s>prakṛta</s>). // MS_2,2.10 //

children.text: karmāntarasya vācakaḥ syāt, upāṃśuyājaṃ yajatīti. kutaḥ? prakṛtānāṃ yāgānām abhāvāt, na cet prakṛtā vidyanta{*2/220*}, kasya samudāyaṃ vakṣyati? nanv idānīm evoktaṃ viṣṇvādiguṇakāḥ prakṛtā yāgā vidyanta iti. na vidyante, na hi, te vidhayo viṣṇur upāṃśu yaṣṭavya ityevamādayaḥ. arthavādā hi te. katham? asmin vākye vidhyantarasya bhāvāt, upāṃśuyājam antarā yajatīti etad etasmin vākye vidhī-yate. yadīme 'pi vidhīyeran, bhidyeta{*2/221*} tarhi vākyam. api ca - yāgasya viṣṇvādināṃ ca saṃbandho 'tra gamyate vākye, na ca yāgasya vidhānam. nanu ca, upāṃśuyājam antarā yajatīty atrāpy antarālasaṃbandho 'vagamyate. vāḍham{*2/222*}, sa tu vidhīyata upāṃśutvādisaṃbandhaḥ. ekaṃ hīdaṃ vākyaṃ nānekaṃ vidhātum arhati. katham? jāmi vā etad yajñasya kriyata ity evam upakramam etad vākyam ajāmitvāyety evam antam, tasya madhye samāmnātaṃ viṣṇvādivākyaṃ tena saṃbandhya-mānaṃ na vākyāntaraṃ bhavitum arhati. tasmād viṣṇur upāṃśu yaṣṭavya ityevamādayo na vidhayaḥ, kiṃ tarhy arthavādāḥ. kaḥ punar arthavādaḥ? āgneyāgnīṣomīyayor nirantaraṃ kriyamāṇayor jāmitādoṣa uktaḥ, taṃ bhiṣajitum, upāṃśuyājam antarā yajatīti vihitam. kathaṃ tena bhiṣajiṣyate? tasmin kriyamāṇe jñāyata eva, yathā viṣṇur yaṣṭavyaḥ prajāpatir agnīṣomau ceti{*2/223*}, tataś ca vyavadhānād ajāmitāvagamyata eva, tenājāmitārthavādaṃ vakṣyāmīti viṣṇvādisaṃbandho 'nūdyate, na tv antarālasaṃbandhasyānyat prayojanam asty ato vidhānāt. kathaṃ viṣṇvādayo yaṣṭavyā ity etad avagamyate? yaṣṭavyān ayaṣṭavyān vā viṣṇvādīn upāṃśuyājābhiṣṭavāya saṅkīrtayatīti gamyate. [146]{*2/224*} tatra kecit tāvad āhuḥ - prāptā eveti. kutaḥ? śākhāntare vidhānād iti. yady apy aprāptiḥ, tathāpy upāṃśutvasāmānyāt prajāpatir devatā viṣṇuś cety anuvādāv eva, upāṃśudharmāṇau hi viṣṇuprajāpatī, tasmād yatkiñcit prājāpatyaṃ yajñe kriyate, tad upāṃśv eva kriyata ityevamādisaṅkīrtanān mantrasamāmnānāc ca viṣṇum aprāptam api prāptam iva vadet. agniṣomayos tu vidhāyakam udāhriyate - etāv abrūyātām{*2/225*} agnīṣomāv vājyasyaiva tāv upāṃśu paurṇamāsyāṃ yajan iti, tasmād yāgāntaram.
children.translated_text: It would denote a different ritual action — 'he sacrifices the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice.' Why? Because the basic sacrifices do not exist. If the basic [sacrifices] do not exist, whose aggregate will it denote? [Objection:] But it was just said that the basic sacrifices qualified by <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the other [deities] do exist. [Reply:] They do not exist. For those [passages] — '<s>Viṣṇu</s> should be worshipped silently' and so on — are not injunctions. They are <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages). How? Because another injunction exists in this sentence: 'he sacrifices the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice in between' — this is what is enjoined in this sentence. If these too were enjoined, the sentence would be split. Moreover, the connection of the sacrifice with <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the other [deities] is understood here in [this] sentence, but the sacrifice itself is not [newly] enjoined. [Objection:] But in 'he sacrifices the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice in between' too, the in-between connection is understood. [Reply:] Indeed, but the connection with the <s>upāṃśu</s> quality and the like is [what is] being enjoined. For this is a single sentence — it cannot enjoin multiple [things]. How? This sentence begins with 'this creates kinship-monotony in the sacrifice' and ends with 'for the sake of non-kinship.' The <s>Viṣṇu</s>-passage recited in the middle thereof, being connected with [the whole sentence], cannot constitute a separate sentence. Therefore, '<s>Viṣṇu</s> should be worshipped silently' and so on are not injunctions, but rather <s>arthavāda</s>. But what kind of <s>arthavāda</s>? The fault of kinship-monotony was stated when the <s>Āgneya</s> and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [offerings] are performed without interruption. To remedy that, 'he sacrifices the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice in between' was enjoined. How will that remedy [it]? When that is being performed, it is known that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and <s>Agni</s>-<s>Soma</s> are to be worshipped; and from that separation, non-kinship is understood. Thus [the text says] 'I shall state the <s>arthavāda</s> about non-kinship' — the connection with <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like is restated, but the in-between connection has no other purpose beyond this injunction. How is it understood that <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others are to be worshipped? Whether <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others are to be worshipped or not, [the text] mentions them for the purpose of praising the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice — this is understood. Some indeed say: they are already established [as objects of worship]. Why? Because they are enjoined in another <s>Śākhā</s> (Vedic branch). Even if they were not established, still, because of the commonality of the <s>upāṃśu</s> quality, <s>Prajāpati</s> as deity and <s>Viṣṇu</s> are merely restated, for <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> have the <s>upāṃśu</s> quality. Therefore, whatever <s>Prājāpatya</s> (for <s>Prajāpati</s>) [offering] is performed in the sacrifice is performed silently — from such mentions and from the <s>mantra</s>-tradition, one would speak of even the unestablished <s>Viṣṇu</s> as if established. But for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, an injunctive [passage] is cited: 'Those two said' — <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> [are relevant] in the [context of] the ghee; those two [should be worshipped] silently on the full-moon day when sacrificing. Therefore, [the <s>Upāṃśu</s>-sacrifice] is a different sacrifice.

children.text: guṇopabandhāt // MS_2,2.11 //
children.translated_text: Because of the attachment of a subsidiary quality. // MS_2,2.11 //

children.text: yad ucyate, na jñāyate, katamo 'sāv upāṃśuyājasaṃjñako yāga iti, yasyāyaṃ guṇa upabaddhaḥ, upāṃśu paurṇamāsyāṃ yajan iti. tasmān na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: What is said — 'it is not known which sacrifice is designated by the name <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>' — to this: that to which the subsidiary quality is attached — 'he sacrifices silently on the full-moon day.' Therefore, there is no defect.

children.text: prāye vacanāc ca // MS_2,2.12 //
children.translated_text: Because of the statement in a context dominated [by the principal]. // MS_2,2.12 //

children.text: pradhānakarmaprāye vacanam, pradhānakarmatām upodbalayati, yathā, agryaprāye likhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaved ayam agrya iti matiḥ. tasmān na samudāyaśabda iti.
children.translated_text: The statement occurs in a context dominated by the principal ritual action; it supports the principal-action nature. Just as, upon seeing a written [record] in a context dominated by the foremost, one would judge 'this must be the foremost.' Therefore, it is not a term for the aggregate.

children.text: āghārāgnihotram arūpatvāt // MS_2,2.13 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Āghāra</s> and <s>Agnihotra</s> [are not different sacrifices], because of the absence of a distinctive form. // MS_2,2.13 //

children.text: āghāram āghārayatīti{*2/226*} śrūyate, tathemāny aparāṇi, ūrdhvam āghārayati, santatam āghārayati, ṛjum āghārayatītyevamādi{*2/227*}. idaṃ cāgnihotraṃ juhoti, tathā, dadhnā juhoti, payasā juhotītyevamādi. tatra sandehaḥ - kim ūrdhvam [147]{*2/228*} āghārayati, dadhnā juhotītyevamādibhir āghārā homāś ca vihitāḥ, teṣām āghāram āghārayati, agnihotraṃ juhotīty etau samudāyānuvādau, utaitāv evāpūrvayor āghārahomayor vidhātārāv iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? nāpūrvayor vidhī iti. kutaḥ? arūpatvāt, na hi, etayoḥ pūrvebhyo homāghārebhyo viśiṣṭaṃ rūpam asti. yataḥ karmāntaram adhyavaseyam. ataḥ prakṛtatvāt{*2/229*} prakṛtānuvādau.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'He performs the <s>āghāra</s> (pouring oblation).' Similarly, these other [statements]: 'He pours upward, he pours continuously, he pours straight' and so on. Also: 'He offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>'; similarly, 'He offers with curds, he offers with milk' and so on. There, the doubt arises: are the <s>āghāra</s> (pourings) and <s>homa</s> (oblations) enjoined by 'he pours upward, he offers with curds' and the like, while 'he performs the <s>āghāra</s>' and 'he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>' are aggregate restatements of those? Or are these very [terms] the enjoiners of novel <s>āghāra</s> and <s>homa</s> [rites]? What is first arrived at? They are not injunctions of novel [rites]. Why? Because of the absence of a distinctive form — for these [terms] have no distinctive form different from the previously [mentioned] oblations and pourings, by which a different ritual action could be determined. Therefore, because of the [already] existing [basic rites], they are restatements of the basic [rites].
