children.text: saṃjñopabandhāt // MS_2,2.14 //
children.translated_text: Because of the attachment of a designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>). // MS_2,2.14 //

children.text: saṃjñopabandhaś ca bhavati, agnihotraṃ nāma homaṃ juhotīti, āghārasaṃjñakaṃ karma karotīti, saṃjñāviśiṣṭāvāghārahomau vidhīyete. na ca vijñāyate{*2/230*}, ko 'sāv āghāro nāma karmaviśeṣaḥ, kaś āgnihotrasaṃjñaka iti. nanu vijñāyate, āghāraṇam āghāraḥ, havanaṃ homaḥ. yady āghāraṇasāmānyaṃ homasāmānyaṃ ca vidhīyete, vijñātapūrvau tarhy āghārahomau, tenānuvādau. athāvyutpannā ubhayor api saṃjñā, tathāpi nāghārāgnihotrasāmānyam ucyeta, viśeṣāśrayatvāt saṃjñāyāḥ. na ca, sa viśeṣo gamyata ity apūrvāvāghārahomavidhī nāvakalpyete. api ca kathaṃ kriyā sādhanaśabdenocyeta? īpsitatamaṃ hi yat sādhanam, tat dvitīyāntenocyate, kriyā tiṅantena. anuvādapakṣe kriyāṇāṃ samudāyo 'rthāntaram, tat īpsitatamaṃ sādhanaṃ bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: And there is the attachment of a designation: 'he offers the oblation called <s>Agnihotra</s>'; 'he performs the ritual act called <s>āghāra</s>' — the <s>āghāra</s> and <s>homa</s> are enjoined as distinguished by their designations. And it is not known what particular ritual act is called <s>āghāra</s>, and which is designated by the name <s>Agnihotra</s>. [Objection:] But it is known — <s>āghāra</s> is the act of pouring, <s>homa</s> is the act of offering. [Reply:] If the general [acts of] pouring and offering are enjoined, then the <s>āghāra</s> and <s>homa</s> are previously known, and therefore they are merely restatements. But even if the designation is underived for both, still the general [sense of] <s>āghāra</s> and <s>Agnihotra</s> would not be stated, because the designation is based on a specific [referent]. And that specific [referent] is not known — hence the injunctions of novel <s>āghāra</s> and <s>homa</s> cannot be construed. Moreover, how can a ritual action be expressed by a word denoting an instrument? For the most desired instrument is expressed by the accusative [case-ending], while the action is expressed by the finite verb. In the restatement view, the aggregate of actions constitutes a different meaning — that will be the most desired instrument.

children.text: aprakṛtatvāc ca // MS_2,2.15 //
children.translated_text: And because [they are] not basic (<s>prakṛta</s>). // MS_2,2.15 //

children.text: na ca, prakṛtam api dravyadevatam āghāre vidyate. yena rūpavān syāt. tasmād etāv api samudāyaśabdāv iti.
children.translated_text: Nor is there any basic substance-and-deity [combination] found in the <s>āghāra</s>, by which it would have a distinctive form. Therefore, these too are terms for the aggregate.

children.text: codanā vā śabdārthasya prayogabhūtatvāt, tatsannidher guṇārthena punaḥ-śrutiḥ // MS_2,2.16 //
children.translated_text: Or [they are] injunctions, because the meaning of the word serves as the performance; the repetition [of the word] in their proximity is for the purpose of the subsidiary element. // MS_2,2.16 //

children.text:
na caitad asti, samudāyaśabdāv iti, karmāntaracodane syātām. kutaḥ? śabdārthasya prayogabhūtatvāt, āghārayati, juhotīti, homāghārau prayoktavyāv iti śabdārthaḥ, tena karmāntare vidhīyeta ity avagacchāmaḥ. āghārāgnihotraśabdau ca havanāghāraṇasāmānyavācinau prajñātau, ato nāvijñātārthau. tena rūpavantau santau vidhīyete.
yad uktam, ūrdhvam āghārayati, dadhnā juhotītyevamādibhir vihitatvād anuvādāv iti. naitad evam, na hy ete homāghārau vidhātuṃ śaknuvanti. ūrdhvam āghārayati, dadhnā juhotīti ca naitad uktaṃ bhavati, āghāraḥ kartavyaḥ, homaḥ kartavya iti, kiṃ tarhi, ūrdhvatāghārasaṃbandhaḥ kartavyaḥ, dadhihomasaṃbandhaḥ kartavya iti. tasmād arāptatvān nānuvādau. nanu saṃbandhe vihita arthād dhomāghārau bhaviṣyataḥ. naitad evam, asmin hi sati vidhānena saṃbandhaḥ. tasmān nārthād āpadyete homāghārau, ato 'pūrvau vidhīyeta iti brūmaḥ.
nanv āghārayati, juhotīti homāghāragato vyāpāraḥ śrūyate, na dadhyūrdhvatādisaṃbandhaḥ. satyaṃ na śrūyate. tasmin nidher guṇārthena vyāpāraśravaṇam avakalpiṣyate. nanu padārthāntaragataṃ vyāpāraṃ śrutir na śaknoti vaditum. satyam evam etat, svapadārthagataṃ vakṣyati, taṃ tu svapadārthaṃ guṇaśabdo viśekṣyati, sa eva{*2/232*} viśiṣṭaḥ pratyeṣyata iti bhaved etat, viśiṣyāt svapadārthaṃ guṇaśabdaḥ, na tv eṣa{*2/233*} guṇagato vyāpāraḥ pratīyeta. tatra kiṃ bhaviṣyati? avyāpriyamāṇe 'pi guṇe śabdārthāvakḷpto bhaviṣyati. guṇavacanasannidhir idānīṃ kim arthaḥ? anarthakas tu. kathaṃ punar anarthako [149]{*2/234*} nāma vedo{*2/235*} bhavitum arhati? saty arthe nānarthakaḥ, asati tv arthe kim anyad ucyeta. evaṃ tarhi vākyād bhaviṣyati, śrutyarthe sati na vākyārtho 'vakalpyate. satyam evam etat. avivakṣite tv avakalpiṣyate. katham avivakṣā? guṇavacanasyāpramādapāṭhāt, svapadārthasya ca śabdāntareṇa vihitatvāt. tasmāt siddham - guṇārthena dadhnā juhotītyevamādīnāṃ punaḥśrutiḥ{*2/236*}. juhoter uccāraṇaṃ cānuvādo guṇasaṃbandhārthaḥ. yadi juhotīty anuvādaḥ,
kenedānīṃ guṇo vidhīyate? dadhiśabdeneti mā vocata. nanv idānīm eva vākyād guṇavyāpāro{*2/237*} gamyata ity uktam. satyam evam etat, avidhīyamānas tu kuto gamyata iti, pramāṇam asya nāvagamyeta. asati pramāṇe vyāmohaḥ syāt. evaṃ tarhi vidhāyakau juhotyāghārayatiśabdau. kasya tarhy anuvādaḥ? dhātvarthasyeti brūmaḥ.
yadi vidhāyakau, pūrvam eva vihite svārthe, kim arthaṃ punar uccāryete? vākyārtho yas taṃ vidhātum ity adoṣaḥ. tasmāt karmāntaracodane. yad uktam - nāsty āghāre prakṛtaṃ dravyadevatam iti. kim evaṃ sati dravyadevatena, yadā prasiddhārthābhidhānān nirjñātam evāsya rūpam. api ca, caturgṛhītaṃ vaitad abhūt tasyāghāram āghāryety ājyamasya dravyam, māntravarṇiko devatāvidhiḥ, indra ūrdhvo 'dhvaro divi spṛśatu mahato yajño yajñapata indravān svāhetyāghāram āghārayatīti{*2/238*}, evam asāv indravān yady asyendro devatā, tad yadi devatābhidhānam etad āghārasya, tato 'nenāghāraḥ kṛto bhavati. tasmāt karmāntare, na samudāyaśabdāv iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
Nor is it the case that they are aggregate-words, [for] they would [then] enjoin a different ritual action. Why? Because the meaning of the word pertains to [ritual] performance. '<s>Āghārayati</s>' (he pours the <s>āghāra</s>-libation), '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers) — the meaning of the word is that the <s>homa</s> (oblation) and <s>āghāra</s> (libation) are to be performed. From that, we understand that a different ritual action is being enjoined. And the words <s>āghāra</s> and <s>agnihotra</s> are known as generic terms for the acts of offering and pouring. Therefore, they are not terms with unknown meanings. Hence, having [known] form, they are enjoined.
As to what was said — 'Because they are [already] enjoined by [passages such as] "he pours the <s>āghāra</s> upwards" and "he offers with curds," they are re-statements' — this is not so. For these [passages] are not capable of enjoining the <s>homa</s> and <s>āghāra</s> [themselves]. 'He pours the <s>āghāra</s> upwards' and 'he offers with curds' — this does not say 'the <s>āghāra</s> is to be performed' or 'the <s>homa</s> is to be performed'; rather, [it says] 'the connection of upward-direction with the <s>āghāra</s> is to be made' and 'the connection of curds with the <s>homa</s> is to be made.' Therefore, since [the <s>homa</s> and <s>āghāra</s> themselves] are not attained [from those passages], they are not re-statements. [Objection:] Surely, when the connection is enjoined, the <s>homa</s> and <s>āghāra</s> will follow by implication. This is not so, for the connection exists only when it is [specifically] enjoined. Therefore, the <s>homa</s> and <s>āghāra</s> do not arise by implication; hence, we say they are enjoined as unprecedented.
[Objection:] But in '<s>āghārayati</s>' and '<s>juhoti</s>,' the activity inherent in the <s>homa</s> and <s>āghāra</s> is heard, not the connection with curds, upward-direction, and so on. True, [the connection] is not heard [directly]. But when [the <s>homa</s> and <s>āghāra</s>] are deposited [i.e., already established], the hearing of [their] activity will be construed as serving the purpose of [their] qualities. [Objection:] But scripture cannot speak of an activity that belongs to another referent. True, that is so — it will speak of [the activity] belonging to its own referent; but the quality-word will qualify that very referent, and that qualified [referent] will be understood. It may be so — the quality-word would qualify its own referent — but this activity pertaining to the quality would not be understood. What then would result? Even when the quality is not active, it would be construed from the meaning of the word. But what then is the purpose of the proximity of the quality-expression? It would be purposeless. But how can the <s>Veda</s> be purposeless? When there is a meaning, it is not purposeless; but when there is no meaning, what else can be said? In that case, it will [be understood] from the sentence — but when there is a meaning from direct hearing (<s>śruti</s>), a sentence-meaning is not construed. True, that is so. But when [the direct meaning] is not intended, [the sentence-meaning] will be construed. How is [the direct meaning] not intended? Because the quality-expression is not an erroneous recitation, and because its own referent is [already] enjoined by another word. Therefore, it is established — for the purpose of [specifying] the quality, '<s>dadhnā juhoti</s>' (he offers with curds) and similar [passages] involve a re-hearing [of the verb]. And the utterance of '<s>juhoti</s>' is a re-statement for the purpose of connecting the quality. If '<s>juhoti</s>' is a re-statement,
then by what is the quality now enjoined? Do not say 'by the word <s>dadhi</s> (curds).' For it has just been said that the quality-activity is understood from the sentence. True, that is so. But how is [the quality] understood when it is not being enjoined? Its authoritative basis would not be known. And in the absence of an authoritative basis, there would be confusion. In that case, '<s>juhoti</s>' and '<s>āghārayati</s>' are injunctive words. Of what, then, are they re-statements? Of the root-meaning, we say.
If they are injunctive, then since their own meaning was [already] enjoined before, why are they uttered again? To enjoin the sentence-meaning — there is no defect [in this]. Therefore, [they enjoin] a different ritual action. As to what was said — 'In the <s>āghāra</s>, there is no established substance and deity' — what need for substance and deity, when the form [of the ritual] is already known from the expression of well-known meanings? Moreover, there was [already] the four-fold taking [of ghee]: 'For that [<s>āghāra</s>], he pours the <s>āghāra</s>-libation' — ghee is its substance. The deity-injunction is from the <s>mantra</s>-wording: '<s>Indra</s>, may the upward sacrifice touch heaven, great [is] the sacrifice, O lord of sacrifice, endowed with <s>Indra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>' — he pours the <s>āghāra</s>-libation. Thus, if <s>Indra</s> is [invoked as] 'endowed with <s>Indra</s>' and if this is the deity-designation of the <s>āghāra</s>, then by this [mantra] the <s>āghāra</s> has been performed. Therefore, [these words enjoin] a different ritual action, and they are not aggregate-words — this is established.
Page 150

children.text: dravyasaṃyogāc codanā paśusomayoḥ, prakaraṇe hy anarthako dravyasaṃyogo na hi tasya guṇārthena // MS_2,2.17 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*2/240*}, tatredam āmananti, hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyati, atha jihvāyāḥ, atha vakṣasa iti{*2/241*}. tathā{*2/242*} somena yajeteti, tatrāpi{*2/243*}, aindravāyavaṃ gṛhṇāti, maitrāvaruṇaṃ gṛhṇāti, āśvinaṃ gṛhṇātītyevamādi. tatra saṃśayaḥ, kim avadyati gṛhṇāti{*2/244*} - coditānāṃ karmaṇām evālabhatiyajatī samudāyasyānuvaditarau, athāpūrvayoḥ karmaṇor vidhātārāv iti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? samudāyasyeti. kutaḥ? ye ime ālabhatiyajatibhyāṃ karmaṇī vidhīyeyātām iti cintyete, pūrvam eva ta avadyatigṛhṇātibhyām avagamite. na cāvagamito 'rtho vidhīyate. hṛdayādīṃs tu paśuśabdenānuvadati, somaśabdena ca rasam. tasmāt somena yajetety anuvādo yajatiḥ yajeta svargakāma iti{*2/245*} phalasambandhārthaḥ. paśum ālabheteti cālabhatir agnīṣomasaṃbandhārthaḥ. api ca, daśaitān adhvaryuḥ prātaḥsavane grahān gṛhṇātīti samuccayo dṛśyate. tathāśvino daśamo gṛhyate, tṛtīyo hūyata iti ca kramaḥ. yadi cāpūrvau yāgau vidhīyete, tatraindravāyavādibhir devatā vidhīyeran, tā ekārthāḥ santyo vikalperan. yathā, khādire badhnāti, pālāśe badhnāti rohitake badhnātīti. tatra kramasamuccayadarśane nopapadyeyātām, atha punar asmin samudāyavacane, yajatau samyag etad avakḷptaṃ bhavati. tasmāt samudāyānuvādau.
[151]{*2/246*} evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - apūrvayoḥ karmaṇor vidhānacodane paśusomayoḥ. kutaḥ? soma-śabdaḥ kṣīriṇyāṃ latāyāṃ prasiddho na rase, ākṛtivacano hi somaśabdo na vyaktivacanaḥ. tathā, śṛṅgiṇi pucchavati lomaśe catuṣpadi dravyaviśeṣe paśuśabdam ākṛtivacanam upacaranti, na ca, evam ākṛtikadravyāḥ prakṛtā yāgā vidyante. yeṣām imau samudāyasyānuvaditārau bhaveyātām. nanu paśu-vikāro hṛdayādiḥ paśuśabdenāgnīṣomasaṃbandhārtham anūdyate. naitad evam, paśur agnīṣomīyo bhavatīty etāvad ucyate, nāyaṃ prakṛto hṛdayādiḥ paśur iti. tatra yadi, laukikasya paśor grahaṇaṃ tato mukhyaḥ paśuśabdaḥ, yadi hṛdayādeḥ, tato jaghanyo vikārasaṃbandhena. tathā, somaśabdo 'pi vikārasaṃbandhenānuvādaḥ syāt. tasmād apūrve karmaṇī vidhīyeyātāṃ nānuvādau. athaindravāyavādiṣu prakṛteṣu yāgeṣu latā vidhīyeteti. ucyate - na, sā śakyā vākyenaindravāyavī jñātum, śrutyā hi rasa aindravāyavaḥ. tasmād dravyasaṃyogavacanaḥ prakṛteṣu yāgeṣv api satsu vidhātum anuvadituṃ vā na śaknuvann anarthakaḥ syāt. tasmād apūrvakarmaṇī vidhīyeyātām, na prakṛtānām anuvādāv iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: 'He who is consecrated, when he sacrifices the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s> animal.' And there they teach: 'He cuts at the tip of the heart, then of the tongue, then at the chest.' Similarly, 'One should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>,' and there too: 'He takes the <s>Aindravāyava</s> cup, he takes the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> cup, he takes the <s>Āśvina</s> cup,' and so on. Here the doubt arises: Do 'he cuts' and 'he takes' — [being uttered when] the ritual actions have already been enjoined by '<s>ālabhate</s>' (he sacrifices [the animal]) and '<s>yajate</s>' (he sacrifices [with <s>Soma</s>]) — merely re-state the aggregate, or do they enjoin two unprecedented ritual actions?
What is the prima facie view? They [merely re-state] the aggregate. Why? Those two ritual actions that one might think are being enjoined by '<s>ālabhati</s>' and '<s>yajati</s>' — those were already known from '<s>avadyati</s>' (he cuts) and '<s>gṛhṇāti</s>' (he takes). And a meaning already known is not [again] enjoined. By the word <s>paśu</s> (animal), he re-states the heart and so on; by the word <s>soma</s>, the juice. Therefore, 'One should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>' — '<s>yajati</s>' is a re-statement for the purpose of connecting with the fruit: 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>.' And '<s>ālabhate</s>' in 'he should sacrifice the animal' is for the purpose of connecting with <s>Agni</s>-<s>Soma</s>. Moreover, 'the <s>adhvaryu</s> takes these ten cups at the morning pressing' — an accumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>) is observed. Similarly, 'the <s>Āśvina</s> is taken tenth, and offered third' — a sequence too [is observed]. If two unprecedented sacrifices were being enjoined, the <s>Aindravāyava</s> and other deities would be enjoined there, and being for the same purpose, they would become alternatives — just as 'he ties [the sacrificial post] of <s>khadira</s> wood, of <s>palāśa</s> wood, of <s>rohitaka</s> wood.' In that case, the observations of sequence and accumulation would not be justified. But in this aggregate-expression, where [they are] sacrifices, all this is well construed. Therefore, they are re-statements of the aggregate.
When this is the prima facie position, we say: The injunctions of the animal and <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices] enjoin two unprecedented ritual actions. Why? The word <s>soma</s> is well-known [as referring to] a creeping plant with milky sap, not to juice; for the word <s>soma</s> denotes the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>), not the individual (<s>vyakti</s>). Similarly, the word <s>paśu</s> is metaphorically applied (<s>upacaranti</s>) to the universal form of a specific substance — one with horns, a tail, hair, and four legs — and not [to its parts]. Thus, no sacrifices with <s>ākṛti</s>-level substances as their basis exist in the established context, of which these two could be re-statements. [Objection:] Surely, the modification (<s>vikāra</s>) of the animal — the heart and so on — is re-stated by the word <s>paśu</s> for the purpose of connecting with <s>Agni</s>-<s>Soma</s>. This is not so. What is said is merely 'the animal is <s>āgnīṣomīya</s>' — not 'this [particular] heart and so on, being the established animal, is the animal.' In that case, if the worldly animal is meant, the word <s>paśu</s> is primary; if the heart and so on [are meant], then it is secondary through connection with modification. Similarly, the word <s>soma</s> too would be a re-statement through connection with modification. Therefore, two unprecedented ritual actions are being enjoined, not re-statements. [Objection:] But the creeping plant might be enjoined in the already-established <s>Aindravāyava</s> and other sacrifices. [Reply:] No. It is not possible to know [the creeping plant] as <s>Aindravāyavī</s> by the sentence, for by direct hearing the juice is <s>Aindravāyava</s>. Therefore, the substance-connection expression — even when established sacrifices exist — would be unable to either enjoin or re-state, and would thus be purposeless. Therefore, two unprecedented ritual actions are being enjoined, not re-statements of established ones.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/240: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.1.11.6} {2/241: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.3.10.4} {2/242-246: Variant readings and edition cross-references}]

children.text: acodakāś ca saṃskārāḥ // MS_2,2.18 //
children.translated_text: And the preparatory rites are non-injunctive. // MS 2.2.18 //

children.text: evaṃ tāvat, prakṛteṣu satsv api nānuvādāv ity uktam, athedānīm, prakṛtā eva yāgā na santīty ucyate. kutaḥ? acodakāḥ saṃskārāḥ, na ca, aindravāyavādibhir yāgā vidhīyante, tena grahaṇam upakalpanamātraṃ dṛṣṭārtham, upakalpyamāne tu devatā[152{*2/247*}]saṅkīrtanam adṛṣṭāya. ataḥ, aindravāyavaṃ gṛhṇātītīndravāyubhyāṃ saṃkalpayatīty etāvad uktaṃ bhavati, tatra yāgam antareṇa saṃkalpayatīty etan na yujyata iti yāgaḥ kalpyeta, sa evāmnāto yāgaḥ, yasmin sati saṃkalpo 'vakalpyeta. tasmān na, aindravāyavaṃ gṛhṇātītyevamādibhir yāgā vidhīyeran, prakṛtānāṃ yāgānām abhāvān na samudāyaśabdo yajatiḥ, tathā labhatiśabda{*2/248*} iti.
children.translated_text: Thus far, it has been said that even when established [sacrifices] exist, they are not re-statements. Now it is said that established sacrifices themselves do not exist. Why? The preparatory rites are non-injunctive. By '<s>Aindravāyava</s> [cup] he takes' and similar [expressions], sacrifices are not enjoined. Consequently, the 'taking' (<s>grahaṇa</s>) is merely a preparation — serving an observable purpose. But when the preparation is being done, the mention of the deity serves a transcendent (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) purpose. Therefore, '<s>Aindravāyavaṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' means only 'he dedicates [the cup] to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Vāyu</s>.' In that case, to say 'he dedicates without a sacrifice' is improper — so a sacrifice is construed. That very sacrifice is the one taught [in scripture] — the one in whose presence the dedication would be construed. Therefore, since the <s>Aindravāyava</s> and similar [expressions] do not enjoin sacrifices, and since established sacrifices do not exist, '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) is not an aggregate-word; similarly, the word '<s>ālabhati</s>' (he sacrifices [the animal]).

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/247: Edition cross-references} {2/248: E2,4,5,6 correctly read <s>tathālabhatiśabda</s>}]

children.text: tadbhedāt karmaṇo 'bhyāso dravyapṛthaktvād anarthakaṃ hi syād bhedo dravyaguṇībhāvāt // MS_2,2.19 //
children.translated_text: Because of the differentiation of that [ritual action], repetition of the ritual act [would follow]; and because of the separateness of the substance, the differentiation would be purposeless, since the substance would become a quality. // MS 2.2.19 //

children.text: paśau vṛttā kathā daśame punar udbhaviṣyati, soma idānīṃ vartate. kathaṃ kramasamuccayāv iti. indravāyvādyā devatā naivaṃ śrūyante, indravāyubhyāṃ yāgo nirvartayitavyaḥ, mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ yāgo nirvartayitavya iti, yady evam aśroṣyanta, yāgaṃ prati devatā vyakalpiṣyanta, kevalayā hi devatayā tadā yāgo nirvartyata iti vihitam abhaviṣyat. atha punar imāḥ adṛṣṭārthaṃ gṛhṇāti saṃskāraṃ prati devatā vidhīyante, tatrendravāyusaṃkalpād anyo mitrāvaruṇasaṃkalpaḥ, tena gṛhṇātau tatkṛtād adṛṣṭād adṛṣṭāntaram utpādayati, evam apareṣv api grahaṇeṣu, tasmāt samuccayaḥ. grahaṇaṃ tu{*2/249*} niyataparimāṇeṣūrdhvapātreṣu prādeśamātreṣu niyataparimāṇeṣūdakakalaśeṣu saṃskṛtasya daśamuṣṭiparimitasya kṛtsnasya somasya nāvakalpate. yady api cāvakalpeta, tathāpi nityavihitānāṃ devatānāṃ vikalpapakṣe tāvat prayogavacano mā bādhīty ava[153]{*2/250*}yavagrahaṇam eva nyāyyam, kṛtsnagrahaṇe hi tad evendravāyubhyāṃ saṃkalpitam, tad eva mitrāvarūṇābhyām iti nāvakalpeta. tasmāt kalpanabhedāt pṛthagavasthitaḥ somo nānādevatatvād eva naikyena śakyaḥ kartum. na cāsati devatāyāge devatābhyaḥ śakyate saṃkalpayitum. tasmād avaśyaṃ yathāsaṃkalpitā devatā yaṣṭavyāḥ, tāsu cejyamānāsu jyotiṣṭomena yajeteti śruto yāgo nirvṛtta eva bhavati, na devatāntaram ākāṅkṣati, kṛtsnena ca daśamuṣṭinā somena yāgaḥ śrutaḥ, so 'saty abhyāse nāvakalpata ity arthāt sa guṇo bhaviṣyatīty abhyasitavyo yāgaḥ, na hy anabhyastaḥ sarvābhir devatābhiḥ sarveṇa ca{*2/251*} somena saṃpanno bhaviṣyati. tasmiṃś cābhyasyamāne kramasamuccayau yuktāv eva bhavataḥ, tasmāt tayor darśanaṃ yujyate eveti.
children.translated_text: The discussion concerning the animal [sacrifice] has been completed and will arise again in the tenth [<s>adhyāya</s>]; now the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] is being discussed. How do sequence (<s>krama</s>) and accumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>) [apply]? The deities such as <s>Indra-Vāyu</s> and others are not heard [enjoined] thus: 'The sacrifice is to be accomplished for <s>Indra-Vāyu</s>'; 'The sacrifice is to be accomplished for <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>' — if they had been heard thus, the deities would have been placed in alternatives with respect to the sacrifice, for then it would have been enjoined that the sacrifice is to be accomplished with a single deity. But rather, these [deities] are drawn [i.e., the <s>Soma</s> cups are drawn] for an unseen purpose — the deities are enjoined with respect to the consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>). And there, the consecration for <s>Indra-Vāyu</s> is different from that for <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>. Therefore, in the drawing [of cups], from the unseen [result] produced by one [consecration], another unseen [result] is produced — and so too in the other drawings. Therefore, [they are to be] accumulated [not alternated]. But the drawing [of cups] does not work when the entire <s>Soma</s> — consecrated and measured at ten handfuls — [is used] in vessels of fixed measure, upright cups of one span's measure, and water-pots of fixed measure. And even if it did work, still, in the alternative view regarding permanently enjoined deities, lest the statement of performance be overridden, it is proper that only a portion be drawn — for in drawing the whole, that very same [<s>Soma</s>] consecrated for <s>Indra-Vāyu</s> would be [the same as that] for <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>, and the alternative would not work. Therefore, since the <s>Soma</s> is separately established due to the difference in consecrations, it cannot be made one because of the multiplicity of deities. And without a deity-sacrifice, one cannot consecrate [the <s>Soma</s>] for the deities. Therefore, the deities as consecrated must necessarily be worshipped. And when they are being worshipped, the sacrifice heard in 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' is indeed accomplished — it does not expect another deity. And the sacrifice is heard [as performed] with the entire ten handfuls of <s>Soma</s>. Without repetition, that does not work — therefore, by implication, this quality [of repetition] must be practiced, and the sacrifice must be repeated. For without repetition, it will not be accomplished with all the deities and with all the <s>Soma</s>. And when it is being repeated, both sequence and accumulation are indeed appropriate. Therefore, the observation of both [sequence and accumulation] is justified.
[TEXTUAL NOTES: E1,5,6 read <s>tu</s>, E2,4 read <s>ca</s>; edition page numbers — E2: 3,79; E4: 3,174; E5: 2,478; E6: 1,105; E2,4 omit <s>ca</s>.]

children.text: saṃskāras tu na bhidyeta, parārthatvād dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt // MS_2,2.20 //
children.translated_text: But the consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) should not be divided, because the substance (<s>dravya</s>) serves another's purpose and is subordinate. // MS 2.2.20 //

children.text: yad apy ucyate - yathā khādire badhnāti, pālāśe badhnātīti khādirādayaḥ saṃskāre vikalpante, tadvad devatā vikalpayiṣyanta iti, tac ca naivaṃ yuktam, tatra saṃskāram abhinirvartayituṃ khādirādayaḥ śrūyante. yadi cendravāyvādyā api grahadevatā yāgam abhinirvartayituṃ śrūyeran, tato 'trāpi vikalpaḥ syāt, na tv etā yāge śrutāḥ. tasmāt samuccīyeran.
children.translated_text: As for what is said — just as <s>Khadira</s>-wood, <s>Palāśa</s>-wood, etc. are placed in alternatives with respect to the consecration, [as in] 'he ties [the victim] to a <s>Khadira</s> [post],' 'he ties to a <s>Palāśa</s> [post]' — so too the deities should be placed in alternatives — this is not proper. There, <s>Khadira</s> and the like are heard [as serving] to accomplish the consecration. If <s>Indra-Vāyu</s> and other cup-deities were also heard [as serving] to accomplish the sacrifice, then here too there would be an alternative. But these [deities] are not heard [enjoined] with respect to the sacrifice [in that way]. Therefore, they should be accumulated.

children.text: pṛthaktvaniveśāt saṅkhyayā karmabhedaḥ syāt // MS_2,2.21 //
children.translated_text: Through the assignment of separateness, [there is] division of ritual actions by number. // MS 2.2.21 //

children.text:
asti vājapeyaḥ, vājapeyena svārājyakāmo yajeteti, [154]{*2/252*} tatra prājāpatyāḥ paśavaḥ, saptadaśa prājāpatyān paśūn ālabhate, saptadaśo vai prajāpatiḥ, prajāpater āptyai śyāmāstūparā ekarūpā bhavanti, evam eva hi prajāpatiḥ samṛddhyai{*2/253*}. tatra sandihyate - kiṃ saptadaśaitāni karmāṇi, atha saptadaśapaśuguṇakam ekaṃ karmeti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? ekaṃ karmeti. kutaḥ? prajāpataye saptadaśa paśavaḥ saṅkalpyante. kim ekaṃ yāgam abhinivartayitum uta bahūn iti saṃśaye ekam iti nyāyyaṃ, yo hi bahūn yāgān kalpayati, kalpayaty asāv ekam, tatraikasminn eva parikḷpte saptadaśānām eva paśūnāṃ parikalpanam upapannaṃ bhavati, kena ca dvitīyādīn yāgān avakalpayema. evaṃ saty{*2/254*} alpīyasy adṛṣṭānumānaprasaṅgakalpanā bhavati. tasmād eko yāgaḥ saptadaśabhiḥ paśubhir nirvartyate{*2/255*}.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - saṅkhyayā karmabhedo bhavet, pṛthaktve paśūnāṃ sati saptadaśasaṅkhyā niviśeta, tac ca paśūnāṃ pṛthaktvaṃ bahuṣu yāgeṣv avakalpate, naikasmin. katham? ekādaśabhir avadānair asau yāgo nivartayitavya ity evaṃ codakaḥ pratidiśati, tāni caikasmād eva paśor avāpyante, tatra dvitīyāder ālambho nāvadānasaṃpādanāya bhavitum arhati, ekam ālabhyamānam anvālabhyerann adṛṣṭārthāyāpare, tathāsaty{*2/256*} atadarthatvān na te prājāpatyā bhaveyuḥ, tatra prājāpatyān iti śravaṇam uparudhyeta{*2/257*}. tenaikasmin paśau pṛthaktve niveśinī saptadaśasaṅkhyā nāvakalpyeta, bahuṣu yāgeṣu bahubhir evāvadānagaṇaiḥ prayojanam, tena saptadaśabhyo yāgebhyaḥ saptadaśa paśūn upādadīraṃs tatra saṅkhyāsāmaṃ jasyaṃ bhaviṣyati, tasmāt saptadaśa yāgāḥ.
nanv ekasminn api yāge saptadaśabhir avadānagaṇair yakṣyate vacanāt. naitad evam, paśuṣu hiṃ sā saṅkhyā śrūyate, nāvadānagaṇeṣu. avadānāni havīṃṣi yāgasādhanāni, na paśvākṛtiḥ, sā hy avadānaprakṛtidravyaṃ viśiṣantī prakṛtau pradhānasyopakṛtavatīti [155]{*2/258*} vikṛtāv apy avadānaprakṛtidravyaṃ viśiṣantī pradhānasyopakariṣyati, tatra ca paśoḥ saptadaśasaṅkhyā vikārikā, nāvadānagaṇasya, tasmād ekasmai avadānagaṇāyaikaḥ paśur ālabdhavyaḥ prāpnoti, tatra saptadaśasaṅkhyā nopapadyate, evam evāvakalpiṣyate. yadi śṛṅgābhiprāyā varṇābhiprāyā rūpābhiprāyā vābhiviṣyan saptadaśapaśavaḥ śvetaḥ kṛṣṇo rohita ityevamādayaḥ, teṣām anyatamo gṛhyata iti, athavā tūparāḥ śṛṅgiṇa ekaśṛṅgā ityevamādayaḥ, teṣām anyatama iti, te hi śyāmās tūparā ekarūpāḥ śrūyante, tadeṣu bahuṣu yāgeṣūpapadyate, naikasmin. tasmāt saptadaśa yāgā iti. prayojanam ekasminn aṣṭe duṣṭe kṛtsnaḥ paśugaṇa āvarteta, ekam ālabhyamānam anvālabheran, pūrvapakṣe 'dṛṣṭārtham. siddhānta eka eva paśur āvartate, na hi karmabhede paśuḥ paśvantaram ākāṅkṣatīti.
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>Vājapeya</s> [sacrifice] — 'One who desires sovereignty should sacrifice with the <s>Vājapeya</s>.' There, the animals [belong] to <s>Prajāpati</s>: 'He immolates seventeen animals for <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed the seventeenth; for the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s> — they should be dark, with upward [horns], of uniform color — for thus indeed <s>Prajāpati</s> [prospers] for prosperity.' There a doubt arises: are these seventeen [separate] ritual actions, or is it a single action qualified by seventeen animals? What is the prima facie view? It is a single action. Why? Seventeen animals are consecrated for <s>Prajāpati</s>. When there is doubt whether they accomplish one sacrifice or many, [the answer] 'one' is proper. For one who postulates many sacrifices also postulates one [at minimum]; when that one alone is postulated, the postulation of all seventeen animals is established [within it]. And by what means would we postulate second and subsequent sacrifices? Thus, there will be less recourse to inferring unseen [entities]. Therefore, one sacrifice is accomplished with seventeen animals.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: There should be division of ritual actions by number. When there is separateness of animals, the number seventeen would apply — and that separateness of animals works in many sacrifices, not in one. How? 'This sacrifice is to be accomplished with eleven portions (<s>avadāna</s>)' — thus the injunction prescribes. And those [eleven portions] are obtained from a single animal. There, the immolation of a second animal and beyond cannot be for the purpose of supplying portions. [In the prima facie view,] after immolating one, the others would be immolated in succession for an unseen purpose. In that case, since they would not serve that [Prajāpati-related] purpose, they would not be 'belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>' — and the scriptural statement 'animals belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>' would be obstructed. Therefore, the number seventeen, which requires separateness, cannot work with a single animal. In many sacrifices, the purpose is served by many sets of portions. Therefore, from seventeen sacrifices one would take seventeen animals — there the number would be consistent. Therefore, [there are] seventeen sacrifices.
[Objection:] But even in a single sacrifice, one will sacrifice with seventeen sets of portions, because of the [scriptural] statement. [Reply:] This is not so. The number is heard with respect to the animals, not the sets of portions. The portions are the oblation-materials, the means of sacrifice — not the animal-form. For [the animal-form], qualifying the primary material of the portions, has served the primary [sacrifice] in the archetype — and in the modified [sacrifice] too, qualifying the primary material of the portions, it will serve the primary [sacrifice]. And the number seventeen of the animals is a modification, not [the number] of the set of portions. Therefore, one animal must be immolated for one set of portions — this follows. And there the number seventeen does not work — it will work only thus [with seventeen separate sacrifices]. If the seventeen animals were intended by horn-type, color, or form — 'white, black, reddish' and the like — then any one of them would be taken. Or 'with upward [horns], horned, single-horned' and the like — any one of them. For they are heard as 'dark, with upward [horns], of uniform color' — that works in many sacrifices, not in one. Therefore, [there are] seventeen sacrifices. The practical consequence: if one [animal] is defective when a single [sacrifice is assumed], the entire group of animals would have to be replaced; [in the prima facie view] after immolating one, the rest would be immolated in succession for an unseen purpose. In the established view, only one animal is replaced, for when the ritual actions are separate, one animal does not expect another.

athaiṣa jyotir athaiṣa viśvajyotir athaiṣa sarvajyotir iti. atra{*2/259*} saṃdehaḥ, kim ebhir nāmadheyaiḥ prakṛtaṃ jyotiṣṭomaṃ saṅkīrtya tatra sahasradakṣiṇādiguṇo vidhīyate, atha vā vakṣyamāṇaviśeṣāṇi karmāntarāṇy upadiśyanta iti. kiṃ prāptam, prakaraṇānugrahāt prakṛtasya guṇavidhānam iti. nanu vākyasāmarthyāj jyotirādīnām ete guṇā vidhāyiṣyante. naiṣa doṣaḥ, jyotiṣṭomasyaivaitāni vācakāni, jyotir iti jyotiṣṭomasya pratīkam upādīyate, viśvajyotir iti trivṛdādīny asya jyotīṃṣi vākyaśeṣasaṅkīrtitāni, tāni sarvāṇy asya, tenāsau viśvajyotiḥ sarvajyotiś ca jyotiṣṭoma iti evaṃ prāptam.
[156]{*2/260*} evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - saṃjñā hi tisro bhedikāḥ, teṣāṃ jyotir ādyāḥ, utpattivākye hy etāḥ śrūyante, tāsām{*2/261*} imāḥ punaḥ śrutayaḥ. tasmād athaiṣa jyotir ity apūrvasya karmaṇo vidhāyakaṃ vākyam, anuvāde hi saty apravṛttiviśeṣakaram anarthakaṃ syāt. prakṛtasya ca guṇavidhāne vikalpo bhavet, tatra pakṣe bādhaḥ, na ca jyotirādayo jyotiṣṭomasya vaditāraḥ, samudāyāntarāṇi hy etāni, na cāvayavena samānena samudāyāntaraṃ tadartham eva bhavati, yathā śālāśabdo gṛhavacanaḥ, tatra na śālāśabdasāmānyān mālāśabdādayo 'pi gṛhavacanā bhavanti. yat tu jyotiṣṭomasya jyotir iti pratīkam upādīyata iti. prakaraṇasāmarthyād dhi tatra jyotiṣṭomaśabdena parokṣenaikavākyatā bhavet, sā pratyakṣaṃ jyotiḥśabdena sahaikavākyatāṃ bādheta, nacaitan nyāyyam, vākyaṃ hi prakaraṇād balīyaḥ. atha punar ayaṃ dyotanārthatvād vā jyotiṣṭomatvād vā karmāntare vatsyati, yac{*2/262*} ca trivṛdādīni jyotīṃṣi teṣāṃ sākalyavacano viśvajyotiḥ sarvajyotir iti cet. neti brūmaḥ, na hi trivṛdādiṣu jyotiḥśabdaḥ prasiddhaḥ, evaṃ bruvan prasiddhaṃ bādheta. yat tu vākyaśeṣāj jyotiḥśabdas trivṛdādivacana iti, tasminn eva vākye sa tatra prayukta iti gamyate pramāṇāntareṇa na śabdena, yatra tu tatpramāṇāntaraṃ nāsti, na tatra vartitum arhati, yathā siṃho devadatta iti siṃhaśabdo devadattavacanaḥ pramāṇāntareṇa, na tu siṃham ālabheteti yatra, tatra tu tatpramāṇāntaraṃ nāsti. tasmān na viśvajyotiḥ sarvajyotir iti{*2/263*} ca jyotiṣṭomasya vaditārau, na cej jyotiṣṭoma ucyate, sarvāṇi kamāntarāṇi{*2/264*}
children.translated_text:
'Now this is <s>Jyotis</s> (light); now this is <s>Viśvajyotis</s> (all-light); now this is <s>Sarvajyotis</s> (complete light).' Here there is doubt: do these names refer to the established <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [sacrifice], enjoining there a quality such as a thousand [cows as] fee, or do they teach different ritual actions with the specific features about to be described? What is the prima facie view? Because of the support of the context, it is a qualificatory injunction of the established [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>]. [Objection:] But by the force of the sentence, these qualities will be enjoined for <s>Jyotis</s> and the like. [Reply:] This is no fault — for these [names] are expressions of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself. '<s>Jyotis</s>' is taken as a condensed form (<s>pratīka</s>) of '<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>'; '<s>Viśvajyotis</s>' [means] that its lights — the <s>Trivṛt</s> and other [<s>Stomas</s>] — are mentioned in the syntactic supplement, and all of them belong to it, hence it is '<s>Viśvajyotis</s>' (having all lights); and it is '<s>Sarvajyotis</s>' (complete light) — thus is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Thus is the prima facie view.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: The three designations (<s>saṃjñā</s>) serve as differentiators — among them, '<s>Jyotis</s>' and the rest. For these are heard in origination-sentences, and these are their [corresponding] scriptural passages. Therefore, 'Now this is <s>Jyotis</s>' is a sentence that enjoins an unprecedented ritual action. If it were a re-statement (<s>anuvāda</s>), it would be purposeless, producing no distinction in performance. And if it were a qualificatory injunction of the established [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], there would be an alternative [among the qualifications] — and in that case, one [alternative] would be excluded. Moreover, '<s>Jyotis</s>' and the rest are not expressions of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, for these are different aggregates [of ritual elements], and a component shared [with another aggregate] does not make that aggregate serve [only] that purpose — just as the word '<s>śālā</s>' (hall) denotes a building, but the similar words '<s>mālā</s>' (garland) and the like do not also denote a building because of a shared element. As for [the claim] that '<s>Jyotis</s>' is taken as a condensed form of '<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — the implicit unity of sentence with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-word through the power of context would be overridden by the explicit unity of sentence with the '<s>Jyotis</s>'-word. And this is not proper, for a sentence is stronger than context. Moreover, this [word '<s>Jyotis</s>'] will apply to a different ritual action either because of its meaning of 'illumination' or because of its <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-nature. And as for [the claim that] '<s>Viśvajyotis</s>' and '<s>Sarvajyotis</s>' [mean] 'having all lights' because the <s>Trivṛt</s> and other [<s>Stomas</s>] are called 'lights' — we say no. For the word '<s>Jyotis</s>' (light) is not well-known [as a designation] for the <s>Trivṛt</s> and the like. One who says so would override established usage. As for [the argument] that the word '<s>Jyotis</s>' denotes the <s>Trivṛt</s> and the like from the syntactic supplement — in that very sentence it is understood through another means of knowledge, not through the word [itself], that it is used [to refer to them] there. But where that other means of knowledge does not exist, [the word] should not apply [in that secondary sense] — just as 'the lion is <s>Devadatta</s>' [uses] the word 'lion' for <s>Devadatta</s> through another means of knowledge, but in 'one should immolate a lion,' that other means of knowledge does not exist [and so 'lion' means lion]. Therefore, '<s>Viśvajyotis</s>' and '<s>Sarvajyotis</s>' are not expressions of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. If the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is not being denoted, [then] all [three are] different ritual actions.

cāturmāsyeṣu vaiśvadeve samāmananti, tapte payasi dadhyānayati sā vaiśvadevy āmikṣā vājibhyo vājinam iti{*2/266*}. tatra sandihyate, kim āmikṣāguṇake karmaṇi vājinaṃ guṇavidhiḥ, uta tasmād vājina-guṇakaṃ karmāntaram{*2/267*}? kiṃ prāptam? guṇavidhir iti. kutaḥ? vājenān nenāmikṣayā vājino viśve-devās tān anūdya vājinaṃ vidhīyate, tenobhayaṃ vaiśvadevam, āmikṣā vājinaṃ ca. tasminn eva ca karmaṇi vājinaguṇavidhiḥ. yathā agnihotraṃ juhotīty ukte dadhnā juhoti, payasā juhotīti{*2/268*}.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - guṇaś cāprakṛtena devatābhidhānena saṃbandhyamānaḥ karmāntaraṃ vidadhyāt, same hi tadaite vākye bhavataḥ, ubhe apy apūrvayor yāgayor vidhātṛṇī. kathaṃ punar apūrvadevatābhidhānam? yadedānīm eva uktam, viśveṣāṃ devānām anuvādo vājinam{*2/269*} iti. tad ucyate - iha viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ devatātvaṃ kvacic chrutyā, kvacit vākyena. tad dhitanirdeśe śrutyā, caturthīnirdeśe vākyena. yatra śrutyā devatātvam, tatrāmikṣayā sahaikavākyatvam. yatra caturthī, tatra vājinena, tatraiṣām ekatra śrutyā devatātvam, vākyena dravyaviśeṣasaṃbandhaḥ. ekatrobhayam api vākyena. tad iha devatātvaṃ prati śrutivākyayor virodhaḥ, virodhe ca śrutir balīyasīty āmikṣāvākye devatātvaṃ viśveṣāṃ devānām, na vājinavākya ity adhyavasīyate, tenāvagamyate, aprakṛtena devatāpadenāsya saṃbandha iti. tasmāt karmāntaram iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites, they teach regarding the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (All-gods) [rite]: 'He brings curds into heated milk; that is the <s>Vaiśvadevī āmikṣā</s> (All-gods' curded milk); for the <s>Vājins</s>, the <s>Vājina</s>-[offering].' There the doubt arises: is the <s>Vājina</s> a subsidiary-quality injunction within the rite having <s>āmikṣā</s> as its subsidiary, or is it a different ritual action having <s>Vājina</s> as its subsidiary? What is the prima facie view? It is a subsidiary-quality injunction. Why? '<s>Vājins</s>, by <s>vāja</s> (nourishment), not by <s>āmikṣā</s>, the <s>Vājin</s>-gods, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>' — by restating them, the <s>Vājina</s> is enjoined. Therefore, both are <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> — both the <s>āmikṣā</s> and the <s>Vājina</s>. And in that very rite, the <s>Vājina</s> is a subsidiary-quality injunction — just as when 'he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>' is stated, 'he offers with curds,' 'he offers with milk' [are subsidiary-quality injunctions].
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: A subsidiary quality, when connected with a deity-designation that does not belong to the current context, would enjoin a different ritual action. For in that case, these two are in the same sentence, and both are injunctive of two unprecedented sacrifices. But how is the deity-designation unprecedented? For it was just now said that 'the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) are being restated, [and] the <s>Vājina</s> [is enjoined].' To this it is said: here, the status of the <s>Viśvedevas</s> as deities [is established] in some cases by direct expression (<s>śruti</s>), in some cases by the sentence. [It is established] by direct expression in the genitive (<s>taddhita</s>) indication, and by the sentence in the dative indication. Where the deity-status [is known] by direct expression, there is sentence-unity with the <s>āmikṣā</s>. Where [there is] a dative, there [it is] with the <s>Vājina</s>. Thus, of these [two], in one case the deity-status is [known] by direct expression, and the connection with the specific substance by the sentence. In the other case, both [are known] by the sentence. Here, with respect to the deity-status, there is a conflict between direct expression and sentence. And in a conflict, the direct expression is stronger. Therefore, in the <s>āmikṣā</s>-sentence the deity-status of the <s>Viśvedevas</s> is [established], not in the <s>Vājina</s>-sentence — this is determined. Hence it is understood that the connection of this [<s>Vājina</s>] is with a deity-term that does not belong to the current context. Therefore, it is a different ritual action.

yuktaṃ yat tatra guṇavidhānam, na tatrāprakṛtena kenacid guṇena saṃbandhaḥ, prakṛtena tv asti yāgena. tasmād anupavarṇanam etat.

children.translated_text:
It is proper that there the subsidiary-quality injunction [applies] — there, [the subsidiary quality] is not connected with any deity that does not belong to the current context, but it is connected with the contextually relevant sacrifice. Therefore, this is a supplementary illustration.
Alternatively, [this is] a separate topic: 'he offers with curds' and similar [expressions] are different ritual actions, [and the doubt is] set up in order to resolve the alternative. But that very ritual action is understood from the word '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers), not a different action. Therefore, the subsidiary-quality injunction applies there, and the alternative is established from the [Vedic] statement — this is the conclusion.

children.text:
agnihotraṃ prakṛtya samāmananti, dadhnendriyakāmasya juhuyād ityevamādi{*2/271*}. tatra saṃśayaḥ, kim agnihotrahomād dhomāntaraṃ dadhyādihomaḥ, uta dadhyāder guṇāt phalam iti. kiṃ prāptam? homāntaram iti. kutaḥ? phalaśruteḥ, phalam iha śrūyate, tac ca karmaṇo nyāyyam.
kiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ hi karmaṇaḥ phalam? kṛṣyādito vrīhyādi. neti brūmaḥ, na hy etad dṛṣṭenānena sidhyati, yadi darśanaṃ hetuḥ [159]{*2/272*} phalajñāne, kṛṣyādau padārthe taddarśanam, na home. atha kṛṣau dṛṣṭam anyatrāpi bhavati. dravyād api prasajyate. atha kṛṣisadṛśād bhavatīty ucyate, kṛṣisadṛśo homaḥ kriyātvāt, na dravyam, asadṛśaṃ hi tad iti. homo 'py asadṛśaḥ, mantradevatādisādhanatvād dhomasya, lāṅgalādisādhanatvāc ca kṛṣeḥ. tyāgātmakatvād dhomasya, pāṭanātmakatvāc ca kṛṣeḥ. atha kiṃcit sādṛśyaṃ gṛhyate. dravyasyāpi sad anityam ityevamādi kiṃcit sādṛśyam asti. atha dravyād anyat sadṛśataram astīti kṛtvā na dravyaṃ sadṛśam ity ucyate. homād apy anyat kṛṣeḥ sadṛśataram asti dṛṣṭārtham iti kṛtvā homo 'py asadṛśaḥ syāt. na caitat siddham, yat kvacit dṛśyate, tad anyasmin sadṛśamātre 'dṛṣṭam api bhavitum arhatīti, yad dhi yasya kāraṇabhūtaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ siddhe, tac cet sādhye 'pi kāraṇabhūtam ity avagamyate, bhavati tat tasya sādhakam, yan na jñāyate kāraṇabhūtam iti, na tat sadṛśam api sādhakam. tasmāt sadṛśam api sādhakam asādhakaṃ veti parīkṣitavyam iti. atha yat karma tat phalavad dṛṣṭam, homo 'pi karma, tenāpi phalavatā bhavitavyam iti. uparate karmaṇi dravyāṇāṃ tatsaṃyogānāṃ ca dravyāntaraṃ phalaṃ dṛṣṭam iti dravyam api phalavat syāt. api ca kṛṣer nādṛṣṭam iti tatsādṛśyād dhomād api nādṛṣṭaṃ bhavet, kṛṣisādṛśyād vā vrīhir eva bhavet, nendriyam. tasmān naivaṃjātīyakeṣv etad bhavati dṛṣṭād adṛṣṭasiddhir iti. kathaṃ tarhi homān nyāyyaṃ phalam iti. ucyate, śabdenāvagamyate tatphalam, yataḥ phalam iti śabda āha, tato nyāyyam, homāc ca phalam iti śrutyā śabdena gamyate, dadhnaḥ phalam iti vākyena, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī. tasmāt homāt phalam iti nyāyyam, dadhnaḥ phalam iti cānyāyyam.
api ca dadhy ubhayam asamartham, kartuṃ phalam, sādhayituṃ homaṃ ca. [160]{*2/273*} nanu kambalanirṇejanavad etad bhaviṣyati, nirṇejanaṃ hy ubhayaṃ karoti, kambalaśuddhiṃ pādayoś ca nirmalatām. na brūmaḥ, ekasyobhayaṃ prayojanam abhiniṣpādayituṃ sāmarthyaṃ nāstīti, kiṃ tarhi phale guṇabhūtaṃ dadhi home cety ekaṃ vākyaṃ vaditum asamartham iti. yadi phalaṃ dadhnā kuryād iti brūyāt, na dadhnā homam iti, atha dadhnā homaṃ sādhayed iti brūyāt, na phalam iti. ubhayavacane bhidyeta vākyam, abhinnaṃ cedam upalabhyate. tasmān na guṇāt phalam ity agnihotrahomād dadhihomaḥ karmāntaram iti.

children.translated_text:
In the context of the <s>Agnihotra</s>, they teach: 'One who desires the senses should offer with curds' and so forth. There the doubt arises: is the curds-offering and the like a different <s>homa</s> from the <s>Agnihotra</s>-<s>homa</s>, or does the result [come] from the subsidiary quality of curds and the like? What is the prima facie view? It is a different <s>homa</s>. Why? Because a result is heard (<s>phalaśruti</s>). A result is heard here, and that is properly [connected] with a ritual action.
But is a result from a ritual action directly perceived? [Objection:] Yes — from agriculture and the like, rice and so forth [are produced]. [Reply:] We say no. For this is not established by such direct perception. If direct perception is the reason for knowing the result, then the perception of the result exists in the case of agricultural activity, not in the case of <s>homa</s>. [Objection:] But what is perceived in agriculture [applies] elsewhere too. [Reply:] Then it would apply to substances as well. [Objection:] It applies only to what is similar to agriculture. [Reply:] <s>Homa</s> is similar to agriculture because of being an action — but a substance is not, being dissimilar. [Reply:] <s>Homa</s> too is dissimilar — for <s>homa</s> is accomplished by <s>mantras</s>, deities, and the like, while agriculture by plough and the like; <s>homa</s> is of the nature of relinquishing, while agriculture of the nature of splitting. [Objection:] But some similarity is grasped. [Reply:] Even of a substance, some similarity — such as being non-eternal — exists. [Objection:] But something more similar to agriculture than a substance exists, therefore the substance is called dissimilar. [Reply:] Something more similar to agriculture than <s>homa</s> exists — [something] with a directly perceived purpose — and therefore <s>homa</s> too would be dissimilar. Nor is this established: that what is perceived in one case must exist in another merely similar case. For what is perceived as the cause in an established [case] — if that is understood as the cause in the [case] to be established as well — then it becomes the proof for that. But what is not known as a cause — that, even if similar, is not a proof. Therefore, even what is similar must be examined as to whether it is probative or not. [Objection:] What is a ritual action has been seen to have a result; <s>homa</s> too is a ritual action; therefore it too should have a result. [Reply:] When the ritual action ceases, substances and their conjunctions produce another substance as a result — this is observed. So a substance too would have a result. Moreover, agriculture produces no unseen [result] — so, by similarity to it, <s>homa</s> too would produce no unseen result. Or, by similarity to agriculture, [<s>homa</s>] would produce only rice, not sense-organs. Therefore, in [cases] of this kind, the establishment of the unseen from the seen does not work. How then is a result properly [connected] with <s>homa</s>? It is said: it is understood from the word (<s>śabda</s>), [Page 159] since the word says 'from this, a result.' That alone is proper. And that the result is from <s>homa</s> is understood from direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) — by the word; that the result is from curds is [understood] from the sentence. And direct expression is stronger than the sentence. Therefore, [the result is] properly from <s>homa</s>, and [the claim that the result is] from curds is improper.
Moreover, curds is incapable of both — producing a result and accomplishing the <s>homa</s>. [Page 160] [Objection:] But this will be like [the analogy of] washing a blanket — for washing accomplishes both: the cleanliness of the blanket and the cleanliness of the feet. [Reply:] We do not say that one thing cannot accomplish two purposes. Rather, [we say] a single sentence cannot express that curds is subsidiary both to the result and to the <s>homa</s>. If it were to say 'he should produce the result with curds,' it would not [say] 'he should produce the <s>homa</s> with curds.' And if it were to say 'he should accomplish the <s>homa</s> with curds,' not the result. If both were stated, the sentence would be split — but it is perceived as unsplit. Therefore, the result is not from the subsidiary [curds], and the curds-offering is a different ritual action from the <s>Agnihotra</s>-<s>homa</s>.
[Edition notes: Tait.Br. 2.1.5.6; E2: 3,106; E4: 3,234; E5: 2,507; E6: 1,109; E2: 3,109; E4: 3,235; E5: 2,512; E6: 1,109]

children.text:
tuśabdāt pakṣo viparivartate, na karmāntaram, kiṃ tu guṇāt phalam iti. katham? atulye hy ete vākye, agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāma ity atra karmasamabhivyāhṛtaṃ phalaṃ svargakāmo homena kuryād iti, dadhnendriyakāmasya juhuyād iti guṇasamabhivyāhṛtam. na hy atra homa indriyāya kartavya iti pratīyate, kiṃ tarhi dadhnā homa indriyakāmasyeti, homasya dadhisaṃbandha indriyāya, na homasyotpattiḥ, ya indriyakāmaḥ syāt, sa dadhnā homaṃ kuryād iti. katamo 'tra śabdaḥ puruṣaprayatnasya vakteti. juhuyād iti brūmaḥ.
nanu śrutyā homasaṃbaddham eṣa puruṣaprayatnaṃ vadati, vākyena dadhisaṃbandham, na ca, vākyaṃ śrutim apabādhitum arhati. na ca, yugapad ubhayasaṃbandho na virudhyate, vākyaṃ hi tathā bhidyeteti. atrocyate - ye bhavadīyaṃ pakṣam āśrayeran, te śrutim apabādher antarām{*2/274*}, asmadīye tu punaḥ pakṣe juhuyād iti dhātvarthaḥ kevalo 'pabādhito bhavati, yuṣmadīye tu kṛtsna eva dadhneti śabdaḥ. taṃ cāpramādyantaḥ samāmanantīti gamyate. na caitat pramattagītam, [161]{*2/275*} ity uktam, tulyaṃ hi sāṃpradāyikam iti. tasmān na karmasamabhivyāhṛtaṃ phalam, guṇasamabhi-vyāhṛte tu na kaścit pramādapāṭhaḥ, avaśyaṃ hi, juhuyād iti dadhnendriyakāmayoḥ saṃbandhavi-dhānārthaṃ vaktavyaṃ bhavati. nanūcyamāne 'pi na kevalaḥ karoty artho 'vagamyate, kevale na vacaḥprayojanam, sa ca homasaṃbaddhaḥ, tasmād asamañjasam iti. neti brūmaḥ, homasaṃbaddho 'py asau karoty artha eva, kevalaṃ tv asya homasaṃbandhe viśeṣaḥ, na tu karoty arthatāṃ bādhate, indriyakāmasya homasaṃbaddhaṃ prayatnaṃ dadhisaṃbaddhaṃ kuryād iti. nanv evaṃ sati sa eva doṣaḥ, homasamabhivyāhṛtaṃ phalam iti. ucyate - juhuyād iti śabdasyaitatsāmarthyam, yad dhomaviśiṣṭaṃ prayatnam āha, na tv atra homaḥ sādhanatvena vidhīyate, sādhyatvena viśiṣṭas tu prayatno vākyena dadhyāśrito 'vagamyate, ata eva ca vṛttikāreṇoktam - homam āśrito guṇaḥ phalaṃ sādhayiṣyatīti, yathā rājapuruṣo rājānam āśrito rājakarma karotīti. tasmād dadhnaḥ phalam, ya indriyakāmaḥ, sa dadhnā kuryād indriyam iti. katham iti. anayāgnihotretikartavyatayeti. kuta etat? phalasādhanasya dadhna itikartavyatākāṅkṣatvāt, asyāś cetikartavyatāyāḥ sannidhānāt, codanāliṅgasya ca juhoty arthasya darśanāt. yasmād eva cāyaṃ juhoty 'rtho 'nuvādaḥ, tasmād avidhāyakaḥ. na ca, anyad dhomasya vidhāyakaṃ nāstīti, tasmān na karmāntaram, tasmād dadhnaḥ phalam iti. atha vā dadhiśabdasya vivakṣitārthatvād dadhihomasaṃbandho 'yaṃ vākyena vidhīyate, tena dadhno homena saṃbadhyamānāt phalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text:
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the position — it is not a different ritual action; rather, the result is from the subsidiary quality. How? For these two sentences are unequal. In '<s>Agnihotra</s> — one who desires heaven should offer,' the result is stated in conjunction with the ritual action — 'one who desires heaven should produce [the result] by <s>homa</s>.' In 'one who desires the senses should offer with curds,' [the result is stated] in conjunction with the subsidiary quality. For it is not understood here that '<s>homa</s> is to be performed for the sake of sense-organs'; rather, 'the <s>homa</s> with curds is for one who desires sense-organs' — the connection of <s>homa</s> with curds is for sense-organs, not the origination of <s>homa</s>. Whoever desires sense-organs should perform the <s>homa</s> with curds — thus [it is understood]. Which word here expresses a person's effort? We say: '<s>juhuyāt</s>' (he should offer).
[Objection:] But by direct expression, this [verb] expresses the person's effort as connected with <s>homa</s>; by the sentence, as connected with curds. And the sentence cannot override the direct expression. Nor is there a contradiction in the simultaneous connection with both — for the sentence would be split [if both were simultaneous]. To this it is said: those who would adopt your position would override the direct expression even more. In our position, only the root-meaning of '<s>juhuyāt</s>' — [the meaning] 'oblation' alone — is overridden. In your position, the entire word '<s>dadhi</s>' (curds) [would be overridden]. And that [word], uttered by those who do not err, is [part of] the tradition — that is understood. Nor is this a chant of the careless, [Page 161] for it has been said that 'what is handed down in tradition is equally [authoritative].' Therefore, the result is not stated in conjunction with the ritual action. In the case [where the result is] stated in conjunction with the subsidiary quality, there is no careless recitation — for '<s>juhuyāt</s>' must necessarily be stated in order to enjoin the connection of curds with [the rite for] one desiring sense-organs. [Objection:] But even when stated, the meaning of '<s>karoti</s>' (produces/effects) alone is not understood; in the [meaning of] 'alone' there is no purpose for the [additional] word; and that [effect-meaning] is connected with <s>homa</s>. Therefore, [the position] is inconsistent. [Reply:] We say no. Even though connected with <s>homa</s>, that [verb] has precisely the meaning of producing/effecting. Only, its specialization is with the <s>homa</s>-connection — it does not, however, override the producing/effecting meaning. [The meaning is:] one who desires sense-organs should make the <s>homa</s>-connected effort curds-connected. [Objection:] But if so, that very defect [arises] — the result is stated in conjunction with the <s>homa</s>. [Reply:] It is said: the capacity of the word '<s>juhuyāt</s>' is that it expresses an effort qualified by <s>homa</s>. But <s>homa</s> here is not being enjoined as an instrument — rather, the effort, qualified [by <s>homa</s>] as something to be accomplished, is understood from the sentence as depending on curds. And for this very reason the <s>vṛttikāra</s> (commentator) said: 'the subsidiary quality, relying on the <s>homa</s>, will accomplish the result' — just as a king's servant, relying on the king, does the king's work. Therefore, the result is from curds — whoever desires sense-organs should produce sense-organs with curds. How? By this <s>Agnihotra</s> procedure. Whence this [conclusion]? Because curds, which is the means of the result, expects a procedure, and because this procedure is proximate, and because the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the meaning of '<s>juhoti</s>' is observed. And precisely because this meaning of '<s>juhoti</s>' is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), it is non-injunctive. And there is no other injunction of <s>homa</s>. Therefore, it is not a different ritual action; therefore, the result is from curds. Alternatively, because the meaning of the word '<s>dadhi</s>' (curds) is intended [as significant], the connection of curds with <s>homa</s> is being enjoined by the sentence. Therefore, the result will come from curds being connected with <s>homa</s>.

children.text:
trivṛd agniṣṭud agniṣṭomas tasya vāyavyāsv ekaviṃśam agniṣṭomasāmakṛtvā brahmavarcasakāmo yajeteti, etasyaiva revatīṣu vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā paśukāmo hy etena yajeteti. atrāyam arthaḥ sāṃśayikaḥ, kiṃ tasyaivāgniṣṭuto 'gniṣṭomasya guṇād vāravantīyāt paśavaḥ phalam, etena yajeteti anuvādaḥ, atha kim etena yajeteti karmāntaram iti. kiṃ prāptam? na karmāntaraṃ guṇāt phalam iti. kutaḥ? etena yajeteti viditasyaitad vacanam, nāviditasya, ato na vidhyantaram, paśukāma evaṃ yajetety ucyate, na yajeteti, kathaṃ kṛtvā? vāravantīyaṃ kṛtveti. api ca, etasyaiveti vispaṣṭam akarmāntaravacanam. tasmād guṇāt phalam ity evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sameṣv evaṃjātīyakeṣu bhinnavākyeṣu karmayuktaṃ phalaṃ bhavet, etasyaiva revatīṣu vāravantīyaṃ kṛtveti, na hy etasya revatyaḥ santi, yāsv asya vāravantīyaṃ bhavet, tatra revatyo [163]{*2/277*} bhavanti, tāsu ca vāravantīyaṃ vidhīyeteti vākyam bhidyeta. athocyeta, asya pūrvā revatīr upādāya tāsu ca vāravantīyaṃ kṛtvā, etena yajetety anuvadatīti. tathāgniṣṭomasāmeti nāvakalpyeta. athāgniṣṭomasāmakārye bhavatīty ucyate. etasyaivety etad avivakṣitaṃ syāt. ubhayasmin vivakṣyamāṇe bhidyeta vākyam, tasmāt karmāntaram.
atha karmāntare katham avākyabhedaḥ. revatīṣu ṛkṣu vāravantīyaṃ sāma kṛtvā paśukāmo yajetety apūrvo yāgaḥ sarvair viśeṣaṇair viśiṣṭo vidhīyate, tenaikārthatvam, vibhāge ca sākāṅkṣatvam ity ekavākyatvam upapadyate. nanv arthabhedo yāgaś caivaṃ hy apūrvaḥ kartavyaḥ, revatīṣu vāravantīyam apūrvam iti. neti brūmaḥ, nirvṛttavāravantīyarevatīguṇako yāgo vidhīyate, na vāravantīyanirvṛttiḥ, arthād revatīṣu vāravantīyam abhinirvartsyati, śakyate ca tan nirvartayitum. ucyate - revatīnāṃ vāravantī yasya ca saṃbandho na vihitaḥ syāt, tatra ca revatīṣv anyāny api sāmāni bhaveyuḥ. vāravantīyaṃ cānyāsv api ṛkṣu. naiṣa doṣaḥ, kṛtvety abhinirvṛttaḥ saṃbandho yāgāyocyate, tena saṃbandho gamyate, dvāv apy etāv arthau kṛtvety eṣa śabdaḥ śaknoti vaditum, abhinirvṛttiṃ pūrvakālatāṃ ca, yathā śoṇamānaya - iti raktaguṇasaṃbaddho 'śvaḥ śabdenaivānayato{*2/278*} vidhīyata iti, na vākyabhedo bhavati, evam atrāpi draṣṭavyam.
nanv evam api bahavo 'rthāḥ, revatyaḥ, vāravantīyam, tatsaṃbandhaḥ, yāgaḥ, paśukāmaś ceti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, bahavaḥ śrūyante, eko 'tra vidhīyate, yāgo viśiṣṭaḥ. nanu revatyo 'pi vidhīyante, vāravantīyam api, yadi na vidhīyeran, naiva tadviśiṣṭo yāgaḥ pratīyeta, na hy avidhāya viśeṣaṇam, śakyate viśiṣṭo vidhātum, tasmād bahuṣu vidhīyamāneṣu naikārthyam. atrocyate - artha iti prayojanam abhidhīyate, yāvanti padāny ekaṃ prayojanam abhi[164]{*2/279*}nirvartyanti, tāvanty ekaṃ vākyam, na ca, atra bahūni prayojanāni, na hi, atrānekasyābhipretasyānekaṃ padaṃ vidhāyakam asti, revatīṣv iti naitat kevalaṃ revatīnāṃ vidhāyakam, revatīṣu vāravantīyam iti. atrāpi padadvaye vāravantīyaśabdo dvitīyāntaḥ, nāsmāt saṃbandho 'bhipreto gamyate, prātipadikārthasyāvyatirekāt, kṛtvety api karotir na saṃbandhamātre paryavasitaḥ paraprayojanasaṃbandham āha. evaṃ viśiṣṭas tu yajatir na parārthaḥ, tad ekam eṣāṃ padārthānāṃ prayojanam, tasmād ekavākyatvam. guṇe punaḥ phale prakalpyamāna agniṣṭomasāmnaḥ kārye vāravantīyam, etasya ca yadagniṣṭomasāmeti vākyabhedaḥ syāt.
athocyate, revatyādisarvaviśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭo yāga etasyāgniṣṭuto vidhīyeta. tathāpi paśukāmasaṃbandhād bhidyeta vākyam. athaivam ucyeta, revatīṣu kṛtena vārayantīyena paśukāmo yajeteti. naivaṃ śakyam, ṛgantarapragāṇād viśeṣahānād vaiguṇyaṃ syāt. nanv idānīm evoktam, śakyate hi revatīṣu vāravantīyaṃ kartum iti. sati vacane śakyam, asati vacane na vāravantīyagrahaṇena gṛhyante. vacanaṃ tarhi bhaviṣyati, paśukāmo revatīṣu vāravantīyam abhinirvartayet, tato yajeteti yajatir anuvādaḥ. yadi vacanaṃ revatīṣu vāravantīyasaṃbandhasya, siddhaṃ karmāntaram, nāgniṣṭuto guṇavidhiḥ. nanu tato yajeteti yāgānuvādād yāgenāsyāṅgaprayojanasaṃbandho bhaviṣyati. naivaṃ śakyam, yāgaṃ pratyaṅgabhāve vidhīyamāne{*2/280*} paśukāmaṃ pratyasaṃbandhaḥ, ubhayasaṃbandhe vākyaṃ bhidyeta. atha yāgasaṃbandho 'nuvādaḥ, prakareṇa cāṅgatā. nedam upapannam, prakaraṇād dhi vākyaṃ balavattaram, tasmāt karmāntaram, yāgaguṇakaṃ vā revatīṣu vāravantīyam, tadguṇako vā yāgaḥ, tatra yāgapaśukāmayoḥ saṃbandhasya vidhātrīṃ yajater uparitanīṃ vibhaktim upalabhāmahe liṅgam, na tu revatīvāravantīyasaṃbandhasya [165]{*2/281*} vidhāyakaṃ sākṣāt kiṃcid upalabhyate. tasmāt sarvaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭo yāgaḥ, paśukāmasya vidhīyata iti siddham.
atha punar viśiṣṭe yāge vidhīyamāne, tad revatīṣu vāravantīyaṃ katham agniṣṭomasāma bhavatīti? ucyate - vacanād agniṣṭomasāmnaḥ kārye bhaviṣyatīti, kim iva hi vacanaṃ na kuryāt, nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ. atha yad uktam etasyaiveti, anantarāpekṣaṃ vacanam iti tatrāpy avirodhād etaddharmakasyeti lakṣaṇāśabdo bhaviṣyati. tasmān na guṇāt phalam, karmāntaram evaṃ dharmakam iti, siddhaṃ sameṣv evaṃjātīyakeṣu karmayuktaṃ phalam iti.
children.translated_text:
The <s>Trivṛt Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma</s> — 'for this [sacrifice], having made the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold) as the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s> in the <s>Vāyavya</s> [hymns], one desiring the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> should sacrifice'; 'for this very same [sacrifice], having made the <s>Vāravantīya</s> as the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s> in the <s>Revatī</s> [hymns], one desiring cattle should sacrifice with this.' Here the meaning is doubtful: does the fruit — cattle — arise from the subsidiary element <s>Vāravantīya</s> of this very <s>Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma</s>, with 'he should sacrifice with this' being a restatement? Or does 'he should sacrifice with this' [indicate] a different ritual action? What is the prima facie view? It is not a different ritual action; the fruit arises from the subsidiary element. Why? Because 'he should sacrifice with this' is a statement about what is [already] known, not about what is unknown — hence it is not a different injunction. 'One desiring cattle should sacrifice thus' is said, not '[he should perform] a [new] sacrifice.' How should he do it? 'Having made the <s>Vāravantīya</s>.' Moreover, 'of this very same' is clearly a statement that it is not a different ritual action. Therefore, the fruit arises from the subsidiary element — this is the prima facie view.
When this has been arrived at, we say: in such cases of equal [expressions], with separate sentences, the fruit would be connected with the ritual action. 'Of this very same, in the <s>Revatī</s> [hymns], having made the <s>Vāravantīya</s>' — but this [<s>Agniṣṭoma</s>] does not have <s>Revatī</s> [hymns] in which its <s>Vāravantīya</s> would occur. Where the <s>Revatī</s> hymns are, the <s>Vāravantīya</s> would [need to] be enjoined in those — and thus the sentence would be split. If it were said that having taken the earlier <s>Revatī</s> hymns of this [sacrifice] and having made the <s>Vāravantīya</s> in those, [the passage] restates 'he should sacrifice with this' — then '<s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>' could not be construed. But if it is said [to mean] 'it functions in the domain of the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>' — then 'of this very same' would be unintended. When both are intended, the sentence would be split. Therefore, it is a different ritual action.
But if it is a different ritual action, how is the sentence not split? A novel sacrifice qualified by all the qualifiers — 'having made the <s>Vāravantīya sāman</s> in the <s>Revatī</s> verses, one desiring cattle should sacrifice' — is enjoined. Therefore, there is unity of purpose, and in separation there would be syntactic incompleteness — hence unity of sentence is established. [Objection:] But the meaning-differentiation and the sacrifice — this novel [sacrifice] must be performed; the <s>Vāravantīya</s> in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns is the novel element. [Reply:] We say no — what is enjoined is the sacrifice qualified by the accomplished <s>Vāravantīya</s> and <s>Revatī</s> qualities, not the accomplishment of the <s>Vāravantīya</s> [itself]. By implication, the <s>Vāravantīya</s> will be accomplished in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns, and that can be accomplished. It is said: the connection of the <s>Revatī</s> hymns and the <s>Vāravantīya</s> would not have been enjoined [elsewhere]. In that case, other <s>sāmans</s> too could occur in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns, and the <s>Vāravantīya</s> in other verses too. This is not a defect — 'having made' (<s>kṛtvā</s>) states the accomplished connection for the purpose of the sacrifice; from that, the connection is understood. The word <s>kṛtvā</s> can express both meanings — accomplishment and temporal priority — just as 'bring the red [horse]': by the word alone, a horse connected with the quality of redness is enjoined [to be brought], and the sentence is not split. The same should be seen here.
[Objection:] But even so, there are many meanings — the <s>Revatī</s> hymns, the <s>Vāravantīya</s>, their connection, the sacrifice, and the one desiring cattle. [Reply:] This is not a defect. Many [items] are heard, but one [thing] is enjoined here — the qualified sacrifice. [Objection:] But the <s>Revatī</s> hymns are also being enjoined, and the <s>Vāravantīya</s> too — if they were not enjoined, the sacrifice qualified by them would not be understood, for without enjoining the qualifiers, the qualified cannot be enjoined. Therefore, when many things are being enjoined, there is no unity of purpose. [Reply:] To this it is said: 'purpose' (<s>artha</s>) means 'objective.' As many words as accomplish one objective — that many constitute one sentence. And here there are not many objectives. For here, there is no separate enjoining word for each of the multiple intended [items]. '<s>Revatīṣu</s>' (in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns) does not by itself enjoin only the <s>Revatī</s> hymns — [it says] 'the <s>Vāravantīya</s> in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns.' Even in this pair of words, the word <s>Vāravantīya</s> in the accusative does not convey the intended connection from [its case-ending] alone, since the meaning of the nominal stem does not go beyond [itself]. And <s>kṛtvā</s> — the verb 'to make' does not end merely at [expressing] the connection; it expresses a connection serving another purpose. But the qualified '<s>yajati</s>' does not serve another's purpose — that is the single purpose of these word-meanings. Therefore, there is unity of sentence. But in the view that the fruit arises from the subsidiary element, the <s>Vāravantīya</s> [would be] in the domain of the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>, and 'of this [very <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>] that is an <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>' — the sentence would be split.
If it is said that the sacrifice qualified by all the <s>Revatī</s> and other qualifiers is enjoined for this <s>Agniṣṭut</s> — even so, the sentence would be split because of the connection with 'one desiring cattle.' If it is said thus: 'one desiring cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Vāravantīya</s> made in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns' — this cannot be, for there would be a defect of deficiency due to the singing of other <s>ṛc</s>-verses and loss of specificity. [Objection:] But it was just said that the <s>Vāravantīya</s> can be made in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns. [Reply:] When there is a [Vedic] statement, it can be; when there is no statement, [the <s>Revatī</s> hymns] are not captured by the mere grasping of the <s>Vāravantīya</s>. Then there will be a statement: 'one desiring cattle should accomplish the <s>Vāravantīya</s> in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns; then he should sacrifice' — in that case, '<s>yajati</s>' is a restatement. If there is a statement about the connection of the <s>Vāravantīya</s> with the <s>Revatī</s> hymns, then a different ritual action is established — it is not a subsidiary-element injunction of the <s>Agniṣṭut</s>. [Objection:] Since '<s>yajati</s>' is a restatement of the sacrifice, the connection with the sacrifice would serve a subsidiary purpose. [Reply:] This cannot be — when subsidiary status with respect to the sacrifice is being enjoined, there is no connection with 'one desiring cattle'; if connected with both, the sentence would be split. If the connection with the sacrifice is a restatement and subsidiarity comes from the context — this is not proper, for the sentence is stronger than the context. Therefore, it is a different ritual action. Whether the <s>Vāravantīya</s> in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns is a quality of the sacrifice, or the sacrifice is qualified by it — in either case, we perceive the upper case-ending of '<s>yajati</s>' as the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for the injunction of the connection between the sacrifice and the one desiring cattle, but we do not perceive anything that directly enjoins the connection of the <s>Revatī</s> and <s>Vāravantīya</s>. Therefore, it is established that the sacrifice qualified by all qualifiers is enjoined for the one desiring cattle.
But again, when a qualified sacrifice is being enjoined, how does the <s>Vāravantīya</s> in the <s>Revatī</s> hymns become the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>? It is said: by the statement, it will function in the domain of the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>. For what indeed would a statement not accomplish? There is no excessive burden for a statement. As for what was said 'of this very same' — the statement refers to what is immediately proximate; and even there, without contradiction, [the word] 'of this' will function figuratively as 'of one having this quality.' Therefore, the fruit does not arise from the subsidiary element; [this is] a different ritual action having this quality. Thus it is established: in such cases of equal [expressions], the fruit is connected with the ritual action.

children.text: saubhare puruṣaśruter nidhanaṃ kāmasaṃyogaḥ // MS_2,2.28 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Saubhara</s> [chant], because of the mention of a person, the ending (<s>nidhana</s>) involves a [separate] connection with desire. // MS_2,2.28 //

children.text:
yo vṛṣṭikāmo yo 'nnādyakāmo yaḥ svargakāmaḥ, sa saubhareṇa stuvīta sarve vai kāmāḥ saubhara iti{*2/282*} samāmnāya tataḥ samāmananti, hīṣiti vṛṣṭikāmāya nidhanaṃ kuryāt, ūrgityannādyakāmāya, ū - iti svargakāmāyeti{*2/283*}. tatra vicāryate, kiṃ saubharam, vṛṣṭer nimittam, hīṣ ity etad aparaṃ vṛṣṭer nimittam, atha saubharam eva vṛṣṭer nimittam? yadā tad vṛṣṭer nimittam, tadā hīṣ iti saubharasya nidhanaṃ kartavyam iti (evaṃ ūrgityannādyakāmasya, ū - iti svargakāmasya ca tulyo vicāraḥ.){*2/284*} kathaṃ nidhanād aparaṃ phalam? kathaṃ vā nidhanavyavasthārthaṃ śravaṇam iti, yady evam abhi[166]{*2/285*}saṃbandhaḥ kriyate, hīṣ iti vṛṣṭikāmāya kuryād iti, tato nidhanād aparaṃ phalam, athaivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ, hīṣ iti nidhanaṃ kuryād iti, tadā nidhanavyavasthārthaṃ śravaṇam, tadā vṛṣṭikāmāyeti saubharaviśeṣaṇaṃ kriyate, na hīṣā saṃbandhaḥ.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? saubhare nidhane 'paraḥ kāmo vidhīyata iti. kutaḥ? puruṣaśruteḥ, puruṣaprayatnasyātra śravaṇaṃ bhavati, kuryād iti, tad vṛṣṭikāmasya hīṣaś ca saṃbandhe kartavye vaktavyaṃ bhavati, na tu saubharanidhanasaṃbandhe, tatra hi sāṅgaṃ saubharaṃ kuryād iti prayogavacanasāmarthyād eva siddham. tasmāt kuryād iti puruṣaprayatnavacanād avagacchāmaḥ, yatarasmin pakṣe puruṣaprayatnavacanam arthavat tataro 'yaṃ pakṣa iti, tatra asmin pakṣe 'rthavat, nidhanād aparaṃ phalam iti. tasmāt saubhara ekaḥ kāmaḥ, bhedena nidhanād api dvitīyaḥ kāma iti.
atha vā vṛṣṭikāmāyeti puruṣaśrutiḥ, vṛṣṭiṃ yaḥ kāmayate, sa puruṣo vṛṣṭikāmaśabdenocyate, tad asmin pakṣe śrutir viniyoktrī, itarasmin pakṣe punar vṛṣṭikāmaśabdena puruṣavacanena satā saubharaṃ lakṣyeta, tathā lakṣaṇāśabdaḥ syāt. śrutilakṣaṇāviṣaye ca śrutir nyāyyā, na lakṣaṇā. tasmāt paśyāmo nidhane dvitīyaḥ kāma iti. evaṃ ca phalabhūyastvaṃ bhaviṣyati, tasmān nidhane 'paraḥ kāmaḥ.
children.translated_text:
One who desires rain, one who desires food, one who desires heaven — he should chant with the <s>Saubhara</s>. 'All desires [are fulfilled by] the <s>Saubhara</s>' — having thus taught, they then teach: 'One should make the ending (<s>nidhana</s>) as <s>hīṣ</s> for one desiring rain, as <s>ūrk</s> for one desiring food, as <s>ū</s> for one desiring heaven.' There it is examined: is the <s>Saubhara</s> [itself] the cause of rain, and <s>hīṣ</s> a separate cause of rain? Or is the <s>Saubhara</s> alone the cause of rain? When the <s>Saubhara</s> is the cause of rain, then the ending <s>hīṣ</s> is to be made for [the one performing] the <s>Saubhara</s> (and similarly, the examination is the same for <s>ūrk</s> for one desiring food, and <s>ū</s> for one desiring heaven). How can there be a fruit separate from the ending? Or how can the hearing [of the desirative expression] serve the purpose of determining the ending? If the syntactic connection is made thus: 'one should make [the ending] <s>hīṣ</s> for one desiring rain' — then there is a fruit separate from the ending. But if the connection is thus: 'one should make the ending as <s>hīṣ</s>' — then the hearing serves the purpose of determining the ending, and then 'for one desiring rain' qualifies the <s>Saubhara</s>, not the connection with <s>hīṣ</s>.
What is the prima facie view? In the <s>Saubhara</s>, a separate desire is enjoined for the ending. Why? Because of the mention of a person. The mention of personal effort occurs here — 'one should make' (<s>kuryāt</s>). This [word] must be spoken when the connection between the one desiring rain and <s>hīṣ</s> is to be made, not in the connection of the ending with the <s>Saubhara</s>, for there [the fact that] one should perform the <s>Saubhara</s> with its subsidiaries is already established by the mere force of the sentence prescribing the performance. Therefore, from the word <s>kuryāt</s> which denotes personal effort, we understand: in whichever view the word denoting personal effort is meaningful, that is the [correct] view. And in this view it is meaningful — the fruit is separate from the ending. Therefore, in the <s>Saubhara</s>, there is one desire [for the chant as a whole], and by differentiation, a second desire from the ending.
Alternatively, 'for one desiring rain' is the mention of a person — the person who desires rain is denoted by the word 'one desiring rain.' In this view, the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) assigns [the function]; in the other view, the word 'one desiring rain,' being a word denoting a person, would figuratively indicate the <s>Saubhara</s> — and thus it would be a figurative word. And in a domain where both direct expression and figurative usage [are possible], direct expression is proper, not figurative usage. Therefore, we see that in the ending there is a second desire. And thus there will be an abundance of fruits. Therefore, a separate desire [exists] in the ending.

children.text: sarvasyoktakāmatvāt{*2/286*} tasmin kāmaśrutiḥ syāt, nidhanārthā punaḥśrutiḥ // MS_2,2.29 //
children.translated_text: Since all [desires] have been stated [as belonging to the whole <s>Saubhara</s>], the mention of desire should pertain to that [whole chant]; the repetition is for the purpose of [specifying] the ending. // MS_2,2.29 //

children.text:
vāsabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti, yad uktam, nidhane 'paraḥ kāma iti, naivaṃ saṃbandhaḥ kriyate, vṛṣṭikāmāya hīṣ iti kuryād iti. kathaṃ tarhi? hīṣ iti nidhanaṃ saubharasyeti. katham? hīṣo vṛṣṭikāmasaṃbandhe kriyamāṇe, nidhanaṃ [167]{*2/287*} kuryād iti saṃbandho na kṛtaḥ syāt, tatra hīṣ iti nidhanam iti nāvakalpyeta, tatrobhayasaṃbandhe vākyabhedaḥ, tatra nidhanaśabdaḥ pramādasamāmnāta iti gamyeta{*2/288*}, nacaivaṃjātīyakaḥ pramādasamāmnāta ity uktam, tasmān na hīṣo vṛṣṭikāmena saṃbandhaḥ, tena na nidhanād aparaṃ phalam.
atha hīṣo nidhanasaṃbandhe katham avākyabheda iti. ucyate, vṛṣṭikāmāya saubharam asty eva, saubharasya nidhanaṃ (saubharaprāptir){*2/289*} asty eva, tatra hīṣ iti kuryād ity eṣa evārtho vidhīyate. tasmād avākyabheda iti, ato nidhanavyavastheti gamyate. evam eva ūrg iti, ū - iti ca vaditavyam, sarvasya saubharasya ūrgvṛṣṭisvargakāmatvāc chakyate kāmavacanaiḥ saubharaṃ lakṣayitum. kim arthaṃ lakṣyata iti. nidhanārthā punaḥśrutir (nidhanavyavasthāṃ kariṣyatīty arthaḥ){*2/290*}.
children.translated_text:
The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) excludes the [previous] position. And it is not the case, as was stated, that there is a different fruit in the closing syllable (<s>nidhana</s>). The connection is not made thus — 'for one desiring rain, one should employ the syllable <s>hīṣ</s>.' How then? '<s>Hīṣ</s> is the closing syllable of the <s>Saubhara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>].' How [is this established]? If the connection of <s>hīṣ</s> with the desire for rain were being made, then the connection 'one should employ as a closing syllable' would not have been made; in that case, '<s>hīṣ</s> is the closing syllable' could not be construed. And if both connections [were attempted], there would be a splitting of the sentence. In that case, the word '<s>nidhana</s>' (closing syllable) would be understood as erroneously transmitted — but it has been stated that [a word] of this kind is not erroneously transmitted. Therefore, there is no connection of <s>hīṣ</s> with the desire for rain; hence there is no fruit other than [that of] the closing syllable.
But if <s>hīṣ</s> is connected with the closing syllable, how is there no splitting of the sentence? It is said: the <s>Saubhara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] for one desiring rain certainly exists; and the closing syllable of the <s>Saubhara</s> (the attainment of the <s>Saubhara</s>) certainly exists. There, the meaning 'one should employ <s>hīṣ</s>' is enjoined. Therefore, there is no splitting of the sentence — hence it is understood as a determination of the closing syllable. The same should be said for <s>ūrk</s> and <s>ū</s> — since the entire <s>Saubhara</s> is [connected with] the desires for vigor, rain, and heaven, [the <s>Saubhara</s>] can be indicated by the desire-expressions. For what purpose is it indicated? The re-hearing is for the purpose of the closing syllable (it will establish the determination of the closing syllable).
