children.text: guṇas tu kratusaṃyogāt karmāntaraṃ prayojayet saṃyogasyāśeṣabhūtvāt // MS_2,3.1 //
children.translated_text: But a quality, because of the connection with the sacrifice (<s>kratu</s>), would enjoin a different ritual action, since the connection has the nature of a remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>). // MS 2,3.1 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeteti, taṃ prakṛtya śrūyate, yadi rathantarasāmā somaḥ syāt, aindravāyavāgrān grahān gṛhṇīyāt, yadi bṛhatsāmā śukrāgrān, yadi gajatsāmā{*2/292*}, āgrayaṇāgrān iti. tatra sandihyate - kiṃ grahāgratāviśeṣo jyotiṣṭomasya vidhīyate, uta karmāntarasya rathantarasāmno bṛhatsāmnaś ceti. yadi rathantarasāmagrahaṇena bṛhatsāmagrahaṇena ca jyotiṣṭomo 'bhidhīyate, tatas tasya grahāgratāviśeṣaḥ, atha nābhidhīyate, tataḥ karmāntarasyeti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? prakaraṇāt, jyotiṣṭomasya. iti prāpte ucyate - guṇas tu kratusaṃyogād iti, tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati, naitad asti, jyotiṣṭomasyeti. kutaḥ? kratusaṃyogāt. kathaṃ tarhi? karmāntarasyeti. nanu jyotiṣṭomakrator evaiṣa evaṃjātīyako vādaḥ, rathantarasāmā bṛhatsāmeti. neti brūmaḥ - yadi na kṛtsnakratusaṃyogo bhavet, jyotiṣṭomasya vādaḥ, kṛtsnakratusaṃyogas tu eṣaḥ. kathaṃ kṛtsnakratusaṃyogo bhavati? kathaṃ vā na kṛtsnakratusaṃyoga iti. yadi rathantarasattā vā, bṛhatsattā vā nimittaṃ grahāgratāviśeṣasya, tato na kṛtsnakratusaṃyogaḥ, rathantaraṃ bṛhad vā yadi sāmāsti, tata aindravāyavāgratā śukrāgratā ceti, tato jyotiṣṭomasya guṇavidhiḥ. atha rathantarasāmasattā bṛhatsāmasattā vā na [169]{*2/293*} nimittam, tataḥ kṛtsnakratusaṃyogaḥ. yadi rathantarasāmeti ko 'rthaḥ? ayam arthaḥ, yadi rathantarasāma asya viśeṣaṇaṃ krator iti. kuta etat? samāsapadasāmarthyāt, samarthānāṃ hi padānāṃ samāso bhavati, sāmarthyaṃ ca bhavati viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāve, asādhāraṇaṃ ca bhavati viśeṣaṇam, tatrāyam arthaḥ, yadi rathantaram eva sāma, bṛhad eva vā nānyad iti. jyotiṣṭomasya ca bahūni sāmāni gāyatrādīni. tasmān na jyotiṣṭomasya vācakāv etau śabdāv iti. tena yady api prakaraṇāj jyotiṣṭomasya guṇavidhir iti gamyate, tathāpi tad bādhitvā vākyena rathantarasāmno bṛhatsāmnaś ca bhavitum arhati.
nanu yathā jyotiṣṭomo na rathantarasāmā, evam anyo 'pi na rathantarasāmā kaścid asti. ucyate - karmāntaraṃ rathantarasāmakaṃ kalpayiṣyaty etad vākyam, yadi rathantarasāmā somaḥ syād iti. nanu nāsty atra vidhāyakaḥ śabdaḥ. ucyate - asti ya eṣaḥ syād iti. āha - naiṣa vidhātuṃ śaknoti, yadiśabdasaṃbandhād vidyamānasya nimittārthenaivaṃjātīyakaḥ śabdo bhavati, na vidhānārtheneti. atra brūmaḥ - yad etat sayadikaṃ vākyam, yadi rathanatarasāmā somaḥ syād iti, atrāvāntaravākyam asti, rathantarasāmā somaḥ syād iti, yad avāntaravākyaṃ tasyānyo 'rthaḥ, anyaś ca sayadikasya, sayadiko na śaknoti vidhātum, yata avāntaravākyam, tadvidhāsyati. na ca, rathantarasāmno bṛhatsāmno vā bhāvo nimittatvena śrūyamāṇo 'py arthavān bhavati. tasmād avivakṣito yadisaṃbandhaḥ, tasmiṃś cāvivakṣite padadvayam idaṃ rathantarasāmā somaḥ syād iti śaknoti rathantarasāmānaṃ kratuṃ vidhātum, yadīty anarthakam.
atha vā yadi rocetety adhyāhāraḥ. atha vā yathaitad bhavati, payasā ṣāṣṭikaṃ bhuñjīta, yadi śāliṃ bhuñjīta, tatra dadhyupasiñced [170]{*2/294*} iti. evaṃjātīyakena vākyena śālibhojanaṃ vihitaṃ bhavati, evam atrāpi vihitaṃ draṣṭavyam, yadi rathantarasāmā somaḥ syāt, aindravāyavāgrān grahān gṛhṇīyād iti. kathaṃ punaḥ śālibhojanaṃ tena vākyena vihitaṃ bhavatīti. ucyate - vyatyāsena saṃbandhaḥ kalpyeta, yadi dadhyupasecanam icchet, śāliṃ bhuñjīteti.
nanu na khalv icchateḥ parāṃ liṅvibhaktim upalabhāmahe, siñcater hi tāṃ parāṃ samāmnantīti. siñcateḥ khalu sā parā samuccarantī kamer arthaṃ gamayati, kāmapravedane hi tāṃ manyāmaha iti, evam ihāpi yady aindravāyavāgrān grahān gṛhṇīyād iti grahītum icched ity arthaḥ, tato rathanatarasāmānaṃ kratuṃ kuryād iti. nanv evaṃ saty icchāmātraṃ bhavet, na grahāgratviśeṣavidhānam. ucyate - yathāsmin laukike vākye, yadi dadhyupasecanam icchet, śāliṃ bhuñjīteti dadhyupasecanasaṃkīrtanād dadhyupasiktaṃ śāliṃ bhuñjīteti tenaikavākyatvād gamyate, evam atrāpi grahāgratāviśeṣasaṅkīrtanāt tenaikavākyatvād grahāgratāviśiṣṭo rathantarasāmā gamyate. atha vātra hetuhetumator liṅ, rathantarasāmā soma aindravāyavāgrāṇāṃ grahāṇāṃ hetuḥ kartavya iti. tasmāt kṛtsnakratusaṃyogād guṇaḥ karmāntaraṃ prayojayet, evaṃ kṛtsnakratusaṃyogo 'rthavān bhaviṣyati.
api ca pūrveṇa nimittena bhavitavyam, pareṇa naimittikena. katham? sati hi nimitte naimittikaṃ bhavitum arhati, nāsati, yac ca bhaviṣyat tan na sat, bhaviṣyac ca rathantarasāma, tat kathaṃ pūrvakālasya grahāgratāviśeṣasya nimittaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. api ca niḥsandigdhaṃ jagatsāmā karmāntaram, tatsāmānyād itarad api karmāntaram iti gamyate. tasmān na jyotiṣṭomasya guṇavidhānam iti.
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — and with reference to that, it is heard: 'If the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] has the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>, one should take the cups beginning with the <s>Aindravāyava</s>; if it has the <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>, [one should take the cups] beginning with the <s>Śukra</s>; if it has the <s>Jagat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>, [beginning with] the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>.' There, the doubt arises: is a specific ordering of the cups (<s>graha</s>) being enjoined as a quality of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, or for a different sacrifice (<s>kratu</s>) — one having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>, and another having the <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>? If the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is denoted by [the expression] 'having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>' and 'having the <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>,' then the specific ordering of cups is its [quality]. But if it is not so denoted, then [the ordering belongs to] a different sacrifice.
What is the prima facie view? Because of the context, [it is a quality] of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Having arrived at this, it is said: But a quality, because of the connection with the sacrifice — the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) excludes the [previous] position — this is not the case, that [it is a quality] of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Why? Because of the connection with the sacrifice. How then? [It belongs to] a different sacrifice. [Objection:] But this kind of discussion applies precisely to the sacrifice called <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — 'having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>, having the <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>.' [Reply:] No, we say. If there were no connection with the entire sacrifice, [it would be] a quality of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; but there is indeed a connection with the entire sacrifice. How does the connection with the entire sacrifice occur? And how does it not? If the existence of the <s>Rathantara</s> or the <s>Bṛhat</s> is the cause of the specific cup-ordering, then there is no connection with the entire sacrifice — [the meaning would be:] if the <s>Rathantara</s> or the <s>Bṛhat</s> is the <s>Sāman</s>, then the <s>Aindravāyava</s>-priority or the <s>Śukra</s>-priority [follows]. In that case, it would be a quality-injunction of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. But if the existence of the <s>Rathantara-sāma</s> or <s>Bṛhat-sāma</s> is not the cause, then there is a connection with the entire sacrifice. [In the expression] 'if having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>' — what is the meaning? The meaning is: 'if the <s>Rathantara</s> alone is the <s>Sāman</s> of this sacrifice' — [this is understood as] a qualifier. How so? From the capacity of the compound words: for a compound occurs among words that have capacity [for mutual relation], and the capacity consists in the qualifier-qualified relationship; and the qualifier is exclusive. Thus the meaning is: 'if the <s>Rathantara</s> alone is the <s>Sāman</s>, or the <s>Bṛhat</s> alone, and no other.' But the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> has many <s>Sāmans</s> — <s>Gāyatra</s> and others. Therefore, these two words do not denote the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Hence, even though from the context one understands [it as] a quality-injunction of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, nevertheless, overriding that [contextual inference] by the sentence, it ought to belong to [sacrifices] having the <s>Rathantara</s> and the <s>Bṛhat</s> as their <s>Sāmans</s>.
[Objection:] But just as the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> does not have [only] the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>, so too no other [sacrifice] has it. [Reply:] It is said: this sentence will postulate a different sacrifice having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s> — 'if the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] has the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>.' [Objection:] But there is no injunctive word here. [Reply:] It is said: there is — namely, this word <s>syāt</s> (would be). [Objection:] But this word cannot enjoin, because in connection with the word 'if' (<s>yadi</s>), a word of this kind is used for the condition of something already existing, not for the purpose of injunction. [Reply:] To this we say: this sentence containing 'if' — 'if the <s>Soma</s> has the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>' — has a sub-sentence: 'the <s>Soma</s> has the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>.' The sub-sentence has one meaning, and the whole sentence with 'if' has another. The whole sentence with 'if' cannot enjoin, but the sub-sentence can. And the existence of the <s>Rathantara-sāma</s> or <s>Bṛhat-sāma</s>, even though heard as a condition, cannot be meaningful [merely as a condition]. Therefore, the connection with 'if' is not intended; and when that [connection] is not intended, the two words 'rathantarasāmā somaḥ syāt' can enjoin a sacrifice having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>; the word 'if' is meaningless.
Or alternatively, [one should supply:] 'if one should choose.' Or alternatively, just as this [sentence] works: 'One should eat <s>ṣāṣṭika</s> rice with milk; if one eats <s>śāli</s> rice, one should pour curds on it.' By a sentence of this kind, the eating of <s>śāli</s> rice is enjoined. Similarly, here too, an injunction should be seen: 'if the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] has the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>, one should take the cups beginning with the <s>Aindravāyava</s>.' But how is the eating of <s>śāli</s> rice enjoined by that sentence? It is said: the connection should be construed in reverse order — 'if one desires a curds-topping, one should eat <s>śāli</s> rice.'
[Objection:] But we do not find the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) form of the verb 'to desire' (<s>iṣ</s>), for [the grammarians] teach the optative as belonging to the verb 'to sprinkle' (<s>sic</s>). [Reply:] Indeed, the optative of 'to sprinkle,' when uttered, conveys the meaning of 'to desire' — for we consider the optative to express desire. Similarly here too, 'if he should take the cups beginning with the <s>Aindravāyava</s>' means 'if he desires to take' — then he should perform a sacrifice having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>. [Objection:] But in that case, there would be merely a desire, not an injunction of the specific cup-ordering. [Reply:] It is said: just as in the worldly sentence 'if one desires a curds-topping, one should eat <s>śāli</s> rice,' because curds-topping is mentioned together [with the eating], and because of the syntactic unity, it is understood as 'one should eat <s>śāli</s> rice topped with curds' — similarly here too, because the specific cup-ordering is mentioned together, and because of the syntactic unity, a sacrifice having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s> together with the specific cup-ordering is understood. Or alternatively, the optative here [expresses] a cause-effect relationship: a <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] having the <s>Rathantara</s> as its <s>Sāman</s> is to be the cause of [the specific] cup-ordering. Therefore, because of the connection with the entire sacrifice, a quality [of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] would [actually] enjoin a different ritual action — thus the connection with the entire sacrifice becomes meaningful.
Moreover, the condition should come first, and the conditioned result after. How? For when a condition exists, the conditioned [result] can occur — not when it does not exist. And what will exist in the future is not [yet] existing; and the <s>Rathantara-sāma</s> will exist [in the future]. How then can it be the condition of the prior cup-ordering? Moreover, [the sacrifice] having the <s>Jagat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s> is indubitably a different sacrifice; by analogy with that, the other [two] are also understood as different sacrifices. Therefore, this is not a quality-injunction of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.

children.text:
tuśabdāt pakṣo 'nyathā bhavati, naitad asti, yad uktam, kratvantaram iti. kathaṃ tarhi? jyotiṣṭomasyaiva grahāgratāviśeṣa iti. kutaḥ? prakaraṇasāmarthyāt. nanv etad uktam - vākyasāmarthyāt kratvantarasya rathantarasāmno bṛhatsāmnaś ceti. parihṛtam etaj jyotiṣṭoma eva rathantarasāmā bṛhatsāmā ceti. punar dūṣitam anekasāmatvāj jyotiṣṭomasya, viśeṣaṇaṃ rathantareṇa bṛhatā vā na prakalpata iti. tad ucyate - prakalpate viśeṣaṇam, bṛhadrathantarayor vaikalpikatvāt, bhavati sa prayogaḥ, yatra rathantaraṃ nāsti. bhavati ca sa prayogaḥ, vidyamānarathantarasāmakaḥ, tad etat rathantaraṃ sattayaivāsādhāraṇatvād viśeṣakam. tasmāj jyotiṣṭoma eva rathanatarasāmā bṛhatsāmā ceti.
atha yad uktam - pūrveṇa nimittena bhavitavyam, uttareṇa naimittikeneti. naitat, niyogato bhavati hi bhaviṣyad api nimittam, yathā varṣiṣyatīti kṛṣigṛhakarmānuṣṭhānam, api ca tad dṛṣṭam, idaṃ ca vācanikaṃ nimittam, tad yathāvacanaṃ bhavitum arhati. syād iti ceyaṃ liṅ triṣv api kāleṣu bhavati. tasmād bhaviṣyad api nimittam. yat tu jagatsāmeti karmāntaram, tatsāmānyād rathantarasāmāpi karmāntaram iti. jagatsāma, asaṃbhavāt karmāntaraṃ saṃbhavati, rathantarasāmno bṛhatsāmnaś ca jyotiṣṭomasyābhidhānam, tasmān na karmāntaram iti.
children.translated_text:
By the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), the position changes. This is not the case — that it is a different sacrifice. How then? It is a specific cup-ordering of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself. Why? Because of the capacity of the context. [Objection:] But it was stated — because of the capacity of the sentence, [it belongs to] a different sacrifice having the <s>Rathantara</s> and the <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>. [Reply:] This is refuted — the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself has the <s>Rathantara</s> and the <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>. [Objection:] It was further argued — since the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> has many <s>Sāmans</s>, qualification by the <s>Rathantara</s> or the <s>Bṛhat</s> does not work. [Reply:] To this it is said: the qualification does work, because the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are alternatives. There is a performance where the <s>Rathantara</s> is absent, and there is a performance with the <s>Rathantara-sāma</s> present — and so the <s>Rathantara</s>, by its very presence [in one but not the other], serves as an exclusive qualifier. Therefore, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself has the <s>Rathantara</s> and the <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s>.
As for what was said — 'the condition should come first and the conditioned result after' — this is not so. Even what will exist in the future can necessarily be a condition, just as [one says:] 'It will rain — [therefore] agricultural and domestic work [should be done].' Moreover, that [argument about temporal priority] pertains to observable [conditions], while this is a scriptural condition — it should be [accepted] as scripture states. And the optative <s>syāt</s> applies to all three tenses. Therefore, even what will exist in the future can be a condition.
As for [the argument] that the [sacrifice] having the <s>Jagat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s> is a different sacrifice, and by analogy the [sacrifice having] the <s>Rathantara</s> and <s>Bṛhat</s> as its <s>Sāman</s> is also a different sacrifice — [the response is:] the <s>Jagat-sāma</s>, because [it] cannot [apply to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], is a different sacrifice. But the <s>Rathantara-sāma</s> and <s>Bṛhat-sāma</s> do denote the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; therefore, [they do] not [denote] a different sacrifice.

children.text:
sati rājasūyaḥ, rājā rājasūyena svārājyakāmo yajeteti. taṃ prakṛtyāmananty aveṣṭiṃ nāmeṣṭim, āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇetyevamādi. tāṃ prakṛtya vidhīyate, yadi brāhmaṇo yajeta bārhaspatyaṃ madhye nidhāyāhutim āhutiṃ hutvābhighārayet, yadi rājanya aindram, yadi vaiśyo vaiśvadevam iti. tatra sandihyate, kiṃ brāhmaṇādīnāṃ prāptānāṃ nimittārthena śravaṇam, uta brāhmaṇādīnām ayaṃ yāgo vidhīyata iti. kathaṃ nimittārthatā bhavet? kathaṃ vā yāgavidhānam iti. yadi rājaśabdo brāhmaṇādiṣv api kenacit prakāreṇa, tato nimittārthatā. atha kṣatriya eva, tataḥ prāpakāṇy evaṃjātīyakāni śravaṇāni.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? nimittārthateti, tata evaṃ tāvad upavarṇyate, yaugiko rājaśabda iti, rājyaṃ yasya karma, sa rājā. kiṃ punā rājakarma? janapadapuraparirakṣaṇe, tataś coddharaṇe rājyaśabdam āryāvartanivāsinaḥ prayuñjante. rājñaḥ karma rājyam iti cābhiyuktā upadiśanti. tena manyāmahe, yasyaitat karma sa rājeti, yathā ya udameghaṃ nāma kaṃcit puruṣaṃ nāvediṣuḥ, tasya tu putram audameghir ity evaṃ viduḥ, śaknuyus te yas tasya pitā, sa udamegha iti kalpayitum, udameghaputrasyaivaṃ samabhivyāhāro bhavatīti. evaṃ rājyayogād rājaśabda iti vijñāyate.
nanu janapadapuraparirakṣaṇavṛttim anupajīvaty api kṣatriye rājaśabdam āndhrāḥ prayuñjante prayoktāraḥ. na brūmaḥ, na prayuñjata iti, kiṃ tarhi karmaviśeṣanimittatvād rājaśabdasya, tadyogād api [173]{*2/297*} rājaśabdo bhavatīty etad upapādayāmaḥ. prayuñjate ca tad yukte rājaśabdam akṣatriye 'pi, tad asminn upapanne prakaraṇavaśāt, yadiśabdasamabhivyāhārāc ca rājasūyasyaiva guṇavidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati, na brāhmaṇasya vaiśyasya ca karmāntaraṃ vidhāyiṣyatīti.
atha vāsārvalaukikasya prayogasya sārvalaukikena prayogeṇa virudhyamānasyāprāmāṇyaṃ syāt, abhyupagacchanti hi te janapadinaḥ, sārvabhaumaṃ prayogam. api cāvipragītā laukikā arthā vipragītebhyaḥ pratyayitatarā bhavanti, tathāryāvartanivāsināṃ śabdārthopāyeṣv abhiyuktānām abhivyāharatāṃ karmāṇi cānutiṣṭhatām antyajanapadavāsibhyo mlecchebhyaḥ samīcīnatara ācāro bhavati. tasmād yaugiko rājaśabdaḥ, nimittārthāni śravaṇāni, rājasūyasya guṇavidhir na karmāntaram iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - aveṣṭau tu khalu kratupradhānaṃ brāhmaṇādiśravaṇam, brāhmaṇādīnām aveṣṭiyāgaṃ vidhātum, na nimittārtham. kutaḥ? aprāptatvād brāhmaṇavaiśyayoḥ. katham aprāptiḥ? kṣatriyasya rājasūyavidhānāt, rājā rājasūyena yajeteti. nanūktam - yaugiko rājaśabda iti. etad apy ayuktam, yataḥ jātivacana iti. nanūbhayābhidhāne yadiśabdasaṃbandhāt, prakaraṇāc ca na karmāntaravidhānaṃ nyāyyam ity uktam. atrocyate - nobhayābhidhānam avakalpate. kutaḥ? yadi tāvaj jātiśabdo rājeti, tataḥ tatkarmatvāj janapadaparipālane rājyaśabdo bhaviṣyati, tenāryāvartanivāsināṃ prayogo na virotsyate. atha yadi rājyaśabdaḥ paripālane nityasaṃbaddho bhaviṣyati, tatas tasya karteti rājaśabdaḥ kṣatriyajātau tannimitto bhaviṣyati, tatrāndhrāṇāṃ prayogo na virotysyate. tasmān na prayogadarśanād ubhāv api rājarājyaśabdau jātiparipālanābhyāṃ nityasaṃbaddhāv ity abhyupagantavyam. ko nu khalu nirṇayaḥ? rājajātīyasya karma [174]{*2/298*} ity ataḥ paripālanaṃ rājyaśabdenocyate, evaṃ hi smaranto 'bhiyuktāḥ tasya karmeti ṣyañpratyayaṃ vidadhati, na tu tasya karteti pratyayalopaṃ vā, prātipadikapratyāpattiṃ vā samāmananti. tasmād rājñaḥ karma rājyam, na rājyasya kartā rājā.
nanu yo yo janapadapuraparirakṣaṇaṃ karoti, taṃ tu loko rājaśabdenābhivadati. ucyate - yogāl lokaḥ prayuṅkte, paripālane rājyaśabdaḥ prasiddha iti, sa tu paripālane rājyaśabdo rājayogād ity asmābhir uktam, tasmād rājaśabdaḥ prasiddher mūlam, tadyogād rājyaśabdaḥ, tadayogād{*2/299*} api brāhmaṇavaiśyayo rājaśabdaḥ prayujyate. na tv evaṃ smaranti, rājyayogād rājeti.
yat tūktam - anumānād rājyasya kartā yaḥ sa rājā, yathā audamegheḥ pitodamegha iti. ucyate - anumānāt prayogo balavān, rājyasya kartāraṃ rājety anumimīmahe, kṣatriye tu pratyakṣaṃ prayuñjānān upalabhāmahe. tathā yogam apy anumimīmahe, rājyasya kartā rājeti. rājñaḥ karma rājyam iti tu smaranti. anumimānāś ca smṛtiṃ anumimate sma, smarantas tu pratyakṣam upalabhante, tena tatra smṛtir balīyasīti. āha - yo yo rājyaṃ karoti, tatra rājaśabdaṃ prayuñjate, na yad rājñaḥ karma tad rājyam iti, tena manyāmahe, rājyayogo rājaśadapravṛttau nimittam, na tu rājayogo rājyaśabdapravṛttāv iti. na brūmaḥ, prayogād vayaṃ rājayogaṃ rājyaśabdapravṛttau nimittam avagacchāma iti. kathaṃ tarhi? smaraṇāt, prayogāc ca smṛtir balīyasī, prayogād dhi smṛtir anumīyeta.
[175]{*2/300*} api ca rājyayogasya nimittatā vyabhicarati, janapadaparipālanam akurvaty api rājety āndhrā vadantīty uktam. nanu rājayogād rājyam ity etad api vyabhicarati, na hi rājñaḥ syanditaṃ{*2/301*} nimiṣitaṃ ca sarvaṃ rājyam ity ucyate. yadi vayaṃ prayogān nimittabhāvaṃ brūyām, tata evam upālabhyemahi. smṛtyā tu vayaṃ nimittabhāvaṃ brūmaḥ, tena yad yad rājajātīyasya karma jātyā viśeṣyate, tad rājyam ity abhyupagacchāmaḥ. yat tūktam - āndhrā api rājyayogād rājānam abhyupa-gacchantīti, parihṛtam etat, prayogo durbalaḥ smṛter iti. yad uktam - āryāvartanivāsinaḥ, pramāṇam itarebhya ācārebhya iti. tulyaḥ śabdaprayoga ācāreṣv ity uktam. tasmāj jātinimitto rājaśabdaḥ, evaṃ ced yajñasaṃyogāt kṣatriyasya rājasūyena, yāgavidhir aveṣṭir iti.
children.translated_text:
Given [that it is established], the <s>Rājasūya</s> [sacrifice exists]: 'A king should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s>, one who desires sovereignty.' Taking that [<s>Rājasūya</s>] as the basis, they teach the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> sacrifice: 'An <s>Āgneya</s> (related to <s>Agni</s>) eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake], with gold as the sacrificial fee,' and so on. Taking that as the basis, it is enjoined: 'If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should sacrifice, he should place a <s>Bārhaspatya</s> (related to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) [offering] in the middle and pour ghee offering after offering; if a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, an <s>Aindra</s> (related to <s>Indra</s>) [offering]; if a <s>Vaiśya</s>, a <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (related to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>) [offering].' Here the doubt arises: Is the mention of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the others for the purpose of [specifying] the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) for those [already] entitled [to the <s>Rājasūya</s>], or is this sacrifice being enjoined for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the others [as new eligible performers]? How would it serve as an occasion? Or how would it be an injunction of a sacrifice? If the word <s>rāja</s> (king) applies to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the others in some way, then it serves as an occasion. But if [it applies] only to a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, then the statements of this kind are injunctions of [new] eligibility.
What is the prima facie view? It serves as an occasion. Thus it is first explained: The word <s>rāja</s> is etymologically derived (<s>yaugika</s>) — he whose activity is ruling (<s>rājya</s>), he is a king (<s>rāja</s>). What then is the king's activity? The protection of the people and cities, and governance (<s>uddharaṇa</s>) — the inhabitants of <s>Āryāvarta</s> use the word <s>rājya</s> for this. And the learned instruct: 'The king's activity is kingship (<s>rājya</s>).' Therefore, we consider that he whose activity this is, he is a king — just as those who did not know a certain person named <s>Udamegha</s>, but knew his son as <s>Audameghi</s>, could construe 'he whose son this is, he is <s>Udamegha</s>' — because the son of <s>Udamegha</s> has this designation. Similarly, from the connection with kingship, the word <s>rāja</s> is understood.
[Objection:] But the <s>Āndhra</s> people use the word <s>rāja</s> even for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> who does not engage in the activity of protecting people and cities. [Reply:] We do not say that they do not use [it thus]. Rather, since the word <s>rāja</s> has its origin in a specific activity, we demonstrate that from the connection with that [activity] too, the word <s>rāja</s> applies. And they do use the word <s>rāja</s> even for a non-<s>Kṣatriya</s> who is connected with that [activity]. Given this, by the force of context and by the co-occurrence with the word 'if' (<s>yadi</s>), it will be a quality-injunction of the <s>Rājasūya</s> itself, and will not enjoin a different ritual action for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Alternatively, a non-universal usage, when contradicted by a universal usage, would be non-authoritative — for the inhabitants of a [particular] region accept the universal practice. Moreover, undisputed worldly conventions are more credible than disputed ones. Similarly, the usage and practice of the inhabitants of <s>Āryāvarta</s>, who are experts in word-meanings, are more correct than those of barbarians (<s>mlecchas</s>) dwelling on the borders of the regions. Therefore, the word <s>rāja</s> is etymologically derived; the statements [about <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the others] serve as occasions; it is a quality-injunction of the <s>Rājasūya</s>, not a different ritual action.
Having arrived at this position, we say: In the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>, the mention of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the others is principally for the purpose of [enjoining the] sacrifice — to enjoin the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>-sacrifice for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the others, not for the purpose of [specifying] an occasion. Why? Because the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> are not [otherwise] entitled [to perform the <s>Rājasūya</s>]. How are they not entitled? Because the <s>Rājasūya</s> is enjoined for the <s>Kṣatriya</s> — 'A king should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s>.' But was it not said that the word <s>rāja</s> is etymologically derived? That too is improper, because [the word <s>rāja</s>] denotes a class (<s>jāti</s>). But was it not said that since both [meanings] are expressed, by the connection with 'if' and by the context, it is not proper to enjoin a different ritual action? To this we say: Both [meanings] cannot be construed [simultaneously]. Why? If the word <s>rāja</s> is a class-term, then because [ruling] is the activity of that [class], the word <s>rājya</s> (kingship) will apply to the protection of the people — thus the usage of the inhabitants of <s>Āryāvarta</s> will not be contradicted. But if the word <s>rājya</s> is permanently connected with [the activity of] protection, then the word <s>rāja</s> — [meaning] 'its agent' — will apply to the <s>Kṣatriya</s> class on account of that [connection], and thus the usage of the <s>Āndhra</s> people will not be contradicted. Therefore, from the observation of usage, one should not accept that both the words <s>rāja</s> and <s>rājya</s> are permanently connected with class and protection [respectively]. What then is the definitive determination? [The word] <s>rājya</s> denotes the activity of one who belongs to the king's class — thus protection is called <s>rājya</s>. For this is how the learned remember — 'his activity' — and they form the suffix <s>ṣyañ</s> [to derive <s>rājya</s>]; they do not teach 'its agent' with the deletion of a suffix or recovery of the <s>prātipadika</s> (stem). Therefore, <s>rājya</s> is the activity of the king; the king is not [defined as] the agent of <s>rājya</s>.
But whoever performs the protection of people and cities — him the world addresses with the word <s>rāja</s>. It is replied: The world uses [the word] through connection (<s>yoga</s>). The word <s>rājya</s> is well-known in [the sense of] protection — but that word <s>rājya</s> [denoting] protection is [so called] because of its connection with the king (<s>rāja</s>), as we have stated. Therefore, the word <s>rāja</s> is the root of the convention, and from its connection comes the word <s>rājya</s>. And even without that connection, the word <s>rāja</s> is used for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> [who rule]. But they do not remember it as 'from the connection with kingship, [one is called] king.'
As for what was said — 'By inference, whoever is the agent of kingship is a king, just as from <s>Audameghi</s>, [one infers] that his father is <s>Udamegha</s>' — it is replied: Usage is stronger than inference. We infer 'the agent of kingship is a king,' but we directly observe [people] using [the word <s>rāja</s>] for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>. Similarly, we also infer a connection — 'the agent of kingship is a king.' But they remember 'the king's activity is kingship.' And those who infer rely on memory (<s>smṛti</s>), while those who remember rely on direct observation — therefore, memory is stronger. He says: 'Whoever performs kingship, for him they use the word <s>rāja</s> — not [in the sense] that what is the king's activity is kingship.' Therefore, we think that connection with kingship is the cause of the usage of the word <s>rāja</s>, not connection with [the class of] king the cause of the usage of the word <s>rājya</s>. We do not say that from usage we understand that connection with king is the cause of the usage of the word <s>rājya</s>. How then? From memory (<s>smṛti</s>) — and memory is stronger than usage, for memory is inferred from usage.
Moreover, the [argument from] the causal connection with kingship is subject to deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) — [for] the <s>Āndhra</s> people say <s>rāja</s> even for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> who does not protect the people, as stated. [Objection:] But the other [view] too — that kingship derives from [the class of] king — is also subject to deviation, for not every twitching and blinking of a king is called kingship. [Reply:] If we were deriving the causal connection from usage, we would be open to this criticism. But we derive the causal connection from memory. Therefore, whatever activity of the king-class is specified by the class, that is kingship — this we accept. As for what was said — 'even the <s>Āndhra</s> people accept [the word <s>rāja</s>] from the connection with kingship' — that has been answered: usage is weaker than memory. As for what was said — 'the inhabitants of <s>Āryāvarta</s> are authoritative over other customs' — it was [also] said that word-usage is the same across customs. Therefore, the word <s>rāja</s> has class (<s>jāti</s>) as its cause. If so, because of the connection with sacrifice, the <s>Rājasūya</s> is [restricted to] the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> is an injunction of [a separate] sacrifice [for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s>].

idaṃ samāmananti, vasante brāhmaṇo agnīn ādadhīta, grīṣme rājyanyaḥ, śaradi vaiśya iti{*2/303*}. tatra sandihyate - kiṃ brāhmaṇādiśravaṇaṃ nimittārtham, brāhmaṇādaya ādadhānā vasantādiṣv ādadhīrann iti, uta brāhmaṇādīnām ādhānaṃ vidhīyata iti. kathaṃ nimittārthatā syāt? kathaṃ cādhānavidhānam iti. yadi brāhmaṇo vasanta iti padadvayaṃ parasparaṃ saṃbaddham, tato nimittārthaṃ śravaṇam. atha brāhmaṇa ādadhīteti, ādhānavidhānaṃ brāhmaṇasya. evaṃ rājanyādiṣv api.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? nimittārthaṃ śravaṇam iti. kutaḥ? nimittasarūpā ete śabdāḥ. kiṃ nimittasārūpyam? brāhmaṇā[176]{*2/304*}dīnāṃ vasantādibhiḥ samuccāraṇam, tac cāviditaṃ vedyata iti. nanu brāhmaṇādīnāṃ ādadhati nāpy asti samuccāraṇam. vāḍham{*2/305*} asti samuccāraṇam, na tv amīṣām ādhānasaṃbandho na viditaḥ. kena prāpto vidita iti. kāmaśrutibhiḥ. kāḥ kāmaśrutayaḥ? agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajetetyevamādayaḥ. kathamābhiḥ śrutibhir ādhānaṃ prāptam iti. ucyate - sāmarthyāt, yathāgnihotram abhinirvartyate, tathā kuryāt. yathā darśapūrṇamāsāv abhinirvartyete, tathā kuryāt. na ca, gārhapatyāhavanīyānvāhāryapacanādibhyo vinā, etāni karmāṇi sidhyanti, samāmananti hi, yad āhavanīye juhoti, tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prīto bhavatītyevamādi{*2/306*}. tena sāmarthyād etad uktaṃ bhavati - āhavanīyādi kartavyam iti, tac cādhānena vinā na sidhyatīty ādhānam api kartavyam ity avagamyate. tat kena kartavyam? yasya kāmaśrutayaḥ. tāś cāviṣeśeṇa brāhmaṇādīnām. tasmād amīṣām ādhānasaṃbandho vidita iti. api ca, ubhābhyāṃ brāhmaṇādīnāṃ saṃbandhe vidhīyamāne vākyam bhidyeta. na hi, tadānīm eko 'rtho vidhīyate. ato nimittārthāḥ śrutaya ity evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ādhāne sarvaśeṣatvāt{*2/307*} prāpakāṇyādhānasyaitāni śravaṇāni. kutaḥ? sarvakarmaṇāṃ śeṣabhūtam ādhānam iti na śrutiliṅgādīnām anyatamenocyate, kiṃ tarhi, agnīnāṃ sarvaśeṣatvāt, taccheṣatvāc cādhānasya. kim ataḥ? yady evam, agnayaḥ kāmaśrutibhiḥ prāpnuvanti, nādhānm iti. nanv agnīnām abhyupāya ādhānam iti. ucyate - naiteṣām arjane ādhānam evaiko 'bhyupāyaḥ, kiṃ tarhi yathānyeṣāṃ dravyāṇām utpādane [177]{*2/308*} krayaṇādayaś cābhyupāyāḥ, evam agnīnām apīti na niyogataḥ utpādanam eva, tena pakṣe ādhānaṃ prāpnoti, pakṣe na. yatarasmin pakṣe 'prāptiḥ, tataraḥ pakṣa utpattiṃ prayojayiṣyati brāhmaṇādīnām ādhānasya, brāhmaṇa ātmārtham ādadhīteti yadaitad vacanam, tadātmārtham evāhitā āhavanīyādayo bhavanti, nānyathā. evaṃ ca sati, na kṛtrimeṇa yācitena vā karmāṇy agnihotrādīny anuṣṭhātavyānīti gamyate. tenākṛtrima eva kevalo 'gnis teṣāṃ sādhaka iti niścīyate. kathaṃ cātmārthatādhānasya gamyata iti. kartrabhiprāye hi kriyāphala ādadhītety etad ātmanepadaṃ saṃbhavati. asatyasmin vacane kāmaśrutiparigrahe nādhānasyātmārthatā bhavet.
api ca satīṣv etāsv ādhānaśrutiṣu na kāmaśrutayaḥ śaknuvanty aparām ādhānaśrutiṃ kalpayitum, yathā prāptasyādhānasya punaḥśrutayaḥ etā bhaveyuḥ, asatīṣv etāsv ādhānaśrutim aparigṛhṇantaḥ{*2/309*} kāmaśrutayo 'śakyān agnihotrādīn vadantīti parigṛhṇīyur ādhānaśrutim. satīṣv etāsu yeṣām ādhānam uktam, tān adhikṛtyottarakālāḥ kāmaśrutayo bhavantīti gamyate.
atrāha - asti kevalasyādhānasya vidhāyikā śrutiḥ, evaṃ sapatnaṃ{*2/310*} bhrātṛvyam avarti sahate, ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatta iti, tayā prāptasya nimittārthāni brāhmaṇādīnāṃ śravaṇāni bhaviṣyanti. ucyate - saṃbhāravidhānārthā punaḥśrutir eṣā.
neti brūmaḥ, bhinnaṃ hīdaṃ vākyam saṃbhāravidhānavākyāt, anyo hy artha ādhatta iti, anya apa upasṛjatīti, ekārthavidhāne hy ekaṃ vākyaṃ bhavati, bhinnau cemāv arthau, tasmād atra vākyabheda iti.
ucyate - vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnīn ādadhītety asyāṃ śrutau satyāṃ punaḥśrutiḥ kevalasyādhānasyāvidhāyikā, apām upasarjanaṃ tu [178]{*2/311*} vidhīyate, tad ekasminn arthe vidhīyamāne nānekārthaṃ bhavati. nanv ādhānasyaitad vidhānam, guṇārthā sā punaḥśrutiḥ. neti brūmaḥ, sā brāhmaṇādisaṃbaddhā prathamā śrutiḥ, iyaṃ kevalā punaḥśrutiḥ. kutaḥ? sā hi śabdena vidadhāti, tatra liṅgam uccarantīṃ paśyāmaḥ, iyaṃ praśastam ādhānam ity āha. tataḥ praśastatām ādhānasyānumanyāmahe. evaṃ ca, vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnīn ādadhītety eṣā vidhāyikā śrutir iti brūmahe, naitat praśaṃsāvacanam asmatpakṣaṃ bādhate, śakyate hy anyena vihitam anyena praśastam iti vaditum. yadi tv etad vidhāyakam ity ucyate{*2/312*}, tato 'smatpakṣaṃ virudhyeta. katham? ajñātasya jñāpanaṃ vidhānam etat, yadi prāśaṃsāvacanenāpūrvaṃ vijñāpyeta, tadā liṅgā nāpūrvaṃ jñāpitaṃ bhavet, tatrāpūrvajñāpanavacanaḥ śabdaḥ uparudhyeta. na tu liṅgā vihite praśaṃsāvacanam uparudhyate, vihite 'pi hi vākyāntareṇa praśaṃsāvacanam avakalpate. api ca yal liṅgā vidhānam, tat śrutyā, vākyena tu praśaṃsā gamyate, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī.
nanv idam api vākyam, brāhmaṇo 'gnīn ādadhīteti. ucyate - svapadārtham atra śrutir vidadhāty ādhānam, brāhmaṇādisaṃbandhena parapadārthaṃ praśaṃsati, ya evaṃ sapatnaṃ{*2/313*} bhrātṛvyam avarti sahata iti. nanv anekaguṇavidhānaṃ tvayā vākyenādhyavasitaṃ bhavati. naiṣa doṣaḥ, aguṇavidhipare hi vākye bhavaty anekaguṇavidhānam ity uktam, tadguṇās tu vidhīyerann avibhāgād vidhārthe na ced anyena śiṣṭā iti{*2/314*}. tasmād brāhmaṇādisaṃyuktā vidhāyikā śrutiḥ, iyam api kevalasyādhānasya punaḥśrutiḥ saṃbhāravidhānam upakramitum iti siddham.
yad uktam - anekaguṇavidhāne vākyaṃ bhidyeteti, yadīmau guṇavidhānaviśiṣṭau{*2/315*} vidhīyeyātām, bhaved vākyabhedaḥ, dvābhyāṃ tu viśeṣaṇābhyāṃ viśiṣṭam ekam ādhānaṃ vidhāyiṣyate, [179]{*2/316*} tena na bhaviṣyati vākyabhedaḥ. tasmād brāhmaṇādīnāṃ ādhānasya prāpakāṇi śravaṇānīti siddham.
children.translated_text:
They teach in the revealed tradition: 'In spring a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the [sacred] fires; in summer a <s>Kṣatriya</s>; in autumn a <s>Vaiśya</s>.' There a doubt arises: is the mention of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like for the purpose of [specifying] the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) — that <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like, when establishing fires, should do so in spring and the like — or is the fire-establishment itself being enjoined for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like? How would the occasion-interpretation work? And how would the injunction of fire-establishment [work]? If the two words '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' and '<s>vasanta</s>' (spring) are connected with each other, then the statement serves the purpose of [specifying] the occasion. But if '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' is connected with '<s>ādadhīta</s>' (should establish), then the fire-establishment is being enjoined for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. And similarly for <s>Kṣatriya</s> and the others.
What is the prima facie view? The statement serves the purpose of [specifying] the occasion. Why? Because these words have the form of occasion-indicators. What is the similarity to occasion-indicators? The co-utterance of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like with spring and the like — and that [co-utterance] makes known what was unknown. [Objection:] But the co-utterance of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like with the fire-establishment also exists. [Reply:] Indeed, the co-utterance exists, but the connection of these [<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>] with fire-establishment is not unknown. [Objection:] By what means is it already known? [Reply:] Through the desire-statements (<s>kāmaśruti</s>). What are the desire-statements? 'One who desires heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>'; 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — and the like. How is fire-establishment arrived at through these statements? It is said: by implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>). One should do whatever is needed to accomplish the <s>Agnihotra</s>. One should do whatever is needed to accomplish the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. And without the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, <s>Āhavanīya</s>, <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> and other [fires], these rituals cannot be accomplished. For they teach: 'When he offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, thereby that [deity] of his, being duly worshipped, becomes pleased' — and so forth. Therefore, by implication, this amounts to saying 'the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires] must be established.' And that cannot be accomplished without fire-establishment — hence it is understood that fire-establishment too must be performed. By whom must it be performed? By those for whom the desire-statements [apply]. And those [desire-statements apply] without distinction to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like. Therefore, the connection of these [<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>] with fire-establishment is [already] known. Moreover, if the connection of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like [with fire-establishment] were being enjoined by both [the direct statement and the desire-statements], the sentence would be split. For in that case, a single purpose would not be being enjoined. Therefore, the statements serve the purpose of [specifying] the occasion — thus is the prima facie view.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: Because fire-establishment is subsidiary to all [rituals], these statements bring about the fire-establishment [for the persons mentioned]. Why? 'Fire-establishment is subsidiary to all ritual actions' — this is not stated by any one of the [hermeneutic authorities such as] direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and the like. Rather, [it follows] from the fires being subsidiary to all [rituals], and fire-establishment being subsidiary to those [fires]. What follows from this? If so, the fires are arrived at through the desire-statements, not the fire-establishment. [Objection:] But fire-establishment is the means of obtaining them. [Reply:] It is said: Fire-establishment is not the only means of obtaining them. Rather, just as for other substances, purchase and other means exist for their production, so too for the fires — it is not necessarily the case that only [ritual] production [is the means]. Therefore, in one case fire-establishment is arrived at, in another it is not. In whichever case it is not arrived at, that case will give rise to the [need for an] injunction of fire-establishment for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like — '<s>brāhmaṇa</s> should establish [fires] for his own sake.' When this statement [is operative], the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires] are established for one's own sake alone, not otherwise. And this being so, it is understood that the ritual acts of <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like should not be performed with [fires that are] artificially produced or obtained from others. Therefore, it is determined that only a fire [produced through ritual establishment], not an artificial one, is effective for those [rituals]. And how is the 'for one's own sake' nature of fire-establishment understood? Because the verb '<s>ādadhīta</s>' is in the <s>Ātmanepada</s> (middle voice), which is possible when the fruit of the action is intended for the agent himself. Without this statement, if [fire-establishment] were merely included in the desire-statements, it would not have the character of being 'for one's own sake.'
Moreover, when these fire-establishment statements exist, the desire-statements cannot produce yet another fire-establishment statement. [The argument is:] those statements, for which fire-establishment has [already] been stated, would be re-hearings [of what is already enjoined]. In the absence of these [statements], [the desire-statements], not embracing a fire-establishment statement, would be speaking of <s>Agnihotra</s> and similar [rites] as impossible [to perform] — and so they would [have to] embrace the fire-establishment statement. When these [statements] exist, it is understood that the desire-statements pertain to those for whom fire-establishment has been stated, [applying] to subsequent occasions.
To this [the opponent] says: There is a statement that enjoins fire-establishment by itself — 'One who, knowing thus, establishes fire, thus overcomes the hostile adversary' — and this, having established [fire-establishment independently], the statements about <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like would serve the purpose of [specifying] the occasion. [Reply:] It is said: This is a re-hearing for the purpose of [specifying] the requisite materials (<s>saṃbhāra</s>).
[Reply:] We say no — for this is a different sentence from the sentence [specifying] the requisite materials. For the meaning of '<s>ādadhatte</s>' (he establishes) is different from '<s>apa upasṛjati</s>' (he releases the waters [into the fire]). When a single purpose is being enjoined, there is one sentence. But these two purposes are different. Therefore, here there is sentence-division.
[Reply:] It is said: When the statement 'In spring a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish fires' exists, the re-hearing of fire-establishment by itself does not enjoin [it anew]. Rather, the releasing of waters is what is enjoined. When a single purpose is being enjoined, it is not multi-purpose. [Objection:] But this is an injunction of fire-establishment; that re-hearing is for the purpose of [specifying] the quality. [Reply:] We say no — that [statement about <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>] is the primary statement connected with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like; this is a mere re-hearing [of fire-establishment] by itself. Why? Because that [first statement] enjoins by means of the word; and we see an indicatory mark being uttered there. This [second statement] says 'fire-establishment is praiseworthy.' From that, we infer the praiseworthiness of fire-establishment. And this being so, we say that the statement 'In spring a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish fires' is the injunctive statement. This laudatory statement does not override our position, for it can be said: what is enjoined by one [statement] can be praised by another. But if this [laudatory statement] were said to be injunctive, then it would contradict our position. How? An injunction is the making known of what was unknown. If the unprecedented [purpose] were made known by the laudatory statement, then it would not have been made known by the indicatory mark — and in that case, the word [of the indicatory mark] that makes known the unprecedented [purpose] would be obstructed. But a laudatory statement is not obstructed when [fire-establishment] is [already] enjoined [by the indicatory mark], for a laudatory statement works even when [the thing] has been enjoined by another sentence. Moreover, what is enjoined by the indicatory mark [is enjoined] by direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), while the praise is understood from the sentence — and direct statement is stronger than a sentence.
[Objection:] But this too is a sentence — 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish fires.' [Reply:] It is said: Here, the direct statement (<s>śruti</s>) enjoins its own word-meaning — fire-establishment — while it praises through the connection with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like, which is the meaning of another word — 'One who thus overcomes the hostile adversary.' [Objection:] But a multiple-quality injunction is what you have accepted [as possible] in a sentence. [Reply:] This is no fault, for it has been said that multiple-quality injunction [occurs] in a sentence whose primary purpose is not quality-injunction. 'But those qualities would be enjoined that, because of non-differentiation, are part of the injunctive purpose, if not [already] taught by another [statement].' Therefore, the statement connected with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like is the injunctive statement, and this [other] re-hearing of fire-establishment by itself is the introduction to [specifying] the requisite materials — this is established.
As for what was said — 'In a multiple-quality injunction, the sentence would be split' — if these two [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Vasanta</s>], each distinguished by quality-injunction, were being enjoined [separately], there would be sentence-division. But a single fire-establishment, qualified by both qualifiers, will be enjoined — hence there will be no sentence-division. Therefore, it is established that the statements bring about fire-establishment for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like.

children.text: ayaneṣu codanāntaraṃ saṃjñopabandhāt // MS_2,3.5 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>ayanas</s> (seasonal rituals), [there is] a different injunction, because of the attachment of a designation. // MS 2.3.5 //

children.text: darśapūṇamāsau prakṛtyāmananti, dākṣāyaṇayajñena yajeta prajākāmaḥ, sākaṃprasthāpyena{*2/317*} yajeta paśukāmaḥ, saṃkramayajñena yajetānnādyakāma iti{*2/318*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ darśapūrṇamāsayor eva guṇāt phalam, uta karmāntaram evaṃjātīyakam iti? kiṃ prāptam? karmāntaram iti. kutaḥ? saṃjñopabandhāt, yady api prakaraṇād yajatiśabdāc ca sa eva pūrvaprakṛto yāga iti gamyate, tathāpi nāsāv evaṃsaṃjñaka iti yāgāntaraṃ vidheyaṃ gamyate.
children.translated_text: They teach the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> as the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>): 'One who desires progeny should sacrifice with the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice'; 'One who desires cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Sākaṃprasthāpya</s>'; 'One who desires food should sacrifice with the <s>Saṃkramayajña</s>.' There a doubt arises: do these [involve] a fruit arising from a quality of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifices] themselves, or are they different ritual actions of this kind? What is the prima facie view? They are different ritual actions. Why? Because of the attachment of a designation. Even though from the context and the word '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), it is understood that the previously mentioned sacrifice [i.e., the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>] is meant, still, since it does not bear such a designation [as <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>], a different sacrifice that is to be enjoined is understood.

children.translated_text: And because of [an injunction] not [merely] of a quality, [it is] an injunction of a [new] ritual action. // MS 2.3.6 //

children.text: na ca, atra guṇa uparudhyate kaścit, yad vidhānārthā codanā bhavet, yadi ca na yāgāntaram, ānarthakyam eva. api ca, yadi guṇa upabadhyeta, tato yāgaguṇasaṃbandho gamyata iti tad anuṣṭhānaṃ vidhīyetety ananubadhyamāne{*2/319*} yāgamātraṃ gamyata iti tad anuṣṭhānaṃ vihitaṃ gamyate.
children.translated_text: And here, no quality is obstructed [i.e., excluded by context], so that the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) would serve the purpose of enjoining [a quality]. And if it is not a different sacrifice, [the passage] would be entirely purposeless. Moreover, if a quality were being attached, the connection of the quality with the sacrifice would be understood, and the performance of that [qualified sacrifice] would be enjoined. But when [a quality] is not being attached, the sacrifice alone is understood, and the performance of that [sacrifice] is understood as enjoined.

NOTES:

children.text: samāptaṃ ca phale vākyam // MS_2,3.7 //
children.translated_text: And the sentence is complete with the fruit. // MS 2.3.7 //

children.text: itaś ca karmāntaram. katham? phale samāptaṃ vākyam, prājākāmo yajeteti, prajākāmasya yāga upayo vidhīyate. vidhīyate cet, karmāntaram.
children.translated_text: For this reason too it is a different ritual action. How? The sentence is complete with the fruit — 'one who desires progeny should sacrifice.' The sacrifice is enjoined as the means for one who desires progeny. And if it is being enjoined, it is a different ritual action.

children.text: vikāro vā prakaraṇāt // MS_2,3.8 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] a modification (<s>vikāra</s>), because of the context. // MS 2.3.8 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor evādhikāra evaṃjātīyakaḥ syād dākṣāyaṇayajñādiḥ, evaṃ prakaraṇam anugṛhītaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: In the domain of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifices] themselves, there could be [a modification] of this kind — the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice and the like. Thus the context would be supported.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_2,3.9 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // MS 2.3.9 //

children.text: liṅgam apy etam arthaṃ darśayati, triṃśataṃ varṣāṇi darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta, yadi dākṣāyaṇayājī syāt, atho api pañcadaśaiva varṣāṇi yajeta, atra hy eva sā saṃpadyate, dve hi paurṇamāsyau yajeta dve amāvasye, atra hi eva khalu sā saṃpad bhavatīti. yadi dākṣāyaṇayajño darśapūrṇamāsāv eva, evaṃ tarhi triṃśatsaṃpadā prayojanam, tatas tasya triṃśatsaṃpadanugraho yujyate, tasmād api na karmāntaram.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark too shows this meaning: 'For thirty years one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, if one would be a <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>-sacrificer; or else one should sacrifice for fifteen years only — for it is therein that it is accomplished. For one should sacrifice two full-moon [sacrifices] and two new-moon [sacrifices] — for it is therein indeed that the accomplishment occurs.' If the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice is the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> itself, then the purpose of the thirty-year accomplishment [is served], and the support of the thirty-year accomplishment is justified. Therefore, from this too it is not a different ritual action.

children.text: guṇāt saṃjñopabandhaḥ // MS_2,3.10 //
children.translated_text: The designation arises from the quality. // MS 2.3.10 //

children.text: yad uktaṃ saṃjñopabandhāt karmāntaram iti, yadi dākṣāyaṇaśabdo na kenacid api prakāreṇa darśapūrṇamāsavacanaḥ śakyate kalpayitum, tata ucyeta karmāntaram iti. śaknoti tv āvṛttiguṇasaṃbandhād viditum, ayanam ity āvṛttir ucyate, dakṣasya ime dākṣāḥ, teṣām ayanaṃ dākṣāyaṇam. kaḥ punar dakṣaḥ? utsāhī. tathā sākaṃprasthāpye{*2/321*} 'pi, sahaprasthānaṃ guṇasaṃbandhaḥ, evaṃ sarvatra. śakyate ced darśapūrṇamāsayor guṇasaṃbandho vaditum, kim iti sa eva yāgaḥ pratīyamāno 'nya ity ucyate? kim iti vā prakaraṇaṃ bādhyate.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'because of the attachment of a designation, it is a different ritual action' — if the word <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> cannot be construed in any way whatsoever as a word for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, then one would say it is a different ritual action. But it can be understood through the connection of the quality of repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>): '<s>ayana</s>' means repetition; '<s>Dākṣa</s>' means 'belonging to <s>Dakṣa</s>' (the diligent ones); their repetition (<s>ayana</s>) is the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>. But who is <s>Dakṣa</s>? The industrious one. Similarly in the <s>Sākaṃprasthāpya</s> too — 'setting forth together' is the quality-connection. And so everywhere. If the quality-connection with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> can be stated, why is the very sacrifice that is being understood [as the same] said to be another? And why would the context be overridden?

children.text:
NOTES:
*{2/321: E1,6; E2,4: sākaṃprasthāyīye, E5: sākaṃprasthāyye}*

children.text: samāptir aviśiṣṭā // MS_2,3.11 //
children.translated_text: The completion is not distinctive. // MS_2,3.11 //

children.text: yad uktam, phale vākyaṃ samāptam, prajākāmāder yāgānuṣṭhānaṃ vidhīyata iti{*2/322*}. naivam, aviśiṣṭā phale samāptiḥ, yāni [181]{*2/323*} anyāni muktasaṃśayāni guṇe phalasya vidhāyakāni vākyāni guṇasya phalavacanāni paryavasitāni (yathā dadhnendriyakāmasya juhuyāt, ityevamādīni){*2/324*}{*2/325*}, tair etad aviśiṣṭam, atrāpi hi guṇāt phalam ucyate. kathaṃ naitad evaṃ saṃbadhyate, prajākāmasya yajñam anutiṣṭhed iti? kathaṃ tarhi prajākāmasyāvṛttiyajñam anutiṣṭhed iti, āvṛttiyajña iti yajñāvṛtti-saṃbandho 'nuṣṭhātavyo nirdiśyate, na yajñaḥ? tasmāt prakṛtayor darśapūrṇamāsayor guṇāt phalam ucyate, na yāgāntaraṃ vidhīyata iti. evaṃ sākaṃprasthāpye{*2/326*} saṃkramayajñe ca draṣṭavyam iti.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'the sentence is completed in the fruit, and the performance of the sacrifice for one desiring offspring and the like is enjoined' — this is not so. The completion in the fruit is not distinctive. Those other undoubted sentences that enjoin a fruit from the subsidiary quality — sentences that conclude with a statement of fruit for the subsidiary (such as 'one who desires the senses should offer with curds' and the like) — from those, this is not distinctive. For here too, the fruit is stated [as arising] from the subsidiary. How is this not construed thus: 'one desiring offspring should perform the sacrifice'? Rather thus: 'one desiring offspring should perform the repetition-sacrifice' — '<s>āvṛtti-yajña</s>' indicates that the connection of the sacrifice with repetition is to be performed, not the sacrifice [itself]. Therefore, the fruit is stated from the subsidiary for the basic <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and a different sacrifice is not enjoined. The same should be understood for the <s>Sākaṃprasthāpya</s> and the <s>Saṃkrama</s>-sacrifice.

NOTES:
Cf. MS 2.3.7 | [Page refs: E2: 3,175; E4: 3,374; E5: 2,575; E6: 1,124] | [Bracketed in E1] | Cf. Tait.Br. 2.1.5.6 | [Variant: E1,6; E2,4 read 'sākaṃprasthāyīye'; E5 reads 'sākaṃprasthāyye']

children.text: saṃskāraś cāprakaraṇe 'karmaśabdatvāt // MS_2,3.12 //
children.translated_text: And the preparation [would be] outside the context, because [the verb] is not a word for a [separate] ritual action. // MS_2,3.12 //

children.text:
anārabhyādhīyate kiṃcit, vākyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ{*2/327*}; sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāmaḥ{*2/328*}; darśapūrṇamāsayor apy āmananti - īṣām ālabheta; caturo muṣṭīn nirvapatīti. tatrāyam arthaḥ sāṃśayikaḥ, kiṃ darśapūrṇamāsike{*2/329*} ālambhe ālambho guṇavidhir darśapūrṇamāsike{*2/330*} ca nirvāpe nirvāpo guṇavidhir uta na prakṛtim apekṣate itaraś cetavaraś ceti? yadā na prakṛtim apekṣate, tadāpi kiṃ yāvad ukte, uta yajimaty ete karmaṇīti?
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? prakṛtayor ālambhanirvāpayor guṇavidhīti. kutaḥ? akarmaśabdatvāt, nātra karmaṇo vidhāyakaḥ [182]{*2/331*} śabdo 'sti. nanv ālabheta nirvaped iti ca. naitau vidhātārāv aviditasyārthasya vaktā vidhāyako bhavati, na caitayor avidito 'rthaḥ, ālambhaḥ kartavyaḥ, nirvāpaḥ kartavya iti. tasmād anuvaditārau. kim artham anuvadataḥ? ālambhane śvetaṃ vidhātum, nirvāpe ca carum. tasmān nālambhāntaraṃ nirvāpāntaraṃ ca. prakṛtayor eva guṇavidhīti.
children.translated_text:
There are passages studied outside [the main context]. The sentence 'one desiring prosperity should immolate a white [animal]'; 'one desiring the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> should cook a <s>Saurya</s> (solar) <s>caru</s> (oblation).' And in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> too they teach: 'he immolates the <s>īṣā</s> (ritual pole animal)'; 'he cooks four handfuls.' There this meaning is doubtful: is the immolation in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [ritual] a subsidiary-quality injunction with respect to the [basic] immolation, and likewise the cooking — a subsidiary-quality injunction with respect to the [basic] cooking? Or does it not depend on the basic [model], [meaning that] one is an immolation and the other is a cooking [as independent rites]? When it does not depend on the basic [model], then too — is it [only] as much as is stated, or are these ritual actions involving the verb '<s>yajati</s>' (sacrifice)?
What is the prima facie view? They are subsidiary-quality injunctions of the basic immolation and cooking. Why? Because [the verb] is not a word for a [separate] ritual action — there is no word here that enjoins a [separate] ritual action. [Objection:] But [there are] '<s>ālabheta</s>' (he should immolate) and '<s>nirvaped</s>' (he should cook). [Reply:] These two are not enjoiners — a speaker who states the meaning of what is [already] known is an enjoiner. And the meaning of these two is [already] known — 'immolation is to be done, cooking is to be done.' Therefore, they are restaters. For what purpose do they restate? To enjoin 'white' with respect to the immolation, and '<s>caru</s>' (oblation) with respect to the cooking. Therefore, it is not a different immolation or a different cooking. They are subsidiary-quality injunctions of the basic [rites] alone.

NOTES:
Tait.S. 2.1.1.1 | Tait.S. 2.3.2.3 | [Variant: E1,6; E2,4,5 read 'dārśapūrṇamāsike'] | [Same variant] | [Page refs: E2: 3,175; E4: 3,375; E2: 2,577; E6: 1,125]

children.text: yāvad uktaṃ vā, karmaṇaḥ śrutimūlatvāt // MS_2,3.13 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] as much as is stated, because ritual action has scripture as its root. // MS_2,3.13 //

children.text:
na caitad asti, prākṛtayor guṇavidhīti, kiṃ tarhy ālambhāntaraṃ vidhīyata iti nirvāpāntaraṃ ca, yady ālambhanirvāpau vidhīyete, tato na prākṛtau tau vihitau. yadi na vidhīyete, tataḥ prākṛtau lakṣyete, yāv ālambhanirvāpau kartavyāv iti, tataḥ tau lakṣayitvā śveto vidhātavyo bhavati, caruś ca, tau ca bhūtikāmasya brahmavarcasakāmasya ceti dvāv apy athā vidheyau syātām, tatra vākyam bhidyeta. atha vā yo 'sau vidhāyakaḥ śabdaḥ, sa lakṣayitavyopayukta iti vidhāyakābhāvād eko 'py artho na śakyate vidhātum. atha sa eva lakṣayiṣyati, tenaiva ca vidhāyiṣyate guṇa iti. na, mitho vidhānalakṣaṇasaṃbandho 'vakalpate. atha dhātvartho 'nuvādaḥ, pratyayo vidhātum iṣyata ity ucyate, ya ālambhaḥ sa etadguṇaḥ kartavya iti. tathāpi na prākṛto lakṣyeta, laukiko 'pi hy ālambho 'sti, pratyayārthe 'nūdyamāne prākṛto 'nūdyeteti, sa hi kartavyo nirjñāto na laukikaḥ, ato na prākṛtānuvādo ghaṭa iti yāvad uktam ālambhamātraṃ nirvāpamātraṃ{*2/332*} cāpūrvaṃ kartavyam, karmaṇaḥ śrutimūlatvāt, śrutimūlaṃ hi karmety uktam, codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharma iti{*2/333*}. tasmāt karmāntare.
[183]{*2/334*}
children.translated_text: This is not the case — that they are subsidiary-quality injunctions of the basic [rites]. Rather, a different immolation is enjoined, and a different cooking. If the immolation and cooking are being enjoined, then the basic ones are not [what is] enjoined. If they are not being enjoined, then the basic ones are figuratively indicated — 'the immolation and cooking that are to be done' — and having figuratively indicated those, 'white' and '<s>caru</s>' would have to be enjoined; and those [would have to be enjoined] for one desiring prosperity and one desiring the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> — both of those too would have to be enjoined. In that case, the sentence would be split. Alternatively, that very enjoining word, being employed for figurative indication — because of the absence of an enjoiner, not even a single meaning can be enjoined. If it both figuratively indicates and also enjoins the quality — no, a mutual relation of injunction and figurative indication cannot be construed. If the verb-root meaning is a restatement and the suffix is intended to enjoin — [such that] 'that which is an immolation, that should be done with this quality' — even then the basic [rite] is not figuratively indicated, for there exists a worldly immolation too. When the suffix-meaning is being restated, the basic [rite] would be restated — for that [basic rite] is known as 'to be done,' not the worldly one. Therefore, the restatement of the basic [rite] does not work. Hence, as much as is stated — merely the immolation and merely the cooking — is [what is enjoined as] an unprecedented [ritual act]. Because ritual action has scripture as its root — for it has been said that 'ritual action has scripture as its root': 'the object characterized by injunction is <s>Dharma</s>.' Therefore, it is a different ritual action.

NOTES:
[Variant: E2,4 omit 'nirvāpamātraṃ'] | MS 1.1.2 | [Page refs: E2: 3,178; E4: 3,383; E5: 2,579; E6: 1,125]

children.text: yajatis tu dravyaphalabhoktṛsaṃyogād eteṣāṃ karmasaṃbandhāt // MS_2,3.14 //
children.translated_text: But [the verb] '<s>yajati</s>' [applies], because of the conjunction of substance, fruit, and enjoyer — because of the connection of these with ritual action. // MS_2,3.14 //

children.text:
yad uktam, na prākṛtayor guṇavidhīti, etad gṛhṇīmaḥ. yat tūktam, ālambhamātraṃ vidhīyate,
nirvāpamātram iti, etad apajānīmahe, yajimatī ete karmaṇīti. kutah? dravyaphalabhoktṛsaṃyogād
(dravyadevatāsaṃyogāt){*2/335*}, dravyadevatāsaṃyogo 'tra vidhīyate, bhūtikāmasya brahmavarcaskāmasya ca. katham? na hi, idam evocyate, tataḥ śvetam ālabheteti, yadi hy etāvad evocyeta, tataḥ śvetālambhasaṃbandho 'vagamyate, iha hi śvetaṃ vāyavyam ālabhetety ucyate, tena śvetavāyavyasaṃbandho vidhīyate, yathā paṭaṃ vayeti paṭavayanasaṃbandho{*2/336*} vidheyo 'vagamyate, paṭaṃ dīrghaṃ vayeti paṭasya dīrghatā vidhīyate, dīrghaśabdaprayogāt, evam ihāpi sauryavāyavyaśabdaprayogād dravyadevatābhisaṃbandho vidheya iti gamyate, itarathā devatāśabdaḥ pramādasamāmnāta iti gamyate.
nanv atrāpi śvetaṃ vāyavyaṃ kuryāt, taṃ cālabhetety arthadvayavidhānād bhidyetaiva vākyam. neti brūmaḥ, na hy ālabhetety asyāyam atibhāraḥ, yad dravyadevatāsaṃbandhena puruṣaprayatnaṃ brūyāt, taṃ cālabhetety arthaviśiṣṭam. śrutyaiva hi puruṣaprayatno viśiṣṭo gamyate, vākyena ca dravyadevatāśraya iti nātra dvābhyāṃ vākyābhyāṃ prayojanam, yathā raktam aśvaṃ yojayeti yadā guṇavidhiparaṃ bhavati vākyam, tadā dvābhyāṃ vākyābhyāṃ prayojanam, guṇadvayavidhāne. atha śoṇamānayety ucyate, tatra guṇavidhipare 'pi vākye paryavasita eva guṇadvayavidhānam, śrutyaiva viśiṣṭaguṇadravyasya pratītatvāt, na bhavaty ekasya vākyasyātibhāraḥ, evam ihāpīti. saṃbandhaś ca bahubhiḥ padair viśiṣṭa eka evocyata ity ekārthatvam, vibhajya[184]{*2/337*}mānāni cātra padāni sākāṅkṣāṇīty upapannam ekavākyatvam, na ca, yāgam antareṇa devatāyai dravyaṃ saṅkalpitavyam, ity eṣa saṃbandho 'vakalpate. tasmād yajimatī ete karmaṇīti.
children.translated_text:
As to what was said — that they are not subsidiary-quality injunctions of the basic [rites] — we accept that. But as to what was said — 'merely the immolation is enjoined, merely the cooking' — we reject that. These are ritual actions involving the verb '<s>yajati</s>' (sacrifice). Why? Because of the conjunction of substance, fruit, and enjoyer (i.e., substance-and-deity conjunction). The substance-deity conjunction is enjoined here, for one desiring prosperity and one desiring the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>. How? For it is not said merely 'from that, he should immolate a white [animal]' — if only that much were said, then only the connection of 'white' with immolation would be understood. Here it is said: 'he should immolate a white <s>Vāyavya</s> (for <s>Vāyu</s>) [animal].' Therefore, the white-<s>Vāyavya</s> conjunction is being enjoined. Just as 'he weaves a cloth' — the cloth-weaving conjunction is understood as to be enjoined; 'he weaves a long cloth' — the longness of the cloth is being enjoined because of the use of the word 'long.' Similarly here too, because of the use of the words <s>Saurya</s> and <s>Vāyavya</s>, it is understood that the substance-deity conjunction is to be enjoined. Otherwise, the deity-word would be understood as recited through carelessness.
[Objection:] But here too, 'he should make a white <s>Vāyavya</s> [animal], and immolate it' — because of the enjoining of two meanings, the sentence would be split. [Reply:] We say no — for this is no excessive burden on '<s>ālabheta</s>' (he should immolate), that it should state the personal effort together with the substance-deity conjunction and then immolate — the meaning is qualified. For by the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) itself, the personal effort is understood as qualified, and by the sentence, as depending on substance and deity — hence two sentences are not needed here. Just as 'yoke the red horse' — when the sentence is about enjoining a quality, two sentences are needed for the enjoining of two qualities. But [if] 'bring the red [horse]' is said — even in a sentence about enjoining a quality, the enjoining of two qualities concludes in one [sentence], because the direct expression itself makes known the substance qualified by the quality. There is no excessive burden on a single sentence — so too here. And the conjunction, qualified by many words, is stated as a single [thing] — hence unity of purpose. And the words, when separated, are syntactically incomplete — hence unity of sentence is established. And without a sacrifice, one cannot dedicate the substance to the deity — hence this conjunction is construed. Therefore, these are ritual actions involving the verb '<s>yajati</s>'.

NOTES:
