children.text: liṅgādarśanāc ca // MS_2,3.15 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_2,3.15 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ khalv apy etam arthaṃ darśayati, saumāraudraṃ caruṃ nirvaped iti{*2/338*} prakṛtya, pariśrite yājayed iti{*2/339*} pariśrayaṇavidhiḥ, etasya vākye yajatiśabdena saṅkīrtanam avakalpate, yadi yajimatī ete karmaṇī. atha prakṛtau guṇavidhānaṃ yāvad uktaṃ vā, yajatiśabdenānuvādo nāvakalpeta. tasmād avagacchāmo yajimatīti.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) too shows this meaning. Having cited '<s>Saumāraudra</s> (for <s>Soma</s>-<s>Rudra</s>), he should cook the <s>caru</s> (oblation),' [the text says] 'he should have [the priest] sacrifice in the enclosed area (<s>pariśrita</s>)' — this is an injunction of enclosure. The mention of [this rite] by the word '<s>yajati</s>' (sacrifice) in the sentence is construed [only] if these are ritual actions involving '<s>yajati</s>.' But if [they were] subsidiary-quality injunctions of the basic [rites], or merely as much as stated, the restatement by the word '<s>yajati</s>' would not be construed. Therefore, we understand that [these are] ritual actions involving '<s>yajati</s>'.

NOTES:
Tait.S. 2.2.10.1 | Tait.S. 2.2.10.2

children.text: viśaye prāyadarśanāt // MS_2,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Because of the observation that it generally [falls] within the domain [of sacrifice]. // MS_2,3.16 //

children.text:
kim ihodāharaṇam? na tāvat śūtreṇaiva parigṛhītam, yathā, aveṣṭau yajñasaṃyogāt kratupradhānam ucyata iti{*2/340*}. nāpi ca sādhyaṃ pratijñātam, yathā, ayaneṣu codanāntaram iti{*2/341*}{*2/342*}. kevalaṃ viśaye saṃśaye prāyadarśanaṃ hetur iti nirdiśyate, kasyāyaṃ hetur iti na vijānīmaḥ. prakṛtaṃ yajimad etat karmeti{*2/343*}, tad api na saṃbandhyamānam iva paśyāmaḥ, tad etad agamakaṃ{*2/344*} sūtram eva tāvad anarthakam. atha kātra pratijñā? kaś ca sandeha iti vaktavyam. vṛttikāravacanāt, pratijñāṃ saṃśayaṃ cāvagacchāmaḥ. atra bhagavān ācārya idam udāhṛtya vatsam ālabheta vatsanikāntā hi paśava iti{*2/345*}, imaṃ saṃśayam upanyasyati sma, kiṃ yajimadabhidhāna eṣa ālabhatiḥ, utālambhamātravacana iti? upapadyate caitad udāharaṇam, [185]{*2/346*} saṃśayaś ca. tatra ca pūrvapakṣaṃ pratijānīte sma, yajimad abhidhāna iti. idaṃ tu pratyudāharaṇasūtraṃ pūrvasyādhikaraṇasya, nātra pūrva-pakṣeṇātīva prayojanam, tathāpi puruṣāṇām uccāvacabuddhiviśeṣān ālocya bhavati mandānāṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭenāpy āśaṅkā, sāpi nivartanīyā, na hi, mandaviṣeṇa vṛścikenāpi daṣṭo mriyeta na jātucit kadāpi, tatra cikitsā nādareṇa kartavyā bhavet. atastāṃ nivartayituṃ pūrvapakṣam upanyasyati sma, ālabhatir asmābhiḥ prāṇisaṃyukto yajimad abhidhāno dṛṣṭaḥ, ayam apy ālabhatiḥ prāṇisaṃyuktaḥ eva, tenāyam api yajimadvacana eveti bhavati kasyacid āśaṅkā. atha vā yajimadabhidhāno dṛṣṭa ālabhatiḥ prāṇisaṃyuktaḥ, tasyāyam anuvādo vatsavidhānārthaḥ, tathā ca phalam na kalpayitavyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - asmin saṃśaye ālambhamātraṃ saṃskāraḥ. kutaḥ? prāyadarśanāt, yatrānyāny{*2/347*} api saṃskārakarmāṇi prāyabhūtānīty ucyante, tatraitad api śrūyate. prāyād api cārthaniścayo bhavati, yathā, agryaprāye likhito 'grya iti gamyate. nanu liṅgaṃ prāyadarśanam, katham anena siddhir iti. ucyate - yathā prāyadarśanena sidhyati, tathā varṇayitavyam. kathaṃ ca prāyadarśanaṃ hetuḥ? nyāyataḥ prāptau satyām. kaḥ punar nyāyaḥ? devatāsaṃbandhābhāvān na yāgavacano 'dṛṣṭārthatvāc ca, vatsa ālabhyamāno gāṃ prastāvayiṣyatīti. tasmād evaṃ nyāyaprāpte prāyadarśanaṃ dyotakaṃ bhavati. tasmād ālambhamātraṃ saṃskāraḥ.
children.translated_text:
What is the example here? It is not encompassed by the <s>sūtra</s> itself, as in '<s>aveṣṭau</s>: because of the connection with the sacrifice, [it is] principally for the rite.' Nor is the thesis explicitly stated, as in 'In the <s>ayanas</s>, [there is] a different injunction.' Only the subject-matter, the doubt, and 'the preponderance of observation is the reason' are indicated — we do not know whose reason this is. The contextual [topic is] 'this ritual action involves [the verb] <s>yaj</s>' — but we do not seem to see that being connected [with this <s>sūtra</s>]. Therefore, this <s>sūtra</s>, being uninstructive, is itself purposeless. But then what is the thesis? And what is the doubt? — this must be stated. From the <s>vṛttikāra</s>'s (commentator's) statement, we understand the thesis and the doubt. Here, the revered teacher, having cited 'He should seize the calf; for animals are fond of calves' as the example, [Page 185] raised this doubt: does this [verb] '<s>ālabhati</s>' denote [an act involving the verb] '<s>yaj</s>' (sacrifice), or does it merely denote seizing? And this example and doubt are well-founded. There, he stated the prima facie view as: it denotes [an act involving] '<s>yaj</s>.' But this is the counter-example <s>sūtra</s> of the previous topic — there is not much need for a prima facie view here. Nevertheless, considering the varying intellectual capacities of people, even those of lesser [understanding] may have a doubt based on general reasoning, and that too must be dispelled — for one should not say 'since the scorpion has mild venom, the person bitten will never die; therefore, treatment need not be done attentively.' Therefore, he sets up the prima facie view to dispel that [doubt]: we have observed that '<s>ālabhati</s>' connected with an animal denotes [an act involving] '<s>yaj</s>'; this '<s>ālabhati</s>' too is connected with an animal; therefore, this too denotes [an act involving] '<s>yaj</s>' — thus someone might suspect. Alternatively: '<s>ālabhati</s>' connected with an animal has been seen to denote [an act involving] '<s>yaj</s>'; this is a re-statement of that, for the purpose of enjoining the calf; and thus no [separate] result should be posited.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: in this doubt, [<s>ālabhati</s>] is merely seizing, a preparatory act (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Why? Because of the preponderance of observation — where other preparatory actions are said to predominate, there this too is heard. And from preponderance too, certainty of meaning results — just as in a register where the majority are '<s>agrya</s>' (first-class), one listed [among them] is understood as '<s>agrya</s>.' [Objection:] But the preponderance-observation is [merely] an indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>) — how can it establish [anything]? [Reply:] It is said: it should be explained how it is established by the preponderance-observation. And how is the preponderance-observation a reason? When there is a conclusion arrived at by reasoning. And what is the reasoning? Because of the absence of a deity-connection, [<s>ālabhati</s>] is not a sacrifice-word; and because of having an observable purpose — the calf, when seized, will bring the cow forth. Therefore, when this conclusion has been reached by reasoning, the preponderance-observation serves as a confirming indicator. Therefore, [<s>ālabhati</s>] is merely seizing, a preparatory act.

NOTES:
[MS 2.3.3; E2,4,6 omit <s>iti</s>; MS 2.3.5; Cf. MS 2.3.14; E2 reads <s>gamakaṃ</s>; Cf. Tait.S. 2.1.4.8; Edition: E2: 3,181; E4: 3,388; E4: 2,583; E6: 1,127; E2,4 read <s>atrānyāny</s>]

children.text: arthavādopapatteś ca // MS_2,3.17 //
children.translated_text: And because of the propriety of [it being] a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>). // MS 2.3.17 //

children.text: arthavādaś ca bhavati, vatsanikāntā hi paśava iti{*2/348*}, [186]{*2/349*} yasmād vatsapriyāḥ paśavaḥ, tasmād vatsa ālabdhavya iti, yadi gāṃ prastāvayitum{*2/350*} ālabhyate, tatraitad vacanam avakalpate, atha saṃjñapayitum, tatraivaṃjātīyakaṃ vacanaṃ nopapadyate. tasmād apy ālambhamātraṃ saṃskāra iti siddham.
children.translated_text: And there is a laudatory passage: 'for animals are fond of calves.' [Page 186] Since animals are fond of calves, therefore the calf should be seized. If [the calf] is seized in order to bring the cow forth, then this statement is appropriate. But if [it is seized] in order to slaughter [it], a statement of this kind would not be appropriate. Therefore, from this too, it is established that [<s>ālabhati</s>] is merely seizing, a preparatory act.

NOTES:
[Cf. Tait.S. 2.1.4.8; Edition: E2: 3,183; E4: 3,393; E5: 2,585; E6: 1,128; E1,6; E2,4,5 read <s>prasnāvayitum</s>]

children.text: saṃyuktas tv arthaśabdena tadarthaḥ śrutisaṃyogāt // MS_2,3.18 //
children.translated_text: But when connected with a word denoting a purpose, [it serves] that purpose, because of the connection with direct expression (<s>śruti</s>). // MS 2.3.18 //

children.text:
asty agniḥ, tatra naivāraś carur bhavati, ity uktvā, yad enaṃ carum upadadhātīti samāmananti. tatra sandihyate, kiṃ carur yāgārtho yāgaṃ kṛtvāvaśiṣṭa upadhātavyaḥ, utopadhānārtha eveti. yāgārtha iti brūmaḥ, caror hi prasiddhaṃ kāryaṃ yāgo nopadhānam. ucyate - yady api yāgārthatā caroḥ prasiddhā, tathāpi devatāvacanasaṃbandhābhāvād yajatiśabdāsaṃbandhāc ca na yāgārthateti gamyate. tad ucyate - tasyaiva vākyaśeṣe śrūyate, bṛhaspater vā etad annaṃ yan nīvārā iti, tena devatāvacanena sannihitenaikavākyatā bhaviṣyatīti bṛhaspatidevatāka upadhātavya iti. tasmād yāgārthaś carur ity evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - saṃyuktas tv arthaśabdena kāryaśabdenopadadhātīti tad arthaḥ eva syād upadhānārthaḥ. upadadhātinā cāsya pratyakṣam ekavākyatvam, parokṣaṃ devatāvacanenānumeyam, carum upadadhātīti hi pratyakṣaṃ vākyam. bārhaspatyam upadadhātīty ānumānikam. tasmāt kṛtsnaś carur upadhātavyaḥ, tataś ccet kiṃcid ijyāyāṃ viniyujyeta, tad anyatra śrutam anyatra kṛtaṃ bhavet. yat tu bārhaspatyā nīvārā iti, arthavādaḥ sa iti. yat tūktam - prasiddhā caror yāgārthateti, prasiddhir vākyena bādhyate. tasmād upadhānārtha iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
There is [a rite called] '<s>Agni</s>' (fire-piling). There it is said: '<s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice) porridge is [prepared].' After stating this, they teach: 'When he places down this porridge.' There the doubt arises: is the porridge for the purpose of sacrifice — [i.e.,] having performed the sacrifice, the remainder is to be placed down — or is it solely for the purpose of placing down? We say it is for the purpose of sacrifice — for the well-known function of a porridge is sacrifice, not placing down. [Reply:] It is said: even though the sacrifice-purpose of the porridge is well-known, still, because of the absence of a connection with a deity-word and because of the absence of a connection with the word '<s>yajati</s>,' it is understood that [the porridge] is not for sacrifice-purpose. To this it is said: in the syntactic complement of that very [sentence] it is heard: 'For this food of wild rice indeed belongs to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.' By the unity of sentence with that proximate deity-word, [the porridge] having <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as its deity is to be placed down. Therefore, the porridge is for the purpose of sacrifice — this is the prima facie view.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: But when connected with a word denoting a purpose — [namely,] the activity-word '<s>upadadhāti</s>' (he places down) — it should serve precisely that purpose, the purpose of placing down. And its sentence-unity with '<s>upadadhāti</s>' is directly perceived, while [its sentence-unity] with the deity-word is inferential and indirect. 'He places down the porridge' — this is the directly perceived sentence. '<s>Bārhaspatya</s> (belonging to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) he places down' — this is inferred. Therefore, the entire porridge is to be placed down. And if some part of it were employed in sacrifice, that would be a case of 'heard in one place, done in another.' As for [the statement] 'the <s>nīvāras</s> belong to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>' — that is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>). As for the objection 'the sacrifice-purpose of the porridge is well-known' — that well-known [purpose] is overridden by the sentence. Therefore, it is established that [the porridge is] for the purpose of placing down.
Page 187

children.text: pātnīvate tu pūrvatvād avacchedaḥ // MS_2,3.19 //
children.translated_text: In the case of the <s>Pātnīvata</s> (belonging to the sacrificer's wife), because of priority, [there is] a curtailment. // MS 2.3.19 //

children.text:
tvāṣṭraṃ pātnīvataṃ vidhāyedam ucyate{*2/352*}, yat paryagnikṛtaṃ pātnīvatam utsṛjantīti. tatra sandehaḥ, kiṃ tvāṣṭrasya paryagnikṛtasyaiṣa utsargo vidhīyate, uta tasmād yāgāntaram iti. yadi paryagnikṛtam utsṛjantīti padadvayaṃ paraspareṇa saṃbaddham, tatas tvāṣṭrasyotsargaḥ, atha pātnīvataśabda utsṛjatinā saṃbadhyeta, tato yāgāntaram.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? yāgāntaram iti. kutaḥ? pūrvas tvāṣṭraḥ pātnīvataś ca, ubhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaḥ kathaṃ pātnīvataśabdenānūdyeta. api ca tvāṣṭrasyotsarge vidhīyamāne paryagnikṛtam iti viśeṣaṇaṃ nāvakalpeta. ato brūmaḥ - paryagnikṛtasya pātnīvatatā vidhīyate, sa eva yāga iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - na karmāntaram, pūrvasyaivotsṛjatiśabdenāvacchedo vidhīyate. kim evaṃ bhaviṣyati. yajimattā tāvat kalpayitavyā na bhaviṣyati, utsṛjatiśabdaś ca śrutyotsargaṃ vidadhad vākyena na bādhito bhaviṣyati, karmāntarapakṣe vākyena pātnīvatatāyāṃ vidhīyamānāyām arthāt prāpta utsargo dhātunānūdyeta. api ca paryagnikṛtasya pātnīvatatā pūrvasya viditaiva, sā vidhātum na śakyate. tasmāt pūrvasya karmaṇo 'vacchedaḥ. yat tūktam, tvāṣṭrasyotsargo vidhīyamāne paryagnikṛtam iti viśeṣaṇaṃ tāvan nāvakalpeteti, naiṣa doṣaḥ, atantram evātra pātnīvataśabdo
nāsau viśeṣyate, ata eva tvāṣṭraḥ pātnīvata ubhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaḥ kevalena pātnīvataśabdena lakṣaṇayānūdyeteti na doṣaḥ. tasmād avaccheda iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
Having enjoined the <s>Tvāṣṭra Pātnīvata</s> (offering belonging to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, associated with the sacrificer's wife), this is stated: 'They release the <s>Pātnīvata</s> that has been circumambulated with fire.' There the doubt arises: is a release of the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> that has been circumambulated with fire being enjoined, or is it a different ritual action? If the two words 'circumambulated with fire' and 'they release' are connected with each other, then it is the release of the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s>. But if the word '<s>Pātnīvata</s>' is connected with '<s>utsṛjati</s>' (he releases), then it is a different ritual action.
What is the prima facie view? It is a different ritual action. Why? The <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> is prior, and the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [likewise] — [the sacrifice being] qualified by both qualifiers, how could it be restated by the word '<s>Pātnīvata</s>' alone? Moreover, if a release of the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> were being enjoined, the qualifier 'circumambulated with fire' would not be appropriate. Therefore, we say: the <s>Pātnīvata</s>-nature of what has been circumambulated with fire is being enjoined — that is the very same ritual action.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: it is not a different ritual action. Rather, a curtailment (<s>avaccheda</s>) of the prior [ritual action] is being enjoined by the word '<s>utsṛjati</s>' (he releases). What will follow from this? First, the sacrifice-nature (<s>yajimattā</s>) will not need to be posited. And the word '<s>utsṛjati</s>,' which by direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) enjoins release, will not be overridden by the sentence. In the alternative-ritual-action view, when the <s>Pātnīvata</s>-nature is being enjoined by the sentence, the release that is contextually established would be restated by the verbal root — [but then it would lose its injunctive force]. Moreover, the <s>Pātnīvata</s>-nature of what has been circumambulated with fire is already known from the prior [rite] — it cannot be enjoined [again]. Therefore, it is a curtailment of the prior ritual action. As for the objection that 'when a release of the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> is being enjoined, the qualifier "circumambulated with fire" would not be appropriate' — this is no fault. Here, the word '<s>Pātnīvata</s>' simply serves no independent [qualifying] purpose — it is not being qualified [separately]. For this very reason, the <s>Tvāṣṭra Pātnīvata</s>, being qualified by both qualifiers, is restated by the word '<s>Pātnīvata</s>' alone through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — so there is no fault. Therefore, it is established that [there is] a curtailment.
Page 188

children.text: adravyatvāt kevale karmaśeṣaḥ syāt // MS_2,3.20 //
children.translated_text: Because of being non-substantial, when [the name] alone [is heard], it should be a supplement to the [existing] ritual action. // MS 2.3.20 //

children.text:
na kasyacid api prakaraṇe śrūyate, eṣa vai haviṣā havir yajate yo 'dābhyaṃ gṛhītvā somāya yajata iti, tathā parā vaitasyāyuḥ prāṇa eti yo 'ṃśuṃ gṛhṇātīti{*2/354*}. tatra sandehaḥ, kiṃ yāgāntaram etad grahaṇakam, uta jyotiṣṭomayāge grahavidhir iti.
kiṃ prāptam? yāgāntaram iti. kutaḥ? apūrvanāmadheyasaṃyogāt, na prakṛtāv etan nāmadheyako yāgo 'sti, na grahaḥ kaścid yo 'bhyasyeta. tasmād yāgāntaram. nanu dravyadevataṃ na śrūyate. mā bhūd dravyadevatam, sākṣād eva yajatiśabdo vidyate. tasmāt karmāntaram adābhyasaṃjñakam, aṃśusaṃjñakaṃ ca yāgaṃ karotīty evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - adravyadevatāke kevale nāmadheye śrūyamāṇe brūmaḥ, jyotiṣṭome eva grahābhyāsaviśeṣavidhānam iti. kutaḥ? etat tāvad grahasya nāmadheyaṃ na yāgasya, grahaṇena sākṣāt saṃbandhāt, vyavahitatvād yāgasya. aṃśur iti ca muktasaṃśayam eva grahanāmadheyam, na ca grahabhede yāgabhedo bhavati, na ca, dravyadevataṃ śrūyate. yato gṛhṇātir yajimadvacano bhavet, yad apy uktam, sākṣād atra yajatiśabdo vidhāyaka iti, naivaṃ śakyaṃ karmāntaraṃ vidhātum, vihitayāgavacano hi saḥ, viśeṣābhāvāt. tasmād yajatinā jyotiṣṭoma evocyate, aṃśvadābhyaśabdābhyām apy aparau grahābhyāsau vidhīyeta iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
Not heard in the context of any [particular sacrifice], it is taught: 'He indeed sacrifices an oblation with an oblation, who, having taken the <s>Adābhya</s> [cup], sacrifices to <s>Soma</s>'; and likewise, 'His life-breath goes beyond, who takes the <s>Aṃśu</s> [cup].' There the doubt arises: is this [an injunction of] a different ritual action involving a [cup-]taking, or is it an injunction of a [cup-]taking within the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice?
What is the prima facie view? It is a different ritual action. Why? Because of the connection with an unprecedented name — no ritual action with this name exists in the established [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>]; nor is there any [cup-]taking that is repeated [under this name]. Therefore, it is a different ritual action. [Objection:] But the substance and deity are not heard [for it]. [Reply:] Even without substance and deity, the word '<s>yajati</s>' itself is directly present. Therefore, it is a different ritual action named '<s>Adābhya</s>,' and one named '<s>Aṃśu</s>' that performs a sacrifice — this is the prima facie view.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: when the name alone is heard, without substance and deity, we say it is an injunction of a specific [cup-]taking repetition within the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself. Why? First, this is a name of the [cup-]taking, not of the sacrifice — because of the direct connection with taking, and because the sacrifice is remote [syntactically]. And '<s>Aṃśu</s>' (ray) is indisputably a name of the [cup-]taking. And a difference in [cup-]taking does not entail a difference in sacrifice. Nor are substance and deity heard — from which '<s>gṛhṇāti</s>' (he takes) could be a sacrifice-word. As for the objection that the word '<s>yajati</s>' itself is directly present as an injunction [of a new sacrifice] — it is not possible to enjoin a different ritual action in this way, for that [word '<s>yajati</s>'] denotes the [already] enjoined sacrifice, because no specific [new sacrifice] is differentiated. Therefore, '<s>yajati</s>' refers to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself, and the words '<s>Aṃśu</s>' and '<s>Adābhya</s>' enjoin two additional [cup-]taking repetitions — this is established.
Page 189

children.text: agnis tu liṅgadarśanāt kratuśabdaḥ pratīyeta // MS_2,3.21 //
children.translated_text: But '<s>Agni</s>' (fire), because of the observation of an indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>), should be understood as a ritual-name (<s>kratuśabda</s>). // MS 2.3.21 //

children.text:
asty agniḥ, ya evaṃ vidvān agniṃ cinuta iti, evaṃ vidhāya śrūyate, athāto 'gnim agniṣṭomenaivānuyajati, tam ukthena, tam atirātreṇa, taṃ ṣoḍaśinetyevamādi{*2/356*}. tatra sandehaḥ, kim ayam agniśabdo yāgavacano jyotiṣṭomādibhyaḥ karmāntaraṃ cinuta ity ākhyātena vidhīyate, uta dravyavacano jyotiṣṭomādiṣu guṇavidhānam iti.
kiṃ prāptam? yāgavacana iti. kutaḥ? liṅgadarśanāt, liṅgaṃ hi dṛśyate, agneḥ stotram agneḥ śastram iti tathā, ṣaḍupasadḥ 'gneḥ cityasya bhavantīti, yasya stotraṃ śastram upasadaś ca tasyāgniśabdo vācaka iti gamyate, yāgasyaitat sarvam, tasmāt yāgavacana iti. nanu liṅgam asādhakam, prāptir ucyatām iti. atrocyate - athāto 'gnim agniṣṭomenaivānuyajatīti yāgam abhinivartayatīty ucyate, tam agnim iti viśinaṣṭi. tasmād agnisaṃjñaka iti gamyate. anuśabdo 'py upasargo yajater viśeṣaka evam upapadyate, yady agnir yāgaḥ. tasmāt kratuśabdaḥ pratīyeta.
children.translated_text:
There is [the rite of] <s>Agni</s> (fire-piling). After enjoining 'He who, knowing thus, piles up the fire,' it is heard: 'Then he follows up the fire with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> itself; with the <s>Uktha</s>; with the <s>Atirātra</s>; with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>' and so forth. There the doubt arises: is the word '<s>Agni</s>' here a sacrifice-word, [denoting] a different ritual action from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like, enjoined by the verb '<s>cinute</s>' (he piles up)? Or is it a substance-word, [indicating] a subsidiary-quality injunction in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like?
What is the prima facie view? It is a sacrifice-word. Why? Because of the observation of an indicatory sign. For an indicatory sign is observed — 'the <s>stotra</s> (chant) of [the rite called] <s>Agni</s>,' 'the <s>śastra</s> (recitation) of <s>Agni</s>' — and likewise, 'the six preparatory rites (<s>upasads</s>) belong to <s>Agni</s>, the fire-piler.' That whose <s>stotra</s>, <s>śastra</s>, and <s>upasads</s> these are — the word '<s>Agni</s>' denotes that — this is understood. All of these belong to a sacrifice. Therefore, it is a sacrifice-word. [Objection:] But an indicatory sign is non-probative — state the [proper] establishment. [Reply:] To this it is said: 'Then he follows up the fire with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> itself' — it is said that [this] brings about a [new] sacrifice. 'That fire' — this specifies [it]. Therefore, it is understood that [it is] designated by the name '<s>Agni</s>.' The prefix '<s>anu</s>' too, as a modifier of '<s>yajati</s>,' is appropriate in this way — if '<s>Agni</s>' is a sacrifice [name]. Therefore, it should be understood as a ritual-name.

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 5.5.2.1]

children.text: dravyaṃ vā syāc codanāyās tadarthatvāt // MS_2,3.22 //
children.translated_text: Or [<s>Agni</s>] may be a substance[-word], because the injunction serves that purpose. // MS 2.3.22 //

children.text: dravyaṃ vāgniśabdenocyeta. katamad dravyam? yad etaj jvalanaḥ, atra hy eṣa prasiddhaḥ. cinuta ity eṣā hi codanā cayanārthā na yajaty arthaṃ śaknoti vaditum, cayanenainaṃ saṃskurute citau sthāpayatīti. anuśabdaś ca paścād artho bhaviṣyati, cayane nirvṛtte paścād agniṣṭomena yāgena yajatīti.
children.translated_text: Or the word <s>agni</s> (fire) may denote a substance. Which substance? This [actual] fire (<s>jvalana</s>), for [the word] is well-known in this [sense]. For the injunction '<s>cinuta</s>' (pile up) is for the purpose of [fire-altar] construction — it cannot express the meaning of '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices). He consecrates it by construction, establishing it on the altar (<s>citi</s>). And the prefix <s>anu</s> will have the meaning of 'afterward' — after the construction is completed, he afterward sacrifices with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice.
Page 190

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/357: Edition cross-references}]

children.text: tatsaṃyogāt kratus tadākhyaḥ syāt tena dharmavidhānāni // MS_2,3.23 //
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with that [fire-altar], the ritual would be named after it; by that, [the passages are] injunctions of its properties. // MS 2.3.23 //

children.text: yat tu liṅgadarśanam uktam, yāgavacano 'gniśabda iti, tat teṣv eva liṅgasaṃyukteṣu vacaneṣu, na sarvatra, teṣu cityāgnisaṃyogāt, yāge lakṣaṇaśabdaḥ, tena kratuvacanāni taddharmavidhānānīty adoṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: As for the observation of the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that was stated — that the word <s>agni</s> denotes a sacrifice — that [applies] only in those passages connected with the indicatory mark, not everywhere. In those [passages], because of the connection with the constructed fire-altar (<s>cityāgni</s>), the word serves as a designation (<s>lakṣaṇaśabda</s>) for the sacrifice. Therefore, [the statements about the] ritual (<s>kratu</s>) and its property-injunctions are [named after that fire-altar] — there is no defect.

children.text: prakaraṇāntare prayojanānyatvam // MS_2,3.24 //
children.translated_text: In a different context, [the statement] has a different purpose. // MS 2.3.24 //

children.text:
kuṇḍapāyinām ayane śrūyate, māsam agnihotraṃ juhoti, māsaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajata ityevamādi. tatra sandihyate, kiṃ niyate 'gnihotre niyatayoś ca darśapūrṇamāsayor māso vidhīyate kālaḥ, atha kiṃ niyatāgnihotrān niyatābhyāṃ ca darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ karmāntaravidhānam iti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? niyateṣu kālavidhir iti. kutaḥ? kālavidhisarūpa eṣa śabdo māsam iti. kathaṃ kālavidhisarūpatā? yad agnihotraṃ juhotīti viditam, māsam ity aviditam. evaṃ cāgnihotraśabdo darśapūrṇamāsaśabdaś ca nārthāntaravṛttau bhaviṣyataḥ, tasmāt kālavidhiḥ. nanu kuṇḍapāyinām ayanaprakaraṇaṃ bādhyetaivam. kāmaṃ bādhyatām, vākyaṃ hi balavattaram.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - prakaraṇāntare śrūyamāṇaṃ vākyaṃ yasya prakaraṇe, tasya vācakaṃ bhavitum arhati. nanu pratyakṣo 'gnihotrasya darśapūrṇa[191]{*2/358*}māsayoś ca guṇavidhiḥ. na, ity ucyate. katham? upasiddhaś caritveti hy uktvedam abhidhīyate, na ca, upasado 'gnihotrasya darśapūrṇamāsayoś ca santi. tasmād aśakyas tatra māsavidhiḥ. athocyate, upasado 'pi vidhīyanta iti. tathā guṇavidhānārtho 'smin vākye 'nekaguṇavidhānād vākyaṃ bhidyeta. asmin pakṣe punar atantram agnihotraśabdo na karma viśekṣyati, tena vākyabhedo na bhaviṣyati. tasmāt karmāntaram iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>ayana</s> (year-long rite) of the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s>, it is heard: 'For a month he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>; for a month he sacrifices with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites],' and so on. Here the doubt arises: Is a month being enjoined as the time for the already-established <s>Agnihotra</s> and the already-established <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, or is this an injunction of different ritual actions from the established <s>Agnihotra</s> and <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>?
What is the prima facie view? It is an injunction of time for the established [rites]. Why? The word 'a month' (<s>māsa</s>) has the form of a time-injunction. How does it have the form of a time-injunction? That 'he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>' is [already] known; 'for a month' is [newly] unknown. And thus the words <s>Agnihotra</s> and <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> will not apply to a different meaning. Therefore, it is a time-injunction. [Objection:] But the context of the <s>ayana</s> of the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s> would be overridden in this way. [Reply:] Let it be overridden — for the sentence is stronger [than context].
Having arrived at this position, we say: A sentence heard in a different context ought to be expressive of [the meaning proper to] that context. [Objection:] But a quality-injunction for the <s>Agnihotra</s> and <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is directly perceived. [Reply:] No, it is said. How? Because after saying 'having performed the <s>Upasad</s> [preparatory rites],' this is stated — but the <s>Upasad</s> rites do not belong to the <s>Agnihotra</s> or the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Therefore, a month-injunction is impossible there. If it is said that the <s>Upasad</s> rites too are being enjoined [for them] — in that case, since this sentence would serve to enjoin a quality, the sentence would be split by the injunction of multiple qualities. On the other hand, [if these are different ritual actions,] the word <s>Agnihotra</s> being unconstrained [by the established rites] will not qualify a [particular] ritual action — therefore, the sentence will not be split. Hence, it is established that these are different ritual actions.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/358: Edition cross-references}]

children.text: phalaṃ cākarmasannidhau // MS_2,3.25 //
children.translated_text: And the fruit [is stated] in the absence of [proximity to] a ritual action. // MS 2.3.25 //

children.text:
anārabhya kiṃcic chrūyata āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped rukkāmaḥ{*2/359*}; agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāmaḥ{*2/360*}; aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet prajākāma iti{*2/361*}. atra sandihyate, kiṃ prākṛteṣv āgneyādiṣu phalaṃ vidhīyate, uta prākṛtebhyaḥ karmāntarāṇy etāni?
kiṃ prāptam? prākṛteṣu phalavidhir iti. kutaḥ? viditā āgneyādayaḥ pratyabhijñāyante, tasmāt teṣām anuvādaḥ phalasaṃbandhārtha iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - phalaṃ ca bhedakam akarmasannidhau śrūyamāṇam. katham? anuvāde sati na śakyeta phalaṃ vidhātum, vidhāyakasyābhāvāt, na hi, avidhīyamāno hy upāyo ruco bhavatīti gamyate. api ca rukkāme 'tra vidhīyamāne kāmasya [192]{*2/362*} anityatvāt, āgneyādīnāṃ nityatvāt saṃbandho nāvakalpeta. evaṃ sarvatra. tasmāt karmāntarāṇi.
children.translated_text:
Without reference to [an established ritual], it is heard: 'One who desires radiance should offer an <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake]'; 'One who desires the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> should offer an <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s> eleven-<s>kapāla</s> [cake]'; 'One who desires offspring should offer an <s>Aindrāgna</s> eleven-<s>kapāla</s> [cake].' Here the doubt arises: Is a fruit being enjoined for the already-established <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings], or are these different ritual actions from the established [ones]?
What is the prima facie view? It is a fruit-injunction for the established [rites]. Why? The <s>Āgneya</s> and the others are [already] known and recognized; therefore, [these passages] are re-statements of them for the purpose of connecting with the fruit.
Having arrived at this position, we say: The fruit too is a differentiating factor when heard in the absence of [proximity to] a ritual action. How? If [the <s>Āgneya</s> and others are] re-statements, the fruit cannot be enjoined, because there is no enjoining element. For it is not understood that 'an instrument that is not being enjoined becomes the [means to] radiance.' Moreover, when 'one who desires radiance' is being enjoined here, because the desire is impermanent while the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings] are permanent, a connection cannot be construed. Similarly everywhere. Therefore, these are different ritual actions.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/359: Cf. <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.3.3} {2/360: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.3.3.3} {2/361: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.1.1} {2/362: Edition cross-references}]

children.text: sannidhau tv avibhāgāt phalārthena punaḥśrutiḥ // MS_2,3.26 //
children.translated_text: But in proximity [to an established rite], because of non-differentiation, the re-hearing serves the purpose of [specifying] the fruit. // MS 2.3.26 //

children.text: asty aveṣṭiḥ, āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ puroḍāśo bhavatītyevamādiḥ, tāṃ prakṛtyocyate, etayānnādyakāmaṃ yājayeteti. tatra sandehaḥ - kiṃ karmāntaram aveṣṭer utāveṣṭir eveti? kiṃ prāptam, karmāntaram iti, uktena nyāyena. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sannidhau phalārthena punaḥśrutir aveṣṭer eva, na karmāntaram iti. kutaḥ? avibhāgāt, etayety eṣa śabdo na śaknoty aveṣṭyā vibhaktaṃ yāgam anyaṃ vaktum, sannihitasya pratinirdeśaka eṣa śabdaḥ. tasmād aveṣṭir evānnādyakāmasya vidhīyata iti. kiṃ prayojanam? yady aveṣṭiḥ, āgneyādīni havīṃṣi. atha karmāntaram, anyahaviṣko yāga iti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> [sacrifice]: 'There is an <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake),' and so on. Taking that as the basis, it is said: 'With this, one should have the one who desires food sacrificed.' Here the doubt arises: Is this a different ritual action from the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>, or is it the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> itself? What is the prima facie view? It is a different ritual action, by the reasoning stated [above]. Having arrived at this position, we say: In proximity [to the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>], the re-hearing serves the purpose of the fruit for the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> itself, not a different ritual action. Why? Because of non-differentiation — the word 'with this' (<s>etayā</s>) cannot express a sacrifice different from, [i.e.,] separated from, the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>; this word designates what is proximate. Therefore, the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> itself is enjoined for one who desires food. What is the practical consequence? If it is the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>, the <s>Āgneya</s> and other oblation-materials [apply]. But if it is a different ritual action, it would be a sacrifice with different oblation-materials.

children.text: āgneyasūktahetutvād abhyāsena pratīyeta // MS_2,3.27 //
children.translated_text: Because of the causal connection with the <s>Āgneya</s>-<s>sūkta</s>, repetition [of the sacrifice] should be understood. // MS 2.3.27 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyābhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavatīti vidhāya punar ucyate, āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ bhavatīti. tatra sandehaḥ - kim amāvāsyāyāṃ dvir āgneyena yaṣṭavyam, uta sakṛd iti. kiṃ prāptam? āgneyasūktahetutvād abhyāsena pratīyate, ekasyaivaṃ punaḥśrutir aviśeṣād anarthakaṃ hi syād iti{*2/363*}.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, having enjoined 'An <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] exists on both the new-moon and full-moon [days] without fail,' it is stated again: 'An <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] exists on the new-moon day.' Here the doubt arises: Should one sacrifice twice with the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] on the new-moon day, or only once? What is the prima facie view? Because of the causal connection with the <s>Āgneya</s>-<s>sūkta</s>, repetition should be understood — for the re-hearing of the very same [offering] without differentiation would be purposeless.
Page 193

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/363: MS 2.2.2} {2/364: Edition cross-references}]

children.text: avibhāgāt tu karmaṇā{*2/365*} dvir ukter na vidhīyate // MS_2,3.28 //
children.translated_text: But because of the non-differentiation from the [same] ritual action, what is stated twice is not [separately] enjoined. // MS 2.3.28 //

children.text: naitad asti, punar abhyasitavya āgneya iti. kutaḥ? na, abhyāsasya vācakaḥ śabdo 'stīti. nanv āgneyaḥ punaruccaritaḥ paraṃ karma vidhāsyati. neti brūmaḥ, śabdaḥ punaruccarito{*2/366*} na punar arthaḥ kartavya iti śaknoti vaditum, yo 'sya prathamam uccaritasyārthaḥ, śatakṛtvo 'py uccaritasya sa evārtho bhaviṣyati, nānyaḥ. nanu vihitam eva punar viśiṣṭaṃ vidadhad anarthako bhavati. bhavatu kāmam anarthakatvam, na tv anyaṃ śaknoti vaditum, bhaved upapannam anarthakatvam, na tv arthāntaravacanatā. tasmān na dvir abhyasyeteti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] should be repeated. Why? Because there is no word that expresses repetition. [Objection:] But the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering], being uttered again, will enjoin another ritual action. [Reply:] We say no — a word uttered again cannot say 'the referent should be done again.' Whatever was the referent when it was first uttered — even if uttered a hundred times, that very same referent it will have, not another. [Objection:] But if it [merely] enjoins what has already been enjoined, without qualification, it would be purposeless. [Reply:] Let it be purposeless as it may — but it cannot express something else. Purposelessness is a possible [outcome]; but expressing a different referent is not. Therefore, the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] should not be repeated.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{2/365: E1,6; E2,4,5: karmaṇo}*
*{2/366: E2,4: punaruccārito}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/365: E1,6; E2,4,5 read <s>karmaṇo</s>} {2/366: E2,4 read <s>punaruccārito</s>}]

children.text: anyārthā vā punaḥśrutiḥ // MS_2,3.29 //
children.translated_text: Or, the re-hearing serves a different purpose. // MS 2.3.29 //

children.text: atha vā, nānarthikā punaḥśrutiḥ, arthavādārthā bhaviṣyatīty ucyate. kim arthavādena prayojanam? yadā pūrvenaiva vākyena sārthavādakena vihitaḥ āgneyaḥ, kamanyam arthaṃ vidhātum śrutiḥ{*2/367*} prayujyeta? śrutimātraṃ{*2/368*} yan na kasyacid vidhānārtham, tad anarthakam, ity uktam, āmnāyasya kriyārthatvād ānarthakyam atadarthānām iti{*2/369*}, śrutaś cāśrutaś{*2/370*} ca tāvān eva so 'rthaḥ, yathā śrutā cāśrutā{*2/371*} ca devatā aṅgabhāvaṃ sādhayati, evam etad iti. tad ucyate - anyārthā vā punaḥśrutiḥ, na āgneyaṃ vidhātum, aindrāgnavidhānārthā, āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ bhavaty eva, na kevalenāgninā sa sādhur bhavatītīndrasahito 'gniḥ samīcīnataraḥ, tasmād aindrāgnaḥ kartavya iti.
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the re-hearing is not purposeless; it will serve the purpose of a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), it is said. What is the purpose of the <s>arthavāda</s>? When the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] has already been enjoined by the previous sentence along with its <s>arthavāda</s>, for what other purpose would the scriptural statement be employed? A [scriptural] hearing (<s>śruti</s>) alone, which serves the purpose of no injunction, is purposeless — as was stated: 'Because the <s>samāmnāya</s> (codified teaching) has ritual action as its purpose, those [statements] that do not serve that purpose are purposeless.' And whether heard or unheard, the referent remains just the same — just as a deity, whether praised or unpraised, accomplishes its subsidiary status. To this it is said: Or, the re-hearing serves a different purpose — not to enjoin the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering], but for the purpose of enjoining the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (related to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>) [offering]. The <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] does indeed exist on the new-moon day — but [the sacrifice] is not excellent with <s>Agni</s> alone; <s>Agni</s> combined with <s>Indra</s> is more proper. Therefore, the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [offering] should be performed.
Page 194

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/367-372: Variant readings; MS 1.2.1 cited; Edition cross-references}]

children.text: yāvajjīviko 'bhyāsaḥ karmadharmaḥ prakaraṇāt // MS_2,4.1 //
children.translated_text: The lifelong [nature] is a repetition that is a property of the ritual action, because of the context. // MS 2.4.1 //

children.text: bahvṛcabrāhmaṇe śrūyate - yāvajjīvam agnihotraṃ juhotīti, yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyām yajeteti. atra sandeheḥ - kiṃ karmadharmo 'bhyāso yāvajjīvikatā, uta kartṛdharmo niyamaś codyate yāvajjīvikateti. kathaṃ karmadharmo 'bhyāsaḥ, kathaṃ vā kartṛdharmo niyama iti. yadi juhotir anuvādaḥ, yāvajjīvam iti vidhiḥ. tataḥ karmadharmo 'bhyāsaḥ, yadi viparītam, tataḥ kartṛdharmo niyama iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam, karmadharmo 'bhyāsaḥ. kutaḥ? prakaraṇāt, yadīyaṃ vacanavyaktiḥ, juhotiyajatiśabdāv anuvādau, yāvajjīvam iti ca vidhiḥ, tataḥ prakaraṇam anugṛhyate, tasmād abhyāsaḥ. evaṃ kṛtvā satrasaṃstavo yukto bhaviṣyati, jarāmaryaṃ vā etat satraṃ yad agnihotram, darśapūrṇamāsau ceti dīrghakālasāmānyāt. tasmād abhyāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bahvṛca Brāhmaṇa</s>, it is heard: 'One offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> for as long as one lives'; 'One sacrifices with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites] for as long as one lives.' Here the doubt arises: Is the lifelong nature a repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>) that is a property of the ritual action, or is the lifelong nature a restriction (<s>niyama</s>) that is a property of the agent being enjoined? How would it be a repetition as a property of the ritual action? Or how a restriction as a property of the agent? If '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers) is a re-statement and '<s>yāvajjīvam</s>' (for as long as one lives) is the injunction, then it is a repetition as a property of the ritual action. If the reverse, then it is a restriction as a property of the agent. What is the prima facie view? It is a repetition as a property of the ritual action. Why? Because of the context — if the articulation of this sentence is such that the words '<s>juhoti</s>' and '<s>yajati</s>' are re-statements and '<s>yāvajjīvam</s>' is the injunction, then the context is supported. Therefore, [it is] repetition. Having done so, the comparison with a <s>sattra</s> (soma session) will be justified — 'The <s>Agnihotra</s> and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> are indeed a <s>sattra</s> lasting until old age and death' — because of the similarity of long duration. Therefore, [it is] repetition.

children.text: kartur vā śrutisaṃyogāt // MS_2,4.2 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] a [property] of the agent, because of the connection with [direct] scripture. // MS 2.4.2 //

children.text: atra brūmaḥ - yāvajjīviko 'bhyāso na syāt, kartur dharmo niyamaś codyata iti. kutaḥ? śrutisaṃyogāt. evaṃ śrutiparicchinno 'rtho bhaviṣyati, itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt. katham? yāvajjīvanam, tāvatā kālena kuryād iti, tad etat pradoṣaparisamāptam agnihotram anabhyasya, na śakyate yāvajjīvanakālena kartum, paurṇamāsyam āvāsyāparisamāptau ca darśapūrṇamāsau. yady ucyeta - jīvanakālasyaikadeśe 'pi kṛtaṃ tena kālena kṛtaṃ bhavatīti. naitad evam, [195]{*2/373*} arthaprāptaṃ hi tan na vidhātavyaṃ śabdena, jīvanaparimitaḥ kālo yaḥ, tena parisamāpayitavyam ity arthād abhyāsaḥ, sa hi kartavyatayā śrūyate, na cāsāv juhotiyajatibhyām ucyate, lakṣaṇayā tu gamyate. yāvajjīvaṃ juhuyāt, yāvajjīvam abhyasyed iti, śrutiś ca prakaraṇād balīyasī. yadīyaṃ vacanavyaktir asya vākyasya, yāvajjīvam ity anuvādo juhoti yajatīti ca vidhānam, ity evaṃ yajatijuhotiśabdau svārthāv eva bhaviṣyataḥ, yāvajjīvaśabdo 'pi jīvanavacana eva, nābhyāsalakṣaṇo bhaviṣyatīti jīvane nimitte karma vidhīyate, jīvaṃś ced dhotavyam iti, jīvanaṃ nimittam, na kālaḥ, niyatanimittatvān niyataṃ karma tenocyate, kartur dharmo niyamaś codyata iti.
children.translated_text: Here we say: The lifelong [nature] should not be a repetition; rather, a restriction is being enjoined as a property of the agent. Why? Because of the connection with [direct] scripture. The meaning will thus be delimited by scripture; otherwise, there would be secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). How? The <s>Agnihotra</s>, which is completed at dusk, cannot be performed for the entire duration of one's life without repetition — nor can the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites], which are completed on the full-moon and new-moon days. If one were to say: 'Even when performed during a portion of the lifetime, it is performed during that [lifetime]' — this is not so. For what is obtained by implication need not be enjoined by a word. That the time delimited by one's lifetime should be fully utilized — this implies repetition, for that is heard as something to be done, and it is not expressed by the words '<s>juhoti</s>' and '<s>yajati</s>' but understood through secondary designation. [The meaning would be:] 'One should offer for as long as one lives,' [i.e.,] 'one should repeat for as long as one lives' — and direct scripture (<s>śruti</s>) is stronger than context. If the articulation of this sentence is such that '<s>yāvajjīvam</s>' is the re-statement and '<s>juhoti</s>' and '<s>yajati</s>' are the injunctions — in that case, the words '<s>yajati</s>' and '<s>juhoti</s>' will retain their own meaning, and the word '<s>yāvajjīva</s>' too will simply denote 'living,' not bearing the characteristic of repetition. Thus, 'living' being the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>), the ritual action is enjoined — 'If alive, one must offer' — living is the occasion, not the time. Because the occasion is fixed, the ritual action too is fixed — therefore, it is said [that] a restriction is being enjoined as a property of the agent.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {2/373: Edition cross-references}]

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca, karmadharme hi prakrameṇa niyamyeta, tatrānarthakam anyat syāt // MS_2,4.3 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>); for if it were a property of the ritual action, it would be restricted by progression, and the other [statement] would be purposeless. // MS 2.4.3 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca bhavaty api ha vā eṣa svargāl lokāc chidyate yo darśapūrṇamāsayājī paurṇamāsīm amāvāsyāṃ vātipātayeteti. kathaṃ liṅgam? karmadharme hi prakrāntaṃ satraṃ yāvajjīvanakālena parisamāpyeta, na tatra kālātipātaḥ syāt. tatra cānarthakam anyat syāt prāyaścittādi vidhīyamānam.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark too is observed: 'He is indeed cut off from the heavenly world who, being a sacrificer of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites], lets the full-moon or new-moon [day] pass.' How is this an indicatory mark? If it were a property of the ritual action, the <s>sattra</s> (soma session) once commenced would be completed by the duration of one's lifetime — there would be no missing of the time. And in that case, the other [statement — about expiation] being prescribed would be purposeless.

children.text: vyapavargaṃ ca darśayati, kālaś cet karmabhedaḥ syāt // MS_2,4.4 //
children.translated_text: And it shows completion: if time were the differentiator of rituals. // MS_2,4.4 //

children.text: vyapavargasya samāpanasya darśanaṃ bhavati, darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā somena yajeteti. yadi darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā somasya kālo 'sti, vyaktaṃ na yāvajjīvanakālena tau parisamāpyete. atha jīvanaṃ nimittam, upapadyate karmabhedaḥ, darśapūrṇamāsau parisamāpya somaṃ karmāntaraṃ kuryād iti. [196]{*2/374*} api cāhitāgnir vā eṣa yo 'gnihotraṃ juhoti na darśapūrṇamāsau yajeta, yā āhutibhājo devatās tā anudhyāyinīḥ karotīty anudhyāyinīvacanaṃ bhavati, niyato ya āhutibhāgaḥ, tasmin adīyamāne 'nudhyāyinīvacanaṃ bhavati. yas tv aniyata āhutibhāgas tam{*2/375*} anudhyāyanti, idaṃ no bhaviṣyatīti, niyataś ca bhāgo niyamapakṣe bhavati, na kāmyapakṣe, karmadharme ca kāmyam agnihotraṃ ca darśapūrṇamāsau ca, tasmān niyamapakṣaḥ. api ca śrūyate, jarāmaryaṃ vaitat satraṃ yad agnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsau ca, jarayā ha vaitābhyāṃ nirmucyate mṛtyunā ceti jarāmaraṇanirmocanāvadhāraṇavacanaṃ ca niyamapakṣa upapadyate. kāmyapakṣe hy aprayogād api mucyeta.
children.translated_text: There is evidence of completion (<s>vyapavarga</s>): "Having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>." If after sacrificing with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> there is a time for <s>Soma</s>, clearly those two [rites] are not completed within a lifelong period. But if life is the cause, then differentiation of rituals is possible — having completed the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one would perform <s>Soma</s> as a different ritual. [196] Moreover, "He who has established the sacred fires and offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> but does not perform the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> makes the deities who share in the oblation discontented" — this statement about discontentment arises. When a fixed share of oblation is not given, the statement about discontentment applies. But when the share of oblation is unfixed, they are discontented thinking "this will come to us." A fixed share exists under the obligatory view (<s>niyamapakṣa</s>), not under the optional view (<s>kāmyapakṣa</s>). And under the view that it is a property of the ritual, the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> would be optional; therefore the obligatory view [is correct]. Moreover, it is heard: "This is a lifelong session (<s>sattra</s>) — the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — one is released from them only by old age or by death." This statement determining release by old age and death is possible only under the obligatory view. Under the optional view, one could be released even by non-performance.

children.text: anityatvāt tu naivaṃ syāt // MS_2,4.5 //
children.translated_text: But because of non-permanence, it should not be so. // MS_2,4.5 //

children.text: tuśabdo 'nvācaye, itaraś ca paśyāmaḥ, kartur dharmo niyamaś codyata iti. yadi pūrvasya homasya guṇavidhir bhavet sa ekaikaḥ pūrvo 'gnihotrahomo 'nityaḥ syāt, kāmasaṃyogena śruto nānyaḥ kaścin nityaḥ, tatra liṅgaṃ virudhyeta, jarāmaryaṃ vaitat satraṃ yad agnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsau, jarayā vaitābhyāṃ nirmucyate mṛtyunā ceti. kathaṃ virudhyate? jarāmaraṇanirmocanādhāraṇavacanaṃ niyamapakṣa upapadyate, kāmyapakṣe 'prayogād api mucyeta.
children.translated_text: The word "but" (<s>tu</s>) is for continuation. And we observe the other [view] — that obligation (<s>niyama</s>) is enjoined as a property of the agent. If the subsidiary injunction of the earlier oblation were [a property of the ritual], each individual <s>Agnihotra</s> oblation would be non-permanent, heard in connection with desire; no other would be permanent. There the indicative mark would be contradicted: "This is a lifelong session — the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; one is released from them only by old age or by death." How is it contradicted? The statement determining release by old age and death is possible under the obligatory view; under the optional view, one could be released even by non-performance.

children.text: virodhaś cāpi pūrvavat // MS_2,4.6 //
children.translated_text: And there is also a contradiction, as before. // MS_2,4.6 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmo na pūrvābhyāso guṇaś codyata iti. kutah? virodhāt, virodho bhavati, darśapūrṇamāsavikārāḥ sauryādayo 'pi yāvajjīvam abhyasitavyā bhaveyuḥ. so 'nārabhyārthaḥ pratijñātaḥ syāt. ato 'pi paśyāmo niyama iti satrasaṃstavaś ca santatabhāvam upapatsyate.
children.translated_text: From this too we observe that repetition of the prior [rite] is not enjoined as a subsidiary. Why? Because of contradiction — a contradiction arises: the modifications of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, such as the <s>Saurya</s> and others, would also have to be repeated throughout life. That would be the pointless consequence that was asserted [to be avoided]. From this too we observe that [it is] an obligation (<s>niyama</s>), and the praise as a session (<s>satrasaṃstava</s>) will be consistent with continuous performance.

children.text: kartus tu dharmaniyamāt kālaśāstraṃ nimittaṃ syāt // MS_2,4.7 //
children.translated_text: But since obligation is a property of the agent, the temporal instruction would serve as the cause. // MS_2,4.7 //

children.text: yadi kartur dharmo niyamaś codyeta, tato jīvanaṃ nimittam, jīvane nimitte karma vidhīyate. tatra prayoge parisamāptaṃ karma, tathā vyapavargasya darśanam akḷptaṃ bhavati, tasmāt kartṛdharmo niyamaś codyata iti siddhaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: If obligation is enjoined as a property of the agent, then life is the cause; with life as the cause, the ritual is enjoined. When performed, the ritual is completed; thus the evidence of completion becomes unproblematic. Therefore it is established that obligation is enjoined as a property of the agent.

children.text: nāmarūpadharmaviśeṣapunaruktinindāśaktisamāptivacanaprāyaścittānyārthadarśanāc chākhāntareṣu karmabhedaḥ syāt // MS_2,4.8 //
children.translated_text: Because of differences in name, form, special properties, repetition, blame, capacity, statements of completion, expiations, and evidence of other purposes, there should be differentiation of rituals across [different Vedic] branches. // MS_2,4.8 //

children.text:
iha śākhāntarāṇy udāharaṇam, kāṭhakaṃ kālāpakaṃ paippalādakam ityevamādīni. tatra sandehaḥ, kim ekasyāṃ śākhāyāṃ yat karmāgnihotrādi śrūyate, tac chākhāntare punaḥ śrūyamāṇam bhidyeta tasmāt, uta na bhidyeta? bhidyeteti paśyāmaḥ. kutaḥ? nāmabhedāt, ekaṃ kāṭhakaṃ nāma, anyat kālāpakaṃ nāma, evaṃ nāmabhedād bhedaḥ. nanu granthanāmaitat. satyam, karmaṇām apīti brūmaḥ, karmabhir apy evamādīnāṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyam ekavibhaktitvaṃ ceti.
rūpabhedāc ca, ekasyāṃ śākhāyām agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālam āmananti, ekasyāṃ dvādaśakapālam, evaṃ bhinnaṃ rūpam{*2/377*}, katham iva na karmāntaraṃ bhaviṣyati.
dharmaviśeṣāc ca, kārīrīvākyāny adhīyānās taittirīyā bhūmau bhojanam ācaranti, apare śākhino nācaranti, tathāgnim adhī[198]{*2/378*}yānāḥ kecid upādhyāyasyodakumbhānāharanti, apare na, aśvamedham adhīyānāḥ kecid aśvasya ghāsam āharanti, apare na, pare 'nyaṃ dharmam ācaranti, aśvaghāsāder ekeṣām upakāram ākāṅkṣaty aśvamedhādiḥ, ekeṣāṃ nākāṅkṣati, sa evaikaḥ kathaṃ nākāṅkṣeta kathaṃ vānyad ākāṅkṣitum arhati, ato gamyata anyad iti. punaruktiprasaṅgāc ca, yadi sarvaśākhāpratyayam ekaṃ karma, ekasyāṃ śākhāyāṃ vihitasya karmaṇaḥ śākhāntare vacanaṃ punaruktam anarthakaṃ syāt. na tu bhedapakṣa eṣa doṣo 'sti, tasmād api karmabhedaḥ.
nindāvacanāc ca prātaḥ prātaranṛtaṃ te vadanti purodayā{*2/379*} juhvati ye 'gnihotraṃ divākīrtyam ādivā kīrtayantaḥ sūryo jyotir na tadā jyotir eṣām iti kecic chākhino 'nuditahomaṃ nindanti, apare punar uditahomaṃ nindanti, yathātithaye pradrutāyānnam āhareyus tādṛk tad yady udite juhvatīti{*2/380*}, sarvaśākhyāpratyaye viruddham, na tu karmabhede, tasmād api bheda iti. aśakteś ca, na śaknuyuḥ khalv api sarvaśākhāpratyayam upasaṃhartum, tatrānārabhyo 'rtho vidhīyata iti pratijñātaṃ bhavet, śakyaṃ tu karmabhede, ataḥ karmabheda iti.
samāptivacanāc ca, asamāpte 'pi samāpter vacanaṃ bhavati, kecid āhuḥ, atrāsmākam agniḥ parisamāpyata iti, apare 'nyaparisamāptiṃ vyapadiśanti, tad ekakarmatve nopapadyate, na hi tatra ca{*2/381*} parisamāpyeta, anyatra na. bhede tu yuktam, tasmād bheda iti.
prāyaścittavidhānāc ca, kecid anuditahomavyatikrame prāyaścittam āmananti, kecid uditahomavyatikrame vṛddhe ca prāyaścittam, na ca karmaikatva ubhayathā vṛddhiḥ saṃbhavati, karmabhede tu yad anudite homakarma, tad udite vṛddham, itarad apy udite, tasmād api bhedaḥ.
anyārthadarśanāc ca, idaṃ śrūyate, yadi purā didīkṣāṇāḥ syuḥ yadi vaiṣāṃ gṛhapatir gṛhapater vānusatriṇa iti, ta enam eva [199]{*2/382*} bṛhatsāmānaṃ kratum upeyur upetaṃ hy eṣāṃ rathantaram, atha yady adidīkṣāṇā itīṣṭavatām aniṣṭapūrvāṇāṃ ca dvādaśāhe darśanam upapadyate yadi karmabhedaḥ, ekakarmatve nāvakalpyate. katham? tāṇḍake{*2/383*} śrūyate, eṣa vāva prathamo yajño yajñānām, yaj jyotiṣṭomaḥ, ya etenāniṣṭvāthānyena yajeta gartapatyam eva taj jāyeta pravām īyata iti{*2/384*}, tat sarvatra syāt, tatrādidīkṣāṇāṃ dvādaśāhe darśanaṃ nopapadyate, tasmād api karmabhedaḥ.
athāparaṃ liṅgadarśanam, yat pakṣasamitāṃ pinuyāt kanīyāṃsaṃ yajñakratum upeyāt kanīyasīṃ prajñāṃ kanīyasaḥ paśūn kanīyo 'nnādyaṃ pāpīyān syāt, atha yadi vedisaṃmityā minotīti{*2/385*} pakṣasamāne pratiṣiddhe vedisaṃmānasya darśanaṃ bhavati, tat tu karmabheda upapadyate, pākṣikasya vedisaṃmānasya darśanam ekakarmatve nopapadyate. katham? eke hi samāmananti, rathākṣamātrāṇi yūpāntarālāni bhavantīti{*2/386*}, tat sarvatra syāt, tatra ca no pakṣasaṃmānaṃ no vedisaṃmānaṃ syāt, vedisaṃmānadarśanaṃ nopapadyate, tasmād api karmabhedaḥ.
aparaṃ ca liṅgadarśanam, keṣāṃcij jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, dve saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyeta iti, pareṣāṃ tisraḥ saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyanta ity ekakarmatve virodhaḥ, nānākarmatve kasmiṃścij jyotiṣṭome dve, kasmiṃścit tisraḥ, tasmāt karmabheda iti.
api ca sārasvate śrūyate, ye puroḍāśinas te upaviśanti ye sānnāyinas te vatsān vārayanti. sānnāyina iṣṭaprathamayajñāḥ, puroḍāśino viparītāḥ, ubhayeṣāṃ sārasvate darśanam avakalpate karmabhede, ekakarmatve sarveṣāṃ jyotiṣṭomapūrvatvaṃ syāt, tatra darśanaṃ nopapadyate.
api ca śrūyate - upahavyo niruktaḥ{*2/387*}, agniṣṭomo yajñaḥ rathantara[200]{*2/388*}sāmā, aśvaḥ śyāvo dakṣiṇā, pareṣāṃ śrūyate, upahavyo 'niruktaḥ, uktho{*2/389*} yajño bṛhatsāmā, aśvaḥ śveto rukmalalāṭo dakṣiṇeti, karmaikatve rathantaravacanaṃ bṛhadvacanaṃ cānarthakam, śākhādvayapratyayatvād bṛhatsāmā rathantarasāmā vā syāt, sa cāyaṃ prakṛtita evaṃlakṣaṇakaḥ prāptaḥ, nānākarmatve tv anyo bṛhatsāmānyo rathantarasāmeti yuktaṃ bhavati, tasmāc chākhāntare karmabhedo bhavitum arhati.
children.translated_text:
Here the different Vedic branches are the illustration — the <s>Kāṭhaka</s>, <s>Kālāpaka</s>, <s>Paippalādaka</s>, and so forth. There a doubt [arises]: is a ritual such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> heard in one branch, when heard again in another branch, different from it, or not? We hold it is different. Why? Because of difference in name — one is called <s>Kāṭhaka</s>, another <s>Kālāpaka</s>; thus difference arises from difference in name. But is this not merely the name of the text? True, but we say it is [the name] of the rituals too, since terms like these share co-reference and co-inflection with the rituals.
And because of difference in form — in one branch they teach the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [cake] on eleven potsherds, in another on twelve potsherds; thus the form is different — how could the ritual not be different?
And because of special properties (<s>dharmaviśeṣa</s>) — the <s>Taittirīyas</s> who study the <s>Kārīrī</s> passages practice eating on the ground; other branch-followers do not. Likewise, some who study the [section on] fire bring water-pots for the teacher, others do not; some who study the <s>Aśvamedha</s> bring fodder for the horse, others do not, while yet others practice a different observance. The <s>Aśvamedha</s> and similar [rites] require the service of horse-fodder etc. from some, not from others. If it were one and the same [ritual], how could it not require [this], or how could it require something else? From this we understand it is different. And because of the consequence of repetition — if one ritual were the object of all branches, the statement of a ritual enjoined in one branch would be a pointless repetition in another branch. But under the view of differentiation, this defect does not exist; therefore too there is differentiation of rituals.
And because of statements of blame — "Morning after morning they speak untruth, they who offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> before sunrise, reciting what should be recited by day as if reciting at dawn; the sun is the light, that [fire] is not their light" — some branch-followers blame the offering before sunrise, while others blame the offering after sunrise: "as if one would bring food for a guest who has already departed, such is it if they offer after sunrise." [This] is contradictory if it is the object of all branches, but not under the view of different rituals; therefore too there is differentiation. And because of incapacity — they would indeed be unable to collect [all injunctions] as the object of all branches; there, the pointless consequence would be established that something purposeless is enjoined. But this is possible under differentiation of rituals; hence differentiation.
And because of statements of completion — though incomplete, there are statements of completion: some say "here our fire is completed," while others declare completion elsewhere. That is not possible under the view of one ritual, for it cannot be completed there and not elsewhere. But under differentiation it is fitting; therefore differentiation.
And because of prescriptions of expiations — some teach expiation for transgressing the pre-sunrise offering, some for transgressing the post-sunrise offering, and some for excess. Under the view of one ritual, excess in both ways is not possible; but under differentiation of rituals, the ritual [enjoining] offering before sunrise — for that, [offering] after sunrise is the excess, and vice versa; therefore too there is differentiation.
And because of evidence of other purposes — this is heard: "If they were about to be consecrated, or if their householder or a fellow-<s>sattra</s>-participant's [householder were about to be consecrated]," [199] "they should resort to this very <s>Bṛhatsāman</s> rite; for the <s>Rathantara</s> has already been attained by them. But if they had not been consecrated" — the evidence of a <s>Dvādaśāha</s> for both those who have sacrificed and those who have not is possible under differentiation of rituals, but cannot be explained under the view of one ritual. How? In the <s>Tāṇḍaka</s> it is heard: "This indeed is the first sacrifice among sacrifices — the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; whoever, without having sacrificed with this, sacrifices with another, falls into a pit, goes to ruin." That would apply everywhere; then the evidence of a <s>Dvādaśāha</s> for the unconsecrated would be impossible; therefore too there is differentiation of rituals.
And there is another indicative evidence: "Whoever would measure with wing-measurement would attain a lesser sacrificial rite, lesser progeny, fewer cattle, less food, and become worse; but if he measures with altar-measurement..." — when wing-measurement is prohibited, the evidence of altar-measurement arises; that is possible under differentiation of rituals, but the evidence of optional altar-measurement is not possible under the view of one ritual. How? For some teach: "The intervals between the sacrificial posts should be the measure of a chariot-axle." That would apply everywhere, and then there would be neither wing-measurement nor altar-measurement; the evidence of altar-measurement would be impossible. Therefore too there is differentiation.
Another indicative evidence: in some [branches], regarding the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: "Two [stanzas] of the <s>saṃstuta</s> practitioners exceed the <s>Virāj</s> meter"; for others: "Three of the <s>saṃstuta</s> exceed the <s>Virāj</s>." Under the view of one ritual, there is contradiction; under different rituals, in one <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> two, in another three; therefore differentiation.
Moreover, in the <s>Sārasvata</s> [rite] it is heard: "Those who have <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes sit down, those who have <s>sānnāyya</s> hold back the calves." The <s>sānnāyya</s>-offerers have the <s>iṣṭi</s> as their first sacrifice; the <s>puroḍāśa</s>-offerers are the reverse. The evidence of both in the <s>Sārasvata</s> is possible under differentiation; under the view of one ritual, all would have the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> first, and then the evidence would be impossible.
Moreover, it is heard: "The invitee is specified — the sacrifice is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, with <s>Rathantara</s> <s>Sāman</s>; a dark horse is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>." [200] For others it is heard: "The invitee is unspecified — the sacrifice is the <s>Uktha</s>, with <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>Sāman</s>; a white horse with a golden blaze is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>." Under the view of one ritual, the mention of <s>Rathantara</s> and the mention of <s>Bṛhat</s> would be purposeless, since being the object of both branches, it would be either <s>Bṛhatsāman</s> or <s>Rathantarasāman</s>; and this, being of such character, is already established from the archetype. But under differentiation of rituals, one is <s>Bṛhatsāman</s> and another <s>Rathantarasāman</s> — this is fitting. Therefore there should be differentiation of rituals across different branches.

children.text: ekaṃ vā saṃyogarūpacodanākhyāviśeṣāt // MS_2,4.9 //
children.translated_text: Or [the ritual is] one, because there is no difference in the connection [of means to ends], form, injunction, and designation. // MS_2,4.9 //

children.text: na caitad asti, yad uktam - śākhāntareṣu karmabheda iti, sarvaśākhāpratyayaṃ sarvabrāhmaṇapratyayaṃ caikaṃ karma, arthasaṃyogasyāviśeṣāt, tad eva prayojanam uddiśya tad eva vidhīyamānaṃ pratyabhijānīmaḥ. rūpam apy asya tad eva dravyadevatam, puruṣaprayatnaś ca tādṛśa eva codyate, nāmadheyaṃ cāviśiṣṭam, tena tad eva karma sarvaśākhādiṣv iti pratyayaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so — what was stated, that there is differentiation of rituals across branches. The ritual is one, the object of all branches and all <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> texts, because there is no difference in the connection of purpose (<s>arthasaṃyoga</s>). We recognize the same [ritual] as being enjoined for the same purpose. Its form too is the same — the material substance and deity — and the human effort enjoined is of the same kind; the name too is undifferentiated. Therefore the conviction is that it is the same ritual in all branches and so forth.

children.text: na nāmnā syād acodanābhidhānatvāt // MS_2,4.10 //
children.translated_text: It should not be [differentiated] by name, because [the name] denotes what is not an injunction. // MS_2,4.10 //

children.text: yad uktam - nāmabheda iti, parihṛtaṃ tad granthanām ata iti. atha yad uktam - karmaṇo 'pi nāmasāmānādhikaraṇyadarśanād iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, granthasaṃyogāt karma kāṭhakādi, na karmasaṃyogād granthaḥ kāṭhakaḥ. kathaṃ gamyate? yat karma kāṭhakādisaṃyuktam, tat kāṭhakādiśabdenocyate. kim ato 'pi? yad granthasaṃyogāt kāṭhakaṃ kālāpakaṃ karmocyate. ekatve 'pi kāṭhakagranthasaṃyogāt kāṭhakam, kālāpakagranthasaṃyogāt tu kālāpakaṃ bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'because of the difference of names' — that has been refuted by [the argument] 'because of the composition of texts.' Now, as for what was said — 'because even of rites, a co-referential use of names is observed' — this is not a fault. The rite [is called] <s>Kāṭhaka</s> and so on because of the connection with the text (<s>grantha</s>), not the text [called] <s>Kāṭhaka</s> because of the connection with the rite. How is this known? That rite which is connected with the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> and other [texts] is referred to by the word '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>' and the like. What follows from this? That the rite is called <s>Kāṭhaka</s> or <s>Kālāpaka</s> because of the connection with the text. Even though [the rite] is one, it will be [called] <s>Kāṭhaka</s> because of the connection with the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> text, and <s>Kālāpaka</s> because of the connection with the <s>Kālāpaka</s> text.
Page break marker: 201

children.text: sarveṣāṃ caikakarmyaṃ syāt // MS_2,4.11 //
children.translated_text: And there would be unity of rite for all [recensions]. // MS 2,4.11 //

children.text: yadi śabdabhedād bhedo bhavet, śabdaikyāt tarhi karmaikyaṃ bhavet. tatra kāṭhakaśabdābhidhānād aikyaṃ bhaved agnihotrasya darśapūrṇamāsayor jyotiṣṭomasya ca, tacchabdatvāt, na caitad evam. tasmād apy abhedaḥ.
children.translated_text: If there were difference because of the difference of words, then because of the unity of words there would be unity of rite. In that case, because of being denoted by the word '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>,' there would be unity of the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, since they bear that same name. But this is not so. Therefore, from this too, [there is] non-difference [of the rite].

children.text: kṛtakaṃ cābhidhānam // MS_2,4.12 //
children.translated_text: And the designation is artificial (<s>kṛtaka</s>). // MS 2,4.12 //

children.text: idānīṃtanaṃ caitad abhidhānaṃ bhavet, asya na pūrvam āsīt, yataḥ prabhṛti kaṭhasya prakṛṣṭaṃ vacanam, tataḥ prabhṛti pravṛttam, pūrvaṃ nāsīd bhedaḥ, idānīṃ bheda iti viruddham.
children.translated_text: Moreover, this designation would be of recent origin — it did not exist previously. From the time when the utterance of <s>Kaṭha</s> became prominent, from that time it came into use. Previously there was no difference; [that there is] now a difference — this is contradictory.

children.text: ekatve 'pi param // MS_2,4.13 //
children.translated_text: Even with unity, the other [view holds]. // MS 2,4.13 //

children.text: ekakarmatve 'pi rūpabhedo bhavati vacanāt, na ca, vācanike rūpabhede, asatyām api bhedabuddhau karmaṇo bhedo 'bhyavasīyeta.
children.translated_text: Even with unity of rite, there is a difference of form because of [Vedic] statement. But with a merely verbal difference of form, without there being a cognition of difference, a difference of rite should not be concluded.

children.text: vidyāyāṃ dharmaśāstram // MS_2,4.14 //
children.translated_text: In [the case of] knowledge, [it is] a <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (rule of conduct). // MS 2,4.14 //

children.text: atha yo dharmaviśeṣa uktaḥ, vidyāgrahaṇārthaḥ saḥ, na karmaṇa upakārakaḥ. kathaṃ gamyate? śrutyādīnām abhāvāt, vidyāsaṃyogāc ca na karmaprayukta iti.
children.translated_text: Now, the particular <s>dharma</s> that was mentioned — that is for the purpose of acquiring knowledge, not beneficial to the rite. How is this known? Because of the absence of <s>śruti</s> and so forth, and because of the connection with knowledge — [hence] it is not prompted by the rite.

children.text: āgneyavat punarvacanam // MS_2,4.15 //
children.translated_text: There is repetition, as in the <s>Āgneya</s> [case]. // MS 2,4.15 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - yathāmāvāsyāyām{*2/391*} āgneyasya punaruktadoṣān madhyamaḥ pakṣo nirastaḥ, evam ayam api tasmād eva doṣāt karmaikatvapakṣo nirasitavya iti, etat parihartavyam. (ity ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram){*2/392*}.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was said — just as in the <s>amāvāsyā</s> (new-moon rite), the middle position was rejected because of the fault of the <s>Āgneya</s> being repeated, so too this position of unity of rite should be rejected because of that same fault — this must be refuted. (This is a prima-facie-concluding <s>sūtra</s>.)
Page break marker: 202

children.text: advirvacanaṃ vā śrutisaṃyogāviśeṣāt // MS_2,4.16 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] not a repetition, because of the non-distinction of the connection with <s>śruti</s>. // MS 2,4.16 //

children.text: naiva khalv etat dvirvacanam, sa evāyam arthaḥ punaḥ śrāvito 'gnihotrādir bahukṛtvo bahubhis tu puruṣaiḥ, na caiko 'rtho bahubhir ucyamānaḥ punarukto bhavati. yadi bhavet, ekasminn eva vede bahubhir ucyamāne bhavet, tasmān na bahukarmasamavāyo 'yam, ekam evedaṃ karmeti.
children.translated_text: This is indeed not a repetition. This very same meaning — <s>Agnihotra</s> and so on — has been taught again, [but] by many persons many times. And a single meaning being stated by many [persons] does not constitute repetition. If it did, it would be [repetition] even when stated by many within a single <s>Veda</s>. Therefore, this is not a convergence of many rites — this is one and the same rite.

children.text: vākyāsamavāyāt // MS_2,4.16a //{*2/394*}
children.translated_text: Because of the non-convergence of sentences. // MS 2,4.16a //

children.text:
NOTES:
*{2/394: Dieses Sūtra wurde von Śabara nicht kommentiert, es findet sich jedoch bei Kumārila. In E2,4,5 ist es aufgenommen worden. Dies bedingt eine von E1,6 abweichende Zählung der folgenden Sūtras}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{2/394: This <s>sūtra</s> was not commented on by <s>Śabara</s>, but is found in <s>Kumārila</s>. In E2,4,5 it has been included. This causes a numbering of subsequent <s>sūtras</s> that differs from E1,6}]

children.text: arthāsannidheś ca // MS_2,4.17 //
children.translated_text: And because of the proximity of meaning. // MS 2,4.17 //

children.text: arthāsannidheś ca śākhāśabda upapanno bhaviṣyati, śākhā iva homāḥ śākhāḥ, tad yathā vṛkṣasya śākhāḥ, evam ihāpi vṛkṣasthānīyasya vedasya śākhāḥ. kiṃ śākhāsārūpyam? yathā nānāvasthānam, na caikaikasyāṃ kṛtsnaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ sannihitam, evam ihāpi, naikaikasyāṃ kṛtsaṃ guṇakāṇḍaṃ sannihitam, ity arthāsannidheḥ śākhāśabdopapattiḥ. tasmād apy ekaṃ karmeti.
children.translated_text: And because of the proximity of meaning, the word '<s>śākhā</s>' (branch) will be justified. Oblations [divided] like branches [of a tree] are '<s>śākhās</s>' — just as there are branches of a tree, so too here there are branches of the <s>Veda</s>, which occupies the place of the tree. What is the resemblance to branches? Just as [branches] have different positions, and in each one not all the flowers and fruits are found together, so too here, in each [<s>śākhā</s>] not all the subsidiary elements (<s>guṇakāṇḍa</s>) are found together — thus the justification of the word '<s>śākhā</s>' [comes] from the proximity of meaning. Therefore, from this too, [the rite] is one.

children.text: na caikaṃ prati śiṣyate // MS_2,4.18 //
children.translated_text: And [the rite] is not taught with reference to a single [recension]. // MS 2,4.18 //

children.text: na ca, yat kāṭhake 'gnihotram, tat kāṭhakam evaikaṃ puruṣaṃ prati vidhīyate. taittirīyasyāpi tadvihitam eva, puruṣaviśeṣavacanābhāvāt, yac cāgnihotrasya kiṃcid aṅgaṃ vidhīyate, sarvāvasthasya tad agnihotrasya, yac ca kāṭhakasyāgnihotraṃ, tac ca taittirīyakasyeti, viśeṣavacanābhāvāt, tasmāt sarvaśākhyābhir ekaṃ samāptaṃ karmocyata iti.
children.translated_text: And the <s>Agnihotra</s> that is in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> is not enjoined for a single person belonging only to the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [school]. The <s>Taittirīya</s>'s [<s>Agnihotra</s>] too is enjoined by that very [injunction], because of the absence of a statement specifying particular persons. And whatever subsidiary element is enjoined for the <s>Agnihotra</s>, that is for the <s>Agnihotra</s> in all its forms. And the <s>Agnihotra</s> of the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> is the same as that of the <s>Taittirīya</s> — because of the absence of a statement of distinction. Therefore, by all <s>śākhās</s> together, one complete rite is stated.
Page break marker: 203

children.text: samāptivac ca saṃprekṣā // MS_2,4.19 //
children.translated_text: And the consideration is like [the case of] completion. // MS 2,4.19 //

children.text: atrāsmākam agniḥ parisamāpyata ity utprekṣitāro bhavanti, anvāroheṣu maitrāyaṇīyānām agniḥ parisamāpyate, asmākaṃ teṣu na parisamāpyata iti, yady anyad eva maitrāyaṇīyānām, anyac ca teṣām, kathaṃ te brūyur eṣv asmākaṃ na parisamāpyata iti, ekatvam upapannam, teṣām api hi te santi.
children.translated_text: Here, those [belonging to certain schools] speculate: 'Our <s>Agni</s> [rite] is completed [here]' — in the <s>anvāroha</s> (supplementary) [texts], the <s>Agni</s> [rite] of the <s>Maitrāyaṇīyas</s> is completed; 'ours is not completed in those [texts]' — if the [rite] of the <s>Maitrāyaṇīyas</s> were one thing and theirs another, how could they say 'ours is not completed in these [texts]'? Unity is established — for those [texts] belong to them too.

children.text: ekatve 'pi parāṇi nindāśaktisamāptivacanāni // MS_2,4.20 //
children.translated_text: Even with unity, the other [statements about] blame, capacity, and completion [are explained]. // MS 2,4.20 //

children.text:
na hi nindā nindyaṃ nindituṃ prayujyate. kiṃ tarhi ninditād itarat praśaṃsitum, tatra na ninditasya pratiṣedho gamyate. kiṃ tarhi ninditāditarat praśaṃsitum, tatra na ninditasya pratiṣedho gamyate. kiṃ tv itarasya vidhiḥ, tatraikasminn agnihotre dvau kālau vihitau vikalpyete, ato na kaścid virodhaḥ.
tathāsamarthānām ekasminn api vede vihitaṃ kṛtsnam{*2/396*} aṅgajātam upasaṃhartum aśaktiḥ, samarthānāṃ tu sarvaśākhābhyo 'py āgamitam adhikaṃ vidhim upasaṃhartum śaktir astīti tenaikakarmatve 'pi na viruddham iti.
tathaikasminn api karmaṇi kiṃcid vastu samāptam iti kṛtvā samāptiśabdaḥ prayujyate, yathā, ādhvaryave samāpte jyotiṣṭomasya, samāpto jyotiṣṭoma iti bhavati.
children.translated_text:
For blame is not employed to blame the blameworthy. Rather, [it is employed] to praise what is other than the blamed. There, no prohibition of the blamed is understood. Rather, [it serves as] an injunction of the other. There, in one <s>Agnihotra</s>, two times are enjoined as alternatives — thus there is no conflict.
Similarly, for those who are incapable, there is inability to assemble the entire set of subsidiary elements enjoined even in a single <s>Veda</s>; but for those who are capable, there is the ability to assemble even the additional injunctions obtained from all <s>śākhās</s> — thus even with unity of rite, there is no contradiction.
Similarly, even in a single rite, the word 'completion' is used with reference to something [partially] completed — just as when the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s [work] is completed in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is said 'the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is completed.'

children.text:
NOTES:
*{2/396: E2,4: vihitaṃ kṛtsnam}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{2/396: E2,4: <s>vihitaṃ kṛtsnam</s>}]

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ nimittena // MS_2,4.21 //
children.translated_text: The expiation is [explained] by the occasion. // MS 2,4.21 //

children.text: yad uktam - uditahomasyāpi prāyaścittāntā{*2/397*} nāvṛddhatā{*2/398*} gamyate, anuditahomasyāpi, tad ekatve virudhyate, [204]{*2/399*} aviruddhaṃ nānātva iti, tat parihartavyam. (ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram){*2/400*}.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — that for the offering [performed] after sunrise too, the [teaching of] expiation does not [indicate] non-increase, and for the offering [performed] before sunrise too [the same applies], and this contradicts unity, [while] non-contradiction [obtains] with plurality — that must be refuted. (This is a prima-facie-concluding <s>sūtra</s>.)
