children.text: prakramād vā niyogena // MS_2,4.22 //
children.translated_text: Or [the expiation is explained] by the undertaking and the obligation. // MS 2,4.22 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naiṣa doṣaḥ, udite hoṣyāmīti prakānte 'nyathā kriyamāṇe bhavati doṣaḥ, tatra prāyaścittasya viṣayo bhaviṣyatīti karmaikatve 'pi na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) dismisses the [previous] position. This is not a fault — when one has undertaken 'I will offer after sunrise' and then acts otherwise, there is a fault; there, the expiation will have its scope. Thus, even with unity of rite, there is no fault.

children.text: samāptiḥ pūrvattvād yathājñāte pratīyeta // MS_2,4.23 //
children.translated_text: Completion is [understood] with reference to what has come before, as it would be recognized as known. // MS 2,4.23 //

children.text: pūrvavati samāptivacanaṃ bhavati, yat prārabdhaṃ tat parisamāpyate, tatrāsmākaṃ parisamāpto 'gnir iti yo 'smābhir jñāyate, prārabdhaś ca parisamāpyata ity abhiprāyaḥ{*2/401*}.
children.translated_text: The statement about completion has reference to what has come before — what has been commenced is completed. There, 'our <s>Agni</s> [rite] is completed' — the intention is: what is known by us and has been commenced is completed.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{2/401: E2,4,5,6: parisamāpyate. prārabdhaś cety abhiprāyaḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{2/401: E2,4,5,6: <s>parisamāpyate. prārabdhaś cety abhiprāyaḥ</s>}]

children.text: liṅgam aviśiṣṭaṃ sarvaśeṣatvān na hi tatra karmacodanā tasmād dvādaśāhasyāhāravyapadeśaḥ syāt // MS_2,4.24 //
children.translated_text: The indicatory mark is non-specific, because of [its] being subsidiary to all; for there is no injunction of the rite there. Therefore, the designation of the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> (twelve-day rite) as a food-provider should apply. // MS 2,4.24 //

children.text: yad uktam - yadi purā didīksāṇā iti, dvādaśāha iṣṭaprathamayajñānām aniṣṭaprathamayajñānāṃ ca darśanaṃ karmabheda upapadyate, na sarvaśākhāpratyayaikakarmaṇīti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, yadi didīkṣāṇā dvādaśāhena, adidīkṣāṇā dvādaśaśāhenety evaṃ tat, na hi sāmavede jyotiṣṭomasya vidhānam. kim ato 'pi? yatra vihitas tatrānūdyate, tena karmabhede 'pi sarvajyotiṣṭomānām eṣa dharmaḥ prāthamyaṃ nāma. ato nānākarmapakṣe 'py avaśyaṃ dvādaśāhasyāhāravyapadeśaḥ kalpanīyas tasmād adoṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — if 'those who are about to be consecrated,' in the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>, the observation of both those whose first sacrifice is established (<s>iṣṭaprathamayajña</s>) and those whose first sacrifice is not established justifies a difference of rites, not a single rite [established] through the cognitions of all <s>śākhās</s> — this is not a fault. Whether 'those about to be consecrated in the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>' or 'those not about to be consecrated in the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>' — this is the case; for the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is not enjoined in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. What follows? Where it is enjoined, there it is restated. Therefore, even with difference of rites, this <s>dharma</s> — namely, priority — belongs to all <s>Jyotiṣṭomas</s>. Hence, even in the position of multiple rites, the designation of the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> as a food-provider must necessarily be postulated. Therefore, there is no fault.
Page break marker: 205

children.text: dravye cācoditatvād vidhīnām avyavasthā syān nirdeśād vyavatiṣṭheta tasmān nityānuvādaḥ syāt // MS_2,4.25 //
children.translated_text: And regarding the substance, because of [its] not being enjoined, there would be indeterminacy of the injunctions; through specification it would be established. Therefore, [it should be understood as] a perpetual restatement. // MS 2,4.25 //

children.text: dravye cāgnāv acoditatvād ekādaśinyāḥ saṃmānaparimāṇaṃ parti naiṣā vyavasthā syāt, naivāgnāv ekādaśinī codyate, kutaḥ pakṣasaṃmānaṃ vedisaṃmānaṃ vā syāt? dvayam apy etat parārthaṃ kīrtyate, paśvekādaśinīvidhānārtham, yadi pakṣasaṃmitā syād ayaṃ doṣaḥ syāt, vedisaṃmāne na doṣo bhavet, ka etat saṅkaṭamadhyavasānam{*2/403*} arhati? ekasmin yūpa ekādaśa paśavo niyoktavā iti, vācastomādiṣu tu yūpaikādaśinyām asya nityānuvādatvād rathākṣamātrāṇy eva yūpāntarālāni bhaviṣyanti, nityānuvādatvāc cāsaty api pakṣasaṃmāne vedisaṃmāne vaikādaśinīvidhānārthaṃ vacanam upapadyata eveti na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: And regarding the substance — the fire — since the <s>ekādaśinī</s> (eleven-[<s>yūpa</s>] row) is not enjoined [with respect to the fire], this determination regarding the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) measurement would not hold. For the <s>ekādaśinī</s> is not enjoined with respect to the fire [itself]. From where would [the measurement] be that of the [sacrificial] wing or that of the altar (<s>vedi</s>)? Both of these are stated for another purpose — for the purpose of enjoining the animal-<s>ekādaśinī</s>. 'If it were measured by the wing, this fault would arise; with the altar measurement, no fault would arise' — who would accept such a difficult determination? Eleven animals are to be tied to one sacrificial post. But in the <s>Vācasstoma</s> and other [rites], since its being a perpetual restatement in the <s>yūpa</s>-<s>ekādaśinī</s> [context], only the intervals between the posts will be of the measure of a chariot-axle. And because of [its] being a perpetual restatement, even without the wing measurement or the altar measurement, the statement is justified for the purpose of enjoining the <s>ekādaśinī</s> — thus there is no fault.

children.text: vihitapratiṣedhāt pakṣe 'tirekaḥ syāt // MS_2,4.26 //
children.translated_text: Because of the enjoined prohibition, there would be excess in one position. // MS 2,4.26 //

children.text: atirātre gṛhṇāti ṣoḍaśinam iti vihitaḥ ṣoḍaśī, nātirātre gṛhṇāti ṣoḍaśinam iti pratiṣiddhaḥ, tena pakṣe dvayoḥ stotrīyayor atirekaḥ, pakṣe tisṝṇām, tasmād adoṣaḥ. kathaṃ punar ayaṃ dvayos tisṝṇāṃ vātirekaḥ? trivṛd bahiṣpavamānam, tat tāvan navakam. pañcadaśāny ājyāni, tāni [206]{*2/404*} tāvac catvāri, tena sā ṣaṣṭiḥ. pañcadaśo mādhyaṃdinaḥ pavamānaḥ, tayā pañcadaśasaṃkhyayā saha, pūrvayā ca navasaṃkhyayā caturaśītiḥ. saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni catvāri, saptadaśa ārbhavaḥ pavamānaḥ, pañcasaptadaśakāni tānīti pañcāśītiḥ. pūrvayā caturśītyā sahaikonasaptatiśatam. ekaviṃśaṃ yajñāyajñiyam, tayaikaviṃśatyā saha tasya navatiśataṃ stotriyā{*2/405*} iti brāhmaṇavādaḥ. agniṣṭomamātram abhipretyocyate, sā virāṭ saṃpūrṇā virāḍ iti daśakākhyāḥ{*2/406*}, traya ekaviṃśakā ukthaparyāyāḥ, sā triṣaṣṭiḥ. ekaviṃśaḥ ṣoḍaśī, tayaikaviṃśatyā saha caturaśītiḥ. pañcadaśakā rātriparyāyās trayaḥ, tatraikaikaparyāyaḥ catuḥstotraḥ, tad aśītiśataṃ saṃpūrṇā virāṭ. trivṛd rathantaraṃ pañcasāma, tan navakam, tataś caturaśīter ekaṃ navakam āgacchati, tathā tisraḥ saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyante, yadā ṣoḍaśī na gṛhyate, tadaikaviṃśatyā vinā dve saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyete, evam ekakarmatve 'pi liṅgam upapadyate.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Atirātra</s>, 'he takes the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>' — the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is enjoined; 'in the <s>Atirātra</s> he does not take the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>' — [the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>] is prohibited. Thus, in one position there is an excess of two <s>stotrīya</s> (stanzas for chanting), in [another] position of three. Therefore, there is no fault. But how is there this excess of two or three? The <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> (outer <s>pavamāna</s> chant) is in <s>trivṛt</s> (nine-versed [<s>stoma</s>]); that makes a group of nine. The <s>ājya</s> [stotras] are in <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-versed); those are four — thus that makes sixty. The midday <s>pavamāna</s> is <s>pañcadaśa</s>; with that fifteen-count and the previous nine-count, [the total is] eighty-four. The <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [stotras] are four in <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-versed); the <s>ārbhava pavamāna</s> is <s>saptadaśa</s> — five groups of seventeen make eighty-five. With the previous eighty-four, [the total is] one hundred and sixty-nine. The <s>yajñāyajñīya</s> is <s>ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-versed); with that twenty-one, its [total of] <s>stotrīya</s> [verses] is one hundred and ninety — thus says the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> passage. This is stated with reference to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> alone. That is the complete <s>virāj</s> — 'the complete <s>virāj</s>' being the designation of groups of ten. Three <s>ekaviṃśa</s> <s>uktha</s>-rounds make sixty-three. The <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is <s>ekaviṃśa</s>; with that twenty-one, [the total is] eighty-four. The night-rounds of <s>pañcadaśa</s> are three; there each round has four <s>stotras</s> — that makes one hundred and eighty, the complete <s>virāj</s>. The <s>rathantara</s> is <s>trivṛt</s>, a five-<s>sāman</s> [<s>stotra</s>]; that makes nine. Then from the eighty-four, one group of nine arrives; thus three [groups] exceed the <s>virāj</s> of those chanted. When the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is not taken, without the twenty-one, two [groups] exceed the <s>virāj</s> of those chanted. Thus, even with unity of rite, the indicatory mark is justified.

children.text: sārasvate vipratiṣedhād yadeti syāt // MS_2,4.27 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sārasvata</s> [rite], because of the conflict, [the resolution] should be by means of 'whichever' (<s>yad</s>). // MS 2,4.27 //

children.text: yad uktam - puroḍāśināṃ sānnāyināṃ ca sārasvate darśanaṃ bhavatīti, jyotiṣṭomapūrvakatvāt sarvakarmaṇām, vipratiṣiddham etad iti, tena yadā sānnāyinaḥ puroḍāśina{*2/407*} iti kalpyate.
children.translated_text: As for what was stated — that there is evidence of both <s>puroḍāśa</s>-offerers and <s>sānnāyya</s>-offerers in the <s>Sārasvata</s> [rite], and that this contradicts the principle that all rituals presuppose the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> as prior — therefore, when <s>sānnāyya</s>-offerers are posited as <s>puroḍāśa</s>-offerers [the difficulty is resolved].

children.text: upahavye 'pratiprasavaḥ // MS_2,4.28 //
children.translated_text: In the case of the invitee (<s>upahavya</s>), there is no counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>). // MS_2,4.28 //

children.text: atham yad uktam - upahavye bṛhadrathantaravidhānaṃ prakṛtiprāptam eva, ekakarmatve pratiprasavatayāpy asaṃbhavād vidhīyamānam anarthakaṃ syād iti, tat parihartavyam. ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was stated — that in the case of the invitee, the prescription of <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> is already established from the archetype, and under the view of one ritual it would be purposeless since being enjoined it could not apply even as a counter-exception — that must be addressed. [This is] a sūtra ending with a statement (<s>ābhāṣānta</s>).

children.text: guṇārthā vā punaḥśrutiḥ // MS_2,4.29 //
children.translated_text: Or, the repeated mention serves the purpose of a subsidiary quality. // MS_2,4.29 //

children.text: yadā rathantarasāmā, tadāśvaḥ śveto dakṣiṇā, yadā bṛhatsāmā tadā rukmalalāṭa iti.
children.translated_text: When it is <s>Rathantara</s> <s>Sāman</s>, then a white horse is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; when it is <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>Sāman</s>, then [a horse] with a golden blaze.

children.text: pratyayaṃ cāpi darśayati // MS_2,4.30 //
children.translated_text: And it also shows the understanding [of unity]. // MS_2,4.30 //

children.text: yadā na sarvaśākhāpratyayam ekaṃ karmeti, katham ekasyāṃ śākhāyāṃ samāmnāyate 'nyasyāṃ guṇo vidhīyate? yathā maitrāyaṇīyānāṃ samidādayaḥ prayājā na samāmnāyante, atha ca guṇāḥ śrūyante, ṛtavo vai prayājāḥ samānīya hotavyā iti{*2/409*}. tathā yeṣāṃ śākhināṃ kuṭarur asīty{*2/410*} aśmādānamantro nāmnātaḥ, teṣām api hi dṛśyate, kukkuṭo 'sīty aśmānam upapādatte, kuṭarur asīti veti. tasmād ekaṃ karmeti pratīmaḥ.
children.translated_text: If it is not the case that one ritual is the object of all branches, how is it that [a ritual] taught in one branch has a subsidiary quality enjoined in another? Just as for the <s>Maitrāyaṇīyas</s>, the preliminary offerings (<s>prayāja</s>) such as the fuel-stick and others are not taught, yet subsidiary qualities are heard: "The seasons are the preliminary offerings; they should be offered together." Likewise, for those branch-followers for whom the stone-picking <s>mantra</s> by name is "You are a hatchet" (<s>kuṭarur asi</s>), for them too it is seen: "He takes up the stone [saying] 'You are a rooster' (<s>kukkuṭo'si</s>)" or "'You are a hatchet.'" Therefore we understand it is one ritual.

children.text: api vā kramasaṃyogād vidhipṛthaktvam ekasyāṃ vyavatiṣṭheta // MS_2,4.31 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of connection with sequence, the separateness of injunctions in one [branch] would be established. // MS_2,4.31 //

children.text: yo hy anyaśākhāvasthitān vidhīn upasaṃharati, sa svaśākhāvihitaṃ kramam uparuṇaddhīti, tena śākhāntareṣu karmabheda iti.
children.translated_text: For he who collects the injunctions established in another branch obstructs the sequence prescribed in his own branch; therefore there is differentiation of rituals across branches.

children.text: virodhinā{*2/411*} tv asaṃyogād aikakarmye tatsaṃyogād vidhīnāṃ sarvakarmapratyayaḥ syāt // MS_2,4.32 //
children.translated_text: But since there is no connection with what is contradictory, and since under the view of one ritual there is connection with that, the injunctions would be understood as pertaining to all rituals. // MS_2,4.32 //

children.text: ucyate - naiṣa śākhāntaravihitānām aikakarmye sati virodhinā{*2/412*} saṃyogaḥ. na hi kramo vākyena virudhyate, durbalo hi kramaḥ, balavad vākyam, vākyena ca śākhāntarīyāṇām upasaṃhāraḥ. tasmāt sarvaśākhāpratyayaṃ sarvabrāhmaṇapratyayaṃ caikaṃ karma codyata iti siddhaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: We reply: when the view of one ritual is adopted for those prescribed in other branches, there is no connection with what is contradictory. For sequence does not contradict a sentence — sequence is weak, the sentence is strong — and the collection of [injunctions from] other branches is [established] by the sentence. Therefore it is established that one ritual, the object of all branches and all <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> texts, is enjoined.

children.text: athātaḥ śeṣalakṣaṇam // MS_3,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Now, therefore, the definition of subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>). // MS_3,1.1 //

children.text: nānākarmalakṣaṇaṃ vṛttam, anantaraṃ śeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vartayiṣyāmaḥ. kaḥ śeṣaḥ? kena hetunā śeṣaḥ? kathaṃ ca viniyujyate? iti, śrutyādīni ca viniyoge kāraṇānīti vakṣyate, teṣāṃ ca balavadabalavattā, etat tātparyeṇānyad apy upoddhātādinā.
children.translated_text: The definition of differentiation of rituals has been completed; next we shall set forth the definition of subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>). What is a subsidiary? By what reason is something called a subsidiary? And how is it assigned? It will be stated that <s>śruti</s> (direct statement) and other [criteria] are the causes in assignment, and [the question of] their relative strength and weakness — this is the purport, along with other [matters] such as the introduction.

children.text: śeṣaḥ parārthatvāt // MS_3,1.2 //
children.translated_text: A subsidiary [is so called] because of serving another's purpose. // MS_3,1.2 //

children.text:
iha sūtre śeṣasya lakṣaṇam, yena ca hetunā śeṣa ity ucyate, tad ubhayam ākhyāyate. yaḥ parasyopakāre vartate, sa śeṣa ity ucyate. tad yathā, ye parārthāḥ, te vaktāro bhavanti śeṣabhūtā vayam iheti. nanu yo 'pi pradhānabhūtaḥ, so 'pi kadācit parārthe vartate, yathopādhyāyaḥ pradhānabhūtaḥ śiṣyāṇāṃ vidyāvinayādhāne vartate. satyaṃ vartate. yas tv atyantaṃ parārthaḥ, taṃ vayaṃ śeṣa iti brūmaḥ. yathā, garbhadāsaḥ karmārtha eva svāmino 'naḍvāṃś ca krīyate, vakṣyatīty eva. nanu garbhadāsasyāpi savāmī saṃvidadhāno guṇabhāvamāyāt. neti brūmaḥ, ātmana evāsau saṃvidadhāno guṇabhāvaṃ gacchati, nāntarīyakatvād garbha[209]{*3/2*}dāsasyopakaroti, anaḍuho vā. yas tv atyantaṃ parārthaḥ, taṃ vayaṃ śeṣa iti brūmaḥ.
atha tatra kiṃ vṛttam? yais tu dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate guṇas tatra pratīyeta{*3/3*} iti{*3/4*}. tatrāpūrvārthatā vyāvartitā, dṛṣṭaprayojanānāmākhyātānām. iha tu sarveṣām eva śeṣāṇāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate.
children.translated_text:
In this sūtra, both the definition of subsidiary and the reason why something is called a subsidiary are declared. That which operates for the benefit of another is called a subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>). For example, those who serve another's purpose are speakers [who say] "we are here as subsidiaries." But one who is principal (<s>pradhāna</s>) also sometimes operates for another's purpose — just as a teacher, though principal, operates in imparting knowledge and discipline to students. True, he does operate [thus]. But we call that which is entirely for another's purpose a subsidiary. For example, a born slave exists solely for the work of the master, and a bull is purchased for that very purpose — as will be stated. But does not even the born slave, when the master makes arrangements for him, attain the status of a subordinate? No, we say — when [the master] makes arrangements for himself, he attains the status of a subordinate, [and] incidentally benefits the born slave [209] or the bull. But that which is entirely for another's purpose — that we call a subsidiary.
Now, what was stated there? "When a substance is desired to be produced, a quality is understood in relation to it." There, the purposelessness [objection] was set aside for verbal forms having visible purpose. But here the definition of all subsidiaries is stated.

children.text: dravyaguṇasaṃskāreṣu vādariḥ{*3/5*} // MS_3,1.3 //
children.translated_text: [The term subsidiary applies] to substances, qualities, and consecrations — [so holds] <s>Bādari</s>. // MS_3,1.3 //

children.text:
vādarir{*3/6*} ācāryo 'tra dravyaguṇasaṃskāreṣv eva śeṣaśabda iti mane{*3/7*}, na yāgaphalapuruṣeṣu. dravyaṃ kriyārtham, yadi prayojanavatī kriyā, vyaktaṃ sā dravyeṇa nirvartayitavyā{*3/8*}, tasyā nirvṛttir dravyādṛte na bhavatīti tannirvṛttaye dravyam eṣitavyaṃ bhavati. tasmāt kriyārthaṃ dravyam. guṇaḥ śaknoti viśiṣṭaṃ dravyaṃ coditaṃ lakṣayitum, lakṣitena ca tena prayojanam, viśiṣṭasya kriyāsādhanatvāt. tasmāt so 'pi dravyadvāreṇa kriyāyā upakarotīti{*3/9*} kriyārtha eva. saṃskāro nāma sa bhavati, yasmin jāte padārtho bhavati yogyaḥ kasyacid arthasya, tenāpi kriyāyāṃ kartavyāyāṃ prayojanam iti so 'pi parārthaḥ. tasmād dravyaguṇasaṃskārāḥ parārthatvāc cheṣabhūtāḥ.
na tu yāgaphalapuruṣāḥ. yāgas tāvat kartavyaḥ puruṣasya. na hi, tasmin nirvartite kiṃcid aparam asti kartavyam. sa hi puruṣārthaḥ, yad anyad dravyādi, tat tadarthaṃ tasya śeṣabhūtam. sa tu na kiṃcid abhinirvartayituṃ kriyate. phalam api na tena kriyate, tasmiṃs tu kṛte svayam eva tad bhavati. tasmin kṛte phalam asya bhavatīty etāvad gamyate. nāsti śabdo yāgena kriyate [210]{*3/10*} phalam iti. tasmād yāgo na śeṣabhūtaḥ kasyacid arthasya. phalam api na puruṣaṃ pratyupadiśyate. yaḥ svargaṃ kāmayate, sa yāgaṃ kuryād ity etāvac chabdenodiśyate, nātmanaḥ parasya veti. svargaṃ pratīcchāmātreṇa svargakāma iti bhavati. tasmāt puruṣaṃ prati guṇabhāvena na śrūyate svargaḥ. tasmāt so 'pi na śeṣabhūtaḥ. na cet phalayāgau guṇabhāvena codyete, kasya puruṣaḥ pradhānabhūto bhavati. pratyakṣaś cāsya dravyatvāt karma prati guṇabhāvaḥ. tasmād dravyaguṇasaṃskāreṣv eva śeṣabhāvaṃ vādarir{*3/11*} mena iti.
children.translated_text:
The teacher <s>Bādari</s> holds that the term subsidiary applies only to substances (<s>dravya</s>), qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), and consecrations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), not to sacrifice, result, or person. A substance serves the act — if the act has a purpose, clearly it must be accomplished by the substance; its accomplishment does not occur without the substance, therefore the substance must be sought for its accomplishment. Hence the substance serves the act. A quality can identify a particular substance that is enjoined; with that identified [substance], there is purpose, since the particular [substance] is the means of the act. Therefore it too serves the act through the medium of the substance, and hence serves the act alone. A consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is that upon whose occurrence a thing becomes fit for some purpose; through it too there is purpose when the act is to be performed, hence it too serves another. Therefore substances, qualities, and consecrations are subsidiaries because they serve another's purpose.
But sacrifice, result, and person are not [subsidiaries]. The sacrifice, for its part, is to be performed by the person. For when it has been accomplished, there is nothing else to be done. It serves the person's purpose; whatever else — substance etc. — serves its purpose and is its subsidiary. But it itself is not performed to accomplish anything [beyond itself]. The result too is not produced by it; rather, when it [the sacrifice] is performed, the result arises of its own accord. When it is performed, the result comes to it — only this much is understood. There is no word [saying] "the result is produced by the sacrifice." [210] Therefore the sacrifice is not a subsidiary of any purpose. The result too is not taught with reference to the person [as its subsidiary]. "He who desires heaven should perform the sacrifice" — only this much is indicated by the word, not whether [the result is] for oneself or for another. One becomes a "desirer of heaven" merely by wishing for heaven. Therefore heaven is not heard as being in a subordinate relation to the person. Hence it too is not a subsidiary. And if result and sacrifice are not enjoined in a subordinate relation, to what is the person principal? And it is evident, since it [the person] is a substance, that it is in a subordinate relation to the ritual. Therefore <s>Bādari</s> held that subsidiary-status belongs only to substances, qualities, and consecrations.

children.text: karmāṇy api jaiminiḥ, phalārthatvāt // MS_3,1.4 //
children.translated_text: Rituals too [are subsidiaries] — [so holds] <s>Jaimini</s> — because they serve the result. // MS_3,1.4 //

children.text: jaiminis tu khalv ācāryaḥ karmāṇy api śeṣabhūtāni manyate sma, na vādarir{*3/12*} ivāvadhāraṇām anumene. sa hi dadarśa, na yāgaḥ kartavyatayā codyate, phalakāmasya tu tatsādhanopāyatveneti. evaṃ śruto 'rthaḥ parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati. arthavāṃś copadeśaḥ. enam evārthaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'dhyāye sūtrair eva sādhayiṣyati. iha tu tatsiddhenaiva phalārthatvena śeṣabhāvaṃ yāgasyāpādayati sma. tasmād anavadhāraṇā dravyaguṇasaṃkārāḥ śeṣabhūtāḥ, yāgo 'pi śeṣabhūtaḥ phalaṃ pratīti.
children.translated_text: The teacher <s>Jaimini</s>, however, held that rituals too are subsidiaries; he did not accept the restriction like <s>Bādari</s>. For he saw that the sacrifice is not enjoined as something to be performed [for its own sake], but as a means of accomplishment for one who desires the result. When the meaning is thus understood, it will be properly grasped, and the instruction will be meaningful. He will establish this very meaning with sūtras in the sixth chapter. But here he establishes the subsidiary status of sacrifice through its already-established character of serving the result. Therefore, without restriction — substances, qualities, and consecrations are subsidiaries; sacrifice too is a subsidiary in relation to the result.

children.text: phalaṃ ca puruṣārthatvāt // MS_3,1.5 //
children.translated_text: And the result [is a subsidiary] because it serves the person's purpose. // MS_3,1.5 //

children.text: phalam api puruṣaṃ pratyupadiśyate. yaḥ svargo me bhaved ity evaṃ kāmayate, tasya yāgaḥ. na yaḥ svargaḥ, sa ātmānaṃ labheteti. kutaḥ. ātmanepadaprayogāt, kartrabhiprāya etad bhavati. kriyāphalam anubhavet kathaṃ puruṣa iti yāgaḥ prayujyate. tasmāt phalaṃ puruṣārthaṃ yāgāc chrūyate, nātma-nirvṛttyartham. tasmāc cheṣabhūtam iti.
children.translated_text: The result too is taught with reference to the person. He who desires thus — "may heaven be mine" — for him is the sacrifice. It is not that heaven obtains itself. Why? Because of the use of the middle voice (<s>ātmanepada</s>), this has the agent's intention. "How should the person experience the result of the act?" — thus the sacrifice is employed. Therefore the result is heard as serving the person's purpose from the sacrifice, not for its own accomplishment. Therefore it is a subsidiary.

children.text: puruṣaś ca karmārthatvāt // MS_3,1.6 //
children.translated_text: And the person [is a subsidiary] because of serving the ritual. // MS_3,1.6 //

children.text:
puruṣo 'py audumbarīsaṃmānādiṣu guṇabhūtaḥ śrūyate. tasmād anavadhāraṇaiṣā, dravyaguṇasaṃs-kāreṣu śeṣatvaṃ vādarir{*3/14*} mena iti.
athedānīm atra bhagavān vṛttikāraḥ pariniścikāya - dravyaguṇasaṃskāreṣv eva niyato yajiṃ prati śeṣabhāvaḥ, āpekṣika itareṣām. yāgasya dravyaṃ prati pradhānabhāvaḥ, phalam prati guṇabhāvaḥ, phalasya yāgaṃ prati prādhānyam, puruṣaṃ prati guṇatā, puruṣasya phalaṃ prati pradhānatā, audumbarīsaṃmānādi prati guṇatvam. tasmāt saṃmatāvadhāraṇā, dravyaguṇasaṃskārā yāgaṃ prati niyogato guṇabhūtaiveti.
children.translated_text:
The person too is heard as subordinate in contexts such as the <s>Audumbarī</s> [post] consecration and the like. Therefore there is no restriction [as Bādari held]: <s>Bādari</s> held subsidiary-status belongs only to substances, qualities, and consecrations.
Now here the revered commentator (<s>Vṛttikāra</s>) determined: subsidiary-status in relation to the sacrifice is restricted to substances, qualities, and consecrations alone; for the others it is relative. The sacrifice is principal in relation to the substance, but subordinate in relation to the result. The result is principal in relation to the sacrifice, but subordinate in relation to the person. The person is principal in relation to the result, but subordinate in relation to the <s>Audumbarī</s> consecration and the like. Therefore, there is an agreed restriction: substances, qualities, and consecrations are necessarily subordinate in relation to the sacrifice.

children.text: teṣām arthena saṃbandhaḥ // MS_3,1.7 //
children.translated_text: Their connection is through purpose. // MS_3,1.7 //

children.text:
sto darśapūrṇamāsau, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeteti. tatra śrūyante dharmāḥ, nir-vapaṇam, prokṣaṇam, avahananam ityevamādaya auṣadhadharmāḥ. tathā, utpavanavilāpanayahaṇā-sādanādaya{*3/15*} ājyadharmāḥ. tathā, śākhāharaṇam, gavāṃ prasthāpanam, gavāṃ prastāvanam{*3/16*} ityevamādayo 'pi sāntāyyasya{*3/17*}. teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sarve, auṣadhe ājye sānnāyye ca kartavyāḥ, uta ye yatra kriyamāṇā arthavantaḥ, te tatra kartavyā iti.
nanu saṃyuktā eva{*3/18*} śrūyante, yathā, vrīhīn avahanti, taṇḍulān pinaṣṭīti. bāḍhaṃ saṃyuktāḥ, avaghātādayas tu padārthā vidhīyante śrutyā, vākyenaiṣāṃ vrīhyādisaṃyogaḥ. ato 'sti saṃśayaḥ. [212]{*3/19*} kiṃ tāvat prāptam? teṣām arthena saṃbandhaḥ. arthena prayojanena, ye yatra kriyamāṇāḥ prayojanavantaḥ, te tatra kartavyāḥ. prathanādaya ājyasāntāyyayor{*3/20*} anupakārakā iti na tatra karaṇīyāḥ. evam utpavanādaya auṣadhasānnāyyayoḥ, śākhāharaṇādaya ājyauṣadhayoḥ. nanu śrūyante sarve sarvatra. etad eva na jānīmaḥ, śrūyante na śrūyanta iti, tad vicārāyitavyam. yady api śrūyaran{*3/21*}, tathāpy anupakārakatvān naiva kartavyā bhaveyuḥ.
children.translated_text:
There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites — "He who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>." There, ritual properties are heard: threshing, sprinkling, bringing [the grain to the fire], and similar properties of the herbs; likewise, filtering, melting, taking, placing, and similar properties of the clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>); likewise, fetching the branch, setting the cows in motion, leading the cows, and similar [properties] of the <s>sānnāyya</s>. Regarding these, a doubt [arises]: should all be performed in [connection with] the herbs, the <s>ājya</s>, and the <s>sānnāyya</s>? Or should those which, when performed in a given context, have purpose be performed there?
Now, they are heard in connection — for example, "he threshes the rice grains, he grinds the husked grains." Granted, they are connected. But the operations such as threshing and others are enjoined by direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), [while] their connection with rice and other [substances] is through the sentence (<s>vākya</s>). Hence there is doubt. [212] What then is the prima facie view? Their connection is through purpose (<s>artha</s>) — through utility: those which, when performed in a given context, have utility should be performed there. Pounding and similar [operations] are unhelpful for <s>ājya</s> and <s>sānnāyya</s>, so they should not be performed there. Likewise, filtering and similar [operations are unhelpful] for herbs and <s>sānnāyya</s>; branch-fetching and similar [operations are unhelpful] for <s>ājya</s> and herbs. But are not all heard everywhere? This very thing we do not know — whether they are heard or not — that is to be investigated. Even if they were heard [everywhere], still, being unhelpful, they should not be performed.

children.text: vihitas tu sarvadharmaḥ syāt saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca // MS_3,1.8 //
children.translated_text: But what has been enjoined would have all properties, because of non-differentiation of connection and non-differentiation of context. // MS 3,1.8 //

children.text: ucyate - yo 'rthāt prāptaḥ syāt, sa yatra prayojanaṃ tatraiva kriyeta. śabdena tu sarve 'mī padārthā vihitāḥ, tena na, yatra kevalaṃ prayojanaṃ pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate, tatraiva kartavyāh. kva tarhi? yatra yatra vihitāḥ, te cāmī sarvatra vihitāḥ gamyante. kutaḥ? saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca. sarveṣāṃ tāvad ājyauṣadhasānnāyyānām apūrveṇa sādhyasādhanasaṃyogo 'viśiṣṭaḥ, yatra kriyamāṇā apūrvasya kṛtā bhavatīti vijñāyate. tathā prakaraṇam aviśiṣṭam, yasmin vihitāḥ sarveṣāṃ vihitā bhavantīti gamyate. ataḥ sarve sarvatra kartavyāḥ, yat tv amī na sarvatropakurvantīti, vidhānasāmarthyāt sarvatropakārakā iti gamyate. sa cāyam adṛṣṭa upakāro bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: It is said: what is obtained by implication should be employed only where it serves a purpose. But all these ritual elements have been enjoined by [Vedic] words; therefore, they should not be performed only where a visible purpose is perceived. Where then? Wherever they are enjoined — and they are understood as enjoined everywhere. Why? Because of non-differentiation of connection and non-differentiation of context. For all of them — ghee, grain-medicine (<s>oṣadhi</s>), and <s>sānnāyya</s> (mixed milk-offering) — the connection of means and end through the unprecedented [result] (<s>apūrva</s>) is undifferentiated: it is known that when performed, they accomplish the unprecedented [result]. Similarly, the context is undifferentiated: [for] those who are enjoined in that [context] are understood as enjoined for all [rites]. Therefore, all should be performed everywhere. As for [the objection] that they do not assist everywhere — by the force of the injunction, they are understood as assisting everywhere. And this assistance will be of an unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) nature.

children.text: arthalopād akarma syāt // MS_3,1.9 //
children.translated_text: Because of loss of purpose, there would be no [ritual] action. // MS 3,1.9 //

children.text: naitat, sarve sarvatra karaṇīyā iti, ye yatra nopakurvanti, na te tatra kriyām arhantīty uktam eva. nanu vidhānasāmarthyāt sarve sarvatropkariṣyanti. neti brūmaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that all should be performed everywhere. It has already been stated that those which do not assist in a particular [context] should not be performed there. [Objection:] But by the force of the injunction, all will assist everywhere. [Reply:] No, we say.

children.text: phalaṃ tu saha ceṣṭayā śabdārtho 'bhāvād viprayoge syāt // MS_3,1.10 //
children.translated_text: But the fruit, together with the action, would exist in the absence of the word-meaning [connection], in separation. // MS 3,1.10 //

children.text: nāsti vidhānam, yena sarve sarvatropakurvanti. na ca pratyakṣādibhir upakāram avagacchāmaḥ. arthāpattir api niyogatas tatraiva bhavet, yatraiva śabena codanā bhavati, nānyathā. yadi ca prathanādīnām ājyasānnāyyayor anupakurvatām api tatprakaraṇe samāmnāyo 'nupapanno bhavet, tato 'rthād adṛṣṭa upakāraḥ kalpyeta, te tv avaśyaṃ samāmnānīyā auṣadhārtham. phalaṃ hi saha ceṣṭayāvahananādikayāvagamyate tuṣavimocanādi, prayojanaṃ ca tena, na tasmād ṛte puroḍāśaḥ sidhyati, sati cāsminn arthavān prakaraṇe samāmnāyaḥ. arthavati ca tasmin nādṛṣṭakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇam astīty ato na śakyaṃ kalpayitum. yadi ca tatra taṇḍulādiniṣpādanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nābhaviṣyat, tato viprayoge taṇḍulādīnām abhāvād upakārasya śabdārthamātraṃ dṛṣṭopakārānapekṣaṃ kartavyam ity ājyasānnāyyayor api kriyamāṇānām adṛṣṭam abhaviṣyat. tasmān na prathanādayaḥ sarvatra. evam utpavanādayaḥ śākhāharaṇādayaś ca. tasmān na, sarve sarvtra kartavyāḥ, prathanādayo nājyasānnāyayyoḥ, auṣadhe eva te, utpavanādaya ājyasya, nauṣadhasānnāyyayoḥ, śākhāharaṇādayaś ca sānnāyyasya, nājyauṣadhayor iti siddham.
children.translated_text: There is no injunction by which all [subsidiary elements] assist everywhere. Nor do we perceive the assistance through perception and other [means of knowledge]. Postulation (<s>arthāpatti</s>) too would necessarily apply only where there is an injunction by [Vedic] words, not otherwise. If the teaching of the pounding (<s>prathana</s>) and other [procedures] in the context of ghee and <s>sānnāyya</s> were untenable even without [them] assisting there, then an unseen assistance would have to be postulated. But those [procedures] must necessarily be taught for the sake of the grain-medicine (<s>oṣadhi</s>). For the fruit is perceived together with the action of pounding and the like — [namely,] the removal of husks and the like — and the purpose is from that: without it, the sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) cannot be produced. And when this [visible purpose] exists, the teaching in the context is meaningful. And when the [teaching] is meaningful [as is], there is no basis for postulating an unseen [purpose] — hence [such postulation] cannot be made. If the visible [purpose of] producing rice grains and the like had not existed there, then in separation, in the absence of rice grains and the like, [the teaching] for the sake of mere word-meaning — without regard to visible assistance — would have had to be performed [for ghee and <s>sānnāyya</s> as well], and an unseen [result] would have followed even when performed for ghee and <s>sānnāyya</s>. Therefore, pounding and the like [are] not [performed] everywhere. Similarly, winnowing (<s>utpavana</s>) and the like, and the fetching of branches (<s>śākhāharaṇa</s>) and the like. Therefore, it is not the case that all [should be performed] everywhere: pounding and the like [apply] not to ghee and <s>sānnāyya</s>, but to the grain-medicine alone; winnowing and the like [apply] to ghee, not to the grain-medicine and <s>sānnāyya</s>; and the fetching of branches and the like [apply] to the <s>sānnāyya</s>, not to ghee and the grain-medicine — this is established.

children.text: dravyaṃ cotpattisaṃyogāt tadartham{*3/23*} eva codyeta // MS_3,1.11 //
children.translated_text: And the substance, because of the connection with [its] origination, would be enjoined for that purpose alone. // MS 3,1.11 //

children.text:
sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra samāmananti - sphyaś ca kapālāni ca [214]{*3/24*} agnihotrahavaṇī ca śūrpaṃ ca kṛṣṇājinaṃ ca śamyā colūkhalaṃ ca musalaṃ ca dṛṣṭac copalā caitāni vai daśa yajñāyudhānīti{*3/25*}. tatra saṃdihyate - kiṃ yo ya iha śakyata ebhiḥ kartum, tasmai tasmai padārthāyaitāni samāmnātāni, uta yad yena saṃyuktam, tasmā eveti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? yad yena śakyam iti. kutaḥ? evaṃ vidhayo bhaviṣyanti tathārthanvataḥ{*3/26*}, itarathā te 'nuvādā niṣprayojanāḥ, prakaraṇāviśeṣaś ca sarvapadārthān prati, yajñāyudhānīti ca yajñasaṃyogo 'viśiṣṭaḥ. tasmāt sarve sarvatrety evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - dravyaṃ cotpattisaṃyogāt tadartham eva codyeta, yo yena padārthena sahotpattivākyena saṃyuktaḥ sa padārthaḥ tenaiva kartavyaḥ, yathā sphyenoddhantīty uddhanārthatā sphyasya vākyena, tad uddhaṇanaṃ na sphyād anyena kartavyam. yadā caivam, tadā prāpta eva sphyaḥ, tasyāyam anuvādo bhavitum arhati, etāni vai daśayajñāyudhānīti. evam ekaisyānuvādaḥ, tena tena vacanena prāptasya. yathā - kapāleṣu śrapayati, agnihotrahavaṇyā havīṃṣi nirvapati, śūrpeṇa vivinakti, kṛṣṇājinam adhastād ulūkhalasyāvastṛṇāti, śamyāyāṃ{*3/27*} dṛṣady{*3/28*} upadadhāti, ulūkhala-musalābhyām avahanti, dṛṣad upalābhyāṃ pinaṣṭīti. prakaraṇāt sarvāṇi sarvatra prāpnuyuḥ, vacanāt tu yathāvacanam, yajñāyudhaśabdo 'pi sāmānyena prayojanaṃ vidadhat tad vādhyetaiva{*3/29*}, parokṣaṃ hi sāmānyavacanena viśeṣavidhānaṃ bhavati, pratyakṣaṃ tu viśeṣavacanena viśeṣavidhānam. tasmād yad yenotpattyā saṃyuktam, tat tatraiva viniyujyata iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
Here are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites. There they teach: 'The wooden sword (<s>sphya</s>), the potsherds (<s>kapāla</s>), the <s>Agnihotra</s>-ladle (<s>agnihotrahavaṇī</s>), the winnowing basket (<s>śūrpa</s>), the black antelope skin (<s>kṛṣṇājina</s>), the wooden pin (<s>śamyā</s>), the mortar (<s>ulūkhala</s>), the pestle (<s>musala</s>), the grinding stone (<s>dṛṣad</s>), and the upper grinding stone (<s>upalā</s>) — these are the ten implements of sacrifice (<s>yajñāyudha</s>).' There, the doubt arises: are these taught for whatever ritual element can be [accomplished] with them, or only for that with which each is [specifically] connected? What is the prima facie view? For whatever is possible [with each]. Why? Thus the injunctions will be meaningful and purposeful; otherwise, they would be purposeless re-statements. And the context is undifferentiated with respect to all ritual elements, and the connection with the sacrifice through [the word] 'implements of sacrifice' (<s>yajñāyudha</s>) is undifferentiated. Therefore, all [are used] everywhere — this is the prima facie conclusion.
Having arrived at this, we say: the substance, because of the connection with [its] origination, would be enjoined for that purpose alone. The ritual element that is connected with another element through a sentence [describing their] co-origination — that element should be performed by that [instrument] alone. For example, 'he strikes up [the ground] with the wooden sword' — the purpose of the wooden sword for digging is [established] by the sentence; that digging should not be done by anything other than the wooden sword. And when this is so, the wooden sword is already obtained [for its purpose]; this statement — 'these are the ten implements of sacrifice' — can only be a re-statement of it. Thus, each one is a re-statement of what has been obtained through the respective sentence: 'he bakes in the potsherds,' 'he offers the oblations with the <s>Agnihotra</s>-ladle,' 'he winnows with the winnowing basket,' 'he spreads the black antelope skin beneath the mortar,' 'he places [the grain] on the wooden pin, on the grinding stone,' 'he pounds with the mortar and pestle,' 'he grinds with the grinding stone and the upper stone.' From the context, all would apply everywhere; but from the [specific] sentence, each [applies] as stated. The word 'implements of sacrifice,' even though it generally assigns a purpose, would be overridden by that [specific sentence]; for an injunction of a specific [application] through a general expression is indirect, while an injunction of a specific [application] through a specific expression is direct. Therefore, whatever is connected with whatever through [its] origination — that is to be employed there alone. This is established.

children.text: arthaikatve dravyaguṇayor aikakarmyān niyamaḥ syāt // MS_3,1.12 //
children.translated_text: When there is identity of purpose, there would be a restriction [of substance and quality to a single ritual action] because of unity of ritual action. // MS 3,1.12 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome krayaṃ prakṛtya śrūyate - aruṇayā piṅgākṣyaikahāyanyā{*3/31*} somaṃ krīṇātīti{*3/32*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim aruṇimā kṛtsnaprakaraṇe niviśete, uta kraya evaikahāyanyām iti. kathaṃ punaḥ aruṇayā krīṇātīty evaṃ vispaṣṭe krayasaṃbandhe gamyamāne saṃśaya iti. ucyate - iha hi guṇam aruṇimānam amūrtaṃ santaṃ kriyāyāḥ karaṇam iti śabda upadiśati, yat karaṇābhidhāyinyā tṛtīyāvibhaktyā saṃyujya nirdiśati - aruṇayeti, na cāmūrto 'rthaḥ kriyāyāḥ sādhanaṃ bhavitum arhati, ato 'saṃ-bandhaṃ krīṇātināruṇaguṇasyāvagacchāmaḥ. na cāśaṅkanīyam arthaṃ pramāṇabhūtaḥ śabdo 'bhidhāsyatīty evaṃ prakalpanā kadācid upapadyetāpi. kenacit prakāreṇa saṃbandha iti vacanaprāmāṇyaprakārānveṣaṇe buddhir bhavati, tad yadi param, vicārayantaḥ kriyāsaṃbandhasāmarthyam avagamiṣyāmaḥ, ekavākyatayā kraya evāruṇimānaṃ niveśayiṣyāmaḥ. atha tv apramādyadbhir anviṣyamāṇo na kathaṃcana saṃbandha upapatsyate, tato vākyabhedam abhyupagamya prakaraṇadharmam enam adhyavasāsyāmaḥ{*3/33*}. tasmād avaśyaṃ vicāraṇīyam etad iti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? kṛtsne prakaraṇe niveśaḥ. kasmāt? saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt, prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca. nanu prakaraṇād vākyaṃ balīyo bhavatīty ekavākyatvād aruṇimā krayeṇa saṃbhantsyata iti. naitad evam avagamyate, na hi vacanaśatenāpy anāra[213]{*3/34*}bhyo 'rthaḥ śakyo vidhātum, yo hi brūyāt - udakena dagdhavyam agninā kledayitavyam iti, kiṃ sa vacanaprayojanasāmañjasyam aśnuvīta? na cāmūrto 'rthaḥ kriyāyāḥ sādhanam upapadyate. tasmād aruṇayā krīṇātīti saṃbandhābhāvād ekavākyatā na bhavatīti.
nanu naivāyaṃ guṇavacanaḥ, kiṃ tarhi dravyavacanaḥ. kutaḥ? strīliṅgasaṃbandhāt. dravyaviśeṣā hy ete strī pumān napuṃsakam iti, strīyāṃ yat prātipadikaṃ vartate, tasmāt strīpratyayo bhavatīti, strīpratyayaṃ cāruṇayety upalabhāmahe. tasmād dravyavacanaḥ, aruṇaśabda{*3/35*} iti. tad etad apeśa-lam, tad eva hi dravyam aruṇimnā parichidyamānam aruṇaśabdābhidhānīyatāṃ{*3/36*} labhate, tad evānyaguṇakaṃ nāruṇaśabdaḥ{*3/37*} śaknoty abhivaditum, aruṇimānam eṣa śabdo na vyabhicarati, vy-abhicarati punar dravyam, avyabhicāri ca kāraṇaṃ kāraṇavatām iṣṭam. ato 'sya guṇaḥ svārtha iti gamyate, tad asya pratyakṣato guṇavacanatā gamyate, strīpratyayadarśanāt tu nūnam aruṇāprātipadikaṃ dravyavacanam ity anumānam. pratyakṣaṃ cānumānād balīyaḥ, tasmād guṇavacanaḥ. kathaṃ tarhi strīpratyayasaṃbandhaḥ? bhavati hi guṇavacanasyāpi strīliṅgatā, yathā cāruṇā{*3/38*} buddhiḥ, evam aruṇeti. guṇavacanaś cet krīṇātinā na saṃbadhyate. tasmād vākyabhedaṃ kṛtvā prakaraṇe sarvasminn eva saṃniveśa iti.
atha yadi krīṇātinā na saṃbadhyate, tasmin eva vākye ekahāyanīśabdena saṃbhantsyate, na bhaviṣyati vākyabheda iti. tan na, kevalaṃ hi guṇam aruṇaśābdo{*3/39*} 'bhidadhāti, na dravyaguṇau. kevalaṃ ca dravyam ekahāyanīśabdaḥ, na guṇasahitam iti tayoḥ saṃbandhasya vācikāṃ ṣaṣṭhīm antareṇa kathaṃ saṃbandho gamyate? āha - antareṇāpi ṣaṣṭhīm, ekavibhaktinirdeśāt sāmānādhikaraṇyam [217]{*3/40*} avagamiṣyāmaḥ, yathā nīlam utpalam iti. tad anupapannam, rūpād aruṇaśabdasya{*3/41*} guṇavacanatā, kalpanīyaṃ tv ekavibhaktisaṃyogād ekahāyanīśabdasaṃnidhānāc ca tad ekavākyatām abhyupagamyaikahāyanīśabdasāmānādhikaraṇyam, na ca liṅgād vākyaṃ balīyaḥ. tasmād asad etat.
tatrocyate - yadā kevalaguṇavacanatāyāṃ śabdaḥ pravartamāno nānyena saṃbandhaṃ labhate, tadānupadeśakatvād ānarthakyaṃ mā bhūd iti dravyaparatām āpadyate, tasyām avasthāyām ekavibhaktiyuktenaikahāyanīśabdena saṃnihitenaikavākyatām āpadyamānaḥ samānādhikaraṇo bhavati, tathā ca kṛtvā, nīlam utpalam ity upapadyate. sa cāyam aruṇāśabdas tasyām avasthāyāṃ vartate, na hy asya svārtham abhidadhata ito vicchinnasya prakaraṇe 'py arthavattā. kutaḥ? yenaiva hetunā saṃbadhyate{*3/42*} krīṇātinā na, nāmūrto{*3/43*} 'rthaḥ kriyāyāḥ sādhanaṃ bhavatīti. na ca kriyāsādhanair dravyaiḥ, na hi kevalaguṇavacanaḥ śaknoti dravyam abhidhātum iti sa eva hetuḥ prakaraṇasaṃbandhābhāve 'pi, tatrāpi saṃbadhyamānaḥ kriyābhir vā saṃbadhyeta, tatsādhanair vā dravyaiḥ, tac cobhayam apy anupapannam. ato 'narthakatvaparijihīrṣayā saṃnihitenaikahāyanīśabdenāruṇāśabdaḥ saṃbadhyate. nāsti vākyabhedaḥ.
naitad evam, na hy ayam aruṇāśabda ekahāyanīviśeṣaṇaṃ bhavitum arhati. kiṃ kāraṇam? karaṇavibhaktyā tṛtīyayā samuccarito 'yam, tenaitena tṛtīyāśrutisāmarthyāt kriyāviśeṣaṇena bhavitavyam, kārakāṇāṃ hi kriyayā saṃbandho na dravyeṇeti. sa eṣa śrutisāmarthyāt kriyāviśeṣaṇam, ekavākyatvād{*3/44*} ekahāyanīviśeṣaṇam. śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī, tasmān nāsyaikahāyanīsaṃbandha iti.

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, with reference to the purchase [of <s>Soma</s>], it is heard: 'With a reddish, tawny-eyed, one-year-old [cow] he purchases <s>Soma</s>.' There a doubt arises: does the quality of redness apply to the entire context [of the ritual], or only to the purchase, [specifically] in the one-year-old [cow]? But how, when the connection with the purchase is so clearly understood in 'with a reddish [cow] he purchases,' can there be doubt? It is said: Here, the word teaches that the quality of redness — which is incorporeal — is the instrument of the action, since it indicates [it] by joining [the word] with the instrumental case-ending, which denotes the instrument — 'with a reddish [cow].' But an incorporeal thing cannot be the instrument of an action. Therefore, we understand that the quality of redness has no connection with 'he purchases.' And the supposition 'an authoritative word cannot denote an impossible meaning' might sometimes be justified. [But] in seeking the authoritative mode of the statement [that says] 'there is a connection in some manner,' the mind becomes engaged. Therefore, if [we can find] a higher [interpretation], examining [the matter] we will understand the capacity for connection with the action, and by sentence-unity we will assign the redness to the purchase alone. But if, when diligently sought, no connection whatsoever can be established, then accepting sentence-division, we will determine this as a property of the [entire] context. Therefore, this must certainly be examined.
What is the prima facie view? Assignment to the entire context. Why? Because there is no distinction arising from syntactic connection, and because of the non-distinction of the context. [Objection:] But a sentence is stronger than context — so by sentence-unity, the redness would be connected with the purchase. [Reply:] This is not understood thus. For even by a hundred statements, an unobtainable meaning cannot be enjoined. One who would say 'one should burn with water' or 'one should moisten with fire' — would he achieve consistency of purpose in the statement? And an incorporeal thing cannot be the instrument of an action. Therefore, since in 'with a reddish [cow] he purchases' there is no connection, there is no sentence-unity.
[Objection:] But this [word 'aruṇā'] is not a quality-word; rather, it is a substance-word. Why? Because of the connection with the feminine gender. For these — feminine, masculine, neuter — are substance-distinctions. The feminine suffix attaches to whatever stem applies to a female [referent]. And we observe the feminine suffix in 'aruṇayā.' Therefore, the word 'aruṇa' is a substance-word. [Reply:] This is unsound. For that very substance, being delimited by redness, obtains the designability by the word 'aruṇa.' That same [substance], when possessing a different quality, cannot be denoted by the word 'aruṇa.' This word does not deviate from [the quality of] redness, but does deviate from [particular] substances. And a non-deviating cause is considered the [true] cause by those who [accept] causation. Therefore, its own meaning is understood to be a quality. Thus, its quality-denoting nature is understood directly. But from the observation of the feminine suffix, [there arises] merely the inference that 'the stem aruṇā is a substance-word.' And direct perception is stronger than inference. Therefore, [it is] a quality-word. But how then [is there] a connection with the feminine gender? For even a quality-word can have feminine gender — just as [one says] '<s>cāruṇā buddhiḥ</s>' (a reddish cognition), so too '<s>aruṇā</s>.' And if [it is] a quality-word, it is not connected with '<s>krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases). Therefore, having made sentence-division, [the redness] is assigned to the entire context.
But if [it is] not connected with '<s>krīṇāti</s>,' it will be connected with the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (one-year-old [cow]) in that very sentence — and there will be no sentence-division. [Reply:] No — for the word 'aruṇā' denotes a quality alone, not substance-and-quality. And the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' [denotes] a substance alone, not [substance] combined with a quality. So how, without an intervening genitive [case-ending] expressing [their] connection, can their connection be understood? [Opponent:] It is said: Even without the genitive, we will understand co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) from co-occurrence in the same case-ending — just as in 'blue lotus' (<s>nīlam utpalam</s>). [Reply:] That is untenable. The quality-denoting nature of the word 'aruṇa' [is established] from its form. But the sentence-unity with the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' — [that would need to be] construed from the co-occurrence in the same case-ending and from the proximity of the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>.' But a sentence is not stronger than an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Therefore, this is unsound.
To this it is said: When, functioning as a pure quality-word, the word does not obtain a connection with anything else, then — lest it become purposeless through lack of instructive [function] — it assumes substance-referentiality. In that state, the word, in the same case-ending as the proximate word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>,' entering into sentence-unity [with it], becomes co-referential — and having done so, [the analysis] 'blue lotus' (<s>nīlam utpalam</s>) is justified. And this word 'aruṇā' is in that state. For there is no meaningfulness for it, severed from this [connection], even in the context. Why? By the very same reason by which it is not connected with '<s>krīṇāti</s>' — namely, that an incorporeal thing cannot be the instrument of an action. Nor [can it be connected] with the substance-instruments of the action — for a pure quality-word cannot denote a substance. This very reason [applies] also to the absence of connection with the context — for there too, when connected, it would be connected with either actions or substance-instruments of those actions, and both are untenable. Therefore, to avoid purposelessness, the word 'aruṇā' is connected with the proximate word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>.' There is no sentence-division.
[Reply:] This is not so. For this word 'aruṇā' is not fit to be a qualifier of '<s>ekahāyanī</s>.' For what reason? Because it is uttered in conjunction with the instrumental case-ending (third vibhakti). Therefore, by the capacity of the instrumental case-form, it must be a qualifier of the action, since <s>kārakas</s> (syntactic roles) have a connection with the action, not with a substance. This [word], by the capacity of the direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), is a qualifier of the action, [while] by sentence-unity it is a qualifier of '<s>ekahāyanī</s>.' And direct statement is stronger than a sentence. Therefore, it has no connection with '<s>ekahāyanī</s>'.

children.text:
nanu ca guṇasya kriyāsaṃbandhābhāvād avivakṣitā kāraka[218]{*3/45*}śaktir{*3/46*} ity ekahāyanīsaṃbandho 'yam adhyavasitaḥ. evam api nopapadyate, yadi kārakābhidhānam avivakṣitam iti guṇaśabdenaitena dravyam abhidhātum iṣyate, tadā prātipadikārthasyāvyatireka iti prathamā vibhaktiḥ prāpnoti. na hi tṛtīyāntas tam abhisaṃbandhaṃ śaknoti vaktum, na cānyathānupapattir ity anyo 'syānupapadyamāno 'rthaḥ śakyate kalpayitum, yathāgnau tiṣṭhati māṇavaka ity ukte jvalane 'nupapadyamāno nāśve gavi vā kalpyate, agnisamīpavacana evādhyavasīyate. tadvad ihāpy aprathamāntaḥ śabdo na kathaṃcid apy avyatirikte prātipadikārthe bhavitum arhatīti. tasmāt kāmam anarthako 'vagamyatāṃ nāsyaikahāyanīsaṃbandho 'dhyavasātavyaḥ.
āha - na brūmaḥ, na kārakam aruṇāśabdenābhidhīyata iti, vyaktam aruṇaguṇaviśiṣṭam etena kārakam abhidhīyate. kadācit tu kiṃcid vidhitsitaṃ bhavati, kadācid upasarjanībhūto 'rtho vidhitsitaḥ, pradhānībhūto 'nuvādaḥ. tad yathā, daṇḍīty upasarjanībhūtadaṇḍakapuruṣapradhānakaḥ śabdo 'vagamyate, kadācit tu nirjñāte puruṣe daṇḍaguṇavidhānārtham uccāryate - daṇḍī praiṣānanvāheti. tathā{*3/47*} lohiteṣṇīṣā ṛtvijaḥ pracarantīti. evam ihāpi yady anupasarjanabhūto{*3/48*} 'ruṇo guṇaḥ, pradhānabhūtaṃ kārakam. tathāpy anūdite kārake 'ruṇaguṇavidhānārthaṃ vacanaṃ yujyate. tasmād ekahāyanīsaṃbandha upapadyate, nāsti vākyabheda iti. naitat sāram, atra hy ekahāyanīkrīṇātyor anavabuddhaṃ saṃbandhaṃ bodhayitum ayam ekahāyanīśabda uccaritaḥ, sa eṣa katham ivāruṇāśabena saṃbadhyte, tad etad abhihitam api punaḥ punaḥ paryanuyujjyate. [219]{*3/49*} kathaṃ punar ekahāyanīśabdasya krīṇātinā, aruṇaguṇena ca samāne samabhivyāhāre krīṇātinā saṃbandho 'bhyupagamanīyaḥ, na punar āruṇyeneti. śabdaprāmāṇyāt, bhavati hi kriyāsaṃbandhasya vācikā vibhaktir ekahāyanīśabdam anuniviṣṭā, na tu guṇasaṃbandhasya vācikā. kā punaḥ kriyāsaṃbandhasya vācikā, kā vā guṇasaṃbandhasyeti. kārakalakṣaṇā kriyāsaṃbandhe vivakṣite bhavati dvitīyādiḥ, avivakṣite punaḥ kārake, saṃbandhamātravivakṣāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhī. na cātra ṣaṣṭīṃ paśyāmaḥ, paśyāmas tu khalu tṛtīyām. ataḥ krīṇātinā saṃbandham abhyupagacchāma ekahāyanīśabdasya, nāruṇāśabdeneti.
kathaṃ tarhi bhavaty atra saṃbandhaḥ, nīlam utapalam iti. ucyate - bhavati, na tu śrutilakṣaṇaḥ, kiṃ tu vākyalakṣaṇaḥ, utpalaśabdasaṃnidhāne tadapekṣī nīlaśabdas tenaikavākyatām abhyupagacchan nājahat svārthavṛttir upalaviśeṣābhidhānapara uccāryamāṇaḥ saṃbandham abhyupaiti.
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] But since a quality has no connection with an action, the <s>kāraka</s>-function is unintended — and so the connection with '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' has been established. [Reply:] Even so, this is untenable. If, because the <s>kāraka</s>-denotation is unintended, one wishes this quality-word to denote a substance, then the meaning of the nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>) would be non-different [from the substance] — and so the nominative case-ending (<s>prathamā vibhakti</s>) would apply [instead of the instrumental]. For a word in the instrumental cannot express that connection [with a substance] — nor can an impossibility [be resolved] by construing some other meaning for it. Just as, when it is said 'the boy stands in the fire,' since standing in flames is impossible, [the word 'fire'] is not construed [to refer to] a horse or a cow; rather, it is determined as meaning 'near the fire.' Similarly here, a word not in the nominative case cannot possibly have the meaning of the nominal stem [substance] that is non-different [from the quality]. Therefore, let it be understood as purposeless if need be — but its connection with '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' should not be determined.
[Opponent:] It is said: We do not say that the word 'aruṇā' does not denote a <s>kāraka</s>. Clearly, a <s>kāraka</s> qualified by the quality of redness is denoted by it. Sometimes, however, something is intended to be enjoined, and sometimes the subordinate meaning is intended [to be enjoined] while the primary meaning is a restatement. For example, '<s>daṇḍin</s>' (staff-bearer) — the word is understood as having the staff as subordinate and the person as primary. But sometimes, when the person is [already] known, it is uttered for the purpose of enjoining the quality of [having] a staff — 'the staff-bearer should recite the instructions.' Similarly, 'the priests with red turbans should officiate.' In the same way here, if the quality of redness is subordinate and the <s>kāraka</s> is primary — still, when the <s>kāraka</s> is [already] restated, the statement is justified as serving the purpose of enjoining the quality of redness. Therefore, the connection with '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' is established — there is no sentence-division. [Reply:] This is not sound. For here, the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' is uttered to make known the unknown connection between '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' and '<s>krīṇāti</s>.' How then could it be connected with the word 'aruṇā'? This has been stated, but it is objected to again and again. How, when the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' and '<s>krīṇāti</s>' occur in the same utterance along with the quality of redness, should the connection with '<s>krīṇāti</s>' be accepted but not with the redness? [Reply:] Because of the authority of the word. For there is a case-ending (<s>vibhakti</s>) that verbally expresses the connection of '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' with the action, which has entered into [the word] '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' — but no case-ending that verbally expresses the connection with the quality. And what case-ending verbally expresses the connection with the action? Which one expresses the connection with the quality? The <s>kāraka</s>-defining [case-endings] — the second (accusative) and so on — are used when the connection with the action is intended. But when the <s>kāraka</s> is not intended and merely a connection is intended, the sixth (genitive) [is used]. And here we do not see a genitive; we do see an instrumental (third). Therefore, we accept the connection of the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' with '<s>krīṇāti</s>,' not with the word 'aruṇā.'
But how then does the connection work in [the example] 'blue lotus' (<s>nīlam utpalam</s>)? It is said: It does work, but it is not characterized by direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) — rather, it is characterized by the sentence. The word '<s>nīla</s>' (blue), in the proximity of the word '<s>utpala</s>' (lotus), depending on it, enters into sentence-unity [with it], and without abandoning its own primary meaning, being uttered as subordinate to denoting a specific lotus, enters into connection.

children.text:
nanv ihāpi vākyalakṣaṇas tadvad evāruṇimnā samaṃ saṃbandha ekahāyanyā yujyate. neti brūmaḥ, śrutir hi vākyād balīyasī, śrutiś cāsyāḥ kriyāsaṃbandham āha, na guṇasaṃbandham. yadi punaḥ śrutisāmarthyāt, kriyāsaṃbandho 'bhyupagamyeta, ekavākyatavad api guṇasaṃbandhaḥ. naivaṃ śakyam, yo hy anyena saha saṃbandhum uccāryate, na tatsamīpagato 'py anyas tena saha saṃbanddhum arhati. yathā bhāryā rājñaḥ, puruṣo{*3/50*} devadattasyeti bhāryāviśeṣaṇārtham uccāryamāṇo rājaśabdo na puruṣeṇa saṃbadhyate, tadvad iha krayāviśeṣaṇārtham uccāryamāṇa ekahāyanīśabdo nāruṇāśabdena saṃbandham arhati.
āha - satyam evam etat, asatyām ākāṅkṣāyām ānantaryam akāraṇam, sarvatra tu bodhite padārthe vākyārtha upapadyate, nānyathā, sāmānyavṛtti hi padam, viśeṣavṛtti vākyam, sāmānyenābhipravṛttānāṃ [220]{*3/51*} padārthānāṃ yad viśeṣe 'vasthānam, sa vākyārthaḥ, tad etad uktam - tadbhūtānāṃ kriyārthena samāmnāyo 'rthasya tannimittatvād iti{*3/52*}, tatra pratyakṣataḥ{*3/53*} padārthaḥ, vākyārthaḥ punar ānumānikaḥ, tad etad avagamyatām, kevalasvārthavṛtti padam anupadeśakam iti padāntareṇa saṃnihitenaikavākyatvam abhyupaiti, nānyatheti. tad iha yady apy ekahāyanīśabdaḥ krīṇātinā saṃbandhyamānaḥ kṛtārtho na padāntareṇa saṃbandham ākāṅkṣati, aruṇāśabdas tu padāntareṇa saṃbandham alabhamāno 'narthaka ity ekahāyanīśabdenaikavākyatām abhyupaiti. nanūktam - kriyāsaṃbandhārthaḥ, nāruṇāsaṃbandhārtha iti.
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] But here too, the sentence-meaning (<s>vākyalakṣaṇa</s>) would, just as before, connect the one-year-old [cow] with the reddish quality. [Reply:] We say no. For the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) is stronger than the sentence. And the direct expression states this [word's] connection with the action, not a quality-connection. [Objection:] But if, by the force of the direct expression, the action-connection were accepted, then, just as in the case of sentence-unity, the quality-connection too [should be accepted]. [Reply:] This cannot be so, for that which is uttered to be connected with one [thing] — even another [word] proximate to it should not be connected with that [first thing]. Just as in 'the wife of the king, the servant of <s>Devadatta</s>' — the word 'king,' uttered for the purpose of qualifying 'wife,' is not connected with 'servant.' Similarly here, the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (one-year-old cow), uttered for the purpose of qualifying the purchase, does not merit connection with the word '<s>aruṇā</s>' (reddish).
He says: This is true — in the absence of syntactic expectancy, proximity is not a [sufficient] cause. But in every case, when the word-meaning has been cognized, the sentence-meaning is established — not otherwise. For a word operates in the general, while a sentence operates in the particular. The settling of word-meanings that have been set in motion in the general into a particular [configuration] — that is the sentence-meaning. This has been stated: 'The codified arrangement of those [word-meanings] that have become parts [of the sentence] is for the purpose of the action, because the meaning has that as its basis.' Therein, the word-meaning is [known] directly, while the sentence-meaning is inferential. Let this be understood: a word operating solely in its own meaning is non-instructive, and [therefore] it enters into sentence-unity with another proximate word — not otherwise. Thus, here, even though the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (one-year-old cow), being connected with '<s>krīṇāti</s>' (purchases), has fulfilled its purpose and does not seek connection with another word, still the word '<s>aruṇā</s>' (reddish), not obtaining connection with another word, would be purposeless — and therefore enters into sentence-unity with the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>.' [Objection:] But it was said — [the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>'] is for the purpose of action-connection, not for the purpose of <s>aruṇā</s>-connection.

āha - aruṇāśabdasyānarthakyaparihārāyobhayasaṃbandhārtha iti vadāmaḥ, anyārtham api kṛtam anyārtham api śaknoti kartum, tad yathā śālyarthaṃ kulyāḥ praṇīyante, tābhyaś ca pānīyaṃ pīyata upaspṛśyate ca. evam ihāpi krayasaṃbandhārtham ekahāyanīśabda uccāryamāṇo 'ruṇāśabdena saha saṃbhantyate, na kiṃcid duṣyati. tasmān na vākyabheda iti. naitad asti, yady apy ayam aruṇāśabdo 'narthako mā bhūd ity ekahāyanyā saṃbadhyeta, tathāpi sarvasmin prakaraṇe niveṣṭum arhati. na cainaṃ somaṃ krīṇātīty eṣa śabdaḥ śaknoti viśeṣṭum. na hy ayaṃ viśeṣaṇatvenocāryate, kiṃ tarhi apūrvo 'yaṃ vidhīyate.
nanv apūrvo 'pi vidhīyamāna ekahāyanīśabdavad itareṇa saṃbhantsyate. katham? prayojanāya hy uccāryamāṇaḥ śabdo yenārthaḥ, tasmai tāvat prayojanāyāvakalpyate, saṃnihitś ca buddhau bhavati, tena buddhau saṃnihitena śakyate sākāṅkṣaḥ śabdaḥ saṃbandhayitum iti. naitad evam, yo hy asaṃbadhyamāno 'narthako bhavati, sa saṃbadhyate nānyaḥ. kuta etat? saṃbadhyamāne hi sāmānyaṃ viśeṣe 'vasthāpyeta, tatra vākyena śrutiḥ pīḍitā syāt. na cāyam [221]{*3/54*} asaṃbadhyamānaḥ krīṇātinānarthako bhavati, prakaraṇagatābhiḥ{*3/55*} ekahāyanībhir{*3/56*} abhisaṃbhantsyate.
nanv etad uktam - prakaraṇe 'py asya saṃbandho 'nupapanna iti. nānupapannaḥ, ekasmin vākye 'nyo 'rtho vidhīyamāno nānyena saṃbadhyate, vacanavyaktibhedāt, anyā hi vacanavyaktir vidhīyamānasya, anyā guṇena saṃbadhyamānasya. ajñātavaj jñāpyate vidhīyamāno 'rthaḥ, jñātavad anūdyate guṇasaṃbandhārtham, na ca sakṛd uccāryamāṇo jñātavad ajñātavac ca bhavitum arhati, ekahāyanīśabdaḥ kraye vidhīyamāno 'jñātavat syāt, aruṇāśabdena saṃbadhyamānaś ca jñatavat. vākyabhede punar na doṣo bhavati, prakaraṇe tu vākyāntaraiḥ kriyādravyāntarāṇī ca prāptāni. tair idaṃ vākyāntaravihitaṃ saṃbadhyate, tatrānyasmin vidhīyate, anyasmin vākye 'nūdyata ity upa-pannaṃ bhavati. tasmāt saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca{*3/57*} sarvasmin prakaraṇe dravyeṣu niveśa iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - arthaikatve dravyaguṇayor aikakarmyān niyamaḥ syād iti, yatrārthaikatvaṃ śrūyate dravyaguṇayoḥ, tatra dravyaguṇāv ekasmin padārthe niyamyeyātām. kutaḥ? aikakarmyād ekakāryatvāt, ekaṃ hi kāryaṃ dravyaguṇayoḥ śrūyate krayasaṃbandhaḥ. katham etad avagamyate? ekavākyatvāt. katham ekavākyatvam? aruṇayā piṅgākṣyaikahāyanyety aparyavasito 'rthaḥ sākāṅkṣatvād abhidhātṛpratipatroḥ, somaṃ krīṇātīti tu paryavasyati, tayor evaṃ nairutsukyāt. yady ekakāryatā kim iti vikalpo na bhavati? naitad{*3/58*} evam. ekārthās tu vikalperann iti vikalpadharmāṇau prāpnuta ity ayukto 'yaṃ paryanuyogaḥ. katham? paryanuyogo nāma sa bhavati, yaḥ svapakṣaṃ sādhayati, vipakṣasya ca pratīpam ācarati, na ca [222]{*3/59*} vikalpo 'smatpakṣasya pratīpam ācarati, krayeṇāruṇim āsaṃbandha{*3/60*} ity eṣa naḥ pakṣaḥ. na ca vikalpo nānākāryatvāt.
nanv idānīm evoktam - ekaṃ kāryam iti, tac cāpi viruddham, evaṃ hi pūrvam abhihitam, amūrta-tvād guṇo na kriyayā saṃbadhyata iti, idānīṃ viparītam abhidhīyate - ubhāv api dravyaguṇāv ekārthau krayam abhinirvartayata iti. ucyate, naitad viruddham, na ca vikalpaḥ, ekaṃ kāryam, sāmarthyabhedas tu, sākṣād dhi dravyaṃ kriyāṃ pratyupakaroti. guṇas tu viśiṣṭānāṃ sādhanam. yady evam, na tarhi guṇaḥ kriyām abhinirvartayati, sādhanasyāsau viśeṣaka iti. naitad evam, guṇasya kriyām abhinirvartayata etad eva sāmarthyam, yat sādhanaṃ viśiṣyāt. ākāṅkṣati ca kriyā sādhanaviśeṣaṇam, cihnabhūto hi guṇaḥ sādhanaṃ lakṣayati. asati cihne na lakṣyeta, katamat sādhanaṃ kriyāyā iti. tataḥ kriyā nādhyavasyema kartum iti bhavati kriyāsādhanaṃ gunaḥ. na caiva sati vikalpo bhavati, yathādhikaraṇasya kartrādīnāṃ ca, adhikaraṇaṃ hi kartrādīni dhārayati, tāny adhāryamāṇāni na śaknuvanti kriyām abhinirvartayitum, tathā{*3/61*} kartā karaṇādīni samādhatte, tāny asamāhitāni na śaknuvanti svaṃ svam artham abhinirvartayitum. yasmiṃs tu sādhanopakāre kārye tasminn evopakāre 'nyat sādhanaṃ vidhīyate, tatra vikalpaḥ, yathā vrīhim iryajeta, yavair yajeteti, ubhaye 'pi taṇḍulanirvṛtyarthāḥ.
evaṃ tarhi tad evedaṃ saṃjātaṃ bhavati, ekahāyanīvidhanam, tadviśeṣaṇaṃ cāruṇo guṇaḥ, tatra sa eva doṣo vākyabhedaḥ prasajjyeteti. na brūmaḥ - aruṇāśabda ekahāyanīśabdena saṃbadhyata iti, kiṃ tarhi krīṇātinaiva saṃbadhyate. evaṃ hi śrūyate 'ruṇaguṇena krayam abhinirvartayed iti, yathā ca tena nirvartyate, tathā yatitavya bhavati. na cāviśiṃṣan sādhanam, guṇaḥ kriyā[223]{*3/62*}m abhinivartayatīty arthāt sādhanaviśeṣaṇatāṃ pratipadyate, yathā sthālyāṃ paced iti kriyāsādhanatvena nirdiṣṭe 'rthāt saṃbhavane dhāraṇe ca syālīṃ{*3/63*} vyāpārayati tadvad ihāpi draṣṭavyam. tasmān nāsti vākyabhedaprasaṅga iti.
nanv evam api vākyaṃ bhidyeta. katham? pratyekaṃ vākyaparisamāptir dṛṣṭeti, yathā devadattayajñadattaviṣṇumitrā bhojyantām iti pratyekaṃ bhujiḥ samāpyate, yathā ca yasya pitā pitāmahaḥ somaṃ na pived iti. evam ihāpy aruṇayā krīṇāti, ekahāyanyā krīṇātīti. naitad asmatpakṣasya bādhakam, evam api kraya evāruṇimā nivekṣyati, na sarvasmin prakaraṇa iti. satyam eṣa doṣo na bhavati, kiṃ tv anaruṇayāpy ekahāyanyā krayaḥ prāpnoti, aruṇayā cānekahāyanyā, tatra yad uktaṃ dravyaguṇayor niyama iti, sā pratijñā hīyate. na tarhi brūmaḥ - vākyabheda iti. katham? krayasya hi dravyāruṇimānāv upadiśyete, na krayas tayoḥ. na ca, pradhānaṃ pratiguṇaṃ bhidyate, pratipradhānaṃ hi guṇo bhidyata iti, asti cāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ - samudāye vākyaparisamāptir iti, yathā gargāḥ śataṃ daṇḍyantām iti, tathā abhiṣutya hutvā bhakṣāyantīti. tasmād ubhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaḥ krayo vidhīyate.
kathaṃ punas tasmiṃś cetariṃś ca dṛṣṭānte saty ekāntenāvadhāryate, samudāya eva vākyaparisamāptir na pratyavayavam iti. atra brūmaḥ - iha dravyāruṇimānāv ubhāv api kriyāsaṃbaddhāv upalabhyete paraspareṇāsaṃbaddhau, krayo 'pi dravyāruṇimābhyāṃ viśiṣṭa upalabhyate nānyayatareṇa, tatra yadi dravyaparam aruṇim aparaṃ ca bhavati vacanam idam, tataḥ pratyavayavam asaṃśayaṃ krayasaṃbandhaḥ. atha krayavidhitsayābhidhīyate, tato yathaivāyam ekahāyanīvi[224]{*3/64*}śiṣṭaḥ, evam aruṇim aviśiṣṭa iti niyamata ubhayasaṃbandho 'bhyupagamanīyaḥ. na cātra dravyāruṇimānāv īpsitau, īpsitas tu krayaḥ, tena hi jyotiṣṭomadravyaṃ somaḥ pariprāpyate, dravyāruṇimānau krayārthau santāv īpsitau syātām, nānyathā. tasmāt krayo vidhīyate, sa ca nānyataraviśiṣṭaḥ pratīyata iti samudāye vākyaparisamāptir iha niścīyate. yadā caivam, tadā na, ekahāyanīṃ muktvānyad dravyaṃ krayasādhanam asti, na cāruṇād anyaḥ sādhanasya viśeṣako guṇa iti, niyamaḥ siddho bhavati.
atra vadāmaḥ - yadi krayasya sādhane guṇo 'bhisaṃbandhum upaiti, tadā vākye bhinne 'pi krayasādhanatvād aruṇimāsmin dravye na nivekṣyate, kim artham ekavākyatā prayatnena sādhyata iti. tad etad abhidhīyate - bhinne hi vākya ekāhāyanīsādhanakaḥ krayo 'vabuddho bhavati, aruṇāsādhanam api krayāntaram, na tasminn evaikahāyanīsādhane kraye 'ruṇimā vihito bhavati, tatra yat krayāntaram aruṇaguṇaviśiṣṭam, tatrārthāt prāptam anyad api sādhanaṃ bhavati. tad api viśiṃṣan aruṇo guṇas tena saṃbadhyeta. ekavākyatve tu tat parihṛtaṃ bhavati. tasmāt sādhv abhidhīyate - arthaikatve dravyaguṇayor aikakarmyān niyamaḥ syād iti.
children.translated_text:
[<s>Śabara</s>] says: We say that to avoid the purposelessness of the word '<s>aruṇā</s>' (tawny), [it is] for the purpose of connection with both — [namely,] something made for one purpose can serve another purpose as well. For example, irrigation channels are constructed for the purpose of rice cultivation, and from them water is drunk and [ritual] touching is done. Similarly here too, the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (yearling [cow]), being uttered for the purpose of the purchase-connection, when it connects with the word '<s>aruṇā</s>' (tawny), nothing is vitiated. Therefore, there is no sentence-splitting. [Reply:] This is not so. Even if this word '<s>aruṇā</s>' would be connected with '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' lest it be purposeless, still it ought to apply to the entire context. And the expression 'he purchases this <s>Soma</s>' cannot restrict it. For it is not being uttered as a qualifier — rather, it is being enjoined as something unprecedented.
[Objection:] But even being enjoined as unprecedented, it will connect with the other [word], like the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>.' How? A word being uttered for a purpose, for whichever meaning [it has] a purpose — for that purpose it is first construed, and it becomes present in the mind. With that [word] present in the mind, a syntactically incomplete word can be connected. [Reply:] This is not so. For only that which would be purposeless if not connected is connected — not another. Why is this? For if [<s>aruṇā</s>] were connected [with '<s>ekahāyanī</s>'], the general would be established in the specific; there, the sentence would override the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>). And this [word '<s>aruṇā</s>'], [Page 221] even if not connected [with '<s>ekahāyanī</s>'], is not rendered purposeless by '<s>krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases), [for] it will connect with the yearling [cows] that belong to the context.
[Objection:] But it was said — even in the context, its connection is unjustified. [Reply:] It is not unjustified. In a single sentence, one meaning being enjoined is not connected with another, because of the difference in the mode of expression. For the mode of expression of what is being enjoined is different from that of what is being connected with a qualifier. What is being enjoined is made known as if unknown; what is being connected with a qualifier is restated as if known. And a word uttered once cannot be both 'as if known' and 'as if unknown.' The word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>,' when being enjoined in the purchase, would be 'as if unknown'; when being connected with the word '<s>aruṇā</s>,' 'as if known.' But when the sentences are separate, there is no fault. In the context, [substances] established by other sentences — actions and substances — exist. With those, this [word '<s>aruṇā</s>'], enjoined by another sentence, is connected. There, it is enjoined in one [sentence] and restated in another — this is well-founded. Therefore, because of the absence of a distinguishing factor in the conjunction, and because of the absence of a distinguishing factor in the context, [<s>aruṇā</s>] applies to all substances in the entire context.
When the prima facie view has thus been stated, we say: When there is unity of purpose, there should be a restriction [of the connection] of substance and quality to a single [object], because of their collaboration (<s>aikakarmya</s>). Where the unity of purpose of substance and quality is heard, there the substance and quality should be restricted to a single referent. Why? Because of their collaboration — because they serve a single function. For a single function of the substance and quality is heard: the purchase-connection. How is this known? Because of sentence-unity. How is there sentence-unity? 'With a tawny, yellow-eyed, yearling [cow]' — this meaning is incomplete and syntactically incomplete for both the speaker and the hearer. But 'he purchases <s>Soma</s>' completes [the meaning], because of their mutual [syntactic] completion. If there is a single function, why does no alternative [between substance and quality] arise? [Reply:] This [objection] is not valid. 'Those of a single purpose would be alternatives' — [the objection claims that] the quality of being alternatives would follow — but this cross-examination is improper. How? A cross-examination is [valid only] when it establishes one's own position and acts contrary to the opponent's position. But an alternative does not act contrary to our position. Our position is: '<s>aruṇī</s>' (tawny) is connected with the purchase. And there is no alternative, because of the plurality of functions [involved].
[Objection:] But it was just said that there is a single function — and that too is contradictory. For previously it was stated: 'Because of incorporeality, the quality is not connected with the action.' Now the opposite is stated — 'both substance and quality, having a single purpose, accomplish the purchase.' [Reply:] It is said: this is not contradictory, nor is there an alternative. There is a single function, but the modes of capacity differ. For the substance directly assists the action. But the quality is the means of specifying [the substance]. If so, then the quality does not accomplish the action — it is a specifier of the instrument. [Reply:] This is not so. The capacity of the quality to accomplish the action is precisely this — that it specifies the instrument. And the action expects the specification of the instrument — for the quality, serving as an identifying mark, designates the instrument. In the absence of the mark, [the instrument] would not be identified — 'which is the instrument for the action?' Therefore, one could not resolve to perform the action — so the quality is [an integral part of] the action-instrument. Nor is there an alternative when [the quality] is present — just as between the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) and the agent and the like: the locus supports the agent and the rest; they, unsupported, cannot accomplish the action. Similarly, the agent coordinates the instruments and the rest; they, uncoordinated, cannot accomplish their respective functions. But when a different instrument is enjoined for the same subsidiary function that the [first] instrument serves, there is an alternative — as in 'one should sacrifice with rice' and 'one should sacrifice with barley,' for both serve the purpose of producing cooked grain.
If so, then this is exactly what has resulted: the enjoining of '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (yearling [cow]), with '<s>aruṇa</s>' (tawny) as a qualifying quality — and there the same fault of sentence-splitting would follow. [Reply:] We do not say that the word '<s>aruṇā</s>' is connected with the word '<s>ekahāyanī</s>'; rather, it is connected with '<s>krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases) itself. For thus it is heard: 'He should accomplish the purchase with the tawny quality.' And one should strive to [perform the purchase] as [the word] requires. And [the quality], without specifying the instrument, accomplishes the action — [Page 223] and from that it naturally assumes the status of specifying the instrument. Just as in '[he should cook] in a pot' — when the pot is stated as an instrument of the action, it naturally engages in supporting and holding [the food] — so too it should be seen here. Therefore, the fault of sentence-splitting does not arise.
[Objection:] But even so, the sentence would be split. How? Because the sentence-completion is seen per individual [word] — just as in '<s>Devadatta</s>, <s>Yajñadatta</s>, and <s>Viṣṇumitra</s> should be fed,' the [verb] 'feeding' is completed per individual; and just as in 'He whose father and grandfather have not drunk <s>Soma</s>.' Similarly here too: 'he purchases with a tawny [cow]'; 'he purchases with a yearling [cow].' [Reply:] This does not defeat our position. Even so, the tawny quality will apply only to the purchase, not to the entire context. [Objection:] True, this fault does not arise. But the purchase is possible even with a non-tawny yearling, and with a tawny non-yearling — and so the thesis that was stated, 'there should be a restriction of substance and quality,' is undermined. [Reply:] Then we do not say: sentence-splitting. How? For the substance and the tawny quality are taught as [pertaining to] the purchase — the purchase is not [taught as pertaining to] them. And the principal is not split with respect to each subsidiary — rather, the subsidiary is split with respect to each principal. And there is this parallel: 'the sentence-completion pertains to the aggregate' — just as in 'Let the <s>Gargas</s> be fined a hundred [coins]'; and likewise in 'having pressed, having offered, they consume.' Therefore, the purchase qualified by both qualifiers is being enjoined.
But how, when both this and that parallel exist, can it be determined with certainty that the sentence-completion pertains only to the aggregate and not to each component? To this we say: here, the substance and the tawny quality are both perceived as connected with the action but not with each other; and the purchase is perceived as qualified by both the substance and the tawny quality, not by either one separately. If this statement were [intended as] substance-oriented and tawny-quality-oriented, then without doubt the purchase-connection would be per component. But if it is stated with the intention of enjoining the purchase, then just as [the purchase] is qualified by '<s>ekahāyanī</s>,' [Page 224] so too it is qualified by '<s>aruṇā</s>' — and therefore the connection with both must necessarily be accepted as a restriction. And here, the substance and the tawny quality are not what is most desired — rather, the purchase is most desired, for by it the <s>Soma</s>, which is the substance of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, is obtained. The substance and the tawny quality, being for the purpose of the purchase, would be most desired [only insofar as they serve the purchase], not otherwise. Therefore, the purchase is being enjoined, and it is not perceived as qualified by only one of them — so the sentence-completion pertaining to the aggregate is here determined. And when this is so, then no substance other than the yearling [cow] is an instrument of the purchase, and no quality other than tawny is a specifier of the instrument — so the restriction is established.
Here we say: if the quality approaches a connection with the instrument of the purchase, then even when the sentence is split, because of being an instrument of the purchase, the tawny quality would apply to this very substance [the yearling cow] — so why is sentence-unity being laboriously established? To this it is said: when the sentence is split, a purchase accomplished by the yearling-instrument is understood, and separately a purchase with the tawny-quality instrument — [the tawny quality] is not enjoined as pertaining to that very yearling-instrument purchase. In that case, the other purchase — the one qualified by the tawny quality — naturally has another instrument as well. Specifying that [other instrument], the tawny quality would be connected with it [rather than with the yearling cow]. But when there is sentence-unity, that [problem] is avoided. Therefore, it is well said: 'When there is unity of purpose, there should be a restriction of substance and quality to a single [object], because of their collaboration.'
