children.text: asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ - ya evaṃ vidvān somena yajata iti{*3/65*}. [225]{*3/66*} tatra śrūyate - daśāpavitreṇa grahaṃ saṃārṣṭīti, tathāgnihotre srūyate - agnes tṛṇāny apacinotīti, tathā darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - puroḍāśaṃ paryagnikarotīti{*3/67*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ekasya grahasya, ekasyāgneḥ, ekasya puroḍāśasya ca saṃmārjanādi kartavyam, uta sarveṣāṃ grahāṇāṃ sarveṣām agnīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ puroḍāśānām iti. kiṃ prāptam? eko grahaḥ, eko 'gniḥ, ekaḥ puroḍāśa iha grahītavyaḥ. kutaḥ? śrutisaṃyogāt, ekatvaśrutisaṃyuktā ete padārthāḥ, ekaṃ hi dravyam eṣa śrūyate, śabdalakṣaṇe ca hi karmaṇi yac chabda āha, tad asmākaṃ pramāṇam, yathā paśum ālabheta ity ukta eka eva paśuḥ pumāṃś cālabhyate. evam atrāpy eko grahaḥ saṃmārjanīyaḥ, ekasyāgnes tṛṇāny apaceyāni, ekaḥ puroḍāśaḥ paryagnikartavya iti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — 'He who, knowing thus, sacrifices with <s>Soma</s>.' There it is heard: 'He wipes the cup (<s>graha</s>) with [a strainer of] ten [threads].' Similarly, in the <s>Agnihotra</s> it is heard: 'He removes the blades of grass from the fire.' Similarly, in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is heard: 'He carries the fire around the sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>).' There the doubt arises: should the wiping and the like be performed for only one cup, one fire, and one sacrificial cake — or for all the cups, all the fires, and all the sacrificial cakes?

NOTES:
[Tait.S. 3.2.2.3] | [Edition page references: E2: 4,65; E4: 3,583; E6: 1,154] | [ŚPBr 1.2.2.13]

children.translated_text: Or [it would apply] to all, because of the characterizing nature [of the description]; for the characterization is undifferentiated. // MS 3,1.14 //

children.text:
naitad asti - yad uktaṃ grahādiṣv{*3/68*} ekatvayukteṣv amī padārthāḥ kartavyā iti, sarve grahāḥ saṃmārṣṭavyāḥ, sarvebhyo 'gnibhyas tṛṇāny apaceyāni, puroḍāśamātraṃ ca paryagnikartavyam iti. kutaḥ? grahajātyā dravyaṃ lakṣayitvā saṃmārgādi vidhīyate, aviśiṣṭaṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ sarvadravyeṣu, tatra na gamyate viśeṣaḥ, ko grahaḥ saṃmārṣṭavyaḥ, ko neti, sāmānyāvagamād viśeṣān avagamāc ca sarvapratyayaḥ. tathāgnipuroḍāśānām api. nanv ekavacanaṃ śrūyate, tad viśekṣyati. naitad asti, ekatvaṃ hi śrūyamāṇaṃ grahādiṣv ekatvaṃ brūyāt, na dvitīyādīn pratiṣedhet, ekatvasyāsau vācako na dvitīyādeḥ [226]{*3/69*} pratiṣedhakaḥ. tenāpratiṣiddhe dvitīyādau sāmānyavacanena prāptaṃ saṃmārjanādi kim iti na kriyeta.
tatraitat syāt, ekavacanam iha śrūyamāṇaṃ prāpta evaikasmin dravye, dvitīyādiṣu ca, kim anyat kuryād anyataḥ parisaṃkhyāyāḥ, na ced ekavacanaṃ parisaṃcakṣīta dvitīyādīn, anarthakam eva syāt, śaknoti ca dvitīyādīn nivartayitum, yathāśvābhidhānīm ādatta iti gardabhābhidhānaṃ{*3/70*} parisaṃcaṣṭe, evam atrāpi draṣṭavyam iti.
naitad evam, tatra mantrasyābhidhānyāś ca yaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, tad abhidhānaparaṃ vacanam, imām agṛbhṇān ity aśvābhidhānīm iti{*3/71*}, nānena mantreṇa, ādatta iti liṅgenaivādāne prāptatvān mantrasya parisaṃkhyā yuktā. iha punar yad ekavacanaṃ dravye śrūyate, tac chrūyamāṇam apy avidhīyamānatvena na nivartakaṃ bhavitum arhati, yathā kaścid odanaṃ nirdiśya brūyāt - ya enaṃ bhakṣayet kaścic chvā mārjāro vā, sa nivārayitavya iti, tatra yadi bhakṣaṇaṃ nimittatvena vidhīyate, na, śvamārjārasaṃbandhaḥ, tataḥ kāko 'py āgacchan nivāryate. śrūyamāṇe 'pi śuni mārjāre vā śvamārjārasaṃbandhasya nimittatvenāvidhīyamānatvāt. evam ihāpy ekatvasaṃbandhasyāvidhīyamānatvāc chrūyamāṇe 'py ekatve grahamātraṃ saṃmṛjyeteti.
na cātra dravyaikatvasaṃbandhavidhāyakaḥ kaścic chabdo 'sti. nanu saṃmārṣṭīti. na hy etad dravyaikatvasaṃbandhasya vidhāyakam. kasya tarhi? dravyasaṃmārgasaṃbandhasya vidhāyakam, evaṃ śrutyā svapadārtho vihito bhavati, itarathā vākyena parapadārtho vidhīyate. śrutyasaṃbhave ca vākyaṃ kramate, na saṃbhavantyāṃ śrutau. ato 'vidhīyamānaṃ viśeṣaṇatvena, ekatvaṃ na dvitīyādīn pratiṣeddhum arhati. evaṃ sati na dvitīyādau saṃmārgādi kriyamāṇam [227]{*3/72*} acoditaṃ bhavati, pratiṣiddhaṃ vā, yathaiva hi tad ekasya śrutam avagamyate, tathā dvitīyāder api.
ayaṃ cāparo doṣaḥ, na tad ekatvaṃ dravyasya saṃmārgādau viṣaye niyamyeta, na hi saṃmārgādiḥ, yasmin dravya ekatvaṃ niyamyeta, tasya viśeṣaṇatvena bhavati, vidhīyate hy atra saṃmārgādiḥ, na prāpto lakṣaṇatvena dravyasyāmnāyate, na hi yaugapadyena vidhātuṃ śakyate, lakṣaṇatvena coc-cārayitum. prasiddhasaṃbandho hi śaknoti lakṣayitum, na cāvihita evaṃjātīyakaḥ śabdāvagamyaḥ prasiddhasaṃbandho bhavati. vidhīyate ca saṃmārgādiḥ, tasmān na viśeṣakaḥ, na ced viśeṣakaḥ, na dravya ekatvaṃ niyamyata iti śakyam āśrayitum.
athaikatvaṃ saṃmārga ucyate. tatrāpi dvayī gatiḥ syāt, ekatvaṃ pradhānam, saṃmārgo vā, tac cobhayam apy anupapannam. na tāvad ekatvasya saṃmārgaḥ śākyate kartum. na ca dravye kriyamāṇa ekatvasyopakaroti kenacit prakaraṇam. na caikatvasyopakṛtena kiṃcit prayojanam asti, na hi tad guṇabhūtaṃ śrutam. athaikatvaṃ saṃmārgaṃ prati guṇabhūtam iti. tad api na. katham? amūrtatvāt, na hi tat saṃmārgaṃ niṣpādayati. yady apy anyad amūrtaṃ kriyāṃ niṣpādayati sādhanaṃ viśiṃṣat, tathāpy etan na bhavitum arhati, na hy atra grahaḥ saṃmārgārthaḥ, saṃmārgo 'tra grahāya codyate, sa hi prayojanavān, kalpyaprayojanaḥ saṃmārgaḥ. yadi grahaḥ saṃmārgasyopakuryāt, tad upakāriṇa{*3/73*} upakarotīti saṃmārgasyopakārakam ekatvaṃ bhavet. na tv etad evam. tasmād ekatvasaṃmārgayor asaṃbandhaḥ.
nanu pradhānabhutam api grahādi saṃmārgaṃ niṣpādayaty eva, atas tatsādhanaṃ tac ca viśiṃṣat tad upakariṣyati, yathā ijyārthe dadhani payasi ca praṇītā dharmāḥ pāka upakurvanti. paridhānārthe ca [228]{*3/74*} paridau yūpadharmā bandhane. tasmād ayam asamādhir iti. atrocyate - na brūmaḥ, atadarthe sādhake na śaknuvanty upakartum iti. kiṃ tarhi? yadā pradhānabhūtaṃ grahādi lakṣaṇatvenocyate, na tadaikatvasya grahādinā saṃbandhaḥ, na saṃmārgādineti. katham? yāvad iha lakṣaṇatvena kiṃcid ucyate, saṃvādas tatra bhavati, na tu tadvidhīyate vijñānāya. kim arthaṃ tarhy uccāryate? anyat tasya kiṃcid vidhāyiṣyata iti, tad etad grahādi lakṣayitvā tasya saṃmārgādi vidhīyate. tad yady ekatvasaṃbandho 'paro grahadravye{*3/75*} saṃmārgādau vā padārthe{*3/76*} vidhīyeta, dvayoḥ saṃbandhayor vidhānād bhidyeta vākyam. athocyeta - grahādi lakṣayitvā tasyaikatvasaṃbandho vidhīyate, na saṃmārgādisaṃbandha iti, tathā ca saṃmārgādīnām adhyayanaṃ pramāda ity abhyupagataṃ syāt. na caitad evam. tasmād ubhābhyām ekavacanasyāsaṃbandha iti. evam etad ekatvaṃ grahasya na kiṃcid upakāraṃ karoti, na saṃmārgasya, evam eva sadanūdyate. tasmān naitat kiṃcid api kartuṃ vivakṣyata iti sarveṣāṃ grahādīnāṃ saṃmārgādi kartavyam iti. kutaḥ? saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca{*3/77*}.
yady avivakṣitam ekatvam, kathaṃ trahy ekavacanam uccāryate? nanu bahuṣu vivakṣiteṣu bahuvacanena bhavitavyam. ucyate - na vayam etad vicārayāmaḥ, ekavacanam uccārayitavyam, noccārayitavyam iti, uccāryamāṇe sati kiṃ pratipattavyam? ekasminn eva saṃmārgādi, uta sarveṣv iti, tac ca sarveṣv iti sthāpitam. api ca na vibhakter vacanam evaikaṃ prayojanam. kiṃ tarhi? kārakasaṃbandho 'pi, avivakṣita ekatve kārakasaṃbandhārtham asyoccāraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati. tasmān nānarthakam.
api ca grahaḥ prātipadikārtha ekatvaṃ vibhaktyarthaḥ. kim ato [229]{*3/78*} yady evam. etad ato bhavati - prātipadikārthagataṃ hi vibhaktiḥ svam arthaṃ śrutyaiva vadati. athaivaṃ sati kim na, saṃmārgeṇa saṃbhantsyata iti. tena hi saṃbadhyamānaṃ vākyena saṃbadhyeta, na ca śrutyā, anyena saṃbadhyamānaṃ vākyenācchidyānyena saṃbandham arhati. asaṃbadhyamānas tv ekatvena saṃmārgaḥ, yadi naikatvaviśiṣṭaḥ kriyate, na kiṃcid vipannaṃ bhavati, na caikatvaviśiṣṭaḥ saṃmārgādiḥ, grahādimātrasya ca vidhīyata iti kim iti dvitīyasya tṛtīyasya ca na kriyeteti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — what was said, that in the cups and the like, which are connected with oneness, these items are to be performed [only once]: 'All cups should be wiped'; 'Grass should be removed from all fires'; 'Only the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) should be encircled with fire.' Why [is this not so]? The wiping and so on are enjoined by identifying the substance through the class of cup. And the identifying mark is undifferentiated across all substances. Therefore, no differentiation is understood — which cup is to be wiped and which not — and from the understanding of the general, along with the non-understanding of any particular [restriction], there arises the cognition [that it applies] to all. Similarly for fires and sacrificial cakes. [Objection:] But a singular number is heard — that will differentiate. This is not so. For the singularity that is heard would express singularity in the cups and the like — it would not prohibit a second and subsequent [cups]. It is an expression of singularity, not a prohibition of a second and subsequent [items]. Therefore, since the second and subsequent [items] are not prohibited, why should the wiping and so on, which are obtained through the general expression, not be performed?
To this it may be said: The singular number heard here is [already] obtained for one substance; as for the second and subsequent ones, what else would it do other than restrict [by exclusion]? If the singular number did not exclude the second and subsequent [items], it would simply be purposeless; and it can exclude the second and subsequent [items] — just as 'he takes the horse-halter' excludes the donkey-halter. It should be viewed similarly here too.
This is not so. There, the connection between the <s>mantra</s> and the halter — that statement has the halter as its object: '<s>imām agṛbhṇāt</s>' (he seized this one) refers to the horse-halter. Not by this <s>mantra</s> [alone], but because [the act of] taking is already obtained through the indicatory mark '<s>ādatte</s>' (he takes), the exclusion by the <s>mantra</s> is justified. But here, the singular number heard in connection with the substance, even though heard, since it is not being [specifically] enjoined, cannot serve as an excluder — just as if someone, pointing to rice, were to say 'Whoever eats this — whether a dog or a cat — should be driven away,' in that case if the eating is enjoined as the occasion, not the connection with dog or cat, then even a crow that comes would be driven away — even though a dog or cat is heard, because the connection with dog and cat is not enjoined as the occasion. Similarly here too, because the connection with singularity is not enjoined, even though singularity is heard, any cup whatsoever should be wiped.
And here there is no word that enjoins the connection of the substance with singularity. [Objection:] But [the word] '<s>saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (he wipes) [does so]. [Reply:] This is not an enjoiner of the connection of the substance with singularity. Of what then? It is an enjoiner of the connection of the substance with wiping. Thus, by direct hearing, its own referent is enjoined; otherwise, by the sentence, another referent would be enjoined. And the sentence operates [only] when direct hearing is not possible — not when direct hearing is available. Therefore, since singularity is not being enjoined [but only] [serving as] a qualifier, it cannot prohibit the second and subsequent [items]. This being so, the wiping and so on performed on the second and subsequent [items] are neither un-enjoined nor prohibited — for just as that [wiping] is heard and understood for the one, so too for the second and subsequent [items].
And here is another defect: That singularity would not be restricted to the domain of wiping and so on of the substance. For the wiping and so on is not something by which singularity is restricted to the substance — it functions as a qualifier. For the wiping and so on is being enjoined here; [the substance] is mentioned as a characterizing mark, not as [itself] obtained. For one cannot simultaneously enjoin [the wiping] and mention [the substance] as a characterizing mark. For [only] a well-established connection can serve as a characterizing mark, and [a connection] that is not [yet] enjoined — one of this kind, known through the word — does not have a well-established connection. And the wiping and so on is being enjoined. Therefore, [singularity] is not a qualifier. And if it is not a qualifier, it cannot be maintained that singularity is restricted to the substance.
But if singularity is said [to apply] to the wiping — even there, there would be two possibilities: either singularity is the principal [element], or the wiping. And both are untenable. First, wiping cannot be performed on singularity [as such]. Nor does the context support singularity in the substance in any way. And there is no purpose served by assisting singularity, for it is not heard as a subsidiary. But if singularity is subsidiary to the wiping — that too is not so. How? Because it is formless (<s>amūrta</s>). For it does not bring about the wiping. Even if something else formless — serving as an instrument — brings about an action by qualifying [it], even so, this cannot be the case. For here the cup is not for the purpose of wiping; the wiping is enjoined for the sake of the cup. For the cup is purposeful; the wiping has a purpose that must be construed. If the cup were to assist the wiping, then — assisting what assists [it] — singularity would be an assistant of the wiping. But this is not so. Therefore, there is no connection between singularity and wiping.
[Objection:] But even as the principal element, the cup and so on accomplishes the wiping, and therefore, qualifying the instrument, it would assist [it] — just as in the case of curds and milk intended for sacrifice, the properties enjoined [for them assist] in cooking. And for the purpose of wrapping, the properties of the sacrificial post [assist] in tying. Therefore, this [argument from the principal element] is not conclusive. To this it is said: We do not say that something serving a different purpose cannot assist. What then? When the cup and so on is mentioned as a characterizing mark, being the principal element, at that time singularity does not have a connection with the cup and so on — nor with the wiping and so on. How? As long as something is mentioned as a characterizing mark, agreement exists there, but it is not enjoined for [the purpose of] identification. For what purpose then is it uttered? Something else will be enjoined for it — thus, having identified the cup and so on by the characterizing mark, wiping and so on is enjoined for it. If then the connection of singularity with the cup-substance or with the wiping and so on were [separately] enjoined, the sentence would be split by the enjoining of two connections. But if one were to say: 'Having identified the cup and so on by the characterizing mark, the connection of singularity is enjoined [for it], not the connection with wiping and so on' — then the studying of wiping and so on would have to be regarded as erroneous recitation. But this is not so. Therefore, singularity has no connection with either. Thus, this singularity does not assist the cup in any way, nor the wiping — it is merely re-stated. Therefore, since [singularity] is not intended to accomplish anything at all, wiping and so on should be performed on all cups and the like. Why? Because of the connection [between the general expression and all instances] and because of the non-differentiation of the context.
If singularity is not intended, then why is the singular number uttered? [Objection:] Surely, when many [items] are intended, a plural number should be used. [Reply:] It is said: We are not examining whether the singular number should or should not be uttered. When it is being uttered, what should be understood? [Should] wiping and so on [apply] to one only, or to all? And that it [applies] to all has been established. Moreover, the sole purpose of a case-ending is not just [expressing] number. What then? It also [expresses] the case-relation (<s>kārakasaṃbandha</s>). When singularity is not intended, the utterance will serve the purpose of the case-relation. Therefore, it is not purposeless.
Moreover, 'cup' (<s>graha</s>) is the meaning of the nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>), and singularity is the meaning of the case-ending. What follows from this? From this it follows that the case-ending directly expresses its own meaning as pertaining to the meaning of the nominal stem. But if this is so, why will it not be connected with the wiping? For [singularity], being connected with [the cup] by another [means, namely] direct hearing, would be connected with [the wiping] by the sentence. But something being connected [with one thing] by direct hearing should not be disconnected from that and connected with another [thing] by the sentence. However, wiping is not connected with singularity. If wiping is not made to possess singularity, nothing goes wrong. And wiping and so on is not qualified by singularity; it is enjoined for the cup and the like in general — so why should it not be performed for the second and third [cups] as well?

children.text: atha yad uktam - yathā paśum ālabhetety eka eva paśuḥ puṃpaśuś cālabhyate, evam idam apīti, asty atra vaiparītyam iha grahārthaḥ saṃmārgaḥ, tatra punar yāgārthaḥ paśuḥ. kim evaṃ sati bhavati? yo yāgārthaṃ paricchinati{*3/79*}, sa yāgasyopakaroti, aparicchinnena na śakyo yāgaḥ kartum iti. na tu graheṇa kenacid viśiṣṭena saṃmārgaḥ kartavyaḥ, yad grahaṃ viśiṃṣat saṃmārgasyopkuryāt, paśoś caitad ekatvaṃ yāgaṃ pratyupadiśyate. nanūktam - prātipadikārthagataṃ svam arthaṃ vibhaktiḥ śrutyaivābhivadatīti{*3/80*}, yāga etad vākyena vidhāsyati, tatra vākyāc chrutir balīyasīty uktam. satyam, yatra śrauto 'bhisaṃbandho vivakṣyate, avivakṣyamāṇe ca vākyāvagataḥ san aparyudasitavyo{*3/81*} bhavati, tasmād ekaḥ puṃpaśuś cālabhyata iti, grahaikatvaṃ na saṃmārgasyopakarotīti na grahaṃ śaknoti viśeṣṭum. tasmād avivakṣitam iti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'Just as in "he should sacrifice an animal" a single animal, and a male animal, is sacrificed, so too here' — there is a difference here: here the wiping serves the purpose of the cup, but there the animal serves the purpose of the sacrifice. What follows from this? That which delimits [the animal] for the purpose of the sacrifice assists the sacrifice — for without a delimited [animal], the sacrifice cannot be performed. But the wiping is not to be performed on a cup that is [necessarily] qualified in a particular way — such that qualifying the cup would assist the wiping. And this singularity of the animal is indicated with respect to the sacrifice. But was it not said: 'The case-ending directly expresses its own meaning as pertaining to the nominal stem's meaning'? [To which the reply was:] The sacrifice — by the sentence — will enjoin this; and there, direct hearing is stronger than the sentence. True — where the connection from direct hearing is intended [as the meaning]. But when [direct hearing] is not intended, [the singularity] being understood from the sentence, it should not be excluded. Therefore, a single male animal is sacrificed. But the singularity of the cup does not assist the wiping — it cannot qualify the cup. Therefore, [singularity] is not intended.

asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ, tatra śrūyate - daśāpavitreṇa grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭīti. tatraiṣo 'rtho 'dhigataḥ - sarve grahāḥ saṃmārjitavyā iti. idam idānīṃ saṃdihyate - kiṃ camasāpi saṃmārṣṭavyā uta neti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? camasādy api sarvaṃ saṃmārjyam iti. kutaḥ? saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ceti{*3/83*}, yathaiva hi grahāṇām apūrvasaṃbandhaḥ, evaṃ camasānām api, yathaiva ca grahā asmin prakaraṇe, evaṃ camasāpi. tasmāt sarvatra saṃmārgaḥ.
nanu grahāḥ śrūyante, te camasānāṃ nirvartakā bhaviṣyanti. ucyate - pradarśanārthaṃ grahagrahaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati, grahādi somapātram, yasmin gṛhyamāṇaḥ somo vyavasicyeta, ity evam āśaṅkyate, tat sarvaṃ saṃmārjitavyam. yathā bhojanakālo vartate, sthālāni saṃmṛjyantām ity ukte, yāni yāni bhojana upayogam arhanti, tāni tāni sarvāṇi saṃmṛjyante, sthālagrahaṇaṃ lakṣaṇārtham iti gamyate. evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam iti.
ucyate - loke 'rthalakṣaṇaḥ saṃvyavahāraḥ, yena yenārthaḥ saṃmṛṣṭena, ukto 'nukto vā sa sa{*3/84*} saṃmṛjyetaiva. iha tu vede śabdalakṣaṇaḥ, śabdaś ca grahasya saṃmārgam āha, tatra kim arthaṃ śrutau saṃbhavantyāṃ grahaśabdo lakṣaṇayā kalpyate. ucyate - saṃmārṣṭīti saṃmārge puruṣaprayatnaṃ vidhātum eṣa śabdaḥ śaknoti śravaṇenaiva, grahasaṃbandhe tu vākyena, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī. tasmāl lakṣaṇayā grahaśabdo varṇyate, na, yathāśruta iti, tena, yo yaḥ saṃmārjanasaṃskārārhaḥ sa sa saṃmārjitavyaḥ, neti{*3/85*} graheṣv eva vyavatiṣṭhetaivaṃjātīyako guṇa iti.
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. There it is heard: 'He wipes the cup (<s>graha</s>) with a strainer of ten [strands].' There this meaning has been understood: all cups are to be wiped. Now this is doubted: should the <s>camasa</s> (drinking-cups) also be wiped, or not?
What is the prima facie view? The <s>camasas</s> and everything else too should be wiped. Why? Because there is no distinction in [their] connection [with the unseen result], and because there is no distinction in the context — for just as the cups have a connection with the unseen [result], so too do the <s>camasas</s>; and just as the cups are in this context, so too are the <s>camasas</s>. Therefore, wiping [applies] everywhere.
[Objection:] But the cups are heard [in scripture] — they will accomplish [the wiping] for the <s>camasas</s> [as well]. [Reply:] It is said: the mention of cups will be for the purpose of illustration. A cup and the like is a <s>Soma</s>-vessel — that in which the <s>Soma</s> being drawn would be poured — thus it is apprehended. All such [vessels] should be wiped. Just as when it is mealtime and one says 'let the pots be cleaned' — whatever vessels are suitable for use in the meal, all of those are cleaned. The mention of 'pots' (<s>sthāla</s>) is understood as being for the purpose of illustration. The same should be seen here.
It is replied: In the world, the convention is purpose-based — whatever [vessel] serves the purpose, whether mentioned or not, is wiped. But here, in the <s>Veda</s>, [the convention] is word-based, and the word states the wiping of cups. Then why should the word 'cup' (<s>graha</s>) be construed figuratively when the direct meaning is available? It is said: '<s>saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (he wipes) — this word is capable, by mere hearing, of enjoining the personal effort involved in wiping. But the connection with the cup [comes] from the sentence. And the direct expression (<s>śruti</s>) is stronger than the sentence. Therefore, it is not the case that the word 'cup' is explained figuratively, as if [it meant something other than] what is directly heard. Hence, whatever is worthy of the preparatory rite of wiping — that should be wiped. It is not the case that a quality of this kind is restricted to the cups alone.
Page 231

children.text: vyavasthā vārthasya śrutisaṃyogāt, tasya śabdapramāṇatvāt // MS_3,1.17 //
children.translated_text: Or, the restriction of the meaning would be because of the connection with scripture, since that [meaning] has the word as its valid means of knowledge. // MS_3,1.17 //

children.text:
vyavatiṣṭheta vā graheṣv eva saṃmārgaḥ, na camaseṣv api prasajyeteti. kutaḥ? arthasya śrutisaṃyogāt, śrūyamāṇo hi graho notsraṣṭavyaḥ, utsṛjyamāne śrutir eva bādhyate graham iti, pramattagītaṃ tatra bhavatām ity avagamyate, na caitan nyāyyam. tasmād grahaśabdena grahaṃ lakṣayitvā tasya saṃmārgasaṃbandho vidhīyate. na cāvidadhat saṃmārgam, śaknoti tatsaṃbandhaṃ vidhātum, ato vidadhāty evaiṣa śabdaḥ saṃmārgam. na ca śrutir bādhiṣyate. kutaḥ? saṃmārṣṭīti saṃmṛjigataṃ puruṣaprayatnaṃ śrutyā śaknoti vidhātum. na{*3/87*} tatra kaścid viśeṣaḥ, utpādyamāne vā saṃmṛjau{*3/88*}, pareṇa vā saṃbadhyamāna iti. tena na grahasaṃbandhe 'pi śrutir bādhitā bhavati, ato graheṣv eva saṃmārgo vyavasthātum arhatīti.
nanv apūrvasaṃyogāviśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca camaseṣv api prasajyate, na graheṣv evāsya vidhānam ity uktam. atrocyate - prakaraṇavadbhir ekavākyatāṃ kṛtvā śaknoti tatra vidhātum, nākṛtvaikavākyatām. sā ca prakaraṇād anumīyate, iyaṃ punar grahaśabdena saha pratyakṣā, tasmān na prakaraṇe vidhānam, grahaikatvasaṃbandhe punar utsṛjya svārtham, na śaknoti vidhātum. tasmād vaiṣamyam asya{*3/89*}, grahaikatvavidhānena{*3/90*}. yad uktam - yathā sthālāni saṃmṛjyantām iti lakṣaṇā, tadvad ihāpīti, parihṛtam etal loke karmārthaṃ lakṣaṇam{*3/91*}, śabdalakṣaṇaṃ punar veda iti.
children.translated_text:
Or, the wiping would be restricted to the cups alone, and would not extend to the <s>camasas</s>. Why? Because of the connection of the meaning with scripture. For the cup, being heard [in scripture], should not be abandoned. If abandoned, the scripture itself is overridden — 'cup' — and it is understood that 'your [position] involves careless recitation.' And this is not proper. Therefore, having identified the cup through the word 'cup,' the connection of wiping with it is enjoined. And without [first] enjoining the wiping, [the word] cannot enjoin the connection with it — hence this word does indeed enjoin the wiping. Nor is the scripture overridden. Why? '<s>Saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (he wipes) — by the direct expression, [this word] can enjoin the personal effort inherent in wiping. There is no distinction there — whether when the wiping is being produced, or when it is being connected with something else. Therefore, even in the connection with the cup, the scripture is not overridden. Hence, the wiping can properly be restricted to the cups alone.
[Objection:] But because of the non-distinction in connection [with the unseen result] and the non-distinction in context, it extends to the <s>camasas</s> too — it is not enjoined only for the cups, as was said. [Reply:] To this it is said: by achieving sentence-unity with those in the context, [the word] is capable of enjoining [wiping] there — but not without achieving sentence-unity. And that [sentence-unity from context] is inferred from the context, while this [sentence-unity with 'cup'] is directly perceived through the word 'cup.' Therefore, the injunction is not [based] on context. And in the connection of wiping with cups alone, having abandoned its own meaning, [the word] cannot enjoin. Therefore, there is an inequality — because of the injunction of the connection with cups alone. As for what was said — 'just as in "let the pots be cleaned" there is figurative usage, so too here' — this has been refuted: in the world, figurative usage is purpose-based, but in the <s>Veda</s>, it is word-based.
Page 232

children.text:
vājapeye śrūyate - saptadaśāratnir vājapeyasya yūpo bhavatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ saptadaśāratnitā vājapeyasyordhvapātre niviśate, uta paśor yūpe niviśata iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? ūrdhvapātra iti. kutaḥ? vājapeyasya yūpābhāvāt, yad vājapeyasyāsti pātraṃ yūpasadṛśam, tatra bhavitum arhati, asti ca ṣoḍaśipātram, tac ca khādiratvād ūrdhvatvāc ca yūpasadṛśam, tatra niveśe sati vājapeyaśabda āñjasyena bhavati, itarathā vājapeyāṅgapaśuyāge{*3/93*} lakṣaṇayā vājapeyaśabdo vṛtta iti gamyate. nanu tvatpakṣe 'pi yūpaśabdo lakṣaṇayordhvapātre. ucyate, sarvathā vayaṃ lakṣaṇāśabdān na mucyāmahe. matpakṣe tu vājapeyaprakaraṇam anugṛhyate, tasmād ūrdhvapātre niveśa iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ānarthakyāt tadaṅgeṣu, vājapeyaśabdas tāvat somayāgaviśeṣavacanaḥ, tasya sākṣād yūpena na prayojanam, asti tu tasyāṅgaṃ paśuyāgaḥ, tasya tu paśuṃ bandhuṃ yūpena kāryam. sākṣād vājapeyayūpasya yadi saptadaśāratnitā vidhīyate, tasyābhāvād anarthakam eva vacanaṃ prāpnoti, tad anarthakaṃ mā bhūd iti yo 'sya paśuyāge yūpaḥ, tatra niveśam arhati. ūrdhvapātre ca yūpaśabdo lakṣaṇayā syāt. nanv itarasminn api pakṣe vājapeyaśabdo lakṣaṇayeti. neti brūmaḥ, vājapeya eva vājapeyaśabdo bhaviṣyati, śakṣyati ca sa paśuyūpaṃ viśeṣṭum, so 'syāṅgasyopakārakaḥ, yaś ca yasyopakāriṇa upakaroti, bhavati sa tasya saṃbaddho mukhyenaiva saṃbandhena. na caikāntaritam iti kṛtvāsaṃbaddho bhavati, yathā devadattasya napteti, putreṇa cāsāv antaritaḥ, atha ca devadattena mukhyenaiva saṃbandhena saṃbaddhaḥ. tasmād eṣa eva [233]{*3/94*} pakṣa āśrayaṇīyaḥ, na hy etasmin pakṣe kaścid api lakṣaṇaśabdo bhavatīti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Vājapeya</s>, it is heard: 'The sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) of the <s>Vājapeya</s> is seventeen <s>aratis</s> (cubits) [tall].' There the doubt arises: does the seventeen-cubit measure apply to the upright vessel (<s>ūrdhvapātra</s>) of the <s>Vājapeya</s>, or to the sacrificial post of the animal [sacrifice that is] a subsidiary? What is the prima facie view? [It applies to] the upright vessel. Why? Because the <s>Vājapeya</s> has no [separate] sacrificial post. Whatever vessel the <s>Vājapeya</s> has that resembles a sacrificial post — [the measure] should apply there. And there is the sixteen-[spoked] vessel, which, because of being made of <s>Khadira</s>-wood and being upright, resembles a sacrificial post. If [the measure] is placed there, the word '<s>Vājapeya</s>' works directly. Otherwise, it is understood that in the animal sacrifice that is a subsidiary of the <s>Vājapeya</s>, the word '<s>Vājapeya</s>' is used figuratively. [Objection:] But in your view too, the word '<s>yūpa</s>' (sacrificial post) is used figuratively for the upright vessel. [Reply:] It is said: in any case, we cannot avoid figurative words. But in my view, the context of the <s>Vājapeya</s> is supported. Therefore, [the measure] is placed in the upright vessel.
When this has been arrived at, we say: because of purposelessness, [it should apply] to the subsidiary parts of that [sacrifice]. The word '<s>Vājapeya</s>' denotes a specific <s>Soma</s> sacrifice. That [sacrifice] has no direct need for a sacrificial post. But it does have a subsidiary — the animal sacrifice — and that requires a sacrificial post for tying the animal. If the seventeen-cubit measure is enjoined for the sacrificial post of the <s>Vājapeya</s> directly, then, because of [the post's] non-existence, the statement becomes simply purposeless. Lest it be purposeless, [the measure] should properly be placed in the sacrificial post of its animal sacrifice. And in [the case of] the upright vessel, the word '<s>yūpa</s>' would be figurative. [Objection:] But in the other view too, the word '<s>Vājapeya</s>' is figurative. [Reply:] We say no. The word '<s>Vājapeya</s>' will apply to the <s>Vājapeya</s> itself. And it can qualify the animal-post, which is its subsidiary's [post]. That which benefits a subsidiary of something — that is connected with that [thing] by a primary connection indeed. And it does not become unconnected merely because one [thing] is intervening — just as [one says] 'the grandson of <s>Devadatta</s>,' though intervened by a son, is still connected with <s>Devadatta</s> by a primary connection. Therefore, this very view should be adopted — for in this view, no figurative word whatsoever occurs.

NOTES:
[Variant: E2,4 read 'vājapeyāṅgapaśuyāge'] | [Page refs: E2: 4,101; E4: 3,649; E6: 1,160]

children.text: kartṛguṇe tu karmāsamavāyād vākyabhedaḥ syāt // MS_3,1.19 //
children.translated_text: But when [the quality belongs to] the agent, because of the non-inherence with the ritual action, there would be a splitting of the sentence. // MS_3,1.19 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ prayājavākye śrūyate - abhikrāmaṃ juhoty abhijityeti{*3/95*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim abhikramaṇaṃ prayājeṣv eva niviśata uta kṛtsne prakaraṇa iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? kartṛguṇe 'bhikramaṇe brūmaḥ - vākyabhedaḥ syād iti, karmaṇā karmaṇo 'samavāyāt. abhikramaṇaṃ karmāmūrtam, na tat karma havanaṃ sādhayituṃ śaknoti, tasmān na tenaikavākyatāṃ yāti. ataḥ sarvasmin prakaraṇe niviśate, saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ceti{*3/96*}.
nanv anenaiva hetunānyasminn api na nivekṣyate. ucyate - anyatra puruṣaiḥ saṃbhantsyate. nanu prayājeṣv api puruṣaiḥ saṃbadhyeta. naitad evam, juhḥtīti havana eṣa śabdaḥ puruṣaprayatnaṃ vidhātuṃ śaknoti, na puruṣābhikramaṇāsaṃbandham. nanv anyatrāpi puruṣābhikramaṇasaṃbandhasyāvidhānam. naiṣa doṣaḥ, anyatra prakaraṇāmnānād aṅgabhāve nirjñāte prayogavacano 'sya kartavyatāṃ vakṣyati. tasmāt sarvasmin prakaraṇe 'bhikramaṇasya niveśa iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, in the sentence about the preliminary offerings (<s>prayāja</s>), it is heard: 'He offers while stepping forward, having conquered (<s>abhijitya</s>).' There the doubt arises: does the stepping forward apply only to the preliminary offerings, or to the entire context? What is the prima facie view? Regarding the stepping forward, which is a quality of the agent, we say: there would be a splitting of the sentence — because of the non-inherence of the action with the [other] action. The stepping forward is a non-material action; it cannot accomplish the oblation. Therefore, it does not achieve sentence-unity with it. Hence, it applies to the entire context, because of the non-distinction in connection and the non-distinction in context.
[Objection:] But by this very reasoning, it would not apply anywhere else either. [Reply:] It is said: elsewhere, it will be connected with the persons. [Objection:] But in the preliminary offerings too, it could be connected with the persons. [Reply:] This is not so. '<s>Juhoti</s>' (he offers) — this word is capable of enjoining the personal effort involved in the oblation, not the non-connection of the person with stepping forward. [Objection:] But elsewhere too, the connection of the person with stepping forward is not enjoined. [Reply:] This is not a defect. Elsewhere, because of being recited in the context, when the subsidiary status has been determined, the performance-sentence will state its 'to-be-doneness.' Therefore, the stepping forward applies to the entire context.

NOTES:
Tait.S. 2.6.1.4 | Cf. MS 3.1.8

children.text: sākāṅkṣaṃ tv ekavākyaṃ syād asamāptaṃ hi pūrveṇa // MS_3,1.20 //
children.translated_text: But what has syntactic expectancy would form a single sentence, for it is uncompleted by the preceding [word]. // MS_3,1.20 //

children.text: naitad asti - yad uktam abhikramaṇaṃ prakaraṇe niviśata iti. prayā[234]{*3/97*}jeṣv eva bhavitum arhati. kutaḥ? taiḥ sahāsyaikavākyatā, yataḥ sākāṅkṣam etat pūrveṇa padenāsamāptaṃ vākyam, abhikrāmaṃ juhotīty atra paryavasyati, prakaraṇāc ca vākyaṃ balavad iti prayājeṣv evābhikramaṇaṃ niviśate. nanv abhikramaṇam amūrtatvād dhomanirvṛttāv asamartham ity uktam. ucyate, sākṣād asamartham, kartrā saṃbadhyamānaṃ śakṣyati nirvartayitum. katham? abhikramaṇena samāsīdaty āhavanīyaṃ kartā, dvayam abhyupāyabhūtaṃ homasya, dūrād vābhiprasārya hastam, juhuyāt, samāsīded anvābhikramaṇena. tasmād abhikramaṇam upakaroti homasyety avagamyate. ataḥ prayājeṣv eva niveśa iti.
children.translated_text: This is not the case — as was said, that the stepping forward applies to the [entire] context. It should properly apply to the preliminary offerings alone. Why? Because it has sentence-unity with them. For this sentence, having syntactic expectancy, is uncompleted by the preceding word and concludes in 'he offers while stepping forward' (<s>abhikrāmaṃ juhoti</s>). And the sentence is stronger than the context — hence the stepping forward applies to the preliminary offerings alone. [Objection:] But it was said that the stepping forward, being non-material, is incapable of accomplishing the oblation. [Reply:] It is said: it is incapable directly, but being connected with the agent, it will be able to accomplish [it]. How? By stepping forward, the agent approaches the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]; both [stepping forward and approaching] serve as means of the oblation. Or, he might offer by extending his hand from a distance. He should approach by stepping forward. Therefore, it is understood that the stepping forward assists the oblation. Hence, it applies to the preliminary offerings alone.

children.text: saṃdigdhe tu vyavāyād vākyabhedaḥ syāt // MS_3,1.21 //
children.translated_text: But when there is doubt, because of separation, there would be a splitting of the sentence. // MS_3,1.21 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ saptamāṣṭamayor brāhmaṇānuvākayoḥ sāmidhenya uktāḥ, navame nividaḥ, daśame kāmyāḥ sāmidhenīkalpāḥ, idaṃ kāmasyaitāvatīr anubrūyāt, idaṃ kāmasyaitāvatīr iti, ekādaśe ca yajñopavītam āmnātam - upavyayate devalakṣmam eva tat kuruta iti{*3/98*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sāmidhenīr evānubruvāṇa upavyayeta, uta prakaraṇe sarvān eva padārthān anutiṣṭhatā upavyātavyam iti. kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? upavītaṃ sāmidhenīnāṃ prakaraṇe samāmnātam, atha nivṛtte vā tāsāṃ prakaraṇa iti na jñāyate.
nanu darśapūrṇamāsayor eva prakaraṇam idam, paraprakaraṇe sāmidhenyaḥ śrūyante. satyaṃ paraprakaraṇe śrūyante. tathāpi tāsām avāntaraprakaraṇam aparam, bhavati hi, sāmidhenīr anubrūyād iti viśeṣākāṅkṣaṃ vacanam, yena tatsaṃnidhāv abhidhīyamānaṃ tasyeti jñāyate. kathaṃ punar nivṛttaṃ tāsāṃ prakaraṇam ity āśaṅkyate? [235]{*3/99*} nivitpadāni tāsāṃ prakaraṇaṃ vyavadadhatīti. yady evam, katham anuvartate prakaraṇam ity āśaṅkā? parastān nividām, sādmidhenīguṇā eva kāmyā vidhīyamānāḥ śrūyante, yad anantaraṃ yajñopavītam āmnātam, tenānivṛttaṃ sāmidhenīnāṃ prakaraṇam iti bhavati matiḥ. ataḥ paraprakaraṇe nividaḥ samupanipatitā na vyavadadhati. yathā
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, in the seventh and eighth <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sections, the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> [verses] are stated; in the ninth, the <s>nivid</s> (insertion formula); in the tenth, the optional (<s>kāmya</s>) <s>Sāmidhenī</s> variations — 'for this desire, one should recite this many; for that desire, that many'; and in the eleventh, the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>) is taught — 'he puts on the sacred thread; for thus he makes the divine mark.' There the doubt arises: should one put on the sacred thread only while reciting the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> [verses], or should it be worn while performing all the ritual elements in the context?
Whence the doubt? The sacred thread is taught in the context of the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> [verses] — but whether the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> context has ended or not is not known.
[Objection:] But this is the context of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites] itself; the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> verses are heard in another's context. [Reply:] True, they are heard in another's context. But even so, there is a sub-context for them — for the statement 'one should recite the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> verses' has syntactic expectancy for specifics, by which, [when something is] stated in proximity to it, [that thing] is known as belonging to it. But how is it suspected that their context has ended? The <s>nivid</s> passages intervene and disrupt their context. If so, how is it suspected that the context continues? After the <s>nivids</s>, the optional [variations], which are qualities of the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> [verses] themselves, are heard as being enjoined. The sacred thread is taught immediately after that — hence one might think that the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> context has not ended. Therefore, the <s>nivid</s> [passages], having intruded from another context, do not disrupt [the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> context]. Just as —

children.text:
dvādaśopasattāhīnadharmo jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇa iti. tena bhavati saṃdehaḥ.
asmin saṃdehe kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sāmidhenīprakaraṇam anivṛttam, tatropavītaṃ samāmnātam iti. kutaḥ? kāmyānāṃ sāmidhenīkalpānām ānantaryavacanāt, hṛdayam anuviparivartamānāsu sāmidhenīṣu upavītam āmananti, kartuś ca vāsovinyāsamātraṃ guṇo bhavaty upavītaṃ nāma. kiṃ kurvatā tat kartavyam iti bhavati tatra padārthākāṅkṣā, tatra buddhau saṃnihitenāviprakṛṣṭena sāmidhenīvākyenaikavākyatāṃ upagamya sāmidhenīṣūpavītaṃ upavyayata ity eṣa śabdo vidadhātīti gamyate.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - na, asmin saṃdehe yas tv ayoktaḥ, sa nirṇayaḥ. asmin saṃdehe vākyabheda iti nirṇaya iti. kutaḥ? vyavāyāt, iha samāptasya sānubandhasya sāmidhenīvākyasya, asya copavyayata iti vacanasya, nividāṃ vidhāyakena sāmidhenībhir asaṃbaddhena granthena vyavadhānaṃ bhavati, yasya ca paryavasite 'pi vacane tatsaṃbaddham evārthāntaraṃ prakramante, na tatrānanuvṛttaṃ prakaraṇam, āgacchati hi tatsaṃbaddhābhidhāne hṛdayam. yatra tu paryavasite vacane tadasaṃbaddham evārthāntaraṃ prakramante, na tatra buddhau pūrvaḥ padārthaḥ saṃnidhīyate. na ca, buddhāv asaṃnihitenaikavākyatā bhavati. dvābhyāṃ hi buddhābhyāṃ{*3/100*} padārthābhyāṃ vākyārthaḥ saṃjanyate, nānyatareṇa, saṃnidhau samāmnānasyaitad eva prayojanam, katham ubhābhyāṃ padārthābhyāṃ viśiṣṭāṃ buddhim utpādayeyur iti. [236]{*3/101*} anantarāv abuddhena saha vākyārthaḥ śakyate kartum, asaṃbaddhapadoccāraṇe ca nānantarāv abuddho bhavati. tasmād vyavahitena saha naikavākyatā bhavatīti.
athānyena prakāreṇa dhyānādinā pūrvapadārtham avagamya, vākyārthaṃ saṃjanayet. avaidikaḥ sa puruṣabuddhir pūrvako vākyārtho bhavet, yathā, anyasmād anuvākād ākhyātapadaṃ gṛhītvā, anyasmāc ca nāmapadaṃ yo vākyārthaḥ saṃjanyate, tādṛśaṃ tad bhavet, yatrānyena dhyānādinā pūrvapadārtham avagamya, vākyārthaṃ saṃjanayet. tasmān nāsaṃbaddhārthavyavadhānaikavākyatā bhavatīti niścīyate. tasmān na sāmidhenībhir ekavākyatopavītasyeti. nanu sāmidhenīkalpānām anantarabuddhānāṃ saṃnidhāv upavītam āmnāyate, tena sāmidhenībhiḥ saṃbhantsyata iti. neti brūmaḥ - ativṛttam eva hi sāmidhenīnāṃ prakaraṇaṃ nivitpadair vyavadhānāt. vākyena hi
sāmidhenīkalpāḥ kāmyāḥ saṃbandham upagacchanti, na prakaraṇam anuvartate, na ca, punaḥ kalpavacanena sāmidhenyaḥ prakṛtā bhavanti. na hi, tatra tāsāṃ vacanaṃ kartavyā iti. kiṃ tarhi? saṃkhyābhiḥ saṃbandhayitavyā iti, tad api vākyena, na prakaraṇena. tatrāprakṛtāsu samidhenīṣu yasyaikavākyatā guṇasya sāmidhenībhir nāsti, na tasya tābhiḥ saṃbandhaḥ. tasmāt{*3/102*} prakaraṇe{*3/103*} yad anuṣṭheyaṃ tad yajñopavītineti siddham.
children.translated_text:
The twelve-day <s>upasad</s> rites and the rule of diminishment belong to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context — hence there is doubt.
In this doubt, what is the prima facie view? The <s>sāmidhenī</s> context has not ended, and within it the <s>upavīta</s> (sacred thread wearing) is recorded. Why? Because of the statement of sequential proximity (<s>ānantarya</s>) in the optional <s>sāmidhenī</s> formulae — in the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses that revolve around the heart, they record the <s>upavīta</s>. And the <s>upavīta</s> is merely a quality pertaining to the arrangement of the performer's garment. 'What should be done by whom doing what?' — thus there is syntactic expectancy regarding the word-meanings. There, by entering into sentence-unity with the proximate, mentally present <s>sāmidhenī</s> sentence, it is understood that the expression 'he wears the sacred thread over the left shoulder in the <s>sāmidhenī</s> [rites]' enjoins [this practice].
Having arrived at this position, we say: No — in this doubt, that which was stated [in sūtra MS 3.1.21] is the resolution. In this doubt, sentence-division is the resolution. Why? Because of intervention (<s>vyavāya</s>). Here, the <s>sāmidhenī</s> sentence, together with its supplement, has been completed, and between it and the statement 'he wears the sacred thread,' there is an intervening passage — one that enjoins the <s>nivid</s> formulae and is unconnected with the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses. And when, even after the completion of a statement, only a topic connected with it is commenced, the context does not continue — for the mind approaches what is connected with [the current] statement. But when, after the completion of a statement, a topic unconnected with it is commenced, the previous word-meaning is not mentally present. And sentence-unity does not occur with what is not mentally present. For the sentence-meaning arises from two mentally [present] word-meanings, not from just one of them. The very purpose of recording [words] in proximity is this: how can [the two] word-meanings produce a qualified cognition from both [taken together]? Sentence-meaning can be produced with what is proximate and mentally grasped, but when there is utterance of unconnected words, what is proximate is not mentally grasped. Therefore, sentence-unity does not occur with what is intervened.
But if, by some other means such as meditation, one grasps the previous word-meaning and then construes the sentence-meaning — such a sentence-meaning, preceded by human cognition, would be non-Vedic. Just as when one takes a verb from one <s>anuvāka</s> (recitation section) and a noun from another and construes a sentence-meaning — it would be of that kind, where by some other means such as meditation one grasps the previous word-meaning and construes the sentence-meaning. Therefore, it is determined that sentence-unity does not occur through the intervention of unconnected meanings. Therefore, the <s>upavīta</s> does not form a sentence-unity with the <s>sāmidhenī</s> [rites]. [Objection:] But the <s>upavīta</s> is recorded in the proximity of the optional <s>sāmidhenī</s> formulae which are next [in sequence] and mentally present — therefore it will be connected with the <s>sāmidhenī</s> [rites]. [Reply:] We say no — for the <s>sāmidhenī</s> context has already passed due to the intervention of the <s>nivid</s> passages. For the optional <s>sāmidhenī</s> formulae enter into connection through the sentence, not through the continuation of the context. And the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses do not become the topic again merely by the statement of the formulae. For there, the statement is not 'they should be performed'; rather, 'they should be connected with the [appropriate] numbers' — and that too [is established] by sentence, not by context. There, when the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses are not the topic, the quality that does not have sentence-unity with the <s>sāmidhenī</s> [rites] has no connection with them. Therefore, whatever is to be performed in the context should be performed wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder — this is established.

NOTES:

children.text: guṇānāṃ ca parārthatvād asaṃbandhaḥ samatvāt syāt // MS_3,1.22 //
children.translated_text: And because of the subsidiary nature of qualities, there would be no connection [with the principal rite] because of equality [of status]. // MS 3,1.22 //

children.text:
agnyādheye vāraṇavaikaṅkatapātrāṇy ahomārthāni homārthāni [237]{*3/104*} ca śrūyante - tasmād vāraṇo vai yajñāvacaraḥ syāt, na tv etena juhuyāt, vaikaṅkato yajñāvacaraḥ syāj juhuyād eteneti. na ca vāraṇavaikaṅkatānāṃ pātrāṇām agnyādheyena saṃbandhaḥ. kutaḥ? yajñāv acaravacanāt, yajñasyaitāni pātrāṇi, vākyena prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā bhavanti. tatraiṣa saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ pavam āneṣṭiṣu niviśante, uta darśapūrṇamāsādiṣu sarvayāgeṣv iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? pavamānahaviḥṣv iti. kutaḥ? uktam etat pradhāne 'saṃbhavan padārthas tadguṇe kalpyata iti, agnyādheyaprakaraṇe ca samāmnānāt pavamānahaviṣāṃ tadguṇatā. tasmāt pavamānahaviḥṣv ity evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - guṇānāṃ samatvāt, pavamānahaviṣām agnyādheyasya ca na paraspareṇa saṃbandhaḥ. yathādhānam agner guṇaḥ saṃskārārthaḥ, evaṃ pavamānahavīṃṣy apy agner eva guṇabhūtāni. kas tatra paraspareṇa saṃbandha iti. yad uktam - ādhānasya prakaraṇe samāmnāyanta iti, yady api samāmnāyante, tathāpi prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā vākyenāgner bhavanti. kim iha vākyam? yad āhavanīye juhoti{*3/105*} tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prīto bhavatīti.
nanv āhavanīyo 'tra yāgasyādhikaraṇatvena guṇabhūtaḥ śrūyate. satyam, adhikaraṇam āhavanīyaḥ, tathāpi tv āhavanīyārtha eva yāgaḥ, prayojanavattvād āhavanīyasya niṣprayojanatvāt pavamānahaviṣām. katham eṣāṃ niṣprayojanatā? phalāśravaṇāt. kalpyaṃ phalam iti cet. satyaṃ kalpyam, agnisaṃskāras tu tatphalam, na svargaḥ, svarge kalpyamāne dvir adṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta, homāc ca [238]{*3/106*} svargo bhavati, tasya cāhavanīyenāparo 'dṛṣṭaḥ saṃskāra iti. tasmād agnyarthatā pavamānahaviṣām, naiṣām ādhānena saṃbandhaḥ. tasmān nādhāne śrūyamāṇam, pavamānahaviṣāṃ bhavitum arhati. kiṃ tarhi sarvayāgeṣu darśapūrṇamāsaprabhṛtiṣv ādhānasya pradhānabhūteṣu niveśa iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Agnyādheya</s> (fire-establishment rite), vessels of <s>vāraṇa</s> (elephant-warding) and <s>vaikaṅkata</s> (vikankata wood) are heard as both not-for-oblation and for-oblation: 'Therefore, there should be a <s>vāraṇa</s> [vessel] for use in the sacrifice, but one should not offer with it; there should be a <s>vaikaṅkata</s> [vessel] for use in the sacrifice, and one should offer with it.' And the <s>vāraṇa</s> and <s>vaikaṅkata</s> vessels have no connection with the fire-establishment [rite] itself. Why? Because of the statement 'for use in the sacrifice' — these are vessels of the sacrifice [in general]; by the sentence they override the context. There, this doubt arises: do they apply to the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations, or to all sacrifices including the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and others? What is the prima facie view? To the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations. Why? It has been stated that 'a word-meaning not possible in the principal [rite] is assigned to its subsidiary.' And since they are recorded in the <s>Agnyādheya</s> context, the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations have the status of subsidiary to it. Therefore, [they apply] to the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations — this is the prima facie conclusion.
Having arrived at this position, we say: Because of the equality of the qualities — the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations and the fire-establishment have no mutual connection. Just as the establishment of fire is a quality [i.e., subsidiary] serving the purpose of consecrating [the fire], so too the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations are qualities belonging to the fire itself. What connection do they have with each other? As for the objection that they are recorded in the context of fire-establishment — even though they are recorded there, they belong to the fire [itself] by the sentence overriding the context. What is the sentence here? 'He who offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] — by that, [the fire] becomes his, desired and pleased.'
[Objection:] But the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is heard here as a subsidiary in the capacity of the locus of the sacrifice. True, the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the locus; nevertheless, the sacrifice is indeed for the sake of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire], because the <s>Āhavanīya</s> has a purpose while the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations have no [independent] purpose. How are they purposeless? Because no fruit is heard [for them]. If one says the fruit should be postulated — true, it should be postulated, but the fruit is the consecration of the fire, not heaven. If heaven were postulated, an unseen [result] would be postulated twice: from the oblation comes heaven, and for that [fire] the <s>Āhavanīya</s> provides another unseen consecration. Therefore, the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations are for the sake of the fire; they have no connection with the fire-establishment [rite]. Therefore, what is heard in the fire-establishment [context] cannot belong to the <s>pavamāna</s> oblations. What then? They apply to all sacrifices — the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and others that are the principal [rites] of which the fire-establishment is a subsidiary.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/104: Edition cross-references: E2: 4,111; E4: 3,674; E6: 1,163} {3/105: E2,4 read 'juhvati'} {3/106: Edition cross-references: E2: 4,113; E4: 3,675; E6: 1,164}]

children.text: mithaś cānarthasaṃbandhāt // MS_3,1.23 //
children.translated_text: And because of the mutual non-connection of meanings. // MS 3,1.23 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - vārtraghnī paurṇamāsyām anūcyete, vṛdhanvaty amāv asyāyām iti{*3/107*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim anuvākyādvitvasya pradhāne niveśaḥ, utājyabhāgayor iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? pradhāna iti. kutaḥ? paurṇamāsīsamabhivyāhārāt, amāv asyāsamabhivyāhārāc ca. pradhānaṃ paurṇamāsī cāmāv asyā ca nājyabhāgau. tasmāt sākṣād vākyāt pradhānasyeti prāptam.
tatra brūmaḥ - mithaḥ saha dvābhyām anuvākyābhyāṃ na pradhānasya kāryam asti, yatra tu dva anuvākye, tatra tayor vārtraghnatā vṛdhanvattā ca vidhīyate, pradhāne caikānuvākyā, tatra dvitvaṃ vārtraghnatāṃ vṛdhanvattāṃ ca vidadhad vākyaṃ bhidyeta. ājyabhāgayos tu dve prāpte āgneyī saumī ca, tatra vārtraghnatāṃ vṛdhanvattāṃ kevalāṃ śakṣyati vidhātum. nanu pradhānagāmitve 'pi dvayoḥ pradhānayor dve anuvākye, āgneyasyāgnīṣomīyasya ceti. ucyate - ekā [239]{*3/108*} vārtraghny āgneyī, ekā saumī, tathā vṛdhanvatyai, tatra yāgneyī, sā vidhīyamānā saṃbadhyeta na saumī. amāv asyāyāṃ tāvan nāsty eva{*3/109*}, paurṇamāsyām apy agnīṣomīya eva kriyamāṇe kriyeta, tatrāpy ekadevatyā na śaknuyād devatādvitve kāryaṃ kartum. athobha agnīṣomīye prāpte iti. na, ekasya yāgasya dvābhyām anuvākyābhyāṃ prayojanam. upādeyatvena hy anuvākyā codyate, tatraikatvaṃ vivakṣitam, tena tatrāpi na dve. tasmād ājyabhāgayor niveśa iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is heard: 'The <s>vārtraghṇī</s> (victory-bringing) [invocatory verse] is recited at the full moon; the <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> (growth-endowed) [verse] at the new moon.' There the doubt arises: does the quality of having two invocatory verses (<s>anuvākyā</s>) apply to the principal offering, or to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion) offerings? What is the prima facie view? To the principal offering. Why? Because of the explicit mention of the full-moon day, and the explicit mention of the new-moon day. The full-moon and new-moon [days] pertain to the principal [offering], not to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings. Therefore, from the direct sentence, [it applies] to the principal offering — this is the prima facie view.
To this we say: Mutually — with both invocatory verses together — the principal offering has no function. But where there are two invocatory verses, there the <s>vārtraghṇī</s> and <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> qualities are enjoined. For the principal offering has a single invocatory verse; if the duality, along with the <s>vārtraghṇī</s> and <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> [qualities], were to enjoin [these for the principal offering], the sentence would be split. But for the <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings, two [invocatory verses] are already available — one for <s>Agni</s> and one for <s>Soma</s> — and there [the sentence] will be able to enjoin the <s>vārtraghṇī</s> and <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> [qualities] without complication. [Objection:] But even if assigned to the principal offerings, the two principal offerings have two invocatory verses — one for the <s>Āgneya</s> and one for the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s>. [Reply:] One <s>vārtraghṇī</s> [verse] for <s>Agni</s>, and one <s>Saumī</s> [verse] — likewise for the <s>vṛdhanvatī</s>. Of these, the <s>Āgneya</s> one, when being enjoined, would be connected, but not the <s>Saumī</s>. As for the new-moon day, there is simply no [<s>Soma</s>-related verse]; even on the full-moon day, it would apply only to the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s> [offering] when being performed. There too, being of one deity [only], it could not accomplish the function in a dual-deity [context]. [Objection:] But both [verses] are available for the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s>. [Reply:] No — for a single sacrifice has no use for two invocatory verses. For the invocatory verse is enjoined as something to be adopted, and oneness is intended there; therefore, there too [there are] not two. Hence, the assignment is to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/107: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.5.2.5} {3/108: Edition cross-references: E2: 4,115; E4: 3,681; E6: 1,164} {3/109: E2,4 read 'eva somaḥ'}]

children.text: ānantaryam acodanā // MS_3,1.24 //
children.translated_text: Sequential proximity is not an enjoining [factor]. // MS 3,1.24 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - muṣṭīkaroti, vācaṃ yacchati, dīkṣitam āvedayatīti, tathā hastāv avanenikte, ulaparājiṃ stṛṇātīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ muṣṭīkaraṇaṃ vāgyamaś cāvedanārtham, uta kṛtsnaprakaraṇe niveśa iti tathā, hastāv anejanaṃ kim ulaparājiṃ staritum, uta prakaraṇe sarvapadārthān kartum iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? hastāv anejanaṃ hastasaṃskārārtham, vāgyamaḥ puruṣasaṃskārārthaḥ, āmantrayamāṇa ekāgro bhavati, padārthān anutiṣṭhati, tena keṣāṃ keṣāṃ padārthānām ime{*3/110*} saṃskārāv ity ākāṅkṣāsti, satyām ākāṅkṣāyām ānantaryeṇa nirākāṅkṣīkaraṇam. tasmād ānantaryād āvedanārtho vāgyamo muṣṭīkaraṇaṃ ca, hastāv anejanaṃ colaparājiṃ staritum.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sarvaiḥ prakaraṇādhītaiḥ saṃbandha iti. [240]{*3/111*} kutaḥ? vākyabhedāt. kathaṃ vākyabhedaḥ? arthadvayasyābhidhānāt. na hi, dīkṣitam āvedayitum ity asminn artha āvedayatīti, na ca staritum ity asminn arthe stṛṇātīti. staraṇam api vidhīyate 'vanejanaṃ ca. muṣṭīkaraṇaṃ vāgyamaś ca vidhīyate, āvedanaṃ ca. na ca, eṣāṃ paraspareṇa kaścit saṃbandho 'sti, na ca, padārthākāṅkṣāyāṃ satyām ānantaryam ekavākyatve kāraṇaṃ bhavati, tasmāt prakaraṇadharmā evaṃjātīyakāḥ.
NOTES:
*{3/110: E1,6, E4 (v.l.); E2,4: imau}*
*{3/111: E2: 4,119; E4: 3,686; E6: 1,165}*
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'He clenches his fists (<s>muṣṭīkaroti</s>), he restrains his speech (<s>vācaṃ yacchati</s>), he announces the consecrated one (<s>dīkṣitam āvedayati</s>).' Likewise: 'He washes his hands (<s>hastāv avanenkte</s>), he spreads the <s>ulaparāji</s> [grass].' There the doubt arises: are the fist-clenching and speech-restraint for the purpose of the announcement, or do they apply to the entire context? Likewise: is the hand-washing for the purpose of spreading the <s>ulaparāji</s>, or for performing all the elements of the context? What is the prima facie view? Hand-washing serves the purpose of hand-purification; speech-restraint serves the purpose of self-purification — one who is addressing [the deity] becomes focused and performs the ritual elements. Therefore, [one asks:] for which ritual elements are these two purifications? — there is syntactic expectancy. When there is syntactic expectancy, the removal of expectancy occurs through sequential proximity (<s>ānantarya</s>). Therefore, by sequential proximity, the speech-restraint and fist-clenching are for the announcement, and the hand-washing is for spreading the <s>ulaparāji</s>.
Having arrived at this position, we say: There is connection with all the elements within the context. Why? Because of sentence-division. How is there sentence-division? Because two [distinct] meanings are expressed. For [the word] '<s>āvedayati</s>' (he announces) does not [appear] in the meaning 'for the purpose of announcing the consecrated one,' nor does '<s>stṛṇāti</s>' (he spreads) [appear] in the meaning 'for the purpose of spreading.' Spreading too is being enjoined, and hand-washing too. Fist-clenching and speech-restraint are being enjoined, and announcement too. And none of these has any mutual connection with the others. And when there is syntactic expectancy for a word-meaning, sequential proximity is not a cause for sentence-unity. Therefore, such properties belong to the [entire] context.

children.text: vākyānāṃ ca samāptatvāt // MS_3,1.25 //
children.translated_text: And because the sentences are complete. // MS 3,1.25 //

children.text: svena svena padasamūhena paripūrṇam ekaṃ vākyam, tathāparam, tathā sarvāṇi yāny udāhṛtāni. tasmād vispaṣṭam arthadvayam, vibhāge ca nirākāṅkṣatā, tena vākyabhedaḥ. ataḥ saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca{*3/112*} kṛtsne parkaraṇe niveśa iti.
children.translated_text: Each sentence is complete with its own collection of words — one sentence thus, another likewise, and so all those that have been cited. Therefore, the duality of meaning is clearly evident, and when divided, there is no syntactic expectancy. Hence, sentence-division. Therefore, because of the non-differentiation arising from conjunction, and because of the non-differentiation of the context, there is application to the entire context.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/112: Cf. MS 3.1.8}]

children.text: śeṣas tu guṇasaṃyuktaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ pratīyeta mithas teṣām asaṃbandhāt // MS_3,1.26 //
children.translated_text: The remaining [qualities], being connected with [other] qualities, should be understood as common [to all], because of the mutual non-connection among them. // MS 3,1.26 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ samāmnāyate - āgneyaṃ caturdhā karotīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim āgneye 'gnīṣomīye aindrāgne{*3/113*} ca sarvatra caturdhākaraṇam? kiṃ vāgneya eveti. kiṃ prāptam? śeṣaś caturdhākaraṇam, āgneyam iti devatāguṇasaṃyuktaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ pratīyate, agnīṣomīye 'pi syāt, aindrāgne 'pi. kutaḥ? tāv apy āgneyau, yasyāgnir devatā, anyā ca bhavati, asāv āgeyaḥ. tad yathā, yā ḍitthasya ḍavitthasya ca mātā, sā ḍavitthasya [241]{*3/114*} bhavati, evam ihāpi. yady āgneyāgnīṣomasya ca puroḍāśasya mithaḥ saṃbandho na bhavet, tata āgneya eva caturdhākaraṇaṃ vyavatiṣṭheta, bhavati tu saṃbandhaḥ, tasmād avyavasthā, yathāgneyasya mastakaṃ vibhajya prāśitram avadyatīti sarvebhyaḥ prāśitrāv adānam, evaṃ caturdhākaraṇam api.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is taught: 'He divides the <s>Āgneya</s> [cake] into four parts.' There the doubt arises: should the fourfold division [be performed] for all [cakes] — the <s>Āgneya</s>, the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, and the <s>Aindrāgna</s> — or only for the <s>Āgneya</s>? What is the prima facie view? The fourfold division is a subsidiary element; [the word] '<s>Āgneya</s>' is understood as a general [designation] connected with the deity-quality — it would apply to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> too, and to the <s>Aindrāgna</s> as well. Why? Because those too are <s>Āgneya</s> (related to <s>Agni</s>) — whatever has <s>Agni</s> as one deity along with another is also <s>Āgneya</s>. Just as a woman who is the mother of both <s>Ḍittha</s> and <s>Ḍavittha</s> is [the mother] of <s>Ḍavittha</s>, so too here. If the sacrificial cakes of both the <s>Āgneya</s> and the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [offerings are treated as mutual]...

NOTES:
[E2,4,6: caindrāgne] | [Edition page references: E2: 4,119; E4: 3,695; E6: 1,165]

children.text: vyavasthā vārthasaṃyogāl liṅgasyārthena saṃbandhāl lakṣaṇārthā guṇaśrutiḥ // MS_3,1.27 //
children.translated_text: Or there would be a restriction because of the connection with meaning; because of the connection of the indicatory mark with the meaning, the quality-scripture serves the purpose of characterization. // MS 3,1.27 //

children.text:
vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati, vyavatiṣṭheta vā caturdhākaraṇam āgneya eva, na sādhāraṇaṃ bhavitum arhati. kutaḥ? arthasaṃyogāt, agninā devatayārthenaikadevatyasya{*3/115*} saṃyogaḥ, na dvidaivatyasyāgnīṣomīyasyaindrāgnasya{*3/116*} ceti. kutaḥ? yasya hy agnīṣomau devatā, ubhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaḥ saṃkalpaḥ kriyate, tasyāgniḥ somam apekṣamāṇo devatā, na nirapekṣaḥ, yasya cāgniḥ somam apekṣamāṇo devatā, na tasmāt taddhita utpadyate, samarthānāṃ hi sa ucyate, sāpekṣaṃ cāsamartham. tasmān na taddhitāntena nirapekṣāgnidaivatyena{*3/117*} dvidevatyasyābhidhānam{*3/118*}. ato yatra nirapekṣo 'gnir devatā, tatraiva caturdhākaraṇam iti, devatāliṅgasya hi sāmartyena saṃyogo bhavati taddhitārthasya, nāsati sāmarthye.
atha yad uktam, yathā{*3/119*} prāśitrāv adānaṃ sarvebhyaḥ kriyate, evaṃ{*3/120*} caturdhākaraṇam apīti, yuktaṃ prāśitrāv adānena tatraiva{*3/121*} saṃbandhaḥ kriyate, āgneyasya prāśitram avadyatīti. kathaṃ tarhi, āgneyasya mastakaṃ vibhajyeti. ekaṃ hy etad vākyaṃ prāśitram avadyatīti, dvitīyam āgneyasya mastakaṃ vibhajyeti, tatrāgneyasya mastakād avadyatīti gamyate, anyasya mastakāt, anyasmād vety aniyamaḥ. yadi tu tatra kevalāgnidaivatyo{*3/122*} nābhaviṣyat, tadānarthakyaparihārāya dvidaivatyo{*3/123*} 'py agrahiṣyata{*3/124*}.
[242]{*3/125*} yat tu, ḍitthasya māteti, yuktaṃ tatrāvyāsaṅgi mātṛtvam, tato jāto ḍitthaḥ, etāvatā saṃbandhena, mātety ucyate, nātra kiṃcid apekṣyate. sa ca tāvāṃs tatra saṃbandho 'stīti ḍitthasya māteti yuktaṃ vacanam.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) excludes the [previous] position. The fourfold division would be restricted to the <s>Āgneya</s> alone; it should not be treated as general. Why? Because of the connection with meaning — the connection of <s>Agni</s>, as deity, with the meaning [is that of] a single-deity [offering], not of the two-deity <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> or the <s>Aindrāgna</s>. Why? For one whose deities are <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, the resolution is qualified by the distinguishing mark of both; <s>Agni</s> is its deity only in relation to <s>Soma</s>, not independently. And from one whose deity is <s>Agni</s> dependent on <s>Soma</s>, no <s>taddhita</s> [derivative suffix] is produced — for [the <s>taddhita</s>] is said [to apply] to [words that are] independently capable (<s>samartha</s>), and what is dependent (<s>sāpekṣa</s>) is incapable. Therefore, not from a <s>taddhita</s>-derivative...

children.text: arthabhidhānasāmarthyān mantreṣu śeṣabhāvaḥ syāt tasmād utpattisaṃbandho 'rthena nityasaṃyogāt // MS_3,2.1 //
children.translated_text: The subsidiary status [of mantras] would be through the capacity to express meaning; therefore, the origination-connection [arises] from the necessary conjunction with meaning. // MS 3,2.1 //

children.text:
iha mantrā udāharaṇam - bahirdevasadanaṃ dāmītyevamādayaḥ. kiṃ mukhya evābhidheye mantrāṇāṃ viniyogaḥ, uta gauṇe 'pīti. kaḥ punar mukhyaḥ ko vā gauṇa iti. ucyate - yaḥ śabdād evāvagamyate, sa prathamo 'rtho mukhyaḥ, mukham iva bhavatīti mukhya ity ucyate. yas tu khalu pratītād arthāt kenacit saṃbandhena gamyate, sa paścād bhāvāj jaghanam iva bhavatīti jaghanyaḥ, guṇasaṃbandhāc ca gauṇa iti.
yady evaṃ sarva eva mukhyaḥ, sarvo hi śabdād gamyate, yathaiva hy agnir jvalatīty ukte jvalane saṃpratyayaḥ{*3/127*}, evam evāgnir māṇavaka iti śabda evoccārite māṇavake saṃpratyayaḥ. athocyate, yasmin nirupapadāc chabdāt saṃpratyayaḥ sa mukhyaḥ, yasmin sopapadāt sa gauṇa iti. naitad yuktam. yasya hi śabdasya rūpaṃ kasyacid arthasya nimittam, sopapadasyāpi tad eva rūpam, nirupapadasyāpi. na ca śakyaṃ nimitte sati naimittikena na bhavitum. kim ataḥ? yady evam, idaṃ na śakyate vaditum - upapadād ṛte na so 'rtho bhavati, upapade tu saṃjāte so 'rthaḥ saṃjaniṣyata iti. na cāsau samudāyārthaḥ śakyate vijñātum. anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ hi vibhāgo 'vagamyate. atha, vāk-yārtho 'yam ity ucyate. naivaṃ śakyam, na hy ananvitaḥ padārtho bhavati [244]{*3/128*} vākyārthaḥ. tad evaṃ dṛśyatām - agniśabda evāyaṃ jvalanavacanaḥ, agniśabda eva māṇavakasyābhidhāteti. tasmān na gauṇo mukhya iti kaścid viśeṣaḥ. athocyate, yaḥ suṣṭhu prasiddhaḥ sa mukhyaḥ, yo manāg iva sa gauṇa iti. idam api nopapadyate, prasiddhir nāma prajñānam, na ca prajñāne kaścid viśeṣo 'sti. athocyate, yasya bahuśaḥ prayogo 'sti sa mukhyaḥ, alpaśaḥ prayujyamāno gauṇa iti. naitad evam, alpaśo 'pi prayujyamāno nāsati sāmarthye pratyāyayet. ataḥ so 'pi śabdāt pratīyata iti mukhya eva.
children.translated_text:
Here, mantras are the example — such as 'the outer seat of the gods, the binding' and similar ones. [The question is:] is the assignment (<s>viniyoga</s>) of mantras [to be] in the primary meaning alone, or in the secondary meaning as well? What is the primary [meaning] and what is the secondary? It is said: that which is understood from the word itself — that first meaning is the primary (<s>mukhya</s>); it is called <s>mukhya</s> because it is like the face (<s>mukha</s>) [i.e., foremost]. But that which is understood from the cognized meaning through some connection — that, being subsequent, is like the hindquarters (<s>jaghana</s>) and is called <s>jaghanya</s> (secondary); and because of the connection through a quality, it is called <s>gauṇa</s> (qualitative).
If so, then everything is primary, for everything is understood from words. Just as when one says 'the fire blazes,' the cognition [arises] in blazing...

children.text:
atrocyate - asty atra viśeṣaḥ, māṇavako nāgniśabdāt pratīyate. katham avagamyate? uktam - anyāyaś cānekārthatvam iti. kathaṃ na viparyayaḥ? ucyate - anādṛtyaiva māṇavakapratyayaṃ jvalanam agniśabdāt pratiyanto dṛśyante. na tv anādṛtya jvalanam{*3/129*}, mānavakam agniśabdāt pratiyanti. kuta etat? yo yo 'gnisadṛśo vivakṣyate, tatra tatrāgniśabdo niyata iti. ata eva vigatasādṛśyād ayaṃ tu dṛśyate. ato 'gnisādṛśyam asya pravṛttau nimittaṃ na ca jvalane 'pratīte tatsādrṛśyaṃ pratīyate. tasmāj jvalanasyāgniśabdo nimittam, na māṇavakasya. tasmāj jvalane mukhyo na māṇavake. evam eva tṛṇapratyayasya barhiḥśabdo nimittam, na tṛṇasadṛśapratyayasya. tad evaṃ dvaite sati mukhyaparatā śabdasya, uta gauṇaparatāpīti yukto vicāraḥ. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? mukhye gauṇe ca viniyogaḥ. kutaḥ? ubhayasya śakyatvād ubhayam api barhiḥśabdena śakyate pratyāyayitum, tṛṇaṃ ca tṛṇasadṛśaṃ ca, tṛṇaṃ sākṣāt, tṛṇasadṛśaṃ tṛṇapratyayena. yac ca nāma darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ sādhanabhūtena barhiḥśabdena śakyate pratyāyayitum, tat sarvaṃ pratyāyayitavyam, vinigamanāyāṃ hetvabhāvāt.
[245]{*3/130*} api caivam āśrīyamāṇe pūṣādyanumantraṇādīni darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ notkṛṣyante{*3/131*}, tatraiva gauṇenābhidhānena prakṛtāṃ devatām abhivadiṣyanti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - mukhya eva viniyoktavyo mantro na gauṇa iti. kutaḥ? ubhayāśakyatvāt, prakaraṇe hi samāmnānāt pradhānenaikavākyatām upaiti. tatraitad āpatati yac chaknuyād anena mantreṇa sādhayitum, tathā sādhayed iti. sa cāsāv arthābhidhānasaṃyogāc chaknoty upakartum, na gauṇam arthaṃ śakyoty abhidhātum, tasmān na gauṇe viniyogaḥ.
nanu mukhyapratyayāc chakyate gauṇaḥ pratyāyayitum. satyam etat, mukhyapratyāyanenaivāsya prayojanavattā nirvṛtteti na gauṇaṃ prati viniyoge kiṃcit pramāṇam asti. mukhye viniyogena tv ānarthakyaṃ parihriyate, parihṛta ānarthakye na gauṇābhidhānam āpatati. na hy anabhidhāya mukhyam, gauṇam abhivadati śabdaḥ. ataḥ pramāṇābhāvān na gauṇe viniyujyeta.
api ca gauṇasya pratyāyane sāmarthyād bahavo 'bhyupāyāḥ prāpnuvanti, sāmarthyaṃ ca śabdaikadeśa ity uktam - arthād vā kalpanaikadeśātvād iti{*3/132*}, tatra mantre niyogato gauṇaṃ prati viniyujyamāna upāyāntaram, vinā pramāṇena bādhyeta. mantrāmnānaṃ pramāṇam iti cet. na tasyopāyāntaranivṛttau sāmarthyam asti. nanu mukhye 'pi viniyujyamānsyaiṣa eva doṣaḥ. nety ucyate - yadi mukhye 'pi na viniyujyeta, naiva pradhānasyopakuryāt tatra cāsyotpattir anarthikaiva syāt. tasmād asti gauṇe mukhye ca viśeṣaḥ. api ca yo gauṇe mantraṃ viniyuṅkte, sa vaktavyaḥ - kim arthaṃ mukhyaṃ pratyāyayasi [246]{*3/133*} iti. sa ced brūyāt - nānyathā gauṇapratyayo 'stīti, pratibrūyād enam - anye 'pi gauṇapratyayasyābhyupāyāḥ santīti. atha sa evam abhiyuktaḥ pratibrūyāt -mukhyapratyayo 'pi pākṣiko 'bhyupāya iti, brūyād enam - na tarhi niyogato gauṇe viniyojanīyaḥ, yadā gauṇapratyayāya mukham upādatte, tadaitad āpatitaṃ bhavati, mukhya eva viniyoga iti. arthena ca pratītena prayojanam, na pratyāyakena mantreṇa, ato 'nyenāpy upāyena gauṇaḥ praty-āyayitavyaḥ, na sa eva mantra ādartavyaḥ. athāpi mantreṇa pratyāyakena prayojanaṃ syāt, tathāpi mukhyapratyāyanenaiva nirvṛttaṃ prayojanam iti natarāṃ gauṇe viniyujyeta. tasmān mukhyagauṇayor mukhye kāryasaṃpratyaya iti siddham.
children.translated_text: To this it is said: there is a distinction here. A boy (<s>māṇavaka</s>) is not understood from the word <s>agni</s> (fire). How is this known? It has been stated: 'it is improper for [a word] to have multiple meanings.' How is there no reversal [of primary and secondary]? It is said: people are seen understanding blazing from the word <s>agni</s> while disregarding the cognition of a boy. But they do not understand a boy from the word <s>agni</s> while disregarding blazing. How [do we know] this? Wherever something resembling fire is intended, the word <s>agni</s> is invariably [used]. And precisely when the resemblance is absent, this [secondary usage] is observed [to fail]. Therefore, resemblance to fire is the cause of [the word's] application [to a boy]; and without the cognition of blazing, that resemblance is not cognized. Therefore, blazing...

NOTES:

children.text: saṃskārakatvād acodite na syāt // MS_3,2.2 //
children.translated_text: Because [the mantra] has the nature of a sanctifier, [it] should not [be applied] when there is nothing to be sanctified and no injunction. // MS 3,2.2 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - pūṣādyanumantraṇādīnām utkarṣo na bhaviṣyatīti, yuktas teṣām utkarṣaḥ, saṃskārako hi mantraḥ, so 'sati saṃskārye 'narthaka iti yatrārthavāṃs tatra nāyayiṣyate. na ca kaścid doṣo bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — that there would be no transference of mantras such as the <s>Pūṣan</s>-invocation and the like — their transference is proper. For the mantra is a sanctifier; when there is nothing to be sanctified, it is purposeless. Therefore, it will be brought to [the context] where it is meaningful. And there will be no defect.

children.text: vacanāt tv ayathārtham aindrī syāt // MS_3,2.3 //
children.translated_text: But because of [Vedic] statement, [the mantra] addressed to <s>Indra</s> (<s>aindrī</s>) would be [used] contrary to [its] meaning. // MS 3,2.3 //

children.text:
agnau śrūyate - niveśanaḥ saṃgamano vasūnām ity aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti{*3/134*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim indrasyopasthānaṃ kartavyam, uta gārhapatyasyeti. kutaḥ punar gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata ity evaṃ vispaṣṭe vacane saṃśaya iti. ucyate, [247]{*3/135*} yad dhi{*3/136*} vākyenopasthānaṃ{*3/137*} tat stutivacanena saṃskaraṇaṃ na samīpasthānamātram, na ca, aindreṇa mantreṇāgner abhidhānaṃ śakyate kartum. ato gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti na gārhapatyārtham upasthānam etad iti jāyeta śaṅkā - gārhapatya upasthānārtho bhaved iti, tādṛśaś ca śabdo nāsti, tṛtīyāntaḥ saptamyanto vā. tasmād vicāraḥ - katham upapannaṃ bhavatīti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sāmarthyād indropasthānam, aśakyatvāc ca gārhaptyopasthānasya. kathaṃ dvitīyā vibhaktir iti cet. avivaksitepsitārthā vā saṃbandhamātrapradhānā. yad vopasthānaviśeṣaṇaṃ saṃbandhād gārhapatyaśabdaḥ. tasmād gārhapatyaviśiṣṭam upasthānam indrārthaṃ kartavyam iti. gārhapatyaś ca deśena viśiṃṣyān mukhyam eva kāryaṃ mantrāṇām.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - vacanāt tv ayathārtham aindrī syāt. naitad astīndrārtham upasthānam iti, ayathārtham aindrī syāt. kutaḥ? vacanasāmarthyāt, vacanam idaṃ bhavati, aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti, gārhapatye dvitīyā vibhaktiḥ prādhānyam āha, kim iva vacanaṃ na kuryāt, nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ. tasmād gārhapatyārtham upasthānam.
children.translated_text: In [the rite of] the sacred fires, it is heard: 'The establisher, the assembler of the <s>Vasus</s>' — 'one approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] with [a mantra] addressed to <s>Indra</s> (<s>aindrī</s>).' There the doubt arises: should the worship (<s>upasthāna</s>) be directed toward <s>Indra</s>, or toward the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire]? Why should there be any doubt when the statement 'one approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s>' is so clear? It is said: the worship that is [enjoined] by the sentence is a sanctification through a laudatory expression, not merely being in proximity. And the designation of <s>Agni</s> by a mantra addressed to <s>Indra</s> is not possible...

NOTES:
