children.text: guṇād vāpy abhidhānaṃ syāt saṃbandhasyāśāstrahetutvāt // MS_3,2.4 //
children.translated_text: Or the designation would be through a quality, because the connection [between word and meaning] is not caused by scripture. // MS 3,2.4 //

children.text:
atrāha nanv etad uktam - naindreṇa mantreṇa gārhapatyopasthānaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, vacanād bhaviṣyati. āha - na vacanaśatenāpi śakyam etat, indraśabdenāgninaṃ pratyāyayed iti bruvan vihanyeta, yathāgninā siñced iti{*3/138*}, udakena dīpayed iti, na hi śāstrahetukaḥ śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandho bhavati. nityau 'sau lokato 'vagamyata ity uktam - autpa[248]{*3/139*}ttikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandha iti{*3/140*}. nanu śabdalakṣaṇo 'pi bhavati śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ kṛtrimaḥ, yathā devadatto yajñadatta iti. bhavati kaścit, yatra saṃbandhasya vidhāyakaṃ vākyaṃ bhavati, na tv etad vākyaṃ śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhasya vidhāyakam, gārhapatyasyendraśabdo nāmeti, kathaṃ tarhi siddhasaṃbandhenendraśabdena gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti. na ca śakyate paraśabdena paro vaditum. kim atra vacanaṃ kariṣyati?
atrocyate - guṇād vāpy abhidhānaṃ syāt saṃbandhasyāśāstrahetutvād iti, yady api nedaṃ vākyaṃ śabdārthasaṃbandhasya vidhāne hetubhūtam, tathāpy anenendraśabdena śakyaṃ kartum - gārhapatyābhidhānam. kutaḥ? guṇasaṃyogād gauṇam idam abhidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati, bhavati hi guṇād apy abhidhānam, yathā siṃho devadattaḥ, agnir māṇavaka iti. evam ihāpy anindre gārhapatya indraśabdo bhaviṣyati, asti cāsyendrasādṛśyam{*3/141*}, yathaivendro yajñasādhanam, evaṃ gārhapatye 'pīti. athavā indrater aiśvaryakarmaṇa indro bhavati, bhavati ca gārhapatyasyāpi svasmin kārya īśvaratvam. tasmād indraśabdena yaḥ pratyāyate 'rthaḥ sa pratītaḥ sādṛśyād gārhapatyaṃ pratyāyayiṣyati, aiśvaryād vā pratyāyayiṣyatīti na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: To this, [the objection:] was it not said that the <s>Gārhapatya</s> worship cannot be done with a mantra addressed to <s>Indra</s>? [Reply:] It is said: it will be [done] because of the [Vedic] statement. [Objection:] Not even by a hundred statements can this be [done] — one who says 'by the word <s>Indra</s> one should make [the hearer] cognize <s>Agni</s>' would be contradicted, just as [one who says] 'one should sprinkle with fire' or 'one should illuminate with water.' For the connection between word and meaning is not caused by scripture. It is eternal and known from the world — as stated: 'The connection of the word with its meaning is innate (<s>autpattika</s>).'

NOTES:
[E2,4 omit iti] | [Edition page references: E2: 4,166; E4: 4,21; E6: 1,170] | [MS 1.1.5] | [E2,4,6: asti tu cāsyendrasādṛśyam]

children.text: tathāhvānam apīti cet // MS_3,2.5 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, the invocation too — if [you say so]. // MS 3,2.5 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatredaṃ samāmnāyate - haviṣkṛd ehi [249]{*3/142*} iti trir avaghnann āhvayatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim eṣa mantro 'vahantiṃ pratyupadiśyate, uta hantir asya kālaṃ lakṣayatīti. kathaṃ hantiṃ pratyupadiśyate? kathaṃ vā kālaṃ lakṣayet? yady evaṃ saṃbandhaḥ kriyeta - haviṣkṛd ehīty avaghnann iti, tato hantiṃ pratyupadiśyate, athāvaghnann āhvayatīti, tato 'sya kālaṃ lakṣyatīti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? tathāhvānam api, yathaindrī gārhapatyaṃ pratyupadiśyate, evam eṣa mantro hantiṃ pratyupadiśyate. evaṃ śrutir anugṛhītā bhavati, itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt, hantikālasya mantrasya ca saṃbandho bhavet, na hanter mantrasya. evaṃ ca satyāhvayatīty ayam anuvādaḥ, āhvānaṃ karoti, yo hy ehīti brūte sa āhvayati, tatra kenacid guṇena mantro hantiṃ pratyāyayiṣyati, tasmān nāhvāne viniyoktavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Here are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites. There, this is taught: 'Come, <s>Haviṣkṛt</s> (preparer of the oblation)' — 'striking thrice, he invokes.' There the doubt arises: is this mantra instructed with reference to the pounding (<s>avahanti</s>, i.e., the pestle/mortar operation), or does the striking (<s>hanti</s>) indicate its [appropriate] time? How is it instructed with reference to the pounding? And how would it indicate the time? If the connection is construed thus — 'Come, <s>Haviṣkṛt</s>, [addressed to the one who is] striking' — then it is instructed with reference to the pounding. But if 'while striking, he invokes' — then it indicates the time...

NOTES:
[Edition page references: E2: 4,134; E4: 4,23; E6: 1,171]

children.text: na kālavidhiś coditatvāt // MS_3,2.6 //
children.translated_text: It is not a time-injunction, because [the mantra] has [already] been enjoined. // MS 3,2.6 //

children.text: naitad asti - hantiṃ pratyupadiśyata iti. kiṃ tarhi? kālalakṣaṇā syāt. kutaḥ? trir āhvayatīti tritvam atra vidhīyate, yady asminn eva vākye mantro vidhīyeta, anekaguṇavidhānād vākyaṃ bhidyeta. tasmān naivam abhisaṃbandha evam avaghnann iti. kathaṃ tarhi, avaghnann āhvayatīti. nanv asminn api pakṣe mantro vidhīyate kālaś ca, tatra sa eva doṣo bhavet. neti brūmaḥ, avahananakāla evārthena haviṣkṛd āhvātavyā, tatrāyam eva saṃbandho 'nūdyate. kevalā tu trir āvṛttir vidhīyate. yat tu kālalakṣaṇārthaḥ śabda iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, laukikī hi lakṣaṇā. mantro 'pi ca rūpād evāhvāne prāptaḥ, so 'py anūdyata eva, coditaś ca vākyāntareṇāvaghātaḥ śaknoti kālaṃ lakṣayitum. tasmād āhvāne viniyoktavya iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that it is instructed with reference to the pounding. Rather, it would be a time-indication. Why? The number three is enjoined here — 'he invokes thrice.' If the mantra were enjoined in this very sentence, the sentence would be split due to the injunction of multiple qualities. Therefore, the connection is not thus — 'while striking, he invokes.' But what then? [The connection is:] 'while striking, he invokes.' [Objection:] But in this position too, the mantra and the time are being enjoined — the same defect would apply. [Reply:] No, we say. At the very time of the pounding, by implication, the invocation '<s>Haviṣkṛt</s>, come'...

children.text: guṇābhāvāt // MS_3,2.7 //
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of the quality. // MS 3,2.7 //

children.text: idaṃ padottaraṃ sūtram{*3/144*}. atha kasmān na guṇād avahantiṃ brūte? haviṣkaroti hy avahantiḥ, tasmād dhaviṣkṛt. kim evaṃ bhaviṣyati? rūpād evāvahantau mantre prāpte kevalaṃ trir āvṛttim eva vakṣyati na bhaviṣyati vākyabheda iti. atrocyate - guṇābhāvād gauṇam abhidhānam avahantau na saṃbhavatīti. na hy asāv āhūto 'smīty avagacchati, tatrādṛṣṭārtham āhvānaṃ syāt. yajamānasya patnyāṃ haviṣkṛti dṛṣṭārtham āhvānam. tasmān na hantimantra iti.
children.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> follows the [previous] topic. Now, why does [the mantra] not refer to the pounding through the quality? For the pounding operation (<s>avahanti</s>) indeed prepares the oblation (<s>haviṣ</s>), hence [it is] <s>haviṣkṛt</s> (oblation-preparer). What would [the consequence] be? Since the mantra is already obtained for the pounding operation through [its] form, [the text] would merely state the threefold repetition — there would be no splitting of the sentence. To this it is said: because of the absence of the quality, secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) designation is not possible for the pounding operation. For it [the pestle] does not understand 'I have been invoked'; therefore, the invocation would serve a transcendent (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) purpose. [The invocation is] observed [to be directed] toward the sacrificer's wife, [who is] the <s>haviṣkṛt</s> (oblation-preparer)...

children.text: liṅgāc ca // MS_3,2.8 //
children.translated_text: And because of the indicatory mark. // MS 3,2.8 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca bhavati - vāg vai haviṣkṛd vācam evaitad āhvayatīti{*3/145*}, na ca vāco 'vahantinā sādṛśyam asti, asti tu yajamānasya patnyā, sā hi strī, vāg iti ca strīliṅgaḥ śabdaḥ, avahantis tu na strī na pumān na napuṃsakam iti. nanv avahanter api strīliṅgaḥ śabdo 'sti, kriyeti. atra brūmaḥ - na niyogato 'vahanteḥ strīliṅgaḥ śabdaḥ, puṃliṅgo 'pi tasyāsti, avaghāta iti. napuṃsakasiṅgo 'pi, karmeti. api ca, patnyāḥ svarūpeṇa sādṛśyam, avahanteḥ pararūpeṇa śabdena. tasmāt patnyāṃ haviṣkṛti liṅgam anurūpataraṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: There is also an indicatory mark: 'Speech is the <s>Haviṣkṛt</s>; he indeed invokes Speech.' And there is no resemblance between speech and the pounding operation; but there is [resemblance] with the sacrificer's wife — for she is a woman, and the word <s>vāc</s> (speech) is of feminine gender; the pounding operation, however, is neither feminine, nor masculine, nor neuter. [Objection:] But there is also a feminine-gender word for the pounding — [namely,] <s>kriyā</s> (action). To this we say: the pounding does not necessarily have a feminine-gender word; it also has a masculine-gender [word] — <s>avaghāta</s> (striking). And a neuter-gender [word] too — <s>karma</s> (action).

NOTES:
[Cf. ŚPBr 1.1.4.11]

children.text: vidhikopaś copadeśe syāt // MS_3,2.9 //
children.translated_text: And the injunction would be disrupted in the instruction. // MS 3,2.9 //

children.text: avahantimantre saty asmin mantre vidhyantarakopaḥ syāt. apahataṃ rakṣa ity avahanty apahatā yātudhānā ity avahantīti. tatra pakṣe 'bhāvān nityavac chrūtir upadhyeta. tasmād avaghnann [251]{*3/146*} iti kālalakṣaṇārtha iti. mantro 'py ahvānārtha iti{*3/147*}.
children.translated_text: If this mantra were [assigned to] the pounding, another injunction would be disrupted. [The mantras] 'The evil has been struck away' for the pounding, and 'The <s>Yātudhānas</s> have been struck away' for the pounding — [these already exist]. In [one] position, because of the non-existence [of a separate assignment], the scripture would be construed as if it were permanent [i.e., always applying]. Therefore, 'while striking' serves the purpose of indicating the time. And the mantra serves the purpose of invocation.

NOTES:
[Edition page references: E2: 4,138; E4: 4,32; E6: 1,172] | [E2,4,6 omit: mantro 'py ahvānārtha iti]

children.text: tathotthānavisarjane // MS_3,2.10 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, the rising and the dismissal. // MS 3,2.10 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - uttiṣṭhann anvāha, agnīd agnīn vihara iti. tathā - vrataṃ kṛṇuteti vācaṃ visṛjatīti{*3/148*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim utthānaṃ vāgvisarjanaṃ ca prati mantrayor upadeśaḥ, uta kālārthaḥ saṃyoga iti. atra pūrvādhikaraṇyāyo 'tidiśyate. yas tatra pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, sa iha pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. yas tatra siddhāntaḥ, sa iha siddhāṇtaḥ. agnīd agnīn ity evam uttiṣṭhann anvāheti, vrataṃ kṛṇutety evaṃ vācaṃ visṛjatīti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. lakṣaṇābhāvāt, uttiṣṭhann anvāheti siddhānte saṃbandhaḥ. vrataṃ kṛṇutety ucyamāne vācaṃ visṛjatīti. vākyena pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, liṅgena siddhāntaḥ.
yady api ca śakyate, utthānakriyāgnīd agnīn vihareti vaktum, utthānenāgnir idhyate, vahniś ca vihriyata iti. vrataṃ kṛṇuteti ca vāgabhidhānam. tathāpy adṛṣṭārthaṃ vacanaṃ bhavatīti na mantrayor utthānavisarjanārthatā kalpyeta. kalpyamānāyāṃ ca mantrāntaraṃ vihitaṃ bādhyeta - yāḥ paśūnām ṛṣabho vāca iti. api cotthānavāgvisargau prati mantrau vidhīyamānāv adṛṣṭārthau syātām, preṣaṇe tu dṛṣṭhārthau. tal{*3/149*} lakṣaṇaivātra nyāyyā.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'Rising, he recites after [the rite]: O <s>Āgnīdh</s>, remove the fires.' Similarly: 'Make the vow' — 'he dismisses speech.' There the doubt arises: is the instruction of the mantras directed toward the rising and the dismissal of speech, or is the connection for the purpose of [indicating] the time? Here, the principle from the preceding topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) is extended. Whatever was the prima facie view there is the prima facie view here. Whatever was the established conclusion there is the established conclusion here. 'O <s>Āgnīdh</s>, [remove] the fires' — thus 'rising, he recites after'; 'Make the vow' — thus...

children.text: sūktavāke va kālavidhiḥ parārthatvāt // MS_3,2.11 //
children.translated_text: The <s>sūktavāka</s> is either a time-indicator, because it serves another's purpose. // MS 3.2.11 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharatīti{*3/151*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sūktavākaḥ prastaraprakaraṇaṃ pratyupadiśyate, uteyaṃ kālalakṣaṇeti. tad ucyate - kālalakṣaṇeti. kutaḥ? sūktavākasya devatāsaṃkīrtanārthatvāt, prastaraprakaraṇaṃ ca pratyaśakteḥ, prastarasya ca srugdhāraṇārthatvāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is heard: 'He strikes the <s>prastara</s> (grass-bundle) with the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn of praise).' There a doubt arises: is the <s>sūktavāka</s> being taught with reference to the <s>prastara</s> offering, or is it a time-indicator? It is said: it is a time-indicator. Why? Because the <s>sūktavāka</s> serves the purpose of reciting the names of deities, and because it is incapable [of serving] the <s>prastara</s> offering, and because the <s>prastara</s> serves the purpose of being held by the sacrificial ladle.

NOTES:
[{3/151: Cf. <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.4.10.1}]

children.text: upadeśo vā yājyāśabdo hi nākasmāt // MS_3,2.12 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] a teaching [i.e., mantra for the offering], for the word <s>yājyā</s> (offering-verse) is not without reason. // MS 3.2.12 //

children.text: upadeśo vā prastaraprakaraṇaṃ prati mantrasya syāt, evaṃ śrutivihito 'rtho bhavati, sūktavākeneti karaṇavibhaktisaṃyogāt, itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt, sūktavākena lakṣaṇena prastaraṃ prahared iti. evaṃ ca kṛtvā yājyā śabda upapanno bhavati, sūktavāka eva yājyā, prastara āhutir iti.
children.translated_text: Or the teaching would be that the <s>mantra</s> [applies] to the <s>prastara</s> offering. Thus the meaning would be enjoined by scripture. Because of the connection with the instrumental case-ending in '<s>sūktavākena</s>' (by the <s>sūktavāka</s>), [it denotes an instrument]; otherwise there would be secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — [meaning] 'he should strike the <s>prastara</s> at the time indicated by the <s>sūktavāka</s>.' And having done so, the designation <s>yājyā</s> (offering-verse) is justified — the <s>sūktavāka</s> itself is the <s>yājyā</s>, and the <s>prastara</s> is the oblation.

children.text: sa devatārthas tatsaṃyogāt // MS_3,2.13 //
children.translated_text: It [the <s>sūktavāka</s>] serves the purpose of [naming] the deity, because of the connection with that [deity]. // MS 3.2.13 //

children.text:
yad uktam - devatāsaṃkīrtane sūktavākaḥ samarthaḥ, na prastaraprakaraṇa iti. ucyate - na{*3/152*},
devatāvacanaḥ{*3/153*} parkaraṇena saṃbadhyate, prakaraṇaṃ hi yajiḥ, māntravarṇiko devatāvidhiḥ, evam abhisaṃbandhaḥ. agnir idaṃ havir ajuṣatāvīvṛdhata ity{*3/154*} evaṃ devatām anukramya, āśāste 'yaṃ yajamāna ity{*3/155*} uktvā, idam idam āśāsta iti ca yad anena haviṣāśāste tad asya syād [253]{*3/156*} iti{*3/157*} prastaraṃ havir nirdiśati, agnyādīṃś ca devatāviśeṣān, tena praharatir yajatiḥ. evaṃ sūktavākena prastaraḥ prahartuṃ śakyate, yadi praharatir yajatiḥ, agnyādidevatākaś ca. tasmāt sūktavākasya haratisaṃyogo 'pi devatārthatā ghaṭata eva. yady agnir idaṃ havir ajuṣatāvī vṛdhata ityevamādy eva śrūyeta. na, āśāste 'yaṃ yajamāna ityevamādīny aparāṇi, tato 'gnyādaya eveṣṭā nāntaritā ity eva paryavasitaṃ vākyaṃ bhavet. yatas tu khalv āśāste 'yaṃ yajamāna ityevamādīny aparāṇi śrūyante, teneha paryavasānam, agnyādayaḥ puroḍāśādibhir iṣṭāḥ, aparaṃ tu yajamāna āśāste. tad anena prastareṇa prāpnuyād iti.
nanu satsv apy eteṣu devatāsaṃkīrtana eva paryavasyet, puroḍāśādibhir iṣṭā agnyādayaḥ, tata eva yajamāna āyur ādīny apy āśāsānaḥ prāpnuyād iti. ucyate - ubhayathā saṃbandhe sati praharaṇe viniyoktavyaḥ, liṅaṃ ca na bādhitaṃ bhaviṣyati, vākyaṃ cānugrahīṣyata iti.
athavāgnir idaṃ havir ajuṣateti prastara eva havir nidiśyate. evam idam iti saṃnihitavacanam upapannaṃ bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text:
As to what was said — the <s>sūktavāka</s> is capable of reciting the names of deities, not of [serving] the <s>prastara</s> offering — it is replied: No.
The deity-naming [portion] is connected with the offering context, for the context is the sacrifice (<s>yaji</s>), and the deity-injunction follows from the <s>mantra</s>-words — thus [there is] a connection. [The <s>sūktavāka</s> says:] '<s>Agni</s> has relished this oblation, has been magnified' — thus reciting the deity in sequence, [and then] 'This sacrificer desires' — having said this, 'he desires such and such,' and 'may that which he desires through this oblation be his' — [here] it designates the <s>prastara</s> as the oblation, and <s>Agni</s> and the other specific deities; thereby the striking (<s>praharati</s>) is [equivalent to] the sacrifice (<s>yajati</s>). Thus, through the <s>sūktavāka</s> it is possible to strike the <s>prastara</s> [as an offering], if the striking is [equivalent to] the sacrifice, and has <s>Agni</s> and the others as deities. Therefore, even the connection of the <s>sūktavāka</s> with striking is compatible with its serving the deity-naming purpose. If only '<s>Agni</s> has relished this oblation, has been magnified' and such [phrases] were heard [without the rest] — no, [for] 'This sacrificer desires' and such other [phrases follow]. Therefore the completed statement is not merely that <s>Agni</s> and the others alone are being propitiated without intervening [statements]. Since indeed 'This sacrificer desires' and such other [phrases] are heard, the conclusion here [is]: <s>Agni</s> and the others have been propitiated through the <s>puroḍāśa</s> and other [offerings]; further, the sacrificer desires [more] — may he obtain that through this <s>prastara</s> [offering].
But even with these [phrases] present, might it not culminate in deity-recitation alone — [namely,] <s>Agni</s> and the others have been propitiated through the <s>puroḍāśa</s> and other [offerings], and from that alone the sacrificer would obtain long life and other [desired things]? It is replied: When there is a connection with both [interpretations], it should be assigned to the striking, and [thus] the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) will not be overridden, and the [Vedic] sentence will be upheld.
Alternatively, in '<s>Agni</s> has relished this oblation,' the <s>prastara</s> itself is designated as the oblation. Thus the demonstrative word 'this' (<s>idam</s>), referring to what is proximate, will be justified.

children.text:
pratipattir iti cet, sviṣṭakṛdvad ubhayasaṃskāraḥ syāt // MS_3,2.14 //{*3/158*}
atha srugdhāraṇe viniyuktasya prastarasya prakaraṇaṃ pratiprattir ity ucyate. tatra prativacanam -sviṣṭakṛdvad etat syād iti, yathā, ijyārthāt puroḍāśāt, vacanaprāmāṇyāt sviṣṭakṛd ijyate, yāgaś ca sa bhavati, pratipādyate ca puroḍāśaḥ, evaṃ [254]{*3/159*} pratipādyetaiva hi prastaraḥ, yāgaś ca nirvartyata iti na doṣaḥ. pratipādyamāno 'pi hi tyajyate. pratyakṣataḥ pratipādyate, vacanād ijyāṃ sādhayatīty evaṃ gamyate. tasmāt sūktavākaḥ praharatimantra iti.
children.translated_text:
If [you say it is merely] a disposal (<s>pratipatti</s>) [of the <s>prastara</s>], then, like the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>), there would be a dual function (<s>ubhayasaṃskāra</s>). // MS 3.2.14 //
Now, if it is said that the assignment to the <s>prastara</s> offering is merely a disposal of the <s>prastara</s>, which has [already] been assigned to the function of being held by the ladle — to that, the reply is: It would be like the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. Just as the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, [originally] intended for the sacrifice, is [also] offered as <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> by the authority of the [Vedic] word, and that [<s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>] is [indeed] a sacrifice, and the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is [both] disposed of and [sacrificed] — similarly, the <s>prastara</s> too would be disposed of, and a sacrifice would also be accomplished — so there is no fault. For even while being disposed of, it is [also] offered. It is disposed of directly [as a physical act], and by the [Vedic] word it accomplishes the sacrifice — this is how it is understood. Therefore, the <s>sūktavāka</s> is the <s>mantra</s> for the striking [i.e., offering of the <s>prastara</s>].

children.text:
kṛtsnopadeśād ubhayatra sarvavacanam // MS_3,2.15 //{*3/160*}
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharatīti śrūyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ kṛtsnaḥ sūktavākaḥ prayoktavyaḥ, kṛtsno 'māvāsyāyām, uta yathāsāmarthyaṃ niṣkṛṣya yathāyathaṃ prayoga iti. tad ucyate - ubhayatra sarvavacanam iti. kutah? kṛtsno hi mantraḥ sūktavāka ity ucyate, sa padenāpi vinā, sūktavāko na syāt, tatra sūktavākena na prahṛtaṃ bhavet. tasmād ubhayatra kṛtsnaḥ sūktavāko vaditavyaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Because of the teaching of the whole, the complete [<s>sūktavāka</s>] is to be recited at both [the full-moon and new-moon rites]. // MS 3.2.15 //
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is heard: 'He strikes the <s>prastara</s> with the <s>sūktavāka</s>.' There a doubt arises: should the entire <s>sūktavāka</s> be recited at the full-moon [rite], and the entire [<s>sūktavāka</s>] at the new-moon [rite] — or should [the verses] be extracted according to their relevance and recited respectively? It is said: the complete [<s>sūktavāka</s>] is to be recited at both. Why? For the entire <s>mantra</s> is called '<s>sūktavāka</s>'; without even a single word, it would not be the <s>sūktavāka</s>, and then [one could not say] that [the <s>prastara</s>] was struck 'with the <s>sūktavāka</s>.' Therefore, the entire <s>sūktavāka</s> is to be recited at both [rites].

children.text: yathārthaṃ vā śeṣabhūtasaṃskārāt // MS_3,2.16 //
children.translated_text: Or [the recitation should be] according to the [relevant] meaning, because the preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is subsidiary. // MS 3.2.16 //

children.text: ye paurṇamāsīdevatātāvācinaḥ śabdāḥ, te paurṇamāsyāṃ prayoktavyāḥ, nāmāvāsyāyām. ye 'māvāsyādevatāvācinaḥ, te 'māvāsyāyām, na paurṇamāsyāṃ. śeṣabhūtam arthaṃ saṃskurvanto mantrā upakurvanti, nānyathety uktam. tasmād ye yatropakurvanti, te tatra prayoktavyā iti na kṛtsnaḥ paurṇamāsyām, na kṛtsnaś cāmāvāsyāyām iti.
children.translated_text: Those words that refer to the deities of the full-moon [rite] should be recited at the full-moon [rite], not at the new-moon [rite]. Those that refer to the deities of the new-moon [rite] should be recited at the new-moon [rite], not at the full-moon [rite]. <s>Mantras</s> that consecrate the subsidiary meaning assist [the rite] — and not otherwise, as has been stated. Therefore, those that assist in a particular [context] should be recited there — so the complete [<s>sūktavāka</s>] is not [recited] at the full-moon, nor the complete [<s>sūktavāka</s>] at the new-moon [rite].

children.text: vacanād iti cet // MS_3,2.17 //
children.translated_text: [If you say it should be complete] because of the [Vedic] word — // MS 3.2.17 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - vacanam idaṃ bhaviṣyati, sūktavākena praharati [255]{*3/161*} iti. tatra padenāpy ūnena na sūktavākena prahṛtaṃ bhavet, kṛtsnasya hi sūktavākasyopadeśa iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — this will be the [Vedic] word: 'He strikes with the <s>sūktavāka</s>.' There, even with a single word missing, [the recitation] would not be 'with the <s>sūktavāka</s>,' for the teaching is of the complete <s>sūktavāka</s>.

children.text: prakaraṇāvibhāgād ubhe prati kṛtsnaśabdaḥ // MS_3,2.18 //
children.translated_text: Because of the non-division of the context, the word 'complete' (<s>kṛtsna</s>) applies to both [rites together]. // MS 3.2.18 //

children.text:
ubhe paurṇamāsyamāvāsye prati eṣa kṛtsnaśabdaḥ, ubhayoḥ prakaraṇāt, ubhayor asau kṛtsna ucyate, avayave 'vayava iti.
naitad evam, na hi sāpekṣāṇām itikartavyatayā saṃbandhaḥ. na hītikartavyataitad viśiṣṭā śrūyate, itikartavyatāviśiṣṭās tv ete gamyate. kutaḥ? na hītikartavyatāṃ prati karmaṇi vidhīyaṇte, phalaṃ prati teṣāṃ vidhiḥ, itikartavyatā tu karmaṇāṃ vidhīyate, tatra saṃnidhānāviśeṣāt, kasya kiṃ vidhīyate, kasya neti na gamyate viśeṣaḥ. sādhanatvena ca sarveṣāṃ nirdeśād itikartavyatāyāḥ saṃnidhānāc ca, vacanāc cāsya{*3/162*}, prakaraṇaliṅgasyāviśeṣāt, ekaikasya kṛtsnaṃ prakaraṇaṃ nirākāṅkṣasya, na sahāyam apekṣamāṇasya. tasmād ekaikaṃ prati kṛtsnaḥ sūktavāka upadiśyate. sa vibhāge 'pi pradhānānām, kṛtsna eva prayoktavya iti yāni yatrānarthakāni padāni, tāny api tatra prayoktavyāny adṛṣṭāya bhaviṣyanti, sūktavākena praharatīti vacanāt, nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ, guṇena vā kenacid abhidhānaṃ tāsāṃ devatānāṃ nirvartayiṣyantīti.
atrocyate, naitad evam. uktam - mukhyam eva kāryaṃ mantrāṇām, na gauṇam iti{*3/163*}, saṃskārārthatvād votkarṣo{*3/164*} nyāyyaḥ, na gauṇam abhidhānam iti. kas tarhi kṛtsnasaṃyogasya samādhir ucyata iti. eṣa samādhiḥ, na hy etad ekaṃ vākyam, yaḥ [256]{*3/165*} kṛtsnaḥ sūktavākaḥ, bahūny etāni vākyāni, yeṣāṃ pradhānadevatābhidhāyīni padāni madhye, sādhāraṇāni tantrapadāni purastād uccāryante, tathā parastāt. yathā - agnir idaṃ havir ajuṣatāvī vṛdhata mahojyāyokṛtāgnīṣomāvidaṃ havir ajuṣetām avī vṛdhetām ityevamādīni{*3/166*}. teṣāṃ purastāt tantram - yathā, idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīti, parastād api yathā, asyāmṛdhed iti. tāny etāni sarvāṇi sūktavacanena sūktavākaśabdaṃ labhyante. na ca teṣāṃ samudāyaḥ kiṃcid arthaṃ vadati. tasmān na samudāyaḥ sūktavākaḥ, na ca sākṣāt sādhanam, sūktavākasāmānyasyaikatvāt, sūktavāko vartata ity ekavacanaṃ bhavati. sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharatīti tu yena kenacit sūktavākena prahriyamāṇe yathāśrutaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati. tasmāt samudāyaḥ sūktavākaḥ. yat tv amāvāsyādevatāvācīni padāni, na paurṇamāsyāṃ prayujyante, na tatra sūktavākaśabdo bādhyate, prakaraṇaṃ tatra liṅgena bādhitam, tac ca nyāyyam eva. tasmāt paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ ca vibhajya sūktavākaḥ prayoktavya iti.
children.translated_text:
The word 'complete' (<s>kṛtsna</s>) applies to both — the full-moon and the new-moon [rites] together — because of the context of both. It is called 'complete' with reference to both, [meaning] a part in each part.
This is not so — for those that are mutually dependent do not have a connection through the subsidiary ritual procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>). For this [<s>sūktavāka</s>] is not heard as qualified by the subsidiary ritual procedure; rather, it is understood as qualified by the subsidiary ritual procedure. Why? For [the parts of the <s>sūktavāka</s>] are not enjoined with respect to the subsidiary ritual procedure of the ritual actions — they are enjoined with respect to the fruit; and the subsidiary ritual procedure is enjoined for the ritual actions. There, because of the non-differentiation of proximity, it cannot be determined which is enjoined for which and which is not — no distinction is understood. And because all are designated as instruments, and because of the proximity of the subsidiary ritual procedure, and because of the [Vedic] word for this, and because of the non-differentiation of the context-and-indicatory-mark — each individual [part] has a complete context that is self-sufficient, not requiring an associate. Therefore, for each individual [rite], the complete <s>sūktavāka</s> is taught. Even when the principal [elements] are divided, the complete [<s>sūktavāka</s>] alone should be recited — and those words that are purposeless in a particular [rite] should also be recited there for the sake of unseen [merit] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), because of the [Vedic] word 'he strikes with the <s>sūktavāka</s>.' There is no excessive burden on the [Vedic] word, and by some subsidiary [connection] the recitation will accomplish the naming of those deities.
To this it is said: This is not so. It has been stated — the primary function alone is the purpose of <s>mantras</s>, not the secondary — and because of the purpose of consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>), [only] the elevated [function] is proper, not the secondary naming. What then is the resolution of the connection with 'complete'? This is the resolution: This is not a single sentence — that which constitutes the complete <s>sūktavāka</s>. These are many sentences, whose words naming the principal deities are in the middle, and the common <s>tantra</s> (shared) words are recited before, and likewise after. For example: '<s>Agni</s> has relished this oblation, has been magnified, greatly powerful, having done [the rite]'; '<s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> have relished this oblation, have been magnified' — and so on. Before them, the shared [formula]: for example, 'This, O <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth)'; and after, for example, 'May he prosper in this.' All these are called '<s>sūktavāka</s>' by the word '<s>sūktavacana</s>' (hymn-recitation). And their aggregate does not express any [single] meaning. Therefore, the aggregate is not the <s>sūktavāka</s>, nor is it directly the instrument — because of the oneness of the <s>sūktavāka</s> as a general [category], the singular expression 'the <s>sūktavāka</s> is recited' is used. But in 'he strikes the <s>prastara</s> with the <s>sūktavāka</s>,' when the striking is performed with any one <s>sūktavāka</s>, the [Vedic] word is fulfilled as heard. Therefore, the aggregate is the <s>sūktavāka</s>. As for the words referring to the deities of the new-moon [rite] not being recited at the full-moon [rite] — there the word '<s>sūktavāka</s>' is not overridden; the context is overridden by the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and that is entirely proper. Therefore, at the full-moon and new-moon [rites], the <s>sūktavāka</s> should be recited having been divided [according to the relevant deities].

children.text: liṅgakramasamākhyānāt kāmyayuktaṃ samāmnānam // MS_3,2.19 //
children.translated_text: From the indicatory mark, sequence, and designation, the codified teaching (<s>samāmnāya</s>) is appropriate for the <s>kāmya</s> (desire-motivated) rites. // MS 3.2.19 //

children.text:
iha kāmyayājyānuvākyākāṇḍam udāharaṇam - indrāgnī rocanā divaḥ{*3/167*}, pravarṣaṇibhyaḥ{*3/168*}, indrāgnī navatiṃ puraḥ{*3/169*}, ślathad vṛtram{*3/170*} ityevamādyā ṛcaḥ. aparā api kāmyā iṣṭayaḥ - aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet, yasya sajātā viyāyuḥ, aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped bhrātṛvyavān, agnaye vaiśvānarāya dvādaśakapālaṃ [257]{*3/171*} nirvaped rukkāmaḥ, agnaye vaiśvānarāya dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet sapatnam abhidroṣyann ityevamādyāḥ. tad etā yājyānuvākyāḥ prati saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ yāvat kiṃcid aindrāgnaṃ karma, tatra sarvatrānenaindrāgnena yājyānuvākyāyugalena bhavitavyam, utaitasyām evaindrāgnyām iṣṭau kāmyāyām iti. evaṃ vaiśvānarīyayor yājyānuvākyayoḥ, evaṃ sarvatra.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? yāvat kiṃcid aindrāgnaṃ vaiśvāvarīyam agnīṣomīyaṃ jātavedasaṃ ca sarvatraitā yājyānuvākyā bhaveyuḥ. kutaḥ? liṅgāt. nanu kramasamākhyāne viśeṣake bhaviṣyataḥ. satyam, tathāpi kramaṃ samākhyāṃ ca śaknoti liṅgaṃ bādhitum iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - liṅgakramasamākhyānāt tāsv eva kāmyāsv etā yājyānuvākyā iti gamyate, ya eva hi liṅgakrama eṣāṃ karmaṇām, sa evāsāṃ yājyānuvākyānām, tena tāsām eva tāḥ śeṣabhūtā iti.
nanu liṅgaṃ balavattaram ity uktam. satyam etat, iha tu samākhyā balīyasī, na hy etāḥ samākhyānād ṛta eṣāṃ kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ prāpnuvanti, na bhinnadeśānāṃ karmaṇām. kutaḥ? samākhyām antareṇāsām ṛtāṃ yājyānuvākyātvam eva na vijñāyate, kuto bhinnadeśānāṃ karmaṇāṃ yājyānuvākyā bhaviṣyantīti, yā caiṣāṃ samākhyā, sā kāmyānām eva yājyānuvākyātvam ācaṣṭe na sarveṣām. yadi samākhyā nādriyate, yājyānuvākyātvam evaiṣāṃ na bhavati, yady ādriyate, tadā kāmyānām eva. evaṃ hi tat samākhyāyate - kāmyayājyānuvākyākāṇḍam iti.
atha kim artham ubhayam upadiśyate - liṅgakramād iti, samākhyānād iti ca. asti tatra pāthikṛtīyaṃ vrātapatīyaṃ ca karma, sāmidhenīkāryam apy asti, yājyānuvākyākāryam api. yadi liṅgakramād ity etāvad evocyate, sāmidhenīkārye 'pi liṅgena [258]{*3/172*} tāsāṃ viniyogaḥ syāt. atha kim arthaṃ liṅgakramau vyapadiśyete? sarvā yājyānuvākyākārya eva viniyujyeran, sāmidhenīṣu viniyogo na syāt. atha punaḥ samākhyānāl liṅgakramāc ca nirvṛtte yājyānuvākyākārye, sāmidhenīṣu viniyogaḥ siddho bhavati, yathāgnivāruṇyā iṣṭeḥ krame 'tīte saumāraudrīṇām anāgate, manor ṛcas tāḥ sāmidhenīṣu dhāyyā ity ucyante, tathā - pṛthuyājās tam saṃbādha iti dve dhāyye kalpyete. tasmād ubhayaṃ vyapadeṣṭavyam iti.
children.translated_text:
Here, the section on <s>kāmya-yājyā-anuvākyā</s> (sacrificial and invitatory verses for desire-rites) is the example — '<s>Indrāgnī rocanā divaḥ</s>' {*3/167*}, '<s>pravarṣaṇibhyaḥ</s>' {*3/168*}, '<s>Indrāgnī navatiṃ puraḥ</s>' {*3/169*}, '<s>ślathad vṛtram</s>' {*3/170*} — these and similar are the <s>ṛc</s> verses. And there are other <s>kāmya</s> (desire-rite) offerings: 'He should offer an <s>aindrāgna</s> [cake] on eleven potsherds — he whose kinsmen have separated'; 'He should offer an <s>aindrāgna</s> [cake] on eleven potsherds — he who has a rival'; 'He should offer to <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> [a cake] on twelve potsherds [257]{*3/171*} — he who desires radiance'; 'He should offer to <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> [a cake] on twelve potsherds — he who is about to attack an enemy' — and so on. With regard to these <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> (sacrificial and invitatory) verses, there is a doubt: should every <s>aindrāgna</s> rite everywhere employ this <s>aindrāgna</s> pair of <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses, or only in this specific <s>aindrāgnī</s> desire-rite? Similarly for the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> pair of <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses, and similarly everywhere.
What is the prima facie view? For every <s>aindrāgna</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, and <s>Jātavedasa</s> [rite] everywhere, these <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses should apply. Why? Because of the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). [Objection:] But the sequence (<s>krama</s>) and the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>), being specific, will [restrict them]. [Reply:] True, but even so, the indicatory mark can override the sequence and the designation. When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: from the indicatory mark, the sequence, and the designation, it is understood that these <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses belong to those very <s>kāmya</s> (desire-) rites alone. For whatever is the indicatory-mark-sequence of these rites, that is also [the indicatory-mark-sequence] of these <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses; therefore, the latter are subsidiary to the former alone.
[Objection:] But it was said that the indicatory mark is stronger. [Reply:] True, but here the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) is stronger. For these [verses] do not apply to these <s>kāmya</s> rites apart from the designation, nor to rites in different contexts. Why? Without the designation, their very status as <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses is not known — how then could they be <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses for rites in different contexts? And the designation of these proclaims their status as <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> only for the <s>kāmya</s> rites, not for all. If the designation is disregarded, their very <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> status does not hold; if it is respected, then [they apply] only to the <s>kāmya</s> rites. For thus it is designated: 'the section on <s>kāmya-yājyā-anuvākyā</s>.'
Now, why are both mentioned — 'because of the indicatory mark and the sequence' and 'because of the designation'? There are the <s>Pāthikṛtīya</s> and <s>Vrātapatīya</s> rites, which include both <s>sāmidhenī</s> hymns and <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> verses. If only 'because of the indicatory mark and the sequence' were stated, then through the indicatory mark, [the verses] would be assigned even in <s>sāmidhenī</s> [258]{*3/172*} contexts. But why are the indicatory mark and the sequence mentioned? So that [the verses] may be assigned exclusively in contexts requiring <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s>, and the assignment to <s>sāmidhenī</s> hymns would not occur. Moreover, when the designation and the indicatory-mark-sequence have established [the assignment] in the <s>yājyā-anuvākyā</s> context, the assignment to <s>sāmidhenī</s> hymns is settled — just as in the case of the <s>Agnivāruṇī</s> offering, when the sequence [of hymns] has passed and that of the <s>Saumāraudrī</s> [hymns] has not yet arrived, the verses of <s>Manu</s> are said to be placed among the <s>sāmidhenī</s> hymns — similarly, '<s>pṛthuyājās tam saṃbādha</s>' — two [verses] are determined as placed [among the <s>sāmidhenī</s>]. Therefore, both must be mentioned.

children.text: adhikāre ca mantravidhir atadākhyeṣu śiṣṭatvāt // MS_3,2.20 //
children.translated_text: And in [matters subject to] a governing rule (<s>adhikāra</s>), the mantra-injunction [applies] to those not bearing that designation, because [the mantra] is taught [for them]. // MS_3,2.20 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - āgneyyā agnīdhram{*3/173*} upatiṣṭhate{*3/174*}, aindryā sadaḥ, vaiṣṇavyā havir dhānam{*3/175*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ prakṛtābhir evaṃliṅgavatībhir upasthātavyam, uta dāśatayībhya evaṃliṅgā āgamayitavyā iti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam. prakaraṇe ca mantro liṅgena vidhīyamāno dāśatayībhya evāgamayitavyaḥ, āgneyītyevamādibhir hi śakyā dāśatayo 'bhivaditum. yaś cāyaṃ prakṛtaḥ, sa kāryāntare viniyuktaḥ, nehāpy upadeśam arhati. upadiṣṭopadeśo hi na nyāyya evaṃjātīyakasya. kathaṃ jātīyakasya? yaḥ kasmiṃścid viśeṣeṇopadiṣṭaḥ, nāsau sāmānyena liṅgenānyātropadeśam arhati. katham? yadi tal liṅgaṃ tasya lakṣaṇatvena, tataḥ sa viśiṣṭo lakṣyeta [259]{*3/176*} yenānenaivaṃliṅgenaitat karotīti, tato nopadiṣṭo bhavati. athopadiśyate - evaṃliṅgena karotīti, tato na lakṣyate, tenopadiṣṭasyaivaṃjātīyakasyaivaṃjātīyakaḥ punar upadeśo na nyāyyaḥ. tasmād dāśatayā liṅgavanto mantrā grahītavyāḥ.
nanu prakaraṇasāmarthyataḥ prakṛtā grahītuṃ nyāyyāḥ. nety ucyate, liṅgaṃ hi prakaraṇād balīyaḥ. āha, virodhe sati liṅgena prakaraṇaṃ bādhyeta, na caitayor virodhaḥ, na vayaṃ prakaraṇam anujighṛkṣantaḥ prakṛtaṃ liṅgavantam upādadānā liṅgam upabādhemahi{*3/177*}. yadi tu prakṛtaṃ viliṅgam upadademahi{*3/178*}, tato bādhemahi liṅgam. ubhayaṃ saṃpādayiṣyāmaḥ prakaraṇaṃ liṅgaṃ ca. naitad evam, liṅgena pratyayo bhavati, dāśatayenāpi kartavyam iti, dāśatayo 'pi hy āgneyīśabdena śakyante vaditum, sa pratyayo liṅgajanito yan mithyeti kalpyate, tat prakaraṇānurodhāt. sa cet prakaraṇam anurudhyate, mithyeti kalpyate, atha nānurudhyate samyag iti, tasmād virodhaḥ. virodhe ca prakaraṇadaurbalyam.
ucyate - tal liṅgavattānenopasthānenānugrahītavyā, na dāśatayī mantravyāktiḥ, sā ca prakṛte mantra upādīyamāne niravaśeṣā upāttā bhavati, dāśatayāṃ punar mantravyaktāv upādīyamānāyāṃ prakaraṇād yā mantravyaktiḥ prāpnoti, sā bādhitā bhavati, asati virodhe. na ca, iha liṅgaprakaraṇayor virodhaḥ, prakaraṇād vyāktiḥ pratīyate, liṅgāt sāmānyam, anyā ca vyaktiḥ, anyat sāmānyam. tasmāt prakṛto liṅgavān upādeya iti. ucyate, satyam evam etat prakṛta upādīyamāne prakaraṇaṃ na bādhitaṃ bhavati, liṅgam apy anugṛhītam, liṅgajanitas tu pratyayaḥ kaścin mithyeti kalpito bhavati. nanu vyaktir apadārthaḥ, kathaṃ{*3/179*} vyaktāv anupādīyamānāyāṃ pratyayo bādhyeta? ucyate - etad eva na [260]{*3/180*} vijānīmo liṅgavattātrāṅgaṃ na veti. kiṃ tu tad dhitarnirdeśo 'yam, tatra devatāyā mantro lakṣyate, mantravyaktir hi sādhanam, na sāmānyaṃ nāma kiṃcid aparam, devataivātra sāmānyam, yayāsādhanaṃ{*3/181*} lakṣayitavyam. na ca gamyate viśeṣaḥ - ayam asau mantro nāyam asāv iti, anavagamyamāne viśeṣe sarve talliṅgā grahītavyā iti, dāśatayām api mantravyaktau bhavati pratyayaḥ, sa prakaraṇānurodhena bādhyetety anyāyyam. evaṃ sati na dāśataya evopādātavyā bhavanti, prakṛtam apy upādadīran. nanv etad uktam, kāryāntare prakṛtasyopadeśo nāsāv arthāntara upadekṣyata iti. ucyate, na niyogataḥ sa evārthāntare vartate, sa cānyaś ca sāmānyena liṅgena. naivaṃ sati kiṃcid duṣyati. nanv etad duṣyati - nobhayam anugṛhītaṃ bhavati liṅgaṃ prakaraṇaṃ ca. satyam, nānugṛhītaṃ bhavati, kiṃ tv ananugrāhyam eva prakaraṇaṃ liṅgapratyayaviruddhatvāt. api ca na liṅgaṃ prakaraṇaṃ cānugrahītavyam iti, tatparicchinne pravṛttir bhavati, yad avagamyate - etat phalavad iti. tatra pravartate. kim ato yady evam? etad ato bhavati, na liṅgam anugṛhītaṃ kvacid ity aparasmiṃs tatparicchinne na pravṛttir bhavitum arhati. tasmād dāśatayo grahītavyā iti gamyate.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'With an <s>Āgneyī</s> [verse] one approaches the <s>Agnīdhra</s> [fire] {*3/173*}' {*3/174*}; 'with an <s>Aindrī</s> [verse, one approaches] the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall)'; 'with a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> [verse, one approaches] the <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation-repository) {*3/175*}.' There the doubt arises: should one approach with the very [mantras] already prescribed that bear such indicatory marks, or should [mantras] bearing such marks be obtained from the <s>daśatayī</s> (collection of ten)?'
What is the prima facie view? When a mantra in the [present] context is being enjoined through the indicatory mark, [mantras] should be obtained precisely from the <s>daśatayī</s>. For the <s>daśatayī</s> [collections] can be invoked by [words such as] '<s>Āgneyī</s>' and the like. And the [mantra] that is already prescribed has been assigned to another purpose — it does not deserve to be instructed here again. For re-instruction of something already instructed is improper for one of this kind. Of what kind? One who has been instructed in one [place] with a specific [assignment] — that [mantra] does not deserve re-instruction elsewhere through a general indicatory mark. How? If that indicatory mark serves as an identifying mark for it, then it would be identified as 'this one with such a mark performs this [function]' — and thus it is not [freshly] instructed. But if it is instructed — '[the priest] performs [the worship] with [a mantra] bearing such a mark' — then it is not identified [as the previously assigned one]. Therefore, for something of this kind that has already been instructed, a further instruction of the same kind is improper. Hence, mantras bearing the indicatory mark should be taken from the <s>daśatayī</s>.
[Objection:] But from the force of the context, it is proper to take the prescribed [mantra]. [Reply:] No, it is said — for the indicatory mark is stronger than the context. [Objection:] The context would be overridden by the indicatory mark [only] when there is a conflict, but there is no conflict between them. We, wishing to honor the context, while adopting the prescribed [mantra] that bears the indicatory mark, would not be overriding the indicatory mark {*3/177*}. But if we were to instruct the prescribed [mantra] without the [matching] indicatory mark {*3/178*}, then we would override the indicatory mark. We shall satisfy both — the context and the indicatory mark. [Reply:] This is not so. The indicatory mark generates the cognition that [the mantra] should be used from the <s>daśatayī</s> as well — for the <s>daśatayī</s> [mantras] too can be invoked by the word '<s>Āgneyī</s>' — and the cognition generated by the indicatory mark would have to be imagined as false, in deference to the context. If [the cognition] defers to the context, it is imagined as false; but if it does not defer, it is true — therefore there is a conflict. And when there is conflict, the context is weaker.
It is said: That indicatory-mark-possessing worship should be assisted, not the <s>daśatayī</s> mantra-instance. And when the prescribed mantra is adopted, that [assistance] is completely obtained; but when the <s>daśatayī</s> mantra-instance is adopted, the mantra-instance that would be obtained from the context is overridden — [this is problematic] in the absence of conflict. And here there is no conflict between the indicatory mark and the context: from the context a [particular] instance is cognized; from the indicatory mark, a general [class] — and 'instance' is one thing, and 'general' is another. Therefore, the prescribed [mantra] bearing the indicatory mark should be adopted. It is said: True, this is so — when the prescribed [mantra] is adopted, the context is not overridden, and the indicatory mark too is honored; but some cognition generated by the indicatory mark is imagined as false. [Objection:] But an instance is not a [separate] referent — how can the cognition be overridden when the instance is not adopted? [Reply:] This is precisely what we do not know [259]{*3/180*} — whether possessing the indicatory mark here is a subsidiary element or not. Rather, this is a <s>dhitarnirdeśa</s> (denotation statement): there the mantra is identified by the deity. For the mantra-instance is the instrument, and there is no other [thing called] 'general' — the deity alone is the general here, by which the instrument is to be identified. And the specific [identity] is not ascertained — 'this is that mantra, not that other one.' When the specific [identity] is not ascertained, all [mantras] bearing that indicatory mark should be taken — and even in the <s>daśatayī</s> mantra-instance, there is a cognition [of applicability]. That [cognition] being overridden in deference to the context would be improper. This being so, the <s>daśatayī</s> [mantras] alone are not [exclusively] to be adopted; the prescribed [mantra] too may be adopted. [Objection:] But was this not said — that the prescribed [mantra], having been assigned to another purpose, should not be instructed in a different context? [Reply:] It is said: it is not [the case] that necessarily only that [prescribed mantra] operates in the other context — rather, both that one and another [do so] through the general indicatory mark. Nothing goes wrong with this. [Objection:] But this is wrong — both the indicatory mark and the context are not honored. [Reply:] True, [the context] is not honored; but the context is precisely not to be honored, because it conflicts with the cognition from the indicatory mark. Moreover, it is not [the case] that both the indicatory mark and the context must be honored — the engagement arises in what is delimited by that [factor], where one understands: 'this is fruitful.' There one engages. What follows from this? From this it follows that since the indicatory mark is not honored somewhere [i.e., in some other context], the engagement should not occur in another [context] delimited by that [factor alone]. Therefore, it is understood that the <s>daśatayī</s> [mantras] should be taken.

children.text: tadākhyo vā prakaraṇopapattibhyāṃ // MS_3,2.21 //
children.translated_text: Or [the mantra] bearing that designation [should be used], because of the context and logical reasoning. // MS_3,2.21 //

children.text: tadākhyo jyotiṣṭomasamākhyātaḥ{*3/182*} eva grahītavyaḥ. kutaḥ? prakaraṇopapattibhyām, prakṛto hy asau, prakṛtapratyayaś ca nyāyyaḥ. katham? na jyotiṣṭomaṃ prati mantrasya vyāpāravidhānam upapadyate, prāptatvād eva. vyāpāraviśeṣavidhānaṃ tūpapadyate, aprāptatvād vyāpāraviśeṣasya, anapekṣya ca prakaraṇaṃ dāśataye vidhīyamāne vākyaṃ bhidyeta. upasthānaṃ ca kuryāt. tac caivaṃ liṅgeneti.
children.translated_text: The one bearing that designation — the one designated by [the name of] the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> {*3/182*} — should be taken. Why? Because of the context and logical reasoning. For it is [already] prescribed, and the cognition [arising] from what is prescribed is proper. How? A mantra-injunction specifying the [general] function with respect to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is not logically tenable, since [the function] is already obtained. But the injunction of a specific function is logically tenable, since the specific function is not [yet] obtained. And if, disregarding the context, [the mantra] were to be enjoined for the <s>daśatayī</s>, the sentence would be split. And one should perform the worship. And that [worship is to be done] 'with [a mantra] bearing such an indicatory mark.'

children.translated_text: And the instruction would be purposeless because of the absence of connection with something fruitful; for worship is not [independently] fruitful. // MS_3,2.22 //

children.text: nanu ca prakaraṇāj jyotiṣṭomasyopakārakaṃ syāt. yady upasthānajyotiṣṭmasaṃbandho vivakṣyeta, tadopasthānaṃ jyotiṣṭome upadiśyeta, prakaraṇāt tenaikavākyatām iyāt. yadā tu khalūpasthānasya mantrasaṃbandho vivakṣyate sarvopasthāneṣu,tadā mantraḥ prāpnoti, prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā. na prakaraṇaṃ viśeṣakaṃ bhavitum arhati, ubhayasaṃbandhe vākyabhedaḥ. asmatpakṣe na punar ayaṃ doṣaḥ, yenāgneyenaindreṇa vā jyotiṣṭome vyāpāraḥ kriyate, tena upasthānavyāpāraviśeṣaḥ tadā jyotiṣṭomiko vidhīyate, anyat sarvam anūdyata iti na doṣo bhavati. athavā, agnīdhrahavir{*3/184*} dhānasadaḥ saṃbandhamātraṃ vidhīyate, upatiṣṭhata ity ayam anuvādaḥ, anena mantreṇāgnīdhram{*3/185*} upatiṣṭhata iti samāsīdatīty arthaḥ. tasmāt prakṛtā mantrā evaṃjātīyakā upādātavyā iti.
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But from the context, it could be a subsidiary of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. [Reply:] If the connection of the worship with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is intended, then the worship would be instructed in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, and from the context it would form a single sentence with it. But when the connection of the worship with the mantra is intended — [applying] to all worships — then the mantra is obtained, overriding the context. The context cannot serve as a restricting factor — [for] in the case of connection with both, the sentence would be split. In our position, however, this defect does not arise: the [mantra] by which — whether <s>Āgneyī</s> or <s>Aindrī</s> — the function is performed in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, by that same [mantra] the specific function of worship is then enjoined as pertaining to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; everything else is restated — and so there is no defect. Alternatively, [the text] enjoins merely the connection with the <s>Agnīdhra</s> [fire], the <s>Havirdhāna</s> {*3/184*} [repository], and the <s>Sadas</s> (assembly hall); '<s>upatiṣṭhate</s>' (he approaches) is a restatement — 'with this mantra one approaches the <s>Agnīdhra</s> {*3/185*}' means 'one draws near.' Therefore, the prescribed mantras of this kind should be adopted.

children.text: yad apy uktam upadiṣṭā hi te prakṛtāḥ kāryantara iti. tad ucyate, uktottaram etat. api ca na kenacin nopadiṣṭāḥ{*3/186*}, sarve vācāstoma āśvine śasyamāne sūrye 'nudyati, tena na prakṛte kaścid viṣeśaḥ. tasmāt prakṛtasyaiva grahaṇam.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'they are instructed [only] for the basic (<s>prakṛta</s>) [context], [not for] another purpose' — to that it is said: this has already been answered. Moreover, they are not instructed by anyone [for an exclusive context alone] — all [mantras apply] in the <s>Vācastoma</s> [and] when the <s>Āśvina</s> [rite is being] recited [and] the sun does not rise; therefore, there is no specific [restriction to] the basic context. Hence, it is the basic [context] itself that is [to be] adopted.

children.translated_text: Through the indicatory mark and the designation, the <s>anuvāka</s> (Vedic section) serves the purpose of the drinking (<s>bhakṣa</s>). // MS 3,2.24 //

children.text:
bhakṣamantraḥ śrūyate - bhakṣe hi mā viśa dīrghāyutvāya śaṃtanutvāya rāyaspoṣāya varcase suprajāstvāya. ehi vaso purovaso priyo me hṛdo 'sy aśvinos tvā bāhubhyāṃ sadhyāsam. nṛcakṣasaṃ tvā deva soma sucakṣā avakhyeṣam. hinva me gātrā harivo gaṇān me mā vitītṛṣaḥ, śivo me saptarṣīn upatiṣṭhasva mā me 'vāṅ nābhimatigāḥ mandrābhibhūtiḥ ketur yajñānaṃ vāg juṣāṇā somasya tṛpyatu, vasumad gaṇasya rudramad gaṇasyādityavad gaṇasya somadevate matividaḥ prātaḥsavanasya mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya tṛtīyasavanasya gāyatracchandasas triṣṭupchandaso jagacchandaso 'gnihuta{*3/188*} indrapītasya narāśaṃsapītasya pitṛpītasya madhumata upahūtasyopahūto bhakṣayāmītyevamādiḥ{*3/189*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ kṛtsna eṣo 'nuvāko bhakṣaṇe viniyojanīyaḥ, uta kaścid asyāvayavo 'nyatrāpīti.
kiṃ prāptam? liṅgasamākhyānābhyāṃ bhakṣārthatānuvākasya, sarvo 'nuvāko bhakṣaṇe viniyojanīyaḥ. kutaḥ? bhakṣayāmīty eṣa śabdo vyaktaṃ bhakṣaṇe viniyojanīyaḥ, bhakṣaṇam eṣa śaknoti vaditum, nānyat kiṃcit. anyāni cāsya padāni bhakṣaṇaviśeṣaṇavacanāny eva, yatra yatra bhakṣayāmīti, tatra tatra prayujyante.
nanu ehi vaso ityevamādi sadhyāsam ity evam antaṃ grahaṇārtham, svena padasamūhena parasparākāṅkṣiṇaikārtham, vibhinnaṃ bhakṣaṇavākyāt. nṛcakṣasam ityevamādy avakhyeṣam ity evam antam avekṣaṇavacanam. hinva me gātrā hariva ityevamādi ca [263]{*3/190*} mā me vāṅ nābhimatigā ity evam antaṃ samyag jaraṇārtham. tad bahutvād arthānām, bahūni vākyāni. katham etac chakyaṃ vadituṃ sarvam idam ekaṃ vākyaṃ bhakṣaṇe viniyujyata iti.
ucyate - sarvāṇy etāni bhakṣaṇaviśeṣaviśeṣaṇānīty uktam. āha, evam api bhidyeta vākyaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyāṇāṃ yugapad vacanāsaṃbhavāt. ucyate - na viśeṣaṇāni vivakṣiṣyāmaḥ, viśeṣaṇair grahaṇāvekṣaṇādibhir viśiṣṭa eko 'rtho vivakṣyate. naivaṃ samyag bhavati, viśeṣaṇavacanānām avivakṣitasvārthavacanatā, bhakṣaṇaviśeṣaṇaparatā ceti, lakṣaṇayā tu gamyate. śrutilakṣaṇāviṣaye ca śrutir nyāyyā, na lakṣaṇā, tasmān naikaṃ vākyam iti.
atrocyate - yady apy amī grahaṇādayo bahavo 'rthā gamyante, na tu sarva īpsitā iti, bhakṣaṇam evaikaṃ pratyāyayitavyam. tad dhi śrutam, viśeṣaṇāny aśrutāni, na taiḥ pratītaiḥ prayojanam, prayojanaṃ ca yāvataḥ padasamūhasyaikam, tāvad ekaṃ vākyam. tasmād viśiṣṭabhakṣaṇārtham etad ekaṃ vākyam iti bhakṣaṇe viniyoktavyam. samākhyānaṃ ca bhavati - bhakṣānuvāka iti, kṛtsnaś cānuvāko nāvayavaḥ.
nanu ca samākhyā laukikaḥ śabdaḥ kathaṃ vaidikam aṅgaṃ niyaṃsyatīti. yady api laukikaḥ, tathāpy anādiḥ tasyānuvākena saṃbandhaḥ. kim ato yady evam? etad ato bhavati, bhakṣaṇasamabhivyāhṛtam anuvākaṃ brūte, samabhivyāhāraś ca sati saṃbandhe bhavati, yathā pācako lāvaka iti samabhivyāhārāt saṃbandham anumāsyāmahe. āha nānumānagamya evaṃjātīyakeṣv aṅgabhāvaḥ, vidhānād evāvagamyate, nānyathā, na ca samākhyā vidhātrī. atrocyate - samākhyā saṃbandhinau buddhau saṃnidhim upaneṣyati, prayogavacano vidhāsyatīti. tasmāt kṛtsno 'nuvāko bhakṣaṇe viniyoktavya iti.
children.translated_text: The drinking mantra (<s>bhakṣamantra</s>) is heard: 'Enter me for drinking, for longevity, for health, for increase of wealth, for splendor, for good offspring. Come, O <s>Vasu</s>, foremost <s>Vasu</s>, dear to me, you are [dear to] my heart; may I sit with you by the two arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>. O divine <s>Soma</s>, viewer of men, with good sight I have beheld you. Invigorate my limbs, O <s>Hari</s> (tawny one); do not pass by my companies. Be benign; attend upon the seven <s>Ṛṣis</s> for me; do not descend below my navel. The inspiring, overpowering, luminous [word], the banner of sacrifices — may speech, delighting, be satisfied with <s>Soma</s>. Of the troop endowed with wealth, of the <s>Rudra</s>-...

children.text: tasya rūpopadeśābhyām apakarṣo 'rthasya coditatvāt // MS_3,2.25 //
children.translated_text: The withdrawal [of some portions from drinking] is [established] through form and instruction, because the meaning [of those portions] has been enjoined [elsewhere]. // MS 3,2.25 //

children.text:
naitad evaṃ kṛtsno 'nuvāko bhakṣaṇe viniyujyata iti. rūpād grahaṇavākyaṃ grahaṇe viniyujyeta, ehītyevamādi sadhyāsam ity evam antam. nṛcakṣasam ityevamādi cāvakhyeṣam ity evam antaṃ darśane. kutaḥ? mukhyārtham evaṃ tad vākyaṃ bhavati, itarathā lakṣaṇārthatā syāt, mukhyārthatā ca nyāyyā na lakṣyārthatā.
ucyate - viśeṣaṇānām abhidhāne, na kiṃcid asti prayojanam ity uktam. atrocyate - naivaitāni viśeṣaṇāni, pṛthag evaitāni grahaṇādīni svaiḥ svair vākyair ucyanta iti. kutaḥ? asti hi taiḥ prayojanam, coditāni hi tāni, kānicit tu pṛthagvākyaiḥ, kānicid arthaprāptāni, tāny avaśyaṃ prakāśayitavyāni. tāni prakāśayiṣyanty etāni vākyāni. rūpaṃ caiṣāṃ tatprakāśanasāmarthyam, ato nānārthatvān naikaṃ vākyam ucyate. nanu bhakṣaṇavākyaśeṣī bhavitum apy eṣāṃ rūpam iti. ucyate - bāḍham asti rūpam, na tu tadviśeṣaṇāny etāni kalpyante. kasya hetor adṛṣṭārthāni tathā bhavanti? uktair anuktair vā viśeṣaṇais tāvān eva so 'rthaḥ, itarathā grahaṇādīni prakāśayiṣyanti, tathā dṛṣṭārthāni bhaviṣyanti. tasmād rūpopadeśābhyām apakrṣo bhavet keṣāṃcid atreti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — that the entire <s>anuvāka</s> is assigned to the drinking. Through [its] form, the sentence about taking (<s>grahaṇa</s>) would be assigned to the taking — [the portion] beginning with 'come' and ending with 'may I sit.' [The portion] beginning with 'viewer of men' and ending with 'I have beheld' [would be assigned] to the seeing. Why? Thus the sentence has a primary meaning; otherwise, it would have a secondary (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) meaning. And primary meaning is proper, not secondary meaning.
It is said: in the expression of the qualifiers, there is no purpose — this has been stated. To this it is said: these are not [mere] qualifiers...

children.text: guṇābhidhānān mandrādir ekamantraḥ syāt tayor ekārthasaṃyogāt // MS_3,2.26 //
children.translated_text: Because of the expression of a quality, [the portion] beginning with <s>mandrā</s> would be a single mantra; because of the connection of those two with a single purpose. // MS 3,2.26 //

children.text:
bhakṣānuvāke śrūyate - mandrābhibhūtiḥ ketur yajñānāṃ vāgju[265]{*3/192*}ṣāṇā somasya tṛpyatu. vasu-mad guṇasya somadevate matividaḥ prātaḥsavanasya gāyatrachandaso 'gnihuta{*3/193*} indrapītasya madhumata upahūtasyopahūto bhakṣayāmīti{*3/194*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ mandrādiḥ tṛpyatv ity evam anta eko mantraḥ, vasumad gaṇādir aparaḥ, uta mandrādir bhakṣayāmy anta eka eva mantra iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? dvau mantrau, dvau hy etāv arthau, anyā tṛptir anyad bhakṣaṇam, tato 'rthabhedād vākyabhedaḥ. tad uktam - tasya rūpopadeśābhyām apakarṣo 'rthasya coditatvād iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - guṇābhidhānān mandrādir ekamantraḥ syād iti, tṛptir bhakṣaṇāviśeṣaṇatvenābhidhīyata iti{*3/195*}. bhakṣayāmi vāk tarpsyatīti.
nanu tṛpyatv ity eṣo 'nyaḥ śabdaḥ, anyaś ca tarpsyatīti, eṣā bhaviṣyantī kriyāyām upapadabhūtāyāṃ bhavatīti, tatra dvayoḥ kriyayor asti saṃbandho bhakṣayāmi vāk tarpsyatīti. iha punar bhakṣayāmi tṛpyatv iti nāsti kaścit saṃbandhaḥ. ucyate - na hy ayaṃ vidhau tṛpyatv iti vijñāyate. kva tarhi? prārthanāyāṃ vā prāptakāle vā. yadi bhakṣayāmi vāk tarpsyatīty evam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate. yadi vā bhakṣayāṃi vācas tarptuṃ prāptaḥ kāla iti, tena viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvād ekārthatāyām ekavākyatve mantraikyam upapadyate. nanu nirākāṅkṣa ete vākye bhaṅktvā rūpaṃ sākāṅkṣe kriyete. atrocyate -yady apy ete vākye bhinnārthe nirākāṅkṣe dvāv arthāv abhivadeyātām, tathāpi bhakṣaṇasya prakāśanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanaṃ na tarpaṇasya, iti kṛtvaikārthyam eva bhavet. kim aṅga punar guṇabhāve gamyamāna evātra. tasmād guṇābhidhānān mandrādir ekamantraḥ syād iti.
children.translated_text: In the drinking <s>anuvāka</s>, it is heard: 'The inspiring, overpowering, luminous [word], the banner of sacrifices — may speech, delighting, be satisfied with <s>Soma</s>. Of the troop endowed with wealth, whose deity is <s>Soma</s>, known to the wise, of the morning pressing, of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, offered in the fire, drunk by <s>Indra</s>, honey-laden, invoked — having been invoked, I drink.' There the doubt arises: is [the portion] beginning with <s>mandrā</s> and ending with 'may it be satisfied' one mantra, and [the portion] beginning with 'of the troop endowed with wealth' another? Or is [the entire portion] from <s>mandrā</s> to 'I drink' a single mantra? What is the prima facie view?...
