children.text: liṅgaviśeṣanirdeśāt samānavidhāneṣv anaindrāṇām amantratvam // MS_3,2.27 //
children.translated_text: Because of the specification of the indicatory mark, among [offerings with] the same injunction, the non-<s>Aindra</s> (non-<s>Indra</s>-related) ones would be without mantras. // MS 3,2.27 //

children.text: eṣa eva mantra udāharaṇam - iha ca pradānāny aindrāṇy anaindrāṇi ca vidyante, teṣāṃ bhakṣaṇāny api santi. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim aindreṣv anaindreṣu ca mantraḥ, utaindreṣv eva mantraḥ, anaindrāṇām amantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? anaiṇdrāṇām amantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam iti. kutaḥ? samānavidhānāny etāni pradānāni, teṣv indrapītasyeti mantro 'nindrapītaṃ na śaknoti vaditum, na ca samānaprakaraṇa ūhaḥ saṃbhavati, asati vacane 'nyārthānabhidhānāt. tasmād amantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam evaṃjātīyakeṣv iti.
children.translated_text: This very mantra is the example. Here, there are both <s>Aindra</s> (related to <s>Indra</s>) and non-<s>Aindra</s> offerings (<s>pradāna</s>), and there are drinking [rituals] for them as well. There the doubt arises: does the mantra [apply] to both the <s>Aindra</s> and the non-<s>Aindra</s> [offerings], or does the mantra [apply] only to the <s>Aindra</s> ones, while the drinking of the non-<s>Aindra</s> ones is without a mantra? What is the prima facie view? The drinking of the non-<s>Aindra</s> ones is without a mantra. Why? These offerings have the same injunction, and among them, the mantra [containing the phrase] 'drunk by <s>Indra</s>' cannot be uttered for something not drunk by <s>Indra</s>; and being of the same context...

children.text: yathādevataṃ vā tatprakṛtitvaṃ hi darśayati // MS_3,2.28 //
children.translated_text: Or [the mantra would apply] according to the deity, for [the text] shows that [the mantra] has that as its basic form (<s>prakṛti</s>). // MS 3,2.28 //

children.text:
athavā yathādevatam ūhena lakṣayitavyam kasmāt? dhruvacamasā hi prakṛtibhūtāḥ. ke punar dhruvacamasāḥ? ye śukrāmanthipracāre savanamukhīyāḥ, aindrās te bhavanti, teṣāṃ prakṛtibhūtaṃ pradānam, vikṛtibhūtāny anyāni. katham avagamyate? tatprakṛtitvaṃ hi darśayati. katham? anuṣṭupchandasa iti ṣoḍaśiny atirātre bhakṣamantraṃ namatīti. kim atra darśanam? namatīti vipariṇāmaṃ darśayati.
nanu vacanam etat syāt. nety ucyate, naitan namatīti śrūyate. kathaṃ tarhi evaṃ namatīti, anuṣṭupchandasa iti bhakṣamantraṃ namatīti, sa eṣa ūho vikāreṣūpapadyate, [267]{*3/197*} tasmād ete vikārāḥ, ato 'naindreṣv api codakaprāpto mantra ūhitavyo bhavati. ucyate - vikārā eta iti liṅgam apadiṣṭam, nyāyo 'bhidhīyatām iti. ucyate - aindraḥ somo gṛhyate mīyate ca, tenaindreṣu somo 'naindreṣu soma eva nāstīti sarve somadharmā aindreṣv eva, adharmakā itare sākāṅkṣāḥ. kathaṃ punar jñāyate - aindraḥ somo gṛhyate mīyate ceti? mantravarṇāt, indrāya tvā vasumata ityevamādir mantra aindraṃ somaṃ vadituṃ śaknoti nānyam. tasmād aindraḥ somaḥ, tenaindreṣu somadharmāḥ, anyāni tu pradānāni sākāṅkṣāṇi, ato dharmān grahīṣyantīti nyāyaḥ. tasmād yathādevatam ūhitavyo mantra iti.
evaṃ sthitaṃ tāvad aparyavasitam, tata evaṃ sati cintāntaraṃ vartiṣyate.
children.translated_text:
Alternatively, [the mantra] should be indicated through modification (<s>ūha</s>) according to the deity. Why? Because the permanent cups (<s>dhruvacamasas</s>) are the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). Which are the permanent cups? Those that are the initial-pressing cups in the <s>Śukra</s>-<s>Amanthi</s> procedure — they are dedicated to <s>Indra</s> (<s>aindra</s>). Their offering is the archetype; the others are modifications (<s>vikṛti</s>). How is this known? Because it shows their archetypal nature. How? 'Of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter' — in the sixteen-[day soma rite] and the <s>Atirātra</s>, the drinking-mantra 'bows down' (<s>namati</s>). What is the indication here? The word <s>namati</s> ('bows down') shows a transformation.
[Objection:] But this might be a [direct Vedic] statement. [Reply:] No, it is said — for it is not heard as '<s>namati</s>' [in that form]. Then how is it '<s>namati</s>'? 'Of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter' — the drinking-mantra '<s>namati</s>.' This modification (<s>ūha</s>) applies in the derivatives (<s>vikāras</s>). Therefore these are derivatives, and hence in non-<s>Aindra</s> [cups] too, the mantra obtained through injunctive force must be modified. [Objection:] It is said — the indicatory mark that these are derivatives has been pointed out; let the logical principle (<s>nyāya</s>) be stated. [Reply:] It is said — <s>Aindra</s> (dedicated to <s>Indra</s>) Soma is drawn and measured. Therefore, in the <s>Aindra</s> [cups] there is Soma, while in the non-<s>Aindra</s> [cups] there is no Soma at all — hence all the properties of Soma belong to the <s>Aindra</s> [cups] alone, and the others, being without those properties, have syntactic expectancy. But how is it known that the <s>Aindra</s> Soma is drawn and measured? From the mantra-wording: the mantra beginning with '<s>Indrāya tvā vasumate</s>' ('For you, <s>Indra</s>, rich in treasures') is capable of referring to <s>Aindra</s> Soma and not to any other. Therefore [it is] <s>Aindra</s> Soma; hence the properties of Soma belong to the <s>Aindra</s> [cups], while the other offerings, having syntactic expectancy, will therefore adopt [those] properties — this is the logical principle. Therefore, the mantra should be modified according to the deity.
Thus, this has been established so far, but not conclusively. Since this is so, another line of inquiry will be pursued.

children.text: punarabhyunnīteṣu sarveṣām upalakṣaṇaṃ dviśeṣatvāt // MS_3,2.29 //
children.translated_text: In the re-elevated [Soma cups], it would be an inclusive indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for all, because of the two-fold remainder (<s>dviśeṣatva</s>). // MS 3.2.29 //

children.text:
santi punarabhyunnītāḥ somāḥ śukrāmanthipracāra eva savanamukhīyāḥ, teṣāṃ hotur vaṣatkāre 'nuvaṣatkāre ca caturbhir madhyataḥkāriṇāṃ camasair hutvā hotrakāṇāṃ camasaiḥ sakṛt sakṛd vaṣaṭkāra eva hutvā punaḥ saśeṣeṣv eva pātreṣu somo 'bhyunnītaḥ, evaṃ hi tatrādhvaryuḥ saṃpreṣyati, madhyataḥkāriṇāṃ camasādhvaryavo vaṣaṭkṛte 'nuvaṣaṭkṛte jahuta, hotrakāṇāṃ camasādhvaryavaḥ sakṛd dhutvā śukrasyābhyunnīyopāvartadhvam iti. tatra hotrakā nānādevatā yajanti, maitrāvaruṇo mitrāvaruṇau, mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmaha iti{*3/198*}, [268]{*3/199*} brāhmaṇāc chaṃsī indram, indra tvā vṛṣabhaṃ vayam iti{*3/200*}, potā marutaḥ, maruto yasya hi kṣaya iti{*3/201*}. neṣṭā tvaṣṭāraṃ patnīś ca, agne patnīr ihāvaheti{*3/202*}, āgnīdhro 'gnim ukṣānnāya vaśānnāyeti{*3/203*}. tatra taiś camasaiḥ pūrvasmin vaṣaṭkāra indra iṣṭaḥ, punar abhyunnīya mitrāvaruṇādyā devatā iṣṭāḥ, śeṣas tatrendrasya mitrāvaruṇādīnāṃ ca. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ prasthitadevatāyāś cendrasya mitrāvaruṇādīnāṃ copalakṣaṇam, utendro nopalakṣayitavya iti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? punar abhyunnīteṣu sarveṣām upalakṣaṇam. kasmāt? dviśeṣatvāt, camase camase tatra dvayoḥ śeṣaḥ, prakṛtau yasyai hutam, tac cheṣas tatpīta ity uktam. ihāpi tadvad eva vaditavyam. tasmāc camase camase dvayor upalakṣaṇam.
children.translated_text:
There are re-elevated (<s>punarabhyunnīta</s>) Soma [offerings] in the <s>Śukra</s>-<s>Amanthi</s> procedure itself, [which are] the initial-pressing cups. Among these, after offering with four cups of the middle-makers (<s>madhyataḥkāriṇs</s>) at the <s>Hotar's</s> <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> and <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>, and then offering once with the <s>hotraka</s> cups at the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> alone, the Soma is re-elevated in the still-remaining vessels. For thus the <s>Adhvaryu</s> directs there: 'O cup-<s>Adhvaryus</s> of the middle-makers, at the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> and <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>, pour! O cup-<s>Adhvaryus</s> of the <s>hotrakās</s>, having offered once, re-elevate the <s>Śukra</s> and return.' There, the <s>hotrakās</s> sacrifice to different deities: the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest sacrifices to] <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>, with 'We invoke <s>Mitra</s>'; the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> [sacrifices to] <s>Indra</s>, with '<s>Indra</s>, we [call] you, the bull'; the <s>Potṛ</s> [sacrifices to] the <s>Maruts</s>, with 'O <s>Maruts</s>, in whose abode'; the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> [sacrifices to] <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and the wives [of the gods], with 'O <s>Agni</s>, bring hither the wives'; the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [sacrifices to] <s>Agni</s>, with 'For food of bulls, for food of cows.' There, with those cups, at the previous <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, <s>Indra</s> was worshipped; after re-elevation, <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> and other deities are worshipped. The remainder belongs to both <s>Indra</s> and <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> and the others. There the doubt arises: is there an inclusive indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for both the originally-intended deity (<s>prasthitadevatā</s>) — <s>Indra</s> — and <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> and the others, or should <s>Indra</s> not be inclusively indicated?
What is the prima facie view? In the re-elevated [Soma cups], there is an inclusive indication for all. Why? Because of the two-fold remainder — in each cup there is a remainder belonging to two [deities]: the archetype, for whom the offering was made — that remainder — and 'that has been drunk,' as was stated. Here too, it should be stated in the same way. Therefore, in each cup, there is an inclusive indication for both.

children.text: apanayād vā pūrvasyānupalakṣaṇam // MS_3,2.30 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of the removal [of the original deity's portion], there would be no inclusive indication of the former [deity]. // MS 3.2.30 //

children.text: apanītaṃ prasthitadevatāyāḥ śeṣaṃ manyāmahe. kutaḥ? mitrāvaruṇādibhyas tatpātrastham abhyāśrāvyate. katham etat? ucyate - mitrāvaruṇādayo hījyante, tad yathācāryaśeṣaṃ devadatto bhuñjāno yadi śeṣaṃ pūrṇakāya prayacchati, pūrṇako devadattam upalakṣayati, devadattaśeṣaṃ bhuñja iti, nācāryaśeṣam. tasmān na prasthitadevatā indra upalakṣayitavya iti.
children.translated_text: We consider the remainder of the originally-intended deity (<s>prasthitadevatā</s>) to have been removed. Why? Because [it] is offered (<s>abhyāśrāvyate</s>) to <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> and the others from what was [left] in that vessel. How is this? It is said — <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> and the others are worshipped. Just as when the remainder of a teacher's [meal given to] <s>Devadatta</s> who is eating — if [<s>Devadatta</s>] gives the remainder to <s>Pūrṇaka</s>, <s>Pūrṇaka</s> inclusively indicates <s>Devadatta</s> [only], thinking 'Eat the remainder of <s>Devadatta</s>' — not the remainder of the teacher. Therefore, the originally-intended deity, <s>Indra</s>, should not be inclusively indicated.

children.text: grahaṇād{*3/204*} vāpanayaḥ{*3/205*} syāt // MS_3,2.31 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of [the Soma's being] drawn, the removal might [not have occurred]. // MS 3.2.31 //

children.text: na caitad asti, indro nopalakṣaṇīya iti, tasyāpi hy asau śeṣaḥ pratyakṣam avagamyate. nanv apanīta iti. ucyate - nāsāv apanīyate. sakṛd dhutāṃś camasānabhidroṇakalaśād gṛhṇāti, saśeṣaś camaso lakṣaṇam anyasyonnīyamānasya. tataś{*3/206*} camasastho hotum unnetavyaḥ preṣito vā. yat tu yakṣyamāṇā devatāḥ praty āśrā[269]{*3/207*}vita iti. ucyate - āśrāvyate tatra devatābhyo na tv idaṃ vā tad veti. tena{*3/208*} yad dhotuṃ gṛhītaṃ tad āśrāvitam iti gamyate. na ca, āśrāvaṇavelāyāṃ devatābhisaṃbandhaḥ, yad yad devatābhisaṃbaddham, tad āśrāvyate, tasmād astīndraśeṣaḥ, lakṣyate{*3/209*} ca. ataḥ sarveṣām upalakṣaṇam iti. kṛtvācintaiṣā, nātra prayojanaṃ vaktavyam, pūrvādhikaraṇasyaivaitat prayojanam avadhāryate.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that <s>Indra</s> should not be inclusively indicated — for his remainder too is directly perceived. [Objection:] But was it not removed? [Reply:] It is said — it is not removed. [The priest] draws (<s>gṛhṇāti</s>) the once-offered cups from the <s>Droṇakalaśa</s> (Soma-trough). The cup with a remainder is the indication of another [cup] being re-elevated. Therefore, [the Soma that is] in the cup is directed to be offered, or pressed forth. As for the fact that [the Soma] is offered to the deities who are about to be worshipped — it is said: [it] is offered to the deities there, but not 'this or that [specifically].' Hence, what has been drawn for offering — that is what has been offered, it is understood. And the connection with the deity is not [established] at the time of the <s>āśrāvaṇa</s> (call) — whatever is connected with a deity, that is called out. Therefore, the remainder of <s>Indra</s> exists and is [inclusively] indicated. Hence, there is an inclusive indication for all. This inquiry has been conducted for its own sake; no [practical] purpose needs to be stated here, for the purpose is ascertained from the preceding topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) itself.

children.text: pātnīvate tu pūrvavat // MS_3,2.32 //
children.translated_text: But for the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup], [it would be] as before. // MS 3.2.32 //

children.text: asti pātnīvato grahaḥ, yad upāṃśupātreṇāgrayaṇāt pātnīvataṃ gṛhṇātīti, dvidevatyānāṃ śeṣā āgrayaṇasthālyāṃ upanītāḥ, tataḥ pātnīvato gṛhyate. atha hute pātnīvate, tac cheṣe bhakṣyamāṇe bhavati saṃdehaḥ - kim indravāyvādaya upalakṣayitavyā na veti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? upalakṣayitavyāḥ. teṣām api hy asau śeṣo yathā prasthitadevatāyā iti.
children.translated_text: There is a <s>Pātnīvata</s> cup — in that [the priest] draws the <s>Pātnīvata</s> from the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> [cup] with the <s>Upāṃśu</s> vessel. The remainders of the two-deity [offerings] are brought to the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> bowl; from that, the <s>Pātnīvata</s> is drawn. Now, when the <s>Pātnīvata</s> has been offered, regarding its remainder being consumed, the doubt arises: should <s>Indra</s>-<s>Vāyu</s> and the others be inclusively indicated or not? What is the prima facie view? They should be inclusively indicated. For their remainder too is [present] in this, just as [the remainder] of the originally-intended deity.

children.text: grahaṇād vāpanītaṃ syāt // MS_3,2.33 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of [the Soma's being] drawn, [their portion] would have been removed. // MS 3.2.33 //

children.text:
apanīyate hi sa śeṣa iha, na yathāpūrvavat, tatra hi pātralakṣaṇatvena saṃkīrtyate na somo grāhyatvena, iha tu āgrayaṇād gṛhṇātīti, sthālīsthaḥ somo nirdiśyate hotum, yakṣyamāṇadevatāṃ prati. nanu sthālyām āgrayaṇo nāgrayaṇaś{*3/210*} ca, tatra yas tasmād āgrayaṇād gṛhyate, sa pātnīvataḥ, yas tu saṃpātānn āsau pātnīvata iti. ucyate - āgrayaṇo 'pādānam, tasmād yo 'paity āgrayaṇo 'nāgrayaṇo{*3/211*} vā, sa sarvaḥ pātnīvataḥ, āgrayaṇāc caiṣa sarvo 'petaḥ.
[270]{*3/212*} nanv anāgrayaṇād apy apetaḥ. naiṣa doṣaḥ, āgrayaṇāt tāvad apetaḥ, tenāsau pūrvadevatābhiḥ pīta iti na śakyate vaktum. yo hīndrārthasya somasyāvayavaḥ śeṣaḥ sa indrapīta iti prakṛtāv ucyate. ihāpi tadvad eva pūrvadevatārthasyāvayavo vaditavyaḥ. nanu yo 'sau pūrvadevatārthaḥ, tasyaivāyam avayavaḥ. neti brūmaḥ, na hi hutasyāvayavo dṛśyate. nanu prakṛtāv api hutasyāvayavo na dṛśyate. ucyate - hutāhutasya samudāyasya tatrāvayava upalakṣyate taddevatasya. nanv ihāpi samudāya evāsīt taddevatyaḥ, tasyaivāyam avayavaḥ. nety ucyate, āsīd ayaṃ samudāyas taddevatyaḥ, idānīṃ tasyāvayavo 'nyadevatyo jātaḥ, tena samudāyas taddevatyatvād apetaḥ.
āha pūrvadevatāpītasyāsāv avayava āsīt tena bhūtapūrvagatyā bhaviṣyati. ucyate - prakṛtau na bhūtapūrvagatyābhidhānaṃ kṛtam, ihāpi tadvad eva na kartavyam iti. api cendradevatyas tatrendrapīta ity uktam, anapanītā ca tasyendradevatyatā, asya punaḥ pūrvadevatāsaṃbandho 'pagataḥ. tasmān nātra pūrvadevatopalakṣaṇīyeti.
children.translated_text:
That remainder is indeed removed here, not as in the previous [case]. For there [in the previous case], [the Soma] is referred to by the characterization of the vessel — not as Soma to be drawn; but here, [the text says] 'he draws from the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>' — the Soma in the bowl is designated for offering, directed toward the deity to be worshipped. [Objection:] But in the bowl there is both <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> and non-<s>Āgrayaṇa</s> [Soma]. Among these, what is drawn from that <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> — that is the <s>Pātnīvata</s>; but what is from the mixed remnants (<s>saṃpāta</s>) — that is not the <s>Pātnīvata</s>. [Reply:] It is said — the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> is the source (<s>apādāna</s>). Whatever departs from it — whether <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> or non-<s>Āgrayaṇa</s> — all of that is the <s>Pātnīvata</s>, and all of this has departed from the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>.
[Objection:] But it has also departed from the non-<s>Āgrayaṇa</s> [portion]. [Reply:] This is not a defect. It has at least departed from the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>, and therefore one cannot say that it was drunk by the previous deities. For in the archetype, it is said that [the remainder] which is a portion of the Soma intended for <s>Indra</s> — that is drunk by <s>Indra</s>. Here too, it should similarly be said to be a portion of [the Soma intended for] the previous deities. [Objection:] But that which was intended for the previous deities — this is indeed its portion. [Reply:] We say no — for no portion of the offered [Soma] is seen. [Objection:] But in the archetype too, no portion of the offered [Soma] is seen. [Reply:] It is said — there, a portion of the aggregate of offered and unoffered [Soma] is inclusively indicated as belonging to that deity. [Objection:] But here too, there was an aggregate belonging to that deity; this is indeed its portion. [Reply:] No, it is said — there was [indeed] an aggregate belonging to that deity, but now its portion has become [dedicated to] another deity. Hence, the aggregate has departed from belonging to that deity.
[Objection:] The portion of [Soma] drunk by the previous deity was [originally] its part; therefore, by virtue of its former status, it will [still] belong [to that deity]. [Reply:] It is said — in the archetype, the attribution was not based on former status; here too, it should similarly not be made. Moreover, in [the archetype], it was dedicated to <s>Indra</s> as deity, and there it was said to be drunk by <s>Indra</s>, and its status as dedicated to <s>Indra</s> was not removed. But in this [case], the connection with the previous deity has ceased. Therefore, the previous deity should not be inclusively indicated here.

children.text: tvaṣṭāraṃ tūpalakṣayet pānāt // MS_3,2.34 //
children.translated_text: But one should inclusively indicate <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, because of [his] drinking. // MS 3.2.34 //

children.text:
asti pātnīvataḥ somaḥ, tatra mantraḥ, agnā i patnīvan sajūr devena tvaṣṭrā somaṃ pibeti{*3/213*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ tvaṣṭopalakṣayitavyo na veti. kiṃ prāptam? upalakṣayitavyaḥ. kutaḥ? pānāt, pānaṃ śrūyate - sajūr devena tvaṣṭrā [271]{*3/214*} somaṃ pibeti. tenāyam agnaye patnīvate saha tvaṣṭrā dīyata iti gamyate. yasmai ca yena saha dīyate, ubhābhyāṃ tad dīyate, evaṃ tat sahadānaṃ bhavati, yathā devadattāya yajñadattena saha śataṃ dīyatām ity ukte, tatrobhābhyām api dīyate. tasmāt tvāṣṭro 'py asau soma iti tvaṣṭopalakṣayitavyaḥ. asāv apīndra iva{*3/215*} pibatīti.
NOTES:
*{3/213: Tait.S. 1.4.27.1}*
*{3/214: E2: 4,183; E4: 4,122; E6: 1,186}*
*{3/215: E2,4: eva}*
children.translated_text: There is Soma [dedicated to] the <s>Pātnīvata</s>. There is a mantra for it: '<s>Agni</s>, together with the <s>Pātnīvata</s>, in conjunction with the god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, drinks the Soma.' There the doubt arises: should <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> be inclusively indicated or not? What is the prima facie view? He should be inclusively indicated. Why? Because of drinking — drinking is heard: 'In conjunction with the god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, he drinks the Soma.' From this it is understood that this [Soma] is given to <s>Agni Pātnīvata</s> together with <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. And when something is given to someone together with another, it is given to both — such is the nature of joint-giving. Just as when [one says] 'Let a hundred be given to <s>Devadatta</s> together with <s>Yajñadatta</s>' — there it is given to both. Therefore, this is also <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> (belonging to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>) Soma, hence <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> should be inclusively indicated. He too drinks, just like <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: atulyatvāt tu naivaṃ syāt // MS_3,2.35 //
children.translated_text: Because of the inequality, it should not be so. // MS 3.2.35 //

children.text:
naitad evam, śabdapramāṇakā vayam, yac chabda āha, tad asmākaṃ pramāṇam, śabdaś cāgneḥ patnīvataḥ pānam āha tvaṣṭuḥ sahabhāvamātram, na hy ananuṣṭhīyamāne sahabhāvaḥ sidhyatīti tvaṣṭari pānam anumīyate. nanu tvaṣṭre pānaṃ coditam. satyam, coditaṃ mantravarṇena, na codanayā. codanā hi pātnīvataṃ gṛhṇātīti, loke tu kāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā coditam acoditam apy anuṣṭhīyata{*3/216*} eva, lokataś caitat paricchinnam, naivaṃjātīyakena vākyena, tvaṣṭuḥ somaḥ kṛto bhavatīti.
NOTES:
*{3/216: E2,4, E1 (v.l.): coditam acoditam apy anuṣṭhīyata}*
children.translated_text: This is not so. We rely on verbal testimony (<s>śabdapramāṇa</s>). What the word states — that is our authority. And the word states the drinking of <s>Agni Pātnīvata</s>; for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, [it states] mere co-presence (<s>sahabhāvamātra</s>). For co-presence is not established without [the action] being performed — hence the drinking of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is inferred. [Objection:] But the drinking for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is enjoined. [Reply:] True, it is enjoined by the mantra-wording, not by an injunction (<s>codanā</s>). For the injunction is 'He draws the <s>Pātnīvata</s>.' But in the world, [people,] observing an action to be done, perform what is enjoined as well as what is not enjoined. And this [principle] is derived from worldly [convention], not from a sentence of this kind — that the Soma of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> has been created.

children.text: triṃśac ca parārthatvāt // MS_3,2.36 //
children.translated_text: And [because of] the thirty, since [they serve] another's purpose. // MS 3.2.36 //

children.text: tasminn eva pātnīvate mantraḥ - aibhir agne sarathaṃ yāhy arvāṅ nānārathaṃ vā vibhavo hy aśvāḥ. patnīvatas triṃśataṃ trīṃś ca devān anuṣvadham ā vaha mādayasveti{*3/217*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ trayastriṃśato [272]{*3/218*} devānām upalakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? trayastriṃśataṃ devānupalakṣayet. katham? dīyate hi somas trayastriṃśate devebhyaḥ. evaṃ hy agnim agnīd adhīcchati, āyāhy agner 'vācīnam, trayastriṃśatā devaiḥ saha samānaṃ ratham adhiṣṭhāya nānārathair vā vibhavanti hi te 'śvāḥ. tad idam anuṣvadham āvaha trayastriṃśataṃ patnīvato devān āgamaya tarpaya ceti. atra hy agnim agnīd adhīcchati trayastriṃśato devānāṃ tṛptaya iti gamyate, yat pradhānaś cātra mantraḥ, tat paraḥ somaḥ. tasmād ucyate - trayastriṃśad devā upalakṣayitavyā iti.
children.translated_text: In that very <s>pātnīvata</s> (offering to [Agni] with his wives), the mantra is: 'With these, O <s>Agni</s>, come hither together on the same chariot, or on separate chariots, for your horses are powerful. Bring the thirty-three gods of the <s>patnīvat</s> [offering] in proper order and rejoice.' There the doubt arises: should the thirty-three gods be designated (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), or not? What is the prima facie view? The thirty-three gods should be designated. How? For <s>Soma</s> is given to the thirty-three gods. Thus, the <s>Agnīdh</s> (fire-kindler) invites <s>Agni</s>: 'Come, O <s>Agni</s>, facing [us], mounting the same chariot together with the thirty-three gods, or on separate chariots, for your horses are powerful. Bring them in proper order — bring the thirty-three <s>patnīvat</s> gods and satisfy them.' Here, it is understood that the <s>Agnīdh</s> invites <s>Agni</s> for the satisfaction of the thirty-three gods; and the principal mantra here refers to <s>Soma</s> as the supreme [offering]. Therefore, it is said: the thirty-three gods should be designated.

children.text:
nanu codanāyāṃ patnīvān kevalo 'gnir devatātvena śrūyate. satyam, codanāyāṃ patnīvān devatātvena śrūyate, na tu devatāntaraṃ niṣidhyate. kim ato yady evam? etad ato bhavati, māntravarṇikās trayastriṃśad devā aviruddhāś codanāyāṃ pratīyanta iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - na trayastriṃśad devā upalakṣayitavyā iti, nātra mantre 'gnir āhvātā pariveṣṭā vā tarpayitā vādhyeṣyate. nātra trayastriṃśad deveṣv iṣṭeṣu prayojanaṃ nirvartyate. kas tarhi yaṣṭavyaḥ? patnīvān. kuta etat? sa hi codyate - pātnīvataṃ gṛhṇātīti. nanu māntravarṇikānāṃ trayastriṃśato devānām atra saṃkīrtanam. ucyate - parārthatvena tāḥ saṃkīrtyante. katham? na hy aprattam agneḥ, tad bhavati, na ca parakīyasya dānam avakalpate. tasmāt tvam amūbhyas trayastriṃśad devatābhyo dehīty asamañjasaṃ vacanam, agnaye tv anena dānam uktaṃ bhavati. katham? īśāno hi vilaṃbhayati dravyam, tad iha vilaṃbhanaṃ saṃkīrtayan tvam asya īśāna iti pratyāpayati.
[273]{*3/219*} nanu mādayasvety ucyate, na vilaṃbhayeti. ucyate - na hi mādyanti devatāḥ, tasmān madakaraṇasaṃkīrtanam adṛṣṭāya syāt, dṛṣṭāya tu tyāgasaṃkīrtanaṃ lakṣaṇayā, lakṣaṇā hy adṛṣṭakalpanāyā jyāyasī, pramāṇād dhi sā bhavati. nanu tyāge 'pi lakṣyamāṇe 'gniḥ kartādhīṣyate. tad ucyate - agner apy adhyeṣaṇādṛṣṭāyaiva, tasmād agner aiśvaryakaraṇam etad vākyaṃ lakṣayatīti nyāyyam. api ca pātnīvate somaś codyate - pātnīvataṃ gṛhṇātīti.
nanūktam, māntravarṇikaṃ ca pratiṣedhati codaneti. ucyate - tad api māntravarṇikaṃ nāstīty uktam. api ca sāmarthyāt pratiṣedhatīti gamyate. na hi sāpekṣaḥ patnīvac chabdaḥ, tad dhitārthena saṃlakṣyate, tasmāt kevalaḥ patnīvān devateti. etac codanāvaśena mantro varṇanīyaḥ. tasmād yathaivāsmābhir varṇito mantraḥ, tathaiva bhavitum arhatīti, patnīvāṃś cāgnir agne patnīvann iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdiśyate. tasmād agnir upalakṣayitavyo na trayastriṃśad devatā iti.
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] But in the injunction, <s>patnīvat</s> <s>Agni</s> alone is heard as the deity. True, in the injunction, [<s>Agni</s>] with his wives is heard as the deity, but another deity is not prohibited. What follows from this? From this it follows that the thirty-three gods mentioned in the mantra (<s>māntravarṇika</s>) are understood in the injunction as non-contradictory.
Having arrived at this position, we say: The thirty-three gods should not be designated. Here in the mantra, <s>Agni</s> is not being invoked as an inviter, attendant, or satisfier. Nor is any purpose accomplished here by desiring [worship of] the thirty-three gods. Who then is to be worshipped? [<s>Agni</s>] with his wives (<s>patnīvān</s>). How do we know this? Because that is what is enjoined — 'He takes the <s>pātnīvata</s> [cup].' [Objection:] But the thirty-three gods mentioned in the mantra are being celebrated here. [Reply:] They are celebrated for the sake of another [purpose]. How? For what has not been given does not belong to <s>Agni</s>, and a gift of what belongs to another is not proper. Therefore, the statement 'you should give to these thirty-three deities' is improper. But a gift to <s>Agni</s> is stated by this. How? For a lord holds back (<s>vilambhayati</s>) wealth; here, by celebrating [his] holding back, [the text] acknowledges 'you are the lord of this.'
[Objection:] But it says 'rejoice' (<s>mādayasva</s>), not 'hold back.' [Reply:] Deities do not [actually] become intoxicated; therefore, the mention of causing intoxication would serve an unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) purpose. But for a visible purpose, the mention of relinquishment is [understood] through secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — for secondary designation is stronger than postulating an unseen [result], since it proceeds from a valid means of knowledge. [Objection:] But even with relinquishment being designated, <s>Agni</s> is being requested as the agent. To this it is said: The requesting of <s>Agni</s> too is for the sake of the unseen alone; therefore, it is proper that this sentence designates the lordship of <s>Agni</s>. Moreover, in the <s>pātnīvata</s> [offering], <s>Soma</s> is enjoined — 'He takes the <s>pātnīvata</s> [cup].'
[Objection:] But was it not said that [the injunction] prohibits what is mentioned in the mantra? [Reply:] It has been stated that the mantra-mentioned [deities] do not exist [as the intended deities]. Moreover, it is understood that [the injunction] prohibits by force of implication. For the word <s>patnīvat</s> is not dependent [on other deities]; it is recognized as having its own purpose (<s>hitārtha</s>). Therefore, <s>patnīvān</s> alone is the deity. The mantra must be explained in accordance with the injunction. Therefore, just as we have explained the mantra, so it ought to be [understood]. And <s>patnīvān</s> <s>Agni</s> — 'O <s>Agni</s> with your wives' — is indicated by co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). Therefore, <s>Agni</s> should be designated, not the thirty-three deities.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/217: <s>Ṛg Veda</s> 3.6.9} {3/218: Edition cross-references: E2: 4,185; E4: 4,125; E6: 1,186} {3/219: Edition cross-references: E2: 4,187; E4: 4,126; E6: 1,187}]

children.text: vaṣaṭkāraś ca kartṛvat // MS_3,2.37 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation) is like the agent [i.e., not to be designated]. // MS 3,2.37 //

children.text: asty anuvaṣaṭkāradevatā, somasyāgne vīhīty anuvaṣaṭkarotīti{*3/220*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim anuvaṣaṭkāradevatopalakṣayitavyā na veti. kiṃ prāptam? upalakṣayitavyeti, na tatra pārārthyaṃ kiṃcit pūrvad upalakṣyate. tasmād upalakṣayitevyati. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - anuvaṣaṭkāradevatā nopalakṣayitavyā, kartṛvat, yathā kartā nopalakṣyate, hotṛpīta[274]{*3/221*}syādhvaryupītasyeti, evam evānuvaṣaṭkāradevatāpi. na hi sā prakṛtāv upalakṣitā, yac ca nāma prakṛtau kṛtam, tad iha karaṇīyam. tasmān nopalakṣayitavyeti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (subsidiary exclamation) deity — 'Of <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, the rice-grains,' he makes the subsidiary exclamation. There the doubt arises: should the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> deity be designated, or not? What is the prima facie view? It should be designated — for no subsidiary purpose [justifying designation] is perceived there from the preceding [discussion]. Therefore, it should be designated. Having arrived at this position, we say: The <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> deity should not be designated — like the agent. Just as the agent is not designated — as [established by the discussion of] 'drunk by the <s>Hotṛ</s>, drunk by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>' — similarly the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> deity too. For it is not designated in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), and whatever is done in the archetype is to be done here. Therefore, it should not be designated.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/220: <s>Aitareya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.5} {3/221: Edition cross-references: E2: 4,189; E4: 4,131; E6: 1,188}]

children.text: chandaḥpratiṣedhas tu sarvagāmitvāt // MS_3,2.38 //
children.translated_text: But the prohibition of the metre [applies] because of [its] universal applicability. // MS 3,2.38 //

children.text: sthitād uttaram ucyate - naitad asti, yad uktam ūhena mantravad bhakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam iti, amantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam. kasmāt? ucyate - samānavidhānatvāt, nāsty atra prakṛtivikṛtibhāvaḥ. katham? prakaraṇasya tulyatvāt, yal liṅgaṃ uktam{*3/222*}, chandaḥpratiṣedhaḥ sa ity ucyate, tṛtīyasavanatvāj jagatīcchandasa iti prāpte 'nuṣṭupchandasa iti ṣoḍaśini bhakṣamantraṃ namatīti{*3/223*} samānavidhāne 'py avakalpyate. yat tūktam{*3/224*} - aindraḥ somo gṛhyate mīyate ceti, naita aindrā anaindrāś ca bhinnā yāgāḥ, ekasyaivaite 'bhyāsaviśeṣāḥ, na cābhāsaviśeṣāṇāṃ dharmā guṇatvāt, sarva ete yāgadharmāḥ. tena kṛtsnā yāgasya codyante somadharmāḥ, somaś ceti. yac ca, indro gṛhyate mīyate ceti, indrasya mantrāmnānān mantreṇa grahaṇaṃ prakāśayitavyam, itarāsāṃ devatānāṃ dhyānādineti. tasmād anaindrāṇām amantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam iti.
children.translated_text: Following the established [conclusion], a further point is stated: It is not so — what was said, that the drinking (<s>bhakṣaṇa</s>) should be done with a mantra by analogy (<s>ūha</s>). The drinking should be done without a mantra. Why? It is said: because of identical prescription (<s>samānavidhāna</s>) — there is no archetype-modification (<s>prakṛti-vikṛti</s>) relationship here. How? Because of the equality of the context. As for the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that was mentioned — it is said to be a metre-prohibition: when [the mantra] in <s>Jagatī</s> metre would be expected because of [the rite] being in the third pressing, in the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteen-versed [rite]) the drinking-mantra is made in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> metre — this is accommodated even in identical prescription. As for the statement that '<s>Soma</s> belonging to <s>Indra</s> is taken and measured' — these <s>Indra</s>-related and non-<s>Indra</s>-related sacrifices are not different; they are merely varieties of repetition of the same [sacrifice]. And the properties of varieties of repetition are not [independently significant] because of [their] subsidiary nature — all these are properties of the sacrifice. Therefore, the entire [set of] <s>Soma</s>-properties is enjoined for the sacrifice, including <s>Soma</s> itself. And as for '<s>Indra</s> is taken and measured' — because of the recording of <s>Indra</s>'s mantras, the taking with a mantra should be understood [to apply only when <s>Indra</s> is the deity]; for the other deities, [the taking is] through meditation and so on. Therefore, for the non-<s>Indra</s> [offerings], the drinking is without a mantra.

children.text: aindrāgne tu liṅgabhāvāt syāt // MS_3,2.39 //
children.translated_text: But for the [offering] belonging to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, [a mantra] would be [used] because of the presence of the indicatory mark. // MS 3,2.39 //

children.text: evaṃ sthite cintyate - asti tatraindrāgnaḥ somaḥ, aindrāgnaṃ gṛhṇātīti{*3/226*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ mantravad bhakṣaṇam, amantrakaṃ veti. kiṃ prāptam? aindrāgne tu mantraḥ syāt, yasya hīndrāgnī devatā tasya nendraḥ{*3/227*}, śakyate hi sa indrapīta iti vyapadeṣṭum, yasya hy avayavāntaram indreṇa pītam, sa indrapītaḥ, tasyendrāgnibhyāṃ pibadbhyāṃ pītam avayavāntaram indreṇa. tasmān mantravad bhakṣaṇam iti.
children.translated_text: This being established, it is considered: There is here the <s>Soma</s> [offering] belonging to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s> — 'He takes the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [cup].' There the doubt arises: is the drinking with a mantra, or without a mantra? What is the prima facie view? For the [offering] belonging to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, there would be a mantra. For whose deity is <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, for that [offering] <s>Indra</s> is [also the deity] — for it can be designated as 'drunk by <s>Indra</s>': since a portion of it is drunk by <s>Indra</s>, it is 'drunk by <s>Indra</s>,' [and] a portion of what is drunk by <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> is [drunk] by <s>Indra</s>. Therefore, the drinking is with a mantra.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/226: Cf. <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.5.4.1} {3/227: E2,4 omit 'na'}]

children.text: ekasmin vā devatāntarād vibhāgavat // MS_3,2.40 //
children.translated_text: Or, [the mantra applies] to one [deity] alone, because of the separation from another deity, just as [in the case of] division. // MS 3,2.40 //

children.text:
nāsyāvayavāntaram indreṇa pīyate, na cāvayavāntareṇendrapītena tat pītaṃ bhavati, tena pīta iti lakṣaṇāśabdo 'yam. indram uddiśya yaḥ saṃkalpito indro yasya devateti, yathaiva ca sākāṅkṣasya tad dhitārthenāsaṃbandhaḥ, evaṃ samāso 'pīndrapītasyeti sākāṅkṣasya nāvakalpate, tad uktam - vyavasthā vārthasaṃyogād iti{*3/228*}.
āha - nanu tenaivādhikaraṇenaitad gatam{*3/229*}. kim arthaṃ punaś cintyata iti. ucyate - yat tatra vicāritaṃ siddham eva tat. kathaṃ punar vicāryate? naiva sākāṅkṣasya devatāsaṃbandha iti. naiveha devatāsaṃbandha iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, pānamātrasaṃbandho 'treti, pānamātrasaṃbandhena yatra dvābhyāṃ pīyate, tatraikena devatāsaṃbandha ity uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ, tasmān na punaruktam iti.
children.translated_text:
A portion of it is not [actually] drunk by <s>Indra</s>, nor does it become 'drunk' by a portion being drunk by <s>Indra</s>; therefore, the word '<s>indrapīta</s>' (drunk by <s>Indra</s>) is a secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). [The offering is called] 'of <s>Indra</s>' because it is dedicated to <s>Indra</s> — '<s>Indra</s> is the deity for whom it is intended.' And just as a dependent [word] has no connection with its intended meaning, so too the compound '<s>indrapītasya</s>' (of what is drunk by <s>Indra</s>), being dependent [on <s>Agni</s>], does not apply. This was stated: 'Or, the determination is from the connection with meaning.'
He says: But was this not [already] settled by that [previous] topic? For what purpose is it being considered again? [Reply:] What was examined there is indeed established. But how is it being examined [again]? [The question is:] in the previous position, there is simply no deity-connection for a dependent [word] — [that is the first view]. Here too, there is no deity-connection — this is the prima facie view. But the connection is with the drinking alone — and when there is connection with the drinking, where [<s>Soma</s>] is drunk by two, there the deity-connection is with one [of them] — this is the latter view. Therefore, it is not repetitive.

children.text: chandaś ca devatāvat // MS_3,2.41 //
children.translated_text: And the metre, like the deity. // MS 3,2.41 //

children.text: asmin mantre gāyatrachandasa ity ucyate, tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ekacchandasi some mantraḥ, uta nānācchandasyapīti{*3/231*}. ucyate - chandaś ca devatāvat, yathānyasahitendre na mantraḥ, evam anekacchandaske some na syān mantra iti. atrāpi hi gāyatracchandasa iti saviśeṣaṇasya samāso nāvakalpate.
children.translated_text: Regarding this mantra, it is said to be in <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre. There the doubt arises: is the mantra [used] for <s>Soma</s> [offerings] of one metre [only], or for those of multiple metres as well? [Reply:] The metre, like the deity — just as there is no mantra when <s>Indra</s> is combined with another [deity], so too there would be no mantra for <s>Soma</s> [offerings] of more than one metre. For here too, the compound 'of <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre' does not apply when qualified [by multiple metres].

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/231: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.2.5.2}]

children.text: sarveṣu vābhāvād ekacchandasaḥ // MS_3,2.42 //
children.translated_text: Or [the mantra applies] to all, because of the non-existence of one of a single metre. // MS 3,2.42 //

children.text: sarveṣu vā mantraḥ syāt. kutaḥ? abhāvād ekacchandasaḥ, naiva kaścid ekacchandasāḥ somo 'sti, tena yathābhūto 'yam, tathābhūtasya{*3/232*} chando viśeṣaṇam. tasmād anekacchandaske some mantraḥ syād iti.
children.translated_text: Or the mantra would apply to all [<s>Soma</s> offerings]. Why? Because of the non-existence of one of a single metre — there is no <s>Soma</s> [offering] that has only a single metre. Therefore, the metre is a qualifier of [the <s>Soma</s>] as it actually is. Hence, the mantra would apply to <s>Soma</s> [offerings] of multiple metres as well.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vaikamantryam aitiśāyanasya bhaktipānatvāt savanādhikāro hi // MS_3,2.43 //
children.translated_text: For all [offerings], [there would be] a single mantra, because according to <s>Aitiśāyana</s>, the drinking is [metaphorical] partaking; for the [mantra's] jurisdiction is [defined] by the pressing (<s>savana</s>). // MS 3,2.43 //

children.text: yad uktam - anaindrāṇām amantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam iti, tan na, sarveṣāṃ samantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam iti, yathāsamāmnātaś ca mantraḥ syāt. nendrapīta iti soma ucyate. kiṃ tarhi? savanam, prātaḥsavanaśabdena sāmānādhikaraṇyāt. nanu some 'pi ṣaṣṭhī. satyam asti ṣaṣṭhī, na tu tena sāmānādhikaraṇyam. nāsāv indreṇa somaḥ pītaḥ, nāpīndrāya dattaḥ, anya eva pīto datto vā, sa gata eva. na cātītaḥ samudāyo vyapadiśyate, [277]{*3/233*} pratyakṣavacano hy ayaṃ śabdaḥ. savane tu na doṣaḥ, indrapītaṃ bhavati savanam, yatrendreṇa pītam. tasmād anaindro 'pītasavane 'ntarbhavatīti śakyate mantreṇa vaditum. śakyate cet samānavidhāne katham iva mantro na bhaviṣyati. bhaktyā hy apītaḥ pīta ity ucyate. evam eva aitiśāyana ācāryo manyate sma. asmākam apy etad eva matam. ācāryagrahaṇam, tasmād āgatam iti tasya saṃkīrtyartham.
children.translated_text: As for the statement that 'for non-<s>Indra</s> [offerings] the drinking is without a mantra' — that is not so. For all [offerings], the drinking is with a mantra, and the mantra should be as it has been recorded. [The <s>Soma</s>] is not called '<s>indrapīta</s>' (drunk by <s>Indra</s>) with reference to the <s>Soma</s> [itself]. What then? [It refers to] the pressing (<s>savana</s>), because of co-reference with the word '<s>prātaḥsavana</s>' (morning pressing). [Objection:] But there is a genitive case-ending on '<s>soma</s>' as well. True, there is a genitive, but it does not [establish] co-reference. That <s>Soma</s> was not drunk by <s>Indra</s>, nor given to <s>Indra</s>; another [<s>Soma</s>] was drunk or given, and that is gone. And a past aggregate is not designated [as present] — for this word has a directly perceptible referent. But in the case of the pressing, there is no defect — the pressing is '<s>indrapīta</s>' (in which <s>Indra</s> drank), [namely] the pressing in which [<s>Soma</s>] was drunk by <s>Indra</s>. Therefore, even a non-<s>Indra</s> [offering], being included in the 'drunk-pressing,' can be spoken of with a mantra. And if it can [be so spoken of], how in identical prescription would the mantra not apply? For the [metaphorical] partaking (<s>bhakti</s>) — what is not [actually] drunk is called 'drunk.' Thus indeed did the teacher <s>Aitiśāyana</s> hold. This is our view as well. The mention of the teacher's [name] is for the purpose of commemorating [the tradition's] lineage — that it comes from him.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/233: Edition cross-references: E2: 4,195; E4: 4,146; E6: 1,190}]

children.text: śruter jātādhikāraḥ syāt // MS_3,3.1 //
children.translated_text: From [Vedic] statement, the jurisdiction would be based on the class [of Vedic text]. // MS 3,3.1 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - uccair ṛcaḥ kriyate, uccaiḥ sāmnā, upāṃśu yajuṣā iti{*3/234*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ ṛgādijātim adhikṛtyaite śabdāḥ pravṛttāḥ, uta vedam adhikṛtyeti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? jātādhikāraḥ syāt. kutaḥ? śruteḥ, eṣāṃ śabdānāṃ śravaṇād eva jātiṃ pratipadyāmahe, tenopāṃśutvaṃ jātyādhikṛtayā saṃbadhyate, vedānām adhikārakaḥ śabdo nāstīti. api ca - ṛgvedavyatikrāntānām ṛcāṃ yajurveda uccaiḥ prayogo bhaviṣyati, itarathā tasyā eva ṛca ubhau dharmau vaikalpikau syātām, tatra pakṣe bādhaḥ syāt. prakaraṇaṃ caivam anugṛhītaṃ bhavati, itarathā vedasaṃyoge sarvasminn api kratāv upāṃśutvaṃ syāt. tasmāj jātādhikārā ete śabdā iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'The <s>ṛc</s> (verse) is performed aloud; the <s>sāman</s> (chant) [is performed] aloud; the <s>yajus</s> (sacrificial formula) [is performed] in a low voice.' There the doubt arises: are these words employed with reference to the class (<s>jāti</s>) [of Vedic text — i.e., <s>ṛc</s>, <s>sāman</s>, <s>yajus</s> regardless of which Veda they appear in], or with reference to the [individual] Veda? What is the prima facie view? The jurisdiction would be based on the class. Why? From [Vedic] statement — from the very hearing of these words, we understand them as referring to the class. Therefore, the quality of being performed in a low voice is connected with the class of <s>yajus</s>; there is no word establishing the jurisdiction of the Vedas. Moreover, <s>ṛc</s> verses that have crossed over from the <s>Ṛg Veda</s> [into the <s>Yajur Veda</s>] will be performed aloud in the <s>Yajur Veda</s>; otherwise, both properties [loud and soft] would be alternatives for that very same <s>ṛc</s>, and there would be mutual contradiction between the two options. And the context is supported in this way; otherwise, if [the jurisdiction were] by Veda-connection, the low-voice quality would apply in every ritual. Therefore, these words have jurisdiction based on the class.

NOTES:
[Textual apparatus: {3/234: <s>Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā</s> 3.6.5}]

children.text: vedo vā prāyadarśanāt // MS_3,3.2 //
children.translated_text: Or [the terms refer to] the <s>Veda</s>, because of the predominant usage. // MS 3,3.2 //

children.text: vedaṃ vādhikṛtyedam ucyate. kutaḥ? prāyadarśanāt. kim idaṃ prāyadarśanād iti? vedaprāye vākye vedopakrame nigamyamānā ime śabdāḥ śrūyante - prajāpatir vā idam eka āsīt, sa tapo 'tapyata, tasmāt tapas te pānāt trayo devā asṛjyanta - agnir vāyur ādityaḥ, te tapo 'tapyanta tebhyas te pānebhyas trayo vedā asṛjyanta. agner ṛgvedo vāyor yajurveda ādityāt sāmaveda ity evam upakramya nigamana idaṃ śrūyate - uccair ṛcā kriyate, ucchaiḥ sāmnā, [279]{*3/235*} upāṃśu yajuṣeti. etasmāt kāraṇād ebhiḥ prakṛtair upāṃśvādi kartavyam, na jātyā ṛgādibhir ity ucyate. kuta etad avagamyate? vākyopasaṃhāre śrutatvāt, yasmād ita ete vedā jātāḥ, tasmād etair upāṃśvādi kartavyam iti, ṛgādibhir api vedavacanair evopasaṃhāreṇa bhavitavyam. itarathā vākyam eva nāvakalpeta, tatrānarthakā eva bhaveyuḥ, tasmād vedādhikārā iti.
children.translated_text: Or this is said with reference to the <s>Veda</s>. Why? Because of the predominant usage. What does 'because of the predominant usage' mean? In a sentence where the <s>Veda</s> predominates, in the introductory portion of the <s>Veda</s>, these words are heard being concluded — '<s>Prajāpati</s> indeed was alone in the beginning; he performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity); from that <s>tapas</s>, from that heat, three gods were created — <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Āditya</s>; they performed <s>tapas</s>; from them, from that heat, three <s>Vedas</s> were created: from <s>Agni</s> the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, from <s>Vāyu</s> the <s>Yajurveda</s>, from <s>Āditya</s> the <s>Sāmaveda</s>' — having begun thus, in the conclusion this is heard: 'With the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse) [the rite] is performed aloud, with the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) aloud, with the <s>Yajus</s> (formula) in a low voice.' For this reason, the low-voice recitation and such [modes] should be performed with these [terms] as presented — it is said that [the terms refer to] <s>Ṛc</s> and so on not by class but [as Vedic categories]. How is this understood? Because [it is] heard in the concluding portion of the sentence — since from here these <s>Vedas</s> were born, therefore with these the low-voice recitation and such [modes] should be performed — the conclusion must be drawn with <s>Ṛc</s> and other Vedic words as well. Otherwise the sentence itself would not be construed, and [those words] would become purposeless. Therefore, [the terms] have the <s>Veda</s> as their domain.

children.text: liṅgāc ca // MS_3,3.3 //
children.translated_text: And because of the indicatory mark. // MS 3,3.3 //

children.text: liṅgam apy asminn arthe bhavati, yathā ṛgādayaḥ śabdāḥ śaknuvanti vedam abhivaditum iti, ṛgbhiḥ prātardivi deva īyate. yajurvedena tiṣṭhati madhye ahnaḥ. sāmavedenāstamaye mahīyate. vedair aśūnyais tribhir eti sūrya iti{*3/236*}, dvau vedau saṃkīrtya, ṛkśabdaṃ ca triṣu pādeṣu, caturthe pāda upasaṃharati bahuvacanena, vedair aśūnyas tribhir eti sūrya ity ṛkśabdaṃ vedavacanaṃ darśayati. tasmād api paśyāmaḥ. vedādhikārā ete śabdā iti.
children.translated_text: There is also an indicatory mark in this matter — that the words <s>Ṛc</s> and so on are capable of denoting the <s>Veda</s>: 'By the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, in the early morning the god is praised. By the <s>Yajurveda</s> he stands at midday. By the <s>Sāmaveda</s> at sunset he is glorified. With [his] three <s>Vedas</s> undiminished, <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) travels.' Having mentioned two <s>Vedas</s>, and the word <s>Ṛc</s> in three quarters, in the fourth quarter [the text] concludes with the plural — 'With [his] three <s>Vedas</s> undiminished, <s>Sūrya</s> travels' — showing that the word <s>Ṛc</s> is a Vedic term. From this too we see that these words have the <s>Veda</s> as their domain.

NOTES:
[{3/236: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.12.9.1}]

children.text: dharmopadeśāc ca na hi dravyeṇa saṃbandhaḥ // MS_3,3.4 //
children.translated_text: And because of the teaching of <s>dharma</s>, for there is no connection with the material substance. // MS 3,3.4 //

children.text: dharmopadeśaś ca bhavati sāmnaḥ, uccaiḥ sāmneti, sa vedādhikārapakṣe yujyate. jātādhikāre tv ṛca uccais tvena sāmna uccais tvaṃ siddham, nāsya sāmadravyeṇa saha saṃbandho veditavyaḥ, tasmād api vedādhikārā iti.
children.translated_text: There is also a teaching of <s>dharma</s> regarding the <s>Sāman</s> — 'aloud with the <s>Sāman</s>' — and that is appropriate on the view that [the terms] have the <s>Veda</s> as their domain. But on the view that [the terms] have the class as their domain, the loud recitation of the <s>Ṛc</s> would [already] establish the loud recitation of the <s>Sāman</s> [since <s>Sāman</s> is based on <s>Ṛc</s>]; its connection with the material substance of the <s>Sāman</s> need not be understood. Therefore, from this too, [the terms] have the <s>Veda</s> as their domain.

children.text: trayīvidyākhyā ca tadvidi // MS_3,3.5 //
children.translated_text: And [because of] the designation '<s>Trayīvidyā</s>' (threefold knowledge) for one who knows that. // MS 3,3.5 //

children.text: trayī yasya vidyā sa trayīvidyaḥ, yas trīn vedān adhīte, sa evaṃ prakhyāyate{*3/237*}. trayīti caiṣa śabdā ṛksāmayajuḥṣu prasiddhaḥ, yady [280]{*3/238*} ṛksāmayajūṃṣīti trayo vedā ucyante, evaṃ tadvidi trayīvidyākhyā yujyate, bhavati ca. tasmād vedādhikārā ete.
children.translated_text: One whose knowledge is threefold (<s>trayī</s>) is called <s>Trayīvidya</s> — one who studies the three <s>Vedas</s> is so designated. And this word <s>trayī</s> is well-known with reference to <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s>. If <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> are said to be the three <s>Vedas</s>, then the designation <s>Trayīvidyā</s> for one who knows that is appropriate — and it indeed exists. Therefore, these [terms] have the <s>Veda</s> as their domain.

children.text: vyatikrame yathāśrutīti cet // MS_3,3.6 //
children.translated_text: In the case of transgression, [the recitation should be] as heard — if [you say so]. // MS 3,3.6 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - ṛgvedam atikrāntānām ṛcāṃ yajurvede 'py uccais tvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, tatra matpakṣe yathāśrutaḥ prayogo bhaviṣyatīti yad uktam, tatparihartavyam iti. ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram{*3/239*}.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — for <s>Ṛc</s> verses that have transgressed the <s>Ṛgveda</s> [i.e., that appear] in the <s>Yajurveda</s> too, the loud recitation would apply — and there, it was said that on my view the application would be as heard; that [objection] must be addressed. The <s>sūtra</s> extends to the [next] opposing statement.

children.text: na sarvasmin niveśāt // MS_3,3.7 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the application to all. // MS 3,3.7 //

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ, sarvasminn ṛgveda uccais tvaṃ sarvasmiṃś ca yajurveda upāṃśutvam, tatra yady ṛgvedavyatikrāntāyā ṛco yajurveda upāṃśutvaṃ bhavatīti, naitad dūṣyati. vedadharmaḥ san{*3/240*} ṛgdharma iti, vedasya ca na dharmadvayena saṃbandhaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. In the entire <s>Ṛgveda</s> there is loud recitation, and in the entire <s>Yajurveda</s> there is low-voice recitation. Therefore, if for an <s>Ṛc</s> that has transgressed the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, low-voice recitation applies in the <s>Yajurveda</s> — this is not objectionable. Being a property of the <s>Veda</s>, [it is] a property of the <s>Ṛc</s>; and the <s>Veda</s> does not have a connection with two [contradictory] properties.

vedasaṃyogān na prakaraṇena bādhyeta // MS_3,3.8 //
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with the <s>Veda</s>, [the property] would not be overridden by the context. // MS 3,3.8 //

children.text: yad uktam - prakaraṇam evam anugṛhītaṃ bhavatīti, vedasaṃyogād vākyena prakaraṇe bādhyamāne na doṣo bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — that the context would be thus favored — when the context is overridden by the sentence due to the connection with the <s>Veda</s>, there will be no fault.

children.text: guṇamukhyavyatikrame tadarthatvān mukhyena vedasaṃyogaḥ // MS_3,3.9 //
children.translated_text: When there is transgression between the subsidiary and the principal, the connection with the <s>Veda</s> is through the principal, because [the subsidiary] serves the purpose of that [principal]. // MS 3,3.9 //

children.text:
asty ādhānam, ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatta iti{*3/241*}. tad yājurvaidikam, tatra sāmagānam āmananti - ya evaṃ vidvān vāravantīyaṃ gāyati{*3/242*}, ya evaṃ vidvān yajñāyajñīyaṃ gāyati, ya evaṃ vidvān vāmadevyaṃ gāyati{*3/243*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ādhāne sāmagānam uccaiḥ, utopāṃśv iti.
[281]{*3/244*} uccair iti prāptam. kutaḥ? sāmavedenaitat kriyate yad vāravantīyādibhiḥ, tasmād uccair etāni sāmāni geyānīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - guṇānurodhena vā mukhyaṃ vyatikramet, mukhyānurodhena vā guṇam iti, guṇo vyatikramitavyo nyāyyaḥ, mukhyaś cānugrahītavya iti. kutaḥ? mukhyārthatvād guṇasya, guṇasyānuṣṭhānena mukhyaḥ saguṇaḥ kathaṃ syād iti guṇe pravartate, guṇapravṛttyā cen mukhyasya guṇahānir bhavati, guṇapravṛttau phalam eva nāvāptaṃ bhavati. atha pradhānaṃ saguṇaṃ kariṣyāmīti guṇe pravartamāno guṇasya guṇaṃ vinipātayati, nāsya svārtho hīyate. nāsau guṇaṃ saguṇaṃ kartuṃ pravartate, guṇaś ca sāmagānam, pradhānam ādhānam, ādhānasya yājurvaidikatvāt{*3/245*}, upāṃśutā guṇaḥ, sa gaṇadharmam uccais tvaṃ sāmavaidikaṃ{*3/246*} bādhate. tasmād upāṃśu sāmāni geyānīti.
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) [ritual]: 'He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire.' That is of the <s>Yajurveda</s>. There, <s>Sāman</s> chanting is prescribed — 'He who, knowing thus, chants the <s>Vāravantīya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>],' 'He who, knowing thus, chants the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>],' 'He who, knowing thus, chants the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>].' There the doubt arises: should the <s>Sāman</s> chanting in the <s>Ādhāna</s> be aloud, or in a low voice?
The prima facie view is: aloud. Why? Because this is performed through the <s>Sāmaveda</s> — the <s>Vāravantīya</s> and other [<s>Sāmans</s>] — therefore these <s>Sāmans</s> should be chanted aloud.
Having arrived at this, we say: should the subsidiary conform to the principal and [thus its property] be transgressed, or should the principal conform to the subsidiary and [thus its property] be transgressed? It is proper that the subsidiary be transgressed, and the principal be upheld. Why? Because the subsidiary serves the purpose of the principal — the subsidiary operates so that the principal may possess [its] subsidiary; and if the operation of the subsidiary causes the principal to lose its property, then by the operation of the subsidiary, the very purpose is not achieved. But when one says 'I shall make the principal possess [its] subsidiary' and, while operating on the subsidiary, overrides the subsidiary's [own] property — [the subsidiary's] own purpose is not lost. [The subsidiary] does not operate to make the subsidiary possess [its own] subsidiary; and the <s>Sāman</s> chanting is the subsidiary, the <s>Ādhāna</s> is the principal. Because the <s>Ādhāna</s> belongs to the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the low-voice mode is [its] subsidiary property, and that overrides the class-property of loud recitation belonging to the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāmans</s> should be chanted in a low voice.

children.text: bhūyastvenobhayaśruti // MS_3,3.10 //
children.translated_text: When both [<s>Vedas</s>] are heard, [the determination is] by preponderance. // MS 3,3.10 //

children.text:
yajurvede jyotiṣṭomaṃ samāmananti - jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeta iti, tathā sāmavede 'py asyaivam eva samāmnānam. sakṛc ca kṛtāyāṃ buddhau dvitīyaṃ guṇārthaṃ śravaṇaṃ bhavati. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ yājurvaidikam{*3/247*} āmnānaṃ kriyārtham, sāmavaidikaṃ{*3/248*} guṇārtham uta viparītam iti. yatarac cāmnānaṃ kriyārthaṃ taddharmā bhaviṣyanti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sāmavedikaṃ{*3/249*} kriyārthaṃ yājurvedikaṃ{*3/250*} vety aniścayo viśeṣān avagamād iti.
[282]{*3/251*} evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - bhūyastvena guṇānāṃ paricchidyeta, yatra bhūyāṃso guṇāḥ samāmnātāḥ, tatra kriyārthā{*3/252*} codaneti gamyate. yatra hi kartavyatayā codanā, tatretikartavyatākāṅkṣyate, yatrākāṅkṣitetikartavyatā, tatretikartavyatāvacanaṃ nyāyyam. ye ca bhūyāṃso guṇāḥ, setikartavyatā, tad itikartavyatāliṅgena kartavyatācodanām{*3/253*} anumimīmahe, yathā bahuṣu rājapratimeṣūpaviṣṭeṣu yasya śvetaṃ chatraṃ bālavyajanaṃ ca, sa rājety avagamyate, anākhyāto 'pi rājaliṅgena. evaṃ kartavyatāliṅgena guṇānāṃ bhūyastvena jyotiṣṭomasya yājurvaidikasya{*3/254*} codanānumīyate. tasmāj jyotiṣṭomasyopāṃśuprayogaḥ, yajurvedena hi jyotiṣṭomaḥ kriyate, yat tena codyate. acoditaṃ na śakyate kartum iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Yajurveda</s> the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is prescribed: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' Similarly, in the <s>Sāmaveda</s> too there is a prescription of the same. And once the understanding has been formed once, the second hearing serves a subsidiary purpose. There the doubt arises: is the <s>Yajurvaidika</s> (Yajurvedic) prescription the one that enjoins the action, with the <s>Sāmavaidika</s> (Sāmavedic) serving a subsidiary purpose, or is it the reverse? Whichever prescription enjoins the action — the properties of that [<s>Veda</s>] will apply. What then is the prima facie view? Whether the <s>Sāmavedic</s> enjoins the action or the <s>Yajurvedic</s> — there is uncertainty, because no distinguishing [feature] is understood.
Having arrived at this, we say: [the determination] should be by the preponderance of subsidiary [elements]. The [<s>Veda</s>] in which more subsidiary [elements] are prescribed — there the injunction is understood to enjoin the action. For where there is an injunction to act, the subsidiary ritual procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) is expected; where the subsidiary ritual procedure is expected, the statement of subsidiary ritual procedure is appropriate. And those that have more subsidiary [elements] — that [set] constitutes the subsidiary ritual procedure; by the indicatory mark of subsidiary ritual procedure, we infer the injunction to act. Just as when many persons resembling a king are seated, the one who has a white umbrella and a fan is understood to be the king, even though unannounced, by the indicatory marks of kingship — similarly, by the indicatory mark of subsidiary ritual procedure, the preponderance of subsidiary [elements], the <s>Yajurvedic</s> injunction of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is inferred. Therefore the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> has low-voice application, for the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is performed by the <s>Yajurveda</s>, as enjoined by it. What is not enjoined cannot be performed.

children.text: asaṃyuktaṃ prakaraṇād itikartavyatārthitvāt // MS_3,3.11 //
children.translated_text: That which is unconnected [is assigned] from the context, because [it] seeks the subsidiary ritual procedure. // MS 3,3.11 //

children.text:
uktāni viniyogakāraṇāni śrutir liṅgaṃ vākyam iti. śrutir aindryā gārhapatyam iti{*3/255*} dvitīyā vibhaktiḥ, liṅgaṃ mantreṣu vacanasāmarthyaṃ bahirdevasadanaṃ dāmīti{*3/256*}, vākyam aruṇayā krīṇātīti{*3/257*}. atha kim etāvanty eva viniyogakāraṇāni? nety ucyate. kim aparaṃ kāraṇam iti praśnenaivopakramaḥ, bhavati ca praśnenaivopakramaḥ, yathā kā nāmeyaṃ nadī? ko nāmāyaṃ pravataḥ? kim idaṃ phalam iti.
tad ucyate - asaṃyuktaṃ prakaraṇāt, itikartavyatārthitvāt, yad asaṃyuktaṃ śrutyā liṅgena vākyena vā, tat prakaraṇāt, itikartavyatārthitvāt. yad itikartavyatākāṅkṣiṇaḥ saṃnidhau pūraṇasamartham upanipatati yad vacanam, tat{*3/258*} tena prakṛtena sahaikavākyatāṃ yāti. [283]{*3/259*} tasmāt prakṛte viniyujyate. kim ihodāharaṇam? kiṃ ca prayojanam iti. darśapūrṇamāsau prakṛtya śrūyate - samidho yajati, tanūnapātaṃ yajati, iḍo yajati, barhir yajati, svāhākāraṃ yajati{*3/260*} iti{*3/261*}, tāni tatraiva prakaraṇasāmarthyād viniyujyante, nāgnihotre jyotiṣṭome vā.
children.translated_text:
The causes of assignment have been stated: direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and sentence (<s>vākya</s>). Direct statement is the second case-ending [as in] '<s>aindrī gārhapatyam</s>'; the indicatory mark is the power of words in the <s>mantras</s> [as in] 'outside the divine hall, the rope'; the sentence [as in] 'he purchases with a red [cow].' Now, are these alone the causes of assignment? No, it is said. What is the additional cause? The inquiry begins with a question, and it does proceed with a question — just as 'What is the name of this river?', 'What is this mountain?', 'What is this fruit?'
It is said: that which is unconnected [is assigned] from the context, because [it] seeks the subsidiary ritual procedure. That which is unconnected by direct statement, indicatory mark, or sentence — that [is assigned] from the context, because of seeking the subsidiary ritual procedure. The statement that is capable of fulfilling [the expectation] and falls in the proximity of what expects the subsidiary ritual procedure — that enters into a single-sentence relationship with that which is under discussion. Therefore it is assigned to what is under discussion. What is the example here? And what is the purpose? Having set forth the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites, it is heard: 'He sacrifices with the <s>samidh</s> (kindling sticks), he sacrifices to <s>Tanūnapāt</s>, he sacrifices to <s>Iḍā</s>, he sacrifices with the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass), he sacrifices with the <s>svāhākāra</s> (exclamation).' These are assigned there by the force of the context — not in the <s>Agnihotra</s> or the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: kramaś ca deśasāmānyāt // MS_3,3.12 //
children.translated_text: And sequence, because of the similarity of the context. // MS 3,3.12 //

children.text: atha kim etāvanty eva viniyogakāraṇāni. nety ucyate. kiṃ ca? kramaś ca deśasāmānyāt, kramavatām ānupūrveṇopadiśyamānānāṃ{*3/262*} yasya paryāye yaṃ dharmam āmananti, tasya taṃ praty ākāṅkṣānumīyate, satyām ākāṅkṣāyāṃ ekavākyabhāvaḥ, tasmāt tato viniyoga iti. kim ihodāharaṇam? kiṃ ca prayojanam? ānupūrvyavatāṃ yāgānām anumantraṇeṣv āmnāteṣūpāṃśuyājasya krame dabdhir nāmāsīti{*3/263*} samāmnātaḥ, tasyākāṅkṣām utpādya tenaikavākyatāṃ yāt vā tatraiva viniyogam arhatīti, tathā caindrāgnaṃ karma viyātasajātasyāsti bhrātṛvyavataḥ{*3/264*}, tasya yājyānuvākyāyugalam apy āmnāyata aindrāgnam, indrāgnī rocanādivaḥ pravarṣaṇibhya{*3/265*} ity{*3/266*} ekam, aparam indrāgnī navatiṃ puraḥ [284]{*3/267*} ślathad vṛtram iti{*3/268*}. tatra liṅgād viniyoge siddhe viśeṣaviniyogo bhavati, pūrvaṃ yugalaṃ pūrvasyaindrāgnasya, uttaram uttarasyeti, etad udāharaṇaṃ prayojanaṃ ceti.
children.translated_text: Now, are these alone the causes of assignment? No, it is said. What else? And sequence, because of the similarity of the context. For [elements] that are taught in sequence, of those being instructed in order, in whichever turn a particular <s>dharma</s> is prescribed — for that [element], an expectation toward that [<s>dharma</s>] is inferred; when the expectation exists, there is a single-sentence relationship; therefore, the assignment follows from that. What is the example here? And what is the purpose? Among the <s>anumantraṇas</s> (consecrating formulas) prescribed in sequence for the sequential <s>yāgas</s> (sacrifices), there is one prescribed in the sequence of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> (low-voice sacrifice) — [namely,] '<s>Dabdhi</s> was her name' — and having generated an expectation for that [sacrifice], it either enters into a single-sentence relationship with it and merits assignment there. Similarly, the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (related to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>) rite exists for one who has an extended rival of the same class; for that, a pair of <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> (offering and invocatory verses) is also prescribed as <s>Aindrāgna</s>: '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, [shining] from the sky, showerers' — this is one, and the other is '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, ninety fortresses, loosening <s>Vṛtra</s>.' There, when the assignment is established by indicatory mark, the specific assignment is [by] sequence: the first pair for the first <s>Aindrāgna</s> [rite], the second for the second — this is the example and the purpose.

children.text: ākhyā caivaṃ tad arthatvāt // MS_3,3.13 //
children.translated_text: And the designation (<s>ākhyā</s>) [functions] in the same way, because it serves that purpose. // MS_3,3.13 //

children.text: atha kim etāvanty eva viniyogakāraṇānīti. nety ucyate. kiṃ ca? samākhyā caivaṃ syāt. kathaṃ viniyogakāraṇam iti. samākhyā sati saṃbandhe bhavati, yathā pācako lāvaka iti, tatra pācakaśabdam upalabhya pacatināsya saṃbandha iti gamyate, evaṃ vede 'pīti. akṛtakārthasaṃbandhaṃ{*3/269*} samācakṣāṇaṃ śabdam upalabhya bhavati saṃbandhe tasmin saṃpratyayaḥ. kim ihodāharaṇaṃ prayojanaṃ ca? ādhvaryavam iti samākhyātāni karmāṇy adhvaryuṇā kartavyāni, hautram iti ca hotrā. etad udāharaṇaṃ prayojanaṃ ceti.
children.translated_text: Now, are these the only causes of assignment (<s>viniyoga</s>)? No, it is said. What else? The designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) too would function in this way. How is it a cause of assignment? The designation occurs when there is a [pre-existing] connection — just as [in the words] '<s>pācaka</s>' (cook) and '<s>lāvaka</s>' (reaper): upon hearing the word '<s>pācaka</s>,' one understands 'this one has a connection with cooking.' Similarly in the <s>Veda</s> as well. Upon hearing a word that expresses a connection with an unaccomplished purpose {*3/269*}, there arises the cognition of that connection. What is the example and the purpose here? The rites designated as '<s>ādhvaryava</s>' (belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>) are to be performed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; and those [designated as] '<s>hautra</s>' (belonging to the <s>Hotṛ</s>), by the <s>Hotṛ</s>. This is the example and the purpose.
