children.text: śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ samavāye pāradaurbalyam arthaviprakarṣāt // MS_3,3.14 //
children.translated_text: When direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), sentence (<s>vākya</s>), context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), position (<s>sthāna</s>), and designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) co-occur, each successive one is weaker [than the preceding], because of the increasing remoteness of meaning. // MS_3,3.14 //

children.text:
uktāni viniyogakāraṇāni, śrutiliṅgaṃ vākyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sthānaṃ samākhyānam iti, teṣāṃ samavāye kiṃ balīya iti cintyate, ekārthavṛttitvād vāco yugapad asaṃbandhād dvayor dvayoḥ saṃpradhāraṇā. tatra śrutiliṅgayoḥ kiṃ śrutibalīyasy āhosvil liṅgam iti. kiṃ punar atrodāharaṇam? aindryā [285]{*3/270*} gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti, atra cintyate - kim indrasya gārhapatyasya vopasthānaṃ kartavyam ity aniyamaḥ, uta gārhapatyasyaiveti. yadi tulyabale ete kāraṇe tato vikalpaḥ, atha śrutir balīyasī, gārhapatya evopastheyaḥ.
kā punar atra śrutiḥ? kiṃ liṅgam? śrutir gārhapatyaśabdaśravaṇam, liṅgaṃ punaḥ, kadā ca na starīrasi nendrasaścasi dāśuṣe, itīndraśabdasya viśiṣṭadevatābhidhānasāmarthyam. atha kiṃ vākyaṃ nāma? saṃhatya artham abhidadhati padāni vākyam. yady evam idam api vākyam - aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti, idam api - kadā cana starīr asīti{*3/271*}, ubhayatrāpi saṃhatyārtham abhidadhati padāni. tena vākyasya vākyasya caiṣā saṃpradhāraṇā, na śrutiliṅgayoḥ, yadi vā śrutiliṅgavākyāni vivektavyāni, idaṃ śrutivākyayor antaram, idaṃ liṅgavākyayor iti.
tad abhidhīyate - yat tāvac chabdasyārtham abhidhātuṃ sāmarthyam, talliṅgam, yad arthasyābhidhānaṃ śabdasya śravaṇamātrādevāvagamyate, sa śrutyāvagamyate, śravaṇaṃ śrutiḥ. ekārtham anekaṃ padaṃ vākyam ity uktam eva. tad etat sarveṣv eva vākyeṣu samavetaṃ viviktaṃ ca dṛśyate. iha tāvat kadā cana starīr asīty{*3/272*} anena mantreṇa indra upasthātavya iti, naitat kasyacic chabdasya śravaṇād evāvagamyate. nāpi śabdāntarasya samīpa uccāritasya sāmarthyam asti, yenaitad avagamyate. etasyāṃ khalv ṛcīndraśabdo vidyate, yo viśiṣṭāṃ devatām avagamayituṃ śaknoti, tayā cāvagamitayā prayojanam astīti. tenendropasthāna indraśabdaḥ prayujyate, tadekavākyatāc cāvaśiṣṭāni padāni, na tv [286]{*3/273*} evam asyām ṛci kasyacic chabdasya sāmarthyād gārhapatyasyopasthānaṃ bhavati. śravaṇād eva tu gārhapatyaśabdasya, vayam agniṃ pratīmo na liṅgāt. yadi tu liṅgaṃ balīyaḥ, indra upasthātavyaḥ, yadi gārhapatyaśravaṇam, tato gārhapatyaḥ.
evaṃ tarhi liṅgavākye virudhyamāna iha saṃpradhārye na śrutiliṅge, indraśabdasya viśiṣṭadevatābhidhānasāmarthyād indropasthānam, yadi liṅgaṃ balīyaḥ. atha tu vākyam, gārhapatya upastheyaḥ. vākyaṃ hy etad aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti. naitad evam, yady apy etad vākyaṃ śrutir apy atrāsti, yā tv atra śrutiḥ, sā liṅgena virudhyate, na yad vākyam. katham? balīyasy api hi liṅge, aindryopatiṣṭhata ity etad gārhapatyaśabdena sahaikavākyatām upaityaiva{*3/274*}, yadi hi nopeyāt, tato liṅgena virudhyate. yas tu gārhapatyaśravaṇād evārthaḥ pratīyate, sa liṅge balīyasi parityakto bhavati. nāsāv upasthānena saṃbadhyate, tadā hīndraṃ gārhapatyaśabdo 'bhivaded agnisamīpaṃ vā. atha nu śrutiḥ pramāṇaṃ bhavati, tato liṅgenāvagatam indropasthānaṃ bādhyeta. tasmāc chrutiliṅgayor evaiṣa virodhaḥ, na liṅgavākyayor iti. athavā nātraikavākyatvād indraprādhānyaṃ gārhapatyaprādhānyaṃ vopasthānasya. kutas tarhi? indraśabdavattvān mantrasya, indraprādhānyam, dvitīyāvibhaktiśravaṇād gārhapatyaprādhānyam. tasmāc chrutiliṅgayor virodhaḥ.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? tulyabale ete kāraṇa iti. katham? idam api kāraṇam, idam api, śrutir api, liṅgam api{*3/275*}. na hi vijñānasya vijñānasya ca kaścid viśeṣa upalabhyate rūpaṃ prati, asya bhaṅgurasyeva rūpam, asya dṛḍhasyeveti. nanu liṅgasya bhaṅgurasyeva rūpam, savicikitso hi bhavati liṅgāt pratyayaḥ, nirvicikitsaḥ śruteḥ. naitad yuktam, yato liṅgāt [287]{*3/276*} savicikitsaḥ pratyayaḥ, tasya ca śruteś ca naiva saṃpradhāraṇāsti. yatas tu khalu liṅgān nirvicikitsaḥ pratyayaḥ sa śrutyā vikalpitum arhati. nanu naiva kadācil liṅgān nirvicikitsaḥ pratyayo 'sti. naitad evam, evaṃ hi sati naiva liṅgaṃ nāma kiṃcit pramāṇam abhaviṣyat. kāmaṃ mā bhūt pramāṇam, bhavati tu saṃśayo liṅgaparijñāteṣv artheṣu. yadi vā vispaṣṭam evāprāmāṇyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ. katham? samartham etad imam artham abhinirvartayitum iti liṅgād etāvad avagamyate. na ca yad yasya nirvartanāyālam, tad asaty eva vacane tan nirvartayitum arhati. tasmān na liṅgaṃ viniyojakam iti.
atrābhidhīyate - prakaraṇavato 'rthasya saṃnidhāne yam artham āmananti, sa tasya sādhanabhūta ity eva gamyate. kathaṃ khalūpakariṣyatīti saṃdihyamāne bhavati sāmarthyāt pariniścayaḥ. yatrāyaṃ samarthaḥ, tatra śakyo viniyoktam iti, tasmād bhavati liṅgaṃ pramāṇam iti. na ca liṅgaprāmāṇye vinigamanāyāṃ hetur asti. tasmāt tulyabale ete kāraṇe, kadā cana starīr asīti{*3/277*} liṅgād indra upasthātavyaḥ, śruter gārhapatya iti. avirodhāt khalv apīmam evārthaṃ pratipadyāmahe. balīyān api hetur virudhyamānm abalīyāṃsaṃ bādhitum arhati nāviruddham, na ca kaścana virodhaḥ, yad indram upatiṣṭhetānena mantreṇa, gārhapatyam api.
nanv ayam eva virodhaḥ - sakṛd upasthānaṃ coditam, asakṛd abhinirvartyata iti. upastheyabhedāt pratipradhānam āvartante guṇā iti nyāya evaiṣa na virodhaḥ. ayaṃ tarhi virodhaḥ - gārhapatya upasthīyamāne 'gnivacana indraśabdo guṇaṃ kriyāyogaṃ vāpekṣamāṇo bhavitum arhati. indre tūpasthātavye nirapekṣa indra[288]{*3/278*}vacana eva, gauṇamukhyayoś ca mukhye saṃpratyaya iti. neti brūmaḥ - virodhe mukhyena gauṇo bādhyeta, na ca kaścid virodhaḥ, yugapad abhhidhāne hi virudhyeyātām. iha cānyasmin prayoge 'gnivacano 'nyasminn indravacanaḥ. atas tulyabale ete kāraṇe iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - śrutiliṅgayoḥ śrutibalīyasī. kutaḥ? arthaviprakarṣāt. kim idam arthaviprakarṣād iti? arthasya viprakarṣo 'rthaviprakarṣaḥ. kaḥ punar arthaḥ? śrutyārthaḥ. gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti saṃnikṛṣṭaḥ śrutyarthaḥ, indra upastheya iti viprakṛṣṭaḥ. katham? kadā cana starīr asīty{*3/279*} anena mantreṇendra upasthātavya iti na śrūyate. saty apīndrābhidhānasāmarthye vacanābhāvād anupasthānīya indra ity eva gamyate.
nanv idam uktam - prakaraṇāmnānād aṅgam ity avagamyate, sāmarthyād viniyoga iti. naitad asti, uktam evaitat - dharmasya śabdamūlatvād aśabdam anapekṣaṃ syād iti. yad etat prakaraṇaṃ liṅgaṃ cobhayam apy etad śabdam. na cātikrāntapratyakṣaviṣaya evaṃlakṣaṇake 'rthe śabdam antareṇa paricchedo 'vakalpate. ato manyāmahe - viprakṛṣṭaṃ śrutyarthāl liṅgam iti. yady evaṃ śrutir yatra virodhinī na vidyate, tatrāpi na liṅgād arthaparicchedaḥ. tatraitad eva nāsti liṅgaṃ pramāṇam iti. kuta evaitena śrutir virotsyata iti. tatra śrutiliṅgayor balīyastvaṃ prati saṃpradhāraṇaiva nopapadyata iti brūmaḥ.
atrocyate - itikartavyathārthinaḥ prakaraṇavato 'rthasya saṃnidhāv upanipatito mantra āmnānasāmarthyād itikartavyatākāṅkṣasya vākyaśeṣatām abhyupetyaitena mantreṇa yajeteti. kim uktaṃ bhavati? yāgenābhīpsite sādhyamāne 'nena mantreṇopakuryād iti, na cāntareṇendrābhidhānam ayaṃ mantra upakartuṃ śaknoti, [289]{*3/280*} tenaitad uktaṃ bhavati, anenendro 'bhidhātavya iti. ataḥ śrutimūla evāyam arthaḥ. yadi śrutimūlaḥ, na śrutyantareṇa bādhituṃ śakyaḥ. tad etal liṅgaṃ yadi vā naiva pramāṇam, yadi vā śrutyā vikalpitum arhatīti. nāpy apramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati, nāpi vikalpiṣyata iti brūmaḥ. katham? śrutilakṣaṇo 'yam artha ity upapāditam, tasmān nāpramāṇam. yatas tu khalv ānumānikīm ekavākyatāṃ liṅgasāmarthyaṃ cāpekṣya śrauto 'yam arthaḥ, yad indrasyopasthānam anena mantreṇety avagamyate, pratyakṣā tu śrutigārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti, sa eṣo 'rthaviprakarṣaḥ. prathamaṃ tāval liṅgajñānam, tataḥ sāṃarthyāc chabdenāyam artho 'bhihito bhavati, tad etac chrutivirodhe nāvakalpate, vispaṣṭaṃ hy avagatam etat, anena mantreṇa gārhapatya upastheya iti. tatra vijñātam etad evam ayam upakaroti mantra ity etasmiṃś ca nirjñāte kṛtasāmarthyayor vākyaprakaraṇayor naitad evaṃ kalpayituṃ śakyam, indropasthānaṃ śabdenābhihitam iti. tasmād arthaviprakarṣāc chrutyā liṅgaṃ bādhyata iti.
vikalpasya cānyāyyatvāt, anyāyyaś ca vikalpaḥ. tatra hy abhāvaḥ pakṣe nityavac ca, aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhata iti śrūyamāne yad abhāvaḥ pakṣe parikalpyate, tad aśrutaṃ bhavati, śrutaṃ ca hīyate. yāvāṃś ca śrutasyārthasyotsarge doṣaḥ, tāvān aśrutaparikalpanāyām, ubhayatra hi prasiddhir bādhyate. tasmād anyāyyatvād vikalpasya śrutiliṅgayoḥ śrutibalīyasīty avagacchāmaḥ.
atha yad uktam - sati virodhe nyāyyo bādhaḥ, na cātrāsti virodha iti, ayam asti virodhaḥ, yad akṛtasāmarthyayor vākyaprakaraṇayor indropasthānavācinī śrutir bhavati, kṛtasāmarthyayos tu nāvakalpate, na ca vākyaprakaraṇābhyāṃ yugapat kṛtasāmarthyābhyām [290]{*3/281*} akṛtasāmarthyābhyāṃ ca śakyaṃ bhavitum. tasmād virodhaḥ, virodhe ca śrutir liṅgād balīyasīti.
liṅgavākyayor virodhe kim udāharaṇam? syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghṛtasya dhārayā suṣevaṃ{*3/282*} kalpayāmi. tasmin sīdāmṛte pratitiṣṭha vrīhīṇāṃ medha sumanasyamāna iti{*3/283*}. atra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ kṛtsno mantra upastaraṇe puroḍāśāsādane ca prayoktavyaḥ, uta kalpayāmy anta upastaraṇe, tasmin sīdetyevamādiḥ puroḍāśāsādana iti. yadi vākyaṃ balīyaḥ, tataḥ kṛtsna ubhayatra. katham? suṣevaṃ{*3/284*} kalpayāmīty etad apekṣya, tasmin sīdetyevamādiḥ pūrveṇaikavākyatām upaiti - yat kalpayāmi, tasmin sīdeti. atha liṅgaṃ balīyaḥ, tataḥ kalpayāmy antaḥ sadanakaraṇe. katham? syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomīti{*3/285*}, sadanakaraṇam abhivaditum alam iti. tasmin sīdety ayam api puroḍāśaṃ sādayitum iti, sādane viniyujyate.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? tulyabale ete kāraṇa iti, yathā liṅgaṃ prati śruter balīyastvam uktam, na tathā vākyaṃ prati liṅgasyocyate. athavā vākyam eva liṅgād balīyaḥ. kutaḥ? tad dhi śrutyāpi bādhyate, na ca balīyaḥ kāraṇaṃ śakyate bādhitum. tenāsya bhaṅguratām adhyavasyāmaḥ, yas tv ekena bādhyate, śakyo 'sāv anyenāpi bādhitum iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - liṅgavākyayor liṅgaṃ balīya iti. kutaḥ? arthaviprakarṣāt. ko 'trārthaviprakarṣaḥ? prakaraṇavataḥ saṃnidhāv āmnānād darśapūrṇamāsāṅgam ayaṃ mantra ity avagamyate, tasmin sīdeti puroḍāśāsādanābhidhānasāmarthyāt sādane viniyujyamāne kṛtasāmarthyaṃ mantrāmnānam iti, nāsti pramāṇaṃ yenopastaraṇe 'pi viniyujyeta. tathā syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomīty{*3/286*} eṣo 'pi prakaraṇāmnānasāmarthyād eva darśapūrṇamāsāṅgatām āpannaḥ [291]{*3/287*} sāmarthyād evopastaraṇe viniyogāt kṛtaprayojane na puroḍāśāsādane viniyogam arhati, na hy asmin viniyuj-yamānasya kiṃcid api prayojanam asti. evam upastaraṇe tasmin sīdety asya nāsti sāmarthyam. pūroḍāśāsādane 'pi syonaṃ ta ity{*3/288*} asya. pūrveṇaikavākyatām upetyopastaraṇe sāmarthyam, pūrvasya pareṇaikavākyatvāt sādane, na tu svarūpeṇobhayoḥ. tad eṣo 'rthaviprakarṣaḥ.
yat syonaṃ ta ity{*3/289*} asya pratyakṣaṃ sadanakarmaṇo 'bhidhānasāmarthyam, tan mukhyam. tasmin sīdety asya punaḥ pūrveṇa sahaikavākyatām upagatasya bhavati jaghanyam. tad atra pūrvasya mantrasyābhidhānasāmarthyād upastaraṇe viniyoga ukto bhavatīti, saṃnikṛṣṭo liṅgasya śrutyarthaḥ, uttarasya tūpajanite 'bhidhānasāmarthye tataḥ śrutyartha iti liṅgāntarito viprakṛṣṭo bhavati. evam uttarasya sādane saṃnikṛṣṭaḥ pūrvasya ca liṅgāntaritaḥ. tasmād arthaviprakṛṣṭāl liṅgavākyayor liṅgaṃ balavattaram, tataḥ syonam ity{*3/290*} eṣa śabdo yady apy uttareṇākāṅkśita iti sādane 'pi prayogam arhati, tathāpi bhitvā vākyam upastaraṇa eva viniyoktavyaḥ. tasmin sīdety eṣa ca sādane.
nanu syonaṃ ta ity{*3/291*} asya śabdasya yathaivopastaraṇābhidhānasāmarthyam, evam uttareṇaikavākyatām upagantuṃ sāmarthyam, sāmarthyaṃ ca liṅgam ity ucyate. tasmād bhidyamāne vākye liṅgam eva bādhitaṃ bhavatīti. satyam evam, etad api liṅgam, liṅgam api khalv etad evaṃlakṣaṇakaṃ viprakṛṣṭārtham eva bhavati, liṅgād ekavākyatā, tasmād abhidhānasāmarthyam. tataḥ śrutyartha iti viprakṛṣṭārthatā, viprakṛṣṭārthatā ca bādhane hetubhūtā. tasmān na [292]{*3/292*} uttaraṇaikavākyatāṃ yāsyatīti. evaṃ tasmin sīdety uttaraṃ na pūrveṇāpi.
api cottareṇaikavākyatām upagatasya na kiṃcid api dṛṣṭam asti kāryam, upastaraṇapratyāyanaṃ tu dṛṣṭam. kutaḥ? śrutatvād upastaraṇasya sādanasya ca. evam uttarasya sādanapratyāyanam, na tu pūrveṇaikavākyatāyām. na caitau pūrvottarābhyām ekavākyatām antareṇa pṛthag yathāyathaṃ kārye na kurutaḥ. tasmāt pūrvaḥ pūrvatra viniyojanīyaḥ, uttara uttaratreti.
atha yad uktam - śrutyāpi tad bādhitam iti vākyenāpi tad bādhitavyam iti. naitad evam, na hi bādhitasyānyenāpi bādhanam eva nyāyyam, bādhitaṃ hy anugṛhītavyam arthavattvāya, śrutiṃ prati viprakṛṣṭārtham, vākyaṃ prati saṃnikṛṣṭārtham, tasmāl liṅgaṃ balīya iti.
atha vākyaprakaraṇayor virodhe katham iti. kiṃ punaḥ prakaraṇaṃ nāma? kartavyasyetikartavyatākāṅkṣasya vacanaṃ prakaraṇam. prārambho hi sa tasyā vacanakriyāyāḥ, na eṣa vidhyādir vidhyantāpekṣaḥ. vākyaṃ tūktam eva. tayor virodhe kim udāharaṇam? sūktavākanigadaḥ. tatra hi paurṇamāsīdevatā amāvāsyādevatāś cāmnātāḥ, tāḥ paraspareṇaikavākyatāṃ nābhyupayanti. tatra liṅgasāmarthyāt paurṇamāsīprayogād indrāgniśabda utkraṣṭavyo 'māvāsyāyāṃ prayoktavyaḥ. athedānīṃ saṃdihyate, yo 'sya śeṣaḥ, avīvṛdhetāṃ mahojyāyo krātām{*3/293*} iti{*3/294*}, sa kiṃ yāvat kṛtvaḥ sūktavāke samāmnātaḥ, tāvat kṛtva ubhayoḥ paurṇamāsyam āvāsyayoḥ prayoktavyaḥ, prakaraṇaṃ balavattaram iti, uta yatrendrāgniśabda utkṛṣya nītaḥ, tatraiva prayoktavyaḥ, vākyaṃ balavattaram iti. evaṃ sarveṣu saṃśayaḥ.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? tulyabale ete kāraṇa iti. kutaḥ? [293]{*3/295*} itaratrāpy ākāṅkṣā, itaratrāpi, tulyāyām ākāṅkṣāyāṃ nāsti vinigamanāyāṃ hetuḥ, tasmāt tulyabala iti. athavā vākyaṃ durbalam, bādhitaṃ hi talliṅgena.
ity evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - prakaraṇād vākyaṃ balīyaḥ. katham? arthaviprakarṣāt. ko 'trārthavipra-karṣaḥ? vākya ekaikaṃ padaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ sākāṅkṣaṃ bhavati, kṛtsnaṃ paripūrṇaṃ bhavati, tatra pratyakṣa ekavākyabhāvaḥ, prakaraṇe tv apratyakṣaḥ. katham? itikartavyatākāṅkṣasya samīpa upanipatitaṃ pūrṇam iti tasya prakṛtasya sākāṅkṣatvam avagamyate, naikavākyabhūtam ity anumīyate. ekavākyatayā cābhidhānasāmarthyam avakalpyābhihito 'yam evaṃ bhavatīti parikalpanā. eṣo 'trārthaviprakarṣaḥ, yad vākyasya samāsannā śrutiḥ, prakaraṇasya viprakṛṣṭā. tasmāt sūktavākena prastaraṃ{*3/296*} praharatīti paurṇamāsīdevatāvācinām amāv āsyā devatāvācināṃ ca niṣkṛṣya prayoge tac cheṣāṇām api niṣkṛṣya prayogaḥ, tena yady api prakaraṇasāmarthyāt paurṇamāsīdevatāpadaśeṣāṇām amāv āsyā devatāvācibhiḥ sahaikavākyatānumīyate, pratyakṣā tv amāv āsyā devatāpadaiḥ saha, na ca pratyakṣavirodhe 'numānaṃ saṃbhavati. arthavati ca prakaraṇe saṃjāte na nirākāṅkṣāṇām ākāṅkṣā śakyopapādayitum.
atha yad uktam - liṅgenāpi hi tad bādhyate, ataḥ prakaraṇenāpi bādhitavyam iti. na, yad anyenāpi bādhyate, tad bhaṅguram anyatrāpīty avagantavyam. atha bhaṅguram, pramāṇam eva nābhaviṣyat. kiṃcit tu prati kasyacit prabhāvaḥ, vākyasya prakaraṇaṃ prati bādhakaśaktir na tu liṅgaṃ prati, liṅgaṃ prati viprakṛṣṭārtham etat prakaraṇaṃ prati saṃnikṛṣṭārtham, tena vākyena prakaraṇaṃ bādhyata iti.
[294]{*3/297*} atha prakaraṇasya kramasya ca virodhe kim udāharaṇam? rājasūyaprakaraṇe 'bhiṣecanīyakrame śaunaḥśephākhyānādy āmnātam, yadi prakaraṇaṃ balavat, sarveṣāṃ tad aṅgam, yadi kramaḥ, abhiṣecanīyasyaiva. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? tulyabala ete kāraṇa iti. kutaḥ? na tāvad viśeṣam upalabhāmahe, yenāvagacchāma idaṃ balīya iti. tasmāt tulyabale ete kāraṇa iti. api ca prakaraṇaṃ vākyena bādhitam, tasmād bādhyeta krameṇāpīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - prakaraṇaṃ kramād balīyaḥ. kutaḥ? arthaviprakarṣāt. ko 'trārthaviprakarṣaḥ? prakaraṇavataḥ sākāṅkṣatvāt, tatsaṃnidhānāmnātena paripūrṇenāpy avakalpetaikavākyatvam, na tu kramavataḥ krama āmnātena, anekasyāmnāyamānasya saṃnidhiviśeṣāmnānamātraṃ hi kramaḥ. tatra saṃnidhiviśeṣāmnānasāmarthyāt kramavataḥ saṃnidhāv āmnātasyānupalabhyamānam evākāṅkṣāvattvam astīty avagantavyam. prakaraṇe tu prakaraṇavataḥ pratyakṣam, na ca prakaraṇavatā kramavatā ca yaugapadyenaikavākyatā saṃbhavaty āmnātasyeti virodhaḥ. tatra prakaraṇe pratyakṣaṃ sākāṅkṣatvam, krama ānumānikaṃ bādhitum arhati, sākāṅkṣatvād ekavākyatvam. ekavākyatvād abhidhānasāmarthyam, sāmarthyāc chrutyartha iti saṃnikṛṣṭaḥ prakaraṇasya śrutyarthaḥ, viprakṛṣṭaḥ kramasya. tasmāt krama karaṇayoḥ prakaraṇaṃ balavattaram iti.
atha yad uktam - vākyenāpi hi tad bādhitam, ato 'nyenāpi tad bādhitavyam iti. naitat, bādhitasyānugraho nyāyyaḥ, na bādhitaṃ{*3/298*} bādhitavyam iti.
atha kramasamākhyayor virodhe kim udāharaṇam? kiṃ balavattaram iti. pauroḍāśikam iti samākhyāte kāṇḍe sāṃnāyyakrame śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya kramaṇa iti{*3/299*} śundhanārtho mantraḥ samāmnātaḥ. tatra saṃdihyate - kiṃ samākhyānasya balīyastvāt puroḍāśa[295]{*3/300*}pātrāṇāṃ śundhane viniyoktavyaḥ, uta kramasya balīyastvāt sāṃnāyyapātrāṇām iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? tulyabale ete karaṇe{*3/301*} syātām. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, yadi vā samākhyaiva balīyasī, bādhito hi kramaḥ prakaraṇenāpīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - kramo balīyān. kutaḥ? arthaviprakarṣāt. kaḥ punar atrārthaviprakarṣaḥ? nirjñāte prakaraṇena kenāpi sahaikavākyatve yat saṃnidhāv āmnāyate, tatrākāṅkṣāṃ parikalpyate, naikavākyatety avagamyate, laukikaś ca śabdaḥ samākhyā. na ca, loka evaṃvidheṣv artheṣu pramāṇam. tasmāt kramo balīyān iti.
yady evaṃ bhavaty evaṃlakṣaṇakeṣu krameṇa viniyogaḥ, na tv arthāviprakarṣāt kramo balīyān. katham? dvayor hi pramāṇayor balīyastvaṃ prati saṃpradhāraṇam, na caivaṃ sati samākhyā pramāṇam, laukikatvāc chabdasya, puruṣasya pramāṇatā bhavatīti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, nātrāṅgabhāvaḥ puruṣaprāmāṇyād gamyate, pauroḍāśikaśabda etasya kāṇḍasya, ity etad atra puruṣapramāṇakam. bhavati cāsminn arthe puruṣaḥ pramāṇam, yathā sāṃnāyyakrama āmnānaṃ puruṣapramāṇakam, yathā prakaraṇam ekavākyatvam, vedaśabdaś cāyam iti. na hy ete 'nindriyaviṣayā arthā upapadyante, eṣv abhiyuktānāṃ prāmāṇyam, ye tv anindriyaviṣayās teṣv abhiyuktā na pramāṇam. tasmāt samākhyā kāraṇam, kāraṇatve ca sati balīyastvaṃ parīkṣyam iti.
ucyate 'rthaviprakarṣas tarhi vaktavyaḥ samākhyāyāḥ. ayam arthaviprakarṣaḥ. upadiśyate hi krame samāmnānāt sāṃnāyyasaṃbandhaḥ, nopadiśyate samākhyāyām, śabdam uccāryamāṇam upalabhyārthāpattyā nūnam astīti kalpyate. tasmāt pūrvavedārthaviprakarṣāt krameṇa samākhyā bādhyata iti.
atha yat tatra tatrocyate - idam anena bādhyate, idam aneneti. tatra yad bādhyate, tat kiṃ bādhakaviṣayaṃ prāptam utāprāptam [296]{*3/302*} iti. kiṃ cātaḥ? yady aprāptam, kiṃ bādhyate? atha prāptam, kathaṃ śakyeta bādhitum? prāptaṃ bādhakaviṣayaṃ pūrvavijñānam iti brūmaḥ. katham? sāmānyasya kāraṇasya vidyamānatvāt. atha kathaṃ nivartate? mithyājñānam{*3/303*} iti pratyayāntaraṃ bhavati. kiṃ tu{*3/304*} khalv amithyājñānasya svarūpam? yasya bādhakaḥ pratyayo vimṛṣyamāṇasyāpi nopapadyate, na tan mithyā. tad eteṣāṃ śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ yat kāraṇaṃ tat paraṃ paraṃ prati balīyo bhavati, naitasyotpannasya vimṛṣyamāṇasya bādhakaṃ vijñānāntaram asti. tasmāt teṣāṃ samavāye virodhe{*3/305*} paradaurbalyam arthavipralkarṣād iti.

The causes of assignment have been stated: direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), sentence (<s>vākya</s>), context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), position (<s>sthāna</s>), and designation (<s>samākhyā</s>). When they co-occur, which is stronger? — this is considered. Since speech serves a single purpose, they cannot [all] apply simultaneously; therefore, they must be weighed in pairs. Among these, [first consider] direct statement and indicatory mark: is direct statement stronger, or the indicatory mark? What is the example here? 'With an <s>Aindrī</s> [verse] [285]{*3/270*} one approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire]' — here the question arises: should the worship be directed toward <s>Indra</s> or toward the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire], with no restriction, or toward the <s>Gārhapatya</s> alone? If these two criteria are of equal strength, there is an option; but if direct statement is stronger, then the <s>Gārhapatya</s> alone is to be worshipped.
What is the direct statement here? And what is the indicatory mark? The direct statement is the hearing of the word '<s>Gārhapatya</s>.' The indicatory mark, on the other hand, is: '<s>kadā cana starīr asi nendrasaś cāsi dāśuṣe</s>' (You are never barren, nor are you without <s>Indra</s> for the worshipper) — the capacity of the word '<s>Indra</s>' to denote a specific deity. Now, what is a 'sentence' (<s>vākya</s>)? Words that jointly convey a meaning constitute a sentence. If so, this too is a sentence — 'with an <s>Aindrī</s> [verse] one approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s>'; and this too — '<s>kadā cana starīr asi</s>' — in both cases, words jointly convey a meaning. Therefore, this is a weighing of sentence against sentence, not of direct statement against indicatory mark. Unless direct statement, indicatory mark, and sentence are to be distinguished [as follows]: this is the difference between direct statement and sentence, this is [the difference] between indicatory mark and sentence.
This is explained: The capacity of a word to denote its meaning — that is the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). When the denotation of a meaning is understood from the mere hearing of the word — that is understood through direct statement (<s>śruti</s>); hearing is <s>śruti</s>. 'Multiple words [conveying] a single meaning constitute a sentence' — this has already been stated. This [sentence-principle] is seen as both combined and separate in all sentences. Now, in '<s>kadā cana starīr asi</s>' {*3/272*} — that <s>Indra</s> is to be worshipped with this mantra — this is not understood from the hearing of any [single] word. Nor is there the capacity of any other word uttered nearby, by which this could be understood. In this <s>ṛc</s> verse, however, the word '<s>Indra</s>' is present, which can make known a specific deity; and when that [deity] is made known, there is a purpose [served]. Therefore, the word '<s>Indra</s>' is employed for the worship of <s>Indra</s>, and from its sentence-unity, the remaining words [follow]. But [286]{*3/273*} in this <s>ṛc</s> verse, the worship of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> does not arise from the capacity of any word. Rather, it is from the mere hearing of the word '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' that we cognize the fire — not from the indicatory mark. But if the indicatory mark is stronger, then <s>Indra</s> is to be worshipped; if the hearing of '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' [is stronger], then the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
If so, then the indicatory mark and the sentence are what conflict here — not direct statement and the indicatory mark. [That is:] from the capacity of the word '<s>Indra</s>' to denote a specific deity, the worship of <s>Indra</s> [follows], if the indicatory mark is stronger. But if the sentence [is stronger], then the <s>Gārhapatya</s> is to be worshipped — for 'with an <s>Aindrī</s> [verse] one approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s>' is a sentence. This is not so. Even though this is a sentence, direct statement (<s>śruti</s>) is also present here. And the direct statement here conflicts with the indicatory mark, not the sentence. How? Even when the indicatory mark is stronger, 'with an <s>Aindrī</s> [verse] one approaches' forms a single sentence with the word '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' {*3/274*}. For if it did not, it would conflict with the indicatory mark. But the meaning that is cognized from the mere hearing of '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' — that, when the indicatory mark is stronger, is abandoned. It is not connected with the worship; for then the word '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' would either address <s>Indra</s> [as '<s>Gārhapatya</s>'] or denote proximity to the fire. But if direct statement is the valid means, then the worship of <s>Indra</s> — understood through the indicatory mark — would be overridden. Therefore, this conflict is between direct statement and the indicatory mark, not between the indicatory mark and the sentence. Alternatively, neither the primacy of <s>Indra</s> nor the primacy of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> in the worship arises from sentence-unity here. From what then? From the mantra's containing the word '<s>Indra</s>' — the primacy of <s>Indra</s> [follows]; from the hearing of the accusative case-ending [on] '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' — the primacy of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>. Therefore, the conflict is between direct statement and indicatory mark.
What is the prima facie view? These two criteria are of equal strength. How? This too is a criterion, and that too — both direct statement and the indicatory mark {*3/275*}. For no difference is perceived between one cognition and another with respect to [their] form — [one cannot say] 'this one has a fragile form, that one has a firm form.' [Objection:] But the indicatory mark has, as it were, a fragile form — for the cognition arising from the indicatory mark is attended by doubt, while that from direct statement is free from doubt. [Reply:] This is not correct. The indicatory mark from which the cognition is attended by doubt — between that and direct statement, there is no weighing at all. But the indicatory mark from which the cognition is free from doubt — that deserves to be weighed against direct statement. [Objection:] But there is never a doubt-free cognition from the indicatory mark. [Reply:] This is not so. For if it were so, the indicatory mark would never be a valid means of knowledge at all. [Objection:] By all means, let it not be a valid means! [Reply:] But doubt does arise in matters ascertained through the indicatory mark. Or perhaps, clearly, it is simply invalid — not [merely] doubtful. How? 'This is capable of bringing about this meaning' — this much is understood from the indicatory mark. But what is sufficient to bring about something need not necessarily bring it about in the absence of a [Vedic] statement. Therefore, the indicatory mark is not a means of assignment.
To this it is said: When something is recorded in proximity to an object that has a context, it is understood to be a subsidiary of that [object]. When there is doubt about how it will be helpful, the determination is made from [its] capacity. Where it is capable — there it can be assigned. Therefore, the indicatory mark is a valid means of knowledge. And there is no reason to determine that the indicatory mark is not valid. Therefore, these two criteria are of equal strength: from '<s>kadā cana starīr asi</s>' {*3/277*}, <s>Indra</s> is to be worshipped through the indicatory mark; the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, through direct statement. And even from the absence of conflict, we arrive at this very conclusion: even a stronger criterion can override a weaker one [only] when there is a conflict — not [otherwise]. And there is no conflict whatsoever in worshipping <s>Indra</s> with this mantra while also [worshipping] the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
[Objection:] But here is the conflict — the worship has been enjoined [only] once, yet it would be performed more than once. [Reply:] 'When there are multiple objects of worship, the subsidiary elements recur for each principal' — this is a legitimate principle, not a conflict. [Objection:] Here then is the conflict: when the <s>Gārhapatya</s> is being worshipped, the word '<s>Indra</s>' — which denotes fire — must be regarded as either qualitative (<s>gauṇa</s>) or as denoting a connection with the action. But when <s>Indra</s> is to be worshipped, the word '<s>Indra</s>' [288]{*3/278*} is independently denotative of <s>Indra</s>, and between secondary and primary [meanings], the primary [is preferred]. [Reply:] We say no — the secondary would be overridden by the primary [only] when there is a conflict. And there is no conflict here, for they would conflict only if both were to be expressed simultaneously. But here, in one application [the word] denotes fire, and in another it denotes <s>Indra</s>. Therefore, these two criteria are of equal strength.
When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: Between direct statement and the indicatory mark, direct statement is stronger. Why? Because of the increasing remoteness of meaning. What does 'because of the increasing remoteness of meaning' mean? The remoteness of meaning (<s>arthaviprakarṣa</s>) [is the explanation]. What is the 'meaning'? The meaning apprehended through direct statement (<s>śruti</s>). 'One approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s>' — this is the proximate meaning apprehended through direct statement. '<s>Indra</s> is to be worshipped' — this is the remote [meaning]. How? '<s>kadā cana starīr asi</s>' {*3/279*} — that <s>Indra</s> is to be worshipped with this mantra is not directly heard. Even though there is the capacity to denote <s>Indra</s>, because of the absence of a [direct] statement, it is understood merely that <s>Indra</s> is not to be worshipped.
[Objection:] But was it not said — 'from being recorded in a context, [something] is understood as a subsidiary; from capacity, the assignment [is made]'? [Reply:] This is not so. It has already been stated: 'Since <s>dharma</s> is rooted in words, what is wordless is not to be regarded.' Both this context and this indicatory mark are indeed verbal. But in matters of this nature — which are beyond the reach of direct perception — determination without words is not possible. Therefore, we hold that the indicatory mark is remote from the meaning apprehended through direct statement. If so, then even where no conflicting direct statement exists, there would be no determination of meaning from the indicatory mark — [and then] the indicatory mark would simply not be a valid means of knowledge. How then could it challenge direct statement? In such [cases], there is no weighing at all between direct statement and the indicatory mark — we say this.
To this it is said: A mantra that falls near an object having a context and requiring a procedural specification, by virtue of the capacity [derived] from its being recorded, enters into sentence-completion with [the object] that expects a procedural specification — [and one understands:] 'one should sacrifice with this mantra.' What is being said? When the desired [result of the] sacrifice is being accomplished, [one understands that] this mantra would assist — and this mantra cannot assist without denoting <s>Indra</s> [289]{*3/280*}. Therefore, what is being said is: 'by this [mantra], <s>Indra</s> is to be denoted.' Hence, this meaning is indeed rooted in direct statement (<s>śruti</s>). If it is rooted in direct statement, it cannot be overridden by another direct statement. This indicatory mark — either it is simply not a valid means, or it can be weighed against direct statement. [Reply:] It will neither be invalid, nor will it be weighed [as equal] — we say. How? It has been established that this meaning is characterized by direct statement; therefore, it is not invalid. But since [the conclusion that] <s>Indra</s> is to be worshipped with this mantra is understood by depending on the inferential sentence-unity and the capacity of the indicatory mark — this meaning is based on direct statement [only mediately]. Whereas the directly perceptible direct statement is: 'one approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.' This is the remoteness of meaning. First there is the knowledge of the indicatory mark; then, from [its] capacity, this meaning is expressed by the word — and this does not hold up in the face of a conflicting direct statement, for it has been clearly understood: 'with this mantra, the <s>Gārhapatya</s> is to be worshipped.' When this has been ascertained — 'this is how this mantra assists' — and when the capacity of the sentence and the context has been fulfilled, one cannot then conjecture: 'the worship of <s>Indra</s> is expressed by the word.' Therefore, because of the remoteness of meaning, the indicatory mark is overridden by direct statement.
And because an option would be improper — an option is indeed improper. For in that [option], there would be absence [of worship of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>] in one alternative, as if [the injunction were] permanently [suspended]. When 'with an <s>Aindrī</s> [verse] one approaches the <s>Gārhapatya</s>' is heard, if absence [of <s>Gārhapatya</s> worship] is imagined in one alternative, then what is heard is abandoned, and what is unheard is imagined. And whatever defect there is in abandoning what is heard, the same [defect] exists in imagining what is unheard — for in both cases, the established [understanding] is overridden. Therefore, because of the impropriety of an option, we understand: between direct statement and the indicatory mark, direct statement is stronger.
As for what was said — 'an override is proper when there is a conflict, but there is no conflict here' — there is this conflict: when the capacity of the sentence and the context has not [yet] been fulfilled, there is a direct statement (<s>śruti</s>) [supporting] the worship of <s>Indra</s>; but when the capacity has been fulfilled, [that reading] does not hold up. And the sentence and the context cannot simultaneously have both fulfilled and unfulfilled capacity [290]{*3/281*}. Therefore, there is a conflict; and in a conflict, direct statement is stronger than the indicatory mark.
What is the example of a conflict between the indicatory mark and the sentence? '<s>syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi, ghṛtasya dhārayā suṣevaṃ</s> {*3/282*} <s>kalpayāmi. tasmin sīdāmṛte pratitiṣṭha, vrīhīṇāṃ medha sumanasyamānaḥ</s>' {*3/283*} ('I make your seat comfortable; with a stream of ghee I prepare it pleasantly. In that [seat] sit down, established in immortality; O rice, rejoicing, be the marrow'). Here the doubt arises: should the entire mantra be used both in the strewing (<s>upastaraṇa</s>) and in the placing of the sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśāsādana</s>), or should [the portion ending with] '<s>kalpayāmi</s>' [be used] in the strewing, and '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' and the rest in the placing of the cake? If the sentence is stronger, then the entire [mantra is used] in both [rites]. How? Looking to '<s>suṣevaṃ kalpayāmi</s>' {*3/284*} (I prepare pleasantly), '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' and the rest form a single sentence with the preceding — 'what I prepare, in that sit down.' But if the indicatory mark is stronger, then [the portion] ending with '<s>kalpayāmi</s>' [is used] in the seat-making. How? '<s>syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi</s>' {*3/285*} — this is sufficient to denote the seat-making. And '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' — this too is assigned to the placing, as [it can] cause the cake to be placed.
What is the prima facie view? These two criteria are of equal strength — for the stronger status of direct statement over the indicatory mark was stated, but [the stronger status of] the indicatory mark over the sentence was not stated in the same way. Or perhaps the sentence is stronger than the indicatory mark. Why? For [the sentence] is overridden even by direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), and a stronger criterion cannot be overridden. Therefore, we infer its fragility — what is overridden by one [criterion] can be overridden by another as well.
When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: Between the indicatory mark and the sentence, the indicatory mark is stronger. Why? Because of the increasing remoteness of meaning. What is the remoteness of meaning here? From being recorded in proximity to a [rite] having a context, it is understood that this mantra is a subsidiary of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon rites). When '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' is assigned to the placing of the cake because of [its] capacity to denote the placing, the capacity of the mantra-recording is fulfilled — and there is no valid means by which it would also be assigned to the strewing. Similarly, '<s>syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi</s>' {*3/286*} — this too, having attained subsidiary status in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> through the capacity of the context-recording [291]{*3/287*}, being assigned to the strewing by virtue of [its own] capacity — since its purpose has been fulfilled — does not deserve to be assigned to the placing of the cake as well, for there is no purpose whatsoever in assigning it [there]. Thus, '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' has no capacity for the strewing, and '<s>syonaṃ te</s>' {*3/288*} has [no capacity] for the placing of the cake. [Their respective] capacity [arises] through sentence-unity: the latter with the former [gives capacity] for the strewing; the former with the latter, [for] the placing — but not through their own form in both [rites]. This is the remoteness of meaning.
The capacity of '<s>syonaṃ te</s>' {*3/289*} to directly denote the seat-making action — that is primary. But '<s>tasmin sīda</s>,' having entered into sentence-unity with the preceding, has [only] a secondary [capacity]. Thus, the assignment of the first mantra to the strewing has been stated on the basis of [its] denotative capacity — so the indicatory mark's meaning apprehended through direct statement is proximate. But for the latter [mantra], whose denotative capacity arises [only] derivatively — its meaning, being mediated by the indicatory mark, is remote. Similarly, for the latter [mantra], the [meaning in] the placing is proximate; for the former, it is mediated by the indicatory mark. Therefore, because of the remoteness of meaning, between the indicatory mark and the sentence, the indicatory mark is stronger. Therefore, the word '<s>syonam</s>' {*3/290*} — even though it is syntactically expected by the latter [portion] and could thus also be used in the placing — nevertheless, splitting the sentence, it should be assigned to the strewing alone. And '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' [should be assigned] to the placing.
[Objection:] But the word '<s>syonaṃ te</s>' {*3/291*} has the capacity to denote the strewing just as much as it has the capacity to form a single sentence with the latter [portion]; and capacity is what is called 'indicatory mark.' Therefore, when the sentence is split, it is precisely the indicatory mark that is overridden. [Reply:] True, this too is an indicatory mark. But an indicatory mark of this nature — [one that operates through sentence-unity] — has a remote meaning: from the indicatory mark [arises] sentence-unity; from that, denotative capacity; from that, the meaning apprehended through direct statement — thus it is remote. And remoteness of meaning is the cause of being overridden. Therefore [292]{*3/292*}, [the first portion] will not enter into sentence-unity with the latter. Similarly, the latter [portion '<s>tasmin sīda</s>'] will not [enter into sentence-unity] with the former either.
Moreover, when [the latter portion] enters into sentence-unity with the former, there is no visible purpose at all [served]; but the communication of the strewing is a visible [purpose]. Why? Because both the strewing and the placing are heard. Similarly, for the latter [portion], the communication of the placing [is visible], but not sentence-unity with the former. And these two [portions], without sentence-unity with each other, do not fail to perform their respective functions separately as they should. Therefore, the former should be assigned to the former [rite], and the latter to the latter.
As for what was said — 'since [the sentence] is overridden even by direct statement, it should be overridden by [the indicatory mark] as well' — this is not so. For it is not the case that what is overridden by one must also be overridden by another. What is overridden should be supported for the sake of meaningfulness: with respect to direct statement it has a remote meaning, with respect to the sentence it has a proximate meaning. Therefore, the indicatory mark is stronger.
Now, in the conflict between sentence and context — what is the example? What is 'context' (<s>prakaraṇa</s>)? A statement [made] near something to be done that expects a procedural specification — that is the context. For it is the beginning of that verbal activity; this [element] is not an injunction-initial that depends on an injunction-final. The sentence has already been explained. What is the example of their conflict? The '<s>sūktavāka-nigada</s>' (recitation formulae). For therein, the deities of the full-moon [rite] and the deities of the new-moon [rite] are recorded; these do not form a single sentence with each other. There, through the capacity of the indicatory mark, the word '<s>Indrāgni</s>' is to be extracted from the full-moon application and used in the new-moon. Now the doubt arises: the remainder of this [recitation] — '<s>avīvṛdhetāṃ mahojyāyo krātām</s>' {*3/293*} {*3/294*} — should it be used as many times as it is recorded in the <s>sūktavāka</s>, that many times in both the full-moon and new-moon [rites] — because the context is stronger? Or should it be used only where the word '<s>Indrāgni</s>' is extracted and transferred — because the sentence is stronger? Similarly, the doubt applies everywhere.
What is the prima facie view? These two criteria are of equal strength. Why? [293]{*3/295*} There is syntactic expectancy in the one [direction], and in the other too; when the expectancy is equal, there is no reason for determination. Therefore, [they are] of equal strength. Or perhaps the sentence is weak, since it has been overridden by the indicatory mark.
When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: The sentence is stronger than the context. How? Because of the increasing remoteness of meaning. What is the remoteness of meaning here? In a sentence, when each word is separated, it has [unfulfilled] syntactic expectancy; [only] the complete [sentence] is fulfilled. There, the sentence-unity is directly perceptible. But in the context, it is not directly perceptible. How? When something complete falls near [an object] that expects a procedural specification — from that, the syntactic expectancy of that prescribed [object] is understood, and sentence-unity is inferred. And by conjecturing denotative capacity through sentence-unity, the construal '[this element] being thus, is so' is [derived]. This is the remoteness of meaning: the direct statement-meaning of the sentence is proximate, that of the context is remote. Therefore, in the <s>sūktavāka</s>, when 'he strikes the <s>prastara</s> [grass-bundle]' {*3/296*} — in the separate application of words denoting full-moon deities and new-moon deities, the remainder too [undergoes] separate application. Therefore, even though by the capacity of the context the sentence-unity of the remaining words of the full-moon deity-expressions with the new-moon deity-expressions is inferred, the [sentence-unity] with the new-moon deity-words is directly perceptible — and inference is not possible in the face of direct perception. And when the context has become meaningful, the expectancy of those that are syntactically complete cannot be established.
As for what was said — 'since [the sentence] is overridden even by the indicatory mark, it should also be overridable by the context' — no. What is overridden by another is not to be regarded as fragile everywhere. But if [it is] fragile, then it would simply not be a valid means at all. Rather, each [criterion] has power over a specific [other]: the sentence has the overriding power with respect to the context, but not with respect to the indicatory mark. With respect to the indicatory mark, the sentence has a remote meaning; with respect to the context, a proximate meaning. Therefore, the sentence overrides the context.
[294]{*3/297*} Now, in the conflict between context and position — what is the example? In the context of the <s>Rājasūya</s> (royal consecration), in the sequence of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> (consecration rite), the <s>Śunaḥśepha</s> narrative and the like are recorded. If the context is stronger, [the narrative] is a subsidiary of all [the rites]; if position, of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> alone. What is the prima facie view? These two criteria are of equal strength. Why? We do not perceive any distinction by which we could determine 'this one is stronger.' Therefore, they are of equal strength. Moreover, the context has been overridden by the sentence; therefore, it should also be overridable by position.
When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: The context is stronger than position. Why? Because of the increasing remoteness of meaning. What is the remoteness of meaning here? Because the [object] having a context has syntactic expectancy, sentence-unity could be conjectured with something complete recorded in its proximity — but not with something having a [mere] position. For position is merely the recording of a specific proximity-relationship among multiple things being recorded. There, from the capacity of [the recording of] a specific proximity, the syntactic expectancy of [the element] having position must be understood as existing even though not perceived. But in the context, the syntactic expectancy of the [object] having a context is directly perceptible. And sentence-unity of the recorded [element] with both the context-bearing and position-bearing [objects] simultaneously is not possible — hence the conflict. There, the directly perceptible syntactic expectancy belonging to the context can override the inferred [expectancy] belonging to position. From syntactic expectancy [arises] sentence-unity; from sentence-unity, denotative capacity; from capacity, the meaning apprehended through direct statement — thus the meaning apprehended through direct statement is proximate for the context, remote for position. Therefore, between position and context, the context is stronger.
As for what was said — 'since [the context] is overridden even by the sentence, it should be overridable by another too' — no. It is proper to support what has been overridden {*3/298*} — not to override what has been overridden.
Now, in the conflict between position and designation — what is the example? Which is stronger? In the section designated as '<s>pauroḍāśika</s>' (pertaining to the sacrificial cake), in the sequence of the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> (mixture of curds and milk), the mantra '<s>śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇe</s>' {*3/299*} (purify yourselves for the divine rite) — a mantra for the purpose of cleansing — is recorded. There the doubt arises: should it be assigned to the cleansing of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> [295]{*3/300*} vessels — because of the stronger status of the designation — or to the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> vessels — because of the stronger status of position? What is the prima facie view? These two criteria would be of equal strength {*3/301*}. Why? Because of the absence of a distinguishing factor. Or perhaps the designation alone is stronger, since position has been overridden even by the context.
When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: Position is stronger. Why? Because of the increasing remoteness of meaning. What is the remoteness of meaning here? When sentence-unity with something [in the context] has been ascertained, then for what is recorded in proximity, [syntactic] expectancy is conjectured and sentence-unity is understood. But the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) is a worldly word. And in matters of this nature, worldly [convention] is not a valid authority. Therefore, position is stronger.
[Objection:] If so, then in matters of this nature, assignment is through position [alone] — but position is not [actually] stronger because of the remoteness of meaning. How? The weighing for relative strength is [done] between two valid means of knowledge. And if this is so, the designation is not a valid means, since the word is worldly — [only] a person's authority holds. [Reply:] This is not a defect. The subsidiary status is not understood here through the authority of a person. The word '<s>pauroḍāśika</s>' applied to this section — that [naming] is dependent on the authority of a person. And in this matter, a person is a [valid] authority — just as the recording in the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> sequence is dependent on the authority of a person, just as the context [depends on] sentence-unity, and this is a Vedic word. For these matters are not within the range of the senses — in these, the authority belongs to experts. But in matters not within the range of the senses, experts are not authoritative. Therefore, the designation is a criterion; and when it is a criterion, the relative strength must be examined.
It is said: then the remoteness of meaning of the designation should be stated. This is the remoteness of meaning: In the case of position, from the recording in the [<s>sāṃnāyya</s>] sequence, the connection with the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> is taught; it is not taught in the case of the designation. [Rather,] upon perceiving a word being uttered, one conjectures through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) that 'it must be so.' Therefore, because the former is a Vedic [source] and [the designation is] remote from it, the designation is overridden by position.
Now, as for what is said here and there — 'this is overridden by that, this by that' — there, what is overridden: has it entered the domain of the overrider or not [296]{*3/302*}? What follows? If it has not entered, what is being overridden? If it has entered, how can it be overridden? We say: [the overridden element] has entered the domain of the overrider as a prior cognition. How? Because the more general criterion is [already] present. Then how is it set aside? A cognition 'it is false' {*3/303*} arises [subsequently]. But what {*3/304*} is the nature of a cognition that is not false? That for which no overriding cognition is tenable even upon reflection — that is not false. Thus, among these — direct statement, indicatory mark, sentence, context, position, and designation — each preceding criterion is stronger with respect to each succeeding one. For no overriding cognition exists [that would be valid] upon reflection against [the cognition produced by the preceding criterion]. Therefore, when they co-occur, in a conflict {*3/305*}, each succeeding one is weaker, because of the increasing remoteness of meaning.

children.text: ahīno vā prakaraṇād gauṇaḥ // MS_3,3.15 //
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Ahīna</s> [designation] is secondary, because of the context. // MS 3,3.15 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭomaṃ prakṛtya samāmananti - tisra eva sāhnasyopasado dvādaśāhīnasyeti{*3/306*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ dvādaśopasattā jyotiṣṭoma utāhīna iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? jyotiṣṭoma iti. kutaḥ? prakaraṇāt, evaṃ prakaraṇam anugṛhītaṃ bhavati. nanu vākyena bādhyate. na bādhyate, ahīnaśabdena jyotiṣṭomaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ. kutaḥ? na hīyata ity ahīnaḥ, dakṣiṇayā kratukaraṇair vā phalena vā na hīyate, tena jyotiṣṭomo 'hīnaḥ. vāśabdena saṃśayo nivartyate.
children.translated_text: Having set forth the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, [the text] prescribes: 'Indeed three are the <s>upasads</s> (preliminary rites) of the <s>Sāhna</s> (one-day rite), [and] twelve of the <s>Ahīna</s> (multi-day rite).' There the doubt arises: does the [rite with] twelve <s>upasads</s> refer to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> or to the <s>Ahīna</s>? What is the prima facie view? It refers to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Why? Because of the context — thus the context is upheld. [Objection:] But it is overridden by the sentence. [Reply:] It is not overridden; we will explain the word '<s>ahīna</s>' as [referring to] the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. How? [The word] '<s>ahīna</s>' [means] 'that which is not deficient' (<s>na hīyate</s>) — [a rite] not deficient in <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee), in the implements of the rite, or in the fruit. Thus the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is '<s>ahīna</s>.' The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) removes the doubt.
Page break marker: 297

children.text: asaṃyogāt tu mukhyasya tasmād apakṛṣyeta{*3/308*} // MS_3,3.16 //
children.translated_text: But because of the non-connection with the primary [meaning], [the twelve <s>upasads</s>] should be withdrawn [from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>]. // MS 3,3.16 //

children.text: apakṛṣyeta dvādaśopasattā. kutaḥ? asaṃyogāj jyotiṣṭomena. katham asaṃyogaḥ? ahīnenaikavākyatvasya pratyakṣatvāt. nanu jyotiṣṭoma eva gauṇo 'hīnaḥ. nety ucyate, na hi mukhyasaṃbhave gauṇagrahaṇam arhati. nanu nañsamāso bhaviṣyati. neti brūmaḥ, tathā saty ādyudātto 'hīnaśabdo 'bhaviṣyat, madhyodāttas tv ayam{*3/309*}. tasmāt prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvāhīnasya dharmaḥ. api ca vyapadeśo bhavati - tisra eva sāhnasyopasado dvādaśāhīnasyeti. yady anyaḥ sāhno 'nyaś cāhīnaḥ, tata evaṃ vyapadeśo 'vakalpate, vidyate ca vyapadeśavacanam, tasmād ahīnasyeti.
children.translated_text: The [rite with] twelve <s>upasads</s> should be withdrawn [from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>]. Why? Because of the non-connection with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. How is there non-connection? Because the single-sentence relationship with the <s>Ahīna</s> is directly perceptible. [Objection:] But the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself is secondarily [called] '<s>ahīna</s>.' [Reply:] No, it is said — for when the primary meaning is possible, the secondary meaning should not be adopted. [Objection:] But it could be a negative compound (<s>nañ-samāsa</s>). [Reply:] No, we say. If so, the word '<s>ahīna</s>' would have initial accent (<s>ādyudātta</s>), but it has medial accent (<s>madhyodātta</s>). Therefore, overriding the context, [it is] a property of the <s>Ahīna</s>. Moreover, there is a distinctive expression: 'Indeed three are the <s>upasads</s> of the <s>Sāhna</s>, twelve of the <s>Ahīna</s>.' If the <s>Sāhna</s> is one thing and the <s>Ahīna</s> another, then such a distinctive expression is construable — and the distinctive expression does exist. Therefore, [the twelve <s>upasads</s> belong] to the <s>Ahīna</s>.

children.text: dvitvabahutvayuktaṃ vā{*3/310*} codanāt tasya // MS_3,3.17 //
children.translated_text: Or [the <s>pratipads</s> should apply to rites] conjoined with duality or plurality, because of the injunction regarding that. // MS 3,3.17 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svaḥpatī{*3/311*} iti{*3/312*} dvayor yajamānayoḥ pratipadaṃ kuryāt{*3/313*}. ete 'sṛgram indava iti{*3/314*} bahubhyo yajamānebhya iti{*3/315*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - jyotiṣṭoma eva niviśete pratipādāu, uta dviyajñaṃ kiṃcit kulāyādiṃ bahuyajñaṃ ca dvirātrādim utkraṣṭavya iti. kiṃ prāptam? dvitvabahutvayukte jyotiṣṭomenāsaṃyogād{*3/316*} utkṛṣyeyātāṃ pratipadau, na hi [298]{*3/317*} jyotiṣṭomasya dvau yajamānau śrūyete, yathā kulāyasya, etena rājapurohitau sāyujyakāmau yajeyātām iti{*3/318*}.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'For you two are the lords of heaven' — the <s>pratipad</s> (introductory verse) should be used for two sacrificers. 'These drops have rushed forth' — for many sacrificers. There the doubt arises: do the <s>pratipads</s> apply within the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself, or should they be withdrawn to some [rite] with two sacrifices such as the <s>Kulāya</s> and others, and [a rite] with many sacrifices such as the <s>Dvirātra</s> and others? What is the prima facie view? The <s>pratipads</s> [suited to] duality and plurality should be withdrawn from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> because of their non-connection [with it] — for two sacrificers are not heard of in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, as they are in the <s>Kulāya</s> — as in 'the king and the priest should sacrifice together, desiring union.'

children.text: pakṣeṇārthakṛtasyeti cet // MS_3,3.18 //
children.translated_text: Because [the dual/plural quality] is accomplished by a part [of the rite] — if [you say so]. // MS 3,3.18 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi - partipadāv utkraṣṭavya iti. naitad evam, prakaraṇaṃ hi bādhyeta. bādhyatām asaṃyogād dvābhyāṃ yajamānābhyāṃ bahubhiś ca yajamānair jyotiṣṭomasyeti cet. asaty api vacane 'rthād dvau yajamānau bhaviṣyataḥ, ya eko na śakṣyati, samahāyaḥ sa upakraṃsyate, avaśyayaṣṭavye sati yathā śakyate, tathā yaṣṭavyam iti bādhitvāpi kāṃcit prāptiṃ yajamānaḥ sahāyam upādāsyate. evaṃ prakaraṇe pratipadau bhaviṣyataḥ, tasmān notkraṣṭavya iti.
children.translated_text: If you think thus — that the <s>pratipads</s> should be withdrawn — this is not so, for the context would be overridden. [Objection:] Let the context be overridden because of the non-connection of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> with two sacrificers and many sacrificers. [Reply:] Even without an [explicit] statement, by logical necessity there will be two sacrificers — one who alone is unable [to perform the sacrifice] will seek a companion. When the sacrifice must necessarily be performed, it should be performed however possible; so even by overriding [the normal rule of a single sacrificer], the sacrificer will take a companion. Thus, within the context [of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] the <s>pratipads</s> will apply. Therefore they should not be withdrawn.

children.text: na prakṛter ekasaṃyogāt // MS_3,3.19 //
children.translated_text: No, because the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) has connection with one [sacrificer only]. // MS 3,3.19 //

children.text:
prakṛtir hi jyotiṣṭomaḥ, pratyakṣās tatra dharmā āmnātāḥ, na kutaścic codakena prāpyante. kim ataḥ? yady evam, pratyakṣaśrutā na śakyā bādhitum. vikṛtau tu codakaprāptāḥ santa ānumānikā bādhyerann iti, vivakṣitaṃ hi jyotiṣṭome kartur ekatvaṃ pratyakṣaśrutaṃ na sāmarthyena bādhyate. yatrāpi hy avaśyakartavyatā śrūyate, tatrāpy eka eva yajamānaḥ śrūyate - vasante vasante jyotiṣā yajeteti. tasmāj jyotiṣṭomād utkraṣṭavya ete pratipādāv iti.
atha kasmāt patnyabhiprāyam etan na bhavati? ekasyāṃ patnyāṃ yajamāne ca, yuvaṃ hi stha iti, dvayor bahuṣu vā patnīṣv ete 'sṛgram indava iti, yathā kṣaume vasānāv agnimādadhīyātām iti kṣaumavasānaparaṃ vacanam, evam ihāpi pratipad vidhānaparam. ucyate - asaṃbhavāt tatra mukhyasya, lakṣaṇāśabdaḥ puṃso [299]{*3/319*} vācakaḥ striyām, iha tu dviyajñe bahuyajñe ca saṃbhavati na lakṣaṇāśabdo bhavitum arhati, bahubhyo yajamānebhya iti. yad apy etad dvivacanaṃ dvayor yajamānayor iti, atrāpi yaḥ, ekaśeṣaḥ, pumān striyety asāv api lakṣaṇāśabda eva. api ca, upāsmai gāyatā nara iti pratipador niravakāśatvam eva syāt. tasmād utkraṣṭavye ete pratipadāv iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
For the archetype is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; its properties are directly stated and not derived from any inferential source. What follows from this? If so, what is directly heard cannot be overridden. In the modified rite (<s>vikṛti</s>), however, properties derived by inference can be overridden — for the oneness of the performer in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, being directly heard, is not overridden by [mere] logical capability. Even where the necessity of performance is heard, only one sacrificer is heard — 'In every spring one should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' Therefore these <s>pratipads</s> should be withdrawn from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
Now why should this not be understood with reference to the sacrificer's wife? When the sacrificer has one wife, 'You two are [the lords]' [would apply], and when [he has] two or more wives, 'These drops have rushed forth' — just as 'wearing linen garments, the two should establish the fire' is a statement about the linen garment [qualification], so here too the <s>pratipad</s> would serve the purpose of an injunction [about the wife]. It is replied: because of the impossibility of the primary meaning there — the word [in dual/plural] referring to males, [applied to] a woman, is a secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). But here, in a rite with two sacrificers or many sacrificers, the primary meaning is possible — so the secondary designation should not apply, [as in] 'for many sacrificers.' And regarding the dual 'for two sacrificers' — here too, the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> [grammatical reduction of] 'a man and a woman' also yields a secondary designation. Moreover, 'Sing for him, O men' — the <s>pratipads</s> would have no scope [in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>]. Therefore it is established that these <s>pratipads</s> should be withdrawn.

children.text: jāghanī caikadeśatvāt // MS_3,3.20 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>jāghanī</s> (concluding portion), because it is a part [of the rite]. // MS 3,3.20 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - jāghanyā patnīḥ saṃyājayantīti. tatra saṃśayaḥ - kim etad vidhānaṃ darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ, uta paśāv iti. kathaṃ darśapūrṇamāyayoḥ? kathaṃ ca paśāv iti. yadi jāghanyāṃ patnīsaṃyājā vidhīyante tata utkarṣaḥ, atha patnīsaṃyājeṣu jāghanī vidhīyate tato darśapūrṇamāsayor eva. kiṃ prāptam? utkarṣaḥ. kuta etad utkṛṣyate? jāghanyāṃ patnīsaṃyājā vidhīyanta iti. katham? śabdāt patnīsaṃyājānāṃ vidhānam, vākyena jāghanyāḥ, śabdaś ca balavān, na vākyam.
nanu patnīsaṃyājā vihitā eva. satyaṃ vihitāḥ, jāghanyām idānīṃ punar vidhīyante, sā tatsaṃbaddhā kartavyety ucyate. evaṃ sati darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ patnīsaṃyājā vināpi jāghanyā na viguṇāḥ, jāghanī tu tatra pratipādyate. tasmād yatra jāghanī prayojanavatī tatra tasyāḥ pratipattiḥ, paśau ca sā, na darśapūrṇa[300]{*3/320*}māsayoḥ. ekadeśaś ca jāghanī pratipādyamānā na paśuṃ prayokṣyate, tasmād asya vidhānasyotkarṣa iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is heard: 'They have the sacrificer's wife perform the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> (wife's offerings) with the <s>jāghanī</s> (concluding portion).' There the doubt arises: is this an injunction for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, or for the animal sacrifice (<s>paśu</s>)? How [would it apply] to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>? And how to the animal sacrifice? If the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> are enjoined as being [performed] with the <s>jāghanī</s>, then there is withdrawal [to the animal sacrifice]. But if the <s>jāghanī</s> is enjoined for the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s>, then it remains in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. What is the prima facie view? Withdrawal. From what is it withdrawn? It is withdrawn because the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> are enjoined as [performed] with the <s>jāghanī</s>. How? The injunction of the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> is from the [Vedic] word; the <s>jāghanī</s> [is enjoined] by the sentence; and the [Vedic] word is stronger than the sentence.
[Objection:] But the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> are already enjoined. True, they are enjoined; but now they are being enjoined again with the <s>jāghanī</s> — it is being said that they should be performed connected with it. This being the case, the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> are not deficient even without the <s>jāghanī</s>, but the <s>jāghanī</s> is [additionally] taught there. Therefore, wherever the <s>jāghanī</s> serves a purpose, there it is assigned — and that is in the animal sacrifice, not in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. And the <s>jāghanī</s>, being [only] a part, when assigned, will not [by itself] bring in the animal sacrifice. Therefore this injunction involves withdrawal.

children.text: codanā vāpūrvatvāt // MS_3,3.21 //
children.translated_text: Or [the <s>jāghanī</s>] is an injunction, because of [its] novelty. // MS 3,3.21 //

children.text:
jāghanī vā patnīsaṃyājānāṃ guṇatvena vidhīyate. kutaḥ? apūrvatāt, aprāptā jāghanī patnīsaṃyājānāṃ guṇatvena. tatra svaśabdena patnīsaṃyājā vihitā jāghanīsaṃbandhas teṣām avihitaḥ, yatra ca saṃbandho vidhīyate, tatrānyatarasyānyatra vidhānam, saṃbandho nāntarīyakaḥ. yad vā saṃbandhasya vidhānaṃ nāntarīyakau saṃbandhinau, yatrobhau lakṣaṇatvena, tatra svaśabdena saṃbandho vidhīyate, yatra tv anyataro lakṣaṇatvena, tatra ekaṃ lakṣayitvānyataro vidhīyate, lakṣaṇatvena cātra patnīsaṃyājāḥ. katham avagamyate? patnīsaṃbandhān na sarvo yāgaḥ, kaścid eva tu lakṣyate yasya patnyaḥ sādhanatvena.
atha kasmān na jāghanīṃ lakṣayitvā patnīsaṃyājā vidhīyante? nāsyāpūrvasya yāgasya patnyaḥ śak-yante vidhātum, jāghanyāṃ tu lakṣyamāṇāyāṃ yāge sapatnīke vidhīyamāne vākyaṃ bhidyeta. asti tv atra vihitaḥ sapatnīko yāgo ya patnībhir lakṣyate. tasmād yāgaṃ lakṣayitvā jāghanī vidhīyate. yat tu, vākyena jāghanīvidhānaṃ śrutyā yāgasyeti, tad iha yāgavidhānaṃ na saṃbhavatīty uktam, vākyabhedaprasaṅgāt. tasmāj jāghanīvidhānam. evaṃ ced darśapūrṇamāsayor vinā jāghanyā viguṇaḥ patnīsaṃyājayāgaḥ syāt, tasmād anutkarṣam iti.
children.translated_text:
Or the <s>jāghanī</s> is enjoined as a subsidiary of the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s>. Why? Because of novelty — the <s>jāghanī</s>, being previously unobtained, is [now] enjoined as a subsidiary of the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s>. There, the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> are enjoined by their own [Vedic] word, [but] their connection with the <s>jāghanī</s> is not enjoined. And where a connection is enjoined, one of the two [relata] is [newly] enjoined for the other — the connection is not automatic. Or alternatively, the injunction of the connection does not automatically [imply] the two relata — where both have the character of being indicated [rather than directly stated], there the connection is enjoined by its own [Vedic] word. But where one has the character of being indicated, there, having indicated one, the other is enjoined. And here, the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> are the indicated element. How is this understood? Because not every sacrifice involves the sacrificer's wife — only a specific one that has wives as [its] instruments is indicated.
Now why should not the <s>jāghanī</s> be the indicated element, with the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> being enjoined [for it]? For this novel sacrifice, wives cannot be enjoined [as instruments]. But if the <s>jāghanī</s> were indicated, then while a sacrifice possessing wives is being enjoined, the sentence would be split. However, there exists here an already-enjoined sacrifice possessing wives that is indicated [by the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s> term]. Therefore, having indicated the sacrifice, the <s>jāghanī</s> is enjoined. As for the [argument] that the <s>jāghanī</s> is enjoined by the sentence while the sacrifice [is enjoined] by the [Vedic] word — it has been said that here the sacrifice-injunction is impossible, because of the consequence of splitting the sentence. Therefore it is an injunction of the <s>jāghanī</s>. If this is so, the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s> sacrifice in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> would be deficient without the <s>jāghanī</s>. Therefore, there is no withdrawal.

children.text: ekadeśa iti cet // MS_3,3.22 //
children.translated_text: [It is only] a part — if [you say so]. // MS 3,3.22 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - ekadeśo jāghanī na paśuṃ prayokṣyate, tasmād utkarṣa iti. tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — the <s>jāghanī</s>, being [only] a part, will not bring in the animal sacrifice; therefore there is withdrawal — that [objection] must be addressed.
Page break marker: 301

children.text: na prakṛter aśāstraniṣpatteḥ // MS_3,3.23 /
children.translated_text: No, because [the <s>jāghanī</s>] is not produced by scripture in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). // MS 3,3.23 //

children.text: na prakṛtau darśapūrṇamāsayor jāghanī śāstrenocyate. evaṃ paśor niṣpannayā jāghanyā patnīsaṃyājā yaṣṭavyā iti. aviśiṣṭā jāghanī vidhīyate. sā saṃbhavati darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ krītyāpy ānīyamānā, tasmād anutkarṣa iti.
children.translated_text: In the archetype — the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — the <s>jāghanī</s> is not stated by scripture. Thus, the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> should be performed with the <s>jāghanī</s> that is produced [i.e., available] in the animal sacrifice. An unspecified <s>jāghanī</s> is enjoined; and it is obtainable in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> even when brought by purchase. Therefore, there is no withdrawal.

children.text: saṃtardanaṃ prakṛtau krayaṇavad anarthalopāt syāt // MS_3,3.24 //
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃtardana</s> (satiation [rite]) in the archetype should be like the purchase — without loss of purpose. // MS 3,3.24 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome 'bhiṣavaṇaphalake{*3/322*} prakṛtya śrūyate - dīrghasome saṃtṛdyād dhṛtyā iti{*3/323*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ saṃtardanaṃ jyotiṣṭoma eva, āhosvid dīrghakāleṣu someṣv iti. ucyate - naital luptārthaṃ prakṛtau, tasmān notkṛṣyeteti. āha nanv asaṃtardanam api śrūyate - asaṃtṛṇe{*3/324*} bhavata iti{*3/325*}. ucyate - krayaṇavad vikalpiṣyate{*3/326*}, yathā hiraṇyena krīṇāti gavā krīṇātītyevamādīnāṃ vikalpaḥ, evam atrāpi vikalpo bhaviṣyati - saṃtardanam asaṃtardanaṃ vā bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, having set forth the <s>Soma</s>-pressing boards (<s>abhiṣavaṇaphalaka</s>), it is heard: 'In a long <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], one should pierce [the boards] for durability.' There the doubt arises: does the <s>saṃtardana</s> (piercing/satiation) [apply] in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself, or in <s>Soma</s> sacrifices of long duration? It is said: this is not without purpose in the archetype; therefore it should not be withdrawn. [Objection:] But non-piercing is also heard — 'Let there be non-piercing.' [Reply:] It is said: like the purchase, there will be an option — just as there is an option among 'he purchases with gold,' 'he purchases with a cow,' and such [alternatives], so here too there will be an option — either piercing or non-piercing.
