children.text: utkarṣo vā, grahaṇād viśeṣasya // MS_3,3.25 //
children.translated_text: Or withdrawal, because of the mention of a specification. // MS 3,3.25 //

children.text: utkṛṣyate vā saṃtardanam, gṛhyate hi viśeṣaḥ, dīrghasome [302]{*3/327*} saṃtṛdyād iti. jyotiṣṭomam apekṣya satrāṇi kālato dīrghāṇi bhavanti.
children.translated_text: Or the <s>saṃtardana</s> is withdrawn [from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], for a specification is mentioned — 'in a long <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] one should pierce.' In comparison to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the <s>Sattra</s> sacrifices are long in duration.

children.text: kartṛto vā viśeṣasya tannimittatvāt // MS_3,3.26 //
children.translated_text: Or [the specification is] with reference to the sacrificer, because [the word 'long'] is occasioned by that. // MS 3,3.26 //

children.text: notkṛṣyeta vā saṃtardanaṃ jyotiṣṭomāt. evaṃ prakaraṇam anugṛhītaṃ bhavati, dīrghasomaśabdaś ca kartṛto bhaviṣyati, dīrghasya yajamānasya somo dīrghasoma iti.
children.translated_text: Or the <s>saṃtardana</s> should not be withdrawn from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Thus the context is upheld, and the word '<s>dīrghasoma</s>' (long <s>Soma</s>) will refer to the sacrificer — the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice of a tall (<s>dīrgha</s>) sacrificer is '<s>dīrghasoma</s>.'

children.text: kratuto vārthavādānupapatteḥ syāt // MS_3,3.27 //
children.translated_text: Or [the specification is] with reference to the rite, because [otherwise] the explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) would be inapplicable. // MS 3,3.27 //

children.text: na caitad asti - jyotiṣṭome saṃniveśa iti, dīrghakāle some kriyeta, kratuta eva dīrghatvam, na kartṛtaḥ. kutaḥ? arthavādānupapatteḥ, dhṛtyety arthavādo bhavati, dhāraṇāyety arthaḥ, dīrghakāle some punaḥ punar grāvabhir abhihanyamāne somābhiṣavaṇaphalakayor dāraṇaśaṅkāyām, dhṛtyety arthavāda upapadyate, tasmād utkarṣa iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that there is [only] placement in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. [Rather,] it should be performed in a <s>Soma</s> sacrifice of long duration. The 'longness' is of the rite itself, not of the sacrificer. Why? Because of the inapplicability of the explanatory passage. '<s>Dhṛtyā</s>' (for durability) is an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), meaning 'for the purpose of holding.' In a <s>Soma</s> sacrifice of long duration, when the <s>Soma</s>-pressing boards are struck repeatedly by the pressing stones, there is apprehension of breaking; [in that case,] the explanatory passage 'for durability' is applicable. Therefore, [there is] withdrawal.

children.text: saṃsthāś ca kartṛvad dhāraṇārthāviśeṣāt // MS_3,3.28 //
children.translated_text: And the concluding forms (<s>saṃsthās</s>) [would be] like [the argument from] the sacrificer, because there is no difference in the purpose of holding. // MS 3,3.28 //

children.text: idaṃ padottaraṃ sūtram. kāni padāni? atha kim arthaṃ saṃsthāsu na niveśaḥ?. tathā sati prakaraṇam anugṛhītaṃ bhaviṣyati, dīrghasomaśabdaś ca. dīrghakālo hy agniṣṭomam apekṣyokthyādiṣu saṃsthāsu soma iti. ucyate - na saṃsthāsu dīrghakālatve 'pi some 'rthavāda upapadyate, tāvān eva hi tatra somo daśa muṣṭīr mimīta iti vacanāt. tatra dhāraṇe na viśeṣaḥ kaścit, tasmād utkarṣa eva.
children.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> follows [the previous] topic. What are the words [that follow]? Now, why is there not placement in the <s>saṃsthās</s> (concluding rite-forms [like <s>Ukthya</s> etc.])? If so, the context would be upheld, and the word '<s>dīrghasoma</s>' too [would be explained] — for in the <s>saṃsthās</s> such as <s>Ukthya</s> and others, the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] is of longer duration compared to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. It is said: even when there is long duration in the <s>saṃsthās</s>, the explanatory passage is inapplicable for the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice there], for the [quantity of] <s>Soma</s> there is just the same — 'one should measure out ten handfuls' — as stated. There, regarding holding [the boards], there is no difference whatsoever. Therefore, [there is] indeed withdrawal.
Page break marker: 303

children.text: ukthyādiṣu vārthasya vidyamānatvāt // MS_3,3.29 //
children.translated_text: Or in the <s>Ukthya</s> and others, because the purpose [of piercing] exists there. // MS 3,3.29 //

children.text: na caitad asti - utkarṣa iti, prakaraṇānugrahād anutkarṣaḥ, dīrghasomaśabdaś ca dīrghakālatvād upapadyate, tatrāpy adhiko 'gniṣṭomāt somaḥ, pradānāni hi vivardhante. tāny avivṛddhe pradeye na śakyāni vivardhayitum. pūrṇe grahe grahaśabdo bhavati, tena na śakyāni nyūnāni pātrāṇi grahītum. tasmād dāraṇāśaṅkāyāṃ dhāraṇam āśaṃsitavyaṃ bhavati, tatra dhṛtyety upapadyata iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that there is withdrawal. Because of upholding the context, there is no withdrawal. And the word '<s>dīrghasoma</s>' is applicable because of the longer duration [of the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice in those rites]. There too, the <s>Soma</s> is greater than in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, for the offerings (<s>pradānas</s>) increase. And [the offerings] cannot be increased when the offering material is not increased. When the cup (<s>graha</s>) is full, it is called a '<s>graha</s>' (cup); therefore, smaller vessels cannot be used for the cups. Hence, when there is apprehension of breaking, durability should be wished for — and there the [explanatory passage] 'for durability' is applicable.

children.text: aviśeṣāt stutir vyartheti cet // MS_3,3.30 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] the praise would be purposeless because of [the boards'] non-differentiation — // MS 3,3.30 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi - saṃsthāsv apy arthavādo 'vakalpate pradeyavivṛddhyeti, naitad evam, vyarthaiva hi stutir bhavet. kutaḥ? somāviśeṣāt, yāvān evāgniṣṭome somaḥ, tāvān evokthyādiṣv api saṃsthāsu, ukthyādiṣv api daśamuṣṭir eva somo grahītavyaḥ. nanv arthāt pradeyaṃ vivartsyatīti. daśamuṣṭiḥ sa kathaṃ śakyeta vivardhayitum? triparveti ca parvasaṃkhyāniyamān na śakyo bahuparvā grahītum, tasmād dhāraṇāviśeṣād arthavādānupapattiḥ saṃsthāsu syāt, tasmād utkarṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: If you think thus — that the explanatory passage is also construable in the <s>saṃsthās</s> because of the increase of offerings — this is not so, for the praise would indeed be purposeless. Why? Because of the non-differentiation of the <s>Soma</s> — the quantity of <s>Soma</s> in the <s>Ukthya</s> and other <s>saṃsthās</s> is the same as in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; in the <s>Ukthya</s> and others too, only ten handfuls of <s>Soma</s> are to be taken. [Objection:] But by logical necessity the offering material will increase. [Reply:] Being ten handfuls, how can it be increased? And because of the restriction of the number of joints [to] 'three-jointed,' a multi-jointed [<s>Soma</s> plant] cannot be taken. Therefore, because of the non-differentiation in [the need for] holding, the explanatory passage would be inapplicable in the <s>saṃsthās</s>. Therefore, [there is] withdrawal.

children.text: syād anityatvāt // MS_3,3.31 //
children.translated_text: It may [be applicable in the <s>saṃsthās</s>], because of the non-fixity [of the <s>Soma</s> quantity]. // MS 3,3.31 //

children.text: naitad asti - utkarṣa iti, saṃsthāsu syāt, prakaraṇānugrahāt. arthāc ca pradeyavivṛddhyā dāraṇaśaṅkāyām arthavāda upapadyate, kena prakāreṇa pradeyaṃ vivardhiṣyata iti, viprakṛṣṭaparvā somo grahīṣyate. api ca tṛtīye savana 'śur eko 'bhiṣūyate, tasya pramāṇaṃ ca nāmnātam. tam anekaparvāṇaṃ sthūlaparvāṇaṃ ca grahīṣyati, [304]{*3/329*} tena pradeyavivṛddhir bhaviṣyati, ato 'rthavādo 'vakalpiṣyate, tasmāt saṃsthāsu niveśa iti siddham.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that there is withdrawal. [The <s>saṃtardana</s>] may apply in the <s>saṃsthās</s>, because of upholding the context. And because of the increase of offerings, when there is apprehension of breaking, the explanatory passage is applicable through logical necessity. In what manner will the offering material increase? A <s>Soma</s> [plant] with widely-spaced joints will be taken. Moreover, in the third pressing (<s>savana</s>), one additional <s>Soma</s> [plant] is pressed; and its measure is not specified. One will take [a plant] that is multi-jointed and thick-jointed, and thereby the offering material will increase. From this the explanatory passage will be construable. Therefore, placement in the <s>saṃsthās</s> is established.

children.text: saṃkhyāyuktaṃ kratoḥ prakaraṇāt syāt // MS_3,3.32 //
children.translated_text: That which is conjoined with number would [apply to] the rite, because of the context. // MS 3,3.32 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome pravargyaṃ prakṛtya samāmnāyate - na prathamayajñe pravṛñjyād dvitīye tṛtīye vā pravṛñjyād iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ jyotiṣṭome sarveṣv eva prayogeṣu na pravarjitavyam, uta prathame prayoge pratiṣedha iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? jyotiṣṭome pratiṣedhaḥ. kutaḥ? yajñasaṃyogāt, prathamaśabdena yajño 'bhidhīyate jyotiṣṭomaḥ. tasya hi prathamasaṃyogaḥ, evaṃ samāmnāyate - eṣa vāva prathamo yajñānāṃ{*3/330*} yaj jyotiṣṭomo ya etenānṣṭvāthānyena yajeteti. yajñānāṃ prathama iti kṛtvā prathamaśabdena jyotiṣṭomo 'bhidhīyate, evaṃ ca prakaraṇam anugṛhyate, yadi krator eṣa vādaḥ. tasmāt saṃkhyāyuktaḥ pratiṣedho jyotiṣṭomasya pravargyaṃ pratiṣedhed iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, having set forth the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk rite), it is prescribed: 'One should not perform the <s>Pravargya</s> at the first sacrifice; one should perform it at the second or third.' There the doubt arises: is the prohibition in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> for all performances, or is the prohibition for the first performance [only]? What is the prima facie view? The prohibition is for the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [altogether]. Why? Because of the connection with the sacrifice — by the word 'first,' the sacrifice referred to is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. For it has the connection with 'first'; thus it is prescribed: 'This indeed is the first of sacrifices — the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; one who has sacrificed with this should then sacrifice with another.' Considering it the first of sacrifices, by the word 'first' the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is denoted. And thus the context is upheld, if this argument is with reference to the rite. Therefore, the prohibition conjoined with number would prohibit the <s>Pravargya</s> in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/330: E2,4: yajño yajñānāṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{3/330: E2,4: <s>yajño yajñānāṃ</s>}]

children.text: naimittikaṃ vā kartṛsaṃyogāl liṅgasya tannimittatvā // MS_3,3.33 //
children.translated_text: Or [the prohibition is] occasional, because of the connection with the sacrificer, since the indicatory mark is occasioned by that. // MS 3,3.33 //

children.text:
na caitad asti - yajñasyaiṣa vāda iti, caturṣv api vedeṣu na, prathamayajña{*3/331*} ityevaṃsaṃjñakaḥ kaścid yajño 'sti, bhavati tu prathamo [305]{*3/332*} yajñasya prayogaḥ, kartṛsaṃyogāt. pūrvasya dvitīyādīn apekṣya prathamaśabdo bhavati, sa prayogasyopapadyate, na kratoḥ. prayogaḥ śravaṇād gamyate, kratuḥ prayogasaṃbaddhatvāt, śrutiś ca balīyasī na lakṣaṇā. tasmāt prathame prayoge na pravarjitavyam iti.
atha yad uktam - jyotiṣṭomena sāmānādhikaraṇyāt tad vacana iti, laksaṇayā sāmānādhikaraṇyam iti tat parihṛtam. yat tu prathamayajña iti yajñaśabdena sāmānādhikaraṇyam, tad api yajñaśabdasya yāgavacanatvād asmatpakṣasyābādhakam.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — that this argument is with reference to the sacrifice. In none of the four <s>Vedas</s> is there any sacrifice designated '<s>prathamayajña</s>' (first sacrifice); but there is a first performance of a sacrifice — because of the connection with the sacrificer. The word 'first' applies in relation to the second and subsequent [performances]; it is applicable to the performance, not to the rite. The performance is understood from direct hearing; the rite [only] through its connection with the performance; and direct statement (<s>śruti</s>) is stronger, not secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). Therefore, at the first performance the <s>Pravargya</s> should not be performed.
As for what was said — because of the co-referentiality with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, that is [its] statement — the co-referentiality is by secondary designation, and that [objection] has been addressed. And the co-referentiality [in the expression] '<s>prathamayajña</s>' with the word '<s>yajña</s>' — that too does not contradict our view, because the word '<s>yajña</s>' denotes the sacrificial performance.

children.text: pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ vikṛtau pratīyetācodanāt prakṛtau // MS_3,3.34 //
children.translated_text: The grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (offering to <s>Pūṣan</s>) should be understood [to apply] in the modified rite (<s>vikṛti</s>), because there is no injunction in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). // MS 3,3.34 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ samāmananti - tasmāt pūṣā prapiṣṭabhāgo 'dantako hi sa iti{*3/333*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ prakṛtau, uta vikṛtāv iti. kiṃ prāptam? prakṛtāv iti. kutaḥ? prakaraṇāt. nanu prakṛtau pūṣaṇaṃ na kasyacid dhaviṣo devatāṃ samāmanantīti. ucyate - prākṛtīṃ kāṃcid devatāṃ pūṣaśabdo vakṣyati.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - yatra pauṣṇaṃ havir asti, tatra tasya pesaṇaṃ vidhātsuṃ śakyam, na ca prakṛtau pūṣāsti, tasmād utkraṣṭavyaṃ peṣaṇam iti. yad uktam - kāṃcid devatāṃ pūṣaśabdo vakṣyatīti, brūyāt, yady anyatrāpi mukhyaḥ pūṣā na syāt. nanv anyatra kriyamāṇe prakaraṇam uparudhyeta. uparudhyatām, vākyaṃ hy asyoparodhakam. athavā naivātra saṃdehaḥ, evam eva prāptam ucyate - pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ vikṛtau na prakṛtāv iti, nāsti puṣṇaḥ{*3/334*} prakṛtau [306]{*3/335*} codaneti. kim arthaṃ prāptam ucyate? uttaratra kathā vartiṣyate.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is prescribed: 'Therefore <s>Pūṣan</s> has ground offerings as his share, for he is toothless.' There the doubt arises: does the grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> [offering apply] in the archetype or in the modified rite? What is the prima facie view? In the archetype. Why? Because of the context. [Objection:] But in the archetype, no offering material is prescribed with <s>Pūṣan</s> as [its] deity. It is said: the word '<s>Pūṣan</s>' will denote some deity [already present] in the archetype.
Having arrived at this, we say: where there is an offering to <s>Pūṣan</s> (<s>pauṣṇa havis</s>), there grinding can be enjoined for it. But <s>Pūṣan</s> is not [a deity] in the archetype. Therefore the grinding should be withdrawn. As for the statement that the word '<s>Pūṣan</s>' will denote some deity — [one could] say that, if <s>Pūṣan</s> in the primary sense were not available elsewhere. [Objection:] But if [the grinding is] done elsewhere, the context would be disrupted. [Reply:] Let it be disrupted; for the sentence overrides it. Or rather, there is no doubt here at all — it is indeed established that the grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> [applies] in the modified rite, not in the archetype, [because] there is no injunction of <s>Pūṣan</s> in the archetype. For what purpose then is the established [conclusion] stated? The discussion will continue in the subsequent [<s>sūtras</s>].

children.text: tatsarvārtham aviśeṣāt // MS_3,3.35 //
children.translated_text: [The grinding] should be for all of them, because there is no differentiation. // MS 3,3.35 //

children.text: pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ prakṛtau śrūyamāṇaṃ vikṛtāv ity uktam. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ carau, paśau, puroḍāśe ca, uta carāv eveti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? tat sarvatra syāc carau paśau puroḍāśe ca. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, na kaścid viśeṣa ādhhīyate, tasmāt sarvatreti.
children.translated_text: The grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s>, which is heard in the archetype, [applies] in the modified rite — this has been stated. There the doubt arises: does [the grinding apply] in the <s>caru</s> (porridge), the animal sacrifice (<s>paśu</s>), and the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) [offerings to <s>Pūṣan</s>], or only in the <s>caru</s>? What is the prima facie view? It should apply to all of them — in the <s>caru</s>, the animal sacrifice, and the <s>puroḍāśa</s>. Why? Because there is no differentiation — no specification is made. Therefore, [it applies] to all.

children.text: carau vā, arthoktaṃ puroḍāśe 'rthavipratiṣedhāt paśau na syāt // MS_3,3.36 //
children.translated_text: Or [only] in the <s>caru</s>; [regarding] the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, [the purpose is already] accomplished by the [nature of the] thing; in the animal sacrifice, [it] should not [apply], because of contradiction of purpose. // MS 3,3.36 //

children.text:
carau pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ viniyujyeta. puroḍāśe tāvat peṣaṇam arthād eva prāpnoti, naivām yathā puroḍāśo bhavati, tad arthaṃ tāvan na vacanam. paśau ca na syāt, hṛdayādiṣu piṣyamāṇeṣu teṣām ākāravināśaḥ syāt. tatra ko doṣaḥ? hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyatīti{*3/336*} na hṛdayād avadāyiṣyate, tathānyad apy avadānaṃ na yathāśrutād avadāsyate.
nanu śakyate piṣṭebhyo 'pi hṛdayādibhyo 'vadātum. neti brūmaḥ, ākārā hṛdayādayaḥ, na māṃsāni, uktam etad ākṛtiḥ śabdārtha iti{*3/337*}. yady api punas tadākṛtikaḥ kriyate, tathāpy asyotsādanapradeśaṃ prati muhyeyuḥ, tasmāc carau pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīty evam arthaṃ vacanam.
children.translated_text:
The grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> would be assigned to the <s>caru</s> (porridge offering). As for the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake), grinding is already obtained by the nature of the thing itself — for that is how a <s>puroḍāśa</s> is made; so the [Vedic] statement is not for that purpose. And in the animal sacrifice [it] should not [apply] — for when the heart and other [organs] are ground, their form would be destroyed. What is the fault in that? [The text says] 'he cuts off from the front of the heart' — [so] he would not be able to cut off from the heart [if it were ground]; similarly, other portions (<s>avadāna</s>) would not be cut off from their proper [anatomical] form.
[Objection:] But it is possible to cut off even from the ground heart and other [organs]. [Reply:] No, we say. The heart and other [organs] are [defined by their] form, not [merely as] pieces of meat. This has been stated: 'Form is the referent of the word.' And even if [the meat] is then re-shaped into that form, still, regarding the cutting-off location, [the priests] would be confused. Therefore, the grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> will apply in the <s>caru</s> — this is the purpose of the [Vedic] statement.

children.text: carāv apīti cet // MS_3,3.37 //
children.translated_text: Even in the <s>caru</s> — if [you say so]. // MS 3,3.37 //

children.text: iti cet paśyati bhavān - arthavipratiṣedhān na paśvartham [307]{*3/338*} iti. nanu carāv apy arthavipratiṣedhaḥ, viśadasiddha odane caruśabdam upacaranti, piṣyamāṇo hi piṣṭakaṃ yavāgūrvā syāt khalir vā.
children.translated_text: If you think thus — that because of the contradiction of purpose [the grinding does] not [apply] to the animal sacrifice — [then consider:] there is also a contradiction of purpose in the <s>caru</s>. For the word '<s>caru</s>' is used for [porridge] cooked with distinct [grains]; when ground, it would become a <s>piṣṭaka</s> (cake), <s>yavāgū</s> (gruel), or <s>khali</s> (husk-cake).

children.text: na paktināmatvāt // MS_3,3.38 //
children.translated_text: No, because [<s>caru</s>] is a name derived from cooking. // MS 3,3.38 //

children.text: atrocyate - satyaṃ viśadasiddha odane caruśabdaḥ prayujyate, viśadasiddhaś carur dīyata iti, na tv asya viśadasiddhir nimittam. yadi viśadasiddhir nimittaṃ syāt, na piṣṭasiddhe prayujyeta. tatrāpi hi prayujyate, piṣṭakacaruḥ sādhyata iti, ato 'nyad etayoḥ sāmānyam, tan nimittam, tad etad ucyate - na paktināmatvād iti, na carau vipratiṣedhaḥ. katham? paktināmatvāt, paktināmaitat, carur iti. anavasrāvitāntaruṣmapākenābhinirvartyasya bhavati caruśabdo vācakaḥ. tena piṣṭa odane viśadaudane ca prayoktāro bhavanti, carur iti. pakṣoktam eva prayojanam, pūrvapakṣe paśāv api peṣaṇaṃ, siddhānte cārāv eva.
children.translated_text: To this it is said: true, the word '<s>caru</s>' is used for [porridge] cooked with distinct [grains] — 'a <s>caru</s> cooked with distinct [grains] is offered' — but the distinctness of the cooking is not its defining cause. If distinctness of cooking were the defining cause, [the word] would not be used for what is cooked from flour. But it is used there too — '<s>piṣṭakacaru</s> (flour-porridge) is prepared' — therefore, there is some other commonality between these two, and that is the defining cause. This is what is stated: 'No, because [<s>caru</s>] is a name derived from cooking.' There is no contradiction of purpose in the <s>caru</s>. How? Because [<s>caru</s>] is a name derived from cooking — this is a name [derived] from cooking. The word '<s>caru</s>' denotes that which is produced by cooking without draining off the water, with inner heat. Therefore, [the word] is applied both to distinct-grain [porridge] and to flour-[porridge]. Thus the preparers say '<s>caru</s>.' The purpose has been stated in the prima facie view: on the prima facie view, the grinding [applies] also in the animal sacrifice; on the established conclusion, only in the <s>caru</s>.

children.text: ekasminn ekasaṃyogāt // MS_3,3.39 //
children.translated_text: [The offering] at one [fire], because of the connection with one [deity]. // MS 3,3.39 //

children.text: pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ vikṛtau bhavati carāv evety uktam. athedānīṃ saṃdihyate - kim ekadevatye pauṣṇa etad bhavati, uta dvidevatye 'pīti. kiṃ dvidevatya udāharaṇam? rājasūya uttare trisaṃyukte saumāpauṣṇe ekādaśakapāle aindrāpauṣṇaś caruḥ śyāvo dakṣiṇeti, tatraindrāpauṣṇa udāharaṇam. kiṃ prāptam? ekadevatyasyaiva peṣaṇam iti. kutaḥ? kevalasaṃyogāt, yathā caturdhākaraṇe.
children.translated_text: The grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> [offering] applies in the modified rite, in the <s>caru</s> (porridge) alone — this has been stated. Now a further doubt arises: does this apply only to a single-deity (<s>ekadevatya</s>) <s>Pauṣṇa</s> [offering], or also to a two-deity (<s>dvidevatya</s>) [offering]? What is an example of a two-deity [offering]? In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, in the subsequent three-conjoined [offering]: 'a <s>Saumāpauṣṇa</s> (to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>) eleven-kapāla [rice-cake], an <s>Aindrāpauṣṇa</s> (to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>) <s>caru</s>, and a dark [animal] as <s>dakṣiṇā</s>' — there the <s>Aindrāpauṣṇa</s> is the example. What is the prima facie view? Grinding [applies] only for the single-deity [offering]. Why? Because of the connection with [<s>Pūṣan</s>] alone, as in the case of the fourfold division.
Page break marker: 308

children.text: dharmavipratiṣedhāc ca // MS_3,3.40 //
children.translated_text: And because of the contradiction of properties. // MS 3,3.40 //

children.text: dvidevatye vipratiṣidhyeta dharmaḥ, pūṣṇaḥ peṣaṇam, netarasya, tatra yadi pūṣṇo bhāgaḥ piṣyeta, apiṣṭa itarasya syāt. tatra viṣamaḥ pāko bhavet, pākanimittaś ca caruśabdaḥ sa vipratiṣidhyeta. athāvirodhaṃ manyamānā aparasyāpi bhāgaṃ piṃṣyuḥ. bhāgasaṃmohaḥ syāt. tatra ko doṣaḥ? anyasya bhāgo 'nyasymā avadīyeta. tathāyathāśrutaṃ kriyeta, tasmād apy ekadevatye peṣaṇam iti.
children.translated_text: In a two-deity [offering], the property would be contradicted — grinding is for <s>Pūṣan</s>'s [portion], not for the other [deity's portion]. If <s>Pūṣan</s>'s share is ground, the other's would remain unground. Then the cooking would be uneven. And the word '<s>caru</s>,' which is defined by cooking, would be contradicted. Alternatively, thinking there is no contradiction, they might grind the other [deity's] share too. [But then] there would be confusion of the shares. What is the fault in that? One [deity's] share would be cut off for the other. Thus [the rite] would be performed contrary to what is heard. Therefore, grinding [applies only] in a single-deity [offering].

children.text: api vā sadvitīye syād devatānimittatvāt // MS_3,3.41 //
children.translated_text: Or [the grinding] may apply even when [<s>Pūṣan</s>] has a companion [deity], because [the grinding] is occasioned by the deity. // MS 3,3.41 //

children.text: devatānimittam etat peṣaṇaṃ śrūyate - pūṣā prapiṣṭabhāgaḥ kartavya iti, sa ca dvidevatye 'pi bhāge piṣyamāṇe prapiṣṭabhāgaḥ kṛto bhavati, na yathā caturdhākaraṇe, tatra hi tad dhito nirapekṣasya bhavati, na sadvitīyasya, indrapīta iti samāso 'pi nirapekṣasya, na sadvitīyasya. iha tu prapiṣṭaśabdasya bhāgaśabdena sahānyapadārtho bahuvrīhiḥ samāsaḥ, eṣo 'pi samarthayor eva, na tv atra dvidevatye kaścid evaṃjātīyako doṣaḥ. tasmād ekadevatye dvidevatye 'pi vā carāv asya bhāgaḥ peṣṭavya eva.
children.translated_text: This grinding is heard as occasioned by the deity — '<s>Pūṣan</s> should be made to have ground offerings as his share.' And even in a two-deity [offering], when [his] share is ground, he is made to have ground offerings as his share. This is not like the case of the fourfold division — for there, that [qualification] applies to [the deity] who is independent, not to one who has a companion. The compound '<s>indrapīta</s>' (drunk by <s>Indra</s>) also [applies] to the independent [deity], not to one with a companion. But here, the word '<s>prapiṣṭa</s>' (ground) combined with the word '<s>bhāga</s>' (share) forms a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound referring to another entity — and this [type of compound] too [applies] only to [both] capable [referents]. But in this two-deity [case], there is no fault of this kind. Therefore, in a single-deity or even a two-deity <s>caru</s>, his share must indeed be ground.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_3,3.42 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of the indicatory mark. // MS 3,3.42 //

children.text: liṅgam apy evaṃ bhavati - tasmāt pūṣā prapiṣṭabhāgo 'dantako hīti{*3/340*}, devatānimittaṃ peṣaṇam iti stutir darśayati. tathā saumāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapen nemapiṣṭaṃ paśukāma iti{*3/341*} nemapiṣṭatāṃ darśayati. tathārdhaṃ piṣṭam ardham apiṣṭaṃ bhavati dvidevatyatvāyeti devatānimittam eva peṣaṇaṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: There is also an indicatory mark to this effect — 'Therefore <s>Pūṣan</s> has ground offerings as his share, for he is toothless' — the praise shows that the grinding is occasioned by the deity. Similarly, '[one should] prepare a <s>Saumāpauṣṇa</s> <s>caru</s>; let it not be unground, [for one] desiring cattle' — [this] shows the 'not-unground' [quality]. Likewise, 'half is ground and half unground, because of the two-deity nature' — [this] shows that the grinding is indeed occasioned by the deity.
Page break marker: 309

children.text: vacanāt sarvapeṣaṇaṃ taṃ prati śāstravattvād arthābhāvād dvicarāv{*3/343*} apeṣaṇaṃ bhavati // MS_3,3.43 //
children.translated_text: Because of the [Vedic] statement, there would be complete grinding for that [<s>Pūṣan</s>]; because of the existence of scripture [for it]; and because of the absence of purpose, in a two-deity <s>caru</s> there would be non-grinding. // MS 3,3.43 //

children.text: idaṃ padottaraṃ sūtram, nemapiṣṭaṃ bhavatīti kasmād etan na vacanam iti, ucyate, yadi vacanam etad bhavet saumāpauṣṇamātram anūdya sarvatra peṣaṇaṃ vidadhyāc carau paśau puroḍāśe ca, tatra somāpauṣṇasya{*3/344*} carusaṃbandhe nemapiṣṭasaṃbandhe cobhayasmin vidhīyamāne vākyam bhidyeta. tasmād yo yaḥ saumāpauṣṇas tatra tatra nemapiṣṭatā, taṃ prati saumāpauṣṇamātraṃ prati{*3/345*} śāstravattvam ardhapeṣaṇasya, puroḍāśe 'rthāt sarvapeṣaṇe prāpte 'rthābhāvāc ca paśau carau vāpeṣaṇe prāpte vacanam idaṃ bhavet. tatra caruśabdo na vivakṣitasvārthaḥ syāt, pradarśanārthaḥ kalpyeta, peṣaṇānuvādapakṣe punar naiṣa virodho bhavati, tasmād bhavaty eva liṅgam. nanv aṅganāśabhayāt paśor apeṣaṇam. neti brūmaḥ - ardhapeṣaṇe nāṅganāśo 'piṣṭād avadāsyate, peṣaṇaṃ cādṛṣṭārtham.
children.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> follows [the previous] topic. 'Let it not be unground' — why is this not a [Vedic] injunctive statement? It is said: if this were a [Vedic] statement, it would, having referred to the <s>Saumāpauṣṇa</s> alone, enjoin grinding everywhere — in the <s>caru</s>, the animal sacrifice, and the <s>puroḍāśa</s>. In that case, since both the <s>caru</s>-connection of the <s>Saumāpauṣṇa</s> and the 'not-unground'-connection would be enjoined, the sentence would be split. Therefore, for every <s>Saumāpauṣṇa</s>, there is the 'not-unground' quality. For that — for the <s>Saumāpauṣṇa</s> alone — there is the scriptural basis for half-grinding. When complete grinding is already obtained by the nature of the thing in the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, and when non-grinding is obtained in the animal sacrifice and <s>caru</s> because of the absence of purpose, this would be a [Vedic] statement. There, the word '<s>caru</s>' would not have its own literal meaning intended; it would be construed as illustrative. On the view that [the passage] is a restatement of grinding, however, there is no such contradiction. Therefore the indicatory mark indeed holds. [Objection:] But is not the non-grinding in the animal sacrifice [justified] because of the fear of destroying the limbs? [Reply:] No, we say — in half-grinding, there is no destruction of the limbs; the portions would be cut off from the unground [half]. And the grinding serves a transcendent (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) purpose.

children.text: ekasmin vārthadharmatvād aindrāgnavad ubhayor na syād acoditatvāt // MS_3,3.44 //
children.translated_text: Or [the grinding applies] only to a single-[deity offering]; because of the nature as a property of the thing, like the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (offering to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>), it should not apply to both, because of [one deity's share] not being enjoined [for grinding]. // MS 3,3.44 //

children.text:
ekadevatye vā pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ bhavitum arhati, naindrāpauṣṇe. kutaḥ? naiṣa devatādharmo vidhīyate, pūṣṇo bhāgaḥ piṣṭa upayoktavya iti. kasya tarhi? arthasya dharmaḥ. kaḥ punar arthaḥ? yāgaḥ. katham avagamyate? na devatādharma iti. ucyate - na hi tasyā bhāgo 'sti.
nanu yad devatāyai dīyate, tat tasyā bhāgo bhavati. ucyate - etad dhi devatām uddiśya tyajyate, na ca tyāgamātreṇa devatāsvatvaṃ bhavati. parigrahaṇena hi svasvāmisaṃbandha āpadyate, na ca parigṛhītaṃ devatayeti kiṃcana pramāṇam asti. yaś{*3/346*} ca yaṃ bhajate, sa [310]{*3/347*} tasya bhāgaḥ, na ca havir devatā bhajate, tasmān nāsti pūṣṇo bhāgaḥ.
athāpi kathaṃcid bhaved bhāgaḥ, tathāpi na devatāyā dharmaḥ peṣaṇaṃ bhavitum arhati, niṣprayojano hi tathā syād ayāgadharmatvāt. kathaṃ tarhi prakaraṇāntare samāmnāto yāgadharmo bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, vākyasaṃyogāt. nanu ca devatayaiṣa saṃyogaḥ śrūyate na yāgeneti. ucyate - bhāgābhāvād anarthakatvāc ca na devatāsaṃyoga ity uktam.
tathāpi tu yathā yāgasaṃbandho bhavati, tathā vaktavyam. tad ucyate - ayam atra pūṣṇo bhāgo yaḥ pūṣaṇam uddiśya tyajyate, yasya dravyasya tyāge pūṣā devatā, na caindrāpauṣṇe bhavati pūṣā devatā, na sa caruḥ pūṣṇaḥ svatvena saṃbadhyate. tasmād aindrāpauṣṇe na kaścid asti pūṣṇaś caruṇā saṃbandhaḥ, kevale tu pūṣaṇi devatābhūte tasmai saṃkalpito bhāgo bhavati. katham? yam uddiśya saṃkalpo bhavati sa tasya bhāga iti prasiddhir eṣā, tena yady api pūṣā svenoccāraṇenendrāpūṣṇor upakārakam uccāraṇaṃ kurvann upakārako bhavet, tathāpi na tasya dvidevatyo bhāga ity ucyate, asaṃkalpanāt. kevale pūṣaṇi devatāyāṃ caroḥ peṣaṇaṃ kriyate, naindrāpauṣṇeṣu dvidevatyeṣv iti.
children.translated_text:
Or the grinding of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> should apply [only] to the single-deity [offering], not to the <s>Aindrāpauṣṇa</s>. Why? What is enjoined here is not a property of the deity — [i.e., the rule is not] that <s>Pūṣan</s>'s share should be consumed ground. Of what then? It is a property of the thing [i.e., the ritual act]. And what is the thing? The sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>). How is it understood that it is not a property of the deity? It is said: for [the deity] has no share.
[Objection:] But what is given to a deity becomes her share. [Reply:] It is said: this is indeed abandoned with reference to the deity, but ownership of the deity does not arise by mere abandonment. For the relationship of owned-and-owner arises through acceptance, and there is no evidence that [the offering] is accepted by the deity. And one's share is what one enjoys; and the deity does not enjoy the oblation. Therefore, there is no share belonging to <s>Pūṣan</s>.
Even if there were somehow a share, still the grinding should not be a property of the deity — for it would then be purposeless, not being a property of the sacrifice. Then how will [the grinding,] being prescribed in another context, become a property of the sacrifice? It is said: because of the connection with the sentence. [Objection:] But the connection heard here is with the deity, not with the sacrifice. [Reply:] It is said: because of the non-existence of a share and because of purposelessness, it is not connected with the deity — this has been stated.
But one should explain how the connection with the sacrifice comes about. This is stated: here, '<s>Pūṣan</s>'s share' means what is abandoned with reference to <s>Pūṣan</s> — the offering material for whose abandonment <s>Pūṣan</s> is the deity. And in the <s>Aindrāpauṣṇa</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s> is not the [sole] deity; that <s>caru</s> is not connected with <s>Pūṣan</s> by ownership. Therefore, in the <s>Aindrāpauṣṇa</s>, there is no connection of <s>Pūṣan</s> with the <s>caru</s>. But when <s>Pūṣan</s> alone is the deity, the share is dedicated to him. How? The well-known [principle is]: what is dedicated with reference to someone is his share. Therefore, even though <s>Pūṣan</s> might, by his own utterance, be an assistant contributing to the utterance of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> [together], still the two-deity [offering] is not called his share — because of the absence of dedication. Grinding of the <s>caru</s> is performed [only] when <s>Pūṣan</s> alone is the deity, not in two-deity <s>Aindrāpauṣṇa</s> [offerings].

children.text: hetumātram adantatvam // MS_3,3.45 //
children.translated_text: The toothlessness is merely a reason [for the grinding, not a property of the deity]. // MS 3,3.45 //

children.text: yad uktam - adantako hīti{*3/348*} devatādharmaṃ darśayatīti. arthavāda eṣa itarasminn api pakṣa upapadyate.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'for he is toothless' shows that [the grinding] is a property of the deity — this explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) is applicable on the other view as well.

children.text: vacanaṃ param // MS_3,3.46 //
children.translated_text: The [Vedic] statement is the decisive [argument]. // MS 3,3.46 //

children.text: athāparaṃ yat kāraṇam uktam - nemapiṣṭam iti{*3/349*} dvidevatye peṣaṇaṃ darśayati, ardhapiṣṭaṃ{*3/350*} bhavaty ardham apiṣṭaṃ dvidevatyatvāyeti [311]{*3/351*} devatādharmaṃ darśayatīti. atrocyate - evaṃ sati vacanam idam aprāpte bhavatīti. nanv anekārthavidhidhānam ekaṃ vākyaṃ prāpnoti. ucyate - sati pakṣāntare 'nekārthavidhiḥ pakṣāntarāśrayaṇena parihriyate. asati punaḥ pakṣāntare uccāraṇānarthakyaprasaṅgaparijihīrṣayānekārthaṃ vākyam abhyupagantavyaṃ bhavati. tasmān na dvidevatye peṣaṇam iti siddham.
children.translated_text: As for the other reason that was stated — 'let it not be unground' shows grinding in a two-deity [offering], and 'half is ground, half unground, because of the two-deity nature' shows that [the grinding] is a property of the deity — to this it is said: in that case, this statement would be an injunction for what is not [otherwise] obtained. [Objection:] But a single sentence may enjoin multiple things. [Reply:] It is said: when there is an alternative view, the multiple-purpose injunction is avoided by resorting to the alternative view. But when there is no alternative view, one must accept that the sentence has multiple purposes, in order to avoid the consequence of purposelessness of the utterance. Therefore, grinding does not apply in a two-deity [offering] — this is established.

children.text: nivītam iti manuṣyadharmaḥ śabdasya tatpradhānatvāt // MS_3,4.1 //
children.translated_text: The <s>nivīta</s> (sacred thread worn around the neck) — this is a property of the person, because the [Vedic] word has that as its principal [referent]. // MS 3,4.1 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnātam - nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ prācīnāvītaṃ pitṝṇām upavītaṃ devānām upavyayate devalakṣmam eva tat kuruta iti{*3/353*}. nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām ity atra saṃdehaḥ - kim ayaṃ vidhir utārthavāda iti. yadā vidhiḥ, tadā kim ayaṃ puruṣadharma uta karmadharmaḥ? atha yat prakaraṇe manuṣyāṇām, tatra vidhiḥ, uta manuṣyapradhāne karmaṇi niviśata iti.
kiṃ prāptam? vidhir manuṣyadharmaś ceti, yadi vidhir evam apūrvam arthaṃ vidadhad arthavān bhavati, itarathārthavādamātram anarthakam. vidhiś cet puruṣadharmo nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām iti puruṣapradhāno nirdeśaḥ. katham avagamyate? nātra manuṣyā vidhīyante, manuṣyāṇāṃ nivītaṃ vidhīyate, na cāvihitam aṅgaṃ bhavati. yadi manuṣyā api vidhīyeran vākyaṃ bhidyeta. tasmān nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām upakārakam.
nanu prakaraṇād darśapūrṇamāsayor upakārakam. prakaraṇād dhi vākyaṃ balavattaram. api ca guṇabhūteṣu manuṣyeṣu kārakasaṃbandhasya vivakṣitatvāt tṛtīyā bhavet, ṣaṣṭhī tv eṣā saṃbandhalakṣaṇā, tatra guṇabhūteṣu manuṣyeṣu manuṣyagrahaṇaṃ naiva kartavyaṃ syāt. manuṣyair eva tat kriyamāṇaṃ kriyeta, manuṣyapradhānapakṣe tu kartavyam.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is prescribed: 'The <s>nivīta</s> (round the neck) is for humans; the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> (over the right shoulder) is for the ancestors; the <s>upavīta</s> (sacred thread over the left shoulder) is for the gods — one puts on the sacred thread [and] makes it a mark of the divine.' Regarding '<s>nivīta</s> is for humans,' there is a doubt: is this an injunction or an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>)? If it is an injunction, then is this a property of the person or a property of the ritual? Or, regarding what is in the context of 'for humans' — is it an injunction there, or does [the <s>nivīta</s>] apply to a ritual where humans are the principal [focus]?
What is the prima facie view? It is an injunction, and a property of the person. For if it is an injunction, it becomes meaningful by enjoining something new; otherwise it would be merely a purposeless explanatory passage. And if an injunction, [then] the instruction '<s>nivīta</s> is for humans' has the person as its principal [referent] — it is a property of the person. How is this understood? The humans are not being enjoined here; the <s>nivīta</s> is being enjoined for humans. And what is not enjoined [as a subsidiary] cannot be a subsidiary. If humans were also being enjoined, the sentence would be split. Therefore, the <s>nivīta</s> is an aid for humans.
[Objection:] But from the context, [it is] an aid for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. [Reply:] For the sentence is stronger than the context. Moreover, since for humans in a subordinate [role] the instrumental relationship is intended, there would be the third case-ending (instrumental); but this is the sixth case-ending (genitive), which denotes a [general] relationship. In that case, for humans in a subordinate [role], the mention of 'humans' would not be needed at all — the rite being performed by humans alone, it would [naturally] be performed [by them]. But on the view that the person is the principal [referent], the mention is needed.

children.text: apadeśo vā, arthasya vidyamānatvāt // MS_3,4.2 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is merely] a description (<s>apadeśa</s>), because the meaning [is already] established. // MS 3,4.2 //

children.text: apadeśa iti jñāyamānasya vacanam. sa eṣa na vidhiḥ. anuvāda eṣaḥ. kutaḥ? arthasya vidyamānatvāt. prāpta evārthaḥ, yan nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām, nivītaṃ hi manuṣyāḥ prāyaśaḥ svārthaṃ kurvanti, tasmād anuvādaḥ.
children.translated_text: 'Description' (<s>apadeśa</s>) means stating what is [already] known. This is not an injunction. This is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>). Why? Because the meaning is already established. The meaning — that the <s>nivīta</s> is for humans — is already obtained; for humans generally wear the <s>nivīta</s> for their own purposes. Therefore it is a restatement.

children.text: vidhis tv apūrvatvāt{*3/355*} syāt // MS_3,4.3 //
children.translated_text: But it should be an injunction, because of [its] novelty. // MS 3,4.3 //

children.text: vidhir eva bhavet, tathā prayojanavān, itarathā vādamātram anarthakam, pūrvavān anuvādo bhavati, ayaṃ tv apūrvaḥ, yan niyamena nivyātavyam iti.
children.translated_text: It should indeed be an injunction — thus it is purposeful; otherwise it would be merely a purposeless statement. A restatement has a precedent; but this is novel — [namely,] that the <s>nivīta</s> must be worn as a rule.

children.text: sa prāyāt karmadharmaḥ syāt // MS_3,4.4 //
children.translated_text: [Being an injunction,] because of the predominance [of the context], it should be a property of the ritual (<s>karmadharma</s>). // MS 3,4.4 //

children.text:
yad uktam - vidhir iti, etad gṛhyate. yat tu manuṣyadharma iti, tan nānumatam. kratudharmo{*3/356*} 'yaṃ prakaraṇāt, prakṛtyaiva{*3/357*} hi karmaprāyeṣu dharmeṣūcyamāneṣv etad abhidhīyate, tasmāt karmadharmaḥ.
NOTES:

*{3/357: E2: prakṛtyaivaṃ}*
children.translated_text:
What was said — that it is an injunction — that is accepted. But that it is a property of the person — that is not approved. This is a property of the rite, because of the context. For it is stated in a context where ritual properties predominate — therefore it is a property of the ritual.

[{3/357: E2: <s>prakṛtyaivaṃ</s>}]

children.text: vākyaśeṣatvāt // MS_3,4.5 //
children.translated_text: Because of [its being] the remainder of the sentence. // MS 3,4.5 //

children.text: nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām ity asya vākyaśeṣaḥ samākhyā, ādhvaryavam iti{*3/358*}. yadi darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śeṣaḥ, tato 'dhvaryuṇā kartavyam. tatra samākhyānugṛhīṣyate{*3/359*}.
children.translated_text: '<s>Nivīta</s> is for humans' — the remainder of this sentence is the designation '<s>ādhvaryava</s>' (belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>). If it is a remainder of [the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context], then it should be performed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. There, the designation will be upheld.

children.text: tatprakaraṇe, yat tatsaṃyuktam avipratiṣedhāt // MS_3,4.6 //
children.translated_text: In that context, [it applies to] what is connected with that, because there is no contradiction. // MS 3,4.6 //

children.text: ucyate - prakaraṇāt samākhyānāc ca karmadharmo vijñāyate, [314]{*3/360*} vākyān manuṣyadharmaḥ, tasmād utkarṣam arhati. neti brūmaḥ, prakaraṇa evābhiniviśamānasya manuṣyapradhānatāvakalpiṣyate. katham? yad darśapūrṇamāsayor manuṣyapradhānam, tatra nivekṣyate 'nvāhāryakarmaṇi, prakaraṇaṃ caivam anugrahīṣyate, vākyaṃ ca.
children.translated_text: It is said: from the context and the designation, [the <s>nivīta</s>] is understood as a property of the ritual; from the sentence, [it is] a property of the person — therefore it merits withdrawal [to the <s>ātithya</s>]. No, we say. For one who insists [only] on the context, the predominance of humans will be construed. How? What in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> has humans as its principal [focus] — there [the <s>nivīta</s>] will be placed, in the <s>anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering) ritual. And thus both the context and the sentence will be upheld.

children.text: tatpradhāne vā tulyavat prasaṃkhyānād itarasya tadarthatvāt // MS_3,4.7 //
children.translated_text: Or in [a rite] where that [human element] is principal, because of the equal enumeration — since the other [items] serve that purpose. // MS 3,4.7 //

children.text:
naitad asti - prakaraṇe niveśa iti, manuṣyapradhāne karmaṇi nivītaṃ syād ātithye. kutaḥ? tulyavat prasaṃkhyānāt, tulyāni caitāni prasaṃkhyāyante. yat tāvat, upavītaṃ devānām upavyayata iti, tat prakṛtayor darśapūrṇamāsayor upavītaṃ vidadhāti. yat prācīnāvītaṃ piṭṝṇām iti, tat pitṛpradhāne karmaṇi prācīnāvītaṃ vidadhāti. yad apy etat, nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām iti, tad apy ātithye nirapekṣaṃ vidadhāti. kathaṃ gamyate? manuṣyapradhāne vidadhātīti. manuṣyāṇām iti ṣaṣṭhyantena saṃbandhāt. manuṣyāṇām eva prāpnoti, na manuṣyapradhāne. ucyate - manuṣyāṇāṃ kalpyamāne phalaṃ kalpanīyam, manuṣyapradhāne punaḥ ṣaṣṭhī bhaviṣyati, saṃbandhaś caivam avakalpiṣyate, phalaṃ caivaṃ na kalpanīyam. tad uktam - sameṣu vākyabhedaḥ syād iti{*3/361*}.
nanu{*3/362*} manuṣyapradhānena sahaikavākyatāṃ prāptam, punaḥ prakṛtābhyāṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ekavākyatāṃ yāsyati. na hi dvau saṃbandhāv ekasmin vākye vidhīyete, bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. itarasya manuṣyagrahaṇasya nivītasaṃbandhārthatvāt, tenaiva sahaikavākyatā bhaviṣyati pratyakṣeṇa śabdena, tad ekavākyatayā cārthavattve sati na prakṛtenaikavākyatāvakalpyate. tasmāt prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvātithye nivekṣyata iti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — that [the <s>nivīta</s>] is placed in the context [of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>]. The <s>nivīta</s> should apply in a rite where humans are principal — in the <s>ātithya</s> (hospitality rite). Why? Because of the equal enumeration — these are enumerated equally. First, 'the <s>upavīta</s> is for the gods — one puts on the sacred thread' enjoins the <s>upavīta</s> for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> as the rites under discussion. Then, 'the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> is for the ancestors' enjoins the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> in a rite where ancestors are principal. And likewise, 'the <s>nivīta</s> is for humans' also independently enjoins [the <s>nivīta</s>] in the <s>ātithya</s>. How is it understood that it enjoins [the <s>nivīta</s>] in [a rite] where humans are principal? From the genitive case-ending in 'of humans' (<s>manuṣyāṇām</s>), [indicating] a relationship. [Objection:] [The genitive] can only mean 'belonging to humans,' not 'in [a rite] where humans are principal.' [Reply:] It is said: if [taken as] 'belonging to humans,' a fruit [of the <s>nivīta</s>] would have to be supplied [by implication]. But for 'in [a rite] where humans are principal,' the genitive will apply, and the relationship will be thus construed, and no fruit needs to be supplied. This has been stated: 'When [the sentences are] equivalent, there would be splitting of the sentence.'
[Objection:] But having obtained a single-sentence relationship with [a rite] where humans are principal, will it then also enter into a single-sentence relationship with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> under discussion? [Reply:] Two relationships cannot be enjoined in a single sentence, for the sentence would be split. Since the mention of 'humans' in the other [interpretation] serves the purpose of [connecting with] the <s>nivīta</s>, it will form a single sentence with [the <s>nivīta</s>] by directly perceptible words. And when meaningfulness is achieved through that single-sentence relationship, a single-sentence relationship with the [contextual] subject need not be construed. Therefore, overriding the context, [the <s>nivīta</s>] is placed in the <s>ātithya</s>.

children.text: arthavādo vā prakaraṇāt // MS_3,4.8 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), because of the context. // MS 3,4.8 //

children.text: naitad asti - vidhiḥ sa ca manuṣyapradhāne karmaṇīti. manuṣyāṇām iti manuṣyasaṃbandho 'tra śrūyate, na manuṣyapradhānena karmaṇā saṃbandhaḥ. manuṣyaprādhānye ca sati phalaṃ kalpanīyam. ātithyakarmaṇā tv anirdiṣṭenāprakṛtenānumeyena saṃbadhyeta. tatra ko doṣaḥ? prakaraṇād utkṛṣyeta saṃbhavaṃs tatra. kathaṃ saṃbhava iti cet. arthavāda eṣaḥ sa prakṛtaṃ stuvan prakaraṇe saṃbhaviṣyati, vidhiḥ sann utkṛṣyeta. tasmān na vidhir manuṣyapradhāne karmaṇīti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that it is an injunction and that [it applies] in a rite where humans are principal. 'Of humans' — a connection with humans is heard here, not a connection with a rite where humans are principal. And when humans are the principal [referent], a fruit would have to be supplied. But [on the other view] it would be connected with the <s>ātithya</s> ritual — which is unspecified, not under discussion, and [only] inferred. What is the fault in that? It would be withdrawn from the context, [the <s>nivīta</s>] being applicable there. How is it applicable? This is an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) — praising the [contextual] subject, it will be applicable in the context. As an injunction, it would be withdrawn. Therefore, it is not an injunction in a rite where humans are principal.

children.text: vidhinā caikavākyatvāt // MS_3,4.9 //
children.translated_text: And because of the single-sentence relationship with the injunction. // MS 3,4.9 //

children.text: itaś ca na vidhiḥ, kutaḥ? vidhinaikavākyatvāt - upavyayate devalakṣmam eva tat kurute ity eṣa vidhiḥ, anenāsya sahaikavākyatā bhavati. yadītaro 'pi vidhiḥ syāt, vākyaṃ bhidyeta, na hi vidheś ca{*3/364*} vidheś caikavākyatā bhavati, vacanavyaktibhedāt. tatraikavākyatārūpaṃ bādhyeta. kim ekavākyatārūpam? nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām iti prāptānuvādaḥ. prāptasya kim arthena punar vacanam? upavītastutyarthena. katham upavītastutiḥ? nivītam ayogyaṃ devakarmaṇi darśapūrṇamāsasaṃjñake, manuṣyāṇāṃ hi tat. tathā prācīnāvītaṃ pitṝṇām, na devakarmaṇi. upavītaṃ tu tatra yogyam, tasmād upavyātavyam iti. yathā, yādṛśo 'sya veśaḥ{*3/365*}, tādṛśo naṭānām, yādṛśo devadattasya tādṛśo brāhmaṇānām iti devadattaveśapraśaṃsārtham{*3/366*} itaraveśasaṃkīrtanam{*3/367*}. evam ihāpy upavyānastutyarthena nivītasaṃkīrtanam. nāsty atra vidhāyakaḥ śabdaḥ - nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ kartavyam iti. ātithyaprayogavacanam, tasya kartavyatāvidhāyakam iti cet. naitad evam, [316]{*3/368*} stutyarthenārthavattve sati na śakyaṃ kalpayitum, parokṣaṃ hi tad ānarthakyaparijihīrṣayā kalpyeta. parihṛte tv ānarthakya iha punar na kiṃcit kalpanīyam, tasmād arthavādaḥ. evaṃ ca vākyenāviruddhaṃ prakaraṇam arthavad bhavati.
children.translated_text: For this further reason it is not an injunction. Why? Because of the single-sentence relationship with the injunction — 'one puts on the sacred thread, makes it a mark of the divine' — this is the injunction; this [statement about <s>nivīta</s>] has a single-sentence relationship with it. If the other [i.e., 'nivīta is for humans'] were also an injunction, the sentence would be split — for two injunctions cannot form a single sentence, because of the difference in the utterance-instances. There the single-sentence form would be overridden. What is the single-sentence form? 'The <s>nivīta</s> is for humans' is a restatement of what is [already] obtained. What is the purpose of restating what is obtained? For the purpose of praising the <s>upavīta</s>. How is it a praise of the <s>upavīta</s>? The <s>nivīta</s> is unsuitable for divine ritual actions designated as <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, for it belongs to humans. Similarly, 'the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> is for the ancestors' — not [suitable] for divine ritual actions. But the <s>upavīta</s> is suitable there; therefore one should wear the <s>upavīta</s>. Just as [one might say], 'such is his attire — such is [the attire] of actors; such is <s>Devadatta</s>'s — such is [the attire] of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>' — where the mention of the other's attire serves to praise <s>Devadatta</s>'s attire. Similarly here too, the mention of the <s>nivīta</s> serves to praise the wearing of the <s>upavīta</s>. There is no injunctive word here — [such as] 'the <s>nivīta</s> should be performed for humans.' [Objection:] It is a statement of the application [in] the <s>ātithya</s> rite, and that serves as an injunction of obligation. [Reply:] This is not so — when meaningfulness is achieved through the purpose of praise, [an injunction] cannot be construed. For that [interpretation] would be construed hypothetically, out of a desire to avoid purposelessness. But when purposelessness has been avoided, nothing further needs to be construed here. Therefore, [it is] an explanatory passage. And thus the context, being non-contradicted by the sentence, becomes meaningful.

children.text: a. upavītaṃ liṅgadarśanāt sarvadharmaḥ syāt//
children.translated_text: a. The <s>upavīta</s> (sacred thread), because of the observation of the indicatory mark, should be a property of all [rites]. //

children.text: b. na vā prakaraṇāt tasya darśanam//
children.translated_text: b. Or not, because the observation [of the indicatory mark] is from the context. //

children.text: c. vidhir vā syād apūrvatvāt//
children.translated_text: c. Or it should be an injunction, because of novelty. //

children.text: d. udaktvaṃ cāpūrvatvāt//
children.translated_text: d. And the northward direction (<s>udaktva</s>) [should be an injunction], because of novelty. //

children.text: e. sato vā liṅgadarśanam//
children.translated_text: e. Or the observation of the indicatory mark is of what [already] exists. //

children.text: f. vidhis tu dhāraṇe 'pūrvartvāt//{*3/369*}
children.translated_text: f. But the injunction is for the wearing (<s>dhāraṇa</s>), because of novelty. //

children.text: digvibhāgaś ca tadvat saṃbandhasyārthahetutvāt // MS_3,4.10 //
children.translated_text: And the division of directions is similar, because the connection serves as the reason for the purpose. // MS 3,4.10 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭomaṃ prakṛtya śrūyate - prācīṃ devā abhajanta dakṣiṇāṃ pitaraḥ pratīcīṃ manuṣyā udīcīm asurā iti{*3/370*}. apareṣām, udīcīṃ rudrā iti{*3/371*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ vidhir utārthavādaḥ? [317]{*3/372*} vidhiḥ san kiṃ manuṣyadharmaḥ, uta karmadharmaḥ? atha vā prakaraṇe manuṣyapradhāne karmaṇi niveśaḥ? kiṃ vātithya iti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? digvibhāgaś ca tadvat, saṃbandhasyārthahetutvāt. ya eṣa digvibhāgaḥ, sa nivītavad vicāryaḥ. yo nivīte pūrvapakṣaḥ, sa iha pūrvapakṣaḥ, yo madhyamaḥ, sa madhyamaḥ, yaḥ siddhāntaḥ, sa siddhāntaḥ. arthavattvād vidhir manuṣyasaṃbandhān manuṣyadharma iti pūrvapakṣaḥ. pratyaṅmukhā udaṅmukhā vā pṛṣṭhata ādityaṃ prāṃśu{*3/373*} padārthān anutiṣṭhanti manuṣyā ity anuvādaḥ. vidhir eva prakaraṇānugrahāc ca jyotiṣṭomadharmaḥ, vākyaprakaraṇānugrahāya jyotiṣṭome manuṣyapradhāne dakṣiṇāvyāpāre niveśa ity aparaḥ pakṣaḥ. bhinnatvād vākyānām ātithye niveśa ity aparaṃ matam. arthavādo 'yaṃ prakaraṇānugrahāya, prācīnavaṃśaṃ karotīty anena vidhinaikavākyatvasya pratyakṣasiddhatvād iti siddhāntaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Having set forth the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: 'The gods took the east; the ancestors [took] the south; the humans [took] the west; the <s>Asuras</s> [took] the north.' According to others, 'the <s>Rudras</s> [took] the north.' There the doubt arises: is this an injunction or an explanatory passage? If an injunction, is it a property of the person or a property of the ritual? Or is it placed in the context, in a rite where humans are principal? Or in the <s>ātithya</s>?
What is the prima facie view? The division of directions is similar [to the <s>nivīta</s> discussion], because the connection serves as the reason for the purpose. This division of directions should be examined like the <s>nivīta</s>. Whatever is the prima facie view for the <s>nivīta</s> is the prima facie view here; whatever is the intermediate view is the intermediate view here; whatever is the established conclusion is the established conclusion here. [First view:] Because of meaningfulness, it is an injunction; because of the connection with humans, it is a property of the person — this is the prima facie view. [Second:] Humans face west or north, with the sun behind them, and [thus] carry out their daily activities — this is a restatement. [Third:] It is indeed an injunction, and because of upholding the context, it is a property of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. To uphold both sentence and context, [it is] placed in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> in the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee-distribution) procedure where humans are principal — this is another view. [Fourth:] Because of the splitting of sentences, [it is] placed in the <s>ātithya</s> — another view. [Established conclusion:] This is an explanatory passage for upholding the context, because the single-sentence relationship with the injunction 'he makes the enclosure with [posts extending] to the east' (<s>prācīnavaṃśaṃ karoti</s>) is directly established — this is the established conclusion.

children.text: paruṣi ditapūrṇaghṛtavidagdhaṃ ca tadvat // MS_3,4.11 //
children.translated_text: And [the statements about] what grows on joints (<s>paruṣi</s>), what is full (<s>pūrṇa</s>), ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>), and what is scorched (<s>vidagdha</s>) are similar. // MS 3,4.11 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnātam - yat puruṣi ditaṃ tad devānām, yad antarā, tan manuṣyāṇām, yat samūlam, tat pitṝṇām iti{*3/374*}. tathā - yo vidagdhaḥ, sa nairṛtaḥ. yo 'śṛtaḥ, sa raudraḥ, ya śṛtaḥ, sa sadevatyaḥ{*3/375*}. tasmād avidahatā śrapayitavyaṃ sadevatyāya iti{*3/376*}. jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - yat pūrṇam, tan manuṣyāṇām upari, adho devānām adhaḥ pitṝṇām iti{*3/377*}. tathā - ghṛtaṃ [318]{*3/378*} devānāṃ mastu pitṝṇāṃ niṣpakvaṃ manuṣyāṇām iti{*3/379*}. tatra manuṣyasaṃbaddheṣu, raudre ca saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ dharmā vidhayaḥ, uta karmadharmā anūvādāḥ? atha yat prakaraṇaṃ{*3/380*} manuṣyapradhānam, raudraṃ ca tatra niviśeran, utātithye, utārthavāda iti.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? etāny api tadvat, yo nivīte pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ sa eteṣāṃ pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, yo madhyamaḥ sa madhyamaḥ, yaḥ siddhāntaḥ sa eva siddhāntaḥ. arthavattvān manuṣyasaṃbandhāc ca vidhayo manuṣyadharmāś ceti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. upari mūle cāniyamāl lāghavam, aśṛtaṃ rogatvād raudram, pūrṇe 'pi ślakṣṇatvāl lāghavam. evaṃ ghṛtaṃ{*3/381*} śirasi nihitaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ sukhakaram eva, arthaprāptatvād anuvāda ity uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ. vidhiḥ, karmadharmaprāyāt samākhyānāc ca karmadharma iti pakṣaḥ. anvāhārye dakṣiṇāsu ceti vākyaprakaraṇānugrahāt pakṣaḥ. ātithya iti vākyabhedaprasaṅgāt. arthavāda iti, prakaraṇād vidhinaikavākyatvād iti. parva pratilunāti{*3/382*}, upari vilād gṛhṇāti, navanītenābhyaṅkte, avidahatā śrapayitavyam{*3/383*} ity ebhiḥ sahaiṣām ekavākyabhāvaḥ. tasmād ete na vidhayo 'rthavādā iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is prescribed: 'What grows on the joint is for the gods; what is in between is for humans; what is at the root is for the ancestors.' Similarly: 'What is scorched belongs to <s>Nirṛti</s>. What is raw belongs to <s>Rudra</s>. What is [properly] cooked belongs to the deity.' Therefore, 'one should cook without scorching, for the sake of the deity.' In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'What is full is for humans above; below is for the gods; beneath is for the ancestors.' Similarly: 'Ghee is for the gods; whey is for the ancestors; unbaked [butter] is for humans.' There, regarding those connected with humans, and regarding what belongs to <s>Rudra</s>, the doubt arises: are these injunctions that are properties of humans, or are they properties of the ritual and restatements? Or should they, together with what is <s>Raudra</s> (belonging to <s>Rudra</s>), be placed in [a context] where humans are principal in the rite under discussion? Or in the <s>ātithya</s>? Or are they explanatory passages?
What is the prima facie view? These too are similar [to the <s>nivīta</s>]. Whatever is the first view for the <s>nivīta</s> is the first view for these; whatever is the intermediate view is the intermediate view; whatever is the established conclusion is the established conclusion. [First view:] Because of meaningfulness and the connection with humans, they are injunctions and properties of humans — this is the first view. [Second:] Because of the lack of restriction regarding 'above' and 'at the root,' [these are matters of] convenience; what is raw is <s>Raudra</s> because it causes disease; even what is full has smoothness and hence convenience; similarly ghee placed on the head is comfortable for humans — because of being obtained by the nature of things, [these are] restatements — this is the second view. [Third:] It is an injunction, and because of the designation where ritual properties predominate, it is a property of the ritual — this is [another] view. [Fourth:] In the <s>anvāhārya</s> and the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> — this is [another] view, from upholding both sentence and context. [Fifth:] In the <s>ātithya</s> — because of the consequence of sentence-splitting. [Established conclusion:] They are explanatory passages, because of the context and because of the single-sentence relationship with the injunction. 'He shaves off a joint,' 'he takes from above the sieve,' 'he anoints with butter,' 'one should cook without scorching' — with these [injunctions] these [statements] have a single-sentence relationship. Therefore, these are not injunctions but explanatory passages.
