children.text: akarma kratusaṃyuktaṃ saṃyogān nityānuvādaḥ syāt // MS_3,3.12 //
children.translated_text: What is not a [ritual] action but is connected with the rite — because of [that] connection, it should be a permanent restatement. // MS 3,3.12 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnāyate - nānṛtaṃ vaded iti{*3/384*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ayaṃ pratiṣedho dārśapaurṇamāsikasya padārthasya [319]{*3/385*} prakaraṇa eva niveśaḥ. atha prāyeṇa prāptasya karmaṇaḥ puruṣaṃ prati pratiṣedhaḥ puruṣadharmo 'yam iti. kiṃ prāptam? puruṣadharmaḥ syāt, puruṣasyāyam upadiśyate, na darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ. kutaḥ? puruṣaprayatnasya śravaṇāt, vaded iti vadanam anutiṣṭhed iti śrutyā gamyate, tasya puruṣasaṃbandhaḥ śrutyaiva, karmasaṃbandhaḥ prakaraṇāt. śrutiś ca prakaraṇād balīyasī. itarathā vadanaṃ bhavatīty etāvaty arthe vadanam anutiṣṭhed ity avivakṣitasvārthaḥ parārtho vidhyartho bhavet. puruṣasyopadeśe punar vivakṣitasvārtha eva śabdaḥ. tasmāt puruṣasyopadeśaḥ. yasya copadeśaḥ, tasyāyaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ. sa cāyam artha upanayanakāla eva puruṣasya pratiṣiddhaḥ, tena saṃyogenāyaṃ nityānuvādaḥ.
nanv eṣā śrutis tasyāḥ smṛter mūlam. naiṣā tasyā mūlaṃ bhavitum arhati. yadīyaṃ tanmūlikā bhavet, darśapūrṇamāsayor iti smaryeta, upanayanakāla eva cāsyopadeṣṭāro bhavanti. api ca puruṣadharma ity upadiśanti, tasmān naiṣā smṛtir ataḥ śruter iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon rites) it is prescribed: 'One should not speak untruth.' There the doubt arises: is this prohibition a placement of a <s>Darśapaurṇamāsika</s> element in the context itself, or is it a prohibition directed toward the person regarding an action generally obtained — [meaning] this is a property of the person? What is the prima facie view? It should be a property of the person; this is taught for the person, not for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Why? Because of the hearing of the person's effort — 'he should speak' (<s>vadet</s>) means 'he should carry out speaking,' which is understood by direct statement; its connection with the person is by direct statement itself, while its connection with the ritual is from the context. And direct statement is stronger than context. Otherwise, 'speaking occurs' — for this much meaning alone, 'he should carry out speaking' would have its own meaning not intended and would serve another purpose — the injunctive purpose. But when [it is] taught for the person, the word has precisely its own intended meaning. Therefore, it is taught for the person. And for whom the teaching is [given], for him is this prohibition. And this meaning has already been prohibited for the person at the time of <s>upanayana</s> (initiation); through that connection, this is a permanent restatement.
[Objection:] But this <s>śruti</s> (Vedic statement) is the source of that <s>smṛti</s> (traditional rule). [Reply:] This cannot be its source. If this were the basis of that [<s>smṛti</s>], it would be remembered as '[a rule] of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>'; but the teachers instruct it at the very time of <s>upanayana</s>. Moreover, they teach it as a property of the person. Therefore this <s>smṛti</s> is not from this <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: vidhir vā saṃyogāntarāt // MS_3,4.13 //
children.translated_text: Or it is an injunction, because of a different connection. // MS 3,4.13 //

children.text:
vidhir vāyaṃ darśapūrṇamāsayor nānṛtaṃ vaded iti, nānuvādaḥ. kutaḥ? saṃyogāntarāt. niyamānuṣṭhānena puruṣasya saṃbandhaḥ smaryate, padārthapratiṣedheneha saṃyogaḥ puruṣasya. katham anyac chrūyamāṇam anyasyānuvādo bhaviṣyati, tasmād vidhiḥ pratiṣedhasyāyam. āha gṛhṇāma{*3/386*} etat, vidhir iti. puruṣadharma iti tu gṛhṇāmaḥ{*3/387*} puruṣaprayatnasya śrutatvāt. atra brūmaḥ - sarveṣv ākhyāteṣu kriyānuṣṭhānaṃ śrūyate na kārakaṃ kiṃcit. katham etad gamyate? pratyayāt, yataḥ kriyām anuṣṭheyāṃ pratīmaḥ.
nanu kartāram api pratiyanti. satyaṃ pratiyanti, na tu śabdāt. kutas tarhi? arthāt, yadā kriyānuṣṭhātavyā vidhīyate, [320]{*3/388*} tadārthāt kārakavyāpāro gamyate, yaś cārthād gamyate. na sa śrautaḥ, yaś ca na śrauto na sa vākyād gamyate. katham asau prakaraṇaṃ bādhiṣyate.
āha - prakṛtipratyayau pratyayārthaṃ saha brūta ity ācāryopadeśāt kartā śabdārthaḥ karma cety avagamyate, kartari śap{*3/389*}, karmaṇi yag{*3/390*} iti pratyayārthaṃ kartāraṃ karma ca samāmananty ācāryāḥ, tasmāc chabdārthaḥ kartā karma ceti.
ucyate - nācāryavacanāt sūtrakāravacanād vā śabdārtho bhavati, pratyayād asau gamyate. anuṣṭheyā ca kriyā pratītā satī kārakāṇi pratyāyayatīty avagatam etat. api ca, naiva kartā pratyayārthaḥ karma vety ācāryā āhuḥ. nanu kartari karmaṇi ca lakāraḥ śrūyate. nāsau kartari karmaṇi vā śrūyate kiṃ tv ekasmin, ekavacanam, dvayor dvivacanaṃ bahuṣu bahuvacanam iti tatrāparaṃ vacanam. tatraivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate - ekasmin kartari dvayoḥ kartror bahuṣu kartṛṣv iti. evaṃ karmaṇy ekatvādisaṃbandhaḥ. tatra naivaṃ bhavati - kartari bhavaty ekasmiṃś ceti. kathaṃ tarhi? kartary ekasminn ekavacanam, kartur ekatva ity arthaḥ. evaṃ dvitve bahutve karmaṇi ca. evaṃ varṇyamāne laukikanyāyānugataḥ sūtrārtho varṇito bhavati. sūtrākṣarāṇi ca nyāyānugatāni bhavanti. āgamo 'pi cāyam eva, yadaikatvādayo vibhaktyarthāḥ, tadā karmādayo viśeṣaṇatveneti.
nanv etad apy asti yadā karmādayo vibhaktyarthāḥ, tadaikatvādayo viśeṣaṇatveneti. ucyate - arthaprāptā hi karmādayas te na bhavanti śabdasyābhidheyabhūtāḥ. na tv ekatvādayo 'rthāt prāpnuvanti, tena te śabdārthabhūtāḥ, tasmād api viśeṣaṇam ekatvādayaḥ, tathāpi viśeṣaṇam evābhidhīyate, yathā hiraṇyamālina ṛtvijaḥ pracarantīti hiraṇyamālitvaṃ viśeṣaṇa[321]{*3/391*}tvena, tathāpi tad eva vidhīyate, tasmāt kartur ekatvaṃ śabdārtho na kartā.
nanu kartur ekatvād ekavacanam, kartur dvitvād dvivacanam, kartur bahutvād bahuvacanam. tena nūnaṃ kartā śabdārtha iti gamyate. ucyate - naitad anumānāc chakyam, kartānuṣṭheyakriyāvagamād evāvagamyata iti pratyakṣam. tat tāvat kenacin na bādhyate. ekavacananirdeśe kartrekatvaṃ gamyate, dvivacananirdeśe kartur dvitvam, bahuvacananirdeśe kartṛbahutvam{*3/392*}. tad api pratyakṣam, katarad atrānumāṇaṃ bādhitum arhatīti, yathākṛtivacane śabde dvivacane dravyabhedo 'vagamyate, eka-vacane dravyaikatvam, evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam. tasmān na śrautaḥ, na cec chrautaḥ, na prakaraṇaṃ bādhiṣyate.
yat tu puruṣaprayatno 'narthako bhavati karmadharmapakṣe prayogavacanena kartavyatāvacanād iti. tad ucyate - aṅgaṃ sat prakaraṇena gṛhyeta, na cāvihitam aṅgaṃ bhavati, tasmād aṅgatvāya vidhātavyam, asminn api pakṣe. ato manyāmahe - prākaraṇikasyāyaṃ niṣedha{*3/393*} iti. tasmād tad{*3/394*} aṅgam, yad anṛtaṃ tan na vācyam iti, tena yat saṃkalpitam, tad aṅgam, tad eva kartavyam, vrīhim ayaṃ saṃkalpya na yavamayaḥ pradeyaḥ.
āha yadobhayor api pakṣayor nānṛtaṃ vaditavyam, tadā ko vicāreṇārtha iti. ucyate - pūrvasmin pakṣe puruṣadharmaḥ, tatra bhraṃśe{*3/395*} smārtaṃ prāyaścittam, siddhānte darśapūrṇamāsadharmaḥ, tatra bhraṃśe{*3/396*} yājurvedikaṃ prāyaścittam.
children.translated_text:
Or this is an injunction in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — 'one should not speak untruth' — not a restatement. Why? Because of a different connection. Through the observance of restraint, the person's connection is remembered [from <s>smṛti</s>]; here, the connection of the person is through the prohibition of the [ritual] element. How can the hearing of one thing be a restatement of another? Therefore this is an injunction — of the prohibition. [The commentator] says: we accept that it is an injunction. But we accept [it as] a property of the person, because of the hearing of the person's effort. To this we say: in all verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta</s>), the performance of action is heard, not any agent (<s>kāraka</s>). How is this understood? From the suffix — because we understand the action to be performed from the suffix.
[Objection:] But [verbal suffixes] also convey the agent. [Reply:] True, they convey [the agent], but not from the word. From what then? From the meaning — when the action is enjoined as to-be-performed, the operation of the agent is understood from the meaning. And what is understood from the meaning is not from direct statement (<s>śrauta</s>). And what is not from direct statement does not come from the sentence. How then will it override the context?
[Objection:] It is said: from the grammatical instruction of the teachers — 'the stem and suffix together express the meaning of the suffix' — it is understood that the agent and the object are the meaning of the word. The teachers prescribe: '<s>śap</s> [suffix] in the agent,' '<s>yak</s> [suffix] in the object' — thus accounting for the agent and object as meanings of the suffix. Therefore the agent and object are meanings of the word.
[Reply:] It is said: the meaning of a word does not arise from the statement of teachers or <s>sūtra</s>-makers; it is understood from the suffix. That the action, understood as to-be-performed, conveys the agents — this has been ascertained. Moreover, the teachers do not say that the agent and object are the meaning of the suffix. [Objection:] But the <s>lakāra</s> (finite verb endings) are heard 'in the agent' and 'in the object.' [Reply:] [The <s>lakāra</s>] is not heard 'in the agent' or 'in the object'; rather, [it is heard] 'in one' — singular for one, dual for two, plural for many — this is the other statement. There the correlation is made thus: 'in one agent, in two agents, in many agents.' Similarly, the correlation with oneness etc. in the object. There it is not the case that [the suffix] occurs 'in the agent' and 'in one' [separately]. Rather: singular when the agent is one — meaning oneness of the agent. Similarly for duality, plurality, and in the object. When explained thus, the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s> is explained in accordance with common reasoning. And the <s>sūtra</s>-letters conform to reasoning. And the tradition (<s>āgama</s>) too is this: when oneness etc. are the meanings of the case-endings, then the agent etc. are [merely] qualifiers.
[Objection:] But there is also this [tradition]: when the agent etc. are the meanings of the case-endings, then oneness etc. are [merely] qualifiers. [Reply:] It is said: the agent etc. are obtained from the meaning — they are not the denotata of the word. But oneness etc. are not obtained from the meaning; therefore they are the denotata of the word. Hence, oneness etc. are the qualifiers [expressed by the verbal ending]; even so, it is the qualifier alone that is denoted — just as in 'the priests proceed wearing golden garlands,' the wearing of golden garlands is a qualifier, yet it alone is being enjoined. Therefore, the oneness of the agent is the meaning of the word, not the agent [itself].
[Objection:] But the singular is because of the agent's oneness, the dual because of the agent's duality, the plural because of the agent's plurality — therefore the agent must surely be a meaning of the word. [Reply:] It is said: this cannot be [established] by inference; the agent is understood only from the cognition of the action-to-be-performed — that is direct perception, and nothing can override that for now. When a singular expression is given, oneness of the agent is understood; with a dual expression, duality of the agent; with a plural expression, plurality of the agent. That too is direct perception — which inference is capable of overriding it? Just as in a word denoting form, with a dual [form] a difference of substances is understood, with a singular [form] oneness of substance — so here too it should be viewed. Therefore [the agent] is not from direct statement; and if not from direct statement, it will not override the context.
As for the [objection] that the person's effort would be purposeless on the view that [the prohibition] is a property of the ritual, because the obligation-statement [in the verb] [already states] what is to be done — to this it is said: being a subsidiary, it would be grasped by the context. And what is not [independently] enjoined cannot be a subsidiary; therefore, it must be enjoined for the sake of subsidiarity, even on this view. Hence we hold: this is a prohibition of [an element] belonging to the context. Therefore that [truthfulness] is a subsidiary — what is untruth should not be spoken; thus whatever [offering material] has been intended, that is the subsidiary, and that alone should be performed. Having intended rice, one should not offer barley [instead].
[Objection:] It is said: since on both views untruth is not to be spoken, what is the purpose of the inquiry? [Reply:] It is said: on the first view [it is] a property of the person; there, upon violation, the expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) is from <s>smṛti</s>. On the established conclusion, [it is] a property of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; there, upon violation, the expiation is Yajurvedic.

children.text: ahīnavat puruṣas tadarthatvāt // MS_3,4.14 //
children.translated_text: Like the <s>Ahīna</s> [case], the person [is the referent], because [the statement] serves his purpose. // MS 3,4.14 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - aṅgiraso veta uttamāḥ suvargaṃ [322]{*3/397*} lokam āyante 'psu dīkṣātapasī prāveśayaṃs tīrthe snāti tīrtham eva hi sajātānāṃ bhavatīti{*3/398*}. darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnāyate, tasmāj jañjabhyamāno 'nubrūyāt. mayi dakṣakratū iti. prāṇāpānāv evātmandhatta iti{*3/399*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ayaṃ dharmaḥ prakaraṇe niviśate, uta puruṣasyopadiśyata iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? ahīnavat puruṣaḥ, tadarthatvāt. eṣa vidhiḥ prakaraṇād utkṛṣyeta. kutaḥ? puruṣaśruteḥ, brūyād iti puruṣaprayatnasya vivakṣitatvāt.
nanu prakaraṇaṃ bādhyate. ucyate - bādhyatāṃ prakaraṇam, vākyaṃ tv asya bādhakam, jañjabhyamānasaṃyogāt, prakaraṇād darśapūrṇamāsayor upadiśyata iti gamyate, vākyāj jañjabhyamānasya, vākyaṃ ca prakaraṇād balīyaḥ. tasmād utkṛṣyeteti. phalam apy āmananti, prāṇāpānāv evātmandhatta iti, sa ca saṃyogo bādhyate. tasmāt puruṣadharmaḥ, prakaraṇād utkṛṣyetāhīnavat, yathāhīnasaṃyogād{*3/400*} dvādaśopasattā prakaraṇād utkṛṣyate. evaṃ jañjabhyamānasaṃyogān mayi dakṣakratū iti vacanam.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'The <s>Aṅgirases</s> indeed, the supreme ones, went to the heavenly world; they immersed <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) and <s>tapas</s> (austerity) in the waters. He bathes at a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford), for [the ford] indeed becomes [a source of equality] for those of the same clan.' In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is prescribed: 'Therefore, stammering, he should recite after [the rite]: "In me [may] skill and power [abide]." He indeed places <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath) and <s>apāna</s> (outbreath) in himself.' There the doubt arises: does this property apply in the context, or is it taught for the person? What is the prima facie view? Like the <s>Ahīna</s> [case], [it is] for the person, because [it] serves his purpose. This injunction would be withdrawn from the context. Why? Because of the hearing of [a connection with] the person — 'he should recite' conveys the intended person's effort.
[Objection:] But the context would be overridden. [Reply:] It is said: let the context be overridden; the sentence overrides it, because of the connection with 'stammering' (<s>jañjabhyamāna</s>). From the context, it is understood as [applying] to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; from the sentence, [it applies] to one who is stammering; and the sentence is stronger than the context. Therefore it should be withdrawn. A fruit is also prescribed — 'he places <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> in himself' — and that connection [with a personal fruit] would be overridden [if it were a ritual property]. Therefore it is a property of the person; it should be withdrawn from the context, like the <s>Ahīna</s> [case] — just as the twelve <s>upasads</s> are withdrawn from the context because of the connection with the <s>Ahīna</s>. Similarly, because of the connection with 'stammering,' the statement 'In me [may] skill and power [abide]' [is withdrawn].

children.text: prakaraṇaviśeṣād vā tad yuktasya saṃskāro dravyavat // MS_3,4.15 //
children.translated_text: Or because of the specification of the context, the consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of what is connected with that [context] is like [the consecration of] the ritual substance (<s>dravya</s>). // MS 3,4.15 //

children.text:
na votkraṣṭavyam. kutaḥ? prakaraṇaviśeṣāt, prakaraṇayukta eva jañjabhyamāno vacanena saṃskriyate, yathā yavādidravyaṃ prokṣaṇā[323]{*3/401*}dinā. nanu na śaknoti prakaraṇaṃ jañjabhyamānaśabdam ekadeśe 'vasthāpayitum, vākyaṃ hi prakaraṇād balavattaram iti. ucyate - na brūmo jañjabhyamānaśabdaḥ prakaraṇenāprākaraṇikāt puruṣān nivartyata iti. kiṃ tu phalaṃ tatra kalpanīyam. nanu pratyakṣaṃ śrūyate phalam, prāṇāpānāv evātmandhatta iti. neti brūmaḥ - nātra vidhāyakaṃ śabdam upalabhāmahe, ya eṣaḥ, prāṇāpānāv evātmandhatta iti, vartamānāpadeśa eṣa na vidhāyakaḥ. stāvakas tu bhavati mantravacanasya, tasmād darśapūrṇamāsābhyām anyatraitan na phalavat. ataḥ puruṣasya darśapūrṇamāsau kurvataḥ saṃskārakarmeti gamyate.
āha puruṣasaṃskārakarmeti gṛhyate, darśapūrṇamāsāv eva kurvata ity etan na. katham? yo 'pi hy anyatra darśapūrṇamāsābhyām, jañjabhyate, so 'pi jañjabhyamānaśabdenocyata eva. na ca, prakaraṇena vyāvartyata ity etad uktam, tasmād utkṛṣyate. atrocyate - naiva vyāvartyate, saṃskṛtena tu tena nāsti prayojanam. nanu prakaraṇe puruṣasaṃskāreṇāpi nāsti prayojanam. ucyate - saṃskṛtapuruṣo darśapūrṇamāsāv anuṣṭhāsyati. āha, utkarṣe 'pi sati saṃskṛto 'nyad anuṣṭhāsyati. ucyate - nānyasya saṃskāro guṇo bhavati, aprakṛtatvāt. āha prakṛtasyāpi na guṇaḥ, vākyena puruṣadharma ity avagamāt. ucyate - ānarthakyān na puruṣadharmo 'vagamyate. tasmād asya prakṛtābhyāṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ekavākyatā, nānyena phalavatāpi karmaṇā, prakaraṇābhāvāt, tasmān notkarṣaḥ.
yat tu prakaraṇe niveśa etasmin{*3/402*} pakṣe brūyād - ity anuṣṭhānavacanam avivakṣitasvārtham iti, evaṃ sati atyanuvādo{*3/403*} bhaviṣyati, na puruṣasaṃbandhavidhānasya prayojanam astīti.
children.translated_text:
Or it should not be withdrawn. Why? Because of the specification of the context — the stammering person, being connected with the context, is consecrated by the [Vedic] statement, just as ritual substances like barley etc. [are consecrated] by sprinkling and such [rites]. [Objection:] But the context cannot restrict the word 'stammering' to a particular subset [of stammerers], for the sentence is stronger than the context. [Reply:] It is said: we do not say that the word 'stammering' is turned away from non-contextual persons by the context. Rather, a fruit would have to be supplied [if it is for the person generally]. [Objection:] But a fruit is directly heard — 'he places <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> in himself.' [Reply:] No, we say — we do not find an injunctive word here. This [statement] 'he places <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> in himself' is a present-tense description, not an injunction. But it serves as a praise of the <s>mantra</s>-utterance. Therefore, apart from the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, this [statement] does not have a fruit [attached]. Hence it is understood as a consecrating act (<s>saṃskārakarma</s>) for the person performing the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.
[Objection:] It is said: we accept that it is a consecration of the person; but that [it applies] only to one performing the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — [that] we do not [accept]. How? For even one who stammers outside the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is denoted by the word 'stammering.' And it has been stated that [the stammerer] is not turned away by the context; therefore it is withdrawn. [Reply:] To this it is said: [the stammerer] is indeed not turned away; but there is no purpose in consecrating that [non-contextual person]. [Objection:] But even in the context, there is no purpose in the personal consecration. [Reply:] It is said: the consecrated person will perform the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. [Objection:] Even on the withdrawal [view], the consecrated [person] will perform something else. [Reply:] It is said: the consecration does not become a subsidiary of another [rite], because [that rite] is not under discussion. [Objection:] Even of the [contextual rite] it is not a subsidiary, since from the sentence it is understood as a property of the person. [Reply:] It is said: a property of the person is not understood, because of purposelessness. Therefore, this [statement] has a single-sentence relationship with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> under discussion — not with any other rite, even one that has a fruit — because of the absence of context. Therefore, there is no withdrawal.
As for [the objection] that on this view — placement in the context — 'he should recite' being a statement of performance would have its own meaning not intended [and would become] a mere restatement: in that case, it would be an excessive restatement, and the injunction of the connection with the person would serve no purpose.

children.text: vyapadeśād apakṛṣyate // MS_3,4.16 //
children.translated_text: Because of the designation, [the rule] is extracted [from the context]. // MS_3,4.16 //

children.text: atha yad upavarṇitam - dvādaśopasattā yathotkṛṣyate, tathedam apy utkraṣṭavyam iti. ucyate - tad dhi vākyenāhīnānāṃ vyapadiśyate, phalavantaś cāhīnāḥ. na ca tatra jyotiṣṭome 'hīnaśabdaḥ, gauṇatvāt, vyapadeśāc ca tisra eva sāhnasyopasado dvādaśāhīnasyeti{*3/405*}. tato yuktaṃ dvādaśopasattā yat prakaraṇād utkṛṣyate. na tv iha puruṣasaṃbandho niṣprayojanatvāt, anyasya ca prayojanavataḥ prakaraṇe 'bhāvāt.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was described — that just as [the rule concerning] the twelve preparatory rites (<s>upasad</s>) is extracted [from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context], so too this should be extracted — it is said: that [rule] is designated by the sentence as [belonging to] the <s>Ahīna</s> [rites], and the <s>Ahīna</s> rites have [their own] results. And in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the word '<s>Ahīna</s>' is [used only] in a secondary sense (<s>gauṇa</s>). And because of the designation: 'three preparatory rites for a one-day [rite], twelve for an <s>Ahīna</s>' {*3/405*} — therefore it is proper that the twelve preparatory rites are extracted from the context. But here, the connection with the person is not [extracted], because of purposelessness, and because there is nothing else purposeful in the context [to replace it].

children.text: śaṃyau ca sarvaparidānāt // MS_3,4.17 //
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Śaṃyu</s> [narrative], because of the comprehensive scope [of the prohibition]. // MS_3,4.17 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - devā vai śaṃyuṃ bārhaspatyam abruvan havyaṃ no vaheti prakṛtya, vacanam idaṃ bhavati - kiṃ me prajāyā iti te 'bruvan yo brāhmaṇāyāvaguret taṃ śatena yātayād yo nihanat taṃ sahasreṇa yātayāt, yo lohitaṃ karavat yāvataḥ praskandya pāṃsūn saṃgṛhaṇāt tāvataḥ saṃvatsarān pitṛlokaṃ na prajānīyād iti. tasmān na brāhmaṇāyāvaguren na hanyān na lohitaṃ kuryād iti{*3/406*}.
tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ darśapūrṇamāsayor avagoraṇapratiṣedhaḥ, uta puruṣāsyopadiśyata iti. kiṃ prāptam? prakaraṇād darśapūrṇamāsayor avagoraṇādipratiṣedhaḥ. na darśapūrṇamāsyor brāhmaṇasyāvagoritavyaṃ vadho vā kāryo lohitaṃ vā praskandanīyam. anya upāya āsthātavya ānataye, te nānvāhāryeṇānamanti [325]{*3/407*} iti prakaraṇāt prāpnoti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - śaṃyau ca prakaraṇād utkarṣaḥ. kasmāt? sarvaparidānāt, sarvāvasthasya brāhmaṇasyāyaṃ pratiṣedha uktaḥ, na darśapūrṇamāsagatenaiva nāvagoraṇādi kartavyam iti. nanu prakaraṇād darśapūrṇamāsadharmo 'yam. satyaṃ prakaraṇāt, evaṃ vākyenāvaguramāṇasya dharmaḥ, vākyaṃ ca prakaraṇād balīyaḥ.
nanu jañjabhyamānasyeva prakaraṇe niveśo bhavet. nety ucyate, tatra phalaṃ kalpanīyam, iha kḷptam. asti hy atra vidhāyakavibhaktiḥ - śatena yātayāt, sahasreṇa yātayāt, svargaṃ lokaṃ prajānīyād iti, tasmād utkarṣa evaṃjātīyakasyeti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites it is heard: Having introduced [the narrative] — 'The gods said to <s>Śaṃyu Bārhaspatya</s>: "Carry our oblation"' — this statement follows: '"What [protection will there be] for my offspring?" They said: "Whoever reviles a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, let him be punished with a hundred; whoever kills [one], let him be punished with a thousand; whoever draws blood — for as many [handfuls of] dust as [one could gather from the spilled blood], for that many years he shall not know the world of the ancestors." Therefore, one should not revile a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, nor kill [one], nor draw blood' {*3/406*}.
There the doubt arises: is this a prohibition of reviling, etc. pertaining to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, or is it taught with reference to the person [in general]? What is the prima facie view? From the context, [it is] a prohibition of reviling, etc. pertaining to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites — [meaning:] one should not revile a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> during the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, nor commit murder, nor draw blood. Another means should be adopted for bending [opponents]: 'They do not bend by the <s>Anvāhārya</s> [offering]' [325]{*3/407*} — this would follow from the context. When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: In the <s>Śaṃyu</s> [narrative] too, there is extraction from the context. Why? Because of the comprehensive scope — this prohibition is stated for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in all circumstances, not [merely] that one connected with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> should not revile, etc. [Objection:] But from the context, this is a rule of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. [Reply:] True, from the context; but by the sentence, this is the rule for the one who [would] revile — and the sentence is stronger than the context.
[Objection:] But the [extraction] might be like someone struggling to find a place [for the rule] in the context. [Reply:] No, it is said — there [in the alternative view,] a result would have to be postulated; here it is [already] established. For here there is an injunctive verbal form: 'let him be punished with a hundred,' 'let him be punished with a thousand,' 'he shall know the heavenly world' — therefore, [rules] of this kind are to be extracted [from the ritual context and applied universally].

children.text: prāgaparodhān malavad vāsasaḥ // MS_3,4.18 //
children.translated_text: Because of the prior exclusion [of the wife], like the soiled garment. // MS_3,4.18 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - malavad vāsasā na saṃvadet, nāsyā annam adyād iti{*3/408*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ malavad vāsasā saha darśapūrṇamāsāṅgasya saṃvādasya pratiṣedhaḥ, uta puruṣasya sarvatra pratiṣedha iti. kiṃ prāptam? prakaraṇād darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ pratiṣedhavidhiḥ.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - malavad vāsasā saha saṃvāda utkṛṣyeta, prakaraṇāt. kasmāt? prāgaparodhāt. evaṃ śrūyate - yasya vratye 'hani patny anālambhukā syāt tām aparudhya yajeteti{*3/409*}. patnyā ca saha saṃvādo 'dhvaryor darśapūrṇamāsayor asti - patni patny eṣa te loka iti{*3/410*}, prasajyamānaḥ pratiṣidhyeta, sa cāprāpta [326]{*3/411*} eva prāgaparodhād apanīyatāṃ yāgam anutiṣṭhatām, kathaṃ saṃvādaḥ prasajyeta? yataḥ pratiṣedham arhet. tasmād utkṛṣyeta malavad vāsasā saha saṃvādaḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard: 'One should not converse with one wearing a soiled garment; one should not eat her food' {*3/408*}. There the doubt arises: is this a prohibition of conversation with one wearing a soiled garment pertaining to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, or is it a prohibition for the person everywhere? What is the prima facie view? From the context, [it is] a prohibition pertaining to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites.
When this prima facie view has been stated, we say: The [prohibition of] conversation with one wearing a soiled garment should be extracted from the context. Why? Because of the prior exclusion. It is heard thus: 'On the day of the vow, if the wife is in her impure period, having excluded her, one should sacrifice' {*3/409*}. And there is conversation with the wife in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>: '<s>Patni</s>, O wife, this is your world' {*3/410*} — this [conversation] would be the one being prohibited [if the prohibition applied to the ritual context]. But she has [already] been removed [326]{*3/411*} by the prior exclusion — let her be removed from the sacrifice and let the sacrifice continue. How then would the conversation arise, such that it would deserve a prohibition? Therefore, the [prohibition of] conversation with one wearing a soiled garment should be extracted [from the ritual context and applied universally].

children.text: annapratiṣedhāc ca // MS_3,4.19 //
children.translated_text: And because of the prohibition of food. // MS_3,4.19 //

children.text: annapratiṣedhaś ca bhavati - nāsyā annam adyād abhyañjanaṃ vai striyā annam ity{*3/412*} upagamanapratiṣedha eṣa{*3/413*} vidhīyate, sa ca prakaraṇe na prasakta iti, prakaraṇād utkṛṣṭaḥ puruṣadharma eṣa niścīyate.
children.translated_text: There is also a prohibition of food — 'one should not eat her food; ointment is the food of a woman' {*3/412*} — this is really a prohibition of approaching [her sexually] {*3/413*}. And that [prohibition of approaching] does not apply in the ritual context — therefore, having been extracted from the context, this is determined to be a property of the person.

children.text: aprakaraṇe tu taddharmas tato viśeṣāt // MS_3,4.20 //
children.translated_text: But when not [stated] in a [specific ritual] context, [the rule] is a property of that [thing described], because of the specificity [of the statement]. // MS_3,4.20 //

children.text: anārabhya śrūyate - tasmāt suvarṇaṃ hiraṇyaṃ bhāryaṃ durvarṇo 'sya bhrātṛvyo bhavatīti{*3/414*}. suvāsasā bhavitavyaṃ rūpam eva bibhartīti. tatra kiṃ prakaraṇadharma uta puruṣadharma iti saṃśayaḥ. atrocyate - aprakaraṇe tu tad dharmaḥ, tato viśeṣāt, puruṣadharma evaṃjātīyakaḥ syāt. kutaḥ? tataḥ prakaraṇādhītād{*3/415*} viśeṣo 'sya, nāyaṃ prakaraṇādhītaḥ. yady aprakaraṇe samāmnātaḥ, sarvaprakaraṇadharmaḥ syāt. aprakaraṇe samāmnānaṃ na kaṃcid viśeṣaṃ kuryāt. tasmād evaṃjātīyakaḥ puruṣadharma iti.
children.translated_text: Without reference to [a specific rite], it is heard: 'Therefore, [one should wear] gold; gold [that is] to be worn — [otherwise] his rival becomes ugly' {*3/414*}. 'One should wear fine garments; [for] it supports one's form.' There the doubt arises: is this a property of the ritual context, or a property of the person? To this it is said: When not [stated] in a [specific ritual] context, this is a property of that [person], because of specificity — [rules] of this kind would be properties of the person. Why? Because of the specificity [distinguishing this] from what is learned from a [ritual] context {*3/415*} — this [statement] is not learned from [within] a [ritual] context. If it were recorded outside of any context, it would be a property of all [ritual] contexts. But being recorded outside a context does not create any specificity [toward a particular rite]. Therefore, [rules] of this kind are properties of the person.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/414: Tait.Br. 2.2.4.6}*
*{3/415: E1 gibt prakaraṇādhītād in Klammern}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
*{3/414: <s>Tait.Br.</s> 2.2.4.6}*
*{3/415: E1 gives <s>prakaraṇādhītād</s> in brackets}*

children.text: adravyatvāt tu śeṣaḥ syāt // MS_3,4.21 //
children.translated_text: But because of the absence of a [ritual] substance, [the rule] should be subsidiary [to the rites]. // MS_3,4.21 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttau. na puruṣadharmo bhavet, agnihotrādīnāṃ śeṣaḥ syāt. kasmāt? adravyatvāt, nātra dravyadevataṃ śrūyate, yac{*3/416*} chravaṇāt, bhāryaṃ yaṣṭavyam iti parikalpyeta. asati tu dravyadevatāsaṃbandhe vibhartir ayaṃ dhāraṇāvacanaḥ saṃskāravācī, [327]{*3/417*} saṃskāraś ca śeṣabhūtasyāvakalpate nānyathā, tasmāt karmaṇām agnihotrādīnāṃ śeṣaḥ. evaṃ suvāsasā bhavitavyam iti.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates a shift of position. [The rule] would not be a property of the person; it should be a subsidiary of <s>Agnihotra</s> and other [rites]. Why? Because of the absence of a [ritual] substance — here, no substance or deity is heard {*3/416*}, [so that] one could construe, from the hearing [of those elements], 'gold should be offered.' But in the absence of a connection with substance and deity, this word '<s>bibharti</s>' (he bears) — meaning 'holding' — denotes a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) [327]{*3/417*}. And a consecration is proper [only] for what is subsidiary [to a rite], not otherwise. Therefore, [the rule] is a subsidiary of rites such as <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like. Similarly with 'one should wear fine garments.'

children.text: vedasaṃyogāt // MS_3,4.22 //
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with the <s>Veda</s>. // MS_3,4.22 //

children.text: ādhvaryavam iti vedasaṃyogaḥ śeṣabhūtasya yujyate, śeṣabhūto hy adhvaryuṇā kriyate, na puruṣadharmaḥ, darśapūrṇamāsādīnāṃ hi karmaṇāṃ sāṅgānām aṅgānām ardhvayuḥ kartā. tasmād api karmadharmā evaṃjātīyakā iti.
children.translated_text: The [designation] '<s>ādhvaryava</s>' (belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>) — the connection with the <s>Veda</s> is appropriate for what is subsidiary [to rites]. For what is subsidiary is performed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. It is not a property of the person — for the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is the performer of the rites <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like, together with their subsidiary elements. Therefore, [rules] of this kind are properties of the ritual.

children.text: dravyasaṃyogāc ca // MS_3,4.23 //
children.translated_text: And because of the connection with [ritual] substance. // MS_3,4.23 //

children.text: dravyaparaś cātra bhavati nirdeśaḥ - suvarṇaṃ bhāryam iti dvitīyārthasaṃyogāt. dravyasaṃskāraś ca karmaśeṣapakṣe prayojanavān, anarthakaḥ puruṣadharme.
children.translated_text: The instruction here is also directed toward a substance — 'gold [that is] to be worn' — because of the connection with a second [i.e., accusative] case meaning. And the consecration of a substance is purposeful on the view that [the rule] is subsidiary to the ritual; [it would be] purposeless if [the rule were] a property of the person.

children.text: syād vāsya saṃyogavat phalena saṃbandhas tasmāt karmaitiśāyanaḥ // MS_3,4.24 //
children.translated_text: Or, [the rule] might have a connection with the result, like [one having] a connection [with a rite]; therefore, [according to] <s>Aitiśāyana</s>, [it pertains to] the ritual. // MS_3,4.24 //

children.text:
syād vā phalenaivaṃjātīyakānāṃ saṃbandhaḥ puruṣadharma ity arthaḥ, suvarṇasya vāsaso vā dharmo bhavan niṣprayojanaḥ syāt. nanu saṃskṛtena suvarṇena vāsasā ca karma setsyati. naitad evam, suvarṇasyāṅgaṃ na karmaṇa upakuryāt. śrutyādīnām abhāvān na karmāṅgam. tasmāt durvarṇo 'sya bhātṛvyo bhavatītyevamādinā evaṃjātīyakānāṃ phalena saṃbandhaḥ.
nanu vartamānāpadeśo 'yam. satyam evam etat, ānarthakyaparihārāya phalacodanayā saṃbandha eṣi-tavyo bhavati. anyasmāc caiṣitavyād ekavākyagatasya vipariṇāmo{*3/418*} laghīyān. kutaḥ? [328]{*3/419*} pratyakṣā tenaikavākyatā, parokṣānyena, vipariṇāmaś ca vartamānakālasyāvivakṣā, saṃbandhasya ca tātparyādhyavasānam. tasmād evaṃjātīyakaḥ pradhānakarmopadeśaḥ syāt, yathā prajāpativratānāṃ phalena saṃbandhaḥ. etāvatā hainasāviyukto bhavatīti. evam atrāpi draṣṭavyam. tasmād evaṃjātīyakaḥ puruṣadharma iti.
children.translated_text:
Or perhaps [rules] of this kind have a connection with the result [and are thus] properties of the person — this is the meaning. [The rule about] gold or garments, being a property [of these things, would be] purposeless. [Objection:] But the ritual will succeed with consecrated gold and garments. [Reply:] This is not so — gold as a subsidiary element would not assist the ritual. Because of the absence of direct statement and the like, it is not a subsidiary of the ritual. Therefore, 'his rival becomes ugly' and similar [statements] indicate that [rules] of this kind have a connection with the result.
[Objection:] But this is a statement about the present [state of affairs]. [Reply:] True, this is so; but to avoid purposelessness, a connection with a result-injunction must be sought. And the easier [interpretation is] the transformation of what is within the same sentence, [which is easier than seeking connection] with something else from which [the connection] must be sought {*3/418*}. Why? [328]{*3/419*} Because the sentence-unity with that [result-statement] is directly perceptible, while [the sentence-unity] with the other is not directly perceptible. And the 'transformation' is the non-intention of the present tense and the determination of the purport as [expressing] the connection. Therefore, [rules] of this kind would be instructions pertaining to the principal ritual — just as the <s>Prajāpati</s>-vows have a connection with the result: 'By this much, he becomes freed from evil' — this is how it should be viewed here too. Therefore, [rules] of this kind are properties of the person.

children.text: śeṣo 'prakaraṇe 'viśeṣāt sarvakarmaṇām // MS_3,4.25 //
children.translated_text: [Rules] that are subsidiary [apply], when not in a [specific ritual] context, to all rites because of the absence of specificity. // MS_3,4.25 //

children.text: iha karmasaṃyuktā homā jayādaya udāharaṇam. yena karmaṇetsat{*3/420*}, tatra jayāñ juhuyāt, rāṣṭrabhṛto juhotīti, abhyātānāñ juhotīti{*3/421*}. tatraite kiṃ sarvakarmaṇāṃ kṛṣyādīnāṃ śeṣabhūtāḥ, uta vaidikānām agnihotrādinām iti. śeṣatvaṃ tu nirjñātakarmasaṃbandhāt, phalāśravaṇāc ca. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sarvakarmaṇāṃ śeṣāḥ, viśeṣān abhidhānād iti.
children.translated_text: Here, oblations connected with rites — the <s>Jaya</s> and similar [offerings] — are the example. [The text says:] 'Into whatever rite one enters {*3/420*}, there one should offer the <s>Jaya</s> [oblations]'; 'he offers the <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> [oblations]'; 'he offers the <s>Abhyātāna</s> [oblations]' {*3/421*}. There, are these subsidiary to all rites including agricultural [activities] and the like, or [only] to Vedic [rites] such as <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like? The subsidiary status [is inferred] from the ascertained connection with ritual, and because no result is heard. What is the prima facie view? They are subsidiary to all rites, because no specification is stated.

children.text:

children.text: homās tu vyatiṣṭheran nāhavanīyasaṃyogāt // MS_3,4.26 //
children.translated_text: But the oblations would be restricted [to Vedic rites], because of the connection with the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]. // MS_3,4.26 //

children.text: na caitad asti - sarvakarmaṇāṃ karṣaṇādīnām apy aṅgabhūtā iti. homā ete, ato vyavatiṣṭheran, āhavanīyasaṃyogo bhavati homeṣu. yadāhavanīye juhoti tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prīto bhavatīti{*3/422*}. tena yasyāhavanīyaḥ, tasyaite 'ṅgam. na [329]{*3/423*} ca kṛṣyādīny āhavanīye vartante. na caiṣāṃ gārhapatyo 'sti, yataḥ praṇīta āhavanīyaḥ syāt. tasmān na karmaṇādīnāṃ jayādayaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that they are subsidiary to all rites including agricultural activities and the like. These are oblations (<s>homa</s>); therefore they would be restricted [to Vedic rites], because the connection with the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] pertains to oblations. When one offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, [the deity] becomes satisfied [and] favorably disposed {*3/422*}. Therefore, these are subsidiary to whatever [rite] has an <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]. [329]{*3/423*} And agricultural activities and the like do not involve the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. Nor do they have a <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] from which an <s>Āhavanīya</s> could be derived. Therefore, the <s>Jaya</s> and similar [oblations] do not [belong to] agricultural and similar activities.

children.text: śeṣaś ca samākhyānāt // MS_3,4.27 //
children.translated_text: And [they are] subsidiary, because of the designation. // MS_3,4.27 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmo vaidikānāṃ śeṣabhūtā iti. kutaḥ? sāmakhyānāt, ādhvaryavam iti hi samākhyāte vede jayādayaḥ samāmnātāḥ santo 'dhvaryuṇā kariṣyante. karṣaṇādiṣv adhvaryor abhāvād anadhvaryuṇāpi kriyamāṇāḥ samākhyāṃ bādheran, tasmād vaidikānāṃ śeṣabhūtā iti.
children.translated_text: From this too we see that they are subsidiary to Vedic [rites]. Why? Because of the designation — for the <s>Jaya</s> and similar [oblations], being recorded in the <s>Veda</s> designated as '<s>ādhvaryava</s>' (belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), will be performed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. Since the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is absent in agricultural and similar activities, [these oblations], even if performed by a non-<s>Adhvaryu</s>, would contradict the designation. Therefore, they are subsidiary to Vedic [rites].

children.text: doṣāt tviṣṭir laukike syāc chāstrād dhi vaidike na doṣaḥ syāt // MS_3,4.28 //
children.translated_text: Because of the defect, the [prohibited rite] would be a worldly [impropriety]; but because of the scriptural [context], in a Vedic [rite] there would be no defect. // MS_3,4.28 //

children.text:
asty aśvapratigraheṣṭiḥ - varuṇo vā etaṃ gṛhṇāti, yo 'śvaṃ pratigṛhṇāti, yāvato 'śvān pratigṛhṇīyāt, tāvato vāruṇāṃś catuṣkapālān nirvaped iti{*3/424*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ laukike 'śvapratigraha iṣṭiḥ, atha vaidika iti. kaḥ punar laukiko 'śvapratigrahaḥ? ko vā vaidika iti. loke bhikṣamāṇo vābhikṣamāṇo vā yatrāśvaṃ labhate, tatra laukikāśvapratigrahaḥ. vaidiko 'pi pauṇḍarīke 'śvasahasraṃ dakṣiṇā jyotiṣṭome gauś cāśvaś ceti.
tatrocyate - vaidikatvasāmānyād vaidika iti prāpte. [330]{*3/425*} ucyate - doṣāt tviṣṭir laukike syāt. doṣo hi śrūyate - varuṇo vā etaṃ gṛhṇāti yo 'śvaṃ pratigṛhṇātīti, sa cāyam anuvādo yatra doṣaḥ, tatreti, sa ca laukike 'śvapratigrahe śūdrād anyasmād vā pāpakarmaṇaḥ kṛto bhavatīty upapadyate. doṣasaṃyogāl laukika iti gamyate. āha na doṣasaṃkīrtanaṃ prāyaścittaviṣayaviśeṣaṇam, kiṃ tu prāyaścitta-stutyarthena. ucyate - doṣanirdhātārthe saty evaṃ syāt, varuṇapramocanam idaṃ karma, tal laukike bhavitum arhati, loke varuṇagrahaṇasya vidyamānatvāt. vaidike tv aśvapratigrahe tan na syāt, śāstrād dhi vacanena{*3/426*} tasya kartavyatāvagamyate. yadi ca tataḥ pāpaṃ syāt, na tasya kartavyatāvagamyeta, akartavyaṃ hi pāpaphalam.
nanu vaidike 'pi pratigrahe 'pratigrāhyāt pratigṛhṇataḥ pāpam asti. ucyate - bhaved evam, yadi pratigrahasya kartur iṣṭir bhavet, sā tu khalu yathā hetukartuḥ, tathottarādhikaraṇe vakṣyāmaḥ. tasmān na vedacodite 'śvapratigrahe, iṣṭir ity etāvad ihādhikaraṇe siddham.
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>aśvapratigraheṣṭi</s> (sacrifice for receiving a horse): '<s>Varuṇa</s> indeed seizes him who receives a horse. For as many horses as one receives, one should prepare that many <s>Vāruṇa</s> (offering to <s>Varuṇa</s>) four-kapāla [rice-cakes].' There the doubt arises: does the sacrifice [apply] upon a worldly reception of a horse, or a Vedic one? What is a worldly reception of a horse? And what is a Vedic one? In the world, whether begging or not begging, wherever one obtains a horse — that is a worldly reception of a horse. A Vedic [reception] is also [found in the] <s>Pauṇḍarīka</s> [rite] where a thousand horses are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, and in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> where 'a cow and a horse' [are given].
To this it is said: the prima facie view being that [the sacrifice applies to] a Vedic [reception], because of the commonality of being Vedic — it is said: because of the fault (<s>doṣa</s>), however, the sacrifice should apply to a worldly [reception]. For a fault is heard — '<s>Varuṇa</s> indeed seizes him who receives a horse.' This is a restatement [indicating that] where there is a fault, [the sacrifice applies] there. And that [fault] is applicable in a worldly reception of a horse — [namely,] when done from a <s>śūdra</s> or from another person of evil deeds. Because of the connection with a fault, it is understood as worldly. [Objection:] It is said: the mention of the fault does not qualify the subject of the expiation; rather, it serves the purpose of praising the expiation. [Reply:] It is said: that would be so if [the purpose were merely] the removal of a fault. This rite is the release from <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [grasp]; it is appropriate for the worldly [context], because <s>Varuṇa</s>'s seizure exists in the world. But in a Vedic reception of a horse, there should not be [such a fault], for the obligation is understood from the scripture by [its] statement. And if sin resulted from that, the obligation would not be understood — for what yields sin is not to be done.
[Objection:] But even in a Vedic reception, when one receives from one from whom one should not receive, there is sin. [Reply:] It is said: that would be so if the sacrifice were for the performer of the reception. But as to whether it is [for] the causal agent — we will discuss that in the following topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). Therefore, [the sacrifice] is not [required] for a Vedic reception of a horse — this much is established in this topic.

children.text: arthavādo 'vānupapātāt tasmād yajñe pratīyeta // MS_3,4.29 //
children.translated_text: Or [this is] an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), because of the inapplicability [of the literal meaning]; therefore [the sacrifice] should be understood as [relating to] a [Vedic] sacrifice. // MS 3,4.29 //

children.text:
na caitad asti, yad uktam - yaḥ śūdrād anyasmād vā pāpakṛto loke 'śvaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt sa etām iṣṭiṃ nirvapet. sa hi varuṇagṛhīta ity ucyate, jalodareṇa yo gṛhītaḥ, yasyodaraṃ jalavṛddhyā śvayati. jalodaram ity eva loke tat prasiddham. na ca tasyāśvapratigraho laukiko nidānam iti prati[331]{*3/427*}jñāyate. na cānena vidhīyate. tasmān nāśvapratigrahāj jalodaropapātaḥ.
atha pāpaṃ varuṇaśabdenocyate, vṛṇīta ity eṣo 'bhiprāya iti. tadā prasiddhau tyaktāyāṃ kleśamātram, vṛṇvad varuṇaśabdenocyate, tatra yājñe 'pi pratigrahe varuṇagṛhītaḥ syāt, rakṣaṇapoṣaṇavicikitsādinā kleśena naiṣa pakṣo vyavatiṣṭheta - laukike 'śvapratigraha iti, prasiddhiś ca bādhyeta. tasmād arthavāda eṣaḥ, yāvad{*3/428*} varuṇagṛhītasya varuṇonmocane śreyaḥ, tāvad etety upamānenaiṣā stutiḥ. yo 'sya pratigrahaḥ, tad varuṇagrahaṇam iva, yeṣṭiḥ, sā tad unmocanīva, yathā varuṇagṛhītenonmocanam avaśyakartavyam, tādṛg evaitad iti, tasmād yajñe pratīyeta. laukike hi phalaṃ kalpanīyam, vaidike yasminn aśvapratigrahaḥ, tasyāṅgabhūtā bhaviṣyati. tatra prayogavacanena sahaikavākyatā saṃbandhād avakalpyamānā, parokṣāyāḥ phalavacanena sahaikavākyatāyā laghīyasīti yuktam iṣṭir vaidike dāna iti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — what was said, that one who receives a horse from a <s>śūdra</s> or from another evildoer in the world should perform this sacrifice. For he is said to be seized by <s>Varuṇa</s> — [meaning] one seized by dropsy (<s>jalodara</s>), one whose belly swells with water. That is well-known in the world as 'dropsy.' But it is not accepted that a worldly reception of a horse is the cause of dropsy. Nor is [dropsy] enjoined by this [Vedic text]. Therefore, dropsy does not result from receiving a horse.
Alternatively, if sin is denoted by the word '<s>Varuṇa</s>' — with the idea that [<s>Varuṇa</s>] 'chooses' (<s>vṛṇīte</s>) — then, having abandoned the well-known meaning, [there would be] mere trouble; [and if] what is troublesome is denoted by the word '<s>Varuṇa</s>,' then even in a Vedic reception [of a horse], one would be seized by <s>Varuṇa</s> — through the trouble of protection, feeding, medical treatment, and so forth. This view — that [the sacrifice applies to] a worldly reception of a horse — would not stand; and the well-known meaning would be overridden. Therefore, this is an explanatory passage. Just as the release from <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [grasp] is beneficial for one seized by <s>Varuṇa</s>, so is this [sacrifice] — this is a praise by analogy. His reception [of the horse] is like <s>Varuṇa</s>'s seizure; the sacrifice is like the release from it. Just as release is necessarily performed for one seized by <s>Varuṇa</s>, so is this [sacrifice]. Therefore [the sacrifice] should be understood as [relating to] a [Vedic] sacrifice. For in a worldly [context], a fruit would have to be supplied; in a Vedic [context], where horse-reception exists, [the sacrifice] will be a subsidiary of that [rite]. There, the single-sentence relationship with the performance-statement being construable through connection is simpler than the single-sentence relationship with a hypothetical fruit-statement. Therefore it is proper that the sacrifice is for a Vedic gift.

children.text: acoditaṃ ca karmabhedāt // MS_3,4.30 //
children.translated_text: And [the sacrifice] is for the unenjoyned [agent], because of the difference of actions. // MS 3,4.30 //

children.text: yāvato 'śvān pratigṛṇīyāt, tāvato vāruṇāṃś catuṣkapālān nirvaped iti{*3/429*}. tatraitat samadhigatam - vaidike 'śvapratigraha iṣṭir iti. athedānīṃ saṃdihyate - kiṃ pratigrahakartrā kartavyā, yasmai dīyate, uta hetukartrā, yo dadātīti. kiṃ prāptam? acoditaṃ ca karmabhedāt, na dānasya kartur iṣṭiś codyate, pratigrhakartus tām avagacchāmaḥ - yāvato 'śvān [332]{*3/430*} pratigṛhṇīyāt tāvataś catuṣkapālān vāruṇān nirvaped iti, tasmāt pratigrahītrartvijā kartavyeti.
children.translated_text: 'For as many horses as one receives, one should prepare that many <s>Vāruṇa</s> four-kapāla [rice-cakes].' There it has been ascertained that the sacrifice is for a Vedic reception of a horse. Now the doubt arises: should it be performed by the agent of the reception — [i.e.,] the one to whom [the horse] is given — or by the causal agent — [i.e.,] the one who gives? What is the prima facie view? [The sacrifice is] for the unenjoyned [agent], because of the difference of actions — the sacrifice is not enjoined for the agent of the giving, but we understand it for the agent of the reception: 'for as many horses as one receives, one should prepare that many four-kapāla <s>Vāruṇa</s> [rice-cakes].' Therefore it should be performed by the <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest) who receives.

children.text: sā liṅgād ārtvije syāt // MS_3,4.31 //
children.translated_text: Because of the indicatory mark, [the sacrifice] should be for the priestly function (<s>ārtivijya</s>). // MS 3,4.31 //

children.text:
naiṣā pratigrahakartuḥ, kiṃ tarhi hetukartuḥ syāt. kutaḥ? liṅgāt. kiṃ liṅgam? pūrvapadānām uttaraiḥ padair yathārtham abhisaṃbandhaḥ. idaṃ śrūyate - prajāpatir varuṇāyāśvam anyad iti{*3/431*}, prajāpatir aśvasya dātā kīrtitaḥ, varuṇaḥ pratigrahītā, sa svāṃ devatām ārcchad iti. sa iti sāpekṣaṃ pūrvaprakṛtaṃ vākyaśeṣam apekṣate, sa iti prajāpatiṃ pratinirdiśatīti tena sahaikyavākyatāṃ yāti. sāmānādhikaraṇyāc ca prajāpater eva pratinirdeśo 'vakalpate, na tu varuṇasya, vaiyadhikaraṇyāt. sa paryadīryata ity eṣo 'pi prajāpatim eva pratinirdiśati pūrvaprakṛtam, tena ca sahaikavākyatāṃ yāti. sa evaitaṃ vāruṇaṃ catuṣkapālam apaśyad iti prajāpatir eveti, niravapat{*3/432*} prajāpatir eveti, tato vai sa varuṇapāśād amucyata prajāpatiḥ. varuṇa etaṃ{*3/433*} gṛhṇātīti hetvapadeśo 'yam, yasmād eva prajāpatir varuṇāyāśvaṃ dattvā paridīrṇaḥ, tasmād yo 'śvaṃ prati gṛhṇāti prayacchati{*3/434*} taṃ varuṇo gṛhṇāti, sa paridīryata iti. yatas tu vāruṇena pratimuktaḥ, tasmād anyenāpy aśvaṃ prayacchatā vāruṇo nirvaptavya ity aśvasya dātur vāruṇīṣṭiḥ praśasyate, kartavyānenākhyātena. tasmād aśvaṃ dattvā vāruṇīm iṣṭiṃ nirvaped iti.
āha, nanu yo 'svaṃ pratigṛhṇāti sa nirvaped ity ucyate. evaṃ saty anyathopakrānte vākye 'nyathopasaṃhṛta upakramo 'py anarthakaḥ syāt, upasaṃhāro 'pi. tasmād upakrame vā śabdārtha upasaṃhāravaśena kalpanīyaḥ, upasaṃhāre vopakramavaśena. tatra [333]{*3/435*} prajāpatir varuṇāyāśvam anayad iti, varuṇād aśvaṃ pratyagṛhṇād ity upasaṃhārānurodhena kalpyeta, yad vopakramavaśenopasaṃhāram, yo 'śvaṃ pratigṛhṇātīti, yo 'śvaṃ pratigrāhayatīti. tatra - mukhyaṃ vā pūrvaṃ codanāl lokavad iti{*3/436*} prathamam anugrahītavyaṃ virodhābhāvāt. paścāt tanaṃ tu virodhāl lakṣaṇayā kalpanīyam.
api ca, prajāpatir varuṇāyāśvam anayad iti varuṇād aśvaṃ pratyagṛhṇād iti bahvasamañjasaṃ kalpayitavyam. pratigṛhṇātīty eṣa śabdaḥ, pratigrāhayatīty etam arthaṃ śaknoti yayā kayācic chaktyā vaktum, yo hi tad ācarati, yena ca{*3/437*} kriyā praṇāḍyāpi sidhyati, sa tasyāḥ kriyāyāḥ karteti śakyate vaditum, yathā ṣaḍbhir halaiḥ karṣatīti saṃvidhānaṃ kurvan vilekhanam akurvann apy ucyate, tatsamartham ācaratīti. evam ihāpi sa pratigrahasamartham ācarati yo dadāti{*3/438*}. tasmād dadat pratigṛhṇātīti śakyate vaditum. tasmād adhyavadhāryedam avakḷptam. dadat pratigṛhṇātīty ucyate, tasya ca vāruṇīṣṭir iti.
children.translated_text:
This [sacrifice] is not for the agent of the reception; rather, it should be for the causal agent. Why? Because of the indicatory mark. What is the indicatory mark? The proper correlation of the earlier words with the later words. This is heard: '<s>Prajāpati</s> brought a horse to <s>Varuṇa</s> as a gift.' <s>Prajāpati</s> is mentioned as the giver of the horse; <s>Varuṇa</s> is the receiver. 'He went to his own deity' — the word 'he' (<s>sa</s>) is relative, expecting the sentence-remainder that was stated earlier; 'he' refers back to <s>Prajāpati</s>, and enters into a single-sentence relationship with [what follows]. And because of co-reference, the reference can only be construed as [being to] <s>Prajāpati</s>, not to <s>Varuṇa</s>, because of the non-co-reference [with <s>Varuṇa</s>]. 'He was torn asunder' — this too refers back to <s>Prajāpati</s> who was stated earlier and enters into a single-sentence relationship with [what follows]. 'He indeed saw this <s>Vāruṇa</s> four-kapāla [rice-cake]' — it was <s>Prajāpati</s>. 'He prepared [it]' — it was <s>Prajāpati</s>. 'From that, he was freed from <s>Varuṇa</s>'s noose' — it was <s>Prajāpati</s>. '<s>Varuṇa</s> seizes him' — this is a statement of the reason: because <s>Prajāpati</s>, having given the horse to <s>Varuṇa</s>, was torn asunder, therefore whoever receives — [that is,] gives — a horse, <s>Varuṇa</s> seizes him; he is torn asunder. But because [<s>Prajāpati</s>] was released through the <s>Vāruṇa</s> [offering], therefore anyone else giving a horse should also prepare the <s>Vāruṇa</s> [offering] — thus the <s>Vāruṇa</s> sacrifice is recommended for the giver of the horse, by [the word] 'should prepare' (<s>nirvapet</s>) in the finite verb. Therefore, having given a horse, one should prepare the <s>Vāruṇa</s> sacrifice.
[Objection:] It is said: but 'whoever receives a horse, he should prepare' is what is stated. [Reply:] In that case, the sentence having begun one way and concluded another way, both the beginning and the conclusion would be purposeless. Therefore, the meaning of the words must be construed either in the beginning in accordance with the conclusion, or in the conclusion in accordance with the beginning. Thus, '<s>Prajāpati</s> brought a horse to <s>Varuṇa</s>' should be construed as '<s>Prajāpati</s> received a horse from <s>Varuṇa</s>' — in accordance with the conclusion. Or alternatively, the conclusion should be [construed] in accordance with the beginning: 'whoever receives a horse' as 'whoever causes [a horse] to be received' [i.e., gives]. There, the principle is: 'The primary [meaning] should be upheld first, because of the injunction, as in worldly [usage]' — the first [reading] should be upheld because of the absence of contradiction. The later, more slender [reading] should be construed through secondary designation because of contradiction.
Moreover, to construe '<s>Prajāpati</s> brought a horse to <s>Varuṇa</s>' as '<s>Prajāpati</s> received a horse from <s>Varuṇa</s>' would require much incongruity. The word '<s>pratigṛhṇāti</s>' (receives) can, by some capacity, express the meaning 'causes to be received' (<s>pratigrāhayati</s>). For one who performs that activity, and one through whom the action is accomplished even indirectly, can be called the agent of that action — just as 'he ploughs with six ploughs' is said of one who arranges [the ploughing] even without himself tilling, because he performs what is capable of [bringing about the] ploughing. Similarly here too, one performs what is capable of [bringing about the] reception — [namely,] one who gives. Therefore, the giver can be said to 'receive.' Therefore this is to be firmly established: the giver is said to 'receive,' and the <s>Vāruṇa</s> sacrifice is for him.

children.text: pānavyāpac ca tadvat // MS_3,4.32 //
children.translated_text: And the mishap of [<s>Soma</s>-]drinking is similar. // MS 3,4.32 //

children.text: idaṃ samāmananti - somendraṃ caruṃ nirvapec chyāmākaṃ somavāmina iti{*3/439*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - laukikasya somapānasya vamane saumendraś{*3/440*} caruḥ, uta vaidikasyeti. kiṃ laukikaṃ somapānam? kiṃ ca vaidikam? ucyate - vaidikaṃ somapānaṃ jyotiṣṭome tadvikṛtiṣu ca, laukikaṃ somapānaṃ yat saptarātreṣu [334]{*3/441*} daśarātreṣu dhātusāmyārtham{*3/442*} āsevyamāne some. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? pānavyāpac ca tadvat, laukike vamana iṣṭir bhavitum arhati, na vaidike, tadvad iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ pratinirdiṣṭaḥ, yathā tatra doṣasaṃyogena śravaṇāt, laukike 'śvapratigraha ity uktam, evam ihāpi doṣasaṃyogena śravaṇaṃ bhavati, indriyeṇa vā eṣa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyate yaḥ somaṃ pibatīti{*3/443*} loke dhātusāmyārtham āsevite vamanena vinaṣte dhātusāmyavyāpadā, indriyeṇa vyṛddhir upapadyate, śās-trād dhi vaidike na doṣaḥ syāt. tatra śeṣaḥ pātavya iti śabdāc codite nirvṛtte nāsti doṣaḥ. yady api vamyate, tathāpi pānakriyā tatra nirvartitā, kṛto vacanārtha iti na doṣaḥ syāt. tasmāl laukikasya somapānasya vyāpadi saumendraḥ{*3/444*} syāt.
children.translated_text: This is prescribed: 'One should prepare a <s>Saumendra</s> (offering to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Indra</s>) <s>caru</s> of <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) [for one who has] vomited <s>Soma</s>.' There the doubt arises: is the <s>Saumendra</s> <s>caru</s> for the vomiting of worldly <s>Soma</s>-drinking, or of Vedic [<s>Soma</s>-drinking]? What is worldly <s>Soma</s>-drinking? And what is Vedic? It is said: Vedic <s>Soma</s>-drinking is in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and its modifications. Worldly <s>Soma</s>-drinking is when <s>Soma</s> is consumed during seven-day or ten-day [courses] for the purpose of balancing the bodily humors (<s>dhātusāmya</s>). What is the prima facie view? The mishap of drinking is similar [to the horse-reception case]. The sacrifice should be for a worldly case of vomiting, not for a Vedic one — 'similarly' refers back to the previous prima facie view. Just as there, because of hearing a connection with a fault, it was said [that it applies to] a worldly reception of a horse, so here too there is hearing of a connection with a fault — 'he indeed is deprived of his vigor and strength who drinks <s>Soma</s>.' In the world, when [<s>Soma</s>] consumed for the purpose of balancing the humors is destroyed by vomiting, the disorder of the humors applies — [and then] the deprivation of vigor is applicable. But in a Vedic [context], from the scripture, there should be no fault. There, 'the remainder should be drunk' — when [the rite] is completed by the [Vedic] injunction, there is no fault. Even if [the <s>Soma</s>] is vomited, the act of drinking has been completed there — the purpose of the [Vedic] statement has been fulfilled — so there should be no fault. Therefore, the <s>Saumendra</s> [offering] should be for the mishap of worldly <s>Soma</s>-drinking.

children.text: doṣāt tu vaidike syād arthād dhi laukike na doṣaḥ syāt // MS_3,4.33 //
children.translated_text: Because of the fault, [the sacrifice] should be for a Vedic [context]; for in a worldly [context], by the nature of things, there would be no fault. // MS 3,4.33 //

children.text: vaidikasya pānasya vyāpadi bhavitum arhati, na laukikasya. kasmāt? doṣāt, doṣasaṃbandho 'tra śrūyate - indriyeṇa vā eṣa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyata iti. laukike punar dhātusāmyādyarthaṃ kriyamāṇe na kiṃcid duṣyati, vamanāyaiva hi taṃ pibanti loke. athāpy ayam arthavādaḥ, tathāpi phalakalpanāparīhārāya vaidika eveti kalpanā nyāyyā.
children.translated_text: It should be [applicable] upon the mishap of Vedic drinking, not worldly. Why? Because of the fault — a connection with a fault is heard here: 'he indeed is deprived of his vigor and strength.' But in a worldly [context], when [<s>Soma</s> is] consumed for the purpose of balancing the humors and such, nothing is damaged — for they drink it in the world precisely for the sake of vomiting. And even if this is an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), still, the construal that [the sacrifice applies] to a Vedic [context] is proper — for the sake of avoiding the need to supply a fruit.

children.text: tat sarvatrāviśeṣāt // MS_3,4.34 //
children.translated_text: That [sacrifice] should apply everywhere, because of the lack of differentiation. // MS 3,4.34 //

children.text: tad etat somapānavyāpadi saumendraṃ{*3/445*} karma, sarvatra vamane syāt, ārtvije yājamāne ca. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, na viśeṣaḥ [335]{*3/446*} kaścid āśrīyate 'sya vamane syāt, nāsyeti, tasmāt sarvatra bhavet.
children.translated_text: This <s>Saumendra</s> rite, upon the mishap of <s>Soma</s>-drinking, should apply to vomiting everywhere — both for the priestly function (<s>ārtivijya</s>) and for the sacrificer (<s>yājamāna</s>). Why? Because of the lack of differentiation — no differentiation is relied upon as to 'for this one's vomiting it should [apply]' and 'for this one's it should not.' Therefore, it should apply everywhere.

children.text: svāmino vā tad arthatvāt // MS_3,4.35 //
children.translated_text: Or [the rite would be performed] for the owner [of the sacrifice], because it serves his purpose. // MS_3,4.35 //

children.text: svāminoḥ vā vamane syāt. kutaḥ? tad arthatvāt, tad arthaṃ karma yajamānārtham{*3/447*}, yatra somo vamyate, yat tv atra saumendraṃ{*3/448*} karma. tad api tad artham eva. idaṃ hi somavāmina upakārāya śrūyate, tat somavāminaḥ, yajamānasyopakartuṃ{*3/449*} śaknoti nārtvijaḥ, na hi tad ṛtvig arthaṃ karma, yatra somo vamyate. athocyate - somavāmino 'dhvaryor hotur vātmīyā ṛtvijaḥ, tadīyeṣv agniṣu nirvartayiṣyantīti. tathā sati yadi vā vyṛddhasomasya karmaṇo nāṅgam, na somavāmino 'dhvaryor hotur vā, tatrātyantaguṇabhūtā adhvaryvādayaḥ svair ṛtvigbhiḥ kārayanto na phalaṃ prāpnuvanti. tad arthaṃ ca kriyamāṇaṃ na yajamānasyopakāre vartata iti na ṛtvijo vamane kriyeta.
children.translated_text: Or [the <s>Saumendra</s> rite] would be [performed] in the case of the owner's [i.e., sacrificer's] vomiting. Why? Because it serves his purpose — the rite serves the purpose of the sacrificer {*3/447*}. Where <s>Soma</s> is vomited — and the <s>Saumendra</s> {*3/448*} rite here too serves precisely that purpose. For this [rite] is heard as [intended] for the benefit of the one who vomits <s>Soma</s>; it can benefit the sacrificer {*3/449*}, not the priest. For that rite where <s>Soma</s> is vomited is not for the purpose of the priest. And if one says — [the rite is for] the <s>Adhvaryu</s> or the <s>Hotṛ</s> who vomited <s>Soma</s>, and their own priests will perform [it] in their fires — even so, whether or not [the rite] is a subsidiary of the rite of the one who has vomited <s>Soma</s>, [it is] not [a concern] of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> or the <s>Hotṛ</s> who vomited <s>Soma</s>. There, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the others, being entirely subsidiary [functionaries], having their own priests perform [rites], do not obtain the result. And what is performed for that purpose does not serve the benefit of the sacrificer — therefore, [the <s>Saumendra</s> rite] should not be performed in the case of a priest's vomiting.

*{3/449: E2,4: sadupakartuṃ}*

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_3,4.36 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of the indicatory mark. // MS_3,4.36 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca bhavati, yajamānasya somavāmina iti. katham? somapīthena vā eṣa vyṛdhyate yaḥ somaṃ vamatīti. yajamānaḥ, somasaṃskāre vinaṣṭe viguṇam asya karmeti vyṛdhyeta, na kathaṃcid ṛtvijo vyṛddhiḥ. ṛtvijo yasya somaṃ vamantīti vamanena saṃbandhaḥ syāt, na yaḥ somaṃ vamatīti. tasmād api paśyāmo yajamānasya vamane saumendram{*3/450*} iti.
children.translated_text: There is also an indicatory mark that [the rite is] for the sacrificer who vomited <s>Soma</s>. How? 'He is afflicted by <s>Soma</s>-drinking who vomits <s>Soma</s>' — [this means] the sacrificer. When the consecration of the <s>Soma</s> has been destroyed, his ritual becomes defective — and he is afflicted. The priest is in no way afflicted. [If it were about] a priest — 'whose [priests] vomit <s>Soma</s>' — then the connection with vomiting would be [through the genitive]. But [the text says] 'who vomits <s>Soma</s>' [in the nominative]. Therefore, from this too we see that the <s>Saumendra</s> {*3/450*} [rite is performed] in the case of the sacrificer's vomiting.

children.text: sarvapradānaṃ haviṣas tadarthatvāt // MS_3,4.37 //
children.translated_text: The entire oblation material is to be given [to the deity], because it serves that purpose. // MS_3,4.37 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra sāmāmnāyate - yad āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māv āsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavatīti{*3/452*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ kṛtsnaṃ haviḥ, agnaye pradātavyam, uta śeṣayitavyaṃ kiṃcit, kiṃcid dātavyam iti. kiṃ prāptam? kṛtsnaṃ haviḥ pradīyeta. kutaḥ? tadarthatvāt. puroḍāśa āgneyaḥ kartavya iti vacanam. tasmāt sarvaṃ pradātavyam iti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites. There it is recorded: 'When the <s>Āgneya</s> [cake] on eight potsherds is undiminished on the new-moon and the full-moon [days]' {*3/452*}. There the doubt arises: should the entire oblation material be given to <s>Agni</s>, or should some be retained and some given? What is the prima facie view? The entire oblation should be given. Why? Because it serves that purpose — the statement is: 'The <s>Āgneya</s> <s>puroḍāśa</s> should be prepared.' Therefore, the entire [amount] should be given.

children.text: niravadānāt tu śeṣaḥ syāt // MS_3,4.38 //
children.translated_text: But because of [the rule about] cutting off portions (<s>avadāna</s>), [the oblation] should have a remainder. // MS_3,4.38 //

children.text: niṣkṛṣyāvadānaṃ niravadānam. tad dhi śrūyate - dvir haviṣo 'vadyatīti. aparam api vacanam - dvyavadānaṃ juhotīti, tena{*3/453*} dvyavadānamātraṃ hotavyam, anyat pariśeṣaṇīyam.
children.translated_text: That from which portions have been cut off is '<s>niravadāna</s>' (without [further] portions to cut). For it is heard: 'He cuts from the oblation twice.' And there is also another statement: 'He offers with two cut-off portions' — therefore {*3/453*}, only two cut-off portions should be offered, and the rest should be retained.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/453: E2 om. tena}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
*{3/453: E2 om. <s>tena</s>}*

children.text: upāyo vā tadarthatvāt // MS_3,4.39 //
children.translated_text: Or [the cutting] is a means [of consecration], because it serves that purpose. // MS_3,4.39 //

children.text: na caitad asti - dvyavadānamātraṃ hotavyam iti, yaj juhoti, tad dvir avakhaṇḍanena saṃskartavyam iti, hotavye dvir avakhaṇḍamātraṃ vidhīyate, nādvir avakhaṇḍitasya homaḥ pratiṣidhyate, kṛtsnaṃ ca hotavyam iti tad evaṃ nyāyyam, nānyathā.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that only two cut-off portions should be offered. What is offered should be consecrated by cutting twice — [that is,] in what is to be offered, only the twofold cutting is enjoined; the offering of what has not been cut twice is not prohibited. And the entire [oblation] should be offered — this alone is proper, not otherwise.

children.text: kṛtatvāt tu karmaṇaḥ sakṛtsyād dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt // MS_3,4.40 //
children.translated_text: But because the ritual action is accomplished [with the two portions], [the offering] should be [done] once, since the substance is subsidiary. // MS_3,4.40 //

children.text:
ucyate - yadā dvir avakhaṇḍanaviṣiṣṭaṃ home śrutam, tadā sakṛd [337]{*3/454*} avadānaṃ{*3/455*} yāvac chrutaṃ{*3/456*} tat sarvaṃ kṛtam, tadā nāparaṃ dravyam astīti punar yāgo nāvartitavyaḥ. kathaṃ? tad dhi dravyaṃ yāganirvṛttyartham, na dravyaṃ yāgena saṃbandhayitavyam iti. yadi hi yāgena haviḥ saṃbandhayitavyaṃ syāt, tato yāgena dvyavadāne saṃbandhite, aparam api saṃbandhanīyam astīti, tatsaṃbandhārthaṃ punar yāga āvarteta. na tu yāgo dravyasaṃbandhārthaḥ. kiṃ tarhi, dravyaṃ yāge guṇabhūtam, yāgaḥ kathaṃ nirvṛttim upeyād iti dravyam upādīyate. tena nirvṛtte yāge siddhe ca puruṣārthe{*3/457*} na niyogena guṇānurodhena pradhānāvṛttir yukteti.
kathaṃ na dravyaṃ pradhānam, yenāvṛttir ta bhavet. yato yāgāt phalam, bhūtabhavyasamuccāraṇe bhūtaṃ bhavyāyopadiśyata iti. na ca yāgena dravyasyopakāro nirvartyate pratyakṣaḥ kaścit, tasmād dvyavadānaṃ hutvā śeṣayitavyam iti. yat tūktam - āgneyaṃ havir itivacanāt, sarvaṃ hotavyam iti gamyata iti, tatrānumāniko homasaṃbandhaḥ, iha tu pratyakṣo dvir avadāne. api cākṛtsnasaṃbandhe 'pi tad dhitasyopapattiḥ, tato grahītavyam iti. sāmānyaṃ khalv āgneya iti dvyavadānaṃ juhotīti viśeṣaḥ. tasmāc cheṣayitavyaṃ kiṃcid iti.
children.translated_text:
It is said: When the twofold cutting is heard as qualifying the offering, then once [337]{*3/454*} the cutting {*3/455*} — as much as is heard {*3/456*} — has all been done, then there is no further substance remaining, and the sacrifice should not be repeated. How? For the substance exists for the purpose of accomplishing the sacrifice — the substance is not to be connected with the sacrifice [for its own sake]. If the oblation were to be connected with the sacrifice, then after the two cut-off portions have been connected with the sacrifice, since there is further [substance] to be connected, the sacrifice would be repeated for the purpose of connecting that [remaining substance]. But the sacrifice is not for the purpose of connecting substance. Rather, the substance is subsidiary to the sacrifice — the substance is employed [only to the extent needed for] how the sacrifice may be accomplished. Therefore, when the sacrifice has been accomplished and the purpose of the person has been fulfilled {*3/457*}, repetition of the principal [sacrifice] in deference to the subsidiary [substance] is not proper.
How is the substance not the principal, such that repetition [would follow]? Because the result comes from the sacrifice. [The principle is:] 'In a combined statement of past and future, the past is taught for the sake of the future.' And no visible benefit of the substance is accomplished by the sacrifice. Therefore, having offered the two cut-off portions, [the rest] should be retained. As for what was said — 'from the statement "the oblation is <s>Āgneya</s>," it is understood that the whole should be offered' — there, the connection with offering is inferential; but here, the twofold cutting is directly perceived. Moreover, even with a partial connection, the purpose of the sentence is satisfied — hence [the partial connection] should be accepted. '<s>Āgneya</s>' is the general [statement]; 'he offers with two cut-off portions' is the specific. Therefore, some [of the oblation] should be retained.
