children.text: śeṣadarśanāc ca // MS_3,4.41 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of a remainder. // MS_3,4.41 //

children.text: śeṣād iḍām avadyati śeṣāt sviṣṭakṛtaṃ yajatīty anuvādād asti śeṣa iti paśyāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: 'From the remainder he cuts off the <s>iḍā</s> (portion for tasting)'; 'from the remainder he offers the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to the fire-god)' — from this restatement, we see that a remainder exists.

children.text: aprayojakatvād ekasmāt kriyerañ cheṣasya guṇabhūtatvāt // MS_3,4.42 //
children.translated_text: Because [the individual oblations] are not efficacious [for the remainder-rites], [these rites] should be performed from one [oblation], since the remainder is subsidiary. // MS_3,4.42 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra śeṣakāryāṇi, aiḍaprāśitrasauviṣṭakṛdādīni{*3/459*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ haviṣo haviṣaḥ kartavyāni, utaikasmād dhaviṣa iti. kiṃ prāptam? aprayojakatvād ekasmāt kriyeran, aprayojakāni śeṣakāryāṇi haviṣām. yadi śeṣakāryaiḥ prayuktāni, bhaveyuḥ sarvāṇi prayuktānīti sarvebhyaḥ kriyeran anyathārthāni tv etāni, nāvaśyaṃ śeṣakāryeṣu viniyoktavyāni. saṃnidhānāt tu yataḥ - kutaścid anuṣṭhātavyāni, śeṣo hi sādhanam amīṣām iti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites; there, the remainder-rites — <s>iḍā</s>-tasting, <s>prāśitra</s>-eating, <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>-offering, and the like {*3/459*}. There the doubt arises: should these be performed from each individual oblation, or from one [single] oblation? What is the prima facie view? Because [the individual oblations] are not efficacious [for these rites], they should be performed from a single [oblation]. The remainder-rites are not made necessary by [each individual] oblation. If they were necessitated by the remainder-rites, all [oblations] would be necessitated — and [the rites] would be performed from all. But these [remainder-rites] serve a different purpose and need not necessarily be assigned to [each] remainder-rite. But because of proximity — they should be performed from whichever [oblation] is [nearest], for the remainder is the instrument of these [rites].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/459: E2,4: aiḍaprāśitrasauviṣṭakṛtādīni}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
*{3/459: E2,4: <s>aiḍaprāśitrasauviṣṭakṛtādīni</s>}*

children.text: saṃskṛtatvāc ca // MS_3,4.42 //
children.translated_text: And because [the principal rite] has been consecrated [by one performance]. // MS_3,4.42 //

children.text: sakṛc caivaṃjātīyakena śeṣakāryeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pradhānam iti kṛtvā nāparasmād api kartavyam iti.
children.translated_text: Since the principal [rite] has been consecrated once by a remainder-rite of this kind, [the remainder-rite] need not be performed from another [oblation] as well.

children.text: sarvebhyo vā kāraṇāviśeṣāt, saṃskārasya tadarthatvāt // MS_3,4.44 //
children.translated_text: Or [the remainder-rites should be performed] from all [oblations], because there is no difference in the criterion; because the consecration serves the purpose of that [principal rite]. // MS_3,4.44 //

children.text: sarvebhyo vā havirbhyaḥ śeṣakāryāṇi kartavyāni. kutaḥ? kāraṇāviśeṣāt, yad ekasya haviṣaḥ śeṣakāryakriyāyāṃ kāraṇam, tat sarveṣām. sa hi śeṣaḥ pratipādayitavyaḥ, yasyaiva na pratipādyate, tasya tena saṃskāreṇa varjanaṃ syāt, tasmāt sarvebhyaḥ kartavyānīti.
children.translated_text: Or the remainder-rites should be performed from all the oblations. Why? Because there is no difference in the criterion — whatever is the criterion for performing the remainder-rite from one oblation, that [criterion] applies to all. For the remainder must be utilized; and one whose [remainder] is not utilized would be excluded from that consecration. Therefore, [the remainder-rites] should be performed from all.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_3,4.45 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of the indicatory mark. // MS_3,4.45 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca dṛśyate - devā vai sviṣṭakṛtam abruvan havyaṃ no vaha [339]{*3/460*} iti, so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai bhāgo me 'stv iti, vṛṇīṣveti te 'bruvan, so 'bravīd uttarārdhād eva mahyaṃ sakṛt sakṛd avadyād iti vīpsādarśanam. tasmāt sarvebhyaḥ śeṣakāryāṇīti.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark is also seen: 'The gods said to <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>: "Carry our oblation" [339]{*3/460*}. He said: "I choose a boon — let there be a share for me." "Choose," they said. He said: "From the upper half, let [a portion] be cut off for me each time"' — the word 'each time' (<s>vīpsā</s>) shows [repetition]. Therefore, the remainder-rites [should be performed] from all [oblations].

children.text: ekasmāc ced yathākāmyaviśeṣāt // MS_3,4.46 //
children.translated_text: If [the remainder-rites are to be performed] from one [oblation], then from whichever one, because of the absence of specificity. // MS_3,4.46 //

children.text: atha kṛtvācintā. yadaikasmād bhaveyuḥ{*3/461*}, kiṃ tadā yataḥ - kutaścid uta prathamād iti. kiṃ prāptam? yataḥ kutaścid iti. kutaḥ? na kaścid viśeṣa āśrīyata iti. tasmād aniyama iti.
children.translated_text: Now, [let there be] an inquiry into [which specific oblation to use]. If [the remainder-rites] were to be performed from one [oblation] {*3/461*}, then from which — from whichever one, or from the first? What is the prima facie view? From whichever one. Why? Because no specificity is relied upon. Therefore, there is no restriction.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/461: E2,4: kartavyāni bhaveyuḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
*{3/461: E2,4: <s>kartavyāni bhaveyuḥ</s>}*

children.text: mukhyād vā pūrvakālatvāt // MS_3,4.47 //
children.translated_text: Or [they should be performed] from the principal [oblation], because of [its] temporal priority. // MS_3,4.47 //

children.text: mukhyād vā kartavyāni. kutaḥ? pūrvakālatvāt, tataḥ kartavyeṣu nāsti nimittavighātaḥ, asati nimittavighāte naimittikaṃ kartavyam iti. tataḥ kṛteṣu dvitīyādīnāṃ nimittavidhāta ity akriyā. tasmān mukhyād eva kriyerann iti.
children.translated_text: Or [the remainder-rites] should be performed from the principal [oblation]. Why? Because of [its] temporal priority — when they are performed from that [principal oblation], there is no destruction of the occasion; and when the occasion is not destroyed, the occasioned [rite] should be performed. If performed from that [principal oblation], the occasion for the second and subsequent [oblations] is destroyed — hence [they would] not [be] performed [from those]. Therefore, [the remainder-rites] should be performed from the principal [oblation] alone.

children.text: bhakṣāśravaṇād dānaśabdaḥ parikraye // MS_3,4.48 //
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of hearing [a word for] 'eating,' the word 'giving' [indicates] a purchase-price (<s>parikraya</s>). // MS_3,4.48 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - idaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, idaṃ hotuḥ, idam adhvaryoḥ, idam agnīdha iti{*3/462*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ayam [340]{*3/463*} ṛtvijāṃ vibhāgaḥ parikrayāya, uta bhakṣaṇāyeti. kiṃ prāptam? parikrayārtho vibhāgaḥ. kutaḥ? bhakṣāśravaṇāt, na śrūyate - bhakṣitavyam iti. ya eva śrutasyotsarge doṣaḥ, sa evāśrutaparikalpaṇāyām. karmakarebhyaś ca dīyate, tasmāt parikraya eṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard: 'This is for the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]; this is for the <s>Hotṛ</s>; this is for the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; this is for the <s>Agnīdh</s>' {*3/462*}. There the doubt arises: is this [340]{*3/463*} a distribution to the priests for the purpose of a purchase-price [i.e., their fee], or for the purpose of eating [i.e., ritual consumption]? What is the prima facie view? The distribution is for the purpose of a purchase-price. Why? Because of the absence of hearing [a word for] 'eating' — it is not heard: 'it should be eaten.' And whatever defect there is in abandoning what is heard, the same [defect exists] in imagining what is not heard. And [gifts] are given to workers [as payment]. Therefore, this is a purchase-price.

children.text: tatsaṃstavāc ca // MS_3,4.49 //
children.translated_text: And because of the praise [of this as] a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // MS_3,4.49 //

children.text: eṣā vai darśapūrṇamāsayor dakṣiṇeti dakṣiṇāsaṃstavāc ca parikrayārthaṃ manyāmahe.
children.translated_text: 'This indeed is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites' — because of the praise [of this distribution] as a <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, we consider it to be for the purpose of a purchase-price.

children.text: bhakṣārtho vā dravye samatvāt // MS_3,4.50 //
children.translated_text: Or [the distribution is] for the purpose of eating, because of the equality of the substance. // MS_3,4.50 //

children.text:
bhakṣārtha eṣa vibhāgaḥ. kutaḥ? dānasyābhāvāt. katham abhāvaḥ? prabhavatā hi śakyaṃ dātum,
nāprabhavatā. kathaṃ na prabhutvam? saṃkalpitaṃ hi yajamānena, devatāyā etad iti. na ca devatāyai saṃkalpitena śiṣṭāḥ sveneva vyavaharanti. tasmāc chiṣṭācāram anuvartamānenāśakyaṃ prabhavitum, tasmān na parikrayaḥ.
atha yad uktam - na śrūyate, bhakṣayitavyam iti, yāvāṃś ca śrutasyotsarge doṣaḥ, tāvān aśrutaparikalpanāyām iti. ucyate - idaṃ brahmaṇa ityevamādibhir brahmādīnām, bhāgair abhisaṃbandhaḥ, tatra bhāgā brahmādīnām upakuryur brahmādayo vā bhāgānām. brahmādibhir bhāgānām upakurvadbhir na kiṃcid dṛṣṭam asti, bāgais tu brahmādīnām upakārakaiḥ śakyate kenacit prakāreṇa dṛṣṭa upakāraḥ kartuṃ bhakṣyamāṇaiḥ. tasmād bhakṣaṇāya vibhāga iti. kaḥ punar upakāra iti cet. tṛptānāṃ karmaśeṣaparisamāpane sāmarthyaṃ bhavatīti.
children.translated_text:
This distribution is for the purpose of eating. Why? Because of the absence of a [true] gift. How is there absence? For one who is capable can give, not one who is incapable. How is there no capability? For the sacrificer has resolved: 'This belongs to the deity.' And with what has been resolved [as belonging] to the deity, the learned do not transact as [if it were] their own. Therefore, one who follows the conduct of the learned cannot have the authority [to give it as a purchase-price]. Therefore, it is not a purchase-price.
As for what was said — 'it is not heard that [the oblation] should be eaten'; and 'whatever defect there is in abandoning what is heard, the same [exists] in imagining what is not heard' — it is said: By [the statements] 'this is for the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]' and the like, the shares are connected with the <s>Brahman</s> and the others. There, either the shares would serve [the benefit of] the <s>Brahman</s> and the others, or the <s>Brahman</s> and the others [would serve the benefit of] the shares. The <s>Brahman</s> and the others serving [the benefit of] the shares — no visible [purpose] exists for that. But the shares, being beneficial to the <s>Brahman</s> and the others — a visible benefit can be accomplished in some manner by being eaten. Therefore, the distribution is for the purpose of eating. And what is that benefit? When [the priests are] satiated, they have the capacity to complete the remainder of the ritual.

children.text: vyādeśād dānasaṃstutiḥ // MS_3,4.51 //
children.translated_text: The praise [of this distribution] as a gift [i.e., <s>dakṣiṇā</s>] is [based on] a general analogy (<s>vyādeśa</s>). // MS_3,4.51 //

children.text: atha yad dakṣiṇāsaṃstava iti, vyādeśasāmānyāt tat, aparikrayārthe 'pi bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: As for [the argument that] there is a praise [of this] as a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> — because of the generality of the analogy, that [praise] will apply even when [the distribution] is not for the purpose of a purchase-price.

children.text: ājyāc ca sarvasaṃyogāt // MS_3,5.1 //
children.translated_text: And because of the connection of ghee (<s>ājya</s>) with all [rites]. // MS_3,5.1 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra śrūyate - uttarārdhāt sviṣṭakṛte samavadyatīti{*3/466*}, tathā - iḍām upahvayatīti{*3/467*}, tathānyāni prāśitrāvadānādīni śeṣakāryāṇi{*3/468*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ājyād upāṃśuyājadravyāt sviṣṭakṛd iḍam avadātavyam, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? avadātavyam iti. kutaḥ? sarvasaṃyogāt, sādhāraṇaprakaraṇasamāmnātāt sarveṣāṃ śeṣakāryāṇi. api ca sarvasaṃyogo bhavati, tad yat{*3/469*} sarvebhyo havirbhyaḥ samavadyatīti. tasmād ājyād api śeṣakāryāṇi kriyante.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) rites. There it is heard: 'He cuts off from the northern half for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>).' Similarly: 'He invokes the <s>Iḍā</s> (sacrificial food).' Similarly, there are other residual rites (<s>śeṣakārya</s>) such as the <s>prāśitra</s> portion-cutting and so on. There the doubt arises: should the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> portions be cut from the <s>ājya</s> (ghee), the offering substance of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> (low-voice sacrifice), or not? What is the prima facie view? [They] should be cut. Why? Because of the connection with all — since [the residual rites] are prescribed in a common context, the residual rites [apply] to all [offering substances]. Moreover, there is a connection with all: 'from all the oblation-substances he cuts off together.' Therefore, the residual rites are also performed from the <s>ājya</s>.

children.text: kāraṇāc ca // MS_3,5.2 //
children.translated_text: And because of the explanatory passage (<s>kāraṇa</s>). // MS 3,5.2 //

children.text: kāraṇaṃ śrūyate - devā vai sviṣṭakṛtam abruvan havyaṃ no vaheti, so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai bhāgo me 'stv iti, vṛṇīṣvety abruvan{*3/470*}, so 'bravīd uttarārdhād eva mahyaṃ sakṛt sakṛd avadyād iti, tulyaṃ kāraṇam anyeṣām ājyasya cārthavāde saṃkīrtyate. tasmād apy ājyād avadātavyam iti.
children.translated_text: An explanatory passage is heard: 'The gods indeed said to <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (Agni as oblation-perfector): "Carry our oblation." He said: "I choose a boon — let a share be mine." "Choose," they said. He said: "Let [a portion] be cut off for me from the northern half each time."' An equal explanatory passage is mentioned for the <s>ājya</s> and the others in the <s>arthavāda</s>. Therefore, [portions] should be cut even from the <s>ājya</s>.

children.text: ekasmin samavattaśabdāt // MS_3,5.3 //
children.translated_text: In [a rite with] a single [offering substance], because of the word 'together' (<s>samavatta</s>). // MS 3,5.3 //

children.text: āditye carau prāyaṇīye śrūyate - agnaye sviṣṭakṛte samavadyatīti{*3/471*}, ājyād ekasmāc ca haviṣo 'vadyatīti, miśrasyānyena haviṣā samavadyatīti. yadi cājyād api sviṣṭakṛte 'vadīyeta, tataś codakena prāpaṇīya{*3/472*} ājyāvadāne kriyamāṇe [343]{*3/473*} samavadyatīty upapadyate. itarathā caror ekasmād avadyatīty abhaviṣyat.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Āditya</s> <s>caru</s> (porridge offering) of the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening rite), it is heard: 'He cuts off together for <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.' [This means] from the <s>ājya</s> as one oblation substance he cuts off, [that is,] of a mixed [substance] he cuts off together with another oblation substance. If the residual rite for <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> were also performed from the <s>ājya</s>, then in the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> [rite] — which is enjoined [to have <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>] — when the <s>ājya</s> portion-cutting is performed, the word 'together' (<s>samavadyati</s>) is applicable. Otherwise, it would have been [simply] 'he cuts off from the <s>caru</s> alone.'

children.text: ājye ca darśanāt sviṣṭakṛd arthavādasya // MS_3,5.4 //
children.translated_text: And because the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is observed in the <s>ājya</s> — [as shown by] the explanatory passage. // MS 3,5.4 //

children.text: dhrauve cājye sviṣṭakṛd arthavādo bhavati - avadāyāvadāya dhruvāṃ pratyabhidhārayati, sviṣṭakṛte 'vadāya na dhruvāṃ pratyabhidhārayati. na hi tataḥ parāmāhutiṃ yakṣyan bhavatīti, pratyabhidhāraṇasyaitat prayojanaṃ darśayati - tataḥ patrāmāhutiṃ hoṣyatīti. sauviṣṭakṛte vṛtte{*3/474*} tataḥ parāhutir nāstīti na pratyabhidhāryeta. sviṣṭakṛd arthe dhruvāyāṃ bhavati pratyabhidhāraṇam iti darśayati.
children.translated_text: In the permanent <s>ājya</s> (<s>dhruva</s>), the explanatory passage shows the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>: 'Having cut off [portions] again and again, he holds the <s>dhruvā</s> (permanent ladle) back; but after cutting for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, he does not hold the <s>dhruvā</s> back. For he is not going to sacrifice any further oblation from that.' This shows the purpose of the holding-back — that he will offer a further oblation from it. When the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is completed, since there is no further oblation from that, it should not be held back. [The explanatory passage] shows that the holding-back of the <s>dhruvā</s> is for the purpose of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/474: E2,4: 'vatte}*
aśeṣātvāt tu naivaṃ syāt sarvādānād aśeṣatā // MS_3,5.5 //
children.translated_text: But because of the absence of a remainder, it should not be so — the absence of a remainder [is] because of the complete cutting. // MS 3,5.5 //

children.text: naivam, dhrauvājyāt sviṣṭakṛd iḍam avadātavyam iti. kasmāt? aśeṣatvāt. kuto nāsya śeṣaḥ? sarvādānāt.
children.translated_text: Not so — [the portions for] <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> should not be cut from the permanent <s>ājya</s>. Why? Because of the absence of a remainder. Why is there no remainder? Because of the complete cutting.

children.text: sādhāraṇyān na dhruvāyāṃ syāt // MS_3,5.6 //
children.translated_text: Because of [its being] shared, [the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>] should not be from the <s>dhruvā</s>. // MS 3,5.6 //

children.text:
nanūpāṃśuyājārthaṃ gṛhīte yad dhruvāyāṃ śiṣṭam, tat śeṣabhūtam. naitat, sādhāraṇaṃ hi tat, upāṃśuyājāya, anyebhyaś ca prayojanebhyaḥ. yāvad ājyena yaṣṭavyam, tat tad ājyaṃ prayojayati. yasya yasyājyam, tasya tasyaivaṃ grahītavyaṃ saṃskartavyaṃ ceti, tasmāt sādhāraṇaṃ dhrauvam ājyam. darśayati ca - sarvasmai vā etad yajñāya gṛhyate yad dhruvāyām ājyam iti{*3/475*}. kim ato yady evam iti. yat sādhāraṇam upāṃśuyājāyāvattaṃ dhruvāyām ājyam, tenānyāni prayojanāni kāryāṇi, na [344]{*3/476*} tu tat pratipādyam, yad dhi kṛtaprayojanam ākīrṇakaram avatiṣṭhate, tat pratipādayitavyam iti. kvacic ca, yat pratipādayitavyam tat, evaṃ pratipādayitavyam iti. yat tu prayojanavad upāttaṃ tan na pratipādayitavyam. tasmān na dhruvāyām upāṃśuyājasya{*3/477*} sauviṣṭakṛtaś ca{*3/478*} kaścic cheṣaḥ pratipādanīyaḥ, yathā yatraikasyāmukhyāyāṃ bahūnām odanaḥ śṛto bhavati, tatraikasmin bhuktavati, na tasya śiṣṭaṃ bhṛtyebhyaḥ pratipādanīyamukhāyām astīti gamyate, prayojanavad dhi tat. evam upāṃśuyājājye 'pi draṣṭavyam{*3/479*} iti.
āha - juhvāṃ tarhy ājyasya śeṣo bhaviṣyati, camasavat, yathā camaseṣu graheṣu ca somasya codanayeti. tatra pratyāha -
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] But what remains in the <s>dhruvā</s> after it was taken for the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> — that is the remainder. [Reply:] Not so, for it is shared — shared between the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> and other purposes. For as long as sacrificing with <s>ājya</s> is needed, that <s>ājya</s> serves [that purpose]. For each [rite] that requires <s>ājya</s>, [the ājya] must be thus taken and consecrated. Therefore, the <s>dhruvā</s> <s>ājya</s> is shared. And [the text] shows: 'For indeed it is taken for the whole sacrifice — the <s>ājya</s> that is in the <s>dhruvā</s>.' What follows from this? Since the shared <s>ājya</s> in the <s>dhruvā</s>, allotted to the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>, [must serve] the other purposes too — it should not be [treated as a] residue. For what has served its purpose and remains idle — that is to be disposed of. And in some cases, what is to be disposed of is disposed of in a particular way. But what has been taken with a purpose should not be disposed of. Therefore, there is no remainder of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> or <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> in the <s>dhruvā</s> that needs disposal — just as when food is cooked in a single main pot for many [people], when one has eaten, what remains for him is not understood as 'his leftover to be given to servants' [because] it has [further] purpose. Similarly, the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> <s>ājya</s> should be viewed [the same way].
[Objection:] But there will be a remainder of the <s>ājya</s> in the offering ladle (<s>juhū</s>), like the <s>camasa</s> (cup) — just as there is a remainder of <s>Soma</s> in the cups and ladles by injunction. To this it is replied —

children.text: avattatvāc ca juhvām, tasya ca homasaṃyogāt // MS_3,5.7 //
children.translated_text: And because of the complete taking from the <s>juhū</s>, and because of its connection with the oblation. // MS 3,5.7 //

children.text: dhruvāyāṃ tāvan nāsti śeṣaḥ, upāṃśuyājasya sādhāraṇatvād ity uktam. atha kasmān na juhvāṃ yac chiṣṭam, tena śeṣakāryam, yathā homārthe camase śeṣa iti. ucyate - yaj juhvām avattam, tat sarvaṃ homena saṃbaddham, tasmān na juhvāṃ śeṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: There is no remainder in the <s>dhruvā</s>, because of [the <s>ājya</s>] being shared for the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> — this has been stated. Now, why is there no residual rite with the remainder in the <s>juhū</s>, as [there is] a remainder in the <s>camasa</s> for the oblation purpose? It is said: whatever is taken into the <s>juhū</s> is entirely connected with the oblation. Therefore, there is no remainder in the <s>juhū</s>.

children.text: camasavad iti cet // MS_3,5.8 //
children.translated_text: Like the <s>camasa</s> — if [you say so]. // MS 3,5.8 //

children.text: iti punar yad uktam, tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: What was further said [about this] — that [objection] must be addressed.

children.text: na codanāvirodhād dhaviḥprakalpanatvāc ca // MS_3,5.9 //
children.translated_text: No, because there is no contradiction with the injunction, and because [the cups serve] the purpose of preparing the oblation. // MS 3,5.9 //

children.text: naitad evam. kutaḥ? codanāvirodhāt, somasyāgner{*3/480*} vīhīty{*3/481*} anuvaṣaṭkarotīti{*3/482*} tatra codanā. api ca, tatraindravāyavaṃ gṛhṇātītyevamādīni grahaṇāni na somasaṃyuktāni{*3/483*}, [345]{*3/484*} haviḥprakalpanāny eva, iha punar homasaṃyogaḥ, caturgṛhītaṃ juhotīti{*3/485*}.
children.translated_text: This is not so. Why? Because there is no contradiction with the injunction — 'Of <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, the rice' — he makes the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (secondary exclamation) — there is an injunction there. Moreover, the takings such as 'he takes the <s>Aindrāvāyava</s> [cup]' and others are not connected with <s>Soma</s> [as a completed oblation]; they are merely preparations of the oblation. But here [in the <s>ājya</s> case], there is a connection with the oblation — 'he offers with a fourfold taking.'

children.text: utpannādhikārāt sati sarvavacanam // MS_3,5.10 //
children.translated_text: The statement about 'all' is with reference to what has arisen [as remainder]. // MS 3,5.10 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - tad yat{*3/486*} sarvebhyaḥ havirbhyaḥ samavadyatīti. ucyate - utpannaṃ śeṣam adhikṛtyaitad ucyate, nāviśeṣaṇam, tasmād ya{*3/487*} iha śeṣās tebhyaḥ sarvebhya iti, yathā sarva odano bhuktaḥ, sarve brāhmaṇā bhuktavanta iti prakṛtāpekṣaḥ sarvaśabda evam atrāpīti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'from all the oblation substances he cuts off together' — it is said: this is said with reference to the remainder that has arisen; it is not a [universal] qualifier. Therefore, 'from all' [means] from those here that are remainders — just as 'all the food is eaten,' 'all the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> have eaten' — the word 'all' refers to what is under discussion. So here too.

children.text: jātiviśeṣāt param // MS_3,5.11 //
children.translated_text: Because of the specification of class, [the word 'together' is] secondary. // MS 3,5.11 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - prāpaṇīye{*3/488*} kevale carau samavattaśabdo nāvakalpate, yadi na tatra codakenājyād api sviṣṭṛakṛd avadānam iti. ucyate - asaty apy ājyāc cheṣakārye samavattaśabdo jātiviśeṣāpekṣa upapadyate, odanajātim ājyajātiṃ{*3/489*} cāpekṣya. anuvādo hi saḥ, yathāsaṃbhavaṃ cānuvādaḥ kalpyeta.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — in the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> [rite] with a single <s>caru</s>, the word 'together' (<s>samavatta</s>) cannot be construed unless the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portion is also cut from the <s>ājya</s> along with [the <s>caru</s>] — it is said: even without the residual rite from the <s>ājya</s>, the word 'together' is applicable with reference to the specification of class — with reference to the class of <s>odana</s> (cooked rice) and the class of <s>ājya</s>. For it is a restatement, and a restatement is construed as far as possible.

children.text: antyam arekārthe // MS_3,5.12 //
children.translated_text: The final [portion] is for the purpose of [avoiding] emptying. // MS 3,5.12 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - sviṣṭakṛd arthaṃ dhruvāyām abhidhāraṇaṃ darśayatīti. na tat sviṣṭakṛd artham, śeṣābhāvād ity uktam. tasmād ayaṃ tasyārthaḥ. na hi tata āhutiṃ yakṣyan bhavatīti na rekṣyate, dhruvāto yady āhutir aparā hotavyā bhavet, na ca pratyabhidhāryeta. dhuvātaḥ kila{*3/490*} ricyeta, na rakṣyate, aparasyā āhuter abhāvāt, kiṃ pratyabhidhāraṇeneti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — [the explanatory passage] shows that the holding-back of the <s>dhruvā</s> is for the purpose of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> — [the <s>dhruvā</s>] is not for the purpose of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, because of the absence of a remainder — this has been stated. Therefore, this is its meaning: 'For he is not going to sacrifice any further oblation from that' — therefore it is not guarded [i.e., held back]. From the <s>dhruvā</s>, if another oblation were to be offered, then it would not be held back. [The meaning is:] from the <s>dhruvā</s>, indeed, it would be emptied; it is not guarded because of the absence of a further oblation. What then is the purpose of holding it back?

children.text: sākaṃ prasthāyīye{*3/492*} sviṣṭakṛd iḍaṃ ca tadvat // MS_3,5.13 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sākaṃprasthāyīya</s> (simultaneous departure rite), the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> are similar. // MS 3,5.13 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - sākaṃ prasthāyīyena yajeteti{*3/493*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sviṣṭakṛd iḍam asti, nāstīti. astīti brūmah. kutaḥ? darśapūrṇamāsavikāro hi sākaṃ prasthāyīyam iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - nāstīti. kutaḥ? aśeṣatvāt, sarvādānāc cāśeṣatā. katham? evaṃ tatra śrūyate - ājyabhāgābhyāṃ pracaryāgneyena ca puroḍāśenāgnīdhre srucau pradāya saha kumbhībhir abhikrāmann āheti. tasmān na tataḥ śeṣakāryad iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: 'He should sacrifice with the <s>Sākaṃprasthāyīya</s>.' There the doubt arises: is there a <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s>, or not? We say: there is. Why? Because the <s>Sākaṃprasthāyīya</s> is a modification of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Having arrived at this, we say: there is not. Why? Because of the absence of a remainder — and the absence of a remainder is because of the complete cutting. How? Thus it is heard there: 'Having proceeded with the <s>ājya</s> portions and the <s>Āgneya</s> <s>puroḍāśa</s>, having given the ladles to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-tender), proceeding together with the pots, he says "come."' Therefore, there are no residual rites from that.

NOTES:
[{3/492: E1: <s>prasthāyye</s>}]
[{3/493: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.5.4.3}]

children.text: sautrāmaṇyāṃ ca graheṣu // MS_3,5.14 //
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, regarding the cups (<s>grahas</s>). // MS 3,5.14 //

children.text: asti sautrāmaṇī, tatra grahāḥ{*3/494*} śrūyante, āśvinasārasvataindrāḥ, tatra codakena sviṣṭakṛd iḍaṃ prāptam. athedānīṃ saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ nivartate, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? codakānugrahāya kartavyam iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sautrāmaṇyāṃ ca graheṣu na{*3/495*} kartavyam iti caśabdenātidiśyate{*3/496*}. kutaḥ? aśeṣatvāt, sarvādānād śeṣatā. tatrāpi hi grahair evaṃ hotuṃ pratiṣṭhante, yat payograhāś ca suragrahāś ca gṛhyanta iti. grahasthaṃ khalv api tad dravyam abhigṛhītam abhyanukramam abhyāśrāvitaṃ devatāṃ prati. yathā - gṛhītān grahān ṛtvija ādadate, āśvinam adhvaryuḥ, sārasvataṃ brahmā, aindraṃ pratiprasthāteti, homārtham [347]{*3/497*} aśeṣādānaṃ bhavati. homasaṃyogaś caiṣāṃ śruyate - uttare 'gnau payograhāj juhvati dakṣiṇe 'gnau suragrahāj juhvatīti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> (rite); there the cups are heard — <s>Āśvina</s>, <s>Sārasvata</s>, and <s>Aindra</s>. There, by the injunction, the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> are obtained. Now the doubt arises: does [the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>] apply, or not? What is the prima facie view? It should be performed, for the sake of upholding the injunction. Having arrived at this, we say: in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> too, regarding the cups, [it] should not be performed — [this is indicated] by the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) extending [the rule]. Why? Because of the absence of a remainder — and the absence of a remainder is because of the complete cutting. For there too, they proceed to offer with the cups — both the milk-cups and the <s>surā</s> (liquor)-cups are taken. And the substance in the cups is taken entirely, taken in sequence, and consecrated toward the deity. As [the text shows]: 'Having taken the cups, the priests take [them] — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [takes] the <s>Āśvina</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> [takes] the <s>Sārasvata</s>, the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> [takes] the <s>Aindra</s>' — the complete taking is for the purpose of oblation. And a connection with oblation is heard for these: 'In the northern fire they offer the milk-cups; in the southern fire they offer the <s>surā</s>-cups.'

children.text: tadvac ca śeṣavacanam // MS_3,5.15 //
children.translated_text: And the statement about the remainder is similar. // MS 3,5.15 //

children.text: etam eva nyāyam, śeṣavacanam upodbalayati. ucchinaṣṭi, na sarvaṃ juhotīti{*3/498*}, sarvahome prāpte, pratiṣedho 'vakalpyate. vācanikatvāc ca sviṣṭakṛd iḍaṃ na bhavati, tasyānyatropayogavacanāt, brāhmaṇaṃ parikrīṇīyād uccheṣaṇasya pātāram iti, aparasyāpi śeṣasya vācaniko viniyogaḥ, śatātṛṇāyāṃ vikṣārayantīti.
children.translated_text: This very reasoning is reinforced by the statement about the remainder. 'He leaves some; he does not offer everything' — when the complete offering is expected, a prohibition is construed. And because the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> are established by [Vedic] statement, [they do] not [apply here] — because of the [Vedic] statement assigning that [remainder] to another use: 'He should hire a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> to drink the leavings.' There is also a Vedic assignment for the other remainder: 'They scatter [it] on the <s>śatātṛṇā</s> (hundred-grass plot).'

NOTES:
[{3/498: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.8.6.2}]

children.text: dravyaikatve karmabhedāt pratikarma kriyeran // MS_3,5.16 //
children.translated_text: When the substance is one, because of the multiplicity of rites, [the residual rites] should be performed for each rite. // MS 3,5.16 //

children.text: asti sarvapṛṣṭheṣṭiḥ - indrāya rāthantarāya, indrāya bārhatāya{*3/499*}, indrāya vairūpāya, indrāya vairājāya, indrāya śāknarāyeti. tatra puroḍāśo bahūnāṃ karmaṇāṃ sādhāraṇaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ pratikarma, sviṣṭakṛd iḍaṃ kartavyam, sakṛd eva veti. kiṃ prāptam? codanānugrahāt pratikarma, kartavyam, ekasminn api dravye bahutvāt karmaṇām.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Sarvapṛṣṭheṣṭi</s> (all-<s>Pṛṣṭha</s> sacrifice): 'To <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>], to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Vairūpa</s>, to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Vairāja</s>, to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Śākvara</s>.' There, the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is shared among many rites. There the doubt arises: should the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> be performed for each rite, or only once? What is the prima facie view? Because of upholding the injunction, [they should be performed] for each rite — even with a single substance, because of the multiplicity of rites.

children.text:
NOTES:

children.translated_text:
NOTES:

children.text: avibhāgāc ca śeṣasya, sarvān praty aviśiṣṭatvāt // MS_3,5.17 //
children.translated_text: And because of the non-division of the remainder — since [the remainder] is undifferentiated with respect to all [rites]. // MS 3,5.17 //

children.text: sakṛd eva kartavyam iti brūmaḥ, avibhāgāc cheṣasya. na [348]{*3/500*} atra vibhāgaḥ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ puroḍāśasya, uttarārdhāt sviṣṭakṛd avadātavyam, ekaś cāsau uttarārdhaḥ, tato 'vadīyamāne na gamyate viśeṣaḥ. kasyāvattam, kasya neti, evam iḍāyām api. tasmāt sakṛd avadātavyam iti.
children.translated_text: We say it should be done only once, because the remainder is undivided. There is no division here of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> among all the rites — from the upper half, [the portion] for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is to be cut off, and that upper half is one; when cutting from it, no distinction is discerned — which [portion] has been cut off for whom, and which not — and likewise with the <s>Iḍā</s>. Therefore it should be cut off only once.

children.text: aindravāyave tu vacanāt pratikarma bhakṣaḥ syāt // MS_3,5.18 //
children.translated_text: But in the case of the <s>Aindravāyava</s> [cup], because of a [specific] statement, there should be partaking (<s>bhakṣa</s>) at each ritual act. // MS_3,5.18 //

children.text: asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ - jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeteti. tatraindravāyave grahe saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sakṛd bhakṣaṇam, uta dvir iti. somasaṃskārārthatvāt sakṛd iti prāpte brūmaḥ - aindravāyave dvir bhakṣayitavyam iti. kutaḥ? vacanāt, vacanam idaṃ bhavati, dvir aindravāyavasya bhakṣayati, dvir hy etasya vaṣaṭkarotīti, nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' There, regarding the <s>Aindravāyava</s> cup, a doubt [arises] — should the partaking be once, or twice? When the prima facie view is that it should be once, because [the cup] serves the purpose of <s>Soma</s> preparation, we say — the <s>Aindravāyava</s> should be partaken of twice. Why? Because of a [specific] statement; this statement exists: 'He partakes of the <s>Aindravāyava</s> twice, for he makes the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> exclamation for it twice' — there is no over-burdening of the statement.

children.text: some 'vacanād bhakṣo na vidyate // MS_3,5.19 //
children.translated_text: In the case of <s>Soma</s>, because of the absence of a statement, partaking does not exist. // MS_3,5.19 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome samāmananti somān. teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ{*3/501*} teṣāṃ śeṣo bhakṣayitavyaḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? some bhakṣo na vidyate. kasmāt? avacanāt, na śakyam asati vacane 'dhyavasātuṃ bhakṣaṇam. tasmāt somaśeṣo na bhakṣayitavya iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, they enumerate the <s>Soma</s> cups. Regarding them, a doubt [arises] — should the remainder of these be partaken of, or not? What is the prima facie view? In the case of <s>Soma</s>, partaking does not exist. Why? Because of the absence of a statement — it is not possible to determine partaking in the absence of a statement. Therefore the <s>Soma</s> remainder should not be partaken of.

children.text:

children.translated_text:

children.text: syād vānyārthadarśanāt // MS_3,5.20 //
children.translated_text: Or it would [exist], because of the observation of [its] serving another purpose. // MS_3,5.20 //

children.text: bhaved vā bhakṣaḥ, anyārthaṃ hi vacanaṃ bhakṣaṃ darśayati - sarvataḥ parihāram āśvinaṃ bhakṣayati, bhakṣitāpy āyitāṃś camasān [349]{*3/502*} dakṣiṇasyānaso 'valambe sādayantīti{*3/503*}. nāsati bhakṣaṇa evaṃjātīyakā bhakṣaviśeṣāḥ saṃbhavanti.
children.translated_text: Or rather, partaking would exist, for a statement serving another purpose shows partaking — 'He partakes of the <s>Āśvina</s> [cup] with circumambulation from all sides; having partaken, they set down the arrived <s>camasas</s> (cups) on the support of the southern cart.' Without partaking, such specific varieties of partaking would not be possible.

children.text: vacanāni tv apūrvatvāt tasmād yathopadeśaṃ syuḥ // MS_3,5.21 //
children.translated_text: But the statements, being unprecedented, should therefore follow the [specific] instruction. // MS_3,5.21 //

children.text: nanu darśanam idam, prāptir vaktavyā. ucyate - vacanāni tarhi bhaviṣyanti. sarvataḥ parihāram āśvinaṃ bhakṣayati{*3/504*}. tasmāt sarvā diśaḥ śṛṇotīti viśiṣṭaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate. apūrvatvād bhakṣānuvādo nāvakalpate. api ca, evam apūrvam arthaṃ vidadhato 'rthavattā bhaviṣyati. tasmād yatraiva viśiṣṭaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ śrūyate, tatraiva bhavati, nātiprasajyate.
children.translated_text: Objection: this is [merely] an observation; the entailment must be stated. Reply: the statements then will exist — 'He partakes of the <s>Āśvina</s> [cup] with circumambulation from all sides; therefore he hears from all directions' — a specific partaking is enjoined. Because of [its] unprecedented nature, a restatement of partaking (<s>bhakṣānuvāda</s>) is not possible. Moreover, when thus enjoining an unprecedented meaning, [the statement] will have purposefulness. Therefore, only where specific partaking is heard, there alone does it apply — it is not over-extended.

NOTES:
[{3/504: Cf. <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.4.9.4}]

children.text: camaseṣu samākhyānāt saṃyogasya tannimittatvāt // MS_3,5.22 //
children.translated_text: In the case of the <s>camasas</s> (cups), because of the designation, and because the connection is caused by that [designation]. // MS_3,5.22 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭoma eva śruyate - praitu hotuś camasaḥ pra brahmaṇaḥ prodgātṝṇāṃ pra yajamānasya prayantu sadasyānām iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ camasinām asti bhakṣaḥ, neti. kiṃ prāptam? neti brūmaḥ, nātiprasajyata{*3/505*} ity uktam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - camaseṣv asti bhakṣa iti. kutaḥ? samākhyānāt, hotuś camaso brahmaṇaś camasa udgātuś camasa iti samākhyayā nirdiśyate, hotā yatra camati camiṣyati, acamīd vā sa hotuś camasaḥ. yady atra hotā na camen na hotuś camaso bhavet. tasmāc camatīti.
āha, kāsya liṅgasya prāptir iti. sāmarthyam iti brūmaḥ - hotuś camasena praitavyam. yadi cātra hotā na [350]{*3/506*} camet, na śakyaṃ bhaved dhotuś camasena praitum. na cātrānyad dhotā, odanādi camiṣyati, somacamasa iti hi taṃ samācakṣate. api ca, na tad dhotur dravyaṃ yajamānasya tad dravyam, hotus tatra camanaṃ kartavyam. some ca bhakṣyamāṇe tena homo 'vakalpate. pavitraṃ hi somaḥ, na tasmin bhakṣite pātraṃ vyāpadyate. tatra camasena śakyate hotum. vacanaprāmāṇyād ucchiṣṭena hoṣyatīti cet. naitad evam, asati avakāśe vacanaṃ bādhakaṃ bhavati, asti cāvakāśaḥ somabhakṣaṇam, tasmāc camasibhir bhakṣayitavyaḥ somaḥ iti.
atha takṣaṇādīny āśrīyeran. tathā saṃbandhāpahnavād ataccamasataiva syāt, dravyāntaraṃ syāt. tasmāc cābrāhmaṇasya somaṃ pratiṣedhati, sa yadi rājanyaṃ vaiśyaṃ vā yājayet, sa yadi somaṃ vibhakṣayiṣet, nyagrodhastibhīrāhṛtya tāḥ saṃpiṣya dadhany unmṛja{*3/507*} tasmai bhakṣaṃ prayacchet, na somam iti{*3/508*} bhakṣānivṛttiṃ{*3/509*} darśayati. saiṣa bhakṣāśaṅkaivaṃ saty upapadyate, yadi camasino 'sti bhakṣaḥ, tasmād astīti manyāmahe.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself it is heard: 'Let the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s cup go forth, and that of the <s>Brahman</s>, and those of the <s>Udgātṛs</s>, and that of the sacrificer; let those of the <s>Sadasyins</s> go forth.' There a doubt [arises] — do the cup-holders have partaking, or not? What is the prima facie view? No, we say — it has been stated that [partaking] is not over-extended.
Given this, we say — there is partaking in the <s>camasas</s>. Why? Because of the designation — 'the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s cup, the <s>Brahman</s>'s cup, the <s>Udgātṛ</s>'s cup' — it is designated by name: where the <s>Hotṛ</s> drinks, has drunk, or will drink, that is the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s cup. If the <s>Hotṛ</s> does not drink here, it would not be the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s cup. Therefore he drinks.
[The objector] asks: what is the basis for this inferential mark? We reply: capability — the <s>Hotṛ</s> should go forth with his cup. And if the <s>Hotṛ</s> does not drink here, it would not be possible to go forth with the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s cup. And the <s>Hotṛ</s> will not drink something else here — rice-gruel and the like — for they call it a '<s>Soma</s>-cup.' Moreover, that substance does not belong to the <s>Hotṛ</s> — it belongs to the sacrificer — so the <s>Hotṛ</s> must perform the drinking there. And when <s>Soma</s> is being partaken of, a <s>homa</s> (libation) from it is appropriate, for <s>Soma</s> is a purifier; when it has been partaken of, the vessel is not defiled. There, offering with the cup is possible.
If [the objector] says: because of the authority of the statement, he will offer with the leavings — this is not so, for a statement becomes overriding [only] in the absence of scope, and there is scope [here], namely <s>Soma</s>-partaking. Therefore <s>Soma</s> should be partaken of by the cup-holders.
But if crafting and other [operations] are resorted to, then because of the denial of the connection, it would indeed not be a cup of that [deity], and would be a different substance. Therefore [the text] prohibits <s>Soma</s> for the non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'If he should cause a <s>Kṣatriya</s> or a <s>Vaiśya</s> to sacrifice, and if [the non-Brāhmaṇa] wishes to partake of <s>Soma</s>, having brought <s>nyagrodha</s> bark, crushing it and stirring it into curds, he should give that partaking to him, not <s>Soma</s>' — this shows the non-cessation of partaking. This apprehension of partaking is fitting only if the cup-holders have partaking. Therefore we hold that it exists.

NOTES:
[{3/505: E2,4: <s>bhakṣo nātiprasajyata</s>}]
[{3/506: E2: 4,456; E4: 4,733; E6: 1,237}]
[{3/507: E2,4,6, E1 (variant reading): <s>unmṛjya</s>}]
[{3/508: <s>Aitareya Brāhmaṇa</s> 7.30}]
[{3/509: E2,4: <s>bhakṣa nivṛttiṃ</s>}]

children.text: udgātṛcamasam ekaḥ śrutisaṃyogāt // MS_3,5.23 //
children.translated_text: One alone [should partake of] the <s>Udgātṛ</s>'s cup, because of the connection with the Vedic statement. // MS_3,5.23 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ - jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeteti. tatrāsti - praitu hotuś camasaḥ pra brahmaṇaḥ prodgātṝṇām iti. tatrāsti{*3/510*} samākhyānād bhakṣa ity uktam. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim eka evainaṃ camasam udgātā bhakṣayet, uta sarve [351]{*3/511*} bhakṣayeyuḥ? atha subrahmaṇyavarjitāś chandogā bhakṣayeyuḥ, athavā saha subrahmaṇyeneti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? eko bhakṣayed udgātaiva. kutaḥ? śrutisaṃyogāt, udgātaikaḥ śrutyā saṃyujyate - camasena prodgātṝṇām iti.
nanu bahuvacanaṃ śrūyate - tena bahavo bhakṣayeyuḥ. ucyate, śrūyate bahuvacanam, tad udgātṛprātipadikagatam, tad vivakṣitaṃ sad udgātṛbahutvaṃ brūyāt, ekaś cogātā, tatra bahutvaṃ śrūyamāṇam api na śaknuyād udgātṛbhedaṃ kartum. tasmād avivakṣitaṃ bahuvacanam, anumānaṃ hy etat, bahūnāṃ camasa iti. katham? yad bahuṣu prātipadikaṃ vartate, tato bahuvacanaṃ bhavati, bahuvacanaṃ tu tato dṛśyate, prodgātṝṇām iti. tasmān nūnaṃ bahūnāṃ camasa ity anumānam. pratyakṣaṃ tv eka udgātā, na dvitīyaḥ, na tṛtīyaḥ. anumānāc ca pratyakṣaṃ kāraṇaṃ balavad bhavet. tasmād ekasya camasaḥ, sa codgātur iti.
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' There it is [heard]: 'Let the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s cup go forth, and that of the <s>Brahman</s>, and those of the <s>Udgātṛs</s>.' It has been stated that there is partaking because of designation. There a doubt [arises] — should only one, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> himself, partake of this cup, or should all partake? Or should the chanters (<s>Chandogas</s>) excluding the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> partake, or together with the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>? What then is the prima facie view? One alone should partake — the <s>Udgātṛ</s> himself. Why? Because of the connection with the Vedic statement — the <s>Udgātṛ</s> alone is connected by the Vedic statement with the cup: 'Let the cups of the <s>Udgātṛs</s> go forth.'
Objection: the plural is heard — so many should partake. Reply: the plural is heard, [but] it pertains to the stem '<s>Udgātṛ</s>'; if it were intended [to denote plurality], it would denote multiplicity of <s>Udgātṛs</s>, but there is only one <s>Udgātṛ</s>. There, even though the plural is heard, it cannot create a division of <s>Udgātṛs</s>. Therefore the plural is unintended — for it is [merely] an inference: 'a cup of many [Udgātṛs].' How so? When a stem occurs among many, the plural results; and the plural is seen from that — '<s>prodgātṝṇām</s>' ('of the Udgātṛs'). Therefore this is merely an inference that it is a cup of many. But it is directly perceived that there is one <s>Udgātṛ</s> — not a second, not a third. And direct perception is a stronger authority than inference. Therefore the cup belongs to one, and he is the <s>Udgātṛ</s>.

children.text: sarve vā sarvasaṃyogāt // MS_3,5.24 //
children.translated_text: Or all [should partake], because of the connection of all. // MS_3,5.24 //

children.text: sarve vā bhakṣayeyuḥ, ekasminn udgātari bhakṣayati bahuvacanaṃ pramādādhītam{*3/512*} iti gamyate. na hi tad anūdyate, na vidhīyata iti. nanu sarveṣv api bhakṣayatsūdgātṛśabdaḥ pramādo gamyate. ucyate - lakṣaṇārtho 'pi tāvat saṃbhaviṣyati, udgātṛprabhṛtaya iti.
children.translated_text: Or all should partake — when one <s>Udgātṛ</s> alone partakes, the plural is understood as having been learned by error. For that [plural] is neither restated nor enjoined. Objection: even when all partake, the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' [in the singular] would indicate an error. Reply: even then, a figurative meaning will be possible — '<s>Udgātṛ</s> and those beginning with him.'

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/512: E2,4,6: pramādād adhītam}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{3/512: E2,4,6: <s>pramādād adhītam</s>}]

children.text: stotrakāriṇāṃ vā tatsaṃyogād bahuśruteḥ // MS_3,5.25 //
children.translated_text: Or [those] who perform the <s>Stotra</s> [should partake], because of the connection with that [class] and the plural statement. // MS_3,5.25 //

children.text: ucyate - naitad asti, bahūnāṃ camasa iti. kutaḥ? [352]{*3/513*} udgātṛśabdasya camasena saṃbandhaḥ pratyakṣeṇa vākyena, bahuvacanasya punar udgātṛśabdena śrutyā saṃbandhaḥ. anyena ṛtvijā tu bahuvacanasya naiva kaścid asti saṃbandhaḥ. tasmād bahūnāṃ camasa ity anupapannam iti. atrocyate - śaknoty ayam udgātṛśabdo bahutvaṃ vaditum, kriyāyogena, udnāyantīty udgātāraḥ. ke te? prastotā, udgātā, pratiharteti, tad etena bahuvacananirdeśenānumānikakriyāyoganimitta udgātṛśabdo vivakṣita ity avagamiṣyāmaḥ. bahuvacanaṃ hy evam avakḷptaṃ bhaviṣyati, udgātṛśabdaś ca. tasmāt stotrakāriṇāṃ camasa iti.
children.translated_text: It is said: this is not so — that it is 'a cup of many.' Why? The word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' has a connection with the cup through a directly perceived sentence; but the connection of the plural with the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' is through Vedic usage (<s>śruti</s>). No other priest has any connection whatsoever with the plural. Therefore 'a cup of many' is untenable. To this we reply: the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' is capable of denoting multiplicity — through connection with action: 'those who chant (<s>ud-gāyanti</s>) are <s>Udgātṛs</s>.' Who are they? The <s>Prastotṛ</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, and the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>. Thus, through this plural designation, we will understand that the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' is intended [in its] inferential, action-connected sense. For thus both the plural and the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' will be well-established, and there is no other defect. Therefore the cup belongs to those who perform the <s>Stotra</s>.

children.text: sarve tu vedasaṃyogāt kāraṇād ekadeśo syāt // MS_3,5.26 //
children.translated_text: Rather, all [<s>Chandogas</s> should partake], because of connection with the Veda; [in cases] where there is a reason, a part [of the whole] would apply. // MS_3,5.26 //

children.text:
sarve chandogāḥ sahasubrahmaṇyā bhakṣayeyuḥ. kim iti? gānasaṃyogād iti nāyaṃ pakṣa upapadyate. katham? ekas tatrodgānena saṃbandhaḥ{*3/514*}, itaro gānena, anyad dhi gānam, anyad udgānam, gītimātraṃ gānaṃ laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ ca. dvitīyaṃ sāmnaḥ parva, utpūrvasya gāyater abhidheyaṃ prasiddham. tatraika evodgīthaṃ karotīty eka evodgātā, na bahavaḥ. tasmād gānasaṃyogād bahavo bhaviṣyantīty etad api nopapadyate. kathaṃ tarhi? vedasaṃyogāt, audgātraṃ nāma pravacanam, tathā - audgātrāṇi karmāṇi, audgātrasya kartā vādhyetā vodgātety ucyate. katham? udgātuḥ karma, audgātram iti prasiddham. evaṃ ced vyaktam audgātrasya kartā, udgāteti gamyate. yasyodgātā prasiddhaḥ, tad viśiṣṭaṃ karmānākhyātam apy audgātram iti vadati. śabdaś ca yasyaudgātraṃ prasiddham, sa tasya kartāram udgāteti vadati, anākhyātam api, yathā yasyodameghaḥ prasiddhaḥ, sa tasyānākhyā-tam apy apatyam audameghir iti brūte, yasyaudameghiḥ, sa tasya [353]{*3/515*} pitaram anākhyātam apy udameghaṃ pratipadyate. evam audgātrasaṃbandhād upapadyata udgātṛśabdaḥ, prastotāpy udgātāpi pratihartāpi subrahmaṇyo 'pi. evaṃ bahuvacanam udgātṛśabdaś cobhayam apy upapannaṃ bhaviṣyati, na cānyaḥ kaścid doṣaḥ.
tasmād audgātreṇa saṃbaddhāśvatvāra udgātṛcamasaṃ bhakṣayeyur iti. yatra kāraṇam asti, tatrāpi subrahmaṇyā udgātāraḥ, yathā - udgātṛśabdo viniṣadyodgātāraḥ sāmnā stuvata iti stotrakāriṣu, tathedam{*3/516*} api vacanam, udgātāro nāpavyāhareyur uttamāyām eṣottamā ity apasubrahmaṇyānām eva.
children.translated_text:
All the <s>Chandogas</s>, including the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>, should partake. Why? The view that [only] those connected with chanting [should partake] is untenable. How so? One of them has a connection with the <s>Udgītha</s> (the central chant); the other has a connection with singing (<s>gāna</s>). But singing and <s>Udgītha</s> are different — singing is the mere act of singing, whether worldly or Vedic; [Udgītha] is the second section of the <s>Sāman</s>, the well-known denotation of the verb 'to sing' with the prefix <s>ud-</s>. There only one performs the <s>Udgītha</s>, so only one is the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, not many. Therefore the view that many would result from the connection with singing is also untenable. How then? Because of connection with the Veda — the <s>Audgātra</s> is the name of the [Vedic] recitation; thus: '<s>Audgātra</s> rites,' and 'the performer or student of the <s>Audgātra</s> is called <s>Udgātṛ</s>.' How? The rite of the <s>Udgātṛ</s> is <s>Audgātra</s> — this is well established. If so, it is clearly understood that the performer of the <s>Audgātra</s> is called <s>Udgātṛ</s>. One for whom the <s>Udgātṛ</s> is well established — that specific [Vedic] rite, though unnamed, is called <s>Audgātra</s>. And the word [functions] so that one for whom the <s>Audgātra</s> is well established calls that person's unnamed father <s>Udamegha</s>; and one for whom <s>Audameghi</s> [is established] understands that person's unnamed father as <s>Udamegha</s>. Similarly, through connection with the <s>Audgātra</s>, the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' is applicable — the <s>Prastotṛ</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>, and the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> too. Thus both the plural and the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' will be well-established, and there is no other defect.
Therefore, the four who are connected with the <s>Audgātra</s> should partake of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>'s cup. Where there is a reason, even there the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> [is counted among] the <s>Udgātṛs</s> — just as the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' [is used in]: 'Having sat down, the <s>Udgātṛs</s> chant with the <s>Sāman</s>' — [this applies] to the <s>Stotra</s>-performers. Likewise this statement too applies to [all] except the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>: 'The <s>Udgātṛs</s> should not speak out at the final [pressing]; this is the final one.'

children.text: grāvastuto bhakṣo na vidyate 'nāmnānāt // MS_3,5.27 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Grāvastut</s> does not have partaking, because [it] is not mentioned. // MS_3,5.27 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome grāvastun nāma hotṛpuruṣaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sa somaṃ bhakṣayet, neti. ucyate - grāvastun na bakṣayet. kutaḥ? yato 'sya bhakṣaṃ nāmananti. hāriyojane camasinām adhikāra iti manyamāna evaṃ ha smāha, nāsyāmnāyate bhakṣa{*3/517*} iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the <s>Grāvastut</s> is a priest belonging to the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s group. There a doubt [arises] — should he partake of <s>Soma</s>, or not? We say — the <s>Grāvastut</s> should not partake. Why? Because partaking is not mentioned for him. [<s>Hāriyojana</s>], considering it to be the domain of cup-holders, thus indeed said: 'Partaking is not mentioned for him.'

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/517: E1 gibt hāriyojane camasinām adhikāra iti manyamāna evaṃ ha smāha, nāsyāmnāyate bhakṣa in Klammern}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{3/517: E1 gives <s>hāriyojane camasinām adhikāra iti manyamāna evaṃ ha smāha, nāsyāmnāyate bhakṣa</s> in brackets}]

children.text: hāriyojane vā sarvasaṃyogāt // MS_3,5.28 //
children.translated_text: Or [he should partake] in the <s>Hāriyojana</s> [rite], because of the connection with all. // MS_3,5.28 //

children.text: hāriyojanasya vā grāvastutaṃ bhakṣayitāraṃ manyāmahe, evaṃ hy āmananti - yathā camasam anyāṃś camasāṃś camasino bhakṣayanti. [354]{*3/518*} athaitasya hāriyojanasya sarva eva lipsanta iti. yadā hāriyojanasya sarve lipsante, tadā grāvastud apīti.
children.translated_text: Or we consider the <s>Grāvastut</s> (praiser of pressing stones) to be the one who drinks the <s>Hārīyojana</s> (cup), for thus they teach: "Just as others drink the <s>camasa</s> cups, so do the <s>camasins</s> (cup-holders) drink." [354] Then, "all indeed desire this <s>Hārīyojana</s>." When all desire the <s>Hārīyojana</s>, then the <s>Grāvastut</s> also [desires it].

children.text: camasināṃ vā saṃnidhānāt // MS_3,5.29 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of the proximity of the <s>camasins</s>. // MS_3,5.29 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti grāvastuto hāriyojane bhakṣa iti, camasināṃ tatrādhikāro na sarveṣām. katham? camasinām eṣa vibhāgaḥ, camasino 'nyāṃś camasān, yathā - camasaṃ bhakṣayantīty anūdya, camasina eva vadati, athaitasya hāriyojanasya sarva eva lipsanta iti. ekaṃ hīdaṃ vākyam, athaitasyety athaśabdaprayogāt, anantaravṛttam apekṣate. atha{*3/519*} sarva evety evaśabdaḥ, sāmarthyāt sarvān pūrvaprakṛtān apekṣate, ato manyāmahe - yathā camasam anyāṃś camasāṃś camasino bhakṣayantīty anena pūrveṇa, athaitasya hāriyojanasyety etasyaikavākyatā bhavatīti. tena camasināṃ saṃnihitānām eṣa vibhāgaḥ, yathā camasam anyatra, hāriyojane tu sarva eveti.
children.translated_text: The word "or" sets aside the [previous] position. It is not the case that the <s>Grāvastut</s> has a share in the <s>Hārīyojana</s>; the entitlement there belongs to the <s>camasins</s>, not to all. How so? This division belongs to the <s>camasins</s> — "the <s>camasins</s> [drink] other <s>camasa</s> cups, just as they drink the [regular] <s>camasa</s>" — having stated this, it speaks only of the <s>camasins</s>: "then all indeed desire this <s>Hārīyojana</s>." For this is a single sentence, and the word "then" (<s>atha</s>) in "then of this" (<s>athaitasya</s>) looks to what immediately precedes it. And the word "all" (<s>sarva eva</s>), by its force, refers to all those previously mentioned. Therefore we hold that the earlier [statement] "just as others drink the <s>camasa</s> cups, the <s>camasins</s> drink" forms a single sentence with "then of this <s>Hārīyojana</s>." Thus this division belongs to the <s>camasins</s> who are proximate — in other [cups] as with the regular <s>camasa</s>, but in the <s>Hārīyojana</s>, all indeed [i.e., all camasins].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/519: E2,4 om. atha}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
*{3/519: E2,4 om. atha}*

children.text: sarveṣāṃ tu vidhitvāt tadarthā camasiśrutiḥ // MS_3,5.30 //
children.translated_text: But since it is an injunction for all, the mention of <s>camasins</s> serves that purpose. // MS_3,5.30 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti - camasina eva hāriyojane lipsanta iti, sarve tu vidhīyante hāriyojane, sarve bhakṣayantīti, na punaś camasina iti saṃbandhaḥ śakyate vidhātum. dvau hi saṃbandhāv asmin vākye 'pūrvau na śakyete vidhātum. tasmād anyā vacanavyaktiḥ.
[355]{*3/520*} kā punar asau? yathā camasam anyāṃś camasāṃś camasino bhakṣayantīty anuvādaḥ, camasinaś camasān bhakṣayanty eva, te bhakṣayanto yathā camasam eva, athaitasya hāriyojanasya na kevalaṃ camasinaḥ, sarva eveti. kim evaṃ bhaviṣyati? sarvaśabdaś ca sarvān vadan naikadeśe kalpito bhaviṣyati. na ca, dvau saṃbandhāv apūrvāv ekasmin vākye bhaviṣyataḥ. tasmād eṣa pakṣo jyāyān iti tadarthā hy eṣā camasiśrutiḥ, hāriyojanasya praśāṃsārthā{*3/521*} camasinaḥ kīrtyante hāriyojanaṃ praśaṃsitum. katham? mahābhāgo hi hāriyojanaḥ, yasmāt tatra sarve lipsante, anyāṃś camasān ekaikaḥ, na te mahābhāgāḥ, nyūnā hāriyojanād iti.
children.translated_text:
The word "but" sets aside the [previous] position. It is not the case that only the <s>camasins</s> desire the <s>Hārīyojana</s>; rather, all are enjoined regarding the <s>Hārīyojana</s> — "all drink" — and the connection "only the <s>camasins</s>" cannot be established as an injunction. For two unprecedented connections cannot be established in one sentence. Therefore, a different interpretation of the words [is needed].
[355] What then is it? "Just as others drink the <s>camasa</s> cups, the <s>camasins</s> drink" is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) — the <s>camasins</s> do indeed drink the <s>camasa</s> cups, and they drink just as [they drink] the regular <s>camasa</s>; but of this <s>Hārīyojana</s>, not only the <s>camasins</s>, but all indeed [drink]. What follows from this? The word "all" (<s>sarva</s>), denoting everyone, will not be restricted to only a part. And two unprecedented connections will not arise in one sentence. Therefore this position is stronger — for this mention of <s>camasins</s> serves that purpose; the <s>camasins</s> are mentioned to praise the <s>Hārīyojana</s>. How? The <s>Hārīyojana</s> is of great fortune, since all desire it there; [but] other <s>camasa</s> cups each [are desired by only] one, they are not of great fortune — they are inferior to the <s>Hārīyojana</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/520: E2: 4,463; E4: 4,740; E6: 1,240}*
*{3/521: E1 gibt hāriyojanasya praśāṃsārthā in Klammern}*

children.text: vaṣaṭkārāc ca bhakṣayet // MS_3,5.31 //
children.translated_text: And one should drink because of the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation). // MS_3,5.31 //

children.text: atha kiṃ samākhyaivaikā bhakṣakāraṇam? neti brūmah, vaṣaṭkārāc ca bhakṣayet, vaṣaṭkāraś ca bhakṣaṇe nimittam. katham? vacanāt, evaṃ hi śrūyate - vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣa iti, bhakṣaṇasyāprāptatvāt, na prāthamy avidhānārtha eṣa śabdaḥ, prāthamy aviśiṣṭaṃ bhakṣaṇam eva vidadhātīti.
children.translated_text: Now, is designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) alone the cause of drinking? No, we say — one should drink because of the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> as well; the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is also a cause for drinking. How? Because of a textual statement (<s>vacana</s>), for thus it is heard: "The first drink belongs to the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>." Since drinking is not otherwise established, this word does not prescribe the priority [of drinking], but prescribes drinking itself, which is qualified by priority.

children.text: homābhiṣavābhyāṃ ca // MS_3,5.32 //
children.translated_text: And [one should drink] because of the <s>homa</s> (oblation) and <s>abhiṣava</s> (pressing). // MS_3,5.32 //

children.text: aparam api kāraṇaṃ homābhiṣavau. katham? havirdhāne [356]{*3/522*} grāvabhir abhiṣutyāhavanīye hutvā pratyañcaḥ parety sadasi bhakṣān bhakṣayantīti{*3/523*}. na tāvat, eṣa kramo vidhīyate, home nirvṛtte tato bhakṣaṇasyāprāptatvāt{*3/524*}. dvayoś ca kramayor vidhānāt, abhiṣutya hutveti vākyaṃ bhidyeta. arthena ca prāptatvād asya kramasya. na hy akṛte prayojane kaścit pratipādanam arhati. na ca, bhakṣaṇāṅgabhāvena homābhiṣavau codyete. abhiṣavasya homārthatvāt, homasya ca phalārthatvāt. tasmād dhomābhiṣavayoḥ kartṝṇāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate. ye 'bhiṣuṇvanti juhvati ca, te bhakṣayantīti.
children.translated_text: There is yet another cause — the <s>homa</s> and <s>abhiṣava</s>. How? "Having pressed with the stones in the <s>Havirdhāna</s> [356] and having offered in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, they go back westward and drink the draughts in the assembly." Now, this sequence is not being enjoined — since drinking is not established after the oblation is completed. And since two sequences are enjoined — "having pressed, having offered" — the sentence would be split. And because this sequence is established by the nature of things — for no one deserves instruction in what is already accomplished without purpose. Nor are the <s>homa</s> and <s>abhiṣava</s> prompted as subsidiaries of drinking; rather, pressing is for the sake of oblation, and oblation is for the sake of the [sacrificial] result. Therefore, drinking is enjoined for those who perform the <s>homa</s> and <s>abhiṣava</s>. Those who press and offer — they drink.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/522: E2: 4,466; E4: 4,744; E6: 1,241}*
*{3/523: Vgl. Tait.S. 6.2.11.4}*
*{3/524: E2,4: tato bhakṣaṇam iti, bhakṣaṇasyāprāptatvāt}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
*{3/522: E2: 4,466; E4: 4,744; E6: 1,241}*
*{3/523: Cf. Tait.S. 6.2.11.4}*
*{3/524: E2,4: tato bhakṣaṇam iti, bhakṣaṇasyāprāptatvāt}*

children.text: pratyakṣopadeśāc camasānām avyaktaḥ śeṣe // MS_3,5.33 //
children.translated_text: Because of the explicit instruction regarding the <s>camasa</s> cups, [the general cause] is unmanifest in the remainder. // MS_3,5.33 //

children.text: idaṃ śrūyate - praitu hotuś camasaḥ pra brahmaṇaḥ prodgātṝṇām iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - camaseṣu homābhiṣavayoḥ kartāro vaṣaṭkartāraś ca kiṃ bhakṣayeyuḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? na bhakṣayeyuḥ, pratyakṣopadeśāc camasānāṃ camasinaḥ prati. praitu hotuś camasa ityevamādibhir viśeṣavacanaiḥ, homābhiṣavakāriṇāṃ{*3/525*} sāmānyavākyena, yaḥ somo bhakṣaṇena saṃskartavyaḥ, sa camaseṣu camasibhir iti, athedānīm anyan nimittaṃ kva bhaviṣyati? avyaktaḥ sāmānyanimittaḥ kva? śeṣe bhaviṣyati, yatra na camasinaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is heard: "Let the <s>camasa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> go forth, [let that] of the <s>Brahman</s>, [let those] of the <s>Udgātṛs</s>." There a doubt [arises]: should those who perform the <s>homa</s> and <s>abhiṣava</s> and those who utter the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> drink from the <s>camasa</s> cups, or not? What is the prima facie view? They should not drink, because of the explicit instruction regarding the <s>camasa</s> cups directed to the <s>camasins</s> — "Let the <s>camasa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> go forth" and similar specific statements [are for the camasins], while the general statement for those who perform <s>homa</s> and <s>abhiṣava</s> [means that] the <s>Soma</s> that is to be consecrated by drinking belongs in the <s>camasa</s> cups to the <s>camasins</s>. Now then, where will the other cause [the general one] apply? The unmanifest general cause will apply in the remainder — where the <s>camasins</s> are not [present].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/525: E2,4: homābhiṣavādikāriṇāṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
*{3/525: E2,4: homābhiṣavādikāriṇāṃ}*

children.text: syād vā kāraṇabhāvād anirdeśaś camasānāṃ kartus tadvacanatvāt // MS_3,5.34 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because there is a cause, the non-mention of the <s>camasa</s> cups [is explained by the fact that] the agent [is mentioned] because of being the speaker of that [injunction]. // MS_3,5.34 //

children.text: syād vā camaseṣu vaṣaṭkartrādīnāṃ bhakṣaḥ, prāpyate hi teṣāṃ tatra kāraṇam, na ca pratiṣidhyate. nanu camasināṃ pratyakṣo[357]{*3/526*}padeśān nivarteran. ucyate - anirdeśaś camasānāṃ kartus tadvacanatvāt, praitu hotuś camasa ityevamādayaḥ śabdāḥ na śaknuvanti vaṣaṭkartrādīn pratiṣeddhum, upadeṣṭāro hi te, na pratiṣeddhāraḥ, tasmād vaṣaṭkartrādayo 'pi camaseṣu bhakṣayeyuḥ.
children.translated_text: Or rather, the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterer and others do have a share in the <s>camasa</s> cups, for their cause is established there, and it is not prohibited. But would they not be excluded by the explicit instruction directed to the <s>camasins</s>? [357] We reply: the non-mention of the <s>camasa</s> cups [is explained by the fact that] the agent [is mentioned] because of being the speaker of that — statements like "Let the <s>camasa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> go forth" are unable to prohibit the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterer and others, for they are prescribers, not prohibitors. Therefore the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterer and others should also drink from the <s>camasa</s> cups.

children.text: camase cānyadarśanāt // MS_3,5.35 //
children.translated_text: And because in the <s>camasa</s> cup, others are seen [participating]. // MS_3,5.35 //

children.text: camase cānyāṃś camasino darśayati - camasāṃś camasādhvaryave prayacchati. tān sa vaṣaṭkartre haratīti. eko hi svaś camaso vaṣaṭkartre hriyate, tena bahuharaṇadarśanaṃ nāvakalpate, yadi vaṣaṭkartrādayo na camaseṣu bhakṣayeyuḥ. tasmād bhakṣayantīti.
children.translated_text: And in the <s>camasa</s> cup, others — <s>camasins</s> — are shown: "He gives the <s>camasa</s> cups to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> of the <s>camasa</s>. He carries them to the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterer." For one's own <s>camasa</s> cup alone is carried to the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterer; therefore, the showing of multiple carryings would not be possible if the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterer and others did not drink from the <s>camasa</s> cups. Therefore they do drink.

children.text: atha yatraikasmin pātre bahavo bhakṣayanti, kas tatra krama iti. ucyate -
children.translated_text: Now, where many drink from a single vessel, what is the order there? It is stated:

children.text: ekapātre kramād adhvaryuḥ pūrvo bhakṣayet // MS_3,5.36 //
children.translated_text: When [drinking] from a single vessel, by order, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should drink first. // MS_3,5.36 //

children.text: tasya hi kramo bhakṣayitum, yasya haste somaḥ.
children.translated_text: For the order of drinking belongs to the one in whose hand is the <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: hotā vā mantravarṇāt // MS_3,5.37 //
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Hotṛ</s> [should drink first], because of the wording of the <s>mantra</s>. // MS_3,5.37 //

children.text: hotā vā pūrvo bhakṣayet, mantravarṇāt, mantravarṇo hi tathā - hotuś cit pūrve haviradyam āśateti{*3/527*}, tathā - hoteva naḥ prathamaḥ pāhīti{*3/528*}.
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Hotṛ</s> should drink first, because of the wording of the <s>mantra</s>, for the <s>mantra</s> wording states thus: "Before even the <s>Hotṛ</s>, they have partaken of the oblation-food," and likewise: "Like the <s>Hotṛ</s>, drink thou first for us."

children.text: vacanāc ca // MS_3,5.38 //
children.translated_text: And because of a textual statement. // MS_3,5.38 //

children.text: vacanam idaṃ bhavati - vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣa iti. vacana[358]{*3/529*}m evedam, na mantavyam, anekaguṇavidhānād avivakṣitaṃ prāthamyam iti. aprāptatvāt prāthamyasya, nāyam anuvādaḥ, vidhir eva. samāsena ca vidadhato nānekaguṇavidhānaṃ duṣkaram.
children.translated_text: There is this statement: "The first drink belongs to the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>." [358] This is indeed an injunctive statement; it should not be thought that because it prescribes multiple qualities, the priority is not intended. Since priority is not otherwise established, this is not a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) but an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) indeed. And when prescribing in a compound, establishing multiple qualities is not difficult.

children.text: kāraṇānupūrvyāc ca // MS_3,5.39 //
children.translated_text: And because of the order of causes. // MS_3,5.39 //

children.text: prathaṃ hi vaṣaṭkaraṇaṃ nimittaṃ hotuḥ, tato homo 'dhvaryor nimittam. nimittānupūrvyāc ca naimittikānupūrvye kramānurodhaḥ.
children.translated_text: For first the uttering of <s>vaṣaṭ</s> is the cause, belonging to the <s>Hotṛ</s>; then the oblation (<s>homa</s>) is the cause, belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. And the conformity of the order of effects to the order of causes [supports this].

children.text: vacanād anujñātabhakṣaṇam{*3/530*} // MS_3,5.40 //
children.translated_text: Drinking is [to be done only] after receiving permission, because of a textual statement. // MS_3,5.40 //

children.text: atha ya ekapātre somo 'nekena bhakṣyate, kiṃ tatrānujñāpya, ananujñāpya vā bhakṣayitavyam, utānujñāpyaiveti. lāghavād aniyamo prāpta ucyate - anujñāpya bhakṣayitavyam iti. kasmāt? vacanāt, idaṃ vacanaṃ bhavati - tasmāt somo nānupahūtena peya iti. upahvānaṃ cānujñāpanam. prāptisūtram etat{*3/531*}.
children.translated_text: Now, when <s>Soma</s> is drunk by many from a single vessel, should one drink with or without asking permission, or only after asking permission? Due to simplicity, the prima facie view holds there is no restriction. We say: one should drink only after asking permission. Why? Because of a textual statement — there is this statement: "Therefore <s>Soma</s> should not be drunk without being invited." And the invitation (<s>upahvāna</s>) is the permission. This is the prima facie sūtra.

children.text:
athānujñātena bhakṣayitavyam iti sthite, kiṃ laukikena vacanenānujñāpayitavyam, uta vaidikeneti.
aniyamāl laukikeneti prāpta ucyate -
children.translated_text:
Now, it being established that one should drink with permission, should one grant permission with a worldly expression or a Vedic one?
Since there is no restriction, [the use of] a worldly [expression] is the prima facie view. We say:

children.text: tadupahūta upahūyasvety{*3/532*} anenānujñāpayel liṅgāt // MS_3,5.41 //
children.translated_text: "O invoked one, invite thou" — with this [formula] one should grant permission, because of the indicative mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // MS_3,5.41 //

children.text: anujñāpanaliṅgo 'yaṃ mantraḥ, liṅgāt, anujñāpane samāmnātaḥ, [359]{*3/533*} sāmarthyād vinijujyate, tatra kṛte 'rthe laukiko nivartate.
children.translated_text: This <s>mantra</s> has the indicative mark of granting permission; because of the <s>liṅga</s>, it is traditionally taught in the context of granting permission. [359] By its capacity, it is assigned [to that function], and when that purpose is accomplished thereby, the worldly [expression] ceases.

children.text: tatrārthāt prativacanam // MS_3,5.42 //
children.translated_text: There, from the meaning [of the mantra], the reply [is derived]. // MS_3,5.42 //

children.text:
etad avagatam - tadupahūta upahūyasvety{*3/534*} anenānujñāpayed{*3/535*} iti. atha prativacane saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ laukikaṃ prativacanam utaitad eveti. kiṃ prāptam? etad vaidikam, praśne viniyuktam. laukikam anyat prativacanaṃ bhavitaum arhati. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tatraitad eva prativacanam iti.
nanu praśnaliṅgam etad upahūyasveti{*3/536*}. ucyate - yad asya pūrvam, upahūta iti prativacanasya samartham, tat prativacanakārye baviṣyati. āha - viparītam etat samāmnānam, pūrvaṃ hi praśnena bhavitavyam, tataḥ prativacanena. ucyate - arthāt, pūrvaṃ prativacanakārye bhaviṣyati, artho hi kramād balīyān iti.
children.translated_text:
This is understood: "O invoked one, invite thou" — with this one should grant permission. Now there is a doubt regarding the reply: is the reply worldly or this very [Vedic formula]? What is the prima facie view? This is Vedic, employed in the context of a question; another worldly reply should be possible. Given this, we say: there, this very [formula] serves as the reply.
But is not this "invite thou" (<s>upahūyasva</s>) an indicative mark of a question? We reply: that which precedes it — "O invoked one" (<s>upahūta</s>) — is capable of serving as a reply; it will function for the purpose of reply. [The objector] says: this traditional teaching is in reverse order, for first there should be a question, then a reply. We reply: from the meaning — the first part will serve the purpose of reply. For meaning is stronger than sequence.

children.text: tadekapātrāṇāṃ samavāyāt // MS_3,5.43 //
children.translated_text: That [permission] is for those sharing the same vessel, because of [their] being together. // MS_3,5.43 //

children.text: idaṃ saṃdihyate - kiṃ yaḥ kaścid anujñāpayitavyaḥ, uta samānapātra iti. aviśeṣābhidhānād yaḥ kaścid iti prāpta ucyate - tat khalv anujñāpanam ekapātrāṇāṃ syāt. kutaḥ? anujñāpanam ihāṅgam, anujñāpanasya caitad rūpam, yatrānyena kartavyam anyaś cikīrṣet, so 'numanyasveti brūte, sahabhoja[360]{*3/537*}nādi vācaritukāmaś cittam anyasyānukūlayati. tad etan nānāpātreṣu naiva saṃbhavati. na hi tatrānyena kartavyam, anyo vā cikīrṣatīti{*3/538*}. sahabhojanādau vā padārthe{*3/539*} saṃmānayati. ekapātre tu some sādhāraṇe saṃskartavye nyāyena samo vibhāgaḥ prāpnoti, tatrāvibhajya pīyamāne kadācid anyena pātavyam anyaḥ pibet, tatrānujñāpanaṃ saṃbhavati, tvayārdhaṃ pātavyam, mayār-dham. kadācid aham abhyādhikaṃ nyūnaṃ vā pibeyam, tadanujñātum arhasīti, ekapātre vā pānaṃ tvayā sahācarann ahaṃ tava cittaprasādānaṃ vyāhanyām iti saṃbhavaty anujñāpanā. tasmād eka-pātreṣv evaitat syād iti.
children.translated_text: This is doubted: should anyone at all be asked for permission, or [only] one sharing the same vessel? Since there is no specific designation, the prima facie view holds "anyone at all." We say: that permission should be for those sharing one vessel. Why? Permission here is a subsidiary element, and the nature of permission is such that where something is to be done by one person and another wishes to do it, he says "please consent," or wishing to practice communal eating and the like, he conciliates the mind of another. [360] This is simply not possible with separate vessels, for there what is to be done by one is not [desired by] another, nor does another wish to do it. Or in the case of communal eating and such, he shows respect. But when <s>Soma</s> in a single vessel is a common [substance] to be consecrated, by right an equal share is obtained. There, when it is being drunk without division, at some point what is to be drunk by one, another might drink; there permission is appropriate — "half is to be drunk by you, half by me; at some point I might drink more or less, please grant permission for that." Or, "drinking from one vessel together with you, I might impair the satisfaction of your mind" — thus permission is appropriate. Therefore, this [rule] should apply only in the case of shared vessels.

children.text: yājyāpanayenāpanīto bhakṣaḥ pravaravat // MS_3,5.44 //
children.translated_text: The <s>bhakṣa</s> (ritual eating portion) is removed by the removal of the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), like the <s>pravara</s> (priestly lineage recitation). // MS 3,5.44 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ, tatra ṛtuyāgeṣu śrūyate - yajamānasya yājyā so 'bhipreṣyati hotar etad yajeti svayaṃ yā niṣpadya yajatīti. yadā svayaṃ yajati, tadā saṃdehaḥ - kim asya bhakṣo 'sti, nāstīti. tad ucyate - yājyāyām apanīyamānāyāṃ nāpanīyeta bhakṣaṇam, hotur eva tu bhakṣaṇaṃ syāt, na yajamānasyeti. kutaḥ? anyā hi yājyā, anyad bhakṣaṇam, na cānyasminn apanīyamāne 'nyad apanīyate. yathā tasyām eva yājyāyām apanīyamānāyāṃ pravaro nāpanīyate, tadvad etad apīti.
nanu{*3/540*} yājyāyā adhi vaṣaṭkarotīti, yatra yājyā, tatra vaṣaṭkāraḥ, yatra vaṣaṭkāraḥ, tatra bhakṣaṇam apīti. na [351]{*3/541*} ity ucyate, na tāvad yājyāyām avayavabhūto vaṣaṭkāraḥ, yena yājyāgrahaṇenāsau gṛhyeta{*3/542*}. yat tu tasyā adhi vaṣaṭkarotīti, anyenāpi prayujyamānāyā upari hotā vaṣaṭkariṣyati, yājyāpanayo hi vacanāt, na vaṣaṭkārāpanayaḥ. yāvad vacanam, vācanikaṃ bhavaty eva, vacanaṃ hi tadviṣayam eva.
children.translated_text:
There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; there in the seasonal sacrifices (<s>ṛtuyāgas</s>) it is heard: 'The <s>yājyā</s> of the sacrificer — he commands thus: "O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice with this." He himself, having composed [the verse], sacrifices.' When he himself sacrifices, the doubt arises: does he have a <s>bhakṣa</s> (ritual eating portion), or not? To this it is said: when the <s>yājyā</s> is removed, the <s>bhakṣa</s> should not be removed; rather, the <s>bhakṣa</s> should belong only to the <s>Hotṛ</s> (priest), not to the sacrificer. Why? Because the <s>yājyā</s> is one thing and the <s>bhakṣa</s> is another, and when one thing is removed, the other is not removed. Just as when that same <s>yājyā</s> is removed, the <s>pravara</s> is not removed — so too is this [<s>bhakṣa</s>].
[Objection:] But 'he pronounces the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> over the <s>yājyā</s>' — where there is the <s>yājyā</s>, there is the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>; where there is the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, there is the <s>bhakṣa</s> too. [Reply:] It is said: no — the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is not a constituent part of the <s>yājyā</s>, such that it would be included by the mention of the <s>yājyā</s>. As for 'he pronounces the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> over the <s>yājyā</s>' — even when [the <s>yājyā</s>] is employed by another, the <s>Hotṛ</s> will pronounce the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> over it. For the removal of the <s>yājyā</s> is by [Vedic] statement, not the removal of the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>. What is [covered] by the statement applies precisely to that extent — for the statement is about that subject alone.

children.text: yaṣṭur vā kāraṇāgamāt // MS_3,5.45 //
children.translated_text: Or [the <s>bhakṣa</s> should be] for the sacrificer, because of the arrival of the cause. // MS 3,5.45 //

children.text:
yaṣṭur vā bhakṣaḥ syāt. kutaḥ? kāraṇāgamāt, bhakṣasya kāraṇaṃ vaṣaṭkāraḥ, sa ca yājyāyām āgacchantyām āgacchati. evaṃ hi śrūyate - yājyāyā adhi vaṣaṭkarotīti.
nanv etad uktam - yajamānenāpi prayujyamānāyāṃ hotā{*3/543*} adhi{*3/544*} vaṣaṭkarotīti. naiṣa samādhiḥ, anavānatā yaṣṭavyam, vaṣaṭkāreṇa yāgaḥ kriyate, na yājyāmatreṇa. tasmād ā vaṣaṭkārān nāvānitavyaṃ yajamānena, anyaś ced vaṣaṭkuryād avānyād yajamānaḥ. na ca yajeta. yaṣṭavye cāsau codyate, na yājyāmātravacane, svayaṃ nipadya yajatīti sāṅgasya niṣadyayāge vidhānāt.
children.translated_text:
Or the <s>bhakṣa</s> should be for the sacrificer. Why? Because of the arrival of the cause — the cause of the <s>bhakṣa</s> is the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, and that arrives when the <s>yājyā</s> arrives. For thus it is heard: 'He pronounces the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> over the <s>yājyā</s>.'
[Objection:] But this was said — that even when [the <s>yājyā</s>] is employed by the sacrificer, the <s>Hotṛ</s> pronounces the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> over it. [Reply:] This resolution is not correct — one should sacrifice without interruption; the sacrifice is performed by the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, not by the <s>yājyā</s> alone. Therefore, the sacrificer should not interrupt up to the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>; if another were to pronounce the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, the sacrificer would have to interrupt. And he would not sacrifice. Moreover, he is enjoined in [the context of] 'one should sacrifice,' not in a mere statement about the <s>yājyā</s> — 'he himself, having composed [the verse], sacrifices' — because of the injunction of the sacrifice with all its parts (<s>sāṅga</s>) through the sitting sacrifice (<s>niṣadyayāga</s>).
