children.text: pravṛttatvāt pravarasyānapāyaḥ // MS_3,5.46 //
children.translated_text: Because of [the <s>pravara</s>'s] having already occurred, [there is] no removal of the <s>pravara</s>. // MS 3,5.46 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - yathā pravaro nāpanīyate, evaṃ bhakṣo 'pīti. ucyate - aśakyatvāt pravaro nāpanīyate, atikrānto hi sa katham apanīyeta hotuḥ? bhraṣṭe cāvasare, anuṣṭhīyamāno yajamānasya viguṇaḥ syāt. na ca viguṇaḥ kathaṃcid arthaṃ sādhayet. nātra codakena prāpnoti. athocyate - yac chakyaṃ tac codakena prāpitam, yan na śakyam, na tat prāpitam iti. prakṛtir iyam, [362]{*3/545*} apūrvasyātra vidhānam, yādṛśam uktam, tādṛśaṃ yadi śakyate kartavyam. yadi na śakyate, yatraiva śakyate, tatraiva kāryam. na yatra viguṇam iti. tasmāt pravarasyānapāyo yukto na bhakṣasyeti.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was said — 'just as the <s>pravara</s> is not removed, so too the <s>bhakṣa</s>' — it is said: the <s>pravara</s> is not removed because it is impossible [to remove it], for it has already passed — how could it be removed from the <s>Hotṛ</s>? And since the [proper] occasion has lapsed, if performed [now] it would be defective for the sacrificer. And a defective [rite] cannot in any way accomplish the purpose. The enjoiner does not [intend to] obtain [such a result] here. [Objection:] But it is said: what is possible has been obtained by the enjoiner; what is not possible has not been obtained. [Reply:] This is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>); the injunction of the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) [element] is here. Whatever has been stated — if it can be done, it should be done in that form. If it cannot be done, it should be done only where it can be done — not where it would be defective. Therefore, the non-removal of the <s>pravara</s> is justified, but not [the non-removal] of the <s>bhakṣa</s>.

children.text: phalacamaso naimittiko bhakṣavikāraḥ śrutisaṃyogāt // MS_3,5.47 //
children.translated_text: The <s>phalacamasa</s> (fruit-cup) is an occasional modification of the <s>bhakṣa</s> (ritual eating), because of the connection with the [Vedic] statement. // MS 3,5.47 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - sa yadi rājanyaṃ vā{*3/546*} vaiṣyaṃ vā yājayet, sa yadi somaṃ vibhakṣayiṣet, nyagrodhastibhīr āhṛtya tāḥ saṃpiṣya dadhany unmṛjya tamasmai bhakṣaṃ prayacchen na somam iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ phalacamaso bhakṣavikāraḥ, utejyāvikāra iti. kiṃ phalacamasaṃ bhakṣayed ity arthaḥ, uta phalacamasena yajeteti{*3/547*}. kiṃ prāptam? phalacamaso naimittiko bhakṣavikāraḥ, bhakṣaṇena hi śrutenaikavākyatā bhavatīti, tasmai bhakṣaṃ prayacched iti, na, tena yajetetiśabdo 'sti, tasmād bhakṣavikāraḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'If he should have a <s>kṣatriya</s> or a <s>vaiśya</s> perform the sacrifice, if he should wish to give him <s>Soma</s> to drink, having gathered <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) shoots, having ground them, having mixed them in curds, he should give him that as a <s>bhakṣa</s>, not <s>Soma</s>.' There the doubt arises: is the <s>phalacamasa</s> a modification of the <s>bhakṣa</s>, or a modification of the sacrifice (<s>ijyā</s>)? Is the meaning 'he should eat the <s>phalacamasa</s>,' or 'he should sacrifice with the <s>phalacamasa</s>'? What is the prima facie view? The <s>phalacamasa</s> is an occasional modification of the <s>bhakṣa</s>, for the single-sentence relationship is with the [word] '<s>bhakṣa</s>' that is heard — 'he should give him the <s>bhakṣa</s>' — and there is no word 'he should sacrifice with that.' Therefore, it is a modification of the <s>bhakṣa</s>.

children.text:

*{3/547: E1 gibt kiṃ phalacamasaṃ bhakṣayed ity arthaḥ, uta phalacamasena yajeteti in Klammern}*
children.translated_text:

children.text: ijyāvikāro vā saṃskārasya tadarthatvāt // MS_3,5.48 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a modification of the sacrifice, because the preparation is for that purpose. // MS 3,5.48 //

children.text:
ijyāvikāro vā phalacamasaḥ phalacamasena yajetety arthaḥ{*3/548*}. katham? yad etad bhakṣaṇam, etat somasaṃskārārtham, phalacamasyāpi yadi bhakṣaṇaṃ phalacamasasaṃskārārtham, phalacamasasyānyatrānupayogād anarthakam. atha bhakṣaṇaṃ pradhānam. tathā - na somam [363]{*3/549*} ity anuvādo nāvakalpate. yadi tv ijyāvikāro{*3/550*} bhavet, tataḥ phalacamasasaṃskāro 'vakalpate. tasmād ijyāvikāraḥ.
āha - kathaṃ yajisaṃbandhe 'sati, ijyāvikāro bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate - asti yajisaṃbandhaḥ. katham iti. yadi rājanyaṃ vā{*3/551*} vaiṣyaṃ vā yājayet, nyagrodhastibhīḥ saṃpiṣya tam asmai bhakṣaṃ prayacchet, yājayitum iti gamyate. bhakṣasaṃbandhe hi na pūrvam uttareṇa saṃbadhyate, yadi somaṃ bhakṣaṇena saṃskartum icchen nyagrodhastibhīḥ saṃskuryād iti. tasmān na bhakṣaṇasaṃbandhaḥ. yāgo hi prakṛto 'sti, tena saha saṃbhantsyate, na doṣo bhaviṣyati.
nanu tasmai bhakṣaṃ prayacched itivacanād bhakṣasādhanam iti gamyate, na, yāgasādhanam iti, bhakṣaśabdānantaryāt. ucyate - śrūyamāṇe saṃbandhe 'narthakam iti kṛtvā prakṛtasaṃabdha ity ucyate. kathaṃ tu bhakṣasaṃbandha iti. yad dhi{*3/552*} yāgadravyaṃ bhakṣayitavyam, tac codakena bhavati, tasmād bhakṣasaṃbandhaṃ labhate, bhakṣasaṃbandhena ca yāgasaṃbandha eva lakṣyate, yadi tenejyate, tataḥ sa bhakṣo bhavati, tasmād bhakṣavacanāt sutarāṃ tenejyata iti gamyate, saiṣā vyavadhāraṇakalpanā. tasmai bhaksaṃ prayacchet, tam asmai bhakṣaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ, yathā sa bhakṣo bhavati, tathā kuryād iti, yadi ca tenejyate, tato 'yaṃ bhakṣo bhavati. tasmāt tena yaṣṭavyam iti.
children.translated_text:
Or the <s>phalacamasa</s> is a modification of the sacrifice — the meaning is 'he should sacrifice with the <s>phalacamasa</s>.' How? The <s>bhakṣa</s> (ritual eating) [of <s>Soma</s>] is for the purpose of consecrating the <s>Soma</s>; similarly, if the <s>bhakṣa</s> of the <s>phalacamasa</s> is for the purpose of consecrating the <s>phalacamasa</s>, it would be purposeless without the <s>phalacamasa</s> being used elsewhere [i.e., in sacrifice]. But if the <s>bhakṣa</s> is the primary [purpose], then 'not <s>Soma</s>' cannot be construed as a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>). However, if it is a modification of the sacrifice, then the consecration of the <s>phalacamasa</s> is construable. Therefore, it is a modification of the sacrifice.
[Objection:] It is said: how can it be a modification of the sacrifice without a connection with the verb 'to sacrifice'? [Reply:] It is said: there is a connection with sacrificing. How? 'If he should have a <s>kṣatriya</s> or a <s>vaiśya</s> perform the sacrifice, having ground the <s>nyagrodha</s> shoots, he should give him that <s>bhakṣa</s>' — it is understood as 'in order to have [him] sacrifice.' For in connection with the <s>bhakṣa</s>, the earlier [phrase] is not connected with the later — 'if he should wish to consecrate <s>Soma</s> through the <s>bhakṣa</s>, he should consecrate with <s>nyagrodha</s> shoots.' Therefore, there is no connection with the <s>bhakṣa</s> [alone]. For the sacrifice is under discussion, and [the <s>phalacamasa</s>] will be connected with that — there will be no fault.
[Objection:] But from the statement 'he should give him the <s>bhakṣa</s>,' it is understood as a means for the <s>bhakṣa</s>, not as a means for sacrifice. [Reply:] It is said: when a connection is heard [but would be] purposeless, it is said to be connected with what is under discussion. How then is there a connection with the <s>bhakṣa</s>? Because the sacrificial substance that is to be consumed becomes so through the enjoiner. Therefore, it obtains a connection with the <s>bhakṣa</s>; and through the connection with the <s>bhakṣa</s>, a connection with the sacrifice is indicated. For if one sacrifices with it, then it becomes a <s>bhakṣa</s>. Therefore, from the statement about the <s>bhakṣa</s>, it is understood all the more that one should sacrifice with it. This is the determination by elimination (<s>vyavadhāraṇakalpanā</s>): 'he should give him the <s>bhakṣa</s>' means 'he should make it the <s>bhakṣa</s> for him' — that is, he should make it such that it becomes a <s>bhakṣa</s>; and if one sacrifices with it, then it becomes a <s>bhakṣa</s>. Therefore, one should sacrifice with it.

children.text: homaviśeṣavacanaṃ bhavati - yadānyāṃś camasāñ{*3/553*} juhvati, athaitasya darbhataruṇakenopahatya juhotīti. ijyāvikāre sati darbhataruṇakeneti juhotau guṇavacanam avakalpate. tasmād apījyāvikāraḥ.
children.translated_text: There is a statement specifying a particular oblation: 'When they offer the other cups, then he offers this one, striking [it] with a blade of fresh grass.' When it is a modification of the sacrifice, the qualification 'with a blade of fresh grass' with respect to the oblation verb is construable. Therefore, this too is a modification of the sacrifice.
Page break marker: 364

children.text: camasaiś ca tulyakālatvāt // MS_3,5.50 //
children.translated_text: And because of the simultaneity with the [other] cups. // MS 3,5.50 //

children.text: yadānyāṃś cāmasān unnayanti, athainaṃ camasam unnayantīti. ijyāvikāre saty unnayanadarśanaṃ yujyate, na bhakṣavikāre. tasmād apījyāvikāraḥ.
children.translated_text: 'When they elevate the other cups, then they elevate this cup' — the observation of elevation is appropriate when it is a modification of the sacrifice, not when it is a modification of the <s>bhakṣa</s>. Therefore, this too is a modification of the sacrifice.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_3,5.51 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // MS 3,5.51 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmaḥ - ijyāvikāra iti. kutaḥ? liṅgadarśanāt. kiṃ liṅgaṃ bhavati? somapratiṣedhānuvādaḥ, tasmai bhakṣaṃ prayacchet, na somam iti, ijyāvikāre sati somo na bhakṣyate. tasmāt paśyāmaḥ - ijyāvikāra iti.
children.translated_text: Moreover, we see this — that it is a modification of the sacrifice. Why? Because of the observation of an indicatory mark. What is the indicatory mark? The restatement prohibiting <s>Soma</s> — 'he should give him the <s>bhakṣa</s>, not <s>Soma</s>' — when it is a modification of the sacrifice, <s>Soma</s> is not to be drunk [directly]. Therefore, we see that it is a modification of the sacrifice.

children.text: anuprasarpiṣu sāmānyāt // MS_3,5.52 //
children.translated_text: In [the case of] those who approach, because of the commonality. // MS 3,5.52 //

children.text: asti rājasūye daśapeyaḥ, tatra śrūyate - śataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ somān bhakṣayanti, daśadaśaikaikacamasam anuprasarpantīti. atra rājanyacamase saṃdehaḥ - kim, taṃ rājanyā anuprasarpeyuḥ, uta brāhmaṇā iti. kiṃ prāptam? rājyanyā iti. katham? daśadaśaikaikaṃ camasam anuprasarpeyur ity anuprasarpatāṃ saṃkhyā vidhīyate. ekasyāṃ rājanyajātau daśasaṃkhyā vidhīyate. rājanyajātiḥ saiva, tena taṃ daśa rājanyā anuprasarpeyur evaṃ śataṃ brāhmaṇā rājanyāś ca. teṣu śataśabdo 'nuvādaḥ. anuvādasarūpaś ca, śataṃ bhakṣayantīti. tasmād rājanyā rājanyacamasam anuprasarpeyur iti. kecid āhuḥ - brāhmaṇarājanyānām ekasmiṃś camase bhakṣaṇaṃ [365]{*3/555*} virudhyata iti. na sa doṣaḥ, na hi somenocchiṣṭā bhavantīti śrūyate.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Rājasūya</s> there is the <s>Daśapeya</s> (ten-drinks rite); there it is heard: 'A hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s> drink <s>Soma</s>; ten by ten they approach each cup.' There the doubt arises regarding the <s>rājanya</s>-cup (warrior-cup): should <s>rājanyas</s> (warriors) approach it, or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>? What is the prima facie view? <s>Rājanyas</s>. How? 'Ten by ten should approach each cup' — the number of those who approach is enjoined. In a single <s>rājanya</s> class, the number ten is enjoined. The <s>rājanya</s> class is the same [for the <s>rājanya</s>-cup]; therefore, ten <s>rājanyas</s> should approach that [cup] — thus [there would be] a hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and also <s>rājanyas</s>. Among them, the word 'hundred' is a restatement. And it has the form of a restatement: 'a hundred drink.' Therefore, <s>rājanyas</s> should approach the <s>rājanya</s>-cup. Some say: the drinking of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>rājanyas</s> from a single cup would be contradictory. That is not a fault — for it is not heard that they become defiled by <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇā vā tulyaśabdatvāt // MS_3,5.53 //
children.translated_text: Or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, because of the equivalence of the word. // MS 3,5.53 //

children.text: brāhmaṇā vā rājanyacamasam anuprasarpeyuḥ. katham? śataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ somaṃ bhakṣayantīti vidhiḥ śrutyā brāhmaṇagatām eva saṃkhyām āha. tasmāc chataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ, teṣāṃ bhakṣaṇārtham anuprasarpatām ekaikasmiṃś camase daśadaśopadiśyante. tasmād brāhmaṇāśatasya daśa brāhmaṇā rājanyacamasam anuprasarpeyur iti.
children.translated_text: Or <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should approach the <s>rājanya</s>-cup. How? 'A hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s> drink <s>Soma</s>' — the injunction, through the [Vedic] statement, specifies a number pertaining only to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Therefore, [there are] a hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; for their drinking, those who approach are prescribed as ten by ten for each cup. Therefore, from the hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, ten <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should approach the <s>rājanya</s>-cup.

children.text: sarvārtham aprakaraṇāt // MS_3,6.1 //
children.translated_text: [The general prescription] is for all purposes, because of [its being] outside a specific context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). // MS 3,6.1 //

children.text: anārabhya kiṃcid ucyate - yasya khādiraḥ sruvo bhavati sa chadasām eva rasenāvadyati, sarasā asyāhutayo bhavanti. yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇotīty{*3/557*}evamādi. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ khādiratā sruve, pālāśatā juhvām, prakṛtau niviśate, uta prakṛtau vikṛtau ceti. kiṃ prāptam? sarvārtham aprakaraṇāt, prakṛtivikṛtyartham evaṃjātīyakam. kutaḥ? aprakaraṇāt, na kasya-cid prakaraṇe śrūyante, tāni vākyena sarvatra bhaveyur iti.
children.translated_text: Without reference to any [particular rite], it is stated: 'One whose ladle (<s>sruva</s>) is made of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) wood — he pours the essence of the meters; his oblations become juicy. One whose <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) is made of <s>palāśa</s> (butea) wood — he does not hear an evil report' — and so forth. There the doubt arises: does the <s>khadira</s> [quality] of the <s>sruva</s> and the <s>palāśa</s> [quality] of the <s>juhū</s> apply in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) [alone], or in both the archetype and its modifications (<s>vikṛti</s>)? What is the prima facie view? [It is] for all purposes, because of [its being] outside a specific context — such [prescriptions] are for both the archetype and modifications. Why? Because of [their being] outside a context — they are not heard in any [particular] context; through [their] statement, they should apply everywhere.

NOTES:
[{3/557: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.5.7.1}]

children.text: prakṛtau vādviruktatvāt // MS_3,6.2 //
children.translated_text: Or [they apply] in the archetype, because of the absence of repetition. // MS 3,6.2 //

children.text: prakṛtau vā niviśerann anārabhyādhītāni pātrāṇi. kutaḥ? adviruktatvāt, evam adviruktaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. dviruktāyāṃ ko doṣaḥ? asaṃbhava iti brūmaḥ - yad dhi prakṛtau vikṛtau ca bhavati, asti tat prakṛtau. prakṛtau ced asti, codakenaiva vikṛtiṃ prāpnoti, tato nānārabhya vidhim ākāṅkṣati. tasmād anākāṅkṣitatvād anārabhyavidhir na tatra vidadhāti, tena brūmaḥ - prakṛtyartha eveti.
children.translated_text: Or the ladles prescribed without reference [to any particular rite] should apply in the archetype [alone]. Why? Because of the absence of repetition — thus there will be no repetition. What is the fault in repetition? Impossibility, we say — for what applies in both the archetype and the modification already exists in the archetype. If it exists in the archetype, it reaches the modification through the enjoiner alone; then it does not require an independent general prescription (<s>anārabhyavidhāna</s>). Therefore, because it is not required, the general prescription does not enjoin [it] there; hence we say: it is for the archetype purpose alone.

children.text: tad varjantu vacanaprāpte // MS_3,6.3 //
children.translated_text: That [prescription] should exclude [what is otherwise obtained], when [the ladle material] is obtainable by [Vedic] statement. // MS 3,6.3 //

children.text: aprakaraṇāt prakṛtivikṛtyartham evety ucyate - yat tu coda[367]{*3/558*}kena prāpnotīty anārabhyavidhinā prāpte na codakam ākāṅkṣati. tasmād anārabhyavidhivarjaṃ codakaḥ prāpayiṣyati, anārabhyavidhivākyena pratyakṣeṇa sruve khādiratā, codakavākyenānumānikena vikṛtau. ānumānikāc ca pratyakṣaṃ balavat. tasmāt prakṛtivikṛtyartho 'nārabhyavidhiḥ.
children.translated_text: Because of [its being] outside a context, [the general prescription] is for both the archetype and modifications — so it is said. But what is obtained by the enjoiner (<s>codaka</s>) does not require the general prescription (<s>anārabhyavidhi</s>). Therefore, the enjoiner will convey [the ladle materials] to all except what is [already] conveyed by the general prescription. The <s>khadira</s> quality of the <s>sruva</s> [is conveyed] directly by the sentence of the general prescription; [the same quality] is [conveyed] to the modification by the inferential sentence of the enjoiner. And the direct is stronger than the inferential. Therefore, the general prescription is for the archetype and modifications.

children.text: darśanād iti cet // MS_3,6.4 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, because of observation. // MS 3,6.4 //

children.text: yady anārabhyavidhiś codakād balīyān, anārabhyavidhinā prāpte na codakam ākāṅkṣati, nirākāṅkṣe vaikṛte karmaṇi codako naiva prāpnoti. tatra prayājādīnāṃ darśanaṃ naivopapadyeta, dṛśyante ca prayājādayaḥ kvacit, prayāje prayāje kṛṣṇalaṃ juhotīti{*3/559*}. atha codako balīyān{*3/560*} tata etaddarśanam upapadyate. tasmāt prakṛtyartho 'nārabhyavidhiḥ.
children.translated_text: If the general prescription is stronger than the enjoiner and when [what is already] obtained by the general prescription does not require the enjoiner, then in a modified rite that is already satisfied, the enjoiner would not obtain [anything] at all. In that case, the observation of <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) and the like would not be justified — yet <s>prayājas</s> and the like are observed somewhere: 'at each <s>prayāja</s> he offers a <s>kṛṣṇala</s> (black berry).' But if the enjoiner is stronger, then this observation is justified. Therefore, the general prescription is for the archetype [alone].

children.text: na codanaikārthyāt // MS_3,6.5 //
children.translated_text: No, because the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) has a single purpose. // MS 3,6.5 //

children.text: na prakṛtyarthaḥ, sarvārtha{*3/561*} iti brūmaḥ, aprakaraṇe samāmnānāt. yad uktam, anārabhyavidhinā nirākāṅkṣasya na codaka iti, tan nopapadyate. na hy anārabhyavidhiś codanāṃ nirākāṅkṣīkaroti, prāpte hi codake na sruve khādiratānārabhyavidhinā śakyā vidhātum. asati codake 'nārabhyavidhir api nāsti, na cānārabhyavidhiḥ sruvaṃ prāpayati, tasya ca khādiratām. kutaḥ? codanaikārthyāt. ekārthā hi codanā, yasya khādiraḥ sruvo bhavatīti. na cātra sruvaḥ khādiratā cobhayaṃ vidhīyate, sruvasya sataḥ khādiratām eṣa śabda āha, sa ca codakena prāptaḥ. tasmād asti codakaḥ, sa hy anārabhyavidhivākyasya pratyakṣatvāt taṃ varjayitvānyaṃ prāpayati. tasmāt prakṛtivikṛtyartho 'nārabhyavidhiḥ.
children.translated_text: [The general prescription] is not for the archetype [alone]; we say it is for all purposes, because it is taught outside any [specific] context. As for what was said — that the enjoiner cannot [operate] when [what it would convey] is already satisfied by the general prescription — that is not justified. For the general prescription does not render the injunction unnecessary. When the enjoiner is [already] obtained, the <s>khadira</s> quality of the <s>sruva</s> cannot be enjoined by the general prescription. Without the enjoiner, the general prescription too does not exist. Nor does the general prescription convey the <s>sruva</s> [itself] and its <s>khadira</s> quality. Why? Because the injunction has a single purpose. The injunction has one purpose: 'one whose <s>sruva</s> is of <s>khadira</s> [wood].' Here, it is not both the <s>sruva</s> and the <s>khadira</s> quality that are enjoined — this word states the <s>khadira</s> quality of an already-existing <s>sruva</s>, which has been obtained through the enjoiner. Therefore, the enjoiner exists; and because the sentence of the general prescription is direct, it conveys [the <s>khadira</s> quality] to [all] other [rites], setting aside [the archetype]. Therefore, the general prescription is for the archetype and modifications.

children.text: utpattir iti cet // MS_3,6.6 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, [the argument from] origination. // MS 3,6.6 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi - utpattir eṣāṃ prakṛtividhibhis tulyā, prakṛtāv aṅgāni saṃkṣepeṇa vistareṇa cocyante - pañca prayājān yacatīti saṃkṣepeṇa. samidho yajatīty{*3/563*}evamādinā vistareṇa. ihāpi yasya khādiraḥ sruvo bhavatītyevamādir vistāraḥ, yasyaivaṃrūpāḥ sruva iti saṃkṣepaḥ. evaṃrūpaḥ prakṛtau vidhir dṛṣṭaḥ, ayam apy evaṃrūpaḥ, tasmāt prākṛta iti sāmānyato dṛṣṭānumānam. tasmāt prakṛtyartho 'nārabhyavidhir iti.
children.translated_text: If you see thus — the origination of these [general prescriptions] is similar to the injunctions in the archetype. In the archetype, subsidiary elements are stated both in summary and in detail: 'he offers five <s>prayājas</s>' is the summary; 'he offers the kindling-sticks' and so forth is the detail. Here too, 'one whose <s>sruva</s> is of <s>khadira</s> [wood]' and so forth is the detail; 'one whose <s>sruva</s>s are of such a form' is the summary. This form of injunction is observed in the archetype; this too is of the same form; therefore it is archetypical — this is an inference from general resemblance. Therefore, the general prescription is for the archetype [alone].

NOTES:
[{3/563: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.1.1}]

children.text: na, tulyatvāt // MS_3,6.7 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the equality [of the argument]. // MS 3,6.7 //

children.text: naitad evam. na hy evaṃjātīyakaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ sādhakaṃ bhavati, kevalam atra prākṛtavidhisārūpyam, na tu prakṛtāv etad bhavatīti pramāṇam asti. api ca vikṛtāv api saṃkṣepavistārābhyām{*3/564*} aṅgāni vidhīyante, tisra āhutīr juhotīti{*3/565*} saṃkṣepaḥ, āmanam asyāmanasya devā iti{*3/566*} vistāraḥ{*3/567*}. ato vaikṛtair{*3/568*} apy anārabhyavidhayas tulyāḥ, tasmād ayam ahetuḥ prakṛtiniveśasya.
children.translated_text: This is not so. For an inference from general resemblance of this kind is not probative — there is merely a resemblance to an archetypical injunction, but there is no evidence that this [prescription] belongs to the archetype. Moreover, in the modifications too, subsidiary elements are enjoined both in summary and in detail: 'he offers three oblations' is the summary; '<s>āmanam asyāmanasya devā</s>' is the detail. Therefore, the general prescriptions are equal [in form] even with modified [injunctions]. Hence, this is not a valid reason for placing [them] in the archetype.

children.text: codanārthakārtsnyāt tu mukhyavipratiṣedhāt prakṛtyarthaḥ // MS_3,6.8 //
children.translated_text: But because of the completeness of the purpose of the injunction, because of the conflict with the primary [meaning], [the general prescription] is for the archetype. // MS 3,6.8 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na sarvārtho 'nārabhyavidhiḥ, prakṛtyarthaḥ sa iti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ? codanārthakārtsnyāt, kṛtsnaṃ codakaḥ prāpayati, nānārabhyavidhinā vaikṛtam apūvaṃ? nirākāṅkṣam, pātrāṇāṃ hi tad vākyena na yāgānām. yāgāś codanāliṅgasaṃyogāt prakṛtim apekṣante, tayā sahaikavākyatāṃ yānti. prākṛtāś ca tāñ śaknavanti nirākāṅkṣīkartum, nānārabhya[369]{*3/569*}vidhayaḥ. tasmād avaśyaṃ codaka utpādayitavyaḥ. sa ced utpādyate, nārtho 'nārabhyavidhinā. na cāsau prakaraṇādīnām abhāvāt pravartamāno 'pi vaikṛtena yāgena saṃbadhyeta. tasmād vaikṛtena karmaṇā
nānārabhyavidhiḥ saṃbadhyate. tasya{*3/570*} vaikṛtasya mukhyasya, anārabhyavidhir vākyaśeṣaḥ, prakṛtau veti vipratiṣedhe{*3/571*} codakasāmarthyāt, prākṛte vākyaśeṣe prāpte 'nārabhyavidhir na bhaviṣyati. tasmād anārabhyavidhiḥ prakṛtyartha iti{*3/572*}.
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) dismisses the [previous] position. The general prescription is not for all purposes; we say it is for the archetype. Why? Because of the completeness of the purpose of the injunction — the enjoiner conveys everything completely. Does not the general prescription [convey] what is unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) in the modification? [The modification] is already satisfied — for the [general prescription] is about ladles, not about sacrifices. The sacrifices, because of their connection with injunctions and indicatory marks, depend on the archetype and form a single sentence with it. And the archetypical [injunctions] are able to render them [the modifications] satisfied, not the general prescriptions. Therefore, the enjoiner must necessarily be generated. And if it is generated, there is no need for the general prescription [in the modification]. And [the general prescription], in the absence of context and other [connections], even though operating, would not be connected with the modified sacrifice. Therefore, the general prescription is not connected with the modified rite. [The conflict is:] is the general prescription a sentence-complement of that modified primary [rite], or of the archetype? In this conflict, because of the capacity of the enjoiner, when the archetypical sentence-complement is obtained, the general prescription will not apply [to the modification]. Therefore, the general prescription is for the archetype.

children.text: prakaraṇaviśeṣāt tu vikṛtau virodhi syāt // MS_3,6.9 //
children.translated_text: But because of the specific context, [the general prescription] would conflict in the modification. // MS 3,6.9 //

children.text:
anārabhya, kiṃcit, sāmidhenīnāṃ parimāṇam āmnātam - saptadaśa sāmidhenīr anubrūyād iti{*3/573*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim etat prakṛtau, uta vikṛtāv iti. kiṃ prāptam? pūrveṇa nyāyena prakṛtāv iti prāptam, prakṛtau ca pāñcadaśyam āmnātam, tena vikalpa iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - vikṛtāv evaṃjātīyako vidhiḥ syāt. kasmāt? prakṛteḥ pāñcadaśyena nirākāṅkṣatvāt. nanu vikalpo bhavaiṣyatīty uktam. prakaraṇaviśeṣāt pāñcadaśyena na vikalpaḥ, viṣamaśāsanāt. vikṛtau tv ānumānikaṃ pāñcadaśyaṃ bādhitvā, anārabhyavidhivākyena pratyakṣeṇa sāptadaśyaṃ nivekṣyate. advi[370]{*3/574*}ruktaṃ caitat prayogavacanam upasaṃhariṣyati. tasmād evaṃjātīyakaṃ vikṛtyartham.
children.translated_text:
Without reference [to any particular rite], the number of <s>sāmidhenīs</s> (kindling verses) is taught: 'he should recite seventeen <s>sāmidhenīs</s>.' There the doubt arises: is this [prescription] for the archetype, or for the modification? What is the prima facie view? By the foregoing principle, it is obtained for the archetype; and in the archetype, a fifteen-count (<s>pāñcadaśya</s>) is taught — thus there would be an option.
Given this, we say: such a prescription should apply in the modification [only]. Why? Because the archetype is already satisfied with the fifteen-count. [Objection:] But it was said that there would be an option. [Reply:] Because of the specific context, there is no option with the fifteen-count, as the [two] teachings are unequal. But in the modification, having overridden the inferential fifteen-count, the seventeen-count will be established by the direct sentence of the general prescription. And the non-repetitive application-statement will confirm this. Therefore, such [a general prescription] is for the modification.

children.text: naimittakaṃ tu prakṛtau, tadvikāraḥ saṃyogaviśeṣāt // MS_3,6.10 //
children.translated_text: An occasional [prescription] is for the archetype; its modification [extends] because of the specific connection. // MS 3,6.10 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnātam - godohanena paśukāmasya praṇayed iti, tathā - agnīṣomīye paśau śrūyate yūpaṃ prakṛtya, bailvo brahmavarcaskāmena kartavya iti{*3/575*}. evaṃjātīyakeṣu saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ prakṛtau niveśaḥ, vikṛtau veti{*3/576*}. kiṃ prāptam? vikṛtāv iti, prakṛtīr anyena pātreṇa yūpena ca nirākāṅkṣāḥ. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - prakṛtau naimittikaṃ niviśate, nimittasaṃyogena vidhānāt, khādirapālāśarauhitakā aviśeṣeṇoktāḥ camasaś ca, godohanaṃ bailvaś ca viśeṣavihitau, viśeṣavidhinā cāviśeṣavidhir bādhyate. prakaraṇaṃ sāmānyam, nimittasaṃyogo viśeṣaḥ, sāmānyena yat prāpnoti, tat parokṣaṃ lakṣaṇayā. yat tu viśeṣeṇa, tat pratyakṣaṃ śrutyā, śrutiś ca lakṣaṇāyā balīyasī, pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣāt. tasmāt prakṛtāv eva syāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is taught: 'for one desiring cattle, he should carry [the offering] with a cow-milking [vessel].' Similarly, in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal sacrifice it is heard regarding the sacrificial post: 'one desiring sacred splendor (<s>brahmavarcas</s>) should make [the post] of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) [wood].' In such cases the doubt arises: does [the prescription] apply to the archetype or to the modification? What is the prima facie view? To the modification — since the archetypes are already satisfied with another ladle and post [respectively]. Given this, we say: an occasional [prescription] applies to the archetype, because it is enjoined with a connection to an occasion (<s>nimitta</s>). The <s>khadira</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and <s>rauhitaka</s> [woods] and the <s>camasa</s> (cup) are stated without distinction; but the cow-milking [vessel] and the <s>bilva</s> [post] are enjoined with a specific distinction. And a specific injunction overrides a general injunction. The context is general; the occasional connection is specific. What is obtained through the general is indirect, by implication; but what [is obtained] through the specific is direct, through [Vedic] statement. And [Vedic] statement is stronger than implication, and the direct is [stronger] than the indirect. Therefore, [the occasional prescription] should apply in the archetype alone.

NOTES:
[{3/575: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.1.8.1}]
[{3/576: E1 omits <s>vā</s>}]

children.text: iṣṭyartham agnyādheyaṃ prakaraṇāt // MS_3,6.11 //
children.translated_text: The fire-establishment (<s>Agnyādhāna</s>) is for the purpose of the [<s>Pavamāna</s>] sacrifices (<s>iṣṭi</s>), because of the context. // MS 3,6.11 //

children.text: santi pavamāneṣṭayaḥ - agnaye pavamānāyāṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet, agnaye pāvakāya, agnaye śucaya iti{*3/577*}. tāsāṃ prakaraṇe, samāmnātam - brāhmaṇo vasante 'gnim ādadhīteti{*3/578*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim agnyādheyaṃ pavamāneṣṭyartham, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? [371]{*3/579*} iṣṭyartham iti. kutaḥ? prakaraṇāt, tāsāṃ prakaraṇe śrūyate - atas tadartham.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> (sacrifices to <s>Agni Pavamāna</s>): 'he should prepare an eight-<s>kapāla</s> [rice-cake] for <s>Agni Pavamāna</s>, for <s>Agni Pāvaka</s>, for <s>Agni Śuci</s>.' In the context of these, it is taught: 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the fire in spring.' There the doubt arises: is the <s>Agnyādhāna</s> for the purpose of the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s>, or not? What is the prima facie view? [It is] for the purpose of the sacrifices. Why? Because of the context — it is heard in the context of those [<s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s>]; therefore it is for that purpose.

children.text: na vā tāsāṃ tadarthatvāt // MS_3,6.12 //
children.translated_text: Or not, because those [sacrifices] are for that [fire's] purpose. // MS 3,6.12 //

children.text: pavamāneṣṭayo hy agnyarthāḥ, yady agnir iṣṭyarthaḥ syāt, tatas tadartham agnyādheyam iṣṭīnām upakuryāt. niṣphalās tv iṣṭayaḥ, tadartham agnyādheyam api niṣphalaṃ syāt. kathaṃ punar agnyarthatā pavamāneṣṭīnām? niṣprayojanatvād eva, prayojanavattvāc cāgnīnām. bhāvayitavyā apīṣṭayo bhūtānām agnīnām arthena kriyeran. tasmād agnyādheyaṃ pavamāneṣṭyartham.
children.translated_text: For the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> are for the purpose of the fire. If the fire were for the purpose of the sacrifices, then the <s>Agnyādhāna</s>, being for their purpose, would serve the sacrifices. But the sacrifices are without fruit [of their own]; therefore the <s>Agnyādhāna</s> too would be without fruit for their sake. How then are the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> for the purpose of the fire? Because they are without independent purpose, whereas the fires have purpose. Even the sacrifices, which [ordinarily] must be performed, would be done for the purpose of the fires that are [already] established. Therefore, the <s>Agnyādhāna</s> is for the purpose of the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s>.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_3,6.13 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS 3,6.13 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ darśayati{*3/580*}, yathāgnyarthāḥ pavamāneṣṭaya iti. kiṃ liṅgam? jīryati vā eṣa āhitaḥ paśur yad agniḥ, tad etāny evāgnyādheyasya havīṃṣi saṃvatsare nirvapet, tena vā eṣa na jīryati, tenainaṃ{*3/581*} punar navaṃ karoti tan na sūkṣmam iti{*3/582*}.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark shows that the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> are for the purpose of the fire. What is the indicatory mark? 'This [fire] that has been established indeed decays, as an animal [decays]; he should offer these oblations of the <s>Agnyādhāna</s> during the year; thereby it does not decay; thereby he makes it new again' — this is not a subtle [indication].

children.text:

children.text: tatprakṛtyarthaṃ yathānyenārabhyavādāḥ // MS_3,6.14 //
children.translated_text: That [<s>Agnyādhāna</s>] is for the purpose of the archetype, just as other general prescriptions. // MS 3,6.14 //

children.text: tad etad ādhānaṃ kiṃ prakṛtyartham, uta sarvakarmārtham iti saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ prāptam? ucyate, tat prakṛtyartham. katham? yathānye 'nārabhyavādāḥ prakṛtyarthāḥ, tenaiva hetunā.
children.translated_text: The doubt arises: is this <s>Agnyādhāna</s> for the purpose of the archetype, or for the purpose of all rites? What is the prima facie view? It is said: it is for the purpose of the archetype. How? Just as other general prescriptions are for the purpose of the archetype — by that same reasoning.

children.text: sarvārthaṃ vādhānasya svakālatvāt // MS_3,6.15 //
children.translated_text: Or [the <s>Agnyādhāna</s>] is for all purposes, because the <s>Ādhāna</s> has its own time. // MS 3,6.15 //

children.text:
sarvakarmārthaṃ vādhānam. ko 'rthaḥ? sarvakarmārthaṃ yad agnidravyam, tadartham ādhānaṃ na prakṛtyartham. na prakṛtīḥ prakṛtya śrūyate. na [372]{*3/583*} ca śrutyādayo 'sya santi, ye 'ṅgabhāvam upapādayanti. anyeṣv anārabhyavādeṣv anyato nirjñāte 'ṅgabhāve tato vicāraḥ - kiṃ prakṛter aṅgabhūtāni vikṛter iti, tasmāt teṣu yuktam. iha tv aṅgabhāve na kāraṇam asti, tasmād agniprayuktam ādhānam, na karmaprayuktam, sarvakarmārthā agnaya{*3/584*} iti sarvārtham ity ucyate.
api cāsya svataḥ kālo vidhīyate, sa na vidhātavyaḥ, yadā jyotiṣṭomasya prayogaḥ, tadedaṃ kartavyam. tadā ca vasantaḥ. evaṃ yadā darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ prayogaḥ, tadā kartavyam. tadā paurṇamāsy amāvāsyā vā. aprakṛtyarthaṃ tu na prakṛtiprayoge kriyeta, tatra kālavacanaṃ yuktam. tasmān na prakṛtyartham.
children.translated_text:
Or the <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) is for the purpose of all rites. What is the meaning? The fire-substance (<s>agnidravya</s>) that is for the purpose of all rites — for that purpose is the <s>Ādhāna</s>, not for the purpose of the archetype [alone]. It is not heard in reference to the archetype [specifically]. Nor does it have <s>śruti</s> and other [indicators] that would establish [its] subsidiary status. In other general prescriptions, when the subsidiary status is known from another [source], then the inquiry [arises]: is [the subsidiary] of the archetype or of the modification? Therefore, [the archetype interpretation] is appropriate for those. But here there is no basis for subsidiary status. Therefore, the <s>Ādhāna</s> is prompted by the fire, not prompted by the rite. [Since] the fires are for the purpose of all rites, it is said to be 'for all purposes.'
Moreover, its own time is enjoined independently; it should not be enjoined [by saying] 'when the performance of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [occurs], then this should be done — and that is in spring.' Similarly, 'when the performance of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [occurs], then it should be done — and that is on the full-moon or new-moon day.' But if it were not for the purpose of the archetype, it would not be performed at the archetype's performance-time; there, the statement about time would be appropriate. Therefore, it is not for the purpose of the archetype [alone].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{3/583: E2: 4,505; E4: 4,787; E6: 1,251}*
*{3/584: E2,4: sarvakarmārthās tv agnaya}*
tāsām agniḥ prakṛtitaḥ prayājavat syāt // MS_3,6.16 //
children.translated_text: The fire for those [<s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s>] should be from the archetype, like the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings). // MS 3,6.16 //

children.text: santi pavamāneṣṭavyaḥ - agnaye pavamānāyety{*3/585*}evamādyāḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ pavamāneṣṭisaṃskṛte 'gnau pavamāneṣṭayaḥ kartavyāḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? tāsāṃ khalu pavamāneṣṭīnāṃ pavamāneṣṭisaṃskṛto 'gniḥ prakṛtitaḥ syāt. kutaḥ? codakasāmarthyāt, prayājavat, yathāsu prayājā bhavanti codakena, evaṃ pavamāneṣṭisaṃskṛtā agnayo 'pi bhaveyuḥ.
children.translated_text: There are <s>Pavamāneṣṭi</s> (oblations to the purifying [fire]) — such as "to <s>Agni</s> the purifier" and similar. There a doubt [arises]: should the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> be performed on a fire consecrated by the <s>Pavamāneṣṭi</s>, or not? What is the prima facie view? For those <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s>, a fire consecrated by the <s>Pavamāneṣṭi</s> would be [required] from the archetype. Why? By the force of the injunction, like the preliminary offerings (<s>prayāja</s>) — just as the preliminary offerings exist by [force of] the injunction, so too the fires consecrated by the <s>Pavamāneṣṭi</s> would exist.

children.text: na vā tāsāṃ tadarthatvāt // MS_3,6.17 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, not, because those [Pavamāneṣṭis] serve that purpose [i.e., fire-consecration]. // MS_3,6.17 //

children.text: na veṣṭisaṃskāraḥ, agnīnāṃ pavamāneṣtiṣu syāt. kasmāt? [373]{*3/586*} tāsāṃ tadarthatvāt, tāḥ pavamāneṣṭayo 'gnisaṃskārārthā ity uktam. yac ca nāmāṅgabhūtaṃ tac codakena gṛhyate. agniprayuktaś ca pavamāneṣṭisaṃskāro na darśapūrṇamāsaprayuktaḥ, tena na codakenākṛṣyate. api ca pavamāneṣ-ṭaya iṣṭisaṃskāravarjitāṃ prakṛtim apekṣante, avihitatvāt tasyām avasthāyāṃ pavamāpaneṣṭīnām.
children.translated_text: Or rather, the <s>iṣṭi</s>-consecration should not apply to the fires in the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s>. Why? [373] Because those [Pavamāneṣṭis] serve that purpose — it has been said that those <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> are for the purpose of fire-consecration. And that which is a subsidiary is grasped by the injunction. The <s>Pavamāneṣṭi</s> consecration is prompted by fire, not by the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; therefore it is not attracted by the injunction. Moreover, the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> presuppose an archetype devoid of <s>iṣṭi</s>-consecration, since the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> are not enjoined in that [consecrated] state.

children.text: tulyaḥ sarveṣāṃ paśuvidhiḥ prakaraṇāviśeṣāt // MS_3,6.18 //
children.translated_text: The animal rites are the same for all [victims], because there is no difference in the context. // MS_3,6.18 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome, paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ - yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*3/587*}, tathā savanīyo 'nubandhyaś ca. santi ca paśudharmāḥ, upākaraṇam upānayanam akṣayā bandhaḥ, yūpe niyojanaṃ saṃjñapanaṃ viśasanam ityevamādayaḥ. te kiṃ sarveṣām agnīṣomīyasavanīyānubandhyānām, uta agnīṣomīyasya savanīyasya vā{*3/588*}, utāgniṣomīyasyaiveti. kiṃ prāptam? aviśeṣat, sarvapaśūnām. katham aviśeṣaḥ? jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇe sarve paśavaḥ samāmnātāḥ, tatprakaraṇāpannatvāt sarve paśudharmāḥ{*3/589*} saṃbadhyante, na caiṣāṃ tatra kaścid viśeṣaḥ.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - savanīyasyaite dharmāḥ bhaveyuḥ, tulyaḥ sarveṣāṃ paśuvidhiḥ syāt, yadi prakaraṇe viśeṣo na bhavet. bhavati tu prakaraṇe viśeṣaḥ, savanīyānāṃ prakaraṇe paśudharmāḥ samāmnātāh, āgneyaḥ paśur agniṣṭoma ālabhyaḥ, āgneyo hy agniṣṭomaḥ. aindrāgnaḥ paśur ukthya ālabhyaḥ, aindrāgnāni hy ukthyāni. aindro vṛṣṇiḥ ṣoḍaśiny ālabhyaḥ, aindro vai vṛṣṇir aindraḥ ṣoḍaśī. sārasvatī meṣy atirātra ālabhyā, vāg vai sarasvatī [374]{*3/590*} iti{*3/591*} prakṛtya paśudharmā āmnātāḥ, tasmāt savanīyasya prakaraṇād bhavitum arhati // MS_3,6.18 //
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the victim is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal — "he who is consecrated slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal" — and likewise the <s>Savanīya</s> and <s>Anubandhya</s>. And there are animal rites: the commencement (<s>upākaraṇa</s>), leading [to the post] (<s>upānayana</s>), anointing (<s>akṣa</s>), tying to the sacrificial post, binding to the <s>yūpa</s>, killing (<s>saṃjñapana</s>), cutting (<s>viśasana</s>), and so forth. Do these apply to all — the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, <s>Savanīya</s>, and <s>Anubandhya</s> — or to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> and <s>Savanīya</s>, or to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> alone? What is the prima facie view? Because there is no distinction, [they apply] to all victims. How is there no distinction? All victims are taught in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context; being within that context, all animal rites are connected [to them], and there is no distinction among them there.
Given this, we say: these rites would apply to the <s>Savanīya</s> [alone]; the animal rites would be the same for all if there were no distinction in context. But there is a distinction in context — the animal rites are taught in the context of the <s>Savanīya</s> animals: "The <s>Āgneya</s> victim is to be slaughtered in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, for the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> belongs to <s>Agni</s>. The <s>Aindrāgna</s> victim is to be slaughtered in the <s>Ukthya</s>, for the <s>Ukthya</s> [rites] belong to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>. The <s>Aindra</s> bull is to be slaughtered in the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, for the bull belongs to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> belongs to <s>Indra</s>. The <s>Sārasvatī</s> ewe is to be slaughtered in the <s>Atirātra</s>, [374] for speech is <s>Sarasvatī</s>" — having introduced [these], the animal rites are taught. Therefore they should apply by context to the <s>Savanīya</s>. // MS_3,6.18 //

children.text: sthānāc ca pūrvasya // MS_3,6.19 //
children.translated_text: And because of position, [they belong] to the prior [victim]. // MS_3,6.19 //

children.text: yad uktam - prakaraṇāt savanīyārthā iti, etad gṛhṇīmaḥ, kramāc cāgnīṣomīyasya. tasya hi krama aupavasathye 'hani samāmnātam, tasmād dvayor apīti.
children.translated_text: What was stated — that by context they serve the <s>Savanīya</s> — this we accept; and by sequence, [they belong] to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. For its sequence is taught on the <s>Upavasatha</s> (preparatory) day; therefore [they belong] to both.

children.text: śvas tv ekeṣāṃ tatra prākśrutir guṇārthā // MS_3,6.20 //
children.translated_text: But for some [branch-followers], the prior mention there serves the purpose of a subsidiary quality. // MS_3,6.20 //

children.text: ekeṣāṃ śākhināṃ śvaḥ savanīyānām āmnānam, tad apekṣyeyam eṣāṃ guṇārthā punaḥśrutiḥ. kaḥ punar guṇaḥ? yad arthaiṣā śrutiḥ. ucyate - paśūn saṃkīrtya, yathā vai matsyo 'vidito janam avadhuute{*3/592*}, evam vaite{*3/593*} 'prajñāyamānā janam avadhunvata ity eṣām avijñāne doṣam abhidhāya, ebhiḥ kathaṃ savanāni paśumantītipraśnarūpakeṇa vapāpracāro guṇo vidhīyate, tad arthaiṣā śrutiḥ, vapāpracāreṇaikavākyatvāt. kim ataḥ? yady evam, na, savanīyānāṃ prakaraṇena paśudharmāḥ, kramād agnīṣomīyārthā eveti. kiṃ punas tac chva āmnānam? āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā trivṛtā yūpaṃ parivīyāgneyaṃ savanīyapaśum{*3/594*} upākarotīti.
children.translated_text: For some branch-followers, there is a mention of the <s>Savanīya</s> animals on the day before. Considering that, this repeated mention of theirs serves the purpose of a subsidiary quality. What then is the quality? That for which this statement exists. It is stated: having enumerated the victims, [the text says] "Just as a fish, when unrecognized, shakes off people, so these, being unrecognized, shook off people" — having stated the fault of their non-recognition, [it asks] "How then do the <s>Savanas</s> have victims?" and through this question-form, the <s>vapā</s>-rite (omentum-offering) is enjoined as a subsidiary quality. This statement serves that purpose, being a single sentence with the <s>vapā</s>-rite. What follows? If so, the animal rites do not [belong to] the <s>Savanīya</s> by context; by sequence they serve only the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. What then is that prior-day mention? "Having taken the <s>Āśvina</s> cup, having wrapped the sacrificial post with a three-strand [rope], he commences the <s>Āgneya Savanīya</s> victim."

children.text: tenotkṛṣṭasya kālavidhir iti cet // MS_3,6.21 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that thereby the time of the elevated [rite] is enjoined — // MS_3,6.21 //

children.text: naitad asti - kramād agnīṣomīyārthā eveti, prakaraṇāt savanīyārthāḥ, pūrvedyur evāmnānaṃ vidhānārtham, āśvinavākyaṃ kālaguṇavidhānārtham. katham? tena vapāpracāreṇokṛṣṭasya kāla eṣa vidhīyate, prātaḥsavane vapāpracāre codite sati paśvālambho 'pi tatraiva prapnoti. tatra kālāniyame prāpte, āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītveti kālamātraṃ vidhīyate. trivṛtā yūpaṃ [375]{*3/595*} parivīyopākarotīty{*3/596*} anuvādaḥ. itarathā hi{*3/597*} parivyāṇasya kālo vidhīyeta, upākaraṇasya ca. tatrānekaguṇavidhānād vākyaṃ bhidyeta. tasmāt savanīyārthāḥ paśudharmā iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — [it is not the case] that by sequence they serve only the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. By context, they serve the <s>Savanīya</s>; the prior-day mention is for the purpose of injunction; the <s>Āśvina</s> passage is for the purpose of enjoining a temporal qualification. How? Through that <s>vapā</s>-rite, the time of the elevated [rite] is enjoined: when the <s>vapā</s>-rite is enjoined in the morning pressing (<s>prātaḥsavana</s>), the animal-slaughter too is established there. When there is no restriction of time, "having taken the <s>Āśvina</s> cup" enjoins merely the time. [375] "Having wrapped the sacrificial post with a three-strand [rope], he commences" is a restatement. Otherwise, a time for the wrapping and a [separate] time for the commencement would be enjoined; then, due to the enjoining of multiple qualities, the sentence would be split. Therefore the animal rites serve the <s>Savanīya</s>.

children.text: naikadeśatvāt // MS_3,6.22 //
children.translated_text: Not so, because of being only a part. // MS_3,6.22 //

children.text: naitad evam, agnīṣomīyārthā evaite kramāt. āśvinakālaṃ hy āmnānaṃ vidhānārtham. guṇārtha etasmin vākyaṃ bhidyeta, na vidhānārthe. na hi vapāpracāreṇotkṛṣṭasya kālavidhiḥ saṃbhavati. ekadeśo hi vapādravyaṃ tena saṃnipātino vapāsaṃskārāt, utkarṣen nopākaraṇam.
children.translated_text: This is not so — by sequence these serve the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> alone. For the <s>Āśvina</s>-time mention is for the purpose of injunction. Under the view that it serves a subsidiary quality, the sentence would be split, not under the view that it is for injunction. For a time-injunction for the elevated [rite] through the <s>vapā</s>-rite is not possible — the <s>vapā</s> substance is only a part; through it, the commencement is not elevated because of the <s>vapā</s>-consecration, which accompanies [only] that part.

children.text: artheneti cet // MS_3,6.23 //
children.translated_text: [If one argues] that [it is] through purpose — // MS_3,6.23 //

children.text: āha - arthena tarhy{*3/598*} utkṛṣṭasya kālo vidhīyate. muṣṭinā pidhāya vapoddharaṇam āsīta ā vapāhomād iti śrūyate. pūrvedyur vapoddharaṇaṃ muṣṭinā pidhāya na śaknuyād etāvantaṃ kālamāsīnenāvasthātum, avaśyam āhāravihārādayas tena kartavyā iti.
children.translated_text: [The objector] says: then by purpose, the time of the elevated [rite] is enjoined. It is heard: "Covering with a fistful, having extracted the <s>vapā</s> (omentum), one should sit until the <s>vapā</s>-oblation." If the <s>vapā</s>-extraction were on the day before, covering with a fistful, one would be unable to remain sitting for such a long time; one must necessarily eat, move about, and so forth.

children.text: na śrutivipratiṣedhāt // MS_3,6.24 //
children.translated_text: Not so, because of contradiction with the direct statement (<s>śruti</s>). // MS_3,6.24 //

children.text: naitad evam, śrutivipratiṣedho{*3/599*} bhaved evam, na ca śrutivipratiṣedhaḥ, tṛṇamuṣṭinā parṇamuṣṭinā vā pidhāyiṣyate. nanv āsta ity upaveśane bhavati. nāvaśyam upaveśana eva{*3/600*}, audāsīnye 'pi dṛśyate. tad yathā - gṛhyāṇi parigṛhyāste, kṣetrāṇi parigṛhyāsta ity anupadeśane 'pi bhavati, vyāpāranivṛttau. ihāpi tṛṇamuṣṭinā parṇamuṣṭinā vā pidhāya, ā vapāhomād udāsiṣyate. tasmād āśvinakālam āmnānaṃ vidhānārtham, na savanīyānāṃ prakaraṇe paśudharmāḥ, tasmān na savanīyārthāḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so — there would be a contradiction with <s>śruti</s> in that case. But there is no contradiction with <s>śruti</s>: one would cover with a fistful of grass or a fistful of leaves. But does not "one should sit" (<s>āsta</s>) mean sitting down? Not necessarily sitting down alone — it is also seen in the sense of remaining inactive. For example: "having taken possession of houses, he remains; having taken possession of fields, he remains" — even without instruction, [it means] cessation of activity. Here too, covering with a fistful of grass or leaves, one will remain inactive until the <s>vapā</s>-oblation. Therefore the <s>Āśvina</s>-time mention is for the purpose of injunction; the animal rites are not in the context of the <s>Savanīya</s>; therefore they do not serve the <s>Savanīya</s>.

children.text: sthānāt tu pūrvasya saṃskārasya tad arthatvāt // MS_3,6.25 //
children.translated_text: But because of position, [they belong] to the prior [victim], the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, since the consecration serves that purpose. // MS_3,6.25 //

children.text: nāsti savanīyānāṃ prakaraṇam ity evaṃ sati pūrveṇaiva hetunā sthānena pūrvasyāgnīṣomīyasya bhavitum arhati. saṃskāro 'yaṃ paśuyāgaprayuktaḥ, na jyotiṣṭomaprayuktaḥ, jyotiṣṭomaprayuktatve na viśeṣaḥ paśūnāṃ syāt. paśuyāgā api hi dharmān prayoktum apūrvatvāt samarthāḥ, prakaraṇavantaś ca. tasmāt kramād agnīṣomīyadharmā iti.
children.translated_text: Since there is no context of the <s>Savanīya</s> [animals] — this being the case — by the very first reason, position, they should belong to the prior [victim], the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. This consecration is prompted by the animal sacrifice, not by the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; if prompted by the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, there would be no distinction among the victims. The animal sacrifices too are capable of prompting the rites because of [their] being unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>), and they have context. Therefore by sequence, [these are] rites of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_3,6.26 //
children.translated_text: And because of indicative evidence (<s>liṅga</s>). // MS_3,6.26 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmo 'gnīṣomīyārtāḥ paśudharmā iti. kutaḥ? liṅgadarśanāt. liṅgam asminn arthe bhavati, vapayā prātaḥsavane caranti, puroḍāśena mādhyaṃdine savana iti paśupuroḍāśaṃ darśayati. itarathā samānavidhāneṣu sarveṣu paśuṣv agnīṣomayor devatayoḥ saṃskārārthaḥ san puroḍāśaḥ sāmarthyād agnīṣomīyasya bhaven na savanīyasya, tayor devatayor abhāvāt, darśayati ca. tasmād agnīṣomīyārthā iti.
children.translated_text: From this too we observe that the animal rites serve the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. Why? Because of indicative evidence. There is an indicative mark in this matter: "with the <s>vapā</s> they perform [the rite] in the morning pressing, with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake) in the midday pressing" — it shows the animal-<s>puroḍāśa</s> [connection]. Otherwise, when the injunctions are the same for all victims, the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, serving the purpose of consecrating the two deities <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, would by its capacity belong to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, not to the <s>Savanīya</s>, due to the absence of those deities [in the latter]. And [the text] does show [this]. Therefore they serve the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>.

children.text: acodanā guṇārthena // MS_3,6.27 //
children.translated_text: There is no injunction for the purpose of [filling] a gap. // MS_3,6.27 //

children.text: idaṃ padottaraṃ sūtram{*3/602*}. āha, nanu chidrāpidhānārthaḥ paśupuroḍāśaḥ. neti brūmaḥ, acodanā guṇārthena, tasya chidrāpidhānārthena na codanā, arthavādaḥ sa ity uktam. tasmād devatāsaṃskārārthaḥ, tasmād agnīṣomīyārthatve{*3/603*}, savanīye puroḍāśasya darśanam upapadyate, na sādhāraṇye. tasmād agnīṣomīyārthāḥ paśudharmā iti.
children.translated_text: This is a sūtra supplementing [the previous] word. [The objector] says: but the animal-<s>puroḍāśa</s> serves the purpose of filling a gap (<s>chidrāpidhāna</s>). No, we say — there is no injunction for the purpose of [filling] a gap; that [passage] serving the purpose of gap-filling has no injunctive force — it has been stated to be an <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogy). Therefore it serves the purpose of deity-consecration; therefore, when serving the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, the evidence of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> in relation to the <s>Savanīya</s> is explained, not [as evidence of] commonality. Therefore the animal rites serve the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>.

children.text: dohayoḥ kālabhedād asaṃyuktaṃ śṛtaṃ syāt // MS_3,6.28 //
children.translated_text: Because of the difference in time between the two milkings, the cooked [offering] would be unconnected. // MS_3,6.28 //

children.text: asti sāyaṃdohaḥ, tathāsti prātardohaḥ. santi tu dohadharmāḥ śākhāharaṇam, gavāṃ prasthāpanam, prasāvanam, godohanam ityevamādayaḥ. te kiṃ sāyaṃdohārthāḥ, utobhayārthā iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? dohayos tayor asaṃyuktaṃ dharmaiḥ śṛtaṃ bhavet. kasmāt? sāyaṃdohasya hi krama aupavasathye 'hani śākhāharaṇādīn samāmananti, tasminn evāhani sāyaṃdohaḥ. tasmāt kramāt sāyaṃdohārthā dohadharmā iti.
children.translated_text: There is an evening milking, and likewise a morning milking. And there are milking rites: fetching the branch, setting the cows in motion, leading the cows forward, milking the cows, and so forth. Do these serve the evening milking, or both? What is the prima facie view? Of the two milkings, the cooked [offering] would be unconnected with the rites. Why? For the sequence of the evening milking on the preparatory day teaches the branch-fetching and other [rites]; the evening milking is on that very day. Therefore by sequence, the milking rites serve the evening milking.

children.text: prakaraṇāvibhāgād vā tatsaṃyuktasya kālaśāstram // MS_3,6.29 //
children.translated_text: Or, since there is no division in the context, the temporal instruction [applies] to what is connected with that. // MS_3,6.29 //

children.text: prakaraṇaṃ hi sādhāraṇam, yathaiva dadhna evaṃ payasaḥ, kramāc ca prakaraṇaṃ balavattaram, tasmād ubhayārthā dohadharmāḥ. api ca, na sāyaṃdohasya pūrvedyur āmnānam. kva tarhi? uttaredyuḥ. katham? evam āmananti - aindraṃ dadhy amāvāsyāyām, aindraṃ payo 'māvāsyāyām iti{*3/605*}, amāvāsyāyāṃ hy ubhayaṃ{*3/606*} sāṅgaṃ codyate. sa eṣa sāyaṃdoho 'rthāt pūrvedyur anuṣṭhīyate, svabhāva eṣa dadhnaḥ, yat pūrvedyur upakrāntam aparedyur abhinirvartate. tasmāt sāyaṃdohasya krama āmātā ity etad eva tāvan nāsti. ata ubhayārthā dohadharmā iti.
children.translated_text: For the context is common — just as for curds, so for milk. And context is stronger than sequence. Therefore the milking rites serve both. Moreover, the evening milking is not mentioned on the day before. Where then? On the following day. How? Thus they teach: "<s>Aindra</s> curds on the new-moon day, <s>Aindra</s> milk on the new-moon day" — on the new-moon day, both are enjoined with their subsidiaries. This evening milking is, by the nature of things, performed on the day before — it is the nature of curds that what is commenced on the previous day matures on the following day. Therefore the claim that the sequence of the evening milking is established does not hold. Hence the milking rites serve both.

children.text: tadvat savanāntare grahāmnānam // MS_3,6.30 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the teaching of cups (<s>graha</s>) in another pressing (<s>savana</s>). // MS_3,6.30 //

children.text: asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ - jyotiṣtomena svargakāmo yajeta [378]{*3/607*} iti{*3/608*}. tatraindravāyavādyā grahāḥ prātaḥsavane daśa āmnātāḥ, tatra dharmā śrūyante - upopte 'nye grahāḥ sādyante, anupopte dhruvāḥ. daśāpavitreṇa grahaṃ samārṣṭīti. santy apare mādhyaṃdine savane, apare tṛtīyasavane grahāḥ. teṣu mādhyaṃdinīyeṣu tārtīyeṣu ca savaneṣu saṃdehaḥ{*3/609*} - kiṃ sarveṣu grahadharmāḥ kartavyāḥ, uta prātaḥsavane ye grahās teṣv iti. kiṃ prāptam? prātaḥsavanagraheṣu bhaveyuḥ, teṣāṃ hi krame{*3/610*} samāmnānāt{*3/611*} netareṣām. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - savanāntare prātaḥsavanāt, mādhyaṃdine tṛtīyasavane ca grahāmnānaṃ tadvad eva bhavitum arhati. sarveṣāṃ hi tulyaṃ prakaraṇam, yatraite dharmāḥ samāmnātāḥ, vākyena grahamātrasya vidhīyante. kramāc ca vākyaprakaraṇe balīyasī. tasmāt sarvārthā grahadharmā iti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>: 'one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' There, in the morning pressing (<s>prātaḥsavana</s>), ten cups (<s>grahas</s>) beginning with the <s>Aindrāvāyava</s> are taught, and their <s>dharmas</s> (prescriptions) are heard: 'the cups other [than the <s>dhruvas</s>] are prepared on a strewn [surface]; the <s>dhruva</s> cups on an unstrewn [surface]'; 'he wipes the cup with a ten-strand purifier.' There are other cups in the midday pressing and in the third pressing. Regarding those of the midday and third pressings, the doubt arises: should the cup-prescriptions be performed for all [cups], or only for those cups that belong to the morning pressing? What is the prima facie view? They should apply to the morning-pressing cups, for they are taught in the sequence of those [cups], not of the others. Given this, we say: in the other pressings after the morning pressing — in the midday and third pressings — the teaching about cups should be just the same. For the context is the same for all — where these prescriptions are taught, they are enjoined by [Vedic] statement for cups in general. And [Vedic] statement and context are stronger than sequence. Therefore, the cup-prescriptions are for all purposes.

children.text: raśanā ca liṅgadarśanāt // MS_3,6.31 //
children.translated_text: And the rope (<s>raśanā</s>) [is shared], because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS 3,6.31 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ - yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*3/612*}. tatra raśanā śrūyate, raśanādharmāś ca - trivṛd bhavati, darbhamayī bhavati, prapiṣṭānāṃ{*3/613*} kartavyā ceti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ete dharmā agnīṣomīyaraśanāyāḥ savanīyaraśanāyāś ca sādhāraṇāḥ, utāgnīṣomīyaraśanāyā eveti. kiṃ prāptam? prakaraṇād agnīṣomīyaraśanāyā iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇā iti. kutaḥ? liṅgadarśanāt, liṅgaṃ bhavati, evam āha - āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā trivṛtā yūpaṃ parivīyāgneyaṃ paśum{*3/614*} upākarotīti [379]{*3/615*} savanīyaparivyāṇe raśanāṃ darśayati, sā yadi sādhāraṇī, tata etad darśanam avakalpate. yady agnīṣomīyārthāḥ, tato 'prākṛtāt savanīyaparivyāṇān nivarteta. savanīye ca parivyāṇāntaraprākṛtam, yatra trivṛttvaṃ dṛśyate. katham? sa vai āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvopaniṣkramya yūpaṃ parivyayatīti. tatra yadi na sādhāraṇī raśanā, vāsasā parivyāṇaṃ prāpnoti, raśaṇāṃ tu darśayati. tasmāt sādhāraṇī raśanā, tat sā-dhāraṇyāc ca taddharmā api sādhāraṇāḥ. tad etal liṅgād raśanāsādhāraṇyam. ko 'tra khalu nyāya iti. ucyate - prakaraṇād agnīṣomīyasya, vākyād yūpamātrasyeti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice]: 'one who is consecrated — when he slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.' There a rope (<s>raśanā</s>) is heard, as well as rope-prescriptions: 'it should be threefold (<s>trivṛt</s>), it should be made of <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), it should be made of twisted [strands].' There the doubt arises: are these prescriptions common to both the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> rope and the <s>Savanīya</s> (pressing-related) rope, or only for the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> rope? What is the prima facie view? Because of the context, [they are] for the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> rope [only].
Given this, we say: [the prescriptions] are common to both. Why? Because of the observation of an indicatory mark. There is an indicatory mark — thus it says: 'having taken the <s>Āśvina</s> cup, he wraps the sacrificial post with a threefold [rope], and begins the animal [sacrifice].' [This] shows the rope in the <s>Savanīya</s> wrapping. If [the rope] is common, then this observation is construable. If [the prescriptions] are [only] for the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [rope], then [the rope] would revert from the <s>Savanīya</s> wrapping to the non-archetypical [form]. And in the <s>Savanīya</s> [rite], there is another archetypical wrapping where the threefold [quality] is observed. How? 'Having taken the <s>Āśvina</s> cup, having gone out, he wraps the sacrificial post.' There, if the rope is not common, wrapping with cloth would be obtained; but [the text] shows the rope. Therefore, the rope is common; and because of the commonality, its prescriptions too are common. This commonality of the rope [follows] from the indicatory mark. What is the principle here? It is said: [it is] of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> because of the context; of the sacrificial post in general because of [Vedic] statement.

children.text: ārācchiṣṭam asaṃyuktam itaraiḥ saṃnidhānāt // MS_3,6.32 //
children.translated_text: What is taught at a distance, [being] unconnected with the others, [is connected] because of proximity. // MS 3,6.32 //

children.text: dūrād yac chiṣyate jyotiṣṭomasya, yathaupasadānuvākyākāṇḍe 'ṃśvadābhyau{*3/616*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ jyotiṣṭomasamāmnātā grahadharmāḥ kartavyāḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? na kartavyāḥ, asaṃnidhānāt, yathā - payasā maitrāvaruṇaṃ śrīṇātīti{*3/617*} vacanāt, maitrāvaruṇasyaiva śravaṇam, na sarveṣām. evam idam api dharmajātaṃ prakaraṇasthānām eva, na sarveṣām iti.
children.translated_text: What is taught at a distance from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — as, for example, [the cups] <s>Aṃśu</s> and <s>Ādāb(h)ya</s> in the section on <s>Upasad</s> invocatory verses (<s>anuvākyā</s>). There the doubt arises: should the cup-prescriptions taught in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> be performed [for these cups], or not? What is the prima facie view? They should not be performed, because of the absence of proximity — just as 'he enriches the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [cup] with milk' is stated [only] for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> because of [Vedic] statement, not for all [cups]. Similarly, this set of prescriptions too is for those in the [immediate] context only, not for all.

NOTES:
[{3/616: E2,4: <s>'śvadābhyau</s>}]
[{3/617: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.4.8.2}]

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ vā tadarthatvāc cheṣasya tannimittatvāt // MS_3,6.33 //
children.translated_text: Or [they are] connected, because [the distant cups] are for that [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>'s] purpose, and because the residual [prescriptions] are occasioned by that [cup-nature]. // MS 3,6.33 //

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ vā dharmaiḥ, evaṃjātīyakaṃ syāt, aprakaraṇastham api. kutaḥ? yataḥ prakaraṇād vākyaṃ balīyaḥ. nanv anyatra kriya[380]{*3/618*}māṇā jyotiṣṭomasya nopakuryuḥ. ucyate - upakariṣyanti, aṃśvadābhyayos tadarthatvāj jyotiṣṭomārthatvāc{*3/619*} cheṣo 'yaṃ grahadharmaḥ, grahanimitto jyotiṣṭomasyopakārakaḥ. yāvān graho jyotiṣṭomasyopakaroti, tasya sarvasya bhavitum arhati. tasmād aṃśvadābhyayor api grahadharmāḥ kartavyā iti.
children.translated_text: Or [the distant cups] would be connected with the prescriptions — such [cups] should be [treated] thus, even though not in the [immediate] context. Why? Because [Vedic] statement is stronger than context. [Objection:] But [the prescriptions] performed elsewhere would not benefit the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. [Reply:] It is said: they will benefit [it], because the <s>Aṃśu</s> and <s>Ādāb(h)ya</s> are for the purpose of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. This residual cup-prescription, being occasioned by the cup[-nature], is beneficial to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Whatever cup benefits the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — it deserves to have all [such prescriptions]. Therefore, the cup-prescriptions should be performed even for the <s>Aṃśu</s> and <s>Ādāb(h)ya</s>.

children.text: nirdeśād vyavatiṣṭheta // MS_3,6.34 //
children.translated_text: It would be established by specification. // MS 3,6.34 //

children.text: yad uktam - yathā maitrāvaruṇaṃ payasā śrīṇātīti, tad yuktam, śrayaṇe vacanāt, prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā vyavasthānam. iha tu viparītam, tatra sarveṣu graheṣu prakaraṇam, viśiṣṭeṣu vākyam. iha tu sarveṣu graheṣu vākyam, viśiṣṭeṣu prakaraṇam. tasmād aprakaraṇasthasyāpi dharmā iti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'just as he enriches the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> with milk' — that is justified because [Vedic] statement [specifies the] enrichment, overriding the context to establish [it for that cup alone]. But here it is the reverse: there, the context is for all cups and the [Vedic] statement is for specific ones; here, the [Vedic] statement is for all cups and the context is for specific ones. Therefore, even what is not in the [immediate] context has the prescriptions.

children.text: agnyaṅgaprakaraṇe tadvat // MS_3,6.35 //
children.translated_text: And the fire-subsidiary [elements] in the context are likewise. // MS 3,6.35 //

children.text: anārabhyāgnim ucyate - citriṇīr upadadhāti, vajriṇīr upadadhāti{*3/620*}, bhūteṣṭakā upadadhātīti{*3/621*}. santi tu prakaraṇe, iṣṭakādharmāḥ, akhaṇḍām akṛṣṇalām iṣṭakāṃ kuryād iti. tatha bhasmanā iṣṭakāḥ saṃyujyād iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim aprakaraṇe samāmnātānām ime dharmāḥ kartavyāḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? na kartavyāḥ. kutaḥ? asaṃnidhānād, iti prāpte, ucyate - agnyaṅgam evaṃjātīyakaṃ tadvad eva syāt, yadvad grahāḥ. prakaraṇād dhi vākyaṃ balavat. amūṣāṃ ceṣṭakānām agnyarthatvāt.
children.translated_text: Without reference to [a particular] fire it is stated: 'he places the <s>citriṇī</s> (variegated) [bricks], he places the <s>vajriṇī</s> (thunderbolt) [bricks], he places the <s>bhūteṣṭakā</s> (element-bricks).' But in the context, there are brick-prescriptions: 'he should make an unbroken, non-black brick'; similarly, 'he should join the bricks with ash.' There the doubt arises: should these prescriptions apply to those taught outside the context, or not? What is the prima facie view? They should not, because of the absence of proximity. Given this, it is said: the fire-subsidiary [elements] of this kind should be just the same — like the cups. For [Vedic] statement is stronger than context. And because those bricks are for the purpose of the fire.

children.text: naimittikam atulyatvād asamānavidhānaṃ syāt // MS_3,6.36 //
children.translated_text: An occasional [rite] has a non-identical prescription, because of the inequality. // MS 3,6.36 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - sa yadi rājanyaṃ vā{*3/623*} vaiśyaṃ vā yājayet, sa yadi somaṃ vibhakṣayiṣet, nyagrodhastibhīr āhṛtya tāḥ saṃpiṣya dadhany unmṛjya tamasmai bhakṣaṃ prayacchen na somam iti. jyotiṣṭome santi somadharmāḥ, mānam upāvaharaṇaṃ krayo 'bhiṣava ityevamādayaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ samānavidhānā ime dharmāḥ somasya phalacamasya ca, uta somadharmāḥ, phalacamasasya tu tadvikāratvād iti. guṇakāmānāṃ pravṛttir vā prayojanam adhikaraṇacintāyāḥ{*3/624*}.
kiṃ prāptam? samānavidhānāḥ prakaraṇāvibhāgād iti prāpte, ucyate - naimittikam evaṃjātīyakaṃ asamānavidhānaṃ{*3/625*} syāt. kutaḥ? atulyatvāt, atulyaḥ somena phalacamasaḥ, somo nityavad āmnātāḥ, phalacamaso naimittikaḥ. kim ataḥ? yady evam, dharmā api nityavad āmnātāḥ na śakyā anityavat kartum. yadi sādhāraṇāḥ, tatrānārabhyo 'rtho vidhīyeta. api ca naimittikaḥ phalacamasaḥ sa somadharmān gṛhṇāti, tatra dharmāḥ sādhāraṇāḥ santo dviruktā ity ucyeran. tasmād asamānavidhānāḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'if he should have a <s>kṣatriya</s> or a <s>vaiśya</s> perform the sacrifice, if he should wish to give him <s>Soma</s> to drink, having gathered <s>nyagrodha</s> shoots, having ground them, having mixed them in curds, he should give him that as a <s>bhakṣa</s>, not <s>Soma</s>.' In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there are <s>Soma</s>-prescriptions — measuring, bringing near, purchasing, pressing, and so forth. There the doubt arises: are these prescriptions the same (<s>samānavidhāna</s>) for <s>Soma</s> and for the <s>phalacamasa</s>, or are they <s>Soma</s>-prescriptions [only], with the <s>phalacamasa</s> being a modification of that? Or the purpose of this topic's inquiry is the application for those desiring [specific] qualities.
What is the prima facie view? [They have] identical prescriptions, because of the non-distinction of the context. Given this, it is said: an occasional [rite] of this kind should have a non-identical prescription. Why? Because of the inequality — the <s>phalacamasa</s> is unequal to <s>Soma</s>. <s>Soma</s> is taught as if permanent; the <s>phalacamasa</s> is occasional. What follows? If so, the prescriptions too, being taught as if permanent, cannot be performed as if occasional. If [they were] common, then a purposeless general prescription would be enjoined for them. Moreover, the <s>phalacamasa</s> is occasional and takes the <s>Soma</s>-prescriptions [from the archetype]; there, the prescriptions, being common, would be said to be repeated. Therefore, [they have] non-identical prescriptions.

children.text: pratinidhiś ca tadvat // MS_3,6.37 //
children.translated_text: And a substitute (<s>pratinidhi</s>) is likewise. // MS 3,6.37 //

children.text: asti pratinidhiḥ, śrute dravye 'pacarati, yathā vrīhiṣv apacaratsu nīvārāḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ nīvārāḥ samānavidhānāḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? pratinidhiś ca tadvat, yathā naimi[382]{*3/626*}ttikaṃ nityenāsamānavidhānam, evaṃ pratinidhiḥ, atulyatvāt. kātulyatā? vrīhīṇāṃ vihitāḥ, na nīvārāṇām. iyam atulyatā, vrīhīṇāṃ vihitāḥ, nīvārāṇām arthāpattyā bhavanti.
children.translated_text: There is a substitute — when the [originally] heard substance is unavailable, [another is used], just as <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice) [replaces] <s>vrīhi</s> (cultivated rice) when it is unavailable. There the doubt arises: do the <s>nīvāras</s> have identical prescriptions [as <s>vrīhis</s>], or not? What is the prima facie view? The substitute is likewise — just as an occasional [rite] has non-identical prescriptions with the permanent [rite], so does the substitute, because of the inequality. What is the inequality? [The prescriptions] are enjoined for <s>vrīhis</s>, not for <s>nīvāras</s>. This is the inequality — [they are] enjoined for <s>vrīhis</s>; for <s>nīvāras</s> they obtain through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>).

children.text: tadvat{*3/627*} prayojanaikatvāt // MS_3,6.38 //
children.translated_text: [The substitute] is the same, because of the unity of purpose. // MS 3,6.38 //

children.text: naitad asti - asamānavidhānaḥ pratinidhir iti, tadvat syāt, yadvac chrutaḥ, na prakṛtivikārabhāvaḥ. kutaḥ? vrīhitvaṃ hi vrīhidharmāṇāṃ vrīhivyaktau nimittam. na ca vrīhitvasya sthāne nīvāratvaṃ bhavatīti śrūyate, tasmān na prakṛtivikārabhāvaḥ. kathaṃ tarhi nīvāreṣu dharmā bhavantīti. ucyate -yā vrīhitvena paricchinnā vrīhivyaktayaḥ, nīvāreṣu tāḥ santi. tāsām arthena te dharmāḥ kriyante, tāsāṃ ca vyaktīnām anyāsāṃ ca vrīhigatānāṃ tulya eṣa vidhiḥ. kā tulyatā? ubhaye 'pi vrīhitvalakṣitā iti. tasmāt samānavidhānā iti.
children.translated_text: This is not the case — that the substitute has non-identical prescriptions. It should be the same as what is heard; there is no archetype-modification relationship. Why? For the <s>vrīhi</s>-nature is the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) for <s>vrīhi</s>-prescriptions in a particular instance of <s>vrīhi</s>. But it is not heard that <s>nīvāra</s>-nature takes the place of <s>vrīhi</s>-nature. Therefore, there is no archetype-modification relationship. How then do the prescriptions apply to <s>nīvāras</s>? It is said: those particular instances of <s>vrīhi</s> that are delimited by <s>vrīhi</s>-nature — they exist in <s>nīvāras</s>. Through their purpose, those prescriptions are performed; and for those particular instances and for the other <s>vrīhi</s>-instances, this prescription is the same. What is the sameness? Both are delimited by <s>vrīhi</s>-nature. Therefore, [they have] identical prescriptions.

children.text: aśāstralakṣaṇatvāc ca // MS_3,6.39 //
children.translated_text: And because [the substitute relationship] is not characterized by scripture. // MS 3,6.39 //

children.text: itaś ca na pratinidheḥ śrutena saha prakṛtivikārabhāvaḥ. kutaḥ? arthalakṣaṇatvāt, arthād dhi pratinidhiḥ kriyate. na cārthenaitad avagantuṃ śakyate, vrīhitvasya sthāne nīvāratvaṃ bhavatīti. tasmān na pratinidheḥ śrutena saha prakṛtivikārabhāvo bhavatīti.
children.translated_text: Moreover, for this reason too there is no archetype-modification relationship between the substitute and the [originally] heard [substance]. Why? Because [it] is characterized by purpose (<s>artha</s>) — for the substitute is made on the basis of purpose [i.e., pragmatic inference]. And it cannot be understood through purpose that <s>nīvāra</s>-nature takes the place of <s>vrīhi</s>-nature. Therefore, there is no archetype-modification relationship between the substitute and the [originally] heard [substance].

children.text: niyamārthā guṇaśrutiḥ // MS_3,6.40 //
children.translated_text: The mention of a [specific] quality [in the substitute] is for the purpose of restriction. // MS 3,6.40 //

children.text: atha yaḥ śrutaḥ pratinidhiḥ, tatra kiṃ sāmānavidhyam uta na [383]{*3/628*} iti. yathā - yadi somaṃ na vindeta pūtīkān abhiṣuṇuyād iti{*3/629*}. asāmānavidhyam iti brūmaḥ, aśrutād dhy etad viparītam. evaṃ prāpta ucyate - niyamārthā guṇaśrutiḥ, atrāpy arthalakṣaṇa eva pratinidhiḥ, some 'vidyamāne somasadṛśaṃ dravyaṃ prāptam. tatra susadṛśe dravye prāpta īṣatsadṛśaṃ niyamyate. anyasmin pratinidhātavye 'nyat pratinidhīyate śrutasya sthāne. na yāgadravyatvena.
children.translated_text: Now, where there is a substitute that is heard [in scripture], is there identical prescription or not? For example: 'if one cannot find <s>Soma</s>, one should press <s>pūtīka</s> [as a substitute].' We say: [there is] non-identical prescription, for this is the opposite of [the case of] an unheard [substitute]. Given this, it is said: the mention of a quality is for the purpose of restriction. Here too the substitute is characterized by purpose alone — when <s>Soma</s> is unavailable, a substance similar to <s>Soma</s> is obtained [by inference]. There, when a closely similar substance is obtained, a slightly similar one is restricted [to its place by the scriptural mention]. One [substance] is substituted in place of another that should be substituted, in place of the heard [original] — not in the capacity of being a sacrificial substance [in its own right].

children.text: saṃsthās tu samānavidhānāḥ prakaraṇāviśeṣāt // MS_3,6.41 //
children.translated_text: But the <s>saṃsthās</s> (concluding forms of sacrifice) have identical prescriptions, because of the non-distinction of the context. // MS 3,6.41 //

children.text: asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ, tatra saṃsthāḥ samāmnātā agniṣṭomaḥ, ukthyaḥ, ṣoḍaśī, atirātra iti. tatra dīkṣaṇīyādayo dharmāḥ. teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sarvasaṃsthaṃ jyotiṣṭomaṃ prakṛtya dīkṣaṇīyādayo dharmā uktāḥ, utāgniṣṭomasaṃsthyam{*3/630*} abhipretyeti. kiṃ prāptam? sarvasaṃsthāsu samānaṃ vidhānam. kutaḥ? prakaraṇāviśeṣāt, nāsti prakaraṇe viśeṣaḥ, yena jñāyetāgniṣṭomasaṃsthaṃ prakṛtyeti. tasmāt samānavidhānāḥ saṃsthā iti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; there the <s>saṃsthās</s> are taught — <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>. There are prescriptions such as the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration sacrifice) and so forth. Regarding these, the doubt arises: are the prescriptions such as the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> stated with reference to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> of all <s>saṃsthās</s>, or with reference to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>saṃsthā</s> [alone]? What is the prima facie view? The prescription is identical for all <s>saṃsthās</s>. Why? Because of the non-distinction of the context — there is no distinction in the context by which one could know that [the prescriptions] are stated with reference to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>saṃsthā</s> [alone]. Therefore, the <s>saṃsthās</s> have identical prescriptions.

children.text: vyapadeśaś ca tulyavat // MS_3,6.42 //
children.translated_text: And the designation is equally [applicable]. // MS 3,6.42 //

children.text:
tulya iva prakaraṇe vyapadeśo bhavati - yady agniṣṭomo juhoti, yady ukthyaḥ paridhimanakti, yady atirātra etad eva yajur japan havirdhānaṃ pratipadyeteti sarvāvasthasya viśeṣavacanād avagamyate. yadi api sāmānyam, tad api sarvāvasthasyaiveti. yadi hi na{*3/631*} samānaṃ vidhānam, agniṣṭomasaṃsthasyaiva [384]{*3/632*} syāt. nehāgniṣṭomaṃ saṃkīrtayet, asaṃkīrtyamāne 'pi dharmasaṃbandho bhavatīti, sarvāvasthasya kīrtanāt sarvāvasthaprakaraṇam{*3/633*} ity avagacchāmaḥ.
api ca śrūyate - āgneyam ajam agniṣṭoma ālabheta, aindrāgnaṃ dvitīyam ukthye, aindraṃ vṛṣṇiṃ tṛtī-yaṃ ṣoḍaśinīti dvitīyasya tṛtīyasya ca darśanaṃ sāmānavidhye ghaṭate. ukthye hi dve nimitte staḥ, agniṣṭomastotram ukthyastotraṃ ceti, tatra dvau naimittikāv āgneyaḥ paśuḥ, aindrāgnaś ceti tena dvitīyadarśanaṃ tatra yujyate. evaṃ ṣoḍaśiny atirātre ca. prakṛtivikārabhāve tu pratyakṣaśrutair aindrāgnādibhir atideśena prāpta āgneyo bādhyeta. tatra dvitīyādidarśanaṃ nopapadyeta. bhavati ca. tasmāt sarvāvasthasya jyotiṣṭomasya dīkṣaṇīyādayo dharmā iti.
children.translated_text:
In what seems to be a common context, there is specific designation: "If [he performs] the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, he offers; if the <s>Ukthya</s>, he anoints the enclosing sticks; if the <s>Atirātra</s>, reciting this very <s>yajus</s>, he proceeds to the <s>Havirdhāna</s>" — from the specific statements for all stages, it is understood [that these apply to all]. Even if there is generality, that too is for all stages. For if [384] the injunction were not common, it would belong only to one who concludes with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. It would not mention the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> here — even without mentioning it, the connection of rites would exist. Since all stages are mentioned, we understand the context belongs to all stages.
Moreover, it is heard: "An <s>Āgneya</s> goat is to be slaughtered in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, an <s>Aindrāgna</s> [animal] as the second in the <s>Ukthya</s>, an <s>Aindra</s> bull as the third in the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>" — the evidence of a second and third is consistent with the view of common injunction. For in the <s>Ukthya</s> there are two causes — the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>stotra</s> and the <s>Ukthya</s> <s>stotra</s> — and therefore two caused [victims]: the <s>Āgneya</s> animal and the <s>Aindrāgna</s>; thus the evidence of a second is fitting there. Likewise for the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> and <s>Atirātra</s>. But under the archetype-modification view, the <s>Āgneya</s>, established by <s>atideśa</s> (analogical extension), would be superseded by the explicitly-stated <s>Aindrāgna</s> and others. Then the evidence of a second and so forth would be impossible. But it does exist. Therefore the consecration-rites and other properties belong to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> in all its stages.

children.text:

children.translated_text:
