children.text: vikārās tu kāmasaṃyoge sa nityasya{*3/634*} samatvāt // MS_3,6.43 //
children.translated_text: But the modifications are [optional,] connected with desire, because of equality with the permanent [rite]. // MS_3,6.43 //

children.text:
naitad asti, samānavidhānā iti. kiṃ tarhy ukthyādayaḥ saṃsthāvikārabhūtāḥ syuḥ, agniṣṭomasaṃsthyamurīkṛtya{*3/635*} dīkṣaṇīyādayo dharmāḥ samāmnātāḥ. kutaḥ? ukthyādīnāṃ kāmasaṃyogena śravaṇāt. paśukāma ukthyaṃ gṛhṇīyāt, ṣoḍaśinā vīryakāmaḥ stuvīta, atirātreṇa prajākāmaṃ yājayed iti. kāmyo guṇaḥ śrūyamāṇo nityam arthaṃ vikṛtya niviśate. katham? guṇād evaṃjātīyake kāmye phalanirvṛttiḥ, paśukāma ukthyaṃ gṛhṇīyāt, na jyotiṣṭomakāma ukthyagrahaṇakāmo vā, yathā paśavo bhavanti, tathā gṛhṇīyād ity arthaḥ. katham iti. tatrāvaśyam itikartavyatāpekṣitavyā, saṃnidhānān nityasyetikartavyatayeti gamyate.
kathaṃ punar yeyam itikartavyatā, sā nityasyety avadhāryate, [385]{*3/636*} na punar asyaiva kāmyasya, sādhāraṇī veti. ucyate - yatra yatra guṇe kāmo bhavati, tatra tatra kriyāyāṃ sādhyamānāyāṃ nānyathā. sā tatretikartavyatā, yāntikam upanipatati, sā sādhanasya vā sādhyasya veti saṃdihyamānā sādhyasya bhavitum arhati. nāsau sādhyasyābhavantī sādhanena saṃbadhyate, evaṃ hi sa itikartavyatāviśeṣaś codyate, anena sādhane{*3/637*} sādhakam upakuryād{*3/638*} iti. na cāsti sa prakāraḥ, yenāsādhyamānāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ tena sādhakaḥ kṛto bhavet. tasmāt sādhakasyāpītikartavyatāviśeṣam abhyupagacchatā, sādhyasyāpīty etad abhyupagamanīyam, sādhyaś ca jyotiṣṭomaḥ, sādhikāḥ saṃsthāḥ, tasmāj jyotiṣṭomasya tāvat setikartavyateti siddham.
atha kasmān na sādhāraṇī? nityavad āmnānāt, yadaiva jyotiṣṭomaḥ, tadaiva dīkṣā. yadā tu jyotiṣṭome paśukāmaḥ, tadokthyasaṃsthāḥ, sarvadā jyotiṣṭome dharmāḥ kartavyāḥ, ekadokthyasaṃsthāḥ, tatra sarvadā jyotiṣṭomasya dharmāḥ kartavyāḥ, te cokthyādisaṃsthasyārtheneti pūrvam uttareṇa virudhyate, yadi sarvadā nokthyādīnām arthena. athokthyādīnām arthena na sarvadā, ubhayaṃ viprati-ṣiddham. tasmān na sādhāraṇī. nityavad āmnānaṃ ca yady anityasya syāt, nityavad āmnānaṃ tad anityaṃ kriyeta, tatra nityavad āmnānaṃ bādhyeta. tasmān nityasaṃsthasya jyotiṣṭomasya, na kāmyasyokthyādisaṃsthasyeti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — [they are not] of common injunction. What then? The <s>Ukthya</s> and others would be modifications of the conclusion (<s>saṃsthā</s>); the consecration-rites and other properties are taught with reference to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> conclusion. Why? Because the <s>Ukthya</s> and others are heard in connection with desire: "One desiring cattle should take the <s>Ukthya</s> [cup]; one desiring strength should praise with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>; one desiring progeny should have the <s>Atirātra</s> performed." An optional quality, when heard, settles by modifying a permanent [archetype]. How? From such an optional quality of this kind, the result is produced: "one desiring cattle should take the <s>Ukthya</s>" — not one desiring the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> or desiring the <s>Ukthya</s> cup [itself]; the meaning is: he should take [it] in such a way that cattle arise. How so? There, the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) must necessarily be expected; from proximity, it is understood as the procedure of the permanent [rite].
But how is this procedure determined to belong to the permanent [rite] [385] and not to this very optional one, or to be common? We reply: wherever there is desire in a quality, there [the procedure applies] when the act is being accomplished, not otherwise. The procedure that comes about incidentally there — being doubtful whether it belongs to the means or to what is to be accomplished — should belong to what is to be accomplished. Not belonging to what is to be accomplished, it would be connected with the means; but thus a particular procedure would be enjoined — "through this means it would assist the means" — and there is no way in which, without the act being accomplished, the means would be made effective by it. Therefore, for one who accepts a particular procedure for the means, one must also accept it for what is to be accomplished. And what is to be accomplished is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; the conclusions (<s>saṃsthā</s>) are the means. Therefore it is established that the procedure belongs first to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
And why not common? Because of being taught as if permanent — whenever there is a <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, there is consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>). But when in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> one desires cattle, then the <s>Ukthya</s> conclusion [applies]; the rites of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> must be performed always, but the <s>Ukthya</s> conclusion only once. There, the rites of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> must always be performed, and they serve the <s>Ukthya</s>-concluded [sacrifice] — the earlier contradicts the later, if they do not always serve the <s>Ukthya</s> and others. And if they serve the <s>Ukthya</s> and others but not always — both are contradictory. Therefore it is not common. And if teaching as permanent were for what is non-permanent, the teaching-as-permanent would make it non-permanent, and thereby the teaching-as-permanent would be contradicted. Therefore [the rites belong to] the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> concluding with the permanent [Agniṣṭoma], not to the optional one concluding with <s>Ukthya</s> and others.

children.text: api vā dviruktatvāt prakṛter bhaviṣyantīti // MS_3,6.44 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of being stated twice, [the rites] will belong to the archetype. // MS_3,6.44 //

children.text: nanv agniṣṭomasaṃsthāpi kāmyā śrūyate. dve hi tatrāmnāte{*3/639*}, ekaṃ nityavat, ekaṃ kāmyam, tatra dvayor vākyayoḥ sāmarthyān nitya eva sakāmo bhaviṣyati. nityatāvidhāto [386]{*3/640*} nāstīty agniṣṭomasaṃsthasya jyotiṣṭomasya dīkṣaṇīyādayo dharmā bhaviṣyantīti.
children.translated_text: But the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> conclusion is also heard as optional. For there two [statements] are taught — one as permanent, one as optional. There, by the force of the two sentences, the desire will attach to the permanent one alone. Since there is no injunction of permanence, [386] the consecration-rites and other properties will belong to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> concluding with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: vacanāt tu samuccayaḥ // MS_3,6.45 //
children.translated_text: But because of a [specific] statement, there is accumulation. // MS_3,6.45 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - dvitīyatṛtīyadarśanaṃ samānavidhitve 'vakalpate, nānyatheti, vacanaṃ tad bhaviṣyati, na darśanam. aindrāgna ukthye dvitīyo vidhīyate, tathaindraḥ ṣoḍaśini tṛtīyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was stated — that the evidence of a second and third is possible under the view of common injunction, not otherwise — that would be a [specific] injunctive statement, not merely evidence. The <s>Aindrāgna</s> [victim] is enjoined as the second in the <s>Ukthya</s>; likewise the <s>Aindra</s> [is enjoined] as the third in the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>.

children.text: pratiṣedhāc ca pūrvaliṅgānām // MS_3,6.46 //
children.translated_text: And because of the prohibition of the marks of the prior [stage]. // MS_3,6.46 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmaḥ prakṛtivikārabhāva iti. kutaḥ? pratiṣedhāt pūrvaliṅgānām - yady agniṣṭomo juhoti, yady ukthyaḥ paridhimanakti na juhotīti homābhāvadarśanaṃ na syāt. prāpte nimitte vacanaprāmāṇyāt sāmānavidhye.
children.translated_text: From this too we observe that there is an archetype-modification relationship. Why? Because of the prohibition of the marks of the prior [stage] — "if [he performs] the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, he offers; if the <s>Ukthya</s>, he anoints the enclosing sticks, he does not offer" — there would be no evidence of the absence of oblation [under the other view]. When the cause is established, by the authority of the statement, [it is not possible] under the view of common injunction.

children.text: guṇaviśeṣād ekasya vyapadeśaḥ // MS_3,6.47 //
children.translated_text: The designation of one [stage] is because of a particular subsidiary quality. // MS_3,6.47 //

children.text: atha yad uktam - vyapadeśa iti. ekasyaivādhikṛtasya yathoktena nyāyenāyam anadhikṛtena guṇena vyapadeśaḥ. agniṣṭomagrahaṇaṃ cānuvāda iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was stated about the designation — the designation belongs to one and the same [sacrificer] who is the principal agent, by the aforementioned reasoning, through a quality that is not his principal [one]. And the mention of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>).

children.text: prakaraṇaviśeṣād asaṃyuktaṃ pradhānasya // MS_3,7.1 //
children.translated_text: Because of the specific context, what is unconnected [belongs] to the principal [rite]. // MS_3,7.1 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra barhir barhir dharmāś ca, tathā vedir vedidharmāś ca. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ barhirādayo barhirādidharmāś ca pradhānasyotāṅgapradhānānām iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? prakaraṇaviśeṣād asaṃyuktaṃ pradhānasya, pradhānasya evaṃjātīyakā dharmāḥ. kasmāt? prakaraṇaviśeṣāt, pradhānānāṃ hi prakaraṇaṃ nāṅgānām, prakaraṇena caiṣāṃ saṃbandhaḥ, tasmāt pradhānasya.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites; therein are the sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>) and the rites pertaining to the <s>barhis</s>; likewise the altar (<s>vedi</s>) and the rites pertaining to the altar. There a doubt [arises]: do the <s>barhis</s> and other [items] along with their rites belong to the principal [rite] or to both the subsidiary and principal? What is the prima facie view? Because of the specific context, what is unconnected [belongs] to the principal — rites of this kind belong to the principal alone. Why? Because of the specific context — for the context belongs to the principal rites, not to the subsidiaries, and the connection of these [items] is through context; therefore they belong to the principal.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vā śeṣatvasyātatprayuktatvāt // MS_3,7.2 //
children.translated_text: Or [they belong] to all, because subsidiary-status is not prompted by that [context alone]. // MS_3,7.2 //

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ vāṅgapradhānānām ime dharmāḥ, nātra śeṣatvaṃ prakaraṇād bhavati, upakāralakṣaṇaṃ hi tat. yad yasyopakaroti, tat tasya śeṣabhūtam, sarveṣāṃ cāṅgapradhānānām ime dharmā upakurvanti. katham avagamyate? vākyāt, vedyāṃ havīṃṣy āsādayatīti havirmātraṃ vākyād gamyate, pradhānahavīṃṣi prakaraṇāt. vākyaṃ ca prakaraṇād balīyaḥ, tasmād barhiṣi havīṃṣy āsādayatīti.
āha yadi prakaraṇaṃ vākyena bādhyate, loke 'pi barhiṣām ime dharmā uktā bhavanti. tatra ko doṣaḥ? sarvatra dharmāḥ kartavyāḥ prāpnuvanti. ucyate - prakaraṇād darśapūrṇamāsayor upakārakā eveti gamyate. tasmāl laukikeṣu na kartavyāḥ.
evaṃ ced aṅgāny api na darśapūrṇamāsaśabadakāni, tasmāt teṣv api na prāpnuvanti. ucyate - yady apy aṅgāni na darśapūrṇamāsa[388]{*3/642*}śabdakāni, darśapūrṇamāsayor upakārakāṇi, eṣu kriyamāṇā dharmā darśapūrṇamāsayor upakariṣyanti. tasmād aṅgapradhāneṣu kartavyā iti.
children.translated_text:
Or these rites belong to all — both subsidiary and principal. Subsidiary-status here does not arise from context; rather, it is defined by helpfulness. Whatever helps something is subsidiary to it, and these rites help all — both subsidiary and principal. How is this known? From the sentence — "he places the oblations on the altar" — from the sentence, oblations in general are understood; from context, the principal oblations. And the sentence is stronger than context. Therefore, he places the oblations on the <s>barhis</s> [i.e., for all rites].
[The objector] says: if context is overridden by the sentence, then these rites of the <s>barhis</s> would be stated as applying in worldly [contexts] too. What is the defect there? The rites would apply everywhere. We reply: from context, it is understood that they are helpful only in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Therefore they should not be performed in worldly [contexts].
If so, the subsidiaries too are not denoted by the word "<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>"; therefore [the rites] would not apply to them either. We reply: though the subsidiaries are not denoted by the word "<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>," [388] they are helpful to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; when these rites are performed in them, they will help the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Therefore they should be performed in both subsidiary and principal [rites].

children.text: ārād apīti cet // MS_3,7.3 //
children.translated_text: Even from afar [the objection arises] — // MS_3,7.3 //

children.text: piṇḍapitṛyajñe 'pi barhir dharmair yujyeta, so 'pi dāte barhiṣi vartate, tasya cāpi barhiṣāsti prayojanam. tad apy ārāc chiṣṭadharmavat syāt.
children.translated_text: The <s>barhis</s> rites would also apply in the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (ancestral offering), for that too operates with the <s>barhis</s> that is given, and it too has a purpose involving the <s>barhis</s>. That too, though remote, would be like what is taught regarding the rites.

children.text: na tad vākyaṃ hi tadarthatvāt // MS_3,7.4 //
children.translated_text: Not so, for the sentence is directed to that purpose. // MS_3,7.4 //

children.text: na tasya barhir etair dharmair dharmavat, vākyaṃ hy ekaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ saha dharmāṇām, tena darśapūrṇamāsayor upakārakā dharmāḥ, yad darśapūrṇamāsārtham, tatra prāpnuvanti, nānyatra. tasmāt piṇḍapitṛyajñabarhiṣo na bhaviṣyanti.
children.translated_text: The <s>barhis</s> of that [Piṇḍapitṛyajña] is not endowed with these rites, for the sentence connecting the rites with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is one [unit]. Therefore the rites are helpful to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; they apply where [something] serves the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> purpose, not elsewhere. Therefore they will not apply to the <s>barhis</s> of the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s>.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_3,7.5 //
children.translated_text: And because of indicative evidence. // MS_3,7.5 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ bhavati, evam āha - sa vai dhruvām evāgre 'bhidhārayati, tato hi prathamāvājyabhāgau yakṣyan bhavatīty abhidhāraṇasyājyabhāgārthatāṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: There is indicative evidence — thus it states: "He first holds the <s>Dhruvā</s> [ladle], for then he is about to offer the <s>Ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions)" — showing that the holding (<s>abhidhāraṇa</s>) serves the purpose of the <s>Ājyabhāgas</s>.

children.text: phalasaṃyogāt tu svāmiyuktaṃ pradhānasya // MS_3,7.6 //
children.translated_text: But because of connection with the result, what is connected with the owner [belongs] to the principal [rite]. // MS_3,7.6 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome keśaśmaśruṇor vapanaṃ payovratāni tapaś cāmnātāni. teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kim aṅgapradhānārthāny uta pradhānārthāni? kiṃ tāvat prāptam? aṅgapradhānārthānīti pūrveṇa nyāyena prāptam.
[389]{*3/643*} evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - svāmiyuktam etat, tasmāt pradhānasya. kasmāt? phalasaṃyogāt, puruṣasya yogenāyaṃ saṃbandhaḥ, yāgo 'pūrvasya dātā, puruṣaḥ pratigrahītā. nanv aparo 'py asti saṃbandhaḥ, yāgo nirvartyaḥ, puruṣo 'bhinirvartaka iti. phalena tu saṃbandho bhaviṣyatīty evam arthaḥ puruṣaḥ śrūyate. na hi yāgaṃ sa sādhayati, yāgaḥ sattayā saṃbhantsyata iti. kim iti tarhi nirvartayataḥ phalaṃ bhavatīti. saṃskārāś ca saṃskurvantīty ucyante. yat tasya saṃskartavyasya prayojanam, tatra sāmarthyaṃ janayantīti. phalaṃ ca grahītuṃ puruṣasya prayojanam, na yāgam abhinirvartayitum. tasmād ye puruṣasaṃskārās te puruṣaṃ phalapratigrahaṇasamarthaṃ kurvanti, na yāganirvṛttisamartham. āha, yadi yāganirvṛttau na sāmarthyaṃ janayanti, kathaṃ tarhi yāgadharmās te bhavanti. ucyate - yāgasya svārthaṃ sādhayataḥ sāhāyye vartante. kaś ca tasya svārthaḥ? yad asya kartā phalena saṃbadhyate. tasmāt svāmisaṃskārāḥ pradhānārthā iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, shaving of hair and beard, milk-vows, and austerity are taught. Regarding these, a doubt [arises]: do they serve both subsidiary and principal, or only the principal? What is the prima facie view? By the previous reasoning, they serve both subsidiary and principal.
[389] Given this, we say: this is connected with the owner (<s>svāmin</s>, i.e., the sacrificer); therefore it belongs to the principal. Why? Because of connection with the result — the person's connection is this: the sacrifice gives the unprecedented [result], and the person is the recipient. But is there not another connection too — the sacrifice is what is to be accomplished, and the person is the accomplisher? [Yes, but] the person is heard in this sense: the connection will be through the result. For the person does not accomplish the sacrifice in the sense that the sacrifice will benefit [from his] existence. Why then does the result accrue to the one who accomplishes it? And consecrations are said to consecrate — they generate capacity in what is to be consecrated for its purpose. And the person's purpose is to receive the result, not to accomplish the sacrifice. Therefore those personal consecrations make the person capable of receiving the result, not capable of accomplishing the sacrifice. [The objector] says: if they do not generate capacity in accomplishing the sacrifice, how are they rites of the sacrifice? We reply: they assist the sacrifice in accomplishing its own purpose. And what is its own purpose? That its performer is connected with the result. Therefore the owner's consecrations serve the principal rite.

children.text: cikīrṣayā ca saṃyogāt // MS_3,7.7 //
children.translated_text: And because of connection with the intention [to perform]. // MS_3,7.7 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - ṣaṭtriṃśatprakamā prācī caturviṃśatir agreṇa triṃśaj jaghaneneyati śakyāmaha iti{*3/644*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim eṣā vedir aṅgapradhānārthā, uta pradhānārtheti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? cikīrṣayā ca saṃyogāt pradhānārtheti. kā cikīrṣā? iyati śakṣyāmaha iti. yac cikīrṣitam, tasyārthenaiṣā śrūyate - śakṣyāmahe 'syāṃ kartum iti pradhānaṃ ca tasya cikīrṣitam, nāṅgāni. pradhānaṃ hi phalavan nāṅgāni.
[390]{*3/645*} āha yady aṅgāni na cikīrṣitāni, kim arthaṃ kriyanta iti. ucyate - acikīrṣitāny apy aṅgāni kriyante, yady api tāni na cikīrṣyante, tathāpi tair acikīrṣitair anyāc cikīrṣyate. tasmāt tāni kriyanta iti, yac cikīrṣitam, tasya vediḥ. tasmāt pradhānārtheti, sthitaṃ tāvad aparyavasitam{*3/646*}.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'thirty-six [spans] eastward, twenty-four at the front [end], thirty at the back end — this much we shall be able [to do].' There the doubt arises: is this <s>vedi</s> (altar) for the purpose of both subsidiaries and the principal [rite], or for the purpose of the principal [rite alone]? What is the prima facie view? Because of the connection with the intention (<s>cikīrṣā</s>), [it is] for the purpose of the principal [rite]. What is the intention? 'This much we shall be able [to do].' That which is intended — for its purpose, this [<s>vedi</s>] is heard: 'we shall be able to perform [rites] on it.' And the principal [rite] is intended, not the subsidiaries. For the principal [rite] has fruit, not the subsidiaries.
[Objection:] It is said: if the subsidiaries are not intended, for what purpose are they performed? [Reply:] It is said: even though the subsidiaries are not intended, they are performed — even though they are not intended [for themselves], through them, which are not themselves intended, something else is intended. Therefore, they are performed. The <s>vedi</s> is for what is intended. Therefore, [it is] for the purpose of the principal [rite] — this much stands provisionally without final determination.

children.text: tathābhidhānena // MS_3,7.8 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, because of the designation. // MS 3,7.8 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra śrūyate - caturhotrā paurṇamāsīm abhimṛśet, pañcahotrā amāv āsyām iti{*3/647*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim aṅgapradhānārtham abhimarśanam, uta pradhānārtham iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? pradhānārtham iti, pradhānanāmadheyaṃ caitat{*3/648*}, paurṇamāsy amāvāsyeti ca. tasmāt pradhānasyābhimarśanam iti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon rites); there it is heard: 'with the four-priest [formula] one should touch [the altar] at the full-moon [rite]; with the five-priest [formula] at the new-moon [rite].' There the doubt arises: is the touching for the purpose of both subsidiaries and the principal [rite], or for the purpose of the principal [rite alone]? What is the prima facie view? [It is] for the purpose of the principal [rite] — for this [designation] bears the name of the principal [rite], namely '<s>paurṇamāsī</s>' (full-moon) and '<s>amāvāsyā</s>' (new-moon). Therefore, the touching is of the principal [rite].

NOTES:
[{3/647: <s>Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā</s> 1.9.1}]
[{3/648: E2,4: <s>ca tat</s>}]

children.text: tad yukte tu phalaśrutis tasmāt sarvacikīrṣā syāt // MS_3,7.9 //
children.translated_text: But [the fruit is] heard [as arising] from the combined [whole]; therefore, the intention should be for all [elements]. // MS 3,7.9 //

children.text: sthitād uttaram{*3/649*}. yad uktam - pradhānaṃ cikīrṣitaṃ nāṅgāni, tasmāt pradhānasya vedir iti. tan na, tad yukte phalaśrutiḥ, sāṅgāt phalaṃ śrūyate, tasmāt sāṅgaṃ cikīrṣitam. yady apy aṅgāni na cikī[391]{*3/650*}rṣitāni, tathāpi vedyāṃ kartavyāni. anyathā na sāṅgaṃ vedyāṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: This is the reply to the [previous] provisional position. As for what was said — 'the principal [rite] is intended, not the subsidiaries; therefore, the <s>vedi</s> is for the principal [rite]' — that is not correct. The fruit is heard [as arising] from the combined [whole] — the fruit is heard from [the rite] together with its subsidiaries. Therefore, the whole together with its subsidiaries is intended. Even if the subsidiaries are not [individually] intended, still they must be performed on the <s>vedi</s>. Otherwise, [the rite] together with its subsidiaries would not be [considered as] performed on the <s>vedi</s>.

guṇābhidhānāt sarvārtham abhidhānam // MS_3,7.10 //
children.translated_text: Because of the designation of a subsidiary, the designation is for all purposes. // MS 3,7.10 //

children.text: yad uktam - pradhānanāmatvāt paurṇamāsīśabdasyāmāvāsyāśabdasya ca, pradhānahaviṣām abhimarśanam iti. naitad evam, aṅgahaviṣām apy abhimaṛśanaṃ syāt. kutaḥ? guṇābhidhānāt, guṇo 'bhimarśanam ity abhidhānaṃ bhavati. katamat tadabhidhānam? yat guṇo 'bhimarśanam iti brūte. paurṇamāsīm amāvāsyām iti ca dvitīyāntaṃ paurṇamāsyartham abhimarśanaṃ kartavyam, amāvāsyārtham abhimarśanaṃ kartavyam iti, ato yatra yatra kriyamāṇaṃ paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vopakaroti, tatra tatra kartavyam. yad yat paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vābhisaṃbadhyate, sāksāt, praṇāḍyā vā, tatra tatra kriyamāṇaṃ tayor upakaroti. tasmāt pradhānahaviṣām aṅgahaviṣāṃ ca kartavyam iti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — because of the name '<s>paurṇamāsī</s>' and '<s>amāvāsyā</s>' being names of the principal [rites], the touching is of the principal oblations — this is not so. The touching should apply to the subsidiary oblations too. Why? Because of the designation of a subsidiary — there is a designation that the touching is a subsidiary. Which designation is that? The one that says 'the touching is a subsidiary.' '<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>' and '<s>amāvāsyā</s>' [appear in] the accusative — 'the touching should be performed for the purpose of the full-moon [rite],' 'the touching should be performed for the purpose of the new-moon [rite].' Therefore, wherever the performance [of the touching] benefits the full-moon or new-moon [rite], there it should be performed. Whatever is connected with the full-moon or new-moon [rite] — directly or through a chain of connections — the performance [of the touching] there benefits those [rites]. Therefore, it should be performed for both the principal and subsidiary oblations.

children.text: dīkṣādakṣiṇaṃ tu vacanāt pradhānasya // MS_3,7.11 //
children.translated_text: But the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) are for the principal [rite], because of [Vedic] statement. // MS 3,7.11 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome dīkṣāḥ śrūyate - tisro dīkṣā iti, tathā dakṣiṇāḥ śrūyante - tasya dvādaśaśataṃ dakṣiṇā iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ dīkṣādakṣiṇam aṅgapradhānārtham, uta pradhānārtham iti. kiṃ prāptam? puruṣāṇām aṅgapradhānārthatvād dīkṣādakṣiṇasyāṅgapradhānārthateti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - dīkṣādakṣiṇaṃ pradhānasya. kutaḥ? vacanāt, vacanaṃ hi bhavati, dīkṣāḥ somasya, dakṣiṇāḥ somasyeti, na hi vacanasya [392]{*3/651*} atibhāro nāma kvacit. tasmād dīkṣādakṣiṇaṃ vacanāt somasyeti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the consecration is heard: 'three consecrations,' and similarly the sacrificial fees are heard: 'twelve hundred is his <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.' There the doubt arises: are the consecration and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> for the purpose of both subsidiaries and the principal [rite], or for the purpose of the principal [rite alone]? What is the prima facie view? Because the [ritual] persons serve both subsidiaries and the principal [rite], the consecration and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> too are for both subsidiaries and the principal [rite]. Given this, we say: the consecration and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> are for the principal [rite]. Why? Because of [Vedic] statement — for there is a statement: 'the consecrations are of <s>Soma</s>,' 'the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> are of <s>Soma</s>.' For there is never an excessive burden upon a [Vedic] statement anywhere. Therefore, the consecration and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> are of <s>Soma</s>, because of [Vedic] statement.

children.text: nivṛttidarśanāc ca // MS_3,7.12 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of cessation. // MS 3,7.12 //

children.text: nivṛttiṃ dīkṣāṇāṃ darśayati. katham? adhvaryo yat paśunāyākṣīratha kāsya dīkṣeti yat ṣaḍḍhotāraṃ juhoti sāsya dīkṣeti, asatyām api dīkṣāyāṃ vacanaṃ bhavati. tasmād aṅgānāṃ dīkṣādakṣiṇam iti.
children.translated_text: [The text] shows the cessation of the consecrations. How? 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, when you led [the animal] by the rope — that was his consecration'; 'when he offers the <s>Ṣaḍḍhotra</s> (six-priest oblation) — that is his consecration' — even in the absence of a [formal] consecration, the statement is made. Therefore, the consecration and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> are not for the subsidiaries.

children.text: tathā yūpasya vediḥ // MS_3,7.13 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>vedi</s> (altar) belongs to the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>). // MS 3,7.13 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ - yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*3/652*}. tatra yūpaṃ prakṛtya śrūyate - vajro vai yūpo yad antarvedi muniyāt tan nirdahet, yad barhirvedy anavaruddhaḥ syād ardham antarvedi minoty ardhaṃ bahirvedy anavaruddho bhavati, na nirdahatīti.
tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim antarvedīti yūpāṅgabhāvena vedir upadiśyate, utārdham antarvedy ardhaṃ bahirvedīti deśalakṣaṇārtham ucyata iti. kathaṃ yūpāṅgabhāvena kathaṃ vā deśalakṣaṇeti. yadi yūpārdhasya vedyantarasya ca saṃbandho vivakṣitaḥ, evaṃ vedisaṃbaddho yūpaḥ kartavyaḥ, tato yūpāṅgabhāvena. atha yasmin deśe mīyamānasyārdhaṃ vedyabhyantare 'rdhaṃ ca bahiḥ, sa deśa upadiśyate, tato deśalakṣaṇā.
kiṃ prāptam? tathā yūpasya vediḥ, yathā dīkṣādakṣiṇaṃ pradhānasya, tathā yūpasya vediḥ, tathā yūpo mātavyaḥ, tathā mīyamānasya [393]{*3/653*} ardhaṃ vedyabhyantare bhavati. evaṃ vediśrutir apy anugrahīṣyate, itarathā vediśabdo lakṣayed deśam, śrutilakṣaṇāviṣaye śrutir nyāyyā na lakṣaṇā. tasmād yūpāṅgabhāvena vedir nirdiśyate.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice]: 'one who is consecrated — when he slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.' There, with reference to the sacrificial post, it is heard: 'the <s>yūpa</s> is indeed a thunderbolt; if it were placed entirely within the <s>vedi</s>, it would burn [everything]; if entirely outside the <s>vedi</s>, it would be unrestrained. Half within the <s>vedi</s>, it measures [the correct position]; half outside the <s>vedi</s>, it is unrestrained [yet controlled]; it does not burn.'
There the doubt arises: is the <s>vedi</s> mentioned here as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>, or is 'half within the <s>vedi</s>, half outside the <s>vedi</s>' stated for the purpose of indicating a location? How [would it be] as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>, and how as indicating a location? If the relationship between half of the <s>yūpa</s> and the inner part of the <s>vedi</s> is intended, then the <s>yūpa</s> should be made connected with the <s>vedi</s> — hence as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>. But if the location where, when measured, half [of the <s>yūpa</s>] is within the <s>vedi</s> and half is outside — that location is being indicated — then it is a location-indicator.
What is the prima facie view? Just as the consecration and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> are for the principal [rite], similarly the <s>vedi</s> belongs to the <s>yūpa</s>. The <s>yūpa</s> should be measured thus — such that when measured, half is within the <s>vedi</s>. In this way, the hearing of the <s>vedi</s> [as a subsidiary] will also be upheld. Otherwise, the word '<s>vedi</s>' would merely indicate a location, [but] within the domain of both <s>śruti</s> (direct statement) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), <s>śruti</s> is proper, not <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. Therefore, the <s>vedi</s> is indicated as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>.

children.text: deśamātraṃ vāśiṣyeṇaikavākyatvāt // MS_3,7.14 //
children.translated_text: Or [the word '<s>vedi</s>' indicates] merely a location, because of the single-sentence relationship with what is not taught [as subsidiary]. // MS 3,7.14 //

children.text:
deśāmātraṃ vā vediśabdena lakṣyate na vediyūpāṅgam{*3/654*}. kutaḥ? aśiṣyeṇaikavākyatvāt, ardham antarvedi minoty ardhaṃ bahirvedīty etenaikavākyatā yā, sā śāsitavyena, yadi deśalakṣaṇā, atha yūpāṅgabhāvena vedyā nirdeśaḥ, tato na śāsitavyo bahirvedinirdeśo{*3/655*} bhavati. vedyāṃ yūpasyāṅgabhāvenopadiśyamānāyām, ardhaṃ bahirvedīty etad uccāryamāṇaṃ na kasmiṃścid upakāre vartate.
atha bahirvedideśam api yūpāṅgabhāvenopadiśet. vākyaṃ bhidyeta. tasmād yūpāṅgabhāvena vedyā nirdeśe bahirvediśabdaḥ sarvathā na śāsitavyaḥ. yadi tu deśalakṣaṇā, tato viśiṣṭe deśe lakṣyamāṇe 'vaśyavaktavyo bahirvediśabdo bhavati, anucyamāne vedyabhyantare yasmin kasmiṃś ca pradeśe yūpa iti gamyate. atha punar bahirvediśabde śrūyamāṇe, yatarasmin deśe mīyamānasyārdham antarvedy ardhaṃ bahirvedi, sa deśo lakṣayitum iṣṭo bhavati. sa ca bahirvediśabdena vinā na śakyate lakṣayitum ity, avaśyaṃ śāsitavyo bhavati. tasmād deśalakṣaṇeti.
children.translated_text:
Or merely a location is indicated by the word '<s>vedi</s>' — not a <s>vedi</s>-<s>yūpa</s> subsidiary relationship. Why? Because of the single-sentence relationship with what is not taught [as subsidiary]. 'Half within the <s>vedi</s>, it measures [the correct position]; half outside the <s>vedi</s>' — the single-sentence relationship here is with what is to be taught. If [it is] a location-indicator, [then the specification of 'outside the <s>vedi</s>'] is [something] to be taught. But if the <s>vedi</s> is indicated as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>, then the specification 'outside the <s>vedi</s>' is not [something] to be taught. When the <s>vedi</s> is indicated as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>, the utterance 'half outside the <s>vedi</s>' does not serve any purpose.
[Objection:] But perhaps [the text] indicates the outside-<s>vedi</s> area too as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>. [Reply:] The sentence would be split. Therefore, in the case of the <s>vedi</s> being indicated as a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>, the word 'outside the <s>vedi</s>' is in no way [something] to be taught. But if it is a location-indicator, then when a specific location is indicated, the word 'outside the <s>vedi</s>' must necessarily be stated; without it, [the meaning would be] that the <s>yūpa</s> [could be placed] in any location within the <s>vedi</s>. But when the word 'outside the <s>vedi</s>' is heard, the location where, when measured, half is within the <s>vedi</s> and half outside — that location is intended to be indicated. And that [location] cannot be indicated without the word 'outside the <s>vedi</s>'; thus it must necessarily be taught. Therefore, [it is] a location-indicator.

children.text: svāmidhenīs tad anvāhur iti havirdhānayor vacanāt sāmidhenīnām // MS_3,7.15 //
children.translated_text: 'When they press, they recite the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> (kindling verses) accordingly' — [this refers to] the <s>havirdhāna</s> (Soma-cart shed), because of [Vedic] statement about the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>. // MS 3,7.15 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - uta yat sunvanti sāmidhenīs tad anvāhur [394]{*3/656*} iti, havirdhānayor yasmin havirdhāne sunvanti, tat sāmidhenībhiḥ saṃbandhayed ity arthaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sāmīdhenīnām aṅgabhāvena havirdhānaṃ codyate, havirdhānaviśiṣṭāḥ sāmidhenyo 'nuvaktavyāḥ, uta havirdhānenāmūṣām anūcyamānānāṃ deśo lakṣyata iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sāmidhenīnām aṅgatvena havirdhānaṃ codyate - yasmin havirdhāne sunvanti, tat sāmidhenībhiḥ saṃbandhayed iti, tena havirdhānasaṃbaddhāḥ sāmidhenyo 'nuvaktavyā iti vacanāt sāmidhenyaṅgabhāve sati havirdhānaśrutir anugrahīṣyate. itarathā deśaṃ lakṣayed iti. tasmāt sāmidhenyaṅgaṃ havirdhānam.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'moreover, when they press, they recite the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> accordingly' — the meaning is: in whichever <s>havirdhāna</s> they press, that [<s>havirdhāna</s>] should be connected with the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>. There the doubt arises: is the <s>havirdhāna</s> enjoined as a subsidiary of the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> — [meaning] the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> connected with a specific <s>havirdhāna</s> should be recited — or is the location of those [<s>sāmidhenīs</s>] being recited indicated by the <s>havirdhāna</s>? What is the prima facie view? The <s>havirdhāna</s> is enjoined as a subsidiary of the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> — 'in whichever <s>havirdhāna</s> they press, that should be connected with the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>' — therefore, the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> connected with the <s>havirdhāna</s> should be recited. And because of [Vedic] statement, when the subsidiary status with the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> [obtains], the hearing of the <s>havirdhāna</s> will be upheld. Otherwise, [the word would] merely indicate a location. Therefore, the <s>havirdhāna</s> is a subsidiary of the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>.

children.text: deśamātraṃ vā pratyakṣaṃ hy arthakarma somasya // MS_3,7.16 //
children.translated_text: Or [the <s>havirdhāna</s> indicates] merely a location, for the functional action of <s>Soma</s> is direct. // MS 3,7.16 //

children.text:
deśalakṣaṇārthaṃ vaitad ucyate - yasmin sunvanti, tasmin deśe sāmidhenyo 'nuvaktavyā iti, pratyakṣaṃ hy arthakarma somasya tena kriyate. dakṣiṇe havirdhāne somam āsādayatīti{*3/657*}, somāsādanārthaṃ tāvad etad upādeyam. sāmidhenyo 'py agnisamindhanārtham upādeyā iti. iha tv etāvac chrūyate - yasya havirdhānasya samīpe sunvanti tatsaṃbaddhāḥ sāmidhenyo 'py{*3/658*} agnisamindhanārtham upādeyā{*3/659*} iti, tatra na jñāyate, kiṃ sāmidhenyaḥ saṃbaddhāḥ havirdhānasyopakurvanti? kiṃ havirdhānaṃ sāmidhenīnām iti. tad ucyate - sāmidhenyas tāvad dhavirdhānasya nopakurvanti, na hi tāvad vidhīyante, sāmidhenyo 'nuvaktavyā iti. kiṃ tarhi? havirdhānaviśeṣasaṃbandhas tāsāṃ vidhīyate, [395]{*3/660*} na cāvihitam aṅgaṃ bhavati. nāpy evaṃ vidhīyate, havirdhānamāsām anucyamānānām upādātavyaṃ saṃbandhayitum iti. kathaṃ tarhi? havirdhānīviśeṣasaṃbandhaḥ{*3/661*} sāmidhenīnāṃ śrūyate, havirdhānasaṃbandho{*3/662*} vidhīyate, na ca sāmidhenīsaṃbandho havirdhānasya prāptaḥ, yo viśeṣārtham anūdyeta. kena tarhi havirdhānasya saṃbandhaḥ? pratyakṣaṃ hy arthakarma somasya, na tu sāmidhenīkarma pratyakṣaṃ havirdhānasya. bhavati tu deśasya sāmidhenīsaṃbandhaḥ, apareṇa vedim iti hotur deśo lakṣitaḥ, sa uttarasya dakṣiṇasya vā havirdhānasya samāsannaḥ. tatra yat{*3/663*} sunvanti, tad anvāhur ity upapadyate vacanam. tasmād deśalakṣaṇārthaṃ havirdhānagrahaṇam.
athaivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kasmān na bhavati? yasmin havirdhāne sunvanti, tasya havirdhānasya sāmidhenīsaṃbandha iti. naivaṃ śakyam, evaṃ dvāv arthau vidhātavyau bhavataḥ, havirdhānasaṃbandho havirdhānaviśeṣasaṃbandhaś ca. tatra vākyaṃ bhidyate. tasmān naivam abhisaṃbandha iti.
children.translated_text:
This is said for the purpose of indicating a location — 'in the [<s>havirdhāna</s>] where they press, in that place the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> should be recited.' For the functional action of <s>Soma</s> is done directly by that [<s>havirdhāna</s>]. 'In the southern <s>havirdhāna</s> he places the <s>Soma</s>' — this is to be accepted for the purpose of placing the <s>Soma</s>. And the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> too are to be accepted for the purpose of kindling the fire. But here this much is heard: 'the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> connected with the <s>havirdhāna</s> near which they press should also be accepted for the purpose of kindling the fire.' There it is not known: do the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>, being connected, benefit the <s>havirdhāna</s>? Or does the <s>havirdhāna</s> [benefit] the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>? To this it is said: the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> do not benefit the <s>havirdhāna</s>, for they are not enjoined [for that purpose] — 'the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> should be recited' [is the injunction]. What then? A connection with a specific <s>havirdhāna</s> is enjoined for them, and what is not enjoined is not a subsidiary. Nor is it enjoined thus: 'the <s>havirdhāna</s> should be accepted in order to connect those [<s>sāmidhenīs</s>] being recited.' How then? A connection of the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> with a specific <s>havirdhāna</s> is heard; a <s>havirdhāna</s>-connection is enjoined. But the <s>sāmidhenī</s>-connection of the <s>havirdhāna</s> is not [already] obtained, such that it could be restated for a specific purpose. By what then is the <s>havirdhāna</s> connected? The functional action of <s>Soma</s> is directly [performed there], but the <s>sāmidhenī</s>-action is not directly [the function] of the <s>havirdhāna</s>. However, there is a connection of the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> with the location — 'to the west of the <s>vedi</s>' indicates the location of the <s>Hotṛ</s>, and that is proximate to the northern or southern <s>havirdhāna</s>. There, 'when they press, they recite accordingly' — the statement is justified. Therefore, the mention of the <s>havirdhāna</s> is for the purpose of indicating a location.
[Objection:] But why should the connection not be thus: 'in whichever <s>havirdhāna</s> they press, that <s>havirdhāna</s> has a <s>sāmidhenī</s>-connection'? [Reply:] That is not possible — for then two things would have to be enjoined: a <s>havirdhāna</s>-connection and a specific <s>havirdhāna</s>-connection. There, the sentence would be split. Therefore, the connection is not thus.

children.text: samākhyānaṃ ca tadvat // MS_3,7.17 //
children.translated_text: And the designation is likewise. // MS_3,7.17 //

children.text: samākhyānaṃ ca tadvad eva bhavati, yathāsmābhir nyāya upadiṣṭaḥ - somārthaṃ havirdhānam iti.
children.translated_text: And the designation too is in the same way, according to the principle we have stated: the <s>Havirdhāna</s> serves the <s>Soma</s> [rite].

children.text: śāstraphalaṃ prayoktari tallakṣaṇatvāt tasmāt svayaṃ prayoge syāt // MS_3,7.18 //
children.translated_text: The result of the injunction accrues to the performer, because it is characterized by that; therefore one should perform it oneself. // MS_3,7.18 //

children.text: iha karmāṇy udāharaṇam - agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeteti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim etāni karmāṇi svayam [396]{*3/664*} anuṣṭhātavyāni, utātrotsargamātraṃ svayaṃ kuryāt, śeṣam anyaḥ svayaṃ vā, uta śeṣam anya eveti. kiṃ prāptam? svayaṃ prayoge syāt. kutaḥ? yataḥ svayaṃ prayuñjānasya phalaṃ bhavati. katham avagamyate? tallakṣaṇatvāt, śabdo 'syārthasya lakṣaṇam, svayaṃ prayuñjānasya phalaṃ bhavatīti. katamaḥ sa śabdaḥ? svargakāmo yajeteti, yaḥ svargaṃ kāmayate, sa evocyate, yāge kartā bhavan phalaṃ sādhayed iti. sāṅge ca kartā bhavan phalaṃ prāpnoti, tasmāt svayaṃ prayoge syāt.
children.translated_text: Here the rituals are the illustration: "He who desires heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>; he who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; he who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>." There a doubt [arises]: should these rituals [396] be performed by oneself, or should one perform only the initiation (<s>utsarga</s>) oneself while the remainder is done by another or by oneself, or should the remainder be done by another alone? What is the prima facie view? One should perform [everything] oneself. Why? Because the result accrues to the one who performs it himself. How is this known? Because it is characterized by that — the word is the mark of this meaning: the result accrues to the one who performs it himself. What is that word? "He who desires heaven should sacrifice" — he who desires heaven is the one addressed; being the agent of the sacrifice, he would obtain the result. And being the agent of [the sacrifice] with its subsidiaries, he obtains the result. Therefore one should perform it oneself.

children.text: utsarge tu pradhānatvāc cheṣakārī pradhānasya, tasmād anyaḥ svayaṃ vā syāt // MS_3,7.19 //
children.translated_text: But in the initiation (<s>utsarga</s>), because of [its] primacy, the subsidiary-performer [acts for] the principal; therefore another or oneself [may do the rest]. // MS_3,7.19 //

children.text: utsarge prādhānyam asti. katham? ya utsargaṃ karoti tena sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati. katham? parikraya utsargaḥ, tenānantāḥ sarvaṃ kurvanti. tasmād yaḥ parikrayaṃ karoti tena svayam eva sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati. tasmād utsargamātraṃ svayaṃ kuryāt, śeṣam anyaḥ svayaṃ vā.
children.translated_text: There is primacy in the initiation. How? He who performs the initiation — by him everything is done. How? The initiation is the purchase (<s>parikraya</s>); through it, the hired [priests] do everything. Therefore, by him who makes the purchase, everything is indeed done by himself. Therefore one should perform only the initiation oneself; the remainder [may be done by] another or oneself.

children.text: anyo vā syāt parikrayāmnānād vipratiṣedhāt pratyagātmani // MS_3,7.20 //
children.translated_text: Or the other [alone] should [perform the rest], because of the teaching of purchase and because of contradiction in [applying it to] oneself. // MS_3,7.20 //

children.text: śeṣasyānya eva syāt kartā. kutaḥ? parikrayasyāmnānatvāt. puruṣān atiprakāreṣu bahuṣu prāpteṣu parikrayo niyataḥ. tasmāt parikrayeṇānataiḥ sarve padārthāḥ kartavyā iti. vipratiṣeddhaś cātmani parikrayaḥ. yadi svayaṃ kuryāt, aparikrītena kṛtaṃ syāt, tatra parikrayāmnānānarthakyam, adṛṣṭārtho vā pratijñāyeta. tasmād anyaiḥ parikrītaiḥ śeṣāḥ padārthāḥ kartavyā iti. utsargaṃ tu svayaṃ kurvatā sarvaṃ svayaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: Of the remainder, another alone should be the performer. Why? Because purchase is taught. When the person, having many possible modes of action available, [selects from them,] the purchase is fixed. Therefore all operations are to be performed by those hired through purchase. And the purchase is contradicted if [applied] to oneself — if one performed it oneself, it would be done by one not purchased; there the teaching of purchase would be purposeless, or a purposeless consequence would be asserted. Therefore the remaining operations are to be performed by others who have been purchased. But by one performing the initiation oneself, everything is done by oneself.

children.text: tatrārthāt kartṛparimāṇaṃ syād aniyamo 'viśeṣāt // MS_3,7.21 //
children.translated_text: There, the number of performers would be determined by purpose; [otherwise] there is no restriction, because there is no specific [teaching]. // MS_3,7.21 //

children.text: tatra taiḥ parikrītaiḥ kartavyeṣv aniyamena kartṛparimāṇaṃ syāt. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, na kartṛparimāṇe viśeṣaḥ kaścid āmnāyate. arthena tatparimāṇam, yāvādbhir asāv itikartavyatā nirvartate, tāvato vṛṇīta{*3/666*}.
children.translated_text: There, regarding what is to be performed by those purchased, the number of performers would be unrestricted. Why? Because there is no specific [teaching] — no specific number of performers is taught. Their number [is determined] by purpose — one should select as many as are needed for the procedure to be accomplished.

children.text: api vā śrutibhedāt pratināmadheyaṃ syuḥ // MS_3,7.22 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of distinct statements, there should be [performers] for each designation. // MS_3,7.22 //

children.text: yāvanti kartṛnāmadheyāni karmāṇi śrūyante - tāvanto varītavyā bhidyante, tāni ca{*3/667*} nāmadheyaśravaṇāni. tān puro 'dhvaryur vibhajati, pratiprasthātā manthinaṃ juhoti, neṣṭā patnīm abhyudāyati{*3/668*}, unnetā camasān unnayatīti. tathā - prastotā prastauti, udgātodgāyati, pratihartā pratiharati, subrahmaṇyaḥ subrahmaṇyām āha, hotā prātaranuvākam anubrūte, maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati, cānucāha, acchāvāko yajati, grāvastotrīyām anvāha. etāvadbhiḥ karmaṇi prayojanam, tena te 'vaśyam etāni yathāśrutāni kartuṃ varītavyāḥ, etad vyatirikto 'nyaḥ padārtho na vidyate. yo 'pi vākyena nopadiṣṭaḥ, sa samākhyayā gamyate. tasmād etāvato vṛṇīteti.
children.translated_text: As many ritual designations of performers are heard — that many should be selected; they are differentiated, and those [designations] are heard as names. "The <s>Adhvaryu</s> divides the cakes; the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> offers the <s>Manthina</s>; the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> brings forward the wife; the <s>Unnetṛ</s> raises the cups." Likewise: "the <s>Prastotṛ</s> chants the introduction; the <s>Udgātṛ</s> sings; the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> responds; the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> recites the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> [formula]; the <s>Hotṛ</s> recites the morning litany; the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> commands; the <s>Acchāvāka</s> sacrifices; the <s>Grāvastut</s> recites the <s>Grāvastotrīya</s>." With this many, there is purpose in the ritual; therefore they must necessarily be selected to perform these [functions] as stated. There is no operation beyond these. Even what is not instructed by a sentence is known through designation. Therefore one should select this many.

children.text: ekasya karmabhedād iti cet // MS_3,7.23 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that one [person can do multiple functions] because of differentiation of ritual acts — // MS_3,7.23 //

children.text: evaṃ cet pratijñāyate - etāvato vṛṇīteti. tan na, yo yas tatkarma kariṣyatīti saṃkalpate, sa sa tat tac chabdābhidheyo [398]{*3/669*} bhavati, eko 'pi bahūn padārthān kartuṃ bahubhir nāmadheyair ucyeta, tasmād aniyamaḥ.
children.translated_text: If it is claimed thus — "one should select this many" — [the opponent replies:] no, whoever resolves "I shall perform that ritual act" — he [398] comes to be designated by that name; even one person performing many operations would be called by many names. Therefore there is no restriction.

children.text: notpattau hi // MS_3,7.24 //
children.translated_text: Not so, for [the differentiation occurs] at the time of origination. // MS_3,7.24 //

children.text: naitad evam, utpattau puruṣāṇām, utpādyamāneṣu puruṣeṣu nāmadheyāni bhidyante - brāhmaṇaṃ{*3/670*} vṛṇīte, hotāram vṛṇīte, udgātāraṃ vṛṇīte, adhvaryuṃ vṛṇīta ityevamādi. tasmāt karmaṇi tair evaṃ nāmakaiḥ prayojanam, avaśyante varītavyāḥ. tasmād eṣāṃ varaṇe saṃkīrtanaṃ na vidhiḥ. prayojanasyābhāvan nānuvādaḥ. na vede tāvanto varītavyā iti brūyāt, anarthakam eva syāt. śaknoti cedaṃ pratyāyayituṃ saṃkhyāviśeṣam. tasmād yaḥ saṃkhyāviśeṣo eṣāṃ pratīyate tadartham etad vacanam. tasmāt ṣoḍaśa kartāro varītavyāḥ, somas{*3/671*} tāvat kartṛkaś ca syāt{*3/672*}. evaṃ darśapūrṇamāsayor api.
children.translated_text: This is not so — at the origination of the [priestly] persons, when the persons are being originated [i.e., selected], the names are differentiated: "he selects a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he selects a <s>Hotṛ</s>, he selects an <s>Udgātṛ</s>, he selects an <s>Adhvaryu</s>," and so forth. Therefore there is purpose in the ritual with persons of these designations; they must necessarily be selected. Therefore their enumeration at the time of selection is not [merely] a restatement. Because there is no [other] purpose, it is not a restatement [either]. The <s>Veda</s> would not say "this many should be selected" if it were purposeless. But this [statement] can convey a specific number. Therefore this statement serves the specific number that is understood from them. Therefore sixteen performers should be selected, and the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] should have that many performers. Likewise for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> as well.

children.text: camasādhvaryavaś ca tair vyapadeśāt // MS_3,7.25 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> (cup-bearers) [are separate from them], because of [their] designation by them. // MS_3,7.25 //

children.text:
santi jyotiṣṭome camasādhvaryavaḥ - camasādhvaryūn vṛṇīteti. teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kim eṣām anyatamāḥ, utaitebhyo 'nya iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? etāvatāṃ saṃkīrtanād eṣām evānyatamāḥ. iti{*3/673*} prāpte brūmaḥ - camasādhvaryavaś cāpare bhaveyus tebhyo 'nya iti. kutaḥ? tair vyapadeśāt, taiḥ parigaṇitair eṣāṃ vyapadeśo bhavati - madhyataḥkāriṇāṃ camasādhvaryavaḥ, hotrakāṇāṃ camasādhvaryava iti.
nanu ya eva prakṛtās te camasādhvaryavo bhaveyuḥ. neti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ? tair vyapadeśāt, madhyataḥkāriṇāṃ camasādhvaryavo [399]{*3/674*} hotrakāṇāṃ camasādhvaryava iti, ṣaṣṭhī saṃbandhe sati bhavati. ṛtvigbhis te vyapadiśyante, ṛtvijas teṣāṃ svāmino na yajamānaḥ, yajamānapuruṣebhyaś caite 'nya iti naḥ pratijñātam. na yajamānena camasādhvaryavaṃ{*3/675*} kartuṃ varītavyāḥ, ṛtvigbhis te varītavyā iti. api caiṣām utpattivākya eva bhedaḥ, camasādhvaryūn vṛṇīteti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there are <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> — "he selects the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>." Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: are they among those [already enumerated], or different from them? What is the prima facie view? Since those many have been enumerated, they are among them. Given this, we say: the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> should be others, different from those. Why? Because of [their] designation by them — their designation is by those enumerated [priests]: "the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> of the <s>Madhyataḥkārins</s> (those performing in the middle), the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> of the <s>Hotrakas</s>." 
But would not the already-mentioned ones be the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>? No, we say. Why? Because of designation by them — "the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> of the <s>Madhyataḥkārins</s>, [399] the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> of the <s>Hotrakas</s>" — the genitive case indicates a relationship. They are designated by the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests); the <s>ṛtvijs</s> are their masters, not the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer). And we have established that these are different from the sacrificer's personnel. The <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> are not to be selected by the sacrificer to serve [as such]; they are to be selected by the <s>ṛtvijs</s>. Moreover, their differentiation occurs in the very origination-sentence: "he selects the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>."

children.text: utpattau tu bahuśruteḥ // MS_3,7.26 //
children.translated_text: But at the origination, because of the plural statement. // MS_3,7.26 //

children.text: teṣv va saṃdehaḥ - kim aniyamaḥ, eko dvau bahavo vā, uta bahava eveti? aniyama iti prāpta ucyate - bahava iti. kutaḥ? utpattau bahuśruteḥ, camasādhvaryava ity eṣām utpattau bahuśrutir bhavati, tasmād bahava iti.
children.translated_text: Regarding them, there is a doubt: is there no restriction — one, two, or many — or are there necessarily many? "No restriction" being the prima facie view, we say: many. Why? Because of the plural statement at the origination — "<s>Camasādhvaryus</s>" [in the plural] — there is a plural statement at their origination. Therefore they are many.

children.text: daśatvaṃ liṅgadarśanāt // MS_3,7.27 //
children.translated_text: Ten, because of indicative evidence. // MS_3,7.27 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome santi camasādhvaryavaḥ{*3/676*}, te ca bahava ity uktam. kiyanto bahava iti saṃdehe trayaḥ, bahuvacanasāmarthyād iti prāpte brūmaḥ - daśatvaṃ liṅgadarśanāt. te daśa bhaveyuḥ, tathā hi liṅgaṃ jyotiṣṭomavikāre daśapeye śrūyate - daśa camasādhvaryavo daśa daśaikaikaṃ camasam anusarpantīti, etasmāt kāraṇād daśapeyo bhavatīti bruvan daśa camasādhvaryūn darśayati, yadi trayo bhaveyuḥ, etaddarśanaṃ nopapadyate. tasmāt trīn atītyaiṣā saṃkhyā, yadi ca daśa na bhaveyur nopapadyetaitaddarśanam. tasmād [400]{*3/677*} bhavanti daśa, daśa caiṣāṃ svāminaḥ. tasmāt prayojanabhāvād daśasaṃkhyopādīyate, tasyāṃ copādīyamānāyām aparāpi saṃkhyānugṛhyate, tenāpi daśa bhaveyuḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there are <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>, and it has been said they are many. How many? When the prima facie view holds three, from the force of the plural, we say: ten, because of indicative evidence. They should be ten, for thus an indicative mark is heard in the <s>Daśapeya</s>, a modification of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>: "Ten <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>, ten [cups], each one following one cup" — by saying "this is why it is called <s>Daśapeya</s> (ten-drinks)," it shows ten <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>. If there were [only] three, this evidence would be impossible. Therefore this number goes beyond three. And if there were not ten, this evidence would be impossible. [400] Therefore there are ten, and ten are their masters. Therefore, because there is purpose, the number ten is adopted; and when this [number] is adopted, the other number too is supported — therefore they too should be ten.

children.text: śamitā ca śabdabhedāt // MS_3,7.28 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Śamitṛ</s> (slaughterer) [is separate], because of the difference in designation. // MS_3,7.28 //

children.text: asti śamitā - śamitāram upanayīteti. sa kiṃ saṃkīrtitānām anyatamaḥ, utānyas tebhya iti. kiṃ prāptam? teṣāṃ varaṇe saṃkīrtanāt, teṣām anyatamaḥ, iti prāpte ucyate - śamitā ca śabdabhedāt, śabdo bhidyate, evaṃsaṃjñakenedaṃ karma kartavyam iti, tasmād evaṃsaṃjñaka utpādayitavyaḥ. asya saṃkīrtanāt saṃkhyāv vṛddhir gamyate, tasmād anyaḥ śamitā syāt. api ca - klomā cordhaṃ{*3/678*} vaikartanaṃ ca śamituḥ tad brāhmaṇāya dadyād yadbrāhmaṇaḥ syād ity{*3/679*} abrāhmaṇāśaṅkā bhavati, sā ṛtviji nopapadyate.
children.translated_text: There is a <s>Śamitṛ</s> — "he should bring near the <s>Śamitṛ</s>." Is he one of those already enumerated, or different from them? What is the prima facie view? Since [the priests] are enumerated at the time of selection, he is one of them. Given this, we say: the <s>Śamitṛ</s> is [separate] because of the difference in designation — the designation is distinct, [indicating that] this act is to be performed by one with this particular name; therefore one with this name is to be produced [selected]. His enumeration indicates an increase in the number; therefore the <s>Śamitṛ</s> should be another. Moreover: "the <s>kloman</s> (lung) and half the <s>vaikartana</s> (cut portion) belong to the <s>Śamitṛ</s>; he should give that to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, if he is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>" — there is a doubt whether he might be a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; that doubt is not possible regarding an <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest).

children.text: prakaraṇād votpattyasaṃyogāt // MS_3,7.29 //
children.translated_text: Or [he is one of those already mentioned], because of context and non-connection at origination. // MS_3,7.29 //

children.text: satyaṃ saṃkhyāvivṛddhir gamyate, na tūtpadyamāneṣu, yā tv anutpattis teṣu gamyate, tatraikasya karmabhedād ity evam apy avakalpate. yat tūktam - abrāhmaṇāśaṅkā bhavatīti, yajamānābhiprāyā sā, yady abrāhmaṇo yajamānaḥ syād iti. nanu yady abrāhmaṇaḥ syād iti prakṛtaḥ śamitā saṃbadhyate. ucyate - śamayatīti śamitā, yaugika eṣa śabdaḥ prakṛteṣv apy avakalpate. śāmitram apy ādhvaryave samāmnānād adhvaryuṇā kartavyam. [401] tasmāc chamanād adhvaryuḥ śamitā. evaṃ sati aprakṛto yajamānaḥ saṃbandhyate.
children.translated_text: True, an increase in number is understood, but not at the origination [of priests]. The non-origination that is understood regarding them — in that case, [the explanation] "because of differentiation of ritual acts by one person" also fits. As for what was stated — that there is a doubt whether he might be a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — that pertains to the sacrificer, [i.e.,] if the sacrificer were a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. But would not the <s>Śamitṛ</s> already mentioned be connected? We reply: <s>Śamitṛ</s> means "one who kills" — this is a derivative word (<s>yaugika</s>) and can apply to those already mentioned too. The <s>Śāmitra</s> [act] too, being taught in connection with the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> [duties], is to be performed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. [401] Therefore, by virtue of slaughtering, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is the <s>Śamitṛ</s>. This being the case, the sacrificer, who is not the one mentioned [as Śamitṛ], is connected [with the doubt about being non-Brāhmaṇa].

children.text: upagāś ca liṅgadarśanāt // MS_3,7.30 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Upagās</s> (assistant singers), because of indicative evidence. // MS_3,7.30 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome santy upagā nāma, te śabdabhedāt saṃkhyāvivṛddhiṃ pratyāyayantīty adhvaryvādibhyo 'nya iti prāpte brūmaḥ - teṣām eva kecit syur iti. kasmāt? utpattau parigaṇanāt, yaugikakatvāc ca śabdasya. liṅgam idaṃ bhavati - nādhvaryur upagāyed iti, yady ebhyo 'nye bhaveyur nādhvaryuṃ pratiṣedhet. aprāptatvāt. yatas tu pratiṣedhati, ato 'vagachāmaḥ, utpattau saṃkīrtitānām evānyatama iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there are those called <s>Upagās</s>. Because of the difference in designation, they indicate an increase in number, and thus they are different from the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and others — this being the prima facie view, we say: some of those very [already enumerated priests] would serve [as Upagās]. Why? Because of enumeration at the origination, and because the word is derivative (<s>yaugika</s>). There is this indicative mark: "the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should not sing alongside (<s>upagāyet</s>)" — if they were different from these, he would not prohibit the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, since it would not be applicable [to him]. But since he does prohibit, we understand that they are among those enumerated at origination.

children.text: vikrayī tv anyaḥ karmaṇo 'coditatvāt // MS_3,7.31 //
children.translated_text: But the seller (<s>vikrayin</s>) is another, because [his act] is not enjoined as part of the ritual. // MS_3,7.31 //

children.text: asti somavikrayī, tatra saṃdehaḥ - sa kim adhvaryvādīnām anyatamaḥ, utaibhyo 'nya iti. kiṃ prāptam? teṣāṃ saṃkīrtanāt, teṣām anyatama iti prāpte brūmaḥ - vikrayī tv anyaḥ syād iti, vikrayo na codyate krayacodyate, tatrārthād vikrayaḥ, jyotiṣṭomasya ca padārthān kartum adhvaryvādaya utpādyante, na tu vikrayo jyotiṣṭomasya śrūyate. tasmān nādhvaryvādīnām anyatama iti.
children.translated_text: There is a <s>Soma</s>-seller; there the doubt arises: is he one of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the others, or someone different from them? What is the prima facie view? Because of their [the priests'] being listed, he would be one of them. Given this, we say: the seller should be someone else. The selling is not enjoined — the purchase is enjoined; there, the selling [follows] by implication. And the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and others are produced for performing the constituent elements of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, but the selling is not heard as [a constituent element] of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Therefore, he is not one of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the others.

children.text: karmakāryāt sarveṣām ṛtviktvam aviśeṣāt // MS_3,7.32 //
children.translated_text: Because of [their] being employed in the rite, all have the status of <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest), because of the lack of distinction. // MS 3,7.32 //

children.text:
ya ete puruṣā jyotiṣṭomasya śrūyante, te kiṃ sarva eta ṛtvijaḥ, uta kecid eṣām iti. kiṃ prāptam? sarve. kutaḥ? karmakāryāt, sarve yāgasya sādhanaṃ kurvanti, tasmāt sarva ṛtau yajanti. ye cartau yajanti ta ṛtvijaḥ, na kaścid viśeṣa āśrīyate, ima evartau yajantīty ṛtvijaḥ, ime neti. tasmāt sarveṣām ṛtviktvam.
nanu parisaṃkhyā śrūyate - saumyasyādhvarasya yajñakratoḥ saptadaśa ṛtvija iti. ucyate - parisaṃkhyāyāṃ bahavo doṣāḥ santīti, avayutyavādo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text:
These persons who are heard in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — are all of them <s>ṛtvijs</s>, or only some? What is the prima facie view? All. Why? Because of [their] being employed in the rite — all perform the means of accomplishing the sacrifice; therefore, all sacrifice in the [proper] season (<s>ṛtu</s>). And those who sacrifice in the season are <s>ṛtvijs</s>. No distinction is relied upon [to say] 'these alone sacrifice in the season and are <s>ṛtvijs</s>; these are not.' Therefore, all have the status of <s>ṛtvij</s>.
[Objection:] But an enumeration is heard: 'of the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, the ritual act, there are seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s>.' [Reply:] It is said: there are many faults in the enumeration; this will be [treated as] a statement of subtraction (<s>avayutyavāda</s>).

children.text: na vā parisaṃkhyānāt // MS_3,7.33 //
children.translated_text: Or not all, because of the enumeration. // MS 3,7.33 //

children.text:
na vā sarve. kasmāt? parisaṃkhyānāt, evaṃ hi śrūyate, saumyasyādhvarasya yajñakratoḥ saptadaśa ṛtvija iti, sa eṣa na vidhiḥ, bahutarāṇāṃ prāptatvāt, nānuvādaḥ, paryojanābhāvāt. na cet parisaṃkhyāpi, ānarthakyam eva syāt.
nanu parisaṃkhyāyāṃ svārthahānaṃ parārthakalpanā prāptabādhaś ca. ucyate - svārthahānam adoṣaḥ prāptatvāt. parārthakalpanā ca pratyayāt. katham{*3/681*}? bahūnām ṛtviktve jñāte punaḥ saptadaśa ṛtvija ity ucyate, saptadaśabhir ṛtvikśabdasya saṃbandhaḥ punaḥ prakāśyate, adhikaiś ca na prakāśyate. tatra vijñāyata etat, ṛtvikśabdasya puruṣaiḥ saṃbandhe punaḥ prakāśyamāne saptadaśabhyo 'bhyadhikā varjitā iti gamyate. tatra kiṃ saptadaśabhiḥ saṃbandho [403]{*3/682*} vivakṣitaḥ, kiṃ vādhikānāṃ varjanam iti, saptadaśasaṃbandhasyāprayojakatvād adhikānāṃ varjanaṃ vivakṣitam iti gamyate.
āha - nanu pratiṣidhyamāneṣv apy adhikeṣu pratiṣedho na prāpnoti, na hi ta ṛtau na yajanti, na vartau yajanto na ṛtvijaḥ syuḥ. ucyate - satyam, na, pratiṣedhād ṛtvikśabdena na saṃbadhyate{*3/683*}, kiṃ tu pratiṣedhasāmarthyād dhy ṛtvikkārye na bhavanti. kiṃ punar ṛtvikkāryam? ṛtvija upavasantīti{*3/684*}, ṛtvijo vṛṇīte, ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dadātīti.
āha - yad ṛtvijāṃ kāryam, kathaṃ tat keṣāṃcid ṛtvikśabdakānāṃ na syāt. ucyate - evaṃ tarhi dvividho 'yam ṛtvikśabdaḥ, ṛtuyajananimittaḥ, varaṇabharaṇanimittaś ca, tatra yāganimittasya grahaṇam anarthakam, tasmād varaṇabharaṇanimitto gṛhyata iti.
āha - nanv itaretarāśrayam evaṃ bhavati - ya ṛtvijas te varītavyāḥ, ye vriyante ta ṛtvija iti tad itaretarāśrayam. ucyate - na hy ṛtvijo vṛṇīta ity ayam arthaḥ, ṛtvijaḥ santo varītavyā iti. kathaṃ tarhi? varaṇenartvijaḥ kriyanta iti, evaṃ dvitīyānirdeśo yukto bhaviṣyati, adhvaryaṃ vṛṇīta ity evaṃlakṣaṇaḥ. dṛṣṭārthatā ca varaṇasya bhaviṣyati.
katham ātmecchayādhvaryur bhavatīti cet kaścid brūyāt, bhavatīti brūyām. katham? evaṃśabdakenāyaṃ padārthaḥ kartavya iti, nāsty evaṃśabdakaḥ. yaś ca nāsti, sa yadi śakyate kartum, kartavyo bhavati. yathā - juhvā juhotīty avidyamānā juhūḥ kriyate, evam etad api draṣṭavyam. tatrārthād aniyamenartvikśabdasaṃbandhe kartavye, evaṃ varaṇaviśeṣeṇa kṛtavya iti niyamyate. tasmān netaretarāśrayam. tasmāt saptadaśaiva ṛtvijaḥ[404]{*3/685*} kartavyā iti parisaṃkhyā, saptadaśa ṛtvijaḥ saṃskāraiḥ kartavyā iti.
children.translated_text:
Or not all. Why? Because of the enumeration — for thus it is heard: 'of the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, the ritual act, there are seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s>.' This is neither an injunction — because more [than seventeen] are [already] obtained — nor a restatement — because of the absence of purpose. And if it is not an enumeration either, there would be complete purposelessness.
[Objection:] But in an enumeration there is loss of [the word's] own meaning, postulation of another meaning, and overriding of what is [already] obtained. [Reply:] It is said: loss of the [word's] own meaning is not a fault, because [that meaning] is [already] obtained. The postulation of another meaning is from the suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>). How? When it is known that many have <s>ṛtvij</s>-status, the statement 'seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s>' is made again — the connection of the word '<s>ṛtvij</s>' with seventeen is again made manifest, and with more [than seventeen] it is not made manifest. From this it is understood: when the connection of the word '<s>ṛtvij</s>' with persons is again made manifest, those exceeding seventeen are understood to be excluded. There, is the connection with seventeen intended, or the exclusion of the excess? Since the connection with seventeen is without purpose, the exclusion of the excess is understood to be intended.
[Objection:] It is said: but even when the excess [priests] are negated, the negation does not obtain — for they do sacrifice in the season, and those who sacrifice in the season cannot not be <s>ṛtvijs</s>. [Reply:] It is said: true, but because of the negation, he is not connected with the word '<s>ṛtvij</s>'; rather, by the force of the negation, he does not participate in <s>ṛtvij</s>-functions. What then is the <s>ṛtvij</s>-function? 'The <s>ṛtvijs</s> observe the fast,' 'he selects the <s>ṛtvijs</s>,' 'he gives the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> to the <s>ṛtvijs</s>.'
[Objection:] It is said: what is the function of <s>ṛtvijs</s> — how could that not apply to some who bear the word '<s>ṛtvij</s>'? [Reply:] It is said: then this word '<s>ṛtvij</s>' is of two kinds — occasioned by sacrificing in the season, and occasioned by selection and maintenance (<s>varaṇa-bharaṇa</s>). There, the grasping of [the word as] occasioned by sacrificing is purposeless; therefore, [the word] occasioned by selection and maintenance is grasped.
[Objection:] It is said: but then there is mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>): those who are <s>ṛtvijs</s> are to be selected, and those who are selected are <s>ṛtvijs</s> — that is mutual dependence. [Reply:] It is said: the meaning of 'he should select the <s>ṛtvijs</s>' is not 'those who are already <s>ṛtvijs</s> should be selected.' What then? 'By selection, they are made <s>ṛtvijs</s>.' Thus the accusative case-ending will be justified — the specification being like '<s>adhvaryaṃ vṛṇīta</s>' ('he should select [someone as] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'). And the selection will have a perceptible purpose.
If someone should say 'does one become an <s>Adhvaryu</s> by one's own wish?' — I would say yes. How? The constituent element denoted by such a word is to be performed — but there is no one denoted by such a word. And what does not exist — if it can be made, it should be made. Just as 'he offers with the <s>juhū</s>' — a non-existent <s>juhū</s> is made — so this too should be seen. There, when by implication the connection with the word '<s>ṛtvij</s>' is to be made without restriction, it is restricted by the specific [act of] selection. Therefore, there is no mutual dependence. Therefore, the enumeration [establishes that] exactly seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s> are to be made — seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s> are to be made through the consecrations (<s>saṃskāras</s>).

children.text: pakṣeṇeti cet // MS_3,7.34 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, by the [alternative] position. // MS 3,7.34 //

children.text: evaṃ cen manyase - yathoktapakṣeṇaitad evam ucyate, avayutyavādapakṣeṇa saptadaśa ṛtvija iti, tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: If you think thus — by the stated position this is so, [namely that] by the position of the statement of subtraction, 'seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s>' — that must be refuted.

children.text: na sarveṣām anadhikāraḥ // MS_3,7.35 //
children.translated_text: Not all [are subject to the subtraction], because of the non-applicability of the statement. // MS 3,7.35 //

children.text: naitad evam, nātra sarveṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ vacanam, yān adhikṛtyāvayutyavādo bhaviṣyati. yatra parā saṃkhyā kīrtyate, tatrāvayutyavādo bhavati, yathā - dvādaśakapāle yad aṣṭākapālo bhavatīti, na ca, iha parā saṃkhyā kīrtyate. tasmān nāvayutyavāda iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — the statement here does not apply to all persons with respect to whom the statement of subtraction would apply. The statement of subtraction applies where a higher number is stated — as, for example, 'in the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [offering], when he makes eight-<s>kapāla</s>' — but here, no higher number is stated. Therefore, it is not a statement of subtraction.

children.text: niyamas tu dakṣiṇābhiḥ śrutisaṃyogāt // MS_3,7.36 //
children.translated_text: But the determination is through the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>, because of the connection with <s>śruti</s>. // MS 3,7.36 //

children.text: saptadaśa ṛtvija iti samadhigatam. katame te saptadaśa itīdaṃ cintyate. kiṃ prāptam? ajñānam. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - niyamas tu dakṣiṇābhiḥ, śrutisaṃyogāt, dakṣiṇāsaṃbandhena niyamyeran. evaṃ hy āmnāyate - ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dadātīti, evam abhidhāya dakṣiṇādānakramapare vākye brahmādayaḥ śrūyante - agnīdhe 'gre dadātīti, tato brahmaṇe, tato 'muṣmai cāmuṣmai ceti{*3/686*} kecid eva viśiṣṭāḥ śrūyante - evaṃ ye śrūyante, te tāvad ṛtvijaḥ, tato 'bhyadhikā nānye bhavitum arhanti. dakṣiṇābhir niyama iti.
children.translated_text: That there are seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s> has been ascertained. Which [persons] are those seventeen — this is now considered. What is the prima facie view? Ignorance. Given this, we say: but the determination [is made] through the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>, because of the connection with <s>śruti</s>. They would be determined by their connection with the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>. For thus it is taught: 'he gives the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> to the <s>ṛtvijs</s>' — having stated this, in the subsequent sentence about the order of <s>dakṣiṇā</s>-giving, the <s>Brahman</s> and others are heard: 'he gives first to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, then to the <s>Brahman</s>, then to such-and-such and such-and-such.' Only certain specific [priests] are heard. Thus those who are heard are <s>ṛtvijs</s> to that extent; others beyond [them] should not exist. The determination is through the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>.

children.text: uktvā ca yajamānatvaṃ teṣāṃ dīkṣāvidhānāt // MS_3,7.37 //
children.translated_text: And having stated [their] status as sacrificers, because of the injunction of consecration for them. // MS 3,7.37 //

children.text: ya ṛtvijas te yajamānā ity evam abhidhāya brahmādīnāṃ dīkṣākramapare ca vākye dīkṣāṃ darśayati. katham? adhvaryur gṛhapatiṃ dīkṣayitvā brahmāṇaṃ dīkṣayati, tat udgātāram, tato hotāram. tatas taṃ pratiprasthātā dīkṣayitvārdhino dīkṣayati, brāhmaṇāc chaṃsinaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, prastotāram udgātuḥ, maitrāvaruṇaṃ hotuḥ. tatas taṃ neṣṭā dīkṣayitvā tṛtīyino dīkṣayati, āgnīdhaṃ{*3/688*} brahmaṇaḥ, pratihartāram udgātuḥ, acchāvākaṃ hotuḥ. tatas tam unnetā dīkṣayitvā pādino dīkṣayati, potāraṃ brahmaṇaḥ, subrahmaṇyam udgātuḥ, grāvastutaṃ hotuḥ. tatas tam anyo brāhmaṇo dīkṣayati, brahmacārī vācāryapreṣita iti. dīkṣā ca yajamānasaṃskāraḥ. tasmād brahmādaya ṛtvijaḥ saptadaśa iti.
children.translated_text: Those who are <s>ṛtvijs</s> are [themselves] sacrificers — having stated this, [the text] shows the consecration in the subsequent sentence about the order of consecration for the <s>Brahman</s> and others. How? 'The <s>Adhvaryu</s>, having consecrated the householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>), consecrates the <s>Brahman</s>; then the <s>Udgātṛ</s>; then the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>, having consecrated him, consecrates the half-share [priests]: the <s>Śaṃsin</s> [who is] of the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Prastotṛ</s> [who is] of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [who is] of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, having consecrated him, consecrates the third-share [priests]: the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [who is] of the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> [who is] of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Acchāvāka</s> [who is] of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Unnetṛ</s>, having consecrated him, consecrates the quarter-share [priests]: the <s>Potṛ</s> [who is] of the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> [who is] of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Grāvastut</s> [who is] of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then another <s>brāhmaṇa</s> consecrates him — a <s>brahmacārin</s> sent by the <s>ācārya</s>.' And the consecration is the sacrament (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the sacrificer. Therefore, the <s>Brahman</s> and others — seventeen — are the <s>ṛtvijs</s>.

children.text: svāmisaptadaśāḥ karmasāmānyāt // MS_3,7.38 //
children.translated_text: Including the owner, [they are] seventeen, because of the commonality of the rite. // MS 3,7.38 //

children.text: etad uktam - saptadaśa ṛtvija iti, te ca brahmādayaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim eṣāṃ sadasyaḥ saptadaśaḥ, uta gṛhapatiḥ? kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sadasya iti. sa hi karmakaraḥ, itaraḥ svāmī. yaś ca karmakaraḥ, sa parikretavyaḥ, ṛtvijaś ca parikrīyante, tasmāt sadasyaḥ saptadaśa ṛtvig iti. api ca - tasya camasam āmananti varaṇaṃ ca. ṛtvigvarītavyo na svāmī. tasmāt sadasyaḥ saptadaśa iti prāpte, ucyate - svāmisaptadaśāḥ karmasāmānyāt, svāmy eṣāṃ saptadaśaḥ syāt. kutaḥ? karmasāmānyāt, yajñe kartāra ṛtvijo bhavanti, yajñe ca kartā gṛhapatiḥ, tasmād ṛtvik, [406]{*3/689*} yajñakarmasāmānyāt. yad uktam - taṃ samāmananti, tasya camasam āmananti varaṇaṃ ca, tasmāt sadasyaḥ saptadaśa iti. ucyate - brahmāṇam eva te samāmananti, varaṇam api camasaś ca brahmaṇa eva, sa hi sadasi bhavaḥ, tasmāt svāmisaptadaśāḥ.
children.translated_text: This has been stated: there are seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s>, and they are the <s>Brahman</s> and others. There the doubt arises: is the <s>sadasya</s> (assessor) the seventeenth, or the householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>)? What is the prima facie view? The <s>sadasya</s>. For he is a worker (<s>karmakara</s>); the other [the householder] is the owner (<s>svāmin</s>). And a worker is to be hired; and the <s>ṛtvijs</s> are hired. Therefore, the <s>sadasya</s> is the seventeenth <s>ṛtvij</s>. Moreover, his cup (<s>camasa</s>) and his selection are taught. The <s>ṛtvij</s> is to be selected, not the owner. Therefore, the <s>sadasya</s> is the seventeenth. Given this, we say: including the owner, [they are] seventeen, because of the commonality of the rite. The owner should be the seventeenth among them. Why? Because of the commonality of the rite — in a sacrifice, the agents are the <s>ṛtvijs</s>; and in a sacrifice, the householder is an agent; therefore, he is an <s>ṛtvij</s> — because of the commonality of sacrificial action. As for what was said — they teach his [the <s>sadasya</s>'s listing], they teach his cup and his selection; therefore the <s>sadasya</s> is the seventeenth — it is said: they teach the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] indeed in those [passages]; the selection and cup too belong to the <s>Brahman</s>, for he is the one who sits in the assembly (<s>sadas</s>). Therefore, including the owner, [they are] seventeen.

children.text: te svārthāḥ prayuktatvād agnayaś ca svakālatvāt // MS_3,7.39 //
children.translated_text: They [serve] their own purposes, because of being employed; and the fires [serve] because of their own time. // MS 3,7.39 //

children.text: svāmisaptadaśā jyotiṣṭomasyartvijaḥ samadhigatāḥ. atredānīm ayaṃ saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ sarvaṃ puruṣakāryaṃ taiḥ kāryam, agnibhiś ca gārhapatyādibhir agnikāryam, uta kācid vyavastheti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? te sarvārthāḥ, prayuktatvād agnayaś ca svakālatvāt, te vṛtāḥ sarvasmai puruṣakāryāya syuḥ, agnayaś cāgnikāryāya. kutaḥ? taiḥ kāryair ākāṅkṣitvāt, prati svaṃ grahaṇam eṣām anuvādaḥ, svakālatvād agnayaś ca sarvārthā iti, samadhigatam etat.
children.translated_text: Including the owner, the seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s> of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> have been ascertained. Now the doubt arises here: should all person-functions be performed by them, and fire-functions by the fires such as the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and others, or is there some allocation? What is the prima facie view? They [serve] all purposes — because of being employed, and the fires [serve] because of their own time. Those [priests] who have been selected should serve for all person-functions, and the fires for fire-functions. Why? Because of their requiring those functions. Their individual mention is a restatement. Because of their own time, the fires too serve all purposes — this has been ascertained.
