children.text: tatsaṃyogāt karmaṇo vyavasthā syāt, saṃyogasyārthavattvāt // MS_3,7.40 //
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with that [specific priest], there should be an allocation of rites, since the connection would be purposeful. // MS 3,7.40 //

children.text: tatsaṃyogād viśiṣṭapuruṣasaṃyogāt, vyavatiṣṭheta, ye yena puruṣeṇa samākhyāyante, te tena kartavyāḥ, evaṃ teṣāṃ puruṣasaṃyogo 'rthavān bhaviṣyati. ādhvaryavam adhvaryuṇā, hautraṃ hotrā, audgātram udgātreti.
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with that [specific priest] — because of the connection with a specific person — there should be allocation. Those [rites] that are taught together with a [specific] person should be performed by that person. Thus, their connection with [specific] persons will be purposeful. The <s>ādhvaryava</s> (Adhvaryu-functions) [are performed] by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the <s>hautra</s> (Hotṛ-functions) by the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the <s>audgātra</s> (Udgātṛ-functions) by the <s>Udgātṛ</s>.

children.text: tasyopadeśasamākhyānena nirdeśaḥ // MS_3,7.41 //
children.translated_text: The specification is through instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>) and designation (<s>samākhyāna</s>). // MS 3,7.41 //

children.text: kim eṣa evotsargaḥ? sarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ samākhyātapuruṣaiḥ kartavyam iti. neti brūmaḥ, tasyopadeśād viśeṣasamākhyānāc ca nirdeśaḥ. yathopadeśaḥ - tasmān maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati cānu cāheti{*3/691*}. samākhyā - potrīyā neṣṭrīyeti. eṣa samākhyāyāś cāpavāda iti.
children.translated_text: Is this the sole rule — that everything taught together with [a specific person] should be performed by the persons [so] taught? We say no — the specification is through instruction and through specific designation. What is an instruction? 'Therefore the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> commands and recites' — this is instruction. What is designation? '<s>Potrīyā</s>' (belonging to the <s>Potṛ</s>), '<s>Neṣṭrīyā</s>' (belonging to the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>) — these are designations. And this [instruction] is an exception to the designation.

NOTES:
[{3/691: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.12.9.5}]

children.text: tadvac ca liṅgadarśanam // MS_3,7.42 //
children.translated_text: And the observation of indicatory marks is likewise. // MS 3,7.42 //

children.text: yatra hetuḥ prātaranuvākam anubruvata upaśṛṇuyād iti hotre{*3/692*} prātaranuvāke samākhyayā prāptaṃ hotāraṃ darśayati. tathedam aparaṃ liṅgaṃ bhavati - udgītha udgātṝṇām ṛcaḥ praṇava ukthaśaṃsināṃ{*3/693*} [408]{*3/694*} pratihāro{*3/695*} 'dhvaryūṇām iti, samākhyākṛtaṃ bhedaṃ darśayati. tathedam api liṅgaṃ bhavati - yo vādhvaryoḥ svaṃ veda svavāneva bhavati, etad vādhvaryoḥ svaṃ yad āśrāvayatīti{*3/696*} samākhyākṛtaṃ niyamaṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: Where there is a reason — 'one should listen while the morning litany (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>) is being recited' — in the <s>hautra</s> (Hotṛ's) morning litany, [the text] shows the <s>Hotṛ</s> who is obtained by designation. Similarly, there is another indicatory mark: 'the <s>udgītha</s> [is the share] of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>s; the <s>ṛcas</s> (verses) [are] the <s>praṇava</s>; the <s>pratihāra</s> (response) [is the share] of the <s>Adhvaryus</s>' — [this] shows the distinction made by designation. Similarly, there is also this indicatory mark: 'whoever knows the property of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>s becomes possessed of property. This indeed is the property of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>s — that he calls out (<s>āśrāvayati</s>)' — [this] shows the restriction made by designation.

children.text: praiṣānuvacanaṃ maitrāvaruṇasyopadeśāt // MS_3,7.43 //
children.translated_text: The directive-recitation (<s>praiṣānuvacana</s>) belongs to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, because of instruction. // MS_3,7.43 //

children.text: asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ - yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*3/697*}. tatredaṃ samāmananti - tasmān maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati cānu cāheti. tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ sarvānuvacaneṣu sarvapraiṣeṣu ca maitrāvaruṇaḥ syāt, uta yatrānuvacane praiṣa iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sarvānuvacaneṣu, aviśeṣāt. na hi kaścid viśeṣa āśrīyate - asminn anuvacane maitrāvaruṇo 'smin neti. tasmāt sarvānuvacaneṣu sarvapraiṣeṣu ca maitrāvaruṇaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal — "he who is consecrated slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal." There it is taught: "therefore the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> both directs and recites." There a doubt [arises]: should the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [do this] in all recitations, or in all directives, or in both together?

children.text: puro 'nuvākyādhikāro vā praiṣasaṃnidhānāt // MS_3,7.44 //
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>'s jurisdiction is over the invitatory verse (<s>purānuvākyā</s>), because of proximity to the directive. // MS_3,7.44 //

children.text: puro 'nuvākyaṃ vā maitrāvaruṇo 'nubrūyāt. kutaḥ? yatra praiṣaś cānuvākyā ca sahocyete, tatra maitrāvaruṇaḥ, yatra kevalānuvākyā na tatra maitrāvaruṇaḥ, yatra vā kevalaḥ praiṣaḥ, tatrāpi na. yatrobhe samuccīyete, tatra sa bhavet. tathā hi samuccitayos taṃ samāmananti, tasmān maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati cānu cāheti, caśabdāt samuccitayor iti gamyate.
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> should recite [only] the invitatory verse. Why? Where a directive and an invitatory verse are mentioned together, there the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [functions]; where there is an invitatory verse alone, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [does] not [function]; where there is a directive alone, there too he does not. Where both are present together...

children.text: prātaranuvāke hotṛdarśanāt // MS_3,7.45 //
children.translated_text: Because of the evidence of the <s>Hotṛ</s> in the morning litany. // MS_3,7.45 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmo na sarvānuvacaneṣu maitrāvaruṇa iti. kutaḥ? yataḥ prātaranuvāke hotāraṃ darśayati. katham? yatra hotuḥ prātaranuvākam anubruvata upaśṛṇuyāt, tadādhvayur gṛhṇīyād iti. tasmān na sarvānuvacaneṣu maitrāvaruṇa iti.
children.translated_text: From this too we observe that the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> does not [function] in all recitations. Why? Because the <s>Hotṛ</s> is shown in the morning litany. How? "When one hears the <s>Hotṛ</s> reciting the morning litany, then the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should take [the cup]." Therefore not in all recitations [does the Maitrāvaruṇa function].

children.text: camasāṃś camasādhvaryavaḥ samākhyānāt // MS_3,7.46 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> [offer] the cups, because of designation. // MS_3,7.46 //

children.text: santi camasādhvaryavas teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ camasādhvaryavaś camasāñ juhuyur utādhvaryur iti. camasādhvaryava iti brūmaḥ. kasmāt? camaseṣv ādhvaryavaṃ te kurvantīti camasādhvaryavaḥ, tasmāt te juhuyur iti.
children.translated_text: There are <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>. Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: should the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> offer the cups, or the <s>Adhvaryu</s>? The <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>, we say. Why? Because they perform the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (Adhvaryu's function) in the cups — hence they are called <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>. Therefore they should offer.

children.text: adhvaryur vā tan nyāyatvāt // MS_3,7.47 //
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, because that is the proper method. // MS_3,7.47 //

children.text: adhvaryur vā juhuyāt, esa hi nyāyaḥ - yad ārdhvaryavapadārtham adhvaryuḥ kuryāt, ādhvaryavaś ca homaḥ, tasmād adhvaryur juhuyāt. nanu camasādhvaryava iti viśeṣasamākhyānāc camasādhvaryavo hoṣyantīti. nety ucyate, camaseṣv ete 'dhvaryuvad bhavantīti camasādhvaryavaḥ. yadi tair adhvaryur juhoti, tatas taiś camasādhvaryubhir api hotavyam. yadi camasādhvaryavo juhvati, nādhvaryuḥ. tadā te na tadvat syuś camasādhvaryavaḥ. tasmān na juhuyur iti.
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should offer, for this is the proper method — that the <s>Adhvaryu</s> performs what pertains to the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> operations, and the oblation is an <s>Ādhvaryava</s> act; therefore the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should offer. But would not the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> offer, due to the specific designation "<s>Camasādhvaryu</s>"?

children.text: camase cānyadarśanāt // MS_3,7.48 //
children.translated_text: And because in the cup, another is seen [performing]. // MS_3,7.48 //

children.text: camase cānyaṃ camasādhvaryor darśayati. katham? yamasāṃś ca[410]{*3/699*}masādhvaryave prayacchati, tān sa vaṣaṭkartre harati, anyo hutvā{*3/700*} camasādhvaryave prayacchatīti gamyate. katham? sa{*3/701*} vaṣaṭkartre harati, bhakṣayitum iti gamyate. tasmād dhutasya camasādhvaryave pradānam, yo juhoti, sa prayacchati. tasmād anyo juhotīti. api ca - yo vādhvaryoḥ svaṃ veda svavāneva bhavati, srugvādhvaryoḥ svaṃ vāyavyam asya svaṃ camaso 'sya svam iti. na tāvad asya camasaḥ svam, yajamānasya hi saḥ. camaso 'sya svam iti bruvan, adhvaryoś camasena homaṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: And in the cup, another is shown besides the <s>Camasādhvaryu</s>. How? "He gives the cups [410] to the <s>Camasādhvaryu</s>; he carries them to the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterer" — it is understood that another, having offered, gives [them back] to the <s>Camasādhvaryu</s>. How? He...

children.text: aśaktau te pratīyeran // MS_3,7.49 //
children.translated_text: In case of inability, they [the Camasādhvaryus] would be understood [as offerers]. // MS_3,7.49 //

children.text: atha kathaṃ camasādhvaryava iti samākhyānam? ucyate - aśaktau te pratīyeran, yadā vyāpṛtatvāt, na śaknoty adhvaryur hotum, tadā samākhyāsām arthāt te hoṣyanti.
children.translated_text: But how then is the designation "<s>Camasādhvaryu</s>" [explained]? We reply: in case of inability, they would be understood [as offerers] — when, due to being occupied, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is unable to offer, then by virtue of the designation, they will offer.

children.text: vedopadeśāt pūrvavad vedānyatve yathopadeśaṃ syuḥ // MS_3,7.50 //
children.translated_text: Because of the Vedic instruction, as before; if the <s>Veda</s> is different, [the priests] should be as instructed. // MS_3,7.50 //

children.text: asty audgātre samākhyātaḥ śyenaḥ, ādhvaryave vājapeyaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ śyena udgātṛbhir eva padārthāḥ kartavyāḥ, vājapeye 'dhvaryubhiḥ, utobhayatra nānartvigbhir iti. kiṃ prāptam? vedopadeśāt, samākhyānād ity arthaḥ{*3/702*}, pūrvavat, yathā, ādhvaryavam iti samākhyānāt padārthān adhvaryuḥ karoti, evam eva vedānyatve yathopdeśaṃ syuḥ, yo yena samākhyāte veda upadiṣṭaḥ, tasya padārthās tenaiva kartavyāḥ. sāṅgaḥ sa tatropadiśyate. tasmāc chyena udgātṛbhir vājapeye cādhvaryubhiḥ padārthāḥ kartavyā iti.
children.translated_text: The <s>Śyena</s> (hawk sacrifice) is designated as belonging to the <s>Audgātra</s> (Udgātṛ's function), and the <s>Vājapeya</s> to the <s>Ādhvaryava</s>. There a doubt [arises]: should the operations in the <s>Śyena</s> be performed by <s>Udgātṛs</s> alone, and in the <s>Vājapeya</s> by <s>Adhvaryus</s>, or in both [cases] by various priests? What is the prima facie view? Because of Vedic instruction, [the designation] from designation...

children.text: tadgrahaṇād vā svadharmaḥ syād adhikārasāmarthyāt sahāṅgair avyaktaḥ śeṣe // MS_3,7.51 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of adopting that [archetype], it would have its own properties; by the force of the enjoining authority, together with subsidiaries, what is unmanifest [applies] in the remainder. // MS_3,7.51 //

children.text:
tadgrahaṇāt, prākṛtadharmagrahaṇāt{*3/704*}, vā svadharmaḥ svair dharmaiś codakaprāptaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ{*3/705*} syāt, codakasāmarthyāt sahāṅgaiḥ kuryād iti śrūyate, tāni cāṅgāni jyotiṣṭome santy apekṣyante. tatra jyotiṣṭome nānarvijas tair asya sahaikavākyatā.
nanu pratyakṣā samākhyā, codaka ānumānikaḥ. ucyate - satyam, pratyakṣā samākhyā, laukikī tu sā. tatrānumāya vaidikaṃ śabdaṃ tenaikavākyatā syāt, codake punar viprakṛṣṭādhītayā pratyakṣayetikartavyatayā sahaikavākyatā. tasmāc codako balavattaraḥ.
yat tūktam - samākhyānād iti. tatrocyate - avyaktaḥ śeṣe samākhyāto bhaviṣyati. yaḥ padārtho na codakena prāpnoti, tatra samākhyayā niyamo bhaviṣyati. yathā śyene kaṇṭakair vitudantīty udgātāro
vitotsyanti, vājapeye coṣapuṭair{*3/706*} arpayantīty{*3/707*} adhvaryavo 'rpayiṣyanti.
children.translated_text: Because of adopting that — adopting the properties of the archetype — it would be endowed with its own properties, those established by the injunction. By the force of the injunction, it is heard that one should perform [the rite] together with subsidiaries; and those subsidiaries exist in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and are required...

children.text: svāmikarma parikrayaḥ karmaṇas tadarthatvāt // MS_3,8.1 //
children.translated_text: The purchase (<s>parikraya</s>) is the sacrificer's act, because the ritual serves that purpose. // MS_3,8.1 //

children.text: asti parikrayaḥ, jyotiṣṭome dvādaśaśatam, darśapūrṇamāsayor anvāhāryam{*3/709*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim adhvaryuṇā parikretavyā ṛtvijaḥ, uta svāmineti. kiṃ prāptam? samākhyānād adhvaryuṇeti prāpte brūmaḥ - svāmikarma parikrayaḥ. svayaṃ karotīti gamyate. kasmāt?{*3/710*} karmaṇas tadarthatvāt, phalakāmo hi yajamānaḥ, yaś ca phalakāmaḥ, tena svayaṃ kartavyam. sa yadi parikrīṇīte, tataḥ svayaṃ sarvaṃ karotīti gamyate. atha na parikrīṇīte na sarvaṃ kuryāt. tasmāt svāmī parikrīṇīteti.
children.translated_text: There is a purchase: in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, twelve hundred [cows]; in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the supplementary offering (<s>anvāhārya</s>). There a doubt [arises]: should the <s>Adhvaryu</s> purchase the priests, or the sacrificer? What is the prima facie view? By designation, [it should be done by] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. Given this, we say: [it is] the sacrificer's [act]...

children.text: vacanād itareṣāṃ syāt // MS_3,8.2 //
children.translated_text: Because of a [specific] statement, it would apply to others. // MS_3,8.2 //

children.text: kim eṣa evotsargaḥ? nety ucyate - vacanād itareṣāṃ syāt. yatra vacanaṃ bhavati, tatra vacanaprāmāṇyād bhavati parikrayaḥ. ya etām iṣṭakām upadadhyāt sa trīn varān dadyād iti{*3/711*}.
children.translated_text: Is this the only initiation (<s>utsarga</s>)? No, we say: because of a statement, it would apply to others. Where there is a [specific] statement, there, by the authority of the statement, a purchase occurs: "He who places this brick should give three chosen [gifts]."

children.text: saṃskārās tu puruṣasāmarthye yathāvedaṃ karmavad vyavatiṣṭheran // MS_3,8.3 //
children.translated_text: But consecrations, being within the person's capacity, should be arranged according to the <s>Veda</s>, like the ritual acts. // MS_3,8.3 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - keśaśmaśrū vapate, dato dhāvate, nakhāni nikṛntate, snātīti{*3/713*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim evaṃjātīyakā adhvaryuṇā kartavyāḥ, uta yajamāneneti. kiṃ prāptam? adhvaryuṇā kartavyāḥ, saṃskārā yathāvedaṃ vyavatiṣṭheran samākhyānāt puruṣeṇa karmavat, yathā - anye padārthā yasmin veda āmnātāḥ, tatsamākhyātena puruṣeṇa kriyante, evam ete 'pīti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: "He shaves the hair and beard, brushes the teeth, trims the nails, bathes." There a doubt [arises]: should such acts be performed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, or by the sacrificer? What is the prima facie view? They should be done by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; the consecrations should be arranged according to the <s>Veda</s>, by the person [designated] by designation, like the ritual acts — just as other operations taught in a particular <s>Veda</s> are performed by the person designated therein, so too these.

children.text: yājamānās tu tatpradhānatvāt karmavat // MS_3,8.4 //
children.translated_text: But [they are] the sacrificer's, because [the person] is the principal in that [context], like the ritual. // MS_3,8.4 //

children.text: yajamānena vā kartavyāḥ. kutaḥ? puruṣapradhānatvāt. kathaṃ puruṣaprādhānyam? kartrabhiprāyaṃ kriyāphalaṃ gamyate, tasmāt puruṣasya karmakaraṇasāmarthyam upajanayanti. na ca kaścid yena karmakaraṇena sāmarthyam upajanyate{*3/714*} tad arthaṃ puruṣān krīṇātīti, īpsitebhyaḥ padārthebhyaḥ krīṇāti, yena yasya sāmarthyaṃ bhavati, tat tenaiva kartavyam, karmavat, yathā - pradhānakarmaṇi puruṣārthāni yajamānasya bhavanti, evam etad apīti.
children.translated_text: Or they should be performed by the sacrificer. Why? Because the person is the principal. How is the person principal? The result of the act is understood to be intended by the agent; therefore [the consecrations] generate in the person the capacity for performing the ritual. And no one purchases persons for the purpose of generating capacity for performing the ritual; rather, one purchases from desired operations. That for which one has the capacity — that should be done by that [person] himself, like the ritual — just as in the principal ritual, the things serving the person's purpose belong to the sacrificer, so too this.

NOTES:

children.text: vyapadeśāc ca // MS_3,8.5 //
children.translated_text: And because of the designation [in another voice]. // MS_3,8.5 //

children.text: parasmaipadavyapadeśaś ca bhavati - tam abhyanakti, śareṣīkayānaktīti ca. anyo yajamānasyāñjanam abhyañjanaṃ karotīti gamyate.
children.translated_text: There is designation in the <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice): "he anoints him; he anoints with a reed-splint." It is understood that another performs the anointing and rubbing of the sacrificer.

children.text: guṇatve tasya nirdeśaḥ // MS_3,8.6 //
children.translated_text: The mention of him is when [the person] is in a subordinate role. // MS_3,8.6 //

children.text: yad uktam - samākhyānād yathāvedam iti, naitad evam, guṇatve [414]{*3/715*} tasya nirdeśaḥ, tatra vayaṃ samākhyāṃ niyāmikām icchāmaḥ, yatra karmaṇaḥ prādhānyam, yad arthaṃ kretavyāḥ puruṣāḥ prāptāḥ, tatra samākhyayā niyamaḥ. kalpyo hi saṃbandho vapanādibhiḥ, puruṣāṇām, adṛṣṭārthatvāt, kḷpta ārād upakārakaiḥ. na ca kḷpta upapadyamāne kalpyaḥ śakyaḥ kalpayitum. tasmān na puruṣaprādhānye samākhyā niyāmikā syāt.
children.translated_text: As for what was stated — "by designation, according to the <s>Veda</s>" — this is not so. [414] The mention of him is when [the person] is in a subordinate role. There, we hold that the designation is restrictive where the ritual is principal — where persons are to be purchased for that purpose. But the connection with shaving and similar [acts] is to be construed for the persons [directly], since these serve an unseen purpose; the connection is already established with those who help from afar. And when something is already established, what is to be construed cannot be construed. Therefore, when the person is principal, the designation would not be restrictive.

children.text: codanāṃ prati bhāvāc ca // MS_3,8.7 //
children.translated_text: And because of relating to the injunction. // MS_3,8.7 //

children.text: codanety apūrvaṃ brūmaḥ - apūrvaṃ prati saṃskārā vidhīyante. te hy asaṃbhavād dravyeṣu kalpyante, saṃnikṛṣṭadravyābhāve ca viprakṛṣṭeṣu bhaveyuḥ, yadā tu saṃnikṛṣṭe dravye saṃbhavanti, tadā na viprakṛṣṭeṣu prayoktavyāḥ, kṛtārthatvāt. tasmād yājamānā iti.
children.translated_text: By "injunction" we mean the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>): the consecrations are enjoined in relation to the unprecedented [result]. These, being impossible in [mere] substances, are construed [in relation to persons]; and in the absence of a proximate substance, they would apply to remote ones. But when they are possible in the proximate substance [i.e., the person], then they should not be applied to remote ones, since the purpose is already served. Therefore [the consecrations are] the sacrificer's.

children.text: atulyatvād asamānavidhānāḥ syuḥ // MS_3,8.8 //
children.translated_text: They would be of unequal injunction, because of dissimilarity. // MS_3,8.8 //

children.text:
idaṃ padottaraṃ sūtram{*3/716*}. atha kasmān na samānavidhānā bhavanti? aviśeṣavidhānād dhi puruṣamātrasya prāpnuvanti. tad ucyate - naitat samānaṃ sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ vidhānam. kutaḥ? atulyatvāt, atulyā eta etadvidhānaṃ prati. kātulyatā? yat, yajamānasya vihitā nartvijām. kathaṃ yajamānasya vihitā ity agamyate? arthāt svayaṃ prayoge syād iti.
nanv aviśeṣād ṛtvijām api vihitāḥ. prayojanābhāvād avihitā iti paśyāmaḥ. kathaṃ prayojanābhāvaḥ? ṛtvigbhiḥ kriyamāṇā na yajamānena kṛtā na kāritāḥ, atadarthatvāt parikrayasya. svayaṃkṛtāś ca nārthina upakurvanti. tasmād apryojanāḥ, ata ṛtvijām avihitāḥ, etad atulyatvam. tasmān na samānavidhānā iti.
children.translated_text:
This is a <s>sūtra</s> supplementing [the previous] word. Now, why do they not have identical prescriptions? For because of the non-specific injunction, they would apply to persons in general. To this it is said: this injunction is not the same for all persons. Why? Because of the inequality — these are unequal with respect to this injunction. What is the inequality? That [the vows are] enjoined for the sacrificer, not for the <s>ṛtvijs</s>. How is it known that they are enjoined for the sacrificer? By implication — [they] would apply in one's own performance.
[Objection:] But because of the non-distinction, they are enjoined for the <s>ṛtvijs</s> too. [Reply:] We see that [they are] not enjoined, because of the absence of purpose. How is there an absence of purpose? [Vows] performed by the <s>ṛtvijs</s> are not [considered as] done or caused to be done by the sacrificer, because the hiring is not for that purpose. And [vows] performed by oneself do not benefit those who seek [the benefit]. Therefore, they are without purpose; hence they are not enjoined for the <s>ṛtvijs</s>. This is the inequality. Therefore, [they do] not have identical prescriptions.

children.text: tapaś ca phalasiddhitvāl lokavat // MS_3,8.9 //
children.translated_text: And austerity (<s>tapas</s>) [belongs to the sacrificer], because of [its] producing the result — as in worldly [practice]. // MS 3,8.9 //

children.text: tapaḥ śrūyate - dvy ahaṃ nāśnāti, try ahaṃ nāśnātīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ārtvijaṃ tapaḥ, yājamānam iti. kiṃ prāptam? samākhyānād ārtvijaṃ tapa iti prāptam. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - yājamānaṃ tapa iti. kutaḥ? phalasiddhitvāt, phalasiddhyarthaṃ tapaḥ. tapaḥsiddhasya yāgaphalaṃ siddhyati. katham etad avagamyate? duḥkhaṃ hi tapaḥ, duḥkhaṃ cādharmaphalam, adharmo yāgaphalasya pratibandhako bhavati. aśreyaskaro hi saḥ, tasmin sati na śreyo bhavitum arhati, tasmāt so 'panetavyaḥ, phalabhogena ca virudhyete dharmādharmau. tasmād duḥkhaphalabhogāya dharmaḥ{*3/718*} śrūyate. yat tena duḥkham utpādyaitavyam, idaṃ tad iti. evaṃ dṛṣṭārthaṃ bhavati, nādṛṣṭaṃ kalpayitavyam, tena phalopabhogena kṣīṇo 'dharme 'pratibaddho yāgaḥ phalaṃ dāsyatīti, phalasiddhiś ca yajamānasya kartavyā nartvijām. tasmād yājamānaṃ tapa iti.
children.translated_text: Austerity is heard: 'he does not eat for two days,' 'he does not eat for three days.' There the doubt arises: is the austerity priestly (<s>ārtvija</s>) or belonging to the sacrificer (<s>yājamāna</s>)? What is the prima facie view? Because of the designation, [it is] priestly. Given this, we say: the austerity belongs to the sacrificer. Why? Because of [its] producing the result — the austerity is for the purpose of producing the result. The sacrificial result is produced for one perfected by austerity. How is this known? For austerity is suffering, and suffering is the result of <s>adharma</s> (demerit). <s>Adharma</s> becomes an obstacle to the sacrificial result. For it produces misfortune; in its presence, good fortune cannot arise. Therefore, it must be removed; and <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> conflict with each other in the enjoyment of their results. Therefore, [the austerity] is heard [as being] for the enjoyment of the result of suffering — the suffering that is to be produced by it is this [austerity]. Thus it has a perceptible purpose; an imperceptible [purpose] need not be postulated. When <s>adharma</s> is depleted through the enjoyment of that [suffering] result, the sacrifice, unobstructed, will give its result. And the production of the result is to be done for the sacrificer, not for the <s>ṛtvijs</s>. Therefore, the austerity belongs to the sacrificer.

children.text: vākyaśeṣaś ca tadvat // MS_3,8.10 //
children.translated_text: And the sentence-remainder [confirms] this likewise. // MS 3,8.10 //

children.text: etam evārthaṃ vākyaśeṣo 'pi dyotayati - yadā vai puruṣe na kiṃcin āntarbhavati, yadāsya kṛṣṇaṃ cakṣuṣo naśyati, atha medhyatama iti. yadānaśanam{*3/719*}, tadā medhārha iti. medhaś ca yajñaḥ, yajñaś ca tyāgaḥ, tyāgaṃ kartum arhas tapasā kriyata iti vākyaśeṣo bhavati, tyāgī ca yajamānaḥ. tasmād yājamānaṃ tapa iti.
children.translated_text: The sentence-remainder too illuminates this very meaning: 'when indeed nothing internal remains in a person, when the black [part] of his eye disappears, then he is most fit for the sacrifice.' When [there is] fasting, then he is worthy of the <s>medha</s> (sacrifice). And <s>medha</s> is the sacrifice, and the sacrifice is renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>). One who is worthy to perform renunciation is made [worthy] through austerity — this is the sentence-remainder. And the renouncer is the sacrificer. Therefore, the austerity belongs to the sacrificer.

children.text: vacanād itareṣāṃ syāt // MS_3,8.11 //
children.translated_text: Because of [Vedic] statement, [austerities] of the others [i.e., priests] should also apply. // MS 3,8.11 //

children.text: kim eṣa evotsargaḥ? sarvaṃ tapo yājamānam iti. na{*3/720*}, [416]{*3/721*} vacanād itareṣām, yatra vacanam, tatrartvijām, yathā - sarva ṛtvija upavasantīti.
children.translated_text: Is this the sole rule — that all austerity belongs to the sacrificer? No — because of [Vedic] statement, [austerities] of the others [should also apply]. Where there is [Vedic] statement, there [the austerity is] for the <s>ṛtvijs</s> — just as 'all the <s>ṛtvijs</s> observe the fast.'

children.text: guṇatvāc ca vedena na vyavasthā syāt // MS_3,8.12 //
children.translated_text: And because of [its] being a subsidiary, [there should be] no allocation by designation. // MS 3,8.12 //

children.text:
atha yad uktam - samākhyānād artvijaṃ tapa iti, guṇatvān na samākhyayā gṛhyate, yatra puruṣasya guṇabhāvaḥ, tatra samākhyā niyāmikā.
evaṃ vā śyene śrūyate - lohitoṣṇīṣā lohitavasanā ṛtvijaḥ pracarantīti. tathā vājapeye śrūyate - hiraṇyamālina ṛtvijaḥ pracarantīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ śyena udgātṛbhir lohitoṣṇīṣatā kartavyā, vājapeye cādhvaryubhir hiraṇyamālitvam, utobhayam api sarvartvijām iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? samākhyānāt śyena udgātṛbhir vājapeye 'dhvaryubhir iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - guṇatvāc ca vedena na vyavasthā syāt, guṇo lohitoṣṇīṣatā hiraṇyamālitvaṃ ca, puruṣaḥ pradhānam, ato lohitam uṣṇīṣaṃ hiraṇyamālā ca puruṣaviśeṣaṇatvena śrūyate, na kartavyatayā, tasmāt puruṣaprādhānyam. kim ataḥ? yady evam, puruṣāṇāṃ pradhānabhāve samākhyā na niyāmikety etad uktam.
api ca - guṇatvaśravaṇāt sarvapuruṣāṇām etad vidhānam iti gamyate, pradhānasaṃnidhau hi guṇaḥ śiṣyamānaḥ pratipradhānam upadiṣṭo bhavati. tatra vacanena prāptaṃ kathaṃ samākhyayā vidyamānayāpi niyantuṃ śakyeta? tasmād ubhayatra sarvartvigbhir evaṃjātīyako dharmaḥ kriyeteti.
children.translated_text:
Now, as for what was said — 'because of the designation, the austerity is priestly' — because of [its] being a subsidiary, [there should be] no assignment through designation. Where the person has subsidiary status, there the designation is determinative.
Alternatively, in the <s>Śyena</s> (hawk-shaped [rite]) it is heard: 'the <s>ṛtvijs</s> perform [their duties] wearing red turbans and red garments.' Similarly, in the <s>Vājapeya</s> it is heard: 'the <s>ṛtvijs</s> perform [their duties] wearing golden garlands.' There the doubt arises: should the wearing of red turbans be done in the <s>Śyena</s> by the <s>Udgātṛ</s>s [only], and the wearing of golden garlands in the <s>Vājapeya</s> by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>s [only], or should both be for all <s>ṛtvijs</s>? What is the prima facie view? Because of the designation, [red turbans are] for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>s in the <s>Śyena</s>, and [golden garlands are] for the <s>Adhvaryu</s>s in the <s>Vājapeya</s>. Given this, we say: because of [their] being a subsidiary, there should be no allocation by designation. The red turban and golden garland are subsidiaries; the person is the principal. Therefore, the red turban and golden garland are heard as qualifiers of the person, not as something to be done [by specific priests]. Hence, the person is primary. What follows? If so, when persons are primary, the designation is not determinative — this has been stated.
Moreover, because [these are] heard as qualities, it is understood that this injunction applies to all persons. For a quality, being taught in the proximity of the principal, is understood as [applying] to each principal [individually]. There, how could what is obtained through [Vedic] statement be restricted even by an existing designation? Therefore, in both [rites], such a prescription should be performed by all <s>ṛtvijs</s>.

children.text: tathā kāmo 'rthasaṃyogāt // MS_3,8.13 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, desire (<s>kāma</s>) [belongs to the sacrificer], because of the connection with the purpose. // MS 3,8.13 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome samāmananti - yadi kāmayeta varṣet parjanya iti nīcaiḥ sado minuyād iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ārtvijaḥ kāmaḥ, atha yājamāna iti. kim evam? yadi kāmayetādhvaryur iti, uta yajamāna iti, evaṃ saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ prāptam? ārtvijaḥ kāmaḥ, samākhyānāt. arthī prakṛto 'dhvaryuḥ, sa vākyena saṃbadhyate, minuyād iti. tasmād ārtvijaḥ kāma iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tathā kāmaḥ syāt, yathā
tapaḥ, yājamānaḥ kāma ity arthaḥ{*3/723*}. kutaḥ? arthasaṃyogāt, arthena yāgasya sāṅgasya, yajamānaḥ phalena saṃbadhyata iti gamyate. upagrahaviśeṣāt, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajetety upagrahaviśeṣāś ca minuyād ity adhvaryuḥ parārtham iti gamyate. atha yad uktam - prakṛtenārthinā sahaikavākyatvād iti. ucyate, evam api prakṛtena vākyena{*3/724*} sahaikavākyatā, yajamāne kāmayamāne minuyād iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> they teach: 'if one should desire "let <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god) rain" — one should make the assembly hall (<s>sadas</s>) low.' There the doubt arises: is the desire priestly or belonging to the sacrificer? What is the question? Whether 'if the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should desire' or 'if the sacrificer should desire' — thus is the doubt. What is the prima facie view? The desire is priestly, because of the designation. The <s>Adhvaryu</s> is the person under discussion; he is connected by [Vedic] statement with 'he should make' (<s>minuyāt</s>). Therefore, the desire is priestly. Given this, we say: the desire should be like the austerity — the meaning is: the desire belongs to the sacrificer. Why? Because of the connection with the purpose — by the purpose of the sacrifice together with its subsidiaries, the sacrificer is understood to be connected with the result. Because of the specific subsidiary relationship — 'one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — and the specific subsidiary relationship being 'he should make [it low],' the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is understood to [act] for another's purpose. Now, as for what was said — 'because of the single-sentence relationship with the person under discussion who seeks [the result]' — it is said: even so, the single-sentence relationship is with the sentence under discussion: 'when the sacrificer desires, he [the <s>Adhvaryu</s>] should make [it low].'

children.translated_text: Because of the designation, [the desire] of the others [i.e., priests] should apply [where specified]. // MS 3,8.14 //

children.text: yatra bhavati vyapadeśaḥ, tatrārtvijaḥ kāmo bhavati, yathā - udgātātmane vā yajamānāya vā yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate, tam āgāyatīti, yady ātmana iti yajamānāyeti parikalpyeta, yajamānagrahaṇaṃ vāśabdaś ca na samarthitau syātām. tasmād yajamānavyapadeśād ātmānam evodgātā pratinirdiśatīti gamyate.
children.translated_text: Where there is a designation, there the desire is priestly — as, for example: 'the <s>Udgātṛ</s> sings for whatever desire he desires, whether for himself or for the sacrificer.' If [the options] 'for himself' and 'for the sacrificer' were [merely] alternatives, the mention of 'the sacrificer' and the word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) would not be justified. Therefore, because of the designation mentioning 'the sacrificer,' it is understood that the <s>Udgātṛ</s> refers to himself [only in contrast to the sacrificer].
Page break marker: 418

children.text: mantrāś cākarmakaraṇās tadvat // MS_3,8.15 //
children.translated_text: And <s>mantras</s> that do not express ritual action [belong to the sacrificer] likewise. // MS 3,8.15 //

children.text:
ihaivaṃjātīyakā mantrā udāharaṇam, āyurdā agna āyur{*3/726*} me dehīti, varcodā agne 'si varco me dehīti{*3/727*}. eṣu saṃdehaḥ - kim ārtvijā uta yājamānā iti. samākhyānād ārtvijā iti prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - mantrāś caite tadvad bhaveyuḥ, yathā kāmaḥ, evam ātmābhidhāyipadaṃ yuktaṃ bhavati. āyur me varco ma iti, āyur varca ityevamādibhiḥ karmaphalam abhidhīyate, agne tvaṃ karmaphalaṃ me sādhayeti. tad iha karmaphalam utsāhārthaṃ saṃkīrtyate, yajamānaś ca tenotsahate, nānyaḥ. yad ṛtvijaḥ kramaphalam, na tad artho 'gniḥ, siddhaṃ hi tat. yad yajamānasya, tad artho 'gniḥ, tac cāsiddhaṃ sad āśāsitavyam, yad utsāhaṃ janayaty avaiguṇyāya. ṛtvig api siddhe yad utsahate, tad yajamānasyaiva karmaphalāyotsahate. tatrātmābhidhāyipadaṃ nāvakalpate, yajamāne cātmābhidhāyipadaṃ kalpyamānam agauṇaṃ bhavati, tasmād yājamānāḥ.
children.translated_text:
Here, <s>mantras</s> of this kind are the example: 'O <s>Agni</s>, giver of life, give me life'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, you are the giver of splendor, give me splendor.' Regarding these, the doubt arises: are they priestly or belonging to the sacrificer? Because of the designation, [they are] priestly — this is the prima facie view.
Given this, we say: these <s>mantras</s> too should be like the desire [i.e., belonging to the sacrificer]. Thus the word referring to oneself (<s>ātmābhidhāyipada</s>) is appropriate. 'Life for me,' 'splendor for me' — with [words like] 'life' and 'splendor,' the result of the ritual action is denoted. 'O <s>Agni</s>, accomplish the ritual result for me.' There, the ritual result is mentioned for the purpose of encouragement, and the sacrificer is encouraged by it, not another. The ritual result that belongs to the <s>ṛtvij</s> — <s>Agni</s> is not needed for that, for it is [already] accomplished. But the result that belongs to the sacrificer — <s>Agni</s> is needed for that, and being unaccomplished, it is to be wished for — [the wish] that generates enthusiasm to prevent deficiency. Even the <s>ṛtvij</s>, when he becomes enthusiastic regarding what is [already] accomplished, becomes enthusiastic precisely for the ritual result of the sacrificer. There, the word referring to oneself does not fit [the <s>ṛtvij</s>]; but when the word referring to oneself is construed [as belonging to] the sacrificer, it is non-figurative. Therefore, [these <s>mantras</s>] belong to the sacrificer.

NOTES:

[{3/727: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 1.5.5.4}]

children.text: viprayoge ca darśanāt // MS_3,8.16 //
children.translated_text: And because of observation in the case of separation. // MS 3,8.16 //

children.text: viprayoge cāgnīnāṃ pravāsa upasthānam asti, iha eva san tatra santaṃ tvāgna iti. na ca proṣito 'gnibhya ṛtvig bhavati, karma kurvata eṣa vācakaḥ śabdaḥ. bhavati tu yajamāno 'gnibhyaḥ proṣito 'pi yajamānaḥ, saṃvidhāya so 'gnihotrāya pravasati, śakyate ca videśasthenāpi tyāgaḥ kartum. sa eva proṣitasyopasthānaviśeṣaṃ bruvan yajamānasyopasthānaṃ darśayati, tenaivaivaṃjātīyakā yajamānasya bhaveyur iti.
children.translated_text: And in the case of separation [i.e., being away from home], there is the fire-attendance (<s>upasthāna</s>) during the absence: 'Being here, I [attend] you who are there, O <s>Agni</s>.' But an <s>ṛtvij</s> who has gone abroad does not remain an <s>ṛtvij</s> vis-à-vis the fires — this word [<s>ṛtvij</s>] denotes one who performs the ritual action. But the sacrificer, even when abroad, remains the sacrificer — he makes arrangements for the <s>Agnihotra</s> and then travels; and renunciation can be done even by one who is in a foreign land. He, in describing the specific attendance of one who has gone abroad, shows the attendance of the sacrificer. By this, such [observances] would belong to the sacrificer.
Page break marker: 419

children.text: dvy āmnāteṣūbhau dvy āmnasyārthavattvāt // MS_3,8.17 //
children.translated_text: When [<s>mantras</s> are] taught in two [contexts], both [should recite them], since the dual teaching would be purposeful. // MS 3,8.17 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra dvy āmnātā mantrā ādhvaryave kāṇḍe yājamāne ca. ājyaṃ yair gṛhyate, pañcānāṃ tvā vātānāṃ yantrāya dhartrāya gṛhṇāmīty{*3/729*}evamādayaḥ, tathā srugvyūhanamantrāḥ, srucau vyūhati vājasya mā prasaveneti{*3/730*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ ta ubhābhyām api kartavyā utādhvaryuṇaiveti. kiṃ prāptam? samākhyānād ādhvaryavā iti. iti prāpta ucyate{*3/731*} - ubhāv api tān prayuñjīyātām iti. kutaḥ? dvy āmnātasyārthavattvāt, dvābhyāṃ samākhyānād dvāv api kartārau gamyete, tasmād dvau brūyātām. adhvaryur etena prakāśitam anuṣṭhāsyāmīti, yajamāno na pramadiṣyāmīti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; there, <s>mantras</s> are taught in two [contexts] — in the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (Adhvaryu's) section and in the <s>Yājamāna</s> (sacrificer's) section. [For example,] with which the ghee is taken: 'For the control and support of the five winds I take you' — and so forth. Similarly, the ladle-arranging <s>mantras</s>: 'He arranges the ladles: "[I arrange you] for the production of strength (<s>vāja</s>)".' There the doubt arises: should they be [recited] by both, or by the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone? What is the prima facie view? Because of the designation, [they are] of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. Given this, it is said: both should employ them. Why? Because the dual teaching would be purposeful — since the designation [places them] with both, both are understood as agents. Therefore, both should recite [them]. The <s>Adhvaryu</s> [recites with the understanding] 'I will perform what has been made manifest by this'; the sacrificer [recites with the understanding] 'I will not be negligent.'

NOTES:

[{3/730: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 1.1.13.1}]

children.text: jñāte ca vācanaṃ na hy avidvān vihito 'sti // MS_3,8.18 //
children.translated_text: And [the recitation is to be done] by one who knows, for an unknowing person is not enjoined [as performer]. // MS 3,8.18 //

children.text:
vājapeye śrūyate - kḷptīr yajamānaṃ vācayaty ujjisatīr{*3/732*} yajamānaṃ vācayatīti{*3/733*}. atra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ jñaś cājñaś ca sarvo vācayitavya uta jña eveti. kiṃ prāptam? aviśeṣāj jñaś cājñaś ceti.
iti{*3/734*} prāpte brūmaḥ - jña eveti. kutaḥ? na hy avidvān vihito 'sti, yo hy avidvān nāsāv adhikṛtaḥ sāmarthyābhāvāt. nanu prayogakāle śikṣitvā prayokṣyate, sāmarthyād [420]{*3/735*} adhikriyeteti. neti brūmaḥ - vedādhyayanād uttarakāle prayogaḥ śrūyate, na prayogaśrutigṛhītaṃ vedādhyayanam. kutaḥ? anārabhyakarmaṇi vede{*3/736*} śrūyate - tasmāt svādhyayo 'dhyetavya iti. saty etasmin vacane, agnihotraṃ juhuyād ityevamādibhir vedo 'dhyetavya ity etad uktaṃ bhavatīti na śakyate kalpayitum. tatra homamātre codite vedādhyāyī śakta ity adhikriyate, nāvidvān. kiyatā punar viditena vidvān adhikriyata iti. yāvatā viditena śakto bhavati, yathoktaṃ kratum abhinirvartayitum. tasmāt{*3/737*} tāvad yo veda sa tena kratunādhikriyate.
nanu vedam adhīyīteti vacanāt kṛtsno vedo 'dhyetavya iti bhavati, na vedāvayavenādhīkriyata iti. ucyate - kratūnāṃ jñānārthaṃ vedādhyayanaṃ kāryam. tatrānyasmin kratau kartavye 'nyakratujñānaṃ na dṛṣṭāya bhavati, tasmāt kratvantarajñānam adhikāre nādartavyam, kratvantarajñānāya kratvantaragranthaḥ, sarve kratavaḥ kathaṃ jñāyeran? pṛthak pṛthag iti kṛtsnasya vedasyādhyayanaṃ śrūyate, tasmāt svapadārthajño 'dhikriyeteti. tenāsvapadārthajñasya karmaiva nāsti, kathama asau vācyeta. tasmāt sādhv abhidhīyate, jña eva vācayitavya iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Vājapeya</s> it is heard: "He makes the sacrificer recite the <s>kḷptīs</s> (arrangements); he makes the sacrificer recite the <s>ujjisatīs</s> (victorious [formulas])." Here a doubt [arises]: should everyone — both the knowledgeable and the ignorant — be made to recite, or only the knowledgeable? What is the prima facie view? Since there is no distinction, both the knowledgeable and the ignorant.
Given this, we say: only the knowledgeable. Why? Because an ignorant person is not qualified — one who is ignorant is not entitled, due to lack of capacity. But would he not learn at the time of performance and then perform, being entitled by [his acquired] capacity? No, we say — performance is heard as coming after Vedic study, not Vedic study as included within the hearing of performance. Why? Regarding the <s>Veda</s>, which is not undertaken for any [specific] ritual purpose, it is heard: "Therefore the self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is to be studied." Given this statement, it cannot be construed that "one should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>" and similar [injunctions] mean "the <s>Veda</s> is to be studied." [420] There, when mere oblation is enjoined, one who has studied the <s>Veda</s> is qualified as capable, not the ignorant. With how much knowledge then is one qualified? With as much knowledge as makes one capable of accomplishing the ritual as stated. Therefore, he who knows [that much] is entitled to that ritual.
But since "one should study the <s>Veda</s>" is a statement, the entire <s>Veda</s> is to be studied, not [just a part] — one is not entitled by [knowing only] a portion of the <s>Veda</s>. We reply: Vedic study is to be done for the knowledge of rituals. There, when one ritual is to be performed, knowledge of another ritual does not serve a visible purpose. Therefore, knowledge of other rituals need not be considered for entitlement; the text of other rituals is for knowledge of other rituals. How would all rituals be known? Separately — thus the study of the entire <s>Veda</s> is heard. Therefore, one who knows one's own operations is entitled. Hence, for one who does not know one's own operations, there is no ritual at all — how would he be made to recite? Therefore it is rightly stated: only the knowledgeable should be made to recite.

children.text: yājamāne samākhyānāt karmāṇi yājamānaṃ syuḥ // MS_3,8.19 //
children.translated_text: The acts in the sacrificer's [section] would be the sacrificer's, because of designation. // MS_3,8.19 //

children.text:
sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra karmāṇy{*3/738*} āmnātāni dvādaśa, vatsaṃ copāvasṛjati, ukhāṃ cādhiśrayati, ava ca hanti, dṛṣadupale ca samāhanti, adhi ca vapate, kapālāni copadadhāti, [421]{*3/739*} puroḍāśaṃ cādhiśrayate, ājyaṃ ca, stambayajuś ca harati, abhi ca gṛhṇāti, vedaṃ ca parigṛhṇāti,
patnīṃ ca{*3/740*} saṃnahyati, prokṣaṇīś cāsādayati, ājyaṃ ca, tāni{*3/741*} dvādaśa{*3/742*} dvāndvāni darśapūrṇamāsayor iti{*3/743*}. atra saṃdehaḥ - kim etāny adhvaryoḥ karmāṇi, uta yajamānasyeti. kiṃ prāptam? yajamāne samākhyānāt karmāṇi yājamānaṃ syuḥ. viśeṣasamākhyānād yājamānānīti gamyate, yathā potrīyaṃ neṣṭrīyam iti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites; therein twelve acts are taught: he releases the calf, he puts the pot on the fire, he strikes down, he brings together the upper and lower grinding stones, he sprinkles [grain], he places the potsherds, [421] he puts the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake) on the fire, and the <s>ājya</s> (ghee), he brings the <s>stambayajus</s>, he grasps, he takes hold of the <s>veda</s> (grass-bundle), he girds the wife, he brings the sprinkling waters, and the <s>ājya</s> — these twelve paired [acts] in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Here a doubt [arises]: are these acts the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s or the sacrificer's? What is the prima facie view? Since they are designated in the sacrificer's [section], the acts would be the sacrificer's — from the specific designation they are understood as the sacrificer's, just as [there are acts called] <s>Potrīya</s> (belonging to the Potṛ) and <s>Neṣṭrīya</s> (belonging to the Neṣṭṛ).

children.text: adhvaryur vā tadartho hi nyāyapūrvaṃ samākhyānam // MS_3,8.20 //
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [performs them], for the designation follows the proper method, being preceded by rule. // MS_3,8.20 //

children.text:
adhvaryur vā kuryād etāni, tad artho hy adhvaryuḥ parikrīta iti samākhyānād avagamyate. adhvaryava eva sarva ime padārthāḥ samāmnātāḥ, yājamāna eṣāṃ dvandvatocyate, dvandvatā ca samabhyāśakriyā{*3/744*}. tatrādhvaryuḥ padārthān kariṣyati, yajamānenāpi samabhyāśīkaraṇam{*3/745*} ity etad aśakyam. tatrāṅgaguṇavirodhe ca, tādarthyād iti dvandvatāguṇo bādhitavyaḥ. tasmād ādhvaryavā ete padārthā iti.
yad uktaṃ samākhyānād iti, tat parihartavyam, ucyate - nyāyapūrvaṃ samākhyānam, samākhyānād yajamānena dvandvatā saṃpādayitavyā, idaṃ cedaṃ ca saṃpādayeti yajamāno brūyāt. keṣucic cātra padārtheṣu yajamānasyānumantaraṇam, tannimittā samākhyā bhaviṣyati, apūrvaṃ tv apakṛṣyeta. tad uktam - yathā potrīyam, neṣṭrīyam iti, evam atrāpīti. tad ucyate - yuktaṃ tatra viśeṣa[422]{*3/746*}samākhyānāt. iha tu dvandvatā yājamānīyā, padārthās tv ādhvaryavā eva. tasmād adoṣaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Or the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should perform these, for it is understood from the designation that the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is purchased for that purpose. All these operations are taught as belonging to the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (Adhvaryu's function); their designation as the sacrificer's is [merely] pairing (<s>dvandva</s>), and pairing is participation. There the <s>Adhvaryu</s> will perform the operations; the sacrificer's participation cannot [extend to actual performance]. And when there is a conflict between subsidiary quality and [another principle], because of serving that purpose, the subsidiary quality of pairing should be overridden. Therefore these operations belong to the <s>Ādhvaryava</s>.
As for what was stated — "because of designation" — that must be addressed. We say: the designation follows the rule — from the designation, the sacrificer's pairing is to be accomplished, [meaning] the sacrificer should say "accomplish this and that." And in some of these operations, the sacrificer's consent [is required]; that will be the basis for the designation — but the unprecedented [injunction] would be withdrawn. [422] As was stated — "just as <s>Potrīya</s> and <s>Neṣṭrīya</s>" — so here too. To that we say: there the specific designation is fitting. But here the pairing belongs to the sacrificer, while the operations belong to the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> alone. Therefore there is no defect.

children.text: vipratiṣedhe karaṇaḥ, samavāyaviśeṣād itaram anyas teṣāṃ yato viśeṣaḥ syāt // MS_3,8.21 //
children.translated_text: In case of conflict, [one follows] the instrumental [mantra]; because of the specific connection, another [performs] the other [act]; of those, the distinction would be based on that [qualification]. // MS_3,8.21 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agniṣomīyaḥ, tasya yūpasya parivyāṇe mantrau, ekaḥ - adhvaryoḥ parivīrasīti{*3/747*} karaṇaḥ, aparo hotur yuvā suvāsā iti{*3/748*} kriyamāṇānuvādī. tayoś codakaparamparayā kuṇḍapāyinām ayanaṃ prāptayor bhavati saṃdehaḥ - kaḥ punar asau? tatra ṛtviksamāsa āmnātaḥ - yo hotā so 'dhvaryur iti, kiṃ karaṇam ādhvaryavaṃ hotā kuryāt? kiṃ hautraṃ kriyamāṇānuvādinam iti. kiṃ prāptam? aniyama iti.
iti prāpta uccyate - vipratiṣedhe karaṇaḥ syāt, ādhvaryavaḥ parivīrasīti, na kriyamāṇānuvādī hotur yuvā suvāsā iti. kutaḥ? samavāyaviśeṣāt. dvau tatra samavāyau, hotuś codakena hautreṣu, pratyakṣaśravaṇenādhvaryaveṣu - yo hotā so 'dhvaryur iti. evaṃ pratyakṣam adhvaryoḥ kārye codyate, pratyakṣaṃ cānumānād balīyaḥ. tasmād ādhvaryavaṃ karaṇaṃ parivīrasīti hotā kuryāt. atha hautraṃ viruddhaṃ kaḥ kuryāt? itaram anyaḥ, teṣāṃ yato viśeṣaḥ syāt, anyo hotṛpuruṣa eva syāt, yasyāvyāpṛtatā, prādhānyaviśeṣo vā.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal; for the wrapping of its sacrificial post there are two <s>mantras</s> — one, "O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, thou art the wrapper," is instrumental (<s>karaṇa</s>); the other, belonging to the <s>Hotṛ</s>, "the young one, well-clad," is a description of what is being done (<s>kriyamāṇānuvādin</s>). When both are established through a chain of injunctions leading to the <s>Kuṇḍapāyin</s> [rite], a doubt arises: who [performs the wrapping]? There, a priestly combination is taught — "he who is the <s>Hotṛ</s> is [also] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>" — so should the <s>Hotṛ</s> perform the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> instrumental [act]? Or the <s>Hautra</s> descriptive [act]? What is the prima facie view? No restriction.
Given this, we say: in case of conflict, [one follows] the instrumental — "thou art the wrapper" is <s>Ādhvaryava</s>, not the descriptive "the young one, well-clad" belonging to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Why? Because of the specific connection. There are two connections: the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s with the <s>Hautra</s> acts through the injunction, and explicitly with the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> through direct statement — "he who is the <s>Hotṛ</s> is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>." Thus he is explicitly enjoined in the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s function, and direct statement is stronger than inference. Therefore the <s>Hotṛ</s> should perform the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> instrumental act "thou art the wrapper." And the conflicting <s>Hautra</s> [act] — who should perform it? Another — another person in the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s group itself, whoever is available or has precedence.

children.text: praiṣeṣu ca parādhikārāt // MS_3,8.22 //
children.translated_text: And in the directives, because of another's jurisdiction. // MS_3,8.22 //

children.text:
sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra praiṣāḥ samānātāḥ, prokṣaṇīr āsādayedhmā barhir upasādhaya srucaś saṃmṛḍḍhi{*3/749*} patnīṃ saṃnahyājyenodehīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ ya eva praiṣe, sa eva praiṣārthe, utānyaś ca praiṣe, anyaś ca praiṣārtha iti. kiṃ prāptam? eka eva praiṣapraiṣārthayor iti. kutaḥ? samākhyānāt, anya iti cāśrūtatvāt.
nanv ātmanaḥ praiṣo vipratiṣidhyate. ucyate, na praiṣo bhaviṣyati, prāptakāle loṭaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ. āha, prāptakāle 'pi sati yuṣmadādiṣv evopapadeṣu madhyamādayo vyavasthitāḥ, na puruṣasaṃskaro bhavati. ucyate - satyāṃ vivakṣāyāṃ yuṣmadādiṣu madhyamādayaḥ, yadā tava prāptaḥ kāla iti vivakṣyate, tadā yuṣmad eva madhyamo nāsmadi śeṣe vā. yadā khalu kriyāyāḥ prāptaḥ kāla ity etāvad vivakṣyate, na tava, mama veti, na tadā yuṣmadādīnām anurodhena madhyamādayo bhavitum arhanti. na ca, idaṃ yugapad vivakṣituṃ śakyate, padārthasya prāptaḥ kālaḥ, tava ceti, bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. tena, yadi vā nirjñāte padārthakāle tava kāla iti śakyate vaditum, yadi vā taveti nirjñāte padārthasya kāla iti. tatra padārthasya kālo vaditavyaḥ, na tu yauṣmadarthasya, tena hi smṛtena prayojanam, sa hi kartavya ity avagataḥ, na tu yuṣmadarthaḥ tathā, tasmāt samākhyāyād adhvaryor eva praiṣapraiṣārthāv iti.
iti{*3/750*} prāpte brūmaḥ - praiṣeṣv anyo 'nyas tadartheṣv iti. kutaḥ? parādhikārāt, parasmin hi praiṣa upapadyate, nātmanīti. āha, nanūktaṃ prāptakāle bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, [424]{*3/751*} na, saṃbhavati praiṣa, prāptakālatā nyāyyā. tasya hi yuṣmadartho{*3/752*} gamyamāno na vivakṣita ity ucyate, saṃbhavati cātra praiṣārthaḥ. tasmāt praiṣaḥ, praiṣaś cet, anyaḥ praiṣārtha iti siddham.
children.translated_text:
There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites; therein directives (<s>praiṣa</s>) are taught: "Set out the sprinkling waters; prepare the fuel and the sacrificial grass; clean the ladles; gird the wife; pour with the ghee." There a doubt [arises]: is the same person who [gives] the directive also [the one who performs] the directive's purpose, or is one [person] in the directive and another in the directive's purpose? What is the prima facie view? One and the same person for both the directive and its purpose. Why? Because of designation, and because no "other" is heard.
But a directive to oneself is contradicted. We reply: it will not be a directive; when the time comes, we shall call it an imperative (<s>loṭ</s>). [The objector] says: even when the time has come, the middle voice and other [forms] are established [only] with second-person and other forms like "you" — there is no change in person. We reply: when there is an intention to express [the second person], the middle forms apply with "you" and similar [forms]; when the intention is "the time for your [action] has come," then "you" and the middle [apply], not "I" or the remainder. But when the intention is merely "the time for the act has come" — not "your" or "my" — then the middle forms should not follow "you" and similar [forms]. And it is not possible to intend both simultaneously — "the time for the operation has come and for you" — for the sentence would be split. Therefore, either after knowing the time for the operation, one can say "your time," or after knowing "your [time]," [one can say] "the time for the operation." There, the time for the operation is to be stated, not the meaning of "your"; for by remembering that [operation], there is purpose — it is known as "to be done" — but the meaning of "your" is not so. Therefore, by designation, both the directive and its purpose belong to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone.
Given this, we say: in the directives, one [person gives them], and another [performs] their purposes. Why? Because of another's jurisdiction — the directive is appropriate toward another, not toward oneself. [424] [The objector] says: but it was stated that [the imperative] will apply when the time has come. We reply: no — when a directive is possible, the interpretation as "when the time has come" is proper. For the meaning of "you" that is understood is said not to be intended; but here the purpose of the directive is possible. Therefore it is a directive, and if it is a directive, it is established that another [performs] its purpose.

children.text: adhvaryus tu darśanāt // MS_3,8.23 //
children.translated_text: But [the one who directs is] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, because of evidence. // MS_3,8.23 //

children.text: athaivaṃ gate, idaṃ saṃdihyate - kim adhvaryur agnīdhraṃ preṣyet, utāgnīd adhvaryum iti. aniyamo 'viśeṣād iti prāpte brūmaḥ - adhvaryur uktapraiṣārthakārī syāt. kutaḥ? darśanāt, darśanaṃ bhavati - tiryañ ca sphyaṃ dhārayed yad anvañcaṃ dhārayed vajro vai sphyo vajreṇādhvaryuṃ kṣiṇvīteti{*3/753*}, yaḥ preṣyati, tasya haste sphyaḥ. sphyenādhvaryuṃ kṣiṇvītety anyam adhvaryuṃ preṣakād darśayati. tasmād agnīd adhvaryuṃ preṣyed iti.
children.translated_text: Now, this being the case, this is doubted: should the <s>Adhvaryu</s> direct the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, or the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> direct the <s>Adhvaryu</s>? When "no restriction, because of no distinction" is the prima facie view, we say: the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should be the one who performs the stated directive-purpose. Why? Because of evidence — there is evidence: "He should hold the wooden sword sideways; if he held it lengthwise, the wooden sword being a thunderbolt, he would strike the <s>Adhvaryu</s> with the thunderbolt." The one who directs holds the wooden sword in his hand. "He would strike the <s>Adhvaryu</s> with the wooden sword" — it shows the <s>Adhvaryu</s> as different from the director. Therefore the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> should direct the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.

children.text: gauṇo vā karmasāmānyāt // MS_3,8.24 //
children.translated_text: Or [the designation is] secondary, because of commonality of acts. // MS_3,8.24 //

children.text: naitad asti, agnīdhraḥ praiṣo 'dhvaryoḥ praiṣārtha iti. kiṃ khalv adhvaryur evāgnīdhaṃ preṣyet, evam adhvaryuṇā praiṣaḥ praiṣārthaś cobhāv api kṛtau bhaviṣyataḥ, tatrādhvaryavam iti samākhyānugrahīṣyate. tasmād adhvaryur eva mukhyaṃ{*3/754*} syāt. kim asya mukhyatvam? yad anena sarvaṃ kartavyaṃ samākhyānād iti. atha yad uktam - adhvaryuḥ pracaritā dṛśyata iti. tad ucyate - satyaṃ dṛśyate, na tv asya praiṣārthakaraṇe pramāṇam asti cintyamānam. tasmād etan mithyādarśanam, yasya hi darśanasya pramāṇaṃ nāsti, vyāmohaḥ saḥ. yathā śuktikāyāṃ rajatavijñānam. asti tv agnīdhraḥ praiṣārthakaraṇe pramāṇam. tasmād agnīdhraḥ pracaritā pracaritari [425]{*3/755*} cādhvaryuśabdo dṛśyate. tasmād gauṇaḥ, ādhvaryave vede samāmnātān{*3/756*} padārthān karotīti kṛtvādhvaryur ity ucyate, āgnīdhra iti. tasmād ādhvaryavaḥ praiṣaḥ, āgnīdhraḥ praiṣārtha iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — [it is not the case] that the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>'s directive and the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s directive-purpose [apply]. What if the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone directs the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>? Then both the directive and the directive-purpose would be performed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; there, the designation "<s>Ādhvaryava</s>" would be supported. Therefore the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone would be primary. What is his primacy? That everything is to be done by him, from the designation. Now, as for what was stated — "the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is seen as the practitioner" — to that we say: true, he is seen, but there is no valid evidence, upon examination, for his performing the directive-purpose. Therefore that is a false appearance — an appearance for which there is no valid evidence is delusion, like [perceiving] silver in a shell. But there is valid evidence for the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> performing the directive-purpose. [425] Therefore the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> is the practitioner, and regarding the practitioner, the word "<s>Adhvaryu</s>" is seen [applied]. Therefore it is secondary — because he performs operations taught in the <s>Ādhvaryava Veda</s>, he is called "<s>Adhvaryu</s>," [though he is actually] the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>. Therefore the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> directive, and the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [performs] the directive-purpose.

children.text: ṛtvikphalaṃ karaneṣv arthavattvāt // MS_3,8.25 //
children.translated_text: The result for the priest [accrues] in the instrumental [acts], because of purposefulness. // MS_3,8.25 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor āmananti - mamāgne varco vihaveṣv astv iti pūrvam agniṃ parigṛhṇātīti{*3/757*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ṛtvikphalam āśāsitavyam, agne varco vihaveṣv astv iti, uta yajamānasyeti. kiṃ prāptam? adhvaryor eveti. kutaḥ? evaṃ śrutir ādṛtā bhavisyati, itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt, ātmanā yajamānaṃ lakṣayet. tasmād ṛtvikphalam āśāsitavyam iti. ko 'rthaḥ? anayā samidhā dhāryamāṇe 'gnau yāgaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati. tatra vihaveṣu spardhāsthāneṣv ahaṃ varcasvī bhaviṣyāmīty adhvaryor vacanam, evam utsāhī bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> they teach: 'May my splendor be in the offerings, O <s>Agni</s>!' — 'first he grasps the fire [with fuel].' There the doubt arises: should the <s>ṛtvij</s>'s result be wished for — 'O <s>Agni</s>, may splendor be [mine] in the offerings' — or the sacrificer's? What is the prima facie view? [It is] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s alone. Why? Thus the <s>śruti</s> (direct statement) will be honored; otherwise there would be <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary indication) — it would indicate the sacrificer by [the word] 'self.' Therefore, the <s>ṛtvij</s>'s result is to be wished for. What is the meaning? When fire is sustained by this fuel-stick, the sacrifice will be possible. There, in the offerings — in the places of rivalry — 'I will be splendid' is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s statement; thus he will become enthusiastic.

NOTES:
[{3/757: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 4.7.14.1}]

children.text: svāmino vā tadarthatvāt // MS_3,8.26 //
children.translated_text: Or [the wish is] for the owner [i.e., sacrificer], because the [ritual] action is for his purpose. // MS 3,8.26 //

children.text: yajamānasya vā vacanaṃ tadarthatvāt karmaṇaḥ, yajamānārthaṃ hīdaṃ karma sāṅgam, upagrahaviśeṣāt, sāṅgasyāsya prayojanaṃ yajamānasya phalaniṣpattir nādhvaryoḥ supravaritur{*3/758*} api yaśaḥ. kim ataḥ? yady evam, phalasaṃkīrtanāt phalakartavyatā gamyate, tad etad [426]{*3/759*} agnyanvādhānaṃ yajamānasya phalasaṃkīrtane kriyamāṇe 'nena mantreṇa phalasaṃbandhāt prakāśitaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati, nādhvaryuyaśaḥkīrtanena. tasmād yajamānaphalam āśāsitavyam iti. atha kasmān na yājamāna eṣa mantro bhavatīti. ucyate - agnyanvādhānaṃ samākhyayādhvaryavam. tac caivaṃ guṇo mantraḥ karoty ādhvaryavaḥ, sa ucyate 'nena mantreṇeti, tasmād ādhvaryavo mantraḥ. mama varco 'stv atyapi yajamānasya varco mameti vyapadiśati lakṣaṇayā, yathā rājani jayaṃ vartamānaṃ sainikā asmākam iti vyapadiśanty evam.
children.translated_text: Or the statement is the sacrificer's, because the ritual action is for his purpose. For this ritual action together with its subsidiaries is for the sacrificer's purpose, because of the specific subsidiary relationship. The purpose of this [ritual] together with its subsidiaries is the production of the result for the sacrificer, not the fame of even a most excellent <s>Adhvaryu</s>. What follows? If so, from the mention of the result, the obligation to [produce] the result is understood. This <s>agnyanvādhāna</s> (fire-replenishing), when the mention of the result occurs through this <s>mantra</s>, becomes illuminated and accomplished through the connection with the result, not through the mention of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s fame. Therefore, the sacrificer's result is to be wished for. But why is this <s>mantra</s> not [simply classified as] belonging to the sacrificer? It is said: the <s>agnyanvādhāna</s> is of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> by designation. And the <s>mantra</s>, being a subsidiary in this way, performs [its function] as part of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s [duties]; it is said [to be employed] with this <s>mantra</s>. Therefore, the <s>mantra</s> is of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. [As for] 'may my splendor be' — even so, the sacrificer designates [it] as 'mine' by secondary indication, just as when victory is happening for the king, the soldiers designate it as 'ours.'

children.text: liṅgadraśanāc ca // MS_3,8.27 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS 3,8.27 //

children.text: liṅgam apy amum arthaṃ darśayati, evaṃ hy āha - yāṃ vai kāṃcana ṛtvija āśiṣam āśāsate, yajamānasyaiva sety āśiṣo yajamānārthakatāṃ darśayati. tasmād api brūmaḥ - yajamānaphalam āśāsitavyam iti. pakṣoktam eva prayojanam iti.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark too shows this meaning — for thus it says: 'whatever blessing the <s>ṛtvijs</s> wish for, that is indeed for the sacrificer' — [this] shows that the blessings are for the sacrificer's purpose. Therefore, from this too we say: the sacrificer's result is to be wished for. The purpose has been stated by [the argument of] the [previous] position.

children.text: karmārthaṃ tu phalaṃ teṣāṃ svāminaṃ pratyarthavattvāt // MS_3,8.28 //
children.translated_text: But the result [wished for] is for the ritual action of those [<s>ṛtvijs</s>], being purposeful with respect to the owner. // MS 3,8.28 //

children.text: idaṃ samadhigatam - karaṇeṣu mantreṣu svāminaḥ phalam āśāsitavyam iti. kim eṣa evotsargaḥ? nety āha, kvacid ṛtvijāṃ api phalam āśāsitavyam iti, yatra karmārthaṃ phalam, yathā - [427]{*3/760*} agnāviṣṇū māvakramiṣam{*3/761*} vijihāthāṃ māmā saṃtāptam iti{*3/762*}, asaṃtapto 'dhvaryuḥ karma śaknoti kartum, karmasiddhir yajamānasyopakāriketi, ṛtvikphalam āśāsitavyam atreti.
children.translated_text: This has been ascertained: in the instrumental <s>mantras</s>, the owner's result is to be wished for. Is this the sole rule? No, he says — sometimes the <s>ṛtvijs</s>' result too should be wished for — namely, where the result is for the sake of [performing] the ritual action. For example: 'O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, may I not stumble upon you; open up; do not scorch me.' The <s>Adhvaryu</s>, not being scorched, is able to perform the ritual action; the accomplishment of the ritual action benefits the sacrificer. Therefore, the <s>ṛtvij</s>'s result is to be wished for here.

children.text: vyapadeśāc ca // MS_3,8.29 //
children.translated_text: And because of the designation. // MS 3,8.29 //

children.text: yatra ca vyapadeśo bhavati, tatrārtvijam, dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyādhas tāc catvāra uparavāḥ prāveśamukhyāḥ{*3/763*} pradeśāntarālāḥ, tatra hastau praveśyādhvaryur yajamānam āha, kim atreti, sa āha - bhadram iti. tan nau sahety adhvaryuḥ pratyāheti vyapadeśo bhavati, adhvaryor yajamānasya ca. tan nau sahety ubhayor vacanam adhvaryuyajamānayoḥ. tasmād adhvaryuphalam āśāsitavyam atreti.
children.translated_text: And where there is a designation, there [the result is] priestly. Beneath the southern <s>havirdhāna</s>, there are four <s>uparava</s> (sounding-stones), a span in length, with openings at the front, with intervals between them. There, having inserted his hands, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> says to the sacrificer: 'what is here?' He replies: 'auspicious fortune (<s>bhadra</s>).' 'May that be for us both' — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> replies. Thus there is a designation — of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the sacrificer. 'May that be for us both' is the statement of both the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the sacrificer. Therefore, the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s result is to be wished for here.

NOTES:

children.text: dravyasaṃskāraḥ prakaraṇāviśeṣāt sarvakarmaṇām // MS_3,8.30 //
children.translated_text: The consecration of substances [applies] to all rites, because of the non-distinction of the context. // MS 3,8.30 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor barhirdharmā vedidharmāś ca, teṣu saṃdehaḥ - kim aṅgapradhānārthāḥ, uta pradhānārthā iti. prakaraṇāt pradhānārthā iti. iti{*3/764*} prāpta ucyate, naivam, dravyasaṃskāro 'ṅgapradhānārthaḥ, yathā vyākhyātam{*3/765*} evottaravivakṣayā prāptir eṣā kriyata iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> there are <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) rites and <s>vedi</s> (altar) rites. Regarding them, the doubt arises: are they for both subsidiary and principal [rites], or for the principal alone? Because of the context, [they are] for the principal — this being the prima facie view, it is said: not so — the consecration of substances [applies] to both subsidiary and principal, as has been explained. This derivation is made with the intention of stating [what follows].

children.text: nirdeśāt tu vikṛtāpūrvasyānadhikāraḥ // MS_3,8.31 //
children.translated_text: But because of the specification, what is unprecedented in the modification has no applicability. // MS 3,8.31 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ, yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*3/767*}. tatra śrūyate - barhiṣā yūpāvaṭam avastṛṇāty ājyena yūpam anaktīti. tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ tayor ājyabarhiṣor ājyabarhirdharmāḥ prākṛtāḥ kartavyāḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? kartavyā iti. kutaḥ? vākyaṃ hi barhirmātrasyājyamātrasya ca dharmāṇāṃ vidhāyakam, tad ihāpi vākyaṃ codakena prāptam. na caitad barhir ājyaṃ niṣprayojanam. tasmād atra dharmāḥ kiyerann iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - nirdeśād vikṛtāv apūrvasyānadhikāraḥ, nirdiṣṭā ete dharmāḥ prakṛtau, yatra pradhānasyopakurvanti prākṛtakāryayor ājyabarhiṣoḥ. ye ca pradhānasyopakāriṇo dharmāḥ, ta ihātidiśyante. pradhānaṃ hi codako 'pekṣate, na dharmān. pradhānasya hi codakena sāmānyaṃ na dharmāṇām.
api ca, nānyārtha iti jñātena saṃnihitenāpy ekavākyatā bhavaty anyasaṃbandhopapattau satyām, yathā bhāryā rājñaḥ, puruṣo devadattasyeti. kim aṅga punar viprakṛtena, nirjñātaṃ khalv aṅgatvaṃ pradhānāpekṣāyāṃ bhavati, kevalam ihātideśaḥ kriyate, padārthāpekṣāyām aṅgatvam api sādhayitavyaṃ syāt. dharmāś cāpekṣyamāṇāḥ sādhāraṇā bhaveyuḥ, tathoho nāvakalpeta. liṅgaviśeṣadarśanāc ca vyavatiṣṭheran dharmāḥ, tatra darśanaṃ nopapadyeta, vapayā prātaḥsavane caranti, puroḍāśena mādhyaṃdina iti, tathā na pitā vardhate, na mātā, na nābhiḥ, prāṇo hi sa iti. tasmād yad dvārā prakṛtau kṛtāḥ, tad dvāraiva vikṛtau, nānyadvārāḥ. na ca yūpāvaṭas taraṇaṃ prakṛtāv asti yūpāñjanaṃ [429]{*3/768*} vā. tasmān na tatra prākṛtā dharmā bhaveyur apūrvatvāt.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice]: 'one who is consecrated — when he slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.' There it is heard: 'he strews the <s>yūpa</s>-pit (<s>yūpāvaṭa</s>) with <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass); he anoints the <s>yūpa</s> with ghee.' There the doubt arises: should the archetypical <s>dharmas</s> of that ghee and <s>barhis</s> be performed, or not? What is the prima facie view? They should be performed. Why? For the [Vedic] statement is an enjoiner of the <s>dharmas</s> for <s>barhis</s> in general and ghee in general; here too the [Vedic] statement is obtained through the enjoiner. And this <s>barhis</s> and ghee are not without purpose. Therefore, their <s>dharmas</s> should be performed here.
Given this, we say: because of the specification, what is unprecedented in the modification has no applicability. These <s>dharmas</s> are specified in the archetype, where they benefit the principal through the archetypical <s>ājya</s> and <s>barhis</s>. And those <s>dharmas</s> that benefit the principal are extended here [to the modification]. For the enjoiner looks to the principal, not to the <s>dharmas</s>. The enjoiner has commonality with the principal, not with the <s>dharmas</s>.
Moreover, 'not for another purpose' — even with something known and proximate, single-sentence relationship is possible when there is a possibility of connection with another [entity], just as 'the wife of the king,' 'the man of <s>Devadatta</s>.' How much more so with something modified [from its original context]? For the subsidiary status is known with certainty only when the archetype is expected. Here, [in the modification,] only the extension (<s>atideśa</s>) is made; when the constituent elements are expected, the subsidiary status too would have to be established. And the <s>dharmas</s>, when expected, would be common [to all]; then the [Vedic statement] 'with the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) they act in the morning pressing, with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> in the midday pressing' would not be construable. And because of the observation of specific indicatory marks, the <s>dharmas</s> would be allocated; there, this observation would not be justified — [similarly,] 'the father does not grow, nor the mother, nor the navel; for it is the breath.' Therefore, the <s>dharmas</s> are [applied] through the same channel as they are applied in the archetype — through that same channel in the modification, not through another channel. And the <s>yūpa</s>-pit strewing and <s>yūpa</s>-anointing do not exist in the archetype. Therefore, the archetypical <s>dharmas</s> should not apply there, because of [their] being unprecedented.

children.text: virodhe ca śrutiviśeṣād avyaktaḥ śeṣe // MS_3,8.32 //
children.translated_text: In case of conflict, because of the specific <s>śruti</s>, [the source] is unspecified for the remainder. // MS 3,8.32 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor āmananti - samāvapracchinnāgrau darbhau prādeśamātrau pavitre karoti, tathā - aratnimātre vidhṛtī pavitre, utānyata iti. tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ vedistaraṇārthād barhiṣo vidhṛtī pavitre, utānyata iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? vedistaraṇārthād barhiṣaḥ kārye. kiṃ kāraṇam? tad dhi prakṛtam, dharmāś cāviśeṣāt sarvabarhiṣām arthena, tasmāt tataḥ. iti prāpte brūmaḥ - anyataḥ kriyeta. kutaḥ? virodhāt. kathaṃ virodhaḥ? śrūyate hi - tridhā tu pañcadhā tu vā vedīṃ stṛṇātīti, tad yenāstīryate, kathaṃ tad vidhṛtipavitraṃ kriyeta, na hi saṃbhavaty ekaṃ staraṇāya vidhṛtipavitrāya ca. tad etad upadiṣṭavacanam anekaguṇatvaṃ cobhe apy asaṃbhavinī pratijñāte syātām. tasmān na tataḥ kriyeteti. yadi na tataḥ, kutas tarhi? avyakta evaṃjātīyakaḥ śeṣe, asti tatra paribhojanīyaṃ nāma barhiḥ, tataḥ kartavyam.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> they teach: 'he makes purifying strainers (<s>pavitra</s>) from two blades of <s>darbha</s> grass with cut tips, a span in length'; similarly, 'the two purifying strainers [used as] supports (<s>vidhṛtī</s>) are a cubit in length, or from elsewhere.' There the doubt arises: are the supports and purifying strainers from the <s>barhis</s> intended for strewing the <s>vedi</s>, or from elsewhere? What is the prima facie view? They should be made from the <s>barhis</s> for <s>vedi</s>-strewing. What is the reason? For that is what is under discussion, and the <s>dharmas</s>, because of the non-distinction, [apply] to all <s>barhis</s> by their purpose. Therefore, [they are] from that. Given this, we say: they should be made from elsewhere. Why? Because of conflict. How is there conflict? For it is heard: 'he strews the <s>vedi</s> threefold or fivefold.' What is used for strewing — how could that be made into purifying-strainer supports? For it is not possible for one [set of grass] to serve both strewing and purifying-strainer [purposes]. Thus both the stated instruction and the multiplicity of qualities would be impossible promises. Therefore, they should not be made from that. If not from that, then from what? [The source is] unspecified — for such a remainder: there is something called '<s>paribhojanīya</s>' (for attendant use) <s>barhis</s>; it should be made from that.

children.text: apanayanas tv ekadeśasya vidyamānasaṃyogāt // MS_3,8.33 //
children.translated_text: But the removal is of a part, because of the connection with what is present. // MS 3,8.33 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - puroḍāśaśakalam aindravāyavasya pātre nidadhāti, dhānā āśvinapātre, payasyāṃ maitrāvaruṇapātra iti. tatra saṃśayaḥ - kim anyata eṣāṃ kriyeta, uta prakṛtebhya [430]{*3/769*} iti. kiṃ prāptam? pūrveṇa nyāyenānyata iti. tatrocyate - tata ekadeśasyāpanayaḥ. kutaḥ? vidyamānasaṃyogāt, vidyate hi tatra puroḍāśo dhānāḥ payasyā ca, tatsaṃyoga eva nyāyyo nānyasaṃyoga iti, puroḍāśādīnāṃ eva saṃskāraḥ, nendravāyavādīnām{*3/770*}. kutaḥ? puroḍāśādiṣu dvitīyādarśanāt. pratyakṣaś caikadeśāpanayenopakāraḥ, nendravāyavādisaṃbandhena{*3/771*}, evaṃ prakṛtānugraho bhaviṣyati, tasmāt prakṛtasyopadeśena tat kriyeta. na cātropadiṣṭopadeśa āśaṅkyo 'nekaguṇabhāvaś ca, anyena śakalena homo 'nyaś ca pratipādyata iti{*3/772*}.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'he places a piece of <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) in the <s>Aindrāvāyava</s> vessel; grain (<s>dhānā</s>) in the <s>Āśvina</s> vessel; curd (<s>payasyā</s>) in the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> vessel.' There the doubt arises: should these be made from elsewhere, or from the archetypical [offerings]? What is the prima facie view? By the previous principle, from elsewhere. To this it is said: the removal is of a part from those [archetypical offerings]. Why? Because of the connection with what is present — for the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, grain, and curd exist there [in the archetypical rite]; the connection with them alone is proper, not a connection with something else. The consecration is of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> and the others, not of the <s>Aindrāvāyava</s> and other [vessels]. Why? Because the accusative case is observed with respect to the <s>puroḍāśa</s> and others. And the benefit through partial removal is direct, not through a connection with the <s>Aindrāvāyava</s> and others. Thus there will be support of the archetype. Therefore, it should be done through the instruction of the archetype. And here, the suspicion of stated instruction and the multiplicity of qualities should not arise — for the oblation is performed with one piece, and another is set aside.
