children.text: vikṛtau sarvārthaḥ śeṣaḥ prakṛtivat // MS_3,8.34 //
children.translated_text: In the modification, the residual [rite serves] all purposes, as in the archetype. // MS 3,8.34 //

children.text: idam āmananti - yajñārthavaṇaṃ vai kāmyā iṣṭayaḥ, tā upāṃśu kartavyā iti. atra saṃśayaḥ - kim aṅgapradhānārtham upāṃśutvam, uta pradhānārtham iti. kiṃ prāptam? vikṛtau sarvārthaḥ śeṣaḥ syāt, aviśeṣād aṅgānāṃ pradhānānāṃ ca prakṛtivat, yathā prakṛtau vedidharmā ājyadharmāś cāṅgapradhānārthāḥ, evam atrāpi.
children.translated_text: This is taught: 'the optional sacrifices (<s>kāmyā iṣṭayaḥ</s>) are for the purpose of the sacrifice; they should be performed in a low voice (<s>upāṃśu</s>).' Here the doubt arises: is the low-voice quality for the purpose of both subsidiary and principal [rites], or for the principal alone? What is the prima facie view? In the modification, the residual [rite should serve] all purposes, because of the non-distinction of subsidiary and principal — as in the archetype, where <s>vedi</s>-rites and ghee-rites serve both subsidiary and principal, so too here.

children.text: mukhyārtho vāṅgasyācoditatvāt // MS_3,8.35 //
children.translated_text: Or [the low-voice quality] is for the primary [rite], because the subsidiary is not enjoined [separately]. // MS 3,8.35 //

children.text: pradhānārtho vā eṣa vikṛtiṣu syāt. evam idaṃ sarvārtham ucyeta, prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā vākyenāṅga-pradhānārtham iti, tad evedānīṃ vākyaṃ viśeṣitam - kāmyā iṣṭaya iti. kāmyāś ca pradhānayāgāḥ, aṅgayāgāḥ pradhānārthāḥ, tasmād aṅgacoditam. yat kāmena phalavac codyate, tad evānayopāṃśutvetikartavyatayā [431]{*3/773*} anubadhyate. tasmāt pradhānārtham upāṃśutvam.
children.translated_text: Or this [low-voice quality] in the modifications should be for the principal alone. This [previous view] said 'for all purposes,' [arguing that] the [Vedic] statement overrides the context — [it is] for both subsidiary and principal. But now that very [Vedic] statement has been qualified: 'optional sacrifices' — and the optional [sacrifices] are the principal rites; the subsidiary rites are for the purpose of the principal. Therefore, [the low-voice quality is] enjoined for the principal. What is prompted by desire and has a result — that alone is followed by this <s>upāṃśu</s> (low-voice) mode as a procedural requirement. Therefore, the low-voice quality is for the principal [rite].

children.text: saṃnidhānaviśeṣād asaṃbhave tadaṅgānām // MS_3,8.36 //
children.translated_text: Because of the specific proximity, when [it is] impossible, [the rule applies to] the subsidiaries of that [principal rite]. // MS 3,8.36 //

children.text: śyene śrūyate - dṛtanavanītam{*3/774*} ājyam iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ navanītaṃ pradhānasya, utāṅgānām iti. kiṃ prāptam? pradhānasya, tasya hi prakaraṇam iti vacanaprāmāṇyān navanītena pradhānaṃ nirvartayitavyam iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - asaṃbhava etasmiṃs tadaṅgānāṃ śyenāṅgānāṃ{*3/775*} syāt. kathaṃ asaṃbhavaḥ? somadravyakatvāt pradhānasya. nanu vacanān navanītaṃ bhaviṣyati. na śyene navanītaṃ bhavatīty eṣa vākyārthaḥ. kas tarhi? śyene navanītam ājyaṃ bhavatīti navanītājyasaṃbandho vidhīyate, śyenājyasaṃbandho 'nūdyate. na ca sākṣāc chyenasyājyasaṃbandho 'sti, śyenāṅgānāṃ tu vidyate. yasyāsti, tasyānūdya navanītaṃ vidhīyate, saṃnidhānaviśeṣāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śyena</s> (hawk-shaped rite) it is heard: 'the ghee is [made from] fresh butter from a skin-bag.' There a doubt [arises]: is the fresh butter for the principal [offering], or for the subsidiaries? What is the prima facie view? For the principal, since that is what is under discussion — therefore, by the authority of the [Vedic] statement, the principal should be accomplished with fresh butter. Given this, we say: there being impossibility in this [case], it should be for the subsidiaries, the subsidiary parts of the <s>Śyena</s>. How is there impossibility? Because the principal requires <s>Soma</s> as its substance. But would not the fresh butter apply because of [Vedic] statement? No — 'in the <s>Śyena</s>, fresh butter is the ghee' — this is the sentence-meaning. It is not that 'in the <s>Śyena</s> there is fresh butter [as the principal offering].' What then? 'In the <s>Śyena</s>, fresh butter becomes the ghee' — thus the connection of fresh butter with ghee is enjoined, while the connection of the <s>Śyena</s> with ghee is [merely] restated. And there is no direct connection of the <s>Śyena</s> [principal] with ghee, but there is [such connection] for the subsidiary parts of the <s>Śyena</s>. For whichever [rite] has [such a connection], for that, having restated [the connection], fresh butter is enjoined, because of the specific proximity.

children.text: ādhāne 'pi tatheti cet // MS_3,8.37 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] likewise in the case of the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>) — // MS 3,8.37 //

children.text: evaṃ ced dṛśyate - śyenāṅgānāṃ navanītam iti, ādhāne 'pi pavamāneṣṭiṣu syāt. tā api hi śyenasyopakurvanti, tatsaṃskṛte 'gnau śyeno nirvartata iti.
children.translated_text: If this is how it is seen — that fresh butter is for the subsidiary parts of the <s>Śyena</s> — then it should also apply to the <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> in the fire-establishment. For they too assist the <s>Śyena</s>, since the <s>Śyena</s> is accomplished in the fire consecrated by them.

children.text: nāprakaraṇatvād aṅgasya tannimittatvāt // MS_3,8.38 //
children.translated_text: No, because of not being in the topic, [and] because the subsidiary is occasioned by that [topic]. // MS 3,8.38 //

children.text: na śyenasya prakaraṇe pavamāneṣṭayo 'gnyādhānaṃ vā śrūyate. kim ataḥ? yady evam, ādhānasya ca śyenasya ca na kaścid asti [432]{*3/776*} saṃbandhaḥ, agnīnām ādhānam, agnayaś ca śyenasya, tasmān na pavamānahaviḥṣu navanītam. naitac chyenāṅgatve nimittam, yad ādhānam agnīnām upakaroti. yadi prakaraṇādīnām anyatamad{*3/777*} asti, tan nimittaṃ bhavet. tasmān na śyenāgnyādhānayoḥ saṃbandho 'stīti.
children.translated_text: The <s>Pavamāneṣṭis</s> or fire-establishment are not heard in the topic of the <s>Śyena</s>. What follows from this? If so, there is no connection whatsoever between the fire-establishment and the <s>Śyena</s> — the fire-establishment is of the fires, and the fires are [used in] the <s>Śyena</s>; therefore there is no fresh butter in the <s>Pavamāna</s> offerings. The fact that the fire-establishment assists the fires is not the ground for [its being] a subsidiary of the <s>Śyena</s>. If there were some [connection through] topic or similar [criteria], that would be the ground. Therefore there is no connection between the <s>Śyena</s> and the fire-establishment.

children.text: tatkāle vā liṅgadarśanāt // MS_3,8.39 //
children.translated_text: Or [the fresh butter is] at that time, because of the observation of an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // MS 3,8.39 //

children.text: idam idānīṃ saṃdihyate - kiṃ sutyākālānām aṅgānāṃ navanītam uta sarveṣāṃ iti. sutyākālānāṃ syāt, liṅgadarśanāt. idaṃ śrūyate - saha paśūn ālabhata iti. tatra punar vacanam - agnīṣomīyasya sthāne 'gnīṣomīyaḥ puroḍāśaḥ, anubandhyāyāḥ sthāne maitrāvaruṇīyasyeti{*3/778*}, dve sthāne śrūnye{*3/779*} darśayati, tenāvagamyate śyenasya vacanaṃ sutyākālānām aṅgānāṃ viśeṣaṃ vidadhātīti.
children.translated_text: Now this is doubted: is the fresh butter for the subsidiary parts at the pressing-day (<s>sutyā</s>) time [only], or for all [subsidiaries]? It should be for those at the pressing-day time, because of the observation of an indicatory mark. This is heard: 'he slaughters the animals together.' There is a further statement: 'in place of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal] there is an <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> cake; in place of the <s>Anubandhyā</s> [cow] there is the <s>Maitrāvaruṇīya</s>' — it shows two empty places, and by this it is understood that the statement regarding the <s>Śyena</s> prescribes a distinction for the subsidiary parts at the pressing-day time.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vāviśeṣāt // MS_3,8.40 //
children.translated_text: Or for all, because of non-distinction. // MS 3,8.40 //

children.text: sarveṣām eva cāṅgānāṃ navanītaṃ syāt. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, asati viśeṣe sarveṣām apy aṅgānām iti.
children.translated_text: The fresh butter should be for all subsidiary parts indeed. Why? Because of non-distinction — in the absence of a distinction, [it applies] to all subsidiary parts.

children.text: nyāyokte liṅgadarśanam // MS_3,8.41 //
children.translated_text: The observation of the indicatory mark is [valid only when] stated by proper reasoning. // MS 3,8.41 //

children.text: yad uktaṃ liṅgam, tat pariharaṇīyam. nāsti tāvat pramāṇam, yac chyenasya vacanaṃ tat stutyākālānām{*3/780*} aṅgānām iti. kiṃ tu darśanam? tad apramāṇamūlatvān mithyādarśanaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇāvat. kathaṃ tu madhye paśūnām ālambha iti. nyāyāt. ko nyāyaḥ? kramānugrahaḥ. evaṃ vacanavarjitaḥ kramo 'nugṛhīto bhavatīti{*3/781*}. [433]{*3/782*} tasmāt sarveṣām aṅgānāṃ navanītam iti.
children.translated_text: As for the indicatory mark that was stated, it must be refuted. There is no valid evidence that the statement regarding the <s>Śyena</s> is [restricted to] subsidiary parts at the pressing-day time. What then is the observation? That is a false observation, baseless in valid evidence, like a mirage. But how then [is there] slaughter of animals in the middle? By proper reasoning. What is the proper reasoning? Sequential accommodation. Thus the sequence, being without [specific Vedic] statement, is accommodated. Therefore the fresh butter is for all subsidiary parts.

children.text: māṃsaṃ tu savanīyānāṃ codanāviśeṣāt // MS_3,8.42 //
children.translated_text: But flesh [is used] for the pressing-day [offerings], because of non-distinction in the injunction. // MS 3,8.42 //

children.text: śākyānām ayanaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśatsaṃvatsaram. tatredaṃ samāmananti - saṃsthite saṃsthite 'hāni gṛhapatir mṛgayāṃ yāti, sa tatra yān mṛgān hanti, teṣāṃ tarasāḥ puruḍāśāḥ savanīyā bhavantīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ savanīyānām anyeṣāṃ ca saṃbhavatāṃ puroḍāśānāṃ sthāne tarasā uta savanīyānām eveti. kiṃ prāptam? sarvapuroḍāśānāṃ māṃsamayatā syāt, na śakyate puroḍāśānāṃ ca māṃsamayatā vidhātum, savanīyaśabdena ca puroḍāśān viśeṣayitum, bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. tasmāt sarvapuroḍāśānāṃ māṃsamayateti. iti{*3/783*} prāpte ucyate - māṃsaṃ tu savanīyānāṃ syāt, tarasāḥ savanīyā bhavantīty ayaṃ tv anūdyate. kuta etat? sarvapuroḍāśeṣu savanīyaśabdo 'nuvādo na ghaṭate, puroḍāśaśabdas tu savanīyeṣv avakalpate. tasmāt puroḍāśaśabdo 'nuvāda iti. tasmāt savanīyānāṃ dhānādīnāṃ sthāne māṃsaṃ codanāśeṣād iti.
children.translated_text: The <s>Śākyas</s> have a sacrificial session (<s>ayana</s>) of thirty-six years. There they teach: 'at the conclusion of each [sub-session], the householder goes on a hunt for [several] days; whatever deer he kills there, from their [flesh] the cakes become the pressing-day [offerings].' There a doubt [arises]: should flesh replace the cakes of all [offerings] that can be [so replaced], including both pressing-day and others, or only the pressing-day [offerings]? What is the prima facie view? All cakes should be made of flesh — it is not possible both to enjoin that cakes be made of flesh and to restrict [them] to pressing-day [offerings] with the word 'pressing-day,' for the sentence would be split thereby. Therefore all cakes are made of flesh. Given this, we say: but flesh should be for the pressing-day [offerings only] — 'the [flesh-]cakes become pressing-day [offerings]' is [merely] restated. How is this known? The word 'pressing-day' cannot be a restatement in relation to all cakes, but the word 'cake' fits well in relation to pressing-day [offerings]. Therefore the word 'cake' is the restatement. Therefore, in place of grain and similar [materials] for the pressing-day [offerings], flesh [is used], because of the remainder of the injunction.

children.text: bhaktir asaṃnidhāv anyāyyeti cet // MS_3,8.43 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] the secondary usage (<s>bhakti</s>) is improper in the absence of proximity — // MS 3,8.43 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi - savanīyeṣu puroḍāśaśabdo 'nuvādo bhaviṣyatīti, dhānādiṣu puroḍāśaśabdo na vartate, bhaktiś cānyāyyā mukhye saṃbhavati.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that the word 'cake' will be a restatement in relation to pressing-day [offerings] — [the objection is that] the word 'cake' does not apply to grains and such, and secondary usage is improper when the primary [meaning] is possible.

children.text: syāt prakṛtiliṅgatvād vairājavat // MS_3,8.44 //
children.translated_text: It should be [a secondary usage] because of being an indicatory mark of the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), like the <s>Vairāja</s> [case]. // MS 3,8.44 //

children.text: prakṛtau jyotiṣṭome dhānādiṣv ayaṃ puroḍāśaśabdo bhāktaḥ, saṃnihite{*3/785*} prayuktaḥ, ihāpi bhākta eva prayokṣyate. atrāpi hi savanīyaśabdena te saṃnihitāḥ. prakṛtau liṅgasamavāyāc chabdapravṛttir vikṛtāv api tathaiva, yathā - chatriṇo gacchanti, dhvajino gacchantīti. yathā - ukthyo vairūpasāmā, ekaviṃśaḥ poḍaśī vairājasāmā iti prakṛtiliṅgena sāmaśabdena vairūpapṛṣṭho vairājapṛṣṭha iti gamyate. evam ihāpi savanīyānāṃ māṃsamayateti.
children.translated_text: In the archetype, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, this word 'cake' is used secondarily (<s>bhākta</s>) in relation to grains and such, employed in proximity [to them]; here too it will be employed as a secondary usage. For here too, through the word 'pressing-day,' those [grains] are in proximity. The application of the word occurs in the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) just as in the archetype, due to the co-occurrence of the indicatory mark in the archetype — just as 'the umbrella-bearers go' and 'the flag-bearers go.' Just as: 'the <s>Ukthya</s> [rite] has the <s>Vairūpa Sāman</s>; the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> sixteen-fold [rite] has the <s>Vairāja Sāman</s>' — through the word '<s>Sāman</s>' which is an indicatory mark of the archetype, it is understood as '<s>Vairūpa</s>-backed' and '<s>Vairāja</s>-backed.' Similarly here too, flesh is [used] for the pressing-day [offerings].

children.text: Adhyāya 4:
children.translated_text: <s>Adhyāya</s> 4:
Page break marker: 435

children.text: athātaḥ kratvarthapuruṣārthayor jijñāsā // MS_4,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Now, therefore, [there is] an inquiry into what serves the ritual purpose (<s>kratvarthа</s>) and what serves the person's purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). // MS 4,1.1 //

children.text: tṛtīye 'dhyāye śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānaiḥ śeṣaviniyogalakṣaṇam uktam. ihedānīṃ kratvarthapuruṣārthau jijñāsyete, kaḥ kratvarthaḥ, kaḥ puruṣārtha iti, yāpi prayojakāprayojakaphalavidhyarthavādāṅgapradhānacintā, sāpi kratvarthapuruṣārthajijñāsaiva. katham? aṅgaṃ kratvarthaḥ, pradhānaṃ puruṣārthaḥ. phalavidhiḥ puruṣārthaḥ, arthavādaḥ kratvarthaḥ. prayojakaḥ kaścit puruṣārtho 'prayojakaḥ kratvarthaḥ. tasmāt kratvarthapuruṣārthayor jijñāseti sūtritam. tatrāthātaḥ śabdau prathama evādhyāye prathamasūtre varṇitau. atheti prakṛtaṃ{*4/2*} śeṣaviniyogalakṣaṇam apekṣate. ata iti kratvarthapuruṣārthajijñāsāviśeṣaṃ prakurute. kratave yaḥ sa kratvarthaḥ, puruṣāya yaḥ sa puruṣārthaḥ. jijñāsāśabdo 'pi tatraiva samadhigataḥ - jñātum icchā jijñāseti. tad etat pratijñāsūtram, kratvarthapuruṣārthayor jijñāseti.
children.translated_text: In the third <s>Adhyāya</s>, the characteristic of subsidiary-allocation through <s>śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (topic), <s>sthāna</s> (position), and <s>samākhyā</s> (designation) was stated. Now here, the ritual-purpose and person-purpose are to be investigated — what is ritual-purpose and what is person-purpose — and the examination of motivating and non-motivating, result-prescribing and <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage), subsidiary and principal — that too is precisely the inquiry into ritual-purpose and person-purpose. How so? A subsidiary is ritual-purpose; the principal is person-purpose. A result-prescribing [statement] is person-purpose; an <s>arthavāda</s> is ritual-purpose. The motivating is sometimes person-purpose; the non-motivating is ritual-purpose. Therefore it is formulated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'inquiry into ritual-purpose and person-purpose.' There, the words <s>atha</s> ('now') and <s>ataḥ</s> ('therefore') were explained in the very first <s>sūtra</s> of the first <s>Adhyāya</s>. <s>Atha</s> ('now') refers back to the preceding subsidiary-allocation characteristic. <s>Ataḥ</s> ('therefore') introduces the specific [inquiry into] ritual-purpose and person-purpose. That which is for the ritual (<s>kratu</s>) is ritual-purpose; that which is for the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is person-purpose. The word <s>jijñāsā</s> (inquiry) was also explained there — 'the desire to know is <s>jijñāsā</s>.' This is the thesis-<s>sūtra</s>: 'inquiry into ritual-purpose and person-purpose.'

children.text: yasmin prītiḥ puruṣasya tasya lipsārthalakṣaṇāvibhaktavāt // MS_4,1.2 //
children.translated_text: That in which the person takes delight — its characteristic is [that it is] desired, because [the injunction] is undivided. // MS 4,1.2 //

children.text: atha{*4/3*} kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ kratvarthaḥ, kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārtha iti lakṣaṇaṃ [436]{*4/4*} vācyam, tathā hi laghīyasī pratipattiḥ, pṛṣṭākoṭenopadeśe garīyasī. tad ucyate - yasmin prītiḥ puruṣasya, yasmin kṛte padārthe puruṣasya prītir bhavati{*4/5*} sa puruṣārthaḥ padārthaḥ. kutaḥ? tasya lipsārthena ca bhavati{*4/6*}, na śāstreṇa, kratvartho hi śāstrād avagamyate, nānyathā. avibhakto hi puruṣārthaḥ prītyā. yo yaḥ prītisādhanaḥ sa puruṣārthaḥ. puruṣārthe lakṣite tadviparītaḥ kratvartha iti kratvarthasya lakṣaṇaṃ siddham.
children.translated_text: Now, what is the characteristic of ritual-purpose, and what is the characteristic of person-purpose? The characteristic must be stated, for thus the understanding is easier; instruction given without being asked is more [burdensome]. This is stated: that in which the person takes delight — that substance in which, when accomplished, the person's delight arises — that substance is person-purpose. Why? Because of its being desired by him — and [the desire] arises [not] from scripture but [from delight]; ritual-purpose, on the other hand, is known from scripture alone, not otherwise. For person-purpose is undivided from delight — whatever is a means of delight is person-purpose. Once person-purpose is characterized, what is opposite to it is ritual-purpose — thus the characteristic of ritual-purpose is established.

children.text:
evaṃ vā sūtraṃ varṇyate - darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnāyate - anatidṛśyaṃ stṛṇāti, anatidṛśyam evainaṃ prajayā paśubhiḥ karotīti{*4/7*}, tathā - āhāryapurīṣāṃ paśukāmasya vediṃ kuryāt, vatsajānuṃ paśukāmasya vedaṃ kuryāt, godohanena paśukāmasya praṇayed ityevamādīni. tatra saṃśayaḥ - kim evaṃjātīyakāḥ kratvarthā uta puruṣārthā iti. kiṃ prāptam? kratvartha iti. kutaḥ? pratyakṣa upakāras tebhyo dṛśyate kratoḥ, purīṣaharaṇaṃ vedistaraṇaṃ ca, tad uktam - dravyaguṇasaṃskāreṣu bādarir{*4/8*} iti{*4/9*}. tasmāt kratvarthā ity evaṃ prāptam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - yasmin prītiḥ puruṣasya sa puruṣārtha eveti, prītis tebhyo nirvartate, tasmād ete puruṣārthā iti. nanu pratyakṣa upakāraḥ krator dṛśyata ity uktam. ucyate - satyaṃ dṛśyate, na tu krator upakārāyaibhyaḥ{*4/10*} saṃkīrti tebhyaḥ, phalebhya ete śrūyante. na ca, ya upakaroti sa śeṣaḥ. yas tu yadarthaḥ śrūyate, sa tasya śeṣa ity uktam{*4/11*} - śeṣaḥ parārthatvād iti{*4/12*}.
children.translated_text:
Or the <s>sūtra</s> is explained thus: in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is taught: 'he strews [grass] that is not excessively visible; he makes him not excessively visible through offspring and cattle' — likewise: 'one should make the altar with transported soil for one desiring cattle; one should make the altar calf-knee-high for one desiring cattle; one should lead out with cow-milking for one desiring cattle' — and similar [injunctions]. There a doubt [arises]: are such things ritual-purpose or person-purpose? What is the prima facie view? They are ritual-purpose. Why? Because a direct benefit to the ritual is seen from them — carrying soil and strewing the altar — as stated: '<s>Bādari</s> [holds that subsidiaries] serve substance, quality, and consecration.' Therefore they are ritual-purpose — this is the prima facie view.
Given this, we say: that in which the person takes delight is person-purpose indeed — delight arises from them, therefore they are person-purpose. But was it not stated that a direct benefit to the ritual is seen? We reply: true, it is seen, but these are not heard as benefiting the ritual — they are not designated as [serving] the ritual but are heard with [reference to] results. And it is not the case that one who assists is a subsidiary; rather, one who is heard as having [another] as its purpose is a subsidiary of that — as was stated: 'a subsidiary is [defined] by being for another's purpose.' There, the word referring to oneself does not fit [the ritual]; but when construed with the person, it is non-figurative. Therefore they are person-purpose.

children.text:
evaṃ vā, dravyārjanam udāharaṇam. iha dravyārjanaṃ tais tair niyamaiḥ [437]{*4/13*} śrūyate, brāhmaṇasya pratigrahādinā, rājanyasya jayādinā, vaiśyasya kṛṣyādinā. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ kratvartho dravyaparigraha uta puruṣārtha iti. kiṃ prāptam? kratvartho niyamāt. yady eṣa puruṣārthaḥ syāt, niyamo 'narthako bhavet. pratyakṣeṇaitad avagamyate, niyamād aniyamāc cārjitaṃ dravyaṃ puruṣaṃ prīṇayatīti. tasmāt kratvarthaḥ. kāmaśrutibhiś cāsya sahaikavākyatā dṛṣṭā. itarathā, anumeyena phalavākyena sahaikavākyatāṃ yāyāt. liṅgaṃ cāpi bhavati - agnaye kṣāmavate puroḍāśam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet, yasyāhitāgneḥ sato 'gnir gṛhān dahet{*4/14*}, yasya hiraṇyaṃ naśyed āgneyādīni nirvaped{*4/15*} ityevamādi. tad dhi dravyopaghāte codyate, yadi dravyaparigrahaḥ karmārthaḥ, tata etad api sati saṃbandhe karmārtham ity ucyate, itararthāsati saṃbandhe karmārtham ity anumīyate, phalaṃ cāsya kalpyeta. tasmād yajatiśrutigṛhītaṃ dravyārjanaṃ yena vinā yogo na nirvartate, sa yāgasya śrutyā parigṛhīta iti gamyate. tasmāt kratvartha iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - puruṣārtha iti. etasmin kṛte padārthe prītiḥ puruṣasya bhavati, tasmād asya lipsārthalakṣaṇā śarīradhāraṇārthā, yasya śarīraṃ dhriyate, vyaktaṃ tasyāsti dravyam. śarīriṇaś ca
yāgaḥ śrūyate, tasmād vidyamānadravyasya viniyoga ucyate. na dravyārjanaṃ śrutigṛhītam{*4/16*}, vināpi hi dravyārjanavacanatvena śabdasya, yāgo nirvartata eva, tasmāt puruṣārtho dravyaparigrahaḥ.
api ca, yadi śāstrāt karmārthaṃ dravyārjanam, tan nānyatra viniyujyeta tathārjitam, tatra sarvatantraparilopaḥ syāt. api ca, upakrāntāni sarvakarmāṇi dravyārjanena bhaveyuḥ, tatraitan nopapadyate. api vā eṣa suvargāl{*4/17*} lokācchidyate, yo darśapūrṇamāsayājī [438]{*4/18*} sann amāvāsyāṃ vā paurṇamāsīṃ vātipātayed{*4/19*} iti. evaṃ ca sati, prayogakālād vahir{*4/20*} etad aṅgaṃ sad anupakārakaṃ syāt. na ca, ādhānavad bhavitum arhati, tatra hi vacanam - vasante 'gnim ādadhīteti, na caitad aṅgam.
atha yad uktam - niyamavacanam anarthakam, puruṣārthe dravyaparigrahe satīti. ucyate, naitāvatā puruṣārthatā vyāvartate. pratyakṣā hi sā, tvayā ca parokṣaṃ yuktibuddhyā vyapadiśyate, na ca, parokṣaṃ pratyakṣasya bādhakaṃ bhavati. tasmān niyamavacanāt kāmam aparam adṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta, na tu dṛṣṭahānam. tasmād yat puruṣasya prayojanaṃ prītiḥ, tad arthaṃ dhanasyārjanam ity evaṃ ca sati, vrīhiṇā yāgaḥ kartavyaḥ, prītyartham arjitena vā kratvartham arjitena vā, nātra kaścid viśeṣaḥ.
prītyartham upārjito 'pi vrīhiḥ, vrīhir eva, karmārtham upārjito 'pi vrīhiḥ, vrīhir eva. tasmān{*4/21*} na prayogacodanāgṛhītaṃ dravyārjanam.
atha yad uktam, anumeyenāprakṛtena vā śabdena yuṣmatpakṣe niyamasyaikavākyatā, asmatpakṣe tu dṛṣṭena prayogavacaneneti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, asmatpakṣe 'pi dṛṣṭena bhujinā, na phalavacanena. kathaṃ tarhi? niyamād adṛṣṭaṃ bhavatīti gamyate. yathaiva bhavadīye pakṣe. āha, asmatpakṣe phalavata ekavākyabhāvāt{*4/22*} phalavata upakarotīti gamyate. ucyate, asmatpakṣe 'pi phalavata evaikavākyabhāvaḥ{*4/23*}, etāvāṃs tu viśeṣaḥ, tava śrutaṃ phalam, mama tu dṛṣṭam iti.
atha yal liṅgam uktam - gṛhadāhādiṣu karma śrūyata iti. tatrocyate, yady api na kratvarthaṃ dravyārjanam, tathāpi dāhe nimitte phalāya vā karmāṅgabhāvāya vā jāmavatyādīnāṃ{*4/24*} vidhānam upapadyata eva. tasmāt puruṣārthaṃ dravyārjanam, prītyā hi tadavibhaktam iti.
children.translated_text:
Alternatively, the acquisition of wealth is the example. Here, the acquisition of wealth is heard [as prescribed] with various restrictions: for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through receiving gifts and the like, for the <s>Kṣatriya</s> through conquest and the like, for the <s>Vaiśya</s> through agriculture and the like. There the doubt [arises]: is the acquisition of wealth for the sake of ritual (<s>kratvartha</s>) or for human benefit (<s>puruṣārtha</s>)? What is the prima facie view? It is for the sake of ritual, because of the restriction. If it were for human benefit, the restriction would be purposeless. For it is perceived directly that wealth acquired — whether with restriction or without restriction — pleases the person. Therefore [it is] for the sake of ritual. And its single-sentence relationship (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) with desire-statements (<s>kāmaśruti</s>) is observed. Otherwise, it would form a single-sentence relationship with an inferred result-statement. And there is also indicative evidence (<s>liṅga</s>): 'To <s>Agni Kṣāmavat</s> one should offer a cake on eight potsherds — for one whose established fires burn down his houses'; 'for one whose gold is lost, one should offer the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [oblations]' — and so forth. For that [remedy] is enjoined when wealth is damaged. If the acquisition of wealth is for the sake of ritual, then this too, when there is a connection, is said to be for the sake of ritual; when it is for another purpose and there is no connection, it is inferred as being for the sake of ritual, and a result would have to be postulated for it. Therefore, the acquisition of wealth grasped by the <s>yajati</s>-statement, without which the ritual performance (<s>yoga</s>) cannot be accomplished — that is understood as grasped by the injunction of the sacrifice. Therefore [it is] for the sake of ritual.
Given this, we say: [it is] for human benefit (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). When this object is accomplished, pleasure arises for the person; therefore its characteristic is the desire for acquisition, [serving] the purpose of sustaining the body. One whose body is sustained — clearly he has wealth. And sacrifice is heard [as enjoined] for the embodied being; therefore the employment [in ritual] is stated for one who [already] possesses wealth. The acquisition of wealth is not grasped by scripture — for even without the word being a statement about wealth-acquisition, the sacrifice is accomplished just the same. Therefore the acquisition of wealth is for human benefit.
Moreover, if the acquisition of wealth were for the sake of ritual by scriptural [injunction], then wealth so acquired could not be employed elsewhere; in that case, there would be a collapse of the entire system. Moreover, all rituals would have to begin with wealth-acquisition, and that is untenable. Or [consider]: 'he is cut off from the heavenly world who, being a performer of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, should let the new-moon or full-moon day pass [without performing].' This being so, this subsidiary, being outside the time of performance, would be unhelpful. Nor can it be like the establishment of the sacred fires (<s>ādhāna</s>), for there is a [specific] statement: 'in spring one should establish the fires' — and that is not a subsidiary.
Now, as for what was said — 'the restrictive statement would be purposeless if the acquisition of wealth were for human benefit' — we reply: this much does not negate [its being for] human benefit. For that [human benefit] is directly perceived, whereas you posit [your view] indirectly through reasoning. And the indirect cannot override the direct. Therefore, from the restrictive statement, let some other unseen [result] be postulated, but not the abandonment of what is [directly] seen. Therefore, since the person's purpose is pleasure, the acquisition of wealth is for that purpose. And this being so, whether the sacrifice is to be performed with rice acquired for the sake of pleasure or with rice acquired for the sake of ritual — there is no difference here.
Rice acquired for pleasure is still rice; rice acquired for ritual purposes is still rice. Therefore the acquisition of wealth is not grasped by the ritual-performance injunction.
Now, as for what was said — 'in your view, the single-sentence relationship of the restriction is with an inferred or non-contextual statement, while in our view it is with the directly seen performance-statement' — this is not a defect. In our view too, [the relationship is] with what is directly seen — the enjoyer (<s>bhujin</s>), not with the result-statement. How then? From the restriction, an unseen [result] is understood to arise — just as in your view. [The opponent] says: in our view, because of the single-sentence relationship with what has a result, it is understood to serve what has a result. We reply: in our view too, the single-sentence relationship is with what has a result; this much is the difference — your result is heard [from scripture], while mine is seen [directly].
Now, as for the indicative evidence cited — 'in the cases of house-burning and the like, ritual is heard' — to that we say: even if the acquisition of wealth is not for the sake of ritual, still, when fire [destroying the house] is the occasion, the injunction of [rites like] the <s>Jāmavatī</s> and others is appropriate — whether for a result or as a subsidiary of ritual. Therefore the acquisition of wealth is for human benefit, for it is inseparable from pleasure.

children.text: tadutsarge karmāṇi puruṣārthāya, śāstrasyānatiśaṅkyatvān na ca dravyaṃ vikīrṣyate{*4/26*} tenārthenābhisaṃbandhāt kriyāyāṃ puruṣaśrutiḥ // MS_4,1.3 //
children.translated_text: When that [wealth] is relinquished, the ritual acts are for human benefit (<s>puruṣārtha</s>); because the scripture is not to be doubted, and wealth is not [itself] desired to be distributed — because of the connection with that purpose, the person is heard [as the beneficiary] in the ritual action. // MS 4,1.3 //

children.text:
iha prajāpativratāny udāharaṇam - nodyantam ādityam īkṣeta nāstaṃyantam ityādīni. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ kratvarthāni prajāpativratāny uta puruṣārthānīti. kiṃ prāptam? kratvarthānīti. kutaḥ? evaṃ hi, phalaṃ na kalpayitavyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. nanu śrūyata evaiteṣāṃ phalam, etāvatā hainasāyukto bhavatīti. ucyate - naitat phalaparaṃ vacanam, vartamānāpadeśa evaiṣa śabda iti. tena yatrāditya īkṣitavyaḥ prāptaḥ, tatrāyaṃ pratiṣedha udyato 'staṃyataś ca niyamo vā syāt kaścit karmāṅgabhūtaḥ.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tad utsarge prītyutsargo 'pi{*4/27*}, karmāṇi puruṣārthāya bhaveyuḥ, evaṃjātīyakāni. kartur etāny upadiśyante, na karmaṇaḥ. arthaprāptena kartrā saṃbandho yaḥ, sa vidhitsitaḥ, na karmasaṃbandho 'vidyamāna eva. śāstraṃ cānatiśaṅkyaṃ pitṛmātṛvacanād api pramāṇataram, svayaṃ hi tena pratyeti, indriyasthānīyaṃ hi tat. na caivam ādibhir dravyasya kaścid dṛṣṭa upakāraḥ sādhyate. tasmāt tena puruṣārthenābhisaṃyogāt kriyāyām evaṃjātīyakāyāṃ puruṣaḥ śrūyate.
api ca, puruṣaprayatnaḥ padārthavidhimātraṃ lakṣayitum uccāryeta, svayam avivakṣitaḥ syāt.
atha yad uktam - yatrādityasyekṣaṇaṃ prāptam, tatrodyato 'staṃyataś ca partiṣedha iti, satyaṃ pratiṣedho nyāyyaḥ, tathā śrutir anugahyeta{*4/28*}, [440]{*4/29*} itarathā niyamo lakṣyeteti. kiṃ tv iha niyamaḥ śabdena śrūyate, tasya vratam iti, tena niyama eṣaḥ, nodyann āditya īkṣitavya iti. api ca, etāvatā hainasāyukto bhavatīti puruṣasaṃbaddho doṣaḥ kīrtyate, na karmasaṃbaddhaḥ. tasmāt puruṣārthāni prajāpativratānīti. golakṣaṇāny apy evam eva kartarīkarṇyaḥ kartavyā ityevamādīni.
children.translated_text:
Here the <s>Prajāpati-vratas</s> (observances of <s>Prajāpati</s>) are the example — 'One should not look at the rising sun, nor at the setting [sun]' — and so forth. There the doubt [arises]: are the <s>Prajāpati-vratas</s> for the sake of ritual or for human benefit? What is the prima facie view? They are for the sake of ritual. Why? For thus, no result would need to be postulated. But is not the result of these heard directly — 'by this much one becomes burdened with sin'? We reply: that statement is not result-oriented; this word is merely a description of the present state. Therefore, where looking at the sun is prescribed, there this prohibition — of [looking when it is] rising or setting — would be a restriction, [being] some subsidiary of ritual.
Given this, we say: when that [wealth] is relinquished — 'relinquishment' here means 'relinquishment of pleasure' — the ritual acts would be for human benefit, [meaning] of this kind. These are taught to the agent, not [as subsidiaries] of the ritual action. The connection with the agent that is obtained naturally is what is intended to be enjoined, not the connection with ritual which does not [naturally] exist. And the scripture is not to be doubted — [it is] more authoritative than even the words of father and mother, for one directly comprehends through it; it stands in the place of sense-perception. And no visible benefit to wealth is accomplished by [observances] of this kind. Therefore, because of the connection with that human purpose, the person is heard [as the beneficiary] in ritual action of this kind.
Moreover, the person's effort would be uttered merely to indicate the injunction of an object, [itself] being unintended.
Now, as for what was said — 'where looking at the sun is prescribed, there the prohibition of [looking when it is] rising or setting [applies]' — true, the prohibition is reasonable; thus the scripture would be upheld. Otherwise a restriction would be implied. But here the restriction is heard by the word — 'his observance' (<s>tasya vratam</s>); therefore this is a restriction: 'one should look at the sun [only when it is] not rising [or setting].' Moreover, 'by this much one becomes burdened with sin' — a fault connected with the person is mentioned, not one connected with the ritual. Therefore the <s>Prajāpati-vratas</s> are for human benefit. The <s>go-lakṣaṇa</s> (cow-related observances) too are likewise — 'the ears [of cattle] should be marked' and so forth.

children.translated_text: It is said: if so, these too should be for human benefit — 'he offers with the <s>samidh</s> (fuel-stick),' 'he offers to <s>Tanūnapāt</s>' — and such [injunctions]. Here too there is mention of the person's effort; here too wealth is not desired to be created.

children.translated_text: Or rather, when no cause is apprehended, [they are] for that [human] purpose, because of the non-connection of the object [with ritual]. // MS 4,1.5 //

children.text: api vā naitad{*4/32*} asti, samidādīny api puruṣārthāni prāpnuvantīti, kāraṇāgrahaṇe puruṣārthāni prajāpativratāni bhaveyuḥ. na tatra śrutyādikaṃ kiṃcit kāraṇaṃ gṛhyate, yena karmaṇām aṅgabhūtānīti gamyate, tasmāt tāni puruṣārthāni. arthasya karmaṇo{*4/33*} nābhisaṃbandhaḥ prajāpativrataiḥ. iha tu samidādīnāṃ prakaraṇaṃ nāma kāraṇaṃ gṛhyate, yena karmārthānīti vijñāyante{*4/34*}. tasmād viṣama upanyāsaḥ, puruṣaprayatnaś caivaṃ saty anuvādaḥ.
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is not [a valid objection] — that even the <s>samidh</s>-offerings and the like would be for human benefit. When no cause is apprehended, the <s>Prajāpati-vratas</s> would be for human benefit. No cause — such as scripture and the like — is apprehended there by which they would be understood as subsidiaries of ritual. Therefore they are for human benefit. The object — i.e., the ritual — has no connection with the <s>Prajāpati-vratas</s>. But here, for the <s>samidh</s>-offerings and the like, the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) is indeed apprehended as a cause by which they are understood as being for the sake of ritual. Therefore the comparison is unequal, and the person's effort, this being so, is merely a restatement [of what is already known].

children.translated_text: And similarly in worldly [matters]. // MS 4,1.6 //

children.text: loke 'pi, niṣpannakāryādiṣu prayojanavatsu yad asaṃyuktaṃ phalena śrūyate, tat tadaṅgaṃ vijñāyata iti manyamānā upavāsaṃ japaṃ vā [441]{*4/35*} upadiśyaiva kṛtino manyante, na brutave, idam asya prayojanavato 'ṅgam iti, tathā cāpare 'pi manyamānā na duruktaṃ manyante. tasmāt samidādīni karmāṅgāni, na prajāpativratānīti siddham.
children.translated_text: In the world too, regarding things with accomplished purposes and so forth — that which is heard without connection to a result, that is understood as a subsidiary of those [purposeful things]. Those who think thus, having instructed a fast or recitation for one who has a purpose, consider [the person] virtuous, [yet] do not say 'this is a subsidiary of that which has a purpose.' And others too, thinking [similarly], do not consider it wrong speech. Therefore the <s>samidh</s>-offerings and the like are subsidiaries of ritual, not <s>Prajāpati-vratas</s> — this is established.

children.text: dravyāṇi tv aviśeṣeṇānarthakyāt pradīyeran // MS_4,1.7 //
children.translated_text: But substances (<s>dravya</s>) should be given away without distinction, because of [otherwise being] purposeless. // MS 4,1.7 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatrāmnāyate - sphyaś ca kapālāni cāgnihotrahavaṇī ca śūrpaṃ ca kṛṣṇājinaṃ ca śamyā colūkhalaṃ ca musalaṃ ca dṛṣac copalā caitāni vai daśa yajñāyudhānīti{*4/36*}. tatra saṃśayaḥ. kim etāni dravyāṇi pradātavyāni, uta svena svenārthena saṃbandhanīyāni? tad etat siddhyartham idaṃ cintanīyam, kim eṣa vidhir utānuvāda iti. vidhau sati pradānam anuvāde sati yathārthasaṃbandhaḥ. kiṃ prāptam? vidhir iti, tathā hi pravṛttau viśeṣaḥ, itarathā vādamātram anarthakam. pradāne caiṣāṃ yajñāyudhaśabdo 'nugṛhītaḥ, yajñasyāyudhāni, yajñasya sādhanānīti. itarathoddhananādīnām āyudhāni bhaveyuḥ śravaṇena, lakṣaṇayā yajñasya. saṃkhyā caivam avakalpate, yāgenaikena saṃbandhāt, itarathā nānārthasaṃbandhād daśeti saṃkhyā nāvakalpate. tasmāt pradīyeran, aviśeṣeṇa vihitaṃ prakaraṇena pradhānasya bhavitum arhati.
children.translated_text: ...the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon sacrifices); therein it is taught: 'The wooden sword (<s>sphya</s>), the potsherds (<s>kapāla</s>), the <s>Agnihotra</s> ladle (<s>agnihotrahavaṇī</s>), the winnowing basket (<s>śūrpa</s>), the black antelope skin (<s>kṛṣṇājina</s>), the peg (<s>śamyā</s>), the mortar (<s>ulūkhala</s>), the pestle (<s>musala</s>), the upper grinding stone (<s>dṛṣad</s>), and the lower grinding stone (<s>upalā</s>) — these indeed are the ten sacrificial implements (<s>yajñāyudhāni</s>).' There a doubt [arises]: should these substances be given [as a set], or should each be connected with its own respective purpose? To resolve this, the following must be considered: is this a prescriptive injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) or a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>)? If it is an injunction, then [the implements are to be] given [as a set]; if it is a restatement, then [each is] connected according to its own purpose. What is the prima facie view? It is an injunction — for thus there is a specific [purpose] in the performance; otherwise, it would be mere speech without meaning. And in [the case of] giving them, the word 'sacrificial implements' (<s>yajñāyudha</s>) is supported — 'implements of the sacrifice,' 'instruments of the sacrifice.' Otherwise, they would be 'implements' [only] of digging and the like by literal meaning, and [implements] 'of the sacrifice' only by figurative usage. The number [ten] also fits in this way — because of connection with a single sacrifice; otherwise, because of connection with diverse purposes, the number 'ten' would not hold. Therefore they should be given [as a set]; what is enjoined without specification should, by context, belong to the principal [sacrifice].

NOTES:
[{4/36: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 1.6.8.2}]

children.text: svena tv arthena saṃbandho dravyāṇāṃ pṛthagarthatvāt, tasmād yathāśruti syuḥ // MS_4,1.8 //
children.translated_text: But each substance should be connected with its own purpose, because the substances serve separate purposes; therefore they should be [understood] according to the literal text. // MS 4,1.8 //

children.text: na caitad asti vidhiḥ, pradeyānīti, anuvādaḥ, prāpta[442]{*4/37*}tvāt. sphyenoddhanti{*4/38*}, kapāleṣu śrapayati{*4/39*}{*4/40*}, agnihotrahavanyāṃ{*4/41*} nirvapati, śūrpeṇa vivinakti, kṛṣājinam ulūkhalasyādhastād avastṛṇāti, śamyāyāṃ dṛṣadam upadadhāti, prokṣitābhyām ulūkhalamusalābhyām avahanti, prokṣitābhyāṃ dṛṣadupalābhyāṃ pinaṣṭīty evaṃ svena svena vākyenoddhananādiṣu prāpnuvanti, prāptānāṃ vacanam anuvādaḥ. prakaraṇam api vākyena bādhyate, yajñāyudhaśabdaś cānuvādapakṣe nyāyyaḥ, na vidhipakṣe, gauṇo hi sa āyudhaśabdaḥ sphyādiṣu, saṃkhyāpi pāṭhābhiprāyā bhaviṣyati, vispaṣṭaṃ caitad uddhananādibhiḥ sphyādīni prayuktānīti. bhavati hi tatra vidhiḥ - sphyenoddhantītyevamādiḥ, na tu yajñāyudhāni kartavyānīti. tasmād uddhananādiṣu vākyena prāptānām anuvāda iti.
children.translated_text: This is not an injunction — [the statement] 'they are to be given' — [but rather] a restatement, because [each] is already established. 'With the wooden sword he digs up,' 'on the potsherds he cooks,' 'in the <s>Agnihotra</s> ladle he offers the oblation,' 'with the winnowing basket he winnows,' 'the black antelope skin he spreads beneath the mortar,' 'on the peg he places the upper grinding stone,' 'with the consecrated mortar and pestle they thresh,' 'with the consecrated upper and lower grinding stones he grinds' — thus, by their own respective sentences, [these implements] are obtained for digging and other [purposes]; the statement of what is [already] obtained is a restatement. Context too is overridden by [specific Vedic] sentences; and the word 'sacrificial implements' is proper in the restatement interpretation, not in the injunction interpretation — for the word 'implements' is figurative when applied to the wooden sword and the rest. The number too will be [merely] reflecting the arrangement of the text. And it is clear that the wooden sword and others are employed by [the sentences prescribing] digging and so forth. The injunction there is of this kind — 'with the wooden sword he digs up' and so on — not 'sacrificial implements are to be prepared.' Therefore, [these implements being] already established by sentences for digging and the rest, this is a restatement.

children.translated_text: And [the implements] are enjoined in their respective functional operations. // MS 4,1.9 //

children.text: arthakarmasu codyante puroḍāśādīni, tāny api vikalperan. tatra pakṣe bādhaḥ, na samuccayaḥ. puroḍāśādīnāṃ nirapekṣāṇāṃ yajisaṃbadhāt, sphyādīnāṃ ca. evaṃ vā codyante cārthakarmasu, codyante, paridhānīye karmaṇi - āhitāgnim agnibhir dahanti yajñapātraiś ceti. yadi pradīyeraṃs tatra na bhaveyuḥ, tasmād api na pradātavyānīti.
children.translated_text: In the functional operations, <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cakes) and other [substances] are enjoined — they too could be alternatives. In that case, [there would be mutual] exclusion, not combination. [This is] because the <s>puroḍāśa</s> and others, being independent, are connected with the sacrifice, and the wooden sword and others likewise. Alternatively: 'and they are enjoined in functional operations' — they are enjoined in the funeral rite (<s>paridhānīya karman</s>): 'they burn the consecrated fire-maintainer (<s>āhitāgni</s>) with the sacrificial fires and the sacrificial vessels.' If they were to be given [as a set], they would not be available there; therefore they should not be given [as a set].

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_4,1.10 //

children.translated_text: And by indicative evidence — 'fourteen oblations are offered on the full moon day, thirteen on the new moon day.' From this too, [it is established that] this is a restatement.

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ - yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśuṃ ālabhata iti{*4/43*}. tathā, anaḍvāhau yunaktīti, tathā, aśvamedhe, vasantāya kapiñjalān ālabhata iti{*4/44*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ vivakṣitam, ekatvaṃ dvitvaṃ bahutvaṃ ca, utāvivakṣitam iti. tatraikatvam ayajñāṅgabhūtaṃ na vivakṣitam ity arthaḥ, arthasya guṇabhūtatvāt, nālambhasya guṇabhūtā saṃkhyā niyojanasya vā. kasya tarhi? paśor anaḍuhoḥ kapiñjalānāṃ ca. vibhaktir hi śrutyā prātipadikārthagataṃ saṃkhyārthaṃ brūte, vākyena sā yajñāṅgaṃ brūyāt, vākyāc ca śrutir balīyasī. tasmān na yajñāṅgaṃ vivakṣitam iti.
āha, mā bhūd yajñāṅgam, paśvadīnām aṅgaṃ vivakṣitaṃ tathāpīti. ucyate, na, paśvādīnām aṅgenoktenānuktena vā kiṃcit prayojanam asti, yajñāṅgena hy avipannena prayojanam. vipanne 'pi hi paśvādyaṅge 'viguṇa eva kratur bhavati, yajñāc ca phalaṃ na paśvādeḥ. tasmāt paśvāder guṇenājñātena jñātena vā na kiṃcit prayojanam astīti, na tad vivakṣitam, yad dhi prayojanavat tad vivakṣitam ity ucyate.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal — 'the consecrated one, when he takes the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal for slaughter.' Likewise, 'he yokes two bullocks.' Similarly, in the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, 'he slaughters goats (<s>kapiñjala</s>) for [the deity of] spring.' There a doubt [arises]: is the singular, dual, or plural number intended or unintended? In that case, the singularity is not a limb of the sacrifice — this is the meaning: it is not intended — because the object is subordinate. The number is not subordinate to the slaughter or to the injunction. To what then? To the animal, to the bullocks, and to the goats. For the grammatical inflection, by [its] phonetic form, conveys the numerical meaning belonging to the nominal stem's referent; by the sentence, it would convey a limb of the sacrifice, but phonetic form is stronger than the sentence. Therefore it is not intended as a limb of the sacrifice.
[The objector] says: let it not be a limb of the sacrifice, [but] still, it is intended as a property of the animal and so forth. To that we reply: no — for there is no purpose whatsoever in stating or not stating a property of the animal and so forth, since the purpose lies in a limb of the sacrifice being unimpaired. Even when a property of the animal and so forth is impaired, the rite remains unflawed, and the fruit comes from the sacrifice, not from the animal and the rest. Therefore, since there is no purpose in a property of the animal and so forth being unknown or known, it is not intended; for what has purpose is said to be 'intended.'

NOTES:
[{4/43: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.1.11.6}]
[{4/44: <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.5.1.13}]

children.text: ekaśrutitvāc ca // MS_4,1.12 //
children.translated_text: And because of the occurrence of single phonetic form. // MS 4,1.12 //

children.text: bhavati ca kiṃcid vacanam, yena vijñāyate na tad vivakṣitam iti, yadi somam apahareyur ekāṃ gāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadyād iti{*4/45*}. yadi vivakṣitaṃ bhavet, naikām iti brūyāt, gām ity ekavacanasya vivakṣitatvāt. tathā, avī dve, dhenū dva ity{*4/46*} atrāpi dva iti vacanaṃ jñāpakam, avivakṣitam avīti dvitvam [444]{*4/47*} iti. trīn lalāmān ity{*4/48*} atrāpi trīn iti vacanaṃ liṅgam, lalāmān iti bahuvacanam avivakṣitam iti.
children.translated_text: And there is a [Vedic] statement by which it is understood that [the number] is not intended: 'if they should steal the <s>Soma</s>, one should give one cow as the sacrificial fee.' If [the singularity] were intended, one would not say 'one' (<s>ekām</s>), since the singular number of 'cow' (<s>gām</s>) would already be intended. Likewise, 'two sheep (<s>avī</s>), two, two cows (<s>dhenū</s>), two' — here too the word 'two' (<s>dva</s>) is an indication [that the dual number of the noun is] unintended — the duality in '<s>avī</s>' is unintended. '[He should offer] three spotted ones (<s>lalāmān</s>)' — here too the word 'three' (<s>trīn</s>) is the indication; the plural in '<s>lalāmān</s>' is unintended.

children.text: pratīyata iti cet // MS_4,1.13 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] it is understood [from the inflection]. // MS 4,1.13 //

children.text: evaṃ cet paśyasi - avivakṣitā saṃkhyeti, tan na, pratīyate hi saṃkhyākhyātavacanasyāṅgabhūtā, yathā paśum ānayety ukte, eka evānīyate, paśū iti, dvau. paśūn iti bahava ānīyante, yaś ca pratīyate sa śabdārthaḥ, tasmād yajñasyāṅgabhūtā saṃkhyeti śabdād gamyate, na ca śabdād gamyamānam ṛte kāraṇāt, avivakṣitaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: If you hold thus — that number is unintended — then no, [for] number is understood as a component of the verbal expression, just as when one says 'bring the animal' (<s>paśum ānaya</s>), in the singular, the bringing of one specific animal is understood; when 'two animals' (<s>paśū</s>), two [are understood]; when 'animals' (<s>paśūn</s>) in the plural, many are brought. And what is understood [from an expression] is the meaning of the word; therefore, [the argument goes,] number as a limb of the sacrifice is conveyed by the word, and what is conveyed by the word cannot be [declared] unintended without a reason.

children.text: nāśabdaṃ tatpramāṇatvāt pūrvavat // MS_4,1.14 //
children.translated_text: Not [so], because what is not [independently] expressed is dependent on that [i.e., the word], as before. // MS 4,1.14 //

children.text:
naitad evam, satyaṃ pratīyate, na tv ayaṃ śabdārtho vyāmohādoṣā pratītiḥ. kuta etat? vākyād dhi yajñāṅgam ity avagamyate, vākyaṃ ca śrutyā bādhyate. tasmād aśabdārtho 'yaṃ yajña ekatvād iti. śabdārtho 'pi hi pratīyate, yathā, pūrvo dhāvatīti. sa pūrva ity ucyate, yasyāparo 'sti, tena pūrva ity ukte, aparo gamyate. na tv aparo dhāvatīti śravaṇāt pratīyate. evam ihāpi paśum ity ekatvaṃ gamyate, na tu yajñe. yathaiva hi pūrvam ity ukte 'paro gamyata eva kevalaṃ, na tu sa vidhīyate kasmiṃścid arthe. evam ihāpi saṃkhyā pratīyate eva kevalam, na tu kartavyatayā yajñe vidhīyate na paśau.
kathaṃ na paśau vidhīyata iti cet. vidhāyakasyābhāvāt. ākhyātaśabdo vidhāyako bhaviṣyatīty etad api nopapadyate, dravyadevatāsaṃbandhasya sa vidhāyakaḥ sann ālabhata iti na saṃkhyāsaṃkhyeyasaṃbandhaṃ vidhātum arhatīti. bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. tasmād avivakṣitā saṃkhyeti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so. True, [number] is understood, but this is not the meaning of the word — the understanding is a cognitive error. How so? From the sentence, it is understood that [something] is a limb of the sacrifice, and the sentence is overridden by phonetic form. Therefore [the number] is not the meaning of the word regarding the sacrifice — 'one by virtue of singularity.' Even what is a meaning of the word can be understood [without being intended], as in 'the first one runs' (<s>pūrvo dhāvati</s>). He is called 'first' who has a 'later' [one following him]; thus when 'first' is said, the 'later' is understood. But it is not understood from hearing that 'the later one runs.' Similarly here, from 'animal' (<s>paśum</s>) the singularity is understood, but not [as applicable] in the sacrifice. Just as when 'first' is said, the 'later' is indeed understood, but is not enjoined for any purpose — so here too, number is merely understood, but is not enjoined as obligatory in the sacrifice, nor in the animal.
If [you ask,] how is [number] not enjoined in the animal? Because of the absence of an enjoining [expression]. [The objection that] the verbal expression (<s>ākhyāta</s>) will be the enjoiner — this too is untenable, for the verbal expression, being the enjoiner of the connection between substance and deity — 'he slaughters' (<s>ālabhate</s>) — is not capable of enjoining the connection between number and the numbered [entity]. For the sentence would be split in that way. Therefore, number is unintended.

children.text: śabdavat tūpalabhyate tadāgame hi tad dṛśyate tasya jñānaṃ yathānyeṣām // MS_4,1.15 //
children.translated_text: But [number] is apprehended like a word [meaning]; for when it arrives, it is seen [to make a difference]; its cognition is like that of other [word-meanings]. // MS 4,1.15 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti, na yajñe saṃkhyā śabdena śrūyata iti, ākhyātavācye hy artha upalabhyate, loke paśum ānayety ekavacane sati ekatvapaśuviśiṣṭam ānayanaṃ pratīyate, paśv ānayeti dvitvaviśiṣṭaṃ gamyate, tatra hy ekatvam apaiti, dvitvam upajāyate. yasya cāgame yad upajāyate, sa tasyārtha iti gamyate. tasya jñānaṃ, yathānyeṣāṃ śabdānām, aśvam ānayety ukte 'śvānayanaṃ pratīyate, gām ānayeti gavānayanam, tatrāśvo 'paiti gauś copajāyate, tena jñāyate, aśvaśabdasyāśvo 'rtho gośabdasya gaur iti.
yad uktam - śrutyā vākyārtho bādhyata iti, ucyate, na śrutir brūte - vākyārtho nāstīti, kevalaṃ tu prātipadikārthagatāṃ saṃkhyām āha, nādṛśī saṃkhyā vākyena yajñe vidhīyate, prātipadikārtho hy ākhyātavācyena saṃbadhyate, vibhaktyartho 'pi. tathā hi, tadviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭa ālambho gamyate, tatraikārthatvād ekavākyam avakalpate. paśau hi saṃkhyāyāṃ vidhīyamānāyām eka ākhyātaśabdo na śaknuyāt, ākhyātārthaṃ vidhātum, saṃkhyāsaṃkhyeyasaṃbandhaṃ ca. tasmād yajñe vivakṣitā saṃkhyeti.
children.translated_text:
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the [previous] thesis. This is not [correct] — that number is not heard by the word in the sacrifice. For [number] is apprehended in the meaning expressed by the verbal form — in common usage, when one says 'bring the animal' (<s>paśum ānaya</s>) in the singular, the bringing qualified by singularity and animal is understood; when 'bring the two animals' (<s>paśv ānaya</s>), the bringing qualified by duality is understood — for there the singularity departs and duality arises. And that whose arrival causes [a change] in cognition — that is understood as its meaning. 'Its cognition is like that of other words' — when one says 'bring the horse' (<s>aśvam ānaya</s>), the bringing of a horse is understood; when 'bring the cow' (<s>gām ānaya</s>), the bringing of a cow [is understood]; there the horse departs and the cow arises — from this it is known that the meaning of the word 'horse' is a horse, and of the word 'cow,' a cow.
As for what was said — 'the sentence-meaning is overridden by phonetic form' — to that we say: phonetic form does not say 'the sentence-meaning does not exist'; it merely conveys the number belonging to the nominal stem's referent. Such number is not enjoined by the sentence in the sacrifice — the nominal stem's referent is connected by the verbal expression, and the inflectional meaning too [is connected]. Thus the slaughter qualified by that [number] is understood; there, because of being a single purport, a single sentence is constituted. But if number were enjoined in the animal, a single verbal expression could not [simultaneously] enjoin the meaning of the verbal expression and the connection between number and the numbered [entity]. Therefore number is intended in the sacrifice.

children.text: tadvac ca liṅgadarśanam // MS_4,1.16 //
children.translated_text: And indicative evidence (<s>liṅga</s>) [confirms] this likewise. // MS 4,1.16 //

children.text: kim iti. karṇā yāmyāḥ, avaliptā raudrāḥ, nabhorūpāḥ pārjanyāḥ, teṣām aindrāgno daśama iti{*4/50*}. yadi tritvaṃ vivakṣitaṃ tadaindrāgno daśamo bhavati. tathā kṛṣṇā bhaumāḥ, dhūmrā āntarikṣāḥ, vṛhanto{*4/51*} divyāḥ, śavalā{*4/52*} vaidyutāḥ, siddhās tārakā iti{*4/53*} prakṛtya āha - ardhamāsānāṃ vaitad rūpaṃ yat pañca[446]{*4/54*}daśina iti{*4/55*}. tasmād api paśyāmaḥ, vivakṣitā saṃkhyeti. yat tūktam - ekāṃ gām ity avivakṣāṃ darśayatīti. atrocyate, gosaṃkhyāsaṃbandhaṃ vidhātum, etad ucyate, itarathā hi, godakṣiṇāsaṃbandho vihito gamyeta. tasmād vivakṣite 'pi vācyam etat. avī dve dhenū dve trīn lalāmān iti cānuvādāḥ.
children.translated_text: What [evidence]? 'The [animals with] ears [marked are for] <s>Yama</s>, the anointed ones for <s>Rudra</s>, the sky-colored ones for <s>Parjanya</s> — of these, the tenth is for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>.' If the [implied] triplicity were intended, then the one for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s> would be the tenth. Likewise, 'the black ones for Earth, the smoky ones for the Atmosphere, the large ones for Heaven, the speckled ones for Lightning, the accomplished ones for the Stars' — having set these forth, [the text] says: 'this indeed is the form of the half-months — that they are fifteenfold.' From this too we see that number is intended.

children.text: tathā ca liṅgam // MS_4,1.17 //
children.translated_text: And indicative evidence [supports this] likewise. // MS 4,1.17 //

children.text: evaṃ ca kṛtvā samānaśrutikaṃ liṅgam api vivakṣitaṃ bhaviṣyati, tatra idaṃ darśanam upapadyate, vasante prātar āgneyīṃ kṛṣṇagrīvām ālabhate, grīṣme mādhyaṃdine siṃhīm aindrīṃ śarady aparāhṇe śvetāṃ bārhaspatyām iti{*4/56*}. tatra śrūyate - garbhiṇyo bhavtīti{*4/57*}, garbhaḥ strīṇāṃ guṇaḥ, tena striyo darśayatīti bhaviṣyati. tathā aśva ṛṣabho vṛṣṇir vastaḥ{*4/58*} puruṣa iti te prājāpatyā iti{*4/59*}. tatra śrūyate - muṣkarā{*4/60*} bhavanti sendriyatvāyeti{*4/61*}. muṣkaratvaṃ puṃsāṃ guṇaḥ, tena puṃprāptiṃ darśayatīti.
children.translated_text: And having determined thus, indicative evidence with the same phonetic form will also be [regarded as] intended. There, this is the illustration: 'in spring, in the morning, he slaughters a black-necked [cow] for <s>Agni</s>; in summer, at midday, a lioness for <s>Indra</s>; in autumn, in the afternoon, a white [cow] for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.' There it is heard: 'they should be pregnant' — pregnancy is a quality of females; by that, [the text] indicates females. Similarly, 'a horse, a bull, a ram, a he-goat, a man — these are for <s>Prajāpati</s>.' There it is heard: 'they should be with testicles (<s>muṣkara</s>), for the sake of possessing virility.' Having testicles is a quality of males; by that, [the text] indicates males.

children.text:
adhikaraṇāntaraṃ vā, tathā ca liṅgam iti, saṃkhyādhikaraṇaṃ liṅgādhikaraṇe 'tidṛśyate{*4/62*}. liṅgam avivakṣitam, śrutyā vākyasya bādhitatvāt, na ca, vivakṣitam iva śruyata iti, bhavati liṅgam. strī gauḥ somakrayaṇīti, strīvacanāt somakrayaṇīty avivakṣitam eva liṅgaṃ pratīyate. nanu kathaṃ mṛgīm ānayeti na mṛga ānīyate? naivam, aśābdaṃ tu tat, pūrvo dhāvatīti yathā.
liṅgaṃ vivakṣitaṃ vā{*4/63*} vākyārthasya śrutyāpratiṣiddhatvāt. tathā ca liṅgam, garbhiṇyo bhavantīti, tathā ca muṣkarā bhavanti [447]{*4/64*} iti. yad uktam - strī gauḥ somakrayaṇīti, tatra strīty avivakṣitam, tathā prajāpataye puruṣān hastina ālabhata iti puruṣagrahaṇam avivakṣitam, vispaṣṭo hi nyāya ukto liṅgavivakṣāyām. tasmād vivakṣitaṃ liṅgam iti.
children.translated_text:
Or [this is] another <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), and thus the grammatical gender (<s>liṅga</s>) — the <s>saṃkhyādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on number) is seen extending into the <s>liṅgādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on gender). The gender is not intended (<s>avivakṣita</s>), because the sentence is overridden by [Vedic] statement. And it is not the case that [gender] is heard as if intended — thus gender [arises]. '[The cow] <s>strī gauḥ somakrayaṇī</s>' — from the feminine word, it is understood that the gender in '<s>somakrayaṇī</s>' is indeed not intended. But then, how is it that in '<s>mṛgīm ānaya</s>' (bring the female deer), a male deer is not brought? Not so — for that is non-verbal (<s>aśābda</s>), just as [in] 'the former runs.'
Or the gender is intended, because the sentence-meaning is not prohibited by [Vedic] statement. And thus the gender: '<s>garbhiṇyo bhavanti</s>' (they become pregnant), and thus '<s>muṣkarā bhavanti</s>' (they become male). As for what was said — '<s>strī gauḥ somakrayaṇī</s>' — there '<s>strī</s>' (female) is not intended; similarly in '<s>prajāpataye puruṣān hastina ālabhata</s>' (he sacrifices men and elephants to <s>Prajāpati</s>), the word '<s>puruṣa</s>' (man) is not intended. For a clear rule has been stated regarding the intention of gender. Therefore gender is intended.

NOTES:

children.text: āśrayiṣv aviśeṣeṇa bhāvo 'rthaḥ pratīyeta // MS_4,1.18 //
children.translated_text: In the substrata (<s>āśrayins</s>), the meaning 'existence' (<s>bhāva</s>) should be understood without distinction. // MS 4,1.18 //

children.text: atrāśrayiṇaḥ padārthā udāharaṇam uttamaḥ prayājaḥ paśupuroḍāśaḥ sviṣṭakṛd ity ete yāgā udāharaṇam{*4/65*}. eṣu saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ yajimātraṃ saṃskāro devatāyāḥ, uta yajinādṛṣṭaṃ devatāyāṃ kriyata iti. kiṃ prāptam? āśrayiṣv aviśeṣeṇa bhāvo 'rthaḥ pratīyata{*4/66*} ity{*4/67*} āśrayiṣv evaṃjātīyakeṣv apūrvasya bhāvo 'rthaḥ pratyetavyo 'viśeṣād anyair ākhyātaśabdaiḥ, yajati dadāti juhotīti, uktam etad bhūtaṃ bhavyāvopadiśyata iti.
children.translated_text: Here the substrata (<s>āśrayins</s>) — the examples are: the last <s>prayāja</s> (fore-offering), the animal <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake), and <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> — these sacrifices are the examples. Regarding these, there is doubt: is the sacrifice (<s>yaji</s>) merely a preparation (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the deity, or does an unseen [result] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) arise in the deity through the sacrifice? What is the prima facie view? 'In the substrata, the meaning "existence" should be understood without distinction' — in substrata of this kind, the meaning of existence of the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) is to be understood without distinction from other verbal roots — '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), '<s>dadāti</s>' (he gives), '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers) — it has been said that what is stated [as past] is taught as future.

children.text: codanāyāṃ tv anārambho vibhaktatvān na hy anyena vidhīyate // MS_4,1.19 //
children.translated_text: But in the injunction, there is no commencement [of <s>apūrva</s>], because of separation; for [the unseen result] is not enjoined by another [verbal root]. // MS 4,1.19 //

children.text: asyāṃ tu codanāyām anārambho 'pūrvasya, vibhakto 'yam ākhyātaśabdaḥ, yo dṛṣṭārthaḥ, tato nāpūrvam, yaḥ khalv adṛṣṭārthaḥ, tato 'pūrvam iti, dṛṣṭārthaś cāyam. asmin hi yāge kriyamāṇe devatā [448]{*4/68*} smaryate, sviṣṭakṛty api dravyaṃ pratipādyate. na cānyena śabdenātrāpūrvaṃ vidhīyate. tasmād yajimātraṃ saṃskāra iti.
children.translated_text: But in this injunction there is no commencement of the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>). This verbal root is separated — it has a visible purpose; therefore no <s>apūrva</s> [arises] from it. [Only] that which has an unseen purpose — from that [arises] the <s>apūrva</s>. And this has a visible purpose. For when this sacrifice is being performed, the deity is remembered, and in <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> too the offering material is conveyed. And the <s>apūrva</s> is not enjoined here by another word. Therefore, the sacrifice is merely a preparation (<s>saṃskāra</s>).

children.text: syād vā dravyacikīrṣāyāṃ bhāvo 'rthe ca guṇabhūtatāśrayād dhi guṇībhāvaḥ // MS_4,1.20 //
children.translated_text: Or perhaps, when there is an intention regarding the offering material, existence [of <s>apūrva</s>] is in the purpose; and the subordinate status [of the sacrifice arises] from dependence on the principal (<s>guṇa</s>). // MS 4,1.20 //

children.text: syād vāpūrvamataḥ satyām api devatācikīrṣāyām, tasmin devatāsaṃskārārthe guṇabhūtatā yāgasya, dravyapratipādanena ca, mantreṇa tatra devatā smaryate. tasmin mantreṇa dṛṣṭe 'rthe kriyamāṇe tyāgo 'paro 'dṛṣṭārthaḥ śrūyate, tasya na kiṃcid dṛṣṭam asti, devatāśrayāt tu devatāgataṃ tad apūrvam iti gamyate.
children.translated_text: Or perhaps the <s>apūrva</s> [exists] — even when the intention regarding the deity is present, the sacrifice has subordinate status in the purpose of preparing the deity. And through the conveyance of the offering material, the deity is remembered by the <s>mantra</s>. When that visible purpose indicated by the <s>mantra</s> is being accomplished, another renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>) with an unseen purpose is heard. That has nothing visible; but from dependence on the deity, it is understood that the <s>apūrva</s> pertains to the deity.

children.text: arthe samavaiṣamyam ato dravyakarmaṇām // MS_4,1.21 //
children.translated_text: In the purpose [there is] equality and inequality of material-acts (<s>dravya</s> and <s>karman</s>). // MS 4,1.21 //

children.text: atikrāntas tṛtīyaviṣayaḥ, ataḥ prabhṛti dravyāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ cārthe prayojane{*4/69*} samavaiṣamyaṃ vakṣyate. kvacit sāmyam, kvacid vaiṣamyam, āmikṣāvājinayor vaiṣamyam, krayapāṃsūnāṃ vaiṣamyam, daṇḍasya maitrāvaruṇadhāraṇe yajamānadhāraṇe ca sāmyam, evaṃ tatra tatra draṣṭavyam, sāmyaṃ vaiṣamyaṃ ceti.
children.translated_text: The third topic has been concluded. From here onward, the equality and inequality of materials (<s>dravya</s>) and acts (<s>karman</s>) in [their] purpose will be discussed. In some cases equality, in some cases inequality — [there is] inequality of <s>āmikṣā</s> (curd-mixture) and <s>vājina</s> (whey), inequality of purchase-dust (<s>krayapāṃsu</s>), equality of the staff in the holding by the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and the holding by the sacrificer — thus it is to be seen in each case, equality and inequality.

children.text: ekaniṣpatteḥ sarvaṃ samaṃ syāt // MS_4,1.22 //
children.translated_text: Because of single production, everything should be equal. // MS 4,1.22 //

children.text: cāturmāsyeṣu vaiśvadeve śrūyate - tapte payasi dadhy ānayati, sā vaiśvadevy āmikṣā vācibhyo{*4/71*} vājinam iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ tapte payasi dadhyānayanam āmikṣā prayojayati, na vājinam, utobhayam iti. kiṃ prāptam? ubhayam iti. kutaḥ? yasmin kṛte, yan niṣpadyate prayojanavat, tat tasya prayojakam iti gamyate, dadhyānayane ca kṛta ubhayaṃ niṣpadyate. āmikṣāpi, tata eva yājinam api{*4/72*} tatrānyatarārthaṃ kriyeta, yadi vinigamanāyāṃ hetur bhavet. agamyamāne viśeṣa ubhayārtham ānayanam iti gamyate. tasmād ekāsāv ubhābhyām api prayojitā niṣpattir iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites, in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [offering] it is heard: 'In heated milk he brings curds; that is the <s>Vaiśvadevī āmikṣā</s>; for the <s>vācibhyas</s> [he brings] the <s>vājina</s> (whey).' There the doubt [arises]: does the bringing of curds into heated milk produce [only] the <s>āmikṣā</s> and not the <s>vājina</s>, or both? What is the prima facie view? Both. Why? Because when something is done and something is produced that serves a purpose, that is understood as the cause of it; and when curds are brought, both are produced — the <s>āmikṣā</s> too, and from that very [act] the <s>vājina</s> as well. Either could be the intended purpose of the action, if there were a reason for determination. When no distinction is ascertainable, the bringing is understood as serving both purposes. Therefore, that single production is caused by both.

children.text: saṃsargarasaniṣpatter āmikṣā vā pradhānaṃ syāt // MS_4,1.23 //
children.translated_text: Because of the production from the mixture-flavor, <s>āmikṣā</s> would be the principal. // MS 4,1.23 //

children.text:
naitad asti, ubhayaṃ prayojakam iti, āmikṣā prayoktrī. kutaḥ? nātra yad dadhipayobhyaḥ nirvartyate, tad dhaviḥ. yadi tad dhaviḥ syāt, ubhayaṃ tābhyām eva niṣpadyata iti gamyata{*4/73*} viśeṣaḥ. kiṃ tarhi havir iti. payo dadhisaṃsṛṣṭam. kuta etat? sā vaiśvadevīty ucyate, na tato yan niṣpadyata iti.
nanu strīliṅganirdeśāt, āmikṣā haviḥ, sā ca tato niṣpadyate, vājinaṃ ca haviḥ, tad api niṣpadyata iti. na, ity ucyate - tad eva hi payas taptaṃ dadhisaṃyuktam, āmikṣā bhavati. tasmāt strīliṅgam adoṣaḥ. āha - yadi payo dadhisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ haviḥ, kiṃ tarhy ucyate, āmikṣā prayojiketi. ucyate [450]{*4/74*} - āmikṣāyāṃ dadhipayasī vidyete, na vārjine. katham avagamyate? saṃsargasaniṣpatteḥ, tatra hi dadhipayasoḥ saṃsṛṣṭayo rasa upalabhyate, tena tatra dadhipayasī ity anumānaṃ bhavati, vājine tiktakaṭuko rasaḥ.
āha, tapte payasi dadhany ānīyamāna ubhayaṃ bhavati, dadhnā ca payaḥ saṃsṛjyate vājināc ca vivicyate. tatra saṃsargaś cikīrṣitaḥ, na viveka iti. kuta etat? ucyate - śābdaḥ saṃsargo dadhnā, aśābdo vājinena vivekaḥ payasa iti, sarvanāma ca pūrvoktena śabdenaikavākyatāṃ yāti. itarasmin pakṣe payasi dadhyānayanaṃ vājinavivekalakṣaṇārthaṃ syāt, śrutilakṣaṇāviśaye ca śrutir nyāyyā. tasmād āmikṣārthaṃ dadhyānayanam, āmikṣāśabdaś cātrānuvādaḥ, āmikṣaiva sā bhavati, yatra tapte payasi dadhyānīyate. tasmād āmikṣikā prayoktrī, vājinam aprayojakam iti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — that both are causes. <s>Āmikṣā</s> is the cause. Why? Here, what is produced from curds and milk is not the oblation. If that were the oblation, then it would be understood that both are produced by those two alone — [that would be] the distinction. But what then is the oblation? The milk mixed with curds. How is this known? It is said 'that is the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s>' — not 'what is produced from it.'
But because of the feminine gender designation, <s>āmikṣā</s> is the oblation, and it is produced from that; and <s>vājina</s> is also the oblation, and it too is produced — [so the objection goes]. No, it is replied: that very milk, when heated and combined with curds, becomes <s>āmikṣā</s>. Therefore the feminine gender is no defect. [The objector] says: if the milk mixed with curds is the oblation, then why is it said '<s>āmikṣā</s> is the cause'? It is replied: in the <s>āmikṣā</s>, curds and milk are present; not in the <s>vājina</s>. How is this known? Because of the production from the mixture-flavor — for in the <s>āmikṣā</s> the blended flavor (<s>rasa</s>) of curds and milk is perceived; thereby the inference arises that curds and milk are present there; in the <s>vājina</s> the flavor is bitter and pungent.
[The objector] says: when curds are brought into heated milk, both [products] arise — by the curds the milk is mixed [with it], and from the <s>vājina</s> [the milk] is separated. There the mixing is intended, not the separation. How is this known? It is replied: the mixing with curds is verbal (<s>śābda</s>), while the separation from <s>vājina</s> with the milk is non-verbal (<s>aśābda</s>); and a pronoun enters into syntactic unity with the previously stated word. In the other view, the bringing of curds into milk would serve the purpose of separation of the <s>vājina</s>, and where there is no scope for textual indication, textual indication is proper. Therefore the bringing of curds is for the purpose of <s>āmikṣā</s>; and the word '<s>āmikṣā</s>' here is a restatement — it is indeed <s>āmikṣā</s> wherever curds are brought into heated milk. Therefore <s>āmikṣā</s> is the cause, and <s>vājina</s> is not the cause.

children.text: mukhyaśabdābhisaṃstavāc ca // MS_4,1.24 //
children.translated_text: And because of connection with the primary word. // MS 4,1.24 //

children.text:
na ca, ubhayaṃ prayojakaṃ nyāyyam, nātra vacanam asti, idaṃ prayojakam idaṃ neti, asati prayojake 'narthakaṃ bhavatīti prayojakaṃ kalpyate. tatraikasminn api prayojake siddhe 'rthavaty upadeśe nānyad api prayojakaṃ bhavitum arhati. na ca, na gamyate viśeṣaḥ. kathaṃ gamyate? mukhyaśabdābhisaṃstavāt, mukhyaśabdaḥ saṃstotuṃ nyāyya iti, prāthamyāt tu tasya tāvat prayojakatvajñānam{*4/75*}, tasmin sati prayojake, parikṣatatvād{*4/76*} ānarthakyasya, na dvitīyam api prayojakam, prathamā cāmikṣā, dvitīyaṃ vājinam, tasmād āmikṣā prayoktrī.
api ca mukhyaśabdena ca, āmikṣā stūyate - mithunaṃ vai dadhi ca śṛtaṃ ca, atha yat saṃsṛṣṭaṃ maṇḍam iva mastv{*4/77*} iva pari ca dadṛśe{*4/78*} [451]{*4/79*} garbha eva sa iti, garbhastutāmikṣā{*4/80*}, mithunasya ca garbhaḥ prayojakaḥ, na garbhodakam. tasmād apy āmikṣā prayojiketi manyāmahe. kiṃ bhavati prayojanam? yady ubhayaṃ prayojakam, vājine naṣṭe, punas tapte payasi dadhy ānetavyam, atha vājinam aprayojakam, naṣṭe vājine lopo dadhyānayanasya.
children.translated_text:
And it is not proper that both are causes. There is no statement here [saying] 'this is the cause and this is not.' When without a cause [the injunction] would be purposeless, a cause is postulated. There, even with one cause being established and the teaching having purpose, another should not also be a cause. And it is not that no distinction is ascertainable. How is it ascertained? Because of connection with the primary word — the primary word is proper to be connected with. Because of priority, knowledge of its causal status [comes] first; when that cause is established, because the purposelessness [objection] has been removed, the second too is not a cause. And <s>āmikṣā</s> is first; <s>vājina</s> is second. Therefore <s>āmikṣā</s> is the cause.
Moreover, by the primary word, <s>āmikṣā</s> is praised: 'Curds and heated [milk] are indeed a pair; and what is mixed — like froth, like whey — is seen around — that is indeed the embryo' — the <s>āmikṣā</s> is praised as an embryo; and the embryo of a pair is the cause, not the water of the embryo. Therefore too we consider <s>āmikṣā</s> to be the cause. What is the practical consequence? If both are causes, when the <s>vājina</s> is lost, curds should be brought again into heated milk. But if <s>vājina</s> is not a cause, when the <s>vājina</s> is lost, the bringing of curds is omitted.

children.text: padakarmāprayojakaṃ nayanasya parārthatvāt // MS_4,1.25 //
children.translated_text: The foot-act (<s>padakarman</s>) is not a cause, because the leading is for another's purpose. // MS 4,1.25 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - aruṇayā piṅgākṣyaikahāyanyā somaṃ krīṇātīti{*4/81*}. tatredam aparaṃ śrūyate - ṣaṭ padāny anuniṣkrāmatīti{*4/82*}, tathā, saptamaṃ padaṃ gṛhṇātīti. idam aparam - yarhi havirdhāne prācī pravartayeyus tarhi tenākṣam añjyād{*4/83*} iti{*4/84*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ somakrayaṇyānayanaṃ padapāṃsvartham, uta krayaprayuktam iti. kiṃ prāptam? nayanād ubhayaṃ niṣpadyate, krayaḥ padaṃ ca, tasmād ubhayaṃ prayojakam. na hi gamyate viśeṣa iti, tad uktam - ekaniṣpatteḥ sarvaṃ samaṃ syād iti{*4/85*}.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - padakarmāprayojakam iti. kutaḥ? yasmān nayanaṃ krayārtham, na hi nayanam antareṇa viśiṣṭe deśe kraya upapadyate. tasmāt krayeṇa tāvan nayanaṃ prayuktam iti gamyate. krayaprayuktaṃ cet, na padaprayuktam api bhavitum arhati.
api ca, ekahāyanyāḥ padapāṃsavo grahītavyā iti nāsti śabdaḥ. nanu prakṛtaikahāyanī padapāṃsugrahaṇavākyena{*4/86*} [452]{*4/87*} saṃbhantsyate. neti brūmaḥ - ekahāyanyā krīṇātīti viśiṣṭena vākyena kraye, upadiṣṭaikahāyanī prakṛtatvāt padapāṃsuvākyena saṃbadhyate, prakaraṇāc ca vākyaṃ balīyaḥ. athedānīm, ekahāyanī krayaṇārthaṃ saṃkīrtitā satī saṃnihitatvāt prasaṅgam upajīvatā padapāṃsuvākyena saṃbadhyeta, yāsau parārthā, etasyāḥ padaṃ grāhyam iti. tasmāt krayapayuktaṃ nayanam, aprayojakaṃ padam iti.
kiṃ punaś cintāyāḥ prayojanam? yady ubhayam ekahāyanīnayanasya prayojakam, yadaikahāyanyāḥ saptaṃ padaṃ grāvaṇi nidhīyate, tadā punar ekahāyanī nīyeta saptamāya padāya, yadā padaṃ na prayojakam, tadā naikahāyanī punaḥ ṣaṭ padāny anuniṣkrāmayayitavyeti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'With a reddish, tawny-eyed one-year-old [cow] he purchases <s>Soma</s>.' And here another [thing] is heard: 'She walks six steps' — and similarly, 'He grasps the seventh step.' And this other [thing]: 'When they should roll the <s>Havirdhāna</s> [carts] eastward, then with that he should anoint the axle.' There the doubt [arises]: is the leading of the <s>Soma</s>-purchasing [cow] for the purpose of the foot-dust (<s>padapāṃsu</s>), or occasioned by the purchase? What is the prima facie view? From the leading both are produced — the purchase and the foot[-dust]; therefore both are causes. For no distinction is ascertainable — as was stated: 'Because of single production, everything should be equal.'
Given this, we say: the foot-act is not a cause. Why? Because the leading is for the purpose of the purchase — for without leading, the purchase cannot take place at the designated location. Therefore it is understood that the leading is occasioned by the purchase. And if occasioned by the purchase, it should not also be occasioned by the foot[-dust].
Moreover, there is no statement that the foot-dust of a one-year-old [cow] is to be taken. But the one-year-old [cow] being the topic would be connected with the foot-dust-taking statement through contextual connection. But we say no — the one-year-old [cow] being taught in the specific statement 'with a one-year-old he purchases' is in connection with the purchase; being the topic, it is connected with the foot-dust statement through contextual connection; and contextual connection is stronger than the sentence. Now, the one-year-old [cow], having been mentioned for the purpose of the purchase, being proximate, would be connected by the foot-dust statement through incidental connection — she who serves another's purpose, 'her foot is to be taken.' Therefore the leading is occasioned by the purchase, and the foot[-dust] is not a cause.
What then is the practical consequence of this deliberation? If both are causes of the leading of the one-year-old [cow], when the seventh step of the one-year-old [cow] is placed on the pressing stones, then the one-year-old [cow] should be led again for the seventh step. But when the foot is not a cause, then the one-year-old [cow] need not be led again to walk six steps for the [seventh] step.
