children.text: arthābhidhānakarma ca bhaviṣyatā saṃyogasya tannimittatvāt tadartho hi vidhīyate // MS_4,1.26 //
children.translated_text: And the act that designates the purpose [is determinative]; because the connection with what is yet to come is its cause, it is enjoined for that purpose. // MS_4,1.26 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - kapāleṣu puroḍāśaṃ śrapayatīti{*4/88*}, tathā - puroḍāśakapālena tuṣān upavapatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ubhayaṃ kapālāni prayojayati, puroḍāśaśrapaṇaṃ tuṣopavāpaś ca, uta śrapaṇaṃ prayojakam, na tuṣopavāpa iti. kiṃ prāptam? vinigamanāyāṃ hetor abhāvād ubhayam.
iti prāpte ucyate, arthābhidhānaṃ prayojanasaṃbaddham abhidhānaṃ yasya, yathā puroḍāśakapālam iti, puroḍāśārthaṃ kapālaṃ puroḍāśakapālam. katham etad avagamyate? puroḍāśas tāvat tasmin kāle nāsti, yena vartamānaḥ saṃbandhaḥ kapālena syāt. tenaiva hetunā na bhūtaḥ, sa eṣa kapālasya puroḍāśeṇa bhaviṣyatā [453]{*4/89*} saṃbandhaḥ, bhaviṣyatā saṃbandhaś ca tan nimittasya bhavati. tasmāt puroḍāśena prayuktaṃ yat kapālam, tena tuṣā upavaptavyā iti. evaṃ ca sati carau puroḍāśābhāve yadā tuṣānupavaptuṃ kapālam upādīyate, na tat puroḍāśakapālaṃ syāt. na cen na tena tuṣā upavaptavyā bhavanti. tasmān na tuṣopavāpaḥ kapālānāṃ prayojakaḥ, prayojalkaṃ tu śrapaṇam iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard: 'He cooks the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice cake) on the potsherds,' and likewise: 'He winnows the husks with the <s>puroḍāśa</s>-potsherd.' There a doubt [arises]: do the potsherds serve both purposes — the cooking of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> and the winnowing of husks — or is the cooking the motivating factor, but not the winnowing of husks? What is the prima facie view? In the absence of a reason for choosing between them, both [are motivating factors].
Given this, we say: a purpose-designating act (<s>arthābhidhānakarma</s>) is one whose designation is connected with a purpose — as in '<s>puroḍāśa</s>-potsherd,' meaning 'a potsherd for the <s>puroḍāśa</s>.' How is this understood? The <s>puroḍāśa</s> does not exist at that time, such that a present connection with the potsherd could obtain. For that very reason, it is not [a connection with something] past. Thus, this is a connection of the potsherd with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> that is yet to come, and a connection with what is yet to come belongs to that which is its cause. Therefore, the potsherd that is employed for the <s>puroḍāśa</s> — with that, the husks are to be winnowed. And this being so, in the <s>caru</s> (oblation) when there is no <s>puroḍāśa</s>, when a potsherd is taken up to winnow the husks, it would not be a '<s>puroḍāśa</s>-potsherd.' And if not, then husks should not be winnowed with it. Therefore, the winnowing of husks is not the motivating factor for the potsherds; rather, the cooking is the motivating factor.

children.text: paśāv anālambhāl lohitaśakṛtor akarmatvam // MS_4,1.27 //
children.translated_text: In the animal [sacrifice], because of non-slaughter, the blood and dung have no ritual function. // MS_4,1.27 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agniṣomīyaḥ. tatra śrūyate - hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyaty atha jihvāyā ityevamādi{*4/90*}. tathā, lohitaṃ nirasyati, śakṛt saṃpravidhyati, sthavimato varhiraṃlktāpāsyatīti{*4/91*}{*4/92*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ hṛdayādibhir avadānair ijyā paśoḥ prayoktrī, uta śakṛt saṃpravyādho lohitanirasanaṃ ca tad api prayojakam iti. kiṃ prāptam? ekaniṣpatteḥ sarvaṃ samaṃ syād{*4/93*}, ubhayaṃ prayojakam iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, paśau{*4/94*} śakṛllohitayor aprayojakatvam, na hi tadarthaḥ paśor ālambhaḥ{*4/95*}, sakṛt saṃpravidhyati lohitam apāsyatīty ucyate, na paśor anyasya veti, paśur agnīṣomīyo vākyena, yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*4/96*}. śakṛllohite paśoḥ prakaraṇena bhavetām, prakaraṇaṃ ca vākyena bādhyate. nanv ete śakṛllohite pratipādyete, tena yāgārthasya paśor nānyasyeti niścayaḥ. evaṃ cet, aprayojake śakṛllohita iti. kiṃ bhavati prayojanam? sāmye sati śakṛllohitābhāve 'nyaḥ paśur ālambhanīyaḥ, śakṛllohitayor aprayojakatve lopaḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal. There it is heard: 'He cuts from the front of the heart, then from the tongue' — and so forth. Likewise: 'He discards the blood; he pierces through the dung; he removes [the hide] from the thick [part] after having smeared it with sacrificial grass.' There a doubt [arises]: does the sacrifice of the animal have the <s>avadānas</s> (cut portions) beginning with the heart as its motivating factor, or are the piercing of the dung and the discarding of the blood also motivating factors? What is the prima facie view? Because of single production, everything should be equal — both are motivating factors.
Given this, we say: in the animal [sacrifice], blood and dung have no motivating capacity. For the slaughter of the animal is not for their sake. 'He pierces through the dung, he discards the blood' — it is said [in the context of] the animal, not of anything else. The animal [belongs to] <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> by sentence: 'the initiated one who slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.' Blood and dung would be [connected to] the animal by context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), and context is overridden by sentence. Now, [one might say]: these blood and dung are [specifically] mentioned, and therefore the certainty is that [they pertain to] the animal [sacrificed] for the purpose of offering, not another. If so, blood and dung are non-motivating. What is the consequence? When, in equality, blood and dung are absent, another animal must be slaughtered; but when blood and dung are non-motivating, they are dropped [as criteria].

children.text: ekadeśadravyaś{*4/98*} cotpattau vidyamānasaṃyogāt // MS_4,1.28 //
children.translated_text: And [when the substance serves] a part, because of [its] connection with what exists at the time of production. // MS_4,1.28 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ{*4/99*} śrūyate - uttarārdhāt sviṣṭakṛte samavadyatīti{*4/100*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ puroḍāśasyāgneyayāgaḥ prayojakaḥ, sviṣṭakṛd aprayojaka utobhayam iti. kiṃ prāptam? ekaniṣpatteḥ sarvaṃ samaṃ syād iti{*4/101*}. evaṃ prāpte brumaḥ, ekadeśadravyaś{*4/102*} caivaṃjātīyako 'prayojako bhavet. kutaḥ? vidyamānasaṃyogāt, na, ekadeśakarmāvayavinaṃ prayuṅkte, vidyamānasyāvayavina ekadeśa upādātavya iti, tatrārtho bhavati, nāvayavinam upādadīteti, yathekṣukhaṇḍam asmai prayaccha, modakaśakalam asmai prayaccheti, nekṣum upādadīteti gamyate, sata ikṣoḥ khaṇḍam upādadīta, sato modakāc chakalam upādadīteti. tasmād anyārthaṃ dravyaṃ tasyottarārdhād avadeyam, asti cāgnyarthaḥ puroḍāśaḥ. tasmād viṣṭakṛd aprayojaka iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard: 'He cuts from the upper half for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> [offering].' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>Āgneya</s> sacrifice the motivating factor for the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, while the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is non-motivating, or are both [motivating]? What is the prima facie view? Because of single production, everything should be equal. Given this, we say: one of this kind that [serves only] a part is non-motivating. Why? Because of connection with what [already] exists — a partial-substance act does not motivate the whole; since a part of an existing whole is to be taken, the purpose lies there, not in taking up the whole. Just as [when one says] 'give him a piece of sugarcane' or 'give him a piece of sweetmeat,' it is not understood as 'take the [whole] sugarcane'; rather, one takes a piece from an existing sugarcane, a piece from an existing sweetmeat. Therefore, the substance that exists for another purpose — from its upper half the portion should be cut. And the <s>puroḍāśa</s> exists for <s>Agni</s>'s purpose. Therefore the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is non-motivating.

children.text: nirdeśāt tasyānyad arthād iti // MS_4,1.29 //
children.translated_text: Because of [its] designation as belonging to that [deity], another [substance must be produced] by necessity. // MS_4,1.29 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, aprayojakaḥ puroḍāśasya sviṣṭakṛd iti, naitad evam, agniṃ prati nirdeśāt tasya puroḍāśasya{*4/103*} sviṣṭakṛd artham anyaḥ puroḍāśa utpādayitavyaḥ, yasyottarārdhāt sviṣṭakṛd ijyate, tasyāgnaye saṃkalpitasya neṣṭe yajamānaḥ. katham asau tad anyasyai devatāyai dadyāt. katham agniṃ prati nirdeśa iti. idaṃ śrūyate - aṅgiraso vā ita uttamāḥ suvargaṃ loka[455]{*4/104*}māyaṃs te yajñavāstv abhyāyaṃs te puroḍāśaṃ kūrmaṃ bhūtvā sarpantam apaśyaṃs tam abruvann indrāya dhriyasva bṛhaspataye dhriyasvādityāya dhriyasva sa nādhriyata tam abruvan agnaye dhriyasveti so 'dhriyata yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo{*4/105*} 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavatīti{*4/106*}. tasmāt tena sviṣṭakṛto na saṃbandhaḥ. evaṃ cet tasmād anyad dravyam arthād utpādayitavyam, na hy anutpannasya dravyasyottarārdho bhavatīti.
children.translated_text: If you hold that the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is non-motivating for the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, this is not so. Because of the designation directed toward <s>Agni</s>, another <s>puroḍāśa</s> must be produced for the purpose of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> of that <s>puroḍāśa</s>. The one from whose upper half the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is offered — he who has consecrated it to <s>Agni</s> — the sacrificer does not desire [to give it to another deity]. How could he give it to another deity? How is the designation directed toward <s>Agni</s>? This is what is heard: 'The <s>Aṅgirases</s> were indeed the foremost here; they went to the heavenly world. They strode along the sacrificial ground. They saw the <s>puroḍāśa</s> crawling like a tortoise. They said to it: "Be steady for <s>Indra</s>! Be steady for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>! Be steady for <s>Āditya</s>!" It was not steady. They said: "Be steady for <s>Agni</s>!" It became steady. Because the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-potsherd [cake] on the new-moon and full-moon days remains firm.' Therefore, the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> has no connection with that [cake]. This being so, another substance must be produced by necessity, for there is no upper half of an unproduced substance.

children.text: na śeṣasaṃnidhānāt // MS_4,1.30 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the proximity of the remainder. // MS_4,1.30 //

children.text: naitad evaṃ saṃnihito hi śeṣaḥ, yasminn anutpādyamāne 'rtho na sidhyati, so 'rthād upādyate. saṃnihite ca śeṣe sati sidhyaty uttarārdhād grahaṇam. tasmān nārthād dravyam utpādayitavyam, yad evānyārthaṃ dravyaṃ saṃnihitam, tasyaivottarārdhād grahītavyam. uttarārdhamātraṃ hi sviṣṭakṛte śrūyate nāmuṣya dravyasyeti. na caitāvatā vyavahāro bhavati, sarvo hi kasyacid uttarārdhaḥ, sa eṣa saṃnihitam apekṣate, saṃnihitaṃ ca parārtham. tasmāt parārthād dravyāt sviṣṭakṛd ijyā. ataś cāprayojiketi. yad uktam, anīśānena na śakyaṃ dātum iti, tad ucyate, vācanika eṣa śeṣapratipādanārtha utsargaḥ, sa śakyaḥ kartum. dānaṃ hy utsargapūrvakaḥ parasya svatvasaṃbandhaḥ, sa na śakyo 'nīśānena.
children.translated_text: This is not so, for the remainder is proximate. That without which the purpose is not accomplished — that [alone] is produced by necessity. When the remainder is proximate, the taking from the upper half is accomplished. Therefore, no substance needs to be produced by necessity; from whatever substance that exists for another purpose and is proximate, its upper half is to be taken. For only the upper half is heard [as required] for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, not 'of that particular substance.' And by this alone, no transaction takes place, for everything is someone's upper half. Thus it looks to what is proximate, and what is proximate exists for another's purpose. Therefore, the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> offering is from a substance that exists for another purpose. Hence it is non-motivating. As for what was said — 'one who is not the owner cannot give' — to that we reply: this relinquishment (<s>utsarga</s>) is enjoined by [Vedic] statement for the purpose of establishing the remainder-relationship, and that can be done. For giving is a connection of ownership with another preceded by relinquishment, and that cannot be done by one who is not the owner.

children.text: karmakāryāt // MS_4,1.31 //
children.translated_text: Because of the ritual-action-produced [portion]. // MS_4,1.31 //

children.text: karmanimittaś ca sviṣṭakṛto bhāga iti śrūyate. katham? devā vai sviṣṭakṛtam abruvan havyaṃ no vaheti, so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai [456]{*4/107*} bhāgo me 'stv iti vṛṇīṣvety abruvan so 'bravīd uttarārdhād eva mahyaṃ sakṛt sakṛd avadyād iti. karma kurvato bhāgo 'yam uttarārdhād iti stutir bhavati. yady āgneyasyottarārdhād ity ucyate, tato 'sti karmārthena bhāgena sādṛśyam idam, tadāgneyaṃ havyaṃ yat kila vahasīti, tatra sati sādṛśye stutir upapadyate, prayojakatve cāsati sādṛśye stutisāmañjasyaṃ na syāt. tasmād aprayojakaḥ puroḍāśasya sviṣṭakṛdyāga iti.
children.translated_text: And it is heard that the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>'s share is produced by ritual action. How? 'The gods said to the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>: "Carry our oblation." He said: "I choose a boon — let there be a share for me." "Choose!" they said. He said: "Let [the priest] cut once each time from the upper half for me."' This share from the upper half is a praise (<s>stuti</s>) — that when performing the ritual action, his share is from the upper half. If it is said 'from the upper half of the <s>Āgneya</s>,' then there is similarity with the share [given] for the purpose of ritual service. Since [Agni] carries the <s>Āgneya</s> oblation, when there is this similarity, the praise is fitting; but if the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> were a motivating factor, and in the absence of similarity, the coherence of the praise would not hold. Therefore the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> offering is non-motivating for the <s>puroḍāśa</s>.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_4,1.32 //
children.translated_text: And because of indicatory marks. // MS_4,1.32 //

children.text: liṅgam api bhavati - tad yat sarvebhyo havirbhyaḥ samavadyati, tasmād idam udare viśvarūpam annaṃ samavadhīyata iti, yadi parārthād dravyāt saṃnihitād ijyate, tadā satsaṃnidhānāviśeṣāt sarvebhyo 'vadīyata ity upapadyate. prayojakatve tv ekasmād evāvadīyeta. tasmād apy aprayojakaḥ. tathedam aparaṃ liṅgam - śeṣād iḍām avadyati, śeṣāt sviṣṭakṛtaṃ yajatīti. nanv ayaṃ vidhiḥ syāt. neti brūmaḥ, nātra vidhivibhaktir vartamānāpadeśo hy ayam iti.
children.translated_text: There is also an indicatory mark: 'That which is cut from all the oblations — therefore this multiform food is deposited in the belly.' If the offering is from a proximate substance that exists for another purpose, then because there is no difference in proximity, [the statement] 'it is cut from all [oblations]' is fitting. But if [the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>] were a motivating factor, it would be cut from only one [oblation]. Therefore, by this too, it is non-motivating. Likewise, there is this other indicatory mark: 'From the remainder he cuts the <s>Iḍā</s> portion; from the remainder he offers the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.' Now, this might be [taken as] an injunction. We say no — the subjunctive here is not injunctive but rather a description of what is [already] taking place.

children.text: abhighāraṇe viprakarṣād anuyājavat pātrabhedaḥ syāt // MS_4,1.33 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>abhighāraṇa</s> (anointing with ghee), because of the temporal distance, there should be a separate vessel, as in the case of the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings). // MS_4,1.33 //

children.text: asti vājapeyaḥ, vāyapeyena svārājyakāmo yajeteti. tatra śrūyate - saptadaśa prājāpatyān paśūn ālabhate, saptadaśo vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpater āptyai, iti{*4/108*}, prājāpatyānāṃ kratupaśūnāṃ ca samuccayo vakṣyate - prajāpātyeṣu cāmnānād iti{*4/109*}. asti [457]{*4/110*} tu prakṛtau, prayājaśeṣeṇa havīṃṣy abhighārayatīti{*4/111*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kiṃ prājāpatyānāṃ vapā abhighārayituṃ prayājaśeṣasya dhāraṇārthaṃ pātram aparam utpādayitavyam, tatas tena prājāpatyānāṃ vapā abhighārayitavyāḥ, uta na śeṣo dhārayitavyaḥ, naiva tataḥ prājāpatyānāṃ vapā abhighāraṇīyā iti. kiṃ prāptam? abhighāraṇe prayājaśeṣadhāraṇārthaṃ pātram utpādyeta, prātaḥsavane ca prayājaśeṣo viprakṛṣṭakāle{*4/112*} mādhyaṃdine savane, brahmasāmakāle prājāpatyānām ālabhyaḥ śrūyate - tān paryagnikṛtān utsṛjanti, brahmasāmny ālabhata iti{*4/113*}, vyāpṛtā ca juhūr bhavati. tasmāt pātrāntaram utpādanīyam iti, yathānuyājeṣu pṛṣadājyadhāraṇārthaṃ pātram utpādyate, pṛṣadājyenānuyājān yajatīti{*4/114*} vacanāt, evam atrāpīti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Vājapeya</s> [rite]: 'One desiring sovereignty should sacrifice with the <s>Vājapeya</s>.' There it is heard: 'He slaughters seventeen animals sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>; seventeen is <s>Prajāpati</s>, for the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>.' The combination of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals and the ritual animals will be stated [later]: 'And because of the mention among the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [animals].' Now, in the basic rite (<s>prakṛti</s>), [it is heard]: 'He anoints the oblations with the remainder of the <s>prayāja</s> [offerings].' There a doubt [arises]: should another vessel be produced for holding the <s>prayāja</s>-remainder in order to anoint the <s>omentum</s> (<s>vapā</s>) of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals, and then should the <s>omentum</s> of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals be anointed with it? Or should the remainder not be retained, and hence the <s>omentum</s> of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals not be anointed at all? What is the prima facie view? A vessel should be produced for holding the <s>prayāja</s>-remainder for the <s>abhighāraṇa</s>. [This is because] the <s>prayāja</s>-remainder is at a distant time — the <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals are to be slaughtered at the midday pressing, at the time of the <s>Brahma-sāman</s>, while the morning pressing [comes first]. It is heard: 'They release those [animals] that have been circumambulated with fire; he slaughters at the <s>Brahma-sāman</s>.' And the <s>juhū</s> ladle is already in use. Therefore another vessel must be produced — just as in the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings), a vessel is produced for holding the <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curd-mixed ghee), because of the statement 'he offers the <s>anuyājas</s> with <s>pṛṣadājya</s>,' so too here.

children.text: na vāpātratvād apātratvaṃ tv ekadeśatvāt // MS_4,1.34 //
children.translated_text: No — [there is no need for a new vessel] because of [the existing vessel] not lacking vessel-status; but the part-status [of the substance] is because of [its being] a portion. // MS_4,1.34 //

children.text:
na vā prājāpatyānāṃ vapā abhighāryāḥ. kutaḥ? śeṣābhāvāt. kathaṃ śeṣābhāva iti cet. apātratvāt. katham apātratā? ekadeśatvāt, prayājārthasya hi gṛhītasyājyasya sa ekadeśaḥ śeṣaḥ. kim ataḥ? yady evam, ekadeśavyāpāraḥ śrūyamāṇo nāvayavinam upādeyatvena codayati.
āha, utpattiṃ na codayet, dhāraṇam utpannasyārthād bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, ekadeśatvād abhighāraṇaṃ dravyam eva na prayuṅkta ity ucyate, kṛtārthasya dravyasyāyam ekadeśaḥ pratipādyate, nābhighāraṇam arthakarma. nanu haviṣām, dvitīyānirdeśāt prādhānyaṃ syāt. nety ucyate, adṛṣṭo hi haviṣām upakāraḥ kalpyeta, ājyaprādhānye punar juhvā riktatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam, ājyabhāgārthenājyenāsaṃsargaḥ, juhvā [458]{*4/115*} riktayā prayojanam, nābhighṛtena haviṣā. tasmāt prājāpatyānām abhighāritābhir vapābhiḥ prayojanam eva nāsti, kim arthaṃ śeṣo dhāryata iti.
children.translated_text:
Or rather, the <s>vapās</s> (omentums) of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [victims] should not be basted. Why? Because of the absence of a remainder. How is there an absence of remainder? Because [the ghee] is not a proper vessel [for this purpose]. How is it not a proper vessel? Because it is only a part — for this remainder is a part of the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) taken for the purpose of the preliminary offerings (<s>prayāja</s>). What follows? If so, an operation on a part, when heard, does not enjoin the whole as to be employed.
[The objector] says: it would not enjoin the origination, but the retaining of what has already been produced would follow from the nature of things. We reply: because it is only a part, even the basting substance (<s>abhighāraṇa</s>) is not employed — so it is said. A part of a substance whose purpose has been fulfilled is being indicated, not [a substance for] basting as a purposeful act. But would not the oblations have primacy, since there is no second designation? No, we say — for the benefit to the oblations would be unseen and [merely] conjectured, whereas in the primacy of the <s>ājya</s>, the emptiness of the <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) is a visible purpose — non-contact with the <s>ājya</s> for the <s>ājyabhāga</s> purpose; the purpose is the empty <s>juhū</s>, [458] not the basted oblation. Therefore, for the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [victims], there is simply no purpose served by basted <s>vapās</s> — why should a remainder be retained?

children.text: hetutvāc ca sahaprayogasya // MS_4,1.35 //
children.translated_text: And because of the causal nature of simultaneous performance. // MS_4,1.35 //

children.text: hetutvāc cābhighāraṇasya, sahālabhata iti stutir bhavati, tīrthaṃ vai prātaḥsavanam, yat prātaḥsavane paśava ālabhyante, tīrtha evaitān ālabhate, sayonitvāyārtho vapānām abhighṛtatvāya, ity arthānatareṇa vapābhighāraṇam anugṛhṇan nehāstīti darśayati.
children.translated_text: And because of the causal nature of basting — "he slaughters them together" is a praise. "The morning pressing is the sacred ford; since the victims are slaughtered in the morning pressing, he slaughters them in the sacred ford itself, for the sake of having the same origin" — by praising the basted-ness of the <s>vapās</s> through another purpose, it shows that there is none here.

children.text: abhāvadarśanāc ca // MS_4,1.36 //
children.translated_text: And because of showing the absence [of basting]. // MS_4,1.36 //

children.text: abhāvaṃ khalv apy abhigdhāraṇasya darśayati - savyā vā etarhi vapā yarhy anabhighṛtāḥ, brahma vai brahmasāma, yad brahmasāmny ālabhate tenāsavyāḥ, tenābhighṛtā iti. savyaśabdo rūkṣe bhāṣyate, savyā vapety anabhighṛtatāṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: It also shows the absence of basting: "the <s>vapās</s> are indeed rough (<s>savya</s>) at this time, when unbasted; <s>Brahman</s> is indeed the <s>Brahmasāman</s>; by slaughtering [the victim] with the <s>Brahmasāman</s>, they are made not-rough, thereby basted." The word <s>savya</s> is used in the sense of "rough"; "the <s>vapā</s> is rough" shows the absence of basting.

children.text: sati savyavacanam // MS_4,1.37 //
children.translated_text: The statement about roughness is when [basting] exists. // MS_4,1.37 //

children.text: āha naitad darśanam, saty eva hy abhighāraṇe bhavaty etat savyavacanam, asti hi vapāyā anyad abhighāraṇam - upastṛṇāty ājyaṃ hiraṇyaśakalam, vapā hiraṇyaśakalaṃ tato 'bhighārayatīti{*4/116*}. tasmin sati kathaṃ savyā bhaveyuḥ? brūte{*4/117*} ca, tasmān naitac chakyam avagantum rūkṣās tā vapā dṛśyanta iti, tena nūnam abhighāraṇaṃ prayājaśeṣeṇāstīti, saty asminn abhighāraṇe pratyakṣe, rūkṣās tā iti darśanaṃ vyāmoha iti{*4/118*}.
children.translated_text: [The objector] says: this is not evidence. For this statement about roughness applies when basting indeed exists — for there is another basting of the <s>vapā</s>: "he spreads underneath ghee and a gold flake; [he places] the <s>vapā</s> and a gold flake, then bastes." Given that this exists, how could they be rough? And [the text] states [this]. Therefore this cannot be understood to mean that the <s>vapās</s> appear rough. Therefore, the basting with the <s>prayāja</s> remainder must exist. Given this directly perceived basting, the appearance of "they are rough" is a delusion.

children.text:
NOTES:

children.text: na tasyeti cet // MS_4,1.38 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that [the statement] is not about that — // MS_4,1.38 //

children.text: evaṃ ced dṛśyate, saty abhighāraṇe savyā iti vacanam aliṅgam iti, nāliṅgam, tasyaitad vacanam, yat snehanaṃ karoti. katamat tat? yat prathamam, prathamaṃ hi snehanaṃ karoti, na dvitīyam. snigdhasya tad bhavati, na ca snigdhasya snehanaṃ kriyate, yathā bhavati loke vādaḥ, yad asmābhiḥ kāntārān nirgatair devadattasya gṛhe snigdham bhuktam{*4/120*}, tena vayam arūkṣāḥ kṛtā iti, satsv apy anyeṣu snigdheṣv eva bhojaneṣu, evaṃ tasyārūkṣākaraṇasyābhighāraṇasyābhāvād rūkṣā iti vacanam upapadyate, asmiṃs tu sati nopapadyate. tasmād api prayājaśeṣeṇābhighāraṇaṃ prājāpatyānāṃ nāstīti.
children.translated_text: If it is seen thus — that the statement "they are rough" when basting exists is without indicative mark — [we reply:] it is not without indicative mark. This statement pertains to what produces moistening. Which is that? The first one — for the first produces moistening, not the second. That [statement] applies to what is moistened, and moistening is not applied to what is [already] moistened. Just as there is a saying in the world: "We who have emerged from the wilderness ate a rich meal at <s>Devadatta</s>'s house; thereby we were made not-rough" — even though other rich meals exist — likewise, because of the absence of the basting that removes roughness, the statement "rough" is appropriate; but when it [the prayāja-basting] exists, it is not appropriate. Therefore, the basting of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [victims] with the <s>prayāja</s> remainder does not exist.

children.text: syāt tasya mukhyatvāt // MS_4,1.39 //
children.translated_text: It would [exist], because of the primacy of that [basting]. // MS_4,1.39 //

children.text: idaṃ padottaraṃ sūtram{*4/121*}. yadi prathamasyābhāvāt savyā iti vacanaṃ bhavaty anupapannam, tarhy anyasya prathamasya vidyamānatvāt. katamat tat? yac chrapyamāṇāyā aparam udvāsitāyāḥ. atrocyate - syāt tasya mukhyatvāt, yat prayājaśeṣeṇābhighāraṇam, tasyaivābhāvād etad upapadyate, saty api śrapyamāṇāyā abhighāraṇa udvāsitāyāś ca, yat tāvac chrapyamāṇāyāḥ, tad agner arcīṃṣi dahanti, yad udvāsitāyāḥ, tad agnyavayavā{*4/122*} ūṣmāvayavāś ca nāśayanti, saiṣā rūkṣaiva, idaṃ tu prayājaśeṣeṇa śītāyāḥ kriyate, tat snehayati, tena snigdhāyāḥ padānakālam abhighāraṇaṃ yat, tan na snehayati. tad idaṃ snehanasyābhighāraṇasyābhāvāt savyatāvacanam upapadyata ity uktam, tasmān na prayājaśeṣo dhāryata iti.
children.translated_text: This is a supplementary sūtra. If the statement "rough" is possible because of the absence of the first [basting], then because of the existence of another first [basting]. Which is that? The one while [the vapā is] being cooked, and another after being taken off [the fire]. To this we say: it would [exist] because of the primacy of that — the basting with the <s>prayāja</s> remainder — because of the absence of precisely that, this [statement about roughness] is appropriate, even though the basting while cooking and of the taken-off [vapā] exist. For the basting while cooking — the flames of the fire burn it; the basting of the taken-off — the components of fire and heat destroy [it]. So the [vapā] remains indeed rough. But this [basting] with the <s>prayāja</s> remainder is applied when [the vapā is] cold; that moistens it. Therefore the basting that occurs when the [vapā] is not at the time of moistening does not moisten. This statement about roughness is appropriate because of the absence of the moistening basting — so it has been stated. Therefore the <s>prayāja</s> remainder should not be retained.

children.text: samānayanaṃ tu mukhyaṃ syāl liṅgadarśanāt // MS_4,1.40 //
children.translated_text: But the bringing together would be primary, because of indicative evidence. // MS_4,1.40 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - atihāyeḍo barhiḥ prati samānayatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ samānayanam ājyasya dharmāṇāṃ ca prayojakam, utāprayojakam iti. kiṃ prāptam? aprayojakam iti. kutaḥ? prayājānuyājārthasyājyasyāyam ekadeśaḥ samānīyata iti, pūrveṇa nyāyenāprayojakatā prāptā. tad ucyate - mukhyaṃ samānayanaṃ liṅgadarśanāt. kiṃ liṅgam? caturgṛhītāny ājyāni bhavanti, na hy atrānuyājān yakṣyan bhavatīty ātithyāyāṃ śrūyate, yadi prayājārthaṃ samānayanam, tatas tatraikaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ samānīyate. ekam apy anuyājānāṃ bhavati, tataś cātithyeḍāṃ tā saṃtiṣṭhata ity anuyājābhāva upabhṛti samānayanārtham ekaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ grāhyam, na tv anuyājārtham. tatra bahūnāṃ caturgṛhītānāṃ darśanam upapadyate, itarathā hy anuyājābhāve naivopabhṛti catur gṛhyeta, tatra caturgṛhītānīti bahuvacanaṃ nopapadyate. tasmāt prayojakaṃ samānayanam iti.
nanu liṅgam upadiśyate, kā prāptiḥ? ucyate - dṛṣṭaṃ tatra prayojanaṃ prayājau dvau yaṣṭavyau, tatra juhvām ājyena prayojanaṃ nopabhṛti riktāyām, upabhṛto recanam adṛṣṭārthaṃ juhvāṃ nidhānaṃ dṛṣṭārtham eva. tena prayājahomārtham ājyasamānayanam aupabhṛtam ājyaṃ [461]{*4/124*} prayojayati. tad api hi prayājārtham anuyājārthaṃ ceti vakṣyate.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: "Passing beyond the <s>iḍā</s>, he brings [the ghee] together onto the sacrificial grass." There a doubt [arises]: is the bringing together (<s>samānayana</s>) of the <s>ājya</s> productive of [further] rites, or not? What is the prima facie view? Not productive. Why? Because this remainder of <s>ājya</s> taken for the <s>prayāja</s> and <s>anuyāja</s> purposes is being brought together — by the previous reasoning, non-productivity is established. To this we say: the bringing together is primary, because of indicative evidence. What is the indicative mark? "The <s>ājyas</s> taken four times (<s>caturgṛhīta</s>) exist" — in the <s>Ātithya</s> (hospitality rite), it is heard: "for here he is not about to offer the <s>anuyājas</s>." If the bringing together is for the <s>prayāja</s> purpose, then one <s>caturgṛhīta</s> is brought together there. One [caturgṛhīta] is also for the <s>anuyājas</s>; then [in the phrase] "with these the <s>Ātithya-iḍā</s> is concluded," in the absence of <s>anuyājas</s>, one <s>caturgṛhīta</s> should be taken in the <s>upabhṛt</s> (offering ladle) for the purpose of bringing together, but not for the <s>anuyāja</s> purpose. There, the evidence of many <s>caturgṛhītas</s> is appropriate; otherwise, in the absence of <s>anuyājas</s>, no <s>caturgṛhīta</s> would be taken in the <s>upabhṛt</s>, and the plural "<s>caturgṛhītāni</s>" would not be appropriate. Therefore the bringing together is productive.
But indicative evidence is being taught — what is the prima facie entailment? We reply: the visible purpose there is that two <s>prayājas</s> are to be offered; for that, there is purpose for <s>ājya</s> in the <s>juhū</s>, not in the empty <s>upabhṛt</s>. The emptying of the <s>upabhṛt</s> serves an unseen purpose; the placing in the <s>juhū</s> serves a visible purpose alone. Therefore the bringing together of the <s>upabhṛt</s>'s <s>ājya</s> [461] for the purpose of <s>prayāja</s> oblation makes [that ājya] productive. For it will be stated that it too is for the <s>prayāja</s> and <s>anuyāja</s> purposes.

children.text: vacane hi hetvasāmarthye // MS_4,1.41 //
children.translated_text: For in a [mere] statement, the reason would be unsupported. // MS_4,1.41 //

children.text: atha kasmān na vacanam etat, na caturgṛhītāny ājyānīti. ucyate, vacane hi hetur asamarthitaḥ syāt, na hy atrānuyājān yakṣyan bhavatīti. yadā samānayanaṃ na prayājārtham iti gamyate, tadā vacanam. yadā vacanam, tadā nānuyājābhāvo hetuḥ, asati hetau, na hy atrānuyājān yakṣyan bhavatīti hetuvan nigado nopapadyeta. tasmāt prayājārthaṃ samānayanaṃ prayojakam aupabhṛtasyājyasya. kiṃ bhavati prayojanam? paryājārthe samānayane yāvat prayājārtham, tāvat sarvaṃ samāneyam, ardham aupabhṛtasya, aprayojanakatve na niyogato 'rdhaṃ yāvat tādvat vā.
children.translated_text: But why is this not [merely] a statement — "the <s>ājyas</s> are <s>caturgṛhīta</s>"? We reply: in a [mere] statement, the reason would be unsupported — "for here he is not about to offer the <s>anuyājas</s>." When it is understood that the bringing together is not for the <s>prayāja</s> purpose, then it is a [mere] statement. When it is a statement, then the absence of <s>anuyājas</s> is not the reason; without a reason, the reasoned statement "for here he is not about to offer the <s>anuyājas</s>" would not be appropriate. Therefore the bringing together is for the <s>prayāja</s> purpose and is productive of the <s>upabhṛt</s>'s <s>ājya</s>. What is the [further] purpose? When bringing together is for the <s>prayāja</s> purpose, as much as is [needed] for the <s>prayāja</s> purpose, that much of the whole should be brought together — half of the <s>upabhṛt</s>'s [ghee]. If not productive, then not necessarily half, or any [fixed] amount.

children.text: tatrotpattir avibhaktā syāt // MS_4,1.42 //
children.translated_text: There, the origination would be undivided. // MS_4,1.42 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - caturjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāty aṣṭāv upabhṛti gṛhṇātīti{*4/125*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ jauhavam aupabhṛtaṃ cobhayam ubhayārtham, prayājebhyaś cānuyājebhyaś ca, uta jauhavaṃ prayājebhyaḥ, aupabhṛtam anuyājebhyaḥ? athavā aupabhṛtaṃ prayājebhyo 'nuyājebhyaś ceti. kiṃ prāptam? ubhayam ubhayārtham. kutaḥ? yad yad ājyena kriyate, tasmai tasmai bhavitum arhaty aviśeṣāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: "He takes four [measures] in the <s>juhū</s>; he takes eight in the <s>upabhṛt</s>." There a doubt [arises]: are both the <s>juhū</s>-portion and the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion for both purposes — for both <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> — or is the <s>juhū</s>-portion for the <s>prayājas</s> and the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion for the <s>anuyājas</s>? Or is the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion for both <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s>? What is the prima facie view? Both for both purposes. Why? Whatever act is performed with <s>ājya</s>, it should serve all [such acts], because there is no distinction.

children.text: tatra jauhavam anuyājapratiṣedhārtham // MS_4,1.43 //
children.translated_text: There, the <s>juhū</s>-portion serves to exclude the <s>anuyājas</s>. // MS_4,1.43 //

children.text:
naivam, ubhayam ubhayārtham iti, jauhavaṃ prayājārtham, aupa[462]{*4/126*}bhṛtam ubhayārtham. katham? yaj juhvāṃ gṛhṇāti, ṛtubhyas tad gṛhṇāti, ṛtavo vai prayājā iti jauhavavacanam anuyājapratiṣedhārthaṃ prayājān saṃkīrtayati.
āha, nanu nāsty atrānuyājapratiṣedhārthaṃ vacanam, yad etat prayājebhyas tad gṛhṇātīti{*4/127*}, prayājeṣūpadeśakam etat, nāsty asyānuyājapratiṣedhe sāmarthyam iti. ucyate - na brūmaḥ, pratiṣedhakam etad iti. kiṃ tūtpattivākya ājyānāṃ naiva prayojanābhisaṃbandhaḥ, anena vacanena prayājaprayojanatā kriyate jauhavasya, anuyājaprayojanatāsya vacanābhāvād eva na gamyata iti, anuyājapratiṣedhārthaṃ vacanam ity ucyate.
children.translated_text:
Not so — [it is not the case that] both [serve] both purposes. The <s>juhū</s>-portion is for the <s>prayāja</s> purpose; the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion [462] is for both purposes. How? "What he takes in the <s>juhū</s>, he takes that for the <s>ṛtus</s> (seasons); the seasons are indeed the <s>prayājas</s>" — the statement about the <s>juhū</s>-portion, by mentioning the <s>prayājas</s>, serves to exclude the <s>anuyājas</s>.
[The objector] says: but there is no statement here for the purpose of excluding the <s>anuyājas</s> — this statement "he takes that for the <s>prayājas</s>" is instructive regarding the <s>prayājas</s>, and has no force in prohibiting the <s>anuyājas</s>. We reply: we do not say this is prohibitive. Rather, in the origination-sentence of the <s>ājyas</s>, there is simply no connection with purpose. By this statement, the <s>prayāja</s>-purpose of the <s>juhū</s>-portion is established; the <s>anuyāja</s>-purpose is simply not understood because of the absence of a statement — so it is called "a statement for the purpose of excluding the <s>anuyājas</s>."

children.text: aupabhṛtaṃ tatheti cet // MS_4,1.44 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues that] the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion is likewise — // MS_4,1.44 //

children.text: iti ced dṛśyate, jauhavam anuyājebhyaḥ pratiṣidhyate, aupabhṛtam ubhayārtham iti, bhavatu jauhavaṃ prayājārtham, na tv aupabhṛtam ubhayārtham. tad api tathā syāt, yathā jauhavam. katham? etad apy anuyājārtham eva śrūyate, yad upabhṛti gṛhṇāty anuyājebhyas tad gṛhṇāti chandāṃsi hy anuyājā iti. anuyājārthatāsyeti.
children.translated_text: If it is seen thus — the <s>juhū</s>-portion is excluded from the <s>anuyājas</s>, and the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion serves both purposes — let the <s>juhū</s>-portion be for the <s>prayāja</s> purpose; but the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion should not serve both purposes. It too should be like the <s>juhū</s>-portion. How? It too is heard as serving the <s>anuyāja</s> purpose alone: "What he takes in the <s>upabhṛt</s>, he takes that for the <s>anuyājas</s>; the meters (<s>chandas</s>) are indeed the <s>anuyājas</s>." [This shows] its <s>anuyāja</s>-purpose.

children.text: syāj juhūpratiṣedhān nityānuvādaḥ // MS_4,1.45 //
children.translated_text: It would be an invariable restatement, because of the exclusion from the <s>juhū</s>. // MS_4,1.45 //

children.text: naitad evam, ubhayārthaṃ hy aupabhṛtam, evaṃ hi śrūyate - yad aṣṭāv upabhṛti gṛhṇāti prayājānuyājebhyas tad gṛhṇātīti{*4/128*}. nanūktam, anuyājebhyas tad gṛhṇātīty anuyājārthatāsyeti. ucyate, juhūpratiṣedhān nityānuvādaḥ. ubhayasminn aupabhṛte jauhave ca{*4/129*} ubhayārthe prāpte jauhavam anuyājebhyaḥ pratiṣiddham, naupabhṛtam, tad aupabhṛtasyobhayārthatāyāṃ satyām anu[463]{*4/130*}yājārthatāvacanaṃ nityānuvādo bhavitum arhati, na śaknoti prayājārthatāṃ pratiṣeddhum, pratyakṣaśrutā hi sā, tasmād aupabhṛtam ubhayārtham. samānayanaṃ ca tato juhvāṃ śrūyate, tasmād api prayājārthatā na śakyā bādhitum.
children.translated_text: This is not so — the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion serves both purposes, for thus it is heard: "What eight [measures] he takes in the <s>upabhṛt</s>, he takes that for both <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s>." But was it not stated that "he takes that for the <s>anuyājas</s>" shows its <s>anuyāja</s>-purpose? We reply: because of the exclusion from the <s>juhū</s>, it is an invariable restatement (<s>nityānuvāda</s>). When both the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion and the <s>juhū</s>-portion serve both purposes, the <s>juhū</s>-portion is excluded from the <s>anuyājas</s>, but not the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion. Given the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion's dual purpose, [463] the statement of <s>anuyāja</s>-purpose should be an invariable restatement; it cannot prohibit the <s>prayāja</s>-purpose, for that is heard by direct statement. Therefore the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion serves both purposes. And the bringing together is then heard as [going] into the <s>juhū</s>; therefore the <s>prayāja</s>-purpose cannot be overridden.

children.text: tadaṣṭasaṃkhyaṃ śravaṇāt // MS_4,1.46 //
children.translated_text: Its number of eight is because of the statement. // MS_4,1.46 //

children.text: aṣṭāv upabhṛti gṛhṇātīti{*4/131*} śrūyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ tad aupabhṛtam ājyam aṣṭasaṃkhyena grahaṇena saṃskriyate, uta catuḥsaṃkhyā guṇabhūtā dvayor grahaṇayor iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? aṣṭasaṃkhyā guṇabhūtā, na catuḥsaṃkhye dve iti. kutaḥ? śravaṇād aṣṭasaṃkhyā śrūyate, catuḥsaṃkhyā aṣṭasaṃkhyayā lakṣyate, śrutilakṣaṇāviśaye ca śrutir nyāyyā, tasmād aṣṭasaṃkhyaṃ grahaṇam etad iti.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'He takes eight [measures] in the <s>upabhṛt</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is that <s>aupabhṛta</s> (upabhṛt-portion) ghee sanctified by taking it in the number of eight, or is the number of four subsidiary, [yielding] two takings? What is the prima facie view? The number of eight is subsidiary, not two [takings] of the number four. Why? Because from the Vedic statement the number eight is heard; the number four is indicated by the number eight; and where direct statement and indication are [both applicable], the direct statement is authoritative. Therefore this is a taking of eight.

NOTES:
[{4/131: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.3.5.5}]

children.text: anugrahāc ca jauhavasya // MS_4,1.47 //
children.translated_text: And because of the supportive statement regarding the <s>jauhava</s> (offering into the <s>juhū</s>). // MS_4,1.47 //

children.text: anugrahavādaś ca bhavati - caturgṛhītaṃ vā etad abhūt tasyāghāram āghārya triritaḥ{*4/132*} prācīnaṃ{*4/133*} prayājān yajati samānayate caturgṛhītatvāyeti caturgṛhītānugrahaḥ kathaṃ syād iti. kiṃ caturgṛhītaṃ bhavati samānayanena? neti brūmaḥ, caturgṛhītaṃ prathamam eva tat, āghāre 'py āghārite, yad avaśiṣṭaṃ catuḥsaṃkhyam eva tasya grahaṇam āsīt. kiṃ tarhi caturgṛhītatvāyeti. caturgṛhītasyānugrahārtham, alpaṃ hi caturgṛhītaṃ homāyāparyāptam, tat paryāptaṃ kathaṃ syād iti. evaṃ caturgṛhītaśabdenālpam iti lakṣyate, alpatvaṃ ca bahutvaṃ kasyacid apekṣya bhavati, yadi hy aupabhṛtam aṣṭasaṃkhyam evaṃ caturgṛhītam [464]{*4/134*} alpaṃ bhavati, tatra{*4/135*} caturgṛhītaśabdena alpatā śakyate lakṣayitum. tasmād api paśyāmaḥ, aupabhṛte 'ṣṭasaṃkhyā guṇabhūteti.
children.translated_text: There is also a supportive statement: 'This was indeed <s>caturgṛhīta</s> (taken four times); having poured the <s>āghāra</s> from it, he offers the <s>prayājas</s> three times toward the east; he brings together for the sake of making it <s>caturgṛhīta</s> [again]' — how could the support for the <s>caturgṛhīta</s> apply? Does it become <s>caturgṛhīta</s> by the bringing together? No, we say — it was <s>caturgṛhīta</s> from the very beginning; even after the <s>āghāra</s> has been poured, what remains — the taking of that was of the number four only. Then what does 'for the sake of making it <s>caturgṛhīta</s>' mean? It is for the support of what is [already] <s>caturgṛhīta</s> — for the <s>caturgṛhīta</s> [portion] is small, insufficient for oblation; how could it become sufficient? Thus by the word '<s>caturgṛhīta</s>' smallness is indicated, and smallness and largeness exist relative to something. For if the <s>aupabhṛta</s> [portion] is of the number eight, then the <s>caturgṛhīta</s> [464] is small. In that case, the smallness can be indicated by the word '<s>caturgṛhīta</s>.' Therefore by this too we see that in the <s>aupabhṛta</s>, the number eight is subsidiary.

children.text: dvayos tu hetusāmarthyaṃ śravaṇaṃ ca samānayane // MS_4,1.48 //
children.translated_text: But in [the case of] two, the strength of reasoning and the Vedic statement [support] the bringing together. // MS_4,1.48 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati, dve ete caturgṛhīte, evaṃ hetuḥ samarthito bhavaty ātithyāyām, caturgṛhītāny ājyāni bhavanti, na hy atrānuyājān yakṣyan bhavatīti{*4/136*}, asatsv apy anuyājeṣv etad aṣṭagṛhītam evaupabhṛtaṃ bhavet. yadāṣṭasaṃkhyā guṇabhūtā, na tadā dvayoś caturgṛhītayoḥ satoś caturgṛhītān{*4/137*} ājyānīti bahuvacanam ājyeṣūpapadyate. tasmāc caturgṛhīte dve iti.
āha, liṅgam etat prāptir ucyatām iti. tad abhidhīyate, anārabhya ucyate, caturgṛhītaṃ juhotīti sarvahomeṣu, tena prayājānuyājeṣv api na tad aṣṭagṛhītena śakyate bādhitum, nānāviṣayatvāt. aṣṭagṛhītaṃ hi grahaṇe, caturgṛhītaṃ hi home, asti hi saṃbhavaḥ, yad aṣṭagṛhītaṃ gṛhyeta, caturgṛhītaṃ hūyeta, tad etad ihāṣṭatvam grahaṇe bhavati. kathaṃ dve caturgṛhīte home sampādayet? tasmād dve ete caturgṛhīte, aṣṭagṛhīte gṛhyamāṇe gṛhyete. caturgṛhīte dve nāgṛhītvāṣṭagṛhītaṃ{*4/138*} kaścit sampādayet. tasmād dve ete caturgṛhīte iti.
atha yad uktam, aṣṭagṛhītaṃ śrūyate, śrutiś ca lakṣaṇāyā garīyasīti, ucyate - uktam asmābhir aṣṭasaṃkhyāyāḥ prayojanam, kathaṃ dve caturgṛhīte syātām iti. api ca, aṣṭāv upabhṛti gṛhṇātīty upabhṛti samānīte dve caturgṛhīte kathaṃ syātām iti. itarathāsaty aṣṭaśabde nānāpātrayor gṛhyeyātām. tasmād aṣṭaśabdaśravaṇam adoṣaḥ, sādhv etat, dve caturgṛhīte [465]{*4/139*} upabhṛtīti. prayojanam, dvayoś caturgṛhītayoḥ satoḥ samānayane 'rdhaṃ samānetavyaṃ bhavati, aṣṭagṛhīte sati na niyogato 'rdham. tathā yatrānuyājārthaṃ na grahaṇam, tatrāpy aṣṭagṛhītam, yathā pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. yathā ca siddhāntaḥ, tathā cāturmāsyeṣu caturgṛhītam upabhṛti bhavati.
children.translated_text:
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) refutes the [previous] position. These are two <s>caturgṛhītas</s> — thus the reasoning is established in the <s>Ātithya</s> [rite]: 'The <s>ājyas</s> are <s>caturgṛhīta</s>; for here he is not about to offer the <s>anuyājas</s>' — even though the <s>anuyājas</s> are absent, this <s>aupabhṛta</s> [portion] would be of eight [measures]. When the number eight is subsidiary, the plural '<s>caturgṛhīta</s> <s>ājyas</s>' is not fitting when there are two <s>caturgṛhītas</s> [present in the ladles]. Therefore, [there are] two <s>caturgṛhītas</s>.
[The objector] says: this is an indicatory mark; let the entailment be stated. To that we reply: it is said without reference [to a specific case] — '<s>caturgṛhīta</s> [ghee] is offered' applies to all oblations. By that, in the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> too, it cannot be overridden by [a taking of] eight, because they have different domains. For the eight-[fold] taking applies to the taking, while the <s>caturgṛhīta</s> applies to the offering. There is indeed the possibility that what is taken as eight is offered as <s>caturgṛhīta</s> — so this eightness applies to the taking. How could two <s>caturgṛhītas</s> be effected in the offering? Therefore these are two <s>caturgṛhītas</s>; when taken as eight, they are taken [as two sets of four]. No one could effect an eight-fold taking without taking two <s>caturgṛhītas</s>. Therefore these are two <s>caturgṛhītas</s>.
Now, as to what was said — 'the number eight is heard, and direct statement is weightier than indication' — we reply: the purpose of the number eight has been stated by us — how two <s>caturgṛhītas</s> could exist. Moreover, 'he takes eight in the <s>upabhṛt</s>' — when the two <s>caturgṛhītas</s> are brought together in the <s>upabhṛt</s>, how could [they exist separately]? Otherwise, without the word 'eight,' they could be taken in different vessels. Therefore the hearing of the word 'eight' is not a fault. This is correct: two <s>caturgṛhītas</s> [465] in the <s>upabhṛt</s>. The purpose: when there are two <s>caturgṛhītas</s>, half should be brought together at the bringing-together; when there is [only] an eight-fold taking, not necessarily half. Likewise in the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites, the <s>upabhṛt</s>-portion is <s>caturgṛhīta</s>.

children.text: svarus tv anekaniṣpattiḥ svakarmaśabdatvāt // MS_4,2.1 //
children.translated_text: But the <s>svaru</s> (sacrificial post chip) has a separate production, because of the word denoting its own action. // MS_4,2.1 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ, yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*4/140*}, tatredam āmnātam - khādire badhnāti, pālāśe badhnāti, rohite badhnātīti. tat saṃnidhāv idam aparam āmnāyate, svaruṇā paśum anakti yūpasya svaruṃ karotīti.
athedānīm idaṃ saṃdihyate, kiṃ bhedena yūpāt svarur utpādayitavyaḥ, uta yūpaṃ kriyamāṇam anuniṣpannaḥ śakalo grahītavya iti. tatredaṃ tāvan naḥ parīkṣyam, kiṃ chedanādyutpatteḥ prayojakaḥ svaruḥ, utāprayojakaḥ{*4/141*}? prayojakaś cet, bhedena yūpān niṣpādyeta. na cet prayojakaḥ, yūpaṃ niṣpadyamānam anuniṣpannaḥ śakalo grahīṣyata iti. sa kathaṃ prayojakaḥ syāt? kathaṃ vā na prayojaka iti. yady eṣā vacanavyaktiḥ, svaruśabdavācyaṃ bhāvyate. kathaṃ? joṣaṇādinetikartavyatāviśeṣeṇeti. tataḥ, svaruṇā paśum anaktīti, sa svarur ity avagato grahīṣyate, tataḥ prayojakaḥ. athaivaṃ vijñāyate, svaruṇā paśum anaktīty anavagataḥ svaruḥ. etāvad asya{*4/142*} vijñāyate 'ñjanaṃ tena kriyata iti, idam api, yūpasya svaruṃ karotīti yūpaikadeśaṃ svarukārye 'ñjane viniyuṅkta iti tato 'prayojakaḥ.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? svarus tv anekaniṣpattiḥ svakarmaśabdatvāt, svarur na yūpenaikaniṣpattiḥ syāt, yūpam anapekṣamāṇasya svaror jo[467]{*4/143*}ṣaṇādinotpattiḥ. kutaḥ? svakarmaśabdatvāt. svo hy asya karmaśabdaḥ svarutāyā vidhāyako bhavati, svaruṃ karotīti. evaṃ ca yūpakāṣṭāvayavasya svarutvaṃ kriyata iti, yūpasya svaruṃ karotīti lakṣaṇayā yūpaśabdaḥ, khadirādyavayavasyety arthaḥ. kutaḥ? svarutvabhāvanā hi śrutyā gamyate, svaruṃ karotīti svarum utpādayatīti. yūpāvayavopādānaṃ vākyena, vākyāc ca śrutir balīyasīti. tasmād evaṃ sati na niyogato yūpakāṣṭhād eva svarur utpādayitavyaḥ, nirapekṣād anyasmād api vṛkṣāt kartavyo bhedeneti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is an animal sacred to <s>Agni-Soma</s> (<s>Agnīṣomīya</s>), [as stated]: 'He who is consecrated slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> victim.' There, this is taught: 'He binds [the victim] to a post of <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu) wood, he binds to a post of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma) wood, he binds to a post of <s>rohita</s> wood.' Then in proximity to this, another [statement] is taught: 'He anoints the victim with the <s>svaru</s>; he makes a <s>svaru</s> of the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>).'
Now a doubt arises here: should the <s>svaru</s> be produced separately from the <s>yūpa</s>, or should a chip (<s>śakala</s>) that is produced incidentally while making the <s>yūpa</s> be taken? Here this must first be examined by us: is the <s>svaru</s> the cause of the cutting and other [operations], or is it not the cause? If it is the cause, it should be produced separately from the <s>yūpa</s>. If it is not the cause, a chip incidentally produced while making the <s>yūpa</s> should be taken. How could it be the cause? And how could it not be the cause? If the verbal expression is such [that] what is denoted by the word <s>svaru</s> is to be brought into being — how? By the specific procedural acts of planing (<s>joṣaṇa</s>) and so on. Then, 'he anoints the victim with the <s>svaru</s>' — that understood <s>svaru</s> would be taken, and therefore it is a cause. But if it is understood thus: 'he anoints the victim with the <s>svaru</s>' — the <s>svaru</s> is not [independently] understood; only this much is understood: anointing is performed with it. Also, 'he makes a <s>svaru</s> of the <s>yūpa</s>' means he employs a portion of the <s>yūpa</s> for the <s>svaru</s>-purpose of anointing — therefore it is not a cause.
What is the prima facie view? The <s>svaru</s> has a separate production, not one production together with the <s>yūpa</s>; the <s>svaru</s>, independent of the <s>yūpa</s>, is produced through planing and other [operations] [467]. Why? Because of the word denoting its own action. For its own action-word is what enjoins <s>svaru</s>-ness — 'he makes the <s>svaru</s>.' And thus, 'the <s>svaru</s>-ness of a piece of <s>yūpa</s>-wood is effected' — the word <s>yūpa</s> in 'he makes a <s>svaru</s> of the <s>yūpa</s>' is used figuratively, meaning 'of a piece of <s>khadira</s> and other [wood].' Why? Because the bringing into being of <s>svaru</s>-ness is understood from the direct Vedic statement 'he makes the <s>svaru</s>' — meaning 'he produces the <s>svaru</s>.' The reference to a <s>yūpa</s>-portion as material is by sentence [construction], and the direct statement is stronger than the sentence. Therefore, given this, the <s>svaru</s> need not necessarily be produced from the <s>yūpa</s>-wood alone; it can also be made separately from any other tree independently.

children.text: jātyantarāc ca śaṅkate // MS_4,2.2 //
children.translated_text: And he suspects [the possibility of obtaining it] from another species [of wood]. // MS_4,2.2 //

children.text: itaś ca nirapekṣasya svaror utpattir iti gamyate. kutaḥ? jātyantarād apy āśaṅkā bhavati, vṛkṣāntarāt{*4/144*}. katham? nānyasya svaruṃ kuryāt, yady anyasya vṛkṣasya svaruṃ kuryāt, anye 'sya lokam anvāroheyuḥ, yūpasya svaruṃ karotīti. na hi yūpam anuniṣpannasya garhaṇe jātyantarāśaṅkāvakalpate, yūpaśakalo hi svarukārye tadānīṃ viniyujyate. tasmād api bhedena yūpāt svarur utpādayitavya iti.
children.translated_text: For this reason too, it is understood that the <s>svaru</s> is produced independently. Why? Because there is also a suspicion regarding [wood of] another species — of another tree. How? 'One should not make a <s>svaru</s> from another [tree]; if one were to make a <s>svaru</s> from another tree, others would follow him to the [other] world; he makes a <s>svaru</s> of the <s>yūpa</s>.' For this censure of [wood of] another species does not apply when [the chip] is incidentally produced from the <s>yūpa</s>, since at that time the <s>yūpa</s>-chip is employed for the <s>svaru</s>-purpose. Therefore by this too, the <s>svaru</s> should be produced separately from the <s>yūpa</s>.

children.text: tad ekadeśo vā svarutvasya tannimittatvāt // MS_4,2.3 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a portion of that [yūpa], because of <s>svaru</s>-ness being caused by it. // MS_4,2.3 //

children.text:
vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. yūpaikadeśo hi yūpam anuniṣpannaḥ śakalo grahītavya iti. kasmāt? evam āmnāyate - yady anyasya vṛkṣasya svaruṃ kuryāt, anye 'sya lokam anvāroheyuḥ, yūpasya svaruṃ karotīti. na cātrāyam artho vidhīyate, svarum utpādayatīti. kiṃ tarhi? svarukāryaṃ kartuṃ yam upādatte, taṃ yūpād iti. kutaḥ? svarutvasya tannimittatvāt, svarutvam atra śrūyate svaroḥ, yūpasya svaruṃ karoti [468]{*4/145*} iti. kasyātmīyam? yūpasyeti, ātmīyaś ca samudāyasyaikadeśo bhavati, tasmād idam ucyate, aprāṇinaḥ ṣaṣṭhī pañcamy arthe bhavati, yathā śākasya dehi, śākād dehīti, tathā kvacit tṛtīyārthe, ghṛtasya yajati, ghṛtena yajati. pañcamy arthe, ghṛtād yajati, ghṛtasya yajatīti. dvitīyārthe vā, somasya pibati, somaṃ pibati, somāt pibatīti.
nanūktam, yūpāvayavo 'tra vākyena vidhīyate, śrutyā svaror utpattiḥ, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasīti. ucyate, satyam, evam, yūpasyeti tu śabdo 'vivakṣitārtho bhavati. tatra śrutir api bādhyate, vākyam api. na tv asmatpakṣe kiṃcid avivakṣitārtham, svaruṃ karotīti svārtha evānuvādo bhaviṣyatīti, yūpaśakalo vidhāyiṣyate. svaruśabdaś cāñjanārthena śakale upacarita iti gamyate, avayavaprasiddhiś caitam arthaṃ gamayiṣyati. bhavati hi brāhmaṇam - atha kasmāt svarur nāma? etasmād veṣo{*4/146*} 'vacchidyate, tad asyaitat svam ivārur bhavati, tasmāt svarur nāmeti{*4/147*}.
children.translated_text:
The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) refutes the [previous] position. A portion of the <s>yūpa</s>, a chip produced incidentally from the <s>yūpa</s>, should be taken. Why? For thus it is taught: 'If one were to make a <s>svaru</s> from another tree, others would follow him to the [other] world; he makes a <s>svaru</s> of the <s>yūpa</s>.' And here the meaning enjoined is not 'he produces a <s>svaru</s>.' Then what? That what he takes for the <s>svaru</s>-purpose, he takes from the <s>yūpa</s>. Why? Because <s>svaru</s>-ness is caused by that — <s>svaru</s>-ness is here heard of the <s>svaru</s>: 'he makes a <s>svaru</s> of the <s>yūpa</s>' [468]. Belonging to whom? To the <s>yūpa</s>. And what belongs [to something] is a portion of the whole. Therefore this is stated: for inanimate things, the genitive is used in the sense of the ablative — just as 'give from the vegetables,' 'give of the vegetables'; likewise sometimes in the sense of the instrumental — 'he sacrifices with ghee,' 'he sacrifices of ghee'; in the sense of the ablative — 'he sacrifices from ghee,' 'he sacrifices of ghee'; or in the sense of the accusative — 'he drinks <s>Soma</s>,' 'he drinks of <s>Soma</s>,' 'he drinks from <s>Soma</s>.'
Was it not said that the <s>yūpa</s>-portion is enjoined here by the sentence, while the origination of the <s>svaru</s> is by direct statement, and the direct statement is stronger than the sentence? We reply: that is true. But the word '<s>yūpa</s>' [in our interpretation] does not have an unintended meaning. In that case, both the direct statement and the sentence are overridden. But in our position, nothing has an unintended meaning — 'he makes a <s>svaru</s>' will be a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of what is [already] established; the <s>yūpa</s>-chip will be enjoined. And the word <s>svaru</s> is understood as used figuratively for the chip through [its association with] anointing. The well-known identity of [the chip as] a portion will convey this meaning. For there is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage: 'Now why is it called <s>svaru</s>? From this [yūpa] a piece is cut off, and that becomes like its own (<s>sva</s>) limb (<s>aru</s>); therefore it is called <s>svaru</s>.'

children.text: śakalaśruteś ca // MS_4,2.4 //
children.translated_text: And because of the Vedic statement regarding the chip. // MS_4,2.4 //

children.text: itaś ca yūpam anuniṣpannasya grahaṇam. kutaḥ? śakalaśruteḥ, śakalaśrutir bhavati svaroḥ, yaḥ prathamaḥ śakalaḥ parāpatet, sa svaruḥ kārya iti. śakalaś caikadeśaḥ, ekadeśaś cāprayojakaḥ, saṃbandhiśabdatvāt. tāvatā ca vyavahārāt samudāyāpekṣiṇaḥ. tatra prakaraṇād anyārthena khadirādinā joṣaṇādikarmaviśiṣṭena yāgārthena prakṛtenāsyaikavākyatā, yūpāya khadirādi joṣayate, chinatti, takṣati ca. tatra yaḥ śakalaḥ prathamaḥ parāptitas taṃ ca svarum añjanārthaṃ karotīti. svaruśabdaṃ ca tatrānuvadann evopacarati. tasmān naitad asti, pṛthaṅniṣpattiḥ svarur iti, [469]{*4/148*} yenānyasmād api vṛkṣād iti śaṅkyate. tasmāj jātyantarāśaṅkāvacanaṃ nityānuvādo yūpaśakalastutyarthaḥ.
children.translated_text: For this reason too, [there should be] a taking of what is produced incidentally from the <s>yūpa</s>. Why? Because of the Vedic statement regarding the chip — there is a Vedic statement about the chip of the <s>svaru</s>: 'Whichever chip falls off first, that should be made the <s>svaru</s>.' A chip is a portion, and a portion is non-causative, because of its being a relational term — [it functions] only insofar as it depends on the whole. In that context, by the contextual connection with what is established for another purpose — namely, <s>khadira</s> and other [wood] qualified by the specific ritual actions of planing and so on, [all] for the purpose of the sacrifice, which is the ongoing topic — there is syntactic unity. For the purpose of the <s>yūpa</s>, one planes, cuts, and shapes <s>khadira</s> [wood]. There, whichever chip falls off first, that he makes the <s>svaru</s> for the purpose of anointing. And in restating the word <s>svaru</s> there, he uses it figuratively. Therefore this does not hold — that the <s>svaru</s> has a separate production [469] — such that one might suspect [it could come] from another tree as well. Therefore the statement about suspecting another species is an invariable restatement (<s>nityānuvāda</s>) serving to praise the <s>yūpa</s>-chip.

children.text: pratiyūpaṃ ca darśanāt // MS_4,2.5 //
children.translated_text: And for each <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post), because of observation. // MS_4,2.5 //

children.text: itaś ca na pṛthaṅniṣpattiḥ svaruḥ. kutaḥ? ekādaśinyām, pratiyūpaṃ ca darśanāt, yathā, anupūrvaṃ svarubhiḥ paśūn samajya{*4/149*} madhyame raśanāguṇe sve sve{*4/150*} svaṃ svaṃ yūpaśakalam upagūhatīti svarubahutvaṃ darśayati, yadi ca svaruḥ pṛthaṅniṣpattiḥ syāt, eka evaikādaśinyāṃ tantreṇa kāryaṃ sādhayet. yūpam anuniṣpannasya tu grahaṇe prakṛtau svayūpaśakalenāñjanaṃ kṛtam ity ekādaśinyām api codakaḥ svayūpaśakalam eva prāpayatīti bahutvam upapannaṃ bhavati. svayūpaśakalagrahaṇaṃ ca prākṛtasya grahaṇād adhyavasīyate, yādṛśo 'sau prākṛtaḥ, tādṛśo 'sau garhītavyaḥ, na viśiṣṭa iti. tasmāt svarur utpatter na prayojaka iti.
children.translated_text: And from this too, the <s>svaru</s> (sacrificial chip) is not of separate production. Why? Because in the <s>Ekādaśinī</s> (eleven-victim sacrifice), it is seen for each sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) — as [stated]: 'In order, anointing the animals with the <s>svarus</s>, at the middle rope-strand, each at its own [post], one embraces one's own <s>yūpa</s>-chip' — this shows the multiplicity of <s>svarus</s>. If the <s>svaru</s> were of separate production, a single one in the <s>Ekādaśinī</s> could accomplish the purpose through the archetype (<s>tantra</s>). But when the taking is of what is produced along with the <s>yūpa</s>, in the basic rite the anointing is done with one's own <s>yūpa</s>-chip — thus in the <s>Ekādaśinī</s> too, the injunction yields only one's own <s>yūpa</s>-chip, and the multiplicity is established. The taking of one's own <s>yūpa</s>-chip is inferred from the taking of the archetypal [chip] — of whatever kind that archetypal one is, of that kind it is to be understood, not a special one. Therefore the <s>svaru</s> does not motivate [separate] production.

children.text: ādāne karotiśabdaḥ // MS_4,2.6 //
children.translated_text: The word <s>karoti</s> ('makes') [is used] in the sense of 'taking'. // MS_4,2.6 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, utpattir asya śabdenocyate, svaruṃ karotīti, evaṃ ca karotiśabdo 'vakalpiṣyata iti. ucyate, ādāne karotiśabdo bhaviṣyati, svaruṃ karoti, svarum ādatta iti. yathā kāṣṭhāni karoti, gomayāni karotīty ādāne karotiśabdo bhavati, evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam{*4/151*}.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'its production is stated by the word [karoti], as in "he makes (<s>karoti</s>) the <s>svaru</s>," and thus the word <s>karoti</s> would be taken [in the sense of production]' — we reply: the word <s>karoti</s> will be in the sense of 'taking' — 'he makes the <s>svaru</s>' means 'he takes the <s>svaru</s>.' Just as 'he makes firewood' and 'he makes cow-dung cakes' — the word <s>karoti</s> is [used] in the sense of taking — so too it should be seen here.

children.text: śākhāyāṃ tatpradhānatvāt // MS_4,2.7 //
children.translated_text: In the branch (<s>śākhā</s>), because of the primacy of that [branch]. // MS_4,2.7 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, śākhām adhikṛtya, prācīm āharaty udīcīm āharati prāgudīcīm āharatīti{*4/152*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ - kim ayaṃ digvādaḥ, uta śākhāvāda iti. digvāda iti prāptam, tathā śrutiśabdaḥ, śākhāvāde lakṣaṇeti. tasmād digvāda iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, śākhāvāda iti. kutaḥ? yadi tāvad ayam arthaḥ, prācī dig āhartavyeti, tato 'śakyo 'rthaḥ, atha prācīṃ diśaṃ pratyāharaṇīyeti, tataḥ kāhartavyeti, vākye śākhāśabdasyābhāvād anupapanno 'yaṃ saṃbandhaḥ. atha prakṛtā śākheti, tataḥ prācīśabdena tasyā evābhisaṃbandho nyāyyaḥ. kutaḥ? pratyakṣā hi prācīśabdena harater ekavākyatā, prakaraṇāc chākhāśabdena bhavet. ubhayathātra prācīśabdo lakṣaṇayā prakṛtāṃ vā śākhāṃ lakṣayet, diśo vānīpsitatvāt, vihāradeśam īpsitatamaṃ ayuktam{*4/153*}.
api ca, prācīti saṃbandhiśabdo 'yam, saṃbandhiśabdāś ca sarve sāpekṣāḥ, vinā padāntareṇa, na paripūrṇam artham abhivadanti, sāmānyapadārthasaṃbandhe ca saṃvyavahārānupapattiḥ, sarvasyaiva deśasya kutaścit prāgbhāvāt. tathā śākhāśabdo 'pi saṃbandhiśabdaḥ, vṛkṣasyety etad apekṣate. yadā vṛkṣasyety etad apekṣate, tadā vṛkṣasya śākhā prācī, udīcī, prāgudīcī veti bhavati saṃbandhaḥ, tathā ca saṃvyavahāro 'vakalpate. yat tu śākhāvāde [473]{*4/154*} lakṣaṇeti. ucyate, bhavati lakṣaṇayāpi śabdārthaḥ. tasmāc chākhāvāda iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard with reference to the branch: 'He brings [it] eastward, he brings [it] northward, he brings [it] northeast.' There a doubt [arises]: is this a statement about direction, or a statement about the branch? The prima facie view is that it is a statement about direction — thus the Vedic word (<s>śruti</s>) [directly denotes direction]; in the branch-interpretation it would be figurative (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). Therefore it is a statement about direction. Given this prima facie view, we say: it is a statement about the branch. Why? If the meaning were 'the eastern direction should be the destination,' then the meaning would be impossible. But if [it means] 'it should be brought toward the eastern direction,' then since the word <s>śākhā</s> ('branch') is absent from the sentence, this connection is unfounded. Rather, since the branch is the topic under discussion, the connection of the word <s>prācī</s> ('eastern') with that very [branch] is appropriate. Why? For the syntactic unity of the word <s>prācī</s> with 'bringing' is directly perceived, whereas [its connection] with the word <s>śākhā</s> would be through context. In both cases here, the word <s>prācī</s> would figuratively denote either the branch under discussion, or the direction — since the direction is not the [directly] desired [object], [to say] the place of ritual movement is the most desired would be inappropriate.
Moreover, <s>prācī</s> is a relational word, and all relational words are dependent — without another word they do not convey a complete meaning; and in connection with a general meaning, practical usage would be impossible, since every place is to the east of something. Likewise, the word <s>śākhā</s> ('branch') is also a relational word — it expects [the completion] 'of a tree.' When it expects 'of a tree,' then the connection becomes: the branch of the tree is eastern, northern, or northeastern — and practical usage is possible. As for the objection that 'in the branch-interpretation, it would be figurative' — we reply: meaning is possible through figurative usage too. Therefore it is a statement about the branch.

children.text: śākhāyāṃ tatpradhānatvād upaveṣeṇa vibhāgaḥ syād vaiṣamyaṃ tat // MS_4,2.8 //
children.translated_text: In the branch, because of the primacy of that, the division should be by cutting — that is the disparity. // MS_4,2.8 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ samāmnāyate, mūlataḥ śākhāṃ parivāsyopaveṣaṃ karotīti. tatrāyam arthaḥ sāṃśayikaḥ, kiṃ śākhāchedanasyobhayaṃ{*4/155*} prayojakam, śākhā upaveṣaś ca, uta śākhā prayojakā, upaveṣo 'nuniṣpādīti. kiṃ prāptam? ubhayaṃ chedanān niṣpadyate, śākhā śākhāmūlaṃ ca, ubhayaṃ ca prayojanavat. agreṇa vatsāpākaraṇādi kariṣyate, mūlata upaveṣaḥ, tena viśeṣābhāvād ubhayaṃ prayojakam.
iti prāpte, ucyate, śākhāyāṃ brūmaḥ, tatpradhānatvāt, śākhāpradhānatvād{*4/156*} upaveṣeṇa vibhāgo bhavet. śākhām anuniṣpanno gṛhyate. kathaṃ tatprādhānyam? śākhāṃ parivāsyeti dvitīyānirdeśāt. nanūpaveṣaṃ karotīty api dvitīyā. ucyate, nāsau parivāsayateḥ karma. kasya tarhi? karoteḥ.
āha, kasmād evam abhisaṃbandho na bhavati, śākhāṃ parivāsya mūlata upaveṣaṃ karotīti, śākhāśabdaś ca yathaivāgre tathā mūle 'pi. tatrāyam arthaḥ, chedenāgramūle vibhajet. [474]{*4/157*} kiṃ prayojanam? vibhajya mūlam, upaveṣaṃ kariṣyāmīti{*4/158*}. ucyate, naivam, vyavahitakalpanā hy evaṃ bhavet, avayavadhānena śākhārthaṃ parivāsanam, vṛtte tasminn upaveṣakaraṇam.
nanu prakṛtatvān mūlam upaveṣaśabdena saṃbadhyate. ucyate, ubhayasaṃbandhe virodhaḥ. virodhe ca prakaraṇād vākyaṃ balīyaḥ. atha saṃnihitena saṃbadhyate, tathāpi śākhāprayuktenety āpatati. ataḥ{*4/159*} siddham eva, uvaveṣo{*4/160*} na prayojayati chedanam iti. etad atra vaiṣamyam.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is recorded: 'He strips the branch from the root and makes a cut (<s>upaveṣa</s>).' There, this is the doubtful meaning: are both — the branch and the cut — motivating factors for the cutting of the branch? Or is the branch the motivating factor while the cut is merely a by-product? What is the prima facie view? Both are motivating factors for the cutting — both the branch and the branch-root are produced [from cutting], and both have purpose. With the tip, one will perform the driving away of calves and such; from the root, the cut-piece [is taken]. Given no distinction, both are motivating.
Given this prima facie view, we say: we hold [it is] for the branch, because of the primacy of that — because of the primacy of the branch, the division would be by the cut-piece. The cut-piece is taken as produced along with the branch. How is there primacy of that? Because of the accusative case designation in 'he strips the branch' (<s>śākhāṃ parivāsya</s>). But the accusative also occurs in 'he makes the cut-piece' (<s>upaveṣaṃ karoti</s>). We reply: that [cut-piece] is not the object of 'stripping' (<s>parivāsayati</s>). Of what then? Of 'making' (<s>karoti</s>).
[The objector] says: why should the construction not be thus — 'having stripped the branch, he makes a cut-piece from the root' — and the word <s>śākhā</s> applies to the root just as to the tip? There the meaning would be: by cutting, he divides the tip and root. What is the purpose? Having divided the root, 'I shall make the cut-piece.' We reply: not so, for that would require a forced construction with intervening [elements] — the stripping is for the branch-purpose with [something] intervening, and when that is completed, the making of the cut-piece [follows].
But is not the root connected with the word <s>upaveṣa</s> because it is the topic? We reply: when there is connection with both, there is conflict. And in conflict, sentence [evidence] is stronger than context. But if [one says] it is connected with what is proximate — even then, it follows that [it is connected] with what is brought about by the branch. Therefore it is established that the cut-piece does not motivate the cutting. This is the disparity here.

children.text: śrutyapāyāc ca // MS_4,2.9 //
children.translated_text: And because of the loss of the Vedic word. // MS_4,2.9 //

children.text: śākhayā vatsān apākaroti{*4/161*}, śākhayā gāḥ prāpayati, śākhayā dohayatīty{*4/162*}evamādiṣu śākhāgrahaṇeṣu nopaveṣasya vyāpāras tataḥ śākhāśabdo 'paiti. na hi tanmūlaṃ śākhety ācakṣate. kim ataḥ? yatraivaṃ{*4/163*} yatra śākhāśabdaḥ, tadarthaṃ chedanam, dvitīyānirdeśāt. athāpi mūle śākhāśabdo bhavet, evam api śākhāśabdopadiṣṭeṣu na mūlam, amūlaparivāsitatvāt. yac caivaṃ saṃskṛtayā śākhayā kriyate, tadarthaṃ chedanam. na copadhānaṃ mūlaparivāsitayā kriyate. tasmān na tadarthaṃ chedanam. kiṃ bhavati prayojanam? paurṇamāsyām api śākhotpādyā, yathā pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. yathā siddhāntaḥ, tathā notpādayitavyeti.
children.translated_text: In [passages such as] 'with the branch he drives away the calves,' 'with the branch he brings the cows,' 'with the branch he makes [them] give milk' — in these usages of the word <s>śākhā</s>, the cut-piece (<s>upaveṣa</s>) has no function, and therefore the word <s>śākhā</s> departs [from it]. For they do not call 'that root-piece a branch.' What follows? Wherever the word <s>śākhā</s> occurs, the cutting is for that purpose, because of the accusative case designation. Even if the word <s>śākhā</s> were used for the root-piece, even then in the functions designated by the word <s>śākhā</s>, the root is not [included], because [the branch] has not been stripped of its root. And what is done with the branch thus prepared — the cutting is for that purpose. But the placing-beneath is not done with [a branch] that has been stripped of its root. Therefore the cutting is not for that purpose. What then is the purpose? In the full-moon day too, a branch must be produced, as in the prima facie view. As per the established conclusion, it need not be produced.

children.text: haraṇe tu juhotir yogasāmānyād dravyāṇāṃ cārthaśeṣatvāt // MS_4,2.10 //
children.translated_text: But in the throwing, [the word] <s>juhoti</s> ('offers') [applies], because of similarity of connection; and because the substances are subordinate to the purpose. // MS_4,2.10 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayor āmananti - saha śākhayā prastaraṃ praharatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ śākhāpraharaṇaṃ pratipattikarma, uta [475]{*4/164*} arthakarmeti. kiṃ prāptam? haraṇe tu juhotiḥ syāt, arthakarmety arthaḥ. kutaḥ? yogasāmānyāt, yogo 'syāḥ samānaḥ prastareṇa, saha śākhayā prastaraṃ praharatīti. sahayoge yatra tṛtīyā, tasya guṇabhāvaḥ, yatra dvitīyā tasya prādhānyam. prastare ca vispaṣṭo yajiḥ, śākhāpi tasminn eva yajau prastarasya viśeṣaṇam, samānayogitvāt.
āha, nanu tatra tatra guṇabhūtā śākhā, tasyāḥ pratipattir nyāyyāḥ, itarathānekaguṇabhāvaḥ prasajyeteti. ucyate, dravyāṇāṃ cārthaśeṣatvād utpattyā cikīrṣitasya śeṣabhūtāny eva dravyāṇy upadiśyante, bhūtaṃ bhavyāyopadiśyata iti. tasmād anekaguṇataiva dravyānāṃ nyāyyeti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is stated: 'Together with the branch, he throws the sacrificial grass (<s>prastara</s>).' There a doubt [arises]: is the throwing of the branch a <s>pratipattikarma</s> (act of disposal), or an <s>arthakarma</s> (purposeful act)? What is the prima facie view? In the throwing, [the word] <s>juhoti</s> (offering) would apply — meaning it is a purposeful act. Why? Because of similarity of connection — the connection of this [branch] is the same as that of the sacrificial grass: 'together with the branch he throws the <s>prastara</s>.' In a 'together with' construction, where the instrumental case [is used], that [item] has subordinate status; where the accusative [is used], that has primary status. For the <s>prastara</s>, the offering-character is clear, and the branch too [participates] in that same offering; [it is] a qualifier of the <s>prastara</s>, because of having the same connection.
[The objector] says: but since the branch is subordinate in each instance, its disposal is appropriate; otherwise there would be multiple subordinations. We reply: because the substances are subordinate to the purpose — substances that are taught along with their origination are taught as subordinate to the intended [purpose]; what exists is taught for what is to come. Therefore the multiple subordination of substances is indeed appropriate.

children.text: pratipattir vā śabdasya tatpradhānatvāt // MS_4,2.11 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, it is an act of disposal, because of the primacy of that [branch] in the [Vedic] word. // MS_4,2.11 //

children.text:
pratipattir vā śākhāpraharaṇam, śabdasya tatpradhānatvāt. śabdo 'tra śākhāpradhānaḥ. katham? dvitīyāśravaṇāt. nanv anyatraiva sā dvitīyā, prastare, na śākhāyām. ucyate, prastare dvitīyārthaḥ śākhāyām api. katham? tulyayogāt saha śākhayā, evaṃ prastaraḥ prahṛto bhavati, yadi śākhāpi prahriyate. tena tulyayoge sahaśabdo 'yam. yadi prastaraḥ praharaṇe pradhānam, śākhāpi prastaraviśeṣaṇam, na tarhi{*4/165*} tulyayogaḥ. tasmād yaḥ prastare dvitīyārthaḥ, sa śākhāyām api, ataḥ śākhā pradhānam. api ca, tatra tatra śākhā guṇabhūtā, tasyām anyatropadiśyamānāyām anekaguṇabhāvaḥ{*4/166*}. tatra ko doṣaḥ? dṛṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ hitvādṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta. kṛtaprayojanāyāḥ śākhāyā apanayanena vedivivecanāt sukhapracāro dṛṣṭaṃ kāryam, na tu prahareṇa kiṃcit sūkṣmam api dṛṣṭam asti, tasmāt pratipattir nyāyyā.
[476]{*4/167*} āha, nanu tṛtīyāśravaṇāt parārthena śākhoccāraṇena bhavituṃ nyāyyam. ucyate, bhaved etan nyāyyam, yadi nirjñātakālā śākhā syāt, tataḥ prastarasya kālaparicchedāya kīrtyamānā parārthā uccāryeta, iha punar etad viparītam, nirjñātakālaḥ prastaro 'nirjñātakālā śākhā. tasmāt saty api tṛtīyāśravaṇe prastara eva śākhāyāḥ kālaṃ paricchetsyati. yathā dvitīyānirdiṣṭaḥ{*4/168*}, tathā śākhā draṣṭavyā, yathā tṛtīyānirdiṣṭā{*4/169*}, tathā prastaraḥ. sāmarthyaṃ hi balavattaram iti.
children.translated_text:
Or rather, the throwing of the branch is an act of disposal (<s>pratipattikarma</s>), because of the primacy of that [branch] in the word. The word here has the branch as primary. How? Because of the hearing of the accusative case. But is not the accusative case elsewhere — for the <s>prastara</s>, not the branch? We reply: the accusative meaning for the <s>prastara</s> [applies] to the branch as well. How? Because of equal connection — 'together with the branch'; thus the <s>prastara</s> is [properly] thrown only if the branch too is thrown. Therefore the word <s>saha</s> ('together with') here denotes equal connection. If the <s>prastara</s> is primary in the throwing and the branch is [merely] a qualifier of the <s>prastara</s>, then there is no equal connection. Therefore the accusative meaning that [applies] to the <s>prastara</s> [applies] to the branch as well; hence the branch is primary. Moreover, in each [previous] instance the branch was subordinate — when it is taught as subordinate elsewhere, there would be multiple subordination. What is the fault in that? An observed purpose would be abandoned and an unobserved one conjectured. The observed purpose of removing the branch whose function is fulfilled is easy movement on the <s>vedi</s> (altar); but in the throwing, not even the slightest observed [purpose] exists. Therefore disposal is appropriate.
[465] [The objector] says: but because of the hearing of the instrumental case, it is appropriate for the branch-utterance to be for the benefit of another. We reply: this would be appropriate if the branch had a known time [of disposal]; then being mentioned for the purpose of delimiting the time of the <s>prastara</s>, it would be uttered for another's benefit. But here it is the reverse — the <s>prastara</s> has a known time, while the branch does not. Therefore, even though the instrumental case is heard, the <s>prastara</s> itself will delimit the time for the branch. As the [branch] is designated by the accusative, so it should be understood; as [the prastara] is designated by the instrumental, so the <s>prastara</s> [should be understood]. For capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is indeed stronger.

children.translated_text: If [one argues] that even in a purposeful act [the accusative occurs] — // MS_4,2.12 //

children.text: āha, nanu guṇabhāve 'pi dvitīyā bhavati{*4/170*}, yathā saktu mārutaikakapāleṣu{*4/171*}.
children.translated_text: [The objector] says: but the accusative case occurs even in subordination — as in the <s>saktu</s> (barley meal) [offered on] the wind-deity one-potsherd [cake offerings].

children.translated_text: No, because of the non-applicability of that [argument]; and because the purpose has [already] been accomplished. // MS_4,2.13 //

children.text: naitat saktvādibhis tulyam, tasya saktvāder anyatrānadhikārāt, iha ca śākhayānyasyārthasya kṛtatvād vatsāpākaraṇādeḥ. āha, nanu punaruktam etat saktvādīnāṃ pradarśanaṃ samādhiś ceti. ucyate, na punaruktatā mahān doṣaḥ, bahukṛtvo 'pi pathyaṃ veditavyaṃ bhavati, granthabhayena{*4/172*} punaruktaṃ necchanti. arthāgrahaṇāt tu{*4/173*} bibhyataḥ punar{*4/174*} punar abhidhīyamānaṃ bahu manyanta eva. kiṃ cintāyāḥ prayojanam? yady arthakarma, paurṇamāsyām api śākhotpādyā, atha pratipattir notpādayitavyeti.
children.translated_text: This is not equal to the case of <s>saktu</s> (roasted barley) and the like, because those <s>saktus</s> etc. have no employment elsewhere, whereas here the purpose of another matter has been accomplished by the [Vedic] branch — such as the calf-driving and the like. [The objector] says: but is not this a repetition — the illustration of <s>saktus</s> etc. and the resolution? We reply: repetition is not a great fault; what is beneficial must be known even if stated many times. Those who fear prolixity do not want repetition. But those who fear failure to grasp the meaning consider what is stated again and again as highly valuable. What is the purpose of the inquiry? If it is a purposeful act, then even at the full-moon [sacrifice] a branch should be produced; but if it is [mere] disposal, it need not be produced.
