children.text: utpattyasaṃyogāt praṇītānām ājyavad vibhāgaḥ syāt // MS_4,2.14 //
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of connection with origination, there should be a division of the <s>praṇīta</s> waters, like [the division of] ghee. // MS_4,2.14 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnāyate - apaḥ praṇayaty āpo vai śraddhā śraddhām evālabhya yajata iti{*4/176*}, ubhayatra ca praṇītānāṃ vyāpāraḥ, praṇītābhir{*4/177*} havīṃṣi saṃyautīti, tathā, antarvedi praṇītā ninayatīti. atra{*4/178*} saṃdehaḥ, kim ubhayam āsāṃ prayojakaṃ saṃyavanaṃ ninayanaṃ ca, uta saṃyavanārthānāṃ ninayanaṃ pratipattir iti. kiṃ prāptam? utpattisaṃyogo nāsāṃ kenacit prayojanena, ubhābhyām utpannānāṃ saṃyogaḥ. tasmān na gamyate viśeṣaḥ, agamyamāne viśeṣe ubhayārthānāṃ vibhāgo 'yam, kaścid yāgaḥ{*4/179*} saṃyavane kaścin ninayana iti, ājyavat, yathā sarvasmai vā etad yajñāya gṛhyate yad dhruvāyām ājyam iti{*4/180*}.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon) rites it is heard: 'He leads forth the waters — waters indeed are faith; having obtained faith, he sacrifices.' And the employment of the <s>praṇīta</s> waters is in both [contexts]: 'With the <s>praṇīta</s> waters he sprinkles the oblations,' and likewise, 'He leads the <s>praṇīta</s> waters within the <s>vedi</s> (sacrificial enclosure).' Here a doubt [arises]: are both — the sprinkling and the leading — purposes of these [waters], or is the leading of those [waters] intended for sprinkling a [mere] disposal? What is the prima facie view? There is no connection of their origination with any [single] purpose; the connection belongs to [waters] produced for both [purposes]. Therefore no distinction can be discerned; when no distinction is discerned, this is a division of [waters] serving both purposes — some [sacrificial act] for sprinkling, some for leading — like ghee, just as 'that ghee which is taken in the <s>dhruvā</s> (permanent ladle) is indeed for this entire sacrifice.'

children.text: saṃyavanārthānāṃ vā pratipattir itarāsāṃ tatpradhānatvāt // MS_4,2.15 //
children.translated_text: Or, the leading is [mere] disposal of those [waters] intended for sprinkling, because of the primacy of that [sprinkling]. // MS_4,2.15 //

children.text: saṃyavanārthāḥ praṇītāḥ. kutaḥ? tṛtīyānirdeśāt, saṃyavane 'pāṃ guṇabhāvaḥ, dvitīyānirdeśāc ca ninayane prādhānyam. cintāyāḥ prayojanam, puroḍāśābhāve praṇītānām abhāvaḥ, yathā payasyāyām.
children.translated_text: The <s>praṇīta</s> waters are for the purpose of sprinkling. Why? Because of the instrumental case designation — in sprinkling, the waters have a subordinate status; and because of the accusative case designation in leading, [the waters have] primacy. The purpose of the inquiry [is this]: in the absence of <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice cake), the <s>praṇīta</s> waters would be absent, as in the <s>Payasyā</s> (milk offering).

children.text: prāsanavan maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍapradānaṃ kṛtārthatvāt // MS_4,2.16 //
children.translated_text: The giving of the staff to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest] is like the casting [of the black-antelope horn], because its purpose has been fulfilled. // MS_4,2.16 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - vāg vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat yajñāyātiṣṭhamānā sā vanaspatīn prāviśat saiṣā vāg vanaspatiṣu vadati. yā dundubhau yā ca{*4/182*} tūṇave yā ca{*4/183*} vīṇāyām, yad dīkṣitāya daṇḍaṃ{*4/184*} prayacchati vācam evāvarundhe, krīte{*4/185*} some maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍaṃ prayacchatīti{*4/186*}. maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍaṃ prayacchatīty etad udāharaṇam. tatra saṃśayaḥ, kiṃ dīkṣitadhāraṇe śeṣabhūtasya daṇḍasya maitrāvaruṇadhāraṇaṃ pratipattiḥ, athavārthakarmeti. kiṃ prāptam? maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍadānaṃ pratipattiḥ. kutaḥ? dīkṣitadhāraṇe kṛtārthatvāt. daṇḍena dīkṣayantīti{*4/187*} śeṣabhūtasyānyatra vyāpāraḥ{*4/188*} pratipattir nyāyyā, yathā cātvāle kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ prāsyatīti kaṇḍūyane śeṣabhūtāyāḥ prāsanaṃ pratipattiḥ, evam atrāpi draṣṭavyam. dvitīyā ca daṇḍe vibhaktiḥ. tasmāt prādhānyam iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'Speech indeed departed from the gods when the sacrifice was being extended. It entered the trees. That speech [which resides] in trees [is what] speaks — that which is in the drum, that which is in the bamboo flute, and that which is in the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute). When he gives the staff to the consecrated one (<s>dīkṣita</s>), he thereby obtains speech.' 'When the <s>Soma</s> has been purchased, he gives the staff to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>.' 'He gives the staff to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>' — this is the example. There a doubt [arises]: is the giving of the staff to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> a disposal of the staff that was subsidiary to the <s>dīkṣita</s>'s carrying, or is it a purposeful act? What is the prima facie view? The giving of the staff to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is [mere] disposal. Why? Because its purpose has been fulfilled in the <s>dīkṣita</s>'s carrying. The staff that was subsidiary [to that purpose] — its employment elsewhere is appropriately [understood as] disposal, just as 'he casts the black-antelope horn into the <s>cātvāla</s> (pit)' — the casting of [the horn] that was subsidiary to scratching is [mere] disposal. Thus it should be viewed here also. And the case ending on 'staff' is accusative. Therefore [it is] primacy [of the person, not the staff].

children.text: arthakarma vā kartṛsaṃyogāt sragvat // MS_4,2.17 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a purposeful act, because of the connection with the agent, like [the giving of] the garland. // MS_4,2.17 //

children.text:
arthakarma vā syāt. kutaḥ? kartṛsaṃyogāt, kartṛsaṃyogo bhavati. maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍam iti kartṛdaṇḍasaṃyogo bhavati{*4/189*}, tasmiṃś ca daṇḍo guṇabhūtaḥ, puruṣaḥ pradhānabhūtaḥ. puruṣaṃ hi sa pracarituṃ samarthaṃ karoti. katham? yathā pūrvaṃ{*4/190*} tamo 'vagāhate 'paḥ sarpati{*4/191*} gāṃ ca sarpaṃ ca vārayati, avalambanaṃ ca bhavati. ataḥ puruṣaprādhānyān na pratipattiḥ. sragvac ca draṣṭavyam, yathā srajam udgātre dadāti [479]{*4/192*} ity{*4/193*} asaty apy upakāre puruṣasya prayojanavattvāt, niṣprayojanatvāc ca srajaḥ, bhavati puruṣaprādhānyam, evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam. tasmān na pratipattir iti.
atha yad uktam - dvitīyāśravaṇād daṇḍaprādhānyam iti. ucyate, tathā yuktaṃ{*4/194*} cānīpsitam iti dvitīyā draṣṭavyā. kutaḥ? maitrāvaruṇe caturthīnirdeśāt. saṃpradāne hi caturthī bhavati, saṃpradānaṃ ca karmaṇābhipreyate. tatra daṇḍād abhipretataro maitrāvaruṇa iti gamyate.
children.translated_text:
Or it is a purposeful act. Why? Because of the connection with the agent — there is a connection with the agent. 'The staff to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>' — there is a connection of the agent with the staff, and in that [connection] the staff is subordinate while the person is primary. For it is the person whom [the staff] enables to function. How? Just as before, [the staff enables him to] penetrate darkness, traverse waters, ward off cattle and snakes, and serve as a support. Therefore, because of the primacy of the person, it is not [mere] disposal. And it should be viewed like the garland — just as 'he gives the garland to the <s>Udgātṛ</s>' [479] — even when there is no [further] service [from the garland], because the person has purposefulness and the garland has no [independent] purpose, there is primacy of the person — so too it should be viewed here. Therefore it is not disposal.
As for what was said — 'because of the accusative, there is primacy of the staff' — to that we reply: the accusative should be understood as denoting what is desired and fitting. Why? Because of the dative case designation for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. For the dative is used for the recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>), and the recipient is intended by the action. From that it is understood that the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is more intended than the staff.

children.text: karmayukte ca darśanāt // MS_4,2.18 //
children.translated_text: And because it is seen in connection with [purposeful] action. // MS_4,2.18 //

children.text: daṇḍī praiṣān anvāhety anūdyate, tena pracarato daṇḍaṃ pradarśayati. tad arthakaramaṇi saty upapadyate. pratipattau tu daṇḍo maitrāvaruṇāya dattas tato 'pavṛjyeta, kṛtaṃ ca kartavyam iti na{*4/195*} tena prayojam iti na dhāryeta. tatraitaddarśanaṃ nopapadyate, tathā, ahis tvāṃ daśatīti maitrāvaruṇaṃ brūyād ahir iva hy eṣa iti, tathā{*4/196*}, muśalyan vāheti. muśalaśabdaś ca daṇḍe prasiddhaḥ, yathā kva nu khalu{*4/197*} muśalino māṇavakā gaṅgāṃ avatareyur{*4/198*} iti. tasmād apy arthakarma.
children.translated_text: It is restated that 'the one with the staff announces the commands (<s>praiṣa</s>),' thereby showing the staff of one who is functioning. That is appropriate when there is a purposeful act. But if it were [mere] disposal, the staff having been given to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> would [then] be discarded — the task having been done, there would be no purpose for it, and so it would not be carried. In that case, this observation would not be appropriate. Likewise, 'A snake is biting you' — he should say to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, 'for he is indeed like a snake.' And likewise, 'He carries it like a club (<s>muśala</s>).' The word <s>muśala</s> is well-known [as referring to] a staff, as in 'Where indeed should the club-bearing (<s>muśalin</s>) youths go down to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>?' Therefore, by this too, it is a purposeful act.

children.text: utpattau yena saṃyuktaṃ tadarthaṃ tac chrutihetutvāt tasyārthāntaragamane śeṣatvāt pratipattiḥ syāt // MS_4,2.19 //
children.translated_text: That which is connected at origination with a [certain purpose] exists for that purpose, because of [the Vedic] statement being its cause; when it passes to another purpose, because of its subsidiary status, it should be [mere] disposal. // MS_4,2.19 //

children.text:
yad uktam, yathā kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāprāsanam iti. tatrocyate, yuktaṃ tatrotpadyamānaṃ yat, yena prayojanena saṃbaddham utpadyate, [480]{*4/199*} tat tadartham eva nyāyyam. tasyānyatra gamane pratipattir ity etad upapadyate, yadi na dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanaṃ bhavati. iha tu dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanaṃ maitrāvaruṇasya dhāraṇae{*4/200*}, tasmād viṣamam etat.
athavā - adhikaraṇāntaram, viṣāṇāyāḥ kaṇḍūyanaṃ prāsanaṃ cobhayam api prayojakam iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, ekaniṣpatteḥ sarvaṃ samaṃ syād iti. utttaraḥ pakṣaḥ, kaṇḍūyane tṛtīyānirdeśād viṣāṇāyā guṇabhāvaḥ. prāsane ca dvitīyānirdeśāt, anyatra ca kṛtārthatvāt prādhānyam iti.
children.translated_text:
As for what was said — 'just like the casting of the black-antelope horn' — to that we reply: what is appropriate is that which is produced [in connection] with a [certain] purpose — that which is connected with that purpose at origination — [480] that is properly for that purpose alone. Its going elsewhere is appropriately [understood as] disposal — this is fitting when no visible purpose exists. But here a visible purpose exists for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>'s carrying. Therefore this [comparison] is dissimilar.
Alternatively — this is a separate topic: both the scratching and the casting of the [antelope] horn are motivating — this is the prima facie view, [arguing that] because of single origination everything should be equal. The reply is: because of the instrumental case designation in scratching, the horn has subordinate status; and because of the accusative case designation in casting, and because its purpose has been fulfilled elsewhere, [the horn has] primacy [only in that context].

children.text: saumike ca kṛtārthatvāt // MS_4,2.20 //
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Soma</s> rite, because the purpose has been fulfilled. // MS_4,2.20 //

children.text: asti jyotiṣṭome 'vabhṛthaḥ, vāruṇenaikakapālenāvabhṛtham abhyavapantīti{*4/201*}{*4/202*}. tatrāmnāyate, varuṇagṛhītaṃ vaitad yajñasya yadṛjīṣaṃ yadgrāvāṇa yadaunduvarī{*4/203*} yadabhiṣavaṇaphalake, tasmād yatkiṃcit somaliptaṃ dravyaṃ tenāvabhṛthaṃ yantīti{*4/204*}. tatra saṃśayaḥ, kiṃ somaliptānāṃ dravyāṇām avabhṛthagamanaṃ pratipattiḥ, athavārthakarmeti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? pratipattir iti. kutaḥ? kṛtārthatvāt, kṛtārthāny etāni dravyāṇi tatra tatra, teṣām avabhṛthagamanaṃ pratipattir nyāyyā.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath). It is heard: 'They go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> with a single-potsherd [cake] for <s>Varuṇa</s>.' There it is stated: 'Whatever of this sacrifice is seized by <s>Varuṇa</s> — the <s>ṛjīṣa</s> (Soma dregs), the pressing stones, the <s>audumbarī</s> (Udumbara post), and the pressing boards — therefore whatever thing is smeared with <s>Soma</s>, with those they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is the going of the <s>Soma</s>-smeared things to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> [mere] disposal, or is it a purposeful act? What is the prima facie view? It is disposal. Why? Because their purpose has been fulfilled — these things have fulfilled their purpose in their respective [ritual contexts]; their going to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> is appropriately [understood as mere] disposal.

children.text: arthakarma vābhidhānasaṃyogāt // MS_4,2.21 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a purposeful act, because of connection with the designation. // MS_4,2.21 //

children.text: arthakarma vā, abhidhānena saṃyogāt, tenāvabhṛthaṃ yantīti. tenāvabhṛthasaṃjñakaṃ niṣpādayantīti, tṛtīyā tena [481] iti, dvitīyāvabhṛtham iti. tasmāt somaliptaṃ guṇabhūtam, avabhṛthaḥ pradhānabhūta iti.
children.translated_text: Or it is a purposeful act, because of connection with the designation — 'with those they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>.' 'With those they accomplish what is called <s>Avabhṛtha</s>' — the instrumental 'with those,' the accusative '<s>Avabhṛtha</s>.' Therefore what is smeared with <s>Soma</s> is subordinate, while the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> is primary.

children.text: pratipattir vā tan nyāyatvād deśārthāvabhṛthaśrutiḥ // MS_4,2.22 //
children.translated_text: Or it is disposal, because of the propriety of that [reasoning]; the mention of <s>Avabhṛtha</s> is for the purpose of [indicating] the place. // MS_4,2.22 //

children.text: pratipattir vā. kutaḥ? tannyāyatvād eva. eṣa hi nyāyaḥ, yad anyatra kṛtārtham anyatra pratipādyate, tad iha yadi somaliptaṃ dravyam avabhṛthe karaṇaṃ vidhīyate, tato 'rthakarma. atha somaliptena yānaṃ vidhīyate, tataḥ pratipattiḥ. na hy atra somaliptaṃ vidhīyate 'vabhṛthe, tathā saty avabhṛthasomaliptasaṃbandho 'bhyavayantīty anenākhyātena vidhīyeta. tatra vākyena vidhānaṃ syāt, na tu śrutyā, yāne 'munā vidhīyamāne{*4/205*} śrutyā vidhānam. tat parigṛhītaṃ bhavati, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī, tasmāt pratipattiḥ. atha yad uktam, arthakarmābhidhānena saṃyogād iti. tatra brūmaḥ, evaṃ sati deśārthā avabhṛthaśrutiḥ, avabhṛthaṃ yantīti, avabhṛthena deśaṃ lakṣayati, yasmin deśe 'vabhṛthaḥ, taṃ deśaṃ yantīti. tasmāt pratipattir iti.
children.translated_text: Or it is disposal. Why? Precisely because of the propriety of that [reasoning]. For this is the principle: that which has fulfilled its purpose in one context is disposed of in another. Now, if what is smeared with <s>Soma</s> is enjoined as an instrument in the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>, then it is a purposeful act. But if the going with what is smeared with <s>Soma</s> is [what is] enjoined, then it is disposal. For what is smeared with <s>Soma</s> is not enjoined in the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>; if it were, the connection of the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> with the <s>Soma</s>-smeared things would be enjoined by the verb 'they go' (<s>abhyavayanti</s>). In that case the injunction would be by the sentence, not by the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>). When going with these [things] is enjoined, the injunction is by the [Vedic] word. That [word-based injunction] is adopted, for the [Vedic] word is stronger than the sentence. Therefore it is disposal. As for what was said — 'it is a purposeful act because of connection with the designation' — to that we say: this being so, the mention of <s>Avabhṛtha</s> is for the purpose of [indicating] the place — 'they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>' means [the text] indicates by '<s>Avabhṛtha</s>' the place where the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> [occurs]; they go to that place. Therefore it is disposal.

children.text: kartṛdeśakālānām acodanaṃ prayoge nityasamavāyāt // MS_4,2.23 //
children.translated_text: The agent, place, and time are not enjoined; because of invariable connection in performance [they are understood automatically]. // MS_4,2.23 //

children.text: idaṃ śrūyate - paśubandhasya yajñakratoḥ ṣaḍ ṛtvijaḥ{*4/206*}, darśapūrṇamāsayor yajñakratoś catvāra ṛtvijaḥ{*4/207*}, cāturmāsyānāṃ yajñakratūnāṃ{*4/208*} pañca ṛtvijaḥ{*4/209*}, agnihotrasya yajñakrator eka ṛtvik{*4/210*}, saumyasyādhvarasya yajñakratoḥ saptadaśa ṛtvijaḥ{*4/211*}, tathā, same darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta, prācīnapravaṇe vaiśvadevena yajeta, paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā [482]{*4/212*} yajeta, amāvāsyāyām amāvāsyayeti{*4/213*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ kartṛdeśakālā vidhīyante, utānūdyanta iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? kartṛdeśakālānām acodanam anuvādaḥ{*4/214*}. kutaḥ? prayoge nityasamavāyāt, prayoge nityasamavetā eta iti. na, ṛte kartṛdeśakālebhyaḥ, prayogaḥ sidhyati, tena prayogacodanayaiva prāptānām anuvādaḥ. nanu viṣamādipratiṣedhārtham etad vacanaṃ bhaviṣyati. neti brūmaḥ, upadeśakam evaṃjātīyakaṃ vacanam, na pratiṣedhakam. tasmād anuvāda iti.
children.translated_text: This is heard: 'For the <s>Paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice), the <s>yajñakratu</s> has six <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests); for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the <s>yajñakratu</s> has four <s>ṛtvijs</s>; for the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> rites, the <s>yajñakratus</s> have five <s>ṛtvijs</s>; for the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the <s>yajñakratu</s> has one <s>ṛtvik</s>; for the <s>Saumya</s> (Soma) <s>adhvara</s>, the <s>yajñakratu</s> has seventeen <s>ṛtvijs</s>.' Likewise, 'On level [ground] one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; on an eastward slope one should sacrifice with the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; on the full-moon day one should sacrifice with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> [offering]; on the new-moon day with the <s>Amāvāsyā</s> [offering].' There a doubt [arises]: are the agent, place, and time being enjoined, or are they being restated (<s>anuvāda</s>)? What is the prima facie view? The mention of agent, place, and time without injunctive force is a restatement. Why? Because of their invariable connection with the performance — these are invariably connected with the performance. No performance is accomplished without agent, place, and time; therefore, since they are already obtained through the injunction of performance itself, it is a restatement. [The objector says:] but this statement would serve to prohibit uneven [ground] and the like. We reply: no — a statement of this kind is instructive, not prohibitive. Therefore it is a restatement.

children.text: niyamārthā vā śrutiḥ // MS_4,2.23 //
children.translated_text: Or the scripture is for the purpose of restriction. // MS_4,2.23 //

children.text: ucyate, na caitad asty anuvāda iti, anuvādamātram anarthakam. yadi vidhiḥ, evam apūrvam arthaṃ prakariṣyati, tasmād vidhir iti. nanu prayogāṅgatvāt prāpta eveti. ucyate, niyamārthā śrutir bhaviṣyati. ko 'yaṃ niyamaḥ? aniyatasya niyatatā, prayogāṅgatayā sarve deśāḥ prāpnuvanti, na tu samuccayena. yadā samaḥ, an tadā viṣamaḥ, yadā viṣamaḥ, na tadā samaḥ. sa eṣa samaḥ prāptaś cāprāptaś ca, yadā na prāptaḥ, sa pakṣo vidhiṃ prayojayati. ato viṣamacikīrṣāyām api samo vidhīyate. tasmād viṣamasyāprāptir vidhau sati bhavatīti samo vidhīyate. evam itareṣv api, tasmād vidhir iti.
children.translated_text: It is said: this is not a [mere] restatement, for a mere restatement would be purposeless. If it is an injunction, then it would produce an unprecedented meaning; therefore it is an injunction. [The objector says:] but it is already obtained because of being a component of performance. We reply: the scripture would serve the purpose of restriction (<s>niyama</s>). What is this restriction? It is the making definite of what is indefinite. Through being a component of performance, all places are obtained, but not cumulatively. When [the ground is] level, then it is not uneven; when uneven, then not level. This level [ground], being both obtained and not obtained — when it is not obtained, that alternative activates the injunction. Therefore, even when one desires [to sacrifice on] uneven [ground], level [ground] is enjoined. Hence, the non-obtainment of uneven [ground] follows when the injunction exists, and level [ground] is enjoined. Similarly in the other cases as well; therefore it is an injunction.

children.text: tathā dravyeṣu guṇaśrutir utpattisaṃyogāt // MS_4,2.25 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, in [the case of] substances, the mention of a quality is because of the connection with origination. // MS_4,2.25 //

children.text:
adhikaraṇapradeśo 'yam{*4/215*}. idam āmamanti - vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ{*4/216*}. tathā, somāraudraṃ ghṛte caruṃ nirvapec chuklānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ brahmavarcaskāmaḥ{*4/217*}, tathā, nairṛtaṃ caruṃ nirvapet kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇām iti{*4/218*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ śvetādivarṇo vidhīyata utānūdyate, utānūdyata iti. kiṃ prāptam? anūdyate, dravyaśrutigṛhītatvāt. vidhir vā, pakṣe prāptasya niyamārtha{*4/219*} iti. pakṣoktaṃ prayojanam ubhayor apy adhikaraṇayoḥ.
NOTES:
*{4/215: E2: adhikaraṇātideśo 'yam}*
*{4/216: Tait. S. 2.1.1.1}*
*{4/217: Mait. S. 2.1.5}*
*{4/218: Tait.S. 1.8.9.1}*
*{4/219: E2: prāptasya varṇasya niyamārtha}*
children.translated_text:
This is an <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic of discussion). This is what they state: 'One desiring prosperity should sacrifice a white [animal] to <s>Vāyu</s>.' Likewise, 'One desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance) should offer a <s>caru</s> (rice oblation) of white rice in ghee to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Rudra</s>'; likewise, 'He should offer a <s>caru</s> of black rice to <s>Nirṛti</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is the color such as white being enjoined, or is it being restated? What is the prima facie view? It is being restated, because it is already grasped through the mention of the substance. Or it is an injunction — in the alternative view, it serves the purpose of restricting what is [already] obtained. The purpose as stated in the alternative view applies to both <s>adhikaraṇas</s> (topics).

children.text: saṃskāre ca tatpradhānatvāt // MS_4,2.26 //
children.translated_text: And in the case of a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>), because of the primacy of that [substance]. // MS_4,2.26 //

children.text: ayam apy adhikaraṇāpradeśaḥ. darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate - vrīhīn avahanti, taṇḍulān pinaṣṭīti, tat kim, imau vidhī, utānuvādāv iti. saṃśaye 'rthaprāptatvāt, anuvādāv iti prāpte, niyamārthatvād vidhī iti.
children.translated_text: This too is a topic of discussion. In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: 'He husks the rice grains; he grinds the unhusked grains.' The question is: are these two injunctions, or restatements? When in doubt, since they are obtained by the nature of things, the prima facie view is that they are restatements. [The conclusion is:] because they serve the purpose of restriction, they are injunctions.

children.text: yajaticodanā dravyadevatākriyaṃ samudāye kṛtārthatvāt // MS_4,2.27 //
children.translated_text: The injunction expressed by '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) is fulfilled in the aggregate of substance, deity, and action. // MS_4,2.27 //

children.text: śeṣaviniyoga uktaḥ, kiṃ tat pradhānam, yasyaite śeṣā iti. ucyate, yajati dadāti juhotīty evaṃlakṣaṇam. atha kiṃlakṣaṇako yajatijuhotir{*4/220*} dadātiś ceti. yajaticodanā, tāvad dravyadevatākriyam, dravyaṃ devatā ca, tasya dravasya kriyā, yayā{*4/221*} tayoḥ{*4/222*} saṃbandho bhavati{*4/223*}. samudāye, samuditeṣv eṣu{*4/224*} yajatiśabdo bhavati. loke, iṣṭo 'nena paśupatir iti. tena manyāmahe, dravyadevatākriyasyārthasya yajatiśabdena pratyāyanaṃ [484]{*4/225*} kriyata iti. lakṣaṇakarmaṇi prayojanaṃ na vaktavyam, jñānam evātra prayojanam iti.
children.translated_text: The subsidiary allocation has been stated. What is the principal, of which these are subsidiaries? We reply: it is characterized by [the verbal roots] <s>yajati</s> (he sacrifices), <s>dadāti</s> (he gives), and <s>juhoti</s> (he offers). Now, what characterizes <s>yajati</s>, <s>juhoti</s>, and <s>dadāti</s>? The injunction of <s>yajati</s> [encompasses] substance, deity, and action — substance and deity, and the action pertaining to that substance, by which the connection between those two is established. In the aggregate — when these are combined, the word <s>yajati</s> is used. In common usage: 'By this, <s>Paśupati</s> was worshipped.' Therefore we consider that the meaning of substance, deity, and action is conveyed by the word <s>yajati</s>. In the case of a defining action, the purpose need not be stated — knowledge alone is the purpose here.

children.text: tadukte śravaṇāj juhotir āsecanādhikaḥ syāt // MS_4,2.28 //
children.translated_text: Since that has been stated, <s>juhoti</s> (he offers) would be [like <s>yajati</s>] with the additional [act of] pouring, because of the [Vedic] hearing. // MS_4,2.28 //

children.text:
atha kiṃlakṣaṇako juhotir iti. tad ukte yajaty ukte 'rthe{*4/226*} juhotiḥ śrūyate, āsecanādhike. tasmād yajatir evāsecanādhiko juhotiḥ, hutam anenety evaṃjātīyake vaktāro bhavanti loke. vede 'pi yajaticoditaṃ juhotinānuvadati - saṃgrāmiṇaṃ caturhotrā yājayet, caturgṛhītam ājyaṃ kṛtvā caturhotāraṃ vyācakṣīta, pūrveṇa graheṇārdhaṃ juhuyād uttareṇārdham iti.
atha dadātiḥ kiṃlakṣaṇaka iti. ātmanaḥ svatvavyāvṛttiḥ parasya svatvena saṃbandhaḥ. yajatidadātijuhotiṣu sarveṣūtsargaḥ samānaḥ. tatra yajatir devatām uddiśyotsargamātram, juhotir āsecanādhikaḥ, dadāti{*4/227*} utsargapūrvakaḥ parasvatvena saṃbandha ity eṣa eṣāṃ viśeṣa iti.
children.translated_text:
Now, what characterizes <s>juhoti</s>? When that — i.e., the meaning stated for <s>yajati</s> — has been stated, <s>juhoti</s> is heard with the additional [element of] pouring (<s>āsecana</s>). Therefore <s>juhoti</s> is simply <s>yajati</s> with the addition of pouring. People in the world speak of this kind [of act] as '<s>hutam</s>' (offered). In the <s>Veda</s> too, what is enjoined by <s>yajati</s> is restated with <s>juhoti</s>: 'He should have the warrior sacrifice with the <s>Caturhotra</s>; having made the <s>ājya</s> taken four times (<s>caturgṛhīta</s>), he should recite the <s>Caturhotra</s>; with the first portion he should offer (<s>juhuyāt</s>) half, with the latter half.'
Now, what characterizes <s>dadāti</s> (he gives)? The cessation of one's own ownership and the establishment of connection with another's ownership. In <s>yajati</s>, <s>dadāti</s>, and <s>juhoti</s> — in all [three], relinquishment (<s>utsarga</s>) is the same. There, <s>yajati</s> is mere relinquishment directed toward a deity; <s>juhoti</s> has the additional [element of] pouring; <s>dadāti</s> is the connection with another's ownership preceded by relinquishment — this is the distinction among them.

children.text: vidheḥ karmāpavargitvād arthāntare vidhipradeśaḥ syāt // MS_4,2.29 //
children.translated_text: Because an injunction is fulfilled upon [completion of] the action, there should be an injunctive designation for a different purpose. // MS_4,2.29 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - yad ātithyāyāṃ barhiḥ, tad upasadām, tad agnīṣomīyasyeti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ paradravyasyopadeśaḥ, uta niriṣṭikasya{*4/229*}, athavā dharmavidhipradeśaḥ, athavā dravyasādhāraṇyam iti. kiṃ prāptam? paradravyasyopadeśaḥ. kutaḥ? paradravyasyopadeśasadṛśaḥ śabdaḥ, yad ātithyāyām, tad upasadām iti, yathā yo devadattasya gauḥ, sa viṣṇumitrasya kartavya iti devadattād ācchidya viṣṇumitrāya dīyata iti. ataḥ paradravyasyopdeśa iti. na caitad asti, tathā saty ātithyāyāṃ tasya vidhānaṃ yat pūrvam, tad anarthakaṃ syāt.
evaṃ tarhi niriṣṭikasyopadeśaḥ{*4/230*}, tenātithyāyāṃ yad vihitam, ātithyāyāṃ yad upāttam iti, tathā saty arthavad ātithyāyāṃ tad vacanam. niriṣṭikena{*4/231*} tūpasadaḥ kartavyā bhavanti{*4/232*}. na caiṣa śiṣṭānām ācāraḥ. na ca sarve codakaprāptā dharmā bhaveyuḥ, ato brūmaḥ - vidheḥ karmāpavargitvād arthāntare vidhipradeśaḥ syāt. tad barhiḥ parisamāptāyām ātithyāyām apavṛktam, pūrvaṃ{*4/233*} tad ātithyāyāḥ, upasatkāle{*4/234*} ātithyāsaṃbandhas tasya nāsti. bhūtapūrveṇātithyayā karmaṇā lakṣyeta. lakṣaṇā[486]{*4/235*}śabdaś ca na nyāyyaḥ. tasmād ātithyābarhiṣa āñjasyābhāvād yad dharmakamātithyābarhiḥ, tad dharmakam upasadām agnīṣomīyasya ceti nyāyyam.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'The sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>) that belongs to the <s>Ātithya</s> (hospitality rite) — that [belongs] to the <s>Upasads</s>; that [belongs] to the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> [sacrifice].' There a doubt [arises]: is this an instruction regarding another's substance, or regarding a substance whose [prior] purpose is exhausted, or a designation for a [new] injunctive purpose, or a sharing of the substance? What is the prima facie view? It is an instruction regarding another's substance. Why? The words resemble an instruction about another's substance: 'What belongs to the <s>Ātithya</s>, that belongs to the <s>Upasads</s>' — just as [when one says] 'the cow that belongs to <s>Devadatta</s> should be given to <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>,' it is taken from <s>Devadatta</s> and given to <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>. Hence it is an instruction regarding another's substance. But this is not so — if that were the case, the prior injunction for the <s>Ātithya</s> would be purposeless.
In that case, it is an instruction regarding a substance whose purpose is exhausted — so what was enjoined for the <s>Ātithya</s>, what was employed in the <s>Ātithya</s>, with that exhausted [substance], the <s>Upasads</s> would be performed. But this is not the practice of the learned. And not all duties obtained through injunction would [actually] be [fulfilled]. Therefore we say: because an injunction is fulfilled upon [completion of] the action, there should be an injunctive designation for a different purpose. That sacrificial grass, when the <s>Ātithya</s> is completed, is released — it previously belonged to the <s>Ātithya</s>; at the time of the <s>Upasads</s>, it has no connection with the <s>Ātithya</s>. It could be identified by the prior <s>Ātithya</s> rite. But identification by a word and [identification by] a characteristic mark is not proper. Therefore, since there is no direct designation of the <s>Ātithya</s> sacrificial grass, [the statement means:] the grass having the same properties as the <s>Ātithya</s> grass [belongs] to the <s>Upasads</s> and to the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> — this is proper.

children.text: api votpattisaṃyogād arthasaṃbandho 'viśiṣṭānāṃ prayogaikatvahetuḥ syāt // MS_4,2.30 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the connection with origination, the relation to the purpose, being non-distinct, would be the cause of unity of performance. // MS_4,2.30 //

children.text: api veti pakṣo vyāvartate. utpattisaṃyoga evaiṣo 'sya barhiṣaḥ. yadi hy utpannam ātithyāyāṃ barhir viśiṣṭaṃ syāt, tasya dharmā aupasade barhiṣy atidiśyeran, na tu tad asti kenacid vākyena. evaṃ{*4/236*} prakṛtya, barhiṣo viśeṣo vakṣyate. āśvavālaḥ prastaraḥ, vidhṛtī caikṣavyāv iti. tena na paravihitaṃ barhir ucyate, na niriṣṭikam{*4/237*}, na kutaścid dharmā pratidiśyante. kiṃ tarhi? sādhāraṇam amīṣāṃ barhir ucyate, yad ātithyāyāṃ vidhīyate, tad evopasadām, agnīṣomīyasya ca vidhīyata iti, aviśiṣṭānāṃ barhiṣā saṃyoga ekena sarveṣām, yad ādau barhir lūyate, tal lavanaṃ sarveṣām arthena, sādhāraṇo barhiṣaḥ prayogaḥ. evaṃ śrutiḥ śabdasya, parigṛhītā bhaviṣyati, itarathā dharmalakṣaṇā bhavet, śrutilakṣaṇāviśaye ca śrutir nyāyyā na lakṣaṇā. tasmāt trayāṇāṃ sādhāraṇaṃ barhir iti, pakṣoktaṃ prayojanam.
children.translated_text: The word 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) introduces an alternative view. This connection with origination is indeed [the nature] of this sacrificial grass. For if the grass produced in the <s>Ātithya</s> were distinct, then its properties would be transferred to the <s>Upasad</s> grass — but that is not the case, as there is no statement to that effect. Thus having considered: the distinction of the grass will be stated [later] — 'the <s>prastara</s> (bundle) is of horse-tail [grass]; the two <s>vidhṛtīs</s> (supports) are of sugarcane.' Therefore it is not said that the grass is from another's [rite], nor that its purpose is exhausted, nor are properties transferred from anywhere. Rather, what is meant is that the grass is common to all these — what is enjoined for the <s>Ātithya</s>, that same [grass] is enjoined for the <s>Upasads</s> and the <s>Agniṣomīya</s>. The connection of all with the grass, being non-distinct, is [established] by a single [act]: when the grass is first cut, that cutting is for all purposes. The employment of the grass is shared. Thus the scripture, in terms of the word, would be literally fulfilled; otherwise it would be a characteristic-designation, and where literal meaning is possible, literal meaning is proper, not characteristic-designation. Therefore the grass is common to the three — the purpose as stated in the alternative view [applies here].

children.text: dravyasaṃskārakarmasu parārthatvāt phalaśrutir arthavādaḥ syāt // MS_4,3.1 //
children.translated_text: In [actions involving] substance, preparatory rite, and ritual action, because of serving another's purpose, a statement of result would be an <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage). // MS_4,3.1 //

children.text:
yasya khādiraḥ sruvo bhavati, sa chandasām eva rasenāvadyati, sarasā asyāhutayo bhavanti. yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati, na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇotīti. yasyāśvatthy upabhṛd bhavati, brahmaṇaivāsyānnam avarundhe, yasya vaikaṅkatī dhruvā bhavati, praty evāsyāhutayas tiṣṭhanti. atho praiva jāyate, yasyaivaṃrūpāḥ sruvā{*4/239*} bhavanti, sarvāṇy evainaṃ rūpāṇi paśūnām upatiṣṭhante, nāsyāparūpam ātman jāyata iti{*4/240*}. tathā jyotiṣṭomasaṃskāre{*4/241*} phalaśrutiḥ, yadāṅkte cakṣur eva bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte{*4/242*}, tathā, keśaśmaśrū vapate, dato dhāvate, nakhāni nikṛntati, snāti, mṛtā vā eṣā tvag amedhyaṃ vāsyaitad ātmani śamalaṃ tad evopahate medhya eva medham evam upaiti{*4/243*}. karmaṇi phalaṃ śrūyate, abhīṣū vā etau yajñasya yad ādhārau, cakṣuṣī vā etau yajñasya yad ājyabhāgau{*4/244*}, yat prayājānuyājā ijyante, varma vā etad yajñasya kriyate, varma yajamānasya bhārtṛvyasyābhibhūtyai, iti{*4/245*}.
atra saṃdehaḥ, kim ime phalavidhayaḥ, utārthavādā iti. kiṃ prāptam? phalavidhayaḥ, pravṛttiviśeṣakaratvāt phala[488]{*4/246*}vidheḥ, yathā khādiraṃ vīryakāmasya yūpaṃ kūryāt, pālāśaṃ brahmavarcaskāmasya, bailvam annādyakāmasyeti{*4/247*}. yathaite phalavidhayaḥ, evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ. phalārthavādā iti. kutaḥ? parārthatvāt, kratvarthāny etāni. juhūḥ pradāne guṇabhūtāḥ, upabhṛd upadhāraṇe, sruvā{*4/248*} ājyadhāraṇe, añjanavapanādi ca yajamāne, āghārāv ājyabhāgau prayājānuyājāś cāgneyādiṣu. yadi phale 'pi guṇabhāvaḥ syāt, anyatropadiṣṭānām anyatra punar guṇabhāva upadiṣṭa iti pratijñāyeta. na caitan nyāyyam, parārthatā hi guṇabhāvaḥ, kratvarthā caiṣāṃ śabdena, juhvā juhoti juhvā homam abhinirvartayatīti{*4/249*}, evaṃ sarvatra. tasmān naite puruṣārthāḥ.
children.translated_text:
He whose <s>sruva</s> (ladle) is made of <s>khadira</s> wood — he milks by the essence of the <s>Chandas</s> (meters) alone; his oblations become full of sap. He whose <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) is made of <s>palāśa</s> wood — he does not hear an evil report. He whose <s>upabhṛt</s> (secondary ladle) is made of <s>aśvattha</s> wood — <s>Brahman</s> itself secures food for him. He whose <s>dhruvā</s> (fixed ladle) is made of <s>vikaṅkata</s> wood — his oblations stand firm. And indeed he prospers, he whose ladles are of such kinds; all forms of cattle attend upon him, and no deformed offspring is born to him. Likewise in the consecration of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, there is a fruit-statement: 'When he anoints [himself], he indeed plucks out the eye of his rival.' Similarly: 'He shaves his hair and beard, cleans his teeth, pares his nails, bathes — for this skin is dead, and this is impurity upon his self; he removes precisely that defilement; being pure, he thus approaches the pure sacrifice.' A fruit is heard in connection with the ritual action: 'These two are indeed the reins of the sacrifice — namely the two supports (<s>ādhāra</s>); these two are indeed the eyes of the sacrifice — namely the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> portions.' 'When the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> are offered, an armor is indeed made for the sacrifice — an armor for the sacrificer, for the overpowering of his rival.'
Here a doubt [arises]: are these injunctions of fruit, or are they <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogistic passages)? What is the prima facie view? They are injunctions of fruit, because a fruit-injunction has the capacity to produce a specific inclination [to act] — just as 'one desiring vigor should make the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) of <s>khadira</s> wood; one desiring spiritual luster, of <s>palāśa</s>; one desiring food, of <s>bilva</s>.' Just as these are fruit-injunctions, so too should it be viewed here. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: they are <s>arthavāda</s> concerning fruit. Why? Because of their being for another's purpose — these are for the sake of the ritual act (<s>kratu</s>). The <s>juhū</s> is subordinate in the act of offering, the <s>upabhṛt</s> in holding, the <s>sruvas</s> in holding ghee, and anointing, shaving, etc. [are subordinate] to the sacrificer; the two <s>āghāras</s>, the <s>ājyabhāgas</s>, and the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> [are subordinate] to the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings]. If subordination were to apply to the fruit as well, then it would have to be maintained that things prescribed elsewhere are again prescribed as subordinate in another context. But this is not proper, for subordination means being for another's purpose, and their purpose is for the ritual act, as stated by the [Vedic] word — 'with the <s>juhū</s> he offers, with the <s>juhū</s> he accomplishes the oblation' — and so everywhere. Therefore these are not for human purposes.

children.text: utpatteś cātatpradhānatvāt // MS_4,3.2 //
children.translated_text: And because of the non-primacy arising from origination. // MS_4,3.2 //

children.text:
athocyeta - puruṣam api prati guṇabhāva upadiṣṭaḥ, yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇotītyevamādibhir vākyair iti. tac ca na. kasmāt? utpatter atatpradhānatvāt, tatra{*4/250*}, pālāśyā juhvāpāpaślokaśravaṇaṃ{*4/251*} kriyata iti na{*4/252*} kaścic chabda āha, etāvac chrūyate, yasyāsau bhavati, na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇotīti, etāvad atra śabdena gamyate, yasyaivaṃlakṣaṇā{*4/253*} juhūḥ, tasyāpāpaślokaśravaṇam iti. tatra juhvā tat kriyate, juhūr vā tadartheti, naitac chabda āha.
nanv anumānād etad gamyate, dhruvaṃ pālāśyā juhvā tat kriyate, yatas tasyāṃ satyāṃ tad bhavatīti. atrocyate, na, evaṃjātīyakaṃ kāryakāraṇatve 'numānaṃ bhavati, kāryakāraṇasaṃbandho nāma sa bhavati, yasmin sati yad bhavati, yasmiṃś cāsati yan na bhavati, tatraiva kāryakāraṇasaṃbandhaḥ. iha tu tadbhāve [489]{*4/254*} bhāvo jñātaḥ, nābhāve 'bhāvaḥ. yasya pālāśī na bhavati tasyāpāpaślokaśravaṇaṃ nāstīti, na, evaṃjātīyakaḥ śabdo 'sti, tena na, niyogato 'vagamyate, tenedaṃ kriyata iti, lakṣaṇam etat puruṣasya gamyate, tasmān nānumānam.
api ca, yasyāpi juhūḥ pālāśī bhavati, tasyāpi pāpaślokaśravaṇaṃ bhavati. katham avagamyate? pratyakṣataḥ. nanv evaṃ saty agnihotreṇāpi phalaṃ na sādhyeta. na{*4/255*} hutāmātreṇa phalaṃ dṛśyata iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, na hi tatrocyate, tāvataiva phalaṃ bhavatīti. iha tu vartamānāyāṃ juhūsattāyāṃ vartamānasya pāpaślokaśravaṇasya pratiṣedhaḥ. tasmān na tatrānumānam, idaṃ kāryam, idaṃ kāraṇam iti. agnihotrādiṣu tu śabdenaiva kāryakāraṇasaṃbandha ucyate. tasmāt tatra tatkāle 'dṛśyamāne 'pi phale, kālāntare phalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti gamyate, na tv evaṃjātīyakeṣu, tasmān naivaṃjātīyakebhyaḥ phalam astīti.
nanu yasya pālāśī juhūr bhavati, na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇotīty evam ukte tat eva tat phalaṃ bhavatīti gamyate, tasmād ihāpi kālāntare phalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, satyaṃ gamyate, pramāṇaṃ tatra kim iti vicārayāmaḥ. na tāvat pratyakṣam, nānumānam, netarad dṛṣṭaviṣayam upamānādi, no khalv api śabda ity etad uktam, vākyārtho 'pi padārthopajanito bhavati, nānyathā, tad uktam - tadbhūtānām kriyārthena samāmnāya iti{*4/256*}{*4/257*}. tasmād apramāṇamūlatvān mithyāvijñānam etat. laukikeṣu tu vākyeṣv athaivaṃ{*4/258*} gamyate, tāni hi vijñāte 'rthe prayujyamānāny adhyāhāryapadāni gauṇāni vipariṇatavyavahitārthāni ca prayujyante. tasmāt tatsādṛśyād vacanāvagamyeṣv apy artheṣu bhavati tattvarūpo mithyāpratyayaḥ, yathā mṛgatṛṣṇādiṣu.
[490]{*4/259*} api ca, vartamānāpadeśo 'yam, na ca, ayam artho vartamānaḥ, tasmān na khādirasruvādisadbhāve tatphalaṃ bhavet. tad evam āpatati, khādirādau sati bhavati tatphalaṃ nāpi bhavati, asaty api bhavati vā na veti. naivaṃ vijñāyate, kutas tatphalam iti. tasmād evaṃjātīyakeṣūccariteṣu na kvacit pravṛttir na kutaścin nivṛttir ity ānarthakyam akriyārthatvāt. arthavāde tu sati bhavati prayojanaṃ khadirādeḥ, sruvādiṣu karmārtheṣu prayojanavatsu. yady eṣāṃ kratuṃ prati prayojanavattā na syāt, tata etad eva phalaṃ kasyācic chabdavṛttyā bhaved vā na veti vicāryeta. sati tu pārārthye naiva kācic chabdapravṛttir āśrayituṃ śakyate. kaimarthye hi sā kalpyeta. tasmād evaṃjātīyakā arthavādāḥ, arthavādatve cāvartamāne lakṣaṇayā vartamānaśabdaḥ praśaṃsārtha upapatsyate.
children.translated_text:
Now if it were said — subordination to the person too is prescribed, by sentences such as 'he whose <s>juhū</s> is made of <s>palāśa</s> — he does not hear an evil report,' etc. — that is not so. Why? Because of the non-primacy arising from origination. There, no word says that 'by means of a <s>palāśa</s> <s>juhū</s>, the non-hearing of evil reports is produced.' This much alone is heard: 'He whose [juhū] is such — he does not hear an evil report.' This much alone is understood from the word: 'He whose <s>juhū</s> has such characteristics — for him there is non-hearing of evil reports.' But whether the <s>juhū</s> produces that, or the <s>juhū</s> is for that purpose — the word does not say this.
But, [the objector argues], this is understood through inference: surely by means of a <s>palāśa</s> <s>juhū</s> that [result] is produced, since when it exists, that [result] occurs. To this we reply: no, inference of this kind does not apply in [determining] a cause-effect relationship. A cause-effect relationship is that in which, when the [cause] exists, the [effect] occurs, and when the [cause] does not exist, the [effect] does not occur — only there is a cause-effect relationship. But here, the existence [of the effect] when [the cause] exists is known, not the non-existence [of the effect] when [the cause] is absent. That 'for one who does not have a <s>palāśa</s> [juhū], the non-hearing of evil reports does not exist' — no such word exists. Therefore it is not necessarily understood that 'by this, that is produced.' This is understood as a characteristic of the person; therefore there is no inference.
Moreover, even for one whose <s>juhū</s> is made of <s>palāśa</s>, the hearing of evil reports does occur. How is this known? Through direct perception. But [the objector says], if so, even the fruit of the <s>Agnihotra</s> would not be accomplished. [We reply:] no — a fruit is not seen merely through the offering alone. This is not a defect, for it is not said there that the fruit comes from that alone. But here, while the <s>juhū</s>'s existence is present, the prohibition of the hearing of evil reports, which is [also] present, [is contradicted by perception]. Therefore there is no inference here that 'this is the effect, this is the cause.' In the <s>Agnihotra</s> and similar [rites], however, the cause-effect relationship is stated by the [Vedic] word itself. Therefore, even though the fruit is not seen at that time, it is understood that the fruit will come at another time — but not in cases of this kind. Therefore there is no fruit from cases of this kind.
But [the objector says], when it is stated 'he whose <s>juhū</s> is made of <s>palāśa</s> — he does not hear an evil report,' it is understood that precisely that is the fruit. Therefore here too the fruit should come at another time. We reply: true, it is understood — [but] we examine what the valid means of knowledge is there. It is not perception, not inference, not any other [means] whose domain is the seen, such as analogy, nor indeed the [Vedic] word — as has been stated: 'The meaning of a sentence too arises from the meanings of its words, not otherwise; so it has been said — the enumeration of those that are its constituents is for the purpose of [establishing] action.' Therefore, being without a basis in a valid means of knowledge, this is a false cognition. But in worldly sentences, it is indeed understood thus — for those are employed when the meaning is [already] known, and they employ words to be supplied, figurative expressions, and expressions with displaced or remote meanings. Therefore, by analogy with those, even in meanings understood through [Vedic] statements, a false cognition arises that has the appearance of truth — just as in mirages and the like.
Moreover, this [statement] describes what is present, but the [supposed] meaning is not [actually] present. Therefore, the fruit would not come about when a <s>khadira</s> ladle and such are present. Thus the situation presents itself: when <s>khadira</s> and such [ladles] exist, the fruit either occurs or does not occur; and when they do not exist, it either occurs or does not occur. Since it is not [definitively] known [which], whence the fruit? Therefore, when things of this kind are uttered, there is no inclination [to act] from anywhere, nor cessation [from acting] from anywhere — hence they are purposeless because they do not lead to action. But when they are <s>arthavāda</s>, there is a purpose — praise of the <s>khadira</s> and such [materials] — when the ladles and such serve the ritual act. If these had no purposefulness with respect to the ritual, then one might examine whether this itself is the fruit through some [particular] verbal operation or not. But given their being for another's purpose, no verbal operation can be relied upon. For what purpose would it be posited? Therefore, things of this kind are <s>arthavāda</s>, and being <s>arthavāda</s>, the present-tense word, through figurative usage in what is not [actually] present, will be understood as having a laudatory purpose.

children.text: phalaṃ tu tatpradhānāyām // MS_4,3.3 //
children.translated_text: But fruit [is possible] when that [ritual act] is primary. // MS_4,3.3 //

children.text:
atha yad uktam, yathā, khādiraṃ vīryakāmasya yūpaṃ kuryāt, bailvam annādyakāmasya pālāśaṃ brahmavarcasakāmasyeti, yuktaṃ teṣu, vidhivibhaktiḥ kuryād iti vīryakhādirasaṃbandhasya vidhātrī, na ca vartamānāpadeśinī. tasmāt tatrāvirodha iti. evaṃ hi padavākyārthanyāyavidaḥ ślokam āmananti -
kuryāt, kriyeta, kartavyam, bhavet, syād iti pañcamam/
etat syāt sarvavedeṣu niyataṃ vidhilakṣaṇam//iti.
children.translated_text:
Now, as to what was said — 'just as "one desiring vigor should make the sacrificial post of <s>khadira</s>, one desiring food of <s>bilva</s>, one desiring spiritual luster of <s>palāśa</s>"' — [we reply]: it is proper in those [cases], for the injunctive verbal ending in 'should make' (<s>kuryāt</s>) prescribes the connection between vigor and <s>khadira</s>, and does not describe what is [merely] present. Therefore there is no contradiction there. For those who know the principles of words, sentences, and their meanings recite this verse:
'<s>kuryāt</s>' (he should make), '<s>kriyeta</s>' (it should be done), '<s>kartavyam</s>' (it is to be done), '<s>bhavet</s>' (it would be), and '<s>syāt</s>' (it should be) as the fifth —
this is the fixed characteristic of an injunction in all the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: vidhivibhaktiṃ hi vidhāyikāṃ liṅgaṃ manyamānāḥ ślokam imaṃ samāmananti{*4/260*}. asti cātra vidhivibhaktiḥ. tasmād anupavarṇanam etad iti.
children.translated_text: For those who regard the injunctive verbal ending — the <s>liṅ</s> (optative mood) — as having prescriptive force recite this verse. And here there is an injunctive verbal ending. Therefore this is an explicit description [of an injunction].

children.text: naimittike vikāratvāt kratupradhānam anyat syāt // MS_4,3.4 //
children.translated_text: In the case of a <s>naimittika</s> (occasional rite), because of [its] being a modification, the other [element] would be primary with respect to the ritual act. // MS_4,3.4 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome naimittikam, bārhadgiraṃ brāhmaṇasya brahmasāma kuryāt, pārthur aśmāṃ{*4/262*} rājanyasya, rāyovājīyaṃ vaiśyasyeti, tathāgnau naimittikam, sāhasraṃ prathamaṃ cinvānaś cinvīta, dvisāhasraṃ dvitīyam, trisāhasraṃ tṛtīyam iti{*4/263*}, tathā darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, godohanena paśukāmasya praṇayet, kāṃsyena brahmavarcasakāmasya, mārtikena pratiṣṭhākāmasyety etāni naimittikāni. teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kim etāny eva naimittikāni nityārthe, utānyat tatra tatra{*4/264*} nityārtha iti.
kiṃ prāptam etāny eveti. kutaḥ? atra brahmasāmādibhir avaśyaṃ bhavitavyam, coditāni hi tāni, saṃnihitāni sādhanāny ākāṅkṣanti. na ca, eṣāṃ santi vihitāni sādhanāni, samīpataś ca naimittikāny upanipatanti, taiḥ prakṛtaiḥ saṃnihitair etāni nirākāṅkṣīkriyanta ity etan nyāyyam. katham? naimittikaṃ hi saṃnihitam, vākyād avagamyate nānyac chrūyate, yāvāṃś ca śrutasyotsarge doṣaḥ, tāvān evāśrutakalpanāyām.
āha, nanu nimittārthāni tāni prakṛtāni. ucyate, naiṣa doṣaḥ, anyārtham api prakṛtam anyena saṃbadhyate, yathā, śālyarthaṃ kulyāḥ praṇīyante, tābhyaś ca pānīyaṃ pīyate, upaspṛśyate ca. evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam. athavā, asty evātrāvāntaravākyam, yathā, godohanena praṇayed iti, tad akāmasaṃbaddhaṃ godohanena praṇayanaṃ prāpayati. na ca śakyaṃ śrutam utsraṣṭum. yo 'py ayam, [492]{*4/265*} paśukāmasyeti śabdaḥ, sa paśukāmasaṃbandhaṃ śaknuyāt kartum, nāvāntaravākyasyārthaṃ nivārayitum, na ca gamyamānam, vinā kāraṇena, avivakṣitam iti śakyaṃ vaditum. bhavanti ca dviṣṭhāni{*4/266*} vākyāni, yathā, śveto dhāvati, alambusānāṃ yāteti. tasmān naimittikāny eva nityārthe bhavitum arhantīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, naimittike śrūyamāṇe kratvartham anyat syād iti. kutaḥ? vikāratvād viśeṣe śrutatvād ity arthaḥ{*4/267*}. viśeṣe hi tatra naimittikaṃ śrūyate, tad asati tasmin viśeṣe na bhavitum arhati. yad uktam, avaśyakartavyānīti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, avaśyaṃ kartavyatvāt kariṣyante. yat tu nānyad eṣāṃ vihitaṃ sādhanam iti, sāmānyavihitaṃ bhaviṣyatīti na doṣaḥ. kiṃ tat? abhīvarto brahmasāma, aṣṭādaśamantragato 'gniḥ, vāraṇaṃ praṇayanapātram. atha yad uktam, saṃnihitaiḥ prakṛtair naimittikair brahmasāmādīni saṃbhatsyanta iti. neti brūmaḥ, na hi bārhadgirādīnāṃ prakaraṇam. athocyeta, prakṛtaiḥ stotrādibhiḥ saṃbadhyanta iti, etad api nopapadyate. yady api prakṛtāni nityāni stotrādīni, tathāpi vākyena nimittasaṃyoge śrūyante bārhadgirādīni, vākyaṃ ca prakaraṇād balīyaḥ.
yad uktam, saṃnidhānād vākyād avagato 'yam artha iti. na, evaṃjātīyako vākyārthaḥ sāmānyaṃ padārthaṃ{*4/268*} bādhitum arhati. nimittasaṃyoge hi bārhadgirādīnām arthavattā. tasmāt tatra tatrānyan naimittikād iti.
atha yad uktam, avāntaravākyena godohanam api prāpitaṃ na śakyam utsraṣṭum, ṛte kāraṇāt, avivakṣitaṃ kalpayitum{*4/269*}, [493]{*4/270*} dviṣṭhaṃ hi tad bhavatīti. ucyate, kāraṇād avivakṣitam. kiṃ kāraṇam? na hi, idaṃ yugapad bhavati, paripūrṇena cārthābhidhānam avāntaravākyena ceti. katham? praṇayatīti prapūrve nayatau vidhivibhaktiḥ svapadagatam arthaṃ śrutyā vidadhāti, praṇayanādisaṃbaddham api godohanādi śrutyā, vākyena ca. vastu phalasya godohanādeś ca saṃbandhaḥ. sa hitvā śrutyartham, kevalena vākyena. atha praṇayanasya godohanādisaṃbandham, godohanādeś ca phalena saṃbandhaṃ vadatīty ucyate. na{*4/271*}, dvyarthābhidhānād bhidyeta nitarāṃ vākyam, na caitan nyāyyam.
yat tu, śveto dhāvatītyevamādi, bhavet tatra viśeṣānavagamād ubhayārthāvagatiḥ. iha tu gamyate viśeṣaḥ kamipadoccāraṇam, sa iha śrauto 'rthaḥ. manyeta, yadi godohanādeḥ kriyāsaṃbandho vivakṣyate, kamipadaṃ pramādo bhavet. na cāyaṃ pramādaḥ, naivāvāntaravākyārthe vivakṣite kamipadasaṃbandho 'vakalpate. tasmān na dviṣṭhaṃ vākyam, godohanādikamisaṃbandha evātrābhidhīyate, na nityakārye bhavitum arhatīti, evaṃ sarvatra.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is a <s>naimittika</s> (occasional element): 'He should make the <s>Bārhadgira</s> the <s>Brahmasāman</s> for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>Pārthu Aśma</s> for a <s>Rājanya</s> (Kṣatriya), and the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> for a <s>Vaiśya</s>.' Likewise in the fire-building (<s>Agnicayana</s>) there is a <s>naimittika</s>: 'One building [the fire-altar] for the first time should build with one thousand [bricks], with two thousand for the second, with three thousand for the third.' Similarly in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon) rites it is heard: 'He should convey [the offering] with a cow-milking [vessel] for one desiring cattle, with a bronze [vessel] for one desiring spiritual luster, with an earthen [vessel] for one desiring a firm foundation.' These are <s>naimittika</s> (occasional) elements. Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: do these very <s>naimittika</s> elements serve the invariable (<s>nitya</s>) purpose, or is something else [the invariable element] in each case?
What is the prima facie view? These very [naimittika elements serve the invariable purpose]. Why? Because the <s>Brahmasāman</s> and the like must necessarily exist — for they are enjoined, and being proximate, they seek [their] instruments. And these have no [other] prescribed instruments; and the <s>naimittika</s> elements present themselves from proximity. That these are rendered free of expectancy by the proximate established [elements] — this is reasonable. How? For the <s>naimittika</s> is proximate; the meaning is understood from the sentence, and nothing else is heard. And the fault in abandoning what is heard is equal to that in conjecturing what is unheard.
[The objector] says: but those [naimittika elements] are established for the purpose of the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>). [We] reply: this is not a fault, for even what is established for one purpose can be connected with another — just as channels are dug for the sake of rice, yet water is drunk from them and ablutions are performed. Thus it should be viewed here too. Alternatively, there is indeed a sub-sentence here — for instance, 'he should convey with a cow-milking [vessel]' — that sub-sentence, unconnected with a desire, establishes the conveying with a cow-milking vessel. And what is heard cannot be abandoned. Even [492] the word 'for one desiring cattle' (<s>paśukāmasya</s>) — it can create a connection with the desire for cattle but cannot prevent the meaning of the sub-sentence. And what is understood cannot be said to be unintended without a reason. And there are sentences with dual reference (<s>dviṣṭha</s>), such as 'The white one runs' and 'The <s>Alambusās</s> have gone.' Therefore the <s>naimittika</s> elements alone deserve to serve the invariable purpose.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: when a <s>naimittika</s> is heard, something else should serve the ritual-act purpose. Why? Because of [its] being a modification — the meaning is: because it is heard in a specific [context]. For the <s>naimittika</s> is heard there in a specific [context]; in the absence of that specificity, it should not exist. As for what was said — 'they must necessarily be performed' — this is not a fault, for being necessarily to be performed, they will be performed. And as for 'there is no other prescribed instrument for them' — what is prescribed by the general [rule] will serve, so there is no fault. What is that? The <s>Abhīvarta</s> is the <s>Brahmasāman</s>; the fire consisting of eighteen mantras; and a regular vessel for conveying.
Now, as to what was said — 'the <s>Brahmasāman</s> and other [elements] will be fulfilled by the proximate established <s>naimittika</s> elements' — no, we say, for there is no contextual connection (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) for the <s>Bārhadgira</s> and others. And if it be said that they are connected with the established <s>stotra</s> and other [elements] in the context — this too is not tenable. Even though the invariable <s>stotra</s> and other [elements] are established [in the context], the <s>Bārhadgira</s> and others are heard in connection with a specific occasion by the sentence, and the sentence is stronger than the contextual connection.
As to what was said — 'this meaning is understood from proximity to the sentence' — no, a sentence-meaning of this kind should not override the general word-meaning. For the meaningfulness of the <s>Bārhadgira</s> and others [lies] in their connection with a specific occasion. Therefore in each case, something other than the <s>naimittika</s> [serves the invariable purpose].
Now, as to what was said — 'by the sub-sentence, the cow-milking [vessel] too is established and cannot be abandoned, and without a reason it cannot be supposed to be unintended [493] — for it is a sentence with dual reference' — we reply: it is unintended because of a reason. What is the reason? For this does not occur simultaneously — [namely,] the expression of meaning with the complete [sentence] and with the sub-sentence. How? The injunctive verbal ending in 'he should convey' (<s>praṇayet</s>), [formed from] the root 'nī' with the prefix 'pra,' prescribes by direct statement the meaning belonging to its own word, and also by direct statement and sentence, the cow-milking [vessel] and such connected with the conveying. But the connection of the fruit with the substance of the cow-milking [vessel] and such is by sentence alone, abandoning the meaning of the direct statement. If one says that [the sentence] states the connection of the conveying with the cow-milking and such, and the connection of the cow-milking and such with the fruit — no, the sentence would be excessively split by the expression of two meanings, and this is not reasonable.
As for [the example] 'the white one runs' and such — there the comprehension of both meanings may occur because no distinction is discerned. But here a distinction is discerned — the utterance of the word for desire (<s>kāmi</s>-word), which is the directly-heard meaning here. One might think that if the connection of the cow-milking [vessel] with the ritual act were intended, the desire-word would be an error. But this is not an error — when the meaning of the sub-sentence is not intended, the connection with the desire-word does not arise. Therefore the sentence does not have dual reference; only the connection of the cow-milking [vessel] and such with the desire is stated here; [they] should not serve the invariable ritual purpose — and so in every case.

children.text: ekasya tūbhayatve saṃyogapṛthaktvam // MS_4,3.5 //
children.translated_text: But when a single [element] has dual status, the separation of connections [is the cause]. // MS_4,3.5 //

children.text: agnihotre śrūyate, dadhnā juhotīti, punaś ca, dadhnendriyakāmasya juhuyād iti. tathāgnīṣomīye paśāv āmnāyate, khādire badhnātīti, punaś ca, khādiraṃ vīryakāmasya yūpaṃ kuryād iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim atrāpy anyan nityārtham, [494]{*4/272*} uta naimittikam eveti. kiṃ prāptam? pūrveṇa nyāyenānyad iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ekasyobhayatve nityatve naimittikatve ca{*4/273*} saṃyogapṛthaktvaṃ kāraṇam. tad iha saṃyogapṛthaktvam asti, ekaḥ saṃyogo dadhnā juhotīti, eko dadhnendriyakāmasyeti, tathaikaḥ, khādire badhnātīti, aparaḥ, khādiraṃ vīryakāmasyeti. tasmān nityārthe kāmāya ca dadhikhādirādīti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Agnihotra</s> it is heard: 'He offers with curds (<s>dadhi</s>).' And again: 'One desiring sense-faculties should offer with curds.' Likewise in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice] it is taught: 'He binds [the victim] to a <s>khadira</s> [post].' And again: 'One desiring vigor should make the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) of <s>khadira</s> wood.' There a doubt [arises]: is something else the invariable [element] here too [494], or is it the <s>naimittika</s> itself? What is the prima facie view? By the preceding principle, something else [serves the invariable purpose]. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: when a single [element] has dual status — both invariable and occasional — the separation of connections is the cause. Here there is a separation of connections: one connection is 'he offers with curds,' another is 'one desiring sense-faculties [offers] with curds'; likewise one is 'he binds to a <s>khadira</s> [post],' another is 'one desiring vigor [should have] a <s>khadira</s> [post].' Therefore curds, <s>khadira</s>, and such serve both the invariable purpose and the desire.

children.text: śeṣa iti cet // MS_4,3.6 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues that] it is a subordinate [part of the same sentence] — // MS_4,3.6 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, kasmān na pūrvasyāyam api śeṣo bhavati? yad etad uktam, dadhnā juhoti, khādire badhnātīti, tasyaiva tu dadhnaḥ phalam indriyam, tathā khādirasya vīryam. tac cedaṃ caikaṃ vākyam iti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus: why should not this too be a subordinate part (<s>śeṣa</s>) of the former [statement]? What was stated — 'he offers with curds,' 'he binds to a <s>khadira</s> [post]' — of that very curds, the fruit is sense-faculties; likewise of <s>khadira</s>, the fruit is vigor. And this would be a single sentence.

children.text: nārthapṛthaktvāt // MS_4,3.7 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the separateness of meaning. // MS_4,3.7 //

children.text: naitad evam, pṛthag etāv arthau, yaś ca dadhihomasaṃyogaḥ, yaś ca dadhīndriyasaṃyogaḥ, tathā khādirasya badhnātinā saṃyogo vīryeṇa ca. dvāv etāv arthau, dvāv api ca vidhitsitau, arthaikatvāc caikaṃ vākyaṃ samadhigatam. ihārthadvayena bhidyeta vākyam. katham? juhotisamabhi[495]{*4/274*}vyāhṛtā vidhivibhaktiḥ, asaṃbhave śrautasya homavidhānasya{*4/275*}, guṇaṃ samabhivyāhṛtaṃ vidhātum arhati, tad asaṃbhave guṇaphalasaṃbandham. tatra hy atyantāya śrutir utsṛṣṭā vākyānurodhena syāt, na ca yugapat saṃbhavāsaṃbhavau saṃbhavataḥ. tasmād yad eva naimittikaṃ tad eva nityārtham iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so. These two meanings are separate: the connection of curds with the oblation, and the connection of curds with sense-faculties; likewise the connection of <s>khadira</s> with 'he binds' and with vigor. These are two meanings, and both are intended [to be prescribed]. From unity of meaning, a single sentence was understood. Here, with duality of meaning, the sentence would be split. How? The injunctive verbal ending conjoined with 'he offers' (<s>juhoti</s>) [495] — when the directly-heard ritual injunction cannot apply, the subordinate [element] conjoined [with the verb] can be prescribed; when that too cannot apply, [it prescribes] the connection of the subordinate [element] with the fruit. For in that case, the direct statement would be entirely abandoned in deference to the sentence — and possibility and impossibility cannot occur simultaneously. Therefore what is <s>naimittika</s> is itself the invariable [element].

children.text: dravyāṇāṃ tu kriyārthānām saṃskāraḥ kratudharmaḥ syāt // MS_4,3.8 //
children.translated_text: But for substances that serve ritual acts, their consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) should be a property of the sacrifice. // MS_4,3.8 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome samāmananti - payovrataṃ brāhmaṇasya, yavāgū rājanyasya, āmikṣā vaiśyasyeti{*4/276*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim ayaṃ puruṣadharmaḥ, uta krator iti. prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā vākyena viniyuktaḥ puruṣasyeti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, puruṣāṇāṃ kriyārthānāṃ śarīradhāraṇārtho balakaraṇārthaś cāyaṃ saṃskāro vrataṃ nāma, sa kratudharmo bhavitum arhati, prakaraṇānugrahāya. nanu vākyāt puruṣadharma iti. neti brūmaḥ, tathā sati phalaṃ kalpyam, kḹptam itaratra. prayogavacanenopasaṃhṛtaṃ hi tatpradhānasya. tasmāt kratudharmaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is taught: 'The milk-vow (<s>payovrata</s>) is for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, barley-gruel (<s>yavāgū</s>) for the <s>Rājanya</s> (Kṣatriya), curd-whey (<s>āmikṣā</s>) for the <s>Vaiśya</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is this a property of the person, or of the sacrifice? [The prima facie view:] overriding the contextual connection by the sentence, it is assigned to the person. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: for persons who serve ritual acts, this consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) called 'vow' (<s>vrata</s>) — [which serves] the purpose of maintaining the body and producing strength — should be a property of the sacrifice, in deference to the contextual connection. But [the objector says], by the sentence it is a property of the person. No, we say — in that case, a fruit would need to be conjectured, whereas [a fruit] is [already] established in the other [interpretation]. For it is subsumed by the statement of employment as belonging to the principal [sacrifice]. Therefore it is a property of the sacrifice.

NOTES:
[{4/276: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.2.5.2-3}]

children.text: pṛthaktvād vyavatiṣṭheta{*4/277*} // MS_4,3.9 //
children.translated_text: Because of the separateness [of the connection with the person], it would be a restriction (<s>vyavasthā</s>). // MS_4,3.9 //

children.text: atha puruṣasaṃyogaḥ kim arthaḥ? vyavasthāpanārtha iti brūmaḥ, payovrataṃ jyotiṣṭomasya bhavati, tat tu brāhmaṇakartṛkasyaiva, nānyakartṛkasyeti. evaṃ sarvatra.
children.translated_text: Now, what is the purpose of the connection with the person? We say: it is for the purpose of restriction — the milk-vow belongs to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, but only when performed by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, not when performed by another. And so in every case.

children.text: codanāyāṃ phalāśruteḥ karmamātraṃ vidhīyeta na hy aśabdaṃ pratīyate // MS_4,3.10 //
children.translated_text: When in the injunction there is no mention of a fruit, only the ritual act itself is prescribed; for what is not [expressed] by a word is not apprehended. // MS_4,3.10 //

children.text:
idam āmananti, tasmāt pitṛbhyaḥ pūrvedyuḥ karotīti{*4/279*}, tathā, sarvebhyo vā eṣa devebhyaḥ sarvebhyaś chandobhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pṛṣṭhebhya ātmānam āgurate, yaḥ satrāyāgurate, sa viśvajitātirātreṇa sarvapṛṣṭhena sarvastomena sarvavedasadakṣiṇena yajetety{*4/280*} evaṃlakṣaṇake śrute, bhavati saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ niṣphalam etat karmamātram, uta saphalam iti. kiṃ prāptam? niṣphalam iti. kutaḥ? phalāśruteḥ, śabdapramāṇake karmaṇy evaṃjātīyake. na hy aśabdaṃ pratīyate.
nanu vaidikāni karmāṇi phalavanti bhavantīty evam uktam. ucyate, phaladarśanāt tāni phalavantīty uktam, na vaidikatvāt. evaṃ tarhi kartavyatāvagamāt phalavantīty adhyavasyāmaḥ, sukhaphalaṃ hi kartavyaṃ bhavatīti. ucyate, pratyakṣaviruddham evaṃjātiyakasya kartavyatvam, sākṣād dhi tad duḥkhaphalam agacchāmaḥ. na caivaṃjātīyakaṃ pratyakṣaviruddhaṃ vacanaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavati, yathāmbuni majjanty alābūni, śilāḥ plavante, pāvakaḥ śīta iti. api ca, anumānād atra sukhaphalatā, yasmāt kartavyam ataḥ sukhaphalam iti, pratyakṣaṃ cānumānād balīyaḥ. tasmān niṣphalam evaṃjātīyakam iti.
evaṃ hy atra phalaṃ kalpyeta, yady etat phalavat, evam upadeśo 'rthavān bhavatīti. ucyate, kāmaṃ vākyam anarthakam iti nyāyyaṃ vacanaṃ bhavet, bhavanti hy anarthakāny api vacanāni, [497]{*4/281*} daśa dāḍimāni, ṣaḍapūyā{*4/282*} ity evaṃjātīyakāni. nanu viśvajidvyāpāraḥ sukhaphala iti. uttaram{*4/283*}, sukhaphalaṃ hi bhavaty apūrvam, na vyāpāraḥ, na cāyam apūrvasya kartavyatām āha, phalakartavyatāyāṃ hi satyāṃ tad avagamyate, vākyārthaś ca phalasya kartavyatām āha, na padārthaḥ. na cātra phalasaṃbaddhaṃ vākyam asti. tasmān nāyam apūrvasya vidhāyakaḥ śabdaḥ, vyāpāramātram eva{*4/284*} vidadhāti, sa ca vyāpāro na tadātve sukhaphalaḥ, nāpy āyatyām, bhaṅgitvāt. tatrāpūrvaṃ kalpayitvā phalam avagamyeta, phalaṃ ca kalpayitvāpūrvam. evam itaretarāśrayaṃ bhavati, itaretarāśrayāṇi ca na{*4/285*} prakalpante. tasmān niṣphalam evaṃjātīyakam iti.
āha, adhyāhariṣyāmahe phalavacanam{*4/286*}. ucyate, na śakyaṃ paripūrṇe vākye 'dhyāhartum, paripūrṇaṃ hīdaṃ vākyam, viśvajidyāgaḥ kartavya iti. na, kiṃcit padam asti sākāṅkṣam, yenādhyāhṛtya phalaṃ saṃbadhyeta, yathākṣeme 'pi pathi{*4/287*}, bhavati vipralambhakopadeśaḥ{*4/288*}, kṣemo 'yam, yathā gacchatu bhavān aneneti. paripūrṇam evedaṃ vākyam, nādhyāhāram arhati vipralambhakakartṛkam{*4/289*}, evam idam api paripūrṇaṃ vākyaṃ nādhyāhāram arhati. api ca, adhyāhriyamāṇenaivedaṃ vākyaṃ saṃbadhyeta, viśvajidyāgaḥ kartavyaḥ, idaṃ ca phalaṃ bhavatīti, dvāv imāv arthau, ekārthaṃ ca vākyaṃ samadhigatam. tasmād anarthakam evaṃjātīyakaṃ karmeti.
children.translated_text:
This is what they state: 'Therefore he performs [the rite] for the ancestors on the preceding day.' Likewise: 'He who consecrates himself for the <s>Satra</s> (session) indeed pledges himself to all the gods, to all the meters, and to all the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants. He should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering) <s>Atirātra</s>, with all the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>, with all the <s>Stomas</s>, with all the Vedic texts as sacrificial fees.' When such a [Vedic] statement is heard, a doubt arises: is this action fruitless, being mere [ritual] activity, or is it fruitful? What is the prima facie view? It is fruitless. Why? Because no fruit is stated, and in an action whose authority is the [Vedic] word, of this kind, what is not [stated by] the word is not understood.
But was it not said that Vedic rites are fruitful? We reply: those are said to be fruitful because a fruit is seen [stated for them], not because they are Vedic. Then let us conclude they are fruitful from the understanding that they are to be performed, for what is to be performed has a pleasant fruit. We reply: the obligatoriness of this kind [of rite] is contradicted by direct perception, for we directly see that it has an unpleasant fruit. And a statement of this kind that contradicts direct perception is not a valid means of knowledge — like [saying] 'gourds sink in water, stones float, fire is cold.' Moreover, the pleasant-fruitedness here is [merely] from inference — 'since it is to be performed, therefore it has a pleasant fruit' — and direct perception is stronger than inference. Therefore, things of this kind are fruitless.
Thus the fruit would have to be supposed here: 'if this is fruitful, then the teaching would be meaningful.' We reply: it is proper even that the sentence be meaningless, for there are indeed meaningless statements — [497] such as 'ten pomegranates, six cakes' and the like. But [the objector says], the performance of the <s>Viśvajit</s> has a pleasant fruit. The reply: it is the <s>apūrva</s> (transcendent potency) that has a pleasant fruit, not the [physical] activity. And this [statement] does not teach the obligatoriness of the <s>apūrva</s>, for that is understood only when there is obligatoriness of the fruit; and the sentence-meaning teaches the obligatoriness of the fruit, not the word-meaning [alone]. And here there is no sentence connected with a fruit. Therefore this word does not enjoin the <s>apūrva</s>; it enjoins mere activity. And that activity has no pleasant fruit at the present time, nor in the future, because of [its] transient nature. There, one would understand the fruit by positing the <s>apūrva</s>, and [one would posit] the <s>apūrva</s> by positing the fruit. Thus there is mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>), and mutually dependent [arguments] do not hold.
Therefore things of this kind are fruitless.
[The objector] says: we shall supply the statement of fruit [from elsewhere]. We reply: it is not possible to supply [anything] to a complete sentence, for this sentence is complete: 'the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice is to be performed.' There is no word that is expectant, with which, by supplying, the fruit could be connected. Just as even on a safe road, there can be a deceptive instruction — 'this is safe; let your honor travel by this [road]' — this sentence too is complete and does not deserve supplementation by the deceiver. Similarly, this too is a complete sentence and does not deserve supplementation. Moreover, even if supplemented, this sentence would be connected [thus]: 'the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice is to be performed, and this fruit occurs' — these are two meanings, whereas the sentence has been understood as having a single meaning. Therefore things of this kind are fruitless.

children.translated_text: Or rather, by the capacity of the [Vedic] recitation, [the fruit] may be understood through the purpose of the injunction — for statements are understood as meaningful through the meaningfulness of their contents; for those that are meaningless in content, even when adjacent, there is no connection. Therefore, that [fruit-word] is a part of the [Vedic] text. // MS_4,3.11 //

api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. na caitad asti, aphalam iti, phalacodanā, arthena gamyeta. katamenārthena? kartavyatāvacanena. āha, nanu vyāpārasya pratyakṣaviruddhā kartavyatā. na vyāpārasyocyate. kasya tarhi? vyāpāreṇānyasya kasyacid iti, bhavati tenedānīṃ vākyaṃ sākāṅkṣam. tatrādhyāhāro 'vakalpate, bhavati cādhyāhāreṇāpi kalpanā, yathā dvāraṃ dvāram ity ukte, saṃvriyatām apāvriyatām iti{*4/291*}. kathaṃ punar avagamyate, ihādhyāhāreṇa kalpayitavyam iti. āmnānasāmarthyāt, evam idam āmnānam arthavad bhaviṣyati, śaknoti cārtham avagamayitum. tasmān nānarthakam.
nanu yat padam adhyāhriyate, tat pauruṣeyam, tenāvagataṃ cāpramāṇam. ucyate, nāpūrvam adhyāhariṣyāmaḥ, vaidikenaivāsya, sahānyatra samāmnātena, ekavākyatām adhyavasāmaḥ. āha, naivaṃ śakyam, antikād upanipatitaṃ hi padam{*4/292*}, vākyārtham upajanayitum alaṃ bhavati, na dūrād avatiṣṭhamānam. atrocyate, vyavahitam api hi, parāṇudya vyavadhāyakam, ānantaryeṇa manasi viparivartamānam alam eva bhavati viśeṣam upajanayitum. yathā -
itaḥ paśyasi dhāvantaṃ dūre jātaṃ vanaspatim/
tvāṃ bravīmi viśālākṣi yā pinakṣi jarad gavam// [499]{*4/293*} iti, itaḥ{*4/294*} paśyasīti śabdo buddhau bhavati, saḥ dūre jātaṃ vanaspatim{*4/295*}, etaiḥ padair vyavahitena jarad gavam ity anena śabdena vyavadhāyakāny apodya saṃbadhyamānaḥ saṃbadhyate, arthānāṃ hy arthavattvena hetunā vyavahitāny api vacanāni saṃbadhyante. yāni punar arthato hy asamarthāni, tāny ānantarye 'pi sati na paraspareṇa saṃbandham arhanti, yathā yā pinakṣi jarad gavam ityevamādīni. tasmān na pauruṣeyatā bhaviṣyati. āha, nanv atrāpy apekṣā pauruṣeyī. ucyate, nāpekṣā vede, vedārthapratipattāv abhyupāya eṣa bhavati, ananatarāpekṣāyām asaṃbhavantyām āmnānasāmarthyād itarāpekṣāvṛttir āśrīyate. tasmāc chruty ekadeśaḥ saḥ, phalakāmapadaṃ dūre 'pi sat tasya vākyasyaikadeśabhūtam ity arthaḥ{*4/296*}.
children.translated_text:
The word <s>api vā</s> ('or rather') marks a reversal of position. This [view] does not hold — that [the rite] is fruitless. The injunction of fruit may be understood through the content. By what content? By the statement of obligatoriness. [The objector] says: but the obligatoriness of the [physical] activity is contradicted by direct perception. [We reply:] it is not said of the activity. Of what then? 'Of something else, through the activity' — thereby the sentence becomes expectant [of completion]. There, supplementation is possible, and construction through supplementation does occur — just as when one says 'the door! the door!' it is understood as 'let it be closed' or 'let it be opened.' But how is it understood that here supplementation is to be made? Through the capacity of the [Vedic] recitation — thus this recitation will become meaningful, and it is capable of conveying meaning. Therefore it is not meaningless.
But [the objector says], the word that is supplied is human [in origin]; therefore what is understood through it is not a valid means of knowledge. We reply: we shall not supply something unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>); we shall establish syntactic unity with this [statement] through a Vedic [statement] itself, one that is recorded together [with it] elsewhere. [The objector] says: this is not possible, for a word that has come from proximity is capable of generating sentence-meaning, not one that stands at a distance. To this we reply: even what is separated, by pushing aside the intervening [material], revolving in the mind through contiguity, is indeed capable of generating a specific [meaning]. Just as [in the verse]:
'From here you see [one] running, a tree born afar —
I address you, wide-eyed one, who grind old cattle' —
the word 'from here you see' is in the mind; it, [connected with] 'a tree born afar,' by pushing aside the intervening words — 'who grind old cattle' — is connected with them. For statements are connected even when separated, through the reason of their contents being meaningful. But those that are meaningless in content — even when adjacent, they do not deserve connection with each other — like 'who grind old cattle' and the like. Therefore it will not be of human origin. [The objector] says: but even here the expectation [requiring supplementation] is of human origin. We reply: there is no [such] expectation in the <s>Veda</s>; this is a method for understanding the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>. When the expectation from proximity is impossible, the recourse to expectation from elsewhere is adopted through the capacity of the [Vedic] recitation. Therefore that [fruit-word] is a part of the [Vedic] text — the word denoting desire for fruit, even though distant, is a part of that sentence: this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: And the sentence-meaning is like [that of] a subsidiary [element] with respect to [its] purpose. // MS_4,3.12 //

children.text: indrāya rājñe śūkara{*4/297*} iti{*4/298*} yathā vākyāntarasthena vidhiśabdena guṇavidhānaṃ bhavati, evaṃ phalavidhānam api bhavitum arhatīti, yathā varuṇo vaitam agre pratyagṛhṇād iti{*4/299*} vyavadhāraṇakalpanā. evam{*4/300*} idam api draṣṭavyam.
children.translated_text: Just as in '<s>indrāya rājñe śūkara</s>' ('a boar for <s>Indra</s> the king'), the injunction of a subsidiary is made by an injunctive word standing in another sentence, so too the injunction of fruit should be possible — just as in 'Indeed <s>Varuṇa</s> seized this one first,' the construction is by determination [from context]. So too this should be viewed.
