children.text: tat sarvārtham anādeśāt // MS_4,3.13 //
children.translated_text: That [rite] serves all purposes, because of the absence of specification. // MS_4,3.13 //

children.text: tasmāt pitṛbhyaḥ pūrvedyuḥ karotīti{*4/301*}. viśvajitā yajeteti phalavad evaṃvidhaṃ karmety etat samadhigatam. idaṃ tu saṃdihyate, kiṃ sarvaphalam etat karma, utaikaphalam iti. kiṃ prāptam? tat sarvārtham iti. kutaḥ? anādeśāt, [500]{*4/302*} na kiṃcid ihātidiśyate, idaṃ nāma phalam iti. asti cet, vijñāyeta. tasmāt sarvārtham aviśeṣāt.
children.translated_text: 'Therefore he performs [the rite] for the ancestors on the preceding day.' [It has been] established that a rite of this kind — 'he should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>' — is fruitful. But this is doubted: does this rite serve all purposes, or a single purpose? What is the prima facie view? It serves all purposes. Why? Because of the absence of specification — [500] nothing is specified here [as]: 'this is the fruit.' If there were [such specification], it would be known. Therefore, because of the absence of distinction, it serves all purposes.

children.text: ekaṃ vā codanaikatvāt // MS_4,3.14 //
children.translated_text: Or [it yields] a single [fruit], because of the unity of the injunction. // MS_4,3.14 //

children.text: ekaṃ phalaṃ{*4/303*} syāt, na vā sarvārtham. kutaḥ? codanaikatvāt, sakāṅkṣatvād etad arthipadena saṃbadhyata ity uktam, yac cānekenāpi saṃbaddhuṃ śaknoti, tad ekena saṃbadhyate, ekena saṃbaddhaṃ san nirākāṅkṣaṃ bhavati, na tad apareṇāpi saṃbandham arhati. tasmād ekaiva kartavyatācodanā{*4/304*} nyāyyā, tasmād ekaphalateti.
children.translated_text: It should have a single fruit, and not serve all purposes. Why? Because of the unity of the injunction. It has been said that because of being expectant, this [sentence] is connected with the desiderative word. And what can be connected with many [things] is connected with one — being connected with one, it becomes non-expectant and does not deserve connection with yet another. Therefore a single injunction of obligatoriness alone is appropriate; hence it has a single fruit.

children.text: sa svargaḥ syāt, sarvān pratyaviśiṣṭatvāt // MS_4,3.15 //
children.translated_text: That [fruit] should be heaven, because of [its] being undifferentiated with respect to all [people]. // MS_4,3.15 //

children.text: evaṃjātīyakeṣv evodāhāraṇeṣv{*4/305*} etat samadhigatam, ekaṃ phalam iti. idam idānīṃ saṃdihyate, kiṃ yatkiṃcit, uta svarga iti. yatkiṃcid iti prāptam, viśeṣānabhidhānāt, tata ucyate, sa svargaḥ syāt sarvān pratyaviśiṣṭatvāt, sarve hi puruṣāḥ svargakāmāḥ. kuta etat? prītir hi svargaḥ, sarvaś ca prītiṃ prārthayate. kim ataḥ? yady evam, aviśeṣavacanaḥ śabdo na viśeṣe vyavasthāpito bhaviṣyati, yajeta kuryād iti. tasmāt svargaphalam evaṃjātīyakam iti.
children.translated_text: It has been established in examples of this very kind that the fruit is single. Now this is doubted: is it any [fruit] whatsoever, or is it heaven? The prima facie view is any [fruit] whatsoever, because no specific [fruit] is stated. To this we say: that should be heaven, because of [its] being undifferentiated with respect to all [people] — for all persons desire heaven. How is this [known]? Because heaven is happiness (<s>prīti</s>), and everyone seeks happiness. What follows? If so, a word that does not state a specific [thing] will not be fixed upon a specific [thing] — [words like] 'he should sacrifice,' 'he should perform.' Therefore, things of this kind have heaven as their fruit.

children.text: pratyayāc ca // MS_4,3.16 //
children.translated_text: And because of common understanding. // MS_4,3.16 //

children.text: bhavati ca, anādiṣṭaphale karmaṇi svargaḥ phalam iti pratyayo loke, evam ucyate, ārāmakṛd devadattaḥ, niyato 'sya svargaḥ. [501]{*4/306*} taḍāgakṛd devadattaḥ, niyato 'sya svarga iti. kim ataḥ? yady evam, ittham anena nyāyena svarge saṃpratyayo bhavati, yasmāt svargaphaleṣu karmasu kartavyeṣu phalavacanaṃ naivoccārayanti, gamyata eveti. tasmād apy avagacchāmaḥ, evaṃjātīyakeṣu svargaḥ phalam iti.
children.translated_text: And there is a common understanding in the world that when a rite has no specified fruit, the fruit is heaven. Thus it is said: '<s>Devadatta</s> plants gardens — his heaven is assured.' [501] '<s>Devadatta</s> builds reservoirs — his heaven is assured.' What follows? If so, by this reasoning there is conviction regarding heaven — since in rites that have heaven as their fruit and are to be performed, they never even utter a statement of fruit, [because] it is understood [automatically]. Therefore, from this too we understand that for things of this kind, heaven is the fruit.

children.text: kratau phalārthavādam aṅgavat kārṣṇājiniḥ // MS_4,3.17 //
children.translated_text: In a ritual, a fruit-<s>arthavāda</s> (eulogy) is like a subsidiary [element]; [this is the view of] <s>Kārṣṇājini</s>. // MS_4,3.17 //

children.text: rātrīḥ prakṛtya śrūyate, pratitiṣṭhanti ha vaite, ya etā upayanti{*4/307*}. brahmavarcasvino 'nnādā bhavanti, ya etā upayantīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ te phalārthavādāḥ, uta phalavidhaya iti. kiṃ prāptam? phalārthavādā iti kārṣājinir mene. kutaḥ? phalārthavādasarūpā ete śabdā iti. kiṃ sārūpyam? vidhivibhakter abhāvaḥ, aṅgavat{*4/308*}, yathā yasya khādiraḥ sruvo bhavati, sa chandasām eva rasenāvadyatītyevamādiṣu{*4/309*}.
children.translated_text: With reference to the nights [of consecration], it is heard: 'They indeed become established — those who undertake these [nights]. They become possessors of <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual luster) and eaters of food — those who undertake these.' There a doubt [arises]: are these fruit-<s>arthavādas</s> (eulogistic passages about fruit), or are they injunctions of fruit? What is the prima facie view? They are fruit-<s>arthavādas</s> — so <s>Kārṣṇājini</s> held. Why? Because these words have the form of fruit-<s>arthavāda</s>. What is the similarity? The absence of the injunctive verbal ending — like a subsidiary [element], just as in 'He whose ladle is of <s>khadira</s> wood — he milks by the essence of the meters alone' and similar [statements].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/307: E2: vā ya etā rātrīr upayanti}*
*{4/308: E2: bhaṅgavat}*
*{4/309: Tait.S. 3.5.7.1}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/307: E2: <s>vā ya etā rātrīr upayanti</s>}]
[{4/308: E2: <s>bhaṅgavat</s>}]
[{4/309: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.5.7.1}]

children.text: phalamātreyo nirdeśād aśrutau hy anumānaṃ syāt // MS_4,3.18 //
children.translated_text: The fruit [is real] — [so says] <s>Ātreya</s>, because of the designation; for in the absence of [direct] hearing, there would be inference. // MS_4,3.18 //

children.text:
ātreyaḥ punar ācārya evaṃjātīyakebhyaḥ, phalam astīti mene, na phalārthavāda iti. kutaḥ? aśrutaphalatve 'py amīṣām, phalacodanayā vākyaśeṣabhūtayā bhavitavyam. tasmād anyā vyavahitā satī, avyavahitā kalpanīyā, iyaṃ tv avyavahitā kḹptaiva, pratiṣṭhayā brahmavarcasasattayā ca samabhivyāhāra āsāṃ pratyakṣaḥ, vidhivibhaktimātram anyato 'pekṣyam.
[502]{*4/310*} āha, kathaṃ kevalaṃ vidhivibhaktimātram anyato bhaviṣyati? yad anena pratiṣṭhādinā dhātvarthena saṃbhantsyata iti. ucyate, saha dhātvarthena bhaviṣyati, na kevalam. tasmād adoṣaḥ. athavā rātrīṇāṃ yā vidhāyikā vibhaktiḥ, sā imam api pratiṣṭhādiviśeṣaṃ vidhāsyati prayogavacanena, stutir vā saha pratiṣṭhādibhir vidhātrī bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text:
The teacher <s>Ātreya</s>, however, regarding [passages] of this kind, held that a fruit does exist — not that it is <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogy) of the fruit. Why? Even though the fruit is not directly heard for these [passages], there must be a fruit-injunction that completes the sentence. Therefore, when another [injunction] is separated [from the passage], a proximate one should be postulated; but this one is already proximate and established — the co-occurrence of these [nights] with stability and the possession of <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual luster) is directly perceptible, and only the injunctive verbal ending needs to be sought from elsewhere.
[502] [The objector] asks: how will just the injunctive verbal ending alone come from elsewhere — [i.e.,] that which will be connected with this verbal root meaning of 'stability' etc.? We reply: it will come together with the verbal root meaning, not alone. Therefore there is no fault. Alternatively, the injunctive case ending that enjoins the nights will also enjoin this specific [content of] stability etc. by the statement of performance; or the praise (<s>stuti</s>) together with stability etc. will serve as the enjoiner.

children.text: aṅgeṣu stutiḥ parārthatvāt // MS_4,3.19 //
children.translated_text: In subsidiary elements, it is praise, because of being for another's purpose. // MS_4,3.19 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, yathā yasya khādiraḥ sruvo bhavatītyevamādiṣu{*4/311*} phalaśrutir arthavādo bhavati, evam ihāpi syād iti, yuktaṃ tatra phalārthavādaḥ, phalavidhyasaṃbhavāt, phalārthavādasaṃbavāc ca. tad uktam, dravyasaṃskārakarmasu parārthatvāt phalaśrutir arthavādaḥ syād iti{*4/312*}.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'just as in passages like "he whose <s>sruva</s> (ladle) is made of <s>khadira</s> wood" etc., the fruit-statement is <s>arthavāda</s>, so too it should be here' — it is appropriate there that the fruit is <s>arthavāda</s>, because of the impossibility of a fruit-injunction, and because of the possibility of a fruit-<s>arthavāda</s>. As stated: 'In substance-refinement-actions, because of being for another's purpose, the fruit-statement should be <s>arthavāda</s>.'

NOTES:
[{4/311: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.5.7.1}]
[{4/312: MS 4.3.1}]

children.text: kāmye karmaṇi nityaḥ svargo yathā yajñāṅge kratvarthaḥ // MS_4,3.20 //
children.translated_text: In a <s>kāmya</s> (desire-motivated) rite, <s>svarga</s> (heaven) is invariable — just as in a subsidiary element of a sacrifice, [the fruit] serves the ritual act. // MS_4,3.20 //

children.text: kāmyāni karmāṇy udāharaṇam, sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāma ityevamādīnīti{*4/313*}{*4/314*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim eṣāṃ svargaḥ phalaṃ kāmaś ca, uta kāma eveti. kiṃ prāptam? kāmye karmaṇi nityaḥ svargaḥ syāt. katham? sarvapuruṣārthābhidhāyī sāmānyavacanaḥ śabdo na viśeṣe 'vasthāpito bhavati, śakyate hy asya dūrasthenāpi svargakāmaśabdena saṃbandhaḥ. āha, nanu viśeṣakaḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate, brahmavarcasakāma iti. naiṣa viśeṣakaḥ, upādhikara eṣaḥ, yathā kāṣṭhāny āhartuṃ prasthita ucyate, bhavatā śākam apy āhartavyam iti, kāṣṭhāharaṇe [503]{*4/315*} śākāharaṇam upādhiḥ kriyata iti. kim idam upādhiḥ kriyata iti. kāṣṭhāharaṇādhikārasamīpe dvitīyaṃ karmopadhīyate, sati kāṣṭhāharaṇe, idam aparaṃ kartavyam iti. evam ihāpi svargaphale phalam aparam upadhīyate, brahmavarcasakāmo yāgena svargam abhinirvartayed iti. na hi tatra brahmavarcasaphalavacanaṃ svargaphalasya pratiṣedhakam, yathā yajñāṅge kratvarthaḥ, godohanena paśukāmasya praṇayed iti. yaḥ paśukāmaḥ sa godohanena praṇayanam abhinirvartayed iti.
children.translated_text: The <s>kāmya</s> (desire-motivated) rites are the example — such as 'one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual luster) should offer a <s>caru</s> (oblation) to <s>Sūrya</s>' and the like. There a doubt [arises]: is <s>svarga</s> (heaven) the fruit of these [rites] along with the [specific] desire, or is the desire alone [the fruit]? What is the prima facie view? In a <s>kāmya</s> rite, <s>svarga</s> should be invariable [i.e., always present as a fruit]. How? The word that denotes all human goals — a general term — is not confined to a specific [meaning]; for it can be connected with the word '<s>svargakāma</s>' (desiring heaven) even when that [word] is remote. [The objector] says: but a specifying word is heard — '<s>brahmavarcasakāma</s>' (desiring spiritual luster). [We reply:] this is not a specifier; it is a condition (<s>upādhi</s>) — just as when one who has set out to bring firewood is told, 'You should also bring vegetables,' the bringing of vegetables is made a condition upon the bringing of firewood. [503] What does 'made a condition' mean? A second action is superimposed near the domain of the firewood-bringing — 'given that firewood is [being] brought, this other thing too should be done.' Thus here too, upon the fruit of <s>svarga</s>, another fruit is superimposed — 'one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> should accomplish <s>svarga</s> through the sacrifice.' For the statement of <s>brahmavarcas</s> as fruit does not prohibit the fruit of <s>svarga</s> — just as in a subsidiary element of a sacrifice, [the fruit] serves the ritual act: 'one desiring cattle should have the driving-out performed by [the recitation of the] <s>godohana</s> [hymn].' He who desires cattle should accomplish the driving-out through the <s>godohana</s>.

children.text: vīte ca kāraṇe niyamāt // MS_4,3.21 //
children.translated_text: And when the cause has ceased, because of the rule [regarding completion]. // MS_4,3.21 //

children.text: vīte ca kāraṇe, vītāyāṃ phalecchāyām avāpte vā phale samāptiniyamo dṛśyate, vṛṣṭikāmeṣṭyām, yadi varṣet tāvaty eva juhuyāt, yadi na varṣet, śvobhūte juhuyād iti{*4/316*}. yadi na svargaḥ, kim arthaḥ samāptiniyamo bhavet. tasmān nityaḥ svarga iti.
children.translated_text: And when the cause has ceased — when the desire for the fruit has ceased, or when the fruit has been obtained — a rule of completion is observed. In the <s>Vṛṣṭikāmeṣṭi</s> (rain-desiring sacrifice): 'If it rains, one should offer only that much; if it does not rain, one should offer on the following day.' If <s>svarga</s> were not [a fruit], for what purpose would the rule of completion exist? Therefore <s>svarga</s> is invariable.

NOTES:
[{4/316: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.4.10.1}]

children.text: kāmo vā tatsaṃyogena codyate // MS_4,3.22 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, [the specific] desire is [the fruit], for it is enjoined through connection with that [desire]. // MS_4,3.22 //

children.text: kāmo vā phalaṃ bhavet, na svargaḥ, tatsaṃyogenāsya codanā bhavati, na svargakāmasaṃyogena, ānumāniko 'sya svargakāmenaikavākyabhāvaḥ. pratyakṣas tu kāmavacanena, pratyakṣaṃ cānumānād balīyaḥ. tasmāt kāma eva phalam iti.
children.translated_text: Or rather, the desire [alone] would be the fruit, not <s>svarga</s>. Its injunction comes through connection with that [specific desire], not through connection with the desire for <s>svarga</s>. Its sentence-unity with [the desire for] <s>svarga</s> is [merely] inferential, whereas [its connection] with the desire-statement is directly perceptible, and what is directly perceptible is stronger than inference. Therefore the desire alone is the fruit.

children.text: aṅge guṇatvāt // MS_4,3.23 //
children.translated_text: In a subsidiary element, because of subordinate status. // MS_4,3.23 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, yathā yajñāṅga{*4/317*} iti, yuktam aṅge guṇatvāt. pratyakṣas tatra ṛtunā saṃyogaḥ, kāmena ca. yaḥ paśukāmaḥ syāt, sa godohanena praṇayanam abhinirvartayed iti. na tv atra pratyakṣaḥ śabdo 'sti, yo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ syāt, sa yāgena [504]{*4/318*} svargam abhinirvartayed iti. kathaṃ tarhi? yo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ syāt, sa tad yāgena nirvartayed iti. tasmān nāṅgavad bhavitum arhatīti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'just as in a subsidiary element of a sacrifice' — that is appropriate in a subsidiary element, because of subordinate status. There, the connection with the season (<s>ṛtu</s>) and with the desire is directly perceptible: 'He who desires cattle should accomplish the driving-out through the <s>godohana</s>.' But here there is no direct statement [saying], 'He who desires <s>brahmavarcas</s> should accomplish <s>svarga</s> through the sacrifice.' [504] How then? 'He who desires <s>brahmavarcas</s> should accomplish that through the sacrifice.' Therefore it cannot be like a subsidiary element.

children.text: vīte ca niyamas tadartham // MS_4,3.24 //
children.translated_text: And when [the cause] has ceased, the rule [of completion] is for that purpose [i.e., avoiding reproach]. // MS_4,3.24 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, vītāyāṃ phalecchāyām, avāpte vā phale samāptiniyamo dṛśyata iti. tatra brūmaḥ, vīte niyamas tadartham, vīte niyamo bhavati, tasmai prayojanāya. kasmai? śiṣṭāvigarhaṇāya. upakramyāparisamāpayataḥ, tadanantaram evainaṃ śiṣṭā vigarhayeyaḥ, prākramiko 'yaṃ kāpuruṣa iti vadantaḥ. ye hi devebhyaḥ saṃkalpya haviḥ, na yāgam abhinirvartayanti, tān śiṣṭā vigarhante, tasmād avaśyaṃ samāpayitavyam. tatraitad darśanaṃ yuktaṃ bhaviṣyati, yadi varṣet tāvaty eva juhuyād iti{*4/319*}. tasmāt kāmyānāṃ kāma eva phalam iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'when the desire for the fruit has ceased, or when the fruit has been obtained, a rule of completion is observed' — to that we say: when [the cause] has ceased, the rule exists for that purpose. The rule exists for a [specific] purpose. For what? For avoiding the reproach of the learned. Of one who, having commenced, does not complete [the rite], the learned would reproach him immediately thereafter, saying 'This wretch only starts things.' For those who, having resolved to offer an oblation to the gods, do not accomplish the sacrifice — the learned reproach them. Therefore it must necessarily be completed. In this regard, this observation will be appropriate: 'If it rains, one should offer only that much.' Therefore, the desire alone is the fruit of <s>kāmya</s> rites.

NOTES:
[{4/319: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.4.10.1}]

children.text: sārvakāmyam aṅgakāmaiḥ prakaraṇāt // MS_4,3.25 //
children.translated_text: [The fulfillment of] all desires [comes] from the subsidiary-desire [rites], because of the context. // MS_4,3.25 //

children.text: idam āmnāyate, ekasmai vānyā iṣṭayaḥ kāmāyāhriyante, sarvebhyo darśapūrṇamāsau, ekasmai vānye kratavaḥ kāmāyāhriyante, sarvebhyo jyotiṣṭoma iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim aṅgakāmair aṅgāṅgakāmaiś ca saha, asyānuvādaḥ, athavā vidhir iti. kiṃ prāptam? anuvāda iti, yad etat sārvakāmyam, tad anūdyate, aṅgakāmaiś cāṅgāṅgakāmaiś ca saha, santi hy aṅgakāmāś cāṅgāṅgakāmāś ca, yathā, āhāryapurīṣāṃ paśukāmasya [505]{*4/320*} vediṃ kuryāt, khananapurīṣāṃ pratiṣṭhākāmasyetyevamādayaḥ. tathā, yadi kāmayeta, varṣet parjanya iti nīcaiḥ sado minuyād iti, tad vihitam evedam abhidhīyata ity anuvādaṃ nyāyyaṃ manyāmahe.
children.translated_text: This is heard: 'For one or another desire are other <s>iṣṭis</s> (offerings) performed; for all [desires] are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites]. For one or another desire are other <s>kratus</s> (rituals) performed; for all [desires] is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is this a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) [of what is already known] together with the subsidiary-desire [rites] and the sub-subsidiary-desire [rites], or is it an injunction? What is the prima facie view? It is a restatement. This fulfillment of all desires is being restated together with the subsidiary-desire [rites] and sub-subsidiary-desire [rites]. For there do exist subsidiary-desire [rites] and sub-subsidiary-desire [rites], such as: 'For one desiring cattle, one should make the <s>vedi</s> (altar) with earth brought from outside; for one desiring firm establishment, with earth from excavation' — and the like. Likewise: 'If one desires that it rain — [505] he should make the sitting-place (<s>sadas</s>) low.' Since this has [already] been enjoined, this [statement] merely restates it — thus we consider a restatement appropriate.

children.text: phalopadeśo vā pradhānaśabdasaṃprayogāt // MS_4,3.26 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a teaching of the fruit, because of the connection with the word denoting the primary [rite]. // MS_4,3.26 //

children.text: phalavidhir vā. kutaḥ? pradhānaśabdena phalasaṃyogo bhavati, sarvebhyo darśapūrṇamāsau, sarvebhyo jyotiṣṭoma iti ca, pradhānābhidhānena ca pradhānasya sarvaphalavattā vihitā. tasmān nānuvādaḥ. athāṅgakāmān aṅgāṅgakāmāṃś cāpekṣate, tathā lakṣaṇāśabdaḥ syāt, śrutiś ca lakṣaṇāyā garīyasī. tasmāt prayogavacanena vidhir iti.
children.translated_text: Or it is a fruit-injunction. Why? Because the fruit is connected with the word denoting the primary [rite] — 'for all [desires] are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' and 'for all [desires] is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — by the designation of the primary [rite], the all-fruit-bearing nature of the primary [rite] is enjoined. Therefore it is not a restatement. But if it were looking to the subsidiary-desire [rites] and sub-subsidiary-desire [rites], then the [all-desires] word would be figurative (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), and the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>) is weightier than figurative usage. Therefore, by the statement of performance, it is an injunction.

children.text: tatra sarve 'viśeṣāt // MS_4,3.27 //
children.translated_text: In that [case], all [desires are fulfilled] simultaneously, because of no distinction. // MS_4,3.27 //

children.text: evaṃjātīyakeṣv evodāharaṇeṣv etad uktam, pradhāne sarvakāmānāṃ vidhir iti. idam idānīṃ saṃdihyate, kiṃ sakṛt prayoge sarve kāmāḥ, uta paryāyeṇeti. kiṃ prāptam? sakṛt prayoge sarve kāmā iti. katham? sarveṣāṃ kāmānāṃ darśapūrṇamāsau nimittam, jyotiṣṭomaś ceti, nimittaṃ cet sarveṣāṃ kāmānām, ko 'tra khalu kāmo na bhaviṣyatīti. tasmād yaugapadyena sarve kāmā iti.
children.translated_text: It has been stated regarding examples of just this kind that there is an injunction of all desires in the primary [rite]. Now the question arises: do all desires [come about] in a single performance, or in succession? What is the prima facie view? All desires [come about] in a single performance. How? The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> are the cause of all desires. If [they are] the cause of all desires, what desire indeed would not come about? Therefore, all desires [arise] simultaneously.

children.text: yogasiddhir vārthasyotpattyasaṃyogitvāt // MS_4,3.28 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, accomplishment [comes] in succession, because the [desired] objects are not connected with origination [simultaneously]. // MS_4,3.28 //

children.text: na caitad asti, sarve yugapat kāmā iti, paryāyo yogasiddhiḥ, paryāyeṇa bhaveyuḥ kāmā iti. kutaḥ? arthasyotpattyasaṃyogitvāt, arthā ime kāmā nāma, na sarva eva yugapad utpadyante, asaṃbhavo yugapad utpatteḥ sarveṣām, virodhāt. athavā, utpattyasaṃyogitvād iti, na, kāmānām etad utpattivacanam, utpannānāṃ lakṣaṇatvena vacanam, ye sarve kāmās tebhyo darśapūrṇamāsau jyotiṣṭomaś ceti. na sarve kāmāḥ karmaṇaḥ śrūvante, ye sarve kāmās tebhyo hi karma vidhīyate. tasmān na kāmānāṃ sāhityaṃ gamyata iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that all desires [arise] simultaneously. Rather, the accomplishment is in succession (<s>yogasiddhi</s>) — the desires would come about in turn. Why? Because the objects are not connected with origination simultaneously. These objects called 'desires' do not all arise simultaneously; the simultaneous origination of all of them is impossible, because of mutual contradiction. Alternatively, 'because of non-connection with origination' [means]: this is not a statement about the origination of desires, but a statement in the sense of characterizing those [already] arisen — 'for all those desires, the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [are prescribed].' Not all desires are heard [as arising] from the ritual; rather, the ritual is prescribed for all [pre-existing] desires. Therefore the simultaneity of desires is not understood.

children.text:
tatra sarve 'viśeṣāt // MS_4,3.27 //{*4/322*}
kāmyāni karmāṇy udāharaṇam, sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāmaḥ{*4/323*}, aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet prajākāmaḥ{*4/324*}, citrayā yajeta pasūkāmaḥ{*4/325*}, vaiśvadevīṃ sāṃgrahāyaṇīṃ{*4/326*} nirvaped grāmakāma iti{*4/327*}. teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kim iha loke kāmāḥ, utāmuṣmil loka iti. kiṃ prāptam? tatrāmuṣmil loke{*4/328*} kāmāḥ, aviśeṣāt, yathā svargaḥ, evam ime 'pi, na hy anantaranirvṛtte{*4/329*} karmaṇi phalam upalabhyate paśvādi, yac cānantaram upalabhyate, tat tata iti vijñāyate, yathā yatkālaṃ mardanam, tatkālaṃ mardana[507]{*4/330*}sukham. yac ca kālāntara upalabhyate, tasyāpy anyad eva kāraṇam asti pratyakṣam{*4/331*}, śarīragrahaṇasya tu nādṛṣṭādṛte kiṃcit kāraṇam asti. tasmād viśiṣṭendriyaśarīrādi phalaṃ paśusaṃbandhasamarthaṃ paśuphalāt karmaṇo bhavatīty evaṃ boddhavyam. tad dhi darśayati, kaikayo yajñaṃ vivitsan dālbhyam uvāca, anayā mā rāṣṭrapratipādanīyayeṣṭyā{*4/332*} yājayeti. so 'bravīt, na vai saumya rāṣṭrapratipādanīyāṃ{*4/333*} vettha, amuṣmai kāmāya yajñā āhriyanta iti janmāntaraphalatāṃ darśayati. tasmāj janmāntaraphalāni kāmyānīti.
children.translated_text:
In that [case], all [desires are fulfilled] simultaneously, because of no distinction. // MS_4,3.27 //
The <s>kāmya</s> (desire-motivated) rites are the example — 'one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> should offer a <s>caru</s> to <s>Sūrya</s>'; 'one desiring progeny should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to <s>Indrāgni</s>'; 'one desiring cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Citrā</s> [full-moon rite]'; 'one desiring a village should offer the <s>Vaiśvadevī Sāṃgrahāyaṇī</s>.' Regarding these, a doubt [arises]: are the desires [fulfilled] in this world or in the next world? What is the prima facie view? The desires [are fulfilled] in the next world, because of no distinction — just as <s>svarga</s> [is in the next world], so too are these. For the fruit is not perceived immediately upon the completion of the ritual action — cattle and the like [are not seen immediately]. And that which is perceived immediately is known to be from that [immediate cause] — just as [there is] the pleasure of massage at the very time of massage. But that which is perceived at a later time — for that too there exists another directly perceptible cause. But for the acquisition of a body [in the next life], there is no cause other than the unseen [merit]. Therefore one should understand thus: a distinguished body with [superior] sense-organs etc., capable of connection with cattle, arises from the ritual that has cattle as its fruit. This indeed is shown [by the passage]: '<s>Kaikeya</s>, wishing to perform a sacrifice, said to <s>Dālbhya</s>: "Consecrate me with this <s>Rāṣṭrapratipādanīyā</s> (kingdom-bestowing) offering." He replied: "Indeed, dear one, you do not understand the <s>Rāṣṭrapratipādanīyā</s>; sacrifices are performed for a desire in the next [life]"' — thus showing that the fruits [come in] another birth. Therefore the <s>kāmya</s> rites have their fruits in another birth.

yogasiddhir vārthasyotpattyasaṃyogitvāt // MS_4,3.28 //{*4/334*}
ihaivaiṣāṃ siddhir yogasya, utpattyā yogo na saṃbhavati, yaḥ paśubhyaḥ{*4/335*} kāmayate, sa etena yāgena kuryād iti, nātraitad gamyate, iha janmani na saṃbhavatīti. yac cānantaraṃ nopalabhyata iti. tan na, pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ na gamyate, śabdena tv asti gatiḥ{*4/336*}. yat tu kālāntare 'nyat kāraṇam iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, anyad api bhaviṣyati, etad api. yac cāmuṣmai kāmāya yajñā āhriyanta iti. atrocyate, evam asya ṛṣer matam, iha yasya phalaṃ tena tvāṃ na yājayāmi, yasyāmutra phalaṃ tena ca yājayiṣyāmīti. tasmād etat parihṛtam iti.
children.translated_text:
Or, the accomplishment of connection [is here itself], because the meaning is not connected with origination. // MS_4,3.28 //
The accomplishment of the connection of these [rites with their fruits] is here itself [in this life]. A connection through origination is not possible — [i.e.,] 'he who desires [results] from animals should perform this sacrifice' — it is not understood from this that it is impossible in this birth. As for [the objection] that [the fruit] is not perceived immediately — that is not so; it is not understood through perception or inference, but there is understanding through the [Vedic] word. As for [the argument] that at another time there is another cause — this is not a defect, for that other [cause] too will exist, and this one also. As for [the argument] that sacrifices are undertaken for a particular desire — to this we reply: such is the view of this sage — 'I do not cause you to sacrifice with that whose fruit is here [in this life], but I will cause you to sacrifice with that whose fruit is in the next [world].' Therefore this [objection] has been set aside.

children.translated_text: In [the case of] a connection, because of the purposefulness of the conjunction with the injunction. // MS_4,3.29 //

children.text: agniṃ citvā sautrāmaṇyā yajeta{*4/337*}, vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspati[508]{*4/338*}savena yajeteti{*4/339*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim aṅgaprayojanasaṃbandha eṣaḥ, uta kālārthaḥ saṃyoga iti. aṅgaprayojanasaṃbandha iti brūmaḥ, evaṃ hi śrutiviniyukto 'rthaḥ, itarathā kālo lakṣyeta, śrutilakṣaṇāviśaye ca śrutir nyāyyā na lakṣaṇā. tasmād agnyaṅgaṃ sautrāmaṇī, vājapeyāṅgaṃ bṛhaspatisava iti.
children.translated_text: 'Having built the fire-altar, one should sacrifice with the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>'; 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is this a connection for the purpose of a subsidiary, or is the conjunction for the purpose of [indicating] time? We say: it is a connection for the purpose of a subsidiary. For thus the meaning is allocated by the [Vedic] statement (<s>śruti</s>); otherwise, time would be understood by secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), and where both literal meaning and secondary indication are possible, literal meaning is proper, not secondary indication. Therefore, the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> is a subsidiary of the fire-altar [building], and the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> is a subsidiary of the <s>Vājapeya</s>.

children.text: kālaśrutau kāla iti cet // MS_4,3.30 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues that] when time is heard, [it indicates] time — // MS_4,3.30 //

children.text: evaṃ cet paśyasi, aṅgaprayojanasaṃbandha iti, atha kālavidhānaṃ kasmān na bhavati? kālavidhirūpo hi śabdaḥ, citvā cayane 'bhinirvṛtta{*4/340*} iti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that it is a connection for the purpose of a subsidiary — then why does it not become an injunction of time? For the word has the form of a time-injunction: 'having built' [means] 'when the building has been completed.'

children.text: . śabdārthaś cayanam, tenāsamavāyaḥ syāt saugrāmaṇyā vājapeyena ca bṛhaspatisavasya. prakaraṇaṃ ca bādhyeta, agniprakaraṇe śrūyamāṇo 'gner dharmo gamyate yāgaḥ, vājapeyaprakaraṇe ca vājapeyasya, itarathā tayoḥ prakaraṇe 'nyasya dharmaḥ kālo gamyeta. tasmād aṅgaprayojanasaṃbandha iti.
children.translated_text: The meaning of the word is the building [of the fire-altar]; hence there would be a non-connection of the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> and the <s>Vājapeya</s> with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>. And the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) would be contradicted — what is heard in the context of fire [building] is understood as a rite of fire; and in the context of the <s>Vājapeya</s>, as a rite of the <s>Vājapeya</s>. Otherwise, in the context of those [rites], the rite of another [entity] would be understood as indicating time. Therefore it is a connection for the purpose of a subsidiary.

children.text: ubhayārtham iti cet/74.3.32//
children.translated_text: If [one argues] it is for both purposes — // MS_4,3.32 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor āmananti, saṃsthāpya paurṇamāsīṃ vaimṛdham anunirvapatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim ubhayāṅgaṃ vaimṛdhaḥ, kālārthaḥ paurṇamāsīsaṃyogaḥ, utāṅgaprayojanasaṃbandha iti. kiṃ prāptam? evaṃ ced ubhayārtho vaimṛdhaḥ. kutaḥ? prakaraṇa [509]{*4/342*} ubhayor āmnānasāmarthyāt, kālavidhisārūpyāc ca saṃsthāpyeti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is stated: 'Having completed the full-moon [sacrifice], he offers the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> oblation.' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> a subsidiary of both [the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa], or is the conjunction with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> for the purpose of [indicating] time, or is it a connection for the purpose of a subsidiary? What is the prima facie view? The <s>Vaimṛdha</s> is thus for both purposes. Why? Because of the capacity of being stated in the context of both, and because of the resemblance to a time-injunction in [the word] 'having completed.'

children.text: na śabdaikatvāt // MS_4,3.33 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the unity of the word. // MS_4,3.33 //

children.text: ekaḥ śabdaḥ, anunirvapatīti, ekasminn eva vākye na dvau saṃbandhau śaknoti vidhātum. vaimṛdhasya darśapūrṇamāsābhyām, pūrṇamāsīkālena ca. ekārthatvād dhy ekaṃ vākyaṃ samadhigatam.
children.translated_text: There is a single word — 'he offers' — and a single sentence cannot prescribe two connections: [both] the connection of the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites] and [the connection] with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> time. For it has been established that a single sentence has a single meaning.

children.text: prakaraṇād iti cet // MS_4,3.34 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] 'because of the context' — // MS_4,3.34 //

children.text: prakaraṇād iti yad uktam, tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'because of the context' — that is to be refuted.

children.text: notpattisaṃyogāt // MS_4,3.35 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the connection with origination. // MS_4,3.35 //

children.text: naitad evam, etad eva vaimṛdhasyotpattivākyam, tad darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ vā prakaraṇād ekavākyabhāvam iyāt. pratyakṣaṃ vā paurṇamāsyā, tatra pratyakṣasaṃyogaḥ prakaraṇād balavān, pratyakṣaś ca paurṇamāsyā saṃyogaḥ, parokṣaḥ kālena. tasmāt paurṇamāsyāṅgaṃ vaimṛdha iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — this itself is the origination-sentence of the <s>Vaimṛdha</s>; that [sentence] would either form a syntactic unity with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> through context, or directly with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>. There, the direct connection with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> is stronger than the context. And the connection with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> is direct, while [the connection] with time is indirect. Therefore the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> is a subsidiary of the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>.

children.text: anutpattau tu kālaḥ syāt prayojanena saṃbandhāt // MS_4,3.36 //
children.translated_text: But when it is not an origination[-sentence], time would [be indicated], because of the connection with purpose. // MS_4,3.36 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - āgnimārutād ūrdhvam anuyājaiś caranti, prahṛtya paridhīñ juhoti hāriyojanam iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim aṅgaṃ vidhīyate, uta kāla iti. aṅgavidhāne śrutiḥ, kālavidhāne lakṣaṇā. tasmād aṅgavidhānam iti prāpte [510]{*4/343*} brūmaḥ, anutpattivākye kālaḥ syāt, āgnimārutaṃ somāṅgam, anuyājāḥ paśvaṅgam. tatra na tayoḥ paraspareṇa saṃbandhaḥ. tathā paridhayaḥ paśvaṅgam, hāriyojanam anyad eva pradhānam. anuyājā āgnimārutaṃ ca prāptam. ānantaryam eva tayor na prāptam, tad vidhīyate. tathā hāriyojanasya paridhigrahaṇasya ca. evaṃ ca sati, na hāriyojanasya paridhipraharaṇena kaścid upakāraḥ kriyate, hāriyojanena vā paridhipraharaṇasya. nanu paridhipraharaṇasyopariṣṭād bhāvena tasyopakriyeteti. ucyate, na hy uparibhāvārthaṃ paridhipraharaṇam anuṣṭheyam. vidyata evaitat paśvartham. tasmiṃś ca sati tasyoparibhāvo vidyata eveti. tasmāt kālārthaḥ saṃbandha iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'After the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation], they perform the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings); having cast aside the enclosing sticks (<s>paridhis</s>), he offers the <s>Hāriyojana</s> [oblation].' There a doubt [arises]: is a subsidiary being enjoined, or time? In the subsidiary-injunction there is literal meaning (<s>śruti</s>); in the time-injunction there is secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). Given this, when the prima facie view is that it is a subsidiary-injunction, we say: in a non-origination sentence, time would [be indicated]. The <s>Āgnimāruta</s> is a subsidiary of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice]; the <s>anuyājas</s> are a subsidiary of the animal [sacrifice]. There is no mutual connection between those two. Likewise, the <s>paridhis</s> (enclosing sticks) are a subsidiary of the animal [sacrifice], and the <s>Hāriyojana</s> is an altogether different principal [rite]. What is prima facie obtained is the <s>anuyājas</s> and the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. It is only their sequence that is not [yet] obtained — that is what is being enjoined. Similarly for the <s>Hāriyojana</s> and the casting aside of the <s>paridhis</s>. This being so, the casting aside of the <s>paridhis</s> does not benefit the <s>Hāriyojana</s>, nor does the <s>Hāriyojana</s> [benefit] the casting aside of the <s>paridhis</s>. [The objector says:] but would not [the Hāriyojana] be benefited by the casting aside of the <s>paridhis</s> being performed first? We reply: no, for the casting aside of the <s>paridhis</s> is not to be performed for the purpose of being prior [to the Hāriyojana]. It already exists for the purpose of the animal [sacrifice]. And when that exists, its being prior [to the Hāriyojana] already exists. Therefore the connection is for the purpose of [indicating] time.

children.text: utpattikālaviṣaye kālaḥ syād vākyasya tatpradhānatvāt // MS_4,3.37 //
children.translated_text: When the domain concerns both origination and time, time would [be indicated], because of the primacy of that [time-element] in the sentence. // MS_4,3.37 //

children.text: idam āmnāyate, darśapūrṇamāsau{*4/344*} iṣṭvā somena yajeteti{*4/345*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim etad aṅgasya vidhānam, uta kālasyeti. kiṃ prāptam? śruter aṅgasya, iti prāpte, ucyate, asmin kālāṅgavidhānasaṃśaye kālaḥ syāt, vākyasya tatpradhānatvāt. kālapradhānaṃ hy etad vākyam, na yāgavidhānaparam, atatparatāsya{*4/346*}, rūpāvacanāt. kathaṃ rūpāvacanam? devatābhāvāt. katham abhāvaḥ? aśrutatvāt. yā hi yasya śrūyate, sā tasya devatā bhavati. śrutyā hi devatā gamyate, na pratyakṣādibhiḥ. tasmān nāpūrvasya yāgasya vidhānam, kālārthe 'nuvāde nāyaṃ doṣaḥ, vihitadevatāko hy anūdyate. tasmād [511]{*4/347*} atra kālārthaḥ saṃbandha iti. tac ca darśayati - eṣa vai devaratho yad darśapūrṇamānsau, yad darśapūrṇamāsāv iṣṭvā somena yajate, rathaspaṣṭa evāvasāne vare devānām avasyatīti. pradarśite mārge rathena yātuṃ{*4/348*} sukhaṃ bhavati. evaṃ darśapūrṇamāsāv iṣṭvā somena yaṣṭuṃ{*4/349*} sukhaṃ bhavati. darśapūrṇamāsaprakṛtīni tasya dīkṣaṇīyādīni svabhyas tāni bhavanti. evam arthavādo 'rthavān bhavati.
children.translated_text: This is stated: 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is this an injunction of a subsidiary, or of time? What is the prima facie view? Of a subsidiary, because of the [Vedic] statement. Given this, it is said: in this doubt between time-injunction and subsidiary-injunction, time would [be indicated], because the sentence has that [time-element] as primary. For this sentence has time as its primary [purpose], not the injunction of a sacrifice — because of its not having that as its purport, since the form [of the sacrifice] is not stated. How is the form not stated? Because of the absence of a deity. How is there absence? Because [a deity] is not heard. For a deity that is heard in connection with a [sacrifice] becomes its deity. A deity is understood through the [Vedic] statement, not through perception and the like. Therefore, this is not an injunction of an unprecedented sacrifice. In a restatement for the purpose of [indicating] time, this is not a defect, for what is being restated has its deity [already] enjoined. Therefore, here the connection is for the purpose of [indicating] time. And this is shown [by the following]: 'The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is indeed the chariot of the gods. He who, having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, sacrifices with <s>Soma</s>, enters, as if with a well-prepared chariot, into the best abode of the gods.' When the road has been shown, it becomes easy to travel with a chariot. Similarly, having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it becomes easy to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>. The <s>dīkṣaṇīya</s> and other [rites] of his [Soma sacrifice], having the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> as their archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), naturally belong to them. Thus the <s>arthavāda</s> becomes meaningful.

children.text:
vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet putre jāta iti{*4/350*}. tatra{*4/351*} saṃdehaḥ, kim ātmaniḥśreyasāya, uta putraniḥśreyasāyeti. ātmaniḥśreyasāyeti brūmaḥ, nemāni phaladāni parasya bhavanti karmāṇi. kutaḥ? ādhāna ātmanepadanirdeśāt, yathā yady ekaṃ kapālaṃ naśyed eko māsaḥ saṃvatsarasyāpetaḥ syāt. atha yajamānaḥ pramīyeta dyāvāpṛthivīyam ekakapālaṃ nirvapet. yadi dve naśyeyātām, dvau māsau saṃvatsarasyāpetau syātām. atha yajamānaḥ pramīyeta, āśvinaṃ dvikapālaṃ nirvapet. saṃkhyāyodvāsayati yajamānasya gopīthāyeti{*4/352*}, kapālanāśe nimitta ātmaniḥśreyasaphalaṃ karma darśayati. evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam, tasmād ātmaniḥśreyasārtham iti.
[512]{*4/353*} evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, phalasaṃyogo na syāt pituḥ, phalavacanaṃ śeṣabhūtaṃ putrasya, na pituḥ. katham? evaṃ śrūyate, vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet putre jāte. yad aṣṭākapālo bhavati, gāyatryaivainaṃ brahmavarcasena punāti, yan navakapālo bhavati, trivṛtaivāsamiṃs tejo dadhāti. yad daśakapālo virājaivāsmin annādyaṃ dadhāti, yad ekādaśakapālas triṣṭubhaivāsminn indriyaṃ dadhāti. yad dvādaśakapālo jagatyaivāsmin paśūn dadhāti. yasmiñ jāta etām iṣṭiṃ nirvapati, pūta eva sa tejasvy annād indriyāvī paśumān bhavatīti{*4/354*}. yo jātaḥ, tatra phalaṃ śrūyate, nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ. tasmāt putrasya phalam iti. yad uktam, na parasya phaladāny etāni karmāṇīti. tad ucyate, yat putrasya phalam, ātmanaḥ sā prītiḥ, tasmād ātmanepadaṃ na virudhyate, etām evātmanaḥ prītim abhipretya bhavati vacanam, ātmā vai putra iti.
aṅgād aṅgāt saṃbhavasi hṛdayād abhijāyase/
ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam// iti.
children.translated_text:
'One should offer a twelve-potsherd [cake] to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> when a son is born.' There a doubt [arises]: is [this sacrifice] for the welfare of oneself, or for the welfare of the son? We say: for the welfare of oneself — these ritual acts do not produce fruit for another. Why? Because of the designation in the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) at the [fire-]establishment: 'If one potsherd is destroyed, one month of the year would be lost. Then, if the sacrificer should die, he should offer a single-potsherd [cake] to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>. If two are destroyed, two months of the year would be lost. Then, if the sacrificer should die, he should offer a two-potsherd [cake] to the <s>Aśvins</s>. He removes [the danger] according to the number, for the protection of the sacrificer' — when the destruction of a potsherd is the occasion, it shows that the ritual act has fruit for one's own welfare. Similarly it should be viewed here; therefore it is for the purpose of one's own welfare.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: the conjunction with fruit should not [apply] to the father. The fruit-statement is a remainder belonging to the son, not to the father. How? This is what is heard: 'One should offer a twelve-potsherd [cake] to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> when a son is born. When it is of eight potsherds, it purifies him with the spiritual radiance of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. When of nine potsherds, it places vigor in him through the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma]. When of ten potsherds, the <s>Virāj</s> meter places food in him. When of eleven potsherds, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter places power in him. When of twelve potsherds, the <s>Jagatī</s> meter places cattle in him. He in whose [household a son] is born [and who] offers this <s>iṣṭi</s> — purified indeed, he becomes radiant, a food-eater, possessed of power, possessed of cattle.' The fruit is heard in connection with the one who is born — there is no straining of the statement. Therefore the fruit belongs to the son. As for what was said — 'these ritual acts do not produce fruit for another' — to that we reply: that which is the fruit for the son is one's own satisfaction (<s>prīti</s>); therefore the <s>ātmanepada</s> is not contradicted — the statement is made with this very satisfaction of oneself in mind. 'The self is indeed the son.'
'From limb after limb you are born, from the heart you are produced;
you are indeed the self called "son" — may you live a hundred autumns.'

children.text: aṅgānāṃ tūpaghātasaṃyogo nimittārthaḥ // MS_4,3.39 //
children.translated_text: But the conjunction with the destruction of subsidiaries is for the purpose of [indicating] the occasion. // MS_4,3.39 //

children.text:
atha yad uktam, yady ekaṃ kapālaṃ naśyed ityevamādi. tatrocyate, aṅgānām upaghātasaṃyogo nimittārtha upapadyate, nānyathā. na hi kapāle naṣṭe tad anveṣaṇārthā iṣṭir yuktā. na hi kākinyāṃ naṣṭāyāṃ tad anveṣaṇaṃ kārṣāpaṇena kriyate.
evaṃ vā,
children.translated_text:
Now, as to what was said — 'if one potsherd is destroyed' and so forth — to that we reply: the conjunction with the destruction of subsidiaries is properly understood as being for the purpose of [indicating] the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>), not otherwise. For when a potsherd is destroyed, an offering (<s>iṣṭi</s>) for the purpose of finding it is not proper. For when a <s>kākinī</s> (small coin) is lost, one does not spend a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (larger coin) to find it.
Or alternatively,

children.text:
aṅgānāṃ tūpaghātasaṃyogo nimittārthaḥ // MS_4,3.39 //{*4/355*}
vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet putre jāta iti{*4/356*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ jātamātre, uta kṛte jātakarmaṇīti. jātamātra iti brūmaḥ, saṃprāpte hi nimitte naimittikena bhavitavyam. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, kṛte jātakarmaṇīti. kutaḥ? sāmarthyāt. kṛte hi jātakarmaṇi prāśanaṃ tasya vidhīyate. yadi prāg jātakarmaṇaḥ, iṣṭiḥ kriyate, prāśanakālo viprakṛṣyeta. tatrāsya śarīradhāraṇaṃ na syāt.
atha yad uktam, saṃprāpte nimitte hi naimittikena bhavitavyam iti. ucyate, aṅgānām upaghātasaṃyogo nimittārthaḥ, upaghātaḥ putrajanma, tad bhūtaṃ nimittam. na tatkālo 'ṅgam, tac ca nimittam. kṛte 'pi jātakarmaṇi nāpaiti. itarasmin pakṣe kālo 'peyāt, lakṣaṇā cāsmin pakṣe syāt. tasmāt kṛte jātakarmaṇīti.
atha kim antardaśāhe yasmin kasmin vāhani, uta svakāla iti. kiṃ prāptam? yasmin kasmin vāhanīti, evam aniyamaḥ prāptaḥ. atrocyate, paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā. kutaḥ? śruteḥ, evaṃ hi śrūyate, ya iṣṭvā{*4/357*} paśunā somena vā yajeta, sa paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā yajeteti. nātibhāro vacanasya, itarasmin pakṣe kālo 'peyāt. lakṣaṇāpy asmin pakṣe syāt. anyasyāṃ tithāvantardaśāhe vā kurvan sarvāṇy aṅgāny upasaṃhartuṃ na śaknuyāt. kālaṃ śaucaṃ ca [514]{*4/358*} nopasaṃgṛhṇīyāt. tasmād atīte daśāhe paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā kuryād iti.
children.translated_text:
But the connection of subsidiaries with the occasioning event is for the purpose of [establishing] the occasion. // MS_4,3.39 //
'He should offer a twelve-potsherd [cake] to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> when a son is born.' There a doubt [arises]: is it [to be performed] as soon as [the son] is born, or after the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth ceremony) has been performed? We say: as soon as born, for when the occasion has arrived, the occasional rite must be performed. Given this prima facie view, we say: after the <s>jātakarma</s> has been performed. Why? Because of capability. For after the <s>jātakarma</s> is performed, the feeding of the [child] is enjoined. If the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) is performed before the <s>jātakarma</s>, the time for feeding would be delayed. In that case, the sustaining of his body would not be [possible].
Now, as to what was said — 'when the occasion has arrived, the occasional rite must be performed' — we reply: the connection of subsidiaries with the occasioning event is for the purpose of the occasion; the occasioning event is the birth of a son; that which has occurred is the occasion. Not its [exact] time is the subsidiary, but that [event] is the occasion. Even after the <s>jātakarma</s> is performed, it does not depart. In the other view, the time would depart, and in that view there would be figurative designation. Therefore, [it is to be performed] after the <s>jātakarma</s> has been performed.
Now, [the question is:] within the ten [day purification period], on whichever day, or at its proper time? What is the prima facie view? On whichever day — thus no restriction is obtained. To this we say: on the full-moon day or the new-moon day. Why? Because of the [Vedic] statement, for thus it is heard: 'He who, having sacrificed with an animal or with <s>Soma</s>, would sacrifice [again], he should sacrifice on the full-moon day or the new-moon day.' This is not an excessive burden of the statement; in the other view, the time would depart. Figurative designation too would arise in that view. If performing on another <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) or within the ten days, one would not be able to gather all the subsidiaries. One would not obtain the [proper] time and purity. Therefore, after the ten days have passed, one should perform [the rite] on the full-moon day or the new-moon day.

children.text: pradhānenābhisaṃyogād aṅgānāṃ mukhyakālatvam // MS_4,3.40 //
children.translated_text: Because of connection with the principal, the subsidiaries have primary [i.e., proper] timing. // MS_4,3.40 //

children.text: agniṃ citvā sautrāmaṇyā yajeta{*4/359*}, vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspatisavena yajeteti, aṅgaprayojanasaṃbandha ity uktam. etad idānīṃ saṃdihyate, kiṃ citamātre, tantramadhya eva kartavyam, uta svakāle kartavyam iti. tathā vājapeye kiṃ bṛhaspatisave, uta svakāla iti. mukhyakālatvam anayoḥ syāt. kutaḥ? pradhānākālatvād aṅgānām. eko hi kālaḥ pradhānānām aṅgānāṃ ceti vakṣyate{*4/360*}. aṅgāni tu vidhānatvāt pradhānenopadiśyerann iti. agnicayanaṃ kṛtvā na tāvaty eva sthātavyam, sautrāmaṇīsaṃjñako 'paro yāgaḥ kartavya iti. tathā vājapeyam abhinirvartya naitāvatā kṛtī syāt, bṛhaspatisavasaṃjñakaṃ yāgam abhinirvartayed iti.
children.translated_text: 'Having piled the fire [altar], he should sacrifice with the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>'; 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, he should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>' — [these express] the connection with the purpose of the subsidiary — so it has been stated. Now this is doubted: should [the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>] be performed as soon as [the fire altar] is piled, in the middle of the ritual system itself, or at its proper time? Likewise in the <s>Vājapeya</s>: during the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>, or at its proper time? These should have primary [i.e., proper] timing. Why? Because the subsidiaries have the timing of the principal. For it will be stated that the time is one for both principals and subsidiaries. But the subsidiaries, being [merely] prescribed, would be instructed through the principal — having completed the fire-piling, one should not remain [idle] for that long; another sacrifice called <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> is to be performed. Likewise, having completed the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one would not be satisfied with just that; one should complete the sacrifice called <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>.

NOTES:
[{4/359: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.6.3.4}]
[{4/360: Cf. MS 11.2.7}]

children.text: apavṛtte tu codanā tatsāmānyāt svakāle syāt // MS_4,3.41 //
children.translated_text: But when [the principal rite] is concluded, the injunction, because of similarity with that [type of sacrifice], would be at its own [proper] time. // MS_4,3.41 //

children.text:
apavṛtte yāge codyate yāgāntaram idam, apavṛttiś ca sarveṣu yāgāṅgeṣv akṛteṣu na bhavati. na yathā bhavān manyate, [515]{*4/361*} yāgamātre nirvṛtta iti. kutaḥ? karaṇavibhaktyā saṃyogāt, vājapeyeneṣṭyā vājapeyena phalasya vyāpāraṃ kṛtvā{*4/362*}, sāṅgena ca vyāpāro gamyate, na niraṅgena. bhavet tantramadhye prayogaḥ, vadi vājapeyam abhinirvartyetīpsitabhāvo vājapeyasya syāt, tataḥ pradhānamātraṃ vājapeyasaṃjñakam abhinirvartyeti gamyeta, na tv evam asti. tasmād yathoktāni sarvāṇy aṅgāni kṛtvety arthaḥ. evaṃ cet, nirvṛtte prayoge, atikrānte vājapeyakāle yāga prayujyate. tasya codanāsāmānyāj jyotiṣṭaumike vidhyante prāpte svena codakaprāptena kālena bhavitavyam. sautrāmaṇyāś codanāsāmānyāt, darśapūrṇamāsakāleneti.
āha, vājapeye tāvad iṣṭvetivacanād yāgam abhinirvartyeti gamyate, agnau tu nopapadyate. tatra citvetivacanāc cayanam abhinirvartyety arthaḥ syāt. ucyate, naitad evam. agniṃ citveti hi śrūyate, agni cayanena saṃskṛtyety arthaḥ{*4/363*}. agnir iti jvalano 'bhidhīyate. na tasya sthalasthāpanamātram upakāraḥ, yadi sthalasthite yāgo bhavati, tataś cayanenāgner upakāro 'sti. tam abhinirvartyeti sthalasthite 'gnau yāgam abhinirvartyeti gamyate. yāvat sthalasthite 'gnau yāgo na bhavati, na tāvad agniś cayanenopakriyate. yenāgnir yajamānasyopakaroti, so 'gner upakāro na sthalasthāpanamātram. tasmāt tatrāpi yāgam abhinirvartyeti gamyate.
children.translated_text:
When the sacrifice is concluded, another sacrifice is enjoined. And conclusion does not occur when all the subsidiary elements of the sacrifice have not been performed. It is not as you think — that [the principal rite] is concluded by the mere sacrifice alone. Why? Because of the connection through the instrumental case ending: 'having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>' — having accomplished the purpose of the fruit through the <s>Vājapeya</s>; and the purposeful action is understood to be with all its subsidiaries, not without subsidiaries. Performance in the middle of the ritual system would [only] occur if the optative form 'having completed the <s>Vājapeya</s>' expressed the desired [completion] of the <s>Vājapeya</s> [as a mere principal]. Then it would be understood that only the principal called <s>Vājapeya</s> is to be completed — but it is not so. Therefore the meaning is: having performed all the subsidiaries as stated.
If so, then when the performance is concluded, the <s>Vājapeya</s> time has passed, and the [new] sacrifice is performed [later]. Because of the similarity of its injunction with that of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> type, when it has obtained [its proper time] through its own injunction, it should occur at its own proper time. The <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, because of the similarity of its injunction, [should be performed] at the time of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.
[The objector] says: in the case of the <s>Vājapeya</s>, indeed, from the statement 'having sacrificed,' it is understood that the sacrifice is to be completed. But in the case of the fire [altar], [this] is not applicable. There, from the statement 'having piled,' the meaning would be that the piling alone is to be completed. We reply: this is not so. For it is heard 'having piled the fire' — the meaning is 'having consecrated [the fire] by means of the fire-piling.' The word 'fire' (<s>agni</s>) denotes the flame. Its mere placement on the ground is not the [whole] benefit; when the sacrifice takes place with the fire placed on the ground, then the fire-piling has served its purpose. Having completed that — it is understood that the sacrifice is to be completed with the fire placed on the ground. As long as the sacrifice does not take place with the fire placed on the ground, the fire is not served by the piling. The benefit that the fire renders to the sacrificer — that benefit of the fire is not mere ground-placement. Therefore there too, it is understood that the sacrifice is to be completed.

children.text: prakaraṇaśabdasāmānyāc codanānām anaṅgatvam // MS_4,4.1. //
children.translated_text: Because of the commonality of the context-word, the injunctions are not subsidiary. // MS_4,4.1 //

children.text: santy anumatyādīny aiṣṭikāni karmāṇi, malhādayaḥ paśavaḥ, pavitrādayaḥ somāḥ, valmīkavapāyāṃ homa ityevamādīni dārvihomikāni. tathā yaṣṭauhīṃ dīvyati, rājanyaṃ jināti, śaunaḥśepham{*4/365*} ākhyāpayati, abhiṣicyata iti, eteṣāṃ sannidhau śrūyate, rājasūyena svārājyakāmo yajeteti, sa eṣa rūpavatāṃ yāgānāṃ saṃnidhāv{*4/366*} arūpaḥ śabdaḥ śrūyamāṇaḥ samudāyavācakaḥ samadhigataḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ sarveṣām anumatyādīnāṃ samudāyasya rājasūyaśabdo vācakaḥ, uta keṣāṃcid vācakaḥ keṣāṃcin neti. kiṃ prāptam? sarveṣāṃ vācaka iti. kutaḥ? prakaraṇaśabdasāmānyāt, prakaraṇaśabdaḥ sarveṣāṃ samāno rājasūyeneti. rājā tatra sūyate, tasmād rājasūyaḥ. rājño vā yajño rājasūyaḥ. tat prakaraṇasaṃnidhāne sati, viśeṣābhāve ca sarveṣāṃ vācako bhavitum arhati. yaś ca rājasūyaśabditas tataḥ phalaṃ bhavati. tasmāt sarvāṇi pradhānānīti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) rites such as the <s>Anumati</s>, etc.; the animals such as the <s>malhā</s>, etc.; the <s>Soma</s> rites such as the <s>Pavitra</s>, etc.; the <s>dārvihoma</s> (wood-oblation) rites such as the oblation in a termite-mound <s>vapā</s>, etc. Likewise: 'He plays dice with the <s>yaṣṭauhī</s>; he defeats the prince; he narrates the story of <s>Śunaḥśepha</s>; he is consecrated.' In the proximity of these it is heard: 'One desiring sovereign power should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s>.' This word, being formless (<s>arūpa</s>), heard in the proximity of well-defined sacrifices, is understood as denoting the aggregate. There a doubt [arises]: is the word <s>Rājasūya</s> a designation for the aggregate of all [rites] beginning with the <s>Anumati</s>, or does it designate some but not others? What is the prima facie view? It designates all. Why? Because of the commonality of the context-word — the context-word <s>Rājasūya</s> is common to all [rites] beginning with the <s>Anumati</s>. 'The king is consecrated (<s>sūyate</s>) therein, therefore it is <s>Rājasūya</s>.' Or, 'the sacrifice of the king is <s>Rājasūya</s>.' Given the contextual proximity, and in the absence of any distinction, it should serve as a designation for all. And the fruit comes from what is designated by the word <s>Rājasūya</s>. Therefore all are principal [rites].

children.text: api vāṅgam anijyāḥ syus tato viśiṣṭatvāt // MS_4,4.2 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, the non-sacrificial [rites] would be subsidiary, and hence the other would be principal because of being distinguished [as a sacrifice]. // MS_4,4.2 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. yā anijyās tā aṅgam, yathā videvanādayaḥ. rājasūyasaṃjñakena yāgena svārājyaṃ kuryād ity ucyamāne yāgenaiva svārājyaṃ sādhyate, nāyāgena. ayāgāś ca videvanādayaḥ. tasmād aṅgaṃ bhaveyuḥ, ijyānāṃ phalavatīnāṃ śrūyamānā iti.
children.translated_text: The phrase 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) introduces an alternative view. Those that are non-sacrificial would be subsidiary — such as the <s>videvanā</s> (dice-playing) and the like. When it is said that one should attain sovereign power through the sacrifice called <s>Rājasūya</s>, sovereign power is accomplished through sacrifice alone, not through non-sacrifice. And the <s>videvanā</s> and the like are non-sacrificial. Therefore they should be subsidiaries, being heard [in connection with] the fruit-bearing sacrifices.

children.text: madhyasthaṃ yasya tanmadhye // MS_4,4.3 //
children.translated_text: That which is in the middle of another — [it is subsidiary] to that [in whose] middle [it stands]. // MS_4,4.3 //

children.text: rājasūye 'bhiṣecanīyamadhye, yaṣṭauhīṃ dīvyatīti videvanādayaḥ samāmnātāḥ. te kim abhiṣecanīyasyāṅgam, uta kṛtsnasya rājasūyasyeti saṃśayaḥ. ucyate, madhyāmnānād abhiṣecanīyasyeti, tathānantaryam anugrahīṣyata iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, in the middle of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> (consecration rite), the <s>videvanā</s> (dice-playing) and the like are recorded — 'he plays dice with the <s>yaṣṭauhī</s>.' Are these subsidiary to the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>, or to the entire <s>Rājasūya</s>? This is the doubt. We reply: because of being recorded in the middle [of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>], they are [subsidiary] to the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>. And thus the sequential order will be determined.

children.text: sarvāsāṃ vā samatvāc codanātaḥ syān na hi tasya prakaraṇaṃ deśārtham ucyate madhye // MS_4,4.4 //
children.translated_text: Or [they would be subsidiary] to all [the rites], because of the equality of all the injunctions; for the context of that [<s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>] is not stated [merely] for the purpose of [indicating] location within the middle. // MS_4,4.4 //

children.text: sarvāsāṃ cānumatyādīnāṃ codanānām aṅgaṃ videvanādi syāt. kutaḥ? codanātaḥ samatvāt, samānā etā anumatyādyāś codanāḥ, tāḥ sarvāḥ phalavatyaś ca pradhānabhūtāḥ. sarvāsām āsāṃ prakaraṇam, na hy abhiṣecanīyasya kevalasya. kramād{*4/368*} abhiṣecanīyasya prāpnuvanti, prakaraṇāt sarvāsām, prakaraṇaṃ ca kramād balīyaḥ. tasmān nābhiṣecanīyasya kevalasyeti. abhiṣecanīyasya tu madhye sthānaṃ videvanādīnām, tatra kriyamāṇāḥ sarvāsām upakurvantīti.
children.translated_text: The <s>videvanā</s> and the like would be subsidiary to all the injunctions [of rites] beginning with the <s>Anumati</s>. Why? Because of the equality from the standpoint of the injunctions — these injunctions of the <s>Anumati</s> and the like are all equal, and all are fruit-bearing and principal. The context belongs to all of them, not to the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> alone. By sequence, they pertain to the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>; by context, to all. And context is stronger than sequence. Therefore they are not [subsidiary] to the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> alone. But the placement of the <s>videvanā</s> and the like in the middle of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> — being performed there, they serve all [the rites].

children.text: prakaraṇāvibhāge ca vipratiṣiddhaṃ hy ubhayam // MS_4,4.5 //
children.translated_text: And when the context is undivided, both [interpretations] would be contradictory. // MS_4,4.5 //

children.text:
rājasūya upasadaḥ prakṛtya śrūyate, purastād upasadāṃ saumyena pracaranti, antarā tvāṣṭreṇa, upariṣṭād vaiṣṇaveneti{*4/370*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim upasadaṅgaṃ saumyādayaḥ, utopasatkālā iti. upasadaṅgam iti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ? upasatsaṃyogasya śrutatvāt, kālavidhau sati lakṣaṇā syāt. tasmād upasadaṅgam iti.
nanu kālavad aṅgaṃ bhaviṣyati, tathā saty ubhayam anugṛhyeta, upasatsaṃyogaś ca, purastād iti ca kālābhidhānam, upasacchabdasaṃyogād upasadaṅgatā bhaviṣyati. purastācchabdasāmarthyāc ca pūrvādiṣu prayoga iti. ucyate, vipratiṣiddhaṃ hy ubhayam, na śaknoty upasadām ity eṣa śabdaḥ, saumyādīṃś ca viśeṣṭum, ekasmin vākye, pūrvādīṃś ca. bhidyate hi tathā vākyam. tasmān na kālavad aṅgam.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, with reference to the <s>Upasads</s> (preparatory observances), it is heard: 'Before the <s>Upasads</s>, they proceed with the <s>Saumya</s> [offering]; in between, with the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s>; after, with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: are the <s>Saumya</s> and the others subsidiary to the <s>Upasads</s>, or are they [merely] time-related to the <s>Upasads</s>? We say: they are subsidiary to the <s>Upasads</s>. Why? Because the connection with the <s>Upasads</s> is heard [directly]; if it were an injunction of time, there would be figurative designation. Therefore they are subsidiary to the <s>Upasads</s>.
[The objector says:] but they could be time-related subsidiaries; if so, both would be accommodated — both the connection with the <s>Upasads</s> and the temporal designation 'before' would be [understood]; the subsidiary status would follow from the connection with the word '<s>Upasad</s>,' and the temporal designation 'before' and so forth would [determine] the employment at the first and other [stages]. We reply: both [interpretations] would be contradictory, for the word 'of the <s>Upasads</s>' cannot, in a single sentence, both distinguish the <s>Saumya</s> and the others and [also distinguish] the first and other [stages]. For the sentence would thereby be split. Therefore it is not a time-related subsidiary.

NOTES:
[{4/370: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.8.1.2}]

children.text: api vā kālamātraṃ syād adarśanād viśeṣasya // MS_4,4.6 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, it would be merely a time[-designation], because of the non-perception of any distinction. // MS_4,4.6 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. kālamātraṃ syāt, nāṅgaprayojanasaṃbandhaḥ. kutaḥ? adarśanād viśeṣasya, nānyaiḥ kālābhidhānair asya kaścid viśeṣo lakṣyate, āgnimārutād ūrdhvam anuyājaiś carantītyevamādibhiḥ. atrāpi hi saumyādayo vihitā upasado 'pi. idam ānupūrvyam avihitam, tad vidhīyate. tasmāt kālamātram iti.
children.translated_text: The phrase 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) introduces an alternative view. It would be merely a time-designation, not a connection with subsidiary purpose. Why? Because of the non-perception of any distinction — no distinction of this [statement] is perceived from other temporal designations such as 'after the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [offering], they proceed with the <s>anuyājas</s>' and the like. For there too, the <s>Saumya</s> and the others are prescribed, and the <s>Upasads</s> as well. This sequential order, being unprescribed [elsewhere], is [here] prescribed. Therefore it is merely a time-designation.

children.text: phalavad voktahetutvād itarasya pradhānaṃ syāt // MS_4,4.7 //
children.translated_text: Or the other would be principal, because of being fruit-bearing, since the stated reason [applies]. // MS_4,4.7 //

children.text:
vaiśvadevīṃ sāṃgrahāyaṇīṃ nirvaped grāmakāma iti. tatrāmanahomāḥ śrūyante, āmanasyeti{*4/372*} tisra āhutīr juhotīti. atra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ samapradhānabhūtā āmanahomāḥ sāṃgrahāyaṇīṣṭyā, utāṅgaṃ tasyā iti. kiṃ prāptam? samapradhānabhūtā iti. kutaḥ? tulyahetutvād itarasya. tulyaṃ hi yajimattvam. nanv aphalā homāḥ. ucyate, grāmakāma ity atrānupajyate{*4/373*}. tasmāt samapradhānabhūtā iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, phalavad voktahetutvād itarasya pradhānaṃ syāt. na caitad asti, samapradhānabhūtā homā iṣṭyā iti. phalavad dhy aphalasya pradhānam, phalavatī ceṣṭiḥ, aphalā homāḥ. nanūktam, anuṣaṅgo bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, nānuṣaṅgaḥ prāpnoti. kutaḥ? vyavāyāt. tad uktam, vyavāyān nānuṣajyeteti. kena vyavāyaḥ, paridhimantraiḥ, ugro 'sy ugrastvaṃ deveṣv adhyugro 'haṃ sajāteṣu bhūyāsaṃ priyaḥ, sajātānām ugraś cet tā vasuvid ityevamādibhiḥ, etān anukramya, āmanasyeti{*4/374*} tisra āhutīr juhotīty āmananti. tasmāt sāṃgrahāyaṇyā aṅgam āmanahomā iti.
children.translated_text:
'One desiring a village should offer the <s>Vaiśvadevī Sāṃgrahāyaṇī</s> [offering].' There the <s>āmana</s>-oblations are heard: 'With the [words] "<s>āmanasya</s>" he offers three oblations.' Here a doubt [arises]: are the <s>āmana</s>-oblations co-principal with the <s>Sāṃgrahāyaṇī</s> offering, or are they a subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>) of it? What is the prima facie view? They are co-principal. Why? Because of equal causality with the other [offering]. For the status of being enjoined by 'he offers' (<s>yajimattva</s>) is equal. [The objector says:] but the oblations have no fruit. [We] reply: [the fruit] 'one desiring a village' is carried over (<s>anupajyate</s>) to them. Therefore they are co-principal.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: rather, what has a fruit would be the principal, because of the causality stated for the other. And this is not the case — that the oblations are co-principal with the offering. For what has a fruit is the principal of what has no fruit; the offering (<s>iṣṭi</s>) has a fruit, the oblations have none. [The objector says:] but was it not said that there will be a carry-over (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>)? We reply: no carry-over is possible. Why? Because of an intervening [element] (<s>vyavāya</s>). It has been stated: 'because of an intervening element, there is no carry-over.' What is the intervening element? The enclosing-stick (<s>paridhi</s>) mantras — 'You are fierce; may your fierceness [be] among the gods; may I be supremely fierce among my kinsmen, beloved, fierce among kinsmen, a finder of wealth' — and so forth. After enumerating these, they teach: 'With [the words] "<s>āmanasya</s>" he offers three oblations.' Therefore the <s>āmana</s>-oblations are a subsidiary of the <s>Sāṃgrahāyaṇī</s>.

children.text: dadhigraho naimittikaḥ śrutisaṃyogāt // MS_4,4.8 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dadhi</s>-graha (curd-libation) is <s>naimittika</s> (occasional), because of the connection with the [Vedic] statement. // MS_4,4.8 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, yāṃ vai kāṃcid adhvaryuś ca yajamānaś ca devatām antaritaḥ, tasyā āvṛśceta, yat prājāpatyaṃ dadhigrahaṃ gṛhṇāti, śamayaty evainām iti{*4/376*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ nityo dadhigrahaḥ, uta naimittika iti. kiṃ prāptam? dadhigraho naimittikaḥ syāt śrutisaṃyogāt, devatāntarāye nimitte śrūyate, na ca nityo 'ntarāyaḥ. tasmān naimittika iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'Whatever deity the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the sacrificer have offended, he would cut off [the offense]; when he takes the <s>Prājāpatya</s> curd-libation (<s>dadhigraha</s>), he thereby pacifies that [deity].' There a doubt [arises]: is the curd-libation invariable (<s>nitya</s>), or occasional (<s>naimittika</s>)? What is the prima facie view? The curd-libation should be occasional, because of the connection with the [Vedic] statement — it is heard in connection with the occasion of offending a deity, and the offense is not invariable. Therefore it is occasional.

NOTES:
[{4/376: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.5.9.1}]

children.text: nityaś ca jyeṣṭhaśabdāt // MS_4,4.9 //
children.translated_text: And it is invariable, because of the word 'eldest' (<s>jyeṣṭha</s>). // MS_4,4.9 //

children.text: yad uktam, naimittika iti, tad gṛhyate, kiṃ tu nityaś ca. kutaḥ? jyeṣṭhaśabdāt, jyeṣṭhaśabdo bhavati, jyeṣṭho vā eṣa grahāṇāṃ yasyaiṣa gṛhyate, jyaiṣṭhyam eva gacchatīti{*4/377*}. jyeṣṭhaśabdaś ca prādhānye prāthamye vā syāt. eṣa{*4/378*} prathamaḥ, na pradhānam. yadi nityaḥ, evaṃ praśasyatvād upapadyate, na jātu calācalaṃ hi{*4/379*} praśaṃsanti. tasmān nityaś ca naimittikaś ceti, vināpi nimittena grahītavyaḥ, nimittenāpi punar iti.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — that it is occasional — that is accepted; but it is also invariable. Why? Because of the word 'eldest' — there is the word 'eldest': 'This is indeed the eldest of the libations; for him for whom it is taken, he attains supremacy.' And the word 'eldest' could mean either pre-eminence or firstness. This [libation] is the first, not the pre-eminent. If it is invariable, then the designation of praise is fitting, since they never praise what is unstable. Therefore it is both invariable and occasional — it should be taken even without an occasion, and also again when there is an occasion.

NOTES:
[{4/377: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.5.9.1}]
[{4/378: E2: <s>naiṣa</s>}]
[{4/379: E2 omits <s>hi</s>}]

children.text: sārvarūpyāc ca // MS_4,4.10 //
children.translated_text: And because of [its] all-encompassing nature (<s>sārvarūpya</s>). // MS_4,4.10 //

children.text: sarvarūpatā ca śrūyate, sarveṣāṃ vaitad devānāṃ rūpaṃ yad eṣa graho yasyaiṣa gṛhyate sarvāṇy evainaṃ rūpāṇi paśūnām upatiṣṭhanta iti{*4/380*}. na hi devatārūpam asmākaṃ kiṃcid anyat pratyakṣam, anyad ato nityatvāt. tasmād api nityaś ca naimittikaś ceti.
children.translated_text: An all-encompassing nature is also heard: 'This libation is indeed the form of all the gods; for him for whom it is taken, all forms of cattle attend upon him.' For we have no other direct perception of the form of a deity, [so this must refer to something] other than that — because of its invariability. Therefore by this too, it is both invariable and occasional.

NOTES:
[{4/380: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.5.9.1}]

children.text: nityo vā syād arthavādas tayoḥ karmaṇy asaṃbandhād bhaṅgitvāc cāntarāyasya // MS_4,4.11 //
children.translated_text: Or it should be invariable only; those [statements about the occasion] are <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogistic passages), because of the non-connection of the two with the ritual act and because of the incidental nature of the offense. // MS_4,4.11 //

children.text:
yad uktam, nityo naimittikaś ceti, tatra nitya eva syāt, jyeṣṭhaśabdāt sārvarūpyāc ca. yad uktam, devatāntarāye nimitte śrūyata iti. na devatāntarāyo nimittatvena gamyate. tayor adhvaryuyajamānayoḥ{*4/381*} karmaṇy antarāyeṇa saṃbandhāt. na hy etac chrūyate, adhvaryuṇā devatāntaritavyā yajamānena veti, anityo hi antarāyaḥ. na caivaṃśabdo 'sti, antarāye sati dadhigraho grahītavya iti. vinaiva saṃyogena, dadhigrahasya grahaṇam, antarāyasamādhānaṃ tv asya prayojanam iti. tad etan nityavad grahaṇam, anityaṃ prayojanam. nityaṃ gṛhṇīyāt, anityam antarāyaṃ samādhātum iti nāvakalpate. tatra prayojane 'nityatvād grahaṇe nityavac chrutir bādhyeta, arthavādatve tu na bādhyate. na hi tad antarāyaṃ samādhātuṃ gṛhyate. anyad eva prayojanam asyāstīti praśaṃsitum abhidhīyate. dadhigrahasya tu somāṅgataiva prayojanam iti.
bhaṅgitvāc cāntarāyasya, bhaṅgī cāntarāyo 'nityo nityapraśaṃsārthaṃ saṃkīrtyate. tasmān naiṣa doṣaḥ, nitya eva dadhigraha iti.
children.translated_text:
As to what was said — that it is both invariable and occasional — rather, it should be invariable only, because of the word 'eldest' and because of its all-encompassing nature. As to what was said — 'it is heard in connection with an offense against a deity as the occasion' — the offense against a deity is not understood as an occasion. [This is] because of the non-connection of the two — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the sacrificer — with the offense through a ritual act. For this is not heard: 'The <s>Adhvaryu</s> should offend the deity, or the sacrificer should' — for the offense is non-invariable. And there is no such statement as 'when there is an offense, the curd-libation should be taken.' Without any [such] connection, the taking of the curd-libation [occurs independently], while its purpose is the pacification of the offense. This [means]: the taking is invariable in character, while the purpose is non-invariable. One should invariably take it, [and] the pacification of the non-invariable offense [is a secondary benefit] — this does not work [as an argument for its being occasional]. There, since the purpose is non-invariable, if [that were taken to mean] the taking too is non-invariable, the [Vedic] statement would be overridden; but if it is <s>arthavāda</s>, the statement is not overridden. For it is not taken in order to pacify the offense; there is another purpose for it. What is stated [about the offense] is stated as praise. The purpose of the curd-libation is simply its being a subsidiary of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice].
And because of the incidental nature of the offense — the offense is incidental and non-invariable; it is mentioned for the purpose of praising what is invariable. Therefore this is not a fault — the curd-libation is invariable only.
