children.text: vaiśvānaraś ca nityaḥ syān nityaiḥ samānasaṃkhyatvāt // MS_4,4.12 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [offering] should be invariable, because of having the same number as the invariable [elements]. // MS_4,4.12 //

children.text: asty agniḥ, ya evaṃ vidvān agniṃ cinuta iti{*4/382*}. tatra śrūyate, yo vai saṃvatsaramukhyam abhṛtvāgniṃ{*4/383*} cinute, yathā sāmigarbho vipadyate, tādṛg eva tadārtim ārcchet, vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ purastān nirvapet. saṃvatsaro vāgnir vaiśvānaraḥ, yathā saṃvatsaram āptvā kāla āgate vijāyate, evam eva saṃvatsaram āptvā kāla āgate 'gniṃ cinute, nārtim ārcched iti, eṣā vāgneḥ priyā tanūr yad vaiśvānaraḥ, priyām evāsya tanūm avarundha iti{*4/384*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ nityo vaiśvānaraḥ, atha naimittika iti. kiṃ prāptam? atrāpi nitya eva. arthavādaḥ, ukhyasya saṃvatsarābharaṇena kṛto doṣaḥ, vaiśvānareṇa vihanyata iti. nityaiś cāsya samānasaṃkhyatvaṃ bhavati, trīṇy etāni havīṃṣi bhavanti, traya ime lokā eṣāṃ lokānām ārohāyeti, lokānāṃ haviṣāṃ sāmānyaṃ nāsti. yadi yathā lokā nityās trayaḥ, evam imāni havīṃṣi nityāni trīṇi, evaṃ lokaiḥ saṃstavo ghaṭate. tasmān nityo vaiśvānara iti.
children.translated_text: There is the fire[-altar building]: 'He who, knowing thus, builds the fire-altar.' There it is heard: 'The year indeed pushes him toward [un]stability who, having built the fire, does not become stable. Five are the prior layers (<s>citi</s>). Then he should build the sixth layer.' 'He should offer beforehand a twelve-potsherd [cake] to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. The year is indeed the fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; just as, having reached the year, one is born when the time comes, so too, having reached the year, when the time comes he builds the fire — he would not come to harm.' 'This is indeed the beloved body of <s>Agni</s>, namely <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; he thereby obtains his beloved body.' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> invariable, or occasional? What is the prima facie view? Here too it is invariable only. The <s>arthavāda</s> [states that] the defect created by bearing the <s>ukhya</s> [fire-pot] for a year is removed by the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. And it has the same number as the invariable [elements]: 'These oblations are three; these worlds are three — for the ascent of these worlds.' There is no commonality between worlds and oblations. If the three oblations are invariable just as the three worlds are invariable, then the praise through [comparison with] the worlds is fitting. Therefore the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is invariable.

NOTES:
[{4/382: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.5.2.1}]
[{4/383: E2: <s>abhūtvāgniṃ</s>}]
[{4/384: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.5.1.7}]

children.text: pakṣe votpannasaṃyogāt // MS_4,4.13 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is occasional], because of the connection of what has arisen with the occasion. // MS_4,4.13 //

children.text: utpannasya nimitta ukhyābharaṇe nirghātena saṃyogaḥ. nāsaṃyuktasyotpannasya doṣanirghātaprayojanatā. tasmād iha na dadhigrahavad virodho 'sti. tena nārthavādaḥ, naimittika iti. atha yad uktam, lokaiḥ samānasaṃkhyatvaṃ nityatvād upapadyate, nānyatheti. tatra brūmaḥ, tritvāl lokānāṃ haviṣāṃ ca sāmānyād arthavādo bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: What has arisen has a connection with the occasion — the non-stability of the <s>ukhya</s> [fire-pot] bearing — through the fault. There is no purpose of removing the fault for what has arisen but is not connected [with the fault]. Therefore here there is no contradiction as in the case of the curd-libation. Hence it is not <s>arthavāda</s> — it is occasional. Now, as to what was said — 'the sameness of number with the worlds is fitting because of invariability, and not otherwise' — to that we say: because of the commonality of three-ness between the worlds and the oblations, it will be <s>arthavāda</s>.

children.text: ṣaṭcitiḥ pūrvavattvāt // MS_4,4.14 //
children.translated_text: The fire-altar of six layers (<s>ṣaṭciti</s>) [is invariable], because of the same reasoning as before. // MS_4,4.14 //

children.text: asty agniḥ, ya evaṃ vidvān agniṃ cinuta iti{*4/385*}. tatra [523]{*4/386*} śrūyate, saṃvatsaro vainaṃ pratiṣṭhāyai nudati yo 'gniṃ citvā na pratitiṣṭhati, pañca pūrvāś citayo bhavanti. atha ṣaṣṭhīṃ citiṃ cinuta iti{*4/387*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ yo 'yaṃ nitya evāgniḥ sa evāyaṃ ṣaṭcitika ucyate, utaikacitiko naimittika iti. kiṃ prāptam? tasminn eva nitye 'gnau ṣaṣṭhī citir eṣā vidhīyate, nityāyām eva ṣaṣṭhyām eṣo 'rthavādaḥ. yo 'pi na pratiṣṭhārhaḥ, so 'py anayā ṣaṣṭhyā cityā pratiṣṭhātum arhatīti citipraśaṃsā. kim artham evaṃ varṇyate? ṣaṣṭhīśabdaśravaṇāt. ṣaṇṇāṃ hi pūraṇī ṣaṣṭhī, ekasyāṃ hi citau ṣaṣṭhīśabdo na sāmañjasyena syāt. tasmāt ṣaṭcitiko 'gnir nitya iti.
children.translated_text: There is the fire[-altar building]: 'He who, knowing thus, builds the fire-altar.' There [523] it is heard: 'The year indeed pushes him toward stability — he who, having built the fire, does not become stable; five are the prior layers. Then he should build the sixth layer.' There a doubt [arises]: is this invariable fire-altar itself being called the six-layered, or is a single-layered one occasional? What is the prima facie view? In that very invariable fire-altar, this sixth layer is being prescribed; this <s>arthavāda</s> is about the [already] invariable sixth [layer]: even one who does not deserve stability — he too can become stable through this sixth layer — [this is] praise of the layer. Why is it described thus? Because of the hearing of the word 'sixth.' For 'sixth' is the ordinal of six; in a single layer, the word 'sixth' would not be fitting. Therefore the fire-altar of six layers is invariable.

children.text: tābhiś ca tulyasaṃkhyānāt // MS_4,4.15 //
children.translated_text: And because of being enumerated equally with those [other layers]. // MS_4,4.15 //

children.text: tābhiś ca pūrvābhir asyās tulyavat prasaṃkhyānaṃ bhavati. katham? iyaṃ vāva prathamā citiḥ, oṣadhayaḥ purīṣam. antarīkṣaṃ vāva dvitīyā citiḥ, vayāṃsi purīṣam. asau vāva tṛtīyā citiḥ, nakṣatrāṇi purīṣam. yajño vāva caturthā{*4/388*} citiḥ, dakṣiṇā purīṣam. yajamāno vāva pañcamī citiḥ, prajāḥ purīṣam. saṃvatsaro vāva ṣaṣṭhī citiḥ, ṛtavaḥ purīṣam iti{*4/389*}, tulyānāṃ ca tulyavad anukramaṇaṃ bhavati, yathā - devā ṛṣayo gandharvās te 'nyata āsan. asurā rakṣāṃsi piśācāḥ te 'nyata āsann iti{*4/390*}, tulyavac cāmūṣāṃ citīnām anukramaṇam anayā ṣaṣṭhyā. tasmād etayā tattulyayā bhavitavyam. yadi ca yasminn eva kratau [524]{*4/391*} tāḥ, tasminn evaiṣā, tata etābhis tulyā. tasmād api sa eva nityo 'gniḥ ṣaṭcitika iti.
children.translated_text: And this [sixth layer] is enumerated equally with those prior [five layers]. How? 'This earth is indeed the first layer; plants are its filling. The atmosphere is indeed the second layer; birds are its filling. Yonder [heaven] is indeed the third layer; stars are its filling. The sacrifice is indeed the fourth layer; <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (ritual fees) are its filling. The sacrificer is indeed the fifth layer; offspring are its filling. The year is indeed the sixth layer; seasons are its filling.' And what is equal is enumerated equally — just as 'The gods, the sages, the <s>Gandharvas</s> — they were on one side. The <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s> — they were on the other side.' And the enumeration of those [prior five] layers together with this sixth is on an equal footing. Therefore this [sixth] must be equal to those. And if [the sixth is] in the very same ritual [524] in which those [five] are, then it is equal to them. Therefore by this too, the same invariable fire-altar is six-layered.

children.text: arthavādopapatteś ca // MS_4,4.16 //
children.translated_text: And because the <s>arthavāda</s> is fitting [in this interpretation]. // MS_4,4.16 //

children.text: arthavādaś ca bhavati, ṣaṭ citayo bhavanti, ṣaṭ purīṣāṇi, tāni dvādaśa saṃpadyante, dvādaśā māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ, saṃvatsara eva pratitiṣṭhatīti{*4/392*}, tad ekacitike 'gnau na sāmañjasyena vacanaṃ bhavati. tasmān nitya eva ṣaṭcitikaḥ.
children.translated_text: And there is an <s>arthavāda</s>: 'There are six layers, six fillings; these total twelve. Twelve are the months of the year; one becomes established in the year itself.' This statement would not be fitting in a fire-altar of a single layer. Therefore the six-layered [fire-altar] is invariable only.

NOTES:
[{4/392: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.6.10.3}]

children.text: ekacitir vā syād apavṛkte hi codyate nimittena // MS_4,4.17 //
children.translated_text: Or it should be a single layer, for it is enjoined when [the invariable rite] has been completed, with an occasion. // MS_4,4.17 //

children.text:
ekacitir vā naimittikaḥ{*4/393*} syāt. kutaḥ? apavṛkte hi yāge codyate, apratiṣṭhayā nimittena. yo na pratitiṣṭhati, tasyaiṣā citir ucyate naimittikī, sā na nityā bhavitum arhati.
api cāpavṛkte yāge codyate sā, na vartamāne bhavitum arhati. nanu citveti cayane nirvṛtte, na yāge. ucyate, naitat padārthe nirvṛtte citveti. kiṃ tarhi? vākyārthe. agniṃ citveti, agneś cayanenārtham abhinirvartyeti. kṛte ca yāge cayanenāgner artho nirvartito bhavati, nānyathā. ṣaṣṭhīśabdaś ca, pañca pūrvāś citaya uktāḥ, tā apekṣyāvakalpiṣyate, tasmān nirvṛtte yāga ity ucyate. tasmād vacanād ekacitir agniḥ.
children.translated_text:
Or it should be a single layer, occasional. Why? Because it is enjoined when the sacrifice has been completed, with the occasion of non-stability. For one who does not become stable — for him this layer is stated as occasional; it should not be invariable.
Moreover, it is enjoined when the sacrifice has been completed — it should not belong to the ongoing [sacrifice]. [The objector says:] but [the word] 'having built' (<s>citvā</s>) refers to when the building is complete, not when the sacrifice [is complete]. [We] reply: no, the word [means completion] not of the word-meaning [alone] but of the sentence-meaning. 'Having built the fire' [means] having accomplished the purpose through the building of the fire. And when the sacrifice has been performed, the purpose of the fire is accomplished through building — not otherwise. And the word 'sixth' — five prior layers having been stated, it will be construed in relation to those. Therefore it is said that [it is enjoined] when the sacrifice is complete. Therefore, by [Vedic] statement, the fire-altar is of a single [additional] layer.

children.text: vipratiṣedhāt tābhiḥ samānasaṃkhyatvam // MS_4,4.18 //
children.translated_text: Because of mutual contradiction, [the argument of] having the same number as those [layers is refuted]. // MS_4,4.18 //

children.text: dvayoḥ sūtrayor idam uttaram, tābhiś ca tulyasaṃkhyānāt, [525]{*4/394*} arthavādopapatteś ceti{*4/395*}. tābhir nityābhiḥ{*4/396*} samānasaṃkhyatvaṃ bhaviṣyati, arthavādaś copapatsyate. pañca pūrvāś citayo bhavanti, yābhir asau citibhir na pratitiṣṭhate, atheyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī pratiṣṭhārtham iti. tāś ca sapurīṣā apekṣya dvādaśatvena saṃstavo bhaviṣyati. vipratiṣedhād ekasya, ṣaṭsaṃkhyāyā dvādaśasaṃkhyāyāś ceti. atulyānām api tulyavad anukramaṇaṃ bhavati, yathā - devā manuṣyāḥ pitaras te 'nyata āsann iti{*4/397*}.
children.translated_text: This is the reply to two <s>sūtras</s> — 'and because of equal number with those, [525] and because of the appropriateness of <s>arthavāda</s>.' With those permanent [layers] there will be equality of number, and the <s>arthavāda</s> will be appropriate: 'There are five prior layers; by those layers that [altar] does not become stable; then this sixth [layer] is for the purpose of stability.' And considering those [layers] together with the filling material (<s>purīṣa</s>), the praise will be by the number twelve. Because of contradiction between one [number] — either the number six or the number twelve. Even of unequal [things], enumeration as if equal is possible, as in: 'Gods, men, and ancestors — they were on the other side.'

children.text: pitṛyajñaḥ svakālatvād anaṅgaṃ syāt // MS_4,4.19 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pitṛyajña</s> (ancestor-sacrifice) would be non-subsidiary, because of having its own time. // MS_4,4.19 //

children.text:
asty āmāvāsye karmaṇi pitṛyajñaḥ, amāvāsyāyām aparāhṇe piṇḍapitṛyajñena carantīti{*4/398*}. tatra saṃśayaḥ, kim āmāvāsyasya karmaṇaḥ piṇḍapitṛyajño 'ṅgam, utānaṅgam iti. kiṃ prāptam? aṅgam, phalavat saṃnidhānān niṣkrayavacanāc ca.
āha, nanu phalavat saṃnidhāv aphalaṃ tadaṅgaṃ bhavati, phalavac cedaṃ kalpyeta svargeṇeti. ucyate, satyam, amānāsyayaikavākyatvān na śakyaḥ svargaḥ kalpayitum iti. āha, kālavacanatvān na karmaṇaikavākyatvaṃ saṃbhavatīti. ucyate, lakṣaṇayāpi tāvat karmaikavākyatvaṃ saṃbhavati. svarge kalpye na lakṣaṇā, na śrutiḥ. evaṃ cāmananti, yat pitṛbhyaḥ purvedyuḥ karoti, pitṛbhya etad yajñaṃ niṣkrīya yajamāno devebhyaḥ pratanuta iti{*4/399*}, amāvāsyāṃ prati niṣkretum{*4/400*} ca śrūyate, tasmāt tadaṅgabhūtam iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pitṛyajñaḥ svakālatvād anaṅgaṃ{*4/401*} syāt, [526]{*4/402*} anaṅgabhūtaḥ piṇḍapitṛyajñaḥ. kasmāt? svakālatvāt, svaśabdābhihitena kālenāsya saṃbandhaḥ, na karmaṇā lakṣiteneti, yathā - darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā somena yajeteti{*4/403*}, yathā tad etat{*4/404*} purastād upasadāṃ saumyena carantīti{*4/405*} ca, kāla{*4/406*} evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ śabdo na karmaṇi, karmaṇi{*4/407*} lakṣaṇā, śrutiś ca lakṣaṇāyā balīyasī. yac coktam, laksaṇayā karmaikavākyatā bhaviṣyatīti, tac ca na. kasmāt? anuvāde hi lakṣaṇā nyāyyā, na vidhau. vidhiś cāyam. tasmān nāmāvāsyākarmaṇā saṃbandhaḥ, ekasmin kāle dve karmaṇī paraspareṇāsaṃbaddha iti.
children.translated_text:
In the new-moon rite there is the <s>Pitṛyajña</s> — 'on the new-moon day in the afternoon they perform the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (ancestor-offering with rice-balls).' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> a subsidiary of the new-moon rite, or is it non-subsidiary? What is the prima facie view? It is a subsidiary, because of proximity to [a rite] that has a fruit, and because of the statement about 'buying off.'
[The objector] says: but when there is proximity to [a rite] that has a fruit, [the rite] without a fruit becomes its subsidiary; and this [Pitṛyajña] could be postulated [as having] a fruit of <s>svarga</s> (heaven). We reply: true, [but] because of syntactic unity with the new-moon [rite], <s>svarga</s> cannot be postulated. [The objector] says: because of the time-statement, syntactic unity with the [new-moon] rite is not possible. We reply: even through secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), syntactic unity with the rite is possible. In postulating <s>svarga</s>, there is neither secondary indication nor [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>). And thus they recite: 'What he performs on the previous day for the ancestors — having bought off this sacrifice for the ancestors, the sacrificer extends [it] to the gods.' And it is heard that the buying off is in relation to the new-moon [rite]. Therefore it is a subsidiary of that [new-moon rite].
Given this [prima facie view], we say: the <s>Pitṛyajña</s> would be non-subsidiary, [526] because of having its own time. The <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> is non-subsidiary. Why? Because of having its own time — its connection is with the time denoted by its own word, not with the rite indicated [by secondary indication]. Just as 'having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>,' and just as 'before the <s>Upasads</s>, they perform [the rite] associated with <s>Soma</s>' — here the primary [meaning of the] word is time, not the rite; [the connection] with the rite is secondary indication, and the [Vedic] word is stronger than secondary indication. As for what was said — 'syntactic unity with the rite will come through secondary indication' — that too is not [valid]. Why? For secondary indication is appropriate in a restatement, not in an injunction. And this is an injunction. Therefore there is no connection with the new-moon rite; two rites at one time are mutually unconnected.

children.text: tulyavac ca prasaṃkhyānāt // MS_4,4.20 //
children.translated_text: And because of being counted as equal [to principal rites]. // MS_4,4.20 //

children.text: tulyavac cānyaiḥ pradhānaiḥ prasaṃkhyāyate, catvāro vai mahāyajñāḥ, agnihotram, darśapūrṇamāsau, jyotiṣṭomaḥ, piṇḍapitṛyajña iti, mahāyajñais tulyavat prasaṃkhyāyate. kāsya mahāyajñatā syāt, anyataḥ phalavattāyāḥ. tasmād anaṅgam.
children.translated_text: And it is counted as equal to other principal [rites]: 'Four indeed are the great sacrifices — the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, and the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s>' — it is counted as equal to the great sacrifices. How would its greatness exist, except through having a fruit [of its own]? Therefore it is non-subsidiary.

children.text: pratiṣiddhe ca darśanāt // MS_4,4.21 //
children.translated_text: And because it is shown when [the new-moon rite] is prohibited. // MS_4,4.21 //

children.text:
itaś cānaṅgam, pratiṣiddhe{*4/408*} āmāvāsye piṇḍapitṛyajñaṃ darśayati, paurṇamāsīm eva yajeta bhrātṛvyavān, nāmāvāsyām, hatvā bhrātṛvyam amāvāsyayā yajeta, piṇḍapitṛyajñenaivāmāvāsyāyāṃ prīṇātīti{*4/409*}. asatyām amāvāsyāyāṃ piṇḍapitṛyajñaṃ darśayati, tadanaṅgatva upapadyate. tasmād api nāṅgaṃ piṇḍapitṛyajña iti.
kiṃ prayojanaṃ cintāyāḥ? yadi paurṇamāsyām ādhānam, tato 'nantarāyām amāvāsyāyāṃ na kriyate, yathā pūrvapakṣaḥ. yathā tarhi siddhāntaḥ, tathā kartavyaḥ. idam aparaṃ prayojanam, kuṇḍapāyināmayane māsam agnihotraṃ juhoti, māsaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ [527]{*4/410*} yajeteti, yathā pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, tathā kartavyaḥ piṇḍapitṛyajñaḥ. yathā siddhāntaḥ, tathā na kartavya iti. ślokam apy udāharanti -
ādhānaṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ ced vṛtte darśe kariṣyate/
anaṅgaṃ pitṛyajñaś cet tatraiva{*4/411*} na kariṣyate// iti.
children.translated_text:
And for this further reason it is non-subsidiary: it shows the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> when the new-moon [rite] is prohibited — 'One who has a rival should sacrifice only at the full moon, not at the new moon. Having slain his rival with the new-moon [rite], he should sacrifice [at the new moon again]; at the new moon he gratifies [the ancestors] with the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> alone.' It shows the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> in the absence of the new-moon [rite]; this is appropriate [only] if it is non-subsidiary to that. Therefore, by this too, the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> is not a subsidiary.
What is the purpose of the inquiry? If the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>) is on the full-moon day, then on the immediately following new-moon day it [the Piṇḍapitṛyajña] is not performed — according to the prima facie view. But according to the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), it should be performed. This is another purpose: in the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s>' journey (<s>ayana</s>), one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> for a month, [and] one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [527] for a month — according to the prima facie view, the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> should be performed [as subsidiary]. According to the established conclusion, it should not be performed. And they cite a verse:
'If the fire-establishment is on the full-moon day, when the new-moon has passed, it will be performed;
But if the <s>Pitṛyajña</s> is non-subsidiary, it will not be performed there [in that case alone].'

children.text: paśvaṅgaṃ raśanā syāt tadāgame vidhānāt // MS_4,4.22 //
children.translated_text: The rope (<s>raśanā</s>) would be a subsidiary of the animal, because of its being enjoined at the arrival of that [animal]. // MS_4,4.22 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā trivṛtā yūpaṃ parivīyāgneyaṃ savanīyaṃ paśum upākarotīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ paśvaṅgaṃ raśanā, uta yūpāṅgam iti. kiṃ prāptam? paśvaṅgam. kutaḥ? tadāgame vidhānāt, paśvāgame hi vidhīyate. paśunāsyāḥ saṃbandha utpattivākye śrūyate, parivyāṇaṃ kṛtvopākaroti paśuṃ nānyatheti. evaṃ śrutir bhavati, kālavacane lakṣaṇā syāt, parivyāṇena kālo lakṣyeteti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'Having taken the <s>Āśvina</s> cup (<s>graha</s>), he wraps [the rope] around the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) with a three-fold [wrapping] and prepares the <s>Āgneya</s> animal for the <s>savanīya</s> [pressing].' There a doubt [arises]: is the rope a subsidiary of the animal, or of the post? What is the prima facie view? It is a subsidiary of the animal. Why? Because of its being enjoined at the arrival of that [animal] — for it is enjoined at the arrival of the animal. Its connection with the animal is heard in the origination-sentence: 'Having performed the wrapping, he prepares the animal — not otherwise.' Thus is the [Vedic] word; in the time-statement there would be secondary indication — [i.e.,] the wrapping would [merely] indicate the time.

children.text: yūpāṅgaṃ vā tatsaṃskārāt // MS_4,4.23 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a subsidiary of the post (<s>yūpa</s>), because of being a refinement of that. // MS_4,4.23 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome pratyakṣo hi yūpasya saṃskāraḥ, raśanā hi yā ca yāvatīṃ ca draḍhimno mātrāṃ yūpasya saṃjanayati, draḍhimnā ca prayojanaṃ yūpasya. tasmād yūpasyaiva draḍhimne raśanā syāt. dvitīyā ca vibhaktis tatprādhānya eva bhavati, raśanāyāṃ ca tṛtīyā. tṛtīyā ca guṇatve tasyāḥ, tasmād yūpāṅgam. yat tu, tadāgame vidhānād ity uktam, tatparihartavyam. ucyate, tadāgame vidhānaṃ [528]{*4/412*} vākyam{*4/413*}, dvitīyā ca vibhaktiḥ śrutiḥ pratyakṣaṃ ca, vākyaṃ bādheyātām iti. yat tu lakṣaṇeti, śrutyasaṃbhave lakṣaṇāpi nyāyyaiva.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the refinement of the post is directly perceptible — for the rope generates a certain measure of firmness for the post, and firmness has purpose for the post. Therefore the rope exists precisely for the firmness of the post. And the accusative case ending applies precisely in [establishing] the primacy of that [post], while the instrumental [applies] to the rope. And the instrumental [indicates] its subordinate status. Therefore it is a subsidiary of the post. As for what was said — 'because of its being enjoined at the arrival of that [animal]' — that must be set aside. We say: the injunction at the arrival of that [animal] is [established by] the sentence [528], while the accusative case ending is the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>) — directly perceptible — and [both together] should override the sentence. As for the [argument about] secondary indication — when the [Vedic] word is not possible, secondary indication too is entirely appropriate.

children.text: arthavādaś ca tadarthavat // MS_4,4.24 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>arthavāda</s> accords with that purpose [i.e., the post]. // MS_4,4.24 //

children.text:
evaṃ ca mantrārthavādo 'rthavān bhaviṣyati, yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgāt sa u śreyān bhavati jāyamānaḥ. taṃ dhīrāsaḥ kavaya unnayanti svādhyo manasā devayanta iti{*4/414*}. tasmād yūpāṅgaṃ raśaneti.
kiṃ prayojanaṃ cintāyāḥ? agnau śrūyate, ekayūpa ekādaśa paśavo niyojyā iti. pratipaśu raśanā kāryā, yadi pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. siddhānte dvairaśanyam eva. ślokam apy udāharanti -
paśvaṅgaṃ raśanā cet, yady ekasmin bahūn niyuñjīta/
pratipaśu raśanā kāryā, yūpe ced dvairaśanyaṃ syāt// iti.
children.translated_text:
And thus the <s>mantra</s>-<s>arthavāda</s> will be meaningful: 'A youth, well-dressed, wrapped around, has come; he becomes more excellent at birth. Wise sages raise him up, devoted in mind, seeking the divine.' Therefore the rope is a subsidiary of the post.
What is the purpose of the inquiry? It is heard regarding fire: 'At a single post, eleven animals should be tethered.' A rope should be made for each animal — if the prima facie view [holds]. In the established conclusion, only a double rope [is needed]. And they cite a verse:
'If the rope is a subsidiary of the animal, when many are tethered to one [post],
a rope should be made for each animal; but if of the post, there would be a double rope.'

children.text: svaruś cāpy ekadeśatvāt // MS_4,4.25 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>svaru</s> (peg/pointed end) too, because of being a part [of the post]. // MS_4,4.25 //

children.text: asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ somāṅgabhūtaḥ, yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*4/415*}. tatra śrūyate, svaruṇā svadhitinā vā paśum anaktīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ yūpāṅgaṃ svaruḥ, uta paśvaṅgam iti. kiṃ prāptam? yūpāṅgam iti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ? ekadeśatvāt. ekadeśaḥ svarur yūpasyeti śrūyate, yūpasya svaruṃ karotīti svarum antaṃ yūpaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ{*4/416*}. evaṃ sa yūpo bhavatīti, yathā caṣālam.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal that is a subsidiary of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] — 'the consecrated one who slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.' There it is heard: 'He anoints the animal with the <s>svaru</s> (peg) or with the <s>svadhiti</s> (axe).' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>svaru</s> a subsidiary of the post, or of the animal? What is the prima facie view? We say it is a subsidiary of the post. Why? Because of being a part [of the post]. The <s>svaru</s> is heard as a part of the post — 'he makes the <s>svaru</s> of the post,' meaning 'he should make the post ending in a point (<s>svaru</s>).' Thus it becomes [part of] the post — just like the <s>caṣāla</s> (top piece of the post).

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/415: Tait.S. 6.1.11.6}*
*{4/416: E1 gibt svaruṃ karotīti svarum antaṃ yūpaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ in Klammern}*
*{4/417: E2: 5,99; E6: 2,61}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/415: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.1.11.6}]
[{4/416: E1 gives <s>svaruṃ karotīti svarum antaṃ yūpaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ</s> in brackets}]
[{4/417: E2: 5,99; E6: 2,61}]

children.text: niṣkrayaś ca tadaṅgavat // MS_4,4.26 //
children.translated_text: And the 'buying-off' statement [accords] with it being a subsidiary of that [post]. // MS_4,4.26 //

children.text: yūpāṅgam iva svaruṃ niṣkrayavādo darśayati, apaśyan ha sma vai purā ṛṣayo ye yūpaṃ prāpayanti, saṃbhajya sruvante manyante, yajñavaiśasāya vā idaṃ karmeti, te prastaraṃ sruvaniṣkrayam apaśyan, yūpasya svarum ayajñavaiśasāyeti, niṣkrayaśravaṇāt tadaṅgatā vijñāyate. tasmād yūpāṅgam iti.
children.translated_text: The 'buying-off' statement shows the <s>svaru</s> as if a subsidiary of the post: 'The sages of old could not see those who cause [the animal] to reach the post. They thought — "[The animal] breaks apart, splits apart; this act is indeed sacrificial slaughter." They saw the <s>prastara</s> (grass bundle) as the buying-off (<s>niṣkraya</s>) of the <s>sruva</s> (ladle), and the <s>svaru</s> of the post as [that which ensures] non-violence in sacrifice.' From the hearing of 'buying-off,' the subsidiary-status to that [post] is understood. Therefore it is a subsidiary of the post.

children.text: paśvaṅgaṃ vārthakarmatvāt // MS_4,4.27 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a subsidiary of the animal, because of being a purposeful act. // MS_4,4.27 //

children.text: paśvaṅgaṃ vā, tasya hy añjanārthena svaruṇā prayojanam. tathā hi śrūyate, svaruṇā paśum anaktīti. tad añjanaṃ paśoḥ, svaror utpattiṃ prayojayati. yadi tadartha eṣaḥ svaruḥ, tato dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam. atha yūpārthaḥ, adṛṣṭaṃ prayojanaṃ{*4/418*} tataḥ kalpyam. tasmāt paśvaṅgam iti.
children.translated_text: Or it is a subsidiary of the animal, for the <s>svaru</s> serves the purpose of anointing the animal. For thus it is heard: 'He anoints the animal with the <s>svaru</s>.' That anointing of the animal motivates the production of the <s>svaru</s>. If this <s>svaru</s> is for that [animal's] purpose, then there is a visible purpose. But if it is for the post's purpose, then an unseen purpose would have to be postulated. Therefore it is a subsidiary of the animal.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/418: E2 om. prayojanaṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/418: E2 omits <s>prayojanaṃ</s>}]

children.text: bhaktyā niṣkrayavādaḥ syāt // MS_4,4.28 //
children.translated_text: The 'buying-off' statement would be by way of figurative identification (<s>bhakti</s>). // MS_4,4.28 //

children.text:
kayā bhaktyā? evam āha, yūpaḥ kilāgnau pakṣetavyaḥ, yat svaruḥ prakṣipyate, tena{*4/419*} yūpaḥ prakṣipyata iti sa eṣa niṣkaya iva bhavati, anayā bhaktyā stutir iti.
kiṃ bhavati prayojanam? ekayūpa ekādaśa paśavo yadā niyujyante, tadaikasyaiva paśoḥ samañjanam, pūrvasmin pakṣe. sarveṣāṃ siddhānte. ślokaś ca bhavati -
svarur yūpāṅgam iti ced ekasmaiva samañjanam/
bahūnām ekayūpatve, sarveṣāṃ tu samañjanam// iti.
children.translated_text:
By what figurative identification? He says thus: the post is supposed to be thrown into the fire; since the <s>svaru</s> is thrown [into the fire], thereby the post is [as if] thrown — this is like a buying-off. By this figurative identification, it is praise (<s>stuti</s>).
What is the consequence? When eleven animals are tethered to a single post, only one animal's anointing [is performed] — according to the prima facie view. According to the established conclusion, [anointing] of all. And there is a verse:
'If the <s>svaru</s> is a subsidiary of the post — anointing for one alone;
but when many [are tethered] to a single post, anointing of all.'

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayor ijyāḥ pradhānāny aviśeṣāt // MS_4,4.29 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the offerings (<s>ijyās</s>) are all primary, because of no distinction. // MS_4,4.29 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra śrūyante, āgneyāgnīṣomīyopāṃśuyājaindrāgnasāṃnāyyayāgāḥ. tathā, āghārāv ājyabhāgau, prayājānuyājāḥ, patnīsaṃyājāḥ, samiṣṭayajuḥ, sviṣṭakṛd iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ sarve yāgāḥ pradhānabhūtāḥ, uta kecid guṇabhūtā iti. kiṃ prāptam? darśapūrṇamāsayor yāvatya ijyās tāḥ sarvāḥ pradhānabhūtā iti. yajeta svargakāma ity aviśeṣeṇa yāgebhyaḥ phalaṃ śrūyate, phalavac ca pradhānam, sarve cāmī yāgāḥ. tasmāt sarve pradhānabhūtā iti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites]. There the following are heard: the <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>, <s>Aindrāgna</s>, and <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> offerings. Also: the two <s>āghāras</s> (pourings), the two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions), the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings), <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings), <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> (wife's offerings), <s>samiṣṭayajus</s> (concluding formula), and <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the all-gods' offering). There a doubt [arises]: are all the offerings primary, or are some subsidiary? What is the prima facie view? All the offerings in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> are primary. [The injunction] 'one desiring heaven should sacrifice' — without distinction, the fruit is heard for [all] the offerings; and what has a fruit is primary, and all these are offerings. Therefore all are primary.

children.text: api vāṅgāni kānicid yeṣv aṅgatvena saṃstutiḥ sāmānyo hy abhisaṃstavaḥ{*4/421*} // MS_4,4.30 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, some are subsidiaries — those for which there is praise in terms of subsidiary-status; for the praise is general. // MS_4,4.30 //

children.text: api vā kānicid aṅgāni bhaveyuḥ. kāni punas tāni? yeṣv aṅgatvena saṃstutiḥ, yathā, abhīṣū vā etau yajñasya yad āghārau, cakṣuṣī vaitau yajñasya yad ājyabhāgau{*4/422*}, yat prayājānuyājāś cejyante varma vā etad yajñasya kriyate, varma vā yajamānasya bhrātṛvyasyābhibhūtyai, iti{*4/423*}. abhīśū rathasyāṅgam, cakṣuṣī cakṣuṣmataḥ, varma varmavataḥ. sāmānyo hy abhisaṃstavo yuktaḥ. yadi cāṅgāni tāni saṃstutāni, tataḥ saṃstavo 'rthavān bhavati. tasmād aṅgasaṃstutāny aṅgānīti.
children.translated_text: Or rather, some may be subsidiaries. Which are those? Those that are praised as subsidiaries — as [stated]: 'These two <s>āghāras</s> (libations) are indeed the reins of the sacrifice; these two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions) are indeed the eyes of the sacrifice; when the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> are offered, an armor is indeed made for the sacrifice — an armor for the sacrificer, for the overpowering of his rival.' The reins are a part of a chariot, the eyes of one who possesses sight, the armor of one who is armored. For a common praise is appropriate [only when there is a common relationship]. And if those are praised as subsidiaries, then the praise becomes meaningful. Therefore, those praised as subsidiaries are [indeed] subsidiaries.

NOTES:
[{4/421: E1 (Fn.): <s>sāmānyeṣv abhisaṃstavaḥ</s>}]
[{4/422: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.2.1}]
[{4/423: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.1.5}]
[{4/424: E2: 5,101; E6: 2,62}]

children.text: tathā cānyārthadarśanam // MS_4,4.31 //
children.translated_text: And thus, the observation of [their serving] another purpose [is explained]. // MS_4,4.31 //

children.text: evaṃ ca kṛtvānyārthadarśanam upapannaṃ bhavati, prayāje prayāje kṛṣṇalaṃ juhotīti{*4/425*}. na ca prayājān yajati, na cānuyājān yajatīti ca.
children.translated_text: And having done so, the observation of [their serving] another purpose is established: 'At each <s>prayāja</s> he offers a <s>kṛṣṇala</s> (black grain)'; and '[at that time] he neither offers the <s>prayājas</s> nor offers the <s>anuyājas</s>.'

NOTES:
[{4/425: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.3.2.3}]

children.text: aviśiṣṭaṃ tu kāraṇaṃ pradhāneṣu guṇasya vidyamānatvāt // MS_4,4.32 //
children.translated_text: But the reason is undifferentiated, because of the subsidiary being present in the principal [rites as well]. // MS_4,4.32 //

children.text: aviśiṣṭam etat kāraṇaṃ saṃstavo nāma, āgneyādīnām apy aṅgatvena saṃstutir asti, śiro vaitad yajñasya yad āgneyaḥ, hṛdayam upāṃśuyāgaḥ, pādāv agnīṣomīya iti, śiraḥ śirasvato 'ṅgam, hṛdayaṃ hṛdayavataḥ, pādau pādāvata iti sarvasyaivāṅgatvena saṃstutir iti sarvam evāṅgaṃ prāpnoti. tat{*4/426*} pradhānaṃ na syāt. asati pradhāne kasyāṅgam? tasmān naitad aṅgam iti.
children.translated_text: This reason called 'praise' is undifferentiated — for the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings] too are praised as subsidiaries: 'The <s>Āgneya</s> is indeed the head of the sacrifice, the <s>Upāṃśuyāga</s> (silent offering) is the heart, the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> is the feet.' The head is a limb of what possesses a head, the heart of what possesses a heart, the feet of what possesses feet — thus everything is praised as a subsidiary, and everything would become a subsidiary. In that case, nothing would be primary. In the absence of a primary, of what would [these] be subsidiaries? Therefore these are not subsidiaries.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/426: E1 (Fn.): tatra}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/426: E1 (Fn.): <s>tatra</s>}]

children.text: nānukte 'nyārthadarśanaṃ parārthatvāt // MS_4,4.33 //
children.translated_text: The observation of [serving] another purpose [does not apply] when [the entity] has not been mentioned, because of [its] being for another's purpose. // MS_4,4.33 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, anyārthadarśanaṃ parārthatvāt, na tat sādhakaṃ bhavati. parārthaṃ hi tad vākyam, na dṛśyamānasya prayājādeḥ prāpaṇārtham. tasmād anyad asya pramāṇam anveṣṭavyaṃ śrutyantaraṃ nyāyo vā. tasminn asati, mṛgatṛṣṇādarśanam iva tad bhavati, saṃstutir apy asati nyāye, asādhikaiva.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'the observation of [serving] another purpose, because of being for another's purpose' — that does not establish [the point]. For that sentence is for another's purpose, not for the purpose of establishing the visible <s>prayājas</s> and such. Therefore another means of valid knowledge must be sought for this — either another Vedic text or reasoning. In the absence of that, it becomes like seeing a mirage; and the praise too, in the absence of reasoning, is simply inconclusive.

children.text: pṛthaktve tv abhidhānayor niveśaḥ, śrutito vyapadeśāc ca, tat punar mukhyalakṣaṇaṃ yat phalavattvam, tat saṃnidhāv asaṃyuktaṃ tadaṅgaṃ syāt, bhāgitvāt kāraṇasyāśrutaś cānyasaṃbandhaḥ // MS_4,4.34 //
children.translated_text: But when [the two — primary and subsidiary — are] separate, the placement is of the two designations; and from the [Vedic] text and from the descriptive statement [this is known]. Moreover, the principal characteristic is fruitfulness; what is not connected with that, [being heard] in proximity, would be its subsidiary — because of [its] sharing [in the rite], and because its connection with another [fruit] is not heard. // MS_4,4.34 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. tad uktam, sarvāṇi samapradhānānīti. naitad evam, darśapūrṇamāsaśabdavācyāni pradhānāni karmāṇi. kutaḥ? phalasaṃyogāt, darśapūrṇamāsaśabdakebhyaḥ phalaṃ śrūyate, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeteti{*4/428*}. kāni punar darśapūrṇamāsaśabdakāni? yeṣāṃ vacane paurṇamāsīśabdo 'māvāsyāśabdo vā, āgneyādīni tāni. nanv amāvāsyāśabdakānāṃ naiva phalaṃ śrūyate. ucyate, pṛthaktve samudāyayor niveśa etayor abhidhānayoḥ, paurṇamāsīti cāmāvāsyā iti ca, triṣv āgneyādiṣu yaḥ samudāyaḥ, tatra paurṇamāsīśabdaḥ, itareṣv amāvāsyāśabdaḥ.
kathaṃ paurṇamāsy amāvāsyeti ca dviśabdaḥ śrūyate? dvyarthavad vyapadeśāc ca. kathaṃ tad vyapadeśaḥ? dvivacannirdeśāt, darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iti, ekārthau ca darśāmāvāsyāśabdau. katham? darśo vā etayoḥ pūrvaḥ, pūrṇamāsa uttaras tayor atha yat pūrṇamāsaṃ pūrvam ārabhate tad ayathāpūrvaṃ prakriyate, darśapūrṇamāsam ārabhamāṇaḥ sarasvatyai caruṃ nirvapet, sarasvate dvādaśakapālam amāvāsyā vai sarasvatī, pūrṇamāsaḥ sarasvān. ubhāv etau yathāpūrvaṃ kalpayitvārabhata ṛddhyai ṛdhnoty evārtho mithunatvāyeti{*4/429*}. tatra darśaśabdena prakṛtyāmāvāsyāśabdena bruvann ekārthatāṃ darśayati. śakyate ca candrasyādarśanenāmāvāsyā darśa iti lakṣayitum, yathā cakṣuṣor abhāve sati cakṣuṣmān iti cakṣurbhyāṃ lakṣyate. [533]{*4/430*} etasmād vyapadeśāc ca śrutitaś ca loke śravaṇād{*4/431*} ekārthatām evādhyavasyāmaḥ. tat punar mukhyalakṣaṇam, yat phalavattvam, yad anyat tat saṃnidhau śrūyate, tat tad aṅgam. katham? itikartavyatākāṅkṣasya saṃnidhau śrūyamāṇam, itikartavyatāviśeṣaṇatvena paripūraṇasamarthaṃ tadaṅgaṃ bhavitum arhati. akalpyamāne vākyaśeṣe phalaṃ kalpayitavyaṃ syād iti.
āha, nanu darśapūrṇamāsaphalam evātrānuṣajyate. ucyate, śakyam anuṣaktum, kiṃ tu darśapūrṇamāsavākyaṃ sākāṅkṣam eva syāt. anyāsyetikartavyatāśrutā kalpyeta. eṣām api prayājādīnām anyā kalpyeta. etad itikartavyatāvagamyamānotsṛjyeta, tenāṅgatvam, kāraṇaṃ bhāgīti. eṣāṃ anyena phalena saṃbandho 'śrutaḥ. tasmān na sarvāṇi samapradhānāni, āghārādīni guṇakarmāṇīti.
children.translated_text:
The word <s>tu</s> ('but') marks the reversal of the [prima facie] position. It was said that all [offerings] are equally primary. This is not so — the rites designated by the words <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> are the primary actions. Why? Because of the connection with fruit — the fruit is heard from [the rites] designated by the words <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' But which are designated by the words <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>? Those in whose statement the word <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> (full-moon day) or the word <s>Amāvāsyā</s> (new-moon day) [occurs] — those are the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings]. But the fruit of those designated by the word <s>Amāvāsyā</s> is not at all heard [separately]. We reply: when [the two designations] are separate, the placement of these two designations — <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> and <s>Amāvāsyā</s> — [is as follows]: the word <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> [refers to] the aggregate of the three [offerings] beginning with the <s>Āgneya</s>; the word <s>Amāvāsyā</s> [refers to] the others.
How is the dual word <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> heard? Because of the descriptive statement (<s>vyapadeśa</s>) indicating two meanings. How is that a descriptive statement? Because of the dual-number designation: '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyām</s>' (by means of the <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s>) — and the words <s>darśa</s> and <s>amāvāsyā</s> have the same meaning. How? 'The <s>Darśa</s> is indeed the first of these two; the <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> is the latter. Now, if one begins with the <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> first, that is done out of order. One who begins the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> should offer a <s>caru</s> to <s>Sarasvatī</s> and a twelve-potsherd [cake] to <s>Sarasvat</s>. <s>Amāvāsyā</s> is indeed <s>Sarasvatī</s>; <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> is <s>Sarasvat</s>. Having arranged both in proper order, he begins — for prosperity; he indeed prospers, for the sake of pairing.' There, by using the word <s>Darśa</s> as the natural [equivalent of] the word <s>Amāvāsyā</s>, [the text] shows their identity of meaning. And it is possible to designate [the new-moon day as] <s>Darśa</s> by the non-visibility of the moon — just as one with eyes is designated by [reference to] the eyes when there is absence of the eyes [in another]. [533] From this descriptive statement and from the [Vedic] text — from hearing [it] in the world — we conclude the identity of meaning. Moreover, the principal characteristic is fruitfulness; what is other [than the principal] and is heard in proximity — that is its subsidiary. How? What is heard in proximity to one that expects [the specification] 'how is it to be performed' — being capable of completing [the sentence] as a specification of the procedure — that deserves to be its subsidiary. Otherwise, if the remainder-of-sentence [relationship] is not construed, the fruit would have to be construed [separately].
[The objector] says: but is not the fruit of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> itself attached here? We reply: it can be attached; but then the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sentence would remain expectant [of completion]. Another procedure would have to be construed for it. And for these <s>prayājas</s> and such too, another [procedure] would have to be construed. [But] this [naturally] understood procedure would be abandoned — hence their subsidiary status. The reason is 'sharing' (<s>bhāga</s>). And the connection of these with another fruit is not heard. Therefore not all are equally primary — the <s>āghāras</s> and such are subsidiary rites.

children.text: guṇāś ca nāmasaṃyuktā vidhīyante nāṅgeṣūpapadyante // MS_4,4.35 //
children.translated_text: And subsidiaries connected with specific names are enjoined [only in those specific contexts]; they are not applicable in [all] subsidiary [elements]. // MS_4,4.35 //

children.text: nāmaviśeṣasaṃyuktāś ca guṇaviśeṣā vidhīyante, yathā - caturhotrā pūrṇamāsīm{*4/432*} abhimṛśet, pañcahotrāmāvāsyām iti, sarveṣu pradhāneṣu, asmin samudāye caturhotrā, asmin pañcahotreti vibhāgāvijñānāc cedaṃ nopapadyeta. bhavati caivaṃlakṣaṇakaṃ guṇavidhānam. tasmād asmatpakṣa eveti. api cāṅgatvenādhārādīnāṃ saṃstutir upapannā bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: Specific subsidiary [elements] connected with specific names are enjoined — as: 'One should touch the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> with a four-priest [formula], and the <s>Amāvāsyā</s> with a five-priest [formula]' — in all the principal [rites]. If there were no knowledge of the distinction [between the aggregates] — 'in this aggregate [there are] four-priest [formulas], in this [there are] five-priest [formulas]' — this would not be possible. But such an injunction of subsidiary [specifics] does exist. Therefore our position alone [is correct]. Moreover, the praise of the <s>āghāras</s> and such as subsidiaries will be appropriate.

children.text: tulyā ca kāraṇaśrutir anyair aṅgāṅgisaṃbandhaḥ // MS_4,4.36 //
children.translated_text: And the Vedic statement [regarding subsidiary-praise] is equal [for both]; [the distinction is through] the principal-subsidiary relationship with others. // MS_4,4.36 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, āgneyādīnām apy aṅgatvena saṃstutir aṅgatvaṃ khyāpayed iti. tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'the praise of the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings] too as subsidiaries should make them subsidiaries' — that must be refuted.

children.text: utpattāv abhisaṃbandhas tasmād aṅgopadeśaḥ syāt // MS_4,4.37 //
children.translated_text: The connection at origination [determines the relationship]; therefore there should be an indication of subsidiary status. // MS_4,4.37 //

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ, pradhānānām{*4/434*} apy eṣāṃ satām utpattyapekṣā{*4/435*} śirādistutir abhiviṣyatīti{*4/436*}. jāyamānasya{*4/437*} hi puruṣasyāgre śiro jāyate, madhye madhyam, paścāt pādau, evam āgneyo 'grataḥ, upāṃśuyājo madhye, agnīṣomīyaḥ paścād iti. etasmāt sāmānyādoṣā stutir iti.
children.translated_text: This is not a fault — the praise as 'head' etc. [is made] with reference to the order of origination, even for these that are principal. For just as when a person is being born, the head is born first, the middle [part] in the middle, and the feet at the end — so the <s>Āgneya</s> [comes] first, the <s>Upāṃśuyāga</s> in the middle, and the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> at the end. From this similarity [of order], the praise is without fault.

children.translated_text: And thus, the observation of [serving] another purpose [is explained]. // MS_4,4.38 //

children.text: caturdaśa pūrṇamāsyām āhutayo hūyante, trayodaśāmāvāsyāyām iti, itarathā na caturdaśa paurṇamāsyām āhutayo bhaveyuḥ, na vāmāvāsyāyāṃ trayodaśeti. tasmād āgneyādīni pradhānāni, āghārādīny aṅgānīti siddham.
children.translated_text: Fourteen oblations are offered on the full-moon day, thirteen on the new-moon day — otherwise there would not be fourteen oblations on the full-moon day, nor thirteen on the new-moon day. Therefore the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings] are primary, and the <s>āghāras</s> and such are subsidiaries — this is established.

children.text: jyotiṣṭome tulyāny aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam // MS_4,4.39 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, [all rites] would be equal, for the reason is undifferentiated. // MS_4,4.39 //

children.text: asti jyotiṣṭomaḥ, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeteti. [535]{*4/438*} tatra dīkṣaṇīyādayaś ca yāgā vidyante, sautye cāhani somayāgaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim atra yāgamātra pradhānam, uta somayāga iti. kiṃ prāptam? jyotiṣṭome tulyāni sarvāṇi bhaveyuḥ. kutaḥ? aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam, yāgāt phalaṃ śrūyate, sarve cāmī yāgāḥ, phalavac ca pradhānam. tasmāj jyotiṣṭome sarve yāgāḥ pradhānam iti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' [535] There, both the <s>dīkṣaṇīya</s> (consecration offering) and other sacrifices exist, and on the <s>Soma</s>-pressing day there is the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice. There a doubt [arises]: is every sacrifice here primary, or is the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice [alone primary]? What is the prima facie view? In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, all should be equal. Why? Because the reason is undifferentiated — the fruit is heard from sacrifice, and all of these are sacrifices, and what has fruit is primary. Therefore in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, all sacrifices are primary.

children.text: guṇānāṃ tūtpattivākyena saṃbandhāt kāraṇaśrutis tasmāt somaḥ pradhānaṃ syāt // MS_4,4.40 //
children.translated_text: But because of the connection of the subsidiaries with the origination-sentence, through the Vedic statement — therefore <s>Soma</s> should be the primary [rite]. // MS_4,4.40 //

children.text:
guṇānāṃ tūtpattivākyena saṃbandho bhavati. keṣāṃ guṇānām? jyotiṣāṃ stomānām. katamenotpattivākyena saṃbandho bhavati? jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeteti{*4/439*}, jyotiṣṭomād yāgāt svargaḥ śrūyate, na yāgamātrāt. yatra ca jyotīṃṣi stomāḥ, sa jyotiṣṭomaḥ. kasya jyotīṃṣi stomāḥ? stomayāgasyeti brūmaḥ. evaṃ hy āmnāyate, katamāni vaitāni jyotīṃṣi, ya ete tasya stomāḥ, trivṛt pañcadaśasaptadaśaikaviṃśā etāni vā jyotīṃṣi. tāny etasya stomā iti{*4/440*}, somayāgasya stomā aṅgam, samabhivyāhārāt, grahaṃ vā gṛhītvā camasaṃ vonnīya stotram upākarotīti, te ca stomās trivṛdādayaḥ. katham? trivṛd bahiṣpavamānam, pañcadaśāny ājyānītyevamādibhiḥ śravaṇaiḥ.
tasmāt trivṛdādistomakaḥ somayāgaḥ, sa jyotiṣṭoma iti. yaś ca jyotiṣṭomas tataḥ phalam, yataś ca phalaṃ tad eva pradhānam iti. kathaṃ punas trivṛdādayo jyotīṃṣi? ucyate, bhavantu vā jyotīṃṣi, mā vā bhūvan, jyotiḥśabdena tāvad uktāni. [536]{*4/441*} vacanamātreṇāpi śabdo bhavati, viśeṣato lakṣaṇāyām. api ca dyotater vā dīptikarmaṇo jyotayater vā{*4/442*} jyotiḥśabdaṃ labhante. dyotyate{*4/443*} hi taiḥ śabdaiḥ, dyotayantīti vā stutyām{*4/444*}. tasmāt somayāgo jyotiṣṭomaḥ. sa ca pradhānam, guṇabhūtā dīkṣaṇīyādaya iti.
children.translated_text:
But the subsidiaries have a connection with the origination-sentence. Which subsidiaries? The <s>Jyotis</s> (lights) [and] the <s>Stomas</s> (hymn-patterns). With which origination-sentence do they have connection? 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, heaven is heard, not from mere sacrifice [in general]. And that in which the <s>Jyotis</s> lights are the <s>Stomas</s> — that is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Of what are the <s>Jyotis</s> lights the <s>Stomas</s>? Of the <s>Stoma</s>-sacrifice, we say. For thus it is recorded: 'Which are those <s>Jyotis</s> lights? Those that are its <s>Stomas</s> — the <s>Trivṛt</s>, the <s>Pañcadaśa</s>, the <s>Saptadaśa</s>, the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> — these are the <s>Jyotis</s> lights. These are its <s>Stomas</s>.' The <s>Stomas</s> are subsidiaries of the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, because of their co-occurrence [in the same statement] — 'having taken the <s>graha</s> (Soma cup), having raised the <s>camasa</s> (goblet), he commences the hymn of praise (<s>stotra</s>)' — and those <s>Stomas</s> are the <s>Trivṛt</s> and others. How? Through such [Vedic] statements as 'the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is [set to] the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma],' 'the <s>Ājyas</s> are [set to] the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> [stoma],' and so forth.
Therefore, the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice having the <s>Trivṛt</s> and other <s>Stomas</s> is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. And the fruit [comes] from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; and what has fruit — that alone is primary. But how are the <s>Trivṛt</s> and others <s>Jyotis</s> (lights)? We reply: whether they are [truly] lights or not, they are designated by the word <s>Jyotis</s>. [536] Even by mere usage a word functions, especially in figurative expression. Moreover, from the root <s>dyut</s> ('to shine') denoting illumination, or from [the causative] <s>jyotay</s>, they obtain the word <s>Jyotis</s>. For [the sacrifice] is illuminated by those <s>Stomas</s>; or [they are called lights] because they illuminate — in the sense of praise. Therefore the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. And it is primary, while the <s>dīkṣaṇīya</s> and other [offerings] are subsidiaries.

children.text: śiro vā etad yajñasya yad dīkṣaṇīyetyevamādi ca liṅgaṃ dṛśyate. tathā guṇāś ca jyotiṣṭomavikāre dīkṣaṇīyādayo dṛśyante, caturviṃśati mānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ dīkṣaṇīyāyāṃ dadyāt, prāpaṇīyāyāṃ dve caturviṃśatimāna iti, tulyatve na pravartayiṣyante dīkṣaṇīyādayaḥ. tasmād api somayāgaḥ pradhānam iti.
children.translated_text: The indicatory mark 'the <s>dīkṣaṇīya</s> is indeed the head of the sacrifice' and such is also seen. Likewise, in modifications of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the <s>dīkṣaṇīya</s> and other [offerings] are seen as subsidiaries — 'He should give twenty-four [measures of] gold at the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>, [and] two twenty-four-measure [amounts] at the <s>prāpaṇīyā</s>' — if [they were] equal, the <s>dīkṣaṇīya</s> and such would not be varied [separately]. Therefore too, the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice is the primary [rite].

children.text: śrutilakṣaṇam ānupūrvyaṃ tatpramāṇatvāt//5.1.1//
children.translated_text: The sequence [of ritual acts] is characterized by the [Vedic] text, because of its being the authoritative measure. // MS_5,1.1 //

children.text:
caturthe 'dhyāye prayojakāprayojakalakṣaṇaṃ vṛttam, tan na prasmartavyam. ihedānīṃ kramaniyamalakṣaṇam ucyate, tac chrutyarthapāṭhapravṛttikāṇḍamukhyair vakṣyate, śrutyādīnāṃ ca balābalam. āditas tu śrutikramaś cintyate. kiṃ yathāśruti padārthānāṃ krama āstheyaḥ, utāniyameneti. kiṃ prāptam? ekatvāt kartuḥ, anekatvāc ca padārthānām, avaśyaṃ bhāvini krame lāghavāt prayogaprāśubhāvāc cāniyama ity evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ.
śrutilakṣaṇam ānupūrvyaṃ tatpramāṇatvād iti. śrutir grahaṇam{*4/446*} akṣarāṇām, tan nimittaṃ yasya kramasya, sa sādhuḥ kramaḥ. śrutipramāṇakā hi vaidikā arthāḥ, naiṣām anyat pramāṇam astīty{*4/447*} uktam. kim ihodāharaṇam? satre dīkṣākramaḥ{*4/448*}, ya ṛtvijas te yajamānā ity{*4/449*} uktvā, teṣāṃ dīkṣākramaṃ vidhatte, adhvyaryur gṛhapatiṃ dīkṣayitvā brahmāṇaṃ dīkṣayati, tata udgātāram, tato hotāram, tatas taṃ pratiprasthātā dīkṣayitvārdhino dīkṣayati, brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, prastotāram udgātuḥ, maitrāvaruṇaṃ hotuḥ, tatas taṃ neṣṭā{*4/450*} dīkṣayitvā tṛtīyino dīkṣayati, āgnīdhraṃ brahmaṇaḥ, pratihartāram udgātuḥ, acchāvākaṃ hotuḥ, tatas tam unnetā dīkṣayitvā padino{*4/451*} dīkṣayati, potāraṃ [538]{*4/452*} brahmaṇaḥ, subrahmaṇyam udgātuḥ, grāvastutaṃ hotuḥ, tatas tam anyo brāhmaṇo dīkṣayati, brahmacārī vācāryapreṣita iti. aniyamena kramaḥ kartavyaḥ, yathā pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. yathā tarhi siddhāntaḥ, eṣa eva kramaḥ kartavya iti.
tatrāha, anyāyyaṃ śrutivacanam iti. ucyate, kim ayaṃ{*4/453*} na sādhuḥ? na, na sādhur iti brūmaḥ. nyāyyaṃ tarhi. na brūmaḥ, na sādhuḥ krama iti. kiṃ tarhi? uktasya punarvacanam anyāyyām iti. ucyate, sādhor vacanaṃ bahuśo 'py ucyamānaṃ nyāyyam eva. asādhos tu sakṛd apy anyāyyam. āha, sakṛdvacanena jñātasya punarvacane na prayojanam astīti. ucyate, bhavaty aprasmaraṇam{*4/454*} api prayojanam ity uktam. vṛttikāreṇa tat kāryam iti cet. sūtrakārasyāpy aviśeṣo vṛttikāreṇa.
athavā - arthāntaram evedam, tatra hy anya eva saṃśayo vicāro nirṇayaś ca, śrutipramāṇako dharmaḥ, anyapramāṇaka iti saṃśayaḥ. pratyakṣādīnām adhigamya nimittatvān na tatpramāṇakaḥ, atīndriyatvāc codanālakṣaṇa iti vicāraḥ. codanālakṣaṇa eveti nirṇayaḥ. iha tu siddhe tatprāmāṇye vyavahārakramasya{*4/455*} sādhutvāvadhāraṇam.
athavā - śrutivicāro{*4/456*} 'yam. kiṃ padārthāḥ kartavyā iti vidhānam, kiṃ vā kramo vidhīyata iti. anekārthavidhānānupapatteḥ krame{*4/457*} 'nuvādaḥ padārthānāṃ{*4/458*} vidhiḥ. avadānavākyeṣv iva, padārthavidhānaṃ śrutyā, kramavidhānaṃ vākyena, tasmān na kramo vidhīyata iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. nanv avadānavākyeṣu kramo vidhīyate. satyaṃ vidhīyate, pāṭhena, na śrutyā, ya{*4/459*} ṛtvijas te [539]{*4/460*} yajamānā iti tu, dīkṣāyāḥ prāptatvāt, kramavidhānārthā śrutir iti siddhāntaḥ. tasmād apunaruktam iti.
children.translated_text:
In the fourth chapter, the characteristics of what is motivating and non-motivating have been discussed — that should not be forgotten. Now, the characteristics of the fixed order (<s>kramaniyama</s>) are being stated; these will be set forth by the principal [means of determining order, namely] the [Vedic] statement (<s>śruti</s>), meaning (<s>artha</s>), recitation-order (<s>pāṭha</s>), custom (<s>pravṛtti</s>), and section (<s>kāṇḍa</s>); and the relative strength of the [Vedic] statement and the others [will also be discussed]. First, however, the order [based on] the [Vedic] statement is considered. Should the order of the ritual elements be maintained as per the [Vedic] statement, or is there no fixed rule? What is the prima facie view? Because the agent is one and the ritual elements are many, and since sequence is inevitable, there is no fixed rule, owing to economy and the expeditiousness of performance. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say:
The sequence is characterized by the [Vedic] statement, because that is the valid authority. The [Vedic] statement (<s>śruti</s>) is the apprehension of the syllables [of the Veda]; the sequence that is determined by that is the correct sequence. For Vedic meanings have the [Vedic] statement as their authority — no other authority for them exists, as has been stated [in MS 1.1.2]. What is the example here? The order of consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) in a <s>sattra</s> (communal sacrifice). Having declared 'those who are the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests), they are the sacrificers,' it prescribes their order of consecration: the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, having consecrated the <s>Gṛhapati</s> (householder), consecrates the <s>Brahmā</s> (Brahman priest); then the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (Sāman chanter); then the <s>Hotṛ</s> (reciter). Then the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>, having consecrated him [the Hotṛ], consecrates the 'half-[share] priests' (<s>ardhinas</s>): the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> of the <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Prastotṛ</s> of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, having consecrated him, consecrates the 'third-[share] priests' (<s>tṛtīyinas</s>): the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> of the <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Acchāvāka</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Unnetṛ</s>, having consecrated him, consecrates the 'foot-[share] priests' (<s>padinas</s>): the <s>Potṛ</s> of the <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Grāvastut</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then another <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> consecrates him — a <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) sent by the teacher. [The objector says:] the order should be performed without fixed rule, as per the former view. [The reply:] according to the established conclusion, this very order should be performed.
To this, [the objector] says: the [Vedic] statement is unnecessary. We reply: why is this [order] not correct? [The objector:] no, we do not say that the order is not correct. [We reply:] then it is proper. [The objector:] we do not say [that]. What then? [We say:] the re-statement of what has been stated is unnecessary. We reply: the statement of what is correct, even when stated many times, is proper. But a single statement of what is incorrect is improper. [The objector] says: there is no purpose in re-stating what has been known from a single statement. We reply: non-forgetting (<s>aprasmaraṇa</s>) too can serve as a purpose — as has been stated. [The objector says:] that should be the task of the commentator. [We reply:] there is no difference between the sūtra-author and the commentator [in this respect].
Alternatively — this is indeed a different topic. For there, the doubt, investigation, and conclusion are entirely different: 'Is <s>dharma</s> authoritative through the [Vedic] statement, or through another authority?' — this is the doubt. 'Since perception and the like, having their grounds ascertained, cannot serve as authority for it, and since [dharma] is beyond the senses, it is characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>)' — this is the investigation. 'It is indeed characterized by injunction alone' — this is the conclusion. But here, given that the authority [of the Vedic statement] is established, the ascertainment of the correctness of the conventional order is [the topic].
Alternatively — this is an investigation regarding the [Vedic] statement. [The question is:] does the [Vedic] statement prescribe the ritual elements as 'to be performed,' or does it prescribe their order? Since a single [expression] cannot prescribe multiple meanings, the order is a restatement, and the ritual elements are what is prescribed. As in statements of distribution, the prescription of ritual elements is by the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>), while the prescription of order is by the sentence (<s>vākya</s>). Therefore, the order is not prescribed — this is the prima facie view. But in statements of distribution, the order is prescribed — by the recitation-order (<s>pāṭha</s>), not by the [Vedic] word. But in 'those who are the priests, they are the sacrificers,' since the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) is [already] obtained, the [Vedic] statement is for the purpose of prescribing the order — this is the established conclusion. Therefore it is not a repetition.

children.text: arthāc ca//5.1.2//
children.translated_text: And because of the meaning. // MS_5,1.2 //

children.text:
kim eṣa evotsargaḥ sarvatra śrutivaśenaiva bhavitum arhatīti. uktaṃ hi, codanālakṣṇo 'rtho dharma iti{*4/461*}.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, arthāc ca sāmarthyāc ca{*4/462*} kramo vidhīyata iti, guṇabhūto hi padārthānāṃ kramo bhavati, yaś ca yasya nirvartyamānasyopakaroti, sa tasya guṇabhūtaḥ. yasmiṃś cāśrīyamāṇe padārtha eva na saṃpadyate, na sa guṇabhūtaḥ, vināpi tena, na vaiguṇyam. evaṃ pratyakṣaḥ kramasya guṇabhāvo yatra, tatrārthena sa evāśrayitavyaḥ, yathā jāte varaṃ dadāti, jātam añjalinā gṛhṇāti, jātam abhiprāṇitīti, arthāt pūrvam abhiprāṇitavyam, tato 'ñjalinā grahītavyaḥ, tato varo deya iti. tathā vimokaḥ pūrvam āmnātaḥ, paścāt tadyogaḥ, arthād viparītaḥ kāryaḥ. yājyānuvākye tu viparyayeṇāmnāte, viparyayeṇa kartavye. nātra pāṭhakramo mīyate{*4/463*}. yato devatopalakṣaṇārthānuvākyā, pradānārthā yājyā. agnihotraṃ juhotīti pūrvam āmnātam. odanaṃ pacatīti paścāt. asaṃbhavāt pūrvam odanaḥ paktavyaḥ. praiṣapraiṣārtho tu viparyayeṇāmnātau, tau ca viparyayeṇa kartavyau.
children.translated_text:
But should this alone be the general rule — that [the order] should always be determined by the [Vedic] statement alone? For it has been stated: '<s>Dharma</s> is characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>).'
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: the order is prescribed also by the meaning (<s>artha</s>), i.e., by logical capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). For the order is subordinate to the ritual elements, and whatever assists something being accomplished is subordinate to it. And that whose non-observance would make the ritual element itself impossible is not [merely] subordinate — even without it, there would be no deficiency. Thus, where the subordination of the order is directly perceived, there the very same [order] should be relied upon through the meaning. For example: 'When [the child] is born, he gives a boon; when born, he receives [it] with cupped hands; when born, he breathes upon [it]' — from the meaning, first one should breathe upon [the child], then receive [it] with cupped hands, then give a boon. Likewise, the releasing [of the animal] is stated first, and the yoking [of the substitute] afterward, but from the meaning, the opposite should be done. But the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> [verses], though stated in reverse order, should be performed in reverse order — here the recitation-order is not measured [as authoritative]. Since the <s>anuvākyā</s> serves to indicate the deity, [it comes first]; the <s>yājyā</s> is for the purpose of offering. 'He offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>' is stated first, and 'He cooks the rice' afterward — [but] since [cooking] is impossible [after offering], the rice must be cooked first. The <s>praiṣa</s> (directive) and the object of the <s>praiṣa</s>, though stated in reverse order, should be performed in reverse order.

children.text: aniyamo 'nyatra//5.1.3//
children.translated_text: There is no fixed rule in other [cases]. // MS_5,1.3 //

children.text: asmin viṣaye kramasya niyamo nāsti, yathā darśapūrṇamāsayor yājamānānāṃ prayājānumantraṇādīnāṃ nānāśākhāntarasamāmnātānāṃ vasantam ṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmītyevamādīnām{*4/465*}, eko mametyevamādīnāṃ{*4/466*} ca.
children.translated_text: In this domain, there is no fixed rule for the order — as in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, the mantras accompanying the sacrificer's [rites] such as the <s>prayāja</s>-invocations and the like, which are recorded in various [Vedic] branches — such as 'I gratify the seasons, beginning with spring' and the like, and 'one is mine' and the like.

NOTES:
[{4/465: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 1.6.2.3}]
[{4/466: <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.5.4.11}]

children.text: krameṇa vā niyamyeta kratvekatve tadguṇatvāt//5.1.4//
children.translated_text: Or it would be restricted by the order, when there is a single ritual act, because of [the elements'] being subordinate to that. // MS_5,1.4 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayor āmnātam, samidho yajati, tanūnapātaṃ yajati, iḍo yajati, barhir yajati, svāhākāraṃ yajatīti{*4/467*}. tatra saṃśayaḥ, kim aniyatenaiva krameṇaiṣām anuṣṭhānam, uta yaḥ pāṭhakramaḥ sa eva niyamyeteti. kiṃ prāptam? niyamakāriṇaḥ śāstrasyābhāvād aniyama iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, krameṇaiva niyamyetaikasmin kratāv iti. kutaḥ? tadguṇatvāt. tadguṇatvaṃ hi gamyate padārthānām, yathā - snāyāt, anulimpet, bhuñjīteti ca krameṇānuṣṭhānam avagamyate, vākyāt padārthānām. yathā cādṛṣṭārtheṣūpadiśyamāneṣu, kaścid brūyāt, devāya dhūpo deyaḥ, puṣpāṇy avakaritavyāni candanenānuleptavya upahāro 'smā upahartavyaḥ, evaṃ kṛte devas tuṣyatīti. tam anyaḥ pratibrūte, naitad evam, na prathamaṃ dhūpo dātavyaḥ, prathamaṃ puṣpāṇy avakaritavyānīti. evaṃ manyate, dhūpadānasya prāthamyam anenoktam iti. tasmād vācanika eṣām eṣa krama iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is recorded: 'He worships the kindling-sticks (<s>samidhs</s>); he worships <s>Tanūnapāt</s>; he worships <s>Iḍā</s>; he worships the sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>); he worships the <s>Svāhākāra</s> (exclamation <s>Svāhā</s>).' There a doubt [arises]: should the performance of these be in an unrestricted order, or should the recitation-order be the fixed rule? What is the prima facie view? Because of the absence of a scripture that mandates a fixed rule, there is no fixed rule.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: it should be restricted by the order itself in a single ritual act. Why? Because of [the elements'] being subordinate to that [ritual act]. For the subordination of the ritual elements is understood — just as 'he should bathe, anoint [himself], and eat,' the performance in [that] order is understood from the sentence's [implication regarding] the ritual elements. And just as when one instructs about things for an unseen purpose, someone might say: 'Incense should be offered to the deity, flowers should be scattered, sandalwood paste should be applied, and an offering should be presented. When this is done, the deity is pleased.' If another responds: 'This is not so — incense should not be offered first; flowers should be scattered first' — he [thereby] understands that the primacy of incense-offering was stated by the [first speaker]. Therefore, the order of these [ritual elements] is based on the recitation.

children.text: aśābda iti cet, syād vākyaśabdatvāt//5.1.5//
children.translated_text: If [one objects that the order is] without [its own] word — it would [still be valid], because of being the word of the sentence. // MS_5,1.5 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, athaivaṃ gamyamāne 'śabda eva kramaḥ. katham? padārthapūrvako vākyārthaḥ, padebhyaś ca padārthā evāvagamyante, na kramaḥ. syād etad evam, yadi padārthānāṃ{*4/469*} samūhasya śravaṇaṃ pratyāyakam arthasya syāt, na tu samudāyaḥ pratyāyakaḥ, ity uktaṃ tadbhūtānāṃ kriyārthena samāmnāya ity{*4/470*} atra. tasmāt kramasya vācakaśabdābhāvād vyāmoha eṣa kramo 'vagamyate. evaṃ cāpūrvāsattir anugrahīṣyate, itarathā sāpi viprakṛṣyeta ghaṭīyantra iva. darśayiṣyati ca, hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyati, atha jihvāyāḥ, atha vakṣasa iti. yadi niyāmakaḥ pāṭhakramaḥ, tato na vidhātavyam etat, niyāmake hi pāṭhakrame pāṭhakramād eva prāpnuyāt.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — then when this [order] is understood, the order is indeed without [its own] word. How? The sentence-meaning is preceded by the word-meanings, and from the words, only the word-meanings are understood, not the order. This would be so if the hearing of the aggregate of word-meanings were what conveys the meaning. But it is not the aggregate that conveys [the meaning] — as has been stated: 'The enumeration of those that are its constituents is for the purpose of [establishing] action' [cf. MS 1.1.25]. Therefore, since there is no word that expresses the order, this understanding of the order is a delusion. And if so, the principle of <s>apūrva</s> ('unprecedented') [sequences] will be supported; otherwise, that too would be displaced, like a waterwheel. And it will be demonstrated [later]: 'He cuts from the front of the heart, then from the tongue, then from the chest.' If the recitation-order were the restricting [factor], then this [explicit statement] would not need to be prescribed — for if the recitation-order were the restricting [factor], it would already follow from the recitation-order itself.

NOTES:
[{4/469: E1 (footnote), E2: <s>padānāṃ</s>}]
[{4/470: Cf. MS 1.1.25}]

children.text: arthakṛte vānumānaṃ syāt, kratvekatve parārthatvāt svena tv arthena saṃbandhaḥ, tasmāt svaśabdam ucyeta//5.1.6//
children.translated_text: Or, being produced by the meaning, there would be an inference; when there is a single ritual act, because of serving another's purpose, the connection is through its own meaning; therefore it should be stated by its own word. // MS_5,1.6 //

children.text: ekasmin kratāv ekatvāt kratuḥ, anekasmin padārthe 'rthakṛtatvāt kramasya, tatraiṣa eva kramo niyamyetānumānena. kutaḥ? parārthatvād vedasya, parārtho hi vedo yad yad anena śakyate kartum, tasmai tasmai prayojanāyaiṣa samāmnāyate. śakyate cānena padārtho vidhātum, śakyate ca kriyākāle pratipattum. tasmād vedaḥ padārthāṃś ca vidhātum upādeyaḥ, kriyākāle ca pratipattum. na gamyate{*4/471*} viśeṣaḥ, vidhātum ayaṃ samāmnāyate, na pratipattum iti. agamyamāne viśeṣa ubhayārtham upādīyata [542]{*4/472*} iti gamyate. pratipattuṃ cānena krameṇa śakyate, nānyena. ata eva ca kṛtvā pāṭhakramāpacāre, vinaṣṭa ity ucyate, itarathā hi yad yasya prayojanam, tasmin nirvartamāna eva kiṃ naṣṭaṃ syāt. adṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta, tac cānyāyyaṃ dṛṣṭe sati. tasmāt svaśabdaḥ kramaḥ, ya eva padārthānāṃ vācakaḥ śabdaḥ, sa eva kramasyāpi.
children.translated_text: In a single ritual act, because of the unity of the ritual act, and because of the order being produced by the many ritual elements — in that [case], this very order would be restricted by inference. Why? Because of the <s>Veda</s>'s being for another's purpose. For the <s>Veda</s> serves another's purpose — whatever can be accomplished by it, for each such purpose it is recorded. And by it, a ritual element can be prescribed, and the order can be understood at the time of performance. Therefore the <s>Veda</s> is to be relied upon both for prescribing ritual elements and for understanding [the order] at the time of performance. No distinction is understood — [such as] 'it is recorded for the purpose of prescribing, not for the purpose of understanding [the order].' When no distinction is understood, it is understood that it is relied upon for both purposes. And by this [recitation] order alone can [the performance] be understood, not by another. And precisely because of this, when there is a deviation from the recitation-order, it is said to be 'lost' (<s>vinaṣṭa</s>) — for otherwise, what would be lost when a thing is being accomplished in whatever [order] serves its purpose? An unseen [purpose] would have to be posited, and that is improper when a visible [purpose] exists. Therefore, the order has its own word — the very word that expresses the ritual elements also [expresses] the order.

children.text: tathā cānyārthadarśanam//5.1.7//
children.translated_text: And thus, the observation for another purpose [confirms this]. // MS_5,1.7 //

children.text: evaṃ cānyārthaṃ darśayati, vyatyastam ṛtavyā upadadhāti{*4/473*}. vyatyastaṃ ṣoḍaśinaṃ śaṃsati{*4/474*}. āśvino daśamo gṛhyate, taṃ tṛtīyaṃ juhotīti. yady aniyamenopadhānaṃ śaṃsanaṃ ca, vyatyastavacanam anarthakaṃ syāt. na hi kathaṃcid avyatyāsa iti, tathāśvinasya tṛtīyasya homānuvādo nāvakalpyeta, yadi pāṭhakrameṇa niyama{*4/475*} iti. tathā, abhicaratā pratilomaṃ hotavyam, prāṇān evāsya pratīcaḥ pratiyautīti{*4/476*} kvacit pratilomaṃ vidadhad anulomaṃ darśayati, tad upapadyate, yadi pāṭhakrameṇa prayogaḥ. itarathā, sarvam anulomaṃ syāt, pratilomadarśanaṃ nopapadyeta. tathā caturthottamayoḥ pratisamānayatīty ukte sati, atihāyeḍo barhiḥ pratisamānayatīty ucyate, tena barhiṣaś caturthatāṃ darśayati, sā pāṭhakrame niyāmake 'vakalpate.
children.translated_text: And thus it shows the [same principle] for another purpose: 'He places the seasonal [bricks] in reverse order.' 'He recites the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> [hymn] in reverse order.' 'The <s>Āśvina</s> [cup] is taken as the tenth; he offers it as the third.' If the placement and recitation were without restriction, the statement about reversal would be purposeless. For [if there were no fixed order], there would be no [possibility of] non-reversal at all; likewise, the restatement of the <s>Āśvina</s>'s third-position offering would not be possible if there were no restriction based on the order of textual recitation. Similarly, 'One performing sorcery should offer in reverse order — he thereby strikes back his vital breaths' — by prescribing reverse order in some cases, it shows the normal order [elsewhere]. This is tenable if the performance follows the order of textual recitation. Otherwise, everything would be in normal order, and the indication of reverse order would not be possible. Likewise, when it is stated 'he brings together the fourth and the last,' and then 'passing beyond the <s>iḍā</s>, he brings the sacrificial grass together' — thereby it shows the fourth position of the sacrificial grass. This is possible when the textual order serves as the restricting [principle].

NOTES:
[{4/473: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.3.1.1}]
[{4/474: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 7.1.5.4}]
[{4/475: E2: <s>pāṭhakrameṇāniyama</s>}]
[{4/476: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.4.8.5}]

children.text: pravṛttyā tulyakālānāṃ guṇānāṃ tadupakramāt//5.1.8//
children.translated_text: For subsidiary elements that are simultaneous with the commencement, [their order is determined] by the commencement of that [principal rite]. // MS_5,1.8 //

children.text:
vājapeye saptadaśa prājāpatyān paśūn ālabhata iti śrūyate. teṣu paśuṣu codakaprāptāḥ prokṣaṇādayo dharmāḥ. tatra [543]{*4/477*} prathamaḥ padārtho yataḥ kutaścid ārabdhavyaḥ, dvitīyādiṣu bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ tata eva dvitīyo 'pi padārtha ārabdhavyaḥ, uta dvitīyādiṣv aniyama iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? niyamakāriṇaḥ śāstrasyābhāvād aniyama iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, yataḥ pūrva ārabdhaḥ, tata eva dvitīyādayo 'pi padārthā ārabdhavyā{*4/478*} iti. kuta etat? tadupakramāt, sarve hi padārthāḥ pradhānakālān na viprakraṣṭavyāḥ, pradhānaṃ hi cikīrṣitam, kṛtaṃ vā teṣāṃ{*4/479*} nimittam. sahavacanaṃ hi bhavati, padārthaiḥ saha pradhānaṃ kartavyam iti, bahupadārthasamāmnānāt tv avaśyaṃ bhāvī viprakarṣaḥ, tathāpi tu yāvadbhir nāvyavahitaḥ śakyaḥ padārthaḥ kartum, tāvadbhir vyavadhānam avaśyaṃ kartavyam, tato 'bhyadhikena{*4/480*} na vyavadhātavyam iti. yadi dvitīyaṃ padārtham anyata ārabheta, tato 'dhikair api vyavadadhyāt, tathā prayogavacanaṃ bādheta. nanu tathā sati kaścid alpair vyavahito bhaviṣyati. ucyate, anumatānāṃ vyavadhāyakānāṃ tyāgena kaścid abhyadhiko guṇo bhavatīti, tasmād yataḥ pūrvapadārtha ārabdhaḥ, tata evottara ārambhaṇīya iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Vājapeya</s> it is heard: 'He slaughters seventeen animals sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>.' For those animals, the rites such as sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like are obtained through injunction. There, the first item must be commenced from some [starting point]; regarding the second and subsequent ones, a doubt [arises]: should the second item too be commenced from the same [starting point], or is there no restriction for the second and subsequent ones? What is the prima facie view? Because of the absence of a scripture that creates a restriction, there is no restriction.
Given this prima facie view, we say: the second and subsequent items too should be commenced from the very [point] where the first was commenced. From what [reasoning] is this? Because of the commencement of that [principal rite] — for all the items should not be distanced from the time of the principal, since the principal is what is desired [to be performed], and either intended or already performed, it is the occasion for them. For there is a co-occurrence statement: 'The items should be performed together with the principal.' But because of the enumeration of many items, a separation is necessarily going to occur. Even so, one should intervene only with as many [items] as necessary when the item cannot be performed without such intervening; one should not intervene with more than that. If one were to commence the second item from a different [starting point], one might intervene with even more [items], and thus the statement about performance would be contradicted. [The objector says:] but if so, some [items] will have little intervention. We reply: by abandoning the permitted intervening [items], some additional subsidiary benefit arises. Therefore, the subsequent [item] should be commenced from the very [point] where the first item was commenced.
