children.text: sarvam iti cet//5.1.9//
children.translated_text: 'All [should be completed in one]' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_5,1.9 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, pradhānāviprakarṣeṇa prayogavacanānugraha iti, sarvaṃ tarhi guṇakāṇḍam ekasminn apavarjayitavyam, yathā sauryādiṣu.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that by not distancing [items] from the principal, the statement about performance is accommodated — then the entire subsidiary portion should be completed in a single [round], as in the <s>Saurya</s> and similar [rites].

children.text: nākṛtatvāt//5.1.10//
children.translated_text: No, because of [the resulting] non-performance. // MS_5,1.10 //

children.text: naitad evam, sahaprayoga eva hi nānuṣṭhitaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: This is not so, for the simultaneous performance itself would then not be accomplished.

children.text: kratvantaravad iti cet//5.1.11//
children.translated_text: 'As in other sacrifices' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_5,1.11 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, yathā kratvantareṣu sauryādiṣv iti, tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'as in other sacrifices such as the <s>Saurya</s> and the like' — that is to be refuted.

children.text: nāsamavāyāt//5.1.12//
children.translated_text: No, because of [their] non-inherence. // MS_5,1.12 //

children.text: na teṣām arthāt kramaḥ prāpnoti, yo niyamyeta. aṅgāśrayo hi niyamo bhavitum arhati, anaṅgasamāśrayasya{*4/482*} svayamaṅgatā kalpyeta.
children.translated_text: For those [rites], the sequence is not obtained by the nature of things, such that it would need to be restricted. A restriction should properly be based on subsidiaries; for something that shares no subsidiary relationship, subsidiary status would have to be artificially posited.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/482: E2: anaṅgasamāśritasya}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/482: E2: <s>anaṅgasamāśritasya</s>}]

children.text: sthānāc cotpattisaṃyogāt//5.1.13//
children.translated_text: And because of [the textual] position and the connection with origination. // MS_5,1.13 //

children.text: ekaviṃśenātirātreṇa prajākāmaṃ yājayet, trinavenaujaskāmam{*4/483*}, trayastriṃśena pratiṣṭhākāmam{*4/484*} ityevamādi śrūyate. tatrāgamena saṃkhyāpūraṇam iti vakṣyate{*4/485*}. tatrāgame kriyamāṇe, kim aniyamajakramāḥ{*4/486*} sarvā ṛca āgamayitavyāḥ, uta kāṇḍakramebhya iti{*4/487*}. kiṃ prāptam? aniyameneti. kutaḥ? atirātre triṇavādiśabdārthenaitāḥ prāpnuvanti, tatraitāsāṃ prāpnuvatīnāṃ pāṭhakramo nāstīti. evaṃ prāpta ucyate, yad āsāṃ samāmnāye sthānam, tenaitā atra niyamyante. yāḥ pūrvaṃ samāmnātāḥ, tāḥ pūrvam eva prayoktavyāḥ. ānupūrvyasya hi dṛṣṭam etat prayojanam, yad uttarasphuraṇaṃ{*4/488*} tad api cikīrṣitam eveti. trinavādiśabdair{*4/489*} atirātre yaugapadyenāsāṃ prāpteḥ pāṭhakramasyāviṣaya [545]{*4/490*} ity adhikaraṇāntaram iti bhavati matiḥ.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'He should have one desiring progeny sacrifice with the twenty-one[-versed] <s>Atirātra</s>; one desiring vigor, with the <s>Triṇava</s> [stoma]; one desiring a firm foundation, with the thirty-three[-versed stoma]' and so forth. There, it will be stated that the filling of the number is by augmentation (<s>āgama</s>). When augmentation is being carried out, should all the <s>ṛc</s> (verses) be augmented without any restriction of order, or according to the order of the <s>kāṇḍas</s> (sections)? What is the prima facie view? Without restriction. Why? Because these [verses] are obtained through the meaning of the words <s>Triṇava</s> and the like for the <s>Atirātra</s>, and for those [verses] so obtained there is no textual order [inherently]. Given this prima facie view, we say: they are restricted by their position in the collection (<s>samāmnāya</s>). Those that are recited first [in the collection] should be employed first. For this is the observed purpose of sequence: what is recalled later is also intended [to follow]. Since these [verses] are obtained simultaneously for the <s>Atirātra</s> through the words <s>Triṇava</s> and the like, the textual order has no [obvious] domain — [thus] this is a separate topic, in our opinion.

children.text: samāmnāyapāṭhakramād evātra niyama iti punaruktatā gamyata ity anyathā varṇyate -
children.translated_text: Since the restriction based on the textual order of the collection is understood to involve repetition, it is explained differently —

children.translated_text: And because of [the textual] position and the connection with origination. // MS_5,1.13 //

children.text: sādyaskre{*4/491*} śrūyate, saha paśūn ālabhata iti. tatraiṣo 'rthaḥ samadhigataḥ, savanīyakāle trayāṇām ālambha iti. athātra pāṭhakramāt, kim agnīṣomīyaḥ pūrvam ālabdhavyaḥ, uta sthānakramāt pūrvaṃ savanīya iti. kiṃ prāptam? pūrvam agnīṣomīya iti. kutaḥ? pāṭhakramāt. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, savanīyaḥ pūrvam, sthānāt. yadi pūrvam agnīṣomīyaḥ syāt, savanīyasthānaṃ vyāhanyeta. āśvinaṃ gṛhītvā trivṛtā yūpaṃ parivīyeti. nanv itaratrāpi pāṭhakramo bādhyeta. bādhyatām, tasya hi pratiṣedhārthaḥ sahaśabdaḥ samāmnātaḥ{*4/492*}, apratiṣiddhaṃ cāśvinagrahasthānam. tan na bādhitavyam.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sādyaskra</s> [sacrifice] it is heard: 'He slaughters the animals together.' There the following meaning has been understood: the slaughter of the three [animals takes place] at the time of the <s>savanīya</s> (pressing). Now here, based on the textual order, should the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> [animal] be slaughtered first, or based on positional order, the <s>savanīya</s> first? What is the prima facie view? The <s>Agniṣomīya</s> first. Why? Because of the textual order. Given this prima facie view, we say: the <s>savanīya</s> [is slaughtered] first, because of [its] position. If the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> were first, the position of the <s>savanīya</s> would be contradicted. 'Having taken the <s>Āśvina</s> [cup], he winds the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma] around the sacrificial post.' [The objector says:] but in the other [view] too, the textual order would be contradicted. [We reply:] let it be contradicted — for the word 'together' (<s>saha</s>) has been recorded for the purpose of negating that [textual order]; but the position of the <s>Āśvina</s> cup is not negated. That should not be contradicted.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/491: E1 (Fn.,K): sādyaskraḥ somayāgaviśeṣaḥ}*
*{4/492: E2: sahaśabdasamāmnātaḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/491: E1 (footnote, K): <s>sādyaskraḥ</s> — a particular kind of <s>Soma</s> sacrifice}]
[{4/492: E2: <s>sahaśabdasamāmnātaḥ</s>}]

children.text: mukhyakrameṇa vāṅgānāṃ tadarthatvāt//5.1.14//
children.translated_text: Or [the order is determined] by the primary sequence of the subsidiaries, because of their being for that [principal's] purpose. // MS_5,1.14 //

children.text: sārasvatau bhavataḥ, etad vai daivyaṃ mithunam iti{*4/493*} śrūyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ strīdevatyasya prathamaṃ dharmāḥ, uta puṃdevatyasyeti. niyamakāriṇaḥ śāstrasyābhāvād aniyamaḥ. iti prāpte brūmaḥ, mukhyakrameṇa vā niyamaḥ syād iti, strīdevatyasya hi pūrvaṃ yājyānuvākyayoḥ samāmnānam, praṇo devī sarasvatīti{*4/494*}. tasmāt strīdevatyasya pūrvaṃ pradānena [546]{*4/495*} bhavitavyam, tasmāt strīdevatyasya pūrvaṃ dharmāḥ kāryāḥ. tathā hi pradhānakālatā bhavaty aṅgānām, itarathā, yaiḥ padārthair vyavadhānaṃ sāmarthyād anujñātam, tebhyo 'dhikair api vyavadhānaṃ syāt.
children.translated_text: There are two <s>Sārasvata</s> [offerings]. It is heard: 'This is indeed the divine couple.' There a doubt [arises]: should the rites of the one with a female deity [come] first, or those of the one with a male deity? Because of the absence of a scripture that creates a restriction, there is no restriction — this is the prima facie view. Given this, we say: or the restriction would be by the primary sequence — for the recitation of the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> (invocatory and offering verses) of the one with a female deity is recorded first: '<s>Praṇo devī Sarasvatī</s>' (May the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> [protect] our vital breath). Therefore the offering to the one with a female deity should come first. Thus the subsidiaries have the timing of the principal; otherwise, if items more than those by which intervention is permitted by capability were to intervene, there would be [excessive] intervention.

children.text: prakṛtau tu svaśabdatvād yathākramaṃ pratīyeta//5.1.15//
children.translated_text: But in the basic rite (<s>prakṛti</s>), because of having its own word, [the order] should be understood as per the [textual] sequence. // MS_5,1.15 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ pūrvamauṣadhadharmāḥ samāmnātāḥ, tata ājyasya. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim agnīṣomīyadharmānām, mukhyakrameṇa pūrvam ājyasya dharmāḥ kartavyāḥ, uta yathāpāṭham iti. mukhyakramānugraheṇājyasya pūrvām. iti prāpte brūmaḥ, prakṛtau yathāpāṭhaṃ pratīyeta, svaśabdo hi teṣāṃ pāṭhakramaḥ, so 'nyathā kriyamāṇe bādhitaḥ syāt. sahatvasya punarupasaṃgrāhakaḥ prayogavacanaḥ, svakrameṇa padārthe saṃnikṛṣyamāṇe na bādhito bhaviṣyati. api ca pāṭhakrame svaśabdaḥ, svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya iti. mukhyakrameṇa{*4/496*} prayogavacanaikavākyatā sūkṣmā.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the rites pertaining to the vegetable [offering] (<s>auṣadha</s>) are recorded first, then those of the <s>ājya</s> (ghee). There a doubt [arises]: among the rites of the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> [offering], should the rites of the <s>ājya</s> be performed first by the primary sequence, or as per the textual order? By accommodating the primary sequence, [one would say] the <s>ājya</s> [comes] first. Given this prima facie view, we say: in the basic rite, [the order] should be understood as per the textual order, for the textual order is their own [authoritative] word. If done otherwise, it would be contradicted. The statement about performance, on the other hand, accommodates the co-occurrence; when items are brought near in their own order, it will not be contradicted. Moreover, in the textual order, there is the [authoritative] word — 'the recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is to be studied.' The syntactic unity with the statement about performance through the primary sequence is subtle.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/496: E2: mukhyakrame}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/496: E2: <s>mukhyakrame</s>}]

children.text: mantratas tu virodhe syāt prayogarūpasāmarthyāt tasmād utpattideśaḥ saḥ//5.1.16//
children.translated_text: But when there is contradiction from the <s>mantras</s>, it would be [determined] by the capability of the form of performance; therefore that is the place of origination. // MS_5,1.16 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ, āgneyasya pūrvaṃ mantrapāṭhaḥ, uttaro brāhmaṇasya. tatra saṃdehaḥ, katamaḥ{*4/497*} pāṭho balīyān iti. ucyate, aniyamaḥ, niyamakāriṇaḥ śāstrasyābhāvād iti.
[547]{*4/498*} evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, mantrapāṭho balīyān. kutaḥ? prayogarūpasāmarthyāt. prayogāya mantrasya rūpasāmarthyam. tad asya sāmarthyaṃ yena mantraḥ prayujyate, tasya ca prayujyamānasya kramo dṛṣṭāya bhavati{*4/499*}. nanu ca brāhmaṇapāṭhasyāpi tad eva prayojanam. ucyate, utpattideśaḥ saḥ, aparam api tasya prayojanaṃ karmotpattyarthaṃ bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the <s>mantra</s> recitation of the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] comes first, and that of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [portion] comes later. There a doubt [arises]: which recitation order is stronger? We say: there is no restriction, because of the absence of a scripture that creates a restriction.
Given this prima facie view, we say: the <s>mantra</s> recitation order is stronger. Why? Because of the capability of the form of performance. The <s>mantra</s> has the capability of form for performance. That capability by which the <s>mantra</s> is employed — and when that [mantra] is employed, its sequence pertains to the visible [ritual]. [The objector says:] but the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> recitation order too has the very same purpose. We reply: that is the place of origination — for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has yet another purpose: it will serve the origination of the ritual action.

children.text: tadvacanād vikṛtau yathāpradhānaṃ syāt//5.1.17//
children.translated_text: Because of that statement, in a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>), [the order] should be according to the principal. // MS_5,1.17 //

children.text: asty adhvarakalpā nāmeṣṭiḥ, āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet, sarasvaty ājyabhāgo syād bārhaspatyaś carur iti{*4/500*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim āgneyavikārasya bārhaspatyasya pūrvaṃ dharmāḥ kāryāḥ, codako balavattaraḥ, prayogavacanāt. utopāṃśuyājavikārasya prayogavacano balavattaraḥ, codakād iti. kiṃ prāptam? vikṛtāv asyām, yathāpradhānaṃ syāt, tadvacanāt. teṣāṃ sākṣād vacanakramo vikṛtau. tena saṃnihitānām upasaṃhārakaḥ{*4/501*} prayogavacano hi pratyakṣaḥ, taddharmāṇāṃ cānumānikaḥ, codakena hi sa prāptaḥ. tasmāt pratyakṣaḥ prayogavacano balavattaraḥ, tena codaka ānumāniko bādhyate.
children.translated_text: There is an <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) called <s>Adhvarakalpa</s>: 'He should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to <s>Agni-Viṣṇu</s>; <s>Sarasvatī</s> should have the <s>ājyabhāga</s>; a <s>caru</s> (rice oblation) to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: should the rites of the <s>Bārhaspatya</s>, which is a modification of the <s>Āgneya</s>, be performed first, since the injunction is stronger due to the statement about performance? Or is the statement about performance for the modification of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (silent offering) stronger, [prevailing over] the injunction? What is the prima facie view? In this modification, [the order] should be according to the principal, because of that statement. For those [offerings], the direct statement-order applies in the modification. Therefore the statement about performance, which gathers those that are proximate, is directly perceptible; the statement about the properties of those [offerings] is inferential, for it is obtained through injunction. Therefore the directly perceptible statement about performance is stronger, and by it the inferential injunction is overridden.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/500: Tait.S. 2.2.9.1}*
*{4/501: E2: aṅgānām upasaṃhārakaḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/500: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.9.1}]
[{4/501: E2: <s>aṅgānām upasaṃhārakaḥ</s>}]

children.text: vipratipattau vā prakṛtyanvayād yathāprakṛti//5.1.18//
children.translated_text: Or, in case of conflict, [the order should be] according to the archetype, because of conformity with the archetype. // MS_5,1.18 //

children.text: mukhyāṅgakramavipratipattau vā, yathā prakṛtau, tathaiva vikṛtau bhavitum arhatīti. kutaḥ? prakṛtyanvayāt. yādṛśāḥ prakṛtau dharmāḥ, tādṛśā eva vikṛtau bhavitum arhantīti, mukhyakrameṇa kriyamāṇā na prakṛtivat kṛtāḥ syuḥ. codako hi prayoga[548]{*4/502*}vacanād balavattaraḥ, sa hy utpādayati prāpayati ca. prāpitān abhisamīkṣya prayogavacana upasaṃharati, sa prāpteṣu utpannaḥ prāptinimittaka uttarakālaṃ{*4/503*} pūrvaprāptaṃ na bādhitum arhati codakam, pratyakṣo 'pi san, bahiraṅgatvāt, yathāprāptān evopasaṃhariṣyati. tasmāt pūrvaṃ bārhaspatyasya dharmāḥ, tata ājyasyeti.
children.translated_text: Or, in the doubt regarding the order of principal and subsidiary [elements], just as in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), so it should be in the ectype (<s>vikṛti</s>). Why? Because of conformity with the archetype. Just as the properties are in the archetype, so they should be in the ectype. [If performed] in the primary order, they would not be done as in the archetype. For the enjoining [Vedic] statement is stronger than the statement of performance [548], since it produces and brings about. Having considered what has been brought about, the statement of performance collects them. That [statement of performance], arising after what has [already] been brought about, being based on what has been brought about, being subsequent, should not override the prior enjoining statement, even though it is directly perceptible, because of its being extrinsic (<s>bahiraṅga</s>). It will collect them just as they have been brought about. Therefore, first [come] the properties of the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> [offering], then of the <s>ājya</s> (ghee offering).

children.text: vikṛtiḥ prakṛtidharmatvāt tatkālā syād yathāśiṣṭam//5.1.19//
children.translated_text: The ectype (<s>vikṛti</s>), because of having the properties of the archetype, should have the same timing, as instructed. // MS_5,1.19 //

children.text: cāturmāsyeṣu sākamedhas tṛtīyaṃ parva, tasyāvayavāḥ, agnaye 'nīkavate prātaraṣṭākapālaḥ, marudbhyaḥ sāṃtapanebhyo madhyaṃdine caruḥ, marudbhyo gṛhamedhibhyaḥ sarvāsāṃ dugdhe sāyamodanam iti{*4/504*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim etā dvyahakālā iṣṭayaḥ, uta sadyaskālā iti. kiṃ prāptam? vikṛtis tatkālā bhavitum arhatīti, yathāśiṣṭam, yathā prakṛtir uktā, tathā vikṛtiḥ syāt. prakṛtidharmā hi sā, tasmād yā vikṛtiḥ, sā dvyahakālā bhavitum arhatīti{*4/505*}.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites, the <s>Sākamedha</s> is the third <s>parvan</s> (division). Its constituent parts are: an eight-potsherd [cake] for <s>Agni Anīkavat</s> in the morning, a <s>caru</s> (rice porridge) for the <s>Maruts Sāṃtapanas</s> at midday, and rice boiled in the milk of all [cows] for the <s>Maruts Gṛhamedhas</s> in the evening. There a doubt [arises]: are these offerings that take two days, or are they to be completed the same day? What is the prima facie view? The ectype should have the same timing — as instructed, as the archetype is stated, so the ectype should be. For it has the properties of the archetype; therefore whatever ectype [it is], it should take two days.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/504: Tait.S. 1.8.4.1}*
*{4/505: E1 (Fn.): yā yā vikṛtiḥ, sā sā dvyahakālā bhavitum arhatīti}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/504: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 1.8.4.1}]
[{4/505: E1 (fn.): <s>yā yā vikṛtiḥ, sā sā dvyahakālā bhavitum arhatīti</s>}]

children.text: api vā kramakālasaṃyuktā sadyaḥ kriyeta tatra vidher anumānāt prakṛtidharmalopaḥ syāt//5.1.20//
children.translated_text: Or rather, being connected with a sequential timing, it should be done the same day; for in that [case], from inference of the injunction, there would be a loss of the archetype's properties. // MS_5,1.20 //

children.text: ahnaḥ kāleṣu ye padārthā ucyante, prātar madhyaṃdine sāyam iti, krameṇa ta ekasminn ahanīti pratīyante, yathā devadattaḥ prātar apūpaṃ bhakṣayati, madhyaṃdine vividham annam aśnāti, aparāhṇe [549]{*4/506*} modakān bhakṣayatīty ekasminn ahanīti gamyate. tasmāt sadyaskālā evaṃjātīyakā vikṛtayaḥ, dvyaihakālyaṃ hi codakaprāptam ānumānikam, pratyakṣarūpayā sadyaskālatayā bādhyeta.
children.translated_text: The items that are mentioned at times of the day — morning, midday, and evening — are understood sequentially as [occurring] within a single day. Just as: '<s>Devadatta</s> eats cakes in the morning, eats various food at midday, eats sweetmeats in the afternoon [549]' — it is understood as within a single day. Therefore ectypes of this kind have same-day timing. For the two-day timing, being obtained through the enjoining [statement], is inferential; it would be overridden by the directly perceptible same-day timing.

children.text: kālotkarṣa iti cet//5.1.21//
children.translated_text: If [one argues that] there would be a temporal extension — // MS_5,1.21 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, prāptaḥ sāṅgaṃ śrūyate, tathā madhyaṃdine sāyaṃ ceti, utkarṣo bhaviṣyati, yathaiteṣu kāleṣu sāṅgam. na ca dvyahakālatāyā bādhaḥ, ekasyāhnaḥ prātar anīkavantam upakraṃsyate, dvitīyasya prātar yakṣyeta. evaṃ sāṃtapanīyā{*4/507*} pūrvedyur madhyāṃdina upakraṃsyate, aparedyur madhyaṃdine yakṣyate. tathā gṛhamedhīye sāyam upakramaṇaṃ pūrvedyuḥ, sāyaṃ yāgo 'paredyur iti. nanu vākyād ekam ahar gamyata ity uktam. ucyate, padārthasāmarthyajanito hi vākyārtho bhavati. na cātra padārthasāmarthyam asti, yenaikam ahar gamyeta.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — what is obtained [as starting] in the morning is heard together with its subsidiaries, and likewise [for] midday and evening — there will be a temporal extension, so that [the offering] together with its subsidiaries [fills each time-slot]. And there is no overriding of the two-day timing. On one day's morning he will begin the <s>Anīkavat</s> [offering], on the second day's morning he will sacrifice. Likewise the <s>Sāṃtapanīya</s> — he will begin on the previous day at midday, and sacrifice on the following day at midday. Similarly for the <s>Gṛhamedhīya</s> — the commencement is in the evening of the previous day, the sacrifice in the evening of the following day. [The objector says:] but was it not said that a single day is understood from the sentence? [We] reply: the sentence-meaning arises from the capacity of the word-meanings. And here there is no capacity in the word-meanings by which a single day would be understood.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/507: E1 (Fn.): sāṃtapanīyāḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/507: E1 (fn.): <s>sāṃtapanīyāḥ</s>}]

children.text: na tatsaṃbandhāt{*4/508*}//5.1.22//
children.translated_text: No, because of the connection of that [subsidiary with its principal]. // MS_5,1.22 //

children.text: naitad evam. kasmāt? tatsaṃbandhāt, ekakālasaṃbaddhāni pradhānāny aṅgaiḥ saha śrūyante. katham? sāṅgaṃ hi pradhānaṃ prātaḥkāle śrūyate, tathā madhyaṃdine sāyaṃ ca. nāṅgāni prātaḥkālādiṣu. tatrānyakāleṣv aṅgeṣv anyakāleṣu ca pradhāneṣu, na sāṅgaṃ teṣu kāleṣu kṛtaṃ syāt. tasmāt sadyaskālā evaitā vikṛtaya iti. api ca, dvy ahaṃ sākamedhair iti śrūyate. tat sadyaskālāsūpapadyate.
children.translated_text: This is not so. Why? Because of the connection of that — the principal [offerings] connected with a single time are heard together with their subsidiaries. How? For the principal together with its subsidiaries is heard at the morning time, and likewise at midday and evening. The subsidiaries are not [heard] at morning-time, etc. [separately]. There, when the subsidiaries are at different times and the principals are at different times, the [offering] together with its subsidiaries would not be performed at those [prescribed] times. Therefore these ectypes have same-day timing. Moreover, it is heard: 'Two days with the <s>Sākamedhas</s>.' That is fitting [only] with same-day timing.

children.text: aṅgānāṃ mukhyakālatvād yathoktam utkarṣe syāt//5.1.23//
children.translated_text: Because of the subsidiaries having their primary time, what is stated [in the Vedic text] would apply in [cases of] temporal advancement. // MS_5,1.23 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, āgnimārutād ūrdhvam anuyājaiś carantīty utkarṣaḥ, tathāgnīṣomīye paśau, tiṣṭhantaṃ paśuṃ prayajantīty apakarṣaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim utkarṣe 'nuyājamātram utkṛṣyate, apakarṣe ca prayājamātram, utotkarṣe 'nuyājādi, apakarṣe ca prayājāntam iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? yāvad uktam, utkarṣāpakarṣayoḥ syāt. kutaḥ? aṅgānāṃ mukhyakālatvāt. evam anyeṣāṃ pradhānakālatā bhaviṣyatīti. tatra sahatvasya prāpakaḥ prayogavacano 'nugrahīṣyate.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'After the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation], they proceed with the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings)' — this is an advancement (<s>utkarṣa</s>). Likewise in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice]: 'They offer the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) while the animal is standing' — this is a retraction (<s>apakarṣa</s>). There a doubt [arises]: in the advancement, are only the <s>anuyājas</s> advanced, and in the retraction only the <s>prayājas</s>? Or in the advancement, the <s>anuyājas</s> and everything after, and in the retraction, everything up to the <s>prayājas</s>? What is the prima facie view? As much as is stated should apply in the advancement and retraction. Why? Because of the subsidiaries having their primary time. Thus the other [elements] will have the time of their principal.

children.text: tadādi vābhisaṃbandhāt tadantam apakarṣe syāt//5.1.24//
children.translated_text: That and everything after [would be advanced] in an advancement, and that and everything before in a retraction, because of the connection. // MS_5,1.24 //

children.text: tadādy utkarṣe, tadantam apakarṣe gamyeta. kutaḥ? abhisaṃbandhāt. yad{*4/510*} anuyājānāṃ parastāt samāmnāyate, tat pradhānād antaraṃ{*4/511*} prayogavacanena prāptaṃ bādhitvā pāṭhasāmarthyād anuyājebhyaḥ parastāt kriyate, tathā yas tataḥ paraḥ, sa tataḥ parastāt. evam eka utkṛṣyamāṇaḥ sarvaṃ guṇakāṇḍam utkarṣati, tathāpakṛṣyamāṇo 'pakarṣatīti.
children.translated_text: That and everything after in the advancement, that and everything before in the retraction — this would be understood. Why? Because of the connection. What is taught after the <s>anuyājas</s> — that, having overridden its position immediately after the principal [as obtained] by the statement of performance, is performed after the <s>anuyājas</s> by the force of the textual sequence (<s>pāṭha</s>). Likewise, what comes after that, comes after that. Thus, when one [element] is advanced, it advances the entire group of subsidiaries; likewise, when retracted, it retracts [them].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/510: E1 (Fn.): yadi}*
*{4/511: E2: anantaraṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/510: E1 (fn.): <s>yadi</s>}]
[{4/511: E2: <s>anantaraṃ</s>}]

children.text: pravṛttyā kṛtakālānām//5.1.25//
children.translated_text: For those whose time is determined by [their] operation — // MS_5,1.25 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate prātaranuvākakāle, pratiprasthātaḥ savanīyān [551]{*4/512*} nirvapasveti preṣyatīti savanīyānāṃ nirvāpakālaḥ. asti ca bahiṣpavamāne stute, agnīd agnīn vihara, barhi stṛṇīhi, puroḍāśān alaṃkurv iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ prātaranuvākakāle savanīyān nirūpya pracaraṇīhomādayaḥ saumikāḥ padārthāḥ, uta pauroḍāśāḥ{*4/513*} prāg alaṃkaraṇād iti. kiṃ prāptam? aniyamaḥ, niyamakāriṇaḥ śāstrasyābhāvāt.
ity evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pravṛttyā kṛtakālānām, jñānakālānāṃ padārthānāṃ pravṛttyā niyamaḥ syāt, prayujyamānam eva hi pūrvapadārtham abhiniyacchati. sa tasya parastāt samāmnātaḥ, parastāt kartavyaḥ. saumikasya tu padārthasya pracaraṇīhomasya vacanāt kramo bādhitaḥ. alaṃkaraṇaṃ ca bahiṣpavamānasya parastāt samāmnātam, tasmāt tasya pūrvaḥ padārtho nirvapaṇādīnām antaḥ. tata uttare saumikāḥ padārthāḥ kartavyā iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, at the time of the morning recitation (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>), it is heard: 'He commands the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> [priest]: "Prepare the <s>savanīya</s> [offerings]"' — this is the time for preparing the <s>savanīya</s> offerings [551]. And after the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> <s>stotra</s> has been chanted: 'O <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, separate the fires; strew the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass); prepare the <s>puroḍāśas</s> (rice cakes).' There a doubt [arises]: are the <s>savanīya</s> offerings prepared at the time of the morning recitation, and then the <s>pracaraṇīhoma</s> and other <s>Soma</s>-related items [performed]? Or are the <s>puroḍāśa</s>-related items [performed] before the preparation? What is the prima facie view? There is no fixed rule, because of the absence of a prescriptive text establishing one.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: for those whose time is determined by [their] operation — for items whose time is established by [their being mentioned in] a knowledge[-context], the ordering should be determined by [their actual] operation. For it is only when being actually employed that [an item] constrains the preceding item — [placing it] after itself. What is taught after it must be done after it. But for the <s>Soma</s>-related item, the <s>pracaraṇīhoma</s>, the sequence is overridden by [Vedic] statement. And the preparation is taught after the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s>; therefore the earlier item [in the sequence] is the preparation and such [activities]. After that, the subsequent <s>Soma</s>-related items are to be performed.

children.text: śabdavipratiṣedhāc ca//5.1.26//
children.translated_text: And because of the contradiction in the [Vedic] word. // MS_5,1.26 //

children.text: śabdaś ca vipratiṣidhyate, alaṃkurv ity uktaḥ prokṣaṇādīn pratipadyeta. asmatpakṣe tu, alaṃkurv ity ukte 'laṃkaraṇam eva pratipatsyate. tatrālaṃkaraṇe prāptakāle prāptakālavacano loḍanto 'nugrahīṣyate. tasmād atra prāvṛttikaḥ krama iti.
children.translated_text: The [Vedic] word too would be contradicted — [the word] 'prepare' (<s>alaṃkuru</s>), when stated, would [otherwise need to] apply to the sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and other [acts]. But in our position, when 'prepare' is stated, it will apply to the preparation alone. There, when the time of preparation has arrived, the present-tense imperative (<s>loṭ</s>) ending expressing an arrived-time [action] will be supported. Therefore the ordering here is based on [actual] operation.

children.text: asaṃyogāt tu vaikṛtaṃ tad eva pratikṛṣyeta//5.1.27//
children.translated_text: But because of the non-connection, only the ectype-specific [element] should be retracted. // MS_5,1.27 //

children.text:
asti darśapūrṇamāsaprakṛtike paśāv agnīṣomīye vaikṛtaṃ yūpakarma, tat pratikṛṣyate, dīkṣāsu yūpaṃ chinattīti. tat pratikṛṣyamāṇam arvācīnāny apy agnīṣomapraṇayanādīni prati[552]{*4/514*}karṣati, uta neti saṃśaye, pratikarṣati, saṃbandhād iti gamyate{*4/515*}.
tathā prāpte brūmaḥ, vikṛtāv abhyadhikaṃ yat, tat pratikṛṣyamāṇaṃ tato 'rvācīnāny apy agnīṣomapraṇayanādīni na pratikraṣṭum arhati. katham? asaṃyogāt, pāśukaṃ yūpakarma, tataḥ prācīnaṃ saumikam. na tayoḥ paraspareṇa saṃbandhaḥ. na saumikaḥ padārthaḥ, pāśukasyopakārakaḥ paśor vā. yadi hi tayor upakārakaḥ syāt, tatas tasyopakurvataḥ kramo 'py asya sāhāyyaṃ kurvan guṇabhūtaḥ syāt. na tv etad asti, tasmān naiṣāṃ paraspareṇa krame niyamaḥ. ato yūpamātraṃ pratikṛṣyate. api ca yūpamātraṃ pratikṛsya kṛtārthe śabde saumikānāṃ svakramabādho na bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-based animal [sacrifice], the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [rite], there is an ectype-specific post-related ritual action (<s>yūpakarma</s>). That is retracted — 'during the <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) he cuts the post.' When that is retracted, does it also retract the preceding [elements] like the leading forth of the <s>Agni-Soma</s> (<s>agnīṣomapraṇayana</s>) [552] and others, or not? In the case of doubt — it does retract [them], because of the connection — so it is understood.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: what is additional in the ectype — when that is retracted, it should not retract the preceding [elements] like the leading forth of <s>Agni-Soma</s> and others. How? Because of the non-connection. The post-related ritual is of the animal [sacrifice]; what precedes it is of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice]. There is no mutual connection between those two. The <s>Soma</s>-related item is not a helper of the animal-related [item] or of the animal. For if it were a helper, then its ordering too, assisting that [item], would be subordinate. But this is not the case; therefore there is no fixed ordering of these with respect to each other. Hence only the post-[related item] alone is retracted. Moreover, having retracted only the post-[related item], when the purpose of the [Vedic] word has been fulfilled, there will be no overriding of the natural order of the <s>Soma</s>-related [elements].

children.text: prāsaṅgikaṃ ca notkarṣed asaṃyogāt//5.1.28//
children.translated_text: And an incidental [element] should not be advanced, because of the non-connection. // MS_5,1.28 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, āgnimārutād ūrdhvam anuyājaiś carantīti. anuyājā utkṛṣyamāṇā dākṣiṇāgnikau homāv utkarṣanti, neti saṃśayaḥ. saṃbandhād utkarṣanti.
iti prāpte ucyate, naivāv utkraṣṭum arhanti, ye{*4/516*} tayoḥ sva{*4/517*} 'nuyājāḥ, saṃbaddhās{*4/518*} te, na prayuktāḥ parakīyaiḥ, teṣām artho nirvartita iti. padārthānāṃ ca kramo bhavati, na padārthaprayojanānām, yaugapadyena hi padārthā upakurvantīti vakṣyāmaḥ. padārthānāṃ cotpattiḥ kramavatī, pṛthakśabdatvād utpatteḥ, na padārthaprayojanasya, yugapat prayogavacanenābhihitatvāt. ato 'nuyājotpatter utkarṣikāyā abhāvād dākṣiṇāgnikau homau notkṛṣyeyātām iti. api cānuyājamātram utkṛṣya [553] kṛtārthe śabde dākṣiṇāgnikayor homayoḥ svakramabādho na bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'After the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation], they proceed with the <s>anuyājas</s>.' The doubt is whether the <s>anuyājas</s>, being advanced, advance the two oblations in the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) as well. [The prima facie view:] because of the connection, they do advance [them].
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: they should not advance those two [oblations]. Those whose own <s>anuyājas</s> they are — those are connected [with them], not those employed by others. Their purpose has been accomplished. And the ordering belongs to the items [themselves], not to the purposes of items — for items serve simultaneously, as we shall state. And the origination of items follows a sequence, because origination has separate words; but not [so for] the purpose of items, because [the purpose is] stated simultaneously by the statement of performance. Therefore, since the advancement-origination of the <s>anuyājas</s> does not exist [for the Dakṣiṇāgni oblations], the two oblations in the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> should not be advanced [553]. Moreover, having advanced only the <s>anuyājas</s>, when the purpose of the [Vedic] word has been fulfilled, there will be no overriding of the natural order of the two <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> oblations.

children.text: tathāpūrvam//5.1.29//
children.translated_text: Likewise [for] what is unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>). // MS_5,1.29 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayor vediḥ, havir abhivāsanottarakāle samāmnātā. sāmāvāsyāyāṃ pratikṛṣyate, pūrvedyur amāvāsyāyāṃ vediṃ karotīti. sā tv apakṛṣyamāṇā tato 'rvācīnān padārthān apakarṣati, neti saṃśayaḥ. ucyate, saṃbandhāt pratikarṣati.
ity evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, tathāpūrvam, aprakṛtir pūrvikāyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vedikaraṇaṃ pūrvedyur āmnātam, ubhayor api śvobhūte havir abhivāsanam. abhivāsanaṃ kṛtvāmāvāsyāyāṃ vediḥ kartavyeti na śrutyādīnām anyatamat{*4/519*} kāraṇam asti. tasmān nābhivāsanāntāḥ pratikraṣṭavyā iti. abhivāsane cāpakṛṣyamāṇe havīṃṣi bhasmībhaveyuḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, the <s>vedi</s> (altar) is taught [as occurring] after the time of sanctifying the oblation (<s>havir abhivāsana</s>). On the new-moon day (<s>amāvāsyā</s>) it is retracted — 'on the previous day of the new-moon, he makes the <s>vedi</s>.' When that is retracted, does it retract the preceding items, or not? This is the doubt. [We] reply: because of the connection, it does retract [them].
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: likewise [for] what is unprecedented — the making of the <s>vedi</s> on the previous day of the new-moon (<s>amāvāsyā</s>) is not in the archetype (<s>aprakṛti</s>); it is taught [as occurring] on the previous day. For both [days], the sanctifying of the oblation is on the day after [the previous day]. Having sanctified the oblation, the <s>vedi</s> should be made on the new-moon day — for this there is no reason from [Vedic] word or other [means of knowledge]. Therefore the items up to the sanctifying of the oblation should not be retracted. And if the sanctifying were retracted, the oblations would turn to ash.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/519: E2: anyatamaṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/519: E2: <s>anyatamaṃ</s>}]

children.text: sāṃtapanīyā tūtkarṣed agnihotraṃ savanavad vaiguṇyāt//5.1.30//
children.translated_text: But the <s>Sāṃtapanīya</s> [offering] should advance the <s>Agnihotra</s>, like a <s>savana</s> (pressing), because of the deficiency [that would otherwise result]. // MS_5,1.30 //

children.text: cāturmādyeṣu sākamedhāvayavaḥ sāṃtapanīyā nāmeṣṭiḥ, marudbhyaḥ sāṃtapanebhyo mādhyaṃdine caruṃ nirvapatīti{*4/520*}, sā daivān mānuṣād vā pratibandhād{*4/521*} utkṛṣyamāṇā agnihotram utkarṣet, na veti saṃśaye. ucyate, sāṃtapanīyā tūtkarṣed agni[554]{*4/522*}hotram savanavad vaiguṇyāt. yadi notkarṣet, agnihotrasavana 'gnihotrakāla{*4/523*} uddhṛte 'gnāv agnihotraṃ viguṇaṃ syāt. tasmād utkraṣṭavyam, savanavat, yathā prātaḥsavanaṃ daivān mānuṣād vā pratibandhād{*4/524*} utkṛṣyamāṇaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam utkarṣatīti, evam atrāpi draṣṭavyam.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites, the <s>Sāṃtapanīya</s> is a constituent of the <s>Sākamedha</s> — a certain offering: 'He prepares a <s>caru</s> (porridge) for the <s>Maruts Sāṃtapanas</s> at midday.' If that [offering], being advanced due to a divine or human obstruction, should advance the <s>Agnihotra</s> or not — in this doubt, [we] reply: the <s>Sāṃtapanīya</s> should advance the <s>Agnihotra</s> [554], like a <s>savana</s> (pressing), because of the deficiency [that would otherwise result]. If it does not advance [the Agnihotra], the <s>Agnihotra</s> — [which is performed] at the <s>Agnihotra</s>-<s>savana</s> (pressing-time), when the fire has been lifted for the <s>Agnihotra</s>-time — would become deficient. Therefore it must be advanced, just like a <s>savana</s> — just as the morning pressing, being advanced due to a divine or human obstruction, advances the midday pressing — so it should be viewed here as well.

*{4/523: E2: agnihotram anagnihotrakāla}*
*{4/524: E1 (Fn.): pratibanlād}*

children.text: avyavāyāc ca//5.1.31//
children.translated_text: And because of non-interruption. // MS_5,1.31 //

children.text: evaṃ sāṃtapanīyam agnihotreṇa na vyavahitaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, tatra kramo 'nugrahīṣyate. kramabhede ca doṣaḥ śrūyate, apa vā etad yajñāc chidyate{*4/525*}, yad anyasya tantre vitate 'nyasya tantraṃ pratīyata iti.
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sāṃtapanīya</s> [rite] will not be interrupted by the <s>Agnihotra</s>, and in that [arrangement] the sequence will be supported. And a fault in breaking the sequence is heard: 'This indeed is cut off from the sacrifice — when, while one's own ritual system (<s>tantra</s>) is extended, another's ritual system is resorted to.'

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/525: E1 (Fn.), E2: yajñasya chidyate}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/525: E1 (footnote), E2: <s>yajñasya chidyate</s>}]

children.text: asaṃbandhāt tu notkarṣet//5.1.32//
children.translated_text: But because of the absence of connection, [the Agnihotra] should not be postponed. // MS_5,1.32 //

children.text: nāgnihotrasya sāṃtapanīyāṅgam, na sāṃtapanīyāyā vāgnihotram. tena nāsāv agnihotrasya purastāt kartavyā, ato nāgnihotram utkraṣṭavyam.
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃtapanīya</s> is not a subsidiary of the <s>Agnihotra</s>, nor is the <s>Agnihotra</s> [a subsidiary] of the <s>Sāṃtapanīya</s>. Therefore that [Sāṃtapanīya] need not be performed before the <s>Agnihotra</s>; hence the <s>Agnihotra</s> should not be postponed.

children.text: prāpaṇāc ca nimittasya//5.1.33//
children.translated_text: And because of the arrival of the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>). // MS_5,1.33 //

children.text:
prāptaṃ cāgnihotrasya nimittam, sāyaṃ juhoti, prātar juhoti, udite juhoti, anudite juhoti, prathamāstamite juhoti, saṃdhau juhoti, nakṣatrāṇi dṛṣṭvā juhotīti{*4/526*}, tan nātikramitavyam, tasmād api notkarṣaḥ. yad uktam, vaiguṇyam iti{*4/527*}, utkarṣe 'pi vaiguṇyaṃ kālānyatvāt. aṅgāprāpter jaghanyaḥ kālavidhir bādhyatām iti cet. na, kālasya nimittatvāt, [555]{*4/528*} tad apāye 'śrutam eva sarvaṃ kriyeta, nimittaṃ ca{*4/529*}, anupādeyatvena śravaṇāt. saptamī hy ādhārādiṣv asaṃbhavān nimittasaptamī draṣṭavyā.
atha yad uktam - savanavad utkraṣṭavyam iti{*4/530*}. tad ucyate -
children.translated_text:
And the occasion for the <s>Agnihotra</s> has arrived — 'he offers in the evening, he offers in the morning, he offers when [the sun] has risen, he offers when [it] has not risen, he offers when [it] has first set, he offers at the juncture, he offers having seen the stars.' That [occasion] must not be transgressed; therefore too there is no postponement. As for what was said — 'there will be a deficiency' — even in postponement there is a deficiency, because of the time being different. If [one argues that] the later time-injunction should be overridden because of the non-arrival of the subsidiary — no, because of the time being the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>). [555] In its absence, everything that is done would be unheard [i.e., without Vedic basis] — and the occasion [statement is heard] as not to be disregarded. For the locative case, being impossible in [the sense of] a container etc., should be understood as the occasioning locative.
As for what was said — 'it should be postponed like the <s>savana</s> (pressing)' — to that it is said:

children.text: saṃbandhāt savanotkarṣaḥ//5.1.34//
children.translated_text: The postponement of the <s>savana</s> (pressing) is because of connection. // MS_5,1.34 //

children.text: saṃbaddhaṃ hi savanaṃ savanena, ekakratusaṃbandhāt, tad utkṛṣyate.
children.translated_text: For the <s>savana</s> is connected with [another] <s>savana</s> — because of the connection with a single ritual (<s>kratu</s>); therefore it is postponed.

children.text: ṣoḍaśī cokthyasaṃyogāt//5.1.35//
children.translated_text: And the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> [should be postponed] because of its connection with the <s>Ukthya</s> [offerings]. // MS_5,1.35 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, ṣoḍaśinaṃ prakṛtya, taṃ parāñcam ukthyebhyo vigṛhṇātīti{*4/531*}{*4/532*}. yadā daivān manuṣād vā pratibandhād{*4/533*} ukthyāny utkṛṣyante, kiṃ tadā ṣoḍaśy utkṛṣṭavyaḥ{*4/534*}, neti bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ prāptam? notkraṣṭavyaḥ. kutaḥ? evaṃ stotraṃ svasmin kāle ṣoḍaśinaḥ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, samayādhyuṣite sūrye ṣoḍaśinastotram{*4/535*} upakarotīti. tasmād anutkarṣa iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, ṣoḍaśī cotkraṣṭavyaḥ. kasmāt? ukthyasaṃyogāt, ukthyasaṃyogo hi ṣoḍaśino bhavati, taṃ parāñcam ukthyebhyo vigṛhṇātīti{*4/536*}. tasmād utkraṣṭavyaḥ ṣoḍaśī. yad uktam, ṣoḍaśinastotrakālenāvarjanaṃ{*4/537*} bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, stotrakramam anurudhyamānasya pradhānakramo virudhyeta. tasmān na stotrakramo 'nuroddhavyaḥ, ubhayaṃ na śakyam anugṛhītum{*4/538*}, grahaṃ vā gṛhītvā camasaṃ vonnīya stotram upākarotīti [556]{*4/539*} śrūyate. tasmād utkraṣṭavyaḥ ṣoḍaśīti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard, with reference to the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>: 'He separates him backward from the <s>Ukthya</s> [cups].' When, due to divine or human obstruction, the <s>Ukthya</s> [offerings] are postponed, the question arises: should the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> then be postponed [along with them], or not? What is the prima facie view? It should not be postponed. Why? [Because] thus the hymn of praise (<s>stotra</s>) of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> will be performed at its own time — 'when the sun has passed the midpoint, he commences the hymn of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>.' Therefore no postponement.
Given this [prima facie view], we say: the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> too should be postponed. Why? Because of its connection with the <s>Ukthya</s> [offerings] — for the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> has a connection with the <s>Ukthya</s> [offerings]: 'He separates him backward from the <s>Ukthya</s> [cups].' Therefore the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> should be postponed. As for what was said — 'the attraction [to its own time] will occur because of the time of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>'s hymn' — we reply: if one adheres to the hymn-sequence, the sequence of the principal [rite] would be violated. Therefore the hymn-sequence should not be adhered to; both cannot be accommodated. [556] And it is heard: 'Having taken the cup (<s>graha</s>) or having raised the goblet (<s>camasa</s>), he commences the hymn.' Therefore the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> should be postponed.

children.text: saṃnipāte pradhānānām ekaikasya guṇānāṃ sarvakarma syāt//5.2.1//
children.translated_text: When there is a convergence of principal [rites], for each one [performed], all the subsidiaries should [be completed]. // MS_5,2.1 //

children.text: vājapeye, saptadaśa prājāpatyān paśūn ālabhata iti{*4/540*} śrūyate, agnīṣomīye ca paśau paśudharmāḥ samāmnātāś codakena prāptāḥ. teṣu saṃśayaḥ, kim ekasyāder ārabhya dharmān sarvān kṛtvā, dvitīyasya punarādita upakramitavyāḥ, atha prathamas tāvat sarveṣāṃ kartavyaḥ, tato dvitīya iti. kiṃ prāptam? ekaikasya sarve 'pavarjayitavyā iti. kutaḥ? pradhānāsatter anugrahāya, itarathā pradhānāsattir viprakṛṣyeta. yathā bahuṣv aśveṣu pratigṛhīteṣu ye puroḍāśāḥ, teṣu naikajātīyānusamayaḥ, evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vājapeya</s>, it is heard: 'He slaughters seventeen <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals.' And in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice], the animal-rites are recorded as obtained through injunction. Regarding these, a doubt [arises]: should all the rites be performed starting from the first [animal] and completing [all rites for it], then beginning again from the start for the second? Or should the first [rite] be performed for all [animals], then the second [rite for all]? What is the prima facie view? For each one, all [rites] should be completed. Why? For the sake of supporting the primary [rite]'s presence — otherwise the presence of the primary [rite] would be unduly extended. Just as when many horses are received and [there are corresponding] <s>puroḍāśas</s> (rice cakes) for them, there is no single-type sequential procedure — so too here.

NOTES:
[{4/540: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.3.4.3}]

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vaikajātīyaṃ kṛtānupūrvyatvāt//5.2.2//
children.translated_text: Or rather, for all [animals] the single-type sequential procedure [should be followed], because the sequence has been established. // MS_5,2.2 //

children.text:
ekajātīyānusamayaḥ kartavyaḥ. kim evaṃ bhaviṣyati? sahatvam anugrahīṣyate, tatsahatvaṃ śrūyate, vaiśvadevīṃ kṛtvā paśubhiś carantīti, ekasmin kāle paśūnāṃ pracāraḥ.
nanv evaṃ sati pūrvasya padārthasyottaraḥ padārthaḥ paśvantaravyāpāreṇa vyavadhīyate. naiṣa doṣaḥ, evam api kṛtam evānupūrvyam. yo 'sau paśvantare vyāpāraḥ sa evāsau, na padārthāntaram, padārthāntareṇa vyavadhānaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text:
The single-type sequential procedure should be performed. What will result from this? The simultaneity [of the animals] will be supported — for their simultaneity is heard: 'Having performed the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> [offering], they proceed with the animals' — [meaning] the handling of the animals at a single time.
[The objector says:] but in this case, the [completion of a] prior item (<s>padārtha</s>) would be interrupted by the operation on another animal. [We reply:] this is not a fault — even so, the sequence is maintained. For that operation on another animal is that very same [type of operation], not a different item; interruption occurs through a different item.

children.text: kāraṇād abhyāvṛttiḥ//5.2.3//
children.translated_text: Repetition [of the sequence] is because of a reason. // MS_5,2.3 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, bahuṣu puroḍāśeṣu naikajātīyānusamaya iti, tat parihartavyam. atrocyate, yuktaṃ tatra, yat{*4/542*} kāraṇād abhyāvṛttiḥ, ekajātīyānusamaye hi kriyamāṇe sahasrasyādhiśrayaṇe kṛte prathamaḥ śuṣyet, tasya ca prathamaṃ na śakyeta kartum.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'in the case of many <s>puroḍāśas</s>, there is no single-type sequential procedure' — that must be set aside. Here we say: it is appropriate there, because the repetition is due to a reason — for if the single-type sequential procedure were followed, when a thousand [cakes] are placed on the fire, the first one would dry out, and it would not be possible to do its [subsequent steps] first.

children.text: athavādhikaraṇāntaram -
children.translated_text: Alternatively — this is a separate topic:

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/542: E2: tat}*
kāraṇād abhyāvṛttiḥ//5.2.3//
children.translated_text: Repetition [of the sequence] is because of a reason. // MS_5,2.3 //

children.text: anekasahasrāśvapratigrahe tantrānuṣṭhānam iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. kāṇḍānusamayo 'bhyupetavya iti siddhāntaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the reception of many thousands of horses, the per-ritual-system (<s>tantra</s>) procedure is the prima facie view. The established conclusion is that the per-section (<s>kāṇḍa</s>) sequential procedure should be adopted.

children.text: muṣṭikapālāvadānāñjanābhyañjanavapanapāvaneṣu caikena//5.2.4//
children.translated_text: In [the operations of] taking handfuls, placing potsherds, cutting, anointing, smearing, shaving, and purifying — [the sequential procedure is] by each individual one. // MS_5,2.4 //

children.text: muṣṭyādiṣu saṃśayaḥ, kiṃ muṣṭinānusamayaḥ, uta caturbhir muṣṭibhir iti. kiṃ prāptam? muṣṭineti. kutaḥ? ekamuṣṭinirvāpo hy ekaḥ padārthaḥ, na caturmuṣṭinirvāpaḥ. katham? ekasmin muṣṭau nirupte yatībhāvaḥ{*4/543*} paryavasyati. na śakyaṃ vaditum, na kiṃcin niruptam iti. na ca, nirupte nirvāpo na kṛtaḥ syāt, na ca muṣṭimātreṇa niruptena na prayojanam. na hy [559]{*4/544*} ekasminn anirupte catvāraḥ saṃbhavanti, muṣṭisamānādhikaraṇo hi catuḥśabdaḥ, tasmān muṣṭinānusamayaḥ kāryaḥ. evam, kapālānn upadadhātīti. tathā, madhyād avadyati pūrvārdhād avadyati, tathā, aṅkte 'bhyaṅkte vapati pāvayatīti.
children.translated_text: Regarding the handful-takings and the rest, there is a doubt: is the sequential procedure by handful, or by four handfuls [together]? What is the prima facie view? By handful. Why? For a single handful-offering is one item, not a four-handful-offering. How? When a single handful has been offered, the state of 'having offered' is complete. It cannot be said that nothing has been offered. Nor, when [a handful] has been offered, would the offering not have been performed. Nor is a single handful being offered without purpose. For [559] without one [handful] being offered, four are not possible — for the word 'four' is in apposition with 'handful.' Therefore the sequential procedure should be by handful. Similarly, 'he places the potsherds.' Likewise, 'he cuts from the middle, he cuts from the front half.' And, 'he anoints, he smears, he shaves, he purifies.'

children.text: sarvāṇi tv ekakāryatvād eṣāṃ tadguṇatvāt//5.2.5//
children.translated_text: But all [should be completed together], because of the unity of purpose; because these are subordinate to that [single purpose]. // MS_5,2.5 //

children.text: sarvāṇi tu parisamāpyānusameyāt, naikamuṣṭinirvāpaḥ padārthaḥ, catuḥsaṃkhyatvān nirvāpasya. kathaṃ catuḥsaṃkhyatā? catuḥśabdasya nirvapatinā saṃbandhāt, evaṃ saha karmaṇā, anekaguṇavidhānaṃ nyāyyam. itarathā, muṣṭisaṃbandhe sati vākyabhedaḥ prasajyeta. anirvāpāṅgaṃ ca syāt. tathopadhānādiṣv api, aṣṭākapālam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatīti nirdeśāt. dvir avadyati{*4/545*}, trir abhyaṅkte, ekaviṃśatyā pāvayatīti{*4/546*} saṃkhyādīnāṃ kriyāguṇatvaṃ bhavati. tasmāt samudāyenānusamaya iti.
children.translated_text: But all should be completed [together] before proceeding to the next sequential step. A single-handful offering is not a [complete] item — because the offering has the number four. How does it have the number four? Because of the connection of the word 'four' with 'he offers' (<s>nirvapati</s>) — thus together with the action, the prescription of multiple subsidiaries is appropriate. Otherwise, if connected with 'handful,' a sentence-split would result. And it would be non-subsidiary to the offering. Similarly in the placing [of potsherds] and the rest — because of the designation 'eight-potsherd,' 'eleven-potsherd,' 'he offers.' 'He cuts twice'; 'he smears thrice'; 'he purifies with twenty-one [strokes]' — the numbers have the status of qualifiers of the action. Therefore the sequential procedure is by the aggregate.

NOTES:
[{4/545: <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 4.4.3.9}]
[{4/546: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.1.1.8}]

children.text: saṃyukte tu prakramāt tadaṅgaṃ syād itarasya tadarthatvāt//5.2.6//
children.translated_text: But when [two operations] are conjoined, [the procedure is] from the commencement — [the latter] would be subsidiary to that [former]; for the other serves its purpose. // MS_5,2.6 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, dvir haviṣo 'vadyatīti{*4/547*}. tatra saṃśayaḥ, kim avadānenānusamayaḥ, utāvadānena pradānānteneti. kiṃ prāptam? avadāneneti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ? pṛthakpadārthatvāt, pṛthak padārtho hy avadānam, yatībhāvasya paryavasānāt, avadyativacanāt. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, saṃyukte tu prakramāt tadaṅgaṃ syāt, itarasya tadarthatvāt. nāvadānaṃ pṛthak padārthaḥ, pradānasya sa upakramaḥ, itarathāvadyater adṛṣṭārthatā [560]{*4/548*} syāt. saṃkhyāviśeṣavidhānārthaṃ ca punarvacanam. tasmāt padārthāvayavo 'vadānam, na cāvayavasahatvaṃ prayogavacanenocyate, tasmāt pradānāntenānusamaya iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: 'He cuts from the oblation twice.' There a doubt [arises]: is the sequential procedure by cutting alone, or by cutting together with the giving? What is the prima facie view? By cutting [alone], we say. Why? Because of being a separate item — for cutting is a separate item, since the state of 'having cut' is complete [after cutting], and because of the statement 'he cuts.' Given this prima facie view, we say: when conjoined, [the procedure] is from the commencement — [the giving] would be subsidiary to that [cutting]; for the other [giving] serves the purpose of that [cutting]. Cutting is not a separate item — the giving is its commencement; otherwise the cutting would have an unseen purpose. [560] And the restatement is for the purpose of prescribing the specific number. Therefore cutting is a component of the [complete] item, and the simultaneity of a component is not stated by the statement of performance. Therefore the sequential procedure is by [cutting] together with the giving.

children.text: vacanāt tu parivyāṇāntam añjanādi syāt//5.2.7//
children.translated_text: But because of the [Vedic] statement, [the procedure extends] up to the wrapping — the anointing etc. [should continue to that point]. // MS_5,2.7 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome 'gnīṣomīyapaśau yūpasyāñjanādyāḥ padārthāḥ śrūyante, teṣu yūpaikādaśinyāṃ prāpteṣu saṃśayaḥ, kim añjanādīnām{*4/549*} ekaikenānusamayaḥ, utāñjanādinā parivyāṇānteneti. kiṃ prāptam? parivyāṇāntam añjanādi syāt. kutaḥ? vacanāt, vacanam idaṃ bhavati, añjanādi yajamāno yūpaṃ nāvamṛjed āparivyāṇād iti{*4/550*}. na ca śakyam, bahuṣv añjanādinānusamayaḥ kartum, na cānavasraṣṭum. tasmāt parivyāṇāntenānusamayaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, for the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal, the items of anointing etc. of the post are heard. When these arise in the eleven-post [sacrifice], a doubt [arises]: is the sequential procedure for the anointing etc. by each individual [operation], or by the anointing etc. up to the wrapping? What is the prima facie view? The anointing etc. should extend up to the wrapping. Why? Because of the [Vedic] statement — this statement exists: 'The sacrificer should not wipe the post, beginning from the anointing, until the wrapping.' And it is not possible, when there are many [posts], to perform the sequential procedure by anointing [of each], nor to release [the process]. Therefore the sequential procedure extends up to the wrapping.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/549: E2: añjānādīnām}*
*{4/550: Tait.Br. 3.8.19.1}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/549: E2: <s>añjānādīnām</s>}]
[{4/550: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.8.19.1}]

children.text: kāraṇād vānavasargaḥ syād yathā pātravṛddhiḥ//5.2.8//
children.translated_text: Or, there would be no release because of a reason — as in the case of the vessel-increase. // MS_5,2.8 //

children.text: sahatvasya prāpakaḥ prayogavacano 'nugrahīṣyata iti padārthenānusamayaḥ. anavasargaś ca prakṛtāv arthāt kṛtaḥ, sāhāyyaṃ yajamānenādhvaryoḥ. evaṃ dṛṣṭārthatānavasargasya, itarathādṛṣṭārthatā syāt. na ca, arthāt kṛtaṃ codakaḥ prāpayati. tasmād yūpāntareṇocchrayitavyena{*4/551*} kāraṇenāvasṛjet, yathā pṛṣadājyenānuyājān yajatīty arthāt tasya dhāraṇārthaṃ pātraṃ bhidyate.
children.translated_text: The statement of performance that establishes simultaneity should be supported — [hence] the sequential procedure is by [complete] item. And the non-release in the basic rite is made from the meaning (<s>arthāt</s>) — the assistance of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> by the sacrificer [requires this]. Thus the non-release has a visible purpose; otherwise it would have an unseen purpose. And what is done from the meaning is not established by the injunction. Therefore, because of the reason of [having] another post to be raised, he should release [the process] — just as, [in the statement] 'he offers the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings) with <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curd-mixed ghee),' a vessel is produced from the meaning for the purpose of holding it.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/551: E1 (Fn.): yūpāntareṇocchritavyena}*
*{4/552: E2: 5,137; E6: 2,81}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:

children.text: na vā śabdakṛtatvān nyāyamātram itarad arthāt pātravivṛddhiḥ{*4/553*}//5.2.9//
children.translated_text: Or rather not — because the non-release is established by the [Vedic] word; the other [vessel-increase] is merely a logical principle, [done] from the meaning. // MS_5,2.9 //

children.text: na vaitatpadārthenānusamaya iti, parivyāṇāntena padārthakāṇḍenānusamayaḥ syāt. śabdakṛtaṃ hi prakṛtāv anavasarjanam, śaknoti hy ṛte 'pi yajamānāt, adhvaryur yūpam ucchrayitum. saukaryam iti cet. vidhiśabdo bādhyeta, dṛṣṭārthataivaṃ hi niyamyeta, bhojane prāṅmukhateva. ato 'saṃbhavāt, padārthakāṇḍenānusamayaḥ. prayogavacanasya ca nyāyamātratvam, codakas tato balīyān. pātravivṛddhis tv arthāt kartavyā.
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is not [a procedure] by [complete] item — the sequential procedure should be by the item-section up to the wrapping. For the non-release in the basic rite is established by the [Vedic] word — for the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is indeed capable of raising the post even without the sacrificer. If [one argues] it is for ease — [we reply:] the injunctive word would be overridden; the visible purpose would thus be restricted — like facing east while eating. Therefore, because of [the statement's] impossibility [on that interpretation], the sequential procedure is by the item-section. And the statement of performance has merely the status of a logical principle; the injunction is stronger than that. The vessel-increase, however, is to be done from the meaning.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/553: E2: pātraṃ vivṛddhiḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/553: E2: <s>pātraṃ vivṛddhiḥ</s>}]

children.text: paśugaṇe tasya tasyāpavarjayet paśvekatvāt//5.2.10//
children.translated_text: In a group of animals, [the rites] of each one should be completed, because each animal is a unit. // MS_5,2.10 //

children.text: vājapeye prājāpatyāḥ paśavaḥ. teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kim ekaikasya paśor daivatāny avadāya tataḥ sauviṣṭakṛtāni, tata aiḍāni. atha daivatair devatānām anusamayaḥ, sauviṣṭakṛtaiḥ sauviṣṭakṛtānām, aiḍair aiḍānām iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? ekaikasya kṛtsnāny avadāya tato hotavyam, prakṛtau vacanāt, etat kṛtaṃ prājāpatyeṣv api codakenaiva prāpnoti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vājapeya</s> there are <s>Prājāpatya</s> (sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>) animals. Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: should the deity-portions (<s>daivata</s>) be cut from each animal individually, then the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions, then the <s>Iḍā</s> portions? Or should the procedure be by category — the deity-portions of all the deities [together], the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions of all the <s>Sviṣṭakṛts</s>, and the <s>Iḍā</s> portions of all the <s>Iḍās</s>? What is the prima facie view? All portions should be cut from each animal completely, then offered — because of the statement in the basic rite (<s>prakṛti</s>); this, being established [there], applies to the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [animals] too through the very force of the injunction.

children.text: daivatair vaikakarmyāt//5.2.11//
children.translated_text: By the deity-portions, because of unity of action. // MS_5,2.11 //

children.text: naitad evam, daivatair devatānām, sauviṣṭakṛtaiḥ sauviṣṭakṛtānām, aiḍair aiḍānām iti. kasmāt? aikakarmyāt. evaṃ sahakṛtaṃ bhavati, yac ca vacanāt prakṛtau kṛtsnāvadānam iti, daivatāny [562]{*4/554*} avadāya na tāvaty eva hotavyam, sauviṣṭakṛtāny avadeyāni. sauviṣṭakṛtāny avadāya na tāvaty eva hotavyam, aiḍāny avadeyānīti prakṛtau śrūyate. tad iha daivatair daivatānām anusamayaṃ kurvan nainaṃ{*4/555*} prākṛtaṃ dharmaṃ bādheta. daivatāny avadāya naiva juhoti, sauviṣṭakṛtāny avadyatīti. atha sauviṣṭakṛtāny avadāya naiva juhoti, aiḍāny avadyatīti. tasmāt padārthamātreṇānusamaya iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — the deity-portions of the deities [together], the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛts</s>, and the <s>Iḍā</s> portions of the <s>Iḍās</s>. Why? Because of unity of action. Thus it is done simultaneously. As for what was said — 'because of the statement, in the basic rite the complete cutting [is done]' — [562] having cut the deity-portions, one should not offer immediately [but rather] the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions should be cut. Having cut the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions, one should not offer immediately [but rather] the <s>Iḍā</s> portions should be cut — this is heard in the basic rite. Therefore, here, performing the procedure by category with the deity-portions, one does not violate the archetypal rule. Having cut the deity-portions, one does not offer — the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions are being cut. Then, having cut the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions, one does not offer — the <s>Iḍā</s> portions are being cut. Therefore the procedure is by word-referent alone.

children.text: mantrasya cārthavattvāt//5.2.12//
children.translated_text: And because of the meaningfulness of the mantra. // MS_5,2.12 //

children.text: evaṃ manotāmantras{*4/556*} tantraṃ bhaviṣyati, itarathā paryāyeṇaiva syāt. tasmād daivatair daivatānāṃ sauviṣṭakṛtaiḥ sauviṣṭakṛtānām, aiḍair aiḍānām iti.
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>manotā</s> mantra will function as a single performance (<s>tantra</s>); otherwise it would [have to be used] in alternation. Therefore, the deity-portions of the deities [together], the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> portions of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛts</s>, and the <s>Iḍā</s> portions of the <s>Iḍās</s>.

NOTES:
[{4/556: Cf. <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.6.10.1}]

children.text: nānābījeṣv ekam ulūkhalaṃ vibhavāt//5.2.13//
children.translated_text: When there are different grains, a single mortar [suffices], because of [its] capacity. // MS_5,2.13 //

children.text: asti rājasūye nānābījeṣṭiḥ, agnaye gṛhapataye sutīnām{*4/557*} aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet, somāya vanaspataye śyāmākaṃ carum ityevamādi{*4/558*}. asti tu tatra prākṛto 'vahantiḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ tatraikam ulūkhalaṃ paryāyeṇa, uta yaugapadyena bahūnīti. kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? yadi kṛṣṇājinādhastaraṇādayaḥ pṛthak padārthāḥ, tato bhedaḥ. atha kṛṣṇājināstaraṇādis taṇḍulanirvṛttyanta ekaḥ padārthaḥ, tatas tantram iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? ekam iti. kutaḥ? paryāyeṇa vibhavāt. ekasyopādānena siddher dvitīyasyopādānam anarthakaṃ syāt. tasmāt tantram iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Rājasūya</s> there is the <s>Nānābīja-iṣṭi</s> (offering with various grains): 'He should offer an eight-potsherd [cake] to <s>Agni Gṛhapati</s> of <s>Sutīnām</s>, a <s>caru</s> (porridge) of <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) to <s>Soma Vanaspati</s>' — and so forth. Now, there is a mortar (<s>ulūkhala</s>) that is archetypal in that [rite]. There a doubt [arises]: is a single mortar [used] in succession, or are many [used] simultaneously? Whence the doubt? If the spreading of the black-antelope skin and such are separate word-referents, then there is differentiation. But if the spreading of the black-antelope skin etc. up to the production of rice grains constitute a single word-referent, then it is a single performance (<s>tantra</s>). What is the prima facie view? A single [mortar]. Why? Because of [its] capacity for successive [use]. Since the purpose is accomplished by employing a single one, the employment of a second would be purposeless. Therefore it is a single performance.

children.text: vivṛddhir vā niyamānupūrvyasya tadarthatvāt//5.2.14//
children.translated_text: Or there should be multiplication [of mortars], because of the fixed sequence being for that purpose. // MS_5,2.14 //

children.text: vivṛddhir ulūkhalānāṃ syāt, niyataṃ hy ānupūrvyaṃ pāṭhakṛtaṃ sahatve saty upapadyate, padārthānāṃ cānusamayaḥ, pṛthakpadārthāś cādhastaraṇādayo yatībhāvasya paryavasānāt, adhastaraṇādibhiś{*4/560*} ca padair abhidhānāt. tasmād vivṛddhir iti.
children.translated_text: There should be multiplication of mortars, for the fixed sequence as established by the recitation-order is possible [only] when there is simultaneity; and there is a procedure by word-referents [i.e., categories], and the spreading of the skin and such are separate word-referents — because the ascetic state (<s>yatībhāva</s>) terminates [each unit], and because the words 'spreading' etc. designate [separate items]. Therefore there should be multiplication.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/560: E2: adhastaraṇādeś}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/560: E2: <s>adhastaraṇādeś</s>}]

children.text: ekaṃ vā taṇḍulabhāvād dhantes tadarthatvāt//5.2.15//
children.translated_text: Or a single [mortar], because of [the process] culminating in rice-grain [production]; the pounding is for that purpose. // MS_5,2.15 //

children.text: ekaṃ volūkhalaṃ paryāyeṇa syāt, eko hy adhastaraṇādis taṇḍulaparyantaḥ padārthaḥ, staraṇādir hanter upakramaḥ phalīkaraṇāntaś ca tasyaiva śeṣaḥ{*4/561*}, yato hantis taṇḍulaniṣpattyarthaḥ. evaṃ staraṇādīnāṃ hanteś ca nādṛṣṭārthatā bhaviṣyati. tasmāt tantram iti.
children.translated_text: Or a single mortar [used] in succession — for the spreading of the skin and such, up to the rice grains, constitute a single word-referent. The spreading and such are the beginning of the pounding, and the husking and such are the completion of that very [process], since the pounding is for the purpose of producing rice grains. Thus for the spreading and such and for the pounding, there would be no unseen purpose. Therefore it is a single performance.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/561: E1 (Fn.): phalīkaraṇādayaś ca tasyaiva viśeṣāḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{4/561: E1 (Fn.): <s>phalīkaraṇādayaś ca tasyaiva viśeṣāḥ</s>}]

children.text: vikāre tv anuyājānāṃ pātrabhedo 'rthabhedāt syāt//5.2.16//
children.translated_text: But in a modification, the vessel for the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings) should be different, because of the difference in purpose. // MS_5,2.16 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ, tatra śrūyate, pṛṣadājyenānuyājān yajatīti{*4/562*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ prayājānuyājānām ekaṃ pātram ājyasya pṛṣadājyasya ca dhāraṇārtham, uta bhidyate? kiṃ prāptam? ekam iti. kutaḥ? prakṛtāv ekam, prakṛtivad ihāpy ekena bhavitavyam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pātrabhedaḥ syāt. kutaḥ? arthabhedāt, śuddhasya prayājā arthaḥ, pṛṣato 'py anuyājāḥ, pṛṣati gṛhyamāṇe [564]{*4/563*} prayājānāṃ vaiguṇyam, śuddhe 'nuyājānām. na caikasmin pātre viviktaṃ śakyaṃ kartum. maryādāyām api kriyamāṇāyāṃ pradīyamānaṃ saṃsṛjyeta. api cākārabhedād upabhṛta upabhṛttvaṃ vihanyeta. prāṇimātrapuṣkarā{*4/564*} hi sā, ekapuṣkarā ca.
athocyeta, pṛṣadājyam apy ājyam eveti na miśratvaṃ doṣāyeti. naitad evam, prakṛtāv utpavanāvekṣaṇayoḥ prayojanam etat, yad ājyasyāpareṇa dravyeṇāsaṃsargaḥ. evaṃ ced anupapannam, yat prayājā pṛṣadājyenejyerann iti. api ca, evaṃ saty avaśyaṃ haviṣaḥ kācin mātrāpanīyate. na ca śakyam, prayājakārye 'vasite 'nuyājārthaṃ grahītum, prakṛtāv ekakālaṃ grahaṇam. ihāpy ekakālam eva kartavyam. tasmāt pātrabheda iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the animal sacred to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> (<s>Agnīṣomīya</s>). There it is heard: 'He offers the <s>anuyājas</s> with <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curd-mixed ghee).' There a doubt [arises]: should there be a single vessel for the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) of the <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings) and the <s>pṛṣadājya</s> of the <s>anuyājas</s>, or should they be separated? What is the prima facie view? A single [vessel]. Why? In the basic rite there is one, and here too there should be one as in the basic rite.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: there should be a separation of vessels. Why? Because of the difference in purpose — the <s>prayājas</s> are the purpose of the pure [ghee], while the <s>anuyājas</s> [are the purpose] of the <s>pṛṣat</s> (curd-mixed [ghee]). [564] When the <s>pṛṣat</s> is being taken, there would be contamination of the <s>prayājas</s>; when pure [ghee is taken], [contamination] of the <s>anuyājas</s>. And in a single vessel, separation cannot be maintained. Even if a boundary is made, what is being poured would mix [with the other]. Moreover, because of the difference in form, the <s>upabhṛt</s> (secondary ladle) would lose its <s>upabhṛt</s>-nature. For it has a single bowl of palm-measure, and [only] one bowl.
If it were said that <s>pṛṣadājya</s> too is indeed <s>ājya</s> (ghee), so mixing is not a fault — this is not so. In the basic rite, the purpose of the straining and inspection [of ghee] is this: that the <s>ājya</s> should not be mixed with another substance. If this is so, then it would be unfitting that the <s>prayājas</s> be offered with <s>pṛṣadājya</s>. Moreover, if this is the case, necessarily some portion of the oblation must be removed [from the vessel]. And it is not possible, when the <s>prayāja</s>-purpose has been completed, to take [ghee] for the <s>anuyāja</s>-purpose — in the basic rite, the taking is at a single time. Here too it must be done at a single time. Therefore there should be separation of vessels.

NOTES:
[{4/562: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.3.11.6}]
[{4/563: E2: 5,140; E6: 2,83}]
[{4/564: E2: <s>pāṇimātrapuṣkarā</s>}]

children.text: prakṛte pūrvoktatvād apūrvam ante syān na hy acoditasya śeṣāmnānam//5.2.17//
children.translated_text: In the basic rite, what has been stated earlier [comes first]; the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) [element] should be at the end — for the remainder-recitation of what has not been enjoined [would not be appropriate]. // MS_5,2.17 //

children.text: agnau{*4/565*} nakṣatreṣṭyāṃ{*4/566*} śrūyate, agnaye kṛttikābhyaḥ puroḍāśam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped{*4/567*}. so 'tra jūhoti, agnaye svāhā, kṛttikābhyaḥ svāhetyevamādi{*4/568*} homāḥ samāmnātāḥ. santi tu prakṛtau nāriṣṭahomāḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ nāriṣṭahomāḥ pūrvam, utopahomā iti saṃśaye ucyate, prākṛtaṃ pūrvam, vaikṛtam ante syād iti. kutaḥ? coditasya paripūrṇasya śeṣa āmnāyate, yathā jātasya putrasya krīḍanakam.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Agni-Nakṣatra-iṣṭi</s> (fire-constellation offering) it is heard: 'He should offer an eight-potsherd <s>puroḍāśa</s> to <s>Agni</s> [presiding over] the <s>Kṛttikās</s>.' There [it continues]: 'He offers there: "To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!"' — and such supplementary offerings (<s>upahoma</s>) are recorded. Now, in the basic rite there are <s>nāriṣṭa</s> (apotropaic) offerings. There a doubt [arises]: do the <s>nāriṣṭa</s> offerings [come] first, or the supplementary offerings? Given the doubt, it is said: the archetypal [element comes] first, and the modified [element] should be at the end. Why? The remainder is recorded for what has been fully enjoined — like a toy for a child that has [already] been born.

NOTES:
[{4/565: E2 omits <s>agnau</s>}]
[{4/566: E2: <s>nakṣatreṣṭiḥ</s>}]
[{4/567: E2: <s>nirvaped iti</s>}]
[{4/568: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.1.4.1}]
[{4/569: E2: 5,142; E6: 2,83}]

children.text: mukhyānantaryam ātreyas tena tulyaśrutitvād aśabdatvāt prākṛtānāṃ vyavāyaḥ syāt//5.2.18//
children.translated_text: <s>Ātreya</s> [holds that] the immediate proximity to the principal [rite determines order]; therefore, because of equal textual [authority], and because the archetypal [elements] are without [explicit] statement, there would be an intervention [of the modified elements]. // MS_5,2.18 //

children.text: ātreyo manyate sma, mukhyānantaryaṃ vaikṛtasya, paścāt tu prākṛtaṃ prayujyeta. pradhānānantaraṃ vaikṛtasya pāṭhaḥ pratyakṣaḥ, tasmāt pūrvam upahomās tato nāriṣṭhahomā iti. prākṛtānāṃ vyavāyaḥ syāt, yatas te na śrūyante.
children.translated_text: <s>Ātreya</s> held that the modified [element] has immediate proximity to the principal [rite], and the archetypal [element] should be employed afterward. The recitation of the modified [element] immediately after the principal [rite] is directly perceived. Therefore the supplementary offerings [come] first, then the <s>nāriṣṭa</s> offerings. There would be an intervention of the archetypal [elements], since they are not [explicitly] heard [in that position].

children.text: ante tu bādarāyaṇas teṣāṃ pradhānaśabdatvāt//5.2.19//
children.translated_text: But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds that the modified elements come] at the end, because of [the archetypal elements] being grasped by the word of the principal [rite]. // MS_5,2.19 //

children.text: bādarāyaṇas tv ācāryo manyate sma, ante vaikṛtānāṃ prayoga iti. kutaḥ? pradhānaśabdagṛhītatvāt, prākṛtānām aṅgānām pradhānaśabdagṛhītatvam, tatpradhānaśabdagṛhītāni hi prākṛtāny aṅgāni, tasmāc ca pradhānaśabdāt param etat, so 'tra juhoty agnaye svāhā kṛttikābhyaḥ svāhetyevamādi. tasmāt pratyakṣād eva kramān nāriṣṭahomebhyaḥ parāṃ copahomā iti.
children.translated_text: But the teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> held that the modified [elements] should be employed at the end. Why? Because the archetypal subsidiary elements are grasped by the word of the principal [rite] — indeed, the archetypal subsidiary elements are grasped by the word of the principal [rite]. And after that word of the principal [rite], this [comes]: 'He offers there: "To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!"' — and so forth. Therefore, from the directly perceived sequence, the supplementary offerings come after the <s>nāriṣṭa</s> offerings.

children.text: tayā cānyārthadarśanam//5.2.20//
children.translated_text: And [the observation of something serving] another purpose [confirms] this. // MS_5,2.20 //

children.text: anyārtho 'pi caitam arthaṃ darśayati, adhvarasya pūrvam athāgner upapraity etat karma, yad agnikarmeti. paścāt samāmnātasya paścāt prayogaṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: What serves another purpose also shows this meaning: 'First [comes] the ritual of the <s>Adhvara</s> (sacrifice), then [the ritualist] approaches the fire-ritual — that action which is the fire-ritual [comes afterward].' This shows that what is recorded afterward is employed afterward.

children.text: kṛtadeśāt tu pūrveṣāṃ sa deśaḥ syāt tena pratyakṣasaṃyogān nyāyamātram itarat//5.2.21//
children.translated_text: But because of the place of what has [already] been accomplished, the former [elements take] that place — because of the direct connection with perception, the other is mere reasoning. // MS_5,2.21 //

children.text: rājasūye śrūyate, akṣair dīvyati śaunaḥśeṣam{*4/570*} ākhyāpayati, abhi[566]{*4/571*}ṣicyata iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ devanādīnām{*4/572*} ante prayogaḥ, utābhiṣekāt pūrvam iti. kiṃ prāptam? ante tu bādarāyaṇa ity ante prayogaḥ kartavya iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, kṛtadeśād abhiṣekāt pūrvaṃ tu prayogaḥ, kṛtadeśo hy abhiṣekaḥ, māhendrasya stotraṃ pratyabhiṣicyata iti pratyakṣānugrahāyābhiṣekāt pūrvaṃ prayoktavyam. nyāyamātram itarat, ante tu bādarāyaṇa iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Rājasūya</s> it is heard: 'He plays with dice, has the <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> [legend] narrated, [566] is consecrated (<s>abhiṣicyate</s>).' There a doubt [arises]: should the dice-playing and such be performed at the end, or before the consecration? What is the prima facie view? '[The modified elements come] at the end' — according to <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, the performance should be at the end. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: because of the place of what has been accomplished, the performance is before the consecration. For the consecration has a fixed place — 'He is consecrated at the <s>Māhendra</s> hymn of praise' — [so] for the sake of direct textual support, it should be employed before the consecration. The other [view that places it at the end] is mere reasoning — '[the modified elements come] at the end' according to <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{4/570: E1: śaunaḥśepam; E6: śaunaḥśepham}*
*{4/571: E2: 5,143; E6: 2,84}*
*{4/572: E2: videvanādīnām}*

children.text: prākṛtāc ca purastād yat//5.2.22//
children.translated_text: And because [it is stated] before the archetypal [element]. // MS_5,2.22 //

children.text: asti agniḥ, ya evaṃ vidvān agniṃ cinuta iti{*4/573*}. tatra dīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ pūrvaṃ sāvitrahomāḥ, ukhāsaṃbharaṇam, iṣṭakāḥ paśuś cety etad āmnātam. kiṃ tad eva pūrvaṃ kartavyam, uta dīkṣaṇīyeti. kiṃ prāptam? vaikṛtānām ante prayogaḥ, ante tu bādarāyaṇa iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pūrvaṃ sāvitrahomāḥ, iṣṭakāḥ, paśur ukhāsaṃbharaṇaṃ ca. kutaḥ? pratyakṣapāṭhāt, punas tatra dīkṣaṇīyāmnātā, tasyāś ca purastāt sāvitrahomāḥ, iṣṭakāḥ paśur ukhāsaṃbharaṇaṃ ca. tasmāt teṣāṃ pūrvaṃ prayoga iti.
children.translated_text: There is the fire[-altar ritual]: 'He who, knowing thus, builds the fire[-altar].' There, before the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration offering), the <s>Sāvitra</s> offerings, the collecting of the pot (<s>ukhā-saṃbharaṇa</s>), the bricks, and the animal are recorded. Should those very [elements] be performed first, or the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>? What is the prima facie view? The modified [elements] are employed at the end — '[modified elements come] at the end' according to <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: first [come] the <s>Sāvitra</s> offerings, the bricks, the animal, and the collecting of the pot. Why? Because of the directly perceived recitation-order — moreover, there the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> is recorded, and before it [are] the <s>Sāvitra</s> offerings, the bricks, the animal, and the collecting of the pot. Therefore their performance is first.
