children.text: saṃnipātaś ced yathoktam ante syāt//5.2.23//
children.translated_text: If there is a convergence [of both types], [the performance] should be as stated [in the text], at the end. // MS_5,2.23 //

children.text:
agnau dīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ parato rukmapratimocanādy āmnātam, [567]{*4/574*} tasminn eva krame codakena dīkṣitasaṃskārāḥ prāptāḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim aniyamaḥ, uta pūrvaṃ rukmapratimocanādi, uta dīkṣitasaṃskārā iti. kiṃ prāptam? aniyamaḥ. athavā, yathā pratyakṣapāṭhakramād dīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ purata ukhāsaṃbharaṇādayaḥ, evaṃ rukmapratimocanādīnīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, dīkṣitasaṃskārāḥ pūrvaṃ kartavyā iti. kutaḥ? dīkṣaṇīyāṃ prati yaḥ pāṭhakramaḥ, yathā ca codakaḥ, tathobhaye 'pi parastād dīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ kāryāḥ. yas teṣāṃ parasparāpekṣaḥ kramaḥ, tatra na kaścid ukhāsaṃbharaṇasyeva pratyakṣaḥ pāṭhakramaḥ pūrvatvaṃ sādhayati. asti tu saṃskāraṇāṃ prakṛtau pūrvaṃ pāṭhaḥ, vikṛtau rukmapratimocanasyottaraḥ, tena yathokta eva kramaḥ syāt, ante vaikṛtam iti. atha kim arthaṃ saṃnipāta āśaṅkyate? nanv ayaṃ saṃnipāta eva vyaktaḥ. asaṃdigdhe saṃdigdhavacanam etat. yathā -
children.translated_text:
In the fire[-altar ritual], after the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>, the releasing of the gold piece (<s>rukma-pratimocana</s>) and such are recorded; [567] and in that very sequence, the consecrated-one's purificatory rites (<s>dīkṣita-saṃskāras</s>) are obtained through the injunction. There a doubt [arises]: is there no fixed rule, or do the <s>rukma-pratimocana</s> and such [come] first, or the purificatory rites of the consecrated one? What is the prima facie view? No fixed rule. Or alternatively, just as from the directly perceived recitation-order the collecting of the pot and such [come] before the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>, so too the <s>rukma-pratimocana</s> and such [should come first].
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: the purificatory rites of the consecrated one should be performed first. Why? With respect to the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>, there is the recitation-order, and as the injunction [shows], both should be performed after the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>. As for their mutual sequence — there is no directly perceived recitation-order [such as existed] for the collecting of the pot that establishes priority. But there is the recitation of the purificatory rites earlier in the basic rite, and the <s>rukma-pratimocana</s> later in the modification — therefore the sequence should be as stated: the modified [element] at the end. But why is the convergence doubted? Is not this convergence quite evident? This is a statement of doubt in a case that is undoubted. Just as [the verse]:

children.text:
ījānā bahubhir yajñair brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ/
śāstrāṇi cet pramāṇaṃ syuḥ, prāptās te paramāṃ gatim// iti.
children.translated_text:
'<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who have sacrificed with many sacrifices, who have reached the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s> —
if the <s>śāstras</s> are indeed authoritative, they have attained the supreme goal.'

children.text: tasmān na doṣa iti.
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no fault.

children.text: Adhyāya 5:
children.translated_text: Chapter 5:

children.text: vivṛddhiḥ karmabhedāt pṛṣadājyavat tasya tasyopadiśyeta{*5/2*} // MS_5,3.1 //
children.translated_text: There should be multiplication [of ritual implements], because of the difference in ritual acts — like the <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curd-mixed ghee); [specifics] should be taught for each [individual case]. // MS_5,3.1 //

children.text: agnīṣomīye paśau śrūyate{*5/3*}, ekādaśa prayājān yajati{*5/4*}, ekādaśānuyājān yajatīti{*5/5*}. cāturmāsyeṣu, nava{*5/6*} prayājān yajati, navānuyājān yajatīti{*5/7*}. agnau śrūyate, ṣaḍ upasada iti{*5/8*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ prati prayājam ekādaśasaṃkhyā praty anuyājaṃ ca, tathā cāturmāsyeṣu navasaṃkhyā, tathāgnau copasatsu ṣaṭsaṃkhyā, uta sarvasaṃpādyā saṃkhyeti. kiṃ prāptam? pratipradhānaṃ saṃkhyā bhidyata iti. kutaḥ? bhinnāni hi tāni karmāṇi, tāni ca pradhānāni prati, saṃkhyā śrūyate. pradhānasaṃnidhau ca guṇaḥ śiṣyamāṇāḥ pratidhānaṃ bhidyate, yathā{*5/9*} pṛṣadājyenānuyājān yajatīti pratyanuyājaṃ pṛṣattā guṇo bhidyate, evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice] it is heard: 'He performs eleven <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings)'; 'He performs eleven <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings).' In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites: 'He performs nine <s>prayājas</s>; he performs nine <s>anuyājas</s>.' Regarding the fire [altar], it is heard: 'Six <s>Upasads</s> (preparatory observances).' There a doubt [arises]: does the number eleven apply to each <s>prayāja</s> and each <s>anuyāja</s> [individually], and likewise the number nine in the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s>, and the number six for the <s>Upasads</s> in the fire [altar] — or is the number to be fulfilled collectively? What is the prima facie view? The number is divided per principal [rite]. Why? For those ritual acts are distinct, and the number is heard with reference to those principals. And a subsidiary prescribed in proximity to a principal is divided per principal — just as 'he offers the <s>anuyājas</s> with <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curd-mixed ghee),' the quality of being mixed with curds is divided per each <s>anuyāja</s> — so here too.

children.text: api vā sarvasaṃkhyatvād vikāraḥ pratīyeta // MS_5,3.2 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the number being collective, the modification should be understood [accordingly]. // MS_5,3.2 //

children.text: sarvasaṃpādyā saṃkhyā kalpyeta. kutaḥ? pṛthaktvaniveśinī hi saṃkhyāsati pṛthaktve 'bhyāsena kalpyeta, yāvaty asaṃbhavo bhedasya, tāvaty evābhyasyeta{*5/10*}, yāvati saṃbhavati, tāvati pṛthaktvaniveśa eva nyāyyaḥ, tasmāt sarvasaṃpādyaiva saṃkhyā. yat tu, pṛṣadājyavad iti, na, pṛṣattā ekasya na saṃbhavati, nāsau pṛthaktvaniveṣinī. na ca, ekasya kriyamāṇā sarveṣāṃ tantreṇopakarotīti{*5/11*}. [569]{*5/12*} tasmād avaśyaṃ bhettavyā, tantreṇa tūpakaroti saṃkhyā. itarāpekṣā hi sā bhavati. evaṃ sati sahatvasya prāpakaḥ prayogavacano 'nugrahīṣyata iti.
children.translated_text: The number should be arranged as collectively fulfilled. Why? For number, which inhabits distinctness, when distinctness is not [possible], should be fulfilled through repetition. As far as the division is impossible, that much should be repeated; as far as [the division] is possible, the inhabiting of distinctness alone is proper. Therefore the number is indeed collectively fulfilled. As for [the analogy] 'like the <s>pṛṣadājya</s>' — no, the quality of being mixed with curds is not possible for a single [offering]; it is not something that inhabits distinctness. Nor can it, when applied to one, benefit all [the others] through unified performance (<s>tantra</s>). Therefore [the curd-quality] must necessarily be divided. But the number benefits through unified performance, for it [the number] is dependent on the other [elements]. This being so, the statement about performance that establishes simultaneity will be supported.

children.text: svasthānāt tu vivṛdhyeran{*5/13*} kṛtānupūrvyatvāt // MS_5,3.3 //
children.translated_text: But they should increase from their own positions, because of the order being [already] established. // MS_5,3.3 //

children.text:
upasatsu saṃdehaḥ. kim āvṛttir daṇḍakalitavat, uta svasthānād vivardhanta iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? āvartanīyānām arthānām eṣa dharmaḥ, yad uta daṇḍakalitavat. yo hy ucyate, trir anuvākaḥ paṭhyatām iti, sa ādita ārabhya parisamāpya punar ādita ārabhyate, tasmād daṇḍakalitavad āvṛttiḥ.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, svasthānād vivardhitum arhati. kutaḥ? kṛtānupūrvyatvāt, kṛtam ānupūrvyam upasatsu, prathamāṃ kṛtvā madhyamā kartavyā, tata uttameti. tatra yadi daṇḍakalitavad āvṛttiḥ syāt, uttamāṃ kṛtvā punarādyāyā abhyāse kriyamāṇe 'sthāne sā vivṛddhiḥ kṛtā bhavati. svasthānavivṛddhau naiṣa doṣaḥ. tasmāt svasthāne vivṛddhir iti.
children.translated_text:
Regarding the <s>Upasads</s>, a doubt [arises]: is the repetition like the staff-and-engraving [method] (i.e., returning to the beginning each time), or do they increase from their own positions? What is the prima facie view? This is the nature of things that are to be repeated — namely, like the staff-and-engraving [method]. For when one says 'let the chapter be recited three times,' one begins from the beginning, completes it, and begins again from the beginning. Therefore the repetition is like the staff-and-engraving [method].
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: they should properly increase from their own positions. Why? Because of the order being [already] established — the sequence has been established for the <s>Upasads</s>: having performed the first, the middle one should be performed, then the last. There, if the repetition were like the staff-and-engraving [method], then after performing the last, when the first is repeated again, the augmentation would be done out of its [proper] place. In augmentation from one's own position, this defect does not arise. Therefore the augmentation is from one's own position.

children.text: samidhyamānavatīṃ samiddhavatīṃ cāntareṇa dhāyyāḥ syur dyāvāpṛthivyor antarāle samarhaṇāt // MS_5,3.4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dhāyyās</s> (inserted verses) should be placed between the [verse with] '<s>samidhyamānavatī</s>' and the [verse with] '<s>samiddhavatī</s>', because of the praise [of the space] between heaven and earth. // MS_5,3.4 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ sāmidhenyaḥ sāmidhenīr anvāheti{*5/14*}. [570]{*5/15*} tatra kāmyāḥ sāmidhenīkalpāḥ, ekaviṃśatim anubrūyāt pratiṣṭhākāmasyety{*5/16*}evamādayaḥ, tatrāgamena saṃkhyā pūraṇaṃ vakṣyate{*5/17*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim āgantūnām ante niveśaḥ, uta samidhyamānavatīṃ{*5/18*} samiddhavatīṃ{*5/19*} cāntareṇa niveśa iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? ante niveśaḥ, ante tu bādarāyaṇaḥ{*5/20*}, ity anena nyāyeneti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, samidhyamānavatīṃ samiddhavatīṃ cāntareṇa niveśa iti. kutaḥ? dyāvāpṛthivyor antarāle samarhaṇāt saṃstavād ity arthaḥ{*5/21*}. iyaṃ vai samidhyamānavatī{*5/22*}, asau samiddhavatī{*5/23*}, yad antarā, tad dhāyyā, ity antarikṣasaṃstute{*5/24*} 'sminn{*5/25*} antarāle vidhīyante. tasmān nānte syur iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> (kindling verses) [are recited]: 'He recites the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> (kindling verses).' There, optional <s>sāmidhenī</s> arrangements are found, such as 'He should recite twenty-one [verses] for one desiring a firm foundation,' etc. There, the filling of the number by augmentation (<s>āgama</s>) will be stated [later]. There a doubt [arises]: should the added [verses] be placed at the end, or between the [verse with] '<s>samidhyamānavatī</s>' and the [verse with] '<s>samiddhavatī</s>'? What is the prima facie view? Placement at the end, following the principle '[<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> says] at the end.' Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: they should be placed between the [verse with] '<s>samidhyamānavatī</s>' and the [verse with] '<s>samiddhavatī</s>.' Why? Because of the praise [of the space] between heaven and earth — meaning, because of the eulogy (<s>saṃstava</s>). 'This [earth] is indeed the [verse with] <s>samidhyamānavatī</s>; that [heaven] is the [verse with] <s>samiddhavatī</s>; what is in between — those are the <s>dhāyyās</s>' — being praised in connection with the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>), they are prescribed in this interval. Therefore they should not be at the end.

children.text: tacchabdo vā // MS_5,3.5 //
children.translated_text: Or [they are placed] because of the word [<s>dhāyyā</s>]. // MS_5,3.5 //

children.text:
atha vā yā dhāyyāśabdikāḥ, tās tatra bhavitum arhanti. tena hi śabdena tatra saṃstavaḥ, saṃstavāc ca vidhānam, yathā, pṛthupājavatyau{*5/26*} dhāyye, uṣṇikkakubhau dhyāyye iti. kāḥ punar etā dhāyyā iti{*5/27*} nāma? nāsya śabdasya prasiddhim upalabhāmahe. ucyate, sāmidhenyo dhyāyyāḥ. kutaḥ? evaṃ hi bhagavataḥ pāṇiner vacanam - pāyyasāṃnāyyanikāyyadhāyyā mānahavirnivāsasāmidhenīṣv{*5/28*} iti, asmād vacanāc chrutim anumimīmahe. katamāsu sāmidhenīṣv iti. ucyate, aviśeṣāt sarvāsvati gamyate. iha tu samidhyamānavatīṃ samiddhavatīṃ cāntareṇa dhyāyyāḥ syur iti. sarvāsu sāmidhenīṣu satīsu dhyāyyāvacanād viśiṣṭānāṃ sāmidhenīnāṃ dhāyyāśabda iti gamyate.
nanu pāṇinivacanād viśeṣeṇa sarvā dhāyyāḥ. nety āha, viśiṣṭāsv api vacanam upapadyata eva. yadi viśiṣṭāḥ, tataḥ [571]{*5/29*} kā iti. ucyate, yāsu dhāyyāśabdaḥ śrūyate, tās tāvad dhāyyāḥ. tāsu ca dhāyyāsu satīṣu vacanam arthavad bhavati. arthavati ca sati vacane nānyā dhāyyāḥ, pramāṇābhāvād iti.
children.translated_text:
Alternatively, those that bear the designation '<s>dhāyyā</s>' should be placed there. For by that word, there is a eulogy there, and from the eulogy, a prescription [follows] — as in 'the <s>Pṛthupājā</s> verses are <s>dhāyyās</s>; the <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> [verses] are <s>dhāyyās</s>.' But what indeed are these '<s>dhāyyās</s>' by name? We do not find any established [meaning] for this word. We reply: the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> are <s>dhāyyās</s>. How do we know? For thus is the statement of the venerable <s>Pāṇini</s>: '<s>pāyya</s>, <s>sāṃnāyya</s>, <s>nikāyya</s>, <s>dhāyyā</s>, <s>māna</s>, <s>havis</s>, <s>nivāsa</s>, <s>sāmidhenī</s>' — from this statement we infer the [Vedic] usage. In which <s>sāmidhenīs</s> [does this apply]? We reply: since there is no specification, it is understood [to apply] to all. But here [it is stated]: 'The <s>dhāyyās</s> should be between the [verse with] <s>samidhyamānavatī</s> and the [verse with] <s>samiddhavatī</s>.' Since among all the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> the word '<s>dhāyyā</s>' is applied, it is understood that the designation '<s>dhāyyā</s>' belongs to the specified <s>sāmidhenīs</s>.
[The objector says:] but from <s>Pāṇini</s>'s statement, all [sāmidhenīs] are specifically <s>dhāyyās</s>. Not so, he says — the statement is appropriate even for the specified ones. If [they are] specified, then which [are they]? We reply: those in which the word '<s>dhāyyā</s>' is heard — those at least are <s>dhāyyās</s>. And when those <s>dhāyyās</s> exist, the statement becomes meaningful. And when the statement is meaningful, there are no other <s>dhāyyās</s>, since there is no authoritative basis [for extending the term].

children.text: uṣṇikkakubhor ante darśanāt // MS_5,3.6 //
children.translated_text: Because the <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> [verses] are seen at the end. // MS_5,3.6 //

children.text: uṣṇikkakubhoḥ ca ante prayogo dṛśyate, yaj jagatyā paridadhyād antaṃ{*5/30*} yajñaṃ gacchet, atha yat triṣṭubhā paridadhāti nāntaṃ gacchatīti. nanu triṣṭub atrānte dṛśyate, noṣṇikkakubhāv iti. ucyate, triṣṭubham evāyam uṣṇikkakumāv iti brūte. katham? triṣṭubho vīryam ity evaṃ ante{*5/31*} saṃstuteḥ, triṣṭubho vā etad vīryaṃ yad uṣṇikkakubhāv iti kāraṇe kāryavad upacāraḥ kṛtaḥ//
children.translated_text: And the employment of the <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> [verses] is seen at the end: 'If he were to enclose with the <s>Jagatī</s> [meter], he would go to the end of the sacrifice; but when he encloses with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, he does not go to the end.' Now, it is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> that is seen here at the end, not the <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s>. We reply: this [passage] speaks of the <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> as the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. How? Because of the eulogy at the end [which states:] 'the power of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>' — 'the <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> are indeed the power of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>' — a figurative usage of the effect for the cause has been employed.

*{5/31: E2 om. ante}*

children.text: stomavivṛddhau bahiṣpavamāne purastāt paryāsād āgantavaḥ syus tathā hi iṣṭaṃ dvādaśāhe // MS_5,3.7 //
children.translated_text: In <s>stoma</s>-augmentation, the added [chants] in the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> should be before the concluding portion (<s>paryāsa</s>), for thus it is observed in the twelve-day [sacrifice]. // MS_5,3.7 //

children.text: santi vivṛddhastomakāḥ kratavaḥ, ekaviṃśenātirātreṇa prajākāmaṃ yājayeyus{*5/32*} triṇavenaujaskāmaṃ trayastriṃśena pratiṣṭhākāmam iti{*5/33*}. tatrāgamena saṃkhyā pūraṇaṃ vakṣyate{*5/34*}. atha bahiṣpavamāne vaikṛteṣv ānīyamāneṣu bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ vaikṛtānām ante niveśaḥ, uta prāk paryāsād iti. kiṃ prāptam? purastāt paryāsād āgantavaḥ syuḥ. tathā hi dṛṣṭaṃ dvādaśāhe, stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ, vṛṣaṇvantastṛcā bhavanti. tṛca uttamaḥ paryāsa iti, ihāpi prāk paryāsād āgantubhir bhavitavyam.
children.translated_text: There are sacrifices with augmented <s>stomas</s> (chant-structures): 'One should have one desiring progeny sacrifice with the twenty-one[-versed] <s>Atirātra</s>; one desiring vigor, with the <s>Triṇava</s> [stoma]; one desiring a firm foundation, with the thirty-three[-versed stoma].' There, the filling of the number by augmentation will be stated [later]. Now, when modifications are being introduced in the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> [chant], a doubt arises: should the modifications be placed at the end, or before the concluding portion (<s>paryāsa</s>)? What is the prima facie view? The added [chants] should be before the concluding portion. For thus it is observed in the twelve-day [sacrifice]: 'The <s>stotrīya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> are <s>tṛca</s> (three-verse) [sets]; the <s>Vṛṣaṇvat</s> [verses] are <s>tṛca</s> [sets].' The last <s>tṛca</s> is the concluding portion (<s>paryāsa</s>) — so here too, the added [chants] should be before the concluding portion.

children.text: paryāsa iti cāntākhyā // MS_5,3.8 //
children.translated_text: And the word '<s>paryāsa</s>' denotes 'the end.' // MS_5,3.8 //

children.text: prayāsaśabdaś cāntavacano loke dṛśyate, yathā, kṣetraparyāsaḥ, nadīparyāsa iti. evaṃ paryāso 'nte kṛto bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>paryāsa</s>' is seen in the world as denoting 'end' — as in 'the boundary of the field' (<s>kṣetraparyāsa</s>), 'the bend of the river' (<s>nadīparyāsa</s>). Thus the <s>paryāsa</s> will be [that which is] placed at the end.

children.text: ante vā tad uktam // MS_5,3.9 //
children.translated_text: Or, at the end — that has been stated. // MS_5,3.9 //

children.text: ante vaivaṃjātīyakaṃ vaikṛtaṃ syāt. uktam, ante tu bādarāyaṇa iti{*5/36*}.
children.translated_text: Or, a modification of this kind should be at the end. It has been stated: 'At the end, [says] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>.'

children.text: vacanāt tu dvādaśāhe // MS_5,3.10 //
children.translated_text: But in the twelve-day [sacrifice], because of the [specific] statement. // MS_5,3.10 //

children.text: atha yad uktam{*5/37*}, tathā hi dṛṣṭaṃ{*5/38*} dvādaśāha iti, tat parihartavyam. atrocyate, vacanād dvādaśāhe bhavati, stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ vṛṣaṇvantas tṛcā bhavanti, tṛca uttamaḥ paryāsa iti. na hi vacanasyātibhāro 'sti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'for thus it is observed in the twelve-day [sacrifice]' — that is to be refuted. To this we reply: in the twelve-day [sacrifice], it is because of the [specific] statement — 'the <s>stotrīya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> are <s>tṛca</s> [sets]; the <s>Vṛṣaṇvat</s> [verses] are <s>tṛca</s> [sets]; the last <s>tṛca</s> is the concluding portion.' For there is no straining of the statement [in that case].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/37: Vgl. zu MS 5.3.7}*
*{5/38: E2: hīṣṭaṃ}*
atadvikāraś ca // MS_5,3.11 //
children.translated_text: And [the case at hand] is not a modification of that [twelve-day sacrifice]. // MS_5,3.11 //

children.text: na cāyaṃ tadvikāraḥ, yat tato dharmān gṛhaṇīyād iti.
children.translated_text: And this [case] is not a modification of that [twelve-day sacrifice], such that one could derive rules from it.

children.text: tadvikāre 'py apūrvatvāt // MS_5,3.12 //
children.translated_text: Even in a modification [of it], because of being unprecedented. // MS_5,3.12 //

children.text: yo 'pi tadvikāraḥ, tatrāpy anta eva niveśaḥ. kutaḥ? apūrvāt, vṛṣaṇvatāṃ tṛcānām, vṛṣaṇvanta{*5/39*} eva prākparyāsāt, yāvad vacanaṃ vācanikam, na sadṛśam upasaṃkrāmati.
children.translated_text: Even in what is a modification of that [twelve-day sacrifice], the placement is indeed at the end. Why? Because of the unprecedented nature of the <s>Vṛṣaṇvat</s> <s>tṛca</s> verses — the <s>Vṛṣaṇvat</s> [verses] alone are before the concluding portion, and whatever is stated [specifically] by a [Vedic] statement remains limited to that statement and does not transfer to a similar [case].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/39: E2: vṛṣaṇvantāv}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/39: E2: <s>vṛṣaṇvantāv</s>}]

children.text: ante tūttarayor dadhyāt // MS_5,3.13 //
children.translated_text: But [the added chants] should be placed at the end of the latter two [<s>pavamānas</s>]. // MS_5,3.13 //

children.text: ihāpi vivṛddhastomakāḥ kratava udāharaṇam. tatrottarayoḥ [573]{*5/40*} pavamānayoḥ sāmnām āgama iti vakṣyate{*5/41*}. tatrāgamyamāneṣu sāmasu saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ teṣām ante niveśaḥ, uta gāyatrībṛhatyanuṣṭupsv iti. kiṃ prāptam? anta uttarayor dadhyāt. ukto 'tra nyāyaḥ, ante bādarāyaṇa iti{*5/42*}. tasmād ante niveśa iti.
children.translated_text: Here too, the sacrifices with augmented <s>stomas</s> serve as the example. There, in the latter two <s>pavamānas</s> (purification chants), the augmentation of the <s>sāmans</s> (melodies) will be stated [later]. When the <s>sāmans</s> are being augmented, a doubt [arises]: should they be placed at the end, or among the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meters]? What is the prima facie view? [The added chants] should be placed at the end of the latter two. The principle has been stated here: 'At the end, [says] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>.' Therefore placement is at the end.

children.text: api vā gāyatrībṛhatyanuṣupsu vacanāt // MS_5,3.14 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, [they should be placed] among the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meters], because of the statement. // MS_5,3.14 //

children.text: gāyatrībṛhatyanuṣṭūpsu niveśaḥ. kasmāt? vacanāt, trīṇi ha vai yajñasyodarāṇi gāyatrībṛhatyanuṣṭub iti. atra hy evāvapanti, ata evodvapantīti vacanenāsty upālambhaḥ. tasmān naiṣām ante niveśa iti.
children.translated_text: [They should be placed] among the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. Why? Because of the statement: 'Three are indeed the bellies of the sacrifice — the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.' 'For here they deposit [offerings], and from here they remove [them]' — by this statement there is a basis [for placement there]. Therefore these should not be placed at the end.

children.text: graheṣṭakam aupānuvākyaṃ savanacitiśeṣaḥ syāt // MS_5,3.15 //
children.translated_text: The brick belonging to the cup-offering sequence is related to the <s>aupānuvākya</s> (supplementary recitation) and is a remainder of the pressing and piling. // MS_5,3.15 //

children.text: aupānuvākye kāṇḍe grahā iṣṭakāś ca samāmnātāḥ, eṣa vai haviṣā havir yajate, yo dābhyaṃ{*5/43*} gṛhītvā somāya yajata iti{*5/44*}. tathā, parā vā etasyāyuḥ prāṇa eti yo 'śuṃ gṛhṇātīti. tatheṣṭakāś citriṇīr upadadhāti, vajriṇīr upadadhāti{*5/45*}, bhūteṣṭakā upadadhātīti{*5/46*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ graheṣṭakamaupānuvākyaṃ savanaśeṣaś citiśeṣaś ca. atha kiṃ kratuśeṣo 'gniśeṣaś ceti. [574]{*5/47*} kiṃ prāptam? savanacitiśeṣaḥ. kutaḥ? grahaiḥ savanāny ārabhyante, iṣṭakābhiś citayaḥ, yac ca yenārabhyate tat tad aṅgam.
children.translated_text: In the <s>aupānuvākya</s> (supplementary) section, the cups (<s>grahas</s>) and the bricks (<s>iṣṭakās</s>) are recorded: 'He who, having taken the <s>Dābhya</s> [cup], sacrifices to <s>Soma</s>, sacrifices indeed with an oblation through an oblation.' Likewise, 'The life-breath of one who takes the <s>Aṃśu</s> [cup] departs.' And regarding the bricks: 'He places the <s>citriṇī</s> bricks; he places the <s>vajriṇī</s> bricks; he places the <s>bhūta</s> bricks.' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>aupānuvākya</s> section of cups and bricks a remainder of the pressings (<s>savana</s>) and of the fire-altar layers (<s>citi</s>), or a remainder of the sacrifice (<s>kratu</s>) and of the fire (<s>agni</s>) [respectively]? What is the prima facie view? It is a remainder of the pressings and layers. Why? The pressings are commenced by means of cups, and the layers by means of bricks; and that by which something is commenced is its subsidiary.

NOTES:
[{5/43: E2: <s>'dābhyam</s>}]
[{5/44: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.3.4.3}]
[{5/45: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.7.3.1}]
[{5/46: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.6.3.1}]
[{5/47: E2: 5,151; E6: 2,89}]

children.text: kratvagniśeṣo vā coditatvād acodanānupūrvasya // MS_5,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a remainder of the sacrifice and the fire, because of [the cups and bricks] being enjoined, [while] the order of the non-enjoined [pressings and layers is secondary]. // MS_5,3.16 //

children.text: kratvagniśeṣaḥ syāt. kutaḥ? coditatvāt, agniś cetavyaḥ śrūyate, ya evaṃ{*5/48*} vidvān agniṃ cinuta iti{*5/49*}. na citiś cetavyā, iṣṭakācayanenāgniś cetavyaḥ śrūyate, agnim iti dvitīyānirdeśāt. tathā, yo dābhyaṃ{*5/50*} gṛhītvā somāya yajata ity adābhyasya yajatinā saṃbandhaḥ, tathāṃśoḥ. tasmāt sakṛd yāgasaṃbandhaṃ kṛtvā kṛtārthaḥ śabdo bhavati, śrutaṃ saṃbandham abhinirvartya. tathā sakṛd agnisaṃbandhaṃ kṛtvā kṛtī manyeta, acodanā citisavanayoḥ, na hi te kartavyatayā codyete, parārthaṃ hi tayoḥ śravaṇam. kiṃ prayojanam? savanacitiśeṣatve, pratisavanaṃ grahaṇam, praticiti ceṣṭakopadhānam. kratvagniśeṣatve sakṛd grahaṇopadhāne.
children.translated_text: It would be a remainder of the sacrifice and the fire. Why? Because of [their] being enjoined. The fire is heard as that which is to be built: 'He who, knowing thus, builds the fire.' It is not the layer that is to be built; rather, the fire is heard as that which is to be built by means of brick-laying — because of the accusative designation 'the fire' (<s>agnim</s>). Likewise, 'He who, having taken the <s>Dābhya</s> [cup], sacrifices to <s>Soma</s>' — the <s>Dābhya</s> has a connection with the sacrifice (<s>yajati</s>); so too the <s>Aṃśu</s>. Therefore, having once established the connection with the sacrifice, the word fulfills its purpose — having accomplished the heard connection. Likewise, having once established the connection with the fire, one should consider oneself fulfilled. The pressings and layers are not enjoined [independently] — they are not enjoined as things to be done; for they are heard for another's purpose. What is the practical consequence? If [they are] a remainder of the pressings and layers, then the taking [of cups] is repeated for each pressing, and the placement of bricks for each layer. If a remainder of the sacrifice and fire, the taking and placement are done once only.

NOTES:
[{5/48: E2: <s>ya ca evaṃ</s>}]
[{5/49: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.5.2.1}]
[{5/50: E2: <s>'dābhyaṃ</s>}]

children.text: ante syur avyavāyāt // MS_5,3.17 //
children.translated_text: [They] would be at the end, because of non-interruption. // MS_5,3.17 //

children.text: aupānuvākye śrūyate, citriṇīr upadadhāti, vajriṇīr upadadhātīti{*5/51*}. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim etāḥ pañcabhyāṃ citāv upadheyāḥ, uta madhyamāyām iti. kiṃ prāptam? pañcabhyām eveṣṭakāḥ kṛtakramāḥ, anyā naitābhir vyaveṣyante.
children.translated_text: In the <s>aupānuvākya</s> section it is heard: 'He places the <s>citriṇī</s> bricks; he places the <s>vajriṇī</s> bricks.' There a doubt [arises]: should these be placed in five layers, or in the middle [layer]? What is the prima facie view? The bricks, having a fixed order, [are placed] in the five [layers] only; other [bricks] would not be interspersed with these.

NOTES:
[{5/51: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.7.3.1}]

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_5,3.18 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_5,3.18 //

children.text: āvapanaṃ vottamā citiḥ. anyā iṣṭakā upadadhātīti.
children.translated_text: Or the last layer is the filling. [It is said:] 'He places other bricks.'

children.text: madhyamāyāṃ tu vacanād brāhmaṇavatyaḥ // MS_5,3.19 //
children.translated_text: But [they are placed] in the middle [layer], because of the statement, [since] they are bricks with <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passages]. // MS_5,3.19 //

children.text: naivaitāntyāyāṃ citau. kasyāṃ tarhi? madhyamāyām. kutaḥ? brāhmaṇavatya etā iṣṭakāḥ, tāsāṃ madhyamā citir āmnāyate. yāṃ vai kāṃcid brāhmaṇavatīm iṣṭakām abhijānīyāt, tāṃ madhyamāyāṃ citāv upadadhyād iti. nanu sarvā eveṣṭakā brāhmaṇavatyaḥ. nety āha, aparā liṅgakramāt samākhyānāc ca. tasmād etā nānte syur iti.
children.translated_text: Not in the last layer at all. In which then? In the middle. Why? These bricks have <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passages], and the middle layer is recorded for them: 'Whatever brick that has a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage] one identifies, that he should place in the middle layer.' [The objector says:] but all bricks have <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passages. He replies: no — the other [bricks are differentiated] because of the indicatory-mark sequence and because of the designation. Therefore these should not be at the end.

children.text: prāg lokaṃpṛṇāyās tasyāḥ saṃpūraṇārthatvāt // MS_5,3.20 //
children.translated_text: Before the <s>Lokaṃpṛṇā</s> [brick], because of its being for the purpose of filling. // MS_5,3.20 //

children.text: aupānuvākye kāṇḍa iṣṭakāḥ samāmnātāḥ, vajriṇīr upadadhāti, citriṇīr upadadhāti{*5/53*}, bhūteṣṭakā upadadhātīti{*5/54*}. tatredaṃ samadhigatam, madhyamāyāṃ citāv upadheyā iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ prāg lokāṃpṛṇāyāḥ, uta paścād iti{*5/55*}. kiṃ prāptam? ante tu bādarāyaṇa iti{*5/56*}. evaṃ prāpte, ucyate, prāg lokaṃpṛṇāyāḥ tasyāḥ saṃpūraṇārthatvāt, saṃpūraṇārthatā tasyāḥ śrūyate, yad evāsyonam, yac chidram, tad anayā{*5/57*} pūrayati, lokaṃ pṛṇa, chidraṃ pṛṇa iti{*5/58*}. apūrvatvāc vārthasya{*5/59*}, vidhir evāyaṃ saṃstaveneti{*5/60*} gamyate. tasmāt prāg lokaṃpṛṇāyāḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>aupānuvākya</s> section, bricks are recorded: 'He places the <s>vajriṇī</s> bricks; he places the <s>citriṇī</s> bricks; he places the <s>bhūta</s> bricks.' There it has been understood that they are to be placed in the middle layer. There a doubt [arises]: before the <s>Lokaṃpṛṇā</s> [brick], or after? What is the prima facie view? At the end, according to <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>. Given this prima facie view, we say: before the <s>Lokaṃpṛṇā</s>, because of its being for the purpose of filling. Its filling purpose is heard: 'Whatever is deficient in this [altar], whatever gap there is — that he fills with this [brick]. Fill the world, fill the gap.' Or because of the unprecedented nature of the meaning, this is understood to be an injunction itself by means of the <s>saṃstava</s> (praise). Therefore [these bricks] should be before the <s>Lokaṃpṛṇā</s>.

NOTES:
[{5/53: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.7.3.1}]
[{5/54: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.6.3.1}]
[{5/55: Cf. <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 4.2.4.4}]
[{5/56: Cf. on MS 5.2.19}]
[{5/57: E2: <s>tad etayā</s>}]
[{5/58: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 4.2.4.4}]
[{5/59: E2: <s>cārthasya</s>}]
[{5/60: E2: <s>saṃstavo neti</s>}]
[{5/61: E2: 5,152; E6: 2,90}]

children.text: saṃskṛte karma saṃskārāṇāṃ tadarthatvāt // MS_5,3.21 //
children.translated_text: The ritual action [takes place] when [the fires are] consecrated, because the preparatory rites are for that [ritual action's] purpose. // MS_5,3.21 //

children.text:
ādhāne santi pavamāneṣṭayaḥ. santi ca niyatāni karmāṇi, agnihotrādīni. aniyatāni caindrāgnādīni. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ pavamāneṣṭīḥ kṛtvā karmāṇi pratipattavyāni, utāhitamātreṣv agniṣv iti. kiṃ prāptam? āhitapātreṣv iti. kutaḥ? āhitamātreṣv asāv agniṣu karmāṇi kartuṃ samartho bhavati, yathā, āhitāgnir na klinnaṃ dārvā dadhyād iti. darśayati{*5/62*} ca, agniṃ vai sṛṣṭam agnihotreṇānudravantīty āhitamātreṣv agnihotraṃ darśayati. tasmān na pavamāneṣṭayaḥ pratīkṣitavyā iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pavamāneṣṭibhiḥ saṃskṛteṣv agniṣu karmāṇi varteran. kutaḥ? saṃskārāṇāṃ tadarthatvāt, saṃskāraśabdā eta āhavanīyādayaḥ, saṃskārasya kasyacid abhāvena, āhavanīyādiṣu pratipattiḥ syāt. tasmāt saṃskṛteṣv agniṣu karmāṇīti.
children.translated_text:
At the establishment [of the fires], there are the <s>Pavamāna</s> offerings (<s>iṣṭis</s>). And there are fixed (<s>niyata</s>) rites such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, and optional (<s>aniyata</s>) ones such as the <s>Aindrāgna</s> and the like. There a doubt [arises]: should the rites be undertaken after performing the <s>Pavamāna</s> offerings, or with the fires having merely been established? What is the prima facie view? With the fires merely established. Why? One is able to perform rites with merely established fires — as [it is heard]: 'One who has established the fires should not place wet firewood [on them].' And it shows that the <s>Agnihotra</s> [takes place] with merely established fires: 'They run after the newly created fire with the <s>Agnihotra</s>' — it shows the <s>Agnihotra</s> with merely established fires. Therefore the <s>Pavamāna</s> offerings need not be awaited.
Given this prima facie view, we say: the rites should take place with the fires consecrated by the <s>Pavamāna</s> offerings. Why? Because the preparatory rites are for that [ritual action's] purpose. The <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires] are designated by the word 'consecration' (<s>saṃskāra</s>); in the absence of some consecration, the designation as <s>Āhavanīya</s> and the like would apply [only as a formality]. Therefore, the rites [should take place] with consecrated fires.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/62: E2: klinnaṃ dārvabhyādadhyād ityevamādīny āhitāgnivratābhyāhitamātreṣv eva bhavantīti darśayati}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:

children.text: anantaraṃ vrataṃ tadbhūtatvāt // MS_5,3.22 //
children.translated_text: The observance (<s>vrata</s>) [comes] immediately after, because of [the sacrificer's] having become that [an <s>āhitāgni</s>]. // MS_5,3.22 //

children.text: yat tu, āhitāgnir na klinnaṃ dārvā dadhyād{*5/63*}ityevamādi. yuktam{*5/64*}, yad āhitamātreṣu kriyate, āhitāgnes tadvratam ucyate. sa ca, āhitamātreṣv āhitāgniḥ saṃvṛttaḥ. tasmād anantaraṃ vrataṃ syāt, tadbhūtatvāt.
children.translated_text: As for [the statement] 'One who has established the fires should not place wet firewood [on them]' and the like — it is proper that what is done with merely established fires [is the observance]. The observance is said [to belong] to one who has established the fires. And he has become an <s>āhitāgni</s> (one who has established the fires) with merely established fires. Therefore the observance should come immediately after, because of [the sacrificer's] having become that.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/63: E2: dārvabhyādadhyād}*
*{5/64: E2: yuktaṃ tatra}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/63: E2: <s>dārvabhyādadhyād</s>}]
[{5/64: E2: <s>yuktaṃ tatra</s>}]

children.text: pūrvaṃ ca liṅgadarśanāt // MS_5,3.23 //
children.translated_text: And [the <s>Agnihotra</s> comes] first, because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_5,3.23 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, āhitamātreṣv agnihotraṃ{*5/65*} darśayati, pūrvam iṣṭibhya iti, tasya kaḥ parihāra ity ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'it shows the <s>Agnihotra</s> with merely established fires, [i.e.,] before the offerings' — what is the refutation of that? This is a <s>sūtra</s> that concludes with the discussion.

children.text: arthavādo vārthasya vidyamānatvāt // MS_5,3.24 //
children.translated_text: Or it is an <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage), because of the meaning already existing. // MS_5,3.24 //

children.text: arthavāda eṣaḥ. kutaḥ? arthasya vidyamānatvāt. vidyamāno hi tatrānya evāgnihotrahomaḥ. kathaṃ hotavyam agnihotraṃ na hotavyam iti mīmāṃsante brahmavādinaḥ. yad yajuṣā juhuyād ayathāpūrvam āhutī juhuyāt, yadi na juhuyād agniḥ parāpatet. tūṣṇīm eva hotavyam iti. tasya tūṣṇīṃ homasya praśaṃsārtho 'yam arthavādaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is an <s>arthavāda</s>. Why? Because the meaning already exists. For there already exists another <s>Agnihotra</s> oblation. The <s>Brahmavādins</s> (Vedic scholars) deliberate: 'How should the <s>Agnihotra</s> be offered? Should it be offered or not?' [They say:] 'If one offers with a <s>yajus</s> (formula), one would offer the oblations not in the proper order. If one does not offer, the fire would go away. [Therefore] it should be offered silently.' This <s>arthavāda</s> serves to praise that silent oblation.

children.text: nyāyavipratiṣedhāc ca // MS_5,3.25 //
children.translated_text: And because of contradiction with the principle. // MS_5,3.25 //

children.text: nyāyavipratiṣedhaś ca bhavet. yady anantaram agnihotrādayaḥ syuḥ, yaḥ pūrvokto nyāyaḥ{*5/67*}, sa vipratiṣidhyeta, na vā tāsāṃ tadarthatvād iti. tasmāt saṃskṛte karmāṇi bhaveyur iti.
children.translated_text: And there would be a contradiction with the principle. If the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like were [performed] immediately after [fire-establishment], the principle stated earlier would be contradicted — 'or their [fires'] being for that [ritual] purpose' [i.e., the fires serve the sacrifice]. Therefore the rites should take place with consecrated [fires].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/67: Vgl. zu MS 3.6.12}*
saṃcite tv agnicid yuktaṃ prāpaṇān nimittasya // MS_5,3.26 //
children.translated_text: But when [the fire-altar] has been piled, one becomes an <s>agnicit</s> (fire-builder), which is proper because of the arrival of the occasion. // MS_5,3.26 //

children.text: agnicid varṣati na dhāvet, na striyam upeyāt, tasmād agnicitā pakṣiṇo nāśitavyā ityevamādayaḥ padārthāḥ śrūyante. teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ saṃcitamātre pratipattavyā uta kratvanta iti. kiṃ prāptam? saṃcitamātra eveti. agniṃ yaś citavān so 'gnicid iti tasya śrūyamāṇāś citavato 'nantaram eva prāpnuvanti, prāpte nimitte naimittikaṃ kartavyam. tasmād anantaram eva.
children.translated_text: 'One who has built the fire (<s>agnicit</s>) should not run in the rain; should not approach a woman. Therefore, one who has built the fire should not destroy birds' — such items are heard. Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: should they be observed as soon as [the fire-altar] has been piled, or until the end of the sacrifice? What is the prima facie view? As soon as piled only. One who has piled the fire is an <s>agnicit</s> — these [observances], being heard of one who has piled, pertain to him immediately after. When the occasion has arrived, the occasional [observance] must be performed. Therefore, immediately after.

children.text: kratvante vā prayogavacanābhāvāt // MS_5,3.27 //
children.translated_text: Or [they apply] until the end of the sacrifice, because of the absence of a statement about performance. // MS_5,3.27 //

children.text: prayogavacano hy atra tān padārthān prāpayati, yeṣāṃ kratvarthatvam. na caiṣāṃ kratvarthatvam asti, puruṣārthā hy ete. katham? pratiṣedhe puruṣaḥ śrūyate, varṣati na dhāvet, na striyam upeyād ityevamādi. na ca kratvarthā ete prasaktāḥ, yena pratiṣedhaḥ krator upakuryāt.
children.translated_text: For the statement about performance conveys to those items a connection with the sacrifice. But these have no connection with the sacrifice's purpose — for these serve the person's purpose. How? In the prohibition, the person is heard — 'he should not run in the rain; he should not approach a woman' and the like. And these are not connected with the sacrifice's purpose, such that the prohibition would benefit the sacrifice.

children.text: nanu puruṣārthā api citavataḥ śravaṇāc cayanānantaraṃ prāptāḥ. neti brūmaḥ,
children.translated_text: [The objector says:] but even though they serve the person's purpose, they are obtained immediately after the piling, because they are heard of one who has piled. We reply: no —

children.text: agneḥ karmatvānirdeśāt{*5/69*} // MS_5,3.28 //
children.translated_text: Because the fire is not designated as a [mere] ritual action. // MS_5,3.28 //

children.text: agnyarthaṃ cayanaṃ tat, yad agneḥ svaṃ kāryaṃ kurvataḥ sāhāyye vartate, tat tadartham. kaś ca tasya svārthaḥ? yāgāsiddhiḥ, siddhe ca yāge cayanenopakṛtaṃ bhavati. tasmāt siddhe yāge 'gnicit, tena kratvanta iti.
children.translated_text: The piling is for the fire's purpose — that which assists the fire in performing its own function, that is for the fire's purpose. And what is [the fire's] own purpose? The accomplishment of the sacrifice; and when the sacrifice is accomplished, the piling has served [the fire]. Therefore, when the sacrifice is accomplished, one becomes an <s>agnicit</s>; hence [the observances apply] until the end of the sacrifice.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/69: E2: karmatvānirdeśāt}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/69: E2: <s>karmatvānirdeśāt</s>}]

children.text: pareṇāvedanād dīkṣitaḥ syāt sarvair dīkṣābhisaṃbandhāt // MS_5,3.29 //
children.translated_text: One becomes a <s>dīkṣita</s> (consecrated person) after the communication (<s>āvedana</s>) [to the priests], because of the connection with all the consecration [elements]. // MS_5,3.29 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped dīkṣiṣyamāṇa iti{*5/70*}. tathā, daṇḍena dīkṣayati{*5/71*}, mekhalayā dīkṣayati, kṛṣṇājinena dīkṣayatīty{*5/72*}evamādi. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ sarvair dīkṣito bhavati, atha veṣṭyante dīkṣita iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? sarvair iti. kutaḥ? dīkṣābhisaṃbandhāt, dīkṣāsaṃbandho bhavati, daṇḍena dīkṣayati, dīkṣām asya karotīty arthaḥ{*5/73*}. yadīṣṭyante dīkṣitaḥ syāt, [579]{*5/74*} katham asya daṇḍena dīkṣāṃ kuryāt. teneṣṭyā na dīkṣitaḥ. na ca, asyeṣṭyante dīkṣitaśabdaṃ paśyāmaḥ, āvedane tv asya dīkṣitaśabdaḥ, tasmān na tāvati dīkṣitaḥ syāt. na ca saṃbhavati sam-uccaye vikalpo nyāyyaḥ, pakṣe bādhaḥ syāt. tatra prayogavacano bādhyeta. tasmād bhinneṣv api dīkṣāsaṃbandhavākyeṣu prayogavacanena sahaikavākyatety āvedanakāle dīkṣitaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'One who is about to undergo consecration should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to <s>Agni-Viṣṇu</s>.' Likewise, 'He consecrates with the staff; he consecrates with the girdle; he consecrates with the black-antelope skin' and the like. There a doubt [arises]: does one become a <s>dīkṣita</s> through all [these elements], or is one [already] consecrated at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering)? What is the prima facie view? Through all. Why? Because of the connection with <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) — there is a connection with consecration: 'he consecrates with the staff' — meaning 'he performs his consecration.' If one were consecrated at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s>, how could he perform his consecration with the staff? Therefore one is not consecrated by the <s>iṣṭi</s> [alone]. And we do not see the word <s>dīkṣita</s> (consecrated) applied to him at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s>; but the word <s>dīkṣita</s> is [used of him] at the communication [to the priests]. Therefore he would not be consecrated until that point. And where cumulation is possible, an alternative is not proper — for in an alternative, there would be contradiction. In that case, the statement about performance would be contradicted. Therefore, even though the sentences about the connection with consecration are separate, through syntactic unity with the statement about performance, he becomes a <s>dīkṣita</s> at the time of the communication.

children.text: iṣṭyante vā tadarthā hy aviśeṣārthasaṃbandhāt // MS_5,3.30 //
children.translated_text: Or at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s>, because the [elements] are for that [offering's] purpose, since the connection with the meaning is non-specific. // MS_5,3.30 //

children.text:
iṣṭyante vā dīkṣitaḥ syāt, tadarthā hi sā dīkṣaṇārthā{*5/75*}. katham? dīkṣiṣyamāṇasya adīkṣitasya sā bhavati, yadi tasyā uttarakāle dīkṣitaḥ, evaṃ sā dīkṣiṣyamāṇasya. tasmād vākyād avagamyate, bhavati tadā dīkṣita iti, dīkṣākāraṇe padārthe nirvṛtte kim iti na dīkṣitaḥ syāt? vākyaṃ hi nirapekṣaṃ dīkṣita iti jñāpayati.
yat tu, dīkṣāsaṃbandho daṇḍena dīkṣayatīti. kathaṃ sa dīkṣitatve syād iti daṇḍenaivaṃ dīkṣitaṃ saṃpādayatīty{*5/76*} avagacchāmaḥ. yat tu, anantaraṃ dīkṣitaśabdo nāstīti. na śabdasyāprayogo 'rthābhāve hetuḥ. saty apy arthe tadavasarābhāvān na prayujyate śabdaḥ. anyena ca dīkṣita ity avagamyate vākyena, āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped dīkṣyamāṇa iti. yac ca, āvedanakāle dīkṣitaśabda iti. iṣṭyante 'pi dīkṣitasyāsāv aviruddhaḥ, prayogavacanaś cāviruddhaḥ, yata ekaṃ dīkṣākāraṇam, anyair dīkṣitaṃ saṃpādayatīti gamyate.
children.translated_text:
Or, at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering), one would be consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>), for that [iṣṭi] is for the purpose of consecration. How? It [the iṣṭi] belongs to one who is about to be consecrated, to one who is not yet consecrated. If after it [the iṣṭi] he is consecrated, then it is for one about to be consecrated. Therefore it is understood from the sentence that at that point he is consecrated — when the items that are the cause of consecration have been accomplished, why should he not be consecrated? For the sentence, without depending [on anything else], indicates [that he is] consecrated.
As for [the argument about] the connection of consecration through 'he consecrates with the staff' — we understand that thus: 'he effects the status of being consecrated through the staff.' As for [the argument] that 'the word <s>dīkṣita</s> does not occur immediately after [the iṣṭi]' — the non-use of a word is not evidence for the absence of the thing. Even when the thing exists, the word may not be used because there is no occasion for it. And by another sentence it is understood that [he is] consecrated: 'He should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to <s>Agni-Viṣṇu</s> when about to be consecrated.' And as for [the argument] that 'the word <s>dīkṣita</s> occurs at the time of announcement' — even at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s>, that [word] is not contradicted for one who is [already] consecrated. And the statement of performance is not contradicted, since one [element] is the cause of consecration, and [the other] elements effect the status of being consecrated — thus it is understood.

children.text: samākhyānaṃ ca tadvat // MS_5,3.31 //
children.translated_text: And the designation (<s>samākhyāna</s>) [supports] the same. // MS_5,3.31 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmaḥ, iṣṭadīkṣaṇārthā, iṣṭyante ca pravṛttir iti. kasmāt? samākhyānaṃ ca tadvad iti yadvan nyāya upadiṣṭaḥ. katham? dīkṣaṇīyeti tādarthyakarī samākhyā bhavati, yathā snānīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ceti. tasmāc ca paśyāmaḥ, iṣṭir dīkṣaṇārthā, iṣṭyante ca pravṛttir iti.
children.translated_text: For this further reason we see [that] the <s>iṣṭi</s> is for the purpose of consecration, and the engagement [of further elements begins] at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s>. Why? Because the designation too [supports] the same — as the principle was instructed. How? '<s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s>' — this designation indicates being for that purpose, just as '<s>snānīya</s>' (for bathing) and '<s>bhojanīya</s>' (for eating). Therefore by this too we see [that] the <s>iṣṭi</s> is for the purpose of consecration, and the engagement [begins] at the end of the <s>iṣṭi</s>.

children.text: aṅgavat kratūnām ānupūrvyam // MS_5,3.32 //
children.translated_text: The sequence of sacrifices (<s>kratu</s>) is like [the sequence of] subsidiaries. // MS_5,3.32 //

children.text: iha kāmyā iṣṭaya udāharaṇam. aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped{*5/78*} ityevamādayaḥ, gavādayaḥ, somāḥ, saumyādayaḥ, paśavaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ yena krameṇādhītāḥ, tenaiva krameṇa prayoktavyāḥ, utāniyama iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? kratūnām ānupūrvyaṃ yat pāṭhe, tad eva prayoge bhavitum arhati. evaṃ pāṭhakramo 'nugṛhīto bhaviṣyati, itarathā pāṭhakramo bādhyeta, tan mā bhūd iti krameṇānuṣṭhātavyam.
children.translated_text: Here the <s>kāmya</s> (desire-motivated) offerings are the example: 'He should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to <s>Indrāgni</s>' and the like; [offerings associated with] cows and such; <s>Soma</s> sacrifices; offerings starting with the <s>Saumya</s> [offerings]; animal [sacrifices]. There a doubt [arises]: should they be performed in the same sequence in which they are studied, or is there no fixed rule? What is the prima facie view? The sequence of sacrifices as in the textual order (<s>pāṭha</s>) should apply in practice as well. Thus the textual order will be supported; otherwise the textual order would be violated — to prevent that, they should be performed in sequence.

NOTES:
[{5/78: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.1.1}]

children.text: na vāsaṃbandhāt // MS_5,3.33 //
children.translated_text: Or there should be no [fixed sequence], because of the absence of connection. // MS_5,3.33 //

children.text: na vā, ayaṃ{*5/79*} kramo niyamyeta. kutaḥ? asaṃbandhāt. pṛthak pṛthag eṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ prayogavacanāni, tāni svapadārthānām upasaṃhārakāṇi. yo yasya nopakārakaḥ, sa tasya na krameṇa, notkramaṇa. yo yasyopakaroti kasyacit, tasyopakurvataḥ kramaḥ sāhāyye vartate. na caitāni karmāṇy anyonyasyopakurvanti. tasmān naiṣāṃ kramaḥ sāhāyye vartate. tasmād asaṃbandha iti.
children.translated_text: Or rather, this sequence should not be fixed. Why? Because of the absence of connection. These rites have separate statements of performance; those collect their own items. What does not assist another — that has no [fixed] sequence with the other, nor departure from sequence. What assists something — the sequence of that assisting [element] operates in [the context of] helping [the principal]. But these rites do not mutually assist each other. Therefore their sequence does not operate in [the context of] helping. Therefore there is no connection.

children.text: kāmyatvāc ca // MS_5,3.34 //
children.translated_text: And because of [their] being desire-motivated. // MS_5,3.34 //

children.text: kāmyāni caitāni karmāṇi, kāmāś ca krameṇotpadyante, tena nimittasyākramatvān na kramavanta iti.
children.translated_text: And these rites are desire-motivated, and desires arise without [fixed] sequence. Therefore, because the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) has no [fixed] sequence, [the rites] have no [fixed] sequence.

children.text: ānarthakyān neti cet // MS_5,3.35 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that [the textual order would be] purposeless — // MS_5,3.35 //

children.text: iti yad uktaṃ pūrvapakṣe, tad eva punar ucyate parihartum. evaṃ krameṇa pāṭho 'rthavān bhaviṣyatīti. etad ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram.
children.translated_text: What was stated in the prima facie view is now restated in order to refute it: 'Thus the textual order would have a purpose.' This <s>sūtra</s> ends with a statement to be refuted.

children.text: syād vidyārthatvād yathā pareṣu sarvasvārāt // MS_5,3.36 //
children.translated_text: It would have a purpose through being for the sake of knowledge, as in the case of the <s>sarvasvāra</s> (all-accent [chant]) for the subsequent [rites]. // MS_5,3.36 //

children.text: syād arthavān kramapāṭhaḥ, asaty api prayoge krame, vidyāgrahaṇārthatvāt, karmāvabodhanārthāyāṃ vidyāyāṃ kramaniyamādṛṣṭaṃ tadāśrayam eva bhaviṣyatīti, yathā, tvatpakṣe, pareṣu sarvasvārāt, yasyāpi kramo 'ṅgam iti pakṣaḥ, tasyāpi sarvasvārāt pareṣāṃ sarvasvāreṇa yaḥ kramas tasyādṛṣṭārthatāvaśyaṃ kalpanīyā.
children.translated_text: The sequential textual order would have a purpose — even without a [fixed] sequence in practice — because it is for the purpose of acquiring knowledge. In the knowledge meant for understanding the rites, the unseen [merit] pertaining to sequential fixity will belong to that [knowledge] itself. Just as, in your [opponent's] position, regarding the <s>sarvasvāra</s> for the subsequent [rites] — even for the position that sequence is a subsidiary [of the rites] — for the <s>sarvasvāra</s> of the subsequent [rites], the unseen-purpose nature must necessarily be postulated.

children.text: ya etenety agniṣṭomaḥ prakaraṇāt // MS_5,3.37 //
children.translated_text: 'He who by this [sacrifice]' — this refers to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, because of the context. // MS_5,3.37 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, eṣa vāva prathamo yajñānāṃ{*5/81*} yaj jyotiṣṭomaḥ, ya etenāniṣṭvāthānyena yajeta gartapatyam eva taj jāyate pra vā mīyata iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, ya eteneti kasya [582] ayaṃ vāda iti praśnenaivopakramaḥ. ucyate, ya etenety agniṣṭomasya vādaḥ. kutaḥ? prakaraṇāt, tasya hi prakaraṇe bhavaty etad vacanam. prakṛtavācīni ca sarvanāmāni bhavanti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'This is indeed the first of sacrifices, namely the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. He who, without having sacrificed by this, would sacrifice by another — his [sacrifice] merely results in a pit-fall, or he dies.' [582] There a doubt [arises]: 'he who by this' — the inquiry begins with the very question: whose statement is this? [We] reply: 'he who by this' is a statement about the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. Why? Because of the context — for this statement occurs in its context. And pronouns refer to what is contextually established.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/81: E2: yajño yajñānāṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/81: E2: <s>yajño yajñānāṃ</s>}]

children.text: liṅgāc ca // MS_5,3.38 //
children.translated_text: And because of the indicatory mark. // MS_5,3.38 //

children.text: liṅgam api bhavati, tatra śrūyate, yasya{*5/82*} navatiśataṃ stotrīyā{*5/83*} iti, agniṣṭomasya hi bhavanti navatiśataṃ stotrīyāḥ. katham? trivṛd bahiṣpavamānam, pañcadaśāny ājyāni, tāni catvāri. sā ekonasaptatiḥ. pañcadaśo mādhyaṃdinaḥ pavamānaḥ, tena caturaśītiḥ. saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni, tāni catvāri sāṣṭaṣaṣṭiḥ, caturaśītyā saha dvipañcāśac chatam. saptadaśa ārbhavaḥ pavamānaḥ, tena ṣaṣṭyadhikaṃ śataṃ nava ca. ekaviṃśaṃ yajñāyajñīyam iti tad etan navatiśatam agniṣṭomasya, tasmād apy agniṣṭomaḥ.
children.translated_text: There is also an indicatory mark. It is heard there: 'He whose <s>stotrīya</s> (hymn-verses) number one hundred and ninety.' For the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has one hundred and ninety <s>stotrīya</s> verses. How? The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> has the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma] (nine-fold); the <s>ājya</s> [stotras] have the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-fold); those are four — that makes sixty-nine. The midday <s>Pavamāna</s> has the <s>Pañcadaśa</s>; with that, eighty-four. The <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [stotras] have the <s>Saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-fold); those are four — sixty-eight; together with eighty-four, one hundred and fifty-two. The <s>Ārbhava Pavamāna</s> has the <s>Saptadaśa</s>; with that, one hundred and sixty-nine. The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> has the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold) — thus this totals one hundred and ninety for the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. Therefore by this too it is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

NOTES:
[{5/82: E2: <s>tasya</s>}]
[{5/83: <s>Aitareya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.41}]

children.text: athānyeneti saṃsthānāṃ saṃnidhānāt // MS_5,3.39 //
children.translated_text: 'And then by another' — this refers to the <s>saṃsthās</s> (concluding forms), because of proximity. // MS_5,3.39 //

children.text: athānyeneti kiṃ saṃsthānāṃ vādaḥ, atha jyotiṣṭomavikārāṇām evaikāhādīnām iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? saṃsthānām iti. kutaḥ? saṃnidhānāt, saṃnihitās tasmin prakaraṇe saṃsthāḥ, tāsāṃ vādaḥ prakaraṇānugrahāya.
children.translated_text: 'And then by another' — is this a statement about the <s>saṃsthās</s> (concluding forms), or about the ectypes (<s>vikāras</s>) of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> alone, such as single-day (<s>ekāha</s>) rites and the like? What is the prima facie view? It is about the <s>saṃsthās</s>. Why? Because of proximity — the <s>saṃsthās</s> are proximate in that context; it is their statement, in deference to the contextual connection.

children.text: tatprakṛter vāpattivihārau hi na tulyeṣūpapadyete // MS_5,3.40 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a statement about [rites that are] ectypes of that [Agniṣṭoma], for the <s>āpatti</s> (adaptation) and <s>vihāra</s> (distribution) apply only to ectypes, not to those that are equal. // MS_5,3.40 //

children.text: tatprakṛter vā gavāder vādaḥ syāt, āpattivihārau hi prakṛtivikāramātreṣūpapadyete, na tulyaśabdeṣv eva jyotiṣṭoma[583]{*5/84*}śabdakeṣu. naivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate, athānyena jyotiṣṭomaśabdakeneti. kathaṃ tarhi? anyeneti prakṛtād itarad bravīti, na, sa jyotiṣṭomena viśiṣyate, na hi śabdasyārthaḥ samīpagatena kṛtaprayojanenaikadeśe 'vasthāpayitavyo bhavati, na hi vākyena śrutir bādhyate. atha, jyotiṣṭomād anyenety abhisaṃbadhyate, tato natarāṃ saṃsthāvādaḥ. kathaṃ punar āpattivihārau? prajāpatir vāgniṣṭomaḥ, sa uttarān ekāhān asṛjata te sṛṣṭvā abruvan{*5/85*}, na vai svenātmanā prabhavāma iti. tebhyaḥ svātantryaṃ prāyacchat, tathā ca te prābhavan tad, yathā vā idam agner jātād adhyagnayo{*5/86*} vihriyante. evaṃ vā, etasmād yajñād anye yajñakratavo vihriyante, yo vai trivṛd anyaṃ yajñakratum āpadyate, sa taṃ dīpayati, yaḥ pañcadaśam, sa tam, yaḥ saptadaśam, sa tam, ya ekaviṃśam, sa tam ityevam āhur eko yajña iti. ete vai sarve jyotiṣṭomāḥ bhavantīti. evaṃ vaikṛtānāṃ saṃkīrtanāt, teṣām eva vāda iti gamyate. katham? athānyeneti, yo 'sāv anyaḥ, tatra prākṛtān dharmān vihṛtān darśayati, ato manyāmahe, yasya yato vihṛtiḥ, tenānyeneti.
children.translated_text: Or it is a statement about ectypes of that [Agniṣṭoma] — [rites such as those involving] cows and such. For the <s>āpatti</s> (adaptation) and <s>vihāra</s> (distribution) apply [only] to mere archetype-ectype [relationships], not to those that equally bear the designation '<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' [583] The connection is not made thus: 'and then by another that bears the designation <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' Rather, 'by another' speaks of what is different from the archetype, not [what is] distinguished by [the name] <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. For the meaning of a word should not be restricted to one part by something nearby whose purpose has been fulfilled. For the [Vedic] word is not overridden by a sentence. Now, if it is connected as 'by another [sacrifice] than the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>,' then all the more it is not a statement about the <s>saṃsthās</s>. But how [do] the <s>āpatti</s> and <s>vihāra</s> [apply]? '<s>Prajāpati</s> indeed is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. He created the subsequent single-day [rites]. Those, having been created, said: "We cannot prevail by our own nature." He gave them independence. And thus they prevailed — just as from fire, once kindled, other fires are distributed. So too, from this sacrifice, other sacrificial rites are distributed. He who adapts another sacrificial rite through the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma] — he kindles it; he who through the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> — he [kindles] it; he who through the <s>Saptadaśa</s> — he [kindles] it; he who through the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> — he [kindles] it. Thus they say: it is one sacrifice. All these are <s>Jyotiṣṭomas</s>.' Since the ectypes are thus mentioned, it is understood that the statement is about them. How? 'And then by another' — that which is the 'other,' there it shows the archetypal properties as distributed. Therefore we consider: that from which there is distribution — it is with reference to 'another' than that.

children.text: praśaṃsā vā viharaṇābhāvāt // MS_5,3.41 //
children.translated_text: Or it is [mere] praise, because of the absence of distribution. // MS_5,3.41 //

children.text: yady evaṃ na tarhi tadvikārāṇāṃ vādaḥ, tatra na vihāro nāpattiḥ prakaraṇādibhiḥ, te dharmā jyotiṣṭomasya, yadi hi{*5/87*} gavādayo{*5/88*} vihriyeran prakaraṇādīni bādhyeran. tadāpattiḥ pratyakṣaviruddhā, praśaṃsā tv eṣā, āpattivihārābhāvāt.
children.translated_text: If so, then it is not a statement about the ectypes of that — there is neither distribution nor adaptation through context and the like; those properties belong to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. For if the [rites involving] cows and the like were distributed, the context and the like would be overridden. The adaptation [in that case] contradicts direct perception. Rather, this is [mere] praise — because of the absence of adaptation and distribution.

children.text: vidhipratyayād vā na hy akasmāt praśaṃsā syāt // MS_5,3.42 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is a statement about ectypes] because of the injunctive verbal ending; for praise would not arise without a reason. // MS_5,3.42 //

children.text: atrocyate, yady apy āpattivihārau na vidhīyete, te{*5/90*} tathāpi codakena vidhīyete. ye prakṛtau kartavyāḥ, te codakavacanād vikṛtāv api kartavyā gamyante. tadāpattivihārāv iva yatra bhavataḥ, tenānyeneti gamyate. na hy akasmāt praśaṃsā syāt, yo 'sāv anyaḥ, sa katham anayā praśaṃsayā lakṣyetetyevamarthā praśaṃsā.
children.translated_text: To this it is said: even if the <s>āpatti</s> and <s>vihāra</s> are not being prescribed, those [properties] are nevertheless prescribed by the enjoining [statement]. Those that are to be performed in the archetype — from the enjoining statement, they are understood as to be performed in the ectype as well. The <s>āpatti</s> and <s>vihāra</s> — wherever they occur — it is 'by another' that is understood. For praise would not arise without a reason — that which is the 'other,' how would it be indicated by this praise? The praise has this very purpose.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/90: E2 om. te}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:

children.text: ekastome vā kratusaṃyogāt // MS_5,3.43 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is a statement about] the single-<s>stoma</s> [rites], because of the connection with a sacrifice. // MS_5,3.43 //

children.text: ya etenāniṣṭvā, athānyena yajeteti śrūyate. tatraiṣo 'rthaḥ samadhigataḥ, tadvikārāṇāṃ vāda iti. athedānīṃ saṃdihyate, kim ekastomakasya, anekastomakasya ceti. kiṃ{*5/91*} prāptam? ekastomakasya vādaḥ. kutaḥ? kratusaṃyogāt, ekastome kratusaṃyogo bhavati, yo vai trivṛd anyaṃ yajñakratum āpadyate sa taṃ dīpayati, yaḥ pañcadaśaṃ{*5/92*} sa tam, yaḥ saptadaśaṃ{*5/93*} sa tam, ya ekaviṃśaṃ{*5/94*}, sa tam. trivṛdādaya ekastomakāḥ. tasmāt teṣāṃ vāda iti.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'He who, without having sacrificed by this, would sacrifice by another.' Therein this meaning was understood: it is a statement about the ectypes of that [Agniṣṭoma]. Now a doubt arises: is it about single-<s>stoma</s> [rites], or about multi-<s>stoma</s> [rites] as well? What is the prima facie view? It is a statement about the single-<s>stoma</s> [rites]. Why? Because of the connection with a sacrifice — there is a connection with a sacrifice in [the context of] single-<s>stoma</s> [rites]: 'He who adapts another sacrificial rite through the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma] — he kindles it; he who through the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> — he [kindles] it; he who through the <s>Saptadaśa</s> — he [kindles] it; he who through the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> — he [kindles] it.' The <s>Trivṛt</s> and the others are single-<s>stoma</s> [rites]. Therefore it is a statement about them.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vā codanāviśeṣāt praśaṃsā stomānām // MS_5,3.44 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is a statement] about all [rites], because of no distinction in the injunction; the [mention of] <s>stomas</s> is [mere] praise. // MS_5,3.44 //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ caiṣa{*5/95*} vādaḥ, ekastomakānām anekastomakānāṃ ca. kutaḥ? aviśeṣavacanād anyaśabdasya. nanv ekastomakāḥ kratavaḥ saṃkīrtyante. satyaṃ saṃkīrtyante, praśaṃsārtham, na [585]{*5/96*} viśeṣārtham. kaḥ punaḥ praśaṃsārthaḥ? yo vai trivṛd anyaṃ yajñakratum āpadyate sa taṃ dīpayati, codakaprāptā dharmā abhyastāḥ prakṛtau, vikṛtau sukhaṃ pratipadyante.
children.translated_text: This is a statement about all [rites] — both single-<s>stoma</s> and multi-<s>stoma</s>. Why? Because of the lack of distinction in the word 'another' (<s>anya</s>). [The objector says:] but single-<s>stoma</s> sacrifices are mentioned. True, they are mentioned — for the purpose of praise [585], not for the purpose of distinction. What then is the purpose of the praise? 'He who adapts another sacrificial rite through the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma] — he kindles it' — the properties obtained through the enjoining [statement] are practiced in the archetype [and] are easily understood in the ectype.

children.text: kramako yo 'rthaśabdābhyāṃ śrutiviśeṣād arthaparatvāc ca // MS_5,4.1 //
children.translated_text: A <s>kramaka</s> (ritual manual) is that which [deals] with both purpose and word, because of the specific [Vedic] statement and because of being purpose-oriented. // MS_5,4.1 //

children.text:
iha pāṭhakramasya śrutyarthakramābhyāṃ saha bādhāṃ prati vicāraṇam{*5/98*}. kiṃ pāṭhakramas tābhyāṃ tulyaḥ, uta bādhyata iti. kiṃ prāptam? tulyabalāv etau, pāṭho 'pi hi kāraṇaṃ śrutyarthāv api. na ca prāmāṇye kaścid viśeṣo 'sti, tasmād aniyama iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pāṭhakramo hi bādhyate śrutyā, arthena ca. kutaḥ? śrutiviśeṣāt, arthaparatvāc ca. śrutiviśeṣaḥ kaḥ? yatra śravaṇaṃ tatra pratyakṣaṃ kāraṇam, pāṭhakramas tv ānumānikaḥ, pāṭhakrameṇa smaraṇam, evam abhinirvartayitavyam ity avagamyate. tasyārthavattvenaikayopapattyā tasyaivānuṣṭhānam{*5/99*}. śrutyā punar anuṣṭhānam eva, evaṃ bhavatīti pratyakṣād avagamyate.
tathārthena. kutaḥ? arthaparatvāt, arthārthaṃ hi sarvaṃ pradhānārtham{*5/100*}, pradhānam abhinirvartayatīti sarvaṃ kriyate. tasmāt pāṭhas tābhyāṃ bādhyate.
kim udāharaṇaṃ prayojanaṃ ca? śrutyām{*5/101*} āśvino daśamo gṛhyate, taṃ tṛtīyaṃ juhoti, atra pāṭhakramasya balīyastve tṛtīyasya grahaṇam, siddhānte tu daśamasya. arthe, agnihotrahomaḥ pūrvam āmnāyate, paścāc chrapaṇam. evaṃ kartavyam, yadi pāṭho balavān. siddhānte śrapaṇaṃ pūrvam, tato homaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Here the investigation concerns the overriding of the recitation-order (<s>pāṭhakrama</s>) by the [Vedic] word-order (<s>śruti</s>) and the meaning-order (<s>artha</s>). Is the recitation-order equal to those two, or is it overridden? What is the prima facie view? These two are of equal strength — for the recitation too is a cause, and the [Vedic] word and meaning are also. And there is no distinction in their validity. Therefore there is no fixed rule. Given this prima facie view, we say: the recitation-order is overridden by the [Vedic] word and by the meaning. Why? Because of the specificity of the [Vedic] word, and because of the purposefulness of the meaning. What is the specificity of the [Vedic] word? Where there is [explicit] hearing, there the cause is directly perceptible; but the recitation-order is [merely] inferential — from the recitation-order one remembers, and [from that] one understands 'it should be accomplished in this way.' Since there is purposefulness [in that inference], by the fitness of one [interpretation] alone, precisely that performance [follows]. But through the [Vedic] word, the very performance [is established] — 'it is so' is directly understood.
Likewise with the meaning. Why? Because of purposefulness — for everything serves the purpose of the principal [rite]; everything is done to accomplish the principal [rite]. Therefore the recitation-order is overridden by those two.
What are the example and the purpose? Regarding the [Vedic] word: the <s>Āśvina</s> [cup], taken tenth, is offered third. Here, if the recitation-order prevails, the third [cup] is taken; but in the established conclusion, the tenth. Regarding the meaning: the <s>Agnihotra</s> offering is stated first, and the cooking [of the rice] afterward. It should be done thus if the recitation [order] prevails. In the established conclusion, cooking [comes] first, then the offering.

children.text: avadānābhighāraṇāsādaneṣv ānupūrvyaṃ pravṛttyā syāt // MS_5,4.2 //
children.translated_text: In cutting, basting, and bringing [to the fire], the sequence would be through custom (<s>pravṛtti</s>). // MS_5,4.2 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra pūrvaṃ dadhno dharmāḥ samāmnātāḥ, paścād āgneyasya, pradānaṃ cāgneyasya pūrvam. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ prāvṛttikena krameṇa pūrvaṃ dadhno 'vadānābhighāraṇāsādanāni, uta mukhyakrameṇa pūrvam āgneyasyeti. kiṃ prāptam? aniyama ity. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, avadānādiṣu prāvṛttikena pūrvaṃ dadhna iti. kutaḥ? evam anujñātebhyo vyavadhāyakebhyo nābhyadhiko 'nyo vā vyavadhāyakaḥ kalpito bhaviṣyati, darśayati ca dadhnaḥ pūrvam eva deyam{*5/103*} iti.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites]. There, first the properties of the curd [offering] are stated, then those of the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering]; but the giving of the <s>Āgneya</s> [comes] first. There a doubt [arises]: by the customary order, should the cutting, basting, and bringing of the curd [come] first, or by the principal order, should those of the <s>Āgneya</s> [come] first? What is the prima facie view? No fixed rule. Given this prima facie view, we say: in cutting etc., the curd [comes] first by the customary [order]. Why? Thus, no intervening [element] other than those [already] sanctioned by the intervening [elements] will need to be postulated. And [the text] shows that the curd should be given first.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/103: E2: pūrvam avadeyam}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/103: E2: <s>pūrvam avadeyam</s>}]

children.text: yathāpradānaṃ vā tadarthatvāt // MS_5,4.3 //
children.translated_text: Or it should be according to the giving-order, because [the cutting etc.] serve that purpose. // MS_5,4.3 //

children.text:
yathāpradānaṃ vā kartavyāni, yasya pradānaṃ pūrvam, tasyāvadānāni pūrvam, tasmād āgneyasya. kutaḥ? pradānacodanāgṛhītatvād{*5/104*} avadānādīnām, pradānopakramā ete na pṛthakpadārthā ete{*5/105*} ity uktam. abhighāraṇam avadānaṃ ca tasya pradānacikīrṣayaiva kriyate. āsādanam api pradānārtham evāsann akaraṇam{*5/106*}, evaṃ dṛṣṭārthatā bhavati. tasmān mukhyakrameṇāṅgānāṃ prayoga iti.
yat tu, dadhnaḥ pūrvaṃ pravṛttir iti. arthāt pūrvaṃ pravṛttiḥ, na pāṭhāt. prāvṛttikāc ca mukhyakramo balīyān, mukhyakrame gṛhyamāṇe prathama ekaḥ padārtho viprakṛṣṭakālaḥ syāt, prāvṛttike punar gṛhyamāṇe sarveṣāṃ viprakarṣaḥ. tasmān mukhyakramo balīyān iti. atha yal liṅgam uktam, dadhnaḥ pūrvam avadeyam [588]{*5/107*} iti. atrocyate, śṛtābhiprāyam{*5/108*} etad bhaviṣyati. tasmād adoṣaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Or [the cutting etc.] should be done according to the giving-order — whichever's giving [comes] first, its cuttings [come] first; therefore, [those] of the <s>Āgneya</s>. Why? Because the cutting etc. are subsumed by the injunction of giving — it has been stated that these are the commencements of giving, not separate items. The basting and cutting of that [oblation] are done precisely with the intention of giving. The bringing too is for the purpose of giving — [since] when it is not present, it cannot be performed; thus there is a visible purpose. Therefore the subsidiaries are employed according to the principal order.
As for [the argument] that 'the curd is customarily [done] first' — [we reply:] the custom of priority comes from the meaning, not from the recitation. And the principal order is stronger than the customary [order]. When the principal order is adopted, only one item — the first — would have a distant time; but when the customary [order] is adopted, all [items] have distant times. Therefore the principal order is stronger. As for the indicatory mark cited — 'the curd should be cut first' [588] — here we say: this will be understood as referring to the cooked [offering]. Therefore there is no fault.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_5,4.4 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_5,4.4 //

children.text: liṅgam apy asminn arthe bhavati, sa vai dhruvām evāgre 'bhighārayati, tato hi prathamāv ājyabhāgau yakṣyan bhavatīti. tasmād api mukhyakrameṇa niyama iti.
children.translated_text: There is also an indicatory mark supporting this interpretation: 'He first bastes the <s>dhruvā</s> (permanent ladle), for from that he will be about to offer the first two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions).' Therefore too, the fixed rule is according to the principal order.

children.text: vacanād iṣṭipūrvatvam // MS_5,4.5 //
children.translated_text: The priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) is because of the [Vedic] statement. // MS_5,4.5 //

children.text: iṣṭipūrvatvaṃ samānātam. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim iṣṭipūrvatvam, somapūrvatvaṃ vā vikalpaḥ{*5/109*}, athaveṣṭipūrvatvam eveti. kiṃ prāptam? iṣṭipūrvatvam eva syāt. kutaḥ? vacanāt, vacanam idaṃ bhavati, eṣa vai devaratho yad darśapūrṇamāsau, yo darśapūrṇamāsāv iṣṭvā somena yajate, rathaspaṣṭa evāvasāne vare devānām avasyatīti{*5/110*}, nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ. tasmād iṣṭipūrvatvam eveti.
children.translated_text: The priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> has been stated [as a principle]. There a doubt [arises]: is the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> and the priority of <s>Soma</s> an option, or is it the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> alone? What is the prima facie view? It should be the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> alone. Why? Because of the [Vedic] statement — this statement exists: 'This indeed is the chariot of the gods — the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. He who, having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, sacrifices with <s>Soma</s> — on a well-prepared chariot, as it were, enters into the finest abode of the gods.' There is no excess burden on the statement. Therefore it is the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> alone.

NOTES:
[{5/109: E2: <s>vikalpyate</s>}]
[{5/110: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.5.6.1}]

children.text: somaś caikeṣām agnyādheyasyartunakṣatrātikramavacanāt tadantenānarthakaṃ hi syāt // MS_5,4.6 //
children.translated_text: And for some [authorities], <s>Soma</s> [has priority] — because of the statement in the fire-establishment about the transgression of the season and constellation; for with that ending [interpretation], it would be purposeless. // MS_5,4.6 //

children.text: iṣṭipūrvatvam ity etad gṛhṇīmaḥ, kiṃ tu somaś caikeṣāṃ{*5/111*} pūro{*5/112*} darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ syāt. kutaḥ? agnyādheyasyartunakṣatrātikramavacanāt. yaḥ somena yakṣyamāṇo 'gnīn ādadhīta, nartuṃ sa{*5/113*} pratīkṣen na nakṣatram iti. yaḥ somayāgaṃ kartum ādadhīt, sa na pratīkṣeta nakṣatraṃ nāpy ṛtuṃ tāvaty evādadhītety ānantaryam ucyate. itarathā, ṛtunakṣatrātikramavacanam anarthakaṃ syāt [589]{*5/114*}, ānantarye 'napekṣyamāṇe yasyaivartunakṣatre ukte tasyaiva tayor anādaraḥ kīrtitaḥ syāt, tasmād asti somādhānayor ānantaryam iti. api ca vispaṣṭā cādyatanī vibhaktiḥ, somena yakṣyamāṇa iti, sā ca neṣṭipūrvatvam{*5/115*} anujñāya vivakṣyate, na tadādyatanakālavivakṣā, tatrāyaṃ śabdo vipratiṣidhyeta. tasmād ānantaryavivakṣety avagamyate.
children.translated_text: We accept the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s>; however, for some, <s>Soma</s> too would precede the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Why? Because of the statement in the fire-establishment (<s>agnyādheya</s>) about the transgression of the season (<s>ṛtu</s>) and constellation (<s>nakṣatra</s>): 'He who would establish the fires intending to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> — he should not wait for the season, nor for the constellation.' He who would establish [the fires] in order to perform the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice should not wait for the constellation nor for the season — he should establish them immediately. This states immediacy. Otherwise, the statement about transgression of the season and constellation would be purposeless [589] — if immediacy were not intended, when the season and constellation have been stated [as requirements] for the very one [who is doing the fire-establishment], the disregard of those two would [merely] be stating the obvious. Therefore there is immediacy between the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] and the fire-establishment. Moreover, the present-tense suffix is clear — '<s>yakṣyamāṇa</s>' (one who is about to sacrifice) — and that is not stated granting the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s>; it is not a statement about the time of that [iṣṭi]-day — otherwise, this [present-tense] word would be contradicted. Therefore it is understood as intending immediacy.

children.text: tadarthavacanāc ca nāviśeṣāt tadarthatvam // MS_5,4.7 //
children.translated_text: And because of the statement of purpose for that [Soma]; it is not because of non-distinction that [the fire-establishment] is for that purpose. // MS_5,4.7 //

children.text: itaś ca somādhānayor ānantaryam. kutaḥ? tadarthavacanāt, yaḥ somena yajeta sa agnim ādadhīteti ca. sarvair apy asau yakṣyamāṇo 'gnim ādhatte somenāgnihotrādibhiś ca, nāsati somasya viśeṣe somārthatā syāt. ayam asau viśeṣaḥ syāt, yad ānantaryaṃ somādhānayor iti.
children.translated_text: And for this further reason there is immediacy between <s>Soma</s> and the fire-establishment. Why? Because of the statement of purpose for that [Soma]: 'He who would sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> should establish the fire.' He too [who] is about to sacrifice with everything — <s>Soma</s>, <s>Agnihotra</s>, and the rest — establishes the fire. Without a distinction for <s>Soma</s> [specifically], the for-<s>Soma</s>-purpose would not be [stated]. This is the distinction: that there is immediacy between <s>Soma</s> and the fire-establishment.

children.text: ayakṣyamāṇasya ca pavamānahaviṣāṃ kālanirdeśād ānantaryād viśaṅkā syāt // MS_5,4.8 //
children.translated_text: And for one who is not going to sacrifice [with Soma], the time-designation of the <s>Pavamāna</s> offerings [suggests immediacy]; from the immediacy, there would be doubt. // MS_5,4.8 //

children.text: somenāyakṣyamāṇasya ca pavamānahaviṣāṃ kālo nirdiśyate, yaḥ somenāyakṣyaṃāṇo 'gnim ādadhīta, sa purā saṃvatsarād dhavīṃṣi nirvaped iti, na khalu kaścid ayakṣyamāṇaḥ, sarvasya vihitatvāt. tasmād anantaram ayakṣyamāṇa iti gamyate.
children.translated_text: And for one who is not going to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>, a time is designated for the <s>Pavamāna</s> offerings: 'He who, not intending to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>, would establish the fire — he should offer the [Pavamāna] oblations before the year [is complete].' Surely no one is 'not going to sacrifice' [permanently], since [Soma sacrifice] is enjoined for all. Therefore 'not going to sacrifice' is understood as [meaning] 'not immediately [going to sacrifice].'

children.text: iṣṭir ayakṣyamāṇasya, tādarthye somapūrvatvam // MS_5,4.9 //
children.translated_text: The <s>iṣṭi</s> [applies] to one not going to sacrifice [with Soma]; when [the fire-establishment] is for its [Soma's] purpose, then <s>Soma</s> has priority. // MS_5,4.9 //

children.text: idaṃ prayojanasūtraṃ varṇyate. kṣīṇam adhikaraṇam. kiṃ prayojanaṃ cintāyāḥ? iṣṭir ayakṣyamāṇasya somena nirabhisaṃdhika ādhāne. tadarthatve tu somapūrvatvam{*5/116*}, somārthatāyāṃ tv ādhānasya somapūrvatvaṃ syāt.
children.translated_text: This is the purpose-sūtra being explained. The topic is concluded. What is the purpose of the inquiry? The <s>iṣṭi</s> [applies] to one not going to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> — in a fire-establishment without [immediate] intent [toward Soma]. But when [the fire-establishment] is for the purpose of that [Soma], there is priority of <s>Soma</s> — when the fire-establishment is for the purpose of [the] <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], <s>Soma</s> would have priority.

children.text:

*{5/117: E2: 5,166; E6: 2,99}*
