children.text: utkarṣād brāhmaṇasya somaḥ syāt // MS_5,4.10 //
children.translated_text: Because of advancement, <s>Soma</s> would [come first] for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // MS_5,4.10 //

children.text: asty ādhānam, tatraiṣo 'rhaḥ samadhigataḥ, iṣṭipūrvatvaṃ somapūrvatvaṃ ceti. idānīṃ saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ trayāṇāṃ varṇānām iṣṭipūrvatvaṃ somapūrvatvaṃ vā, uta brāhmaṇasya somapūrvatvam eva, uta kevalā paurṇamāsy utkṛṣyate, brāhmaṇasyobhau kalpāv iti. atha vā karmāntaram idam, yad ūrdhvaṃ somāt, atha vaikaṃ havir utkṛṣyate, brāhmaṇasyobhāv eva kalpāv iti. kiṃ prāptam? trayāṇāṃ varṇānām iṣṭipūrvatvaṃ somapūrvatvaṃ vā. kutaḥ? aviṣeśāt. na kiṃcid viśeṣam avagacchāmaḥ. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, brāhmaṇasya somapūrvatvaṃ syāt. kasmāt? utkarṣāt, utkarṣo hi śrūyate, āgneyo vai brāhmaṇo devatayā, sa someneṣṭvāgnīsomīyo bhavati. yad evādaḥ paurṇamāsaṃ haviḥ, tatra hy{*5/118*} anunirvapet, tarhy ubhayadevatyo bhavatīti. kim iva hi vacanaṃ na kuryāt. tasmād brāhmaṇasya somapūrvatvam eveti.
children.translated_text: There is the fire-establishment. There, this entitlement has been ascertained — [both] the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> and the priority of <s>Soma</s>. Now a doubt [arises]: is it the priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> or the priority of <s>Soma</s> for all three classes (<s>varṇas</s>), or is it the priority of <s>Soma</s> alone for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or is only the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> (full-moon offering) advanced, with both options for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>? Or is this a different rite — that which is beyond <s>Soma</s> — or is it [that] one oblation is advanced, with both options for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>? What is the prima facie view? The priority of the <s>iṣṭi</s> or the priority of <s>Soma</s> [applies] to all three classes. Why? Because of non-distinction — we do not perceive any distinction. Given this prima facie view, we say: <s>Soma</s> would have priority for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Why? Because of advancement — for advancement is heard: 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed of <s>Āgneya</s> deity; having sacrificed with <s>Soma</s>, he becomes <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> (belonging to both <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>). Let him offer that <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> oblation over there — then he becomes of both deities.' What word indeed would it not produce? Therefore the priority of <s>Soma</s> alone [applies] for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/118: E2: tat tarhy}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/118: E2: <s>tat tarhy</s>}]

children.text: paurṇamāsī vā śrutisaṃyogāt // MS_5,4.11 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is only] the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> [that is advanced], because of the connection with the [Vedic] word. // MS_5,4.11 //

children.text: yad uktam, brāhmaṇasya somapūrvatvam eveti, tan na, tasyāpy ubhau kalpau. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, na hi kalpayor brāhmaṇasya kaścid viśeṣa āmnāyate. nanv idānīm evoktam, brāhmaṇasyotkarṣa iti. neti brūmaḥ, paurṇamāsīmātrasya tatrotkarṣaḥ. śrutisaṃyogaḥ paurṇamāsyās tatra, yad evādaḥ paurṇamāsaṃ havir iti, yāvad vacanaṃ vācanikam, tatra na nyāyaḥ kramate. tulyayor ekadeśa utkṛṣṭe nūnam aparo 'py ekadeśa utkṛṣyata iti.
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'the priority of <s>Soma</s> alone for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — that is not so; for him too, both options [exist]. Why? Because of non-distinction — for no distinction between the options is stated for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [The objector says:] but was it not just now said — 'there is advancement for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'? We reply: no — the advancement there is of the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> alone. The connection of the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> with the [Vedic] word there [is seen in]: 'that <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> oblation over there.' What is stated [explicitly] by the word is verbal, and there logical reasoning does not extend. When one part of equals is advanced, it does not follow that the other part is also advanced.

children.text: sarvasya vaikakarmyāt // MS_5,4.12 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, of the entire [Darśapūrṇamāsa], because of the unity of the rite. // MS_5,4.12 //

children.text: yad ucyate, kevalā paurṇamāsy utkṛṣyata iti. tan na, kṛtsnasya darśapūrṇamāsakarmaṇa utkarṣaḥ, evaṃ phalena saṃbandhaḥ, itarathā na syāt phalam. ekadeśatvāt paurṇamāsyāḥ, kevalāyām utkṛṣyamāṇāyām avaśiṣṭasya pūrvatra kriyamāṇasya na phalaṃ syāt, ekadeśatvāt, aphalatvāc coktam api na kriyeta. samudāye cotkṛṣyamāṇe bhavati phalam. tasmād arthāt samudāyasyotkarṣaḥ, evaṃ kṛtsnopadeśo 'rthavān bhaviṣyatīti. tasmāt sarvasyotkarṣaḥ, somapūrvatvam eva brāhmaṇasyeti.
children.translated_text: As for what is said — 'only the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> is advanced' — that is not so; the advancement is of the entire <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rite. [For] thus there is connection with the fruit; otherwise there would be no fruit. Since the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> is [only] a part — when it alone is advanced, the remainder being performed earlier [on its own] would have no fruit, because of being [only] a part; and being fruitless, even what has been stated would not be performed. But when the aggregate is advanced, there is fruit. Therefore, from the meaning, the advancement is of the aggregate — thus the instruction concerning the whole will be meaningful. Therefore the advancement is of the entire [rite]; the priority of <s>Soma</s> alone [applies] for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: syād vā vidhis tadarthena // MS_5,4.13 //
children.translated_text: Or there would be a [separate] injunction, for that purpose [mentioned in the text]. // MS_5,4.13 //

children.text: naitad asti{*5/120*}, yad evaṃ samudāyasyāsati vacana utkarṣaḥ parikalpyeta, tasmād anyad evaivaṃ nāmakaṃ karma, ūrdhvaṃ somāt syāt. evam ekadeśasyāśrutaṃ phalaṃ na kalpayitavyaṃ bhaviṣyati. nāmadheyaṃ tu dvayoḥ karmaṇor ekam, akṣāḥ pādāḥ māṣā iti yathā. paurṇamāsadharmakaṃ vā karmāntaraṃ codyata iti karmavidhānam, śruter etad bhavati, tad vākyasya bādhakam. tasmāt karmāntaram iti.
children.translated_text: This is not [correct] — that the advancement of the aggregate should be postulated in the absence of a [Vedic] statement. Therefore it is a different rite entirely bearing that very name, [performed] after <s>Soma</s>. Thus, the unheard fruit of a part will not need to be postulated. The name is one for both rites — like 'dice,' 'feet,' '<s>māṣas</s>' [can refer to different things]. Or, a different rite having the characteristics of the <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> is being enjoined — this is a rite-injunction. This comes from the [Vedic] word, and that overrides the sentence. Therefore it is a different rite.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/120: E2: naitad asti kṛtsnotkarṣa iti}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/120: E2: <s>naitad asti kṛtsnotkarṣa iti</s>}]

children.text: prakaraṇāt tu kālaḥ syāt // MS_5,4.14 //
children.translated_text: But from the context, [it would indicate] time. // MS_5,4.14 //

children.text: karmāntarasyaitadvācakam iti pramāṇābhāvaḥ. prakṛtasya karmaṇo vācakam iti pratyakṣam, yac ca sapramāṇakam, tad grāhyam, anyāyaś cānekārthatvam. dharmagrahaṇe lakṣaṇāśabdaḥ śrutisaṃbhave kalpyaḥ syāt. api cāsya rūpaṃ na gamyate, rūpāvacanān na karmāntaram. tasmāt prasiddhena nāmnā prakṛtasya karmaṇo grahaṇaṃ kālavidhānārthaṃ syāt. phalavattvāc ca kṛtsnasyotkarṣaḥ, brāhmaṇasya [592]{*5/121*} ca tathaiva. yat tu, śrutir vākyād balīyasīti, atrocyate, yatra phalaṃ na śrūyate, vākyārtho 'pi tāvat tatra gṛhyate. na ca, iha phalasya śravaṇam asti. kalpyaṃ phalam iti yad ucyate, na tat, phalavacanam{*5/122*} antareṇa. tatra phalavacanaḥ śabdaḥ kalpyeta, tena ca sahaikavākyatā. kālavacanena tu saha pratyakṣeṇaikavākyateti. tasmān na karmāntaram. sthitaṃ tāvad aparyavasitam adhikaraṇam{*5/123*}.
children.translated_text: There is no valid basis [for the view that] this is a designation of a different ritual act. That it is a designation of the ritual act under discussion — this is directly perceived. And what has a valid basis should be accepted; and being multi-referential is improper. If one were to construe a figurative expression in grasping the <s>dharma</s>, that would be possible [only] when a literal understanding is not possible. Moreover, the form of this [supposed other ritual] is not apprehended — because of the absence of a statement about form, it is not a different ritual. Therefore the grasping [of the familiar name] by its well-known name is for the purpose of prescribing the time of the ritual act under discussion. And because of the fruitfulness of the whole, there is an elevation [in time] of the entire [rite]; [592] and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage confirms] the same. As for what was said — 'the [Vedic] statement is stronger than the sentence' — to this we reply: where a fruit is not heard, even the sentence-meaning is grasped there. And here, there is no hearing of a fruit. As for the claim that 'the fruit is to be posited' — that is not so without a statement of fruit. There, a word stating the fruit would have to be posited, and syntactic unity with that [posited word would have to be established]. But with the word stating the time, the syntactic unity is directly perceived. Therefore it is not a different ritual. This topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) is thus settled as inconclusive.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/121: E2: 5,186; E6: 2,100}*
*{5/122: E2: phalaṃ vacanam}*
*{5/123: E2: adhikaraṇam. antarā cintāntaraṃ vakṣyate}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:

[{5/122: E2: <s>phalaṃ vacanam</s>}]
[{5/123: E2: <s>adhikaraṇam. antarā cintāntaraṃ vakṣyate</s>}]

children.text: svakāle syād avipratiṣedhāt // MS_5,4.15 //
children.translated_text: [The <s>Soma</s> sacrifice] should be at its own time, because there is no conflict. // MS_5,4.15 //

children.text: yaḥ somena yakṣyamāṇo 'gnim ādadhīta, nartuṃ sa{*5/124*} pratīkṣen{*5/125*} na nakṣatram iti. atra saṃdehaḥ, kim ādhānasyāyaṃ kālaviśeṣabādhaḥ, uta somasyeti. kiṃ prāptam? ādhānasya kālabādhaḥ, svakāle syāt somaḥ. kutaḥ? avipratiṣedhāt, aṅgam ādhānam, tasya kālabādho nyāyyaḥ, na pradhānasya. aṅgaguṇavirodhe ca tādarthyād iti vakṣyate{*5/126*}.
children.translated_text: 'He who, being about to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>, establishes the fires — he should not wait for the season nor for the [appropriate] constellation.' Here a doubt [arises]: does this override the time-restriction of the fire-establishment, or of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice]? What is the prima facie view? It overrides the time of the fire-establishment; the <s>Soma</s> should be at its own time. Why? Because there is no conflict — the fire-establishment is a subsidiary; overriding its time is proper, not [overriding] the principal's [time]. And 'in a conflict between a subsidiary and an attribute, [the subsidiary yields] because of serving another's purpose' — this will be stated [later].

children.text: apanayo vādhānasya sarvakālatvāt // MS_5,4.16 //
children.translated_text: Or the displacement is from the fire-establishment, because of [the fire-establishment's] being for all times. // MS_5,4.16 //

children.text: apanayo vādhānāt{*5/127*} somakālasya syāt. kutaḥ? ādhānasya sarvakālatvāt, naivādhāne kaścit kālaniyamo 'sti, yad ahar evainaṃ śraddhopanamet{*5/128*} tad ahar ādadhīteti{*5/129*}. aprāptam eva tad ādhānasya, yat pratiṣidhyate. tasmāt somasya kālabādha iti.
children.translated_text: Or the displacement of the <s>Soma</s> time would be from the fire-establishment. Why? Because the fire-establishment is for all times — there is absolutely no time-restriction for the fire-establishment: 'On whatever day faith seizes him, on that day he should establish [the fires].' What is being prohibited is something not [yet] obtained for the fire-establishment. Therefore the time-override is of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice].

NOTES:

[{5/128: E1 (v.l.): <s>yajña upanamet</s>}]
[{5/129: <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 2.1.3.9}]
[{5/130: E2: 5,169; E6: 2,101}]

children.text: paurṇamāsy ūrdhvaṃ somād brāhmaṇasya vacanāt // MS_5,4.17 //
children.translated_text: The full-moon [offering alone is shifted] to after the <s>Soma</s>, because of the statement of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // MS_5,4.17 //

children.text: sthitād uttaram. na vaitad{*5/131*} asti, kṛtsnau darśapūrṇamāsāv utkṛṣyete, ūrdhvaṃ somāt, kevalā paurṇamāsy utkṛṣyate. kutaḥ? vacanāt, vacanam idam, yad evādaḥ paurṇamāsaṃ havis tat tarhy anunirvaped iti, nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ. tasmāt paurṇamāsīmātram utkṛṣyeta. yat tu phalaṃ nāstīti, samudāyād eva phalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, vacanād evaṃ vijñānāt. tasmād adoṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: [This follows] from what has been established. It is not the case that both the <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> are elevated — [shifted] to after the <s>Soma</s>. Only the <s>Pūrṇamāsī</s> alone is elevated. Why? Because of the [Vedic] statement — this statement [exists]: 'Whatever full-moon oblation is yonder, that he should offer at that time.' There is no overloading of the statement. Therefore only the <s>Pūrṇamāsī</s> should be elevated. As for [the objection] that 'there is no fruit [for a partial observance]' — the fruit will come from the aggregate itself — this is understood from the [Vedic] statement. Therefore there is no fault.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/131: E2: caitad}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/131: E2: <s>caitad</s>}]

children.text: ekaṃ{*5/132*} śabdasāmarthyāt prāk kṛtsnavidhānāt // MS_5,4.18 //
children.translated_text: Or a single [oblation is shifted], because of the capacity of the word [being limited to that]; [and] because the complete [rite] is prescribed before [<s>Soma</s>]. // MS_5,4.18 //

children.text: ekaṃ vā havir utkṛṣyeta, na kṛtsnā paurṇamāsī. kutaḥ? śabdasāmarthyāt, ekaṃ havir utkraṣṭuṃ śabdaḥ samarthaḥ, yad evādaḥ paurṇamāsaṃ havir iti śrūyate, yāvad vacanaṃ vācanikam, tāvad vacanenotkraṣṭuṃ śakyate, nānyad api. prāk somāt kṛtsnaṃ vidhīyate. tato yad vacanenotkṛṣyate, tad ūrdhvaṃ somāt, yan notkṛṣyate, tat prāg bhavitum arhati. tasmād ekaṃ havir utkraṣṭavyam, brāhmaṇasyobhau kalpāv iti.
children.translated_text: Or a single oblation should be elevated, not the entire <s>Pūrṇamāsī</s>. Why? Because of the capacity of the word — the word is capable of elevating a single oblation: 'whatever full-moon oblation is yonder' is heard. As much as can be elevated by the statement — the verbal [instruction extends] as far as the statement [goes] — that much alone can be elevated by the statement, not anything else. Before <s>Soma</s>, the complete [rite] is prescribed. Therefore what is elevated by the statement is after <s>Soma</s>; what is not elevated should properly be before. Therefore a single oblation is to be elevated — the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [allows for] both interpretations.

children.text: puroḍāśas tv anirdeśe tadyukte devatābhāvāt // MS_5,4.19 //
children.translated_text: But it is the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, when there is no [further] specification, because of the absence of another deity connected with that [context]. // MS_5,4.19 //

children.text: idaṃ śrūyate, āgneyo vai brāhmaṇo devatayā, sa someneṣṭvāgnīṣomīyo bhavati, yad evādaḥ paurṇamāsaṃ havis tat tarhy anunirvapet, tarhy ubhayadevatyo bhavatīti. yasmāt tasmin kāle so [594]{*5/133*} 'gnīṣomīyo bhavati, na prācīne kāle tasmād ado havir anunirvaped iti, agnīṣomīyatvaṃ vidhāya dvidevatākatvaṃ hetutvena nirdiśyate. tasmād agnīṣomīyaṃ havir hetumat syāt, nānyadevatākam, tadāsāv agnīṣomau yaṣṭum arhati, na prāk sāsya devateti bhavati puruṣasyāpi yaṣṭur devatābhisaṃbandhaḥ. tasmāt puroḍāśo 'gnīṣomīyo nānyad dhavir iti siddham.
children.translated_text: This is heard: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed [sacred to] <s>Agni</s> by deity. Having sacrificed with <s>Soma</s>, he becomes [sacred to] <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>. Whatever full-moon oblation is yonder, that he should offer at that time; then he becomes [sacred to] both deities.' [594] Since at that time he becomes [sacred to] <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, not at an earlier time — therefore 'he should offer that oblation.' Having prescribed the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> nature [of the oblation], the two-deity status is indicated as the reason. Therefore the oblation connected with <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> would have a reason [for being shifted]; not one with another deity. Then he deserves to worship <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, not before [<s>Soma</s>] — that is his deity. Thus there is a connection of the deity with the sacrificing person as well. Therefore it is the <s>Agnīṣomīya puroḍāśa</s>, and no other oblation — this is established.

children.text: ājyam apīti cet // MS_5,4.20 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues:] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) also — // MS_5,4.20 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasy agnīṣomīyatvāt puroḍāśa iti, ājyam api hy agnīṣomīyam. tasmāt tad apy utkṛṣyeta.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that because of [its] being <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, it is the <s>puroḍāśa</s> [that is elevated] — the <s>ājya</s> too is <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. Therefore that too should be elevated.

children.text: na miśradevatatvād aindrāgnavat // MS_5,4.21 //
children.translated_text: No, because of [its] having mixed deities — like the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [offering]. // MS_5,4.21 //

children.text: miśradevataṃ hy ājyam, agnīṣomīyam, prājāpatyam, vaiṣṇavam iti ca. puroḍāśas tv agnīṣomīya eva. na tv atra miśradevatasya vādaḥ, miśradevatasya hi prāg api bhāvo 'vakalpyate. yad api tadānīṃ yajamāno nāgniṣomīyas taddevatārhaḥ, tathāpy ājyaṃ haviḥ kariṣyaty eva, prajāpatiṃ yakṣyati, viṣṇuṃ vā. tasmāt tasyordhvabhāve na eṣa hetur agnīṣomīyatvaṃ nāma. yathā caturdhākaraṇaṃ miśradevatatvād aindrāgnena bhavati, tadvat tatrāgneya iti, aindrāgno na śakyate vaditum, tad dhitaḥ sākāṅkṣān notpadyata iti. evam ihāgnīṣomīyaśabdena na śakyam ājyaṃ vaditum agnīṣomīyo hi asau{*5/134*}. tasmāc chakyaṃ prāg yajamānena kartum iti. tasmān na tasyotkarṣe 'gnīṣomīyatā yajamānasya hetur iti, miśradevatasya grahaṇasāmānyād{*5/135*} aindrāgnavad ity uktam.
children.translated_text: For the <s>ājya</s> has mixed deities — it is <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> as well. But the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> alone. The argument here is not about what has mixed deities, for what has mixed deities can be construed as existing even before [<s>Soma</s>]. Even though the sacrificer at that time is not [yet qualified] for the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> deity, he will still make the <s>ājya</s> oblation — he will sacrifice to <s>Prajāpati</s> or to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Therefore the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> status is not the reason for its being [shifted] to after [<s>Soma</s>]. Just as the fourfold division (<s>caturdhākaraṇa</s>) is accomplished with the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [offering] because of [its] having mixed deities — likewise there with the <s>Āgneya</s>, one cannot say it is <s>Aindrāgna</s> since the [Aindrāgna identity] does not arise because [the sentence] is expectant. Similarly here, the <s>ājya</s> cannot be designated by the word <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, for it [the ājya] is not [exclusively] <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>. Therefore it can be performed by the sacrificer before [<s>Soma</s>]. Hence the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> status of the sacrificer is not the reason for its elevation — it is said 'like the <s>Aindrāgna</s>' because of the commonality of grasping what has mixed deities.

children.text: vikṛteḥ prakṛtikālatvāt sadyaskālottarā vikṛtis tayoḥ pratyakṣaśiṣṭatvāt // MS_5,4.22 //
children.translated_text: Because the modification has the time of the archetype, the modification is after the one-day [rite]; because both are taught by direct [Vedic] statement. // MS_5,4.22 //

children.text: iha vaikṛtāni karmāṇy udāharaṇam, aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped ityevamādīni. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim etā vikṛtayaḥ sadyaskālāḥ, uta dvyahakālā iti. kiṃ prāptam? vikṛtiḥ prākṛtān dharmāṃś codakena gṛhṇāti, atas te dharmā ānumānikāḥ, paurṇamāsī cānyaḥ kālaḥ. sa yadi vā prakṛtyā gṛhyeta, yadi vā vikṛtyā, asaṃbhave 'nyatarasyāḥ kālas tyaktavyaḥ, tatrānumāniko vaikṛtasya tyajyatām, na pratyakṣaśrutaḥ prākṛtasyeti nyāyyam. tasmāt sadyaskālā etā vikṛtayo bhaveyur iti.
children.translated_text: Here, modified ritual acts are the example — 'he should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to <s>Indrāgni</s>' and the like. There a doubt [arises]: are these modifications one-day [rites] or two-day [rites]? What is the prima facie view? A modification takes the archetypal rules through the force of the injunction; therefore those rules are inferential. The <s>Pūrṇamāsī</s> is [performed on] a different day. Whether that [time] is grasped through the archetype or through the modification — when one of the two is impossible, a time must be abandoned. There, the inferential [time] of the modification should be abandoned, not the one directly heard for the archetype — this is proper. Therefore these modifications would be one-day [rites].

children.text: dvaiyahakālye tu yathānyāyam // MS_5,4.23 //
children.translated_text: But when performed as two-day [rites], it is done according to proper procedure. // MS_5,4.23 //

children.text: dvaiyahakālye kriyamāṇe yathānyāyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati, tasmād dvaiyahakālyaṃ syāt. codakas tathānugṛhīto bhavati, prakṛtau hi śrūyate, pūrvedyur agniṃ gṛhṇāti, uttaram ahar devatāṃ yajatīti. tasmād dvyahakālam ekam abhinirvartyam, tadahar evopakramyāparedyuḥ parisamāpayet.
children.translated_text: When performed as a two-day [rite], it is done according to proper procedure; therefore it should be a two-day [rite]. The injunction is thus supported — for in the basic rite it is heard: 'On the preceding day he takes the fire; on the following day he sacrifices to the deity.' Therefore one [rite] should be accomplished over two days — beginning on that [first] day, one should complete it on the following day.

children.text: vacanād vaikakālyaṃ syāt // MS_5,4.24 //
children.translated_text: Because of the [Vedic] statement, it should be performed on a single day. // MS_5,4.24 //

children.text: naitad evam, dvyahakālā vikṛtayo bhaveyur iti, sadyaskālāḥ syuḥ. kasmāt? vacanam idaṃ bhavati, iṣṭyā{*5/137*} paśunā somenāgrayaṇena vā yakṣyamāṇaḥ sa paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā yajeteti, sāṅgasyaitad vacanam. tasmāt sāṅgaṃ paurṇa[596]{*5/138*}māsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā kurvīteti gamyate, tena sadyaskālā vikṛtayaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that the modifications should be two-day [rites]; they should be one-day [rites]. Why? This statement exists: 'He who is about to sacrifice with an offering (<s>iṣṭi</s>), with an animal, with <s>Soma</s>, or with the <s>Agrayaṇa</s> — he should sacrifice on the full-moon day or the new-moon day.' This is a statement about [the rite] together with its subsidiaries. Therefore it is understood that the [rite] together with its subsidiaries should be performed on the full-moon [596] or new-moon day. Hence the modifications are one-day [rites].

children.text: sāṃnāyyāgnīṣomīyavikārā ūrdhvaṃ somāt prakṛtivat // MS_5,4.25 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> modifications [are performed] after <s>Soma</s>, like their archetypes. // MS_5,4.25 //

children.text: iha sāṃnāyyavikārāś cāgnīṣomīyavikārāś codāharaṇam, sāṃnāyyavikārās tāvad yathā, āmikṣā{*5/139*} paśur iti, agnīṣomīyam{*5/140*} ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapec chyāmākam, brāhmaṇo vasante brahmavarcaskāma ity{*5/141*}evamādyaḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim ete prāg ūrdhvaṃ ca somāt, utordhvam iti. kiṃ prāptam? prāg ūrdhvaṃ ca, viśeṣānavagamāt. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, ūrdhvaṃ somād syur iti, prakṛtir hy eṣām ūrdhvaṃ somāt, codakena ebhir api ūrdhvaṃ somāt bhavitavyam. sānnāyyasya ūrdhvaṃ somāt, vacanena, asomayājī saṃnayed iti. agnīsomīyasyāpi, āgneyo vai brāhmaṇo devatayā sa someneṣṭvā bhavati{*5/142*}, yad evādaḥ paurṇamāsaṃ haviḥ, tat tarhy anunirvaped iti, tarhi sa ubhayadevatyo bhavatīti, tadvikṛtir api somād ūrdhvaṃ bhavitum arhati.
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> modifications and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> modifications are the example. First, the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> modifications — such as the <s>āmikṣā</s> (curds), the animal [offering]; and the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [modifications] — 'One should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] of <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) [to Agni-Soma]; a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> desiring spiritual luster [should offer] in spring' — and the like. There a doubt [arises]: should these be [performed] both before and after <s>Soma</s>, or [only] after? What is the prima facie view? Both before and after, because of the absence of a distinguishing [rule]. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: they should be after <s>Soma</s> — for their archetype is after <s>Soma</s>, and through the force of the injunction, these too must be after <s>Soma</s>. The <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> is after <s>Soma</s> by [Vedic] statement: 'One who has not sacrificed with <s>Soma</s> should prepare the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>' [i.e., only the non-<s>Soma</s>-sacrificer uses the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> as a substitute]. The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> too [is after Soma]: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed [sacred to] <s>Agni</s> by deity; having sacrificed with <s>Soma</s>, he becomes [Agnīṣomīya]. Whatever full-moon oblation is yonder, that he should then offer' — then he becomes [sacred to] both deities. Its modification too should properly be after <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: tathā somavikārā darśapūrṇamāsābhyām // MS_5,4.26 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>Soma</s> modifications [are performed] after the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. // MS_5,4.26 //

children.text: somavikārā gavādaya ekāhāḥ. teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ darśapūrṇamāsāt prāg ūrdhvaṃ ca prayoktavyāḥ, utordhvam iti. kiṃ prāptam? aniyamaḥ, aviśeṣāt. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, tathā [597]{*5/143*} somavikārāḥ, darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ūrdhvaṃ syuḥ, jyotiṣṭomo darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ūrdhvaṃ bhavati, darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā somena yajeteti{*5/144*}. codakenaiṣa dharmo gavādiṣv apy ekāheṣu prāpnoti. tasmāt te 'pi darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ūrdhvaṃ kartavyā iti.
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> modifications are the <s>Gava</s> and other one-day (<s>ekāha</s>) rites. Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: should they be employed before or after the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, or [only] after? What is the prima facie view? No fixed rule, because of the absence of a distinction. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: likewise, [597] <s>Soma</s> modifications should be after the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is after the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>: 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>.' This rule, through the force of the injunction, extends to the <s>Gava</s> and other one-day [rites] as well. Therefore they too should be performed after the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.

children.text: dravyāṇāṃ karmasaṃyoge guṇatvenābhisaṃbandhaḥ//6.1.1//
children.translated_text: When substances are connected with a ritual act, the connection is as a subsidiary. // MS_6,1.1 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajetetyevamādi samāmnāyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ svargo guṇataḥ, karma pradhānataḥ, uta karma guṇataḥ, svargaḥ pradhānata iti. kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? iha svargakāmo 'pi nirdiśyate, yajetety api. atra svargakāmayāgayoḥ saṃbandho gamyate. tasmiṃś ca saṃbandhe kiṃ yāgaḥ sādhanatvena saṃbadhyate, uta sādhyatveneti bhavati vicāraṇā.
tatra yadi svargakāmasya puruṣasya yāgaḥ kartavyatayā codyate, svargakāmena yāgaḥ kartavya iti, svargecchāviśiṣṭasya sa sidhyatīti gamyate. svargecchā tatra puruṣasya yāgaṃ pratyupadiśyate, tena tasya sa sidhyati nānyasyeti. yaḥ svargakāmaḥ, sa śaknoti puruṣo yāgaṃ sādhayitum.
atha svargakāmasya kāmaḥ kartavyatayā codyate, tato yāgaviśiṣṭā kartavyateti yāgaḥ sādhako 'bhyupagamyate. sa cāyam ubhayor apy artha ekasmād uccaritād vākyād gamyate{*5/146*}, yāgo vā kartavyaḥ kāmo veti. na caitad yaugapadyena saṃbhavati, yadā kāmaḥ, na tadā yāgaḥ, yadā yāgaḥ, na tadā kāmaḥ, vacanavyaktibhedāt. upapannaḥ saṃśayaḥ.
[599]{*5/147*} tathedam aparaṃ saṃdigdham. kiṃ prītiḥ svargaḥ, uta dravyam iti. yadi dravyaṃ svargaḥ, tataḥ pradhānaṃ karma, dravyaṃ guṇabhūtam. atha prītiḥ svargaḥ, tato yāgo guṇabhūtaḥ, svargaḥ pradhānam iti. kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? nāsty atra kāmasya guṇatvena prādhānyena vā śrutiḥ, saṃbandhamātraṃ tv asya yāgena gamyate, dravyasya tu karmārthatā svabhāvataḥ, puruṣaprayatnasya ca phalārthatā.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? svargo guṇataḥ, karma pradhānata iti. tatra tāvad{*5/148*} varṇayanti, dravyaṃ svarga iti. katham avagamyate? sarveṣām eva śabdānām arthajñāne laukikaḥ prayogo 'bhyupāyaḥ, tasmiṃś ca laukike prayoge dravyavacanaḥ svargaśabdo lakṣyate, kauśikāni{*5/149*} sūkṣmāṇi vāsāṃsi svargaḥ, candanāni svargaḥ, dvyaṣṭavarṣāḥ striyaḥ svarga iti. yad yat prītimad dravyam, tat tat svargaśabdenocyate. tena sāmānādhikaraṇyāt prītimad dravyaṃ svarga iti mānyāmahe, upamānāc chabdapravṛttir iti cet. na hi kasmiṃścid anupamite{*5/150*} loke prasiddhaḥ, yasyaitad upamānaṃ syāt, tasmān nopamānam. ato dravyaṃ svarga iti.
netyāha, prītiḥ svarga iti, na dravyam, vyabhicārāt, tad eva hi dravyaṃ kasyāṃcid avasthāyāṃ na svargaśabdo 'bhidhāti. prītiṃ tu na kasyāṃcid avasthāyāṃ na{*5/151*}, nābhidadhāti. tasmād anvayavyatirekābhyām etad avagamyate, prītau svargaśabdo vartata iti.
naitad asti, prīter abhidhāyakaḥ svargaśabda iti. kutaḥ? viśeṣaṇatvāt{*5/152*}. yad viśeṣaṇam, na tac chabdenocyate. tad yathā, daṇḍīti daṇḍanimittaḥ puruṣavacanaḥ, daṇḍo 'sya [600]{*5/153*} nimittam, nābhidheyaḥ. evam eṣa na prītivacanaḥ prītisādhanavacanas tv eṣa svargaśabda iti.
nanu svargaśabdo loke prasiddho viśiṣṭe deśe. yāsmin noṣṇam, na śītam, na kṣut, na tṛṣṇā, nāratiḥ, na glāniḥ, puṇyakṛta eva pretya tatra gacchanti, nānye. atrocyate, yadi tatra kecid amṛtvā gacchanti{*5/154*}, tata āgacchanty ajanitvā, na tarhi sa pratyakṣo deśa evaṃjātīyakaḥ, na tv anumānād gamyate{*5/155*}.
nanu{*5/156*} cānye siddhāḥ kecid dṛṣṭavantaḥ, te cākhyātavanta iti cet. na tatra pramāṇam asti, siddhā evaṃjātīyakāḥ santi, te ca dṛṣṭvācakṣīrann iti. tasmād evaṃjātīyako deśa eva nāsti.
nanu ca lokād ākhyānebhyo vedāc cāvagamyate, deśa evaṃjātīyakaḥ svarga iti. tan na, puruṣāṇām evaṃvidhena deśenāsaṃbandhād apramāṇaṃ vacaḥ. ākhyānam api puruṣapraṇītatvād anādaraṇīyam. vaidikam api svargākhyānaṃ vidhiparaṃ nāsty eva, bhavati tu vidhyantareṇaikavākyabhūtaṃ stutiparam. yady api kevalasukhaśravaṇārthāpattyā tādṛśo deśaḥ syāt, tathāpy asmatpakṣasyāvirodhaḥ, prītisādhane svargaśabda iti. tena deśena vyavahārābhāvāt, kutas tasyābhidhāyakaḥ svargaśabdo bhaviṣyatīti{*5/157*}.
yadā prītimad dravyaṃ svargaḥ, tadā brūmaḥ, dravyāṇāṃ karmasaṃyoge guṇatvenābhisaṃbandha iti, yāgo 'tra kartavya iti śrūyate svargakāmasya. tatrāvaśyaṃ svargasya yāgasya ca saṃbandhaḥ, tatra bhūtaṃ dravyam, bhavyaṃ karma. bhūtasya ca bhavyārthatā nyāyyā, dṛṣṭārthatvāt. na tu bhavyasya bhūtārthatā, tatra dṛṣṭa upakāras tyajyeta.
kathaṃ punar avagamyate, yāgaḥ kartavyatayā codyata iti, [601]{*5/158*} yadā kāmasyāpi kartavyatāsmād vākyād avagamyate. ucyate, kāmasya kartavyatā vākyāt, yajyarthasya kartavyatā śruteḥ, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī. tasmād ayam arthaḥ, svargakāmo yāgaṃ kuryād iti svargakāmasya yāgaḥ kartavya iti. kartavyaś ca sukhavān, akartavyo duḥkhavān. kartavya iti cainaṃ brūte. tasmāt sukhaphalo yāgo bhaviṣyati, sa tu yasyecchā, tasya sidhyati nānyasyeti gamyate. tena svargecchā yāgasya guṇabhūtā, sarvasyāpi karmaṇo dravyecchā bhavati guṇabhūtā, tayā dravyam ānetuṃ yatate, dṛṣṭenaiva dvāreṇa. iha tu svargasaṃjñakadravyecchaiva niyamyate, yathaiva sā guṇabhūtā prāptā. tathaiva sati niyamyate, dṛṣṭenaiva dvāreṇa, nādṛṣṭenopakāreṇa. tena svargechayā guṇabhūtayā svargadravyaṃ prati yatiṣyate yāgaṃ sādhayitum. athāpy adṛṣṭena, tathāpi na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text:
It is recorded: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>'; 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — and so forth. There a doubt [arises]: is heaven (<s>svarga</s>) secondary, with the ritual action primary? Or is the ritual action secondary, with heaven primary? Whence the doubt? Here, 'one desiring heaven' is mentioned, and 'he should sacrifice' as well. From this, the connection between the desire for heaven and the sacrifice is understood. In that connection, the question arises: is the sacrifice connected as a means [to an end], or as the end [itself]?
If the sacrifice is enjoined as something to be done by the person who desires heaven — 'the sacrifice should be performed by one desiring heaven' — then it is understood that it is accomplished for one who is characterized by the desire for heaven. There, the desire for heaven is being indicated to the person as [a qualification] for the sacrifice; thereby it is accomplished for him and not for another. He who desires heaven — that person is able to accomplish the sacrifice.
But if the desire of the one desiring heaven is enjoined as something to be done, then the 'to-be-done-ness' is qualified by the sacrifice, and the sacrifice is accepted as the means. And this meaning of both [interpretations] is understood from a single uttered sentence — whether the sacrifice is to be done, or the desire [is to be fulfilled]. And this cannot [apply to both] simultaneously: when it is the desire, it is not the sacrifice [that is primary]; when the sacrifice, not the desire — because of the difference in the manifestation of the statement. The doubt is well-established.
Furthermore, there is this other doubt: is heaven pleasure (<s>prīti</s>), or a substance (<s>dravya</s>)? If heaven is a substance, then the ritual action is primary, and the substance is secondary. But if heaven is pleasure, then the sacrifice is secondary and heaven is primary. Whence this doubt? There is no [Vedic] statement [showing] the desire [for heaven] either as secondary or as primary; only its connection with the sacrifice is understood. But it is the nature of a substance to serve the purpose of an action, and of human effort to serve the purpose of a result.
What is the prima facie view? Heaven is secondary, the ritual action is primary. On this [view], they first explain: heaven is a substance. How is this understood? For understanding the meaning of all words, common usage in the world is the method. And in that common usage, the word <s>svarga</s> is observed to denote a substance: 'Silk garments are heaven'; 'Sandalwood is heaven'; 'Women of sixteen years are heaven.' Whatever substance that is delightful is called by the word <s>svarga</s>. Therefore, because of co-referentiality, we hold that a delightful substance is heaven. [If one says:] the word is applied through comparison — [we reply:] no, there is nothing uncompared well-known in the world of which this would be a comparison. Therefore it is not a comparison. Hence heaven is a substance.
He [the opponent] says: no — heaven is pleasure, not a substance, because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). For that very substance, in some condition, is not denoted by the word <s>svarga</s>. But pleasure — there is no condition in which it is not [so denoted]. Therefore, by the method of agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), this is understood: the word <s>svarga</s> applies to pleasure.
This is not so — that the word <s>svarga</s> denotes pleasure. Why? Because [pleasure functions as] a qualifier. What is a qualifier is not denoted by the word. Just as in '<s>daṇḍin</s>' (staff-bearer) — the word refers to a person by reason of the staff; the staff is his reason [for the designation], not the [primary] denotation. Similarly, this word <s>svarga</s> is not a word for pleasure but a word for the means of pleasure.
[The objector says:] but the word <s>svarga</s> is well-known in the world [as referring to] a specific place — where there is no heat, no cold, no hunger, no thirst, no displeasure, no weariness; only those of meritorious deeds go there after death, not others. To this we say: if some [people] go there without dying, [and] come from there without being born — then that kind of place is not directly perceived; nor is it known through inference.
[If one argues:] but certain accomplished beings have seen [it] and they have described [it] — [we reply:] there is no valid means of knowledge [to establish] that accomplished beings of this kind exist and that, having seen [heaven], they would describe it. Therefore, a place of this kind simply does not exist.
[The objector says:] but it is understood from the world, from narratives, and from the <s>Veda</s> that a place of this kind is heaven. No — because human beings have no connection with a place of this kind, [such] speech is not a valid means of knowledge. Narrative too, being composed by humans, is not to be relied upon. And even the Vedic narrative about heaven is not independent of [serving] an injunctive purpose; rather, it forms a syntactic unity with some other injunction and serves the purpose of praise. Even if such a place existed through the implicature (<s>arthāpatti</s>) of hearing about unmixed pleasure, even so there is no contradiction with our position — that the word <s>svarga</s> [refers to] the means of pleasure. For in the absence of any transaction with that place, how could the word <s>svarga</s> come to denote it?
When heaven is a delightful substance, then we say: in the connection of substances with ritual actions, the connection is as secondary. The sacrifice is heard as something to be done by one who desires heaven. There, the connection between heaven and the sacrifice is necessary. There, the substance [heaven] already exists; the ritual action is yet to be performed. And it is proper for what already exists to serve the purpose of what is yet to be — because [such a relationship] has visible application. But it is not [proper] for what is yet to be to serve the purpose of what already exists — for there, a visible benefit would be abandoned.
But how is it understood that the sacrifice is enjoined as something to be done, when the 'to-be-done-ness' of the desire too is understood from this sentence? We reply: the 'to-be-done-ness' of the desire is from the sentence, [while] the 'to-be-done-ness' of the sacrifice is from the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>); and the [Vedic] word is stronger than the sentence. Therefore the meaning is this: one desiring heaven should perform the sacrifice — the sacrifice is to be performed by one desiring heaven. And what is to be done is [that which is] pleasant; what is not to be done is painful. And [the Veda] tells him 'it is to be done.' Therefore the sacrifice will have pleasure as its fruit. But it is understood that it is accomplished for one whose desire [for heaven] exists, not for another. Therefore the desire for heaven is secondary to the sacrifice; just as in any action, the desire for a substance is secondary — through that [desire] one strives to obtain the substance, through a visible means alone. Here too, the desire for the substance called <s>svarga</s> is simply restricted — just as that [desire] has been obtained as secondary, so when restricted, it is restricted through a visible means alone, not through an unseen benefit. Therefore, through the desire for heaven, which is secondary, one will strive to accomplish the sacrifice in order to obtain the heavenly substance. And even if [the means is] through the unseen, even so there is no defect.

children.text: asādhakaṃ tu tādarthyāt//6.1.2//
children.translated_text: But [the ritual] is not an accomplisher [of a result], because of [its] being for that [heaven's] purpose. // MS_6,1.2 //

children.text:
tuśabdena pakṣo vyāvartyate. tata etāvat{*5/159*} tāvad varṇayanti, prītiḥ svarga iti. kutaḥ? evam uktaṃ bhavatā, prītiviśiṣṭe dravye svargaśabdo vartata iti. yady evam, pūrvaṃ tarhi prītau vartitum arhati. tāṃ hi sa na vyabhicarati. vyabhicarati punar dravyam. yasyaiva prītisādhanasya dravyasya vaktā svargaśabaḥ, tad eva yadā na prītisādhanaṃ bhavati, tadā na svargaśabdenābhidhīyate. tasmāt prītivacano 'yam.
yat tūktam, daṇḍiśabdavad iti, so 'pi prīte śabdād daṇḍe, daṇḍini pratyayam ādadhāti, antargatas tatra daṇḍaśabdaḥ, sa daṇḍasya vācakaḥ. iha punaḥ svargaśabdaḥ eva prīter abhidhātā.
prītivacanaś cet, yāgo guṇabhūtaḥ prītiḥ pradhānam. kutaḥ? tādarthyāt puruṣaprayatnasya, prītyarthaṃ hi puruṣo yatate, tena na [602]{*5/160*} prītir yāgasādhanam iti vijñāyate. dravyaṃ hi yāgasādhanam, narte dravyād yāgo bhavati, yasmād dravyadevatākriye yajatiśabdo vartate. asatyām api prītyāṃ bhavati yāgaḥ. yadi ca yāgo na prītyartho bhavet, asādhakaṃ karma bhavet, sādhayitāraṃ nādhigacchet. yo hi prītyarthaḥ, sa śadhyate, nānyaḥ.
nanu kartavyatayā yāgaḥ śrūyate. ucyate, satyaṃ kartavyatayā śrūyate, kāmo 'pi kartavyatayāvagamyate. āha, śrutyā yāgasya, vākyena kāmasya. na cobhayoḥ, vākyabhedaḥ prasaṅgāt{*5/161*}. ucyate, yady api yāgaḥ kartavyaḥ śrūyate, tathāpi na kartavyaḥ, sukhadaḥ kartavyo bhavati, duḥkhado yāgaḥ. tasmāt pratyakṣeṇākartavyaḥ, pratyakṣeṇa ca duḥkhadaḥ. kartavyatāvacanād anumānena sukhado bhavatīti. ucyate, anumānaṃ ca pratyakṣavirodhān na pramāṇam. tasmād akartavyo yāgaḥ, yadi na prītyarthaḥ.
athānyena{*5/162*} phalavacanena saṃbhantsyata iti. ucyate, saṃbadhyamāno{*5/163*} 'py avidhīyamāno na samīpavacanamātreṇa phalavān vijñāyate. tasmād anarthako mā bhūd iti svargasya kartavyatā gamyate, puruṣaprayatnaś ca yāgaviśiṣṭa iti yāgas tasya karaṇaṃ syāt. tasmāt suṣṭhūktaṃ yāgo guṇabhūtaḥ, svargaḥ pradhānabhūta iti.
children.translated_text:
By the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), the [previous] position is overturned. This much they first explain: heaven is pleasure. Why? It has been said by you that the word <s>svarga</s> applies to a substance qualified by pleasure. If so, it should first apply to pleasure itself, for it never deviates from that. But it does deviate from the substance. The very substance of which [you say] the word <s>svarga</s> is a designator as a means of pleasure — that very [substance], when it is not a means of pleasure, is not denoted by the word <s>svarga</s>. Therefore this [word] denotes pleasure.
As to what was said — 'like the word <s>daṇḍin</s>' — that too, [when] the word is pleased with <s>daṇḍa</s> (staff), places the suffix on the staff-bearer; the word <s>daṇḍa</s> is contained within it, and that is the designator of the staff. But here, the word <s>svarga</s> itself is the designator of pleasure.
If it denotes pleasure, then the sacrifice is secondary and pleasure is primary. Why? Because of human effort being for that [pleasure's] purpose — for a person strives for the sake of pleasure. Therefore it is not understood that pleasure is a means of the sacrifice. For a substance is a means of the sacrifice — without a substance, no sacrifice takes place, since the word <s>yajati</s> applies in [the context of] substance, deity, and action. Even without pleasure, a sacrifice takes place. And if the sacrifice were not for the purpose of pleasure, the ritual action would be non-accomplishing — it would not find anyone to accomplish it. For what serves the purpose of pleasure is accomplished, not anything else.
[The objector says:] but the sacrifice is heard as something to be done. We reply: true, it is heard as something to be done; the desire [for heaven] too is understood as something to be done. He says: the sacrifice [as to-be-done] by the [Vedic] word, the desire by the sentence. [We reply:] and not both [by the same means] — for there would follow a splitting of the sentence. We reply: even though the sacrifice is heard as something to be done, still it would not be to be done [if it causes suffering] — for what gives pleasure is to be done, and the sacrifice is painful. Therefore, by direct perception it is not to be done, and by direct perception it is pain-giving. By the statement of 'to-be-done-ness,' it is inferred to be pleasure-giving. We reply: inference that contradicts direct perception is not a valid means of knowledge. Therefore the sacrifice is not to be done, if not for the purpose of pleasure.
[If one argues] that it will be connected with a result-statement by another [sentence] — we reply: even when connected, if not [specifically] enjoined, it is not understood as having a result merely by proximity of statement. Therefore, lest [the sacrifice] be purposeless, the 'to-be-done-ness' of heaven is understood; and human effort is qualified by the sacrifice — the sacrifice would be its instrument. Therefore it is well said: the sacrifice is secondary, heaven is primary.

children.translated_text: And because of the connection with each purpose, the connection is from the ritual action; therefore the instruction should be about the ritual action. // MS_6,1.3 //

children.text:
na kevalam ānarthakyabhayād yāgasya guṇabhāvaṃ brūmaḥ. kiṃ tarhi? svargasaṃjñakam arthaṃ prati karaṇatvena yāgo vidhīyate. nanu yāgaḥ kartavyatayā śrutyā vidhīyate. satyam evam, ānarthakyaṃ tu tathā bhavati, svargaṃ pratyavihite yāge, svargakāmaḥ, tasmin niṣphale vidhīyamāno 'pi niṣprayojanaḥ syāt. tatrāsya [603]{*5/164*} upadeśavaiyarthyam, dvayoś ca vidhīyamānayoḥ paraspareṇāsaṃbaddhayor vākyabhedaḥ prasaṅgaḥ{*5/165*}. ato na svargakāmapadena svārtho vidhīyate. kiṃ tarhi? uddiśyate. tatra vākyād avagatasya kāmasya kartavyatāvagamyate, yāgasya ca karaṇatā. evaṃ ca yāgakartavyatāyāṃ{*5/166*} na pratyakṣavirodho bhaviṣyati. tasmāt karmopadeśaḥ syāt, karma svargaṃ praty upadiśyate, na svargaḥ karma prati.
kim ato yadi svargo nopadiśyate? etad ato bhavati. na hy anupadiṣṭo 'rthaprāptaś ca guṇo bhavati. tasmāt svargaḥ pradhānataḥ, karma guṇata iti.
api ca, yasya svarga iṣṭaḥ syāt, sa yāgaṃ nirvartyed ity asaṃbaddham iva, anyad icchati, anyat karotīti{*5/167*}.
atha matam, tataḥ svargo bhavatīti saṃbandhād idaṃ gamyata{*5/168*} iti. na śabdapramāṇakāmām antareṇa śabdam avagatir nyāyyā. vākyād evāsmād imaṃ saṃbandham avagacchāmaḥ, yathā kāṣṭhāny āhartukāmo 'raṇyaṃ gacched iti yadi brūyāt, brūyād etat, dṛṣṭaṃ tatra pramāṇāntareṇāraṇyāgamanasya kāṣṭhāharaṇasāmarthyaṃ vidyata iti.
atha manyate{*5/169*}, upadeśānarthakyaṃ mā bhūd ity arthāpattir bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, nopadeśānarthakyasyaitat sāmarthyam, yad antareṇa phalavacanam, yāgasya prītiḥ phalam avagamyeta. kāmam asyānarthakyaṃ bhavatu{*5/170*}, na jātucit sāmarthyam asya jāyate. na hi dagdhukāmasyodakopādānam asati dāhe 'narthakam iti dahanaśaktim asya janayet. atha vā, svargakāmasya yāgo vidhīyata iti pakṣāntarāvalambenāsyārthavattā bhaviṣyati.
nanv itarasminn api pakṣe svargakāmasya yāgo vidhīyate, na yāgāt svargaḥ. naitad evam. tasmin khalu pakṣe svargaṃ prārthayamānasyānuṣṭhānam anūdya yāgas tasyopāyatvena vidhīyata iti na [604]{*5/171*} doṣaḥ. tad anuṣṭhānaṃ svargaṃ pratīti nāsti vacanam iti cet. iṣṭam arthaṃ praty anuṣṭhānaṃ bhavati, svargakāmasya ca svarga iṣṭaḥ, tadanuṣṭhānaviśeṣagrahaṇārtham eva svargakāmaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇam iti niravadyam. tasmāt svargakāmasya yāgakarmopadeśaḥ syāt, ataḥ svargaḥ pradhānataḥ, karma guṇata iti svargakāmam adhikṛtya, yajeteti vacanam. ity adhikāralakṣaṇam idaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text:
We do not say that the sacrifice has subordinate status merely out of fear of purposelessness. Rather, the sacrifice is prescribed as an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) for the purpose designated by the word 'heaven' (<s>svarga</s>). [The objector says:] but the sacrifice is prescribed as 'to be performed' by the [Vedic] statement. True, it is so; but purposelessness would arise if the sacrifice is not prescribed with respect to heaven. [For] the sacrifice, being prescribed for one who desires heaven yet being fruitless [in itself], would be purposeless even though prescribed. In that case, there would be the futility of the instruction, and the splitting of the sentence would follow when two things being prescribed are unrelated to each other. Therefore, the word '<s>svargakāma</s>' (desiring heaven) does not prescribe its own [independent] meaning. Rather, it indicates [heaven]. Then, from the sentence, the desirability of the desire [for heaven] that has been understood is grasped, along with the instrumentality of the sacrifice. And when the sacrifice's being-to-be-performed [is understood] thus, there will be no contradiction with perception. Therefore it should be an instruction regarding the ritual action — the ritual action is instructed as the means to heaven, not heaven as the means to the ritual action.
What follows if heaven is not instructed? This follows: a subsidiary that is neither instructed nor obtained through the nature of things does not exist. Therefore heaven is the principal, and the ritual action is the subsidiary — thus the statement 'one desiring heaven should sacrifice' is with reference to one desiring heaven. This is the established characteristic of <s>adhikāra</s> (eligibility/entitlement).
Moreover, 'he whose heaven is desired should perform the sacrifice' — this seems disconnected: he desires one thing but does another.
[The objector says:] but from the connection 'heaven comes from that [sacrifice],' this is understood. [We reply:] for meanings whose authority is the [Vedic] word, understanding without the word is not proper. We understand this connection from this very sentence — just as if one were to say 'one wishing to fetch firewood should go to the forest,' one would say: 'It is observed through another means of knowledge that going to the forest has the capacity [to lead to] fetching firewood.'
[The objector] thinks: lest the instruction be purposeless, [the connection] will be understood through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). We reply: it is not the capacity of purposelessness of instruction to generate — without a statement of fruit — the understanding that the sacrifice's fruit is satisfaction. Let its purposelessness be so — its capacity never arises. For a person wishing to burn [something], the fetching of water, being purposeless in the absence of burning, would not generate burning capacity in it. Alternatively, [the objector says], the meaningfulness [of the instruction] will come from relying on the alternative view — 'the sacrifice is prescribed for one desiring heaven.'
[We reply:] but in the other view too, the sacrifice is prescribed for one desiring heaven — [in our view,] heaven does not [come] from the sacrifice. This is not so. In that [our] view, having restated the activity of one who seeks heaven, the sacrifice is prescribed as its means — [and there is] no defect. [The objector says:] but there is no statement that 'that activity is toward heaven.' [We reply:] activity arises in relation to a desired object; and for one desiring heaven, heaven is desired; therefore the qualification '<s>svargakāma</s>' is taken precisely for the purpose of understanding the specific activity — this is flawless. Therefore it should be an instruction of the ritual action for one desiring heaven; hence heaven is principal and the ritual action is subsidiary — with reference to one desiring heaven, the statement is 'he should sacrifice.' Thus this characteristic of <s>adhikāra</s> (eligibility) is established.

children.text: phalārthatvāt karmaṇaḥ śāstraṃ sarvādhikāraṃ syāt//6.1.4//
children.translated_text: Because the ritual action is for the purpose of its fruit, the scripture would entitle all [beings]. // MS_6,1.4 //

children.text:
idam āmnananti, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajetetyevamādi. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ yāvat kiṃcit sattvam, tat sarvam adhikṛtyaitad ucyate, uta samartham adhikṛtyeti. kiṃ prāptam? sarvādhikāraḥ, aviśeṣāt. nanu vṛkṣādayo na kiṃcit kāmayante, katham teṣām adhikāraḥ syāt? ucyate, mā bhūd acetanānām, tiraścas tv adhikṛtya yajeteti brūyāt. nanu tiryaṃco 'pi na kiṃcit kāmayante. neti brūmaḥ, kāmayante sukham, evaṃ hi dṛśyate, dharmopataptāś chāyām upasarpanti, śītena pīḍitā ātapam.
āha, nanu tiryaṃca āsannaṃ phalaṃ cetayante, na kālāntaraphalaṃ prārthayante, kālāntaraphalāni ca vaidikāni karmāṇi. ucyate, kālāntare 'pi phalaṃ kāmayamānā lakṣyante, śunaś caturdaśyām upavasataḥ paśyāmaḥ, śyenāṃś cāṣṭamyām. na caiṣāṃ vyādhyāśaṅkā, niyatanimittatvāt, nānāhārāṇām api tasmin kāle darśanāt, [605]{*5/172*} samānāhārāṇām apy anyasmin kāle 'darśanāt. liṅgāni ca vede bhavanti, devā vai satramāsatety{*5/173*}evamādīni devatānām ṛṣīṇāṃ vanaspatīnām adhikāraṃ darśayanti.
nanu kārtsnyena vidhim upasaṃhartuṃ na śaknuvantīty anadhikṛtāḥ. ucyate, yāgaṃ kartuṃ śaknuvanti kecit, tasmāt yajetetyevamādīny adhikariṣyanti śaknuvataḥ, viṣṇukramādivacanāni{*5/174*} tv aśaktān nādhikariṣyanti. tatra yo 'nupadiṣṭaviṣṇukramādikaḥ sa kevalaṃ yāgaṃ kariṣyati, kas tasya doṣaḥ? dravyaparigraho 'pi devagrāmaḥ, hastigrāmaḥ, ṛṣabhasya grāma ity upacārād asty eveti. tasmād amanuṣyāṇām api śaknuvatām adhikāra iti.
children.translated_text:
This is stated: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>'; 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — and so forth. There a doubt [arises]: is this said with reference to whatever being exists, all of them, or with reference to those who are capable? What is the prima facie view? All are entitled, since there is no distinction. [The objector says:] but trees and the like do not desire anything — how could they be entitled? We reply: let the non-sentient ones not [be entitled], but the statement 'he should sacrifice' could be said with reference to animals (<s>tiryañcas</s>). [The objector says:] but animals too do not desire anything. We say: that is not so — they desire pleasure, for thus it is observed: scorched by heat, they approach shade; afflicted by cold, [they seek] sunlight.
[The objector] says: but animals perceive only proximate fruits, they do not seek fruits at another time, and Vedic ritual acts have fruits at another time. We reply: animals are also observed desiring fruit at another time — we see dogs fasting on the fourteenth [lunar day], and hawks on the eighth. And this is not due to fear of illness, because [the fasting] has a fixed occasion; for even among those with varied diets, [fasting] is observed at that time, and even among those with the same diet, it is not observed at other times. And there are indicatory marks in the <s>Veda</s>: 'The gods indeed sat in a <s>sattra</s> (communal sacrifice)' — such [passages] beginning with this show the entitlement of deities, sages, and trees.
[The objector says:] but they cannot complete the injunction in its entirety, so they are not entitled. We reply: some of them are able to perform the sacrifice; therefore statements like 'he should sacrifice' will entitle those who are capable, while statements about the <s>Viṣṇukrama</s> (strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) and the like will not entitle the incapable. In that case, the one for whom the <s>Viṣṇukrama</s> and the like are not prescribed will perform the sacrifice alone — what defect is there? Even the ownership of property [is possible]: '<s>Deva</s>-village,' 'elephant-village,' 'the bull's village' — such [expressions] exist through figurative usage. Therefore, even non-humans who are capable would be entitled.
The purpose [of this discussion] has been stated by the [prima facie] view. Some say: a ritual act [lasting] a thousand years should not be necessarily arranged in [ordinary] days; in the prima facie view, this is because of the possibility for deities and the like who have such lifespans; in the established conclusion, even though possible for them, it should be arranged in [ordinary] days only. But this we will explain later.

children.text: kartur vā śrutisaṃyogād vidhiḥ kārtsnyena gamyate//6.1.5//
children.translated_text: Or, because of the connection of the agent with the [Vedic] statement, the injunction is understood as complete. // MS_6,1.5 //

children.text:
vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti, tiryagādīnām apy adhikāra iti. kasya tarhi? yaḥ samarthaḥ kṛtsnaṃ karmābhinirvartayitum. na caite śaknuvanti tiryagādayaḥ kṛtsnaṃ karmābhinirvartayitum, tasmād eṣāṃ na sukhasyābhyupāyaḥ karmeti. kathaṃ yo na śakyate kartum, so 'bhyupāyaḥ syād iti. na devānām, devatāntarābhāvāt, na hy ātmānam upadiśya tyāgaḥ saṃbhavati, tyāga evāsau na syāt, narṣīṇām, ārṣeyābhāvāt. na bhṛgvādayo bhṛgvādibhiḥ sagotrā bhavanti, na caiṣāṃ sāmarthyaṃ pratyakṣam.
[606]{*5/175*} api ca niryañco na kālāntaraphalenārthinaḥ, āsannaṃ hi te kāmayante.
nanu coktam, kālāntaraphalārthinas tiraścaḥ paśyāmaḥ, śunaḥ śyenāṃś caturdaśyām aṣṭabhyāṃ copavasata iti. ucyate, na janmāntaraphalārthina upavasanti. katham avagamyate? vedādhyayanābhāvāt, ye vedam adhīyate ta etad viduḥ, idaṃ karma kṛtvā, idaṃ phalam amutra prāpnotīti. na caite vedam adhīyate, nāpi smṛtiśāstrāṇi, nāpy anyebhyo 'vagacchanti. tasmān na vidanti dharmam. avidvāṃsaḥ katham anutiṣṭheyuḥ? tasmān na dharmāyopavasantīti.
kim arthaṃ tarhy eṣām upavāsaḥ? ucyate, rogād arucir eṣām. kathaṃ punar niyate kāle rogo bhavati? ucyate, niyatakālā api rogā bhavanti, yathā tṛtīyakāś cāturthakāś ceti. tasmān manuṣyāṇām adhikāra iti. na ca tiraścāṃ dravyaparigrahaḥ, na hy ete dravyaṃ svecchayopayuñjānā dṛśyante. tasmād anīśānā dhanasya. yat tu, devagrāmo hastigrāma iti, upacāramātraṃ tat. tasmād api na tiraścām adhikāra iti.
yāni punar liṅgāni, devā vai satram āsatetyevamādīni, arthavādās te vidhiprarocanārthāḥ, vidyate hi vidhir anyas teṣu sarveṣu. na ca vidher vidhinaikavākyabhāvo bhavati, vacanavyaktibhedāt. stutis tu sā, itthaṃ nāma satrāṇy āsitavyāni, yat kṛtakṛtyā apy āsate devāḥ, āsannacetanā api tiryañcaḥ, acetanā api vanaspatayaḥ, kim aṅga punar vidvāṃso manuṣyā iti.
nanu viṣṇukramādiṣv anadhikṛtāḥ kevalaṃ yāgaṃ kariṣyanti. [607]{*5/176*} naivam, guṇā yāgaṃ praty upadiśyante, na kartāraṃ prati, tena yāgamātre kriyamāṇe vaiguṇyam iti na phalasaṃbandhaḥ syāt. kathaṃ punar yāgaṃ praty upadiśyanta iti cet. itikartavyatākāṅkṣasya yāgavacanasyāntikād upanipatitāḥ śaknuvanti taṃ nirākāṅkṣīkartum, itarathā hi kartṝn adhikurvatsu guṇavacaneṣv anivṛttākāṅkṣaṃ phalavacanam anarthakam eva syāt, anuṣaṅgaś{*5/177*} ca phalavacanam abhiviṣyat, tatra sākāṅkṣatvād vākyam uparotsyate. athaitad eva vākyaṃ samarthānāṃ saguṇaṃ karma vidhāsyati, asamarthānāṃ viguṇam iti. tan na, sakṛd uccāraṇa ubhayaśaktivirodhād vākyaṃ bhidyeta, sākāṅkṣaṃ hi tad itikartavyatāṃ prati. tasmāt sāṅgayāgopadeśaḥ sa iti niraṅgayāgopadeśābhāvaḥ. tasmān manuṣyāṇām evādhikāra iti.
prayojanaṃ pakṣoktam, kecid āhuḥ sahasrasaṃvatsaraṃ karma na niyogato divaseṣu kalpayitavyam, pūrvapakṣe{*5/178*} tadāyuṣāṃ devatādīnāṃ saṃbhavātīti{*5/179*}, siddhānte tatra saṃbhavad api{*5/180*} divaseṣv eva kalpayitavyam iti. tat tūpariṣṭād{*5/181*} vyākhyāsyāmaḥ.
children.translated_text:
The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) overturns the [previous] view. This is not the case — that animals and the like too are entitled. For whom then? For one who is capable of accomplishing the ritual action in its entirety. And these animals and the like are not able to accomplish the ritual action in its entirety; therefore for them the ritual action is not the means to happiness. How can what cannot be performed be a means? Not for the gods, because of the absence of another deity — for self-directed relinquishment (<s>tyāga</s>) is not possible; that would not be relinquishment at all. Nor for the sages, because of the absence of <s>ārṣeya</s> (sagehood-lineage) — the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and the like are not of the same <s>gotra</s> as the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and the like, and their capability is not directly perceived.
Moreover, animals do not seek fruits at another time, for they desire only what is proximate.
[The objector says:] but it has been said — 'we observe animals desiring fruit at another time; dogs and hawks fast on the fourteenth and eighth [lunar days].' We reply: they do not fast seeking fruit in another birth. How is this known? Because of the absence of Vedic study — those who study the <s>Veda</s> know this: 'Having performed this ritual action, one obtains this fruit in the other [world].' But these [animals] neither study the <s>Veda</s>, nor the <s>smṛti</s> scriptures, nor do they learn from others. Therefore they do not know <s>dharma</s>. Being ignorant, how would they practice [dharma]? Therefore they do not fast for <s>dharma</s>'s sake.
For what purpose then is their fasting? We reply: it is loss of appetite due to illness. But how does illness come at a fixed time? We reply: there are indeed illnesses that come at fixed times, like tertian and quartan fevers. Therefore humans alone are entitled. And animals do not possess property — for these are not seen using wealth by their own will. Therefore they have no authority over wealth. As for '<s>Deva</s>-village,' 'elephant-village' — that is mere figurative usage. Therefore animals too are not entitled.
As for the indicatory marks — 'the gods indeed sat in a <s>sattra</s>' and the like — these are <s>arthavādas</s> (eulogistic passages) for the purpose of commending the injunction. For there exists another injunction in all those [passages]. And an injunction does not form a syntactic unity with another injunction, because of the difference in verbal expression. Rather, it is a praise: 'Communal sacrifices (<s>sattras</s>) should indeed be performed in such a manner that even the gods, though already fulfilled, perform them; even animals, though of proximate awareness, [perform them]; even trees, though non-sentient — how much more so learned humans!'
[The objector says:] but those not entitled to the <s>Viṣṇukrama</s> and the like will perform the sacrifice alone. Not so — the subsidiaries are prescribed with respect to the sacrifice, not with respect to the agent. Therefore, when only the sacrifice is performed [without subsidiaries], there is a deficiency, and no connection with the fruit would exist. But how are [the subsidiaries] prescribed with respect to the sacrifice? The statement of the sacrifice, expecting its <s>itikartavyatā</s> (procedure), being proximate — [the subsidiaries] are able to make it complete. Otherwise, when subsidiary-statements qualify the agents, the fruit-statement, its expectation unfulfilled, would be purposeless, and the fruit-statement too would become an appendage. There, because of the [sentence] having unfulfilled expectation, the sentence would be disrupted. [The objector says:] but this very sentence will prescribe the ritual action with subsidiaries for those who are capable, and without subsidiaries for the incapable. Not so — a single utterance, because of the contradiction of dual capacity, would split the sentence, for it has an expectation regarding the procedure. Therefore it is an instruction of the sacrifice with its subsidiaries — and there is no instruction of a sacrifice without subsidiaries. Therefore only humans are entitled.
The purpose has been stated by the [prima facie] view: some say a ritual of a thousand years need not necessarily be arranged in [ordinary] days — in the prima facie view because of its possibility for deities and the like of that lifespan; in the established conclusion, even though possible there, it should be arranged in [ordinary] days only. But this we will explain later.

children.text: liṅgaviśeṣanirdeśāt puṃyuktam aitiśāyanaḥ//6.1.6//
children.translated_text: Because of the specification of a particular grammatical gender, <s>Aitiśāyana</s> [holds that] males [alone are entitled]. // MS_6,1.6 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajetetyevamādi samāmnāyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ svargakāmaṃ pumāṃsam adhikṛtya yajetety eṣa śabda uccaritaḥ, atha vāniyamaḥ, striyaṃ pumāṃsaṃ ceti{*5/182*}. kiṃ prāptam? puṃliṅgam adhikṛtaṃ mene aitiśāyanaḥ. kutaḥ? liṅgaviśeṣanirdeśāt. puṃliṅgena viśeṣeṇa nirdeśo [608]{*5/183*} bhavati svargakāmo yajeteti{*5/184*}. tasmāt pumān ukto yajeteti, na strī.
children.translated_text: It is stated: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' and so forth. There a doubt [arises]: is this statement uttered with reference to a male who desires heaven, or is there no restriction — both women and men [being entitled]? What is the prima facie view? <s>Aitiśāyana</s> held that the masculine gender is the referent. Why? Because of the specification of a particular grammatical gender — the specification is made with the masculine gender in particular: '<s>svargakāmaḥ</s> (masculine: one desiring heaven) <s>yajeta</s> (he should sacrifice).' Therefore a male is indicated by 'he should sacrifice,' not a woman.

children.translated_text: And because [it is] said of that [male], the hearing of a defect [applies to] one who is not [properly] qualified. // MS_6,1.7 //

children.text:
avijñāte garbhe hate bhrūṇahatyānuvādo bhavati, tasmād avijñātena garbheṇa hatena bhrūṇahā bhavatīti. bhrūṇahā pāpakṛttamaḥ, yaś cobhayor lokayor upakaroti, tasya hantā bhrūṇāhā, yajñahantā bhrūṇahā, sa yajñasādhanabadhakārī{*5/185*}. tasmād yajñaṃ bhrūṇaśabdenābhidadhāti. sa hi bibharti vā sarvam, bhūtiṃ vānayati. ato bhrūṇahā yajñabadhakārī{*5/186*}, sa puṃyuktatvād anuvādo 'vakalpate. avijñāte garbhe hanyamāne kadācit pumān hanyeta, tatra yajñādhikṛtasya hatatvād yajñabadho{*5/187*} bhrūṇahatyā syāt. itarathā, yady ubhayor adhikāraḥ, tato vijñāte cāvijñāte ca yajñavadhaḥ{*5/188*} syāt. tatrāvijñātagrahaṇam atantram iti kalpyeta. tasmād vivakṣitā puṃliṅgasya vācikā vibhaktir iti.
tathā, ātreyīṃ hatvā bhrūṇahā bhavati, ātreyīm āpannagarbhām āhuḥ, atra kukṣāv{*5/189*} asyā vidyata ity ātreyī. tasmād api puṃso 'dhikāro gamyate. yathā, paśum ālabheteti{*5/190*} puṃpaśur evālabhyate, liṅgaviśeṣanirdeśāt{*5/191*}. evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ,
children.translated_text:
When an unrecognized embryo is killed, there is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of embryo-killing (<s>bhrūṇahatyā</s>). Therefore, by killing an unrecognized embryo, one becomes a <s>bhrūṇahan</s> (embryo-killer). A <s>bhrūṇahan</s> is the worst sinner; and he who kills one who assists both worlds — his killer is a <s>bhrūṇahan</s>. The sacrifice-destroyer is a <s>bhrūṇahan</s> — one who obstructs the means of sacrifice. Therefore [the text] designates the sacrifice by the word <s>bhrūṇa</s>. For it (the sacrifice) either sustains all, or brings about prosperity. Thus a <s>bhrūṇahan</s> is one who obstructs the sacrifice; and since it is connected with the masculine gender, the restatement is appropriate. When an unrecognized embryo is killed, sometimes a male is killed — there, because one qualified for sacrifice is killed, the obstruction of sacrifice would be embryo-killing. Otherwise, if both [male and female] had the right [to sacrifice], then in both recognized and unrecognized [embryos], sacrifice-destruction would occur. In that case, the specification 'unrecognized' would be purposeless. Therefore the grammatical masculine gender is intentionally significant.
Likewise, 'having killed an <s>Ātreyī</s>, one becomes a <s>bhrūṇahan</s>' — they call an <s>Ātreyī</s> a pregnant woman: 'There is within her womb one who has knowledge (<s>atra</s>)' — hence <s>Ātreyī</s>. From this too, the right of the male [alone] is understood. Just as 'he should slaughter the animal' — only a male animal is slaughtered, because of the specification of the masculine gender. So too it should be viewed here. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say:

children.text: jātiṃ tu bādarāyaṇo 'viśeṣāt, tasmāt stry api pratīyeta jātyarthasyāviśiṣṭatvāt//6.1.8//
children.translated_text: But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds that] it is the class (<s>jāti</s>), because of non-distinction; therefore a woman too would be understood [as qualified], because of the non-distinction of the class-meaning. // MS_6,1.8 //

children.text:
tuśabaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti, puṃso evādhikāra iti{*5/192*}, jātiṃ tu bhagavān bādarāyaṇo{*5/193*} 'dhikṛtāṃ manyate sma. āha, kim ayaṃ [609]{*5/194*} svargakāma iti jātiśabdaḥ samadhigataḥ? nety āha. kathaṃ tarhi? yaugikaḥ, svargecchāyogena vartate. kena tarhi śabdena jātir uktā, yādhikṛteti gamyate? naiva ca{*5/195*} vayaṃ brūmaḥ, jātivacana iha śabdo 'dhikāraka iti. kiṃ tarhi, svargakāmaśabdenobhāv api strīpuṃsāv adhikriyete iti, ato na vivakṣitaṃ puṃliṅgam iti. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, na hi śaknoty eṣā vibhaktiḥ svargakāmaṃ liṅgena viśeṣṭum. katham? lakṣaṇatvena śravaṇāt, svarge kāmo yasya, tam eṣa lakṣayati śabdaḥ, tena lakṣaṇenādhikṛto yajeteti śabdenocyate. tac ca lakṣaṇam aviśiṣṭaṃ striyāṃ puṃsi ca. tasmāc chabdenobhāv api strīpuṃsāv adhikṛtāv iti gamyate. tatra kenādhikāraḥ striyā nivartyate.
vibhaktyeti cet. tan na. kasmāt? puṃvacanatvāt strīnivṛttāv aśaktiḥ. puṃso vibhaktyā punarvacanam anarthakam iti cen. na, ānarthakye 'pi strīnivṛtter abhāvaḥ, parisaṃkhyāyāṃ svārthahāniḥ parārthakalpanā prāptabādhaś ca. na cānarthakyam, nirdeśārthatvāt. tasmāt stry api pratīyeta jātyarthasyāviśiṣṭatvāt.
children.translated_text:
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the [prima facie] position. This is not [correct] — that only males have the right [to sacrifice]. Rather, the revered <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> held that the class [as a whole] is qualified. [The objector] asks: is the word [609] '<s>svargakāma</s>' (one desiring heaven) established as a class-word? No, he says. How then? [It is] derivative (<s>yaugika</s>) — it functions through the connection with the desire for heaven. By what word then is the class stated, such that [we] understand it is qualified? We do not say that a class-word here is what confers qualification. Rather, by the word '<s>svargakāma</s>' both women and men are qualified — therefore the masculine gender is not intentionally [restrictive]. Why? Because of non-distinction — for this case-ending is not capable of specifying '<s>svargakāma</s>' by gender. How? Because it is heard as a characterization (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) — 'one in whom there is desire for heaven' — this word characterizes him; by that characterization, [one who is] qualified is told 'he should sacrifice' by the [Vedic] word. And that characterization is undifferentiated in woman and man. Therefore it is understood from the word that both women and men are qualified. Then by what is the woman's qualification negated?
If [one says] 'by the case-ending' — that is not so. Why? Because of its being a masculine-denoting [form], it is incapable of negating the woman. If it is said that the masculine case-ending makes re-stating the male purposeless — [we reply:] no, even in purposelessness there is [simply] absence of negation of the woman; in an exclusion (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>), there would be abandonment of one's own meaning and postulation of another's meaning, and contradiction of what is obtained. Nor is there purposelessness, because [the masculine form] serves the purpose of designation. Therefore a woman too would be understood [as qualified], because of the non-distinction of the class-meaning.

children.text: coditatvād yathāśruti//6.1.9//
children.translated_text: Because [the word] is enjoined, [it should be understood] as heard [literally]. // MS_6,1.9 //

children.text:
atha yad uktam, paśum ālabheteti{*5/196*} puṃpaśur ālabhyate puṃliṅgavacanasāmarthyāt, evam ihāpi puṃliṅgavacanasāmarthyāt pumān adhikriyate yāgavacaneneti. tat parihartavyam. atrocyate, nātra jātir dravyasya lakṣaṇatvena śrūyate, yadi hi lakṣaṇatvena śrūyate, tataḥ striyā api yāga ukto na puṃvacanena nivartyeta, idaṃ tu paśutvaṃ yāgasya viśeṣaṇātvena śrūyate. tatra paśutvasya yāgasya ca saṃbandho na dravyayāgayoḥ, yathā paśutvaṃ yāgasaṃbaddham, [610]{*5/197*} evaṃ puṃstvam ekatvaṃ ca, so 'yam anekaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭo yāgaḥ śrūyate. sa yathāśruty eva kartavyaḥ, upādeyatvena coditatvāt.
yac ca, doṣaśrutir avijñāte garbhe hate, ātreyāṃ ca puṃyuktatveneti, tat parihartavyam. atrocyate, avijñātena garbheṇety anuvādaḥ praśaṃsārthaḥ, ātreyī ca na hantavyeti. itthaṃ garbho na hantavyaḥ, yad avyaktenāpy enasvī bhavati. puṃliṅgavibhaktiḥ śrūyamāṇā na śaknoti striyaṃ nivartayitum. kim aṅga punar avijñātagarbhavacanaṃ liṅgam. tathā gotrapraśaṃsārtham ātreyā abadhasaṃkīrtanam{*5/198*}. na cāpannasattvā ātreyī, gotraṃ hy etat. na hy atraśabdādayaṃ taddhita utpannaḥ, samarthānāṃ hi taddhita utpadyate. na cātraśabdasya sāmarthyam asti.
children.translated_text:
Now, as for what was said — 'he should slaughter the animal' — a male animal is slaughtered because of the force of the masculine gender-statement; similarly here too, because of the force of the masculine gender-statement, only a male is qualified by the word enjoining sacrifice — that must be set aside. Here we say: the class (<s>jāti</s>) of the substance is not heard here as a characterization; for if it were heard as a characterization, then the sacrifice would be stated for a woman too and would not be negated by the masculine form. But here, the animal-hood is heard as a qualifier of the sacrifice. There, the connection is between animal-hood and the sacrifice, not between the substance and the sacrifice. Just as animal-hood is connected with the sacrifice, [610] so too are masculinity and oneness — thus this sacrifice is heard as qualified by multiple qualifiers. It should be performed exactly as heard, because it is enjoined as something to be employed.
As for the hearing of a fault in the killing of an unrecognized embryo, and [the argument about] <s>Ātreyī</s> being connected with the masculine [gender] — that must be set aside. Here we say: 'by an unrecognized embryo' is a restatement for the purpose of praise — that even by an unrecognizable [killing] one becomes sinful; thus an embryo should not be killed. The masculine case-ending, when heard, is unable to negate the woman. How much less then can the statement about the 'unrecognized embryo' serve as an indicatory mark [for male-only qualification]? Similarly, the mention of <s>Ātreyī</s> not being killed is for the purpose of praising the lineage (<s>gotra</s>). And the <s>Ātreyī</s> [in this context] is not one bearing a conceived being — for this is a lineage name. The secondary suffix (<s>taddhita</s>) here is not derived from the word <s>atra</s> (knowledge); for secondary suffixes are formed from words with syntactic capacity. And the word <s>atra</s> has no [such] syntactic capacity.

children.text: dravyavattvāt tu puṃsāṃ syāt, dravyasaṃyuktam, krayavikrayābhyām adravyatvaṃ strīṇāṃ dravyaiḥ samānayogitvāt//6.1.10//
children.translated_text: But it would [belong] to men, because of their having property; [for the sacrifice] is connected with substances. Because of buying and selling, women have non-property-status, because of being equal in status to substances. // MS_6,1.10 //

children.text: puṃsāṃ tu syād adhikāraḥ, dravyavattvāt, dravyavanto hi pumāṃso na striyaḥ, dravyasaṃyuktaṃ caitat karma, vrīhibhir yajeta, yavair yajetetyevamādi. katham? adravyatvaṃ strīṇām, krayavikrayābhyām, krayavikrayasaṃyuktā hi striyaḥ, pitrā vikrīyante, bhartrā krīyante, vikrītatvāc ca pitṛdhanānām anīśiyaḥ. krītatvāc ca bhartṛdhanānām. vikrayo hi śrūyate, śatam adhirathaṃ duhitṛmate{*5/199*} dadyāt, ārṣe gomithunam{*5/200*} iti. na ca, etad dṛṣṭārthe saty ānamane 'dṛṣṭārthaṃ bhavitum arhati. evaṃ dravyaiḥ samānayogitvaṃ strīṇām.
children.translated_text: But the qualification would belong to men, because of their having property — for men have property, not women. And this ritual action is connected with substances — 'he should sacrifice with rice,' 'he should sacrifice with barley,' and so forth. How? Women have non-property-status. Because of buying and selling — for women are connected with buying and selling: they are sold by the father, bought by the husband. Because of being sold, they have no ownership over paternal property. Because of being bought, [they have no ownership] over the husband's property. For selling is heard: 'One should give a hundred [coins] upon the chariot to one who has a daughter'; 'in an <s>Ārṣa</s> [marriage], a pair of cattle.' And when a visible purpose exists, this cannot become [merely] for an unseen purpose, like a payment. Thus women are equal in status to substances.

children.text: tathā cānyārthadarśanam//6.1.11//
children.translated_text: And thus the observation of [serving] another's purpose [confirms this]. // MS_6,1.11 //

children.text: yā patyā krītā saty athānyaiś caratīti krītatāṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: 'She who, though bought by a husband, then lives with others' — [this text] shows [her] bought status.

children.text: tādarthyāt karmatādarthyam//3.1.12//
children.translated_text: Because she is for that [husband's] purpose, [her] ritual action too is for that purpose. // MS_6,1.12 //

children.text: āha, yad anayā bhaktotsarpaṇena vā kartanena vā dhanam upārjitam, tena yakṣyata iti. ucyate, tad apy asyā na svam, yadā hi sānyasya svabhūtā, tadā yat tadīyam, tad api tasyaiva. api ca, svāminas tayā karma kartavyam, na tat parityajya svakarmārhati kartum. yat tayānyena prakāreṇopārjyate, tat patyur eva svaṃ bhavitum arhatīti. evaṃ smarati -
children.translated_text: [The objector] says: whatever wealth she has earned through rice-distribution or through cutting [grass etc.] — with that she will sacrifice. We reply: that too is not her own. For when she has become the property of another, then whatever belongs to her belongs to him as well. Moreover, her owner's work must be done by her; she cannot abandon that to do her own work. Whatever she earns by another means — that properly becomes the husband's own property. Thus it is remembered:

children.text:
bhāryā dāsaś ca putraś ca nirdhanāḥ sarva eva te/
yat te samadhigacchanti, yasya te tasya taddhanam iti//{*5/202*}
children.translated_text:
'Wife, slave, and son — all these are without property;
whatever they acquire, the wealth of whomever they belong to, that is his.'

children.text:
NOTES:

children.translated_text:
