children.text: phalotsāhāviśeṣāt tu//6.1.13//
children.translated_text: But because of the non-distinction regarding the eagerness for the fruit. // MS_6,1.13 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti, nirdhanā strīti, dravyavatī hi sā, phalotsāhāviśeṣāt, smṛtiprāmāṇyād asvayā tayā bhavitavyaṃ phalārthinyāpi, śrutiviśeṣāt, phalārthinyā yaṣṭavyam. yadi smṛtim anurudhyamānā paravaśā nirdhanā ca syāt, yajetety ukte sati na yajeta. tatra smṛtyā śrutir bādhyeta. na caitan nyāyyam. tasmāt phalārthinī satī smṛtim apramāṇīkṛtya dravyaṃ parigṛhṇīyād yajeta ceti.
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the [prima facie] position. This is not [correct] — that a woman has no property. For she does have property, because of the non-distinction regarding eagerness for the fruit. Even though, by the authority of <s>smṛti</s> (traditional law), she should be non-independent and desirous of the fruit — [yet] because of the specificity of the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>), one desirous of the fruit must sacrifice. If, adhering to the <s>smṛti</s>, she were dependent and without property, then when 'one should sacrifice' is stated, she would not sacrifice. In that case, <s>smṛti</s> would override <s>śruti</s>. And that is not proper. Therefore, being desirous of the fruit, she should disregard the <s>smṛti</s> as non-authoritative, take property, and sacrifice.

children.text: arthena ca samavetatvāt//3.1.14//
children.translated_text: And because of being conjoined with property. // MS_6,1.14 //

children.text: arthena cāsyāḥ samavetatvaṃ bhavati. evaṃ dānakāle saṃvādaḥ kriyate, dharme cārthe ca kāme ca nāticaritavyeti. yat tūcyate{*5/203*}, bhāryādayo nirdhanā iti, smaryamāṇam api nirdhanatvam anyāyyam eva, śrutivirodhāt. tasmād asvātantryam anena prakāreṇocyate, saṃvyavahāraprasiddhyartham.
children.translated_text: And she is conjoined with property. Thus at the time of giving [in marriage], an agreement is made: 'In <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), [the husband] shall not transgress [her rights].' As for what is said — 'wife and others are without property' — even though the propertylessness is remembered [in smṛti], it is indeed improper, because of contradiction with <s>śruti</s>. Therefore non-independence is stated in this manner [only] for the purpose of worldly convention.

children.text: krayasya dharmamātratvam//6.1.15//
children.translated_text: The 'buying' is merely a [customary] practice (<s>dharma</s>). // MS_6,1.15 //

children.text: yat tu krayaḥ śrūyate, dharmamātraṃ tu tat, nāsau kraya iti. krayo hi uccanīcapaṇyapaṇo{*5/205*} bhavati. niyataṃ tv idaṃ dānaṃ śatam atiratham{*5/206*}, śobhanām aśobhanāṃ ca kanyāṃ prati. smārtaṃ ca śrutiviruddhaṃ vikrayaṃ nānumanyante. tasmād avikrayo 'yam iti.
children.translated_text: As for the buying that is heard — that is merely a [customary] practice, not [actually] a buying. For buying involves the exchange of merchandise for high or low prices. But this giving is fixed — 'a hundred upon the chariot' — [equally] for a beautiful or unbeautiful maiden. And [the authorities on] <s>smṛti</s> (traditional law) do not approve of selling that contradicts <s>śruti</s>. Therefore this is not a sale.

children.text: svavattām api darśayati//6.1.16//
children.translated_text: [The text] also shows her ownership status. // MS_6,1.16 //

children.text: patnī vai pāriṇayyasyeṣṭe patyaiva gatam anumataṃ{*5/207*} kriyate{*5/208*}. tathā, bhasadā patnīḥ{*5/209*} saṃyājayanti{*5/210*}, bhasadvīryā hi patnayaḥ, bhāsadā vā etāḥ paragṛhāṇām aiśvaryam avarundhata iti.
children.translated_text: 'The wife is indeed [the one who participates] in the <s>Pāriṇayyā</s> offering — [but] by the husband's [direction] alone, what is approved is performed.' Likewise, 'They cause the wives to sacrifice with the buttocks — for wives have the power of the buttocks; by the buttocks indeed do these women obtain sovereignty over others' households.'

children.text: svavatos tu vacanād aikakarmyaṃ syāt//6.1.17//
children.translated_text: But because of the statement of [her] ownership, there would be unity of the ritual act. // MS_6,1.17 //

children.text:
svavantāv ubhāv api daṃpatī ity evaṃ tāvat sthitam. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ pṛthak patnī yajeta, pṛthag yajamānaḥ, uta saṃbhūya yajeyātām iti. kiṃ prāptam? pṛthaktvena{*5/211*}. kutaḥ? ekavacanasya vivakṣitatvāt. upādeyatvena kartā yajeteti śrūyate{*5/212*}. tasmād ekavacanaṃ vivakṣyate, yathā na dvau puruṣau saṃbhūya yajeyātām, tathātrāpi draṣṭavyam.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, svavatos tu vacanād aikakarmyaṃ syāt, vacanāt tayoḥ sahakriyā. evaṃ hi smaranti, dharme cārthe ca kāme ca [613]{*5/213*} nāticaritavyeti, tathā sahadharmaś caritavyaḥ, sahāpatyam utpādayitavyam iti. ucyate, smṛtivacanena na śrutivacanaṃ yuktaṃ bādhitum. neti brūmaḥ, iha kiṃcit karma strīpuṃsakartṛkam eva, yathā darśapūrṇamāsau jyotiṣṭoma iti, yatra patnyavekṣitena yajamānāvekṣitena cājyena homa ucyate, tatrānyatarābhāve vaiguṇyam.
nanu puṃso yajamānasya yajamānāvekṣitam ājyam, striyā yajamānāyāḥ patnyavekṣitaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. nety āha, nāyam īkṣitṛsaṃskāraḥ, īkṣituḥ saṃskāro yadi, tadaivaṃ syāt. ājyasaṃskāraś cāyam, guṇabhūtāv īkṣitārau, tatrānyatarāpāye niyataṃ vaiguṇyam, sarvāṅgopasaṃhārī ca prayogavacanaḥ. tatraitat syāt, strī yajamānā pumāṃsaṃ parikreṣyaty ājyasyekṣitāram, pumāṃś ca striyaṃ tv avekṣitrīm iti. tac ca na, patnīti hi yajñasya svāminīty ucyate, na krītā. patnīti saṃbandhiśabdo 'yam, yajamāna iti ca svāmī, na krītaḥ. tasmāt strīpuṃsayor ekam evaṃjātīyakaṃ karmeti.
tatra śrutisāmarthyād yaḥ kaścit, yayā kayācit saha{*5/214*} saṃbhūya yajeteti prāpte, idam ucyate, yas tvayā kaścid dharmaḥ kayācit saha kartavyaḥ, so 'nayā saheti, tena na śrutivirodhaḥ smṛter iti gamyate. atha yad uktam, kevalasya puṃso 'dhikāraḥ, kevalāyāś ca striyā yajetety ekavacanasya vivakṣitatvād iti, tat parihartavyam. idaṃ tāvad ayaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ, yajetety ekavacane vivakṣite, kathaṃ ṣoḍaśabhir ṛtvigbhiḥ saha yāgo bhavatīti. evam ucyate, prati[614]{*5/215*}kārakaṃ kriyābhedaḥ, yajamānān eva padārthān parikrayādīn kurvan, yajata ity ucyate yajamānaḥ, ādhvaryavān eva kurvan adhvaryur yajatīty evam ucyate, yathā saṃbharaṇam eva kurvatī sthālī paktiṃ karotīty ucyate, yasya ca kārakasya ya ātmīyo vyāpāraḥ, sa ekavacane vivakṣita ekena kartavyo bhavatīti. evaṃ ced yāvān vyāpāro yajamānasya sa{*5/216*} tāvāt, na saṃbhūya kartavyaḥ, ekenaiko yājamāno 'pareṇāparaḥ. dvādaśo vā śata ekena ṣaṭpañcāśat, apareṇāpi ṣaṭpañcāśad iti. iha tu patnīvyāpāro 'nya eva, na tatra patnī pravartamānā yajamānasyaikatvaṃ vihanti, yathādhvaryur ādhvaryaveṣu pravartamānaḥ. avaśyaṃ ca saha patnyā yaṣṭavyam, madhyakaṃ hīdaṃ daṃpatyor dhanam, tatra yāgo 'vaśyaṃ saha patnyā kartavyaḥ, itarathānyatarānicchāyāṃ tyāga eva na saṃvarteta, tathā hi dvitīyayā patnyā vinā tyāgo naivāvakalpate, yasya dvitīyā patny asti, tatra kratvarthān ekā kariṣyati. kartṛsaṃskārārtheṣu naiva doṣaḥ, saṃbhavanti hi tāni sarvatreti.
children.translated_text:
Thus it has been established that both husband and wife (<s>daṃpatī</s>) are possessors [of wealth]. There a doubt [arises]: should the wife sacrifice separately, the sacrificer separately, or should they sacrifice jointly? What is the prima facie view? Separately. Why? Because of the singular number being intended — 'the agent should sacrifice' is heard with acceptance [of a single agent]. Therefore the singular is intended; just as two men should not sacrifice jointly, so too it should be viewed here.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: because of the statement regarding [their] having ownership, there should be a joint ritual (<s>aikakarmya</s>) — from the statement, the two should perform the rite jointly. For thus the <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition) states: 'In <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> [613] she should not be disregarded.' Likewise: 'Religious duty (<s>dharma</s>) should be practiced jointly; offspring should be produced jointly.' [The objector] says: it is not proper to override the Vedic statement by a <s>Smṛti</s> statement. No, we say — here, certain ritual acts require both man and woman as agents, such as the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, where the oblation is made with ghee that has been inspected by the wife and inspected by the sacrificer; in the absence of either, there is a deficiency.
[The objector says:] for a man who is the sacrificer, the wife-inspected [ghee] will be the sacrificer-inspected one; for a woman who is the sacrificer, the sacrificer-inspected [ghee] will be the wife-inspected one. No, [the commentator] says — this is not a consecration of the inspector; if it were a consecration of the inspector, then this would be so. But this is a consecration of the ghee, and the inspectors are subsidiary; in the absence of either, there is necessarily a deficiency. And the statement of performance collects all the subsidiaries. In that case, a woman who is the sacrificer might hire a man as an inspector of the ghee, and a man might hire a woman as an inspectress. But that is not so — for the word <s>patnī</s> (wife) refers to the owner of the sacrifice, not a hired person. The word <s>patnī</s> is a relational word; and <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) means owner, not hired person. Therefore a rite of this kind requires both man and woman.
Therein, when from the capacity of the [Vedic] statement it is obtained that any person should sacrifice jointly with any [woman], [614] this is stated: 'whatever religious duty of yours is to be performed with anyone, that [should be performed] with this [wife]' — thereby it is understood that there is no contradiction between <s>Smṛti</s> and <s>Śruti</s>. Now, as to what was said — 'only an individual man is qualified, and only an individual woman, because of the intended singular in "he should sacrifice"' — that must be refuted. This much should first be asked of that [proponent]: when the singular is intended in 'he should sacrifice,' how does the sacrifice take place together with sixteen <s>ṛtvik</s> (priests)? The reply is thus: per agent, there is a differentiation of action — when the sacrificer performs only the yajamāna-related items such as hiring [the priests] and the like, it is said 'the sacrificer sacrifices'; when [the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priest] performs only the <s>Adhvaryu</s>-related [items], it is said 'the <s>Adhvaryu</s> sacrifices' — just as a cooking-pot that merely holds [the rice] is said to 'cook.' And for whichever agent that which is his own operation — that [alone] is intended in the singular, [meaning] it is to be done by one [person]. If so, then [only] as much operation as belongs to the sacrificer — that much should not be done jointly; one [person] performs one set of sacrificer-operations, another performs another. Or [in the case of a twelve-day rite], one [person performs] fifty out of the hundred and twelve, and the other also fifty. But here, the wife's operation is entirely different — the wife, engaging [in her own operations], does not impair the oneness of the sacrificer, just as the <s>Adhvaryu</s> engaging in <s>Adhvaryu</s>-operations [does not]. And the sacrifice must necessarily be performed together with the wife, for this wealth belongs jointly to the couple; therefore the sacrifice must necessarily be performed together with the wife. Otherwise, in the case of the other's unwillingness, even a separation would not take effect. For thus, without a second wife, a separation simply does not work — for one who has a second wife, the first will perform the ritual-purpose [operations]. In the consecrations of the agent (<s>kartṛsaṃskāra</s>), there is no defect at all, for they are possible everywhere.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca//6.1.18//
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_6,1.18 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ khalv api dṛśyate, yoktreṇa patnīṃ saṃnahyati, mekhalayā yajamānaṃ mithunatvāyeti{*5/217*}. yadi strīpuṃsāv ekatra, yoktrasya mekhalāyāś ca vibhāgo vākyād gamyate, mithunasaṃstavaś ca, tad etat strīpuṃsasādhanake karmaṇy upapadyate, nānyathā.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark is indeed observed: 'He binds the wife with a girdle (<s>yoktra</s>); the sacrificer with a belt (<s>mekhalā</s>) — for the sake of coupling (<s>mithunatva</s>).' If both man and woman [are in the same rite], the distinction between the girdle and the belt is understood from the sentence, as well as the praise of the couple — this is fitting in a rite that requires both man and woman as its instruments, and not otherwise.

NOTES:
[{5/217: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.1.3.5}]

children.text: krītatvāt tu bhaktyā svāmitvam ucyate//6.1.19//
children.translated_text: But because [the wife] is purchased, her ownership is stated by figurative identification. // MS_6,1.19 //

children.text: sthitād uttaram ucyate. tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti, yad uktaṃ svavatī strīti, krītā hi sā, dṛṣṭārthatvād adhirathaśatadānasya{*5/218*}, ato yad asyāḥ svāmitvam ucyate, tad bhaktyā, [615]{*5/219*} yathā pūrṇako 'smākaṃ balīvardānām īṣṭa iti, evaṃ patny api pāriṇayyasyeṣṭa iti.
children.translated_text: This is stated as a [counter-argument] after the established [conclusion]. The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) refutes the [previous] position. This is not the case — that the woman has ownership, as was said. For she is purchased, since the giving of one hundred chariots [as bride-price] has a visible purpose. Therefore her ownership is stated by figurative identification (<s>bhakti</s>) [615] — just as '<s>Pūrṇaka</s> is a favorite among our oxen,' so too 'the wife is a favorite of the married one.'

children.text: phalārthitvāt tu svāmitvenābhisaṃbandhaḥ//6.1.20//
children.translated_text: But because of being one who desires the fruit, the connection is through ownership. // MS_6,1.20 //

children.text: naitad asti, krayo mukhyaḥ, gauṇaṃ svāmitvam iti, phalārthinī hi sā, smṛtir nādariṣyate, smṛtyanurodhād asvā syāt, svavatī śrutyanurodhāt.
children.translated_text: This is not the case — that purchase is primary and ownership figurative. For she is one who desires the fruit. The <s>Smṛti</s> should not be disregarded. By deference to <s>Smṛti</s>, she would be without ownership; [but] she possesses ownership by deference to <s>Śruti</s>.

children.text: phalavattāṃ ca darśayati//6.1.21//
children.translated_text: And [the Vedic text] shows [that she is] one who has a fruit. // MS_6,1.21 //

children.text: saṃ patnī patnyā sukṛtena gacchatāṃ yajñasya dhuryāyuktāv abhūtām. saṃjānānau vijahītām arātīr divi jyotir ajaramāram etām iti{*5/220*} daṃpatyoḥ phalaṃ darśayati. tasmād apy ubhāv adhikṛtāv iti siddham.
children.translated_text: 'May the wife join with the wife through meritorious deeds; [the two,] yoked as the draft-animals of the sacrifice, have become [a team]. May they, knowing [each other], abandon hostilities; may they reach the undecaying, immortal light in heaven.' This shows the fruit for both husband and wife. Therefore by this too it is established that both are qualified [as sacrificers].

NOTES:
[{5/220: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.7.5.11}]

children.text: dvyādhānaṃ ca dviyajñavat//6.1.22//
children.translated_text: And [the rule of] dual fire-establishment corresponds to [the rule of] dual sacrifice. // MS_6,1.22 //

children.text:
asty ādhānam, ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatta iti. tatredam āmananti, kṣaume vasānāv agnim ādadhīyātām iti. tatraiṣo 'rthaḥ sāṃśayikaḥ, kiṃ dvau puruṣāv ādadhīyātām utaikaḥ puruṣa iti. kathaṃ saṃśayaḥ? ucyate, ihaitac chrūyate, vasānāv ādadhīyātām iti. tatra vacanam arthaprāptaṃ punaḥ śrūyate, tat kiṃ puṃliṅgasaṃbandhārtham, uta kṣaumavidhyartham iti. ubhayor vidyamānatvād bhavati saṃśayaḥ, yadi liṅgasaṃbandhārtham, ubhau puruṣāv ādhāsyete. atha kṣaumasaṃbandhārthaṃ tata ekaḥ.
kiṃ prāptam? dvyādhānaṃ tu dviyajñavat syāt, yathā, etena dvau [616]{*5/221*} rājapurohitau sāyujyakāmau yajeyātām iti dvayoḥ puruṣayor dviyajño bhavati, evaṃ dvyādhānaṃ dvayoḥ puruṣayoḥ syāt, tato 'viśeṣāt, vasānāv iti śravaṇād eva puruṣau gamyete. na padāntaragatena kṣaumeṇāsya saṃbandhaḥ, śrutyavagataṃ hi śravaṇād avagatam, padāntarasaṃbandhaṃ vākyād avagatam, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī. vasānaśabdagataś cārtha ādhānena saṃbadhyate, na kṣaumaśabdagataḥ.
āha, vasānāv iti nāyaṃ kevalaṃ puṃliṅga eva, strīpuṃsayor apy abhidhāyako bhavati, yathā kukkuṭaś ca kukkuṭī ca kukkuṭau, śūkaraś ca śūkarī ca śūkarāv iti. evaṃ vasānaś ca vasānā ca vasānau syātām iti. atrocyate, yatra nārthaḥ, prakaraṇaṃ vā viśeṣakam, vidhāyakaś ca śabdaḥ, nāsty anuvādas{*5/222*}. tatra dvau pumāṃsau gamyete, yathā dvāv ānayety uktaḥ pumāṃsāv ānayati. dve ānayeti striyau, tena striyo vācakam ekārāntaṃ dvivacanam iti gamyate, aukārāntam api dvayoḥ puṃsor vācakam iti. yatredānīṃ strīpuṃsayoḥ prayujyamānam aukārāntaṃ dṛśyate, tatra kiṃ pumān sadvitīyas tasya nimittam, uta strī sadvitīyā iti{*5/223*}. ucyate, puṃsi sadvitīye dṛṣṭaḥ, yathā brāhmaṇāv ānayeti, ihāpi pumān sadvitīyo 'rthaḥ. tasmāt puṃnimittam iti gamyate.
atrāha, prayogo yadi dṛsṭaṃ pramāṇaṃ dvayoḥ puṃsor dṛṣṭaḥ, katham ekasmin syāt? atrocyate, puṃsi ca dvitve ca dṛṣṭa iti śakyate vaditum, na dvayor dravyayor iti, puṃbhāvaṃ dvitvaṃ caiṣa śabdo na vyabhicarati, dravyaṃ punar vyabhicarati. api ca yugapadadhikaraṇavacanāyā{*5/224*} dvaṃdvasmṛter dvivacanabahuvacanopapatteś ca, [617]{*5/225*} pra mitrayor varuṇayor iti ca darśanāt. itaretarayoge cārthe samāsavidhānād dvandvāpavādatvāc caikaśeṣasya, yathaiva khadirau ca dhavalau{*5/226*} ceti nirdarśanaṃ kriyate, evam atrāpi draṣṭavyam. tasmāt puṃsi dvitve ca vartata iti gamyate. na ca strīdvitve dṛṣṭaḥ.
atrāha, nanv atraiva darśanāt, strīpuṃsayor vācaka iti gamyate. atrocyate, uktam etat, anyāyaś conekārthatvam iti pumān sadvitīyo 'syārtho bhaviṣyati, strīpuṃsau cety anyāyyam. athedānīṃ sadvitīyasya puṃso vidhau ko 'nyaḥ sahāya{*5/227*} iti. striyā anabhidheyatvāt, avaśyaṃ bhāvitvāc ca dvitīyasya, aparaḥ sadvitīyaḥ pumān, evam itaro 'pītareṇa sadvitīyaḥ, itaro 'pītareṇeti dvāv eva pumāṃsāv upādīyete. tasmād iha dvau pumāṃsāv ādhāne vidhīyeta ity ucyate.
nanu strīpuṃsayor vācakam aukārāntaṃ dvivacanaṃ smaranti. naiṣā smṛtir astīti brūmaḥ. āha, bhagavataḥ pāṇiner vacanāt smṛtim anumāsyāmahe, pumān striyā{*5/228*} iti. ucyate, na pāṇiner vacanam kukkuṭāv ity aukāraḥ strīpuṃsayor vācaka iti. kathaṃ tarhi? yatra strīpuṃsayoḥ sahavacanam, tatra sadvitīyo vā pumān iti kṛtvākārāntasyaukāraḥ prāpnoti, sadvitīyā vā strīti kṛtvaikāraḥ. puṃśabdas tatra sādhur na strīśabda iti pāṇiner vacanam. pumān śiṣyata iti ca brūte, tena sutarāṃ gamyate, puṃsor vācaka aukāra iti. tasmād dvayoḥ puṃsor adhikāra iti.
nanu kṣaumavidhānaparam etad vākyam syāt, kṣaumasaṃbandhasya [618]{*5/229*} arthavattvāt{*5/230*}, itarathā kṣaumavacanam anarthakaṃ syāt. atrocyate, vasānāv ādadhīyātām ity asti saṃbandhaḥ, na kṣaume ādadhīyātām iti. tasmāt saṃnikṛṣṭam api na tatsaṃbaddham ādhānena. āha, vasānaśabdena saha saṃbadhyamānam arthavad bhaviṣyati. vasānasaṃnikṛṣṭe api kṣaume na vidhīyate, vidhāyakasya śabdasyābhāvāt. na hi vasānaśabdo vidhāyakaḥ, na kṣaumaśabdaḥ, nānayoḥ samudāyaḥ. kas tarhi vidhātuṃ śaknoti? ādadhīyātām ity atra yā liṅ.
āha, sā khalu vidhāsyati? ucyate, sā svaśabdagatam ādhānaṃ śaknoti vidhātum, śravaṇāt vihitatvād ādhānasya, ānarthakye, vasānāv iti śaknoti vākyena vidhātum, bhavati hi vasānayor ādhānasaṃbandhaḥ, tatra nātyantāya svārthaḥ parityakto bhavati, kṣaumavasānasaṃbandhe tu vidhātavye, ādadhīyātām ity ādhānam utsṛjya vidadhāno 'tyantāya śrutiṃ jahyāt. ādhānasaṃnikṛṣṭe ca liṅge vidhātavye śrutir viprakṛṣṭaṃ na kṣaumavasānasaṃbandhaṃ vidhātum utsahate, arthaviprakarṣāt. api cotsṛjya śrutim, kṣaumavasānasaṃbandhe vidhīyamāne kṣaumaṃ vasānasyāṅgaṃ syān nādhānasya. tatra kṣaumābhāve 'pi nādhānaṃ viguṇam iti kṣaumābhāve 'py ādhānaṃ syāt.
āha, vasānaguṇatāyāṃ tarhi ko 'rtho vivakṣyate? ucyate, na kaścit, ata evāsya pakṣasya parityāgaḥ. āha, kṣaumavasānaśravaṇam idānīṃ katham{*5/231*} iti. ucyate, na śakyata ubhayaṃ vidhātuṃ kṣaumaṃ liṅgaṃ ca, bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. tasmāt akṣaumayoḥ{*5/232*} kṣaumaśabdo 'nuvādaḥ, arthaprāpte ca vasane, vasānau pumāṃsāv ity arthaḥ. te ca prāyeṇa viceṣṭamānasya maline kṣaumasadṛśe bhavataḥ, viceṣṭamānasya vā vasane śabdavatī bhavata iti. tasmād dvayoḥ puṃsor adhikāra iti.
children.translated_text:
There is the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>): 'He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire.' There they state: 'Wearing linen (<s>kṣauma</s>), the two should establish the fire.' There this meaning is doubtful: should two persons establish [the fire], or one person? How is there doubt? We reply: here it is heard — 'wearing [linen], the two should establish.' There, the [word about] wearing is heard again, [even though it is] already understood from the context. Is this for the purpose of establishing the masculine-gender connection, or for the purpose of enjoining linen? Because both [interpretations] exist, there is doubt. If for the purpose of gender-connection, both [i.e., two] men will establish [the fire]. If for the purpose of the linen-connection, then [only] one.
What is the prima facie view? The establishment by two [persons] should be like a sacrifice by two — just as 'By this [rite], two [616] royal chaplains desiring union should sacrifice' prescribes a sacrifice by two for two persons — so too the establishment should be by two persons. Therefore, because of no distinction, from hearing '<s>vasānau</s>' ('the two wearing'), two persons are understood. The connection of linen — which belongs to another word — is not with this [word]; for what is understood through the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>) is grasped by hearing, while what is understood through connection with another word is grasped by the sentence, and the [Vedic] word is stronger than the sentence. The meaning contained in the word <s>vasāna</s> ('wearing') is connected with the fire-establishment, not the meaning contained in the word <s>kṣauma</s> ('linen').
[The objector] says: the [form] <s>vasānau</s> does not refer exclusively to the masculine gender — it can denote both a woman and a man, just as <s>kukkuṭau</s> ('a rooster and a hen') and <s>śūkarau</s> ('a boar and a sow'). Similarly, <s>vasānaś ca vasānā ca vasānau</s> ('a man wearing and a woman wearing = the two wearing'). To this we reply: where neither the meaning nor the context provides a differentiating [factor], and the word is injunctive, not a restatement — there, two males are understood, just as when told 'bring two' (<s>dvāv ānaya</s>), one brings two males. [When told] 'bring two' (<s>dve ānaya</s>), [one brings] two females. From this it is understood that the dual ending in <s>-e</s> denotes females, and the ending in <s>-au</s> also denotes two males. Now, where the ending in <s>-au</s> is seen used of a male-and-female [pair], there is the question: is the man with a second [companion] the reason for [that usage], or is the woman with a second [companion]? We reply: it is observed [used] when a man is with a second — as in '<s>brāhmaṇāv ānaya</s>' ('bring the two <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>'). Here too, 'a man with a second' is the meaning. Therefore it is understood that the reason [for the -au ending] is a male.
To this [the objector] says: if usage is the valid evidence, and it is observed [referring to] two males, how could it [apply] to one? To this we reply: it can be said that [the form] is observed [in use] with masculinity and duality — not [necessarily] with two substances. This word does not deviate from masculine-ness and dual-ness, but it deviates from [two] substances. Moreover, since [617] the <s>dvandva</s> compound is recalled as denoting things that occupy the same locus simultaneously, and because of the appropriateness of dual and plural endings [with compounds], and because of seeing [forms like] '<s>pra mitrayoḥ varuṇayoḥ</s>' ('of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>') — and because the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (single-remainder) [rule], which is an exception to <s>dvandva</s>, is prescribed for <s>itaretarayoga</s> (mutual connection) meanings — just as the illustration is given '<s>khadirau ca dhavalau</s>' ('two <s>Khadira</s> [sticks] and two white [ones]'), so too it should be viewed here. Therefore it is understood that [the form] applies when masculine and dual. And it is not observed in the female dual.
To this [the objector] says: but from the very observation here [of its application to a male-female pair], it is understood that [the form] denotes both male and female. To this we reply: it has been stated — 'being multi-referential is improper.' 'A man with a second' will be its meaning; 'a man and a woman' is improper. Now then, in the injunction concerning a man with a second, who is the other companion? Since a woman cannot be denoted [by this form], and since a second [person] must necessarily exist, [the companion is] another man with a second. Thus the other too [has] a second with the other — so only two males are taken. Therefore here it is said that two males are enjoined in the fire-establishment.
But they recall that the dual ending in <s>-au</s> denotes both male and female. We say: no such tradition (<s>smṛti</s>) exists. [The objector] says: from the statement of the venerable <s>Pāṇini</s>, we shall infer the tradition — '<s>pumān striyā</s>' [Pāṇini 1.2.67: 'the masculine (is used) with the feminine']. We reply: <s>Pāṇini</s>'s statement is not that 'the <s>-au</s> ending denotes male and female in <s>kukkuṭau</s>.' Rather, [it is] this: where there is a joint reference to male and female, there — thinking 'the man is with a second' — the <s>-au</s> ending is appropriate for the <s>-ā</s>-final [stem], or thinking 'the woman is with a second,' the <s>-e</s> ending [would be appropriate]. <s>Pāṇini</s>'s statement is that the masculine word is correct there, not the feminine word. And he also says 'the masculine is retained' (<s>pumān śiṣyate</s>) — by which it is even more clearly understood that the <s>-au</s> ending denotes two males. Therefore [the fire-establishment is] the domain of two males.
But [the objector says], this sentence might have the purpose of enjoining linen, [618] since the linen-connection would be meaningful; otherwise the mention of linen would be purposeless. To this we reply: the connection is '<s>vasānau ādadhīyātām</s>' ('the two wearing should establish'), not '<s>kṣaume ādadhīyātām</s>' ('they should establish in linen'). Therefore even [the word] linen, though proximate, is not connected with the fire-establishment. [The objector] says: it will become meaningful when connected with the word <s>vasāna</s> ('wearing'). [We reply:] even though linen is proximate to <s>vasāna</s>, it is not enjoined [by it], because of the absence of an injunctive word. For neither the word <s>vasāna</s> is injunctive, nor the word <s>kṣauma</s>, nor their aggregate. What then can enjoin? The <s>liṅ</s> (optative ending) in '<s>ādadhīyātām</s>' ('they should establish').
[The objector] says: will it [the liṅ] then enjoin? We reply: it is capable of enjoining the fire-establishment contained in its own word — because of hearing, because of the fire-establishment having been enjoined, [and] when purposelessness [would result], it is capable of enjoining through the sentence '<s>vasānau</s>' ('the two wearing'). For there is a connection between the fire-establishment and the two wearing ones; there, one's own meaning is not wholly abandoned. But if the connection of wearing-linen were to be enjoined, then the [liṅ], abandoning the fire-establishment in '<s>ādadhīyātām</s>,' would wholly abandon the [Vedic] word when enjoining [something else]. And when the <s>liṅ</s> is proximate to the fire-establishment and is to enjoin [something], the [Vedic] word does not venture to enjoin the remote linen-wearing connection — because of the remoteness of the meaning. Moreover, if the [Vedic] word is abandoned and the linen-wearing connection is what is being enjoined, the linen would be a subsidiary of wearing, not of the fire-establishment. In that case, even in the absence of linen, the fire-establishment would not be deficient — and [so] even without linen, the fire-establishment would take place.
[The objector] says: then what meaning is intended by [linen's] being subsidiary to wearing? We reply: none — for this very reason this position is abandoned. [The objector] says: then how [should we understand] the hearing of 'linen wearing'? We reply: it is not possible to enjoin both — linen and the [dual] number — for the sentence would be split. Therefore, for the two who are not [specifically] wearing linen, the word <s>kṣauma</s> is a restatement. And since wearing is already understood from context, '<s>vasānau pumāṃsau</s>' — 'two men wearing' — is the meaning. And their [garments] generally, of one who is moving about, are soiled, linen-like. Or [alternatively], a garment of one moving about has the quality [described by] the word [<s>kṣauma</s>]. Therefore [the fire-establishment is] the domain of two males.

children.text: guṇasya tu vidhānatvāt patnyā{*5/234*} dvitīyaśabdaḥ syāt//6.1.23//
children.translated_text: But because of [the sentence's purpose being] the enjoining of a subsidiary, [the word] <s>patnyā</s> ('with the wife') is [to be understood as the meaning of] the 'second' word. // MS_6,1.23 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti, yad uktaṃ dvau puruṣāv ādadhīyātām iti, eka evādadhīta. vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnim{*5/235*} ādadhīteti{*5/236*}, ekavacanaṃ hi vivakṣitam. tasmād eka evādadhīta. nanv idaṃ vacanaṃ dvau pumāṃsāv ādadhīyātām iti. nety āha, guṇasya tu vidhānatvāt, kṣaumavidhānam asmin vākye nyāyyam, tathā hy apūrvo 'rtho vihito bhavati, gamyate hi viśeṣaniyamaḥ. itarathā kṣaumavacanam anuvādamātraṃ syāt, vādamātraṃ cānarthakam. pakṣe cānuvādaḥ, na caikapakṣavacana eṣa śabdaḥ. gauṇatve ca sādhāraṇaṃ sādṛśyam. tasmāt pramādādhyayanam{*5/237*} avagamyeta vinaiva hetunā.
āha, nanu pumāṃsau vidheyau, tadvidhāne ca na kṣaumavidhānam, vākyabhedo hi tathā syāt, śrutigamyau ca pumāṃsau, vākyagamyaṃ ca kṣaumaṃ bādheyātām iti. atrocyate, na pumāṃsau vidheyau, prāpta evātra sadvitīyaḥ pumān so 'nūdyate. katham? eko 'tra pumān śrūyate, tasya patnyā dvitīyaśabdaḥ syāt. na ca, yat prāg vacanād gamyate, tad vidheyaṃ bhavati. tasmāt kṣaumavidhānam, na vākyabhedo bhavati.
yad ucyate, na kṣaumasya vidhāyako 'stīti. tad ucyate, ādadhīyātām iti tad vidhāsyati. nanv etad ādhānaṃ śrutyā vidhātuṃ samartham, nānyad iti. ucyate, śabdāntareṇa vihitatvād ādhānasya na vidhāyakam, vihitatvāc ca puṃsaḥ sa[620]{*5/238*}dvitīyasya, tasyāpi na vidhāyakam, atas tadasaṃbhavāt kṣaumasya vidhāyikā liṅ bhaviṣyati, vākyasāmarthyāt. yat tv asmin pakṣe 'tyantāya svārthaṃ jahātīti. nātyantāya hāsyati, ādhāne vāsaḥ kṣaumaṃ kuryād iti. asmin pakṣe puṃśabdaḥ strīpuṃsayor vṛtta iti gamyate. asti hi tatra tasya nimittaṃ pumān sadvitīyaḥ, evamādi ca dṛṣṭvā bhagavatā pāṇininā sūtraṃ praṇītam, pumān striyā{*5/239*} iti, tasya viṣayaḥ puṃśabdaḥ śiṣyamāṇaḥ sādhur bhavati, na strīśabda iti. tasmād ekaḥ pumān ādadhīta na dvāv iti.
children.translated_text:
The word <s>tu</s> ('but') overturns the [prima facie] position. This is not [correct] — what was said, 'two men should establish [the fire].' Rather, one alone should establish. 'In spring, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the fire' — for the singular number is intended. Therefore one alone should establish. But [the objector says]: this statement [says] 'two males should establish.' He replies: no — because of [the sentence's purpose being] the enjoining of a subsidiary. It is proper that this sentence enjoins linen, for thus an unprecedented meaning is enjoined; a specific restriction is understood. Otherwise, the mention of linen would be a mere restatement, and a mere restatement is purposeless. And on the [opposing] view, it is a restatement; and this word is not a statement for only one view. When [linen is] subsidiary, the similarity [with other garments] is common [to all]. Therefore, it would be understood as a recitation due to error — without any reason.
[The objector] says: but the two males are what is to be enjoined; and in their injunction, there is no linen-injunction — for that would split the sentence. And the two males are understood by the [Vedic] word, while linen is understood by the sentence — so [the males] would override [linen]. To this we reply: the two males are not what is to be enjoined — the man with a second is already obtained here and is being restated. How? One man is heard here; his 'second' word would be the wife (<s>patnī</s>). And what is understood before the [Vedic] statement is not what is to be enjoined. Therefore the linen-injunction [is the purpose]; there is no splitting of the sentence.
As for what is said — 'there is no injunctive [word] for linen' — to that we reply: '<s>ādadhīyātām</s>' ('the two should establish') will enjoin it. But [the objector says]: this [liṅ] is capable of enjoining the fire-establishment by the [Vedic] word, and nothing else. We reply: because the fire-establishment has been enjoined by another word, [the liṅ] is not its injunctive [here]; and because the man with a second [620] [is already obtained], it is not its injunctive either. Therefore, because of the impossibility of those [other referents], the <s>liṅ</s> will be the injunctive of linen — through the capacity of the sentence. As for [the objection] that 'on this view it would wholly abandon its own meaning' — it will not wholly abandon it; '[in] the fire-establishment, one should make the garment linen' — this is the meaning. On this view, the masculine word is understood as applying to male and female [together]. For there is a reason for it — a man with a second [i.e., the wife]. And having observed this and the like, the venerable <s>Pāṇini</s> composed the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>pumān striyā</s>' — its scope is: the masculine word, when retained, is correct; not the feminine word. Therefore one man alone should establish, not two.

children.text: tasyā yāvad uktam āśīr brahmacaryam atulyatvāt//6.1.24//
children.translated_text: For her, [the observance lasts] as long as stated — the benediction (<s>āśīḥ</s>) and the celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) — because of inequality. // MS_6,1.24 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajetetyevamādiṣv etad uktaṃ strīpuṃsayoḥ sahādhikāra iti. athedānīṃ saṃdihyate, kiṃ sarvaṃ yājamānaṃ patnyā kartavyam, uta yāvad uktam āśīr brahmacaryaṃ ceti. kiṃ prāptam? sarvaṃ yājamānaṃ patnyāḥ syāt, sāpi hi yajamānā, tulyatvāt. tasmāt sarvaṃ tasyā iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, tasyā yāvad uktaṃ syāt, vacanaprāmāṇyāt, āśīḥ brahmacaryaṃ ca syāt. kasmāt? atulyatvāt, atulyā hi strīpuṃsāḥ, yajamānaḥ pumān vidvāṃś ca, patnī strī cāvidyā ca.
kim ataḥ? yady evaṃ hy etad{*5/240*} atulyatvam. etad ato bhavati, [621]{*5/241*} kratvartheṣu yāni yājamānāni śravaṇāni, teṣūpādeyatvena śravaṇād vivakṣitaṃ liṅgam, tena teṣu patnī na syāt, yāni ca kratvarthāni samantrakāṇi teṣv avidyatvāt patnī na syāt. tat patnyā adhyayanasya prayojakaṃ syād iti yady ucyeta. tan na, asaty api prayojakatve tasya nirvṛttir bhaviṣyati. asti hi tasya pumān nirvartakaḥ, yac ca kartvartham, tad ekena yena kenacin nirvartayitavyam. tasmāt pratiṣiddhasya patnyā adhyayanasya punaḥ prasave, na kiṃcid asti pramāṇam. atas tad api patnī na kuryāt, yās tv āśiṣaḥ, yac ca brahmacaryam, tat puruṣaṃ prati guṇabhūtam, na tatrānyatareṇa kṛte sidhyati, anyatarasya hi saṃskāro hīyeta. na ca tatropādeyatvena yajamānasya śravaṇam. tasmāl liṅgam apy avivakṣitam. ata āśīr brahmacaryaṃ cobhayor api syāt. yac cāhatyocyate, yathā, patnyājyam avekṣata iti. tasmād atulyatvād asamānavidhānā patnī yajamānena bhavitum arhatīti.
children.translated_text:
In [statements such as] 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>,' 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — it has been stated that the husband and wife have joint eligibility. Now the doubt arises: should the wife perform all the sacrificer's [duties], or only as much as is stated — the blessings (<s>āśīs</s>) and the vow of celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>)? What is the prima facie view? The wife should [perform] all the sacrificer's [duties], for she too is a sacrificer, because of equality. Therefore all [duties are] hers.
Given this prima facie view, we say: hers should be only as much as is stated, because of the authority of the [Vedic] statement — the blessings and the vow of celibacy. Why? Because of inequality — for men and women are not equal; the sacrificer is a man and learned, while the wife is a woman and unlearned.
What follows from this? If this inequality exists — the following results: in the sacrificer's [duties] that are heard as pertaining to the ritual's purpose, where the masculine gender (<s>liṅga</s>) is intended through the hearing of the [male] agent, in those the wife would not [participate]. And in those that serve the ritual's purpose and are accompanied by <s>mantras</s>, in those the wife would not [participate] because of her being unlearned. If it were said that this would provide a reason for the wife's Vedic study — that is not so, for even without this reason, the accomplishment of that [Vedic study] will occur. For a man is the accomplisher of that; and what serves the agent's purpose is to be accomplished by anyone whosoever. Therefore, in the renewed permission of what is prohibited — the wife's Vedic study — there is no valid basis. Hence the wife should not do that either. But the blessings and the vow of celibacy — these are secondary with respect to the person; in those, the accomplishment does not occur when only one of the two performs them, for the consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of one of them would be deficient. And there, the sacrificer is not heard [exclusively] as the agent. Therefore the masculine gender too is not intended [in those contexts]. Hence the blessings and vow of celibacy should belong to both. And what is directly stated [about the wife], such as 'the wife observes the <s>ājya</s> (ghee)' — [that too applies]. Therefore, because of inequality, the wife cannot have the same ritual prescriptions as the sacrificer.

children.text: cāturvarṇyam aviśeṣāt//6.1.25//
children.translated_text: All four <s>varṇas</s> [are eligible], because of the absence of any distinction. // MS_6,1.25 //

children.text: āgnihotrādīni karmāṇy udāharaṇam, teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ tāni bhaveyuḥ, utāpaśūdrāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ varṇānām iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? cāturvarṇyam adhikṛtya, yajeta, juhuyād ityevamādi śabdam uccarati vedaḥ. kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt, na hi kaścid viśeṣa upādīyate. tasmāc chūdro na nivartate.
children.translated_text: The <s>Agnihotra</s> and other rites are the example. Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: do they belong to all four <s>varṇas</s>, or to [only] three <s>varṇas</s> excluding the <s>Śūdra</s>? What is the prima facie view? All four <s>varṇas</s> are addressed when the <s>Veda</s> utters [the words] 'he should sacrifice,' 'he should offer,' and the like. Why? Because of the absence of any distinction — for no distinction is adopted [in the text]. Therefore the <s>Śūdra</s> is not excluded.

children.text: nirdeśād vā trayāṇāṃ syād agnyādheye hy asaṃbandhaḥ kratuṣu, brāhmaṇaśrutir ity ātreyaḥ//6.1.26//
children.translated_text: Or because of the specification, it would be for [only] three — for in the fire-establishment there is no connection [of the <s>Śūdra</s>] with the sacrifices; the [Vedic] statement pertains to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> [and the other two] — thus [says] <s>Ātreya</s>. // MS_6,1.26 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati, trayāṇām adhikāraḥ syāt. kutaḥ? agnyādheye nirdeśāt, agnyādheye trayāṇāṃ nirdeśo bhavati, vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnīn{*5/243*} ādadhīta, grīṣme rājanyaḥ, śaradi vaiśya iti{*5/244*}, śūdrasyādhāne śrutir nāstīty anagniḥ śūdro 'samartho 'gnihotrādi nirvartayitum. tasmād agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāma ityevamādiṣu śūdrasya prāpikā śrutir nāsti. brāhmaṇādīn evādhikṛtya sā pravartate, te hi samarthā agnimattvāt, āhavanīyādayo na śūdrasya, avidhānāt, saṃskāraśabdatvāc cāhavanīyādīnām. tasmād anadhikṛto 'gnihotrādiṣu śūdra ity ātreyo manyate{*5/245*} sma.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' overturns the [previous] position. The eligibility would be of [only] three. Why? Because of the specification in the fire-establishment — in the fire-establishment, the specification is of [only] three: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the fires in spring; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in summer; a <s>Vaiśya</s> in autumn.' There is no [Vedic] statement for the <s>Śūdra</s>'s fire-establishment. Hence the <s>Śūdra</s>, being without fire, is unable to accomplish the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like. Therefore, in [statements such as] 'One desiring heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>' and the like, there is no [Vedic] statement that applies to the <s>Śūdra</s>. It applies only with reference to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two, for they are capable because of possessing fire. The <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires] do not belong to the <s>Śūdra</s>, because of the absence of a prescription [for him] and because the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and the like are designated by the word 'consecration' (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Therefore the <s>Śūdra</s> has no eligibility for the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like — so <s>Ātreya</s> holds.

children.text:

*{5/244: Tait.Br. 1.1.2.6-7}*
*{5/245: E2: ātreyo munir manyate}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:

children.text: nimittārthena bādaris tasmāt sarvādhikāraṃ syāt//6.1.27//
children.translated_text: Because [the specification is] for the purpose of the occasion, [says] <s>Bādari</s>; therefore the eligibility should be universal. // MS_6,1.27 //

children.text:
yad uktam, anadhikāraḥ śūdrasyeti, tan na, sarvaṃ hy arthinam adhikṛtya yajetety ucyate, so 'sati pratiṣedhavacane śūdrān na vyāvarteta. yat tv asamartho 'gnyabhāvād iti, syād evāsyāgnir arthaprāptaḥ, kāmaśrutiparigṛhītatvāt.
atrāha, nanv agnyādheyacodanā brāhmaṇādisaṃyuktā na śūdrasyeti. ucyate, nimittārthena tāḥ śrutayo na prāpikāḥ. katham? nimittasvabhāvā ete śabdāḥ, brāhmaṇa ādadhāno vasante, rājyanyo{*5/246*} grīṣme, vaiṣyaḥ śaradīti brāhmaṇādīnāṃ vasantādibhiḥ saṃbandho gamyate, tena vasantādisaṃbandhārthā brāhmaṇādaya [623]{*5/247*} ity eva gamyate, tathā cādadhātir na vākyena śūdrād vyāvartito bhaviṣyati. tasmād bādariḥ sarvādhikāraṃ śāstraṃ manyate smeti gamyate.
children.translated_text:
As to what was said — 'the <s>Śūdra</s> has no eligibility' — that is not so, for [the Veda] utters 'he should sacrifice' with reference to everyone who has a desire [for the result]. In the absence of a prohibitive statement, he [the <s>Śūdra</s>] would not be excluded. As for [the argument] that he is incapable because of the absence of fire — his fire would be obtained by the nature of things, because he is included by the statement of desire.
To this [the objector] says: but the injunctions of fire-establishment are connected with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two, not with the <s>Śūdra</s>. We reply: those [Vedic] statements are for the purpose of the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>), not for establishing [exclusive] eligibility. How? These words are of the nature of occasions — '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> establishing [fire] in spring, <s>Kṣatriya</s> in summer, <s>Vaiśya</s> in autumn' — the connection of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two with spring and the other [seasons] is understood. Therefore it is understood as [meaning]: '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two [are mentioned] for the purpose of [indicating] their connection with spring and the other [seasons].' And thus the [verb] '<s>ādadhāti</s>' (he establishes) will not be excluded from the <s>Śūdra</s> by the sentence. Therefore <s>Bādari</s> holds that the scripture has universal eligibility — so it is understood.

children.text: api vānyārthadarśanād yathāśruti pratīyeta//6.1.28//
children.translated_text: Or rather, it should be understood as per the [Vedic] statement, since the observation for another purpose [confirms the specification]. // MS_6,1.28 //

children.text: api veti pakṣo vyāvartyate. yathāśruty eva pratīyeta, brāhmaṇādayo hy ādhāne śrūyante, tena brāhmaṇādikartṛkam ādhānam, vasantādiśravaṇāc ca vasantādikālakam. tathā ca, idaṃ śūdravarjitānām evānukramaṇaṃ bhavati, bārhadgiraṃ brāhmaṇasya brahmasāma kuryāt, pārthuraśyaṃ rājanyasya, rāyovājīyaṃ vaiśyasyeti, śūdrasya sāma nāmananti. tathā payovrataṃ brāhmaṇasya, yavāgū rājanyasya, āmikṣā vaiśyasyeti, tathādhāne 'ṣṭasu prakrameṣu brāhmaṇo 'gnim ādadhīta, ekādaśasu rājanyaḥ, dvādaśasu vaiśya iti. evam abrahmasāmakam avratakam aprakramakaṃ ca śūdrasya prayuktam api karma niṣphalaṃ syāt. tasmān na śūdro juhuyād yajeta vā.
children.translated_text: The phrase 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. It should be understood as per the [Vedic] statement — for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two are heard in the fire-establishment; therefore the fire-establishment is performed by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two. And because of the hearing of spring and the other [seasons], it takes place in spring and the other [seasons]. And thus, this enumeration is [shown to be] exclusive of the <s>Śūdra</s>: 'The <s>Bārhadgira</s> <s>Brahma-sāman</s> should be employed for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; the <s>Pārthurasya</s> for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>; the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> for a <s>Vaiśya</s>' — no <s>sāman</s> is named for the <s>Śūdra</s>. Likewise regarding the vow (<s>vrata</s>): 'Milk for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; barley gruel for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>; <s>āmikṣā</s> (curds) for the <s>Vaiśya</s>.' Likewise in the fire-establishment: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the fire in eight steps; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in eleven; a <s>Vaiśya</s> in twelve.' Thus, the <s>Śūdra</s>'s ritual, [performed] without a <s>Brahma-sāman</s>, without a vow, and without the [prescribed] steps, would be fruitless even if performed. Therefore the <s>Śūdra</s> should not offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> or sacrifice.

children.text: nirdeśāt tu pakṣe syāt//6.1.29//
children.translated_text: But in the [alternative] view, because of the specification, [the <s>Śūdra</s>] would [be eligible]. // MS_6,1.29 //

children.text: naitad evam, śūdrasyāgnyabhāvād anadhikāro 'gnihotrādiṣv iti. asti hi śūdrasyādhānam, ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatta iti śāstraṃ sāmānyena. idam api nimittārthaṃ bhaviṣyati, tasmāt sarvādhikāraṃ śāstraṃ bhavitum arhatīti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that the <s>Śūdra</s> has no eligibility for the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like because of the absence of fire. For the <s>Śūdra</s>'s fire-establishment exists — 'He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire' is a scripture of general scope. This too will be [taken as] for the purpose of the occasion; therefore the scripture can be of universal eligibility.

children.text: vaiguṇyān neti cet//6.1.30//
children.translated_text: 'Because of deficiency' — if [one objects thus] — // MS_6,1.30 //

children.text: atha yad uktam{*5/248*}, abrahmasāmakam avratakam aprakramakaṃ ca śūdrasya karma prayuktam api phalaṃ na sādhayed viguṇam iti, tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'the <s>Śūdra</s>'s ritual, [performed] without a <s>Brahma-sāman</s>, without a vow, and without the [prescribed] steps, would not produce fruit even if performed, being deficient' — that is to be refuted.

children.text: na kāmyatvāt//6.1.31//
children.translated_text: No, because of [their] being optional (<s>kāmya</s>). // MS_6,1.31 //

children.text: sa eṣa parihāraḥ, krāmyatvāt, kāmayiṣyate śūdraḥ, abhīvartaṃ nāma brahmasāma{*5/250*}, tad dhi anārabhya kiṃcid āmnātam aviśeṣeṇa, cakṣurvimita ādadhyād iti{*5/251*}, aniyataprakrameṣu śūdrasya niyamyate. vrate 'pi, mastu śūdrasyeti saṃbandhadarśanād adhyavasīyate, mastv eva śūdrasya. tasmāc cāturvarṇyam adhikriyeta.
children.translated_text: This is the refutation: because of [their] being optional, the <s>Śūdra</s> will desire [alternative elements]. The <s>Abhīvarta</s> is a <s>Brahma-sāman</s> that is recorded without reference to any [specific rite] and without distinction; '[the one who is] measured by the eye should establish [the fire]' — among the [options with] unrestricted steps, the <s>Śūdra</s>'s [number] is restricted. Regarding the vow as well, from the observation of the connection — 'buttermilk for the <s>Śūdra</s>' — it is concluded that buttermilk is indeed [the vow-food] of the <s>Śūdra</s>. Therefore all four <s>varṇas</s> should be eligible.

NOTES:
[{5/250: Cf. <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 7.5.1.6}]
[{5/251: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.1.4.1}]

children.text: saṃskāre ca tatpradhānatvāt//3.1.32//
children.translated_text: And in the preparatory rite, because of the primacy of the person. // MS_6,1.32 //

children.text: vrate ca viśeṣo 'vagamyate tatprādhānyaṃ puruṣaprādhānyaṃ hi vrate{*5/252*}. kim ataḥ, yat puruṣapradhānatā? etad ato bhavati, puruṣapradhānaḥ saṃskāro na śaknoty anupasaṃhriyamāṇaḥ, tasyādhikāraṃ vyāvartayitum. tat katham iti. yajeteti hi svargakāme 'bhidhīyamāne tatkāmaḥ śūdro nābhihita iti kathaṃ gamyate? kiṃ hi sa yāgasya puruṣanirvartyaṃ na nirvartayati. vratam iti cet. na, sāmarthyopajananāya hi tad yasyaivocyeta, tasyaiva tena vinā na sāmarthyam, nānyasya. eṣa{*5/253*} eva hi vratasyāṅgabhāvo yat, kartāraṃ samarthaṃ karoti. yasya tu tena prayojanam, sa tadanapekṣyaiva yāgam abhinirvartayati. tasmād api na śūdravarjanam.
children.translated_text: And in the vow, a distinction is understood — the primacy of the person is indeed [what is at stake] in the vow. What follows from the primacy of the person? The following results: a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) that has the person as primary, when not gathered [by an explicit statement], cannot exclude his eligibility. How so? For when 'he should sacrifice' is stated with reference to one who desires heaven, how is it understood that the <s>Śūdra</s> who has that desire is not addressed? For what of the sacrifice that requires a person does he not accomplish? [If one argues:] the vow — [we reply:] no, for that [vow] is stated for the purpose of generating capability for the very person for whom it is stated; without it, he alone lacks capability, not another. For this is precisely the subsidiary nature of the vow — that it makes the agent capable. But one who has no need for it accomplishes the sacrifice without relying on it. Therefore there is no exclusion of the <s>Śūdra</s> on this ground either.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/252: E1 gibt puruṣaprādhānyaṃ hi vrate in Klammern}*
*{5/253: E2,6: evam}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/252: E1 gives <s>puruṣaprādhānyaṃ hi vrate</s> in brackets}]
[{5/253: E2,6: <s>evam</s>}]

children.text: api vā vedanirdeśād apaśūdrāṇāṃ pratīyeta//6.1.33//
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the Vedic specification, it should be understood as [applying to] the [three varṇas] excluding the <s>Śūdra</s>. // MS_6,1.33 //

children.text: evaṃ na prāpakāṇi śravaṇānīty uktam, śakyate tu vaktuṃ prāpakāṇīti, na ca sūtrakāreṇa tad vyapadiṣṭam. naimittikeṣv api teṣu satsu śakya eva śūdraparyudāso vaktum iti, na tadādṛtam, hetvantaraṃ vyapadiṣṭam. api veti pakṣavyāvartanam. [625]{*5/254*} evam api sati naimittike 'pi brāhmaṇādiśravaṇe saty apaśūdrāṇām evādhikāraḥ. kutaḥ? vedanirdeśāt, vede hi trayāṇāṃ nirdeśo bhavati, vasante brāhmaṇam upanayīta, grīṣme rājanyam, śaradi vaiśyam iti, vedābhāvād asamarthaḥ śūdro yaṣṭum. tasmān nādhikriyeta.
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said that the [Vedic] statements are not [exclusively] applicable [to the three]. But it can also be said that they are applicable. And the author of the <s>sūtras</s> did not indicate that [view]. Even when those [seasonal specifications] are indeed occasional, the exclusion of the <s>Śūdra</s> can be stated — yet that was not relied upon. A different reason is indicated. The phrase 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. Even so — even when the [Vedic] statements about <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like are [merely] occasional — the eligibility is of [only] the [three varṇas] excluding the <s>Śūdra</s>. Why? Because of the Vedic specification — for in the <s>Veda</s>, the specification is of [only] three: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be invested with the sacred thread (<s>upanayana</s>) in spring; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in summer; a <s>Vaiśya</s> in autumn.' Because of the absence of Vedic [study], the <s>Śūdra</s> is incapable of sacrificing. Therefore he should not be eligible.

children.text: guṇārthitvān neti cet//6.1.34//
children.translated_text: 'Because of [the Vedic study] being for a subsidiary purpose' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_6,1.34 //

children.text: guṇenādhyayanenārthaḥ{*5/255*}, śūdro 'nupanītaḥ svayam upetyādhyeṣyate, tathāsya sāmarthyaṃ janiṣyata iti.
children.translated_text: The subsidiary — Vedic study — is the purpose. The <s>Śūdra</s>, though uninitiated, will approach [a teacher] on his own and study. Thus his capability will be generated.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/255: E2: guṇenādhyayanenārthī}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/255: E2: <s>guṇenādhyayanenārthī</s>}]

children.text: saṃskārasya tadarthatvād vidyāyāṃ puruṣaśrutiḥ//6.1.35//
children.translated_text: Because the preparatory rite is for that [study's] purpose, the mention of the person pertains to [Vedic] knowledge. // MS_6,1.35 //

children.text: ucyate, vidyāyām evaiṣā puruṣaśrutiḥ, upanayanasya saṃskārasya tadarthatvāt, vidyārtham upādhyāyasya samīpam ānīyate, nādṛṣṭārtham, kuḍyaṃ{*5/256*} vā kartum, saiṣā{*5/257*} vidyāyāṃ puruṣaśrutiḥ. katham avagamyate? ācāryakaraṇam etad abhidhīyate. kutaḥ? ātmanepadadarśanāt, nayatir{*5/258*} ācāryakaraṇe vartate, tadarthasaṃbandhād upanayanam ācāryakaraṇaprayuktam, vedādhyāpanena cācāryo bhavati. tasmād vedādhyayane brāhmaṇādayaḥ śrutāḥ, śūdrasya na śrutaṃ vedādhyayanam, ato 'vedātvād asamarthaḥ śūdro nābhikriyata iti.
children.translated_text: We reply: this mention of the person pertains to [Vedic] knowledge alone. Why? Because the preparatory rite of <s>upanayana</s> (investiture) is for that [knowledge's] purpose — he is brought near to the teacher for the purpose of knowledge, not for an unseen purpose, nor to build a wall. This mention of the person pertains to knowledge. How is this understood? What is being referred to is the making [of someone] into a teacher (<s>ācāryakaraṇa</s>). Why? Because of the observation of the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) — the verb <s>nayati</s> (he leads) is used in the sense of making [someone] into a teacher. Because of the connection with that purpose, the <s>upanayana</s> is occasioned by the making [of someone] into a teacher. And one becomes a teacher through teaching the <s>Veda</s>. Therefore, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two are heard [as eligible] for Vedic study; Vedic study is not heard for the <s>Śūdra</s>. Hence, because of being without [knowledge of] the <s>Veda</s>, the <s>Śūdra</s> is incapable and is not eligible.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/256: E2: nāpi kaṭaṃ kuḍyaṃ}*
*{5/257: E2: dṛṣṭārtham eva saiṣā}*
*{5/258: E2: kathaṃ punar nayatir}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/256: E2: <s>nāpi kaṭaṃ kuḍyaṃ</s>}]
[{5/257: E2: <s>dṛṣṭārtham eva saiṣā</s>}]
[{5/258: E2: <s>kathaṃ punar nayatir</s>}]

children.text: vidyānirdeśān neti cet//6.1.36//
children.translated_text: 'Because of the specification of knowledge' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_6,1.36 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, avaidyatvād{*5/259*} asāmarthyād anadhikṛtaḥ [626]{*5/260*} śūdra iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ, vidyānirdeśāt, vidyāṃ nirdekṣyati, anuktām apy adhyeṣyata iti, śakyate hy anuktam{*5/261*} apy adhyetum. tasmāc cāturvarṇyasyāpy adhikāraḥ//
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that the <s>Śūdra</s> is not eligible because he is incapable due to being without [Vedic knowledge] — this is not a defect. Because of the specification of knowledge — he will acquire knowledge; even what is not [formally] taught, he will study, for it is possible to study even what has not been [formally] taught. Therefore all four <s>varṇas</s> should have eligibility.

children.text: avaidyatvād{*5/262*} abhāvaḥ karmaṇi syāt//6.1.37//
children.translated_text: Because of being without [Vedic knowledge], there would be absence [of eligibility] for ritual action. // MS_6,1.37 //

children.text:
na caitad asti, śūdro 'dhyeṣyata iti, pratiṣiddham asyādhyayanam, śūdreṇa nādhyetavyam iti, adhīyānasyāpy adhyayanaṃ saphalaṃ{*5/263*} na bhavati, doṣaś ca jāyate. ato 'vaidyaḥ śūdraḥ, asyābhāvaḥ karmaṇīti siddham.
athāpi vaidyatvena{*5/264*} sidhyet, tathāpy anagnitvād abhāvaḥ karmaṇi syāt. atha katham anagniteti. prāpakāṇi hi brāhmaṇādīnām ādhāne vākyāni. nanu ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatta ity ādhānasya vidhāyakam. tatra brāhmaṇasya{*5/265*}, vasante 'gnim ādadhīteti nimittārthāni vacanānīti gamyate. atrocyate, brāhmaṇo 'gnim ādadhīteti śrutyā vidhānaṃ gamyate. ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatta iti stutyā, tad ānumānikaṃ pratyakṣaśrutād durbalam. tasmāt prāpakāṇi vacanāni, ataḥ śūdrasyānadhikāraḥ.
children.translated_text:
Nor is it the case that a <s>Śūdra</s> could study [the Veda], for his study is prohibited: 'A <s>Śūdra</s> should not study.' Even if he does study, his study does not bear fruit, and a defect arises. Therefore the <s>Śūdra</s> is without [Vedic] knowledge, and his absence from the ritual act is established.
Even if [his eligibility] were established through [Vedic] knowledge, still, because of not having [sacred] fires, he would have no place in the ritual act. But how is he without fires? For the statements regarding the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>) pertain to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the others [i.e., the three upper varṇas]. [The objector says:] but 'He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire' is the injunctive [statement] for the fire-establishment. There, [the statement] pertains to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'He should establish the fire in spring' — such statements are understood as serving the purpose of [indicating] the occasion. To this we reply: from the [Vedic] statement (<s>śruti</s>) 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the fire,' the prescription is understood. 'He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire' — this is [understood] through praise (<s>stuti</s>), and that which is inferential is weaker than what is directly heard. Therefore the statements [about fire-establishment] are enabling [only for the three varṇas]; hence the <s>Śūdra</s>'s ineligibility [is established].

children.text:
NOTES:

*{5/263: E2: adhyayanaphalaṃ}*
*{5/264: E2: vaidhatvena}*
*{5/265: E2: brāhmaṇo}*

children.text: tathā cānyārthadarśanam//6.1.38//
children.translated_text: And thus, the observation for another purpose [confirms this]. // MS_6,1.38 //

children.text: anyārthadarśanaṃ ca bhavati, yathā na śūdrasyādhyayanam iti. kiṃ liṅgaṃ bhavati? yadyu vā etat śmaśānam, yac chūdraḥ, tasmāc chūdrasamīpe nādhyeyam ity anadhyayanaṃ śūdrasya darśayati. tasmād apaśūdrāṇām adhikāraḥ. nanv āhavanīyād vināpi, yāgo vacanaprāmāṇyāc chūdrasya vidhīyate. [627]{*5/266*} ucyate, nātra yāgasadbhāvo vidhīyate svargakāmasya, kiṃ tarhi svargaphalatā viśiṣṭasya yāgasya. tasmād asaṃbhavaḥ śūdrasyāgnihotrādiṣu.
children.translated_text: And there is an observation for another purpose: 'A <s>Śūdra</s> should not study.' What is the indicatory mark? 'This is indeed a cremation ground — namely the <s>Śūdra</s>; therefore one should not study in the proximity of a <s>Śūdra</s>' — this shows the non-study of the <s>Śūdra</s>. Therefore, the eligibility belongs to those who are not <s>Śūdras</s>. [The objector says:] but even without the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, a sacrifice could be prescribed for the <s>Śūdra</s> by the authority of the [Vedic] statement. We reply: what is prescribed here is not the mere existence of the sacrifice for one desiring heaven, but rather the heaven-producing capacity of a sacrifice endowed with [all] qualifications. Therefore the <s>Śūdra</s> has no possibility [of participation] in the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like.

children.text: trayāṇāṃ dravyasaṃpannaḥ karmaṇo dravyasiddhitvāt//6.1.39//
children.translated_text: Among the three [<s>varṇas</s>], one who possesses property [is entitled], because the ritual act is accomplished through material substance. // MS_6,1.39 //

children.text: agnihotrādiṣv eva saṃdehaḥ, kim adravyasyādhikāro neti. ucyate, trayāṇāṃ dravyasaṃpanno 'dhikriyeta, nādravyaḥ. kutaḥ? na hi śaknoty adravyo dravyasaṃyuktaṃ karmānuṣṭhātum. tasmād adravyasyānadhikāraḥ.
children.translated_text: The doubt pertains specifically to the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like: is one without property entitled or not? We reply: among the three [<s>varṇas</s>], one who possesses property would be entitled, not one without property. Why? For one without property is not able to perform a ritual act that requires material substance. Therefore, one without property is not entitled.

children.text: anityatvāt tu naivaṃ syād arthād dhi dravyasaṃyogaḥ//6.1.40//
children.translated_text: But because of [the propertyless state] being impermanent, this should not be so; for the conjunction with property is from the nature of things. // MS_6,1.40 //

children.text: naivaṃ syāt, yad uktam, adravyasyānadhikāra iti. kutaḥ? anityatvāt, anityo 'dravyasaṃyogaḥ{*5/267*}, na hi kaścij jātyādravya eva puruṣaḥ. asty upāyo yena dravyavān bhavati. yaḥ śaknoti yaṣṭum, tasya yajeteti vācako bhavati, yo na kathaṃcid api śaknoti yāgam abhinirvartayitum, taṃ nādhikaroti yajeta śabadaḥ{*5/268*}. yas tu kenacit prakāreṇa śaknoti, na taṃ varjayitvā pravartate. arthāc ca dravyasaṃyogo bhaviṣyati, jīviṣyati vinā dhanenety etad anupapannam. tasmād{*5/269*} arthād eva dravyasaṃyogaḥ{*5/270*}.
children.translated_text: This should not be so — what was said, that one without property is not entitled. Why? Because of impermanence — the conjunction with the absence of property is impermanent, for no person is by birth without property. There is a means by which one becomes wealthy. The word 'he should sacrifice' speaks to one who is able to sacrifice; one who cannot by any means accomplish the sacrifice — to him the word 'he should sacrifice' does not apply. But one who by some means is able — [the word] does not operate by excluding him. And the conjunction with property will come about from the nature of things — for to say 'one will live without wealth' is untenable. Therefore the conjunction with property [comes] from the nature of things alone.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/267: E2: 'dravyasaṃyogaḥ}*
*{5/268: E2: yajeteti śabadaḥ}*
*{5/269: E2: vipratiṣiddham. tad idam abhidhīyate. tasmād}*
*{5/270: E2 hat noch: adhikāro 'dravyasyāpīti}*
*{5/271: E2: 5,215; E6: 2,124}*

children.text: aṅgahīnaś ca taddharmā//6.1.41//
children.translated_text: And one who is deficient in a limb has the same status as that [propertyless person]. // MS_6,1.41 //

children.text: agnihotrādiṣv evāṅgahīnaṃ prati saṃdehaḥ, kim asāv adhikriyate, uta neti. tatrāpy adhikaraṇātideśaḥ. asamartha iti kṛtvā pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, śakter vidyamānatvād uttaraḥ. tad{*5/272*} idam abhidhīyate, aṅgahīnaś ca taddharmā{*5/273*}. kiṃdharmā? adravyadharmeti.
children.translated_text: The doubt pertains specifically to the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like regarding one who is deficient in a limb: is he entitled or not? Here too there is an extension of the [previous] topic. The prima facie view is non-entitlement, on the grounds of incapability; the [established] conclusion is entitlement, because capability does exist. This is what is stated: one who is deficient in a limb has the same status as that [propertyless person]. What status? The same status as one without property.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/272: E2: ity uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ. tad}*
*{5/273: E2: taddharmeti}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/272: E2: <s>ity uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ. tad</s>}]
[{5/273: E2: <s>taddharmeti</s>}]

children.text: utpattau nityasaṃyogāt//6.1.42//
children.translated_text: At origination, because of invariable conjunction. // MS_6,1.42 //

children.text:
yasya tv apratisamādheyam aṅgavaikalyam, taṃ prati vicāraḥ, kim adhikriyate, neti, pūrvādhikaraṇenādhikriyata iti prāpte brūmaḥ, nādhikriyata iti. kutaḥ? śaktyabhāvāt, nāsau kenacid api prakāreṇa śaknoti yaṣṭum, tasmāt tasyādhikāro na gamyate.
nanu yac chaknoti, tatrādhikriyata iti, cakṣur vikalo vinājyāvekṣaṇena, vinā viṣṇukramaiḥ paṅguḥ, vinā praiṣādiśravaṇena ca badhiraḥ, etān padārthān prati cakṣurvikalādīnām anadhikāra iti. nety ucyate, nājyāvekṣaṇādi puruṣaṃ prati nirdiśyate, yadi hi taṃ prati nirdeśyeta, tato vikalo 'py adhikriyeta, kratuṃ praty eṣām upadeśaḥ, prakaraṇāviśeṣāt, puruṣasya cākhyātenānabhidhānād iti. uktam{*5/274*} etad vidhir vā saṃyogāntarād{*5/275*} ity atra. taiś ca [629]{*5/276*} vinā viguṇaṃ karma prayuktam api na phalaṃ sādhayet. tasmāt tasyānadhikāraḥ.
children.translated_text:
But regarding one whose limb-deficiency cannot be remedied — as to whether he is entitled or not — when, by the previous topic, entitlement is prima facie obtained, we say: he is not entitled. Why? Because of the absence of capability — he is by no means able to sacrifice. Therefore his entitlement is not understood.
[The objector says:] but he is entitled with respect to what he is able [to do] — one who is blind [could sacrifice] without the inspection of the <s>ājya</s> (ghee); one who is lame, without the strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; one who is deaf, without hearing the <s>praiṣa</s> (directive) and the like. With respect to these ritual elements, the blind and the like are not entitled. Not so, we reply — the inspection of the <s>ājya</s> and the like are not prescribed with respect to the person. For if they were prescribed with respect to him, then even a disabled person would be entitled. [Rather,] the instruction of these [elements] is with respect to the ritual act, because of the non-specification of context, and because the person is not designated by name. This has been stated [in the discussion of] 'or it is an injunction because of the conjunction with another' [MS 3.4.13]. And without those [elements], a deficient ritual act, even when performed, would not accomplish the fruit. Therefore he is not entitled.

children.text: atryārṣeyasya hānaṃ syāt//6.1.43//
children.translated_text: One who does not have three <s>ārṣeya</s> [sages in his lineage] would be excluded. // MS_6,1.43 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, ārṣeyaṃ vṛṇīte, ekaṃ vṛṇīte, dvau vṛṇīte, trīn vṛṇīte, na caturo vṛṇīte, na pañcāti vṛṇīta iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim atryārṣeyasyādhikāra uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? atryārṣeyo 'py adhikriyata iti. kutaḥ? ārṣeyaṃ vṛṇīta iti sāmānyavacanam, tasmād ekaṃ variṣyati dvau vā, tac ca darśayati, ekaṃ vṛṇīte dvau vṛṇīta iti, tathā pratiṣedhati, na caturo vṛṇīta iti{*5/277*}, na pañcāti vṛṇīta iti. na hy aprāptasya pratiṣedho 'vakalpate. tasmād atryārṣeyo 'py adhikriyeta{*5/278*}.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, yo na tryārṣeyaḥ, sa nādhikriyeta. kutaḥ? trīn vṛṇīta iti viśeṣavacanāt, vidhiś cāprāptatvāt. nanv ekaṃ vṛṇīta ity api viśeṣavacanam asti. nety ucyate, vidhāyikāyā vibhakter abhāvāt. nanu stutyā vidhāsyante, yathā, trīn vṛṇīta iti. ucyate, trayāṇām eva stutiḥ, sā tritvaṃ vidhāsyeti. ekaṃ vṛṇīta ity avayutyavādo{*5/279*} 'yaṃ trayāṇām eva. tatrāpi tritvam eva stūyate vidhātum. ekam ekavākyena vidhānaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. na caturo vṛṇīte, na pañcātivṛṇīta [630]{*5/280*} iti nityānuvādo bhaviṣyati. tasmāt tryārṣeyasyādhikāro nānyasyeti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: 'He chooses the <s>ārṣeya</s> (sagehood); he chooses one, he chooses two, he chooses three; he does not choose four, he does not choose more than five.' There a doubt [arises]: is one without three <s>ārṣeyas</s> (patriarchal sages) entitled or not? What is the prima facie view? Even one without three <s>ārṣeyas</s> is entitled. Why? Because 'he should choose the <s>ārṣeya</s>' is a general statement; therefore he will choose one or two. And this is shown [by]: 'he chooses one, he chooses two.' Likewise it prohibits: 'he does not choose four,' 'he does not choose more than five.' For prohibition does not apply to what is not [already] obtained. Therefore even one without three <s>ārṣeyas</s> would be entitled.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: one who does not have three <s>ārṣeyas</s> would not be entitled. Why? Because of the specific statement 'he chooses three,' and because of its being an injunction, since [three ārṣeyas] are not [otherwise] obtained. [The objector says:] but 'he chooses one' is also a specific statement. Not so, we reply — because of the absence of an injunctive verbal ending. [The objector says:] but they will be prescribed through a eulogistic [passage], just as 'he chooses three.' We reply: the eulogy is of three only, and that [eulogy] will prescribe the triad. 'He chooses one' — this is a component-restatement (<s>avayutyavāda</s>) of those three alone. There too, only the triad is praised in order to prescribe [it]. 'He chooses one' — the prescription will be through syntactic unity [with that]. 'He does not choose four, he does not choose more than five' — this will be an invariable restatement. Therefore the entitlement belongs to one with three <s>ārṣeyas</s>, not to another.

children.text: vacanād rathakārasyādhāne 'sya sarvaśeṣatvāt//6.1.44//
children.translated_text: Because of the [Vedic] statement, the <s>Rathakāra</s> (chariot-maker) [is entitled] for the fire-establishment, since he is the remainder of all [other varṇas]. // MS_6,1.44 //

children.text: ādhāne śrūyate, varṣāsu rathakāra ādadhīteti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ traivarṇikānām anyatamo rathakāraḥ, āhosvid atraivarṇika iti. kiṃ prāptam? rathakārasyātraivarṇikasyādhānam etat. kutaḥ? vacanāt, na{*5/281*} hi vacanasya kiṃcid akṛtyam asti{*5/282*}, sarvaśeṣaś cātraivarṇika ādhāne, brāhmaṇarājyanyaviśām{*5/283*} uktam ādhānam, pariśeṣād atraivarṇiko rathakāra syāt.
children.translated_text: Regarding the fire-establishment, it is heard: 'The <s>Rathakāra</s> should establish [his fire] in the rainy season.' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>Rathakāra</s> one of the three <s>varṇas</s>, or is he outside the three <s>varṇas</s>? What is the prima facie view? This fire-establishment belongs to a <s>Rathakāra</s> who is outside the three <s>varṇas</s>. Why? Because of the [Vedic] statement — for there is nothing that a [Vedic] statement cannot accomplish. And the one outside the three <s>varṇas</s> is the remainder of all [varṇas] regarding fire-establishment — since the fire-establishment of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>Vaiśyas</s> has been stated, by the remainder, the <s>Rathakāra</s> who is outside the three <s>varṇas</s> would [be meant].

children.text: nyāyyo vā karmasaṃyogāc chūdrasya pratiṣiddhatvāt//6.1.45//
children.translated_text: Or it would be proper [that he is one of the three varṇas], because of connection with the [ritual] action, since the <s>Śūdra</s> is prohibited. // MS_6,1.45 //

children.text: nyāyyo vā syāt, traivarṇiko rathakāraḥ rathakarmaṇā viśeṣeṇocyate, śūdro hy asamarthatvāt pratiṣiddhaḥ. tasmāt traivarṇiko rathakāraḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: Or it would be proper — the <s>Rathakāra</s> would be one of the three <s>varṇas</s>, designated by the specific [term] 'chariot-maker' based on his occupation. For the <s>Śūdra</s> is prohibited because of incapability. Therefore the <s>Rathakāra</s> would be one of the three <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text: akarmatvāt tu naivaṃ syāt//6.1.46//
children.translated_text: But because of [chariot-making] not being a [prescribed] occupation [for the three varṇas], this should not be so. // MS_6,1.46 //

children.text: nāsti traivarṇiko rathakāraḥ, pratiṣiddhaṃ hi tasya śilpopajīvitvam, atraivarṇikas tv asti. tasmād vacanaprāmāṇyāt sa ādhāsyate{*5/284*}.
children.translated_text: There is no <s>Rathakāra</s> among the three <s>varṇas</s>, for livelihood from craft (<s>śilpa</s>) is prohibited for them. But one outside the three <s>varṇas</s> does exist [as a Rathakāra]. Therefore, by the authority of the [Vedic] statement, he shall establish [the fires].

children.text: ānarthakyaṃ ca saṃyogāt//6.1.47//
children.translated_text: And there would be purposelessness because of the conjunction. // MS_6,1.47 //

children.text: brāhmaṇādiṣu vasantādayo niyatāḥ, tān prati varṣā ucyamānā apy asaṃbandhād ānarthakyaṃ prāpnuyuḥ. tasmād atraivarṇiko rathakāra iti.
children.translated_text: For <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the others, the seasons such as spring are fixed [for fire-establishment]. The rainy season, being stated with respect to them, would attain purposelessness because of the lack of connection [with them]. Therefore the <s>Rathakāra</s> is outside the three <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text: guṇārtheneti cet//6.1.48//
children.translated_text: If [one argues it is] for the purpose of a [secondary] quality — // MS_6,1.48 //

children.text: evaṃ cet paśyasi, nāsti traivarṇiko rathakāraḥ, pratiṣiddhatvāc chilpopajīvitvasyeti. guṇārthena kaścid bhaviṣyati rathakāro vaitathyena, tasyedam{*5/286*} ādhānaṃ vijñāyate.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that there is no <s>Rathakāra</s> among the three <s>varṇas</s> because livelihood from craft is prohibited — [then the objector says:] someone may be a <s>Rathakāra</s> through a secondary quality, i.e., figuratively; for him this fire-establishment is understood.
