children.text: uktam animittatvam//6.1.49//
children.translated_text: It has been stated that [the seasonal designations] are not for the purpose of occasion. // MS_6,1.49 //

children.text: uktam, etad asmābhiḥ, na nimittārthāny etāni śravaṇānīti. kim ato yadi na nimittārthāni. etad ato bhavati, prāpakāṇīti, prāptitvāt teṣām ādhānasya, punaḥ prāpakam anarthakam, tena yasyāprāptam, tasya bhaviṣyatīti. athocyeta, etad ekaṃ nimittārthaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. naitad evam avakalpate, vasantādisaṃyuktaṃ tat katham iva varṣābhiḥ saṃbadhyeta. api ca, prāpakapakṣa ādhānaṃ vidhīyate śrutyā, nimittapakṣe punar varṣā vidhātavyā vākyena, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasīti. tasmād atraivarṇikasyedam ādhānam iti.
children.translated_text: It has been stated by us that these statements [about seasons] are not for the purpose of occasion. What follows if they are not for the purpose of occasion? This follows: they are enabling — because of [the seasons'] being the means of obtaining fire-establishment. A further enabling [statement] for what is already obtained is purposeless; therefore [the Vedic statement] will apply to one for whom [fire-establishment] has not [otherwise] been obtained. [The objector says:] but this one [statement about rainy season] could be for the purpose of occasion. Not so — that cannot work, for [the statement] is connected with spring and the like. How could it be connected with the rainy season? Moreover, in the enabling view, the fire-establishment is prescribed by the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>); in the occasion view, the rainy season would need to be prescribed by the sentence (<s>vākya</s>), and the [Vedic] word is stronger than the sentence. Therefore this fire-establishment belongs to one outside the three <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text: saudhanvanās tu hīnatvān mantravarṇāt pratīyeran//6.1.50//
children.translated_text: But the <s>Saudhanvanas</s> should be understood, because of [their] inferior status, from the <s>mantra</s> text. // MS_6,1.50 //

children.text: na tu sarva evātraivarṇiko rathakāraḥ, saudhanvanā ity eṣa [632]{*5/287*} jātivacanaḥ śabdaḥ. saudhanvanā nāma jātir abhidhīyate, hīnās tu kiṃcit traivarṇikebhyaḥ, jātyantaram, na tu śūdrāḥ, na vaiśyāḥ, na kṣatriyāḥ, teṣām idam ādhānam. katham avagamyate? prasiddher mantravarṇāc ca, mantravarṇo hi bhavati, saudhanvanā ṛbhavaḥ sūracakṣasa{*5/288*} iti, ṛbhūṇāṃ tv iti rathakārasyādhānamantraḥ. tasmāt saudhanvanā ṛbhava iti, ṛbhavaś ca rathakārāḥ. api ca, nemiṃ nayanty ṛbhavo yatheti{*5/289*} ye nemiṃ nayanti ta ṛbhava ity ucyante. rathakārāś ca nemiṃ nayanti. tasmād atraivarṇikānām aśūdrāṇām etad ādhānam iti.
children.translated_text: But not every [person] outside the three <s>varṇas</s> is a <s>Rathakāra</s> — '<s>Saudhanvanas</s>' is a word denoting a specific community (<s>jāti</s>). The community called <s>Saudhanvana</s> is designated — they are somewhat inferior to the three <s>varṇas</s>, a different community, but not <s>Śūdras</s>, not <s>Vaiśyas</s>, not <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. This fire-establishment belongs to them. How is this known? From common knowledge and from the <s>mantra</s> text — for there is a <s>mantra</s> text: '<s>Saudhanvanā Ṛbhavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ</s>' (The <s>Saudhanvanas</s>, the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, of sun-like vision) — and the <s>Ṛbhu</s> [passages] serve as the fire-establishment <s>mantras</s> of the <s>Rathakāra</s>. Therefore '<s>Saudhanvanā Ṛbhavaḥ</s>' — and the <s>Ṛbhus</s> are chariot-makers. Moreover, 'as the <s>Ṛbhus</s> fashioned the wheel-rim' — those who fashion the wheel-rim are called <s>Ṛbhus</s>. And chariot-makers fashion the wheel-rim. Therefore this fire-establishment belongs to those outside the three <s>varṇas</s> who are not <s>Śūdras</s>.

children.text: sthapatir niṣādaḥ syāc chabdasāmarthyāt//6.1.51//
children.translated_text: The <s>Sthapati</s> (chief builder) would be a <s>Niṣāda</s>, because of the capacity of the word. // MS_6,1.51 //

children.text:
vāstumadhye raudraṃ caruṃ nirvapet, yatra rudraḥ prajāḥ śamayed ity etām iṣṭiṃ prakṛtyocyate, etayā niṣādasthapatiṃ yājayed iti. niṣādasthapatiṃ prati saṃdehaḥ, kim adhikṛtānām anyatamaḥ, utānya eveti. anyatama iti brūmaḥ, sa hi samarthaḥ, vidvattvād agnimattvāc ca, anyo 'vidvattvād anagnitvād asamartha iti.
nanu niṣādasthapatiśabdas tatra nopapadyate. ucyate, na, nopapadyate, niṣādānāṃ sthapatir iti ṣaṣṭhīsamāso bhaviṣyati, śreṣṭho niṣādānām. tasmād adhikṛtādhikāram etac chāstram iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, sthapatir niṣādaḥ syāt, śabdasāmarthyāt{*5/290*}, niṣāda{*5/291*} eva sthapatir bhavitum arhati. kasmāt? śabdasāmarthyāt, niṣādaṃ hi niṣādaśabdaḥ{*5/292*} śaknoti vadituṃ{*5/293*} śravaṇenaiva, niṣādānāṃ tu sthapatiṃ lakṣaṇayā brūyāt. śrutilakṣaṇā[633]{*5/294*}viśaye ca śrutir nyāyyā, na lakṣaṇā. athocyate, naiṣa doṣaḥ, niṣādaśabdo niṣādavacana eva, ṣaṣṭhī saṃbandhasya vāciketi. tan na, ṣaṣṭhyaśravaṇāt. nātra ṣaṣṭhīṃ śṛṇumaḥ. āha, lopasāmarthyāt ṣaṣṭhyartho 'vagamyata iti. satyam avagamyate, na tu lopena. kena tarhi? niṣadaśabdalakṣaṇayā, tasyāś ca daurbalyam ity uktam. samānādhikaraṇasamāsas tu balīyān. tatra hi svārthe śabdau vṛttau bhavataḥ. dvitīyā ca vibhaktis tantreṇobhābhyāṃ saṃbadhyate, tena dvitīyānirdiṣṭo niṣādo gamyate. tatra ṣaṣṭhyarthaṃ kalpayann aśrutaṃ gṛhaṇīyāt. tasmān niṣāda eva sthapatiḥ syāt.
children.translated_text:
'In the middle of the homestead one should offer a <s>caru</s> (porridge) to <s>Rudra</s>, where <s>Rudra</s> may pacify the offspring' — this offering is stated as the archetype; 'by this [offering], one should cause the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s> to sacrifice.' Regarding the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s>, a doubt [arises]: is he one of those [already] qualified [for sacrifice], or someone entirely different? We say: he is one of those [already] qualified, for he is capable — because of possessing knowledge and possessing the sacred fire. Someone else, lacking knowledge and lacking the fire, would be incapable.
[The objector says:] but the word <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s> would not apply there [to one already qualified]. [We] reply: no, it does apply — 'the chief (<s>sthapati</s>) of the <s>Niṣādas</s>' — this will be a genitive compound, [meaning] the foremost among the <s>Niṣādas</s>. Therefore this teaching concerns those who are [already] qualified. Given this prima facie view, we say: the <s>sthapati</s> should be a <s>Niṣāda</s>, because of the capacity of the word [633]. The <s>Niṣāda</s> himself should be the <s>sthapati</s>. Why? Because of the capacity of the word — for the word <s>Niṣāda</s> can denote a <s>Niṣāda</s> by hearing alone, whereas to say 'the <s>sthapati</s> of the <s>Niṣādas</s>' it would [need to] speak by secondary indication. And where both literal meaning and secondary indication are applicable, the literal meaning is proper, not secondary indication. [The objector] says: this is not a fault — the word <s>Niṣāda</s> indeed denotes the <s>Niṣāda</s>, while the genitive expresses the relation. No, [we reply] — because the genitive is not heard. We do not hear a genitive here. He says: the genitive meaning is understood through the force of elision. True, it is understood — but not through elision. By what then? Through the secondary indication of the word <s>Niṣāda</s> — and the weakness of that [secondary indication] has been stated. But the co-referential compound (<s>samānādhikaraṇa-samāsa</s>) is stronger. For in that [type of compound], both words are used in their own [primary] senses. And the accusative case ending connects with both [words] through the <s>tantra</s> (single operation). Thereby a <s>Niṣāda</s> designated by the accusative is understood. If one were to construe a genitive meaning there, one would accept what is unheard. Therefore the <s>sthapati</s> should be a <s>Niṣāda</s> himself.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca//6.1.52//
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_6,1.52 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ dṛśyate, kūṭaṃ dakṣiṇeti{*5/295*} niṣādasya dravyaṃ darśayati. kūṭaṃ hi niṣādānām evopakārakam, nāryāṇām, evaṃ svam eva tan niṣādānām iti.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark is observed: 'a hammer (<s>kūṭa</s>) as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee)' — this shows the property of the <s>Niṣāda</s>. For a hammer is useful to <s>Niṣādas</s> alone, not to <s>Āryas</s> — thus it is the very own [property] of the <s>Niṣādas</s>.

children.text: puruṣārthaikasiddhitvāt tasya tasyādhikāraḥ syāt//6.2.1//
children.translated_text: Because each individual person achieves his own purpose, each one would have the qualification. // MS_6,2.1 //

children.text:
dvādaśāhena prajākāmaṃ yājayet, ṛddhikāmā upeyuḥ. tathā, tatra tatraivaṃkāmāḥ satram upeyuḥ, saptadaśāvarāś caturviṃśatiparamāḥ satram āsīrann iti. teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ tasya tasya kṛtsnena phalenārthinaḥ satre 'dhikāraḥ, uta parṣado 'rthinyā adhikāra iti. āha, nanv arthino bahusaṃkhyāviśiṣṭā nirdiśyante, katham eṣām ekaśo{*5/297*} 'dhikāro bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, ṛddhikāmā ityevamādi vidhīyamānam ṛddhilakṣiteṣu samasteṣu vyasteṣu ca prāptam, na śakyaṃ bahuvacanena viśeṣe 'vasthāpayitum, tena taṃ tam adhikuryāt parṣadaṃ veti bhavati saṃdehaḥ.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam? ekaiko na samartho bahukartṛkaṃ satraṃ racayitum, parṣadaṃ tu kartrīm arthinīm avagacchāmaḥ. na cākartuḥ phalaṃ bhavati, na caikaḥ kartocyate, tasmāt samastānāṃ phalam. ekaikasya phalāvayayaḥ, madhyakaṃ syāt kṛtsnaṃ phalam iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, tasya tasyārthinaḥ kṛtsnaṃ phalaṃ satrān nirvartate. kutaḥ? puruṣārthasyaikaikasya siddhir yato bhavati, sahakriyamāṇe sarva ekaikaḥ puruṣārthaṃ sādhayati tantreṇa, kartṝṇāṃ phalaṃ ca bhavati, ekaikaś cātra kartā.
[635]{*5/298*} āha, nanv etad uktam, ekaiko na śaknoti bahukartṛkaṃ kartuṃ iti. ucyate, śaknoty ekaikasya svātantryavivakṣāyām, yadaikaikaḥ svātantryeṇa pravartate, tadānyān saṃkhyānirvṛttyarthaṃ sāmādibhiḥ prayokṣyate. ekam ekaḥ puruṣārthaṃ sādhayati, itara itaraś ca, tena sarve kartāraḥ savyapekṣā bhaviṣyanti. sarve cet kartāraḥ, pṛthak pṛthag eva phalena saṃbhantsyante.
children.translated_text:
'One should cause one desiring offspring to sacrifice with the twelve-day [rite]'; 'those desiring prosperity should undertake [the <s>satra</s>].' Likewise: 'Those desiring thus should undertake the <s>satra</s> — not fewer than seventeen, not more than twenty-four should sit for the <s>satra</s>.' Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: does each individual one who desires the complete fruit have the qualification for the <s>satra</s>, or does the assembly (<s>parṣad</s>) that desires [the fruit collectively] have the qualification? [The objector] says: but the desirous ones are designated with a specific number in the plural; how would each one individually have the qualification? [We] reply: statements like 'those desiring prosperity' — being enjoined — are applicable to those characterized by the desire for prosperity, both collectively and individually. It cannot be restricted by the plural to a specific [collective] sense. Hence the doubt arises: does it qualify each individual, or the assembly?
What is the prima facie view? A single individual is incapable of organizing a multi-performer <s>satra</s>. But we understand the assembly as the performer, the one who desires [the fruit]. And there is no fruit for one who is not a performer; and no single [person] is called a performer. Therefore the fruit belongs to all collectively — each one receives a portion of the fruit; the entire fruit would be shared property.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: for each individual who desires [the fruit], the complete fruit is produced from the <s>satra</s>. Why? Because each individual person's purpose is achieved [635] — when performed jointly, each individual achieves his purpose through the single operation (<s>tantra</s>). The performers receive the fruit, and each one here is a performer.
He says: but was it not stated that a single individual cannot perform what requires many performers? [We] reply: he can, when the intention is [for] the independence of each individual. When each individual acts independently, he will employ others for the purpose of fulfilling the number, through persuasion and the like. One achieves his own purpose, and every other does the same. Thus all performers will be mutually dependent. And if all are performers, they will each be connected with the fruit separately.

children.text: api cotpattisaṃyogād yathā syāt sattvadarśanam, tathā bhāvo 'vibhāge{*5/299*} syāt//6.2.2//
children.translated_text: Moreover, because of the connection at origination, the [joint] nature should exist without division, as is observed in the case of seeing a being. // MS_6,2.2 //

children.text:
api ca, naitad viruddham, yad ekaṃ karma bahubhiḥ kriyata iti. yady ucyate, viruddham, ekena karmaṇi kṛte dvitīyaḥ kiṃ kuryād iti. atrocyate, paryāyeṇa kriyāyām evaṃ doṣaḥ, tantreṇa tu kriyāyāṃ bhavati kvacit saṃbhavaḥ, yathā syāt sattvadarśanaṃ tathā bhāvo 'vibhāge{*5/300*} syāt, yathaikaikasya sattvasya hastino 'śvasya vā darśanam ekaikena kṛtsnam abhinirvartyate. evam eva satre tantrabhāvo bhavet, sarveṣāṃ madhyakaṃ dravyam, madhyakasyāhavanīyasyopary adhvaryur apavidhyati{*5/301*}. tatra sarve kartāras tantreṇa bhavanti.
na cātrotpannasaṃyogaḥ, utpattyaiva tu saṃkhyayā karma saṃyujyate. yadi hy utpannaṃ saṃyujyeta, tato 'nekasaṃbandhārtham iti vacanaṃ gamyeta, utpattisaṃyoge tv etan nāsti. tasmād ekaikasya kṛtsnena phalenābhisaṃbandha iti.
children.translated_text:
Moreover, there is no contradiction in this — that one ritual act is performed by many. If it is said to be contradictory — [that] when one action has been performed, what would a second person do? — to this we reply: in performing by turns, there is such a fault; but in performing by a single operation (<s>tantra</s>), there is sometimes possibility. Just as there is the observation of seeing a being — the seeing of each individual being, an elephant or a horse, is fully accomplished by each individual [viewer]. Just so in the <s>satra</s>, the <s>tantra</s>-nature would exist [for all] without division. All share the common property (<s>madhyaka</s>); above the shared <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> makes the offering. There, all become performers through the single operation.
And here there is no connection with [something already] originated — rather, the ritual is connected with the number at its very origination. For if what has [already] originated were [then] connected [with many performers], then the statement would be understood as [meaning] connection with many. But in connection at origination, this does not arise. Therefore each individual is connected with the complete fruit.

children.text: prayoge puruṣaśruter yathākāmī prayoge syāt//6.2.3//
children.translated_text: Because of the hearing of the person in the performance, [the sacrifice] may be performed at will, as one wishes. // MS_6,2.3 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta, jyotiṣṭomena svarga[636]{*5/302*}kāmo yajeteti śrūyate. atra saṃdehaḥ, kim aniyamena, eko dvau bahavo vā yajeran, athavaika eva yajeteti. nanu tṛtīya uktam{*5/303*}, śāstraphalaṃ prayoktarīti. yadā prayoktari, tadā vivakṣitam ekatvaṃ yathā, tathā vakṣyāmaḥ, iha tu tad evākṣipyate, punaś ca nirṇeṣyata iti.
kiṃ prāptam? yathākāmī prayoge syāt. kutaḥ? puruṣaśruteḥ, puruṣaḥ śrūyate, puruṣe yāgaṃ śrāvayitvā kṛtārthaḥ śabda ekasya dvayor bahūnāṃ vā yāgaṃ na vārayati. nāsau puruṣo yāge śrūyate, yāgam abhinirvartayet, yāgena vā phalam abhinirvartayed iti. kathaṃ tarhi? yāgena phalaṃ prāpnuyād iti. yāgasya vā phalanirvṛtter vā nāṅgaṃ puruṣaḥ. yadi hy aṅgam abhaviṣyad yāge phalanirvṛttau vā, tadā saṃkhyā guṇabhūtā tadaṅgaṃ puruṣaṃ paricchindyāt. atha punar aṅgabhūtaṃ puruṣaṃ{*5/304*} prakāśayan lakṣaṇatvenaiva puruṣe 'bhisaṃbadhyeta{*5/305*}, na guṇavacanatayā. tatra cāvivakṣitaṃ saṃkhyāvacanam, yāvān arthī samarthaś ca tāvantaṃ sarvam adhikṛtyaitad ucyamānaṃ na śakyate ekena vacanena viśeṣayitum. kathaṃ ca puruṣaprādhānyam? na phalotpattyā kiṃcit prayojanam asti, na yāgotpattyā, ātmā tu phalasaṃbaddhaḥ sarvasyeṣṭaḥ, tadarthaṃ karma kartavyam, itarathocyamānam api na kriyeta, tatra vacanārthakyaṃ syāt, tasmād yāthākāmyaṃ syāt, eko dvau bahavo vā yajerann iti. tathā ca darśayati, yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svarpatī{*5/306*} iti dvayor yajamānayoḥ pratipadaṃ kuryād iti, ete{*5/307*} asṛgram indava{*5/308*} iti bahubhyo yajamānebhya iti dvayor bahūnāṃ ca yāgaṃ pradarśayati.
children.translated_text:
It is heard: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>'; 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [636].' There a doubt [arises]: is there no fixed rule — may one, two, or many sacrifice? Or should only one sacrifice? [The objector says:] but in the third [adhyāya] it was stated: 'the fruit of the teaching [belongs] to the performer.' When [the fruit belongs] to the performer, the oneness that is intended — we shall explain how. But here that very [point] is raised as a preliminary objection, and it will be settled again.
What is the prima facie view? The sacrifice may be performed at will. Why? Because the person is heard — the person is heard [in the injunction]. Having instructed the person regarding the sacrifice, the word, its purpose fulfilled, does not prevent one, two, or many from sacrificing. That person is not heard as [a subsidiary] in the sacrifice — [as though he were needed to] accomplish the sacrifice, or through the sacrifice to accomplish the fruit. Rather, [he is one who] would obtain the fruit through the sacrifice. The person is not a subsidiary of the sacrifice or of the fruit-production. For if he were a subsidiary of the sacrifice or of the fruit-production, then the number, being subordinate, would delimit that subsidiary person. But the word designating a subsidiary person would connect with the person only as a characterization — not as a statement of a subordinate quality. And the statement of number is not intended there; however many desire [the fruit] and are capable — all of them are qualified. A statement with a single word cannot restrict [the scope]. And how is the person primary? The origination of the fruit has no purpose [for the person]; nor does the origination of the sacrifice. But the self, connected with the fruit, is desired by everyone; for its sake the ritual act is to be performed. [If stated] otherwise, even though stated, it would not be performed, and therein the statement would be purposeless. Therefore [the sacrifice] may be performed at will — one, two, or many may sacrifice. And thus [the <s>Veda</s>] shows: 'You two are indeed the lords of heaven' — for two sacrificers, [the mantra] should be recited for each foot (<s>pāda</s>). 'These drops have surged forth' — for many sacrificers. Thus it shows the sacrifice of two and of many.

children.text: pratyarthaṃ śrutibhāva iti cet//6.2.4//
children.translated_text: If [one argues that] the [Vedic] statement applies to each purpose — // MS_6,2.4 //

children.text: iti cet, idaṃ{*5/309*} cet paśyasi, pratyarthaṃ{*5/310*} śrutibhāvaḥ syāt, [637]{*5/311*} yāgam abhinirvartayet, tataś ca phalaṃ prāpnuyād iti. kutaḥ? etad ubhayaṃ hy etasmād avagamyate, katarad atra jahīma iti nādhyavasyāmaḥ. tasmād ubhayam api pratyetavyam. āha, nanv ekārthavacanatā na nyāyyeti. ucyate, yad avagamyate tan nyāyyam, ubhayaṃ ca pratīyate. tasmād ubhayārthavacanataiva nyāyyā. yāgaṃ prati ca guṇabhāvād vivakṣitam ekavacanam.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — [that] the [Vedic] statement would apply to each purpose [637] — [the person would both] accomplish the sacrifice and thereby obtain the fruit. Why? For both these [meanings] are understood from this [sentence]; which of them should we abandon? — we cannot determine. Therefore both should be accepted. He says: but a statement expressing a single meaning would be improper. [We] reply: what is understood is proper; and both are understood. Therefore a statement expressing both meanings is indeed proper. And the singular, being subordinate with respect to the sacrifice, is intentionally significant.

children.text:

children.text: tādarthye na guṇārthatānukte 'rthāntaratvāt kartuḥ pradhānabhūtatvāt//6.2.5//
children.translated_text: When [the person acts] for that purpose, subordination of the agent is not [appropriate]; because, the [sentence] being unstated [as giving subordination], the meaning would be different — since the agent is primary. // MS_6,2.5 //

children.text: naitad evam, tādarthye puruṣe pradhānabhūte sati nāṅgabhūtaḥ puruṣaḥ pratīyate, anukte hi nyāye na pratīmaḥ, arthāntaraṃ yato guṇabhāvāt pradhānabhāvaḥ, pradhānabhūtaś cātra kartā, vacanasyārthavattvāt. ato na guṇabhāvaḥ kartur avakalpate, codanaikatvāt. ekā hi vidhāyikā codanā, sā yadi phalotpattiṃ yāgotpattiṃ vā vidhatte, tadā kartā na svārthena, yadā punaḥ svārthena, tadā yāgaḥ phalaṃ vā tādarthyena. na caitad yaugapadyena bhavati, svārtha ekaḥ, tadartha itaro vaiparītyena veti, yathobhābhyāṃ bāhubhyām iṣūn asyati devadatta iti gamyate, na ca yaugapadyena, yadā dakṣiṇenāsyati, tadā savyena dhanuḥpṛṣṭhaṃ namayati, na tenāpy asyatīti gamyate, tatra vyāpṛtatvāt. evaṃ yadā puruṣaprādhānyam, tadā yāgasya phalasya vā guṇabhāvo gamyate. tatra vyāpṛtatvān na tayoḥ prādhānyam api gamyate. tasmān na yāge phale vā puruṣasya guṇabhāvaḥ. ato yāthākāmyaṃ syāt, eko dvau bahavo vā yajerann iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so. When the person is primary — his purpose being served — a person as subsidiary is not understood. For we do not accept a principle that is not stated. [It would be] a different meaning — subordination leading to primacy — and the agent here is primary, because of the meaningfulness of the statement. Therefore the subordination of the agent does not apply, because of the unity of the injunction. For there is a single enjoining injunction; if it prescribes the origination of the fruit or the origination of the sacrifice, then the agent [acts] not for his own purpose. But when [acting] for his own purpose, the sacrifice and the fruit are for his sake. And this does not occur simultaneously — [that] one [acts] for his own purpose and the other for that one's purpose, in reverse — just as when <s>Devadatta</s> shoots arrows with both arms, it is understood [that both arms work simultaneously], but not simultaneously [in the same way] — when he shoots with the right, with the left he bends the bow-staff; he does not shoot with that [left arm] also — this is understood because of [the left arm's] being occupied [differently]. Similarly, when the person is primary, the subordination of the sacrifice and the fruit is understood; because of [their] being occupied [in that role], their primacy too is not understood. Therefore the person is not subordinate to the sacrifice or the fruit. Hence [the sacrifice] may be performed at will — one, two, or many may sacrifice.

children.text: api vā kāmasaṃyoge saṃbandhāt prayogāyopadiśyeta, pratyarthaṃ hi vidhiśrutir viṣāṇāvat{*5/313*}//6.2.6//
children.translated_text: Or rather, when connected with desire, [the sacrifice] should be taught for the purpose of performance, because of the connection; for the injunctive [Vedic] statement [applies] to each purpose, like a horn. // MS_6,2.6 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ, prayogāyopadiśyeta kartā, na svārthena. katham? yajetety asyārthaḥ yāgaṃ kuryāt, yāgena vā kuryād iti, sattābhivyaktimātraṃ gamyate, na phalasya kartā dhātā{*5/314*} vā, svargakāmaśabdaś ca svargakāmamātre vartate, na viśeṣam avalambate, ātmanaḥ parasya veti, śabdapramāṇakāś ca vayam īdṛśeṣv artheṣu. kathaṃ tarhi kāmasyātmasaṃbandho 'vagamyate? saṃbandhāt, phalakāmo 'nukte 'pi śabdena, ātmana eva phalaṃ kāmayate, na parasya. yatra tūbhāv arthau vaktavyau bhavataḥ, pratyarthaṃ tatra vidhiḥ śrūyate, yathā, kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā kaṇḍūyati, cātvāle kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ prāsyatīti{*5/315*}. yatraivaṃ dve śrutī vidhātryau bhavataḥ, tatra guṇabhāvaḥ prādhānyaṃ ca gamyate. na tv atraivaṃ dve vidhāyike śrutī vidyete. guṇabhūtas tu puruṣaḥ śrūyate bhāvayed iti, tatra yajyarthaḥ karaṇaṃ, karma vā. saṃbandhāt tu puruṣaprādhānyam, na kasyacit sukhenotpannena prayojanam, sukhasaṃbandhenātmanas tu kṛtyam. tasmāt saṃbandhāt puruṣaprādhānyaṃ gamyate, na śruteḥ. ato guṇabhūtasya puruṣasya saṃkhyā vivakṣiteti.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>api vā</s>' ('or alternatively') reverses the [prima facie] position: the agent is taught for the purpose of performance, not for his own sake. How? The meaning of '<s>yajeta</s>' (he should sacrifice) is 'he should perform the sacrifice' or 'he should accomplish [something] through sacrifice' — only the mere manifestation of existence is understood, not [that he is] the maker or bestower of the fruit. And the word '<s>svargakāma</s>' (one desiring heaven) applies to anyone desiring heaven without distinction — it does not depend on a specification [such as] 'of oneself or of another.' And we rely on the word as our authority in matters of this kind. How then is the self-connection of the desire understood? Through [natural] connection — one who desires the fruit, even without it being stated by the word, desires the fruit for oneself, not for another. But where both meanings need to be stated, an injunction is heard for each meaning — as in 'he scratches with the black-antelope horn; he casts the black-antelope horn into the <s>cātvāla</s>' (pit). Where there are thus two prescriptive statements, subsidiary-status and primacy are understood. But here there are not two prescriptive statements. Rather, the person is heard as subordinate — 'he should cause [the sacrifice] to happen' — there the instrument or the action is for the purpose of sacrifice. But the primacy of the person [is known] from [natural] connection — no one has a purpose with the pleasure produced [for another]; but with the pleasure connected to oneself, there is a task. Therefore, the primacy of the person is understood from connection, not from the [Vedic] word. Hence the singular number of the subordinate person is intentionally meant.

NOTES:
[{5/313: E2: <s>viṣāṇavat</s>}]
[{5/314: E2: <s>dhāratā</s>}]
[{5/315: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.1.3.8}]

children.text: anyasya syād iti cet//6.2.7//
children.translated_text: If [one objects that] it could be for another — // MS_6,2.7 //

children.text: iti ced bhavān paśyati, evaṃ sati yadi svargakāmo 'nyasyāpi svargaṃ kāmayamāno bhavati, anyasya svargaṃ kāmayamāno 'py anyo yajeta. tatra pūrvokto nyāyaḥ pratyuddhṛto bhavati, śāstraphalaṃ prayoktarīti{*5/316*}.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — then, this being so, if one desiring heaven also desires heaven for another, then another too, desiring heaven for [yet] another, would sacrifice. In that case, the previously stated principle would be overturned — [namely that] 'the fruit of the teaching belongs to the performer.'

children.text: anyārthenābhisaṃbandhaḥ//6.2.8//
children.translated_text: The connection is through another's purpose. // MS_6,2.8 //

children.text: na parasya svargakāma ity{*5/318*} evaṃ na yajeta, na, anyasya{*5/319*} svargakāmaśabdo na vācaka iti. kathaṃ tarhi? phalam asau na prāpnotīti. kathaṃ punaḥ phalasyāprāptiḥ? upagrahaviśeṣaśravaṇāt, yajeteti. yad vādhāne, brāhmaṇo vasante 'gnim ādadhīteti, tadā tu kāmaśrutāv upagraho 'nuvāda eva.
children.translated_text: It is not that one desiring heaven for another should not sacrifice [at all] — no, the word '<s>svargakāma</s>' is not non-referential to another. How then? He [simply] does not obtain the fruit. How is there non-attainment of the fruit? Because of the hearing of a specific restrictive condition (<s>upagraha</s>) — [namely the word] '<s>yajeta</s>' (he should sacrifice). As in the fire-establishment — 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the fire in spring' — there, when the desire is heard, the restrictive condition is merely a restatement.

children.text: phalakāmo nimittam iti cet//6.2.9//
children.translated_text: If [one argues that] the one desiring the fruit is the occasion — // MS_6,2.9 //

children.text: evaṃ ced bhavān manyate, na svargakāmaśabdo na vācaka iti, anyo na yajeta phalābhāvāt, nāsya yāga iti, sūktavākaphalārthitayā{*5/320*} tarhi yajeta, āśāste 'yaṃ yajamānaḥ āyur āśāsta iti{*5/321*} prayojayitāraṃ nirdekṣyati hotā, phalavidhiś ca sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharatīti vidhānāt, yadi phalavidhir ayaṃ māntravarṇikaḥ, tarhi{*5/322*} sūktavākena prastaraḥ prahṛto bhavati, itarathādṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta. tasmād ānuṣaṅgikaphalārtham anyasya svargakāmo 'nyo yajeteti.
children.translated_text: If you think thus — that the word '<s>svargakāma</s>' is not non-referential [to another], [but] another should not sacrifice because of the absence of fruit, [i.e.,] there is no sacrifice for him — then he would sacrifice for the purpose of the <s>Sūktavāka</s> fruit: 'This sacrificer wishes; he wishes for life' — the <s>Hotṛ</s> will designate the patron. And there is a fruit-injunction through the <s>Sūktavāka</s>: 'He strikes the <s>prastara</s> (grass bundle) with the <s>Sūktavāka</s>' — because of the injunction [in that form]. If this is a fruit-injunction, [then] from the <s>mantra</s>-content, the <s>prastara</s> is struck with the <s>Sūktavāka</s>; otherwise an unseen [purpose] would have to be postulated. Therefore, for the purpose of an incidental fruit, another who desires heaven for [yet] another would sacrifice.

children.text: na nityatvāt//6.2.10//
children.translated_text: No, because of [the sacrifice being] obligatory. // MS_6,2.10 //

children.text: naitad asti, yasyaiva pradhānakarmaphalam, tasyaivānuṣaṅgikam api bhavitum arhati, evaṃ svārthenādhānaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati. na hy ādhānasya svārthatāyām asti viśeṣaḥ, pradhānaphalaṃ vānuṣaṅgikaṃ vā sarvam evādhātari samavetum arhati, nityakāmyatā ca virudhyeta, yady āyurādikāmo{*5/323*} yajeta, na tarhi nityam, yadi nityaṃ nāyurādikāmaḥ. tasmān nāvasthito nyāyaḥ pratyuddhriyeta{*5/324*}, na{*5/325*} ca puruṣaḥ pradhānabhūtaś codyate guṇabhāvāt tv asya vivakṣitam ekatvam. tasmād eka eva yajeta.
children.translated_text: This is not [correct] — whichever person [has] the fruit of the principal ritual action, the same person deserves to have even the incidental [fruit]. Thus the fire-establishment has been performed for one's own purpose. For there is no distinction in the self-directedness of the fire-establishment — whether the principal fruit or the incidental [fruit], all deserves to come together in the establisher [himself]. And the obligatoriness and desire-motivatedness would be contradicted — if one desiring life and the like were to sacrifice, then it would not be obligatory; if obligatory, then not [motivated by] desire for life and the like. Therefore the established principle should not be overturned; and the person is not enjoined as primary — because of his subordinate status, his oneness is intended. Therefore only one [person] should sacrifice.

children.text: karma tatheti cet//6.2.11//
children.translated_text: If [one argues that] the ritual action is likewise [for multiple agents] — // MS_6,2.11 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, dvayor bahūnāṃ ca yāgaṃ darśayati, yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svaḥpatī{*5/327*} iti{*5/328*} dvayor yajamānayoḥ pratipadaṃ kuryāt, ete asṛgram indava iti{*5/329*} bahubhyo yajamānebhyaḥ pratipadaṃ kuryād iti, dviyajamānake bahuyajamānake ca karmaṇi pratipad vidhāne karma tathā yuktaṃ{*5/330*} syād iti, tat parihartavyam.
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was said — [the text] shows the sacrifice for two or many: '<s>yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svaḥpatī</s>' (for you two are lords of heaven) — for two sacrificers, one would make a <s>pratipad</s> (introductory verse); '<s>ete asṛgram indavaḥ</s>' (these <s>Soma</s> drops have flowed) — for many sacrificers, one would make a <s>pratipad</s>. Since in a ritual with two or many sacrificers, a <s>pratipad</s> is prescribed, the ritual action would likewise be appropriate [for multiple agents] — that must be set aside.

children.text: na samavāyāt//6.2.12//
children.translated_text: No, because of the [pre-existing] combination. // MS_6,2.12 //

children.text: naitad evam, samavetaṃ hi karma vidyate dvābhyāṃ yajamānābhyāṃ bahubhiś ca yajamānaiḥ, vacanena, yathāhīnāḥ, teṣu pratipad vidhānam arthavad bhaviṣyati. tasmād eko yajeteti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — for a ritual that is combined with two sacrificers or many sacrificers does exist, by [Vedic] statement — such as the <s>Ahīna</s> [rites]. In those, the prescription of a <s>pratipad</s> will be meaningful. Therefore, [the rule remains that] one [person] should sacrifice.

children.text: prakramāt tu niyamyetārambhasya kriyānimittatvāt{*5/331*}//6.2.13//
children.translated_text: But [the commenced rite] would be restricted [to completion] from the commencement, because the commencement is the cause of the ritual action. // MS_6,2.13 //

children.text: prajākāmo yajeta, grāmakāmo yajetetyevamādi karma samāmnāyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ prakrāntaṃ niyogataḥ samāpanīyam utecchayā kāryaṃ heyaṃ veti. kiṃ prāptam? niyogataḥ parisamāpayitavyam iti. kutaḥ? evaṃ hi śrūyate, idaṃ kāmo yajeteti, evaṃ tasyākhyātasyārtham upadiśanti, upakramaprabhṛty apavargaparyantam āheti, upakramād ārabhya yāvat parisamāptir ity etāvān vyāpāraviśeṣas tasyārthaḥ, na yathā pākas tyāga iti. tatra hi pākasattāmātraṃ nirdiśyate, nārabhya parisamāpayitavyam [641]{*5/332*} iti. evaṃ cākhyātārthaṃ laukikā api pratipadyante, tatra nārambhe puruṣaprayatnaś codyata iti gamyate. yataś coditaṃ na niyogata ārabhante, niyogataḥ punaḥ parisamāpayanti, tena nobhe ārambhaparisamāptī{*5/333*} śabdārthaḥ. kiṃ tarhi? parisamāptiḥ śabdārthaḥ, parisamāptyām arthaprāptatvād ārambhasya. tasmāt parisamāptiḥ śabdārtha iti gamyate. sā cec chabdārthaḥ, sā kartavyatayā codyate, ārambhe nāsti kartavyatāvacanam. tena na niyogata ārambhaḥ, niyogatas tu parisamāptiḥ. tenopakrānte karmaṇi yadi vīyāt phalecchā, avāpnoti vā phalam, tasyām apy avasthāyām, kartavyam evopakrāntasya parisamāpanam.
children.translated_text: 'One desiring progeny should sacrifice; one desiring a village should sacrifice' — and so forth: ritual actions are recorded. There a doubt [arises]: must what has been commenced be completed by necessity, or can it be done or abandoned at will? What is the prima facie view? It must be completed by necessity. Why? For thus it is heard: 'This [person] desiring should sacrifice' — thus they teach the meaning of that verb: 'From the commencement through to the conclusion, it says' — from the commencement up to the completion, this much extent of operation is its meaning, not like cooking [where one says merely] 'cooking [is] abandonment.' For there, merely the existence of cooking is indicated, not [that it must be] commenced and completed. [641] And worldly people too understand the verb-meaning in this way. There, it is not understood that human effort is enjoined merely at the commencement. Since what is enjoined — people do not commence by necessity, but they do complete by necessity — therefore both commencement and completion are not the word-meaning. What then? Completion is the word-meaning, because at the [point of] completion the commencement is already obtained from the meaning. Therefore it is understood that completion is the word-meaning. And if that is the word-meaning, it is enjoined as what must be done — [but] for the commencement, there is no statement of obligation. Therefore the commencement is not by necessity, but the completion is by necessity. Hence when a ritual has been commenced, even if the desire for the fruit should cease, or [even if] the fruit is obtained — in that condition too, the completion of what has been commenced must be done.

children.text: nanv{*5/334*} arthino yo 'rthaḥ, so 'tra kartavyatayocyate. naitad evam, vākyārtho hi sa bhavati, yāgasya tu kartavyatā śrutyā gamyate. tasmād grāmakāmena{*5/335*} yāga ārabdhaḥ parisamāpanīyaḥ. grāmādikāmanāvacanaṃ nimittatvena tadā bhavati, nimitte cotpanne yat kartavyam ity ucyate, tadvinaṣṭe 'pi nimitte kartavyam eva, upakrāntasya samāpanaṃ kartavyam, na hi tadvinaṣṭam anutpannaṃ bhavati. utpattiś ca nimittam, na bhāvaḥ. tasmād vītāyām api phalecchāyām upakrāntaṃ parisamāpayitavyam. kriyāyā hi nimittam ārambhaḥ, so 'pi parisamāpter iti.
children.translated_text: [The objector says:] but the purpose of one who has a purpose — that is stated here as what must be done. This is not so — for that is the sentence-meaning; but the obligation of the sacrifice is understood through the [Vedic] word (<s>śruti</s>). Therefore a sacrifice commenced by one desiring a village must be completed. The mention of desire for a village etc. is in the role of an occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) — and when what must be done is stated upon the arising of an occasion, even when that occasion is destroyed, it still must be done. The completion of what has been commenced must be done — for that [occasion], having been destroyed, does not become unarisen. Arising is the occasion, not continued existence. Therefore even when the desire for the fruit has ceased, what has been commenced must be completed. For the commencement is the occasion of the ritual act; and that too [serves] for the completion.

children.text: phalārthitvād vāniyamo yathānupakrānte//6.2.14//
children.translated_text: Or, because of being a fruit-desirer, there would be no fixed rule — as in [the case of something] not [yet] commenced. // MS_6,2.14 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. aniyamo vā. kasmāt? phalārthitvāt phalārthinaḥ phalaṃ cikīrṣamāṇasyopāyo{*5/336*} 'yaṃ vidhīyate, na kartavyatā, sā hi vidhīyamānā phalasya vā yāgasya vā syāt. phalasya na tāvad vaktavyā, na hi yo yat kāmayate tasya tat kartavyatopadeṣṭavyā, vedaivāsau{*5/337*} mayaivaitat kartavyam{*5/338*} [642]{*5/339*} iti, upāyaṃ tu na veda, tam ākāṅkṣate. idam upadiśyate, yāga upāya iti, yāgena kriyata iti. na ca yāgasya kartavyatā, pratyakṣavirodhāt, pratyakṣas tu kleśo yāgaḥ, yadi yāgenānyasya kartavyatā, tadā na virodhaḥ. yāgakartavyatāyāṃ phalaṃ kalpyam, na ca kalpyamānasya pramāṇam asti. kartavyopadeśaś ca śakyādiṣv artheṣu bhavati, tasmān na yāgaḥ kartavyaḥ. phalakāmasya yad iṣṭaṃ tat kartavyam anūdya yathāprāptaṃ yāgasya sādhanatā vidhīyate, tena nāvaśyaṃ samāpanīyaṃ bhavati, yathānukrāntaṃ nāvaśyopakramitavyam, evam upakrāntaṃ nāvaśyaṃ samāpayitavyam. yat tu vākyārthaḥ śrutyā bādhyata iti, yatra śrutyartho na saṃbhavati, tatra vākyārtho gṛhyata ity uktam eva. tasmād aniyamaḥ.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' reverses the position. Or there is no fixed rule. Why? Because of being a fruit-desirer — for this is a means prescribed for one desiring the fruit, who wishes to accomplish the fruit; it is not an obligation. For if an obligation were prescribed, it would be either of the fruit or of the sacrifice. Of the fruit, it is certainly not to be stated — for one who desires something, the obligation of that [thing] need not be taught; he already knows [642] 'this is to be done by me.' But he does not know the means — that is what he seeks. This is taught: 'sacrifice is the means' — 'by sacrifice it is accomplished.' Nor is there an obligation of the sacrifice — because of contradiction with direct perception; for sacrifice is manifestly a hardship. If by sacrifice there is an obligation for another [person], then there is no contradiction. But in the obligation of the sacrifice [for oneself], a fruit would have to be postulated, and there is no valid authority for what is postulated. And the teaching of obligation occurs in matters that are possible [for the agent]. Therefore the sacrifice is not obligatory. Having restated the desired [fruit] of one who desires the fruit, the instrumentality of the sacrifice is prescribed as naturally obtained. Therefore it does not necessarily have to be completed — just as what has not [yet been] commenced need not necessarily be commenced, so too what has been commenced need not necessarily be completed. As for [the argument that] the sentence-meaning is overridden by the [Vedic] word — it has been stated that where the meaning of the [Vedic] word is not possible, the sentence-meaning is grasped. Therefore there is no fixed rule.

children.text: niyamo vā tannimittatvāt kartus tat kāraṇaṃ syāt//6.2.15//
children.translated_text: Or there is a fixed rule — because of that [commencement] being the occasion; for the commencement would be the cause for the agent. // MS_6,2.15 //

children.text: ārambho hi nimittaṃ samāpteḥ. katham? tat kartuḥ kāraṇaṃ syāt. kiṃ kāraṇam? satyasaṃkalpatā yo hy ārabdham evaṃjātīyakaṃ samāpayati, na taṃ{*5/340*} śiṣṭā vigarhante, prākramiko 'yam asaṃvyavahārya iti, śiṣṭavigarhaṇā ca doṣaḥ. tasmād ārabhya samāpayitavyam. āha, śiṣṭāḥ punaḥ kim arthaṃ vigarhanta iti. ucyate, vigarhante tāvat, kiṃ no viditena kāraṇeneti.
children.translated_text: For the commencement is the occasion for completion. How? It would be the cause for the agent. What kind of cause? Truthfulness of resolve (<s>satyasaṃkalpatā</s>) — one who completes what has been commenced of this kind — the learned do not reproach him [saying], 'This [person merely] begins things; he is unfit for dealings.' And the reproach of the learned is a fault. Therefore, having commenced, one must complete [the rite]. [The objector] asks: but for what reason do the learned reproach? We reply: they do reproach — what is [accomplished] by knowing the reason?

children.text: loke karmāṇi vedavat tato 'dhipuruṣajñānam//6.2.16//
children.translated_text: Worldly actions are like Vedic ones; from that, the knowledge of the [qualified] person [is derived]. // MS_6,2.16 //

children.text: kenacid gṛham upakrāntaṃ bhavati śakaṭaṃ ratho vā, vītāsya phalecchā, avāpnoti vā phalam. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ tena niyogataḥ parisamāpayitavyam, utecchayotsraṣṭavyam apīti. kiṃ prāptam? loke karmāṇy evaṃjātīyakāny upakramya parisamāpayitavyāni, yathaiva vaidikāni tathaiva tāni niyogataḥ parisamāpayīyāni. kutaḥ? tato 'dhipuruṣajñānam, tatas tatpuruṣajñānaṃ bhavitum arhati. kutaḥ? śāstrāt, āmnāyate hi takṣṇāṃ śāstram, tatrāpi devatāvyāpāro 'ṅgīkriyate, pūrvasyāṃ diśy etā devatā itarāsv etā iti, yadi{*5/342*} śāstrakṛte devatāvyāpāra upakamyāparisamāpyamāne śiṣṭavigarhaṇam, evam ihāpi bhavitum arhati.
children.translated_text: Someone commences [building] a house, a cart, or a chariot, and his desire for the fruit ceases, or he obtains the fruit. There a doubt [arises]: must he complete it by necessity, or can he abandon it at will? What is the prima facie view? Worldly actions of this kind, having been commenced, must be completed — just as Vedic ones, so too these must be completed by necessity. Why? 'From that, the knowledge of the person [is derived]' — from that, knowledge regarding that person properly arises. From what? From scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) — for a scripture of carpenters is recorded; there too, involvement of deities is accepted: 'In the eastern direction, these deities; in the other [directions], these.' If, when an activity prescribed by scripture is commenced but not completed, there is reproach by the learned — so too here it properly applies.

children.text: aparādhe 'pi ca taiḥ śāstram//3.2.17//
children.translated_text: And even in [cases of] offence, there is a <s>śāstra</s> (prescriptive text) by them. // MS_6,2.17 //

children.text: teṣāṃ ca laukikānām aparādhe tais takṣabhiḥ prāyaścittaśāstram āmnāyate, āre bhagna indrabāhur baddhavyaḥ pāyasaṃ ca brāhmaṇo bhojayitavya iti. prāyaścittaṃ ca yady adṛṣṭārtham, na śāstrādṛte. atha prasaṅgaparihārārtham, tato 'py adṛtam eva tad iti gamyate.
children.translated_text: And for those secular [carpenters], in [cases of] offence, an atonement-text (<s>prāyaścitta-śāstra</s>) is recorded involving those carpenters — 'if the axle breaks, <s>Indrabāhu</s> (the arm of <s>Indra</s>) should be bound, and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be fed with milk-rice.' Now, if this atonement is for an unseen purpose, then it does not [exist] apart from a <s>śāstra</s>. But if it is for the purpose of averting an undesirable consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>), then too it is understood to be unregarded.

children.text: aśāstrā tūpasaṃprāptiḥ{*5/344*} śāstraṃ syān na prakalpakam, tasmād arthena gamyetāprāpte vā śāstram{*5/345*} arthavat//6.2.18//
children.translated_text: But the attainment [of the result] is without a <s>śāstra</s>; the <s>śāstra</s> should not be posited [as the source]. Therefore [the result] may be understood through the meaning; or the <s>śāstra</s> would be meaningful when [the result is] not [otherwise] obtained. // MS_6,2.18 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. aśāstrā tv eṣām upasaṃprāptir iti brūmaḥ. smṛter asyāḥ śāstraṃ bhavatānumīyate, na śāstram antareṇa smṛtiḥ, na ca smṛtim antareṇa takṣṇāṃ grantha upapadyata iti. ata ucyate, bhavaty atra smṛtiḥ, evam idaṃ gṛhādi karma ramaṇīyaṃ bhavatīti, nāsmāt karmaṇo 'dṛṣṭaṃ kiṃcid iti. yā cāsau ramaṇīyatā sāntareṇāpi śāstram, śakyā jñātum, jñātvā ca smaryate. tasmāt nāsyāḥ smṛteḥ śāstraṃ
prakalpyam. yady antareṇa śāstram, na prāpyeta, tataḥ śāstram atrārthavad iti prakalpyeta. tasmān nedaṃ śāstroktam, śāstrokte ca sāmikṛte tyakte 'tyantaṃ śiṣṭā garhante, devatāśraye ca. nanv atrāpi devatāḥ parigṛhītāḥ, asyāṃ diśīyaṃ devatā yakṣyate 'syām iyam iti. ucyate, puruṣam anu devatāḥ śiṣṭāḥ smaryante, na graham anu, tasmād adoṣa iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>tu</s> ('but') reverses the [prima facie] position. We say: the attainment of these [results] is without a <s>śāstra</s>. [The objector argues:] from this <s>smṛti</s> (tradition), a <s>śāstra</s> is to be inferred — there is no <s>smṛti</s> without a <s>śāstra</s>, and without a <s>smṛti</s>, the text of the carpenters would not be possible. To this we reply: there is indeed a <s>smṛti</s> here — [namely] 'thus this work of house-building etc. is delightful'; there is no unseen [purpose] from this work. And that delightfulness is knowable even without a <s>śāstra</s>; having been known, it is remembered. Therefore a <s>śāstra</s> should not be posited for this <s>smṛti</s>. If it could not be obtained without a <s>śāstra</s>, then a <s>śāstra</s> would be posited here as meaningful. Therefore this is not stated by a <s>śāstra</s>; and when something stated by a <s>śāstra</s> — something consecrated — is abandoned, the learned completely censure [the person], especially in what depends on deities. But [the objector says]: here too deities are included — 'in this direction, this deity will be worshipped; in that, this one.' We reply: the deities are remembered as assigned according to the person, not according to the house — therefore there is no fault.

children.text: pratiṣedheṣv akarmatvāt kriyā syāt pratiṣiddhānāṃ vibhaktatvād akarmaṇām//6.2.19// idaṃ hy upadiśanti, na kalañjaṃ bhakṣayitavyam, na laśunaṃ na gṛñjanaṃ ceti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim evaṃjātīyakaṃ phalakāmena na bhakṣayitavyam, niṣkāmeṇādyam, atha vā niyogato varjayitavyam eveti. kiṃ prāptam? phalārthinā na bhakṣayitavyam, anarthino 'niyama iti. kutaḥ? niyamo hy ayam ucyate, idaṃ na bhakṣayitavyam iti, evam ukte dvayam āpatati, [645]{*5/346*} yadi vābhakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam iti, yadi vā bhakṣaṇaṃ na kartavyam iti, yadi nañviśiṣṭaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam ity abhyupagamyate, tato 'bhakṣaṇaṃ śrutyā tavyo vidadhāti, nañ bhakṣayati viśeṣaṇam. tadvyāpārāc ca kartavyatayā nañ na saṃbadhyate{*5/347*}. atha nañarthaḥ kartavyaḥ, tato vākyena nidhānam, bhakṣayatiś ca nañviśeṣaṇam, śrutiś ca vākyād balīyasī. tasmād abhakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam iti gamyate, abhakṣaṇaṃ ca bhakṣaṇābhāvaḥ, na tasya kartavyatāsti. tasmād yas tatra mānaso vyāpāraḥ, sa ihopadiśyate, yenopāyena nañviśiṣṭaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ bhavati. pūrvaṃ nañbhakṣayatyoḥ saṃbandhaḥ, tato vidhānam. yathā, nodyantam ādityam īkṣetetyevamādiṣu prajāpativrateṣu kurvataḥ phalam, akurvato na phalaṃ na doṣaḥ, evam ihāpi, vibhaktatvād akarmaṇām, nātra karma pratiṣidhyate, akarmamātram upadiśyate, anyad dhi karma bhakṣaṇaṃ pratiṣidhyamānam, anyad akarma mānasaḥ saṃkalpa iti.
children.translated_text:
In prohibitions, because of being non-actions, the [mental] act would [be the referent]; the prohibited things are separate from non-actions. // MS_6,2.19 //
For they teach this: 'One should not eat <s>kalañja</s> (a type of asafoetida); one should not eat garlic; one should not eat onion.' There a doubt [arises]: should a person desiring the fruit not eat things of this kind, while one without desire may eat; or should they necessarily be avoided? What is the prima facie view? One desiring the fruit should not eat, while there is no restriction for one without desire. Why? For what is said is a restriction — 'this should not be eaten.' When said thus, two [interpretations] arise: [645] either 'non-eating is to be done,' or 'eating is not to be done.' If it is accepted that 'non-eating qualified by the negative particle is to be done,' then the negative particle qualifies eating, and the [Vedic] word enjoins [that qualified thing]. And because of the operation [of the injunctive], the negative particle is not connected with 'to be done.' But if the meaning of the negative particle is what is to be done, then the sentence establishes [this], and 'eating' is qualified by the negative; and the [Vedic] word is stronger than the sentence. Therefore it is understood that 'non-eating is to be done.' And non-eating is the absence of eating — there is no 'to-be-done-ness' for it. Therefore what is taught here is the mental effort involved — the means by which non-eating qualified by the negative particle comes about. First the connection between the negative and 'eating' [is established], then the injunction [operates]. Just as in 'one should not look at the rising sun' — in such observances of <s>Prajāpati</s>, there is a fruit for one who performs [them]; for one who does not perform, there is no fruit and no fault. Similarly here too — because of [the prohibited things] being separate from non-actions. No action is being prohibited here; mere non-action is being taught. For the action 'eating' that would be prohibited is one thing, while the non-action — the mental resolution — is another.

children.text: śāstrāṇāṃ tv arthavattvena puruṣārtho vidhīyate tayor asamavāyitvāt tādarthye vidhyatikramaḥ//6.2.20//
children.translated_text: But because of the meaningfulness of the <s>śāstras</s>, a human purpose is enjoined; because of the non-inherent connection of the two, when [one is] for that purpose, there is a transgression of the injunction. // MS_6,2.20 //

children.text:
upavarṇanāparihāras tāvad ucyate, yuktaṃ yat prajāpativrateṣu śāstrāṇām arthavattvena puruṣārtho vidhīyate. tatra niyamaḥ kartavyatayopadiśyate, yaś ca kartavyaḥ, sa kalyāṇodayaḥ, yo na kartavyaḥ sa pāpodayaḥ. kathaṃ punaḥ prajāpativrateṣu niyamaḥ kartavyatayā codyata iti. ucyate, tasya vratam iti prakṛtya prajāpativratāni samāmnātāni, vratam iti ca mānasaṃ karmocyate. idaṃ na kariṣyāmīti yaḥ saṃkalpaḥ. katamat tad vratam? nodyantam ādityam īkṣeteti, yathā tadīkṣaṇaṃ na bhavati, tathā mānaso vyāpāraḥ kartavyaḥ, tasya ca pālanam. tatra tasmāt puruṣārtho 'stīty avagantavyam. tatra caitāny eva [646]{*5/348*} prakṛtyocyate, etāvatā hainasāyukto bhavatīti, etāvatā kṛtenāyukta enasā bhavatīti{*5/349*}.
atheha tayor asamavāyitvam, iha kriyā pratiṣidhyate, nākriyopadiśyate, na hi kalañjaṃ bhakṣayan pratiṣedhāvidhiṃ nātikrāmati, iha punar ādityaṃ paśyan nātikrāmati vidhim, na hi tasya darśanaṃ pratiṣiddham. niyamas tatropadiṣṭaḥ, yas taṃ niyamaṃ karoti, sa phalena saṃbadhyate, iha tu pratiṣidhyate kalañjādi. katham avagamyate? nātra tasya, vratam iti prakṛtya vacanam asti. na ca, na bhakṣayitavyam ity asya mānaso vyāpāro 'rthaḥ, bhakṣayitavyam iti ca bhakṣaṇaṃ kartavyaṃ śabdenocyate, neti tat pratiṣidhyate śrutyaiva. evaṃ prasiddho 'rtho 'nugṛhīto bhavati, itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt, śrutilakṣaṇāviśaye ca śrutir nyāyyā na lakṣaṇā. tasmād iha pratiṣedhaḥ.
ucyate, astu pratiṣiddhaṃ{*5/350*} nāma, doṣo 'tra na śrūyate. tasmāt pratiṣiddham apy anuṣṭhātavyam iti. kalpayiṣyata iti cet, na, pramāṇābhāvāt. arthāpattiḥ pramāṇam, upadeśavaiyarthaprasaṅgād{*5/351*} iti yady ucyeta. naitad evam, vyartho 'pi hy upadeśo 'jñānāt saṃbhavati. tasmān na kalpyo doṣa ity. ucyate, satyaṃ na kalpanīyaḥ, kiṃ tu kḷpta eva. katham? anantaram evainaṃ śiṣṭā varjayeyuḥ, patitaḥ karmaphalebhya iti vadantaḥ, mahāṃś caiṣa doṣaḥ, yac chiṣṭā varjayanti. tasmān niyogataḥ kalañjādi na bhakṣayitavyam iti, yathā, na sarpāyāṅguliṃ dadyāt, tatra doṣadarśanān niyogato na sarpāyāṅgulir dīyate, kaṇṭako vā na pādenādhiṣṭhīyate, evam idam apīti.
children.translated_text:
First, the elaboration of the non-refutation is stated. It is proper that in the observances of <s>Prajāpati</s>, a human purpose is enjoined through the meaningfulness of the <s>śāstras</s>. There, a restriction is taught as something to be done; and what is to be done leads to good fortune, while what is not to be done leads to sin. But how is a restriction enjoined as something to be done in the observances of <s>Prajāpati</s>? We reply: 'His observance' — having introduced [this], the <s>Prajāpati</s>-observances are recorded. And 'observance' refers to a mental act — the resolution 'I shall not do this.' What is that observance? 'One should not look at the rising sun' — the mental effort should be made such that that seeing does not occur, and its maintenance. There, it should be understood that a human purpose exists. And there, these very [observances] [646] are stated with reference to the archetype — 'by this much sin is he touched'; 'by doing this much, he becomes free of sin.'
But here, there is a dissimilarity between the two. Here, an action is being prohibited — non-action is not being taught. For one who eats <s>kalañja</s> does not transgress the non-injunction of the prohibition [i.e., the text saying 'one should not eat']. But there, one seeing the sun does not transgress the injunction [of the observance] — for his seeing is not prohibited. There, a restriction is taught; one who performs that restriction is connected with the fruit. But here, <s>kalañja</s> and the like are being prohibited. How is this understood? Because here there is no statement 'his observance' as an introduction. And the meaning of 'it should not be eaten' is not a mental effort — 'it should be eaten' states that eating is to be done by the word, and the negative prohibits that by the [Vedic] word itself. Thus the well-known meaning is supported; otherwise there would be figurative usage, and in a domain where both [Vedic] word and figurative usage [are possible], the [Vedic] word is proper, not figurative usage. Therefore here there is a prohibition.
We reply: granted it is prohibited; but no fault is heard here. Therefore, even though prohibited, it might be performed. If it is said [a fault] will be posited — no, because of the absence of a valid means of knowledge. If it is said that implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>) is the valid means — [reasoning that] otherwise the teaching would be purposeless — this is not so, for even a purposeless teaching occurs due to ignorance. Therefore no fault should be posited. We reply: true, it need not be posited, but it is already established. How? The learned would immediately shun him — saying 'he is fallen from the fruits of ritual actions.' And this is a great fault — that the learned shun him. Therefore <s>kalañja</s> and the like must necessarily not be eaten — just as 'one should not put one's finger into a snake's [mouth]': there, from seeing the fault, one necessarily does not put one's finger into a snake's [mouth], or one does not step on a thorn with one's foot. Similarly here.

children.text: tasmiṃs tu śiṣyamāṇāni jananena pravarteran//6.2.21//
children.translated_text: But in that [case], what is being taught would operate through birth. // MS_6,2.21 //

children.text: iha smārtāḥ padārthā udāharaṇam, pratyupasthitaniyamāś cācārāḥ, gurur anugantavyo 'bhivādayitavyaś ca, vṛddhavayāḥ pratyuttheyaḥ saṃmantavyaś ceti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ jātamātrāṇām ime padārthā utopanītānām iti. kiṃ prāptam? aviśeṣopadeśāt jātamātrāṇām. kutaḥ? puruṣe te śiṣyante, jātamātraś ca puruṣo bhavati. tasmāj jātamātrāṇām ime padārthāḥ, ity evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ,
children.translated_text: Here, items from <s>Smṛti</s> (traditional law) are the example — and customary practices with established restrictions: 'the teacher should be followed and greeted'; 'an elder should be offered a seat and respected.' There a doubt [arises]: do these items [apply] from the moment of birth, or from the time of <s>upanayana</s> (initiation)? What is the prima facie view? From the moment of birth, because of the teaching being without distinction. Why? They are taught with reference to the person, and one becomes a person from the moment of birth. Therefore these items [apply] from the moment of birth. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say:

children.text: api vā vedatulyatvād upāyena pravarteran//6.2.22//
children.translated_text: Or rather, they would operate through a means [i.e., initiation], because of being equal to the <s>Veda</s>. // MS_6,2.22 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. upāyena pravarteran upanayanena saha pravarteran{*5/353*}, vedatulyatvāt. vedatulyā hi smṛtiḥ, vaidikā eva padārthāḥ smaryanta ity uktam{*5/354*}. vaidikāś ca padārthā upanayanottarakāle samāmnātāḥ, smārtāś caite vaidikā eva, tasmād upanayanottarakālā eta iti.
children.translated_text: The words <s>api vā</s> ('or rather') mark a reversal of position. They would operate through a means — they would operate together with initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) — because of being equal to the <s>Veda</s>. For <s>Smṛti</s> is equal to the <s>Veda</s>; it has been stated that [what is] remembered [in Smṛti] are indeed Vedic items. And Vedic items are recorded for the time after initiation; and these <s>smārta</s> (traditional) [items] are indeed Vedic. Therefore they belong to the time after initiation.

children.text: abhyāso 'karmaśeṣatvāt puruṣārtho vidhīyate//6.2.23//
children.translated_text: Repetition [of rituals], because of not being a remainder of a [single] ritual action, is enjoined as a human purpose. // MS_6,2.23 //

children.text: idam āmnanati, yāvājjīvam agnihotraṃ juhoti, yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti puruṣārtho 'yaṃ yāgo vidhīyate{*5/356*}, nāyam abhyāsaḥ karmaśeṣa ity uktam. ihedānīṃ saṃdihyate, kiṃ sātatyena hotavyam, uta na sātatyeneti{*5/357*}. kiṃ prāptam? puruṣaṃ pratyupadiṣṭatvāt sātatyena, ayaṃ puruṣaḥ iti sātatyenānuṣṭhātavyam. nanu pradoṣam agnihotraṃ hotavyam, vyuṣṭāyāṃ prātar iti śrūyate, paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyena{*5/358*} yajeta, amāvāsyāyām amāvāsyayena{*5/359*} yajeteti. naiṣa sarvāṅgopasaṃhāreṇa prayogaḥ. ataḥ kālamātre hīne na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: They state: 'Lifelong one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>; lifelong one sacrifices with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' This sacrifice enjoined for the person's purpose is not a repetition that is a remainder of a ritual act — this has been stated. Here now the doubt [arises]: should one offer continuously, or not continuously? What is the prima facie view? Continuously, because of being taught with reference to the person — 'this person' must perform continuously. But it is heard: 'one should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> at dusk, and in the morning after dawn'; 'one should sacrifice on the full-moon day with the <s>Paurṇamāsya</s> [offering], on the new-moon day with the <s>Āmāvāsya</s> [offering].' This is not a performance with the assembly of all subsidiaries. Therefore, when only the time is missing, there is no fault.

children.text: tasminn asaṃbhavann arthāt//6.2.24//
children.translated_text: When [continuous performance] is not possible in that [case], [the restriction is] from the meaning. // MS_6,2.24 //

children.text: naitad asti, yat, juhudhi juhudhīty eva hotavyam iti, yathā śaknoti, tathā juhuyād ity ucyate, na ca sātatyena śakyate, avaśyam anena āhāravihārāḥ kartavyāḥ. tasmād arthāviruddheṣu kāleṣu satataṃ hotavyam{*5/360*} iti.
children.translated_text: This is not [correct] — that one should offer [by repeating] 'offer! offer!' — rather, one should offer as one is able. And continuous [offering] is not possible — one must necessarily take meals and diversions. Therefore one should offer continuously at times not contradicted by the meaning.

children.text:
NOTES:

children.translated_text:

children.text: na kālebhya upadiśyante//6.2.25//
children.translated_text: They are not taught [as being] beyond the [prescribed] times. // MS_6,2.25 //

children.text: na caitad asti, yad uktam, arthāviruddheṣu kaleṣu satataṃ hotavyam iti, kāla eṣaḥ śrūyate, pradoṣam agnihotraṃ hotavyam, vyuṣṭāyāṃ prātar iti. tathā, paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyena{*5/361*} yajeta, amāvāsyāyām amāvāsyayena{*5/362*} yajeteti. tasmān na [649]{*5/363*} sātatyam iti. āha, nanu viguṇasyāpi prayogān na kāla ādaraṇīya iti. atrocyate, na kālo guṇaḥ, nimittaṃ hy etad ity uktam. tasmād anyeṣu kāleṣv avihitatvāt kṛtam apy akṛtaṃ syāt. tasmād āśritakālasya yāvajjīvaṃ prayoga iti.
children.translated_text: And this is not [correct] — what was said, 'one should offer continuously at times not contradicted by the meaning.' A time is heard here: 'The <s>Agnihotra</s> should be offered at dusk; in the morning after dawn.' Likewise: 'One should sacrifice on the full-moon day with the <s>Paurṇamāsya</s>, on the new-moon day with the <s>Āmāvāsya</s>.' Therefore there is no continuity. [649] [The objector] says: but even of a deficient [performance], the performance [is valid]; therefore the time should not be regarded. To this we reply: the time is not a subsidiary; for it has been stated that this is an occasion (<s>nimitta</s>). Therefore, when performed at other times, even what is done would be as if undone, because of not being enjoined [for those times]. Therefore the lifelong performance is [bound] to the prescribed times.

children.text: darśanāt kālaliṅgānāṃ kālavidhānam//6.2.26//
children.translated_text: Because of seeing indicatory marks regarding time, the time is what is prescribed. // MS_6,2.26 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca bhavati, apa vā eṣa svargāl lokāc chidyate yo darśapūrṇamāsayājī san paurṇamāsīm amāvasyāṃ vātipātayed iti{*5/364*}. yadi sarvasmin kāle homaḥ, tadā kasyātipattiḥ syāt. tasmād api na satatam abhyāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: And there is an indicatory mark: 'He who, being one who sacrifices with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, lets pass the full-moon or new-moon day — he is indeed cut off from the heavenly world.' If the offering were at all times, then what would there be to let pass? Therefore too, the repetition is not continuous.

NOTES:
[{5/364: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.5.4}]

children.text: teṣām autpattikatvād āgamena pravarteta//6.2.27//
children.translated_text: Because of [these observances] being innate [to the Vedic system], they would operate through tradition (<s>āgama</s>). // MS_6,2.27 //

children.text:
pradoṣe{*5/365*} agnihotraṃ hotavyam, vyuṣṭāyāṃ prātar iti, tathā, paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyena{*5/366*} yajeta, amāvāsyāyām āmāvāsyayena{*5/367*} yajeteti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ sakṛt pradoṣa hotavyam, uta pradoṣe pradoṣa iti, tathā sakṛd vyuṣṭāyāṃ prātaḥ, uta vyuṣṭāyāṃ vyuṣṭāyām iti, tathā kiṃ sakṛt paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā, utāgata āgate kāla iti. kiṃ prāptam? sakṛt kṛtvā kṛtārthaḥ śabdaḥ, na niyamaḥ paunaḥpunye.
ity evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, āgamena pravarteta, āgata āgate kāle prayogaḥ kartavya iti. kutaḥ? teṣām autpattikatvāt, utpadyamānaṃ karma kālasaṃyuktam evotpadyate, tad uktam, nimittārthāḥ [650]{*5/368*} kālaśrutaya iti, nimitte ca saṃprāpte naimittiko 'rthaḥ kartavyo bhavati. tasmād āgata āgate kāle prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ.
children.translated_text:
'The <s>Agnihotra</s> should be offered at nightfall; in the morning, at dawn.' Likewise, 'On the full-moon day one should sacrifice with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> [offering]; on the new-moon day one should sacrifice with the <s>Āmāvāsyā</s> [offering].' There a doubt [arises]: should one offer at nightfall once only, or at each nightfall? Likewise, at dawn once only, or at each dawn? Likewise, once only on the full-moon or new-moon day, or each time the time arrives? What is the prima facie view? Having performed once, the word has fulfilled its purpose; there is no restriction regarding repetition.
Given this prima facie view, we say: one should continue by recurrence — the performance should be done each time the time arrives. Why? Because of their being origination-based (<s>autpattika</s>) — a ritual action, as it arises, arises connected with a time. As it has been stated: 'The hearings of time are for the purpose of the occasion.' And when the occasion has arrived, the occasional purpose must be fulfilled. Therefore the performance should be done each time the time arrives.

children.text: tathā hi liṅgadarśanam//6.2.28//
children.translated_text: For thus there is observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_6,2.28 //

children.text: apa vā eṣa svargāl lokāc chidyate yo darśapūrṇamāsayājī san paurṇamāsīm amāvāsyāṃ vātipātayed iti{*5/369*}, āgata āgate kāle prayogaṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: 'He who, being a sacrificer of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, should let the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> or the <s>Amāvāsyā</s> pass by — he is indeed cut off from the heavenly world' — this shows the performance at each arrival of the time.

NOTES:
[{5/369: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.5.4}]

children.text: tathāntaḥkratuprayuktāni//6.2.29//
children.translated_text: Likewise, [rites] employed within the sacrifice [are to be repeated]. // MS_6,2.29 //

children.text: bhinne juhoti, skanne juhotīti darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ, sakṛd bhinne skanne ca hutvā kṛtārthaḥ, uta bhinne bhinne, skanne skanne ceti. tatrādhikaraṇātideśaḥ, yaḥ pūrvatra{*5/370*} pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, sa iha pūrvaḥ{*5/371*}, ya uttaraḥ sa ihottara iti. sakṛt kṛtvā kṛtārtha iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, nimittatvāt punaḥ prayoga ity{*5/372*} uttaraḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: 'When [the cake] is broken, he offers; when [the milk] is spilled, he offers.' There a doubt [arises]: having offered once when [the cake is] broken or [the milk is] spilled, is one's purpose fulfilled, or [should one offer] each time it breaks, each time it spills? Here there is a transfer of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic): whichever is the prima facie view in the previous [topic], that is the prima facie view here; whichever is the conclusive view, that is the conclusive view here. 'Having performed once, the purpose is fulfilled' is the prima facie view; 'because of being an occasion, there is repeated performance' is the conclusive view.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{5/370: E2 om. pūrvatra}*
*{5/371: E2: pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ}*
*{5/372: E2: nimittatvād āgata āgate kāla ity}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{5/370: E2 omits <s>pūrvatra</s>}]
[{5/371: E2: <s>pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ</s>}]
[{5/372: E2: <s>nimittatvād āgata āgate kāla ity</s>}]

children.text: ācārād gṛhyamāṇeṣu tathā syāt puruṣārthatvāt//6.2.30//
children.translated_text: In [rites] grasped from custom, it should be likewise, because of [their] being for the person's purpose. // MS_6,2.30 //

children.text: gurur anugantavyo 'bhivādayitavyaś ca, vṛddhavayāḥ pratyuttheyaḥ saṃmantavyaś ceti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim āgata āgate gurau, vṛddhavayasi ca, yad uktam, tat kartavyam, uta sakṛt kṛte kṛtārtheti. ācārād gṛhyamāṇeṣu tathā syāt puruṣārthatvād ity adhikaraṇātideśaḥ. tatra yaḥ pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, sa iha pūrvaḥ{*5/373*}, ya uttaraḥ sa uttaraḥ, sakṛt kṛtvā kṛtārtha iti pūrvaḥ [651]{*5/374*} pakṣaḥ, nimittatvāt punaḥ prayoga ity uttaraḥ.
children.translated_text: 'The teacher should be followed and saluted; an elder should be risen for and honored.' There a doubt [arises]: should what is stated be done each time a teacher or elder arrives, or is the purpose fulfilled once performed? 'In [rites] grasped from custom, it should be likewise, because of [their] being for the person's purpose' — this is a transfer of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s>. The prima facie view here is the same as the prima facie view there; the conclusive view is the same as the conclusive view there. 'Having performed once, the purpose is fulfilled' is the prima facie view; 'because of being an occasion, there is repeated performance' is the conclusive view.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu somavidyāprajam ṛṇavakyena saṃyogāt//6.2.31//
children.translated_text: For the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, Vedic knowledge, and progeny [are obligatory], because of the connection with the debt-statement. // MS_6,2.31 //

children.text:
idaṃ śrūyate, somena yajeta{*5/375*}, garbhāṣṭameṣu brāhmaṇam upanayīta, prajām utpādayed iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ nityāny etāny utānityānīti. kiṃ prāptam? kāmasaṃyogād anityāni.
iti prāpta ucyate, brāhmaṇādīnāṃ somādīni nityānīti. kutaḥ? ṛṇavākyena hi saṃyogo bhavati, jāyamāno ha vai brāhmaṇas tribhir ṛṇavā jāyate, yajñena devebhyo brahmacaryeṇa ṛṣibhyaḥ{*5/376*} prajayā pitṛbhya iti, sa vai tarhy anṛṇo yadā yajvā brahmacārī prajāvān iti{*5/377*}, ṛṇasaṃstavo 'vaśyakartavyānāṃ bhavati, tasmān nityānīti.
nanu liṅgam asādhakam, nyāya ucyatām, yasyaitad dyotakam iti. ucyate, akāmasaṃyuktāny eṣāṃ pṛthag vākyāni bhavanti, vasante vasante jyotiṣā yajeta, yāvajjīvam agnihotraṃ juhoti, yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta. tathā, vidyām adhīyīta. tathā, prajā utpādayitavyeti. evaṃ nityatāyāḥ prāptāyā idaṃ liṅgaṃ bhavatīti.
children.translated_text:
This is heard: 'He should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>'; 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be invested with the sacred thread in the eighth year from conception'; 'One should beget progeny.' There a doubt [arises]: are these obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) or non-obligatory (<s>anitya</s>)? What is the prima facie view? Because of connection with desire, they are non-obligatory.
Given this prima facie view, we say: for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other two, <s>Soma</s> and the like are obligatory. Why? Because of the connection with the debt-statement: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, being born, is born with three debts — with sacrifice to the gods, with Vedic studentship to the seers, with progeny to the ancestors. He is indeed free from debt when he has sacrificed, practiced studentship, and begotten offspring.' The praise of the debt is [directed at] what must necessarily be done; therefore these are obligatory.
[The objector says:] but an indicatory mark is not probative; state the principle, of which this [mark] is the illustrator. We reply: the separate sentences of these [duties] are without connection to desire: 'In each spring he should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>'; 'As long as one lives, one should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>'; 'As long as one lives, one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' Likewise, 'One should study the <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge).' Likewise, 'Progeny should be begotten.' When obligatoriness has thus been obtained, this serves as the indicatory mark.

children.text:
atha vā, ayam anyo 'rthaḥ, brāhmaṇasya tu somavidyāprajam ṛṇavākyena saṃyogāt, somādayo niyatāḥ kiṃ brāhmaṇasyaiva, [652]{*5/378*} rājanyavaiśyayor aniyatāḥ, uta sarveṣāṃ niyatā iti. kiṃ prāptam? brāhmaṇasyaiva niyatā netarayor iti. kutaḥ? evaṃ śrūyate, jāyamāno ha vai brāhmaṇa iti, brāhmaṇasya niyamo dṛśyate, netarayoḥ, brāhmaṇasaṃkīrtanāt. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, sarveṣāṃ niyamaḥ. kutaḥ? aviśeṣeṇa niyamavidhānaṃ yat, tad akāmasaṃyuktaṃ vacanaṃ niyāmakam, tad aviśiṣṭaṃ sarveṣām, tasmāt sarveṣāṃ niyama iti.
nanu jāyamāno ha vai brāhmaṇa iti brāhmaṇasya saṃkīrtanam. ucyate, bhavaty asmin vacane brāhmaṇasaṃkīrtanam, na tv{*5/379*} etan{*5/380*} niyamasya vidhāyakam, etair akāmasaṃyuktair vacanair vihitabhya niyamasyānuvādo 'yam avadānastutyarthaḥ, tasmān nātra brāhmaṇasaṃkīrtanena rājanyasya vaiśyasya vāniyamo vijñāyate. brāhmaṇagrahaṇaṃ tu pradarśanārtham, jāyamāno{*5/381*} brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyo veti{*5/382*}, tathā jāyamāno jātaś ceti.
children.translated_text:
Alternatively, this is another meaning: for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, Vedic knowledge, and progeny [are obligatory] because of the connection with the debt-statement — are <s>Soma</s> and the like obligatory for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> alone, while non-obligatory for the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s>? Or are they obligatory for all? What is the prima facie view? Obligatory for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> alone, not for the other two. Why? Thus it is heard: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, being born' — the restriction is seen for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, not for the other two, because of the mention of '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' Given this prima facie view, we say: the obligation is for all. Why? Because the injunction of obligation that is without distinction — the statement without connection to desire is what creates the obligation — that is undistinguished for all. Therefore the obligation is for all.
[The objector says:] but 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, being born' mentions the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. We reply: in this statement there is indeed a mention of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, but this is not what enjoins the obligation. This is a restatement — for the purpose of the praise of the payment-of-debt — of the obligation that has been enjoined by those statements without connection to desire. Therefore the mention of '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' here does not lead to the understanding that the <s>Kṣatriya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s> has no obligation. The mention of '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' is for the purpose of illustration — 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or a <s>Vaiśya</s>, being born.' Likewise, 'being born' and 'after birth' [mean the same].

children.text: sarvaśaktau pravṛttiḥ syāt tathābhūtopadeśāt//6.3.1//
children.translated_text: The undertaking should be when there is full capability, because of the instruction concerning one who is in that condition. // MS_6,3.1 //

children.text:
bahvṛcabrahmaṇe śrūyate, yāvajjīvam agnihotraṃ juhoti, yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti, nityam agnihotram, nityau ca darśapūrṇamāsau. tatra yad etat kāmaśravaṇād anyad akāmaśravaṇaṃ{*5/384*} dvitīyam, tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ yaḥ kārtsnyena vidhim upasaṃhartuṃ śaknoti, tasyaivādhikāraḥ, uta viguṇam api tat prayoktavyam iti. ekādaśe{*5/385*} kāmasaṃyukte prathame śravaṇe cintayiṣyate sāṅge, iha nitye śravaṇe dvitīya iti.
kiṃ prāptam? sarvaśaktau pravṛttiḥ syāt tathābhūtopadeśāt, yaḥ kārtsnyena vidhim upasaṃhartuṃ śaknoti, sa evānutiṣṭhet, tathābhūtopadeśāt, yathābhūtaṃ hi tat kāmasaṃyuktaṃ śrutam, tathābhūtam eva nityam apy upadiśyate. tasmāt sarvāṅgopahāreṇa prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ. darśapūrṇamāsaśabdaś ca sāṅgasyaiva vācakaḥ. katham? paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ ca sāṅgaṃ vidhīyate. yac ca paurṇamāsyāṃ vihitam, [654]{*5/386*} sā ca paurṇamāsī. yad amāvāsyāyāṃ vihitam, sā cāmāvāsyeti, sāṅgam amāvāsyāyāṃ vihitam, paurṇamāsyāṃ ca, tasmāt sāṅgaṃ darśapūrṇamāsaśabdenocyata iti jaiminir manyate sma{*5/387*}.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Bahvṛca</s> (Ṛgvedic) <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> it is heard: 'As long as one lives, one should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>; as long as one lives, one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — the <s>Agnihotra</s> is obligatory, and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> too is obligatory. There, in addition to the first hearing with desire, there is this second hearing without desire. Regarding it, a doubt [arises]: is the eligibility only for one who is capable of gathering the complete injunction [with all subsidiaries], or should it be performed even if deficient? In the eleventh [<s>adhyāya</s>], it will be considered with respect to the first hearing with desire, together with its subsidiaries; here [we consider] the second, obligatory hearing.
What is the prima facie view? The undertaking should be when there is full capability, because of the instruction concerning one who is in that condition. Only one who is capable of gathering the injunction in its entirety should undertake [the rite] — because of the instruction concerning one in that condition. For just as the [rite] is heard with desire in a particular condition [i.e., with all subsidiaries], so too the obligatory [rite] is instructed in the same condition. Therefore the performance should be done with the full complement of subsidiaries. And the word <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> designates [the rite] together with its subsidiaries. How? On the full-moon day and new-moon day, [the rite] together with its subsidiaries is enjoined. What is enjoined on the full-moon day — that is the <s>Pūrṇamāsī</s>. What is enjoined on the new-moon day — that is the <s>Amāvāsyā</s>. [The rite] together with subsidiaries is enjoined on the new-moon day and on the full-moon day. Therefore [the rite] together with subsidiaries is denoted by the word <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — so <s>Jaimini</s> holds.
