children.text: api vāpy ekadeśe syāt pradhāne hy arthanivṛttir guṇamātram itarat tadarthatvāt//6.3.2//
children.translated_text: Or rather, even with a partial [complement], there should be performance, for the purpose is fulfilled by the principal alone; the rest is merely a subsidiary, because of being for that [principal's] purpose. // MS_6,3.2 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. apy ekadeśe 'ṅgānāṃ syād eva prayogaḥ, yataḥ sāṅgasyāpy anaṅgasyāpi prayujyamānasya pradhānād evāyam artho niṣpadyate, guṇamātraṃ sarvāṅgaprayogeṇa bhavati. ko guṇaḥ? sāṅgāt svargābhinirvṛttiḥ, pradhānamātrād idam anyat phalam. tasmāt svargaprāptyarthaṃ saṃpūrṇāṅgaṃ kariṣyāmīty ārabdham. yadi kānicid aṅgāni na śaknoti kartum, tathāpy asmād ekadeśāṅgaguṇayuktāt pradhānāt phalaṃ bhaviṣyati. tasmāt pradhānamātrasya prayogam āha, nāṅgānām. darśapūrṇamāśabdako 'gnihotraśabdakaś ca pradhānapadārtho 'nyāny aṅgāni tadarthānīti.
children.translated_text: The phrase 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. Even with a partial [complement] of subsidiaries, there should indeed be performance, since the purpose is fulfilled by the principal alone, whether the [rite] is performed with full subsidiaries or without subsidiaries. The full-subsidiary performance produces only a subsidiary [additional] benefit. What is this subsidiary benefit? The accomplishment of heaven from [the rite] with full subsidiaries; from the principal alone, this other fruit [accrues]. Therefore, [thinking] 'I shall perform [the rite] with complete subsidiaries for the purpose of attaining heaven,' one has commenced. If one is unable to perform some subsidiaries, even so, from this principal — endowed with the subsidiary benefit of a partial complement — there will be a fruit. Therefore he states the performance of the principal alone, not of the subsidiaries. The item denoted by the word <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> or <s>Agnihotra</s> is the principal; the other [elements] are subsidiaries for that purpose.

children.text: tadakarmaṇi ca doṣas tasmāt tato viśeṣaḥ syāt pradhānenābhisaṃbandhāt//6.3.3//
children.translated_text: And there is a fault in not performing that [principal]; therefore [the obligatory rite] is distinguished from that [optional rite] because of connection with the principal. // MS_6,3.3 //

children.text: pradhānātikrame doṣaḥ śrūyate, apa vā eṣa svargāl lokāc chidyate yo darśapūrṇamāsayājī san paurṇamāsīm amāvāsyāṃ vātipātayed iti{*5/388*} pradhānātikrame doṣaṃ bruvaṃs tasya nityatāṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: A fault is heard in the omission of the principal: 'He who, being a sacrificer of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, should let the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> or the <s>Amāvāsyā</s> pass by — he is indeed cut off from the heavenly world.' By stating the fault in the omission of the principal, it shows its obligatoriness.

NOTES:
[{5/388: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.5.4}]

children.text: karmābhedaṃ tu jaiminiḥ prayogavacanaikatvāt sarveṣām upadeśaḥ syād iti//6.3.4//
children.translated_text: But <s>Jaimini</s> [holds that] there is no distinction in the ritual action, and because of the unity of the statement about performance, the instruction should be for all [elements]. // MS_6,3.4 //

children.text: yad uktam, nāsti bhedaḥ, imāny aṅgāni, imāni pradhānāni [655]{*5/389*} iti, prayogavacanaikatvād iti jaiminir āha sma. sarveṣām upadeśakaḥ, paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā yajeta, amāvāsyāyām amāvāsyayā yajeteti.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'there is no distinction: these are subsidiaries, these are principals' — <s>Jaimini</s> said this because of the unity of the statement about performance. The instruction is for all: 'On the full-moon day one should sacrifice with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>; on the new-moon day one should sacrifice with the <s>Amāvāsyā</s>.'

children.text: arthasya vyapavargitvād ekasyāpi prayoge syād yathā kratvantareṣu//6.3.5//
children.translated_text: Because the purpose is fulfilled upon [completion of] the ritual action, even with the performance of a single [subsidiary], there should be [fruit] — as in other sacrifices. // MS_6,3.5 //

children.text:
ekāṅgaprayoge 'pi syād viguṇād api phalam ity arthaḥ. kutaḥ? arthasya vyapavargitvāt. vyapavṛktam aṅgebhyaḥ pradhānam, agnihotrasaṃjñakād darśapūrṇamāsasaṃjñakāc ca phalam iha bhavati. tad dhi kartavyatayopadiśyate. yat paurṇamāsyām upadiṣṭam, sā paurṇamāsī, yad amāvāsyāyāṃ sāmāvāsyā, yad āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavatīti{*5/390*}. tasmād agnaye puroḍāśo 'gnīṣomābhyāṃ ca, ājyaṃ cāgnīṣomādibhyaḥ paurṇamāsyām. āgneyasāṃnyāyyādīnām amāvāsyāyām{*5/391*}.
yad uktam, paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā yajeta, amāvāsyāyām amāvāsyayā yajeteti sāṅgasya vidhānāt sāṅgaṃ darśapūrṇamāsaśabdenābhidhīyata iti. naitad evam, siddhe hi darśārthe pūrṇamāsārthe ca sāṅgaṃ phale vidhīyate. tasmān na sāṅgam agnihotrapadavācyaṃ darśapūrṇamāsapadavācyaṃ ca{*5/392*}. yac cāgnihotraṃ tad iha codyate kartavyatayā, yau ca darśapūrṇamāsau. tasmād viguṇam api kartavyam evāgnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsau ca. yathā kratvantareṣu prakṛtivikṛtiṣu parasya dharmāḥ parasya na bhavanti, evaṃ na kāmasaṃyuktasya dharmā nityasya bhavitum arhanti.
children.translated_text:
Even with the performance of a single subsidiary, there should be a fruit from the deficient [rite] as well — this is the meaning. Why? Because of the purpose being fulfilled upon [completion of] the ritual action. The principal is discharged from [i.e., independent of] the subsidiaries. The fruit here comes from what is designated by the name <s>Agnihotra</s> or <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. For that is what is instructed as to be done. What is enjoined on the full-moon day is the <s>Pūrṇamāsī</s>; what [is enjoined] on the new-moon day is the <s>Amāvāsyā</s>. 'The <s>Āgneya</s> eight-potsherd [cake] on the new-moon and full-moon days remains firm.' Therefore the <s>puroḍāśa</s> to <s>Agni</s> and to <s>Agni-Soma</s>, and the <s>ājya</s> to <s>Agni-Soma</s> and the others [are offered] on the full-moon day. The <s>Āgneya</s>, the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>, and the like [are offered] on the new-moon day.
As to what was said — 'On the full-moon day one should sacrifice with the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>; on the new-moon day one should sacrifice with the <s>Amāvāsyā</s>' — [and that] because of the injunction of [the rite] with subsidiaries, [the rite] with subsidiaries is denoted by the word <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — this is not so. For the <s>Darśa</s> purpose and the <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> purpose, being [already] established, have the fruit enjoined with subsidiaries. Therefore it is not the case that [the rite] with subsidiaries is denoted by the word <s>Agnihotra</s> or <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. What is enjoined as to be done is the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [as principals]. Therefore even deficient [rites] must be performed — the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Just as in other sacrifices, in archetype-and-modification [relationships], the rules of one do not belong to the other — so the rules of the one connected with desire should not belong to the obligatory one.

NOTES:
[{5/390: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.3.3}]
[{5/391: E2: <s>amāvāsyayā</s>}]
[{5/392: E2 omits <s>ca</s>}]

children.text: vidhyaparādhe ca darśanāt samāpteḥ//6.3.6//
children.translated_text: And in the transgression of the injunction, because of the observation [of a penalty], until completion. // MS_6,3.6 //

children.text: vidhyaparādheṣu ca samāptiṃ darśayati, tad eva yādṛk{*5/393*} tādṛg hotavyam iti{*5/394*} viguṇasya samāptiṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: And it shows the completion [of the rite] even in cases of procedural error: 'That very [offering], of whatever kind it may be, should be offered' — it shows the completion of a deficient [rite].

children.text: prāyaścittavidhānāc ca//6.3.7//
children.translated_text: And because of the prescription of expiatory rites (<s>prāyaścitta</s>). // MS_6,3.7 //

children.text: vidhyaparādhe ca prāyaścittāni vidhīyante, nimitte karmāṅgabhūtāni, yathā bhinne juhotīti. viguṇe niṣphale sati kasyāṅgabhūtaiḥ prayojanaṃ syāt? tasmāt viguṇānām api prayogaḥ kartavya iti.
children.translated_text: And in cases of procedural error, expiatory rites are prescribed — occasioned [by the error], they are subsidiaries of the ritual act, as in 'when [the vessel] is broken, he offers [an oblation].' If the deficient [rite] were fruitless, what purpose would subsidiaries serve? Therefore, even deficient [rites] should be performed.

children.text: kāmyeṣu caivam arthitvāt//6.3.8//
children.translated_text: And likewise in optional (<s>kāmya</s>) [rites], because of [the performer's] being desirous. // MS_6,3.8 //

children.text: aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet prajākāmaḥ{*5/396*}, sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvaped brahmavarcaskāmaḥ{*5/397*}, vaiśvadevīṃ sāṃgrāhāyaṇīṃ{*5/398*} nirvaped grāmakāma{*5/399*} ityevamādiṣu saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ viguṇam api phalavat, utāviguṇam eva phalavad iti. kiṃ prāptam? kāmyeṣu caivaṃ syāt, viguṇam api phalavad iti. kutaḥ? arthitvāt. yadi viguṇam api phalavad evam arthimātram adhikṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati, anyathā sāmānyaśabdo 'ntareṇa viśeṣam, viśeṣe 'vasthāpito bhaviṣyati. asamarthatvān nādhikriyata iti cet. sāṅgaṃ na samarthaḥ kartum, pradhānamātraṃ tu śaknoti, pradhānamātre 'dhikariṣyati.
children.translated_text: 'One desiring offspring should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] to <s>Indrāgni</s>'; 'One desiring spiritual luster should offer a <s>caru</s> (porridge) to <s>Sūrya</s>'; 'One desiring a village should offer a <s>Vaiśvadevī Sāṃgrāhāyaṇī</s> [oblation]' — in such [cases] a doubt [arises]: is even a deficient [rite] fruitful, or only a non-deficient one? What is the prima facie view? In optional [rites] too, it should be so — even a deficient [rite] is fruitful. Why? Because of [the performer's] being desirous. If even a deficient [rite] is fruitful, then mere desirous persons would be entitled; otherwise, a general word, without a specific [restriction], would be confined to a specific [class]. [The objector says:] because of incapability, he is not entitled. [We reply:] he is not capable of performing [the rite] with its subsidiaries, but he is able [to perform] the principal alone — he would be entitled to the principal alone.

NOTES:
[{5/396: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.2.1.2}]
[{5/397: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.3.2.3}]
[{5/398: E2: <s>sāṃgrahaṇīṃ</s>}]
[{5/399: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.3.9.2}]

children.text: asaṃyogāt tu naivaṃ syād vidheḥ śabdapramāṇatvāt//6.3.9//
children.translated_text: But this should not be so, because of the non-conjunction [with fruit], since the injunction has the [Vedic] word as its authority. // MS_6,3.9 //

children.text: tuśabdāt pakṣo viparivartate. naivaṃ syāt, yad uktaṃ viguṇam api phalavad iti, asaṃyogāt pradhānamātrasya phalena, sāṅgād [657]{*5/400*} dhi phalaṃ śrūyate pradhānāt, na kevalāt. tena yady api kevalam ucyate, tathāpi naivaṃjātīyakaṃ tat kuryāt, na kevalasya phalena saṃyoga iti, śabdapramāṇakaś cāyam artho vidhīyate. śabdaś ca sāṅgāt phalam āheti vakṣyāmaḥ{*5/401*}. tasmān na viguṇaṃ karma kartavyam evaṃjātīyakam iti.
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the view. This should not be so — what was said, that even a deficient [rite] is fruitful — because of the non-conjunction of the principal alone with the fruit. For the fruit is heard [as coming] from the principal together with its subsidiaries, not from [the principal] alone. Therefore, even though the principal alone is stated, one should not perform a rite of this kind [without subsidiaries] — there is no conjunction of the principal alone with the fruit. And this meaning is prescribed with the [Vedic] word as its authority. And we will state that the [Vedic] word says the fruit [comes] from [the rite] together with its subsidiaries. Therefore a deficient ritual act of this kind should not be performed.

children.text: akarmaṇi cāpratyavāyāt//6.3.10//
children.translated_text: And because there is no adverse consequence (<s>pratyavāya</s>) for non-performance. // MS_6,3.10 //

children.text: na cātra pradhānamātrasyākarmaṇi pratyavāya ucyate, yathā darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ. tasmād api na viguṇam evaṃlakṣaṇakaṃ karma prayoktavyam iti.
children.translated_text: And here, for non-performance of the principal alone, no adverse consequence is stated — as [there is] in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Therefore, a deficient ritual act of this kind should not be performed.

children.text: kriyāṇām āśritatvāt dravyāntare vibhāgaḥ syāt//6.3.11//
children.translated_text: Because the ritual actions are dependent [on substances], in [the case of] a different substance, there would be a division [i.e., a different sacrifice]. // MS_6,3.11 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayāgaḥ puroḍāśenoktaḥ, sa ca puroḍāśo vrīhimayaḥ kartavya iti śrūyate. tatraitac cintyate, yadi nīvāramayena puroḍāśena yāgaḥ kriyeta, kiṃ sa eva yāgaḥ syāt, utānya iti. kiṃ prāptam? dravyāntare vibhāgaḥ syāt, anyo yāgaḥ{*5/402*}. kutaḥ? āśritatvāt, āśrayabhedād dhi gamyate viśeṣaḥ. ayam anyo nīvārāśrayo vrīhyāśrayād iti. āśrayabhedas tāvad vispaṣṭa eva, tadbhedād rūpam api bhinnaṃ gamyate. tasmād anyo yāgo dravyāntara iti.
children.translated_text: The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifice is stated [as being performed] with a <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake), and that <s>puroḍāśa</s> is heard as being made of rice (<s>vrīhi</s>). Here the following is considered: if the sacrifice is performed with a <s>puroḍāśa</s> made of <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice), would it be the same sacrifice, or a different one? What is the prima facie view? In [the case of] a different substance, there would be a division — it would be a different sacrifice. Why? Because of [the ritual action's] dependence — for a distinction is understood from a difference in the substratum. 'This one, based on <s>nīvāra</s>, is different from the one based on <s>vrīhi</s>.' The difference of substratum is indeed clear, and from that difference, the form too is understood as different. Therefore the sacrifice is different when the substance is different.

children.text: api vāvyatirekād rūpaśabdāvibhāgāc ca gotvavad aikarmyaṃ syān nāmadheyaṃ ca sattvavat//6.3.12//
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of non-differentiation, and because of the non-division of form and word, there would be unity of ritual action, as with cow-ness [in different cows]; and the designation (<s>nāmadheya</s>) is for the universal, as with beings. // MS_6,3.12 //

children.text:
api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. aikakarmyaṃ syād dravyā[658]{*5/403*}ntare 'pi, yadā kriyā bhavati calanaṃ patanaṃ vā, tadāpi tāvān eva so 'rthaḥ, na ca kaścit tatra vyatirikto viśeṣo hīno vā, no khalv apy anyad eva rūpam, na ca śabdāntaraṃ vācakam.
nanv āśrayabhedo vispaṣṭaḥ. ucyate, bhinnam eva vayam āśrayaṃ pratijānīmahe, na tu tadbhedād āśritasya bhedaḥ, anyatvat. na hi sraji vāsati vā bhinne tadbhedāt puruṣabhedo gamyate. so 'pi tasyātmā bhinna iti cet. naitad evam, viśeṣam upalabhamānair evaṃ śakyaṃ vaktum. na cāsya viśeṣa upalabhyate.
nanv ayam eva viśeṣo yat, eko 'pi{*5/404*} vinaṣṭaḥ, eko 'pi{*5/405*} vartate. na vinaṣṭa iti yad ucyate, tan na, prāg asyopalambhanāt, sattve pramāṇaṃ nāsti, tasmād vinaṣṭaḥ. na ca, pratyabhijñāyate taddravyātiriktaḥ, bhedānupalambhāt. kathaṃ tarhi calatīti pratyaya iti cet. ucyate, deśāntare saṃpratipattidarśanāt, tad deśāntaraṃ gacchad āgacchac ca calatīty ucyate, tatra gantāpi pratyakṣaḥ, deśānatram api, tena gata iti cocyate, āgata iti cocyate. satyam, [659]{*5/406*} vinaṣṭād avinaṣṭo 'nyaḥ, yo 'pi tv asāvanyaḥ, so 'pi yajatiśabdavācya eva, yajatisāmānyaṃ na bhidyate, na ca śabdena nocyate. tasmād yo 'pi nīvārair yāgaṃ kuryāt, tenāpi coditam eva kṛtam, coditaṃ ca kurvata īpsitaṃ bhavati, nāpūrvakṛtam. nāmadheyaṃ ca darśayati, darśa iti vā pūrṇamāsa iti vāsyaiva sāmānyasya, yathā sattveṣu sāmānyasya nāmadheyam{*5/407*}, na vyaktīnām. kiṃ prayojanaṃ cintāyāḥ? uttareṇādhikaraṇenaitad vicāryate.
children.translated_text:
The phrase 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) reverses the view. There would be unity of ritual action even in [the case of] a different substance. When the action is movement or falling, even then the meaning is just that much — there is no distinct particular, whether added or subtracted; nor indeed is there a different form, nor a different word to designate it.
[The objector says:] but the difference of substratum is clear. We reply: we indeed acknowledge the substratum to be different, but from the difference of the substratum, there is no difference of what depends on it, because of [its] being something else [entirely]. For when a garland or garment is different, the difference of the person [wearing them] is not understood from that difference. [The objector says:] but that too is the self of that [person], which is different. Not so — this can be said only by those who perceive a distinction. But no distinction in this [ritual action] is perceived.
[The objector says:] but this itself is the distinction — that one [rite] is destroyed while another [rite] continues. As for saying 'it is destroyed' — that is not so. Before its apprehension [i.e., before the substitute substance is used], there is no evidence for its existence; therefore it is destroyed. And [the substitute rite] is not recognized as different from that [original rite], because of the non-perception of a difference. [The objector asks:] then how is there the cognition 'it moves'? We reply: because of the observation of cognition in another place — that which goes to another place and comes [back] is said to 'move.' There, the traveler too is directly perceived, and the other place too; therefore it is said 'he went' and 'he came.' True, the undestroyed one is different from the destroyed one. But even that other one is expressible by the word '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) — the universal [denoted by] <s>yajati</s> is not divided, nor is it not expressed by the word. Therefore even one who performs the sacrifice with <s>nīvāras</s> has done what was enjoined, and one who does what was enjoined obtains what is desired — he has not done something unprecedented. And the designation (<s>nāmadheya</s>) shows [this] — '<s>Darśa</s>' (new-moon sacrifice) or '<s>Pūrṇamāsa</s>' (full-moon sacrifice) is the designation of this very universal, just as in the case of beings, the designation belongs to the universal, not to individuals. What is the purpose of this inquiry? This is examined in the following topic.

children.text: śrutipramāṇatvāc chiṣṭābhāve nāgamo 'nyasyāśiṣṭatvāt//6.3.13//
children.translated_text: Because the [Vedic] word is the authority, when the prescribed [substance] is absent, there is no introduction of another, because of [the other's] not being prescribed. // MS_6,3.13 //

children.text: agnihotrādīni nityāni karmāṇy udāharaṇam. teṣu śrutadravyāpacāre bhavati saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ pratinidhim upādāya prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ, uta tadantaṃ karmotsraṣṭavyam iti. kiṃ prāptam? śiṣṭasyābhāve nāgamo 'nyasya, tadantam evotsraṣṭavyam. kutaḥ? aśiṣṭatvāt, yad vrīhiyavaguṇakaṃ śrutaṃ phalavat, tan nīvāraguṇakaṃ kriyamāṇam aphalakaṃ bhavati. tasmāt tadantaṃ evotsraṣṭavyam iti.
children.translated_text: Obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) ritual acts such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like serve as the example. Regarding them, when there is a deviation from the heard [i.e., prescribed] substance, a doubt [arises]: should a substitute (<s>pratinidhi</s>) be adopted and the performance carried out, or should the ritual act be abandoned up to [the point of procuring] that [substance]? What is the prima facie view? When the prescribed [substance] is absent, there is no introduction of another — [the rite] should be abandoned up to [the point of procuring] that [substance]. Why? Because of [the substitute's] not being prescribed — what is heard as having the quality of rice and barley [and producing] fruit, when performed with the quality of <s>nīvāra</s>, becomes fruitless. Therefore [the rite] should be abandoned up to [the point of procuring] that [substance].

children.text: kvacid vidhānāc ca//6.3.14//
children.translated_text: And because of prescription in some [cases]. // MS_6,3.14 //

children.text: kvacid vidhīyate, yadi{*5/408*} somaṃ na vindet pūtīkān abhiṣuṇuyād iti. yadi ca pratinidhim upādāya prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ syāt, na vidhīyeta, vidhīyate tu. tasmād yac ca na vidhīyate, na tatra pratinidhir iti.
children.translated_text: In some [cases] it is prescribed: 'If he cannot find <s>Soma</s>, he should press <s>pūtīkas</s> (a substitute plant).' If performance with a substitute were [always] to be done, [this] would not be prescribed — but it is prescribed. Therefore, in cases where it is not prescribed, there is no substitute.

children.text: āgamo vā codanārthāviśeṣāt//6.3.15//
children.translated_text: Or rather, there is the introduction [of a substitute], because of no distinction in the meaning of the injunction. // MS_6,3.15 //

children.text: āgamo vā pratinidheyasya dravyasya. kutaḥ? codanārthāviśeṣāt, yajaticodanācodito hy artho na viśiṣyate vīhibhir nīvārair vā kriyamāṇaḥ, yāgaś cāvaśyakartavyo nityeṣv anityeṣu ca prārabdheṣu.
children.translated_text: Or rather, there is the introduction of a substitute substance. Why? Because of no distinction in the meaning of the injunction — the meaning enjoined by the injunction '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) is not differentiated [whether] performed with rice or <s>nīvāras</s>. And the sacrifice must necessarily be performed — in obligatory [rites] and in optional [rites that have been] commenced.

children.text: niyamārthaḥ kvacid vidhiḥ//6.3.16//
children.translated_text: The prescription in some [cases] is for the purpose of restriction. // MS_6,3.16 //

children.text:
atha yad uktam, kvacid vidhānād iti{*5/410*}. ucyate, niyamārthaḥ kvacid vidhiḥ, somābhāve bahuṣu sadṛśeṣu prāpteṣu niyamaḥ kriyate, pūtīkā{*5/411*} evābhiṣotavyā iti. tasmāt pratinidhim upādāya prayogaḥ kartavya iti.
NOTES:
*{5/410: Vgl. MS 6.3.14}*
*{5/411: E2: pūtikā}*
children.translated_text:
Now, as to what was said — 'because of prescription in some [cases]' — we reply: the prescription in some [cases] is for the purpose of restriction (<s>niyama</s>). In the absence of <s>Soma</s>, when many similar [substitutes] are obtained, a restriction is made: '<s>pūtīkas</s> alone should be pressed.' Therefore, performing with a substitute should be done.
NOTES:
[{5/410: Cf. MS 6.3.14}]
[{5/411: E2: <s>pūtikā</s>}]

children.text: tan nityaṃ taccikīrṣā hi//6.3.17//
children.translated_text: That [restriction] is invariable, for there is the desire to [replicate] that [prescribed substance]. // MS_6,3.17 //

children.text: kathaṃ punar idam avagamyate, niyamārtham eva tad vacanam iti. ucyate, yataḥ prāptāḥ pūtīkāḥ. kathaṃ ca te prāptāḥ? taccikīrṣā hi, tatra sādṛśyacikīrṣety{*5/412*} etad vakṣyāmaḥ{*5/413*}. taccikīrṣayā ca prāptāḥ pūtīkāḥ. tasmāt tan nityam, vacanam etan niyamāya nityam iti gamyate.
children.translated_text: But how is this understood — that the statement is only for the purpose of restriction? We reply: because the <s>pūtīkas</s> are [already] obtained. And how are they obtained? Because of the desire to [replicate] that — 'the desire for resemblance to that' is what we will state [later]. And through the desire to [replicate] that, the <s>pūtīkas</s> are obtained. Therefore that [restriction] is invariable — it is understood that the statement is invariable for the purpose of restriction.

children.text: na devatāgniśabdakriyam anyārthasaṃyogāt//6.3.18//
children.translated_text: Not [substitutable are] the deity, fire, word [of the mantra], and ritual action, because of conjunction with another purpose. // MS_6,3.18 //

children.text:
devatā āgneyo 'ṣṭākapāla{*5/414*} ityevamādyāḥ, agniḥ, yad āhavanīye juhvati tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prīto bhavatīti{*5/415*}. śabdo mantraḥ{*5/416*}, barhir devasadanaṃ dāmītyevamādiḥ{*5/417*}, kriyāḥ [661]{*5/418*} samidho yajati, tanūnapātaṃ yajatītyevamādyāḥ. tatra saṃdehaḥ, devatāgniśabdakriyāṇām apacāre pratinidhir upādeyaḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? pūrvādhikaraṇanyāyena pratinidhāyānyat, prayogaḥ kartavya iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, na devatāgniśabdakriyāṇām apacāre pratinidhinā bhavitavyam iti. kutaḥ? anyārthasaṃyogāt, pratinidhīyamānam anyad etebhyaḥ, anyac ca teṣām arthaṃ na śaknuyāt kartum. kaś ca teṣām arthaḥ? devatā tāvad uddeśenārthaṃ sādhayati, agnim uddiśya, aṣṭākapālaḥ paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ ca tyajyate. yac cānyeṣu haviḥṣu vihitam, na tato darśapūrṇamāsau bhavataḥ. tatrānyoddiśyamānā na śrutāyā uddeśyāyā arthaṃ kuryāt. na hy anyasyām uddiśyamānāyāṃ darśapūrṇamāsau bhavataḥ. tasmān na devatā pratinidhīyate.
tathā, yad āhavanīye juhvatīty āvahanīyāpacāre nānyo 'gniḥ pratinidhātavyaḥ, anyad vā dravyam iti. kutaḥ? anyārthasaṃyogāt, pratinidhīyamānam āhavanīyakārye na vartate. katham? adṛṣṭam āhavanīyasya kāryam, āhavanīyasyopari tyajyamāne yad bhavati, na tad anyasyopari. na hi, yajatiśabdena sāmarthyāt tad gṛhyate, yasyopari tyajyate, na hi, upari yajyamānasya deśaḥ kiṃcid upakarotīti. tasmān nāgneḥ{*5/419*} pratinidhiḥ.
tathā, mantrāpacāre nānyo mantraḥ pratinidhīyate. mantrasya{*5/420*} hy etat prayojanam, yat, smārayati kriyāṃ sādhanaṃ vā, asati smaraṇe na kriyā saṃvarteta, tad apacarite mantre yadi tasyārthe [662]{*5/421*} 'nyaṃ śabdam uccārayati pūrvaṃ pratīte 'rthe śabdam uccārayan, na śabdenārthaṃ pratīyāt. atha pratītam api punaḥ pratinidhiśabdoccāraṇena pratīyāc chabdāt pratītiṃ kuryāt{*5/422*}, evaṃ ca pratinidhiśabdoccāraṇānurodho 'narthakaḥ syāt. na hi, śabdena pratyāpayitavyam iti kiṃcit pramāṇam asti. yad asti, tad viśeṣeṇaivānena śabdena barhirādinety evam, tadabhāve śabdāntarānurodho 'narthakaḥ syāt. tasmān na śabdasya pratinidhiḥ.
kriyāpacāre na{*5/423*} kriyāntaram, anyārthasaṃyogāt{*5/424*}, samidyajimantau darśapūrṇamāsau kartavyau, tāv anyasyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ na tadvantau bhavataḥ. tasmāt kriyāyāṃ na pratinidhir iti.
children.translated_text:
The deity — 'an eight-potsherd [cake] for <s>Agni</s>' and the like; the fire — 'when they offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, by that he [the deity] becomes favorably disposed and pleased'; the word — the <s>mantra</s>, such as 'the <s>barhis</s> is the seat of the gods, the <s>dāmi</s> (restraining rope)' and the like; the ritual actions [661] — 'he offers to <s>Samidh</s>, he offers to <s>Tanūnapāt</s>' and the like. There a doubt [arises]: when the deity, fire, word, or ritual action becomes unavailable, should a substitute (<s>pratinidhi</s>) be adopted, or not? What is the prima facie view? By the principle of the previous topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), having substituted another [element], the performance should be carried out.
Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: when the deity, fire, word, or ritual action becomes unavailable, there should be no substitution. Why? Because of the connection with a different purpose — what is substituted is different from these, and a different [element] could not serve their purpose. And what is their purpose? The deity, for its part, serves its purpose through designation (<s>uddeśa</s>) — designating <s>Agni</s>, the eight-potsherd [cake] is offered on the full-moon and new-moon days. And what is prescribed for other oblations does not thereby constitute the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites]. There, another [deity] being designated would not serve the purpose of the heard designated [deity]. For when another [deity] is designated, the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites] do not result. Therefore the deity is not substituted.
Likewise, 'when they offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>' — when the <s>Āhavanīya</s> becomes unavailable, neither another fire nor another substance should be substituted. Why? Because of the connection with a different purpose — what is substituted does not operate in the function of the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. How? The function of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is unseen — what results when [the oblation] is offered upon the <s>Āhavanīya</s> does not [result when offered] upon another. For by the capacity of the word '<s>yajati</s>' (he offers), what is grasped is [that] upon which it is offered, [but] the place upon which the offering is made does not contribute anything [else]. Therefore there is no substitute for the fire.
Likewise, when the <s>mantra</s> becomes unavailable, another <s>mantra</s> is not substituted. For this is the purpose of the <s>mantra</s> — it reminds [the priest] of the ritual action or the instrument; without the reminding, the action would not take place. If, when the [proper] <s>mantra</s> has become unavailable, one utters [662] another word for the [same] purpose, uttering a word for a meaning already understood — one would not understand the meaning through the [substitute] word. And if one were to understand what is already understood again through the utterance of a substitute word — were to produce understanding from the word — then the accommodation of uttering the substitute word would be purposeless. For there is no valid authority [requiring] that one must be reminded by a word. What there is, is this: [one must be reminded] by this particular word — such as <s>barhis</s> etc. — just so. In its absence, the accommodation of another word would be purposeless. Therefore there is no substitute for the word.
When a ritual action becomes unavailable, no other action [is substituted] — because of the connection with a different purpose. The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites] are to be performed with the <s>samidh</s>-offerings; when another [action] is performed, they would not possess those [required actions]. Therefore there is no substitute for a ritual action.

children.text: devatāyāṃ ca tadarthatvāt//6.3.19//
children.translated_text: And regarding the deity, because of being for that [specific] purpose. // MS_6,3.19 //

children.text: devatāyām aparo viśeṣaḥ, yena na pratinidhīyate, devatā nāma, yad arthaṃ kiṃcic codyate, sā. anyā tasyāḥ sthāne pratinidhīyamānā na devatā syāt. coditā hi devatā bhavati, nācoditā, saṃbandhiśabdaś caiṣaḥ. yā yad arthaṃ codyate, sā tasyaiva devatā, nānyasya. devateti saṃbandhiśabdo na jātiśabdaḥ. tasmād api na devatāyāḥ pratinidhir iti.
children.translated_text: Regarding the deity, there is a further specific [reason] why it is not substituted: the deity, by definition, is that for whose purpose something is enjoined. Another [deity], substituted in its place, would not be a deity [of that rite]. For only an enjoined [deity] is a deity, not an un-enjoined one. And this is a relational word (<s>saṃbandhiśabda</s>). Whatever [deity] is enjoined for whatever purpose — that is the deity of that [rite] alone, not of another. '<s>Devatā</s>' (deity) is a relational word, not a class-word (<s>jātiśabda</s>). Therefore there is no substitute for the deity.

children.text: pratiṣiddhaṃ cāviśeṣeṇa hi tacchrutiḥ//6.3.20//
children.translated_text: And what is prohibited [should not be substituted], without distinction; for such is the [Vedic] statement. // MS_6,3.20 //

children.text: atha yat pratiṣiddham, ayajñiyā vai varakāḥ kodravāḥ, ayajñiyā vai māṣā iti. kiṃ tac chrutadravyāpacāre prati[663]{*5/425*}nidhātavyam, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? pratinidheyam{*5/426*} iti, āgamo vā codanārthāviśeṣād{*5/427*} iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pratiṣiddhaṃ ca na pratinidhātavyam iti, aviśeṣeṇa hy etad ucyate, na yajñārhā māṣā varakāḥ kodravāś ceti, yajñasaṃbandha eṣāṃ pratiṣidhyate. naite yajñāṅgabhāvaṃ netavyā iti, pratinidhīyamānāś cāṅgabhāvaṃ nītāḥ syuḥ. tasmān naite pratinidhātavyā iti.
children.translated_text: Now, regarding what is prohibited — '<s>varakas</s> (a type of millet) and <s>kodravas</s> (another grain) are unfit for sacrifice'; '<s>māṣas</s> (black beans) are unfit for sacrifice.' When the heard substance becomes unavailable [663], should [a prohibited substance] be substituted, or not? What is the prima facie view? It should be substituted — 'a [substitute] or a [related item] is [used], because of no distinction in the purpose of the injunction.' Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: what is prohibited should not be substituted — for this is stated without distinction: '<s>māṣas</s>, <s>varakas</s>, and <s>kodravas</s> are not fit for sacrifice' — their connection with sacrifice is prohibited. They should not be made to serve as subsidiaries of the sacrifice. And if substituted, they would be made to serve as subsidiaries. Therefore these should not be substituted.

children.text: tathā svāminaḥ phalasamavāyāt phalasya karmayogitvāt//6.3.21//
children.translated_text: Likewise for the owner (<s>svāmin</s>), because of the connection with the fruit; because the fruit is connected with the ritual action. // MS_6,3.21 //

children.text: agnihotrādīni karmāṇy udāharaṇam. teṣu svāminy apacarati saṃdehaḥ, kim anyaḥ pratinidhātavyo neti. kiṃ prāptam? pratinidhātavya iti. kutaḥ? āgamo vā codanārthāviśeṣād{*5/428*} iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, tathā svāminaḥ syāt. ko 'rthaḥ? na pratinidhiḥ. kutaḥ? phalasamavāyāt. yo 'rthī svatyāgenartvijaḥ parikrīṇīte, yaś ca svaṃ pradeyaṃ tyajati, sa svāmī. yadi sa pratinidhīyate, svāminā yat kartavyam, tat sarvaṃ kuryāt, tat sarvaṃ kurvan, svāmy eva syāt, na pratinidhiḥ. sa eva hi phalena saṃbadhyate. ya utsargaṃ karoti, sa phalavān bhavati. tad uktam, śāstraphalaṃ prayoktarīti{*5/429*}. tasmān na svāminaḥ pratinidhir iti.
children.translated_text: The <s>Agnihotra</s> and similar rites are the example. In these, when the owner (<s>svāmin</s>, i.e., the sacrificer) becomes unavailable, a doubt [arises]: should another be substituted, or not? What is the prima facie view? He should be substituted. Why? 'A [substitute] or a [related item] is [used], because of no distinction in the purpose of the injunction.' Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: likewise for the owner — the same [applies]. What is the meaning? No substitute. Why? Because of the connection with the fruit. He who, through the relinquishment of his own [property], hires the <s>ṛtvij</s> (priests), and he who relinquishes his own [property] to be given — he is the owner. If he is substituted, [the substitute] would do everything that the owner should do; doing all of that, he would be the owner himself, not a substitute. For it is he who is connected with the fruit. He who makes the relinquishment (<s>utsarga</s>) — he becomes the fruit-bearer. It has been stated: 'The fruit of the teaching [belongs] to the performer.' Therefore there is no substitute for the owner.

children.text: bahūnāṃ tu pravṛtte 'nyam āgamayed avaiguṇyāt//6.3.22//
children.translated_text: But when there are many [sacrificers] and [the rite] has commenced, another should be brought in, because of [avoiding] deficiency. // MS_6,3.22 //

children.text:
satrāṇy udāharaṇam, saptadaśāvarāḥ satram āsīrann iti. teṣu kasmiṃścit svāminy apacarati saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ tatrānyaḥ pratinidhātavyaḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? na svāminaḥ pratinidhir iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, bahūnāṃ yajamānānāṃ pravṛtte karmaṇi, apacarite kasmiṃścit svāminy anyam āgamayet. kutaḥ? evam avaiguṇyaṃ bhavatīti, svāmigatā saptadaśādisaṃkhyā tatrāṅgam, tayā vinā karma viguṇam, tatsaṃpādanāyānya āgamayitavyaḥ.
nanu svāmigatā saṃkhyā, na tv āgamyamānaḥ svāmīti vakṣyāmaḥ. tenāśakyaiva sā saṃkhyopādātum iti. ucyate, svāmigatā na hi bhaviṣyati. na hi sā śakyā kartum iti. idaṃ tu śakyaṃ kartum, ye svāmināṃ padārthāḥ, ta iha saptadaśāvaraiḥ kartavyā ity etad upapāditaṃ bhaviṣyati. tasmāt pratinidhātavyaṃ tatreti.
children.translated_text:
The <s>satras</s> are the example — 'not fewer than seventeen should sit for the <s>satra</s>.' When, among them, some owner (<s>svāmin</s>) becomes unavailable, a doubt [arises]: should another be substituted there, or not? What is the prima facie view? There is no substitute for the owner. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: when there are many sacrificers and the ritual has commenced, another should be brought in when some owner becomes unavailable. Why? For thus there is no deficiency — the number of seventeen and the like, which belongs to the owners, is a subsidiary there; without it, the ritual would be deficient. To fulfill that [number], another should be brought in.
[The objector says:] but the number belongs to the owners, and the one brought in is not an owner — as we shall state. Therefore that number cannot be obtained. [We] reply: it is not that [the number] will belong to owners. For it cannot be effected. But this can be effected — that the items belonging to the owners should be done by not fewer than seventeen — this will have been established. Therefore a substitute should be brought in there.

children.text: sa svāmī syāt tatsaṃyogāt//6.3.23//
children.translated_text: He would be an owner, because of the connection with that [status]. // MS_6,3.23 //

children.text: tasminn āgamyamāna idānīṃ saṃdehaḥ, kim asau svāmī, uta karmakara iti. kiṃ prāptam? sa svāmī syāt. kasmāt? tatsaṃyogāt, tena svāmitvena{*5/431*} saṃyogaḥ. yo hy asāv ānīyate, sa svāmī kriyate, svāminy apacarite 'nyo yadi svāmī kriyate, tataḥ sa pratinidhiḥ kṛto bhavati. tasmāt svāmīti.
children.translated_text: Regarding the one brought in, a doubt now [arises]: is he an owner, or a hired worker (<s>karmakara</s>)? What is the prima facie view? He would be an owner. Why? Because of the connection with that — with ownership. For he who is brought in is made an owner; when the [previous] owner becomes unavailable, if another is made an owner, then he becomes a substitute. Therefore [he is] an owner.

children.text:
NOTES:

*{5/432: E2: 5,259; E6: 2,147}*

children.text: karmakaro vā bhṛtatvāt//3.3.24//
children.translated_text: Or he would be a hired worker (<s>karmakara</s>), because of being hired. // MS_6,3.24 //

children.text: karmakaro vā sa syāt. kutaḥ? bhṛtatvat, bhṛto hy asau taiḥ śiṣṭaiḥ svāmibhiḥ prayuktaḥ, parikrīyamāṇo na svāmī bhavati. yaḥ phalaṃ prāpnoti, sa svāmī, yaḥ parasyopakāre vartate, sa karmakaraḥ, naivāsau phalaṃ prāpnoti. kutaḥ? yo hy ārabhya parisamāpayati, sa phalavān, eṣa hy ākhyātārthaḥ, sa hy upakramaprabhṛty apavargaparyantam āha. nanu te 'pi tatra viguṇaṃ kurvanti, saptadaśānāṃ svāminām abhāvāt. tasmāt te 'pi na svāminaḥ, no cet svāminaḥ, na phalaṃ prāpnuvanti. ucyate, na saptadaśāvarāḥ phalasamavāye bhaveyur iti śrūyate, na saṃkhyā phalaparigrahe guṇabhūtā. kiṃ tarhi? padārtheṣu, saptadaśāvarair yājamānāḥ padārthāḥ kartavyā iti, te ca pratinihitena kriyante, aphalatve 'pi ca satyaṃ saṃkalpaṃ kartum anyam ānayanti. ānīyamānasya ca na tena prayojanam.
children.translated_text: Or he would be a hired worker. Why? Because of being hired — for he is hired, employed by those remaining owners. Being hired, he does not become an owner. He who obtains the fruit — he is the owner; he who operates for another's benefit — he is a hired worker. He [the substitute] does not obtain the fruit. Why? For he who commences and completes [the rite] — he is the fruit-bearer; this is the meaning of the verb. For [the verb] expresses [the entire span] from commencement through to conclusion. [The objector says:] but they too create a deficiency there, because of the absence of seventeen owners. Therefore they too are not owners; if they are not owners, they do not obtain the fruit. [We] reply: it is not heard that not fewer than seventeen should be connected with the fruit — the number is not subordinate in the fruit-connection. Rather, [it is subordinate] in the items — the sacrificer-related items are to be done by not fewer than seventeen. And those are done by the substitute. Even being without fruit, they [the remaining owners] bring in another to make their resolve come true. And for the one being brought in, there is no purpose in that [resolve of theirs].

children.text: tasmiṃś ca phaladarśanāt//6.3.25//
children.translated_text: And because fruit is shown in his case [i.e., even for the deceased]. // MS_6,3.25 //

children.text: tasmiṃś ca diṣṭāṃ gatiṃ gate phalaṃ darśayati, yo dīkṣitānāṃ pramīyetāpi tasya phalam iti. tasmāt karmakara iti.
children.translated_text: And regarding him — the one who has gone to his destined end (died) — fruit is shown: 'Even for one who dies among the consecrated, there is fruit.' Therefore [the substitute is merely] a hired worker.

children.text: sa taddharmā syāt karmasaṃyogāt//6.3.26//
children.translated_text: He should have the properties of that [owner], because of the connection with the ritual action. // MS_6,3.26 //

children.text: bahūnāṃ kasmiṃścid apacarite pratinidheyo 'nya ity etat [666]{*5/433*} samadhigatam. idam idānīṃ tatra saṃdigdham, kim asau svāmidharmā syāt, utartvigdharmā? kiṃ prāptam? ṛtvigdharmā. kutaḥ? parārthaṃ hi sa yajati, yaś ca parārthaṃ yajati, sa ṛtvig iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, sa taddharmā syāt, svāmidharmā{*5/434*}, tasya hi kārye śūyate, yaś ca yasya kāryam adhitiṣṭhati, sa taddharmaiḥ saṃbadhyate, yathā srugdharmaiḥ{*5/435*} svadhitir iti.
children.translated_text: It has been established that when one of many [owners] becomes unavailable, another should be substituted [666]. Now a doubt arises regarding this: should he have the properties of the owner, or the properties of the <s>ṛtvik</s> (priest)? What is the prima facie view? He should have the properties of the <s>ṛtvik</s>. Why? For he sacrifices for another's benefit; and one who sacrifices for another's benefit is an <s>ṛtvik</s>. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: he should have the properties of that [owner] — the properties of the owner. For he is heard as [functioning] in the role of that [owner]; and one who stands in the role of another is connected with the properties of that [other] — just as the <s>svadhiti</s> (axe) [has] the properties of the <s>sruva</s> (ladle).

children.text:
NOTES:

*{5/434: E1 gibt svāmidharmā in Klammern}*
*{5/435: E2: sruvadharmaiḥ}*

children.text: sāmānyaṃ taccikīrṣā hi//6.3.27//
children.translated_text: The commonality [is the criterion]; for the intention [in substitution] is that. // MS_6,3.27 //

children.text: śrute dravye 'pacarati pratinidhim upādāya prayoktavyam iti sthitam. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ yatkiṃcid dravyam upādāya prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ, uta sadṛśam iti. kiṃ prāptam? yatkiṃcid upādāyeti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, sāmānyaṃ yatra gṛhyate, tad upādātavyaṃ sadṛśam iti. kutaḥ? sarve hy ākṛtivacanāḥ śabdāḥ, ākṛtiś ca yady apy aṅgabhāvena śrūyate, tathāpi na sākṣāt tasyāḥ kriyāṃ pratyaṅgabhāvaḥ. yat tu kriyāsādhanaṃ dravyam arthād aṅgabhūtaṃ prāptam, tat paricchindatī kriyāyām aṅgabhāvaṃ yāti, vyakteś cākṛtyā viśeṣāḥ paricchidyante, te viśeṣā aṅgabhūtāḥ. atha tasyām ākṛtāv apacaritāyām arthaprāptaṃ dravyaṃ grahītavyam eva, yasmiṃś ca sadṛśe gṛhyamāṇe teṣāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ kecit saṃgṛhītā bhavanti, sa tatra lābho labhyata iti, tatsadṛśaṃ dravyam upādātavyaṃ bhavati. tasmād vrīhīṇām apacāre nīvārāḥ pratinidheyā iti.
children.translated_text: It has been established that when the heard substance becomes unavailable, having adopted a substitute, the performance should be carried out. There a doubt [arises]: should the performance be carried out by adopting any [substance] whatsoever, or one that is similar? What is the prima facie view? By adopting any [substance] whatsoever. Given this prima facie conclusion, we say: what possesses the commonality [with the original] — that should be adopted, [namely] something similar. Why? For all words denote class (<s>ākṛti</s>). And even though the class is heard as subsidiary, still the class itself is not directly subsidiary to the action. But the substance — obtained by implication (<s>arthāt</s>) as subsidiary — is what [the class] delimits; entering into subsidiarity with respect to the action, the specific features of the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) are delimited by the class. Those specific features are subsidiary. Now, when that class becomes unavailable, a substance obtained by implication must indeed be taken. And when a similar [substance] is taken, some of those specific features are captured — that is the gain obtained therein. Therefore a substance similar [to the original] should be adopted. Hence when rice (<s>vrīhi</s>) becomes unavailable, wild rice (<s>nīvāra</s>) should be substituted.

children.text: nirdeśāt tu vikalpe yatpravṛttam//6.3.28//
children.translated_text: But because of the designation, in an option, [a substitute] similar to what has been employed [should be used]. // MS_6,3.28 //

children.text:
asti jyotiṣṭome paśur agniṣomīyaḥ, yo dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti{*5/437*}, tatra śrūyate, khādire paśuṃ badhnāti pālāśe badhnāti rauhitake badhnātīti. tatra kadācit khadiraguṇake prayoga ārabdhe khadiro vinaṣṭaḥ, tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ vaikalpikasyopādānam uta khadirasadṛśasyeti. kiṃ prāptam? vaikalpikasyeti. kutaḥ? sa hi śrutaḥ, khadirasadṛśo na śrūyate, tasmād vaikalpikasyopādānam iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, vikalpe yat pravṛttam, tatsadṛśam upādeyam, yat pravṛttaṃ yasmin prayoge, tan nirdiṣṭam, tad aṅgabhūtam, vaikalpikam anaṅgam. āśritakhadire prayoge palāśarauhitakāv anaṅgabūtau, tau na śakyete yadā khadiraḥ, tadaiva kartum, aśakyaṃ cāśrutam. tasmād āśritakhadire prayoga itarau nopādeyau, anaṅgabhūtatvāt. khadirasya sadṛśam anveṣitavyam iti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal — 'the consecrated one who slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.' There it is heard: 'He ties the animal to a <s>khadira</s> (catechu) [post]; he ties it to a <s>palāśa</s> (flame of the forest) [post]; he ties it to a <s>rauhitaka</s> (red sandalwood) [post].' There, when a performance employing the <s>khadira</s> quality has been commenced, the <s>khadira</s> [wood] is destroyed. There a doubt [arises]: should one of the options be employed, or something similar to <s>khadira</s>? What is the prima facie view? One of the options. Why? For that is heard [in the Veda]; something similar to <s>khadira</s> is not heard. Therefore an option should be employed.
Given this prima facie view, we say: in an option, [a substitute] similar to what has been employed [should be used]. What has been employed in whichever performance — that is what has been designated; that is a subsidiary. The option is non-subsidiary. In a performance that has adopted <s>khadira</s>, <s>palāśa</s> and <s>rauhitaka</s> are non-subsidiary; they cannot be performed at the time when <s>khadira</s> [is designated], and what is impossible is unheard. Therefore in a performance that has adopted <s>khadira</s>, the other two should not be employed, because of being non-subsidiary. Something similar to <s>khadira</s> should be sought.

NOTES:
[{5/437: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.1.11.6}]

children.text: aśabdam iti cet//6.3.29//
children.translated_text: If [one objects that] it is without [Vedic] word — // MS_6,3.29 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, khadirasadṛśam upādeyam iti, aśabdam evaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati. tasmāc chabdavattvād vaikalpikam upādeyam.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that something similar to <s>khadira</s> should be employed — what is thus done becomes without [Vedic] word. Therefore, because of having a [Vedic] word, one of the options should be employed.

children.text: nānaṅgatvāt//6.3.30//
children.translated_text: No, because of [its] non-subsidiary status. // MS_6,3.30 //

children.text: naitad evam, anaṅgaṃ tasmin prayoge vaikalpikam. āśritakhadiro [668]{*5/438*} hi sa prayogaḥ, yo nirdiṣṭaḥ, tasya nirdeśād itarāv aśrutau. nanu nirdeśābhāve 'ṅgabhāvavirodhaḥ. tena śrutāv iti. kim ataḥ? yady evaṃ yadopāttasyābhāvaḥ, tadā śravaṇam. naitad evam, naimittikaṃ hi tathā pratijñāyeta, sati vacane nimitte, asati khadira itarau śrutāv iti. tatra ko doṣaḥ? sa evāpekṣito 'napekṣitaś ceti virodho bhavet, saṃskārāś ca khadire kartavyāḥ. khadirasadṛśe tadbuddhyā gṛhyamāṇe śrutabuddhyā kṛtā bhavanti, vaikalpikena tu śrutenāsaṃbaddhāḥ. tasmād upāttasadṛśo grāhya iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — in that performance, the option is non-subsidiary. For that performance [668] which has adopted <s>khadira</s> is what has been designated; because of its designation, the other two are unheard. [The objector says:] but in the absence of designation, there would be contradiction with subsidiary-status. [We reply:] hence they are heard [only conditionally]. What follows? If so, [they are] heard when the employed [substance] is absent. This is not so — for such [a conditional rule] would have to be accepted as occasional (<s>naimittika</s>): when there is a statement [serving as] an occasion, when <s>khadira</s> is absent, the other two are heard. What is the fault in that? There would be a contradiction — the very same [khadira] being both required and not required. And the refinements (<s>saṃskāras</s>) must be performed on <s>khadira</s>. When something similar to <s>khadira</s> is taken with the understanding of [being] that [khadira], the [refinements] are done with the understanding of what is heard; but with the option, which is heard [as an alternative], they are unconnected. Therefore something similar to what was employed should be taken.

children.text: vacanāc cānyāyyam abhāve tatsāmānyena pratinidhir abhāvād itarasya//6.3.31//
children.translated_text: And because of the [Vedic] statement, the substitute (<s>pratinidhi</s>) is improper; in the absence [of the principal], by the similarity to that [principal, the substitute is employed]; because of the absence of the other. // MS_6,3.31 //

children.text:
idam āmananti, yadi na somaṃ vindet{*5/439*} pūtīkān abhiṣuṇuyād iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim ayam abhāve nimitte vidhiḥ, uta pratinidhiniyama iti. kiṃ prāptam? abhāve vidhir iti. kutaḥ? vidhānāt, na hi pratinidhir vidhīyate, sādhyasiddhaye sādhanaṃ svayam evopādīyate, idaṃ tu vidhīyate, tat kalpāntarapekṣe 'rthavad bhavati. tasmān na pratinidhiḥ.
ity evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pratinidhiḥ syāt. kutaḥ? vinaṣṭe hi sādhane sādhyasiddhyarthaṃ sādhanāntaram upādīyate, śrutasyābhāvāt. nanv anyāyyāḥ pūtīkāḥ, anyad dhi sadṛśāntaram astīti. tad ucyate, vacanāt. sadṛśe prāpte, bahuṣu vāsadṛśeṣu pūtīkā alpasadṛśā niyamyante. katham? tad dhi [669]{*5/440*} prakrāntaṃ karmāvaśyaṃ kartavyam, tasyām avasthāyām antareṇaiva vacanaṃ pratinidheyaṃ dravyāntaraṃ prāptam eva, prāpte vacanaṃ na vidhir iti gamyate. prāptasyānuvādo bhavitum arhati. kim artham anuvāda iti cet. ucyate, alpasādṛśyam aprāptam, tadvidhānārtham anuvādaḥ. prayojanaṃ pakṣoktam, pratinidhipakṣe somasadṛśasyopādānaṃ pūtīkavināśe, dravyāntaravidhau pūtīkasadṛśam upādeyam.
children.translated_text:
This is recorded: 'If one does not find <s>Soma</s>, one should press <s>Pūtīka</s> [plants].' There a doubt [arises]: is this an injunction [valid only] in the absence [of Soma] as the occasion, or is it a restriction of substitution? What is the prima facie view? It is an injunction in the absence [of Soma]. Why? Because of being an injunction — for a substitute is not [normally] enjoined; a means is employed of its own accord for the accomplishment of the end. But this is being enjoined; that becomes meaningful when another option is expected. Therefore it is not a substitute.
Given this prima facie view, we say: it would be a substitute. Why? For when the [prescribed] means has been destroyed, another means is employed for the purpose of accomplishing the end, because of the absence of what is heard. [The objector says:] but <s>Pūtīkas</s> are improper — for there is another [substance] that is more similar [to Soma]. To this we say: because of the [Vedic] statement. When something similar is obtained, among the many dissimilar [substances], <s>Pūtīkas</s> of slight similarity are specified. How? [669] For that commenced ritual must necessarily be performed. In that situation, even without a [Vedic] statement, another substance as substitute is already obtained. When [a substitute] is [already] obtained, the statement is not an injunction — it is understood [as something else]. It deserves to be a restatement of what is [already] obtained. For what purpose is it a restatement? We reply: the slight similarity is not [otherwise] obtained; the restatement is for the purpose of enjoining that. The purpose was stated in the thesis — in the substitution view, if <s>Pūtīkas</s> are destroyed, something similar to <s>Soma</s> should be employed; in the alternative-substance-injunction [view], something similar to <s>Pūtīka</s> should be employed.

*{5/440: E2: 5,263; E6: 2,150}*

children.text: na pratinidhau samatvāt//6.3.32//
children.translated_text: There is no substitute of a substitute, because of equality [of status]. // MS_6,3.32 //

children.text: idaṃ vicāryate, śrute dravya upātte 'pacarite pratinidhim upādāya prayogaḥ prāptaḥ, yadā so 'pi vinaṣṭaḥ pratinihitaḥ, tadā kiṃ pratinidhisadṛśam upādeyam, utopāttasya vinaṣṭasyeti. kiṃ prāptam? pratinihite vinaṣṭe tatsadṛśam upādeyaṃ pūrveṇa nyāyena{*5/441*}. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, pratinidhau na syāt pratinidhir iti. kutaḥ? samatvāt, yathaivāsau pūrvaḥ pratinihitaḥ śrutacikīrṣayā, na pratinidhicikīrṣayā, evam ayam api śrutacikīrṣayā, na pratinidhicikīrṣayā. tasmān na pratinidhisadṛśam upādeyam upāttanaṣṭasyaiva sadṛśo 'nveṣitavya iti.
children.translated_text: This is being investigated: when a heard substance has been employed and then removed, and [the ritual] has proceeded with a substitute, [then] when that substitute too is destroyed — should something similar to the substitute be employed, or something similar to the [originally] employed substance that was destroyed? What is the prima facie view? When the substitute is destroyed, something similar to it should be employed, by the previous principle. Given this prima facie view, we say: there should not be a substitute of a substitute. Why? Because of equality — just as the first substitute was employed with the desire [to have] what is heard, not with the desire [to have] a substitute; so too this [second one] with the desire [to have] what is heard, not with the desire [to have] a substitute. Therefore something similar to the substitute should not be employed — something similar to the [originally] employed [substance] that was destroyed should be sought.

children.text: syāc chrutilakṣaṇe niyatatvāt//6.3.33//
children.translated_text: It would [apply] in [the case of] a substitute specified by the [Vedic] word, because of [its being] fixed [by that word]. // MS_6,3.33 //

children.text: atha śrutilakṣaṇe katham? yathā, yadi somaṃ na vindet pūtīkān abhiṣuṇuyād iti, pūtīkeṣu vinaṣṭeṣu pūtīkasadṛśam upā[670]{*5/442*}deyam uta somasadṛśam iti. kiṃ prāptam? syāc chrutilakṣaṇe pratinidhau pratinidhisadṛśasyopādānaṃ kartavyam, somābhāve pūtīkavyaktayo vihitāḥ, sa cāyaṃ śrutaḥ somābhāvaḥ{*5/443*}. tasmāt pūtīkavyaktaya upādeyā iti.
children.translated_text: But what about a substitute specified by the [Vedic] word? As in 'If one does not find <s>Soma</s>, one should press <s>Pūtīkas</s>' — when the <s>Pūtīkas</s> are destroyed, should something similar to <s>Pūtīkas</s> be employed, [670] or something similar to <s>Soma</s>? What is the prima facie view? In the case of a substitute specified by the [Vedic] word, something similar to the substitute should be employed — for in the absence of <s>Soma</s>, instances of <s>Pūtīka</s> are enjoined; and this absence of <s>Soma</s> is [indeed] the heard [condition]. Therefore instances of <s>Pūtīka</s> should be employed.

children.text: na, tadīpsā hi//6.3.34//
children.translated_text: No — for the desire is for that [Soma-quality]. // MS_6,3.34 //

children.text: naitad evam, na hi pūtīkavyaktīnām īpsā, pūtīkeṣu yat somasādṛśyam, tan niyamyate, tathā hi pūtīkavidhānaṃ dṛṣṭārtham asadṛśavidhāne 'dṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta. ato yasmiṃs tad apūtīkasadṛśe 'pi dravye bhavati tad grahītavyam, na pūtīkasādṛśyam ādriyeteti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — for it is not instances of <s>Pūtīka</s> [as such] that are desired. What is specified is the <s>Soma</s>-similarity in <s>Pūtīkas</s>. For thus the injunction of <s>Pūtīkas</s> has a visible purpose; in the injunction of something dissimilar, an unseen [purpose] would have to be postulated. Therefore, in whatever substance — even non-<s>Pūtīka</s> — that [Soma-similarity] exists, that should be taken. The <s>Pūtīka</s>-similarity is not to be relied upon.

children.text: mukhyādhigame mukhyam āgamo hi tadabhāvāt//6.3.35//
children.translated_text: When the principal is obtained, [one should use] the principal — for the availability [of the principal makes the substitute unnecessary], because of [the substitute's existence depending on] the absence of that [principal]. // MS_6,3.35 //

children.text: atha yatra vinaṣṭe śrute pratinidhim upādātuṃ prasthito mukhyam evopalabhate, tatra kiṃ pratinidhim evopādadīta, uta tam eva mukhyam iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam? pratinidhim upādātavyaḥ iti, evaṃ saṃkalpitavān asau pratinidhim upādadāna eva satyasaṃkalpo bhavati. tasmāt pratinidhātavyam iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, mukhyādhigame tam evopādadīta. abhāve hi śrutasya, anukalpaḥ pratinidhiḥ, śrute hi sakalā vyaktayaḥ, pratinidhau vikalāḥ. atha yad uktam, saṃkalpabhedadoṣa iti, śruteṣv asau śiṣṭavigarhaṇāyāṃ vā.
children.translated_text: Now, when the heard [substance] has been destroyed and one has set out to employ a substitute, [but then] obtains the principal itself — should one employ only the substitute, or that principal? What is the prima facie view? The substitute should be employed — for having so resolved, by employing the substitute one becomes truthful in one's resolve. Therefore the substitute should be employed. Given this prima facie view, we say: when the principal is obtained, one should employ that very [principal]. For in the absence of what is heard, the substitute is a secondary option. In what is heard, all qualities are complete; in the substitute, they are incomplete. As for what was said — 'the defect of change of resolve' — [the resolve is directed toward] what is heard, or [concern is] about the reproach of the learned.

children.text: pravṛtte 'pīti cet//6.3.36//
children.translated_text: If [one argues that this applies] even when [the process] has commenced — // MS_6,3.36 //

children.text: athāgnihotrādiṣu karmasu śrutadravyāpacāre pratinidhāv upātte kṛteṣu keṣucit saṃskāreṣu yadi tad eva śrutam upalabhyeta, kiṃ śrutam upādīyeta, uta tenaiva pratinihitena samāpayitavyam iti. kiṃ prāptam? śrutam upādīyeta pravṛtte 'pi. tad uktam, āgamo hi tadabhāvād{*5/445*} iti. tasmān na pratinidhātavyam iti.
children.translated_text: Now, in rituals like the <s>Agnihotra</s> etc., when the heard substance has been removed and a substitute employed, [and] some refinements have been performed — if that very heard [substance] is then obtained, should the heard [substance] be employed, or should [the rite] be completed with that very substitute? What is the prima facie view? The heard [substance] should be employed, even when [the process] has commenced. As stated: 'For the availability [makes the substitute unnecessary], because of the absence of that [principal].' Therefore the substitute should not be employed.

children.text: nānarthakatvāt//6.3.37//
children.translated_text: No, because of purposelessness. // MS_6,3.37 //

children.text: naitad evam, yena hi khadirābhāve kadare paśur niyukto bhavati, atha khadiram upalabhate, pravṛtte 'rthe kiṃ khadireṇa kuryāt? arthārthaṃ hi khadiropādānaṃ na khadiropādānārtham eva. tasmān na śrutam upādīyeta.
children.translated_text: This is not so — for when, in the absence of <s>khadira</s>, the animal has been tied to a <s>kadara</s> [wood], and then one obtains <s>khadira</s> — while the matter is already in progress, what would one do with the <s>khadira</s>? For the employment of <s>khadira</s> is for the purpose of accomplishing the [ritual] purpose, not for the purpose of employing <s>khadira</s> [as such]. Therefore the heard [substance] should not be employed.

children.text: dravyasaṃskāravirodhe dravyaṃ tadarthatvāt//6.3.38//
children.translated_text: In a conflict between substance and refinement, [one should prefer] the substance, because of [the refinements'] being for that purpose. // MS_6,3.38 //

children.text:
pravṛtte paśukarmaṇi, yūpakāle 'sti mahat kadaraṃ dravyaṃ takṣaṇādisaṃskārakṣamam, asti khadiradravyam anevaṃjātīyakam. tatra kim upādeyam iti. saṃskārā na parilopsyanta iti kadara upādīyeteti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, dravyasaṃskāravirodhe dravyaṃ praty ādriyeran, na saṃskārān. kutaḥ? tadarthatvāt, saṃskārā hi dravyaṃ karmayogyaṃ kurvanti. tatra saṃskāraparilope dravyam api tāvad gṛhyate, dravyābhāve na dravyam, na saṃskārāḥ. dravyaṃ teṣāṃ dvāram, vacanaprāmā[672]{*5/446*}ṇyāt, tadabhāve naṣṭadvāraṃ nāpūrvaṃ gaccheyuḥ. tasmāt khadiram upādadīrann iti.
NOTES:
*{5/446: E2: 5,266; E6: 2,152}*
children.translated_text:
While an animal rite is in progress, at the time for the post (<s>yūpa</s>), there is a large piece of <s>kadara</s> wood capable of the refinements of carving etc., and there is <s>khadira</s> wood not of that [suitable] kind. There, which should be employed? [The prima facie view:] the <s>kadara</s> should be employed [so that] the refinements are not lost.
Given this prima facie view, we say: in a conflict between substance and refinement, one should attend to the substance, not the refinements. Why? Because of [the refinements'] being for that [substance's] purpose — for the refinements make the substance fit for the ritual act. There, when refinements are lost, the substance is still taken; in the absence of the substance, there is neither substance nor refinements. The substance is the door for those [refinements]; [672] because of the authority of the [Vedic] statement, in its absence, [the refinements], having lost their door, would not achieve the unseen [merit]. Therefore one should employ the <s>khadira</s>.

children.text: arthadravyavirodhe 'rtho dravyābhāve tadutpatter dravyāṇām arthaśeṣatvāt//6.3.39//
children.translated_text: In a conflict between purpose and substance, [one should prefer] the purpose — because the substitute arises in the absence of the substance; because substances are subsidiary to the purpose. // MS_6,3.39 //

children.text: asti yūpakāle khadiralatā paśor aprāgalbhye{*5/447*} na samarthāḥ{*5/448*}, kadaradravyaṃ tu tatsamartham. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim upādeyaṃ khadiradravyam, uta kadaradravyam iti. khadiradravyam ity āha, tad dhi śrutam, tadupādānaḥ śāstravihitaṃ karoti, pratinidhāv aśrutakārī syāt. tasmān na pratinidhātavyam iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, arthadravyavirodhe 'rthaṃ praty ādartavyam, tadarthaṃ hi dravyopādānaṃ niyojanāt, aprāgalabhyaṃ paśor bhaviṣyatīti, na dravyam evopādīyeteti, kadaram upādadāno dravyaśrutiṃ bādhate. arthaṃ tv anugṛhṇāti, khadiralatām upādadāna ubhayaṃ bādhate. tasmāt kadaradravyam upādeyam, dravyābhāve hi tadutpattiḥ, pratinidher utpattir{*5/449*} uktā, dravyāṇy arthaṃ prati śeṣabhūtāni.
children.translated_text: At the time for the post, there are <s>khadira</s> creepers, [but they are] not capable [of bearing] the animal's weight; but <s>kadara</s> wood is capable of that. There a doubt [arises]: should <s>khadira</s> wood be employed, or <s>kadara</s>? [The prima facie view:] <s>khadira</s> wood — for that is heard; by employing it one does what is enjoined by scripture; in a substitute one would be doing what is not heard. Therefore the substitute should not be employed. Given this prima facie view, we say: in a conflict between purpose and substance, one should attend to the purpose — for the employment of substances is for that purpose [of accomplishing the ritual goal], because of the injunction 'there will be inability [to hold] the animal.' It is not [the case] that the substance alone should be employed. One employing <s>kadara</s> overrides the [Vedic] statement about substance, but supports the purpose. One employing <s>khadira</s> creepers overrides both. Therefore <s>kadara</s> wood should be employed — for the substitute arises in the absence of substance; the arising of the substitute has been stated; substances are subsidiary to the purpose.

children.text: vidhir apy ekadeśo syāt//6.3.40//
children.translated_text: The injunction too [prescribes] only a part. // MS_6,3.40 //

children.text: santi vrīhayaḥ, yāvanto dvyavadānamātraṃ nirvartayanti, tathā santi nīvārāḥ śeṣakāryāṇām api paryāptāḥ, tatra kim upādeyam iti. kiṃ prāptam? apy ekadeśe dvyava[673]{*5/450*}dānamātre 'pi nirvartyamāne pratinidhir upādeyaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam? śeṣakāryāṇāṃ saṃpattir bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: There are rice grains — [enough for] just the two cuttings (<s>dvyavadāna</s>) [to be completed]; likewise there are wild rice (<s>nīvāra</s>) sufficient for the remaining operations as well. There, which should be employed? What is the prima facie view? Even when only a part — [672] the two cuttings alone — can be accomplished, the substitute should be employed. What is the reason? The accomplishment of the remaining operations will result.

children.text: api vārthasya śakyatvād ekadeśena{*5/451*} nirvartetārthānām avibhaktatvād guṇamātram itarat tadarthatvāt//6.3.41//
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the possibility of accomplishing the purpose, with a partial [quantity the principal should] accomplish [the main rite]; because purposes are undivided, the other is merely a subsidiary, because of [its] being for that purpose. // MS_6,3.41 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. ekadeśena vrīhīṇāṃ pradhānamātraṃ nirvartayitavyam. kutaḥ? arthasya śakyatvāt, yo 'trārthaḥ, yena kāryaṃ tat tāvat nirvartyate, śeṣakāryāṇi yadi na śakyāni, nāṅgānurodhena pradhānasya guṇo bādhitavyaḥ. tad dhy aṅgam, yat pradhānasyopakaroti, na yad apakāre vartate. tatra ca śeṣakāryāṇi kriyamāṇāni pradhāne vrīhitvaṃ guṇaṃ vihanyuḥ. vrīhitvaṃ ca pradhāne sākṣād aṅgabhūtaṃ śrūyate, vrīhibhir yajeteti. tasmān na teṣv anurodhaḥ kāryaḥ, asati hy aṅgapradhānavibhāga{*5/452*} etad evaṃ syāt, asti hy asau. tasmān na pratinidhir iti. tathā cānyārthadarśanam api bhavati, tad eva yādṛk tādṛg hotavyam iti.
children.translated_text: The words '<s>api vā</s>' reverse the position. With a partial [quantity of] rice, only the principal [rite] should be accomplished. Why? Because of the possibility of accomplishing the purpose — whatever purpose exists here, whatever the task [requires] — that much is accomplished. If the remaining operations are not possible, the subsidiary (<s>guṇa</s>) of the principal [rite] should not be overridden for the sake of conforming to subsidiaries. For that is a subsidiary which assists the principal, not that which works to its detriment. And those remaining operations, when performed, would destroy the rice-nature (<s>vrīhitva</s>) — a quality — of the principal. And rice-nature is directly heard as a subsidiary in the principal: 'he should sacrifice with rice.' Therefore no conformity should be made to those [remaining operations] — for this [argument] would apply if there were no distinction between subsidiary and principal; but there is such [a distinction]. Therefore no substitute [is needed]. And there is also an observation for another purpose: 'that very [substance], of whatever quality it is, should be offered.'

children.text: Adhyāya 6:
children.translated_text: Chapter 6:

children.text: śeṣād dvyavadānanāśe syāt tadarthatvāt // MS_6,4.1 //
children.translated_text: When the two-cut portion is destroyed, it should [be taken] from the remainder, because of [the sacrifice] being for that purpose. // MS_6,4.1 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate: yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ vācuyato{*6/2*} bhavati{*6/3*} iti. tatra yadi dvyavadānamātram uddhṛtaṃ vyāpadyate, kiṃ śeṣāt punar avadeyam, neti bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ prāptam. dvyavadānanāśe, śeṣāt punar avadeyam. kutaḥ? tadarthatvāt, agnyarthaṃ hi tad dhaviḥ, agnaye yāgo nirvartayitavya iti, tadavadāne vinaṣṭe yāgaḥ kartavya{*6/4*} evāvatiṣṭhate, prayojanaṃ ca yāgena. sa cāgneyena kriyamāṇaḥ śruta evābhinirvartito bhavatīti kim iti na kriyeta. tasmāc cheṣād avadātavyam iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard: 'If the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-potsherd [cake] on the new-moon or full-moon day falls off.' There, if only the two-cut portion that has been extracted perishes, is [a fresh portion] to be taken again from the remainder, or not? — this is the doubt. What is the prima facie view? When the two-cut portion perishes, [a fresh one] should be taken from the remainder. Why? Because of [the sacrifice] being for that purpose — for that oblation is for <s>Agni</s>'s purpose; the sacrifice to <s>Agni</s> is to be accomplished. When that [two-cut] portion perishes, the sacrifice still remains to be done, and the purpose is [accomplished] through the sacrifice. And when it is performed as <s>Āgneya</s>, it is accomplished exactly as heard — why then should it not be done? Therefore [a fresh portion] should be taken from the remainder.

NOTES:
[{6/2: E1,6; E2: <s>cācyuto</s>}]
[{6/3: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.3.3}]
[{6/4: E2 (v.l.): <s>kartavyety</s>}]

children.text: nirdeśād vānyad āgamayet // MS_6,4.2 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of the [specific] designation, another [substance] should be brought. // MS_6,4.2 //

children.text:
atha vānyad dhavir āgamayen na śeṣād avadātavyam. kutaḥ. nirdeśāt, nirdeśo hi bhavati, madhyāt pūrvārdhād avadeyam iti, dvyavadānaṃ ca homasaṃbaddham{*6/5*}, dvyavadānaṃ juhotīti. tatrānyac chiṣṭaṃ madhyasya pūrvārdhasya viśeṣaṇārtham. yac ca tad dhomasaṃyuktaṃ tadvinaṣṭam, tac cheṣeṇa kriyamāṇam amadhyenāpūrvārdhena ca kṛtaṃ syāt. nanv avatte yac chiṣṭaṃ tato madhyāt pūrvārdhāc ca grahīṣyate. ucyate, kṛtsnasya yat madhyaṃ pūrvārdhaṃ ca tac coditam, na itarasya.
atha vā nirdeśād iti, vinaṣṭe hy anyad dravyaṃ nirdiśyate, yasya sarvāṇi havīṃṣi naśyeyur duṣyeyur vāpahareyur vā[675]{*6/6*}ājyena tā devatāḥ parisaṃkhyāya yajerann iti, haviṣo nāśa ājyaṃ prāptam. tena na śeṣād avadātavyam iti.
apara āha, śeṣanirdeśād iti, nirdiśyate hi tac chiṣṭam aparebhyaḥ śeṣakāryebhya iti. tan nopapadyate, na hi tāni śeṣakāryāṇi havīṃṣi prayojayanti, na cānivṛttaprayojanaṃ havir anyatra pratipādyam. tasmān nāyam arthaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Or rather, another oblation should be brought — [the portion] should not be taken from the remainder. Why? Because of the designation — for there is a designation: 'from the middle, from the upper half it should be taken.' And the two-cut portion is connected with the offering: 'he offers the two-cut portion.' There, the remainder is for the purpose of qualifying 'the middle' and 'the upper half.' What is connected with the offering has perished — if that is done with the remainder, it would be done with what is not the middle and not the upper half. But [the objector says]: when it is cut [from the remainder], it will be taken from the middle and upper half [of the remainder]. We reply: what is enjoined is the middle and upper half of the whole, not of the other [remainder].
Alternatively, 'because of the designation' means: when [the portion] perishes, another substance is designated — 'He whose oblations all perish, become spoiled, or are stolen — [675] with ghee he should enumerate those deities and sacrifice.' When the oblation is destroyed, ghee is [the prescribed substitute]. Therefore [a fresh portion] should not be taken from the remainder.
Another says: 'because of the designation regarding the remainder' — for that remainder is designated for other remainder-purposes. This is not appropriate, for those remainder-purposes do not require the oblations [again]; and an oblation whose purpose has not been fulfilled should not be employed elsewhere. Therefore this is not the meaning.

children.text: api vā śeṣabhājāṃ syād viśiṣṭakāraṇatvāt // MS_6,4.3 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, it should [result in] the omission of what shares in the remainder, because of [there being] a distinguishing cause. // MS_6,4.3 //

children.text:
atha sviṣṭakṛd artham avattaṃ yadi vinaśyati, tatra kiṃ śeṣād avadeyam uta neti. kiṃ prāptam? punaḥ śeṣād avadeyam iti. kutaḥ? nātra kṛtsnasyottarārdhād avadīyate{*6/7*}. kasya tarhi? saṃnihitasya, sati hi prayojane saṃnihitasyāvadeyam iti, tasmād{*6/8*} avadīyamāne śrutaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati. tasmāt śeṣād avadeyam iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, śeṣabhājāṃ syāl lopaḥ. kutaḥ? viśiṣṭakāraṇāt, viśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ tasyāvadāne, kathaṃ pratipādyeteti. pratipattiś ca viviktakaraṇenopakaroti, tasya viviktakaraṇāya pratipādyamānasya niyamo 'yaṃ sviṣṭakṛd dhomena pratipādayitavyaḥ. tathā hi sa pratipādito bhavati. sa yadi homāyoddhṛto vipadyeta, kṛte viveke na punar grahaṇaṃ prayojayet, pratipādyamānaś ca sviṣṭakṛd dhomena pratipādayitavya iti. pratipādyamānābhāvāl lopa eva sviṣṭakṛtaḥ syāt, pradhāne kṛte śiṣṭaṃ [676]{*6/9*} sarvaśeṣakāryasādhāraṇam. tatraikasyoddhṛtau śiṣṭam anyatra pratipādanīyam.
children.translated_text:
Now, if the [portion] cut for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> purpose perishes — should [a fresh one] be taken from the remainder, or not? What is the prima facie view? It should be taken again from the remainder. Why? Here it is not taken from the upper half of the whole. Of what then? Of what is proximate — when there is a purpose, it should be taken from what is proximate. Therefore when it is taken [from what is proximate], the heard [procedure] is fulfilled. Therefore it should be taken from the remainder.
Given this prima facie view, we say: there should be an omission of what shares in the remainder [i.e., the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>]. Why? Because of a distinguishing cause — for there is a distinguishing cause for its cutting: how should it be disposed of? And the disposal is assisted by [its being] from a distinguished [source]. For that [oblation] being disposed of by a distinguished [method] — this restriction is: 'it is to be disposed of through the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> offering.' For thus it is properly disposed of. If, having been extracted for offering, it perishes — when the distinguishing [procedure] has been done, there is no purpose in taking again. But the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is to be disposed of through offering — when what is being disposed of is absent, [676] there should simply be omission of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>. When the principal [offering] has been done, the remainder is common to all remainder-purposes. When one [portion] has been extracted, the remainder is to be employed for other [purposes].

children.text: nirdeśāc cheṣabhakṣo 'nyaiḥ pradhānavat // MS_6,4.4 //
children.translated_text: Because of the designation, the eating of the remainder [should be done] by others, as with the principal [offering]. // MS_6,4.4 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatra bhakṣāḥ{*6/10*} prāśitracaturdhākaraṇaśaṃyuvākakālāḥ. teṣu saṃdehaḥ, kim anya eva teṣāṃ bhakṣayitāraḥ, uta prakaraṇagatā iti{*6/11*}. kiṃ prāptam? śeṣabhakṣo 'nyair aprakaraṇasthaiḥ kartavyaḥ. kutaḥ? nirdeśāt, nirdiśyante{*6/12*} hy adhvaryādaya iḍābhakṣe, yajamānapañcamā iḍāṃ bhakṣayantīti. sarveṣu bhakṣayitṛṣu{*6/13*} prāpteṣu parisaṃkhyānārtho nirdeśaḥ kriyate. iḍām evaite bhakṣayeyur iti, yathāgneyo 'ṣṭākapāla{*6/14*} iti sarvasminn avayavini yāgāniyame prāpte dvyavadānamātraṃ śrūyate, vidhir vā na{*6/15*}, prāptatvāt, nānuvādo 'narthakatvāt, parisaṃkhyā tv arthavattāya, evam eṣāṃ parisaṃkhyeti. api ca yadi prakṛtā eva bhakṣayeyuḥ, aśvamedhe doṣaḥ syāt, bahutvād bhakṣāṇām, bhakṣayanto mriyeran.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites]. There, the ritual eatings (<s>bhakṣas</s>) [occur at the time of] the <s>prāśitra</s> (fore-portion), the <s>caturdhākaraṇa</s> (fourfold division), and the <s>śaṃyuvāka</s> (recitation). Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: are the eaters of these [portions] persons other [than those in the ritual context], or those present in the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>)? What is the prima facie view? The eating of the remainder should be done by others — those not present in the context. Why? Because of the designation — for the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and others are designated in the <s>Iḍā</s>-eating: 'The sacrificer as fifth, they eat the <s>Iḍā</s>.' When all eaters are [already] obtained, the designation is made for the purpose of exclusive enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>) — 'only these should eat the <s>Iḍā</s>.' Just as 'the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-potsherd [cake]' — when all parts of the oblation are obtained without restriction, only the two-cut portion is heard — whether it is an injunction or not, it is not [an injunction] because [the whole] is already obtained; nor is it a restatement because that would be purposeless; but it is an exclusive enumeration for the sake of meaningfulness. Similarly here, this is an exclusive enumeration. Moreover, if those present in the context alone were to eat, there would be a fault in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) — because of the multiplicity of eatings, the eaters would die.
