children.text: sarvair vā samavāyāt syāt // MS_6,4.5 //
children.translated_text: Or [it should be done] by all, because of being an assembly. // MS_6,4.5 //

children.text: sarvair vā prakṛtair eva bhakṣyeta. tad dhi bhakṣaṇaṃ puruṣasaṃskārārtham, puruṣāḥ saṃskṛtāḥ pracariṣyantīti. teṣu vinigamanāyā abhāvād yāvantaḥ prakaraṇe samavetāḥ, te sarve bhakṣayeyur iti.
children.translated_text: Or it should be eaten by all those present in the context. For that eating is for the purpose of consecrating the persons — the persons, having been consecrated, will proceed [with the ritual]. In the absence of a determining [factor] among them, as many as are assembled in the context — all of them should eat.

children.text: nirdeśasya guṇārthatvam // MS_6,4.6 //
children.translated_text: The designation is for the purpose of a subsidiary. // MS_6,4.6 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, nirdeśād{*6/16*} iti, guṇārthaḥ saḥ, anye karma[677]{*6/17*}karatvād eva prāptāḥ, tatra yajamānas teṣāṃ pañcamo vacanāt nirdiśyate. tatprāptyarthaṃ cedaṃ vacanam. tato na parisaṃkhyā.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'because of the designation' — that is for a subsidiary purpose. The others [i.e., the <s>Adhvaryu</s> etc.] are already obtained by virtue of being ritual agents. [677] There, the sacrificer is designated as their fifth, by the [Vedic] statement. This statement is for the purpose of obtaining him [as a participant]. Therefore it is not an exclusive enumeration.

children.text: pradhāne śrutilakṣaṇam // MS_6,4.7 //
children.translated_text: In the principal [offering], [the rule] is characterized by the [Vedic] text. // MS_6,4.7 //

children.text: yat tu dvyavadānamātraṃ pradhāne nirdiśyate, tad vacanaprāmāṇyāt parisaṃkhyānārtham. na hi tatra kasyacid apūrvasya vidhiḥ, iha yajamāno vidhīyate, vidhiparisaṃkhyāsaṃśaye vidhir jyāyān. tatra svārthe śabdaḥ, parisaṃkhyāyāṃ trayo doṣāḥ, svārthahānam, asvārthaparigrahaḥ, prāptabādhaś ceti. tasmāt prākṛtā eva bhakṣayeyur iti.
children.translated_text: But the two-cut portion alone that is designated in the principal [offering] — that is for the purpose of exclusive enumeration, because of the authority of the [Vedic] statement. For there is no injunction of anything unprecedented there; here [in the Iḍā context] the sacrificer is being enjoined [as a participant]. And in a doubt between injunction and exclusive enumeration, the injunction is stronger. There, the word is in its own meaning; in an exclusive enumeration, there are three faults: abandonment of one's own meaning, acceptance of another's meaning, and overriding of what is [already] obtained. Therefore those present in the context alone should eat.

children.text: arthavad iti cet // MS_6,4.8 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that there would be a purpose [for exclusive enumeration] — // MS_6,4.8 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, aśvamedhe virodhaḥ syāt, bahutvād bhakṣāṇām{*6/18*} iti, tat parihartavyam//
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> there would be a contradiction, because of the multiplicity of eatings' — that must be refuted.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/18: Vgl. Ś ad MS 6.4.4}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/18: Cf. commentary on MS 6.4.4}]

children.text: na codanāvirodhāt // MS_6,4.9 //
children.translated_text: No, because there is no conflict with the injunction. // MS_6,4.9 //

children.text: aśvamedhe na sarvaṃ bakṣayiṣyanti, arthāt sarvaṃ bhakṣayanto 'śvamedhaṃ na samāpayeyuḥ. tatrāśvamedhaśrutiḥ pratyakṣā, sā virudhyamānā codakaprāptaṃ sarvabhakṣaṇaṃ bādhate. prakṛtau tu na virodhaḥ. tasmāt sarvaṃ prakṛtā bhakṣayeyur iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, they will not eat everything — from the meaning, [if] eating everything, they would not complete the <s>Aśvamedha</s>. There, the directly perceived <s>Aśvamedha</s> text, being contradicted, overrides the eating of everything obtained through the [general] injunction. But in the basic rite (<s>prakṛti</s>), there is no contradiction. Therefore all those present in the context should eat everything.

children.text: arthasamavāyāt prāyaścittam ekadeśe 'pi // MS_6,4.10 //
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with the meaning, the atonement (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) [applies] even when [only] a part [is damaged]. // MS_6,4.10 //

children.text: sto darśapūrṇamāsau, tatrāmananti, bhinne juhoti, skanne juhotīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ kṛtsne bhinne skanne ca [678]{*6/19*} prāyaścittam, utaikadeśe 'pi bhinne skanne ceti. kiṃ punaḥ sarvabhinnam, kim ekadeśabhinnam iti, cūrṇīkṛtam ayogyaṃ prayojanāya, kṛtsnabhinnam{*6/20*}. yac chakale vigate 'pi prayojanasamartham, tad ekadeśabhinnam iti. kiṃ prāptam. ekadeśabhinne 'pi prāyaścittam. kasmāt. arthasamavāyāt, samavetaṃ tatra bhedanam, ekadeśabhinnam api bhinnam iti, evaṃ prāpte nimitte naimittikaṃ kartavyaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: There are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites]. There they state: 'When [the cake] is broken, he offers; when [the ghee] is spilled, he offers.' There a doubt [arises]: is the atonement [required] when the whole is broken or spilled, [678] or even when [only] a part is broken or spilled? What constitutes 'wholly broken' versus 'partially broken'? What is pulverized and unfit for purpose — that is wholly broken. What, even with a piece missing, is still capable of serving the purpose �� that is partially broken. What is the prima facie view? Even when partially broken, there is an atonement. Why? Because of the connection with the meaning — 'breaking' is connected [with the concept]; what is even partially broken is indeed broken. When the occasion thus arises, the occasional [rite] must be performed.

children.text: na tv aśeṣe vaiguṇyāt tadarthaṃ hi // MS_6,4.11 //
children.translated_text: But not when [it is broken] entirely, because of deficiency — for [the atonement] is for that [oblation's] purpose. // MS_6,4.11 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. nāśeṣe bhinne{*6/21*} prāyaścittaṃ syāt. vinaṣṭasaṃskārārthaṃ hi prāyaścittam. kutaḥ. etad bhedanavatā prayojanam asti, na homena, tena saṃskṛtena{*6/22*} prayogaḥ kariṣyanta iti prāyaścittaṃ kriyate. na ca, tena cūrṇīkṛtena prayogaḥ śakyate kartum. tasmāt prāyaścittam anarthakam. ekadeśabhinnena tu saṃskṛtena śakyate prayogaḥ, tasmād ekadeśabhinne prāyaścittaṃ syād iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>tu</s> ('but') reverses the position. When [the oblation is] entirely broken, there should be no atonement. For the atonement is for the purpose of consecrating what has perished [i.e., restoring it]. Why? The one that possesses breaking has this purpose — not [merely] by the offering [of atonement]. [Rather], the consecrated [oblation] will be employed — for this [reason] the atonement is performed. But when it is pulverized, the employment cannot be done. Therefore the atonement is purposeless. But with what is only partially broken, the consecrated [oblation] can be employed. Therefore the atonement should be [performed only] when partially broken.

children.text:

children.text: syād vā prāptanimittatvād ataddharmo nityasaṃyogān na hi tasya guṇārthenānityatvāt // MS_6,4.12 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, there would be [atonement even when wholly broken], because of the occasion having arisen — [the atonement] does not have its character [defined by that oblation]; because of the invariable connection [of the atonement with breaking]; for [the offering] is not for the purpose of a subsidiary, because of [its] being occasional. // MS_6,4.12 //

children.text: syād vā prāyaścittam, kṛtsnabhinne 'pi. kutaḥ. prāptanimittatvāt, prāptaṃ hi nimittaṃ bhedanam, prāpte ca nimitte naimittikaṃ kartavyam. yac ca uktam, vyāpannasaṃskārārthaṃ prāyaścittam iti, nāyaṃ tasya dharmaḥ. kutaḥ. nityasaṃyogāt, nityavad dhomaḥ. anityaṃ hi bhedanam, na hi nityam anityasyopakartuṃ codyate. yadi nityaṃ darśapūrṇamāsayor aṅgaṃ nānityasyopakārāya. kutaḥ. kadācid anityaṃ naiva syāt, tatra kathaṃ tasyopakārakaṃ bhavet. tatra ko doṣaḥ. na śakyaṃ [679]{*6/23*} nityenopakartum{*6/24*}, tena nityam upakuryād iti vacanaṃ pralāpa eva. atha naimittikam, na doṣo bhavati. tasmād asmatpakṣa eva. asmin pakṣe yadā bhinnam, tadā homaḥ. yadā na bhinnam, tadā naiva homo vidhīyate. bhavadīye pakṣe bhavati doṣaḥ, nityānityayor nāsti saṃbandha iti. tasmāt bhinnamātre prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: Or rather, there should be atonement even when wholly broken. Why? Because the occasion has arisen — for breaking is the occasion that has arisen, and when an occasion arises, the occasional [rite] must be performed. As for what was said — 'the atonement is for the purpose of consecrating what has perished' — that is not its character. Why? Because of the invariable connection — the offering [of atonement] is like a permanent [obligation]. For breaking is occasional [i.e., not permanent]; and a permanent [rite] is not enjoined to serve the purpose of an occasional [event]. If [the atonement] were a permanent subsidiary of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it would not be for the benefit of an occasional [event]. Why? Because the occasional [event] sometimes simply does not occur — in that case, how could [the atonement] be its benefactor? What is the fault in [the other view]? It would not be possible [679] for a permanent [rite] to benefit [an occasional event]; therefore the statement 'one should permanently benefit by it' would be mere babble. But if [the atonement is] occasional, there is no fault. Therefore our position alone [is correct]. On this view, when [the oblation] is broken, there is the offering; when it is not broken, the offering is simply not enjoined. On your view, there is a fault — that there is no connection between the permanent and the occasional. Therefore the atonement [applies] upon mere breaking.

children.text: guṇānāṃ ca parārthatvād vacanād{*6/25*} vyapāśrayaḥ syāt // MS_6,4.13 //
children.translated_text: And because of subsidiaries being for another's purpose, [there is] recourse to [another substance] because of the [Vedic] statement. // MS_6,4.13 //

children.text: asti vacane na guṇo guṇārtho bhavitum arhati{*6/26*}, prakaraṇataḥ sarvaṃ pradhānārtham. bhinnam api homo 'pi, na ca bhinnam ādhārabhāvenopadiśyate. bhinnasyādhārabhāve hi na homāntaraṃ vidhīyeta. pradhānasyaiva hi tadā bhinno guṇa iti gamyate. tatrāhavanīyasaṃyogo bādhyeta. vacanād vikalpa iti cet. na, nimittatvena saṃbhavāt, homasya ca śrutyā vihitatvāt. yadā homo vidhīyate, tadā śrutyā, yadā bhinno guṇaḥ, tadā vākyena. tasmān nādhāro bhinnaḥ. yady ucyeta, nimittapakṣe 'pi na homāntaram, prakṛtasyaiva homasya nimittaṃ vidhīyeteti. tan na, anupādīyamānaṃ hi nimittam ity ucyate. yadi hi vidhīyeta, nimittam eva tan na syāt. yadi ca yasyāpi nimittaṃ so 'py uddiśyeta, tatra dvayor uddiśyamānayoḥ saṃbandha eva na syāt. na cātra bhedanaṃ kuryād iti vidhīyate. bhedane nirvṛtte yad anyac chrūyate, tad vidhīyate.
children.translated_text: When there is a [Vedic] statement, a subsidiary cannot serve the purpose of another subsidiary. From the context, everything serves the purpose of the principal. The oblation too is separate [from the principal], even though it is also an oblation; but the separate [oblation] is not instructed as having the function of a vessel. For if the broken [potsherd] had the function of a vessel, another oblation would not be enjoined [as a remedy]. For then it would be understood that the broken [potsherd] is merely a subsidiary of the principal. In that case, the connection with the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] would be contradicted. [If one argues:] the alternative is from the [Vedic] statement — [we reply:] no, because it is possible as an occasion [for an expiatory rite], and because the oblation is enjoined by the [Vedic] word. When the oblation is enjoined, it is by the [Vedic] word; when the broken [potsherd] is a subsidiary, it is by the sentence. Therefore the vessel [i.e., potsherd] is not [the one that is] broken [and yet still used]. If it were said that even on the view of it being an occasion, there is no separate oblation — that the occasion of the oblation already established [in the basic rite] is [merely] being enjoined — that is not so. For what is not adopted [as a cause] is called an 'occasion.' For if it were enjoined [as a cause], it would not be an occasion at all. And if the one for whom it is an occasion were also designated [as a cause], then when both are designated, there would be no connection at all. And here it is not being enjoined 'he should break [the potsherd].' When the breaking has occurred, what else is heard [as a prescription] — that is what is enjoined.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/25: E1,6; E2 om. vacanād}*
*{6/26: E2 (v.l.): na guṇā guṇārthā bhavitum arhanti}*

children.translated_text: And it would be purposeless in [the case of] total destruction. // MS_6,4.16 //

children.text: sarvanāśe ca śrūyate, bhinnaṃ kapālam apsu pravahantīti{*6/31*}, tatrānarthakaḥ saṃskāraḥ. nanu tata uddhṛtyopadhāyiṣyate. neti brūmaḥ, anyad upadadhātīti hy āmananti. tasān naimittikaṃ karmāṅgaṃ bhinne juhotīti.
children.translated_text: And in [the case of] total destruction it is heard: 'They float away the broken potsherd in water.' In that case, the consecration [of joining] would be purposeless. [The objector says:] but [the pieces] would be retrieved from the water and placed [back]. We reply: no — for they record 'He places another [potsherd].' Therefore the occasional rite — the subsidiary 'when broken, he offers' — [applies].

children.text: kṣāme tu sarvadāhe syād ekadeśasyāvarjanīyatvāt // MS_6,4.17 //
children.translated_text: But in [the case of] charring, it should be [the expiation for] total burning, because a partial [burning] is unavoidable. // MS_6,4.17 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, atha yasya puroḍāśau kṣāyatas taṃ yajñaṃ varuṇo gṛhṇāti. yadā tad dhaviḥ saṃtiṣṭheta, atha tad eva havir nirvapet. yajño hi yajñasya prāyaścittir iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ sarvakṣāme prāyaścittam, utaikadeśakṣāma iti. kiṃ prāptam. prāptanimittatvāt kṛtsne vaikadeśe vā. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, kṣāme tu sarvadāhe syād iti. tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati, kṣāme sarvadāhe prāyaścittaṃ syāt. kutaḥ. ekadeśasyāvarjanīyatvāt, na śakyata{*6/32*} ekadeśakṣāmatā{*6/33*} varjayitum. niyatam agnisaṃyoge dāhyasya sūkṣmā{*6/34*} avayavāḥ kṣīyante. tapteṣu ca [681]{*6/35*} kapāleṣv adhaḥ pākārthaṃ puroḍāśo 'dhiśrīyate, upari cāṅgārā abhyuhyante, tad avarjanīyam. nimittatvenāpi śrūyamāṇaṃ nityam eva syāt. tatra yasyeti nimittaśravaṇaṃ vivakṣitaṃ syāt. tasmāt sarvakṣāme prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: 'Whose <s>puroḍāśas</s> (cakes) get charred — <s>Varuṇa</s> seizes that sacrifice. When that oblation is restored, then he should offer that very oblation [again]. For sacrifice is the expiation of [a faulty] sacrifice.' There a doubt [arises]: is the expiatory rite for total charring, or for partial charring? What is the prima facie view? Because the occasion has arrived, [it applies] in either total or partial [charring]. Given this prima facie view, we say: charring [here means] in [the case of] total burning. The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [previous] position. The expiatory rite should be in [the case of] total burning. Why? Because a partial [burning] is unavoidable — it is not possible to avoid partial charring. Necessarily, when there is contact with fire, the fine particles of what is to be cooked diminish. And when the potsherds are heated, the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is placed on top for cooking, and embers are heaped above — this is unavoidable. Even though heard as an occasion, it would become obligatory [if applied to every partial burning]. There, the hearing of 'whose' as an occasion would have been intended [for a specific, noteworthy event]. Therefore the expiatory rite is for total charring.

children.text: darśanād vaikadeśe syāt // MS_6,4.18 //
children.translated_text: Because of the observation [of partial charring in the text], it should [apply] even in partial [charring]. // MS_6,4.18 //

children.text: na caitad asti, sarvadāhe prāyaścittam iti, ekadeśe kṣāyati bhavitum arhati. nimittaṃ hy upasaṃprāptaṃ{*6/36*} kṣāṇaṃ nāma. ekadeśakṣāṇam api kṣāṇam eva. yadi tatra na kriyate, śrutaṃ na kriyeta. na caitad yuktam. api ca darśayati, yadā tad dhaviḥ saṃtiṣtheta{*6/37*}, athaitad{*6/38*} eva havir nirvaped iti, tenaiva haviṣā saṃsthānaṃ darśayati. tat sarvakṣāṇe nāvakalpate. tasmād ekadeśa eva kṣāyati prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that the expiatory rite is [only] for total burning. It should [apply] when a part is charred. For the occasion that has arrived is charring (<s>kṣāṇa</s>) by name. Even partial charring is charring indeed. If [the expiation] is not performed there, what is heard [as prescribed] would not be performed — and that is not proper. Moreover, [the text] shows: 'When that oblation is restored' — it shows the completion with that very oblation. This does not fit [the case of] total charring. Therefore the expiatory rite is [applicable] when even a part is charred.

children.text: anyena vaitac chāstrād dhi kāraṇaprāptiḥ // MS_6,4.19 //
children.translated_text: Or, [the completion is possible] by means of another [substance] — for it is from the scripture that the cause is obtained. // MS_6,4.19 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti, yad uktam, ekadeśe 'pi kṣāyati{*6/39*} prāyaścittam iti, kiṃ tarhi. kṛtsnakṣāma eva prāyaścittam. upasaṃprāptaṃ hi nimittam, yac chāstroktaṃ puroḍāśau kṣāyata iti, kṛtsnasya kṣātir{*6/40*} nāvayavasya. na caikadeśakṣāme, tasyāvarjanīyatvāt. atha yad uktam, kṣāmeṇa haviṣā samāptir dṛśyate, yadā tad dhaviḥ saṃtiṣṭheteti. ucyate, saṃsthāne nimitte prāyaścittam. yadāpy anyenāpi haviṣā tat saṃsthāpyate, tadāpi prāyaścittam iti na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. This is not so — what was said, 'the expiatory rite is even when a part is charred.' Rather, the expiatory rite is only for total charring. For the occasion that has arrived is what the scripture states — 'whose <s>puroḍāśas</s> get charred' — the charring of the whole, not of a part. And there is no [special occasion for] partial charring, because of its unavoidability. Now, as to what was said — 'the completion is seen with the charred oblation: when that oblation is restored' — we reply: the expiatory rite [is performed] upon completion. Even when the sacrifice is completed with another oblation, even then the expiatory rite [applies] — so there is no defect.

children.text: taddhaviḥśabdān neti cet // MS_6,4.20 //
children.translated_text: 'Because of the word "that oblation"' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_6,4.20 //

children.text: evaṃ ced ucyate, anyena haviṣā yadā saṃsthāpyata iti. naivam. taddhaviḥśabdāt, taddhaviḥśabdo 'tra bhavati. yadā taddhaviḥ saṃtiṣṭheteti. atrānyena haviṣā saṃsthāpyamāne taddhaviḥśabdo nāvakalpyeteti.
children.translated_text: If it is said thus — 'even when completed with another oblation' — that is not so. Because of the word 'that oblation' (<s>tad haviḥ</s>) — the word 'that oblation' occurs here: 'When that oblation is restored.' If the completion were with another oblation, the word 'that oblation' would not be possible.

children.text: syād anyāyatvād{*6/42*} ijyāgāmī haviḥśabdas talliṅgasaṃyogāt // MS_6,4.21 //
children.translated_text: The word '<s>havis</s>' (oblation) would [here] refer to the sacrifice, because of the connection with its indicatory mark — [this is] because it would be improper [otherwise]. // MS_6,4.21 //

children.text: syād ijyāgāmī{*6/43*} haviḥśabdaḥ. taddhaviḥ saṃtiṣṭheta taddhaviṣka karma saṃtiṣṭheteti{*6/44*}. nanu mukhyābhāve gauṇo gṛhyate, nānyatheti. ucyate, mukhyābhāva evāyam. katham. yadā saṃtiṣṭheta, tat karma tena haviṣeti vākyaṃ bhidyeta. avācakaṃ ca syāt. karmaiva hi saṃtiṣṭhate, na haviḥ, tena nimittam{*6/45*}. tad dhavir ity anuvādaḥ. anuvādaś ced anyahaviṣke 'pi karmaṇi saṃsthite prāyaścittam iti gamyate. kathaṃ punar haviḥśabdaḥ karmaṇi vartata iti. talliṅgasaṃyogāt, haviḥsaṃbaddhaṃ karma haviḥśabdena haviḥsaṃbandhād{*6/46*} avagamyate, yathā prasahyakāritayā devadattasaṃbaddhayā{*6/47*} lakṣyate siṃhaḥ. evaṃ haviṣāpi karma lakṣyate. tasmāt kṛtsnakṣāme prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>havis</s>' (oblation) would refer to the sacrifice. 'That oblation is restored' [means] 'that sacrifice characterized by the oblation is restored.' [The objector says:] but in the absence of the primary [meaning], the secondary is taken, not otherwise. We reply: this is indeed the absence of the primary [meaning]. How? 'When it is restored' — [if taken literally, the sentence would be] 'that sacrifice by that oblation' — and the sentence would be split. And it would be non-referential. For it is the sacrifice that is completed, not the oblation; through it [the sacrifice], the occasion [for expiation arises]. 'That oblation' is a restatement. If it is a restatement, then even when the sacrifice is completed with another oblation, the expiatory rite is understood [to be needed]. How then does the word '<s>havis</s>' apply to the sacrifice? Because of the connection with its indicatory mark — the sacrifice, being connected with the oblation, is understood by the word '<s>havis</s>' through the connection with the oblation, just as a lion is figuratively designated through the boldness (<s>prasahyakāritā</s>) connected with <s>Devadatta</s>. Similarly, even the sacrifice is figuratively designated by the oblation. Therefore the expiatory rite is for total charring.

children.text: yathāśrutīti cet // MS_6,4.22 //
children.translated_text: 'As per the [Vedic] statement' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_6,4.22 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeteti śrūyate, tatra [683]{*6/48*} idam asti vacanam, yasyobhayaṃ havir ārtim ārcched aindraṃ pañcaśarāvamodanaṃ nirvaped{*6/49*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kim ubhayasminn{*6/50*} ārte pañcaśarāvo nirvaptavyaḥ, utānyatarasminn iti. kiṃ prāptam. iti cet paśyasi, evaṃjātīyaka ekasminn{*6/51*} iti.
tatra brūmaḥ, ubhayor iti. kutaḥ. yathāśruti bhavitum arhati, yad yac chrūyate, tad avagamyate. ubhayoś cārtau śrūyate, śrūyamāṇaṃ ca vivakṣituṃ nyāyyam, itarathā yāvad eva havir iti tāvad evobhayaṃ havir iti syāt. tasmād ubhayor ārtyāṃ pañcaśarāva iti.
children.translated_text:
It is heard: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' Regarding that, there is this statement: 'Whose both oblations should come to harm — he should offer a five-vessel <s>odana</s> (rice dish) to <s>Indra</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is the five-vessel [offering] to be prepared when both [oblations] are harmed, or when either one [is harmed]? What is the prima facie view? If you see it thus — in a case of this kind, [it applies] when one [oblation is harmed].
To this we say: when both [are harmed]. Why? It should be as per the [Vedic] statement — whatever is heard, that is understood. And the harm of both is heard. What is heard should properly be intended; otherwise, [the word] 'both' would reduce to 'whichever oblation' — and in that case, just as far as '<s>havis</s>' (oblation) [extends], so far would 'both oblations' [extend]. Therefore the five-vessel [offering is applicable] when both are harmed.

children.text: na tallakṣaṇatvād upapāto hi kāraṇam // MS_6,4.23 //
children.translated_text: No — because [the harm] is the characterizing mark of that [oblation]; for the mishap is the cause. // MS_6,4.23 //

children.text:
naitad evam. upapāto hy ārtisaṃbaddhaṃ dravyam, tatkāraṇam. tasya lakṣaṇaṃ havir ārtiḥ, tad vyastaṃ samastaṃ ca nimittam. na hy ubhayaśabdena śakyaṃ viśiṣṭum, viśiṣyamāṇe{*6/52*} hi vākyam bhidyeta, haviṣa ārtau pañcaśarāvaḥ. sa cobhayasya haviṣa iti.
āha, yadi viśeṣaṇaṃ na mṛṣyate, haviṣāpi te viśeṣaṇaṃ na prāpnoti. tad abhidhīyate, mṛṣyāmahe haviṣā viśeṣaṇam, aviśeṣyamāṇe 'narthakaṃ syāt. yasyārtim ārcched ity aviśeṣe yatkiṃcid iti gamyate{*6/53*}. tatra sarvasyaiva kiṃcid ārtim ṛcchati, antataś caritaṃ nimiṣitaṃ cintitam{*6/54*} iti. tatra yasyeti nimittavacanaṃ nityam anupapannaṃ{*6/55*} gamyate. tasmād avaśyam ārtir viśeṣṭavyā. sā ca haviṣā viśiṣyate, tathā haviḥ [684]{*6/56*} ārtisaṃbandhanirvṛttir animittaṃ pañcaśarāvasya. śaknoti hi śrutyā taṃ saṃbandhaṃ vaktum. havir ubhayasaṃbandhaṃ tu vākyena brūyāt, durbalaṃ ca vākyaṃ śruteḥ.
nanu havir ārtisaṃbandho 'pi vākyenaiva. ucyate, ārtinirvṛttir api tatra gamyate. sā ca śrutyā, havir ubhayasaṃbandhe 'tyantaṃ śrutir avahīyate{*6/57*}. tasmān na tatsaṃbandho nirvartyamāno nirdiśyata iti. kathaṃ tarhy ubhayaśabdaḥ. ubhayam iti nityānuvādaḥ, ekasminn apy ārte 'parasminn api. tasmād uktaṃ yasyobhayaṃ havir ārtim ārcched iti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so. For the mishap (<s>upapāta</s>) is the substance connected with harm — that is the cause. Its characterizing mark is the harm of the oblation; that, whether separate or combined, is the occasion. For the word 'both' (<s>ubhaya</s>) cannot serve as a qualifier — if it were used as a qualifier, the sentence would be split: '[when] harm [comes] to the oblation, [one should offer] the five-vessel [odana].' And that [five-vessel offering applies] to the oblation of both.
[The objector] says: if a qualifier is not tolerated, then the qualification by 'oblation' (<s>havis</s>) too does not obtain for you. To that it is stated: we tolerate the qualification by 'oblation' — for without any qualification it would be purposeless. 'Whose [oblation] should come to harm' — without any specification, [it would mean] 'whatever,' and then some [harm] would come to everything — at minimum, from walking, blinking, thinking. There, the statement of an occasion by 'whose' would be understood as perpetually [applicable] — which is untenable. Therefore the harm must necessarily be qualified. And it is qualified by the oblation; thus the harm-connection with the oblation is the non-occasional [i.e., determining] factor for the five-vessel [offering]. For the [Vedic] word can state that connection. But the dual connection of the oblation [with 'both'] would have to be stated by the sentence — and the sentence is weaker than the [Vedic] word.
[The objector says:] but the harm-connection with the oblation too is [established only] by the sentence. We reply: the occurrence of harm is also understood there. And that [is established] by the [Vedic] word; in the case of the dual connection of the oblation, the [Vedic] word is exceedingly weakened. Therefore that [dual] connection is not being indicated as what is to be produced. How then [should one understand] the word 'both' (<s>ubhaya</s>)? 'Both' is an invariable restatement — [it means] even when one [oblation] is harmed, the other [oblation exists] as well. Therefore, as stated, 'whose both oblations should come to harm' [applies even when one is harmed].

children.text:
atha kasmān na padadvayaviśiṣṭārtir nimittaṃ pratīyata iti, yasyobhayaguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ havir ārtim ārcched iti. atrocyate, kathaṃ tāvad bhavān manyate, viśiṣṭenārthena viśiṣṭārtir nimittam iti. āha, viśiṣṭārthasya saṃnidhānād viśiṣṭo 'rtha ārtisaṃnihitaḥ. kiṃ punaḥ syāt, yady evaṃ bhavet. tata ubhayaviśiṣṭārtir{*6/58*} nimittam iti gamyate.
atrocyate, idaṃ tāvad devānāṃpriyaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ. yasyāpi hi viśiṣṭārtha ārtisaṃnihito bhavati. kiṃ tasyāviśiṣṭo daṇḍaiḥ parāṇudyate. kim ato yan na parāṇudyate. etad ato bhavati, aviśiṣṭagatāpy{*6/59*} ārtir nimittaṃ{*6/60*} pañcaśarāvasya bhavati. nanūbhayaśabdo havir viśekṣyati{*6/61*}. na, haviḥśabdenāsaṃbadhyamānas tan na śaknoti viśeṣṭum. ānantaryāt saṃbhantsyate, tarhi tathāpi na samarthaḥ. na hy asau nivṛttiṃ prayojayati{*6/62*}.
āha, viśeṣavacanatvāt tannirvartako bhaviṣyati, yathā śuklā gaurānīyatām iti. na, evam abhihite kṛṣṇām{*6/63*} ānayanti. śuklaśabda enāṃ gāṃ kṛṣṇādibhyo nivartayati.
ucyate, viṣama upanyāsaḥ, na tatra gavākṛtyā dravyaṃ lakṣayitvā, tasyānayanam ucyate, tatrāpi ced evam abhaviṣyat, naiva enāṃ [685]{*6/64*} śuklaśabdo{*6/65*} vyaśekṣyata. ubhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaṃ tu tatrānayanaṃ pradhānam ucyate. iha punar ārtihaviṣṭvalakṣite dravye pañcaśarāvaḥ{*6/66*}. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇam. pradhānabhūta ākhyātārthe saṃhatya viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavati, parārthe punar viyujyeti{*6/67*}. ucyate, pradhānabhūta ākṛtir guṇo vā tatsaṃbandhārtham ucyate, tatrobhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭa{*6/68*} ekasmād vākyād avagamyate. tad viśiṣṭaṃ ca kṛtvā kṛtī bhavati. anyataraviśiṣṭaṃ kurvann aśrutaṃ kuryāt. yatra punar ākṛtilakṣite dravya ākhyātārthaḥ kīrtyate, tatra sarveṣv eva tajjātīyeṣūkto bhavati. na tatraikasmin nirvṛtte kṛtaṃ{*6/69*} manyeta. aparasminn api hy ākṛtilakṣite tad uktam eva. tatroktam apratiṣiddhaṃ ca kim iti na kriyeta. ākhyātārthe punaḥ pradhāne na tasyākṛtilakṣitena saṃbandhaḥ. tatra tadākṛtikāntare 'nupasaṃhriyamāṇe 'pi kṛtam eva pradhānam, saguṇaṃ ca pradhānaṃ bhavati. na ca kiṃcic chrutaṃ hīyeteti. tasmāt tatra viśeṣaṇaṃ yuktam, na tv iha tathā. iha hi havir ākṛtikasya dravyasyārtau pañcaśarāva ity uktam. tan na śakyaṃ viśeṣavacanena pratiṣedhāvācakena nivartayitum.
api cobhayaśabde haviṣā saṃbadhyamāne 'pi naivobhayaviśiṣṭārtiḥ pratīyate. kiṃ kāraṇam. haviṣobhayaśabdaḥ saṃbadhyate. nārtim ārcched ity anena padena. tatra saṃnihite 'py ubhayaśabde haviḥśabdasya yāvānarthaḥ, tāvataivārtiḥ saṃbadhyate. aviśiṣṭaś ca tatrārthaḥ{*6/70*}. tasmān nobhayaviśiṣṭārtir nimittam iti.
athārtyāśrayavibhaktiyogād ubhayaśabdasya, ubhayaviśiṣṭārtir ity ucyate. tan na, vibhaktisaṃyogo hi havir viśeṣaṇam ubhayaśabdaṃ śaknuyāt kartum, samabhivyāhārāt, nārtiviśeṣaṇam. na hy asyārtyā havir viśiṣṭasya samabhivyāhāro 'sti. [686]{*6/71*} athocyate, asaty api samabhivyāhāra ārtiśabdasaṃnidhānāt tadviśiṣṭaivārthiḥ pratyeṣyata iti. tan na, asatyāṃ hy ākāṅkṣāyāṃ saṃnidhānam akāraṇaṃ bhavati, yathā bhāryā rajñaḥ, puruṣo devadattasyeti. ekavākyagatatvāt tadviśiṣṭaṃ gamyata iti cet. naitad evam. ekasminn api vākye tadavayavabhūtasyānapekṣitasya naiva bhavati saṃbandhaḥ, yathā, aśvena vrajati, śvetena paṭenāvṛta iti, nānapekṣitasyāśvasya śvaityaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavati.
athocyate, ārtiviśiṣṭena haviṣobhayasya{*6/72*} saṃbandha iti. tad api nopapadyate. na hy ārtim ārcched iti havir viśeṣaṇatvenopādīyate. kiṃ tarhi. pañcaśarāvasya nimittatvena, havir ārter ubhayapañcaśarāvasaṃbandhe yaugapadyenābhyupagamyamāne vākyaṃ bhidyeta.
atha havir ākṛtilakṣitena saṃbaddhaṃ ārcched iti punar havir viśiṣṭenobhayaśabdena saṃbadhyeta. tathāpi vākyaṃ bhidyeta. tasmān nobhayaviśiṣṭārtir nimittam.
āha, yathaivākhyātārthaprādhānya ubhayaviśiṣtocyata iti nānyataraviśiṣṭā nimittam gamyate. evam itarasminn api pakṣe ubhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭā sā ucyate, iti yady api svena ātmanāviśiṣṭāviśiṣṭā, tathāpy anyataraviśiṣṭā bhavantī na nimittaṃ bhavitum arhatīti. ko viśeṣa{*6/73*} iti. tad abhidhīyate, matpakṣa upādeyatvena viśeṣaṇadvayam, tvatpakṣe punarlakṣaṇatvena. āha, kim ataḥ, yal lakṣaṇatvena. ucyate{*6/74*}, etad ato bhavati. havirākṛtyā lakṣyate dravyam, tasya kiṃcid vaktavyam iti. tad alakṣitam ucyamānaṃ na vijñāyeta kasya syād iti. athavā sarvasyaiva dravyasyeti gamyeta. tasminn ubhayasminn apy aviśiṣṭe{*6/75*} sati tasyāśrayaṃ lakṣayituṃ havirākṛtir ucyate. [687]{*6/76*} tatra dvayam āpatati. yad dhavirākṛtikaṃ tadārtam iti, yad vā yad dhavirākṛtikam, tad ubhayam iti. yadi tāvad yad dhavirākṛtikaṃ tadārtam ity apekṣyate. tato havirākṛtikam ubhayam anubhayaṃ vārtaṃ nimittaṃ gamyate.
atha yad dhavirākṛtikaṃ tad ubhayam iti tato nārtir haviṣā viśeṣyate. haviṣāviśiṣyamāṇāyam{*6/77*} artāv ubhayaśabdo havir viśekṣyatīti, naitad avakalpate. katham iti. evaṃ kila viśeṣyeta, yad dhavirākṛtikam ubhayam iti, tatra punar vaktavyam, yad dhavirākṛtikam ubhayam, tac ced ārtam iti. kathaṃ tena viśiṣṭenārtiḥ saṃbadhyeteti, na{*6/78*} punar ubhayahaviḥśabdau cārtiviśeṣaṇārtham{*6/79*} uccāryeyātām. atha punaruccāraṇaṃ na kriyate, tathā yady api haviḥśabdas tantreṇārtyubhayāśrayalakṣaṇārthaṃ{*6/80*} noccāryeta. aviśiṣṭam{*6/81*} ārter lakṣaṇaṃ syāt, aviśiṣṭam ubhayasya. viśiṣṭe iṣṭe punaruccāraṇaṃ kartavyam. tatra vākyabhedaḥ.
evam ubhayaśabdo yady ārcchatinā saṃbadhyeta, na havirviśiṣṭaṃ syāt, tatrāviśiṣṭasya haviṣa ārtir nimittam syāt. atha haviḥśabdena saṃbadhyeta, punarārtisaṃbandhārthaṃ haviḥśabdasahitam uccāryeta, tac caitad iti vā sarvanāmnā nirdiśyeta, tatra sa eva vākyabhedaḥ.
upādeyatve punar nānyonyaviśeṣaṇatvena prayojanam. dvayam apy ārtiṃ viśeṣṭum uccāryeta. tatra nānyataraviśiṣṭārtir nimittaṃ bhaviṣyati. lakṣaṇatve tv anyataraviśiṣṭā bhavatīty eṣa viśeṣaḥ.
api ca, sarvasvaiva padasya padāntarasaṃbandhe sati ca, śabdād ṛte tṛtīyena padena satyāṃ gatau saṃnihitenāpi saṃbandho na yuktaḥ, na hi bhavati, bhāryā rājñaḥ puruṣo devadattasyety atra rājā puruṣaviśeṣaṇam. asatyāṃ tu gatāv upādeyasyānekasyāpi pradhānena saṃbandho 'vakalpate vyavahitenāpi. vyava[688]{*6/82*}dhānād artho balīyān iti, lakṣaṇatve tu lakṣaṇadvayasaṃnipāte 'vaśyaṃ heye 'nyatam asmin{*6/83*} vyavahito guṇo vā hātavyo bhavati.

Now, why should not an affliction qualified by both words be understood as the occasion — [namely,] 'he whose offering (<s>havis</s>) qualified by both [characteristics] encounters affliction'? To this we reply: how does the honorable [opponent] think — that an affliction pertaining to what is qualified by a specific meaning is the occasion? He says: because of the proximity of the specific meaning, the specific meaning is proximate to the affliction. And what would follow if this were so? Then an affliction qualified by both [characteristics] would be understood as the occasion.
To this we reply: first, the dear friend should be asked this. Even when the specific meaning is proximate to the affliction — is an unspecified [affliction] repelled by the sticks? What follows from its not being repelled? This follows: even an affliction pertaining to the unspecified [offering] becomes the occasion for the five-saucer [offering]. [The objector says:] but the word 'both' (<s>ubhaya</s>) will qualify the <s>havis</s>. No — the word 'both,' not being connected with the word <s>havis</s>, cannot qualify it. [The objector says:] it will be connected through proximity. Even so, it is not capable [of qualifying it]. For it does not cause cessation [of the unqualified meaning].
He says: because of expressing a specific [meaning], it will produce that [cessation] — just as 'bring a white cow.' No, when thus stated, [people] do not bring a black one. The word 'white' distinguishes that cow from black ones and the like.
We reply: the example is dissimilar. For there, the substance is identified by the generic character 'cow,' and its bringing is stated. If there too it had been otherwise [i.e., like our case], the word 'white' would not have distinguished it at all. But there, the bringing, which is the primary [action], is said of what is qualified by both qualifiers. Here, however, the five-saucer [offering applies] to the substance identified by the generic characters 'affliction' and 'offering.' But what is the reason? [We reply:] when the qualifier is combined for the purpose of the primary verbal meaning, it qualifies jointly; but for another's purpose, it separates.
We reply: the generic character or quality, being primary, is stated for the purpose of connection with that [primary meaning]. There, what is qualified by both qualifiers is understood from a single sentence. And having done what is thus qualified, one is fulfilled. One who does what is qualified by only one [qualifier] would be doing what is unheard. But where the verbal meaning is stated in connection with a substance identified by generic character, there it applies to all things of that kind. One should not consider oneself fulfilled when only one [instance] is accomplished. For in another [instance] too identified by the generic character, that [statement] applies equally. And since what is stated and not prohibited should certainly be performed — why not? But when the primary [meaning] is the verbal action, there is no connection of it with what is identified by generic character. There, even when what is identified by a different generic character is not subsumed [under the primary], the primary is indeed accomplished, and the primary is endowed with its quality. And nothing that is heard is lost. Therefore the qualifier is proper there, but not here in the same way. For here, the five-saucer [offering] is stated with reference to the substance identified by the generic characters 'offering' and 'affliction.' That cannot be overturned by a specific statement that does not express prohibition.
Moreover, even when the word 'both' is connected with the <s>havis</s>, an affliction qualified by both [characteristics] is not understood. What is the reason? The word 'both' is connected with the word <s>havis</s>, not with the phrase 'encounters affliction.' There, even though the word 'both' is proximate, the meaning of the word <s>havis</s> is as much as it is — and with just that much, the affliction is connected. And the meaning there is unqualified. Therefore, an affliction qualified by both [characteristics] is not the occasion.
[The objector says:] but because of the case-ending (<s>vibhakti</s>) connected with the word denoting the substratum of affliction and the word 'both,' an affliction qualified by both is stated. Not so — for the case-ending connection can make the word 'both' a qualifier of <s>havis</s>, through syntactic collocation, but not a qualifier of the affliction. For there is no syntactic collocation of [the word 'both'] with the <s>havis</s> that has been qualified by affliction. [The objector says:] but even without syntactic collocation, because of the proximity of the word 'affliction,' the affliction qualified by that [havis] will be expected. Not so — for in the absence of syntactic expectation (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), proximity is not a [valid] cause — just as 'the wife of the king, the servant of <s>Devadatta</s>' — there the king is not a qualifier of the servant. [The objector says:] because of being in the same sentence, what is qualified by that is understood. Not so — for even within a single sentence, when a component is not expected, there is simply no connection — just as 'he travels by horse, covered with a white cloth' — the whiteness is not a qualifier of the horse, which is not expected [to be qualified by it].
[The objector says:] but the word 'both' has a connection with the <s>havis</s> that is qualified by affliction. That too does not work. For 'encounters affliction' is not employed as a qualifier of the <s>havis</s>. Rather, [it is employed] as the occasion for the five-saucer [offering]. If the connection of the <s>havis</s> with affliction and with 'both' and with the five-saucer [offering] were to be accepted simultaneously, the sentence would be split.
[The objector says:] but the <s>havis</s> is connected with what is identified by generic character through 'encounters [affliction],' and then it could be connected again by the word 'both' with the <s>havis</s> qualified [by affliction]. Even so, the sentence would be split. Therefore, an affliction qualified by both [characteristics] is not the occasion.
He says: just as when the verbal action is primary, what is said to be qualified by both [qualifiers] is not understood as an occasion with only one qualifier — so too in the other view, [the affliction] is said to be qualified by both qualifiers. Even though in itself it is unqualified/qualified, nevertheless, being qualified by only one [of the two], it cannot be the occasion. What is the distinction? This is stated: in my view, the two qualifiers serve as things to be accepted; in your view, they serve as identifiers. He says: what follows from their being identifiers? We reply: this follows. The substance is identified by the generic character of <s>havis</s>; something must be stated about it. If stated without identification, it would not be known to whom it pertains. Or it would be understood as pertaining to every substance whatsoever. Since both [alternatives] are unspecified, the generic character of <s>havis</s> is stated to identify the substratum. There, two [possibilities] arise: 'whatever has the generic character of <s>havis</s>, if afflicted, [triggers the offering]'; or 'whatever has the generic character of <s>havis</s>, if both [types], [triggers the offering].' If 'whatever has the generic character of <s>havis</s>, if afflicted' is expected — then [the occasion is] the affliction of what has the generic character of <s>havis</s>, whether [it is] 'both' [types] or not.
But if 'whatever has the generic character of <s>havis</s>, that is both [types]' — then the affliction is not qualified by the <s>havis</s>. When the affliction is not qualified by the <s>havis</s>, [the objector claims] the word 'both' will qualify the <s>havis</s> — this does not work. How? It would qualify thus: 'what has the generic character of <s>havis</s> and is both [types]' — but then it must further be stated: 'if what has the generic character of <s>havis</s> and is both [types] is afflicted.' How would the affliction then be connected with what is thus qualified? — and the words 'both' and <s>havis</s> would not need to be restated for the purpose of qualifying the affliction. And if there is no restatement, then even if the word <s>havis</s> by <s>tantra</s> (single operation) is not stated for the dual purpose of identifying the substratum of both the affliction and the [word] 'both' — then the identification of the affliction would be unqualified, and the identification of 'both' [would be] unqualified. If specific [identification] is desired, restatement would need to be done. In that case, the sentence would split.
Thus, if the word 'both' is connected with '<s>ārcchat</s>' (encounters), the <s>havis</s> would not be qualified [by it]; then the affliction of the unqualified <s>havis</s> would be the occasion. But if [the word 'both'] is connected with the word <s>havis</s>, [then] for the purpose of reconnecting with the affliction, [the word <s>havis</s>] combined with [the word 'both'] would need to be restated, or referred to by a pronoun 'that' — and there again, the same splitting of the sentence [occurs].
But when [the qualifiers] are things to be accepted, there is no need for mutual qualifying. Both would be stated to qualify the affliction. Then an affliction qualified by only one [qualifier] will not be the occasion. But when [they are] identifiers, an affliction qualified by only one [qualifier] does occur — this is the distinction.
Moreover, when every word is already connected with another word, and when a third word, apart from the [Vedic] statement, has a [different] destination — connection with it even though proximate is not proper. For the king is not a qualifier of the servant [in 'the wife of the king, the servant of Devadatta']. But when there is no [other] destination, even many things to be accepted are properly connected with the primary, even when separated. [In the case of] identification, however, when two identifiers converge, necessarily one of the two or an intervening quality must be abandoned.

jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, havirdhāne grāvabhir abhiṣutyāhavanīye hutvā pratyañcaḥ paretya sadasi bhakṣān{*6/84*} bhakṣayantīti. tatrānyena vacanenābhiṣava uktaḥ, yajatinā homaḥ. tau tāvan na vidhīyate, na ca tayoḥ kramaḥ. arthād eva hi sa prāptaḥ. tasmād ekakartṛkaṃ homābhiṣavābhyāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate. abhiṣave kṛte home ca tatkartṛbhiḥ bhakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam iti. tatraiṣa saṃdehaḥ. kim ubhayaṃ yaḥ karyāt sa eva bhakṣayet, utānyatareṇāpi bhakṣaṇam iti. kim prāptam. homābhiṣavabhakṣaṇaṃ ca tadvat, tadvad eva syāt, yadvad dhaviṣa ārtiḥ. katham. naitad evaṃ saṃbadhyate, abhiṣutya tato hutvā tato bhakṣayed iti. nānenābhiṣavasya homasya ca kramaḥ kīrtyate, abhiṣutya ye juhvati, te bhakṣayantīti. vākyaṃ hy evaṃ bhidyeta, abhiṣutya bhakṣayanti, hutvā bhakṣayantīti.
tasmād dhomābhiṣavayoḥ paraspareṇa saṃbandho nāstīty ekenāpi bhakṣaṇaṃ saṃbadhyeta. apareṇāpi, abhiṣutya bhakṣayantīti{*6/85*}. tasmād anyatareṇa nimittena bhakṣaṇaṃ bhavatīti.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'Having pressed with the stones in the <s>Havirdhāna</s> shed and having offered in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, going westward they consume the shares (<s>bhakṣa</s>) in the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall).' There, the pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>) is stated by another sentence, and the offering (<s>homa</s>) by the word '<s>yajati</s>.' These two are not [independently] enjoined, nor is their sequence [enjoined]. For that [sequence] is obtained from the sense alone. Therefore, the consuming (<s>bhakṣaṇa</s>) is enjoined as having one agent for both the offering and the pressing — when the pressing has been done and the offering [performed], consuming should be done by those very agents. There this doubt [arises]: should only the one who performs both consume, or can one consume by [having performed] either one alone? What is the prima facie view? The offering, pressing, and consuming should be like that — just as it is with the preparation of the <s>havis</s> (oblation material). How? This is not construed thus: 'having pressed, then having offered, then one should consume.' This does not state the sequence of pressing and offering [as]: 'those who press and then offer — they consume.' For the sentence would thus be split: 'having pressed they consume' and 'having offered they consume.'
Therefore there is no mutual connection between the offering and the pressing — so consuming could be connected with even one [of them]. And also: 'having pressed, they consume.' Therefore consuming occurs by reason of either one.

NOTES:

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ vā na hi tayor dharmaśāstram // MS_6,4.25 //
children.translated_text: Or [one should consume] by reason of both; for the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> does not [prescribe this] for those two [independently]. // MS_6,4.25 //

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ vā nimittābhyāṃ bhakṣayet. na bhakṣaṇaṃ homābhiṣavayo[689]{*6/86*}r dharmo vidhīyate. kiṃ hi syād yadi tayor dharmo vidhīyeta. homābhiṣavau{*6/87*} pradhānam iti bhakṣaṇaṃ guṇaḥ pratipradhānaṃ bhidyeta. atha punar ubhābhyāṃ nimittābhyāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate. tasmin vihita eko 'rtho vihito bhavati. tenaikaṃ vākyam, tad etāvati paryavasitaṃ bhavati, abhiṣutya hutvā bhakṣayantīti. tatraitad avāntaraṃ vākyam, hutvā bhakṣayantīti. na ca mahāvākye saty avāntaravākyaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavati, padāntarasya bādhanāt, yathā, nodyantam ādityam īkṣeteti pratiṣedho gamyate mahāvākyāt, avāntaravākyād īkṣaṇavidhānam. tasmād anyataranimittaṃ bhakṣaṇam aśrutam. mahāvākyād idam avagamyate dve nimitte bhakṣaṇasyeti. bhakṣaṇaṃ cānyathā kurvañ chrutaṃ parityajet. tasmād ubhābhyāṃ bhakṣaṇam{*6/88*} iti.
children.translated_text: Or one should consume by reason of both causes. The consuming is not enjoined as a property (<s>dharma</s>) of the offering and the pressing [689]. For what would happen if it were enjoined as their property? The offering and pressing would be the principal, and consuming, being a subsidiary, would be divided according to each principal. But rather, consuming is enjoined by both causes [together]. When one thing is enjoined in that [combined injunction], a single thing is enjoined. Therefore it is a single sentence, and it comes to this conclusion: 'having pressed and having offered, they consume.' Therein this is the subordinate sentence: 'having offered, they consume.' And when the main sentence (<s>mahāvākya</s>) exists, a subordinate sentence is not authoritative, because of overriding another element — just as from the main sentence 'one should not look at the rising sun,' a prohibition is understood, while from the subordinate sentence an injunction to look [would be derived]. Therefore consuming by reason of only one [cause] is unheard. From the main sentence this is understood: there are two causes for consuming. And if one were to perform consuming otherwise, one would abandon what is heard. Therefore consuming [requires] both.

children.text: punarādheyamodanavat // MS_6,4.26 //
children.translated_text: Like the <s>Punarādheya</s> porridge (<s>modana</s>). // MS_6,4.26 //

children.text: agnihotre śrūyate, yasyobhāv anugatāv agnī{*6/89*} abhinimlocet, yasya vābhyudiyāt punarādheyam eva tasya prāyaścittir iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kim anyatarānugamane punarādheyam, utobhayānugamana iti. kiṃ prāptam. punarādheyamodanavat syāt, yathā pañcaśarāvo 'nyatarasyārtau{*6/90*} bhavati. evaṃ punarādheyam anyatarānugamane bhavitum arhati, vākyabhedaprasaṅgād iti, yatheha yakṣye, iha sukṛtaṃ kariṣyāmīty evam evābhisaṃbandha{*6/91*} iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Agnihotra</s> it is heard: 'For one whose both fires, having followed [him], set [before the sun] sets, or for one [before whom the sun] rises — the <s>Punarādheya</s> (re-establishment of fires) alone is his expiation.' There a doubt [arises]: does the <s>Punarādheya</s> [apply] when one [fire] has followed, or when both have followed? What is the prima facie view? It should be like the <s>Punarādheya</s> porridge — just as the five-potsherd [cake] is for [the occasion of] one [fire's] distress. So too the <s>Punarādheya</s> should properly occur when one [fire] has followed, because of the implication of sentence-splitting — just as [one resolves]: 'here I shall sacrifice, here I shall perform a meritorious act' — thus indeed is the connection.

children.text: dravyotpatter vobhayoḥ{*6/93*} syāt // MS_6,4.27 //
children.translated_text: Or it should [apply] to both, because of the production of the substance. // MS_6,4.27 //

children.text: dravye vinaṣṭe tasyaiva dravyasyotpattir atra prāyaścittam. tasya{*6/94*} dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam, kathaṃ dravyaṃ bhaved iti punarādhānaṃ kriyate, tatraiṣa dharmaḥ, dvāv agnī sahotpadyete, na pṛthaktvena. tatrānyatarānugamane na śakyata eka evādhātum. viguṇaṃ syāt{*6/95*}. atha dvitīyam apy ādadhīta. sa yadi tāvad āhavanīyaḥ. tatrāhavanīyo 'nyo homārtho vidyata eveti na sa homāya syāt. yaś ca homārtham utpādyate sa āhavanīyaḥ, yata eṣa saṃskāraśabdaḥ{*6/96*}, saṃskāraśabdaś caikenāpi saṃskāreṇa vinā na bhavati. eṣo 'pi ca saṃskāraḥ, yad dhomārthatā, yad āhavanīye juhotīti{*6/97*} śrūyate{*6/98*}, tad ekasminn anugate, ekasminn ādhīyamāne vaiguṇyam, dvayor api hi{*6/99*} vaiguṇyam eva. tasmān naikasminn anugate punarādheyam aśakyatvād iti.
children.translated_text: When the substance (fire) is destroyed, the production of that very substance is the expiation here. Its purpose is visible — the re-establishment is performed [to answer the question] 'how should the substance (fire) come to be?' There this is the rule: the two fires are produced together, not separately. Therefore, when one [fire] has followed, it is not possible to establish just one [fire]. It would be deficient. But if one were to establish the second also — if that is the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, then another <s>Āhavanīya</s> for the purpose of offering already exists, so that [new one] would not be for offering. And what is produced for the purpose of offering — that is the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, because this is a refinement-word (<s>saṃskāraśabda</s>), and a refinement-word does not apply without at least one refinement. And this too is a refinement — namely, the purpose of offering, as it is heard: 'one offers upon the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.' Therefore, when one [fire] has followed, if one [fire] is to be re-established, there is deficiency — indeed for both there is deficiency. Therefore the <s>Punarādheya</s> is not [performed] when one [fire] has followed, because of impossibility.

children.text: pañcaśarāvas tu dravyaśruteḥ pratinidhiḥ syāt // MS_6,4.28 //
children.translated_text: But the five-potsherd [cake] should be a substitute, because of the hearing of the substance. // MS_6,4.28 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, yasyobhayaṃ havir ārtim ārcched aindraṃ pañcaśarāvamodanaṃ nirvaped{*6/100*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ haviṣy ārte pañcaśarāvaḥ pratinidhiḥ, uta nimitte karmāntaram iti. kathaṃ pratinidhiḥ, kathaṃ karmāntaram iti. yady evam abhisaṃbandho bhavati, pañcaśarāvaṃ nirvapet kuyād{*6/101*} iti, [691]{*6/102*} tataḥ sāṃnyāyasya kārye pañcaśarāvaḥ pratinidhir iti. atha na pañcaśarāvo nirvapatinā{*6/103*}, kiṃ tu devatayā saṃbadhyate{*6/104*} pañcaśarāvam aindraṃ kuryād iti, tato nimitte yajatir vidhīyate. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. pañcaśarāvas tu dravyaśruteḥ pratinidhiḥ syāt. pañcaśarāvaḥ sāṃnyāyyasya{*6/105*} pratinidhiḥ. kutaḥ. dravyaśruteḥ, dravyasya nirvāpe śravaṇam, nendrasaṃbandhaḥ{*6/106*}. kutaḥ. evaṃ nirvāpavidhir bhaviṣyati, tatra śrutir vidhāyikā, itarathā dravyadevatāsaṃbandhe vākyaṃ syāt, tac ca{*6/107*} durbalaṃ śruteḥ. tasmāt pratinidhir iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard: 'For one whose both oblation materials (<s>havis</s>) suffer damage, one should offer a five-potsherd porridge (<s>modana</s>) for <s>Indra</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: when the <s>havis</s> is damaged, is the five-potsherd [cake] a substitute (<s>pratinidhi</s>), or is it a different ritual act occasioned [by the damage]? How [would it be] a substitute, how a different ritual act? If the connection is thus — 'one should offer the five-potsherd [cake] as a performance' [691] — then the five-potsherd [cake] is a substitute for the regular (<s>sāṃnyāyika</s>) [oblation]. But if the five-potsherd [cake] is not connected with the offering-process (<s>nirvapati</s>), but rather is connected with the deity — 'one should perform a five-potsherd [cake] for <s>Indra</s>' — then the sacrificial act (<s>yajati</s>) is enjoined as occasioned [by the damage]. What, then, is the prima facie view? The five-potsherd [cake] should be a substitute for the regular [oblation], because of the hearing of the substance. [That is,] the substance is heard in relation to the offering process, not as connected with <s>Indra</s>. Why? For thus there will be an injunction of offering, and there the hearing (<s>śruti</s>) is the enjoiner; otherwise, the connection of substance and deity would be a sentence [inference], and that is weaker than hearing. Therefore it is a substitute.

children.text: codanā vā dravyadevatāvidhir{*6/108*} avācye hi // MS_6,4.29 //
children.translated_text: Or the injunction is of substance-and-deity; for [the word '<s>aindra</s>'] refers to what cannot be otherwise expressed. // MS_6,4.29 //

children.text: nimitte vā yajatiḥ karmānataram, dravyadevatāvidhiḥ{*6/109*}. dravyadevatam iha śrūyate, pañcaśarāvam aindraṃ kuryād iti. itarathā hy aindram iti pramādapāṭho 'vagamyeta. aindramāhendrayor vāyathārthānuvāda aindram iti syāt. avācye hi te devate, aindraśabdenendro mahendraś ca na śakyo 'nuvaditum. viśeṣaṇatve vākyabhedaḥ. nanu śrutir balīyasīty uktam. satyam evam, kiṃ tv itarasmin pakṣe bādhyatetarāṃ śrutiḥ, aindraśabdasyātantratvāt//
children.translated_text: Or, when occasioned [by damage], the sacrificial act (<s>yajati</s>) is a different ritual, [serving as] an injunction of substance and deity. Substance and deity are heard here: 'one should perform a five-potsherd [cake] for <s>Indra</s>.' Otherwise, the word '<s>aindra</s>' (belonging to <s>Indra</s>) would be understood as a careless reading. Or between '<s>aindra</s>' and '<s>māhendra</s>,' the word '<s>aindra</s>' would be a purposeless restatement. [But it cannot be purposeless,] for that deity cannot be otherwise expressed — by the word '<s>aindra</s>,' both <s>Indra</s> and <s>Mahendra</s> cannot be restated. If [<s>aindra</s>] were a qualifier, there would be sentence-splitting. [The objector says:] but was it not stated that hearing (<s>śruti</s>) is stronger? True, that is so; but in the other view, another hearing is overridden, because of the word '<s>aindra</s>' being non-redundant.

children.text: sa pratyāmanet sthānāt // MS_6,4.30 //
children.translated_text: It should be a substitute (<s>pratyāmnāya</s>) for the [new-moon] day, because of [occupying] its place. // MS_6,4.30 //

children.text: sa eṣa naimittiko yāgaḥ, kim amāvāsyāṃ pratyāmanet, [692]{*6/110*} neti. kiṃ prāptam. sa pratyāmanet, sthānāt, sa eṣa yāgo 'māvāsyāṃ pratyāmnātum arhati. kutaḥ. sthānāt, yāge vinaṣṭe yāga eṣa śrūyamāṇo yadi na naṣṭasyāṅgam, tato 'rthavān bhavati. athāṅgam, niṣprayojanasyārthaṃ{*6/111*} kriyamāṇaṃ niṣprayojanam eva bhavitum arhati, viguṇaṃ ca niṣprayojanam eva, vinaṣṭam āmāvāsyam iti pratyakṣam. idam api kartavyam iti śābdam, yad vinaṣṭam, tan niṣphalam iti na kartavyam. idaṃ ca kartavyam iti pratyāmnāyo 'vagamyate.
children.translated_text: This occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) sacrifice — should it be a substitute for the new-moon day (<s>amāvāsyā</s>) [692], or not? What is the prima facie view? It should be a substitute, because of [occupying] its place — this sacrifice, being heard when the [regular] sacrifice has been destroyed, deserves to be substituted for the new-moon day. Why? Because of [occupying] its place — when the [regular] sacrifice has been destroyed, if this sacrifice being heard is not a subsidiary of what was destroyed, then it has a purpose [of its own]. But if it is a subsidiary, what is being done for [something] purposeless deserves to be purposeless itself, and what is deficient is indeed purposeless — that the <s>Āmāvāsya</s> [rite] is destroyed is evident. That this too must be performed is scriptural; what is destroyed is fruitless and so need not be done. And [yet] this must be done — thus a substitution (<s>pratyāmnāya</s>) is understood.

*{6/111: E2: niṣprayojanasyārthe; E6: niṣprayojanasyātha}*

children.text: aṅgavidhir vā nimittasaṃyogāt // MS_6,4.31 //
children.translated_text: Or it is a subsidiary-injunction, because of connection with the occasion. // MS_6,4.31 //

children.text:
aṅgaṃ vaitad vidhīyate. haviṣy ārtau nimitte yāgaḥ śrūyate, tatra trayam āpatati. yad vā nimitte svatantraṃ kalpyaṃ phalam, yad vāmāvāsyāyā yat kāryaṃ tad asya, yad vā tasyāṅgam iti. svapradhānaṃ tāvan na{*6/112*}, kalpyatvāt phalasya. nāmāvāsyāyāḥ kārye. kiṃ kāraṇam. aśravaṇāt, naivaṃ śrūyate, tasyāḥ kārye vartata iti, kartavyopadeśenāpi nānyatamādhyavasānaṃ triṣv eṣu pakṣeṣu, teṣu ca pakṣeṣu vivakṣiteṣu{*6/113*} kartavyopadeśo 'vakalpyate.
nanv evam abhisaṃbandho bhaviṣyati, yasyobhayaṃ havir ārtim ārcchet sa etena yāgena sādhayet, yat sādhayitukāmaḥ. kiṃ cāsau sādhayitukāmaḥ, yad amāvāsyāyāḥ phalam iti. atrocyate, phalapadena saṃbandhābhāvāt saṃbandhasya vidhāyakaṃ vākyam. śrutyā ca yāgakartavyatā vidhīyate, sā ca vākyād balīyasī. tasmān na tatkārye vartata iti. kiṃ{*6/114*} tarhi prayojanam. tasyā amāvāsyāyā aṅgam. nanv etad api nāsti tasyā aṅgam iti. atrocyate{*6/115*}, tatsaṃbandhena samāmnānāt{*6/116*} tatprayogavacanena gṛhyate, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ phalaṃ [693]{*6/117*} sādhayet sarvair aṅgaiḥ saha. asyāṃ cārtāv eṣa yāga itikartavyateti. tasmād evam avagamyate, vinaṣṭe haviṣy āmāvāsyaṃ yan na śaknoti svakāryaṃ kartum, tad anayetikartavyatayā sahitaṃ śaknotīti. tasmān nimitte karmāṅgam iti.
children.translated_text:
Or this is being enjoined as a subsidiary. When the <s>havis</s> is damaged — [that being] the occasion — a sacrifice is heard. There, three [interpretations] arise: either an independent fruit is to be postulated for what is occasioned; or [it has] whatever result the <s>Āmāvāsyā</s> [rite would have had]; or it is a subsidiary of that [Āmāvāsyā rite]. It is not independently primary, because of the fruit having to be postulated. Nor [does it produce] the result of the <s>Āmāvāsyā</s>. What is the reason? Because of non-hearing — it is not heard thus: 'it operates for the purpose of that [Āmāvāsyā rite]'; and the instruction to perform does not determine any one of these three alternatives — when those alternatives are intended, the instruction to perform is subordinate.
[The objector says:] but the connection will be thus: 'for one whose both <s>havis</s> materials suffer damage, he should accomplish by this sacrifice whatever he desires to accomplish. And what does he desire to accomplish? The fruit of the <s>Āmāvāsyā</s>.' To this we reply: because of the absence of a connection with the word 'fruit,' the sentence [only] enjoins a connection. And by hearing (<s>śruti</s>), the performance of the sacrifice is enjoined, and that is stronger than a sentence [inference]. Therefore it does not operate for the purpose of that [Āmāvāsyā rite]. What then is the purpose? It is a subsidiary of that <s>Āmāvāsyā</s> [rite]. [The objector says:] but this too is not [the case] — that it is a subsidiary of that [rite]. To this we reply: because of being recorded in connection with that, it is grasped by the statement of being performed in connection with that — [namely,] one should accomplish the fruit through the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites [693] together with all subsidiaries. And in this [situation of] damage, this sacrifice is a procedural requirement (<s>itikartavyatā</s>). Therefore it is thus understood: when the <s>havis</s> is destroyed, the <s>Āmāvāsya</s> [rite], which cannot accomplish its own purpose, is able to do so together with this procedural requirement. Therefore the occasional [rite] is a subsidiary of the [principal] ritual action.

children.text: viśvajittvapravṛtte{*6/118*} bhāvaḥ karmaṇi syāt // MS_6,4.32 //
children.translated_text: When [the rite] has proceeded with the <s>Viśvajit</s> character, there should be [a subsidiary] existence for the ritual action. // MS_6,4.32 //

children.text:
etad āmnāyate, sarvābhyo vā eṣa devatābhyaḥ, sarvebhyaḥ pṛṣṭhebhyaḥ, ātmānam āgurate, yaḥ sarvatrāyāgurate, viśvajitātirātreṇa sarvapṛṣṭhena sarvavedasadakṣiṇena yajeta, sarvābhya eṣa devatābhyaḥ, sarvebhyaḥ pṛṣṭhebhyaḥ, ātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīta iti. sarvatrāgoraṇe{*6/119*} nimitte viśvajic chrūyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ sarvatrāgūrya yaḥ sarvatraṃ prayuṅkte, tasya viśvajit, uta yo na prayuṅkte tasyeti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. yaś ca prayuṅkte, yaś ca nety aviśeṣāt. athavā prayuñjānasya{*6/120*}. kutaḥ. nimitte karmāṅgam evaṃjātīyakam ity uktam. tad aprayujyamānasya katham aṅgaṃ syād iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, viśvajit tv apravṛtte bhavet, sarvasya kriyāyā abhāve viśvajit. kiṃ kāraṇam. evaṃ hi śrūyate, yaḥ satrāyāgurate, sa viśvajitātirātreṇa yajeteti. yaḥ satraṃ kariṣyāmīty evam āgurate, sa viśvajitā yāgena sādhayed iti. yad artham asau satraṃ kartum icchati, tad artham iti gamyate. katham. ya āgurate, sa tena yajeta, yāgena nirvartayed iti vākyārtho gamyate, na yāgaṃ nirvartayed iti. kutaḥ. yāgasya guṇatvena śravaṇāt. kathaṃ tasya guṇatvam. [694]{*6/121*} tṛtīyānirdeśāt, prādhānye hi phalaṃ kalpyeta. itarasmiṃs tu pakṣe pratyakṣād vākyāt phalāvagamaḥ.
children.translated_text:
This is recorded: 'From all deities, from all <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], he pledges himself — he who pledges himself to everything; he should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s> <s>Atirātra</s> with all <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants] and with all wealth as <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; from all deities, from all <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], he ransoms himself.' The <s>Viśvajit</s> is heard when the occasion is pledging oneself to everything. There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>Viśvajit</s> for one who, having pledged himself to everything, actually performs [the <s>Sattra</s>], or for one who does not perform? What is the prima facie view? There is no distinction — both for one who performs and one who does not. Or rather, [it is] for one who [actually] performs. Why? It has been stated that 'a subsidiary of such a kind [arises] when the occasion is the ritual act.' How could it be a subsidiary for one who does not perform?
Given this prima facie view, we say: the <s>Viśvajit</s> would be [for one who has] not commenced — the <s>Viśvajit</s> [is prescribed] when there is absence of all ritual activity. What is the reason? For thus it is heard: 'He who pledges himself to a <s>Sattra</s>, he should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s> <s>Atirātra</s>.' He who pledges 'I shall perform the <s>Sattra</s>' — he should accomplish [his goal] through the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice. It is understood that the purpose for which he wishes to perform the <s>Sattra</s> is the same purpose [served by the Viśvajit]. How? The sentence-meaning is understood as: 'He who pledges, he should sacrifice with that — he should accomplish [his goal] through the sacrifice' — not 'he should accomplish the sacrifice.' Why? Because the sacrifice is heard as subsidiary. How is it subsidiary? [694] Because of the instrumental case ending — for if [the sacrifice] were primary, a fruit would have to be postulated. But in the other view, the fruit is understood from the direct [Vedic] sentence.

children.text: niṣkrayavādāc ca // MS_6,4.33 //
children.translated_text: And because of the statement of ransoming. // MS_6,4.33 //

children.text: evaṃ tatra śrūyate, sarvābhyo vā eṣa devatābhyaḥ, sarvebhyaḥ pṛṣṭhebhya yad{*6/122*} ātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīta iti. niṣkrayadvāreṇa ca saṃstavaḥ pravṛtte na yujyate. tasmād apravṛtte viśvajid iti. atha kasmān naivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate. āgūrya satrāya viśvajitā yajeteti. viśvajitaḥ satrasya ca saṃbandho vijñāyeta{*6/123*}, āgoraṇavelāyām{*6/124*} iti. naivam, āgoraṇaviśeṣaṇaṃ{*6/125*} hi satraṃ satraviśvajitsaṃbandhe vyavahitakalpanā syāt. śrutiś ca puruṣeṇa viśvajitaṃ saṃbandhayati, viśvajitā yajeta puruṣa iti, na satreṇa. satrasya viśvajid yāga iti, āgūryeti ca. evaṃ śravaṇam arthavad bhavati. satrāṅgatve tv arthaprāptaṃ na vaktavyam. na ca, āgūrya yajetety āgoraṇānantaryaṃ{*6/126*} śakyaṃ vidhātum. aśabdārtho hi tadāśrīyeta, samānakartṛkatā hi śabdavatī, pūrvakālabhāvasya cārthaprāptatvān na vaktavyatā. tasmād āgūryety atraiva viśvajitaḥ saṃbandhaḥ{*6/127*}. sa cet, āgūrya{*6/128*} na satreṇa yajeta, tasya viśvajid iti.
children.translated_text: Thus it is heard there: 'From all deities, from all <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], he ransoms himself.' And the statement of ransoming is not appropriate when [the Sattra] has [already] commenced. Therefore the <s>Viśvajit</s> [is for one who has] not commenced. Now, why is the syntactic connection not made thus: 'Having pledged himself to the <s>Sattra</s>, he should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>' — [so that] the connection between the <s>Viśvajit</s> and the <s>Sattra</s> would be understood [as being] at the time of pledging? This is not so — for the <s>Sattra</s> qualifies the pledging; in [establishing] a connection between the <s>Sattra</s> and the <s>Viśvajit</s>, there would be the postulation of something intervening. And the <s>śruti</s> connects the <s>Viśvajit</s> with the person: 'The person should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>' — not with the <s>Sattra</s>. [The connection with the Sattra is:] the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice of the <s>Sattra</s>, and [the word] 'having pledged.' Thus the hearing becomes meaningful. But if [the Viśvajit] were a subsidiary of the <s>Sattra</s>, what is obtained by implication need not be stated. And it is not possible to prescribe that 'having pledged, one should sacrifice' means [ritual] immediacy after pledging. For then a meaning without [Vedic] word-basis would be resorted to — since the common agency is based on [Vedic] word, and the temporal priority is already obtained by implication and need not be stated. Therefore the connection of the <s>Viśvajit</s> is with [the word] 'having pledged' itself. If [one has] pledged [but] does not sacrifice with the <s>Sattra</s>, for him the <s>Viśvajit</s> [is prescribed].

children.text: vatsasaṃyoge vratacodanā syāt // MS_6,4.34 //
children.translated_text: In the joining with calves, there would be an injunction of the <s>vrata</s> (observance). // MS_6,4.34 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, barhiṣā vai paurṇamāse vratam upayanti, vatsenāmāvāsyāyām{*6/129*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ [695]{*6/130*} vatsasādhanakaṃ vrataṃ vidhīyate, uta vratasya kāla iti. atha vatso vratāṅgam iti. kiṃ prāptam. vatsasādhanakaṃ vrataṃ vidhīyata iti. amānāsyāyāṃ vatsair vrataṃ kuryād iti, vatsavratasaṃyogo 'pūrvaḥ. sa vidhīyate, tasmiṃś ca vidhīyamāna ubhayam api vihitaṃ bhavati, vatso vrataṃ ca.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) [rites] it is heard: 'With <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) they undertake the <s>vrata</s> at the full moon; with calves at the new moon.' There a doubt [arises]: [695] is a <s>vrata</s> accomplished by means of calves being enjoined, or is this [prescribing] the time of the <s>vrata</s>? Or, [is the question whether] the calf is a subsidiary of the <s>vrata</s>? What is the prima facie view? A <s>vrata</s> accomplished by means of calves is being enjoined. [The reasoning:] 'At the new moon one should perform the <s>vrata</s> with calves' — the conjunction of calves with the <s>vrata</s> is unprecedented. That is what is being enjoined; and when that is being enjoined, both are [thereby] enjoined — the calf and the <s>vrata</s>.

children.text: kālo votpannasaṃyogād yathoktasya // MS_6,4.35 //
children.translated_text: Or [it prescribes] the time, because the conjunction [of the vrata with calves] is [already] established, of what has [already] been stated [elsewhere]. // MS_6,4.35 //

children.text: yathoktasya vacanāntareṇa prāptasya{*6/131*} kālo 'yaṃ vidhīyate. kutaḥ. utpannasaṃyogāt, utpannasaṃyogo 'yaṃ vratasya, notpattisaṃyogaḥ. katham. amāṣamamāṃsaṃ bahusarpiṣkaṃ vrataṃ vratayantīti vihitaṃ pūrvaṃ vratam. aprajñātaś ca kālaḥ. tasmāt kālavidhir iti.
children.translated_text: This [sentence] prescribes the time of what has [already] been stated and obtained through another [Vedic] statement. Why? Because of the established conjunction — this conjunction of the <s>vrata</s> [with calves] is [already] established, not an originating conjunction. How? 'They observe the <s>vrata</s> — [a diet] without <s>māṣa</s> beans, without meat, with abundant ghee' — thus the <s>vrata</s> has been previously enjoined. And the time is unknown. Therefore it is a prescription of time.

children.text: arthāparimāṇāc ca // MS_6,4.36 //
children.translated_text: And because the meaning cannot be delimited. // MS_6,4.36 //

children.text: na ca śakyo{*6/132*} 'trārthaḥ parimātum, vatsena vratam upayantīti kiṃ vatso 'tra vratayitavya evaṃ vatsena vratam upagataṃ bhavati{*6/133*}, kiṃ vatsena hastasthānīyena vratayitavyam ity evaṃ tad upetaṃ bhavati{*6/134*}, uta vatsaṃ saṃnidhāya tad upeyād{*6/135*} iti. naiva vyavatiṣṭhate śāstrārthaḥ. karaṇaṃ hy etan nirdiṣṭam, netikartavyatā. etāvad uktam, vatsasādhanaṃ vrataṃ kuryāt. katham ity etad aviśeṣākāṅkṣam evāvatiṣṭheta. naivārthaḥ paricchidyate, vrate kiṃ vatsena kriyata iti. athavā yad vā tad veti. tathā vatso vratena saṃbadhyamāna iṣṭaḥ syāt, aparārthatām āpadyeta, parārthatāṃ cāsya dyotayati vibhaktis tṛtīyā. sādhakatame hi sā bhavati. tasmād api kālārthaḥ saṃyogaḥ.
children.translated_text: And the meaning here cannot be delimited — 'they undertake the <s>vrata</s> with calves' — what [does this mean]? Is the calf to be observed as a vrata [i.e., a calf-diet], [meaning] thus a <s>vrata</s> is undertaken by means of a calf? Or should one observe the <s>vrata</s> using the calf as a hand-substitute [i.e., instrument], [meaning] thus it is undertaken? Or should one perform [the vrata] having placed the calf nearby? The meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative text) simply does not settle down. For this is designated as an instrument, not as a procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>). This much is stated: one should perform the <s>vrata</s> accomplished by calves. As to 'how?' — that remains unsettled, expecting [further] specification. The meaning is simply not determined — what is done by the calf in the <s>vrata</s>? Or rather, [one might say] 'whatever it may be.' Similarly, if the calf were connected with the <s>vrata</s>, it would be desirable [only if it had a purpose]; [otherwise] it would become purposeless, and the instrumental case indicates its being for another's purpose. For [the instrumental] applies to what is most instrumental. Therefore the conjunction is for the purpose of [indicating] time.

children.text: vatsas tu śrutisaṃyogāt tadaṅgaṃ syāt // MS_6,4.37 //
children.translated_text: But the calf would be a subsidiary of that [vrata], because of the connection with <s>śruti</s>. // MS_6,4.37 //

children.text: yad uktam, vihitatvād vratasyānuvāda iti, satyam etat{*6/136*}. [696]{*6/137*} yad{*6/138*} uktam, kālavidhānārtha iti. tan na, vatsas tadaṅgatvena vidhīyate. kutaḥ. śrutisaṃyogāt, vatse 'ṅge vidhīyamāne śrutir nimittam, kāle lakṣaṇaśabdaḥ{*6/139*} syāt. śrutilakṣaṇāviśaye ca śrutir nyāyyā. tasmād aṅgaṃ vatsya iti.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'the <s>vrata</s> is a restatement because of being [already] enjoined' — that is true. [696] [But] as to what was said — 'it is for the purpose of prescribing time' — that is not so; the calf is enjoined as a subsidiary of that [vrata]. Why? Because of the connection with <s>śruti</s> (direct Vedic statement) — when the calf is being enjoined as a subsidiary, <s>śruti</s> is the basis; for [indicating] time, an inferential expression (<s>lakṣaṇaśabda</s>) would [have to] be [the basis]. And where both <s>śruti</s> and inferential [meaning] are possible, <s>śruti</s> is proper. Therefore the calf is a subsidiary.

children.text: kālas tu syād acodanā // MS_6,4.38 //
children.translated_text: [It prescribes] the time; but it is not an injunction. // MS_6,4.38 //

children.text: kālas tv eṣa nirdiśyate, na vatso 'ṅgaṃ vidhīyate. naiṣa codanā, barhiṣā vai paurṇamāse vratam upayanti. vatsenāmāvāsyāyām{*6/140*} iti. katham avagamyate. vidhinaikavākyatvāt, parastāc ca vidhiḥ samāmnāyate, purā vatsānām upākartor daṃpatī aśrīyatām{*6/141*} iti. yady eṣo 'pi vidhiḥ syāt, vākyam bhidyeta. anuvādaś ca tathābhūtasyārthasya bhavati. na ca vatsāṅgatā aprāptā{*6/142*}, aprāptas{*6/143*} tu kālaḥ.
children.translated_text: This designates the time; the calf is not enjoined as a subsidiary. This is not an injunction — 'With <s>barhis</s> they undertake the <s>vrata</s> at the full moon; with calves at the new moon.' How is this understood? Because of being one sentence with an injunction — for an injunction is recorded after [this statement]: 'Before the separation of the calves, the couple should eat.' If this too were an injunction, the sentence would be split. And a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) is of something that is already [known] in such a form. And the subsidiary status of calves is not unestablished [i.e., it is already known from elsewhere]; but the time is unestablished.

children.text: anarthakaś ca karmasaṃyoge // MS_6,4.39 //
children.translated_text: And [the calf] is purposeless when conjoined with the ritual action. // MS_6,4.39 //

children.text: na ca śakyo vatso 'tra vratayitum, karmasaṃyoge vatsena nārthaḥ śakyate kaścit kartum. tasmād api na vatso 'ṅgam.
children.translated_text: And the calf cannot be employed in the <s>vrata</s> here — when conjoined with the ritual action, no purpose can be accomplished by means of the calf. Therefore the calf is not a subsidiary.

children.text: avacanāc ca svaśabdasya // MS_6,4.40 //
children.translated_text: And because of the absence of a statement of its own word. // MS_6,4.40 //

children.text: na caitad ucyate, viśvasya{*6/144*} śrapitaṃ vatsaṃ vratayiṣyata iti. na ca, asyārthasya svaśabdaḥ śrūyate. vatsa ity ākṛtiśabdo māṃse na vartate. tasmād eṣa kāla iti//
children.translated_text: And this is not stated — 'one will observe as a <s>vrata</s> a cooked calf of every kind.' And no proper word (<s>svaśabda</s>) for this meaning is heard. The word '<s>vatsa</s>' (calf) is a class-term and does not apply to meat. Therefore this [refers to] time.

children.text: kālaś cet saṃnayatpakṣe talliṅgasaṃyogāt // MS_6,4.41 //
children.translated_text: If [it prescribes] time, [it would apply] in the case of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>, because of the connection with its indicator. // MS_6,4.41 //

children.text: kālārthaḥ saṃyoga ity etat samadhigatam, idānīṃ saṃdehaḥ. [697]{*6/145*} kiṃ saṃnayatpakṣa eva kālaḥ, utāsaṃnayato 'pīti. kiṃ prāptam. saṃnayatpakṣe. kutaḥ. evaṃ śrūyate, purā vatsānām apākartor iti. na cāsaṃnayato vatsāpākaraṇam asti. tasmāt saṃnayatpakṣa eṣa kālaḥ. apākaraṇaṃ liṅgam iti//
children.translated_text: It has been determined that the conjunction is for the purpose of [indicating] time. Now a doubt [arises]: [697] Is the time only in the case of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> (mixed milk offering), or also of one who does not? What is the prima facie view? In the case of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>. Why? For thus it is heard: 'Before the separation of the calves.' And there is no separation of calves for one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>. Therefore this time [applies only] in the case of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>. The separation [of calves] is the indicator.

children.text: kālārthatvād vobhayoḥ pratīyeta{*6/146*} // MS_6,4.42 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of [the conjunction] being for the purpose of time, it would apply to both. // MS_6,4.42 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati, na saṃnayatpakṣa eva, asaṃnayato 'py eṣa kālaḥ syāt. kutaḥ. kālārthatvāt, na vatsāpākaraṇena vrate kiṃcit prayojanam asti. kālena tu prayojanam, yena ca tatra prayojanam, sa lakṣyate. kathaṃ punar vatsāpākaraṇaṃ kālārtham iti, parārthatvāt. payase hi te 'pākriyante, tathā hi dṛṣṭārthatā bhavati, itarathādṛṣṭārthatā syāt. tasmān nopādeyatvena vatsāpākaraṇaṃ śrūyata iti. yat tūktam, talliṅgasaṃyogāt saṃnayatpakṣa eveti. tan na, asaṃnayato 'pi kālāhānāt. yasyāpi na sāṃnāyyam, tasyāpi vatsāpākaraṇam eva na syāt, na tu vatsāpākaraṇakālo 'pi, kālena ca naḥ prayojanam, na vatsāpākaraṇena. yathā śaṅkhavelāyām āgantavyam iti. yasminn api grāme śaṅkho nādhmāyate tasminn api sa tathākālo{*6/147*} 'stīti, nāgamanaṃ parihāsyate. evam ihāpy asaty api vatsāpākaraṇe tatkāle bhidyamāne vratam, tasmin kāle na parihāsyata iti.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' reverses the position. Not only in the case of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> — this time would apply also to one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>. Why? Because of [the conjunction] being for the purpose of time — for there is no purpose served by the separation of calves in the <s>vrata</s>. But there is a purpose [served] by the time; and that by which there is a purpose there — that is what is indicated. But how is the separation of calves for the purpose of time? Because of being for another's purpose — for they [the calves] are separated for the sake of milk; thus there is a visible purpose, otherwise there would be an invisible purpose. Therefore the separation of calves is not heard as something to be adopted [as a ritual element]. Now, as to what was said — 'because of the connection with its indicator, [it applies] only in the case of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>' — that is not so, because even for one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>, the time is not lost. Even for one who has no <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>, there would simply be no separation of calves, but the time of the separation of calves [still exists]; and our purpose is with the time, not with the separation of calves. Just as [one says] 'one should come at the time of the conch-blowing' — even in a village where no conch is blown, that same time exists, and the coming is not abandoned. Similarly here too, even when there is no separation of calves, when the <s>vrata</s> falls at that time, it will not be abandoned at that time.
