children.text: prastare śākhā śrayaṇavat // MS_6,4.43 //
children.translated_text: As in the case of placing branches on the <s>prastara</s> (grass bundle). // MS_6,4.43 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeteti. tatra śrūyate, saha śākhayā prastaraṃ praharatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ śākhā [698]{*6/148*} prastarasyāṅgabhūtā, aṅgaprayojanasaṃbandhas tayoḥ. atha kālārthaḥ saṃyogaḥ, prastarapraharaṇakāle śākhā prahartavyeti. kiṃ prāptam. prastare śākhā śrayaṇavat. prastarasyāṅgabhūtā śākhā. kutaḥ. saha śākhayā prastaraṃ praharatīti. sahayukte 'pradhāne tṛtīyā vibhaktir bhavati. sā ca śākhāyāṃ tṛtīyā. tasmāt prastarasya śākhā guṇabhūtā, prastare ca dvitīyā, sahayoge ca tṛtīyā{*6/149*}, tṛtīyā guṇataḥ, dvitīyā pradhānataḥ. nanu na śākhayā prastarasya kaścid upakāraḥ kriyate. satyaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ kriyate, kiṃ tv adṛṣṭaṃ kriyate, śrayaṇavat, yathā payasā maitrāvaruṇaṃ śrīṇātīti dvitīyātṛtīyāsaṃyogād adṛṣṭaś copakāro gamyate. evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites. There it is heard: 'He strikes the <s>prastara</s> (grass bundle) together with the branch.' There a doubt [arises]: is the branch a subsidiary of the <s>prastara</s>, there being a connection between the two for a subsidiary purpose? Or is the connection for the purpose of time — [meaning] the branch should be struck at the time of striking the <s>prastara</s>? What is the prima facie view? The branch is to the <s>prastara</s> as mixing (<s>śrayaṇa</s>) [is to the oblation]. The branch is a subsidiary of the <s>prastara</s>. Why? 'He strikes the <s>prastara</s> together with the branch' — in [a construction with] <s>saha</s> ('together with'), the instrumental case-ending applies to what is subordinate. And the instrumental is on 'branch.' Therefore the branch is subordinate to the <s>prastara</s>; for the <s>prastara</s> there is the accusative [indicating it is the primary object], and in the <s>saha</s>-construction the instrumental [marks] subordination, the accusative [marks] primacy. [The objector says:] but no benefit is rendered to the <s>prastara</s> by the branch. True — no visible benefit is rendered, but an invisible (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) benefit is rendered, as with mixing — just as in 'he mixes the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [offering] with milk,' from the combination of accusative and instrumental, an invisible benefit is understood. So too here.

children.text: kālavidhir vobhayor vidyamānatvāt // MS_6,4.44 //
children.translated_text: Or [it may be] a time-prescription, because of both being already established. // MS_6,4.44 //

children.text: kālavidhir vā syāt. kutaḥ. ubhayor vidyamānatvāt. prastaras tāvat srugdhāraṇārthaḥ prāpto vidyate, tasya praharaṇam api viśiṣṭe kāle vākyāntareṇa vihitam. tataḥ śākhāyāḥ pratipādanārtham, tasyaitat punarvacanam. ucyate, bhavatu prastarasya punarvacanam, śākhā tv atra vidhīyata iti. ucyate, ubhayor api vidyamānatvāt, śākhā pūrvaṃ{*6/150*} vihitā vatsāpākaraṇārthā, idānīṃ punaḥ kiṃ guṇabhūtā codyate, uta pratipādyata iti. pratipādyamānāyāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam, deśaviyogāt pracaritum avakāśaḥ syād yā yāvatī ca mātrā, deśāntarasaṃyogasya na dṛṣṭaṃ kiṃcid asti. tasmāt praharaṇaṃ pratipattis tasyāḥ, tasmāt parataḥ prayojanābhāvāt kālaniyamaḥ{*6/151*} kriyate{*6/152*}. nanu tṛtīyā 'pradhāno bhavati, sā ca śākhāyām. atrocyate, yāsau [699]{*6/153*} śākhāyāṃ tṛtīyā, sā dvitīyārthe. yā ca prastare dvitīyā, sā tṛtīyārthe. katham avagamyate. sahayoge ekasmin{*6/154*} kāla ubhayam api prahartavyam iti. atra yasya nirjñātaḥ kālaḥ, tasyānuvādaḥ, yasya tv anirjñātaḥ, tasya vidhiḥ. śākhāyāś cānirjñātaḥ, prastarasya nirjñātaḥ, tasya punaruccāraṇam anirjñātārtham, tad apradhānam. itarasyoccāraṇaṃ pradhānam, prādhānyaṃ ca dvitīyārthaḥ, tatra tṛtīyā. pārārthyam api tṛtīyārthaḥ, tatra dvitīyā. tasmād ayathārthaṃ vibhaktivacanam.
children.translated_text: Or it may be a time-prescription. Why? Because of both being already established. The <s>prastara</s>, being obtained for the purpose of holding the ladle, already exists; its striking too is prescribed by a separate statement at a specific time. Then, for the purpose of prescribing the branch, this is its restatement. It is said: granted the <s>prastara</s>'s restatement, but the branch is being prescribed here. We reply: because of both being already established — the branch too was previously prescribed for the purpose of driving away the calves; now again, is it being argued as a subsidiary, or is it being prescribed [for time]? When it is being prescribed, there is a visible purpose — because of separation of place, there would be an occasion for it to function [independently], to whatever extent. But for connection with another place, there is no visible [purpose]. Therefore striking is its prescription [for time]; hence, because of the absence of purpose beyond that, a time-restriction is made. [The objector says:] but the instrumental [marks] what is subordinate, and that is on the branch. To this we reply: that instrumental [698] on the branch is in the sense of the accusative. And the accusative on the <s>prastara</s> is in the sense of the instrumental. How is this understood? In the <s>saha</s>-construction, both are to be struck at one time. Here, that whose time is [already] known — its [mention] is a restatement; but that whose time is unknown — its [mention] is a prescription. The branch's [time] is unknown, the <s>prastara</s>'s is known — its reiteration is for the purpose of the unknown. That is subordinate. The other's statement is primary; and primacy is the meaning of the accusative — there the instrumental [is used]. Being-for-another's-purpose too is the meaning of the instrumental — there the accusative [is used]. Therefore the case-endings are not used in their literal sense.

children.text: atatsaṃskārārthatvāc ca // MS_6,4.45 //
children.translated_text: And because of not being for the purpose of that [prastara's] consecration. // MS_6,4.45 //

children.text: na ca, śākhayā prastarasyopakāro dṛṣṭaḥ kriyate. kāṣṭaṃ dahyamānasya tṛṇasya nopakāre vartate. tṛṇaṃ tu kāṣṭhasyopakuryāt. tasmān na śākhā prastarārthā.
children.translated_text: And the branch does not render a visible benefit to the <s>prastara</s>. Wood does not serve to benefit burning grass. But grass could benefit wood. Therefore the branch is not for the <s>prastara</s>'s purpose.

children.text: tasmāc ca viprayoge syāt // MS_6,4.46 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, in separation [from the prastara], it should [still be struck]. // MS_6,4.46 //

children.text: kiṃ bhavati prayojanam, yadi prastarasya guṇabhūtā, tathāpi prastaraprahārakāle śākhā pratipādyata{*6/155*} iti. ucyate, yadi prastarasya prahriyamāṇasyāṅgabhūtā śākhā, tato vinā{*6/156*} prastareṇa, na prahartavyā bhavati. athāṅgabhūtā vināpi prastareṇa prahartavyā. asmābhir uktaṃ prastarakāle prahartavyeti, tasmāc ca viprayoge syāt, tasmād eva kāraṇāt prastaraviprayoge 'pi śākhāyāḥ praharaṇaṃ syād iti.
children.translated_text: What is the purpose if the branch is a subsidiary of the <s>prastara</s> — even so, the branch is prescribed at the time of striking the <s>prastara</s>? We reply: if the branch were a subsidiary of the <s>prastara</s> being struck, then without the <s>prastara</s>, it should not be struck. But [if it is] a subsidiary, even without the <s>prastara</s> it should be struck. We have said it should be struck at the time of the <s>prastara</s>; and therefore in separation — for that very reason, even in separation from the <s>prastara</s>, the branch should be struck.

children.text: upaveṣaś ca pakṣe syāt // MS_6,4.47 //
children.translated_text: And in the [prima facie] view, [the branch] would be placed down [i.e., not struck]. // MS_6,4.47 //

children.text: yathā pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, tathā sati, sāṃnyāyye saty asati ca śākhā [700]{*6/157*} vidyata ity upaveṣo sati cāsati{*6/158*} ca syāt. yathā tu siddhāntaḥ, tathā sāṃnyāyyapakṣe śākhā satī hi pratipādyata iti. tatraivopaveṣo nānyatreti.
children.translated_text: According to the first [prima facie] view, when the normal [prastara-striking] is present or absent, the branch [699] exists — so the placing down (<s>upaveṣa</s>) would [occur] whether [the prastara] is present or absent. But according to the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), in the normal case the branch, being present, is prescribed [for that time]. Therefore the placing down is only there [at that time], not elsewhere.

children.text: abhyudaye kālāparādhād ijyācodanā syāt yathā pañcaśarāve // MS_6,5.1 //
children.translated_text: In the case of the rising [of the moon], because of a lapse in time, there would be an injunction of sacrifice, as with the five-saucer [offering]. // MS_6,5.1 //

children.text:
idam āmananti, vi vā enaṃ prajayā paśubhir ardhayati, vardhayaty asya bhrātṛvyam, yasya havir niruptaṃ purastāc candramā abhyudeti{*6/160*} tredhā{*6/161*} taṇḍulān vibhajet, ye madhyamāḥ syuḥ, tān agnaye dātre puroḍāśam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet, ye sthaviṣṭhās tān indrāya pradātre dadhaṃś carum, ye kṣodiṣṭāḥ, tān viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya śṛte carum{*6/162*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ kālāparādhe yāgāntaram idaṃ codyate, uta teṣv eva prakṛteṣu karmasu nimitte devatāpanayana iti.
kiṃ prāptam. abhyudaye, yaḥ kālāparādhaḥ, tatrejyācodanā syāt. katham. puroḍāśam agnaye dātre madhyamān kurvate{*6/163*}, ye sthaviṣṭhās tān indrāya pradātre dadhani caruṃ kuryāt, kṣodiṣṭhān viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāyeti, yajatis{*6/164*} tu phalabhoktṛsaṃyogād{*6/165*} iti vidhānaṃ{*6/166*} gamyate. yathā pañcaśarāve dravyadevatāsaṃbandhena karmāntaraṃ gamyate, yathā paśukāmeṣṭyām, yaḥ paśukāmaḥ syāt, so 'māvāsyāyām iṣṭvā vatsān apākuryāt, ye sthaviṣṭhāḥ, tān agnaye sanimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet, ye madhyamāḥ, tān viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya śṛte caruṃ ye 'ṇiṣṭhāḥ, tān indrāya pradātre dadhaṃś carum iti. evam ihāpīti. api ca na prakṛte dravye devatā [702]{*6/167*} śrūyte, śṛte carum iti hi tatra bhavati vacanam. na cābhyudayakāle śrapaṇaṃ kṛtam asti, tasmāt karmāntaram.
children.translated_text:
They record this: 'He indeed diminishes him in offspring and cattle, [but] increases his enemy — he whose offering (<s>havis</s>), having been prepared, [is such that] the moon rises before [the offering is completed].' 'He should divide the rice grains into three parts: those that are medium — for <s>Agni</s> the Giver he should prepare an eight-potsherd cake; those that are largest — for <s>Indra</s> the Bestower, a sour-milk <s>caru</s> (porridge); those that are smallest — for <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>, a <s>caru</s> cooked [in milk].' There a doubt [arises]: when there is a lapse in time, is this a different sacrifice being enjoined, or is it a change of deities (<s>devatāpanayana</s>) in those very established rites?
What is the prima facie view? At the rising [of the moon], when there is a lapse in time, there would be an injunction of sacrifice. How? They make the medium [grains into] a cake for <s>Agni</s> the Giver; the largest — for <s>Indra</s> the Bestower, a <s>caru</s> in sour-milk; the smallest — for <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>; and the word <s>yajati</s> ('he sacrifices'), through its connection with the enjoyer of the fruit, is understood as a prescription [of a new sacrifice]. Just as in the five-saucer [offering], through the connection of substance and deity, a different rite is understood — as in the <s>Paśukāmeṣṭi</s> (animal-desiring sacrifice): 'He who desires cattle should, having sacrificed on the new-moon day, drive away the calves; those that are largest — for <s>Agni Sanimit</s>, he should prepare an eight-potsherd [cake]; those that are medium — for <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>, a <s>caru</s> cooked [in milk]; those that are smallest — for <s>Indra</s> the Bestower, a sour-milk <s>caru</s>.' So too here. Moreover, the deity is not heard in connection with the established substance — for there is the statement 'a <s>caru</s> cooked [in milk].' And at the time of the rising, the cooking has not been done; therefore [this is] a different rite.

children.text: apanayo vā vidyamānatvāt // MS_6,5.2 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] a change of deity, because of [the rites] being already established. // MS_6,5.2 //

children.text: devatāpanayo vā. kutaḥ. vidyamānatvāt, vidyante hi karmāṇi prakṛtāni, teṣu vidyamāneṣu punar devatāsaṃbandho haviṣo nopapadyate. yasyānupapattyā yāgaḥ kalpyeta. tasmān na yāgāntaram, teṣv eva haviḥṣu devatāntarāṇi vidhīyante.
children.translated_text: Or [it is] a change of deity. Why? Because of being already established — for the established rites exist; when they are already established, the connection of another deity with the offering is not appropriate — [for] on the basis of such inappropriateness, a [separate] sacrifice would be postulated. Therefore it is not a different sacrifice; in those very offerings, different deities are prescribed.

children.text: tadrūpatvāc ca śabdānām // MS_6,5.3 //
children.translated_text: And because of the words having that form [i.e., indicating deity-change]. // MS_6,5.3 //

children.text: devatāpanayasarūpāś cāmī śabdā bhavanti, ye madhyamāḥ, teṣāṃ devatāntaraṃ vidhīyate. tatra dravyaṃ prāptam, aprāptā devatā vidhīyate. kathaṃ punar devatāvidhānārthe nānekaguṇvidhānadoṣo jāyeteti. ucyate, naivātrāneko guṇo vidhīyate kasmiṃścid vākye. taṇḍulān{*6/168*} vibhajed ity atra tāvad vibhāgamātraṃ vidhīyate. anyat sarvam anūdyate, tasmād adoṣaḥ. ye madhyamāḥ, teṣām agnir devatā vidhīyate, anyat puroḍāśādy anūdyate. ye sthaviṣṭhāḥ, teṣāṃ dadhisahitānām indro devatāsmin vākye vidhīyate. tatrārthaprāpte{*6/169*} śrapaṇe sati carutā, saha saptamyarthenārthaprāptenaivāsmin vākye 'nūdyate. ye kṣodiṣṭhāḥ, teṣāṃ śṛtasahitānāṃ viṣṇuḥ śipiviṣṭo devatā vidhīyate, anyat sarvam anūdyate. tasmād adoṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: And these words are of the form of a deity-change: 'those that are medium' — for them a different deity is prescribed. There the substance is [already] obtained; the unobtained deity is prescribed. But how is it that in prescribing the deity, the fault of prescribing multiple subsidiaries does not arise? We reply: here no multiple subsidiary is prescribed in any single sentence. In 'he should divide the rice grains' — there, only the division is prescribed; everything else is restated — therefore there is no fault. 'Those that are medium' — for them <s>Agni</s> is prescribed as the deity; the rest — the cake etc. — is restated. 'Those that are largest' — for them combined with sour-milk, <s>Indra</s> is prescribed as the deity in this sentence. There, when the cooking is established by implication, the <s>caru</s>-nature [follows], together with the meaning of the locative case — it is restated in this very sentence as something established by implication. 'Those that are smallest' — for them combined with what is cooked, <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s> is prescribed as the deity; everything else is restated. Therefore there is no fault.

NOTES:

*{6/169: E1,6; E2: tatrārdhaprāptā}*

children.text: ātañcanābhyāsasya darśanāt // MS_6,5.4 //
children.translated_text: Because of seeing the repetition of the sprinkling (<s>ātañcana</s>). // MS_6,5.4 //

children.text: ātañcanābhyāsaṃ ca darśayati. katham. evaṃ śrūyate, yadi [703]{*6/170*} bibhīyād abhimodeṣyatīti mahārātre havīṃṣi nirvapet. phalīkṛtais taṇḍulair upāsīta, ardhaṃ dadhi havir ātañcanārthaṃ nidadhyāt, ardhaṃ na. yady abhyudiyād anenātacya{*6/171*} pracaret, yady u na{*6/172*}, brāhmaṇaṃ{*6/173*} bhojayed iti. yadi karmāntaram, upādeyatvena tadā taṇḍulā dadhi śṛtaṃ ca. tasmāl laukikāny upādeyāni, na hy eṣa tadā prakṛtānāṃ vyāpāraḥ, tatrāvinaṣṭe dadhani, aparedyur āmāvāsye kriyamāṇe vidyate dadhīti nātañcanam āvarteta. tasyām evābhyuditeṣṭau dadhi vidyata iti nātañcanaṃ syāt. atha nimitte devatāpanayaḥ, tatas tasmin dadhani caruḥ kṛta iti, punar āmāvāsye dohe ātañcanena kāryam, evam ātañcanābhyāsasya darśanaṃ devatāvidhāne yujyata iti.
children.translated_text: And a repetition of the sprinkling is observed. How? Thus it is heard: 'If [703] he fears that [the moon] will rise — at midnight he should prepare the offerings. He should sit with parched rice grains; half the sour-milk he should set aside for the purpose of sprinkling, and half not. If [the moon] rises, having sprinkled with this, he should proceed; if not, he should feed a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' If [this were] a different rite, the rice, sour-milk and cooked [milk] would be freshly procured. Therefore worldly [i.e., already available] materials are to be used — for there is no employment of the established [rite's materials] for that [new rite] at that time. When the sour-milk is not spoiled, on the next day when the new-moon [rite] is being performed, the sour-milk exists — so the sprinkling would not repeat. In that very rising-rite (<s>abhyuditeṣṭi</s>), the sour-milk exists — so there would be no sprinkling. But if [it is] a change of deity upon an occasion, then since a <s>caru</s> has been made with that sour-milk, again in the new-moon [rite], the sprinkling must be done with fresh milking — thus the observation of the repetition of sprinkling is appropriate when [it is] a deity-prescription.

children.text: apūrvatvād vidhānaṃ syāt // MS_6,5.5 //
children.translated_text: Because of being unprecedented, it would be a [separate] prescription. // MS_6,5.5 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, yathā paśukāmeṣṭyāṃ karmāntaram, yaḥ paśukāmaḥ syāt, so 'māvāsyām iṣṭvā vatsān apākuryād iti. tat parihartavyam. tatrocyate, yuktaṃ yat tatra karmāntaravidhānam. kutaḥ. apūrvatvāt, na tatra kaścit pūrvaprāpto yāgo vidyate, so 'māvāsyām iṣṭveti hi parisamāpte tasminn idam ārabhyate. tatra dravyadevatāsaṃyukto nirvapatiśabdo nāntareṇotsargam, dravyadevatayoḥ saṃbandho vidyata{*6/174*} iti yajatiṃ gamayati. na tv ihaivam, iha hi yāgaḥ prakṛto gamyate, tasminn eva vidyamānasya dravyasya devatāsaṃbandhamātraṃ vidhīyata iti na doṣo bhavati.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'as in the <s>Paśukāmeṣṭi</s>, it is a different rite: he who desires cattle should, having sacrificed on the new-moon day, drive away the calves' — that must be refuted. To that we reply: it is proper that there the prescription of a different rite [applies]. Why? Because of being unprecedented — there, no previously obtained sacrifice exists. 'Having sacrificed on the new-moon day' — when that is completed, this [new rite] is commenced. There, the word <s>nirvapati</s> ('he prepares'), being connected with substance and deity, does not [function] without an offering-act (<s>utsarga</s>); the connection of substance and deity exists — so it indicates [the word] <s>yajati</s> ('he sacrifices'). But here it is not so — here a sacrifice is understood as [already] established; in that very established [sacrifice], only the connection of a deity with the substance is prescribed — so no fault arises.

children.text: payodoṣāt pañcaśarāve 'duṣṭaṃ hītarat // MS_6,5.6 //
children.translated_text: Because of a fault in the milk, in the five-saucer [offering] the other [substance] is undamaged. // MS_6,5.6 //

children.text: atha yad upavarṇitam, yathā pañcaśarāve karmāntaraṃ vidhīyate, [704]{*6/175*} evam ihāpīti, tat parihartavyam iti. atrocyate, yuktaṃ pañcaśarāve karmāntaram. duṣṭaṃ hi tatra dravyam, yasya devatā vidhīyate. tatrāvaśyaṃ dravyam upādeyatvena codayitavyam, tasminn upādīyamāne devatāntare cāpūrvaḥ saṃbandho vidhīyate, tad yāgāntaraṃ bhavatīti. itarad iha dravyam aduṣṭam, tad anūdya, prakṛte yāge devatā vidhīyata ity uktam, tasmād adoṣa iti.
children.translated_text: Now, what was described — that just as in the <s>pañcaśarāva</s> (five-saucer offering) a different ritual action is prescribed, so too here — that must be refuted. To this we reply: it is fitting that a different ritual action [is prescribed] in the <s>pañcaśarāva</s>. For there, the substance (<s>dravya</s>) is defective, for which a deity is prescribed. There, the substance must necessarily be enjoined as something to be accepted; when it is being accepted, and a connection with a different deity is prescribed as unprecedented, that becomes a different sacrifice. But here the substance is not defective; that [substance] being referred to, it has been stated that a deity is prescribed in the original sacrifice — therefore there is no fault.

children.text: sāṃnyāyye 'pi tatheti cet // MS_6,5.7 //
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is likewise with the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> — // MS_6,5.7 //

children.text: evaṃ cet paśyasi, sāṃnyāyye 'pi doṣaḥ. tad api hy abhyudaye tatkālāpabhraṃśād duṣṭam iti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus, [there is] a fault with the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> as well. For that too, during the <s>abhyudaya</s> (rising [of the moon]), is defective due to the loss of proper timing.

children.text: na tasyāduṣṭatvād aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam // MS_6,5.8 //
children.translated_text: No, because it is not defective — for the cause is undistinguished. // MS_6,5.8 //

children.text: naitad evam, pañcaśarāve hi duṣṭaṃ dravyam, iha tādṛśam evāvatiṣthate. nanu kālāpabhraṃśena duṣṭam. na duṣyati, aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam. abhyudaye prāyaścittavidhānaṃ duṣṭe 'py upapadyate, kālāparādhe 'duṣṭe{*6/176*} 'pi tat. akāle hy abhipravṛttasya śakyate devatāvidhānam, na tu vinaṣṭasya.
children.translated_text: This is not so. For in the <s>pañcaśarāva</s> the substance is defective, but here it remains exactly the same. [The objector says:] but it is defective due to the loss of proper timing. [We reply:] it is not defective, for the cause is undistinguished. The prescription of atonement (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) during the <s>abhyudaya</s> is applicable even to what is defective; that [prescription applies] even when there is no fault in timing but a temporal transgression. For a deity can be prescribed for [an offering] that has commenced at an improper time, but not for one that has been destroyed.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/176: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: kālāparādhenāduṣṭe}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:

children.text: lakṣaṇārthā śṛtaśrutiḥ // MS_6,5.9 //
children.translated_text: The statement about 'cooked' (<s>śṛta</s>) is for the purpose of characterization. // MS_6,5.9 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, na prakṛte dravye devatā śrūyate, śṛte carum iti tatra bhavati vacanam, na cābhyudayakāle śrapaṇaṃ kṛtam astīti, tat parihartavyam. atrocyate, lakṣaṇārtheyaṃ śṛtaśrutiḥ, dharmalakṣaṇārthā{*6/177*} śṛte, śṛtasahacaritadharmaka iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — that a deity is not heard regarding the original substance, and the statement 'a <s>caru</s> (porridge) in what is cooked' applies there, and cooking has not been done at the time of the <s>abhyudaya</s> — that must be refuted. To this we reply: this statement about 'cooked' (<s>śṛta</s>) is for the purpose of characterization — it is for the purpose of characterizing the <s>dharma</s> (ritual property): 'in what is cooked' [means] 'in what possesses the property associated with cooking.'

children.text: upāṃśuyāje 'vacanād yathāprakṛti // MS_6,5.10 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (silent offering), because of the absence of a [specific] statement, [it should be] as in the original [rite]. // MS_6,5.10 //

children.text: tasminn evābhyudaye saṃśayaḥ. kim upāṃśuyāge 'pi devatāpanayo bhaven neti. kiṃ prāptam. upāṃśuyājo yathāprakṛti syāt. kasmāt. avacanāt, yathāmīṣu vacanam, madhyamānām agnaye dātre puroḍāśāḥ{*6/179*} sthaviṣṭhānām indrāya pradātre dadhani caruḥ, kṣodiṣṭhānāṃ viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya śṛte caru iti. naitad upāṃśuyāje 'sti. tasmāt sa yathādevataṃ syāt.
children.translated_text: Regarding that very <s>abhyudaya</s>, a doubt [arises]: should deity-removal (<s>devatāpanaya</s>) apply to the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> as well, or not? What is the prima facie view? The <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> should be as in the original rite (<s>prakṛti</s>). Why? Because of the absence of a [specific] statement — just as in those [other offerings] there is a statement: 'Of the middling [grains], cakes for <s>Agni</s> the Giver; of the largest, a <s>caru</s> of curds for <s>Indra</s> the Bestower; of the smallest, a <s>caru</s> in what is cooked for <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>.' But this does not exist for the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s>. Therefore it should retain its original deity.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/179: E1,6; E2: puroḍāśaḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/179: E1,6; E2: <s>puroḍāśaḥ</s>}]

children.text: apanayo vā pravṛttyā yathetareṣām // MS_6,5.11 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, there is removal [of the deity], because of the procedure, just as for the others. // MS_6,5.11 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. upāṃśuyājasyāpanayaḥ. kena kāraṇena. pravṛttyā, akāle tantrapravṛttir devatāpanayasya kāraṇam. kutḥ. na hy atrābhyudaye sati taṇḍulā vibhāgārtham upādīyante. kiṃ tarhi. abhyuditasya haviṣo vibhāga ucyate, abhyudayenāparāhnasyeti{*6/180*}. katham avagamyate. yasyābhyudiyād ityaviśeṣaśravaṇāt, sarvasyaiva hy aparādhenābhyudeti, aparādhaś cākāle tantrapravṛttiḥ. evaṃ ca sati na tad dhavis taṇḍulaiḥ śakyaṃ viśeṣṭum. tasmād upāṃśuyāgasyāpi{*6/181*} vibhāgaḥ. tredhā taṇḍulān vibhajed iti hy anena vākyena devatāpanayaḥ kriyate, vidhir hy atra vibhajed iti. vibhāgaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ{*6/182*}. katham iti. vibhāge viśeṣaparāṇy uttarāṇi vākyāni. idam idaṃ ca dravyam asyai devatāyai, idam idaṃ cāsyā iti. yasya dravyasya viśeṣavibhāgo nāsti, tasyāpi vibhajed iti sāmānyavibhāgaḥ. tasmād yathaivetareṣāṃ vibhāgaḥ, evam upāṃśuyājasyāpīti. athavā, upāṃśuyājadravyāt [706]{*6/183*} pūrveṇa vākyenāpanītā devatā. na tad apareṇa vākyena devatāntare{*6/184*} saṃyojitam. tasmāt prahīṇam eva tat.
children.translated_text:
The word <s>vā</s> ('or') reverses the position. There is removal [of the deity] even for the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s>. For what reason? Because of the procedure — the commencement of the <s>tantra</s> (collective ritual operation) at an improper time is the cause of deity-removal. How so? For here, during the <s>abhyudaya</s>, rice grains are not taken up for the purpose of portioning. Rather, the portioning of the offering that has undergone <s>abhyudaya</s> is stated — 'through the <s>abhyudaya</s>, of the afternoon's [offering].' How is this understood? Because of the unqualified statement 'of whatever [offering] undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s>' — for everything indeed undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s> through a temporal transgression, and the transgression is the commencement of the <s>tantra</s> at an improper time. This being so, that offering cannot be distinguished by the rice grains. Therefore there is portioning even of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s>. For the statement 'he should divide the rice grains into three parts' effects the deity-removal through this sentence, since the injunction here is 'he should divide' — meaning 'he should perform the division.' How? The subsequent sentences specify the division — 'this and this substance for this deity, this and this for that [deity].' For the substance whose specific division is not [stated], even so, the general division [applies] through 'he should divide.' Therefore, just as there is division for the others, so too for the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s>.
Alternatively, the deity has been removed from the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> substance by the former sentence. That [substance] has not been connected with another deity by the latter sentence. Therefore it is simply abandoned.

children.text: nirupte syāt tatsaṃyogāt // MS_6,5.12 //
children.translated_text: It should [apply] when [the offering] has been portioned (<s>nirupta</s>), because of the connection with that. // MS_6,5.12 //

children.text: asminn evodāharaṇe saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ yadi nirupte 'bhyudayo 'vagamyate, tadābhyuditeṣṭiḥ, utānirupte 'pīti. kiṃ prāptam. nirupte 'vagate 'bhyuditeṣṭiḥ syāt. kutaḥ. tatsaṃyogāt, nirvāpasaṃyogo hi bhavati, yasya havir niruptam iti. tasmād anirupte naitad vidhānam iti.
children.translated_text: Regarding this very example, a doubt [arises]: is the <s>abhyuditeṣṭi</s> (rite upon rising) understood only when [the offering] has been portioned, or even when it has not been portioned? What is the prima facie view? The <s>abhyuditeṣṭi</s> should [apply] when [the offering] has been portioned. How so? Because of the connection with that — for there is a connection with portioning, [as in] 'of one whose offering has been portioned.' Therefore this procedure does not [apply] when [the offering] has not been portioned.

children.text: pravṛtte vā prāpaṇān nimittasya // MS_6,5.13 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, [it applies] when [the ritual] has commenced, because of [that being] the attainment of the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>). // MS_6,5.13 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. akāle tantrapravṛttimātre syād etad vidhānam. prāptaṃ hi tāvaty eva nimittam, yasya havir abhyudetīti havir grahaṇaṃ lakṣaṇatvena. yasya havir abhyudetīti havir lakṣita udayo nimittam, pravṛttaṃ havir lakṣayati, nodāsīnam. tasmāt, havir abhyudetīty ucyamāne pravṛttaṃ havir abhyudetīti gamyate. na hi tan niruptam ity etena śakyaṃ viśeṣayitum. bhidyeta hi tadā vākyam. yasya havir niruptam, nāniruptam{*6/185*} ity evam apekṣyaṃāṇe havir abhyudetīti na śakyate vidhātum. tasmād anirupte 'pīṣṭir iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>vā</s> ('or') reverses the position. This procedure should [apply] upon the mere commencement of the <s>tantra</s> at an improper time. For the occasion is attained just to that extent — 'of one whose offering undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s>' — the word 'offering' (<s>havis</s>) serves as a characterization. The rising characterized by the offering is the occasion, and an offering that has commenced characterizes [the event], not one that is [merely] present. Therefore, when 'the offering undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s>' is stated, it is understood [as meaning] 'a commenced offering undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s>.' For it cannot be distinguished by 'that [offering] has been portioned' — for then the sentence would be split. When the [statement] 'of one whose offering has been portioned, not one whose has not been portioned' is thus expected, [the statement] 'the offering undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s>' cannot be prescribed. Therefore the <s>iṣṭi</s> (rite) [applies] even when [the offering] has not been portioned.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/185: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2 om. nāniruptam}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/185: E1,6,E2 (variant); E2 omits <s>nāniruptam</s>}]

children.text: lakṣaṇamātram itaram // MS_6,5.14 //
children.translated_text: The other [word, 'portioned'] is merely a characterization. // MS_6,5.14 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, niruptasaṃyogo bhavati, yasya havir niruptam iti, lakṣaṇamātram etan niruptam iti. kasmiṃścit padārthe tasya pravṛtta ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'there is a connection with portioning, [as in] of one whose offering has been portioned' — [the word] 'portioned' is merely a characterization. [It means] 'that which has commenced in some [stage of the] procedure' — this is the meaning.

children.text: tathā cānyārthadarśanam // MS_6,5.15 //
children.translated_text: And so there is an observation for another purpose. // MS_6,5.15 //

children.text: anyārtho 'pi caitam arthaṃ darśayati, sa yady agṛhītaṃ havir abhyudiyāt, prajñātam eva. tadaiṣā vratacaryā, yat pūrvedyur dugdhaṃ dadhi havir ātañcanaṃ tat kurvanti, pratimuñcanti vatsān, tān eva tat punar apākurvanti, tān aparāhṇe parṇaśākhayāpākaroti. tad yathaivādeḥ prajñātam āmāvāsyaṃ havir evam eva tad yady u vratacaryāṃ vā nodāśaṃseta, gṛhītaṃ vā havir abhyudiyād itarathā tarhi kuryāt, etān eva taṇḍulān sakṛtphalīkṛtān{*6/187*} iti, agṛhīte haviṣy anyaṃ vidhiṃ bruvan gṛhīte 'py anirupte vābhyudaye prāyaścittaṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: And another purpose also demonstrates this meaning: 'If the offering that has not been taken up undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s>, it is [already] known. Then this is the observance (<s>vratacaryā</s>): what was milked on the day before — the curds, the offering, the straining — that they do; they release the calves; they undo that very [thing] again; in the afternoon he removes [them] with a leaf-branch.' Just as from the outset the new-moon offering is known, so too that [case]. 'But if one would not undertake the observance, or if the offering that has been taken up undergoes <s>abhyudaya</s>, then in the other case one should do [as follows] — those very rice grains, once pounded' — thus, by stating a different procedure for when the offering has not been taken up, he shows that atonement [applies] even when [the offering] has been taken up but not [yet] portioned, upon <s>abhyudaya</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/187: E1,6; E2: suphalīkṛtān}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/187: E1,6; E2: <s>suphalīkṛtān</s>}]

children.text: anirupte 'bhyudite prākṛtībhyo nirvaped ity āśmarathyas taṇḍulabhūteṣv apanayāt // MS_6,5.16 //
children.translated_text: When [the offering] has not been portioned and <s>abhyudaya</s> [occurs], one should portion from the original [deities' shares], says <s>Āśmarathya</s>, because the removal [of deities applies] when [the substances] are in the state of rice grains. // MS_6,5.16 //

children.text: pravṛttamātraṃ nimittam iti sthitam. naimittikas tu devatāpanayo devatāntarasaṃyogaś ca, kiṃ nirvāpottarakālaṃ taṇḍulāvasthe haviṣi kartavyo nirvāpas tu prākṛtībhya eva syāt, jñāte 'bhyudaye, uta vaikṛtībhya eveti saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. [708]{*6/188*} anirupte 'bhyudite prākṛtībhyo nirvaped ity āśmarathya ācāryo manyate sma. kutaḥ. taṇḍulabhūteṣv apanayāt. taṇḍulabhūteṣv apanayaḥ śrūyate, yasya havir niruptaṃ purastāc candramā abhyudeti tredhā taṇḍulān vibhajed ity abhyudayāvagamād anantaraṃ taṇḍulavibhāgam āha. so 'taṇḍulabhūteṣu nāvakalpate. tasmād anirupte taṇḍulābhāvād anapanītā devatāḥ prākṛtya iti prākṛtībhya eva nirvaped iti.
children.translated_text: It is established that the mere commencement [of the ritual] is the occasion. But the occasioned [procedures] — deity-removal and connection with different deities — should they be performed after portioning, when the offering is still in the state of rice grains, with the portioning being from the original [deities'] shares once the <s>abhyudaya</s> is known? Or from the modified [deities' shares]? — this is the doubt. What then is the prima facie view? [708] When [the offering] has not been portioned and <s>abhyudaya</s> [occurs], one should portion from the original [deities' shares] — so teacher <s>Āśmarathya</s> held. How so? Because the removal [of deities applies] when [the substances] are in the state of rice grains. The removal is heard when [the substances] are in the state of rice grains: 'of one whose offering has been portioned, before [whom] the moon rises — he should divide the rice grains into three parts' — after knowing the <s>abhyudaya</s>, it states the division of the rice grains. That [removal] is not applicable when [the substances] are not in the state of rice grains. Therefore, when [the offering] has not been portioned, since rice grains are absent, the deities have not been removed from their original [assignments]; hence one should portion from the original [deities' shares] alone.

children.text: vyūrdhvabhāgbhyas tv ālekhanas tatkāritvād devatāpanayasya // MS_6,5.17 //
children.translated_text: But [one should portion] from those [shares] that participate in the subsequent [procedure], says <s>Ālekhana</s>, because the deity-removal is caused by that [commencement]. // MS_6,5.17 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. vyūrdhvaṃ yā bhajante karma, tābhyo nirvaped ity ālekhana ācāryo manyate sma. kutaḥ. tatkāritvād devatāpanayasya, yasmād akāle tantrapravṛttikārito devatāpanayaḥ, tasmād apanītā devateti vyūrdhvabhāgbhyo nirvaptavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: The word <s>tu</s> ('but') reverses the position. One should portion from the [shares] that participate in the subsequent ritual action — so teacher <s>Ālekhana</s> held. How so? Because the deity-removal is caused by that — since the deity-removal is caused by the commencement of the <s>tantra</s> at an improper time, therefore the deities have been removed, and one should portion from the subsequent [modified deities'] shares.

children.text: vinirupte na muṣṭīnām apanayas tadguṇatvāt // MS_6,5.18 //
children.translated_text: When [the offering] has been partially portioned, there is no removal of the [remaining] handfuls, because of their being subordinate to that [already portioned]. // MS_6,5.18 //

children.text: atha prārabdhe caturmuṣṭirnirvāpe 'parisamāpte bhavati saṃśayaḥ, yan niruptaṃ tan niruptam eva, avaśiṣṭaṃ kiṃ prākṛtībhyo nirvaptavyam, kiṃ vaikṛtībhyaḥ, uta tūṣṇīm eveti. kiṃ prāptam. vinirupte sāminirupta ity arthaḥ{*6/189*}. na tatra devatāpanayaḥ syāt. kutaḥ. tadguṇatvāt, nirvāpasya guṇo devatā, na muṣṭīnām, [709]{*6/190*} sa ca nirvāpas tad devatākaḥ. kutaḥ. catuḥsaṃkhyāpūraṇārthatvād abhyāsamātraṃ kartavyam. tac cābhyāsamātraṃ punaḥ kriyate, pūrvam eva kṛte tasmin nirvāpe na devatāpanītā. sa evāyaṃ punaḥ kriyate, punar api kriyamānasyānapanītaiva devatā bhavitum arhatīti prākṛtībhya eva nirvaptavyam. na cottaro muṣṭiḥ pṛthak padārthaḥ, yena devatāpanayo bhavet. kṛtasya nirvāpasya saṃkhyāpūraṇam etat kriyate. tasmād anapanaya iti.
children.translated_text: Now, when the four-handful portioning has commenced but not been completed, a doubt arises: what has been portioned remains as portioned; [but] the remainder — should it be portioned from the original [deities' shares], from the modified [shares], or silently? What is the prima facie view? When [partially] portioned — meaning 'together with what has been portioned' — there should be no deity-removal there. Why? Because of their being subordinate to that — the deity is a subordinate of the portioning, not of the [individual] handfuls. [709] And that portioning has those [original] deities. Why? Because of its being for the purpose of completing the count of four — only a repetition needs to be done. And that mere repetition is done again — [since] in the portioning already done previously, the deity has not been removed. This very [portioning] is done again; when done again, the deity should properly remain unremoved — therefore one should portion from the original [deities' shares] alone. And the subsequent handful is not a separate entity such that deity-removal would [apply to] it. This is a completion of the count of the portioning already done. Therefore there is no removal.

children.text:
NOTES:

*{6/190: E2: 5,309; E6: 2,176}*

children.text: aprākṛtena hi saṃyogas tatsthānīyatvāt // MS_6,5.19 //
children.translated_text: Rather, [there is] connection with the non-original [deities], because of [the remaining handfuls] being substitutes for that [already portioned]. // MS_6,5.19 //

children.text:
na prākṛtībhyo nirvaptavyam. kābhyas tarhi. vaikṛtībhyaḥ. kutaḥ. aprākṛtena devatāviśeṣeṇa saṃyogaḥ śrūyate, nādhikṛtena, tredhā taṇḍulān vibhajed iti prākṛtībhya ācchidya vaikṛtībhyo nirvaptavyo vidhīyate, tā idānīṃ tatsthānīyāḥ.
tasmād vinirupte nivṛttā devatā anyāḥ, anyāś copajātāḥ. tasmād vaikṛtīnāṃ saṃyogena nirvāpaśeṣaḥ kartavya iti.
children.translated_text:
[The remaining handfuls] should not be portioned from the original [deities' shares]. From which then? From the modified [shares]. Why? Because a connection with non-original deity-specifications is heard, not with the prescribed [original ones] — 'he should divide the rice grains into three parts' — prescribes that one should portion by cutting away from the original [shares] and portioning from the modified [shares]. Those [modified shares] are now the substitutes for that.
Therefore, when [the offering] has been partially portioned, the [original] deities have ceased, and other [deities] have arisen. Therefore the remainder of the portioning should be done with the connection to the modified [deities].

children.text: abhāvāc cetarasya syāt // MS_6,5.20 //
children.translated_text: And because of the absence of the other [half], [the portioning] should [simply stop]. // MS_6,5.20 //

children.text: abhāvād itarasyārdhasya devatāsaṃyuktasya, na nirvāpo bhavati devatāsaṃyuktaḥ. yadi nirvāpo 'rdhaṃ{*6/191*} anyadevatyo 'rdho 'py anyasyai devatāyai, naiva nirvāpa itaradevatāko vetaradevatāko vā{*6/192*}. tasmāt tūṣṇīm eva nirvaptavyam, avaśyam anyataratra saṃkalpabhedo bhavati.
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of the other half — [the half] not connected with a deity — there is no portioning connected with a deity. If the portioning [is such that] one half [goes] to one deity and the other half to another deity, there is simply no portioning [that is exclusively] for one deity or the other. Therefore one should portion silently — inevitably there is a difference of intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) regarding one or the other [deity].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/191: E2: nirvāpe 'rdho}*
*{6/192: E1,6; E2: itaradevatākaḥ prākṛta itaradevatāko vā}*
*{6/193: E2: 5,310; E6: 2,177}*

children.text: sāṃnāyyasaṃyogān nāsaṃnayataḥ syāt // MS_6,5.21 //
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> (mixed oblation of curds and milk), [the rule] should not [apply] to one who does not perform the <s>saṃnaya</s> (mixing). // MS_6,5.21 //

children.text: abhyuhiteṣṭir{*6/194*} evodāharaṇam. tatra śrūyate, dadhani caruṃ, śṛte carum iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ saṃnayato bhavaty abhyudaye prāyaścittam, utāviśeṣeṇeti. kiṃ prāptam. saṃnayato 'bhyudaye prāyaścittam. kutaḥ. sāṃnāyyasaṃyogāt, saṃnyāyyasaṃyogo hi bhavati, śṛte carum, dadhani carum iti, śṛtādyabhāvāt, nāsaṃnayato bhavitum arhati, vaiguṇyaṃ hi tathā syāt.
children.translated_text: The <s>Abhyuditeṣṭi</s> itself is the example. There it is heard: 'a <s>caru</s> (porridge) in curds, a <s>caru</s> in boiled milk.' There a doubt [arises]: does the expiatory rite apply [only] to the <s>Abhyudaya</s> (prosperity rite) of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> (mixed milk offering), or without distinction [to anyone]? What is the prima facie view? The expiatory rite [applies only] to the <s>Abhyudaya</s> of one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>. Why? Because of the connection with the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> — for there is a connection with the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>: 'a <s>caru</s> in boiled milk, a <s>caru</s> in curds.' Because of the absence of boiled milk and the like [for one who does not perform the Sāṃnāyya], it is not proper for [the expiatory rite] to apply to one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>, for there would be deficiency in that case.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/194: E1; E2,6: abhyuditeṣṭir}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/194: E1; E2,6: <s>abhyuditeṣṭir</s>}]

children.text: auṣadhasaṃyogād vobhayoḥ // MS_6,5.22 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of the connection with herbs, [it applies] to both. // MS_6,5.22 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. ubhayor api syāt, na kevalasya saṃnayataḥ, auṣadhasaṃyogāt{*6/195*}, ye madhyamā ye sthaviṣṭhā ye kṣodiṣṭhā iti bhavaty auṣadhasaṃyogaḥ, sa ca śakyo 'saṃnayatāpīti. tasmān nāsati kāraṇe 'saṃnayato nivarteta. ubhayor{*6/196*} api pakṣayoḥ prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. It should apply to both — not only to one who performs the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>. Because of the connection with herbs — 'those that are medium, those that are largest, those that are smallest' — there is a connection with herbs, and that is possible even for one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>. Therefore, in the absence of a [sufficient] reason, one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> should not be excluded. The expiatory rite [applies] in both cases.

children.text:
NOTES:

*{6/196: E1,6; E2: ata ubhayor}*

children.text: vaiguṇyān neti cet // MS_6,5.23 //
children.translated_text: 'Because of deficiency, it does not [apply]' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_6,5.23 //

children.text: iti yad uktam, asaṃnayato dadhnaḥ śṛtasya cābhāvāt tadadhikaraṇatā nāsti. tasmād vaiguṇyaṃ tasmin pakṣa iti, tat parihartavyam iti.
children.translated_text: Thus it was said: for one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>, because of the absence of curds and boiled milk, there is no substrate for that [rite]. Therefore there is deficiency in that case — this [objection] should be addressed.

children.text: nātatsaṃskāratvāt/76.5.24//
children.translated_text: No, because [curds and boiled milk] are not refinements of that [caru]. // MS_6,5.24 //

children.text: naitad evam. na hi dadhyadhikaraṇa caroḥ śrapaṇe śrūyate. kiṃ tu yathā sthaviṣṭhā indrāya pradātre, evaṃ dadhy api devatāsaṃbandhārthaṃ [711]{*6/197*} vidhīyate, na carusaṃbandhārtham iti. bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam, sthaviṣṭhā devatāyai, dadhani ca te kartavyā iti. saptamīsaṃyogas tu prāpte 'rthe 'nuvādaḥ. tasmād avivakṣitaṃ teṣāṃ sāhityam, lakṣaṇatvena hi te śrūyanta iti, na hi payo dadhi ca nāstīti sthaviṣṭhānāṃ na devatāpanayo bhavati. asaṃnayato 'py arthād apsu śrapayiṣyata iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so. For the cooking of the <s>caru</s> (porridge) in curds as a substrate is not heard. Rather, just as the largest [herbs are offered] to <s>Indra</s> the Giver, so too curds are enjoined for the purpose of connection with the deity, not for the purpose of connection with the <s>caru</s>. For otherwise the sentence would be split: 'the largest [herbs] for the deity, and curds too are to be prepared for those.' The locative conjunction is a restatement of what is already established. Therefore the co-presence of these [curds, etc., with the caru] is not intended — for they are heard as characterizing marks. For it is not the case that when milk and curds are absent, the offering to the deity of the largest [herbs] does not take place. Even for one who does not perform the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s>, [the caru] will evidently be cooked in water.

children.text: sāmyutthāne viśvajitkrīte vibhāgasaṃyogāt // MS_6,5.25 //
children.translated_text: In the case of the <s>Sāmyutthāna</s> (collective rising [from a Sattra]), when [the Soma] has been purchased in the <s>Viśvajit</s>, because of the connection with distribution. // MS_6,5.25 //

children.text: idam āmananti, yadi satrāya dīkṣitā atha{*6/198*} sāmyut tiṣṭheran, somam apabhajya viśvajitā atirātreṇa sarvastomena sarvapṛṣṭhena sarvavedasadakṣiṇena yajerann iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ krītarājakasyotthāne viśvajit, uta pravṛttamātrasyeti. kiṃ prāptam. sāmyutthāne viśvajit krīte syāt. kutaḥ. vibhāgasaṃyogāt, somam apabhajya viśvajitā yajerann iti. ye hy akrīte rājany uttiṣṭanti, teṣāṃ somavibhāgābhāvād vaiguṇyaṃ syāt. tasmāt krītarājakā uttiṣṭhanto viśvajitaṃ kuryuḥ.
children.translated_text: This is recorded: 'If those consecrated for a <s>Sattra</s> should collectively rise up (<s>sāmyutthāna</s>), having distributed the <s>Soma</s>, they should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s> <s>Atirātra</s> with all <s>Stoma</s> [chants], all <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], and with all wealth as <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>Viśvajit</s> [performed] when there is a rising up after the king [Soma] has been purchased, or when [the Sattra has] merely commenced? What is the prima facie view? The <s>Viśvajit</s> [should be performed] in the case of <s>Sāmyutthāna</s> when [the Soma] has been purchased. Why? Because of the connection with distribution — 'having distributed the <s>Soma</s>, they should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>.' For those who rise up when the king [Soma] has not been purchased, there would be deficiency due to the absence of <s>Soma</s> distribution. Therefore those who rise up after the king [Soma] has been purchased should perform the <s>Viśvajit</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/198: E2: dīkṣitānāṃ; E2 (v.l.), E1,6: dīkṣitā atha}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/198: E2: <s>dīkṣitānāṃ</s>; E2 (variant reading), E1,6: <s>dīkṣitā atha</s>}]

children.text: pravṛtte vā prāpaṇān nimittasya // MS_6,5.26 //
children.translated_text: Or, [the Viśvajit is] when [the Sattra has] merely commenced, because of the arrival of the occasion. // MS_6,5.26 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. pravṛttamātrasyotthāne syāt. kutaḥ. prāpaṇān nimittasya, sāmyutthānaṃ nimittaṃ viśvajitaḥ, [712]{*6/199*} tac ca prāptam, na ca tac chakyaṃ viśeṣayitum, krīte some{*6/200*} sāmyutthānam iti.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. [The Viśvajit] should be when [the Sattra has] merely commenced and the rising up occurs. Why? Because of the arrival of the occasion — the <s>Sāmyutthāna</s> (collective rising) is the occasion for the <s>Viśvajit</s>, and that [occasion] has arrived. And it is not possible to specify that 'the <s>Sāmyutthāna</s> [occurs only] when the <s>Soma</s> has been purchased.'

children.text: ādeśārthetarā śrutiḥ // MS_6,5.27 //
children.translated_text: The [Vedic] statement is for the purpose of instruction, while the rest [is restatement]. // MS_6,5.27 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, akrīte rājany uttiṣṭhanto vibhāgābhāvād viguṇaṃ kuryur iti. tat pratihartavyam. atrocayate, na vibhāgo vidhīyate. bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam. sāmyutthāne viśvajitā yajeran, somasya tv apabhāgaṃ{*6/201*} kṛtveti. tenāpabhajyety anuvādaḥ. katham prāptir iti cet. arthād uttiṣṭhatāṃ vibhāgo bhavati dhanasya. so 'yaṃ sarvadravyāṇāṃ vibhāgaḥ somavibhāgena lakṣyate, somaṃ vibhajyānyāni ca dravyāṇīty ādeśārthetarā śrutir bhavati. tasmāt krīte cākrīte ca rājany uttiṣṭhatāṃ viśvajid iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'those who rise up when the king [Soma] has not been purchased would perform [the Viśvajit] deficiently due to the absence of distribution' — that should be refuted. Here it is stated: distribution is not being enjoined [as a new requirement]. For otherwise the sentence would be split: 'In the case of <s>Sāmyutthāna</s>, they should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>; but having distributed the <s>Soma</s>...' Therefore 'having distributed' is a restatement. How is the [Soma distribution already] established? For those who rise up, there is evidently a distribution of property. This distribution of all goods is indicated by the distribution of <s>Soma</s> — 'having distributed the <s>Soma</s> and other goods as well' — [thus] the [Vedic] statement is for the purpose of instruction, while the rest is another [purpose]. Therefore the <s>Viśvajit</s> [applies] to those who rise up whether or not the king [Soma] has been purchased.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/201: E1,6; E2: vibhāgaṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/201: E1,6; E2: <s>vibhāgaṃ</s>}]

children.text: dīkṣāparimāṇe yathākāmyaviśeṣāt // MS_6,5.28 //
children.translated_text: Regarding the measure of <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration), [there is] no restriction, because of the absence of a distinguishing [statement]. // MS_6,5.28 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭomaṃ prakṛtya śrūyate, ekā dīkṣā, tisra upasadaḥ, pañcamīṃ prasuta{*6/202*} iti. tisro dīkṣāḥ, dvādaśa dīkṣā iti bahūni dīkṣāparimāṇāny āmnātāni. teṣu saṃdehaḥ. kim aniyamaḥ, yad vā tad vā parimāṇam upādeyam, uta dvādaśa dīkṣā iti. kiṃ prāptam. dīkṣāparimāṇe yathākāmī syāt. nāsti niyamaḥ. kutaḥ. aviśeṣāt, na kaścana [713]{*6/203*} viśeṣa upādīyate. tasmād yatkiṃcit parimāṇam upādeyam iti.
NOTES:
*{6/202: E1,6; E2: pañcamī prasṛta}*
*{6/203: E2: 5,314; E6: 2,179}*
children.translated_text:
With reference to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: 'one <s>dīkṣā</s> [day], three <s>upasad</s> [days], on the fifth [day] he is released [for the pressing].' [Also:] 'three <s>dīkṣā</s> [days],' 'twelve <s>dīkṣā</s> [days]' — many measures of <s>dīkṣā</s> are recorded. Regarding these, a doubt [arises]: is there no restriction — any measure may be adopted — or [should it be] twelve <s>dīkṣā</s> [days]? What is the prima facie view? Regarding the measure of <s>dīkṣā</s>, one may choose as one wishes. There is no restriction. Why? Because of the absence of a distinguishing [statement] — no distinction is adopted. Therefore any measure may be adopted.
NOTES:
[{6/202: E1,6; E2: <s>pañcamī prasṛta</s>}]
[{6/203: E2: 5,314; E6: 2,179}]

children.text: dvādaśāhas tu liṅgāt syāt // MS_6,5.29 //
children.translated_text: But [the period of] twelve days should be [the measure], because of an indicatory mark. // MS_6,5.29 //

children.text: dvādaśāha eva parimāṇam upādīyeta. kutaḥ. liṅgāt sāmarthyād ity arthaḥ{*6/204*}. kiṃ sāmarthyam. dvādaśa rātrīr dīkṣito bhṛtiṃ vanvīteti{*6/205*} nityavad āmnāyate, na pākṣikam. tad eva nityaṃ kurvan, na śaknoty anyat parimāṇam upādātum. tasmād dvādaśāha eva parimāṇaṃ niyamyeta, anyāni parimāṇāni vikṛtau bhaviṣyatīti naiṣām ānarthakyam iti.
children.translated_text: The measure of twelve days alone should be adopted. Why? Because of an indicatory mark — meaning, because of a logical implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>). What is the logical implication? 'For twelve nights the consecrated one should earn wages' — this is recorded as invariable, not as optional. One who invariably observes this [twelve-day period] cannot adopt any other measure. Therefore the measure should be restricted to twelve days alone; the other measures will apply in modified [rites] — thus there is no purposelessness of those [other measures].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/204: E1 hat sāmarthyād ity arthaḥ in Klammern}*
*{6/205: E1,6; E2: nvatīveti(?)}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/204: E1 puts <s>sāmarthyād ity arthaḥ</s> in brackets}]
[{6/205: E1,6; E2: <s>nvatīveti</s>(?)}]

children.text: paurṇamāsyām aniyamo 'viśeṣāt // MS_6,5.30 //
children.translated_text: Regarding the full-moon [day], there is no restriction, because of the absence of a distinguishing [statement]. // MS_6,5.30 //

children.text: gavāmayane śrūyate, purastāt paurṇamāsyāś caturahe dīkṣerann iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kasyāḥ paurṇamāsyā iti. kiṃ prāptam. paurṇamāsyām aniyama iti. kutaḥ. aviśeṣāt, nātra kaścid viśeṣavacanaḥ śabda upādīyate.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Gavāmayana</s> (year-long Soma sacrifice) it is heard: 'Four days before the full-moon day they should consecrate themselves (<s>dīkṣā</s>).' There a doubt [arises]: before which full-moon day? What is the prima facie view? Regarding the full-moon day, there is no restriction. Why? Because of the absence of a distinguishing [statement] — no word specifying a distinction is adopted here.

children.text: ānantaryāt tu caitrī syāt // MS_6,5.31 //
children.translated_text: But [it should be] the <s>Caitrī</s> [full-moon day], because of proximity. // MS_6,5.31 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitat, aniyama iti, caitrī, paurṇamāsī tu bhavet. kutaḥ. ānantaryāt, paurṇamāsīm uktvānantaraṃ vākyaśeṣe caitrī saṃkīrtyate, purasāt paurṇamāsyāś caturahe dīkṣeran. ṛtumukhaṃ vaiṣā paurṇamāsī saṃvatsa[714]{*6/206*}rasya, yā caitrī paurṇamāsīti. atra saṃdigdheṣu vākyaśeṣād{*6/207*} iti caitrī niyamyeta.
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [previous] position. It is not so — that there is no restriction. The <s>Caitrī</s> full-moon day should be [the one intended]. Why? Because of proximity — having mentioned 'the full-moon day,' immediately in the continuation of the sentence the <s>Caitrī</s> [full-moon] is mentioned: 'Four days before the full-moon day they should consecrate themselves. This full-moon day is indeed the commencement of the seasons of the year — the <s>Caitrī</s> full-moon day.' In this case of doubt, from the continuation of the sentence, the <s>Caitrī</s> [full-moon] should be determined.

children.text: māghī vaikāṣṭakāśruteḥ // MS_6,5.32 //
children.translated_text: Or the <s>Māghī</s> [full-moon day], because of the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> statement. // MS_6,5.32 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti caitrīti. kiṃ tarhi. māghīti. kutaḥ. ekāṣṭakāśruteḥ, kraye hy ekāṣṭakāśrutir bhavati. teṣām ekāṣṭakāyāṃ krayaḥ saṃpadyata iti. tasmān māghyāḥ purastāc caturahe dīkṣitasyaikāṣṭakāyāṃ krayaḥ śakyate kartum, na caityāḥ. tad etat sāmarthyaṃ nāma liṅgam, tat vākyasya bādhakaṃ bhavati. tasmān māghī paurṇamāsīti.
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. It is not the <s>Caitrī</s>. Rather, the <s>Māghī</s> [full-moon day]. Why? Because of the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> statement — for the statement of the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> occurs at the [Soma] purchase. The purchase is accomplished for them on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> day. Therefore, for one who consecrates himself four days before the <s>Māghī</s> [full-moon], the purchase can be performed on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>, but not [if one consecrates] before the <s>Caitrī</s>. This logical implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and that overrides the sentence [continuation]. Therefore the <s>Māghī</s> full-moon day [is intended].

children.text: anyā apīti cet // MS_6,5.33 //
children.translated_text: 'Other [Aṣṭamīs] too [could serve]' — if [one argues thus] — // MS_6,5.33 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, māghī paurṇamāsī, evam ekāṣṭakāyāṃ krayaḥ saṃpatsyata iti. tan na, asarvā aṣṭamya{*6/208*} ekāṣṭakāḥ, dvādaśaikāṣṭakā iti, tena na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — the <s>Māghī</s> full-moon day [is intended], so that the purchase will fall on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> — that is not [a problem]. Not all eighth days (<s>Aṣṭamī</s>) are <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>s — 'there are twelve <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>s' — therefore there is no defect [in the argument].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/208: E1,6; E2: sarvā apy aṣṭamya}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/208: E1,6; E2: <s>sarvā apy aṣṭamya</s>}]

children.text: na bhaktitvād eṣā hi loke // MS_6,5.34 //
children.translated_text: No, because this [Ekāṣṭakā] is the primary one, being [so known] in common usage. // MS_6,5.34 //

children.text: naitad evam, bhākto hy anyāsv aṣṭamīṣv ekāṣṭakāśabdaḥ. eṣā hi mukhyā, yā māghyāṃ vṛttāyām{*6/209*}, mukhyagauṇayoś ca mukhye saṃpratyayaḥ. tasmān māghy eva paurṇamāsīti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — the word '<s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>' as applied to other eighth days is secondary (<s>bhākta</s>, figurative). For this one is the primary [Ekāṣṭakā] — the one that occurs when the <s>Māghī</s> [full-moon] has passed. And between primary and secondary [meanings], the primary [meaning] is understood. Therefore the <s>Māghī</s> full-moon day alone [is intended].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/209: E1,6; E2: vṛttā}*
dīkṣāparādhe cānugrahāt // MS_6,5.35 //
children.translated_text: And because of the <s>dīkṣā</s> transgression being remedied. // MS_6,5.35 //

children.text: ekāṣṭakāyāṃ dīkṣeran, eṣā vai saṃvatsarasya patnī, yad ekāṣṭakā{*6/210*}, ity uktvā punaḥ, caturahe purastāt paurṇamāsyā dīkṣāṃ vidhāya, teṣām ekāṣṭakāyāṃ krayaḥ saṃpadyate, tenaikāṣṭakāṃ [715]{*6/211*} na chaṃvaṭ kurvantīti, dīkṣātaḥ pracyutām ekāṣṭakāṃ krayeṇa tu gṛhṇan māghyāḥ paurṇamāsyā adhikāraṃ darśayati. asyāṃ ca māghyām aṣṭamyām abhījyamānāyāṃ bhavati mantraḥ,
children.translated_text: 'They should consecrate themselves on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>; this <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> is indeed the wife (<s>patnī</s>) of the year' — having stated this, again, having prescribed the <s>dīkṣā</s> four days before the full-moon day, [the text says:] 'The purchase falls for them on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>; therefore they do not impede the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>' — [this means that] by grasping the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> that has lapsed from the <s>dīkṣā</s> [period] through the purchase, [the text] demonstrates the authority of the <s>Māghī</s> full-moon day. And on this <s>Māghī</s> eighth day, when the sacrifice is being performed, there is a <s>mantra</s>:

children.text:
yāṃ janāḥ pratinandanti rātrīṃ dhenum ivāyatīm/
saṃvatsarasya yā patnī sā no astu sumaṅgalī//
children.translated_text:
'The night that people welcome as she approaches, like a cow;
she who is the wife of the year — may she be auspicious for us.'

children.text: ity{*6/212*} aṣṭakāyai surādhase svāheti, yāsau māghy aṣṭamī, tām ekāṣṭakāṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: [The mantra continues:] '<s>svāhā</s> to the <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, the generous one' — that <s>Māghī</s> eighth day is shown to be the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>.

children.text: utthāne cānuprarohāt // MS_6,5.36 //
children.translated_text: And because of the re-sprouting at the time of rising. // MS_6,5.36 //

children.text: utthāne cānuprarohaṃ darśayati. tān uttiṣṭhata auṣadhayo vanaspatayo 'nuttiṣṭhantīti{*6/213*}, vasanta utthānaṃ darśayati. tasminn oṣadhayo vanaspatayaś cottiṣṭhanti. tasmād api sā niyamyate.
children.translated_text: And [the text] shows the re-sprouting at the time of rising: 'When they rise up, the herbs and trees rise up along [with them]' — [this] shows the rising in spring. In that [season], herbs and trees rise up. Therefore from this too, that [Māghī full-moon] is determined.

NOTES:
[{6/213: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 7.4.8.3}]

children.text: asyāṃ ca sarvaliṅgāni // MS_6,5.37 //
children.translated_text: And in this [Māghī full-moon] all the indicatory marks [converge]. // MS_6,5.37 //

children.text: ārtaṃ vā ete saṃvatsarasyābhidīkṣante, ya ekāṣṭakāyāṃ dīkṣanta{*6/214*} iti. ārtā yasmin kāle bhavanti, sa ārtaḥ kālaḥ. śītena cārtā bhavanti. tasmān māghy aṣṭamy ekāṣṭaketi. tathā, vyastaṃ vā ete saṃvatsarasyābhidīkṣante, ya ekāṣṭakāyāṃ dīkṣanta iti. ayanaparivṛttir vyastaśabdenocyate. tathā, apo nābhinandanto 'vabhṛtham abhyavayantīti caitryāṃ dīkṣitā abhinandanto 'bhyaveyuḥ. tasmād api māghī paurṇamāsīti.
children.translated_text: 'They consecrate themselves at the distressed [time] of the year — those who consecrate on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>.' The distressed time (<s>ārta</s>) is the season in which [beings] are distressed. And they are distressed by cold. Therefore the <s>Māghī</s> eighth day is the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>. Likewise, 'They consecrate themselves at the turning point (<s>vyasta</s>) of the year — those who consecrate on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>.' The turning of the [sun's] path is denoted by the word '<s>vyasta</s>.' Likewise, 'Not welcoming the waters, they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath)' — those consecrated at the <s>Caitrī</s> [full-moon] would indeed welcome [the waters when they go to the bath]. Therefore the <s>Māghī</s> full-moon day [is intended].

children.text: dīkṣākālasya śiṣṭatvād atikrame niyatānām anutkarṣaḥ prāptakālatvāt // MS_6,5.38 //
children.translated_text: Because the time of <s>dīkṣā</s> is fixed, when there is a transgression [of the prescribed period], there is no extension for the fixed [rites], because their time has arrived. // MS_6,5.38 //

children.text: idaṃ śrūyate, tasmād dīkṣito na dadāti, na pacati, na juhotīti, jyotiṣṭome samāmananti. yadi{*6/216*} tu daivān mānuṣād vā pratibalād dīkṣitākāla utkṛṣyate, tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ dānahomapākānām utkarṣaḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam. anutkarṣaḥ, niyatā hi dānahomapākāḥ, yāvaj jīvam, agnihotraṃ juhotītyevamādibhiḥ śrutibhis teṣām apavādaḥ, yeṣv ahaḥsu sāṅgo jyotiṣṭomo vihitaḥ, tāvanty ahāni muktvānyeṣv ahaḥsu kartavyāḥ. jyotiṣṭomavidhānakālāt parato 'pratiṣiddhāḥ. tasmāt kartavyāḥ, prāpto hi teṣāṃ kāla iti.
children.translated_text: This is heard: 'Therefore the consecrated one (<s>dīkṣita</s>) does not give gifts, does not cook, does not offer oblations' — [this] is recorded in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. But if, due to divine or human [causes] or an overpowering obstacle, the time of the consecrated one is extended, there a doubt [arises]: should the giving, offering, and cooking [of regular rites] also be extended [i.e., suspended for the extended period], or not? What is the prima facie view? There is no extension — for giving, offering, and cooking are fixed [obligations]: 'As long as one lives, one should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>' — by such <s>śruti</s> statements, their suspension [applies only] for those days during which the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is enjoined with all its subsidiaries. Excluding those days, on the other days [these regular rites] must be performed. [The regular rites] are not prohibited beyond the prescribed time of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> injunction. Therefore they must be performed, for their time has arrived.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/216: E1,6; E2: samāmananti, tiṣṭo dīkṣā ityevamādi. yadi}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/216: E1,6; E2: <s>samāmananti, tiṣṭo dīkṣā ityevamādi. yadi</s>}]

children.text: utkarṣo vā dīkṣitatvād aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam // MS_6,5.39 //
children.translated_text: Or, there should be an extension [of suspension] because of the state of being consecrated; for the cause [of suspension] is undifferentiated. // MS_6,5.39 //

children.text: vāśabdāt pakṣo viparivartate. yad uktam, naiṣam utkarṣa iti, naitad evam. utkṛṣṭavyāḥ{*6/217*}. kutaḥ. dīkṣitatvāt, dīkṣitasya te pratiṣiddhāḥ, na dīkṣito yasmin kāle. lakṣaṇā hi evaṃ syāt, yathā tu vayaṃ brūmaḥ, tathā śrutiḥ kāraṇam. prāk cāvabhṛthāt, ayaṃ dīkṣita eva. aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam, yad eva jyotiṣṭomavidhānakāle, tad evātikrānte 'pi. ubhayatra hi dīkṣitatvaṃ hi kāraṇam. tasmāt teṣām utkarṣa iti.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' reverses the position. What was said — 'there is no temporal advancement (<s>utkarṣa</s>) of these' — that is not so. They should be advanced. Why? Because of the state of being consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>) — those [offerings] are prohibited for the consecrated one, not [prohibited for] the period when one is consecrated. For that would be secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). But as we state it, the direct hearing (<s>śruti</s>) is the basis. And before the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), this one is indeed consecrated. For the basis is undifferentiated — what [applies] at the time of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> prescription [also applies] even when [that time] has passed. For in both cases, the state of being consecrated is the basis. Therefore there is temporal advancement of those [offerings].

children.text: tatra pratihomo na vidyate, yathā pūrveṣām // MS_6,5.40 //
children.translated_text: There is no counter-offering (<s>pratihoma</s>) there, as with the previous ones. // MS_6,5.40 //

children.text:
tatrotkṛṣyamāṇe jyotiṣṭome{*6/219*}, akṛteṣu homeṣu kiṃ parisaṃkhyāya homāḥ kartavyāḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam. parisaṃkhyāya homāḥ kriyeran. kiṃ kāraṇam. avaśyakartavyatayā hi te vihitā homāḥ. atipannā api kartavyā eva. tathā hy eṣām avaśyakartavyatā anugṛhītā bhaviṣyati. pradhānamātraṃ tu niyatam, nātra kālānurodhaḥ kartavyaḥ, nadīvegasthānīyatvāt. yady apy atikrāntāḥ kālāḥ, atikrāntānāṃ parisaṃkhyāya pradhānamātrāṇi kartavyāni, yathāvaśyakartavyaṃ bhuktibhṛtakadānādi, yad atikrāntaṃ bhavati, tat parisaṃkhyāya kriyate, evam idam apīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, tatra pratihomo na vidyate, yathā pūrveṣām, kartavyam akṛtvā kuryāt, nākartavyam. akartavyāś caite, pratiṣiddhatvāt, yathā pūrveṣām asati kālātikrame 'kṛtānāṃ na pratihomaḥ, evam eṣām apīti.
children.translated_text:
There, in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> being advanced, when offerings have not been performed — should the offerings be counted up and performed, or not? What is the prima facie view? The offerings should be counted up and performed. What is the reason? For those offerings are enjoined as necessarily to be performed. Even if [their time has] passed, they must still be performed. For thus their necessarily-to-be-performed character will be upheld. Only the principal [rite] is fixed [in time], and no conformity to time need be made here, because of [time] being like a river's current. Even if the times have passed, the principal [rites] of those whose [time has] passed should be counted up and performed — just as necessarily-to-be-performed [obligations] like meals, wages, gifts, etc., when their time has passed, are counted up and performed; so too with this.
Given this prima facie view, we say: there is no counter-offering there, as with the previous ones — one should do what ought to be done [but] has not been done, not what ought not to be done. And these ought not to be done, because of being prohibited. Just as with the previous ones, when there is no passage of time, there is no counter-offering for those not performed — so too with these.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/219: E1 (v.l.) jyotiṣṭomakāle}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/219: E1 (variant reading): <s>jyotiṣṭomakāle</s>}]

children.text: kālaprādhānyāc ca // MS_6,5.41 //
children.translated_text: And because of the primacy of time. // MS_6,5.41 //

children.text: kālaprādhānyaṃ ca bhavati, nimittatvena tasya śrutatvāt. tadabhāve vihitam eva na bhavati. pradhānamātraṃ yady api niyamyeta, tathāpi nimitte kāle. sa ca nadīvegasthānīyaḥ kāle 'tikrāntaḥ, ato na pratihomaḥ kartavya iti.
children.translated_text: And time has primacy, because it is heard as the occasion. In its absence, what is enjoined simply does not exist [as an obligation]. Even if only the principal [rite] is fixed [in time], still [it is fixed] in time as the occasion. And that [time], being like a river's current, has passed. Therefore no counter-offering should be performed.

children.text: pratiṣedhāc cordhvam avabhṛthād eṣṭeḥ{*6/221*} // MS_6,5.42 //
children.translated_text: And because of the prohibition, [there is no counter-offering for what is] above [i.e., after] the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> up to the concluding <s>iṣṭi</s>. // MS_6,5.42 //

children.text:
ūrdhvam avabhṛthād ā udavasānīyāyā iṣṭer ye homāḥ, teṣv atipanneṣu daivena mānuṣeṇa vā pratibalena bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ pratihomaḥ kartavyaḥ, uta neti. kiṃ prāptam. kartavya iti, unmuktadīkṣo hi sa tadā bhavati, dīkṣāṇām unmocanārtho hy avabhṛthaḥ. tasmāt kartavyāḥ, te na kṛtā iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, ūrdhvam avabhṛthāt, ā udavasānīyāyā iṣṭeḥ, atipannānāṃ na pratihomaḥ syāt. kutaḥ. pratiṣedhāt, pratiṣedho hi bhavati, etayā punarādheyasasmitayeṣṭyāgnihotraṃ{*6/222*} hotavyam iti, prāg udavasānīyāyāḥ, homasya pratiṣedhaḥ. yāvad udavasānīyotkṛṣyate, tāvat pratiṣedhaḥ. evaṃ śrutiḥ, itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt. tasmād akartavyāḥ, te na kṛtā iti, na syāt pratihoma iti.
children.translated_text:
After the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>, up to the <s>Udavasānīya</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> (concluding offering), when offerings have lapsed — whether by divine [cause] or a powerful human [obstacle] — there is a doubt: should a counter-offering be performed, or not? What is the prima facie view? It should be performed — for at that time he has been released from the consecrations, since the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> is for the purpose of releasing the consecrations. Therefore they should be performed — [since] they have not been done.
Given this prima facie view, we say: after the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>, up to the <s>Udavasānīya</s> <s>iṣṭi</s>, there should be no counter-offering for those that have lapsed. Why? Because of the prohibition — for there is a prohibition: 'With this <s>Punarādheya</s>-equivalent <s>iṣṭi</s>, the <s>Agnihotra</s> should be offered,' [meaning] before the <s>Udavasānīya</s>, the offering is prohibited. As long as the <s>Udavasānīya</s> is being advanced, so long [extends] the prohibition. Thus is the hearing (<s>śruti</s>); otherwise there would be secondary indication. Therefore they ought not to be done — [since] they have not been done, there should be no counter-offering.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/221: E6 (?); E2,6: iṣṭeḥ}*
*{6/222: E1,6; E2: ādheyasaṃmitayeṣṭvāgnihotraṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/221: E6 (?); E2,6: <s>iṣṭeḥ</s>}]
[{6/222: E1,6; E2: <s>ādheyasaṃmitayeṣṭvāgnihotraṃ</s>}]

children.text: pratihomaś cet sāyam agnihotraprabhṛtīni hūyeran // MS_6,5.43 //
children.translated_text: If there is a counter-offering, the evening <s>Agnihotra</s> and subsequent [offerings] should be offered [first]. // MS_6,5.43 //

children.text: eteṣv evodāharaṇeṣu bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ pratihome sāyam agnihotraprabhṛtīny ārabhyeran{*6/223*}, uta prātaragnihotraprabhṛtīnīti. nanu nāsty eva pratihoma iti sthitam. ucyate, astīti kṛtvā cintayāmaḥ. kṛtvā cinteyam, anyeṣu sadṛśanyāyeṣūdāharaṇeṣv asyāḥ prayojanam asti [719]{*6/224*} iti cintyate. kiṃ prāptam. aniyamaḥ, arthakṛtatvāt. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, yadi pratihomaḥ kriyate, sāyam agnihotraprabhṛtīni hūyeran. kutaḥ{*6/225*}. sāyam agnihotrād ārabhyātipannāni, tenaivānupūrveṇa pratihotavyānīti.
children.translated_text: In these very examples, a doubt arises: if counter-offerings are [to be made], should they begin from the evening <s>Agnihotra</s>, or from the morning <s>Agnihotra</s>? [One might say:] but it has been established that there is no counter-offering at all. [We] reply: assuming there is [a counter-offering], we investigate — [for] having assumed [this], the investigation has a purpose in other examples with analogous principles. What is the prima facie view? There is no fixed rule, because of [the matter] being determined by purpose. Given this prima facie view, we say: if counter-offerings are performed, the evening <s>Agnihotra</s> and subsequent [offerings] should be offered. Why? Starting from the evening <s>Agnihotra</s>, [the offerings] have lapsed — they should be counter-offered in that very sequence.

children.text:
NOTES:

*{6/224: E2: 5,319; E2: 2,182}*
*{6/225: E2 om. sāyam agnihotraprabhṛtīni hūyeran. kutaḥ}*

children.text: prātas tu ṣoḍaśini // MS_6,5.44 //
children.translated_text: But [beginning from] the morning [Agnihotra] in the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> [Soma sacrifice]. // MS_6,5.44 //

children.text: ṣoḍaśisaṃsthe somo 'tipanneṣu{*6/226*} homeṣu saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ sāyam agnihotreṇeti, uta prātar iti{*6/227*}. kiṃ prāptam. sāyam agnihotreṇeti pūrvasminn adhikaraṇa uktam, utsargeṇa sarvatraivam iti prāptam. tathā prāpta ucyate, prātas tu ṣoḍaśini, ṣoḍaśisaṃsthe prātaragnihotrādīny atipannānīti prātaragnihotrād eva samārabhyānīti.
children.translated_text: In a <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] concluded with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> [cup], when offerings have lapsed, a doubt [arises]: should [the counter-offerings begin] from the evening <s>Agnihotra</s>, or from the morning? What is the prima facie view? From the evening <s>Agnihotra</s> — as was stated in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), by the general rule this applies everywhere. Given this prima facie view, we say: but in the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> [concluded sacrifice], from the morning — in a [sacrifice] concluded with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, what has lapsed beginning from the morning <s>Agnihotra</s> should be commenced from the morning <s>Agnihotra</s> itself.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/226: E1,6; E2: jyotiṣṭome 'tipanneṣu}*
*{6/227: E2: agnihotreṇa pratihotavyam uta prātar agnihotreṇeti}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
