[{6/227: E2: <s>agnihotreṇa pratihotavyam uta prātar agnihotreṇeti</s>}]

children.text: prāyaścittam adhikāre sarvatra doṣasāmānyāt // MS_6,5.45 //
children.translated_text: The expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) applies everywhere within the [ritual] domain (<s>adhikāra</s>), because of the commonality of the fault. // MS_6,5.45 //

children.text: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate, bhinne juhoti skanne juhotīti. tatra kiṃ darśapūrṇamāsayor evaitat, bhinne skanne ca prāyaścittam uta yatra bhidyate skandati ceti. kiṃ prāptam. [720]{*6/228*} prakaraṇe yat prāyaścittam evaṃjātīykaṃ kiṃcid utpannam, tat sarvatra yatra yatra bhidyate skandati vā, tatra tatra syāt. kasmāt. doṣasāmānyāt, samānaṃ nimittaṃ skandanaṃ bhedanaṃ vā. sa evātra doṣa ity abhipretam. prakaraṇād darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ prāyaścittam, vākyād anyatrāpi, prakaraṇāc ca vākyaṃ balīyaḥ. tasmāt sarvatra skanne bhinne ca prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites it is heard: 'When [the milk] is split, one offers; when [the milk] is spilled, one offers.' There [the question arises]: does this expiation apply only to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites, for splitting and spilling, or wherever there is splitting and spilling? What is the prima facie view? [720] Whatever expiation of this kind arises in the context — that should apply everywhere, wherever there is splitting or spilling. Why? Because of the commonality of the fault — the occasion is the same, [namely] spilling or splitting. That very fault is what is intended here. From the context, [the expiation applies to] the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; from the sentence, to other [rites] also; and the sentence is stronger than the context. Therefore the expiation [applies] everywhere, when there is spilling or splitting.

children.text: prakaraṇe vā śabdahetutvāt // MS_6,5.46 //
children.translated_text: Or [it applies only] in the context, because of [the sentence's] being based on the [Vedic] word. // MS_6,5.46 //

children.text: prakaraṇa eva bhinne skanne vā prāyaścittam. kutaḥ. śabdahetutvāt, tena prākṛtenārthena sahaikavākyatā, eṣāṃ homānām. tato homavato yāgasya pratyāyane prakṛto yajeteti śabdo hetuḥ. evaṃ cet tadupakāreṇārthavān bhaviṣyatīti, itarathā vinā vākyena, phalaṃ kalpayitavyaṃ syāt. tasmāt vākyaṃ phalābhāvenaiva bādhitam iti kṛtvā prakaraṇam anugṛhītavyam iti.
children.translated_text: The expiation [applies] only in the context — only when there is splitting or spilling [in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>]. Why? Because of [the sentence's] being based on the [Vedic] word — syntactic unity with that contextual meaning pertains to these offerings. Therefore the word '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice), which is the basis for establishing the sacrifice possessing the offerings, is contextual. If [that syntactic unity holds], it will be meaningful through connection with that [context]. Otherwise, without a sentence [connection], a fruit would have to be postulated. Therefore, the sentence being overridden by the very absence of [independent] fruit, the context should be upheld.

children.text: atadvikāraś ca // MS_6,5.47 //
children.translated_text: And [the expiation does not apply to] what is not a modification of that [archetype]. // MS_6,5.47 //

children.text: na ca, atadvikāro 'gnihotraṃ jyotiṣṭomo vā. na darśapūrṇamāsavikāraḥ. yadi tadvikāro bhavet, tatrāpi skanne bhinne vā prāyaścittaṃ syād iti.
children.translated_text: And neither the <s>Agnihotra</s> nor the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is a modification of that [<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>]. It is not a modification of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. If it were a modification of that, then there too, when there is spilling or splitting, the expiation would apply.

children.text: vyāpannasyāpsu gatau yad abhojyam āryāṇāṃ tat pratīyeta // MS_6,5.48 //
children.translated_text: Regarding what is spoiled (<s>vyāpanna</s>) — when cast into the waters, what is unfit to be eaten by <s>Āryas</s> should be understood [as the meaning]. // MS_6,5.48 //

children.text: vyāpannam apsu praharatīti śrūyate. kiṃ vyāpannam ity ucyata iti tad abhidhīyate, vyāpannam, dūṣitaṃ yena kāryena [721]{*6/229*} kriyate. kiṃ tat. yad abhojyam āryāṇām, keśakīṭāv apannam{*6/230*} anyena vopaghātenopahatam, tad vyāpannam iti.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'What is spoiled, one casts into the waters.' What is meant by 'spoiled' — that is being stated. [Something is] spoiled — corrupted by whatever [contaminating] cause [721]. What is that? What is unfit to be eaten by <s>Āryas</s> — [something that has] fallen upon hair or insects, or is damaged by some other injury — that is 'spoiled.'

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/229: E2: 5,320; E6: 2,183}*
*{6/230: E1,6; E2: abhidhīyate, keśakīṭāv apannam, anyena vopaghātenopahatam, tadvyāpabhojyam āryāṇām, śeśakīṭāv apannam}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/229: E2: 5,320; E6: 2,183}]
[{6/230: E1,6; E2: <s>abhidhīyate, keśakīṭāv apannam, anyena vopaghātenopahatam, tadvyāpabhojyam āryāṇām, śeśakīṭāv apannam</s>}]

children.text: vibhāgaśruteḥ prāyaścittaṃ yaugapadye na vidyate // MS_6,5.49 //
children.translated_text: Because of the hearing of division, there is no expiation in [the case of] simultaneity. // MS_6,5.49 //

children.text: prastotrudgātror{*6/231*} udgātṛpratihartor vā yatrāpacchedaḥ{*6/232*}. kiṃ tatra prāyaścittaṃ syāt, neti bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. prāyaścittaṃ yaugapadye na vidyate. kutaḥ. vibhāgaśruteḥ, vibhakte 'pacchede prāyaścittam āmananti. apacchedaś cāyaṃ vibhāgaḥ, sa ubhābhyāṃ sādhyate, iha caikena sādhyamāne śrūyate prāyaścittam, udgātrā pratihartrā vā. na ca yad apareṇa saha kriyate, tat kevalena kṛtaṃ bhavati. yadi hi kevalena kṛtaṃ syāt, tena kṛtam{*6/233*}, aparaḥ kiṃ kuryāt. tasmān na yugapad apacchinnayoḥ prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: When there is a break (<s>apaccheda</s>) between the <s>Prastotṛ</s> (the initiating chanter) and the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (the lead chanter), or between the <s>Udgātṛ</s> and the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> (the responding chanter) — is there an expiation there, or not? — this is the doubt. What, then, is the prima facie view? There is no expiation in [the case of] simultaneity. Why? Because of the hearing of division — they record the expiation when the break is divided [i.e., sequential]. And this break is a division [between chanters], which is accomplished by both [together]. But here [in the Vedic text], when accomplished by one [alone], the expiation is heard — by the <s>Udgātṛ</s> or the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>. And what is done together with another is not [the same as what is] done by one alone. For if it were done by one alone, that [one] having done it, what would the other do? Therefore there is no expiation when [the break occurs] simultaneously for both.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/231: E1,6; E2: jyotiṣṭome prastotrudgātror}*
*{6/232: E1,6; E2: yatra yugapad apacchedaḥ}*
*{6/233: E1,6; E2: kṛte}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/231: E1,6; E2: <s>jyotiṣṭome prastotrudgātror</s>}]
[{6/232: E1,6; E2: <s>yatra yugapad apacchedaḥ</s>}]
[{6/233: E1,6; E2: <s>kṛte</s>}]

children.text: syād vā prāptanimittatvāt kālamātram ekam // MS_6,5.50 //
children.translated_text: Or there would be [an expiation] even in simultaneity, because of the occasion being obtained — the time alone is one. // MS_6,5.50 //

children.text: syād vā prāyaścittaṃ yaugapadye 'pi. prāptaṃ hi nimittam apaccheda udgātuḥ pratihataś{*6/234*} ca. yatra hi dvayor apacchedaḥ, tatra dvāv apy apacchinnau, eko 'py aparo 'pi. saṃyuktasya hi pṛthagbhāvo 'pacchedaḥ, sa cobhayastho 'pi. ekenāpi tatrāpacchedaḥ kriyate 'napekṣyāparam, apareṇāpi. kālamātraṃ tu tatraikam, na ca [722]{*6/235*} kālaikyād apacchedayor aikyaṃ bhavati. tasmāt prāyaścittaṃ yugapad apacchede 'pi.
children.translated_text: Or there would be an expiation even in simultaneity. For the occasion — the break — is obtained for [both] the <s>Udgātṛ</s> and the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>. For where there is a break between two, there both are broken apart — the one as well as the other. For the separation of what is joined is the break, and that pertains to both. By even one [of them] a break is made there, without depending on the other, and by the other as well. The time alone is one there, and from the oneness of time there is no oneness of the breaks. Therefore there is an expiation even when the break is simultaneous.

children.text: tatra vipratiṣedhād vikalpaḥ syāt // MS_6,5.51 //
children.translated_text: There, because of mutual contradiction, there should be an option. // MS_6,5.51 //

children.text: yady udgātṛpratihartroḥ yugapad apacchedo bhavati, tatra saṃdehaḥ. kim adākṣiṇyam, sarvasvaṃ vā vikalpaḥ{*6/236*}, uta samuccaya iti. kiṃ prāptam. tatra vipratiṣedhād vikalpaḥ syāt. viruddhau hy etau kalpau, sarvasvam adākṣiṇyaṃ ca. tasmād vikalpo bhavitum arhati.
children.translated_text: If the break occurs simultaneously between the <s>Udgātṛ</s> and the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>, there a doubt [arises]: [should the expiation be] discourtesy (<s>adākṣiṇya</s>), or all one's property (<s>sarvasva</s>), or an option [between the two], or a combination? What is the prima facie view? There, because of mutual contradiction, there should be an option. For these two prescriptions are mutually opposed — all one's property and discourtesy. Therefore there should properly be an option.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/236: E1,6; E2: veti bhavati vikalpaḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/236: E1,6; E2: <s>veti bhavati vikalpaḥ</s>}]

children.text: prayogāntare vobhayānugrahaḥ syāt // MS_6,5.52 //
children.translated_text: Or, in another performance, both should be upheld. // MS_6,5.52 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti, vikalpa iti, ubhayor vidhānāt. sarvāṅgopasaṃhārī prayogavacana evam upapadyate. vikalpe hi pakṣe bādhaḥ, tasmāt samuccayaḥ. atha yad uktam, virodhād vikalpa iti. ucyate, prayogāntare vobhayānugrahaḥ syāt, tena punar yajetety ucyate. dvis tasya prayogaḥ. tatraikasmin prayoge, ekaḥ kalpaḥ. anyasminn aparo bhaviṣyati. evam avirodhaḥ, tasmād ubhayaṃ prāyaścittam iti.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' reverses the position. This is not so — that there is an option — because both are enjoined. The performance-statement that gathers all subsidiaries is thus made meaningful. For in the option view there is overriding; therefore [there should be] a combination. Now, as to what was said — 'because of contradiction there is an option' — [we] reply: or, in another performance, both should be upheld; for it is stated 'let him sacrifice again.' His performance is twofold. In one performance, one prescription [applies]; in the other, the other will apply. Thus there is no contradiction; therefore both expiations [apply].

children.text: na caikasaṃyogāt // MS_6,5.53 //
children.translated_text: Not so, because of connection with one [performance]. // MS_6,5.53 //

children.text: na caitad evam. kutaḥ. ekasaṃyogāt, sa eva yāgaḥ punaḥ kriyeta. yady anyatareṇa vinā vaiguṇyam ity avadhāryeta, sarvasve kriyamāṇe 'dakṣiṇyābhāvād viguṇaḥ syāt. nānyasmin prayoge kriyamāṇe 'nyaḥ prayogo 'nugṛhyate, na cādākṣiṇyasya [723]{*6/237*} sarvasvadānasya ca prādhānyam, guṇavatā prayogeṇa karma saṃbandhayitavyam. tasmād vikalpaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so. Why? Because of connection with one [performance] — that very same sacrifice would be performed again. If the deficiency due to the absence of one [expiation] were ascertained, then when all one's property is given, [the performance] would be deficient because of the absence of discourtesy. A performance done in another [iteration] does not uphold another performance. And neither discourtesy [723] nor the giving of all one's property is primary — the ritual act should be connected with a performance that has [all its] subsidiaries. Therefore there is an option.

children.text: paurvāparye pūrvadaurbalyaṃ prakṛtivat // MS_6,5.54 //
children.translated_text: In [the case of] sequence, the weakness of the earlier [is like] the archetype. // MS_6,5.54 //

children.text:
yatrānupūrveṇa bhavaty apacchedaḥ, tatra kiṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prāyaścittam, utottaranimittam iti bhavati saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ prāptam. pūrvasya balīyastvam, pūrvāpacchede yan naimittikaṃ prāptam, tasmin sati tadviruddhaṃ na śakyaṃ kartum. na cāśakyam upadeśārhaṃ bhavati, pūrvavijñānaṃ prāptam iti na saṃśayaḥ. tasmāt tadavirodhenānyat kāryaṃ na viruddham. kva tarhi tat syāt. yatra kevalaṃ nimittam. tasmāt pūrvavijñānaṃ balavat.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, paurvāparye pūrvadaurbalyaṃ syāt. kutaḥ. ākhyātena hi yo 'rthaḥ kartavya ity ucyate, tatraitad anubuddhaṃ yathā śakyeta, tatheti. tat pūrvavijñānabādhena{*6/238*} śakyate, nānyathā. tena pūrvavijñānaṃ bādhitvedaṃ kartavyam iti bhavati śabdārthaḥ.
nanu pūrvavijñāna idaṃ upapadyate, yad anyad virodhakaṃ vijñānaṃ bhaviṣyati, tan mithyeti. abhūtaṃ hi tan na{*6/239*} śakyam āśrayitum, idaṃ nāma tad iti. na ca, apratiṣiddhe tasmin na pūrvavijñānaṃ saṃbhavati. tasmād apratiṣiddhaṃ bhaviṣyat{*6/240*}, yadā tu tad bhavati, tadā pūrvavijñānaṃ bādhamānam evotpadyate. tad idānīṃ bādhitaṃ na śaknoty uttaraṃ bādhitum iti, prakṛtivat. yad dhi prākṛtaṃ vaikṛtena bādhyate, tatrāpy etad eva kāraṇam. nābādhitvā pūrvavijñānaṃ vaikṛtaṃ saṃbhavatīti, prākṛtaṃ ca pūrvam, yato vikṛtau tad apekṣā.
pratyakṣatvād vaikṛtam ānumānikaṃ prākṛtaṃ bādhata iti [724]{*6/241*} cet. pratyakṣatve 'pi sati naiva bādheta, yadi yathāvarṇito 'yam ākhyātārtho na bhavet. sati pūrvavijñāne 'śakyatvāt prākṛtaṃ{*6/242*} bādhetaiva. tasmāt parabalīyastvaṃ nyāyyam eveti.
children.translated_text:
Where there is a sequential lapse (<s>apaccheda</s>), there a doubt arises: is the expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) occasioned by the earlier [lapse], or by the later one? What is the prima facie view? The earlier is stronger — when an occasional [rite] has been obtained upon the earlier lapse, while that [rite] exists, something contradictory to it cannot be performed. And what is impossible does not deserve instruction; there is no doubt that the earlier knowledge has been obtained. Therefore, non-contradictorily with that, another [rite] should be done — not one that contradicts it. Where then would that [later expiation] apply? Where there is only [a single] occasion. Therefore the earlier knowledge is stronger.
Given this prima facie view, we say: in a sequence, the earlier would be weaker. Why? For what is stated by the verb as 'to be done' — there this is understood: 'in whatever way it is possible.' And that is possible [only] by overriding the earlier knowledge, not otherwise. Therefore the word-meaning is: 'having overridden the earlier knowledge, this must be done.'
[The objector says:] but in the earlier knowledge this is established — that whatever contradictory knowledge will arise in the future, that is false. For what has not [yet] come into being cannot be relied upon [with the thought] 'this is that.' And [we reply:] that is not so — while that [later knowledge] is not negated, the earlier knowledge is [indeed] possible. Therefore the future [knowledge] is un-negated; but when it does arise, it arises precisely as overriding the earlier knowledge. Being now overridden, [the earlier knowledge] cannot override the later — just like the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). For what belongs to the archetype is overridden by the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) — there too this very reason [applies]: without overriding the earlier knowledge, the modification is not possible; and the archetype is prior, since in the modification there is dependence upon it.
[The objector says:] because of being directly [stated], the modification overrides the inferential archetype. [We reply:] even being directly [stated], it would not override at all if the verb-meaning were not as described. Given the earlier knowledge, because of [the later knowledge's] impossibility, [the modification] would override the archetype. Therefore the strength of the later [knowledge] is indeed proper.

children.text: yady udgātā jaghanyaḥ syāt punaryajñe sarvavedasaṃ dadyād yathetarasmin // MS_6,5.55 //
children.translated_text: If the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter) is the later [to lapse], in the re-sacrifice one should give the entire wealth as [one would] in the other [case]. // MS_6,5.55 //

children.text:
yadā pratihartuḥ pūrvam apacchedaḥ tata udgātuḥ, tatrādakṣiṇeneṣṭvā{*6/243*} punar yaṣṭavyam. tatra saṃdehaḥ. punar yāge kiṃ dvādaśaśataṃ dātavyam uta sarvasvam iti. kiṃ prāptam. dvādaśaśatam. kutaḥ. evaṃ hy āmnāyate, tatra tad dadyāt, yat pūrvasmin dāsyan{*6/244*} syāt{*6/245*}. pūrvasmiṃś ca prayoge jyotiṣṭomadakṣiṇaiva prāptā. tasmād dvādaśaśatam iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, tatra punaryajñe sarvaṃ{*6/246*} dadyāt, yathetarasmin pūrvasminn ahani sarvasvam{*6/247*}. kathaṃ tatra sarvasvam iti cet{*6/248*}. pratihartur apacchedāt. pratihartary apacchinne dvādaśaśataṃ bādhitvā sarvasvaṃ dāsyan{*6/249*} bhavati.
nanu pūrvasminn ahani dvādaśaśatam apy asau dāsyann āsīt. satyam, sarvasvadānena ta ubhayaṃ{*6/250*} pradattaṃ bhavati. tasmāt tad deyaṃ. nanv arvāg api dvādaśaśatāt sarvasvam. naitad evam, adhikṛte{*6/251*} dvādaśaśate sarvasvam apy adhikaṃ bhavati. api ca pūrvasminn ahani naiva dvādaśaśataṃ dāsyan{*6/252*} bhavatīti{*6/253*}. etāvad dāsyann{*6/254*} ity ucyate, yasyottarakāle tāvad dānaṃ{*6/255*} bhavati. na ca, pūrvasminn ahani dvādaśaśataṃ dīyate, tasmān na tad dāsyann{*6/256*} ity avagamyate, mithyābuddhiḥ sā, tattvena vyavahāraḥ.
[725]{*6/257*} nanu ca sarvasvam api pratiṣiddhaṃ bhavati, tad apy asau na dāsyann iti, sāpy asya mithyābuddhiḥ. nety āha, sābhyāsasya jyotiṣṭomasya prayogaḥ. tatra prathamaprayoge 'dākṣiṇyavirodhāt sarvasvaṃ bādhyate. dvitīyaprayoge taddānaṃ codyate. tatra virodho nāsti, tasyaiva yajñasya sa eva prayogaḥ. pratihartā ca tasminn apacchinna iti dvādaśaśataṃ bādhitvā sarvasvam eva dāsyan{*6/258*} bhavati. tasmāt sarvasvaṃ tatra deyam iti.
children.translated_text:
When the lapse of the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> (respondent) occurs first and then of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, there, having sacrificed without proper <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, one must re-sacrifice. There a doubt [arises]: in the re-sacrifice, should twelve hundred [cows] be given, or all one's wealth? What is the prima facie view? Twelve hundred. Why? For thus it is recorded: 'There he should give what he would have been going to give in the earlier [sacrifice].' And in the earlier performance, only the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> <s>dakṣiṇā</s> was applicable. Therefore twelve hundred.
Given this prima facie view, we say: in that re-sacrifice one should give all [one's wealth], just as in the other [case] — on the earlier day, all one's wealth. How is there all one's wealth in that [earlier case]? Because of the lapse of the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>. When the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> has lapsed, overriding the twelve hundred, one would be going to give all one's wealth.
[The objector says:] but on the earlier day, he was also going to give the twelve hundred. True — by giving all one's wealth, both [amounts] are covered. Therefore that should be given. [The objector:] but all one's wealth is less than twelve hundred! This is not so — when twelve hundred is accepted [as the standard], all one's wealth also counts as exceeding [that]. Moreover, on the earlier day he was not [actually] going to give twelve hundred. 'He would be going to give this much' is said of one whose later giving is that much. And twelve hundred is not given on the earlier day; therefore the understanding that he was 'going to give' that is a false notion — the transaction [proceeds] according to reality.
[725] [The objector:] but even all one's wealth is prohibited — so he was not going to give that either, and that too would be a false notion. No, he says — the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> with repetition has [multiple] performances. In the first performance, all one's wealth is overridden because of conflict with [the requirement of] having <s>dakṣiṇā</s> [for later performances]. In the second performance, its giving is enjoined. There is no conflict — it is the very same performance of the same sacrifice. And the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> has lapsed in that [sacrifice]; therefore, overriding the twelve hundred, one would be going to give all one's wealth. Therefore all one's wealth should be given there.

ahargaṇe yasminn apacchedas tad āvarteta karmapṛthaktvāt // MS_6,5.56 //
children.translated_text: In a series of days (<s>ahargaṇa</s>), whichever [day] has the lapse — that [day alone] should be repeated, because of the separateness of ritual actions. // MS_6,5.56 //

children.text: ahargaṇe yadā bhavati kasmiṃścid ahany udgātur apacchedaḥ, tadā saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ kṛtsno 'hargaṇa āvartate, uta tad evāhar iti. kiṃ prāptam. kṛtsno 'hargaṇaḥ. kutaḥ. aparair ahobhir vinā, tadā{*6/259*} viguṇaṃ{*6/260*} bhavati, tasmād gaṇa{*6/261*} evāvarteteti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, yasminn apacchedaḥ, tad evāvarteta. kutaḥ. karmapṛthaktvāt, pṛthag etāni karmāṇi, nānyad ahar anyasya guṇabhūtam, iṣṭveti ca yāgaṃ parisamāpyeti gamyate, na sāṅgam iti. yāny aharantarāṇi sāhāyyenopakariṣyanti, vidyanta eva tāni. ataḥ{*6/262*} sāhāyyaṃ kariṣyantīti. tasmāt tad evāvarteta.
children.translated_text: In a series of days, when on some [particular] day there is a lapse of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, there a doubt [arises]: should the entire series of days be repeated, or only that [particular] day? What is the prima facie view? The entire series. Why? Without the other days, [the series] would be deficient; therefore the entire series should be repeated. Given this prima facie view, we say: whichever [day] has the lapse — only that [day] should be repeated. Why? Because of the separateness of ritual actions — these ritual actions are separate; one day is not a subsidiary of another; and 'having sacrificed' [means] 'having completed the sacrifice' — it is understood [as referring to] the sacrifice alone, not with subsidiaries. And those intervening days that will assist [the repeated day] as auxiliaries — they do exist. Therefore they will render assistance. Therefore only that [day] should be repeated.

children.text: saṃnipāte 'vaiguṇyāt prakṛtivat tulyakalpā yajeran // MS_6,6.1 //
children.translated_text: In a gathering [of multiple sacrificers], because of non-deficiency, those of equal custom (<s>kalpa</s>) should sacrifice, like the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). // MS_6,6.1 //

children.text: satrāṇy udāharaṇam, saptadaśāvarāḥ satram āsīran, ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ satram āsate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ satram upayantīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ samānakalpānām bhinnakalpānāṃ ca sahādhikāra uta samānakalpānām eveti. ke punaḥ samānakalpāḥ. rājanyātribadhryaśvavasiṣṭhavainyaśunakānāṃ kaṇvakaśyapasaṃkṛtīnāṃ nārāśaṃso dvitīyaḥ prayājaḥ, tanūnapād itareṣām. evaṃ kecin nārāśaṃsakalpāḥ, kecit tanūnapātkalpāḥ. tatra kiṃ tāvat prāptam. saṃnipāte bahūnāṃ yajamānānāṃ ya eva tulyakalpāḥ{*6/264*}, ta eva saha satram āsīran. kutaḥ. avaiguṇyāt, itarathā yasya kalpo nopasaṃhriyeta, tasya vaiguṇyaṃ syāt. yathā prakṛtāv eva vinā sādguṇyena, phalābhāva evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: <s>Sattras</s> (communal sacrifices) are the illustration — 'Not fewer than seventeen should sit for a <s>Sattra</s>; those who are learned thus sit for a <s>Sattra</s>; those who are learned thus undertake a <s>Sattra</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is there joint eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) for those of the same custom and those of different customs, or only for those of the same custom? Who then are 'of the same custom'? For the <s>Rājanya</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Badhrya</s>, <s>Aśva</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vainya</s>, and <s>Śunaka</s> [lineages], and for the <s>Kaṇva</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and <s>Saṃkṛti</s> [lineages], <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> is the second <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering); for the rest, [it is] <s>Tanūnapāt</s>. Thus some follow the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> custom and some the <s>Tanūnapāt</s> custom. There, what is the prima facie view? In a gathering of many sacrificers, only those of the same custom should sit together for a <s>Sattra</s>. Why? Because of non-deficiency — otherwise, for one whose custom is not accommodated, there would be deficiency. Just as in the archetype [rite] itself, without excellence [of all qualities], there is absence of fruit — so here too.

children.text: vacanād vā śirovat syāt // MS_6,6.2 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of the [Vedic] statement, it would be like the <s>śiras</s> (head) [case]. // MS_6,6.2 //

children.text: vāśabdāt pakṣo viparivartate. na caitad asti, bhinnakalpānām anadhikāra iti, te 'py adhikriyeran. kutaḥ. aviśeṣeṇa{*6/265*} sarveṣāṃ yajamānānāṃ prāptiḥ. na ca bhinnakalpānāṃ pratiṣedhaḥ. nanu vaiguṇyaṃ bhinnakalpānām. atrocyate, [727]{*6/266*} vacanāt, sāmānyavacanena bhinnakalpā api gṛhītāḥ. tatra śirovad bhādhaḥ syāt, yathā, puruṣaśīrṣam upadadhātīti{*6/267*} vacanasāmarthyāc chavaśirasāṃ sparśanaṃ smṛtivipratiṣiddham api kriyate, evam ihāpi. athavā, āśiravat, yathā, ṛtapeye ghṛtavrato bhavatīti vacanād vrataduhi nivṛttāyām anyāmāśire gāṃ kalpayanti. evam etad api vacanād bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' reverses the position. This is not [correct] — that there is no eligibility for those of different customs; they too should be eligible. Why? Because without distinction, all sacrificers are eligible. And there is no prohibition of those with different customs. [The objector says:] but there is deficiency for those with different customs. To this we say: [727] because of the [Vedic] statement — by the general statement, even those with different customs are included. There, the overriding would be like [the case of] the head — just as in 'one places a human head' [where], by the force of the [Vedic] statement, the touching of a corpse-head, though prohibited by <s>smṛti</s>, is performed — so here too. Or rather, like the <s>āśir</s> (fresh milk) [case] — just as in 'In the <s>Ṛtapeya</s>, one observes a ghee-vrata' [where], because of the [Vedic] statement, when the <s>vrata</s>-cow ceases [to give milk], they designate another cow for fresh milk — so too this will be [done] because of the [Vedic] statement.

NOTES:
[{6/265: E1,6; E2: <s>kutaḥ. aviśeṣāt. aviśeṣeṇa</s>}]
[{6/266: E2: 5,326; E6: 2,187}]
[{6/267: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 5.2.9.2}]

children.text: na vānārabhyavādatvāt // MS_6,6.3 //
children.translated_text: No, or rather [they should not be eligible], because of [the general statement] not being a non-initiatory statement (<s>anārabhyavāda</s>). // MS_6,6.3 //

children.text: naitad asti, yad uktam, bhinnakalpānām apy adhikāra iti, samānakalpā evādhikriyeran. kutaḥ. avaiguṇyāt. atha yad uktam, vacanād vaiguṇyenāpi{*6/268*} setsyatīti. tan na, anārabhyavādatvāt, tad dhi vacanāt prakalpyate, yasminn akalpyamāne vacanam anarthakaṃ bhavati. yadi hy ārabhya bhinnakalpān, etad ucyeta, tato vacanam anarthakaṃ bhavatīti bhinnakalpānām api satram abhyupagamyeta, na tv ārabhya bhinnakalpān etad ucyate. samānakalpeṣv arthavattāsya vacanasya bhaviṣyati. tasmān na bhinnakalpānām adhikāra iti.
children.translated_text: This is not [correct] — what was said, that even those of different customs are eligible — [rather,] only those of the same custom should be eligible. Why? Because of non-deficiency. Now, as to what was said — 'because of the [Vedic] statement, it will succeed even with deficiency' — that is not so, because of [the statement] not being a non-initiatory statement. For [only] that is established by the [Vedic] statement which, if not established, would make the statement purposeless. If, having begun with those of different customs, this is stated, then the statement would be purposeless — [only] then would the eligibility of those with different customs be conceded. But this is not stated having begun with those of different customs. The meaningfulness of this statement will be [found] among those of the same custom. Therefore those of different customs are not eligible.

children.text: syād vā yajñārthatvād audumbarīvat // MS_6,6.4 //
children.translated_text: Or there may be eligibility for those of different customs, because of the custom being for the purpose of the sacrifice, like the <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood pillar). // MS_6,6.4 //

children.text: syād vā bhinnakalpānām adhikāraḥ. kutaḥ. yajñārthatvāt kalpasya. vasiṣṭhādīnāṃ nārāśaṃsakalpo yajñasya sādhakaḥ. sa ca yajñaḥ sarveṣāṃ sādhāraṇaḥ, parakalpenāpi siddhaḥ siddho{*6/269*} bhavati. yathā, yajamānena saṃmāyaudumbarīṃ{*6/270*} parivāsayantīti yasya kasyacit parimāṇena siddho yajño 'nyeṣām api siddho bhavati. ucyate, nanu prayājasya vākyena puruṣasaṃbandhaḥ. sa ca prakaraṇaprāptāṃ yāgārthatāṃ bādhiṣyata iti. neti brūmaḥ. phalaṃ [728]{*6/271*} hi tadā kalpayitavyam. nanv itarathāpy adṛṣṭam avaśyaṃ kalpanīyam. tatrocyate, satyaṃ kalpanīyam. pramāṇena tu prayogavacanaikavākyena, dvitīye tu pakṣe kalpayitvā śabdam, tenaikavākyatā syāt. athocyeta, kvacit samāmnātena sahaikavākyatā bhaviṣyati. tathāpy aprakṛtena vyavahitena ca kalpyamānā prakṛtakalpanāyā gurutarā syāt.
children.translated_text: Or there may be eligibility for those of different customs. Why? Because the custom is for the purpose of the sacrifice. The <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> custom of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others is an instrument of the sacrifice. And that sacrifice is common to all — [what is] accomplished even by another's custom is [still] accomplished. Just as 'they season the <s>audumbarī</s> according to the sacrificer's measurement,' [where] the sacrifice accomplished by anyone's measurement is accomplished for the others as well. [The objector] says: but by [Vedic] statement, the <s>prayāja</s> has a connection with the person. And that will override the purpose-relation with the sacrifice obtained from context. To this we say: no. For [728] then a fruit would have to be postulated. [The objector:] but in the other [view] too, an unseen [purpose] must necessarily be postulated. To this we say: true, it must be postulated — but by a valid means of knowledge, [namely] one-sentence-hood with the statement of performance. In the second view, having postulated [the connection with] the word, one-sentence-hood would [result] from that. [The objector:] but somewhere there will be one-sentence-hood with [something already] recorded. Even so, [a connection] postulated with something unrelated and intervening would be weightier than a postulation related to what is at hand.

children.text: na, tatpradhānatvāt // MS_6,6.5 //
children.translated_text: No, because of that [sacrifice] being primary. // MS_6,6.5 //

children.text: naitad evam, tatpradhānatvāt. puruṣārtho hy eṣa kalpaḥ. katham. vasiṣṭhādīnāṃ{*6/272*} nārāśaṃso yajñāṅgam iti. yac ca yasya yajñāṅgam, tena saha phaladaṃ karma tasya bhavati. tenaivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate, vasiṣṭhānāṃ{*6/273*} nārāśaṃsena sahitaṃ karma phaladaṃ bhavatīti.
children.translated_text: This is not so, because of that [ritual] being primary. For this alternative (<s>kalpa</s>) is for the person's purpose. How? The <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> [cup] is a subsidiary of the sacrifice for the <s>Vasiṣṭhas</s> and others. And whatever is a subsidiary of whose sacrifice — the rite together with that becomes fruit-giving for him. Thus the connection is made: for the <s>Vasiṣṭhas</s>, the rite combined with the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> becomes fruit-giving.

children.text: audumbaryāḥ parārthatvāt kapālavat // MS_6,6.6 //
children.translated_text: The <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood post) [is] for another's purpose, like the potsherd. // MS_6,6.6 //

children.text: atha yad upavarṇitam, yathaudumbarī tatheheti. pārārthyam{*6/274*} audumbaryāḥ, yajamāno guṇatvena śrūyate. nanu tatrāpi prayogavacanaḥ puruṣaprādhānyaṃ kuryāt. naiṣa doṣaḥ, ekenāpi yajamānena saṃmitā ceyaṃ sarveṣāṃ yajamānasaṃmitā bhavati. na tv ihaikasya saṃgṛhīte{*6/275*} sarveṣāṃ saṃgṛhītaḥ. tasmād{*6/276*} audumbaryāḥ pārārthyam, kapālavat, yathā, puroḍāśakapālena tuṣā upavapantīti{*6/277*} parārthakapālena tuṣā upavaptavyā ity upādīyate, evam etad apīti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was described — 'as with the <s>audumbarī</s>, so here.' The <s>audumbarī</s> is for another's purpose — the sacrificer is heard as subordinate. [The objector says:] but there too, the performance-statement would make the person primary. This is no fault — for even though measured by one sacrificer, this [post] being measured by all sacrificers, [the measurement applies to all]. But here, when one [alternative] is accepted, it is not accepted for all. Therefore the <s>audumbarī</s> is for another's purpose, like the potsherd — just as in 'with the cake-potsherd they scatter the husks,' the husks are to be scattered with a potsherd that is for another's purpose — thus it is employed. So too this.

children.text:

children.text: anyenāpīti cet // MS_6,6.7 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that by another also — // MS_6,6.7 //

children.text: evaṃ ced bhavān paśyati, yajamānena saṃmānam, tat prayo[729]{*6/278*}janaṃ svenānyena{*6/279*} vā yajamāneneti. tathā prayogāntare yo yajamānas tenāpi saṃmānaṃ prāpnoti.
children.translated_text: If the honorable [opponent] sees it thus — the measurement is by the sacrificer — then the purpose [729] is [accomplished] by one's own or another sacrificer. Thus in another performance, the measurement is obtained by whatever sacrificer [performs it].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/278: E2: 5,328; E6: 2,189}*
*{6/279: E1,6; E2: na svenānyena; E2 (v.l.): tatsvenānyena}*

children.text: naikatvāt tasya cānadhikārāc chabdasya cāvibhaktatvāt // MS_6,6.8 //
children.translated_text: No, because of oneness, and because of his non-entitlement, and because of the word being undivided. // MS_6,6.8 //

children.text: atrocyate, na prayogāntarasya yajamānaḥ prasajyate. na tu yajamānaśabde kaścid viśeṣaḥ, yato yajamānaśabdād vyavasthā syāt. kiṃ tarhi. ekatvasya vivakṣitatvāt, na dvābhyāṃ yājamānāni kartavyānīti nānya ānīyate. āha, anya eva tarhi sarvayājamāneṣu bhavatu. naivam, kāminaṃ hy adhikṛtya, sāṅgasya yāgasya vacanam. yajamānaśabdaś cāvibhakta ihaudumbaryāḥ saṃmāne. tasmān nānyo bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: To this we reply: the sacrificer of another performance is not implicated. And there is no distinction in the word 'sacrificer' by which a determination could be made from the word 'sacrificer.' What then? Because oneness is intended — the sacrificer's [rites] are not to be performed by two — another is not brought in. He says: then let another alone [perform] in all sacrificer's [rites]. Not so — for the statement of the sacrifice with all its subsidiaries is made with reference to one who has a desire (<s>kāmin</s>). And the word 'sacrificer' is undivided here in the measurement of the <s>audumbarī</s>. Therefore another will not [be the referent].

children.text: saṃnipātāt tu nimittavighātaḥ syād bṛhadrathantaravad vibhaktaśiṣṭatvād vasiṣṭhanirvartye // MS_6,6.9 //
children.translated_text: But because of conjunction, there would be obstruction of the occasion — like [the case of] <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>, because of being prescribed as divided, in what is to be accomplished by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // MS_6,6.9 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. bahuṣu yajamāneṣu saṃnipātān nimittavighātaḥ syāt. kutaḥ. vibhaktiśiṣṭatvāt, vasiṣṭhanirvartye prayoge nārāśaṃso naimittikaḥ. anyasmiṃs tanūnapān naimittikaḥ. yatredānīm ubhaye kartāraḥ samahāyena, tatra nirvṛttir na kevalena. tasmān na kevalaḥ kartā. na ced vāsiṣṭhaḥ kevalaḥ kartā, tasmāt tannimittaṃ tatra na kartavyam, na cetaranimittam, ubhayor apy anyonyena vighātaḥ, bṛhadrathantaravat, tad yathā, bṛhadrathantaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavatīti na bṛhadsādhanakam, na rathantarasādhanakam iti, naiva tatra bṛhan nimittaṃ bhavati, na rathantaraṃ vā. evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>tu</s> ('but') reverses the position. When many sacrificers conjoin, there would be obstruction of the occasion. Why? Because of being prescribed as divided — in the performance to be accomplished by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> is occasional. In another [performance], <s>Tanūnapāt</s> is occasional. Now, where both [groups of] performers [join] together in a shared [sacrifice], there the accomplishment is not by one alone. Therefore one alone is not the performer. And if a <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> alone is not the performer, therefore that which is occasioned by him should not be done there, nor that occasioned by the other — there is mutual obstruction of both — like [the case of] <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>. Just as in '<s>Bṛhadrathantara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant)' — it is neither accomplished by <s>Bṛhat</s> alone nor by <s>Rathantara</s> alone — thus neither <s>Bṛhat</s> is the occasion there nor <s>Rathantara</s>. So too here.

children.text: api vā kṛtsnasaṃyogād avighātaḥ pratīyeta{*6/281*} svāmitvenābhisaṃbandhāt // MS_6,6.10 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the connection with the whole, there would be no obstruction — it should be understood through ownership. // MS_6,6.10 //

children.text: api veti pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. kṛtsnaṃ prati kevalasya kartṛtvena saṃyogo bhavati, tasmād avighātaḥ naimittikānām. kathaṃ punaḥ kārtsnyena kartavyatvam{*6/282*}. svāmitvenābhisaṃbandhāt, karma prati svāmitvena kevalānāṃ vasiṣṭhādīnām abhisaṃbandho bhavati, karma puruṣāṇam upakārakam, tad dhy ekaikasya śaknoti phalaṃ nirvartayitum. tasmād ekaikaḥ kṛtsnasya karteti tan naimittikaṃ sarvaṃ prāpnoti. yathā tuṇḍamātre dīyatām iti. yady api sā tuṇḍaḍapitthayor mātā, tathāpi tasyai dīyate. kārtsnena hi tasya sā mātā bhavati. na hi vyāsajyate mātṛtvam. tadvad ihāpi draṣṭavyam. tasmād asamānakalpānām anadhikāraḥ.
children.translated_text: The words '<s>api vā</s>' reverse the position. Each individual has a connection with the whole as performer; therefore there is no obstruction of the occasional [rites]. But how is the performance of the whole [possible for each]? Because of the connection through ownership — each of the <s>Vasiṣṭhas</s> and others individually has a connection with the rite through ownership. The rite is beneficial to the persons; for it is capable of producing the fruit for each one. Therefore each one is the performer of the whole — and thus obtains all the occasional [elements]. Just as in 'let it be given to the mother of <s>Tuṇḍa</s>' — even though she is the mother of both <s>Tuṇḍa</s> and <s>Ḍapittha</s>, nevertheless it is given to her. For she is wholly his mother — motherhood is not divided. So too it should be seen here. Therefore those not of the same alternative have no entitlement.

*{6/282: E1,6; E2: kartṛtvam}*

children.text: sāmnoḥ karmavṛddhyaikadeśena saṃyoge guṇatvenābhisaṃbandhas tasmāt tatra vighātaḥ syāt // MS_6,6.11 //
children.translated_text: Of the two <s>Sāmans</s>, because of the connection through a single portion of the increase of the ritual action, [there is] a connection as subordinate; therefore there would be obstruction. // MS_6,6.11 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, bṛhadrathantaravad iti, tat pariharaṇīyam. bṛhadrathantarayoḥ sāmnor naimittikakarmavṛddhyaikadeśena saṃyogo bhavati. tatra hy ubhayoḥ sādhakatvam naikasya. stotraikadeśena tu tatra sāmnoḥ saṃbandhaḥ, na kṛtsnena stotreṇa. guṇatvena hi tatra sāma śrūyate, stotraṃ prādhānyena. tasmāt tatra vighātaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'like <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>' — that must be refuted. The two <s>Sāmans</s>, <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>, have a connection through a single portion of the increase of the occasional ritual action. There, both have the capacity [to produce the result], not one alone. But there, the connection of the <s>Sāmans</s> is through a single portion of the <s>stotra</s> (praise-hymn), not through the whole <s>stotra</s>. For there, the <s>Sāman</s> is heard as subordinate, and the <s>stotra</s> as primary. Therefore there would be obstruction.

children.text: vacanāt tu dvisaṃyogas tasmād ekasya pāṇitvam // MS_6,6.12 //
children.translated_text: But because of the statement, there is a double connection; therefore one [of the two performs] the priestly function. // MS_6,6.12 //

children.text:
idaṃ samāmananti, etena rājapurohitau sāyujyakāmau [731]{*6/283*} yajeyātām iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ rājño dvau purohitau yajeyātām, uta rājā ca purohitaś ceti. kiṃ prāptam. rājño dvau purohitāv iti. kutaḥ. purohitaśabdāt paraṃ dvivacanaṃ śrūyate, tacchabdavācyasya dvitvaṃ śaknoti vaditum. purohitaś ca tacchabdavācyaḥ śrutyā, na rājā. purohitavacanaḥ purohitaśabdaḥ. lakṣaṇayā yugapad adhikaraṇavacanatāyāṃ hi tad bhavati. nanv ekasya dvau purohitau na staḥ. purohitaṃ vṛṇīta iti hy upādīyamānasya vivakṣitam ekatvam iti. ucyate, vacanād etad bhaviṣyati. kiṃ hi vacanaṃ na kalpayet. etenaiva kāraṇena dvau bhaviṣyataḥ, yathā vacanenāñjalinā juhotīty ekasyaiva dvau pāṇī bhavataḥ, yady api savyo prāptas{*6/284*} tathāpīti.
NOTES:
*{6/283: E2: 5,330; E6: 2,190}*
*{6/284: E1; E2,6: savyo 'prāptas}*
children.translated_text: They record this: 'With this [sacrifice], a king and priest desiring union [731] should sacrifice.' There a doubt [arises]: should two priests of the king sacrifice, or a king and a priest? What is the prima facie view? Two priests of the king. Why? After the word 'priest' (<s>purohita</s>), the dual number is heard — the dual can refer to the one denoted by that word. And 'priest' is the one denoted by that word according to <s>śruti</s>, not the king. The word <s>purohita</s> denotes the priest. For it to denote both [king and priest] simultaneously would be by figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). [The objector says:] but one [king] does not have two priests — for in 'he should choose a priest,' the oneness of what is being employed is intended. We reply: this will be [explained] from the [Vedic] statement. For what can a [Vedic] statement not bring about? For this very reason there will be two [priests] — just as by the statement 'he offers with folded hands (<s>añjali</s>),' a single person has two hands; even though [only] the left [alone] might be obtained, nevertheless [both are used].

children.text: arthābhāvāt tu naivaṃ syāt // MS_6,6.13 //
children.translated_text: Not so, because of the absence of purpose. // MS_6,6.13 //

children.text: tuśabdāt pakṣo viparivartate{*6/285*}. naivaṃ syāt, dvau purohitāv iti. kutaḥ. arthābhāvāt, naivāyam artho 'sti, dvau purohitāv iti. ekasya rājña eka eva purohita upādeyatvena hi śrūyate, purohitaṃ karotīti, ekatvaṃ vivakṣitam. nanu vacanād ity uktam. ucyate, na tu vacanād etac chakyam, saṃskāranimittatvāt purohitaśabdasya. kriyamāṇo 'pi na purohitaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: The word <s>tu</s> reverses the position. It should not be so — [i.e.,] two priests. Why? Because of the absence of purpose — this purpose does not exist, [namely] two priests. For one king, a single priest alone is heard as to be employed — 'he makes [someone] a priest' — oneness is intended. [The objector says:] but it was said, 'because of the statement.' We reply: this cannot be [brought about] by the statement, because the word <s>purohita</s> is based on a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Even when [another is] being appointed, he would not become a priest.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/285: E2 (v.l.): vyāvartyate}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/285: E2 (v.l.): <s>vyāvartyate</s>}]

children.text: arthānaṃ ca vibhaktatvān na tacchrutena saṃbandhaḥ // MS_6,6.14 //
children.translated_text: And because of the purposes being divided, there is no connection with that [dual] as heard. // MS_6,6.14 //

children.text: arthānāṃ ca vibhaktatvaṃ śrūyate, tejaḥsaṃstavo brāhmaṇasya, vīryasaṃstavo rājanyasya. tābhyāṃ varṇābhyāṃ tena tena phalena saṃbandho 'nūdyate. tasmād api na dvau purohitāv iti{*6/286*}.
children.translated_text: And a division of purposes is heard: 'The praise of splendor belongs to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; the praise of valor belongs to the <s>Kṣatriya</s>.' The connection of those two <s>varṇas</s> (classes) with their respective fruits is restated. Therefore too, there are not two priests [of one king].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/286: E1,6; E2: purohitāv ekasya rājña iti}*
*{6/287: E2: 5,331; E6: 2,191}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/286: E1,6; E2: <s>purohitāv ekasya rājña iti</s>}]
[{6/287: E2: 5,331; E6: 2,191}]

children.text: pāṇeḥ pratyaṅgabhāvād asaṃbandhaḥ pratīyeta // MS_6,6.15 //
children.translated_text: Because of the hand being a sub-limb, it should be understood that there is no [parallel] connection. // MS_6,6.15 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, etasmād eva kāraṇād ekasyaiva puruṣasya dvau pāṇī bhavata iti. yuktaṃ tatra, pāṇeḥ pratyaṅgabhūtatvāt, añjaliṃ pratyaṅgabhūto{*6/288*} dakṣiṇasya pāṇeḥ svayaḥ pāṇiḥ. tena vināñjalir eva na bhavati. na hi dvābhyāṃ dakṣiṇābhyām añjalir ity ucyate. tasmād rājā ca purohitaś ca syāt. nanu tatra rājapurohitaś ca rājapurohitaś ca rājapurohitau yajeyātām iti. ucyate, na tau sāyujyakāmau bhavataḥ. sa rājā purohitena sahaikakāryo bhavati, na tu purohitaḥ purohitena. ubhāv api tau hi rājānam abhicarantau purohitāv ity ucyete, na hi tāv{*6/289*} icchantau, saṃskāraśabdo hi purohita iti. nanu lakṣaṇā bhavati bhavatpakṣe. ucyate, śrutyabhāve lakṣaṇayāpi vyavahāro bhavati, yathā, agnau tiṣṭhati, avaṭe tiṣṭhatīti. tasmād rājā ca purohitaś ca rājapurohitāv iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'for this very reason, a single person has two hands' — that is appropriate there, because of the hand being a sub-limb. The right hand is a sub-limb of the left hand with respect to the folded hands (<s>añjali</s>) — it is itself a hand. Without it, there simply is no <s>añjali</s>. For it is not said that an <s>añjali</s> is [made] with two right hands. Therefore it should be [understood as] the king and the priest. [The objector says:] but there, <s>rājapurohita</s> means 'a king's priest and a king's priest — two king's priests should sacrifice.' We reply: those two would not desire union (<s>sāyujya</s>). That king, being united in purpose with [his] priest, [they sacrifice together]; but a priest [does not seek union] with [another] priest. For both those two [priests], serving the king, are called 'priests' — they do not desire [union with each other]. For <s>purohita</s> is a consecration-term (<s>saṃskāraśabda</s>). [The objector says:] but there would be figurative usage in your view. We reply: in the absence of a direct [Vedic] statement, usage through figurative meaning also occurs — just as 'he stands in the fire' [means 'near the fire'], 'he stands in the pit' [means 'near the pit']. Therefore 'king and priest' [together] are <s>rājapurohitau</s>.

children.text:

children.text: satrāṇi sarvavarṇānāṃ aviśeṣāt // MS_6,6.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Satras</s> (sacrificial sessions) [are] for all <s>varṇas</s> (classes), because of non-distinction. // MS_6,6.16 //

children.text: iha satrāṇy udāharaṇam. ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ satram āsate, ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ satram upayantīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ satrāṇi trayāṇām api varṇānām, uta brāhmaṇānām eveti. kiṃ prāptam. satrāṇi sarvavarṇānāṃ bhaveyur iti. [733]{*6/290*} kasmāt. aviśeṣāt, na hi kaścid viśeṣa āśrīyate. amīṣāṃ varṇānāṃ satrāṇi bhavanti, amīṣāṃ neti. tasmāt trayāṇām api varṇānām adhikāra iti.
children.translated_text: Here, <s>satras</s> are the example. 'Those who, being learned thus, sit in a <s>satra</s>; those who, being learned thus, approach a <s>satra</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: are <s>satras</s> for all three <s>varṇas</s>, or for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> alone? What is the prima facie view? <s>Satras</s> should be for all <s>varṇas</s>. [733] Why? Because of non-distinction — for no distinction is resorted to [stating] 'these <s>varṇas</s> have <s>satras</s>, these do not.' Therefore all three <s>varṇas</s> have entitlement.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_6,6.17 //
children.translated_text: And because of seeing an indicatory mark. // MS_6,6.17 //

children.text: itaś ca paśyāmaḥ, trayāṇāṃ satrāṇīti. kutaḥ. liṅgadarśanāt. kiṃ liṅgaṃ bhavati. evam āha, bārhadgiraṃ brāhmaṇasya brahmasāma kuryāt, pārthuraśyaṃ{*6/291*} rājanyasya rāyovājīyaṃ vaiśyasyeti dvādaśāhe bhavati vacanaṃ brāhmasāmavidhānaparam, tasmin rājanyavaiśyānāṃ darśanaṃ bhavati. tasmād api sarvavarṇānām adhikāra iti.
children.translated_text: And we see this further — that <s>satras</s> are for three [<s>varṇas</s>]. Why? Because of seeing an indicatory mark. What is the indicatory mark? Thus it states: 'The <s>Bārhadgira</s> [Sāman] should be the <s>brahma-sāma</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; the <s>Pārthuraśya</s> [Sāman] of the <s>Kṣatriya</s>; the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> [Sāman] of the <s>Vaiśya</s>' — this statement occurs in the twelve-day [rite] for the purpose of prescribing the <s>brahma-sāma</s>; in it, <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> are observed. Therefore too, all <s>varṇas</s> have entitlement.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/291: E1; E2,6: pārthuraśmaṃ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/291: E1; E2,6: <s>pārthuraśmaṃ</s>}]

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ vetarayor{*6/292*} ārtvijyābhāvāt // MS_6,6.18 //
children.translated_text: Or [they are] for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> [alone], because of the absence of priestly function for the other two. // MS_6,6.18 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti, trayāṇām api varṇānām iti{*6/293*}. kiṃ tarhi. brāhmaṇānām eva syāt. kutaḥ. itarayor ārtvijyābhāvāt. itarayor hi varṇayo rājanyavaiśyayor ārtvijyaṃ pratiṣiddham. svayam evārtvijyena ca vinā viguṇatvam. tasmād brāhmaṇānām eva syāt.
children.translated_text: The word <s>vā</s> reverses the position. This is not so — that all three <s>varṇas</s> [have entitlement]. What then? It should be for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> alone. Why? Because of the absence of priestly function (<s>ārtvijya</s>) for the other two. For the other two <s>varṇas</s> — <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> — priestly function is prohibited. And without priestly function by oneself, there is deficiency. Therefore it should be for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> alone.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/292: E1,6; E2: cetarayor}*
*{6/293: E1,6; E2: varṇānām adhikāra iti}*
children.translated_text:

children.text: vacanād iti cet // MS_6,6.19 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] because of a [Vedic] statement — // MS_6,6.19 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, rājanyavaiśyayor vaiguṇyam āpadyata iti. vacanād yajamānāḥ santa ṛtvijo bhaviṣyanti, ye yajamānās ta ṛtvija iti. ke punar yajamānāḥ. ye tatra phalaṃ{*6/294*} kāmayamānāḥ satrakarmaṇi pravṛttās te rājanyā api vaiśyā api. teṣām ṛtvikkarma vidhīyate. tatraitat syāt, yeṣām ārtvijyaṃ śakyaṃ kartum, teṣām eva tad brāhmaṇānām{*6/295*}. pratiṣiddhaṃ [734]{*6/296*} hi rājanyavaiśyānām, na teṣām idam ārtvijyavidhānam iti. naitad evam, yathaiva brāhmaṇānāṃ yajamānānām aprāptaṃ vacanavidhānād bhavati, evam abrāhmaṇānāṃ api yajamānānāṃ vacanaprāmāṇyād eva bhavitum arhatīti. tasmād ārtvijyasaṃskṛtā rājanyavaiśyā api satram āsīrann iti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that there is a deficiency for the <s>Rājanya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> [castes] — [we reply:] by the [Vedic] statement, the sacrificers (<s>yajamāna</s>) being [also] priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) — 'those who are sacrificers, they [are] the priests.' Who then are the sacrificers? Those who, desiring the fruit [734], have engaged in the <s>satra</s> ritual — they [include] <s>Rājanyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> as well. For them, priestly action is enjoined. There one might [object]: only for those who are capable of performing the priestly function — that is, for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> alone. For it is prohibited [734] for <s>Rājanyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s>; this is not an injunction of priestly function for them. This is not so — just as for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sacrificers what is not [otherwise] obtained becomes [operative] by the injunction of the statement, so too for non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sacrificers it should properly become [operative] by the very authority of the statement. Therefore <s>Rājanyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> too, refined by [the performance of] priestly functions, would sit for the <s>satra</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/294: E1,6; E2: satraphalaṃ}*
*{6/295: E1,6; E2: brāhmaṇānāṃ śakyam}*
*{6/296: E2: 5,333; E6: 2,192}*
na svāmitvaṃ hi vidhīyate // MS_6,6.20 //
children.translated_text: For ownership (<s>svāmitva</s>) is not what is being enjoined. // MS_6,6.20 //

children.text: naitad evam. svāmitvam anena vacanena vidhīyate, evaṃkāmāḥ satram āsīrann iti vidhīyate, nārtvijyam. atha ye yajamānās ta ṛtvija ity anena vacanena vihitam ārtvijyam iti. ucyate, tad api na. katham. nātraiṣā vacanavyaktiḥ. ye yajamānā ity uddeśapadam{*6/297*}, ṛtvija iti vidheyapadam. tathā hi sati, ārtvijyam aṅgaṃ yajamānasaṃskārakaṃ vidhīyeta, na yajamānā ārtvijyasyāṅgam. tatra prākṛtārthatā naiṣām ārtvijyānāṃ syāt, saṃskāraś cādṛṣṭaḥ kalpyeta. sa ca yajamānaviṣaya iti, punar adṛṣṭam. tasmān na yajamānānāṃ satām ārtvijyāḥ padārthā vidhīyante. kiṃ tarhi. ārtvijānāṃ padārthānām ananyakartṛkatā. eṣā ca vacanavyaktiḥ, ṛtvija ity uddeśapadam. ta iti vidhīyate, ye yajamānās ta evartvijo bhavanti, nānya iti, ārtvijeṣu padārtheṣu yajamānāḥ kartāro vidhīyante, pratyāmnānāt. anye nivartante. evaṃ sati prākṛtaprayojanā evārtvijāh padārthāḥ. na yajamānasaṃskāro 'dṛṣṭo vidhīyata iti. yajamānakartṛkalpanāyām apy eṣām adṛṣṭam iti yadi kalpyeta. tatra brūmaḥ, itarasminn api pakṣe yajamānaviṣayaḥ so 'dṛṣṭaḥ saṃskāra iti [735]{*6/298*} avaśyaṃ kalpanīyam. yaś cobhayoḥ pakṣayor doṣo na tam ekaś codyo bhavati.
children.translated_text: This is not so. Ownership is [what is] enjoined by this statement — 'those having such desires should sit for the <s>satra</s>' is what is enjoined, not priestly function. [The objector says:] but priestly function is enjoined by this statement: 'those who are sacrificers, they [are] the priests.' [We] reply: that too is not [so]. How? This is not the construction (<s>vacanavyakti</s>) of the sentence [in that way]. 'Those who are sacrificers' is the referent term (<s>uddeśapada</s>); 'priests' is the term to be predicated (<s>vidheyapada</s>). If it were so [i.e., enjoining priestly function], then priestly function would be enjoined as a subsidiary that refines the sacrificer — [but] the sacrificers are not a subsidiary of the priestly function. In that case, these priestly functions would not have the purpose of the archetype, and an unseen refinement would have to be postulated. And [to say] that it pertains to the sacrificer — [that is] yet another unseen [postulation]. Therefore, for those who are [already] sacrificers, the items of priestly function are not being enjoined. What then? [It is] the non-other-agency of the items of priestly function. And this is the sentence-construction: 'priests' is the referent term; 'those' (<s>ta</s>) is what is being predicated — 'those who are sacrificers, they alone are the priests, not others' — in the items of priestly function, the sacrificers are enjoined as the agents, because of the counter-statement (<s>pratyāmnāna</s>). Others are excluded. This being so, the items of priestly function serve the purpose of the archetype alone. No unseen refinement of the sacrificer is being enjoined. Even in the assumption of sacrificer-agency, if an unseen [purpose] for these is postulated — to that we say: in the other view too, that unseen [purpose] pertaining to the sacrificer [735] must necessarily be postulated. And a fault that belongs to both views cannot be raised against one [alone].

children.text: gārhapate{*6/299*} vā syātām avipratiṣedhāt // MS_6,6.21 //
children.translated_text: Or they would [function] in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire duties], because of no contradiction. // MS_6,6.21 //

children.text: gārhapate{*6/300*} padārthe rājanyavaiśyau bhaviṣyataḥ, na ca, tatrārtvijaprayojanam. tasmād avipratiṣedhas teṣām iti.
children.translated_text: The <s>Rājanya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> would [function] in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] duties — and there, there is no purpose of priestly function. Therefore there is no contradiction for them.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/299: E2 (v.l.): gārhapatye}*
*{6/300: E2 (v.l.): gārhapatye}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/299: E2 (variant reading): <s>gārhapatye</s>}]
[{6/300: E2 (variant reading): <s>gārhapatye</s>}]

children.text: na vā kalpavirodhāt // MS_6,6.22 //
children.translated_text: Or not, because of conflict with the rules (<s>kalpa</s>). // MS_6,6.22 //

children.text: na caitad asti, gārhapate vā padārthe rājanyavaiśyāv iti. kalpavirodho hi syāt, yajamānacamasaḥ somamaya ekeṣām, phalamayacamasa{*6/301*} ekeṣām. tathā, brahmasāma bārhadgiraṃ brāhmaṇānām, pārthuraśmaṃ rājanyānām, rāyovājīyaṃ vaiśyānām. tasmād gārhapate niveśa ity etad api nāsti.
children.translated_text: And this is not [the case] — that the <s>Rājanya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> [would function] in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> duties. For there would be a conflict with the rules — the sacrificer's cup (<s>yajamānacamasa</s>) is made of <s>Soma</s> according to some, and a fruit-wood cup according to others. Likewise, the <s>Brahma-sāman</s> is the <s>Bārhadgira</s> for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Pārthuraśma</s> for <s>Rājanyas</s>, and the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> for <s>Vaiśyas</s>. Therefore the placement in <s>Gārhapatya</s> [duties] — this too does not hold.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/301: E1,6; E2: phalacamasamaya}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/301: E1,6; E2: <s>phalacamasamaya</s>}]

children.text: svāmitvād itareṣām ahīne liṅgadarśanam // MS_6,6.23 //
children.translated_text: Because of the ownership of the others [i.e., priests], in the <s>Ahīna</s> [rite there is] the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_6,6.23 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, liṅgadarśanād iti. tat parihartavyam. atrocyate, ahīnam eva satraśabdena vakṣyati, yataḥ svāmitvam ṛtvijāṃ vidhīyate. ata ṛtvijāṃ svāmitvād rājanyavaiśyānāṃ satraṃ nāvakalpata iti. tasmād ahīne liṅgadarśanam.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'because of the observation of an indicatory mark' — that must be addressed. To this we say: the word '<s>satra</s>' will refer to the <s>Ahīna</s> [rite] alone, since therein ownership of the priests is being enjoined. Therefore, because of the priests' ownership, the <s>satra</s> is not available to <s>Rājanyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s>. Therefore in the <s>Ahīna</s> is the observation of the indicatory mark.

children.text: vāsiṣṭhānāṃ vā brahmatvaniyamāt // MS_6,6.24 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of the restriction of the <s>Brahman</s>-[priesthood] to <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>. // MS_6,6.24 //

children.text:
etat samadhigataṃ brāhmaṇānām eva satram, na rājanyavaiśyānām [736]{*6/302*} iti. athedānīm idaṃ saṃdigdham, kiṃ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇānām, uta vāsiṣṭhānāṃ sa, uta bhṛguśunakavasiṣṭhān varjayitvānyeṣām iti. kiṃ prāptam. sarveṣām aviśeṣāt. na hi kaścid viśeṣa āśrīyate 'mīṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ satram amīṣāṃ neti. tasmāt sarveṣām iti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, vāsiṣṭhānāṃ brahmatvasya niyamāt, vāsiṣṭhānāṃ satraṃ syāt, nānyeṣām. kutaḥ. brahmatvasya niyamo bhavati, vāsiṣṭho brahmā bhavatīti, ato vāsiṣṭhānām, tat samānakalpānāṃ ca satraṃ syād iti.
children.translated_text:
This has been ascertained: the <s>satra</s> belongs to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> alone, not to <s>Rājanyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> [736]. Now this is in doubt: [does it belong] to all <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, or to <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s> [alone], or to [all] others excluding <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Śunaka</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>? What is the prima facie view? To all, because of no distinction. For no distinction is relied upon [such as] 'the <s>satra</s> belongs to these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, not to those.' Therefore to all.
Given this prima facie view, we say: because of the restriction of the <s>Brahman</s>-[priesthood] to <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, the <s>satra</s> should belong to <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, not to others. Why? Because there is a restriction of the <s>Brahman</s>-[priesthood]: 'A <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> should be the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].' Therefore [it belongs] to <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, and to those of the same custom (<s>samānakalpa</s>) as them.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vā pratiprasavāt // MS_6,6.25 //
children.translated_text: Or [it belongs] to all, because of the counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>). // MS_6,6.25 //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vā satraṃ syāt, aviśeṣāt. nanu vāsiṣṭho brahmety ucyate. nety āha. punaḥ pratisūyate, ya eva kaścana stomabhāgam adhīyīta sa eva brahmā bhaved iti. vāsiṣṭhopadeśa idānīṃ kim artha iti cet. stomabhāgapraśaṃsārthaḥ, stomabhāgān adhīyāno 'vāsiṣṭho 'pi vāsiṣṭhakāryaṃ samarthaḥ kartum iti.
children.translated_text: Or the <s>satra</s> should belong to all, because of no distinction. [The objector says:] but is it not stated 'a <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> [should be] the <s>Brahman</s>'? No, he says — there is a counter-exception: 'whoever has studied the <s>Stomabhāga</s> [hymns], he alone should be the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].' [If one asks:] what then is the purpose of the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> instruction? [It is] for the purpose of praising the <s>Stomabhāga</s> [hymns] — even a non-<s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, by studying the <s>Stomabhāga</s> [hymns], is capable of performing the function of a <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: viśvāmitrasya hautraniyamād bhṛguśunakavasiṣṭhānām anadhikāraḥ // MS_6,6.26 //
children.translated_text: Because of the restriction of the <s>Hotṛ</s>-[priesthood] to <s>Viśvāmitras</s>, the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, <s>Śunakas</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭhas</s> have no qualification. // MS_6,6.26 //

children.text: bhṛgvādīnām anadhikāraḥ syāt. kutaḥ. vaiśvāmitrasya hautraṃ niyamyate, viśvāmitro hotā bhavatīti. tasmād vaiśvāmitrāṇām, taiś ca samānakalpānām adhikāra iti.
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhṛgus</s> and others would have no qualification. Why? Because the <s>Hotṛ</s>-[priesthood] is restricted to <s>Vaiśvāmitras</s> — 'A <s>Viśvāmitra</s> should be the <s>Hotṛ</s> [priest].' Therefore the qualification belongs to <s>Vaiśvāmitras</s> and those of the same custom as them.

children.text: vihārasya prabhutvād anagnīnām api syāt // MS_6,6.27 //
children.translated_text: Because of the sufficiency of the [common] enclosure (<s>vihāra</s>), even those without [their own] fires should be eligible. // MS_6,6.27 //

children.text: satrāṇy evodāharaṇam, ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ satram āsate, ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ satram upayantīti. teṣu saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ sāgnīnām angnīnāṃ ca tāni bhavanti, uta sāgnīnām eveti. kiṃ prāptam. sāgnīnām anagnīnāṃ ca. kutaḥ. vihārasya prabhutvāt. prabhavati hi parakīyo 'pi vihāraḥ sarveṣām upakartum. kartavyo{*6/304*} hi tena sidhyatīti, sa yadīyena tadīyena vā siddhim upaiti. tasmād anagnīnām api bhavitum arhatīti.
children.translated_text: <s>Sattras</s> are the illustration — 'Those who are learned thus sit for a <s>satra</s>; those who are learned thus undertake a <s>satra</s>.' Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: do those [sattras] apply to both those who maintain fires (<s>sāgni</s>) and those without fires (<s>anagni</s>), or only to those who maintain fires? What is the prima facie view? To both those with and without fires. Why? Because of the sufficiency of the enclosure — for even another's enclosure is capable of serving all. For what is to be done is accomplished through it — and it achieves accomplishment whether it belongs to this one or that one. Therefore those without fires too should be eligible.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/304: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: kratvartho}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/304: E1,6, E2 (variant reading); E2: <s>kratvartho</s>}]

children.text: sārasvate ca darśanāt // MS_6,6.28 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation in the <s>Sārasvata</s> [satra]. // MS_6,6.28 //

children.text: sārasvate ca satre bhavati darśanam. pararathair vā ete svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti, ye 'nāhitāgnayaḥ satram āsata iti. anāhitāgnīnāṃ satraṃ darśayati. tasmād api sarveṣām.
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Sārasvata satra</s> there is an observation: 'By others' chariots they go to the heavenly world — those who, without having established the [sacred] fires, sit for a <s>satra</s>.' It shows [that] those without established fires [perform] a <s>satra</s>. Therefore [the satra belongs] to all.

children.text: prāyaścittavidhānāc ca // MS_6,6.29 //
children.translated_text: And because of the injunction of an expiation. // MS_6,6.29 //

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate, agnaye vivicaye 'ṣṭākapālaṃ puroḍāśaṃ nirvapet, yasyāhitāgner anyair agnibhir agnayaḥ saṃsṛjyerann iti, saṃsarge 'gnīnāṃ prāyaścittaṃ darśayati. sa evaṃ syād anāhitaiḥ, nānyathā. tasmād apy anagnīnāṃ satrāṇīti.
children.translated_text: An expiation is enjoined: 'One should offer an eight-potsherd cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) to <s>Agni Vivici</s>, for one whose fires — [the fires of one] who has not established [his own fires] — become mingled with other fires.' It shows an expiation for the mingling of fires. That could be [the case] only with those who have not established [their own fires], not otherwise. Therefore, from this too, <s>sattras</s> [belong] to those without [their own] fires.

children.text: sāgnīnāṃ veṣṭipūrvatvāt // MS_6,6.30 //
children.translated_text: Or [only] for those with fires, because of [the satra] being preceded by an <s>iṣṭi</s>. // MS_6,6.30 //

children.text: sāgnīnāṃ vā satrāṇi, nānagnīnām. kasmāt. iṣṭipūrvatvāt, iṣṭipūrvatvaṃ somānām āmnātam, darśapūrṇamāsāv iṣṭvā somena yajeteti jyotiṣṭomasyeṣṭipūrvatvam. tac co[738]{*6/305*}dakaparamparayā satrāṇi prati prāptam. tasmād anagnīnāṃ tāni bhaveyur iti.
children.translated_text: Or <s>sattras</s> [belong] to those with fires, not to those without fires. Why? Because of being preceded by an <s>iṣṭi</s> — the precedence of an <s>iṣṭi</s> for <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices] is recorded: 'Having performed the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites], one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>' — [thus] the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is preceded by an <s>iṣṭi</s>. And by a chain of injunctive [statements], this extends to <s>sattras</s> [738]. Therefore those without fires should not have those [sattras].

children.text: svārthena ca prayuktatvāt // MS_6,6.31 //
children.translated_text: And because of being employed for one's own purpose. // MS_6,6.31 //

children.text: svārthena cāgnayaḥ prayuktāḥ. katham. upagrahaviśeṣāt, upagrahaviśeṣo hi bhavati, agnīn ādadhīteti. tasmād anyasyāgnibhir anyasya na siddhiḥ, yady api kratvarthā agnaya iti.
children.translated_text: And the fires are employed for one's own purpose. How? Because of the specific manner of taking them up (<s>upagraha</s>) — for there is a specific manner of taking up: 'one should establish the fires.' Therefore, by another's fires, another does not achieve accomplishment — even though the fires serve the purpose of the ritual.

children.text: saṃnivāpaṃ ca darśayati // MS_6,6.32 //
children.translated_text: And [the Veda] shows the <s>saṃnivāpa</s> (combining of fires). // MS_6,6.32 //

children.text: sāvitrāṇi hoṣyantaḥ saṃnivaperann iti, tenāpi sāgnayaḥ satrāṇy upāsata iti gamyate. evaṃ liṅgaparihārāv aśiṣṭe 'dhikaraṇe 'nyac cintyate.
children.translated_text: 'Those about to offer the <s>Sāvitra</s> [offerings] should combine [their fires]' — from this too it is understood that those with fires sit for <s>sattras</s>. Thus, [with both] the indicatory mark and [its] rebuttal [being] undecided, in this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) something else is considered.

children.text: juhvādīnām aprayuktatvāt saṃdehe yathākāmī pratīyeta // MS_6,6.33 //
children.translated_text: Because the <s>juhū</s> and other [ladles] are not [specifically] employed [for any one sacrificer], when there is doubt, one may [decide] as one wishes. // MS_6,6.33 //

children.text: kiṃ juhvādīni pātrāṇi kasyacid eva yajamānasya, upādāya prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ, utānyāni sādhāraṇāni kartavyāni. kiṃ{*6/306*} prāptam. yasya{*6/307*} kasyacid eva yajamānasyopādāya prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ. kutaḥ. na hi svaṃ pātraṃ yajamānaḥ prayuṅkte. svena pātreṇa prayogaḥ kartavya iti. tasmāt parakīyapātrair anye yajerann iti.
children.translated_text: Should the <s>juhū</s> and other ritual vessels belong to just one particular sacrificer, [so that] the performance is carried out by borrowing them, or should other common [vessels] be made? What is the prima facie view? The performance should be carried out by borrowing [the vessels] of some particular sacrificer. Why? For the sacrificer does not employ his own vessel — [rather,] the performance should be carried out with one's own vessel. Therefore the others should sacrifice with borrowed vessels.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/306: E1,6; E2: kartavyānīti. asmin saṃśaye, ucyate. kiṃ}*
*{6/307: E1,6; E2: prāptam juhvādiṣu yathākāmī bhavet. yasya}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/306: E1,6; E2: <s>kartavyānīti. asmin saṃśaye, ucyate. kiṃ</s>}]
[{6/307: E1,6; E2: <s>prāptam juhvādiṣu yathākāmī bhavet. yasya</s>}]

children.text: api vānyāni pātrāṇi sādhāraṇāni kurvīran vipratiṣedhāc chāstrakṛtatvāt // MS_6,6.34 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, other common vessels should be made, because of [avoiding] contradiction, [and] because of [the vessels'] being made by scriptural [injunction]. // MS_6,6.34 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. naitad evam, anyāni hi pātrāṇi sādhāraṇāni kartavyāni. kasmāt. vipratiṣedhāt, vipratiṣedho bhavati{*6/308*}. kadācit tāni pātrāṇy upāttāni bhaveyuḥ. atha maraṇaṃ kasyacid yajamānasyāpadyeta, tatra vipratiṣedhaḥ syāt, āhitāgnim agnibhir dahanti yajñapātraiś ceti, yadi taṃ tair daheyuḥ, itareṣāṃ yajño virudhyeta. atha tair yajñaṃ samāpayeyur{*6/309*} itarasya śarīrasaṃskārāḥ parilupyeran{*6/310*}, anyeṣu punaḥ sādhāraṇeṣūpādīyamāneṣu na kiṃcid api virudhyeta. tasmāt tathā kāryam{*6/311*} iti.
children.translated_text: The words '<s>api vā</s>' reverse the position. This is not so — rather, other common vessels should be made. Why? Because of contradiction — for a contradiction arises: at some point those vessels may [already] be in use. And if some sacrificer should die, there would be a contradiction — 'one who has established the fires is cremated with [his] fires and sacrificial vessels.' If they were to cremate him with those [vessels], the sacrifice of the others would be obstructed. But if they were to complete the sacrifice with those [vessels], the bodily rites of the other [deceased] would be lost. When other common [vessels] are procured, however, nothing at all is contradicted. Therefore it should be done thus.

children.text: prāyaścittam āpadi syāt // MS_6,6.35 //
children.translated_text: The expiation [applies] in [the case of] a calamity. // MS_6,6.35 //

children.text: athedānīṃ pūrvoktasya liṅgasya parihāra ucyate. prāyaścittam asmatpakṣe parikalpiṣyate. katham. araṇye kāntāre gacchatāṃ sthitānāṃ vā dasyubhayāt śvāpadabhayād vā trāse jāte dāvāgninā vā saṃsṛjyeran, mitho vā sa viṣayaḥ prāyaścittasya bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: Now the rebuttal of the previously stated indicatory mark is stated. The expiation in our view will be explained. How? When those traveling or staying in a forest or wilderness — because of fear of bandits or fear of wild animals — [experience] fright, or [their fires] become mingled by a forest fire — that is the domain of the expiation.

children.text: puruṣakalpena vā vikṛtau kartṛniyamaḥ syād yajñasya tadguṇatvād abhāvād itarān pratyekasminn adhikāraḥ syāt // MS_6,6.36 //
children.translated_text: Or, by the principle of [substituting] a person, in a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) there should be a restriction of the agent; because the sacrifice has the quality of that [archetype]; because of the absence [of that quality] with respect to the others, each one would have [separate] qualification. // MS_6,6.36 //

children.text: adharakalpā{*6/313*} udāharaṇam, āgrayaṇeṣṭiḥ paśur ityevaṃlakṣaṇakāni karmāṇi, yeṣu saptadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ, teṣu saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ trayāṇām api varṇānām ebhiḥ karmabhir adhikāraḥ, uta vaiśyasyaiveti. kiṃ prāptam. etasyāṃ vikṛtau puruṣakalpena kartā niyamyeta. kutaḥ. yajño{*6/314*} 'yam adhvarakalpādiḥ, etat saṃkhyāguṇakaḥ. iyaṃ ca saṃkhyā vaiśyasyoktā, tena{*6/315*} vaiśya eva etat karma kṛtsnaṃ kartuṃ samarthaḥ. saptadaśaguṇakam etat karma, tac ca sāptadaśyam avaiśyena kriyamāṇam asādhu. itarān prati hi tan na codyate. tena yajetety asāmarthyād brāhmaṇakṣatriyān nādhikariṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: The lower customs are the illustration — rituals characterized as the <s>Āgrayaṇeṣṭi</s> (first-fruits offering), the animal [sacrifice], and the like, in which there are seventeen <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses. Regarding these, a doubt [arises]: is there eligibility for all three <s>varṇas</s> (classes) for these rituals, or only for the <s>Vaiśya</s>? What is the prima facie view? In this modification, the agent would be restricted by the person-custom. Why? This sacrifice belongs to the <s>adhvara</s>-custom type and has this number as its quality. And this number is stated for the <s>Vaiśya</s>; therefore only the <s>Vaiśya</s> is capable of performing this entire ritual. This ritual has the quality of seventeen, and that group-of-seventeen, when performed by a non-<s>Vaiśya</s>, is improper. For with respect to the others [i.e., Brāhmaṇa and Kṣatriya], that is not enjoined. Therefore, because of incapacity [to fulfill] 'one should sacrifice,' it will not make <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s> eligible.

children.text: liṅgāc cejyāviśeṣavat // MS_6,6.37 //
children.translated_text: And because of the indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>), like the specific sacrifice [restricted to a Vaiśya]. // MS_6,6.37 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca bhavati, yathā vaiśyasya sāptadaśyam iti, saptadaśo vaiśya{*6/316*} iti. tena vaiśyasya{*6/317*} sāptadaśyam. ato vaiśyasyaivaṃjātīyakāni karmāṇi, yathejyāviśeṣo vaiśyasya bhavati, vaiśyo vaiśyastomena yajeteti, vaiśyasaṃbandhāt. evaṃ sāptadaśyaṃ tasyaiveti.
children.translated_text: And there is an indicatory sign — as in 'the group-of-seventeen belongs to the <s>Vaiśya</s>,' [and] 'the <s>Vaiśya</s> is [characterized by] seventeen.' Therefore the group-of-seventeen belongs to the <s>Vaiśya</s>. Hence rituals of this kind belong to the <s>Vaiśya</s>, just as the specific sacrifice (<s>ijyāviśeṣa</s>) belongs to the <s>Vaiśya</s> — '<s>Vaiśya</s> should sacrifice with the <s>Vaiśyastoma</s>' — because of the connection with the <s>Vaiśya</s>. Similarly, the group-of-seventeen belongs to him alone.

children.text: na vā saṃyogapṛthaktvād guṇasyejyāpradhānatvād asaṃyuktā hi codanā // MS_6,6.38 //
children.translated_text: Or not, because of the separateness of the conjunction; because the quality is subsidiary to the sacrifice; for the injunction is unconjoined [with a specific person]. // MS_6,6.38 //

children.text: na caitad asti. pṛthag etau saṃyogau, ekaṃ vākyaṃ saptadaśa vaiśyasya [741]{*6/318*} anubrūyād iti. vākyāntaram adhvarakalpādiṣu saptadaśānubrūyād iti, sa ca guṇa ijyāpradhāno bhavati, nejyā guṇārthā. kim ataḥ. yady evaṃ yatrejyā, tatra tadguṇena bhavitavyam. na yatra guṇaḥ, tatrejyayā, vaiśyasya guṇānurodhenejyāpi. trayāṇāṃ varṇānām ijyā. sā tatra guṇam ākāṅkṣatīti{*6/319*}. api cejyāguṇabhūtasyāparā codanā{*6/320*}, na sā vaiśyasaṃyuktā. sā tv avaiśyakaṃ guṇaṃ pratyāyayati. prathamaṃ savaiśyakam iti cet. na, vaiśyasya pradhānatvāt. pradhānabhūtas tatra vaiśyaḥ śrūyate. tasmāt sarvādhikāraḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so. These conjunctions are separate — one sentence [says] 'one should recite seventeen for the <s>Vaiśya</s>.' [741] Another sentence [says] 'one should recite seventeen in the <s>adhvara</s>-custom [rites].' And that quality is subsidiary to the sacrifice, not [that] the sacrifice is for the purpose of the quality. What follows from this? If so, wherever there is a sacrifice, there the quality [of seventeen] should be present. Not [that] wherever the quality is, there the sacrifice [must occur only for the Vaiśya]. [In this view,] the sacrifice of the <s>Vaiśya</s> [has the quality of seventeen] in conformity with the quality; [but] the sacrifice of all three <s>varṇas</s> [also has it]. That [sacrifice] requires the quality there. Moreover, there is another injunction of the quality as subsidiary to the sacrifice, and that [injunction] is not conjoined with the <s>Vaiśya</s>. But that establishes the quality for the non-<s>Vaiśya</s> [as well]. [The objector says:] the first [statement] is with the <s>Vaiśya</s>. No — because in that [first statement] the <s>Vaiśya</s> is primary. The <s>Vaiśya</s> is heard there as primary. Therefore [there is] eligibility for all.

children.text: ijyāyāṃ tadguṇatvād viśeṣeṇa niyamyeta // MS_6,6.39 //
children.translated_text: In the sacrifice, because of being a quality of that [sacrifice], it would be restricted by [connection with] the specific [person]. // MS_6,6.39 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, vaiśyastome yathā, tathehāpīti. yuktaṃ tatra, ijyā vaiśyasya śrūyate. tatra vācanikenaiva viśeṣeṇa niyamyeta. tasmāt tatrādoṣa iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'just as in the <s>Vaiśyastoma</s>, so here too' — that is appropriate there [because] the sacrifice is heard [as belonging to] the <s>Vaiśya</s>. There it would be restricted by the specific [person] stated in the [Vedic] word itself. Therefore there is no fault in that [case].

children.text: svadāne sarvam aviśeṣāt // MS_6,7.1 //
children.translated_text: In giving of one's own, [one should give] everything, because of non-distinction. // MS_6,7.1 //

children.text: idam āmananti viśvajiti, sarvasvaṃ dadātīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ yāvat kiṃcit svaśabdenocyate, yathā mātā pitetyevamādy api sarvaṃ{*6/322*} deyam, uta yatra prabhutvayogena svaśabdas tad eva deyam iti. kiṃ prāptam. aviśeṣāt, mātā pitetyevamādy api dātavyam. nanu dānam ity ucyate svatvanivṛttiḥ, parasvatvāpādanaṃ ca. tatra pitrādīnām aśakyaṃ svatvaṃ nivartayitum. na hi kathaṃcit pitā na pitā bhavati. ucyate, satyaṃ nāsau na pitā bhavati. śakyate tu paravidheyaḥ kartum, parasvatvāpādanaṃ ca dānam. arthāc{*6/323*} ca svatvatyāgaḥ. tasmāt sarvaṃ deyam iti.
children.translated_text: This is recorded in the <s>Viśvajit</s>: 'He gives all his wealth.' There a doubt [arises]: whatever is denoted by the word 'one's own' (<s>sva</s>) — [including] mother, father, and such — should all that be given, or [only] that where the word 'one's own' applies through ownership? What is the prima facie view? Because of non-distinction, even mother, father, and such should be given. [The objector says:] but 'giving' means the cessation of one's own ownership and the production of another's ownership. There, the ownership of father and such cannot be terminated. For in no way does a father become not-a-father. [We] reply: true, he does not become not-a-father. But he can be made subject to another's control; and the production of another's ownership is giving. And the relinquishment of one's own ownership [follows] by implication. Therefore everything should be given.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/322: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: api tat sarvaṃ}*
*{6/323: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: dānaṃ dadāter arthaḥ. arthāc}*

NOTES:
