[{6/323: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: <s>dānaṃ dadāter arthaḥ. arthāc</s>}]

children.text: yasya vā prabhuḥ syād itarasyāśakyatvāt // MS_6,7.2 //
children.translated_text: Or, [one should give only] that over which one is master, because of the impossibility of the other. // MS_6,7.2 //

children.text:
vāśabdena pakṣo viparivartate. yasya prabhutvayogena svatvam, tad eva deyaṃ netarat. kasmāt. prabhutvayoginaḥ śakyatvāt, itarasya cāśakyatvāt. na hi pitrādīnāṃ śakyate svatvaṃ parityaktum.
nanu coktaṃ paravidheyīkaraṇaṃ tasya śakyam iti. ucyate, prabhutvayoginaḥ svasyātra dīyamānasya sarvatvam ucyate. nāprabhutvayoginaḥ svasya dānam, na caitan nyāyyam, yat pitrādīnāṃ paricārakatvam. yasya caitan nyāyyam api bhavet, sa dadyād api. [743]{*6/324*} atrāha, nanu yatra svaśabdo vartate, tad deyam ity ukte pitrādayo dātavyā gamyante. tasmāt tān prati prabhutvāya smṛtiṃ bādhitvāpi yatitavyam iti.
atrocyate, svaśabdo 'yam ātmīyadhanajñātīnāṃ pratyekaṃ vācako na samudāyasya. tatrātmīye sarvatāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ kṛte śāstrārthe, nāśakyeṣu jñātiṣu{*6/325*} sarvatā kalpanīyā, nāpi smṛtir bādhitavyā. api ca gavādīnām ātmīyānāṃ codakena prāptau satyām avaśyam ātmīyagatā sarvatopadeyā. tasyāṃ copāttāyāṃ kṛtaḥ śāstārtha iti jñātīnām upādāne na kiṃcit kāraṇam asti, tasmān na pitrādayo{*6/326*} deyāḥ. tasmād yatraiva prabhutvayogena svatvam, tad eva deyam iti.
children.translated_text:
The word '<s>vā</s>' reverses the position. Only that over which one has ownership through mastery should be given — not the other. Why? Because what is subject to mastery is possible [to give], and the other is impossible. For the ownership of father and such cannot be relinquished.
[The objector says:] but was it not said that making [them] subject to another's control is possible? [We] reply: the totality (<s>sarvatva</s>) is stated here of what is one's own through mastery-connection and is being given. There is no giving of what is one's own not through mastery-connection; nor is it proper that there be servitude of father and others. And even if someone for whom this were proper — he might give [them] too. [743] Here [the objector] says: but since whatever is covered by the word 'one's own' is to be given, father and others are understood [as] to be given. Therefore one should strive to override even <s>smṛti</s> (traditional law) for the purpose of having mastery over them.
To this we say: the word 'one's own' (<s>sva</s>) here denotes separately one's own property and relatives — not the aggregate. There, when totality has been accomplished with respect to one's own [property], the purpose of the <s>śāstra</s> has been served; totality need not be postulated with respect to relatives who cannot [be given], nor need <s>smṛti</s> be overridden. Moreover, when one's own [property] such as cows etc. is obtained by the enjoiner, the totality with respect to one's own [property] must necessarily be adopted. And when that is adopted, the purpose of the <s>śāstra</s> has been served — so there is no reason for adopting relatives. Therefore father and others should not be given. Therefore only that over which one has ownership through mastery — that alone should be given.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/324: E2: 5,340; E6: 2,198}*
*{6/325: E2 (v.l.): nāśakyajñātiṣu}*
*{6/326: E2 (v.l.): mātāpitrādayo}*
na bhūmiḥ syāt sarvān pratyaviśiṣṭatvāt // MS_6,7.3 //
children.translated_text: Land should not [be given], because of non-distinction with respect to all. // MS_6,7.3 //

children.text:
atraiva sarvadāne saṃśayaḥ, kiṃ bhūmir deyā, neti. kā punar bhūmir atrābhipretā. yad etan mṛdārabdhaṃ dravyānatraṃ pṛthivīgolakam, na{*6/327*} kṣetramātraṃ mṛttikā vā. tatra kiṃ prāptam. aviśeṣād deyā. prabhutvasaṃbandhena hi tatra svaśabdo vartate, śakyate ca mānasena vyāpāreṇa svasya svatā{*6/328*} nivartayitum iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, na bhūmir deyeti. kutaḥ. kṣetrāṇām īśitāro manuṣyā dṛśyante, na kṛtsnasya pṛthivīgolakasyeti.
āha, ya idānīṃ sārvabhaumaḥ, sa tarhi dāsyati. so 'pi neti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ. yāvatā bhogena{*6/329*} sārvabhaumo bhūmer īṣṭe, tāvatānyo 'pi. na tatra kaścid viśeṣaḥ, sārvabhaumatve 'sya{*6/330*} tv etad adhikam, yad asau pṛthivyāṃ saṃbhūtānāṃ vrīhyādīnāṃ rakṣaṇena [744]{*6/331*} nirviṣṭasya kasyacid bhāgasyeṣṭe, na bhūmeḥ. tannirviṣṭāś ca ye manuṣyāḥ, tair anyat sarvaprāṇināṃ dhāraṇavikramaṇādi{*6/332*} yad bhūmikṛtam, tatreśitvaṃ prati na kaścid viśeṣaḥ. tasmān na bhūmir deyā.
children.translated_text:
In this very 'giving of all,' a doubt [arises]: should land be given, or not? Now, what land is meant here? This material substance — the globe of earth commenced from soil — not merely a field or soil. There, what is the prima facie view? Because of non-distinction, it should be given. For the word 'one's own' applies there through the connection of mastery, and it is possible to terminate one's ownership through a mental act. Given this prima facie view, we say: land should not be given. Why? Men are seen as masters of fields, not of the entire globe of earth.
[The objector] says: then one who is now a universal sovereign — he would give. To him too we say: no. Why? To whatever extent a universal sovereign rules the earth by [his degree of] enjoyment, to that same extent another [person] also [rules]. There is no distinction there. His universal sovereignty has this additional [feature]: that he rules over a portion — yielded by the protection of rice and such produced on the earth — [but] not over the earth [itself]. And those men who yield [that portion] — with respect to the other [uses] that the earth performs for all living beings, such as support and walking-ground — regarding mastery over those, there is no distinction [between anyone]. Therefore land should not be given.

children.text: akāryatvāc ca tataḥ punar viśeṣaḥ syāt // MS_6,7.4 //
children.translated_text: And because of [its] non-transferability, there should be a further distinction from that. // MS_6,7.4 //

children.text: viśvajity eva saṃdehaḥ. kim aśvādayo deyāḥ, neti. kiṃ prāptam. sarvasya vihitatvāt, deyā aśvā iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, yasya ca dānam akāryam, tac ca na deyam, yathāśvānām. teṣāṃ hi dānam akāryam. eṣa hi viśeṣo 'śvānām, anyebhyo dravyebhyaḥ, yad eṣāṃ dānaṃ pratiṣidhyate, na kesariṇo dadāti nobhayatodataḥ pratigṛhṇātīti viśvajity eva samāmnāyate. tasmān nāśvā deyā iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Viśvajit</s> itself [there is] a doubt: should horses and such be given, or not? What is the prima facie view? Because everything is enjoined [to be given], horses should be given. Given this prima facie view, we say: that whose giving is improper — that should not be given, such as horses. For the giving of those is improper. For this is the distinction of horses from other substances — that their giving is prohibited: 'one does not give a maned [animal]; one does not accept a [beast] with teeth on both sides' — this is recorded in the <s>Viśvajit</s> itself. Therefore horses should not be given.

children.text: nityatvāc cānityair nāsti saṃbandhaḥ // MS_6,7.5 //
children.translated_text: And because of permanence, there is no connection with non-permanent [things]. // MS_6,7.5 //

children.text:
viśvajity eva saṃdehaḥ sarvasvaṃ dadātīti, kim arjayitvopakaraṇāni yāvanti manuṣyasya, yāvanti ca śaknoty upārjayitum, sarvāṇi tāni dadyāt kṛtabhāṇḍādīni{*6/333*}, uta yāny evāsya vidyante, tāni sarvāṇi deyāni, nāvidyamānāni kartavyānīti. kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ. ubhayathā vacanavyakteḥ saṃbhavāt, [745]{*6/334*} yadi vaivaṃ vacanaṃ vyajyate, yāni sarvāṇi svāni, kāni tāni, yāni puruṣasyopakārakāṇi śayanādīni, tāni sarvāṇi dadyād iti vidhīyate. yad vā yāni svāni puruṣasya dāne śakyāni, tāni sarvāṇīti sarvatvaṃ vidhīyate. yadi dānaṃ vidhīyate, tato 'prāptadānānāṃ kṛtabhāṇḍakānām api dānam. atha sarvatā{*6/335*} vidhīyate, tato vidyamānānām eva.
kiṃ tāvat prāptam. kṛtabhāṇḍakāni deyānīti, tathā dānavidhāne śrutir anugṛhyate, itarathā vākyam. tayoś ca śrutir balīyasī. tasmāt kṛtabhāṇḍakāni deyānīti.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, nityatvāc cānityair nāsti saṃbandhaḥ, caśabdo 'nvādeśe. nāśvā dātavyā ity uktam, kṛtabhāṇḍakāni ca na deyānīti. nityaṃ hi viśvajiti dānaṃ codakena prāptam anūdyate. anityāni ca kṛtabhāṇḍakāni{*6/336*}, na śakyāni sarvāṇi viśvajiti kriyamāṇa upasaṃhartum. tatra kṛtabhāṇḍakānāṃ syāt, na{*6/337*} nityam, nityavac ca tac codakena vidhīyate, na nimittasaṃyogena. tasmād avaśyam etad abhyupagantavyam, sākalpyaṃ deyānāṃ prāptānāṃ vidhīyata iti, śrutyasaṃbhave ca vākyārtho gṛhītavya eva bhavati, tasmān na kṛtabhāṇḍakāni dātavyāni.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Viśvajit</s> itself [there is] a doubt — 'he gives all his wealth': should one, having produced equipment — as many [things] as a person [possesses] and as many as he is able to produce — give all those manufactured goods etc., or should one give only whatever [already] exists [in one's possession], without having to produce things that don't exist? What is the source of the doubt? Because the statement can be construed either way. [745] If the statement is construed thus — 'whatever are all one's possessions, whichever those are, whichever are useful to a person such as beds etc. — one should give all of those' — [this] is prescribed. Or [if construed as] — 'whatever possessions a person is able to give — all of those' — then totality is prescribed. If giving is prescribed, then even manufactured goods not previously destined for giving [must be given]. If totality is prescribed, then [it applies] only to existing [possessions].
What is the prima facie view? Manufactured goods should be given — for in that [view where] giving is prescribed, <s>śruti</s> (direct hearing) is upheld; otherwise it would be [merely] a sentence [inference]. And of these two, <s>śruti</s> is stronger. Therefore manufactured goods should be given.
Given this prima facie view, we say: because of permanence, there is no connection with non-permanent [things] — the word '<s>ca</s>' indicates a continuation. Horses should not be given — that was stated; and manufactured goods should not be given [either]. For in the <s>Viśvajit</s>, the giving, being permanent [i.e., always applicable], is obtained by the enjoiner and is being restated. And manufactured goods are non-permanent — it is not possible to gather all [possible manufactured goods] in the <s>Viśvajit</s> being performed. Of manufactured goods there might be [giving], but not permanently; and that [giving] is enjoined by the enjoiner just like [something] permanent, not by connection with an occasion. Therefore this must necessarily be accepted — that the totality of things that are to be given [and already] obtained is being prescribed. And when <s>śruti</s> is not possible, the sentence-meaning must indeed be grasped. Therefore manufactured goods should not be given.

children.text: śūdraś ca dharmaśāstratvāt // MS_6,7.6 //
children.translated_text: And [one should not give] a <s>Śūdra</s> [servant], because of [the Śūdra's connection with] <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> (religious law). // MS_6,7.6 //

children.text: viśvajity eva saṃdihyate, kiṃ paricārakaḥ śūdro deyaḥ, neti. kiṃ prāptam. sarvasya svasya{*6/338*} vihitatvād deya iti. [746]{*6/339*} evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, śūdraś ca na deya ity anvādeśaḥ. kutaḥ. dharmaśāstratvāt, dharmaśāsanopanatatvāt{*6/340*} tasya. evam asau tasmai traivarṇikāyopanata idaṃ śuśrūṣamāṇo dharmeṇa saṃbhantsyata iti. so 'nyasmai dīyamāṇo necched api. na cānicchatas tasya sa prabhavati, na ca balāt svīkartavyaḥ. yas tv anyāyena svīkuryāt, sa dadyād api. dharmopanatamātreṇa tu na śakyo dātum.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Viśvajit</s> itself [there is] a doubt: should a <s>Śūdra</s> servant be given, or not? What is the prima facie view? Because everything of one's own is enjoined [to be given], [he] should be given. [746] Given this prima facie view, we say: and a <s>Śūdra</s> should not be given — this is a continuation. Why? Because of [the Śūdra's connection with] <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> — because he is obtained through the instruction of <s>dharma</s>. Thus he is obtained by that twice-born [master with the understanding]: 'serving me thus, he will be connected with <s>dharma</s>.' Being given to another, he might not even wish [to go]. And of one who does not wish, [the master] has no authority over him, nor should he be forcibly appropriated. But one who would appropriate [a Śūdra] unjustly — he might give [him] too. But merely by [the Śūdra] being obtained through <s>dharma</s>, he cannot be given.

children.text: dakṣiṇākāle yat svaṃ tat pratīyeta tad dānasaṃyogāt // MS_6,7.7 //
children.translated_text: At the time of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee), whatever is one's own property — that should be understood [as what is to be given], because of the connection with the gift. // MS_6,7.7 //

children.text: viśvajity eva saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ prāg dakṣiṇākālāt, vidyamānaṃ niyogato dakṣiṇākāle nidhātavyam{*6/341*}, ūrdhvaṃ ca dakṣiṇākālād bhaviṣyad anāgatam api dakṣiṇākāle deyam, uta yad eva dakṣiṇākāle vidyate, tad eva deyam iti. kiṃ prāptam. yasyāpi prāg ūrdhvaṃ ca svatā, tad api deyam, svamātrasya dānavidhānat. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, dakṣiṇākāle yat svaṃ vidyate, tad eva deyam, na yat prāg ūrdhvam ca. kutaḥ. svasyātra dānam anūdya sākalyaṃ vidhīyate. tac ca dānaṃ dakṣiṇākāle prāptatvāt tasminn eva kāle 'nūdyate. tasmād dakṣiṇākāla eva vidyamānaṃ deyam iti.
children.translated_text: The doubt is in the <s>Viśvajit</s> itself. Should [property] existing before the time of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> be obligatorily set aside for the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> time, and should future [property] not yet arrived after the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> time also be given at the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> time — or should only what exists at the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> time be given? What is the prima facie view? Even the property [one owns] before and after [the dakṣiṇā time] should be given, because of the injunction to give all one's property. Given this prima facie view, we say: only whatever is one's own property at the time of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be given — not what [existed] before or after. Why? Here, the giving of one's property is restated (<s>anuvāda</s>), while the totality is what is enjoined. And that giving, having been established at the time of <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, is restated at that very time. Therefore only what exists at the time of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be given.

children.text: aśeṣatvāt tadantaḥ{*6/343*} syāt karmaṇo dravyasiddhitvāt{*6/344*} // MS_6,7.8 //
children.translated_text: Because of [the giving] being without remainder, the sacrifice would end with that, since the ritual action is accomplished through material goods. // MS_6,7.8 //

children.text: tasminn eva viśvajiti saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ dakṣiṇākāla eva viśvajid{*6/345*} utsraṣṭavyaḥ, uta na sarvaṃ{*6/346*} dātavyam, parisamāpanīya iti. kiṃ prāptam. utsraṣṭavya iti. kutaḥ. aśeṣatvāt. katham aśeṣatā. viśvajiti sarvasvaṃ dadātīti, na ca śakyam antareṇa dravyam, parisamāpayitum. tasmāt tadantaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: The doubt is in that very <s>Viśvajit</s>. Should the <s>Viśvajit</s> be abandoned at the time of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> itself, or should one not give everything [at once] but complete [the sacrifice first]? What is the prima facie view? It should be abandoned. Why? Because of [the giving] being without remainder. How is there no remainder? In the <s>Viśvajit</s>, one gives all one's property — and it is not possible to complete [the sacrifice] without material goods. Therefore the sacrifice would end with that [giving].

children.text:
NOTES:

children.text: api vā śeṣakarma syāt kratoḥ pratyakṣaśiṣṭatvāt // MS_6,7.9 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, there should be a remainder for the ritual action, because [the sacrifice's completion] is directly enjoined. // MS_6,7.9 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. śeṣakarma syāt, na sarvasvaṃ dakṣiṇākāle deyam, yāvatā tatkarma parisamāpyate, tāvac cheṣayitavyam. kutaḥ. kratoḥ pratyakṣaśiṣṭatvāt. kratoḥ parisamāptiḥ pratyakṣaśiṣṭā, viśvajitā yajeteti viśvajitam upakramya, parisamāpayed ity arthaḥ. parisamāpayatā yac chakyate dātum, tāvat sarvam ity arthaḥ. tasmān na tadantam utsraṣṭavyam iti.
children.translated_text: The phrase 'or rather' (<s>api vā</s>) overturns the [previous] position. There should be a remainder for the ritual action — not all one's property should be given at the time of <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; as much [property] as is needed to complete the sacrifice, that much should be retained. Why? Because [the sacrifice's completion] is directly enjoined by the sacrifice itself. Having commenced the <s>Viśvajit</s> by 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>,' the meaning is that one should complete it. And one who is completing [the sacrifice] should give as much as can be given — that is all [that is meant]. Therefore the sacrifice should not be abandoned at that point.

children.text: tathā cānyārthadarśanam // MS_6,7.10 //
children.translated_text: And thus the observation of another purpose [is explained]. // MS_6,7.10 //

children.text: evaṃ ca kṛtvānyārthadarśanam upapadyate, avabhṛthād udetya vatsatvacamāc chādayatīti śeṣe saty avakalpate.
children.translated_text: And having done thus, the observation of another purpose is accounted for: 'After rising from the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), one covers oneself with a calf-skin' — this is fitting when there is a remainder [of the sacrifice to complete].

children.text: aśeṣaṃ tu samañjasādānena śeṣakarma syāt // MS_6,7.11 //
children.translated_text: But [if the giving is] without remainder, [then] through the consistency of [subsequent] acquisition, there should be a remainder for the ritual action. // MS_6,7.11 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. etat samañjasābhūtam, yad aśeṣaṃ [748]{*6/347*} pratīyata iti, evaṃ sarvasvaṃ dadātīit śabda upapanno bhavatīti. yat tu pratyakṣā samāptir iti. tatra brūmaḥ, ādānena śeṣakarma bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate,
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [previous] position. This is consistent — that [the giving is] understood as without remainder: [748] thus the statement 'one gives all one's property' is vindicated. But as to what was said — 'the completion [of the sacrifice] is directly [enjoined]' — to that we reply: through [subsequent] acquisition there will be a remainder for the ritual action. It is stated:

children.text: nādānasya nityatvāt // MS_6,7.12 //
children.translated_text: No, because acquisition is not permanent. // MS_6,7.12 //

children.text: ādānaṃ tv anuityam, nityaṃ ca śeṣakarma. na hi tayoḥ saṃbandho 'vakalpate. tasmāc cheṣayitavyaṃ kiṃcid iti.
children.translated_text: But acquisition is impermanent, while the remainder for the ritual action is permanent [i.e., necessary]. A connection between the two is not fitting. Therefore something should be retained [as a remainder].

children.text: dīkṣāsu tu vinirdeśād akratvarthena saṃyogas tasmād avirodhaḥ syāt // MS_6,7.13 //
children.translated_text: But because of the specification in the <s>dīkṣā</s> [texts], the connection is with what is not for the purpose of the sacrifice; therefore there would be no contradiction. // MS_6,7.13 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti, kiṃcic cheṣayitavyam iti. dīkṣāsu tu vinirdeśo bhavati, prakṛtāv eva jyotiṣṭome. sa iha codakena prāptaḥ, idaṃ kratvartham{*6/348*}, idaṃ bhakṣyārtham, idam ānamanāyeti. tad iha yad ānamanāya dātavyam, tasyāyaṃ vikāraḥ sarvatā nāma. kuta etat. yataḥ svaṃ dadātīty anūdyate, sarvataiva{*6/349*} vidhīyate. tena nādātavyasya dānaṃ vidhīyate, na ca bhakṣyārthaṃ{*6/350*} kratvarthaṃ ca dātavyam. tasmād avirodho bhaviṣyatīti.
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [previous] position. This is not so — that something should be retained [as a remainder]. But in the <s>dīkṣā</s> [texts] there is a specification, in the archetype <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself. That is established here by the injunction: 'this is for the purpose of the sacrifice, this is for the purpose of food, this is for the purpose of returning.' Here, whatever is to be given for returning — this [Viśvajit] is a modification of that [Jyotiṣṭoma], with the name 'totality.' How is this [known]? Because 'one gives one's property' is restated, and 'totality' is what is enjoined. Therefore the giving of what is not to be given is not enjoined — and what is for the purpose of food and for the purpose of the sacrifice is not to be given. Therefore there will be no contradiction.

children.text:
NOTES:

*{6/349: E2 (v.l.): sarvatā}*
*{6/350: E1,6; E2: bhakṣārthaṃ; E2 (v.l.): muktyarthaṃ}*

children.text: ahargaṇe ca taddharmā syat sarveṣām aviśeṣāt // MS_6,7.14 //
children.translated_text: And in a series of days (<s>ahargaṇa</s>), [the Viśvajit] would have the same characteristics [as the archetype], because of the absence of distinction among all [Viśvajits]. // MS_6,7.14 //

children.text: asty ahargaṇo 'ṣṭarātraḥ, athaitasyāṣṭarātrasya viśvajid abhijitāv ekāhāv abhitaḥ, ubhayato jyotir madhye ṣaḍahaḥ, paśukāmo hy etena yajeteti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kim ahargaṇasthasyāpi sarvasvam eva dakṣiṇā{*6/351*} syāt, āho{*6/352*} dvādaśaṃ śatam iti. kiṃ prāptam. sarvasvam. kutaḥ. sarveṣāṃ viśvajitām aviśeṣāt. ya eva prakṛtau viśvajito dharmaḥ, sa eva cāsya codakena bhaviṣyati. tasmāt sarvasvaṃ deyam iti.
children.translated_text: There is a series of days — the eight-day [sacrifice]. And of this eight-day [sacrifice], the <s>Viśvajit</s> and the <s>Abhijit</s> are single-day [rites] on either side; in between is a six-day [rite] flanked by <s>Jyotis</s> [chants]: 'One who desires cattle should sacrifice with this.' There a doubt [arises]: should all one's property be the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> even for one situated in a series of days, or twelve hundred? What is the prima facie view? All one's property. Why? Because of the absence of distinction among all <s>Viśvajit</s>s. Whatever is the characteristic of the <s>Viśvajit</s> in the archetype — that same [characteristic] will apply here too by the injunction. Therefore all one's property should be given.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/351: E1,6; E2: dakṣiṇāḥ}*
*{6/352: E1,6; E2: āhosvit}*
dvādaśaśataṃ vā prakṛtivat // MS_6,7.15 //
children.translated_text: Or twelve hundred [should be given], as in the archetype. // MS_6,7.15 //

children.text: dvādaśaśātaṃ vā deyam iti. prakṛtivat kartavyam. jyotiṣṭomaś ca prakṛtiḥ. tatra dharmā vihitāḥ, na viśvajiti kṛtsnāḥ pratīyante. tasmād dvādaśaśatam atra deyam iti.
children.translated_text: Or twelve hundred should be given. It should be done as in the archetype. And the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is the archetype. The rules prescribed there do not all apply in the <s>Viśvajit</s>. Therefore twelve hundred should be given here.

children.text: atadguṇatvāt tu naivaṃ syāt // MS_6,7.16 //
children.translated_text: But this should not be so, because [the ahargaṇa Viśvajit] does not have those [Jyotiṣṭoma] characteristics. // MS_6,7.16 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naivaṃ bhavitum arhati. kutaḥ. naiva{*6/353*} yato viśvajito guṇo dvādaśaśatam. nāmadheyena hy atra dharmagrahaṇam. tasmād viśvajito bhaviṣyati{*6/354*}, na jyotiṣṭomād iti.
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [previous] position. This should not be so. Why? Because twelve hundred is not a characteristic of the <s>Viśvajit</s>. For here the adoption of characteristics is through the name (<s>nāmadheya</s>). Therefore the [characteristics] will be those of the <s>Viśvajit</s>, not from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/353: E1,6; E2: naiṣa}*
*{6/354: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: grahīṣyati}*

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_6,7.17 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_6,7.17 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ khalv api darśayati. kiṃ liṅgaṃ bhavatīti. evam āha, hīyate vā eṣa paśubhir yo viśvajiti sarvaṃ{*6/355*} na dadātīti niyataṃ sarvasvadānaṃ darśayaty ahargaṇe.
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark is indeed observed. What is the indicatory mark? Thus it states: 'He is diminished in cattle who does not give everything in the <s>Viśvajit</s>' — [this] shows that the giving of all one's property is invariable in the <s>ahargaṇa</s> [Viśvajit as well].

NOTES:
[{6/355: E1,6, E2 (variant reading); E2: <s>sarvasvaṃ</s>}]
[{6/356: E2: 5,346; E6: 2,202}]

children.text: vikāraḥ sann ubhayato 'viśeṣāt // MS_6,7.18 //
children.translated_text: Being a modification, [the ahargaṇa Viśvajit applies] in both [cases — whether one's wealth is more or less than twelve hundred], because of the absence of distinction. // MS_6,7.18 //

children.text: viśvajiti sarvasvaṃ dadātīti. tatraiṣo 'rthaḥ sāṃśayikaḥ, kiṃ yasya dvādaśaśatam adhikam, ūnaṃ vā vidyate, tasyāpi viśvajitādhikāraḥ{*6/357*}, uta yasya sakalam adhikaṃ vā tasyaiveti. kiṃ prāptam. vikāraḥ sann ubhayato 'viśeṣāt. na viśeṣaḥ kaścid āśrīyate. yasya dvādaśaśatam adhikam, ūnaṃ vāstīti. tasmāt sarvasya viśvajitādhikāra{*6/358*} iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Viśvajit</s> one gives all one's property. There this is a debatable point: does one whose [wealth] of twelve hundred is in excess or in deficit also have eligibility for the <s>Viśvajit</s>, or only one whose [wealth] is complete or in excess? What is the prima facie view? Being a modification, [the eligibility applies] in both [cases], because of the absence of distinction. No distinction is relied upon [between one] whose twelve hundred is in excess or in deficit. Therefore all [persons] are eligible for the <s>Viśvajit</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/357: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: viśvajity adhikāraḥ}*
*{6/358: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: viśvajity adhikāra}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/357: E1,6, E2 (variant reading); E2: <s>viśvajity adhikāraḥ</s>}]
[{6/358: E1,6, E2 (variant reading); E2: <s>viśvajity adhikāra</s>}]

children.text: adhikaṃ vā pratiprasavāt // MS_6,7.19 //
children.translated_text: Or [one must have] more [than twelve hundred], because of the counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>). // MS_6,7.19 //

children.text: na caitad asti, sarvasya viśvajitādhikāra{*6/359*} iti. kasya tarhi. yasya dvādaśaśatam asti, adhikaṃ veti. kutaḥ. pratiprasavāt. pratiprasavo hi jyotiṣṭome sarvasvasyocyate. dvādaśaśataṃ vidhāyāha, etāvatā vāva ṛtvija āneyā api vā sarvasveneti. yadi etāvatā neccheyuḥ, sarvasvenāpy ānamayitavyā iti. tad yadi dvādaśena śatena necchanti{*6/360*}, necchantitarāṃ tato nyūnena. tasmād dvādaśaśataṃ jyotiṣṭome. yad vā sarvasvam, tad ihobhayam api prāptam. tatraikaḥ pakṣo niyamyate, sarvasvaṃ deyam iti. sa eṣa na vidhiḥ, prāptatvāt. aniyataprāptas tu niyamyate. sa cen niyamyate, yādṛśas tatra, tādṛśa eveha. tatra ca dvādaśaśatam adhikaṃ vā sarvasvam. ihāpi tadvad eva. tasmān na nyūnadhanasyādhikāra iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that all are eligible for the <s>Viśvajit</s>. For whom, then? For one who has twelve hundred or more. Why? Because of the counter-exception. For the counter-exception concerning all one's property is stated in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Having prescribed twelve hundred, [the text] says: 'With this much indeed the <s>ṛtvij</s>s (priests) are to be engaged; or else with all one's property.' If they do not agree for this much, they should be won over even with all one's property. If they do not agree for twelve hundred, they will agree even less for less than that. Therefore twelve hundred [is the minimum] in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. Or [alternatively,] all one's property — both are established [as possibilities] there. Of these, one option is restricted [here]: all one's property should be given. This is not an [independent] injunction, because it is [already] established. But what is established without restriction is [now] restricted. And if it is restricted, it should be the same here as it was there. And there [in the Jyotiṣṭoma], [the giving of] all one's property [applies to one] whose twelve hundred is in excess. Here too it should be the same. Therefore one of deficient wealth is not eligible.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/359: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: viśvajity adhikāra}*
*{6/360: E2 om. necchanti}*

children.text: anugrahāc ca pādavat // MS_6,7.20 //
children.translated_text: And because of inclusion, like a quarter [in a whole coin]. // MS_6,7.20 //

children.text: caśabdenānvācayaḥ. itaś cādhikaṃ sarvasvam, adhike hi [751]{*6/361*} dīyamāne tadantargatatvād dvādaśaśatam api dattaṃ bhavati, pādavat, yathā, kārṣāpaṇe dīyamāne pādo 'pi datto bhavati, evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) introduces an additional [argument]. For this reason too, all one's property [should exceed twelve hundred] — for when the excess is given, the twelve hundred is also given since it is included within it, [751] like a quarter — just as when a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin) is given, the quarter too is [thereby] given; so it is here as well.

children.text: aparimite śiṣṭasya saṃkhyāpratiṣedhas tac chrutitvāt // MS_6,7.21 //
children.translated_text: When 'unlimited' is [stated], the negation of number applies to what has been specified [as numbered]; [this is understood] because of that being a [Vedic] hearing. // MS_6,7.21 //

children.text: ādhāne śrūyate, ekā deyā, ṣaḍ deyāḥ, dvādaśa deyāḥ, caturviṃśatir deyāḥ, śataṃ deyam, sahasraṃ deyam, aparimitaṃ deyam iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ yat parimitam ekā deyetyevamādi, tan na dātavyam iti pratiṣedho vidhīyate, utāparimitaṃ nāma kiṃcit, tasya dānaṃ vidhīyata iti. kiṃ prāptam. aparimite śrūyamāne brūmaḥ, śiṣṭasyaikādeḥ saṃkhyeyasya yā saṃkhyā, sā pratiṣidhyate. kutaḥ. tacchrutitvāt, parimitaśabdaśravaṇād gaṇitam avagamyate. tac caikādikam, tasya naśabdena pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate. tatra śruto 'rthaḥ kṛto bhavati, itarathāparimitaśabde prasiddhis tyajyeta. lakṣaṇayā bahutvam asyārthaḥ kalpyeta. tasmāt aprimitasya pratiṣedha iti.
children.translated_text: In the [rite of] fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>) it is heard: 'one [cow] should be given, six should be given, twelve should be given, twenty-four should be given, a hundred should be given, a thousand should be given, an unlimited [number] should be given.' There a doubt [arises]: does 'unlimited' negate the numbered [amounts] — 'one should be given' and so forth — meaning the numbered [amounts] should not be given? Or is 'unlimited' a specific thing, and its giving is being enjoined? What is the prima facie view? When 'unlimited' is heard, we say: the number of what has been specified — 'one' and so forth, the countable — that number is negated. Why? Because of that being a [Vedic] hearing — because of hearing the word '<s>parimita</s>' (measured/numbered), what is counted is understood. And that is 'one' and so forth; the negation of that is made by the word '<s>na</s>' (not). There the heard meaning is accomplished. Otherwise, in the case of the word '<s>aparimita</s>' (unlimited), the conventional meaning would have to be abandoned. By secondary usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), 'abundance' would have to be postulated as its meaning. Therefore [it is] a negation of what is measured.

children.text: kalpāntaraṃ vā tulyavat prasaṃkhyānāt // MS_6,7.22 //
children.translated_text: Or it is an alternative procedure, because of equal enumeration, like [the others]. // MS_6,7.22 //

children.text:
kalpāntaraṃ vā syāt. aparo dānakalpo vidhīyate, yathaikā deyeti dānavidhikalpaḥ. evam eṣo 'pi dānavidhikalpa eva syāt. tena{*6/362*} hi pūrveṇa, tulyam evedaṃ prasaṃkhyāyate. kāsya pūrveṇa tulyatā. pratijñātasyārthasyāvagamikā [752]{*6/363*} śrutir astīti. pūrvatra hi deyaśabdaśrutyā dānaṃ vidhīyata iti, ihāpi deyaśadaśrutiḥ. sā śrūyamāṇā{*6/364*} śaknoti dānaṃ vidhātum. pratiṣedhe hi vidhīyamāne vākyasya{*6/365*} vyāpāraḥ. tac ca durbalaṃ śrutiṃ prati{*6/366*}. tasmāt kalpāntaram. yac cāparimitaśabde prasiddhir bādhyata iti, samudāyaprasiddhir avayavaprasiddher bādhikaiva samadhigatā.
nanu nātra prasiddhiḥ, lakṣaṇeyam. yad bahu, tan na śakyaṃ parimātum. tasmād aparimitatvena lakṣyate bahutvam iti. tac ca na, anekasminn aśakyaparimāṇe sati bahuṣu rūḍhaḥ. aparimitam asya dhanam, bahv iti gamyate. yathā, kuśalaḥ, pravīṇa iti. bahuṣu kuśānāṃ lāturguṇeṣu satsu nipuṇatāyām eva kuśalaśabdo rohād rūḍhiśabda{*6/367*} eva bhavati. bahuṣu ca vīṇāv ādasya guṇeṣu satsu nipuṇa eva pravīṇaśabdo vartamāno rūḍha ity ucyate. tasmāt saty api lakṣaṇātve śrutisāmarthyād rohatiśabdaḥ. tasmāt samudāyaprasiddhyāparimitaśabde 'vayavaprasiddhir bādhyate, aśvakarṇaśabdavat. ataḥ kalpānataram iti.
children.translated_text:
Or it would be an alternative procedure. Another procedure of giving is being enjoined — just as 'one should be given' is a procedure of giving, so too this should be a procedure of giving. For by the earlier [enumeration], this too is equally enumerated. What is its equality with the earlier? There is a [Vedic] hearing (<s>śruti</s>) that conveys the meaning of the stated [proposition]. For in the earlier [cases], the giving is enjoined by the hearing of the word '<s>deyā</s>' (should be given); here too there is a hearing of the word '<s>deyā</s>.' That hearing, when heard, is capable of enjoining giving. But if a negation were being enjoined, [752] the operation would be that of the sentence. And that is weaker against hearing (<s>śruti</s>). Therefore it is an alternative procedure. As to what was said — 'the conventional meaning of the word <s>aparimita</s> is overridden' — the conventional meaning of the whole (<s>samudāya</s>) is indeed established as overriding the conventional meaning of the parts (<s>avayava</s>).
[The objector says:] but there is no conventional meaning here — this is a secondary usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). What is abundant cannot be measured. Therefore 'abundance' is secondarily indicated by [the word] '<s>aparimita</s>.' But that is not so — [the word] is established (<s>rūḍha</s>) in [the meaning of] abundance from among many [possible meanings for which] the impossibility of measurement [applies]. 'His wealth is unlimited' — [this] is understood as 'abundant.' Just as '<s>kuśala</s>' (literally 'skilled with kuśa grass') — from among many qualities of kuśa-grass handlers, the word '<s>kuśala</s>' is established (<s>rūḍha</s>) in [the meaning of] dexterity alone and is called a conventional term. And '<s>pravīṇa</s>' (literally 'skilled with the vīṇā') — from among many qualities of vīṇā-takers, the word '<s>pravīṇa</s>', being current in [the meaning of] dexterity alone, is called conventional. Therefore, even when there is secondary derivation, by the force of hearing (<s>śruti</s>), it is an established term (<s>rūḍhi</s>). Therefore, by the conventional meaning of the whole, the conventional meaning of the parts of the word '<s>aparimita</s>' is overridden — like the word '<s>aśvakarṇa</s>' (literally 'horse-ear' [but denoting a tree]). Hence it is an alternative procedure.

children.text: aniyamo 'viśeṣāt // MS_6,7.23 //
children.translated_text: There is no restriction, because of non-distinction. // MS_6,7.23 //

children.text: aparimite kalpānataram iti samadhigatam. athedānīṃ saṃdihyate{*6/368*}. kiṃ sahasrād ūnam aparimitam, uta sahasrād adhikam iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. aniyamo 'viśeṣāt. na kaścid iha bahutve viśeṣa{*6/369*} āsrīyate, sahasrād ūnam adhikaṃ veti. anāśrīyamāṇe yathākṛtaṃ tathā sādhu{*6/370*}. tasmād aniyamaḥ.
children.translated_text: It has been ascertained that [the number] is unlimited — not otherwise fixed. Now a doubt arises: is 'unlimited' [meaning] less than a thousand, or more than a thousand? What is the prima facie view? There is no restriction, because of non-distinction. No specific distinction regarding multiplicity is relied upon here — whether less than or more than a thousand. When no [distinction] is relied upon, however it is done, it is good. Therefore there is no restriction.

children.text: adhikaṃ vā syād bahvarthatvād itareṣāṃ{*6/372*} saṃnidhānāt // MS_6,7.24 //
children.translated_text: Or it should be more [than a thousand], because of [the word's] meaning 'many,' and because of the proximity of the others. // MS_6,7.24 //

children.text: veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. naitad asti, adhikam ūnaṃ vā sahasrād iti. kiṃ tarhi. adhikam eveti. kutaḥ. bahvarthatvād aparimitaśabdasya, bahuṣu hīmaṃ śabdam upacarantīty etad uktam. bahutvaṃ cāpekṣikam, kiṃcid apekṣya tato 'dhikaṃ bahv ity ucyate. asatyām apekṣāyām apraripūrṇam etat, yathā, putra iti kiṃcid apekṣya bhavati, nānyathā. tatra prakṛtaṃ saṃnihitaṃ cāpekṣya nirṇayaḥ, sahasraṃ ca saṃnihitam. tasmāt tato 'dhikam aparimitam iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>vā</s> ('or') reverses the position. This is not [correct] — that [it can be] either more or less than a thousand. Rather, it is necessarily more. Why? Because of the word <s>aparimita</s> ('unlimited') meaning 'many' — for they use this word figuratively for large quantities, as stated. And 'manyness' is relative — in relation to something, what exceeds it is called 'many.' Without a [point of] reference, this [term] is incomplete — just as 'son' exists in relation to something, not otherwise. There, the determination is made in relation to what is present in the context, and a thousand is present [in the context]. Therefore 'unlimited' means more than that.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/372: E2 (v.l.): itarair}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/372: E2 (variant): <s>itarair</s>}]

children.text: arthavādaś ca tadvat // MS_6,7.25 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) [supports] the same. // MS_6,7.25 //

children.text: katham evam. tatrotkṛṣṭaṃ vai aparimitam iti tadūnatāṃ sahasrasya darśayati.
children.translated_text: How is this so? There, 'the unlimited is indeed the excellent' — [the <s>arthavāda</s>] shows the inferiority of the thousand [in relation to it].

children.text: parakṛtipurākalpaṃ ca manuṣyadharmaḥ syād arthāya hy anukīrtanam // MS_6,7.26 //
children.translated_text: Precedent from others' practice (<s>parakṛti</s>) and ancient custom (<s>purākalpa</s>) would be a rule for humans, for the recounting is for a purpose. // MS_6,7.26 //

children.text: iha parakṛtayaḥ purākalpāś codāharaṇam. yathā, iti ha smāha bakurvāṣṇir māṣān me pacata, na vā eteṣāṃ havir gṛhṇantīti. purākalpaḥ, ulmukair ha sma pūrve samājamustān ha asurā rakṣāṃsi nirjaghnur ityevamādayaḥ. teṣu saṃdehaḥ. kim ete manuṣyadharmā vidhayaḥ, uta tadgotrāṇām. athavā [754]{*6/373*} arthavādā iti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. manuṣyadhamā vidhaya iti. kutaḥ. arthāya prayojanāyānukīrtanam etad bhavati. kartṛmanuṣyasaṃbandhakīrtanena kriyā praśastā bhavati. praśastaṃ ca pratipādyam. sa eṣa vidhir eva, anena prakāreṇa. ataḥ parair api manuṣyaiḥ kartavya iti gamyate.
children.translated_text: Here, precedents from others' practice and ancient customs serve as examples. For instance, precedent from another's practice: 'Thus <s>Bakurvāṣṇi</s> used to say: cook beans for me — they do not take the offering of those.' Ancient custom: 'In ancient times, with firebrands, they drove out the <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s> who had gathered' — and others of this kind. Regarding these, a doubt [arises]: are these rules (<s>dharma</s>) for [all] humans, or for those of those [specific] lineages? Or are they <s>arthavādas</s> (laudatory passages)? What is the prima facie view? They are rules for humans — injunctions. Why? The recounting is for a purpose — it serves a purpose. By recounting the connection with human agents, the action is praised. And what is praised is to be practiced. This is indeed an injunction, in this manner. Therefore it is understood that other humans too should do this.

children.text: tad ukte ca pratiṣedhāt // MS_6,7.27 //
children.translated_text: And because of the prohibition when that [action has been] stated. // MS_6,7.27 //

children.text: evaṃjātīyakasya vidheḥ pratiṣedho bhavati, tad u{*6/374*} tathā na kuryād iti, prasaktasya ca pratiṣedho nyāyyaḥ. tasmād api vidhaya iti.
children.translated_text: There is a prohibition of such an injunction — 'one should not do it thus' — and prohibition is proper only of what is applicable. Therefore they are indeed injunctions.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/374: E2 om. u}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/374: E2 omits <s>u</s>}]

children.text: nirdeśād vā taddharmaḥ syāt pañcāvattavat // MS_6,7.28 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the specification [of persons], [it] would be the rule of those [specific lineages], like the <s>pañcāvatta</s>. // MS_6,7.28 //

children.text: manuṣyadharmo 'yaṃ vidhir evaṃjātīyaka iti gṛhyate. tatra tu viśiṣṭagotrāṇāṃ nirdeśāt teṣām eva dharma iti gamyate. stutyā hy ayaṃ kartavya iti jñāyate, sa ca viśiṣṭagotrāṇāṃ śrūyate, tasmāt tadgotrāṇām eva kartavyaḥ, pañcāvattavat, yathā, pañcāvattaṃ jamadagnīnām{*6/375*} iti tadgotrāṇām eva bhavati, evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: It is accepted that this is an injunction, a rule for humans of this kind. But there, because of the specification of particular lineages, it is understood as a rule for those [lineages] alone. For this is known to be enjoined by a praise, and that [praise] is heard regarding specific lineages. Therefore it should be done only by those lineages — like the <s>pañcāvatta</s>: just as 'the <s>pañcāvatta</s> belongs to the <s>Jamadagnis</s>' applies to those lineages alone, so too here.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/375: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: jāmadagnīnām}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/375: E1,6,E2 (variant); E2: <s>jāmadagnīnām</s>}]

children.text: vidhau tu vedasaṃyogād upadeśaḥ syāt // MS_6,7.29 //
children.translated_text: But when there is an injunction, because of connection with the Veda, [the specification] would be instructive [of praise, not restriction]. // MS_6,7.29 //

children.text: tuśabdād eṣo 'pi pakṣo vyāvartate{*6/376*}. vidhāv eteṣām upadeśaḥ syāt. vidhau vedena stutinirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ, na vidhyāśraye puruṣe. puruṣagrahaṇaṃ vidhipraśaṃsārtham. vidhir iti kriyāmāha. etasyāḥ [755]{*6/377*} kriyāyā bhāvo yasmād anena puruṣeṇa kriyate, tasmāt sādhur iti. na tv atra puruṣaḥ kriyāsaṃbandhena nirdiśyate, kiṃ tu stotavyatvena. kuta etat. stutipadasyānyasyābhāvāt. api ca kriyānirdeśe śrutyā vidhānam, kriyāpuruṣasaṃbandhanirdeśe vākyena, ataś ca{*6/378*} durbalam. tasmāt puruṣamātrasya vidhānaṃ prāpnoti, na tadgotrāṇām iti.
children.translated_text: By the word <s>tu</s> ('but'), this position too is reversed. When there is an injunction, the specification would be instructive [i.e., for laudatory purposes]. In the injunction, the praise-specification is made by the Veda, not regarding the person who is the basis of the injunction. The mention of the person is for the purpose of praising the injunction. 'Injunction' refers to the action. [755] The existence of this action is praised because it is performed by such a person — therefore it is good. But here the person is not specified in connection with the action, but rather as something to be praised. How [do we know] this? Because of the absence of any other term of praise. Moreover, when action is specified, [it is] prescribed by the [Vedic] text; when the connection of action and person is specified, [it is] by the sentence — and therefore weaker. Therefore the injunction applies to humans in general, not to those [specific] lineages.

children.text: arthavādo vā vidhiśeṣatvāt tasmān{*6/379*} nityānuvādaḥ syāt // MS_6,7.30 //
children.translated_text: Or it is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage), because of being subsidiary to an injunction; therefore it would be a constant reference (<s>nityānuvāda</s>). // MS_6,7.30 //

children.text: eṣo 'pi pakṣo vāśabdād vinivṛttaḥ{*6/380*}. nāyaṃ tadgotrāṇāṃ vidhiḥ. na manuṣyamātrasya vā vidhiḥ, vidhir eva veti, ayam arthavādas{*6/381*} tu. kutaḥ. vidhiśeṣatvāt, anyaṃ tv atra vidhim āmananti, parakṛtyudāharaṇe tāvat, tasmād āraṇyam evāśnīyād iti, purākalpodāharaṇe, gṛhapater evāgriṣu nirmathya nirvaperann iti. na ca dvayor vidhyor ekavākyabhāvo 'sti. vidhinā hi saṃbadhyamānayoḥ parakṛtipurākalpavacanayor anyā vacanavyaktiḥ. anyā tu stutyarthapravṛttayoḥ. na cobhayaṃ yaugapadyena saṃbhavati. tasmād arthavāda iti.
children.translated_text: This position too is reversed by the word <s>vā</s>. This is not a rule for those [specific] lineages, nor an injunction for humans in general — it is not an injunction at all, but an <s>arthavāda</s>. Why? Because of being subsidiary to an injunction — for they record another injunction here. In the case of precedent from another's practice, [the injunction is:] 'therefore one should eat only what grows in the forest.' In the case of ancient custom, [the injunction is:] 'from the householder's [fire] alone, having churned by <s>araṇis</s>, one should portion out.' And there is no sentence-unity of two injunctions. For when the statements of others' practice and ancient customs are connected with an injunction, there is one mode of expression; but when they are connected as [arising] for the purpose of praise, there is another. And both [modes] cannot occur simultaneously. Therefore it is an <s>arthavāda</s>.

children.text: sahasrasaṃvatsaraṃ tadāyuṣām asaṃbhāvān manuṣyeṣu // MS_6,7.31 //
children.translated_text: The thousand-year [<s>sattra</s>] — because of the impossibility [of such a lifespan] for humans whose lives [are limited]. // MS_6,7.31 //

children.text: asti sahasrasaṃvatsaram, pañcapañcāśatas{*6/382*} trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ, pañcapañcāśataḥ pañcadaśāḥ, pañcapañcāśataḥ saptadaśāḥ, pañcapañcāśata ekaviṃśā viśvasṛjāmayanaṃ sahasrasaṃvatsaram iti. tatra [756]{*6/383*} saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ ye sahasrāyuṣas teṣām anena adhikāraḥ, uta manuṣyāṇām iti. yadāpi manuṣyāṇām, tadāpi bahavo vikalpā vakṣyamānāḥ{*6/384*}, athavā divaseṣu saṃvatsaraśabda iti. kiṃ prāptam. sahasrāyuṣāṃ bhavitum arhati. kutaḥ. asaṃbhavān manuṣyeṣu, na manuṣyāṇām etāvad āyur vidyate, gandharvādayas tv etāvad āyuṣa iti bhavati smṛtiḥ. upacāro 'nyārthadarśanaṃ ca. prajāpatiṃ vai prajāḥ sṛjamānaṃ pāpmā mṛtyur abhijaghāna, sa tapo 'tapyata sahasrasaṃvatsarān pāpmānaṃ vijihāsann iti. vispaṣṭaṃ cedaṃ sahasrasaṃvatsaram. tasmān na manuṣyāṇām iti.
children.translated_text: There is [a rite lasting] a thousand years — fifty-five <s>Trivṛt</s> years, fifty-five <s>Pañcadaśa</s> years, fifty-five <s>Saptadaśa</s> years, fifty-five <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> years — [this is] the <s>Viśvasṛjām Ayana</s> lasting a thousand years. There, [756] a doubt [arises]: do those who live a thousand years have eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) for this, or [ordinary] humans? Even when [it is] for humans, there will be many alternatives to be stated. Or perhaps the word 'year' [is used] for 'days.' What is the prima facie view? It should apply to those who live a thousand years. Why? Because of the impossibility [of such a lifespan] for humans — humans do not have such a lifespan. But <s>Gandharvas</s> and others are traditionally known to have such a lifespan. There is also figurative usage and evidence for another purpose: '<s>Prajāpati</s>, while creating beings, was struck by sin and death; he performed austerities for a thousand years, wishing to be free of sin' — here the thousand years are clearly [literal]. Therefore it is not for humans.

children.text: api vā tadadhikārān manuṣyadharmaḥ syāt // MS_6,7.32 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of [human] eligibility for that [rite], it would be a rule for humans. // MS_6,7.32 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. na gandharvādīnām, manuṣyāṇām evādhikāra iti. kutaḥ. tadadhikārāt, manuṣyādhikāraṃ śāstraṃ samadhigatam iti. te hi śaknuvanti kārtsnyena yathoditaṃ vidhim upasaṃhartum iti. āha, nanu naitāvad āyuṣo manuṣyāḥ. ucyate, rasāyanair āyur dīrghaṃ prāpsyantīti.
children.translated_text: The words <s>api vā</s> ('or rather') reverse the position. It is not for <s>Gandharvas</s> and others — humans alone have eligibility. Why? Because of eligibility for that — it has been ascertained that the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) is of human eligibility. For they are able to complete the prescribed injunction in its entirety. He says: but humans do not have such a lifespan. [We] reply: by <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy) they will obtain a long life.

children.text: nāsāmarthyāt // MS_6,7.33 //
children.translated_text: Not so, because of incapability. // MS_6,7.33 //

children.text: na rasāyanānām etat{*6/385*} sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭam, yena sahasrasaṃvatsaraṃ jīveyuḥ. etāni hy agner vardhakāni, balīpalitasya nāśakāni{*6/386*}, svaravarṇaprasādakāni, meghājananāni. naitāvad āyuṣo dātṝṇi dṛśyante. nanu svaravarṇaprasādādidarśanād eva jyogjīvanam{*6/387*} apy anumāsyate. neti brūmaḥ. kutaḥ. śatāyur vai puruṣa [757]{*6/388*} ity anuvādaḥ. sa{*6/389*} evaṃ jyogjīve{*6/390*} nāvakalpate. atrocyate, śatāny āyur asyeti vigrahīṣyāmaḥ. naivaṃ saṃkhyāśabdānāṃ samāsa iṣyate. na ca gamakāni bhavanti, dvivacanabahuvacanāntānām asamāsa iti cābhiyuktavacanāt.
children.translated_text: Such capability of <s>rasāyanas</s> has not been observed by which they would live a thousand years. For these [<s>rasāyanas</s>] increase digestive fire, destroy graying and wrinkling, produce clarity of voice and complexion, and generate vigour. They are not observed as bestowers of such a [long] lifespan. [The objector says:] but from the observation of clarity of voice and complexion, longevity too should be inferred. We say: no. Why? [Because] 'a hundred years is the lifespan of a person' [757] — this is a reference [to an established fact]. That [reference] is inapplicable to living long. To this we reply: we shall analyze it as '<s>śatāni āyuḥ asya</s>' ('he whose lives are in hundreds'). [But] such compounding of number-words is not accepted. Nor are they indicative [of the intended meaning], as stated by experts — 'number words in dual and plural endings cannot be compounded.'

children.text: saṃbandhādarśanāt // MS_6,7.34 //
children.translated_text: Because of the non-observation of a connection. // MS_6,7.34 //

children.text: na hy etāvad āyuṣā rasāyanānāṃ saṃbandho dṛṣṭapūrvaḥ, na ca saṃbandhādarśane 'numānam asti. nanu sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati. dṛśyante tāvad alpasya sthirabhāvasya kārakāṇi. evam abhyasyamānāni vīryavattamāni sthiraśarīratām utpādayiṣyanti. śatāyuḥ puruṣa iti saty api vacane, adhikaṃ jīvanaṃ dṛśyata eveti. atrocyate, nāyam ekāntaḥ, kadācidyām ca yāvantīṃ ca śarīrasthiratām utpādayeyuḥ, na prāg apy adṛṣṭakālām, yathā prakrāmanto 'bhyāsāt prakramāṇāṃ vṛddher yāṃ ca yāvantīṃ ca mātrāṃ prāpnuvanti, na tv abhyasyantaḥ puruṣāyuṣeṇāpi yojanamātraṃ prakrameyuḥ. evam ihāpi saṃbandhābhāvāt sahasrāyuṣṭvaṃ prāpnuyur na veti saṃdigdham. saṃdigdhaṃ cet, sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ na pramāṇam, na cādṛṣṭo 'rthaḥ pramāṇam antreṇa śakyo 'bhyupagantum. tasmād asaṃśayaṃ naitāvad āyuṣaḥ santīti puruṣavacanenoktam. kathaṃ tarhīti.
children.translated_text: For a connection of <s>rasāyanas</s> with such a [long] lifespan has never been observed before, and in the non-observation of a connection, inference is not [valid]. [The objector says:] but there will be a <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (inference from general observation). For [<s>rasāyanas</s>] are observed to produce stability of a small [extent]; thus, when practiced assiduously, being most powerful, they will produce stability of the body. Even though it is stated 'a hundred years is the lifespan of a person,' living longer is indeed observed. To this we reply: this is not invariable — whatever and however much bodily stability they may produce, [they do] not [produce] a duration never observed before — just as those who walk, through practice, attain whatever and however much increase in walking distance, but even with practice over a human lifetime they could not walk as far as a <s>yojana</s>. Similarly here, because of the absence of a connection, whether they would attain a thousand-year lifespan is doubtful. And if it is doubtful, <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference is not a valid means of knowledge; and an unobserved object cannot be accepted without a valid means of knowledge. Therefore it is stated by the [Vedic] statement about a person that they assuredly do not have such a lifespan. How then [should it be done]?

children.text: sa kulakalpaḥ syād iti kārṣṇājinir ekasminn asaṃbhavāt // MS_6,7.35 //
children.translated_text: It would be a lineage-practice (<s>kulakalpa</s>), says <s>Kārṣṇājini</s>, because of the impossibility for a single [person]. // MS_6,7.35 //

children.text: sa manuṣyādhikārapakṣe kulakalpo bhaviṣyatīty evaṃ kārṣṇājinir ācāryo manyate sma. kutaḥ. ekasminn asaṃbhavāt, puruṣāṇām idam anuśāsanam, na caitad ekaḥ śaknoti pārayitum. yathā śakyate, tathā pārayitavyam iti gamyamāne, bahavaḥ śaknuvantaḥ pravarteran. anye 'pi tatkulīnā anyenārabdhaṃ samāpayeyur iti.
children.translated_text: In the view that [the rite is] of human eligibility, it will be a lineage-practice — so teacher <s>Kārṣṇājini</s> held. Why? Because of the impossibility for a single [person] — this instruction is for humans, but one [person] alone cannot complete it. When it is understood that 'it should be completed to whatever extent possible,' many who are capable would undertake it. Others of that very lineage would complete what was begun by another.

children.text: api vā kṛtsnasaṃyogād ekasyaiva prayogaḥ syāt // MS_6,7.36 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of connection with the entirety, it should be the performance of one person alone. // MS_6,7.36 //

children.text:
śāstraphalaṃ hi prayoktari{*6/391*} samadhigataṃ{*6/392*}, yaś ca kārtsnyena vidhiṃ upasaṃhartuṃ samarthaḥ. sa evādhikriyata iti. tasmān na kulakalpo 'vakalpyate. kathaṃ tarhi. saṃpradāyamātreṇa dharma ity adhyavasīyate. evaṃ śrūyate, svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya iti. evaṃ tarhy etad adhyavaseyam, vacanaprāmāṇyād etat karma kurvatām āyur varddhata iti. tac ca na, pramāṇābhāvāt. na hy etasminn arthe vākyam anyad vā pramāṇam asti. nanv arthāpattiḥ, anyathānarthakyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, nānarthakyam, adhyayanād eva hy adṛṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati. tathā hi sāmānyenādṛṣṭaṃ kalpayitum laghīyaḥ, na tu karmaṇāyur vardhata iti viśeṣādṛṣṭakalpanā. athavānarthakyam evābhyupagamyeta, nāyukti phalaṃ kalpyam{*6/393*}. athocyeta, ardhatṛtīyāni śatāni dīkṣiṣyante, catubhir varṣaiḥ samāpyanta{*6/394*} iti. evam api niyataparimāṇaṃ hīyeta{*6/395*}, caturviṃśatiparamāḥ saptadaśāvarāḥ satram āsīrann iti. vacanasya tv ānarthakyaparihārāya parimāṇaṃ hāpayiṣyata iti cet. tad ayuktam, adhyayanāt phalam asti. tasmān naiṣā kalpaneti.
kathaṃ tarhi. evam,
children.translated_text:
For the fruit of the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative text) is understood to be in the performer — who is capable of accomplishing the entire procedure. He alone is entitled. Therefore no clan-alternative (<s>kulakalpa</s>) is posited. How then? By tradition (<s>saṃpradāya</s>) alone it is determined to be <s>dharma</s>. Thus it is heard: 'The <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study) should be studied.' Then it should be determined thus: by the authority of the [Vedic] statement, 'the lifespan of those who perform this rite increases.' But that is not so, because of the absence of a valid means of knowledge. For there is no sentence or other means of knowledge for this meaning. [The objector says:] but [there is] implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>) — otherwise there would be purposelessness. We reply: there is no purposelessness, for an unseen [result] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) will [accrue] from study alone. For it is easier to postulate an unseen [result] in general than to postulate a specific unseen [result that] 'the lifespan increases through the rite.' Or rather, let purposelessness simply be accepted — an improper fruit should not be postulated. But if it is said: 'Two hundred and fifty will be initiated; they complete in four years' — even so, the fixed measure would be diminished — 'Twenty-four at most, seventeen at minimum, sat in the <s>satra</s>.' [The objector says:] but for the sake of avoiding purposelessness of the statement, the measure will be abandoned. That is improper — there is fruit from study. Therefore this is not a [valid] postulation.
How then? Thus:

children.text: vipratiṣedhāt tu guṇyanyataraḥ{*6/397*} syād iti lāvukāyanaḥ // MS_6,7.37 //
children.translated_text: But because of conflict, one of the two would be figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) — thus [says] <s>Lāvukāyana</s>. // MS_6,7.37 //

children.text: anyataro 'tra gauṇaḥ śabdaḥ syāt. yadi vāsaṃvatsare saṃvatsaraśabdaḥ, yadi vā pañcapañcāśata iti śabdo gauṇa iti. kuta etat. vipratiṣedhāt, vipratiṣedho hi bhavati, ubhayasmin vihite. katham. vākyaṃ hi bhidyeta. yadi pañcapañcāśatas trivṛtaḥ, na saṃvatsarāḥ. atha saṃvatsarās trivṛtaḥ, na pañcapañcāśataḥ. tasmād virodhād anyatarad vacanaṃ gauṇam iti lāvukāyana ācāryo manyate sma. ācāryagrahaṇaṃ pūjārtham, nātmanaḥ pratiṣedhārtham{*6/398*}.
children.translated_text: One of the two words here would be figurative. Either the word 'year' (<s>saṃvatsara</s>) is [used figuratively] for what is not a year, or the word 'fifty-five' is figurative. Whence [is this known]? Because of conflict — for there is conflict when both are prescribed. How? The sentence would be split. If fifty-five <s>trivṛt</s> [days], then they are not years. But if years of <s>trivṛt</s> [type], then not fifty-five. Therefore, because of contradiction, one of the two statements is figurative — so teacher <s>Lāvukāyana</s> thinks. The mention of 'teacher' is for the purpose of honor, not for the purpose of refuting [the view as] his own.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/397: E1 (v.l.): guṇād anyataraḥ}*
*{6/398: E1,6; E2: nātmīyamatapratiṣedhārtham}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/397: E1 (v.l.): <s>guṇād anyataraḥ</s>}]
[{6/398: E1,6; E2: <s>nātmīyamatapratiṣedhārtham</s>}]

children.text: saṃvatsaro vicālitvāt // MS_6,7.38 //
children.translated_text: [It is] the year [that is figurative], because of being variable. // MS_6,7.38 //

children.text: etad uktam, anyatarad gauṇam{*6/399*} iti. tad avadhārayitvayam. tad ucyate, saṃvatsaravacanaṃ gauṇam iti. kutaḥ. vicālitvāt, vicālī hi saṃvatsaraśabdaḥ sāvano 'pi gaṇitadivasakaḥ, śītoṣṇavarṣālakṣaṇo 'pi, cāndramaso 'pi. sa evaṃlakṣaṇako 'nuvādaḥ śakyate kalpayitum. pañcapañcāśata ity ayaṃ tu vyaktaparimāṇasyārthasya{*6/400*} vācakaḥ, ekenāpy ūne na bhavati.
children.translated_text: This was said — 'one of the two is figurative.' That is now to be determined. It is said: the word 'year' is figurative. Why? Because of being variable (<s>vicālin</s>) — for the word 'year' is variable: it [can mean] a civil [year] counted by days, or [a year] characterized by cold, heat and rain seasons, or a lunar [year]. That, having such characteristics, can be construed as a restatement. But [the expression] 'fifty-five' is a designator of a meaning with a definite measure — it cannot be [applied] even with one less.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/399: E1,6; E2: anyatarad vacanaṃ gauṇam}*
*{6/400: E1 (v.l.): uktaparimāṇasyārthasya}*

NOTES:
[{6/399: E1,6; E2: <s>anyatarad vacanaṃ gauṇam</s>}]
[{6/400: E1 (v.l.): <s>uktaparimāṇasyārthasya</s>}]

children.text: sā prakṛtiḥ syād adhikārāt // MS_6,7.39 //
children.translated_text: That archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) would be [the referent], because of the subject-matter (<s>adhikāra</s>). // MS_6,7.39 //

children.text:
gavāmayane māsāḥ prakṛtāḥ, māseṣu ca saṃvatsaraśabda uktaḥ, yo vai māsaḥ saṃvatsara iti. tasmāt pañcapañcāśato māsā iti. nanv etasmin pakṣe sahasrasaṃvatsaraśabdo nāvakalpate. ucyate, nāmadheyam etat sahasrasaṃvatsaraśabda [760]{*6/401*} iti, na guṇavidhiḥ. nāmadheyaṃ ca na vidhīyate, avidhīyamānaṃ ca yena kenacid guṇenāvakalpyate{*6/402*}.
naiṣo 'pi pakṣo yujyate, atrāpi hi sa eva doṣaḥ, na tāvaj jīvanam asti, yāvataitad avakalpyeta{*6/403*} dārāgnikālasomapūrvatvāpekṣayeti. tenaitasmiṃś ca kriyamāṇe 'parisamāpta evāyuḥ{*6/404*} paryupayuktaṃ syāt. tathā cādhyayanād evādṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta. evaṃ tarhi, dvādaśāhaḥ prakṛtir iti pañcapañcāśato dvādaśāhā bhaviṣyantīti. tathā ca dṛśyate dvādaśa vai rātrayaḥ saṃvatsarasya pratimā iti. tatra sa doṣo na bhaviṣyati. naivam, tatra saṃvatsaraśabdasya sākṣāt pratimāśabdena saṃyogāt{*6/405*}. api ca, pañcapañcāśatas trivṛta ity uktam, trivṛc chabdaś ca dvādaśāhe divase dṛṣṭaḥ, na dvādaśarātre. tasmān naivam.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Gavāmayana</s> (cow-procession rite), months are the archetype; and in the months, the word 'year' is stated: 'whatever is a month, that is a year.' Therefore, fifty-five months. [The objector says:] but in this view, the word 'thousand-year' does not work. We reply: the word 'thousand-year' [760] is a name (<s>nāmadheya</s>), not a subsidiary-prescription. And a name is not prescribed; what is not prescribed is established by whatever quality [it has].
This view too is not appropriate — for even here the same fault [applies]: there is not enough lifespan for this to work, considering the precedence required of marriage, fire-establishment, <s>kāla</s>-rites, and <s>soma</s>-rites. Therefore, even when this is being performed, the lifespan would be exhausted without completion. And thus an unseen [result] would be postulated from study alone. Then let the twelve-day [rite] be the archetype — there will be fifty-five twelve-day [rites]. And thus it is seen: 'Twelve nights are indeed the image of the year.' There, that fault would not [arise]. Not so — there, because of the direct connection of the word 'year' with the word 'image.' Moreover, it was said 'fifty-five <s>trivṛt</s>' — and the word <s>trivṛt</s> is seen [applied] to a day in the twelve-day [rite], not to a twelve-night [period]. Therefore not so.

NOTES:

children.text: ahāni vābhisaṃkhyatvāt // MS_6,7.40 //
children.translated_text: Or [it refers to] days, because of being countable. // MS_6,7.40 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. na caitad asti, pañcapañcāśato dvādaśarātrā iti. ahāny eva trivṛc chabdenākhyāyante. tasmād ahaḥsu saṃvatsaraśabda iti. athavā, vāśabdaḥ pakṣāntaraṃ{*6/406*} vyāvartayati, na pañcapañcāśāto māsāḥ. kiṃ tarhi divasāḥ. dvādaśāhe trivṛdahaḥ prakṛtam. tatra saṃvatsaraśabdo dṛśyate. ādityo vā sarva ṛtavaḥ, sa yadaivodityatha{*6/407*} vasantaḥ, yadā saṃgavo 'tha grīṣmaḥ, yadā madhyaṃdino 'tha varṣā, yadāparāhno 'tha śarat, yadāstamety atha hemantaśiśirāv iti, sarvān ṛtūn ahani saṃpādayati. sarve cartavaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ. tasmād āhaḥ [761]{*6/408*} saṃvatsaraśabdenocyate. api ca pañcapañcāśatas trivṛta iti trivṛtāṃ pañcapañcāśattvam. na ca dvādaśarātras trivṛt, ekaṃ hi dvādaśāhe trivṛdahaḥ, na tatra trivṛt saṃkhyāyā dvādaśarātreṇa mukhyayā vṛttyā sāmānādhikaraṇyam. trivṛdahaḥ saṃbandhalakṣaṇayā syāt. abhisaṃkhyaṃ trivṛdahaḥ, tena śrutyaiva sāmānādhikaraṇyam, śrutiś ca lakṣaṇāyā jyāyasī. tasmāt pañcapañcāśad ahāni saṃvatsaraḥ syād iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>vā</s> reverses the position. This is not so — that [there are] fifty-five twelve-night [periods]. Days alone are designated by the word <s>trivṛt</s>. Therefore the word 'year' [is used] for days. Alternatively, the word <s>vā</s> reverses another position — not fifty-five months. What then? Days. In the twelve-day [rite], the <s>trivṛt</s> day is the archetype. There, the word 'year' is seen [applied]. 'The sun indeed is all the seasons — when it rises, that is spring; when it is forenoon, that is summer; when it is midday, that is the rains; when it is afternoon, that is autumn; when it sets, that is winter and the cool season' — it makes all the seasons converge in a day. And all the seasons [together] are a year. Therefore a day [761] is denoted by the word 'year.' Moreover, 'fifty-five <s>trivṛt</s>' — [this means] the fifty-five-ness of <s>trivṛt</s> [days]. And a twelve-night [period] is not <s>trivṛt</s> — for in the twelve-day [rite], one day is a <s>trivṛt</s> day; the number '<s>trivṛt</s>' does not have co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with a twelve-night [period] in its primary sense. A <s>trivṛt</s> day would [require] relational figurative usage (<s>saṃbandhalakṣaṇā</s>). A countable <s>trivṛt</s> day — with that, there is co-referentiality by <s>śruti</s> (direct meaning) itself; and <s>śruti</s> is stronger than figurative usage. Therefore fifty-five days would be a 'year.'

children.text: iṣṭipūrvatvād akratuśeṣo homaḥ saṃskṛteṣv agniṣu syād apūrvo apy ādhānasya sarvaśeṣatvāt // MS_6,8.1 //
children.translated_text: Because of being preceded by the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering), the <s>homa</s> (oblation) that is not a remainder of a sacrifice should be [performed] in consecrated fires; even an unprecedented [homa], because of the fire-establishment being subsidiary to all [rites]. // MS_6,8.1 //

children.text: iha caturhotṛṣv āmnāyate, prajākāmaṃ caturhotrā yājayec caturgṛhītam ājyaṃ gṛhītvā caturhotāraṃ vyācakṣīta pūrveṇa graheṇārdhaṃ juhuyāt, taduttareṇārdham{*6/410*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ pavamāneṣṭisaṃskṛteṣu agniṣv evamādayaḥ, uta asaṃskṛteṣv api{*6/411*}. tathā pakṣāntarāśrayaṇam api vakṣyamānaṃ vicārayiṣyate. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. saṃskṛteṣv agniṣv evaṃjātīyako 'kratuśeṣo 'pi homaḥ syāt. yady apy apūrvā darvihomā na kutaścid dharmān ākāṅkṣanti, tathāpy āhavanīyādayo homādīn ākāṅkṣanti{*6/412*}, yad āhavanīye juhoti, tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prīto bhavatītyevamādibhiḥ śrutibhiḥ. evam iṣṭipūrvatvāt sarvahomānām, saṃskṛtāgnivṛttitvam{*6/413*} evaṃjātīyakānām iti.
children.translated_text: Here, in the <s>Caturhotra</s> [rites] it is recorded: 'One who desires progeny should have [the priest] sacrifice with the <s>Caturhotra</s>; having taken four-fold ghee, he should recite the <s>Caturhotāra</s> [formula]; with the first <s>graha</s> (ladle-full) he should offer half; with the subsequent one, half.' There a doubt [arises]: should these [offerings] be [performed] in fires consecrated by the <s>Pavamāneṣṭi</s>, or even in unconsecrated [fires]? The resort to another view, which will be stated [later], will also be examined. What is the prima facie view? In consecrated fires, even such a <s>homa</s> that is not a remainder of a sacrifice should [be performed]. Even though unprecedented ladle-oblations (<s>darvihomas</s>) do not require properties from any [other source], nevertheless the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires] require oblations and the like — [as stated in <s>śrutis</s> such as] 'When he offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, thereby [the deity] becomes pleased and satisfied.' Thus, because of all <s>homas</s> being preceded by the <s>iṣṭi</s>, those of this kind [must be performed] in consecrated fires.

children.text: iṣṭitvena tu saṃstavaś caturhotṝn asaṃskṛteṣu darśayati // MS_6,8.2 //
children.translated_text: But a praise (<s>saṃstava</s>) in the manner of an <s>iṣṭi</s> shows the <s>Caturhotra</s> [rites] to be in unconsecrated [fires]. // MS_6,8.2 //

children.text:
tuśabdāt pakṣo viparivartate. caturhotṛhomā asaṃskṛteṣv agniṣu bhaveyuḥ. tathā hi darśayati, eṣā vānāhitāgne[763]r{*6/414*} iṣṭir yac caturhotāra iti, anāhitāgner iṣṭayo na vidyante. ye tv ete caturhotārāḥ, tasyaiṣaiveṣṭir iti, anāhitāgner evaṃjātīyakān homān darśayati. tasmād asaṃskṛteṣu bhaveyuḥ.
nanu liṅgam asādhakam, prāptir vaktavyeti. tad ucyate,
children.translated_text:
The word <s>tu</s> reverses the position. The <s>Caturhotra</s> oblations should be [performed] in unconsecrated fires. For thus it shows: 'This is indeed the <s>iṣṭi</s> of one who has not established his fires [763] — namely the <s>Caturhotāra</s>' — one who has not established his fires has no [proper] sacrifices. But these <s>Caturhotāras</s> — this alone is his <s>iṣṭi</s> — [thus] it shows oblations of this kind for one who has not established his fires. Therefore they should be [performed] in unconsecrated [fires].
[The objector says:] but an indicatory mark is not probative; the [actual] obtaining must be stated. To that it is said:

children.text: upadeśas tv apūrvatvāt // MS_6,8.3 //
children.translated_text: But [it is] a prescription, because of being unprecedented. // MS_6,8.3 //

children.text: evaṃ tarhi, akratuśeṣāṇāṃ vidhir eṣā{*6/415*} bhaviṣyati, eṣā anāhitāgneḥ{*6/416*} kriyeti. evam arthavadvacanaṃ bhaviṣyati. vādamātram anarthakaṃ bhavati, asya cāsti vidhisāmarthyam. tasmād vidhir asaṃskṛteṣv iti.
children.translated_text: Then let this be the prescription for those that are not remainders of a sacrifice — 'this is the rite of one who has not established fires.' Thus the statement will be meaningful. A mere assertion without [prescriptive] meaning would be purposeless, and this [statement] has the capacity for prescription. Therefore [it is] a prescription for unconsecrated [fires].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/415: E1,6; E2: eṣa; E2 (v.l.): eva}*
*{6/416: E1,6; E2: eṣā vānāhitāgner}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/415: E1,6; E2: <s>eṣa</s>; E2 (v.l.): <s>eva</s>}]
[{6/416: E1,6; E2: <s>eṣā vānāhitāgner</s>}]

children.text: sa sarveṣām aviśeṣāt // MS_6,8.4 //
children.translated_text: That [applies] to all, because of non-distinction. // MS_6,8.4 //

children.text: āha, etad gṛhyate vidhir iti. yat tu, akratuśeṣāṇām iti, tan na, sarveṣāṃ kratuśeṣāṇām akratuśeṣāṇāṃ ca caturhotṛhomānām. kutaḥ. aviśeṣāt, na kratuśeṣāṇām evāyaṃ dharma{*6/417*} ucyate, nākratuśeṣāṇām iti. tasmāt{*6/418*} sarveṣām.
children.translated_text: He says: it is accepted that this is a prescription. But that [it is only] for those that are not remainders of a sacrifice — that is not so; [it is] for all <s>Caturhotra</s> oblations, both remainders of a sacrifice and non-remainders. Why? Because of non-distinction — this rule is not stated [only] for remainders of a sacrifice, nor [only] for non-remainders. Therefore [it is] for all.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/417: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: aviśeṣāt. caturhotṝṇām ayaṃ dharma}*
*{6/418: E1,6; E2: na viśeṣaḥ kratuśeṣāṇām akratuśeṣāṇāṃ ceti. tasmāt}*
