[{6/418: E1,6; E2: <s>na viśeṣaḥ kratuśeṣāṇām akratuśeṣāṇāṃ ceti. tasmāt</s>}]

children.text: api vā kratvabhāvād anāhitāgner aśeṣabhūtanirdeśaḥ // MS_6,8.5 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the absence of sacrifice for one who has not established fires, it is a statement of [the rite] as not being a remainder. // MS_6,8.5 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. akratuśeṣāṇām evāyaṃ dharmo na kratuśeṣāṇām. kutaḥ. anāhitāgneḥ kratvabhāvāt. na hy anāhitāgneḥ kratavaḥ santi. na ca kratvaṅgaṃ kevalaṃ prayujyamānaṃ kasmaicit prayojanāya syāt. na cāsyānyat phalaṃ prakalpyeta{*6/419*}, pramāṇābhāvāt. vacanasya hy anyad api prayojanam asti. na cānena vacanena śakyate 'nāhitāgneḥ kratuḥ kalpayitum. tasmād akratuśeṣāṇām ayaṃ dharma iti.
children.translated_text: The words '<s>api vā</s>' mark a reversal of position. This rule is only for those that are not remainders of a sacrifice, not for remainders. Why? Because of the absence of sacrifice (<s>kratu</s>) for one who has not established fires. For one who has not established fires has no sacrifices. And a subsidiary of a sacrifice, when performed alone, would not serve any purpose. Nor should another fruit be postulated for it, because of the absence of a valid means of knowledge. For the [Vedic] statement has another purpose as well. And by this statement, one cannot postulate a sacrifice for one who has not established fires. Therefore this rule is for those that are not remainders of a sacrifice.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/419: E2 (v.l.): cāsmāt phalaṃ kalpyeta}*
*{6/420: E2: 5,358; E6: 2,211}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/419: E2 (v.l.): <s>cāsmāt phalaṃ kalpyeta</s>}]
[{6/420: E2: 5,358; E6: 2,211}]

children.text: japo vānagnisaṃyogāt // MS_6,8.6 //
children.translated_text: Or [it would be merely] a recitation (<s>japa</s>), because of the non-connection with fire. // MS_6,8.6 //

children.text: vāśabdāt pakṣo viparivartate. nāsaṃskṛteṣv agniṣv evaṃjātīyakā homḥāḥ syuḥ. kutaḥ. ādhānasya sarvaśeṣatvāt{*6/421*}. nanu vacanam idam, eṣā anāhitāgner{*6/422*} iṣṭir iti. neti brūmaḥ, japārthavada eṣa bhaviṣyati. ye japarūpās teṣām arthavādaḥ{*6/423*}, na sarveṣāṃ caturhotṝṇām, evaṃ yadāhavanīye johotītyevamādīnāṃ vacanānām arthavattā bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: The word <s>vā</s> reverses the position. Oblations of this kind should not be [performed] in unconsecrated fires. Why? Because of the fire-establishment being subsidiary to all [rites]. [The objector says:] but there is this statement: 'This is the <s>iṣṭi</s> of one who has not established fires.' We say: no — this will be a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) for recitations (<s>japa</s>). For those that are in the form of <s>japa</s>, it is a laudatory passage — not for all <s>Caturhotras</s>. Thus the meaningfulness of statements such as 'when he offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>' and the like will be [maintained].

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/421: E2 (v.l.): sarvaśeṣatvād eva}*
*{6/422: E1,6; E2: vānāhitāgner}*
*{6/423: E2 (v.l.): ye japas teṣām ayam anuvādaḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/421: E2 (v.l.): <s>sarvaśeṣatvād eva</s>}]
[{6/422: E1,6; E2: <s>vānāhitāgner</s>}]
[{6/423: E2 (v.l.): <s>ye japas teṣām ayam anuvādaḥ</s>}]

children.text: iṣṭitvena tu saṃstute homaḥ syād anārabhyāgnisaṃyogād itareṣām avācyatvāt // MS_6,8.7 //
children.translated_text: But when [it is] characterized as an <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering), there should be an oblation (<s>homa</s>), because of the connection with fire being a non-initiatory [statement]; because the others cannot be expressed [otherwise]. // MS_6,8.7 //

children.text:
yad uktam, eṣā vānāhitatāgneḥ kriyā iṣṭitulyeti japānām eṣa vāda iti. tan na, naiṣā{*6/424*}
vacanavyaktiḥ. yaiṣānāhitāgneḥ kriyā, seṣṭitulyeti. kiṃ kāraṇam. sādṛśyamātrānuvādo 'narthakaḥ syāt. itarasmin pakṣe vidhir arthavān. yeyam iṣṭiḥ, eṣānāhitāgner iti, tadiṣṭisaṃstavād dhomānām eva vādaḥ. katham. iṣṭir yāgaḥ, sa evāsecanādhiko homaḥ. yad uktam, sarvahomārtha āhavanīya iti. tan na, caturhotṝn evādhikṛtyocyate. kiṃ tv aviśeṣeṇa homān. sa caturhotṛṣv asaṃbhavād anyeṣu bhaviṣyati. caturhotṛṣu cānāhitāgner ucyamāneṣv āhavanīyo nāṅgam iti.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'this is the action of one without established fires, equivalent to an <s>iṣṭi</s>' — that this is the position regarding the recitations (<s>japa</s>) — that is not [correct]; this is not the sentence-construction. [The construction is:] 'this action of one without established fires is equivalent to an <s>iṣṭi</s>.' What is the reason? A mere statement of similarity would be purposeless. In the other view, an injunction is meaningful. 'This <s>iṣṭi</s> — this is [the rite] of one without established fires' — because of being characterized as an <s>iṣṭi</s>, it is a statement only of oblations. How? An <s>iṣṭi</s> is a sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), and that is an oblation with the additional [feature of] sprinkling. As to what was said — 'the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is for the purpose of all oblations' — that is not [correct]; it is said only with reference to the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations]. Rather, [it refers to] oblations without distinction. And since [it is] impossible in the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations], it will [apply] to the others. And when the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations] are stated for one without established fires, the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is not a subsidiary.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/424: E1,6; E2: na. katham. naiṣā}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/424: E1,6; E2: <s>na. katham. naiṣā</s>}]

children.text: ubhayoḥ piṭṛyajñavat // MS_6,8.8 //
children.translated_text: [It applies] to both, like the ancestor-sacrifice (<s>pitṛyajña</s>). // MS_6,8.8 //

children.text: naitad asti, anāhitāgner eva caturhotāra iti. ubhayoḥ syuḥ, pitryajñavat, yathā pitṛyajña āhitāgner anāhitāgneś ca, [765]{*6/425*} evaṃ caturhotāro 'pi. katham avagamyate. varṇitam etat. yadānuvādapakṣaḥ, tadāhitāgneḥ, yadā vidhipakṣaḥ, tadānāhitāgneḥ. ubhayathā vacanavyaktiḥ pratīyate. na ca pratīyamāno 'rthaḥ śakyate 'pahnotum. tasmād ubhayoś caturhotāra iti.
children.translated_text: This is not [correct] — that the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations belong] only to one without established fires. They should [belong] to both, like the ancestor-sacrifice — just as the ancestor-sacrifice [belongs] to one who has established fires and to one who has not [765], so too the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations]. How is this understood? This has been explained: when [there is] the restatement view, [it is] for one who has established fires; when the injunction view, for one without established fires. The sentence-construction is understood in both ways. And a meaning that is understood cannot be denied. Therefore the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations belong] to both.

children.text: nirdeśo vānāhitāgner anārabhyāgnisaṃyogāt // MS_6,8.9 //
children.translated_text: Or the designation is of one without established fires, because of the connection with fire being a non-initiatory [statement]. // MS_6,8.9 //

children.text: na caitad asti, ubhayoś{*6/426*} caturhotāro bhaveyur iti. katham. eṣa hy anāhitāgninirdeśaḥ. eṣā veṣṭir anāhitāgner iti vacanenādhikṛtaḥ, nāhitāgniḥ, nirdeśasāmarthyāt. arthavāde copakṣīṇaṃ tatraiva na virudhyata iti. yadāhavanīye juhotīti vacanaṃ na caturhotṝn evādhikṛtyocyata ity uktam. tasmād anāhitāgner evaṃjātīyakā homāḥ.
children.translated_text: And this is not [correct] — that the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations] should belong to both. How? For this designation is of one without established fires. 'This <s>iṣṭi</s> is of one without established fires' — by this statement, [the person] without established fires is designated, not one who has established fires, by the force of the designation. And what is said in the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) does not contradict [what is applicable] there alone. As for the statement 'one offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>' — it was stated [that this] is not said only with reference to the four <s>Hotṛ</s> [recitations]. Therefore oblations of this kind [belong] only to one without established fires.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/426: E1,6; E2: asti, pitṛyajñavad ubhayoś}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/426: E1,6; E2: <s>asti, pitṛyajñavad ubhayoś</s>}]

children.text: pitṛyajñe saṃyuktasya punarvacanam // MS_6,8.10 //
children.translated_text: In the ancestor-sacrifice, it is a re-statement of what is [already] connected. // MS_6,8.10 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, pitṛyajñavad iti, yuktaṃ pitṛyajñe. tatrāhitāgnisaṃyuktasya punar etadvacanaṃ bhavati, apy anāhitāgninā kārya iti. etadvacanam anāhitāgner apīty anāhitāgnāv anvāhāryakaṃ karoti{*6/427*}, iha tathā nāsti vacanam. niyogata eko nirdeśaḥ, eṣā vānāhitāgner iti. nātrāpiśabdo 'sti. tasmāt pitṛyajñenātulyam etat.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'like the ancestor-sacrifice' — it is appropriate in the ancestor-sacrifice. There, for one who has established fires [and] is [already] connected [with the rite], there is this further statement: 'it should also be performed by one without established fires.' This statement [that it is] also for one without established fires [means that] even one without established fires performs the <s>Anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering); here [in our case] there is no such statement. The designation is exclusively one: 'this is for one without established fires.' There is no word '<s>api</s>' (also) here. Therefore this is not analogous to the ancestor-sacrifice.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/427: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: anāhitāgninānvācayaṃ karoti}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/427: E1,6, E2 (variant reading); E2: <s>anāhitāgninānvācayaṃ karoti</s>}]

children.text: upanayann ādadhīta homasaṃyogāt // MS_6,8.11 //
children.translated_text: One initiating [a student] should establish [the fires], because of the connection with the oblation. // MS_6,8.11 //

children.text: idam āmananti, upanayaṃs tisṛbhir juhuyād iti. tatra [766]{*6/428*} saṃdehaḥ. kim ayaṃ homa ādhānasaṃskṛteṣv agniṣu, utāsaṃskṛteṣv iti. kiṃ prāptam. uapanayann ādadhīteti. kutaḥ{*6/429*}. homasaṃyogād āhavanīyasya, yad āhavanīye juhoti, tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prīto bhavatīti. tasmād ādhānottarakālā ete homā iti sthitiḥ{*6/430*}.
children.translated_text: This is recorded: 'The one initiating (<s>upanaya</s>) should offer with three [mantras].' There [766] a doubt [arises]: should this oblation [be performed] on fires refined by [the rite of] establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>), or on unrefined [ordinary fires]? What is the prima facie view? The one initiating should establish [the fires]. Why? Because of the connection of the oblation with the <s>Āhavanīya</s> — 'one who offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, by that [the deity] becomes favorably disposed and pleased toward him.' Therefore these oblations [come] after the time of fire-establishment — this is the position.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/428: E2: 5,360; E2: 2,212}*
*{6/429: E1,6; E2: ādadhīteti. saṃskṛteṣv iti. kutaḥ}*
*{6/430: E2 om. sthitiḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/428: E2: 5,360; E2: 2,212}]
[{6/429: E1,6; E2: <s>ādadhīteti. saṃskṛteṣv iti. kutaḥ</s>}]
[{6/430: E2 omits <s>sthitiḥ</s>}]

children.text: sthapatīṣṭival laukike vā vidyākarmānupūrvatvāt // MS_6,8.12 //
children.translated_text: Or [it should be] on the ordinary [fire], like the <s>Sthapati</s>-<s>iṣṭi</s>, because of the sequence of knowledge [before] action. // MS_6,8.12 //

children.text: na caitad asti, ādhāyaivaṃjātīyakaṃ hotavyam iti. kiṃ tarhi. laukika eva pravarteteti. kutaḥ. vidyākarmānupūrvatvāt. vidyāgrahaṇārthā ime homāḥ. vidyāvataś cādhānenādhikāraḥ{*6/431*}, sāmarthyāt. ata ādhānottarakālatā naiṣām avakalpate, yathā sthapatīṣṭyām.
children.translated_text: And this is not [correct] — that having established [the fires], oblations of this kind should be offered. Rather, [one] should proceed with the ordinary [fire]. Why? Because of the sequence of knowledge [before] action — these oblations are for the purpose of acquiring knowledge. And one who possesses knowledge has the qualification for fire-establishment, because of capacity. Therefore the post-fire-establishment status does not apply to these, just as in the <s>Sthapati</s>-<s>iṣṭi</s>.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/431: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: cādhānādhikāraḥ}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/431: E1,6, E2 (variant reading); E2: <s>cādhānādhikāraḥ</s>}]

children.text: ādhānaṃ ca bhāryāsaṃyuktam // MS_6,8.13 //
children.translated_text: And fire-establishment is connected with [having] a wife. // MS_6,8.13 //

children.text: ādhānaṃ ca bhāryāsaṃyuktaṃ śrūyate. vidyāgrahaṇottarakālaś ca dārasaṃgrahaḥ. tasmād api nāvakalpate pūrvakālatādhānasya.
children.translated_text: And fire-establishment is heard as connected with [having] a wife. And the taking of a wife [comes] after the time of acquiring knowledge. Therefore too, the pre-fire-establishment status does not apply.

children.text: akarma cordhvam ādhānāt tatsamavāyo hi karmabhiḥ // MS_6,8.14 //
children.translated_text: And [marriage] is without ritual purpose after fire-establishment; for the connection of that [marriage] with ritual actions [is the basis]. // MS_6,8.14 //

children.text: tatrāha, yā pūrvam ādhānād dārakriyā, sā karmārthā bhaviṣyati, vacanāc cordhvam ādhānāt, apatyārthā. dvayor api kālayoḥ, piṇḍapitṛyajñavan naiṣa doṣo bhaviṣyatīti. atrocyate, akarma ca dārakriyā, yādhānottarakāle{*6/432*}. kutaḥ. āhavanīyādisamavāyo hi karmabhir bhavati, svārthaṇ ca [767]{*6/433*} agnaya ādhātavyā iti niyamaḥ. tasmād ubhayasminn api kāle dārasaṃgraha ity etat nāsti.
children.translated_text: [The objector] says: the marriage that [occurs] before fire-establishment will be for the purpose of ritual action, and [the marriage] after fire-establishment, by [Vedic] statement, will be for the purpose of offspring. At both times, there will be no fault, like the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> [which also applies in two contexts]. To this we reply: and the marriage that is after fire-establishment is without ritual purpose. Why? For the connection with ritual actions [requires] the connection with the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires], and the fires should be established for one's own purpose — this is the restriction. Therefore [the claim] that there is marriage at both times — this does not hold.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/432: E1,6; E2: dārakriyāyā ādhānottarakāle}*
*{6/433: E2: 5,361; E6: 2,213}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/432: E1,6; E2: <s>dārakriyāyā ādhānottarakāle</s>}]
[{6/433: E2: 5,361; E6: 2,213}]

children.text: śrāddhavad itit cet // MS_6,8.16 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues it is] like the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor-memorial rite) — // MS_6,8.16 //

children.text: naivam, śrutivipratiṣedho hi bhavati, evaṃ kriyamāṇe dārakarmaṇi vidyāgrahaṇottarakālaṃ śrūyamāṇam, pūrvaṃ kriyata iti vipratiṣiddham. arthād anyad evedam iti cet. na, arthaprāptasyaiva kālaniyama eṣaḥ. upanayanaṃ ca karmārtham. tad dvitīyasyāṃ vipratiṣidhyeta.
children.translated_text: This is not so — for there is a contradiction with <s>śruti</s>: when the marriage is performed thus, [it being] heard as [occurring] after the time of acquiring knowledge, [but now] being performed before — this is contradicted. [The objector says:] but this [marriage before initiation] is for a different purpose. No — this is a time-restriction of what is [already] obtained by its [natural] sense. And the initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) is for the purpose of ritual action. That [marriage] would be contradicted at the second [time].

children.text: sarvārthatvāc ca putrārtho na prayojayet // MS_6,8.17 //
children.translated_text: And because [marriage] is for all purposes, the purpose of [having] a son would not motivate [a second marriage]. // MS_6,8.17 //

children.text: athocyate, prāgādhānāc ca, karmārthaiva, ūrdhvaṃ cāpatyārthaivāsya bhaviṣyati. tenaivaṃ saty asya na kiṃcid virotsyata iti. ucyate, naitad evam. svārthā hi sā, na kevalam apatyārthatām eṣyati. tad uktam, phalotsāhāviśeṣād iti. tasmād api na dvir dārasaṃgrahaḥ. api caivaṃ smaryate, dharme cārthe ca kāme ca nāticaritavyeti. evaṃ saty aticaritā syāt. ato na{*6/434*} dvir dārasaṃgrahaḥ. ekaiva bhāryā karmārthāpatyārthā ca. tasyāś ca vidyāgrahaṇottarakālatā. ato nādhānasaṃskṛteṣv ete homā iti.
children.translated_text: And it is said: before fire-establishment, [marriage] is for the purpose of ritual action alone; and after, it will be for the purpose of offspring alone. Being thus, nothing will contradict for him. [We] reply: this is not so. For she [the wife] serves her own purpose — she will not merely serve the purpose of offspring. That was stated: 'because of no distinction in the incentive of the fruit.' Therefore too, there is no second marriage. Moreover, this is remembered (<s>smṛti</s>): 'In <s>dharma</s>, in <s>artha</s>, and in <s>kāma</s>, one should not transgress [the marriage bond].' Being thus, she would be transgressed. Therefore there is no second marriage. The wife is one alone — for the purpose of ritual action and for the purpose of offspring. And her [time comes] after acquiring knowledge. Therefore these oblations are not on fires refined by establishment.

children.text: somapānāt tu prāpaṇaṃ dvitīyasya tasmād upayacchet{*6/436*} // MS_6,8.18 //
children.translated_text: But because of <s>Soma</s>-drinking, the bringing-near of a second [wife]; therefore one should take [a wife]. // MS_6,8.18 //

children.text: gṛhyata etat, prāgupanayanān nāsti patnīti. yad uktam ekaiva patnīti. tan na mṛṣyate, yathaiva smṛtiḥ, dharme cārthe ca kāme ca nāticaritavyeti. dharmaprajāsaṃpanne dāre nānyāṃ kurvīteti ca. evam idam api smaryata eva, anyatarāpāye 'nyāṃ kurvīteti. tasmād yasya na dharmasaṃpannā, na prajāsaṃpannā vā patnī, so 'nyāṃ kurvīteti. somapānād iti cārthavādaṃ vyapadiśati sma. somapo na dvitīyāṃ jāyām abhyaṣūyata iti dvitīyām api jāyāṃ darśayati.
children.translated_text: This is accepted: before initiation there is no wife. As to what was said — 'there is only one wife' — that is not accepted. Just as the <s>smṛti</s> [says]: 'In <s>dharma</s>, in <s>artha</s>, and in <s>kāma</s>, one should not transgress' — [and] 'when the wife is accomplished in <s>dharma</s> and offspring, one should not take another.' Similarly this too is remembered: 'when one [wife] is lost, one should take another.' Therefore, for one whose wife is not accomplished in <s>dharma</s>, or not accomplished in offspring — he should take another. And [the sūtra] cites the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) regarding <s>Soma</s>-drinking: 'A <s>Soma</s>-drinker did not find fault with a second wife' — it shows [the possibility of] a second wife also.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/436: E1 (v.l.): upayaccheta}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/436: E1 (variant reading): <s>upayaccheta</s>}]

children.text: pitṛyajñe tu darśanāt prāgādhānāt pratīyeta // MS_6,8.19 //
children.translated_text: But in the ancestor-sacrifice, because of [Vedic] observation, it should be understood as before fire-establishment. // MS_6,8.19 //

children.text: atha kathaṃ pitṛyajñasya dvau kālāv iti. ucyate, vacanaṃ hi tatra dṛśyate. apyanāhitāgninā kāry iti. tasmāt prāgādhānāt pitṛyajña iti.
children.translated_text: Now, how does the ancestor-sacrifice have two times? [We] reply: for a statement is seen there — 'it should also be performed by one without established fires.' Therefore the ancestor-sacrifice [occurs] before fire-establishment.

children.text: sthapatīṣṭiḥ prayājavad agnyādheyaṃ prayojayet tādarthyāc cāpavṛjyeta // MS_6,8.20 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Sthapati</s>-<s>iṣṭi</s> is like [the case of] the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) — it would motivate fire-establishment; and because of being for that purpose, it would be relinquished [afterwards]. // MS_6,8.20 //

children.text: asti sthapatīṣṭiḥ, etayā niṣādasthapitaṃ yājayeteti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kim ādhānasaṃskṛteṣv agniṣu syāt, uta laukikeṣv iti. kiṃ prāptam. saṃskṛteṣv iti. katham. [769]{*6/437*} yadāhavanīye juhotītyevamādivacanāt. nanu śūdrasyāhavanīyābhāvān nāsti tasya śrutir iti. ucyate, sā hy āhavanīyaṃ prayojayet, yathā prayājān aśrutān prayojayati. evaṃ codakasāmarthyād iti. tādarthyāc cāpavṛjyeta. sthapatīṣṭyarthaṃ cāhitā agnayaḥ. tasyām apavṛktāyām{*6/438*} apavṛjyeran. dhāraṇaṃ hi teṣāṃ dṛṣṭakāryam āmnātam, atikrānte kārye na syād iti.
children.translated_text: There is the <s>Sthapati</s>-<s>iṣṭi</s> — 'by this [iṣṭi] one should cause the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s> to sacrifice.' There a doubt [arises]: should it [be performed] on fires refined by establishment, or on ordinary [fires]? What is the prima facie view? On refined [fires]. How? [769] Because of the statement 'one offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>' and the like. [The objector says:] but since the <s>Śūdra</s> has no <s>Āhavanīya</s>, there is no hearing [of Āhavanīya] for him. [We] reply: that [Vedic statement] would motivate [the creation of] an <s>Āhavanīya</s>, just as it motivates the <s>prayājas</s> which are not [directly] heard. Thus, by the capacity of the injunctive [statement]. And because of being for that purpose, [the fires] would be relinquished — the fires having been established for the purpose of the <s>Sthapati</s>-<s>iṣṭi</s>, when that [iṣṭi] is concluded, they would be relinquished. For their maintenance has been recorded as having a visible purpose; when the purpose has passed, it should not [continue].

children.text: api vā laukike 'gnau syād ādhānasyāsarvaśeṣatvāt // MS_6,8.21 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, it should be on ordinary fire, because fire-establishment does not serve all [purposes]. // MS_6,8.21 //

children.text: api veti pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ. laukikeṣv agniṣu syān na saṃskṛteṣu. kutaḥ. ādhānasyāsarvaśeṣatvāt. sarvakarmaśeṣabhūtā agnayaḥ, tadaṅgam ādhānam, na karmāṅgam. śrutyādīnām abhāvān na karmaprayuktādhānasya, vākyasāmarthyāc cāgniprayuktatvam. yac ca darśapūrṇamāsaprayuktam, tac codakena prāpyate, na dravyaprayuktam. tasmāl laukikeṣv agniṣu sthapatīṣṭir iti.
children.translated_text: The words '<s>api vā</s>' reverse the position. It should be on ordinary fires, not on refined [ones]. Why? Because fire-establishment does not serve all [purposes]. The fires serve all ritual actions; fire-establishment is their subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>), not a subsidiary of [individual] ritual actions. Because of the absence of <s>śruti</s> and the like, [there is] no fire-establishment motivated by ritual action; rather, because of the capacity of the sentence, [fire-establishment] is motivated by [the need for] fire. And what is motivated by the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is obtained through the injunctive [statement], not [what is] motivated by [specific ritual] substance. Therefore the <s>Sthapati</s>-<s>iṣṭi</s> [is performed] on ordinary fires.

children.text: avakīrṇipaśuś ca tadvad ādhānasyāprāptakālatvāt // MS_6,8.22 //
children.translated_text: And the animal [sacrifice] of one who has broken his vow (<s>avakīrṇin</s>) is likewise, because of fire-establishment not being of the proper time. // MS_6,8.22 //

children.text: asty avakīrṇipaśuḥ, brahmacāryavakīrṇī nairṛtaṃ gardabham ālabheteti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ tadartham ādhānaṃ kartavyam, uta laukikeṣv agniṣu tad varteteti. avakīrṇipaśuś ca [770]{*6/439*} tadvad ity adhikaraṇātideśaḥ. pūrvasyādhikaraṇasya yaḥ pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ{*6/440*}, so 'tra pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. yaḥ siddhāntaḥ, sa siddhāntaḥ. sarvārtham ādhānam, tasmād āhitāgniṣv iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. ādhānasyāprāptakālatvād iti siddhāntaḥ. aprāpto 'yam ādhānasya kāla ity etad uktam. tasmād idam api karma laukikeṣv iti.
children.translated_text: There is the animal [sacrifice] of the <s>avakīrṇin</s> (one who has broken the vow of celibacy): 'A <s>brahmacārin</s> who has broken his vow should slaughter a black donkey for <s>Nirṛti</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: should fire-establishment be performed for that purpose, or should it proceed on ordinary fires? The animal [sacrifice] of the <s>avakīrṇin</s> [770] is likewise — this is an extension of the [previous] <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic). The prima facie view of the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is the prima facie view here; the conclusion is the conclusion [here too]. [Namely:] fire-establishment serves all [purposes], therefore [it should be] on fires of one who has established [them] — this is the prima facie view. The conclusion is: because fire-establishment is not of the proper time — this time is not proper for fire-establishment — that was stated. Therefore this ritual action too [is performed] on ordinary [fires].

children.text: udagayanapūrvapakṣāhaḥ puṇyāheṣu daivāni smṛtirūpānyārthadarśanāt // MS_6,8.23 //
children.translated_text: Rites for the gods [should be performed] during the northward course [of the sun], the bright fortnight, daytime, [and] auspicious days — because of <s>smṛti</s>, form, and the observation of [texts serving] another purpose. // MS_6,8.23 //

children.text: daivāni karmāṇy udāharaṇam upanayanaprabhṛtīni. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kim aniyate kāle daivāni kartavyāni, utodagayanapūrvapakṣāhaḥ puṇyāheṣv iti. aniyata iti prāpte, udagayanādiṣv ity ucyate. kutaḥ. evaṃ smaranti, teṣu kāleṣu daivānīti. rūpārthavādaś ca. etad vai{*6/441*} devānāṃ rūpam, yad udagayanam, pūrvapakṣo 'ha iti{*6/442*}. na ca vayaṃ devādīnāṃ rūpam vidmaḥ. atha tv eṣu kāleṣu daivāni kriyante, tata etena{*6/443*} saṃbandhena rūpavacanam avakalpate. anyārthaṃ ca vākyam etad darśayati, pūrvāhno vai devānām, madhyaṃdino manuṣyāṇām, aparāhnaḥ pitṝṇām iti. tasmād eteṣu kāleṣu daivāni syur iti.
children.translated_text: Rites for the gods are the illustration — initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) and the like. There a doubt [arises]: should rites for the gods be performed at no fixed time, or during the northward course [of the sun], the bright fortnight, daytime, [and] auspicious days? When 'no fixed time' is the prima facie view, [we say:] during the northward course and the like. Why? [Because] thus it is remembered (<s>smṛti</s>) — that rites for the gods [should be performed] at those times. And [because of] the <s>arthavāda</s> of 'form': 'This indeed is the form of the gods — the northward course, the bright fortnight, daytime.' And we do not know the form of the gods and others. But since rites for the gods are performed at these times, therefore by this connection the statement of 'form' is made meaningful. And another [Vedic] sentence shows [the same] purpose: 'The forenoon belongs to the gods, midday to humans, the afternoon to the ancestors.' Therefore rites for the gods should be [performed] at these times.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/441: E1 (v.l.): etad vā}*
*{6/442: E1,6,E2 (v.l.); E2: pūrvapakṣāhar iti}*
*{6/443: E1,6; E2: tad etena}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/441: E1 (variant reading): <s>etad vā</s>}]
[{6/442: E1,6,E2 (variant reading); E2: <s>pūrvapakṣāhar iti</s>}]
[{6/443: E1,6; E2: <s>tad etena</s>}]

children.text: ahani ca karmasākalyam // MS_6,8.24 //
children.translated_text: And the completeness of the ritual [requires] daytime. // MS_6,8.24 //

children.text: ahani ca viśeṣaḥ, sakalaṃ karmāhany eva śakyate kartum iti, na rātrau kariṣyati.
children.translated_text: And there is a specification regarding daytime — the complete ritual can be performed in daytime only; one will not perform [it] at night.

children.text: itareṣu tu pitrāṇi{*6/445*} // MS_6,8.25 //
children.translated_text: But ancestral [rites at] the other [times]. // MS_6,8.25 //

children.text: śrāddhādīny aparapakṣe 'parāhne ca, smṛtirūpānyārthadarśanāt.
children.translated_text: <s>Śrāddha</s> and similar rites [are performed] in the dark fortnight and in the afternoon — because of the observation that <s>smṛti</s>-type [rules serve] another purpose.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/445: E1; E2,6: pitryāṇi}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/445: E1; E2,6: <s>pitryāṇi</s>}]

children.text: yāñcākrayaṇam avidyamāne lokavat // MS_6,8.26 //
children.translated_text: Requesting and purchasing [would apply only] when [the substance] is absent, like [in] the world. // MS_6,8.26 //

children.text: idaṃ samāmnāyate jyotiṣṭome, dvādaśa rātrīr dīkṣito bhṛtiṃ vanvīteti. tathā somaṃ krīṇātīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ yasya na vidyate bhṛtiḥ, tena vanitavyā, yasya ca na vidyate somaḥ, tena kretavyaḥ, utobhathāpi{*6/446*} sati cāsati ca. kiṃ prāptam. yāñcākrayaṇam avidyamāne bhṛtidhane some ca syāt. kasmāt. dravyasadbhāvārthaṃ{*6/447*} yāñcākrayaṇam, tad{*6/448*} vidyamāne 'narthakam. anarthakaṃ coktam api na kartavyam. tasmād avidyamāne bhavet, lokavat. yathā{*6/449*} yasya loke nāsti dravyam, sa yācate krīṇāti ca. evam ihāpi draṣṭavyam.
children.translated_text: This is recorded in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>: 'For twelve nights the consecrated one should win remuneration.' Likewise: 'He purchases <s>Soma</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: should only one who does not possess remuneration-wealth request it, and only one who does not possess <s>Soma</s> purchase it — or [should these be done] in both cases, whether [the substance] exists or not? What is the prima facie view? Requesting and purchasing [would apply only] when the remuneration-wealth and <s>Soma</s> are absent. Why? Requesting and purchasing are for the purpose of obtaining the substance; when [the substance already] exists, [these acts] are purposeless. And what is purposeless, even if stated, should not be done. Therefore it should apply [only] when [the substance] is absent — like [in] the world. Just as in the world, one who does not possess a substance requests and purchases [it] — so too here it should be understood.

children.text: niyataṃ vārthavattvāt syāt // MS_6,8.27 //
children.translated_text: Or [these acts] would be fixed [requirements], because of purposefulness. // MS_6,8.27 //

children.text: niyataṃ vā yāñcākrayaṇam, tad vidyamāne 'vidyamāne ca dravye syāt. evaṃ yāñcākrayaṇam arthavad bhavati{*6/450*}. jyotiṣṭomaprayuktaṃ hi tac chrūyate, na dravyaprayuktam. tac ca nityaṃ jyotiṣṭomasya. naivaṃ vacanaṃ bhavati, yadā dravyaṃ nāsti, tadā kartavyam iti. [772]{*6/451*} jyotiṣṭomasya ca nityam aṅgam uktam, dravyābhāvo nimittam uktam iti parikalpyeta, kalpanāyāṃ śabdo bādhyeta. ato yāñcākrayaṇasaṃskṛtaṃ dravyam ihopayoktavyam, anyathā vaiguṇyaṃ bhavati. tasmāt sati cāsati ca dravye yāñcākrayaṇam anuṣṭātavyam iti. atha yad uktam, lokavad iti. loke karma arthalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati, na śabdalakṣaṇam, yathārthaḥ, tathā kriyate. na, yathā śabdaḥ. vede tu śabdenaivārtho 'vagamyate, tathaivānuṣṭheyam iti. tasmād vidyamāne 'pi kartavyam.
children.translated_text: Or requesting and purchasing are fixed [requirements] — they would apply whether the substance exists or not. Thus requesting and purchasing become purposeful. For they are heard as connected with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, not connected with [the absence of] the substance. And they are permanent [subsidiaries] of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. The statement is not thus: 'when the substance is absent, then it should be done.' [772] And if it were postulated that what is stated as a permanent subsidiary of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is [actually] occasioned by the absence of substance, the [Vedic] word would be overridden by the postulation. Therefore the substance refined by requesting and purchasing is to be employed here; otherwise there would be deficiency. Therefore, whether the substance exists or not, requesting and purchasing must be performed. Now, as to what was said — 'like [in] the world' — in the world, action is characterized by purpose, not characterized by [Vedic] word; as the purpose [requires], so it is done — not as the [Vedic] word [states]. But in the Veda, the meaning is understood by the word itself, and is to be performed exactly so. Therefore even when [the substance already] exists, it should be done.

children.text: tathā bhakṣapraiṣāc chādanasaṃjñaptahomadveṣam // MS_6,8.28 //
children.translated_text: Likewise [this principle applies to] the food-command (<s>bhakṣapraiṣa</s>), covering (<s>chādana</s>), consecration-offering (<s>saṃjñaptahoma</s>), and enmity-[formula] (<s>dveṣa</s>). // MS_6,8.28 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, payo vrataṃ brāhmaṇasya yavāgū rājanyasya, āmikṣā vaiśyasyeti. tathā darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ praiṣaḥ, prokṣaṇīr āsādaya, idhmaṃ bahir upasādaya srucaḥ saṃmṛḍḍhi{*6/452*} patnīṃ saṃnahyājyenodehīti. tathā vājapeye śrūyate, darbhamayaṃ vāso bhavatīti. paśau saṃjñaptahomaḥ, yat paśur māyum akṛtoro{*6/453*} vā padbhir āhata agnir mā tasmād enaso viśvān muñcatvaṃ hasa iti. tathā, yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma iti vacanam. etāny udāharaṇavacanāni.
teṣu saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ yasyāparaṃ bhojanaṃ na vidyate, sa payo vratayet, yavāgūm āmikṣāṃ vā, uta{*6/454*} vidyamāne 'pīti. tathā yo preṣitaḥ praiṣārthaṃ na pratipadyate, sa preṣitavyaḥ, uta pratipadyamāno 'pīti. tathā, yasya sūtramayaṃ vāso nāsti, sa darbhamayaṃ paridadhīta, uta vidyamāne 'pīti. tathā, yasya paśur māyum kuryāt, uro vā pādau vā hanyāt{*6/455*}, sa etena mantreṇa juhuyāt, utānyo 'pīti. tathā, yo dveṣṭi kiṃcit, [773]{*6/456*} anyena ca dviṣyate, sa eva mantraṃ brūyāt, yo 'smān dveṣṭīti, utādviṣann adviṣyamāṇaś cāpīti.
tatrādhikaraṇātideśo 'yam. tatra yaḥ pūrvasminn adhikaraṇe pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, sa iha pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. yas tatra siddhāntaḥ, sa iha siddhāntaḥ. avidyamāne kuryād iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ. niyataṃ vārthavattvād{*6/457*} ity uttaraḥ. sa evātra nyāyaḥ, yaḥ pūrvatra{*6/458*}.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'Milk is the <s>vrata</s>-[diet] of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; gruel of a <s>Rājanya</s>; curdled milk of a <s>Vaiśya</s>.' Likewise in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> there is the command (<s>praiṣa</s>): 'Set down the sprinkling waters; place the fuel and <s>barhis</s>; clean the ladles; gird the wife; pour with ghee.' Likewise in the <s>Vājapeya</s> it is heard: 'The garment is made of <s>darbha</s> grass.' In the animal [sacrifice] there is the consecration-offering: 'When the animal has made a bleating sound or has kicked with its feet — 'O <s>Agni</s>, free me from all that sin'' — thus one offers. Likewise [there is] the statement: 'He who hates us and whom we hate.' These are illustrative statements.
Regarding them, a doubt [arises]: should one observe milk as the <s>vrata</s>-[diet] only when one has no other food — or gruel or curdled milk — or even when [other food] exists? Likewise, should one who has been commanded but does not comply with the purpose of the command be commanded [again], or even one who is complying? Likewise, should one who does not have a thread garment put on a <s>darbha</s>-grass garment, or even when [thread] exists? Likewise, should one whose animal makes a bleating sound or strikes with chest or feet offer with this <s>mantra</s>, or another [sacrificer] too? Likewise, should only one who actually hates someone and is hated by someone recite the <s>mantra</s> 'he who hates us,' or even one who does not hate and is not hated?
Here there is an extension of the [previous] <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic). The prima facie view of the earlier <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is the prima facie view here too. The established conclusion there is the established conclusion here. 'It should be done when [the condition] is absent' is the prima facie view. 'Or [it] is fixed, because of purposefulness' is the latter [view]. The same principle applies here as in the former [case].

children.text: anarthakaṃ tv anityaṃ syāt // MS_6,8.29 //
children.translated_text: What is purposeless would be non-fixed. // MS_6,8.29 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome śrūyate, madhyaṃdine 'pararātre vā{*6/459*} vrataṃ vratayatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ niyatam apararātre vratam, utāniyatam iti. kiṃ prāptam. niyataṃ cārthavattvāt{*6/460*} syād iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, anarthakaṃ tv anityaṃ syāt. yadaivam manyeta, asmin kāle vrataṃ me jariṣyatīti, tadā vratayet. yadā tu khalu manyeta, na samyag jariṣyatīti, tadā tadvrataṃ kriyamāṇam anarthakaṃ syāt. yadi hy ajīrṇena yajamāno mriyeta, tadā tantralopaḥ, tantralope ca sarvalopaḥ. tasmād{*6/461*} aniyataṃ{*6/462*} tasmin kāle vrataṃ vratayitavyam iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: 'At midday or in the last watch of the night one observes the <s>vrata</s>.' There a doubt [arises]: is the <s>vrata</s> necessarily [observed] in the last watch of the night, or [is it] non-fixed? What is the prima facie view? It would be fixed, because of purposefulness. Given this prima facie view, we say: what is purposeless would be non-fixed. Whenever one thinks 'at this time the <s>vrata</s> [food] will be digested for me,' then one should observe the vrata. But when one thinks 'it will not be properly digested,' then that <s>vrata</s> being performed would be purposeless. For if the sacrificer were to die from indigestion, there would be a loss of the whole [ritual] system (<s>tantra</s>), and in the loss of the system, there is total loss. Therefore it is non-fixed — [the rule that] the <s>vrata</s> must be observed at that time.

children.text: paśucodanāyām aniyamo 'viśeṣāt // MS_6,8.30 //
children.translated_text: In the injunction regarding the animal, there is no restriction [as to species], because of non-distinction. // MS_6,8.30 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome paśur agnīṣomīyaḥ, yo{*6/463*} dīkṣito yad agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabhata iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ yaḥ kaścit paśur ā[774]{*6/464*}lambhīyaḥ, uta chāga iti. vakṣyamāṇenābhiprāyeṇa bhavati saṃśayaḥ. nanv ekeṣām āmnāyate, ajo 'gnīṣomīya iti. sarvaśākhāpratyayaṃ caikaṃ karmeti. atrocyate, pratiśākhaṃ bhinnāni karmāṇīti kṛtvā cintā. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. paśucodanāyām aniyamaḥ. utsarge kartavye dravyaṃ śakyata utsraṣṭum, na paśutvam. dravyaṃ hi sādhakam. ato 'tra dravyam antreṇotsargo na saṃbhavatīti dravyam upādīyate. tasminn upādīyamāne 'niyamaḥ, yatkiṃcid utsraṣṭavyam iti. kuta etat. aviśeṣāt. na hi paśutvasaṃbaddheṣu kaścid viśeṣa upalabhyate. tasmād yaḥ kaścit paśur iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal — 'the consecrated one slaughters the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.' There a doubt [arises]: should any animal whatsoever be slaughtered, or [only] a goat? The doubt arises from the following consideration. Some [Vedic schools] record: 'A goat is the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal].' And 'there is one ritual [common to] all Vedic schools.' To this we say: the investigation proceeds on the assumption that the rituals are different for each school. What, then, is the prima facie view? In the injunction regarding the animal, there is no restriction. When a release [of the animal] is to be made, the substance can be released, not the [generic] animal-nature. For the substance is what is efficacious. Hence here, without a substance, the release is not possible — so a substance is adopted. When [a substance is] being adopted, [there is] no restriction — whatever [animal] is to be released. Why? Because of non-distinction — for among those connected with animal-nature, no distinction is observed. Therefore any animal whatsoever.

children.text: chāgo vā mantravarṇāt // MS_6,8.31 //
children.translated_text: Or [it should be] a goat, because of the <s>mantra</s>-content. // MS_6,8.31 //

children.text: vāśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad asti. yatra kvacana dravye paśutvam upādeyam iti. asty utsraṣṭavyasya niyamakāraṇaṃ mantravarṇaḥ. agnaye chāgasya vayāyā{*6/465*} medaso 'nubrūhīti, chāgaprakāśanasamartho mantravarṇaḥ samāmnāyate. yadi chāgo nopādeyaḥ, tatas tatprakāśanasamarthasyopādānam anarthavat. tenāvagamyate, chāgam adhikṛtyotsargaṃ vidadhātīti. māntravarṇiko dravyaniyamavidhir iti.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' reverses the position. This is not so — that animal-nature should be adopted in any substance whatsoever. There is a cause for restricting what is to be released — the <s>mantra</s>-content. 'Recite [the <s>anuvākyā</s>] for [a cake] of <s>Agni</s>, for the fat of a goat' — a <s>mantra</s>-content capable of revealing the goat is recorded. If the goat is not to be adopted, then the adoption of [a mantra-content] capable of revealing it would be purposeless. From this it is understood that [the text] prescribes the release with reference to a goat. [This is] a restriction of substance by the <s>mantra</s>-content.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/465: E1; E2: mantravarṇaḥ. chāgasya vapāyā; E6: mantravarṇaḥ. agnaye chāgasya vapāyā}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/465: E1; E2: <s>mantravarṇaḥ. chāgasya vapāyā</s>; E6: <s>mantravarṇaḥ. agnaye chāgasya vapāyā</s>}]

children.text: na, codanāvirodhāt // MS_6,8.32 //
children.translated_text: No, because of conflict with the injunction. // MS_6,8.32 //

children.text: naitad evam. na śaknoti mantravarṇaś codanāyāṃ pratyarthinyāṃ dravyaṃ niyantum. yatra hi dravyasya prakāśakaṃ na śrūyate, tatrāprakāśitam eva tat kartavyam iti. tasmān na mantravarṇāt prakāśyaniyamavidhiḥ kalpyate, evam atra prakāśyaṃ prakāśayitavyam iti. [775]{*6/466*} atra punaḥ śabdenāvagamyate, paśutvena prakāśayitavyam iti. tasmān na mantravarṇas tatsadbhāve samarthaḥ. mantravarṇād dhi kalpyā prayogavacanaśrutiḥ{*6/467*}. iha kḷptā prayogavacanenopasaṃhartavyā. anya eva paśuśabdasyārthaḥ paśutvam. anyo mantravarṇena niyamyate chāgaḥ. tasmān na mantravarṇaś codanāvirodhena niyantum arhatīti.
children.translated_text: This is not so. The <s>mantra</s>-content cannot restrict the substance when the injunction is in opposition. For where no revealer of the substance is heard, there that [substance], unrevealed, is to be employed [as is]. Therefore, from the <s>mantra</s>-content, a restriction of what is to be revealed is not to be postulated. [The objection:] '[But] thus here the revealed [substance] should be revealed [i.e., specified].' [775] Here rather, it is understood by the [Vedic] word that [the substance] is to be revealed through animal-nature. Therefore the <s>mantra</s>-content is not capable [of establishing a restriction] when that [injunction] exists. For from the <s>mantra</s>-content, the <s>śruti</s> of the performance-statement would have to be postulated. But here [the śruti] is [already] established — it is to be gathered by the performance-statement. The meaning of the word '<s>paśu</s>' (animal) is animal-nature — something different [from what] is restricted by the <s>mantra</s>-content as 'goat.' Therefore the <s>mantra</s>-content, in conflict with the injunction, does not deserve to restrict.

children.text: ārṣeyavad iti cet // MS_6,8.33 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] like the <s>Ārṣeya</s> [case] — // MS_6,8.33 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, na paśutvam anyebhyaḥ paśubhya ācchetavyam iti. yathā, ārṣeyaṃ vṛṇīte, trīn vṛṇīta iti, sāmānyaśrutis triṣv evāvatiṣṭhata iti. tritvaṃ viśeṣo{*6/468*} vivakṣito nānye vivakṣitā iti. evam ihāpi paśutvam, chāgaṃ prakalpayitum vivakṣitam, nānyān viśeṣān iti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that animal-nature should not be taken from other animals — [then consider:] just as 'he chooses the <s>Ārṣeya</s> [Sāman]; he should choose three' — [where] the general <s>śruti</s> settles precisely on three — [meaning] the number three is the intended specification, not others — so too here, animal-nature is intended to establish the goat, not other specifications.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{6/468: E1,6; E2: tritvaviśeṣo}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{6/468: E1,6; E2: <s>tritvaviśeṣo</s>}]

children.text: na, tatra hy acoditatvāt // MS_6,8.34 //
children.translated_text: No, because there [in the Ārṣeya case] the substance is un-enjoined. // MS_6,8.34 //

children.text: naitad evam. tatra hy acoditaṃ dravyam utsraṣṭavyam, mantravarṇe. varaṇe punaś coditam. tatra tritvasaṃkhyāsaṃbandhasya varaṇe coditatvāt, nānyā saṃkhyā kriyate. ārṣeyaśabdād api nānārṣeyam. triśabdasya hi tatsāmarthyam, yenārṣeyaśabdo viśiṣṭasaṃkhyāviṣayo niyamyate. iha na mantrasya sāmarthyam. tasmād aniyama iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so. For there, in the <s>mantra</s>-content, the substance to be released is un-enjoined. But in the selection [of Sāmans], [the number] is enjoined. There, because the connection with the number three is enjoined in the selection, no other number is made. And from the word '<s>ārṣeya</s>' too, [it refers] to what belongs to the <s>Ṛṣis</s>. For that word '<s>tri</s>' (three) has such power that the word '<s>ārṣeya</s>' is restricted to the domain of a specific number. Here the <s>mantra</s> does not have [such] power. Therefore [there is] no restriction.

children.text: niyamo vaikāryaṃ hy arthabhedād bhedaḥ pṛthaktvenābhidhānāt // MS_6,8.35 //
children.translated_text: Or there would be a restriction — for because of difference of meaning, [there is] distinction; [and this is known] from being stated separately. // MS_6,8.35 //

children.text: niyamo vā. aikārthyaṃ hi paśuchāgaśabdayoḥ, sāmānyaṃ paśur iti, chāgādayo viśeṣā ucyante. katham. taiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyāt, paśuś chāgaḥ, paśur uṣṭraḥ, paśur meṣaḥ, paśur usra iti. evaṃ sati na mantravarṇaḥ paśuśabdena virudhyate. tena chāgo [776]{*6/469*} 'py ālabdhavyaś coditaḥ. mantravarṇa upādīyamāne, idam avagamyate. chāgaṃ vivakṣitvāyaṃ paśuśabda uccarita iti, nānyān viśeṣān iti. chāgopakaraṇam asyopadaṃśitam. yad upadaṃśane paśuśabdaś chāgābhiprāya iti gamyate, yathā yugavaratra upadaṃśite{*6/470*}, īṣācakrādisaṃnidhāne ced{*6/471*} akṣamānayety{*6/472*} ucyate{*6/473*}, tadā, yānākṣam adhikṛtya brūta iti gamyate, na tu videvanākṣam iti. yadi hy arthabhedo bhavet paśuchāgaśabdayoḥ, pṛthaktvenābhidhānam, tato bhedaḥ syāt, na chāga eva niyamyeta. avihitaś chāgārtha ity aśvopādānam. api ca chāgapakṣe taṃ mantravarṇaḥ prakāśayet. chāgārthābhidhāne punaḥ paśuśabdasya, chāgaprāptāv anyeṣām aprāptir ity anyasmin prāpte liṅgena niyamaḥ kriyata iti.
children.translated_text: Or there would be a restriction. For the words '<s>paśu</s>' (animal) and '<s>chāga</s>' (goat) have identity of meaning — '<s>paśu</s>' is the genus; goat and such are called the species. How? Because of co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with them — 'an animal [that is] a goat,' 'an animal [that is] a camel,' 'an animal [that is] a ram,' 'an animal [that is] a bull.' This being so, the <s>mantra</s>-content does not contradict the word '<s>paśu</s>.' Therefore the goat too is enjoined to be slaughtered. [776] When the <s>mantra</s>-content is adopted, this is understood: having intended the goat, this word '<s>paśu</s>' is uttered — not other specifications. Its accessory is the goat, [which is] its complement. When the complement is [taken together with '<s>paśu</s>'], the word '<s>paśu</s>' is understood as intending 'goat' — just as when a yoke-strap is complemented [by other cart-parts], if in the presence of pole, wheel, and such one says 'bring the axle,' then it is understood [as] 'bring the axle of the cart' — not 'bring an axle [for weaving].' If there were a difference of meaning between the words '<s>paśu</s>' and '<s>chāga</s>', [i.e.,] a separate designation, then there would be [real] distinction, and [it] would not be restricted to the goat alone. [Then] the goat-meaning would be un-enjoined, and one would have to adopt a horse. Moreover, in the goat-view, the <s>mantra</s>-content would reveal it. But when the word '<s>paśu</s>' has the meaning of 'goat,' [then] upon the goat being obtained, the non-obtainment of others [follows] — [thus] when another [reading] is obtained [as prima facie], the restriction is made by the indicatory sign.

children.text: aniyamo vārthāntaratvād anyatvaṃ vyatirekaśabdabhedābhyām // MS_6,8.36 //
children.translated_text: Or there is no restriction, because of being a different entity; the difference [is established] by exclusion and word-distinction. // MS_6,8.36 //

children.text:
aniyamo vā. yaḥ kaścit paśur upādeyaḥ, arthāntaratvāt. arthāntaraṃ paśutvam, arthāntaraṃ chāgatvam, arthayor atra sāmānādhikaraṇyam, na śabdayoḥ. kathaṃ punar arthāntaraṃ gamyate. vyatirekāc chabdabhedāc ca, vyatireko{*6/474*} hi bhavati, kaścit paśur na chāgaḥ. tathā chāgaḥ paśur iti śabdabhedaḥ. śabdabhedād evārthabhedo nyāyyaḥ. ekasmin vākye samavāyāt, paśuṃ chāgam ānayeti. itarathā, anyatareṇa kṛtārthatvād anyataro vākye na samaveyāt, samavaiti ca. tasmād anyat paśutvam, anyac chāgatvam. tasmād aniyamaḥ, yaḥ kaścit paśur upādeya iti{*6/475*}.
tatrotsūtrikā{*6/476*} pakṣavyāvṛttiḥ, anyatve 'pi sati niyama eva. [777]{*6/477*} kutaḥ. mantrasya prayogavacanena gṛhītatvāt. mantrasādhanaṃ hi karmeti gamyate. yadi chāgam upādāsyāmahe, saguṇaṃ karma śakṣāmaḥ{*6/478*} kartum, mantram upādadānāḥ, mantrasyāpākṣikatvāt. athānyam upādāsyāmahe, mantrasya viṣayābhāvān mantram apajahato na saguṇaṃ karma nirvartayema, ato{*6/479*} na ca śrutiṃ bādhāmahe, anyasmin paśuśabdo vartata iti. na cānyam{*6/480*} upādāsyāmahe, vaiguṇyād bibhyataḥ. tasmāc chāga evopādātavya iti.
nanv aśvam upādadānā{*6/481*} naiva mantravarṇam apahāsyāmaḥ. sa evāśvaś chāgo bhaviṣyati. yaś chinnagamano 'śvaḥ, sa chāgaḥ, chider gameś ca cchāgaśabdaḥ prasiddhaḥ{*6/482*}.
children.translated_text:
Or there is no restriction. Whatever animal may be adopted [is acceptable], because of being a different entity. Animal-ness is one entity; goat-ness is another entity — [it is] a co-reference of the meanings, not of the words. But how is it understood to be a different entity? By exclusion and word-distinction — for there is exclusion: some animal is not a goat. Likewise, 'goat' and 'animal' are word-distinctions. From word-distinction alone, a difference of meaning is proper. Because of co-occurrence in a single sentence — 'bring an animal, a goat.' Otherwise, since the purpose is fulfilled by either one, the other would not co-occur in the sentence — but it does co-occur. Therefore animal-ness is different [from] goat-ness. Therefore there is no restriction — whatever animal is to be adopted.
Thereupon, [there is] a counter-argument reversing the position: even when they are different, there is indeed restriction. [777] Why? Because [the word 'goat'] is grasped through the application-statement of the mantra. For it is understood that the ritual action has the mantra as its instrument. If we adopt a goat, we will be able to perform the ritual act with its qualities, employing the mantra, since the mantra is contingent [on the animal]. But if we adopt another [animal], because of the absence of an object for the mantra, we, having abandoned the mantra, would not accomplish the ritual act with its qualities. Nor would we override the [Vedic] text, [since] the word 'animal' applies to another [as well]. And we would not adopt another, fearing deficiency. Therefore only a goat should be adopted.
[The objector says:] but even adopting a horse, we would not at all abandon the literal meaning of the mantra. That very horse will be [called] a goat. A horse whose movement is cut off (<s>chinnagamana</s>) is a goat (<s>chāga</s>), for the word <s>chāga</s> is well known [as derived] from [the roots] <s>chid</s> (to cut) and <s>gam</s> (to go).

Because of form and characteristic mark. // MS_6,8.37 //
Somewhere it is heard that there will be <s>muṣkaras</s> (testicled [animals]). If without [this] statement, [the animals would be] non-testicled — this is appropriate. Therefore, even a horse whose movement is cut off would be a goat — this will be a nominal designation based on action. To this we reply:

children.text:
chāge na karmākhyā rūpaliṅgābhyām // MS_6,8.38 //{*6/486*}
chāge karmākhyā rūpaliṅgābhyāṃ nāvakalpate. na hi chāgaśabdaś chinnagamanavacanaḥ, samudāyo hy asau pṛthag arthāntare prasiddhaḥ, nāsāv avayavaprasiddhyā bādhitavyaḥ. tasmān nāśvaś chāgaḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the case of a goat, the action-designation is not [applicable], because of form and characteristic mark. // MS_6,8.38 //
The action-designation is not applicable in the case of a goat, because of form and characteristic mark. For the word <s>chāga</s> (goat) is not a word denoting 'cutting of movement' — for that [word] is a composite (<s>samudāya</s>) well known in a different, independent meaning. That [composite meaning] should not be overridden by the well-known meanings of the component parts. Therefore a horse is not a goat.

children.text:
rūpānyatvān na jātiśabdaḥ syāt // MS_6,8.39 //{*6/487*}
idam anyapadottaraṃ{*6/488*} sūtram. atha kasmān na vayovacano [778]{*6/489*} bhavati vayovacanā hy ete śabdāḥ, chāgaś chāgalo vatsa iti. tenāśvo 'pi vayovacano bhaviṣyatīti. ucyate, naitad evam, satyaṃ vayovacanaḥ. ajāpatigataṃ{*6/490*} tu vayo vaditum śaknoti, yathā śoṇa iti varṇavacano 'śvajātigataṃ varṇaṃ vadati, nānyam. tasmād rūpānyatvān na vayomātravacanaḥ, kiṃ tu jātiśabdaḥ syāt. jātyāśrayaṃ vayo vadet. ataś chāga eva niyamyate.
children.translated_text:
Because of the difference of form, it would be a class-word (<s>jātiśabda</s>), not [merely an age-word]. // MS_6,8.39 //
This <s>sūtra</s> follows upon another thesis. Now, why is [the word <s>chāga</s>] not an age-designation? [778] For these words are age-designations — <s>chāga</s>, <s>chāgala</s>, <s>vatsa</s>. Therefore '<s>aśva</s>' (horse) too would be an age-designation. [We] reply: this is not so. True, [<s>chāga</s>] is an age-designation. But it can denote the age [only] of the goat species (<s>ajāpati</s>) — just as <s>śoṇa</s> ('red') is a color-word that denotes the color [only] of the horse species, not of another. Therefore, because of the difference of form, it is not merely an age-designation, but rather it would be a class-word (<s>jātiśabda</s>). It would denote the age dependent on the class. Hence [the restriction] to a goat alone is established.

children.text:
vikāro notpattikatvāt{*6/491*} // MS_6,8.40 //{*6/492*}
idam api padottaram. ihāśvādīnāṃ vikāraś chāgaśabdaḥ. kiṃcid atrāśvādīnām uccāryate, na{*6/493*} kiṃcid anyad eva. tasmād āśvo 'pi chāga iti. na, utpattikatvāt{*6/494*}. autpattiko hi nāmināmnoḥ saṃbandha ity uktam{*6/495*}, nākhyāvikāraḥ saṃbhavatīti. tasmān nāśvaś chāgaḥ. ataś chāga evopādātvaya iti.
children.translated_text:
[It is] not a modification [of name], because of [the name-referent relation] being innate (<s>autpattika</s>). // MS_6,8.40 //
This too follows upon [the previous thesis]. Here, the word <s>chāga</s> is a modification of [the names for] horses and the like. Something of the horses and the like is [partially] expressed [by it], and something else entirely [is also expressed]. Therefore a horse too is a goat. [We reply:] no — because of [the relation] being innate. For it has been stated that the relation between name and named is innate — a modification of designation is not possible. Therefore a horse is not a goat. Hence only a goat should be adopted.

children.text:
sa naimittikaḥ paśor guṇasyācoditatvāt // MS_6,8.41 //{*6/496*}
padottaram evedaṃ sūtram. atha kasmān na chidranimittaś chāgaśabdo bhavati. evaṃ śrūyate, śuṣiro{*6/497*} vā etarhi paśuḥ. yarhi vapām utkhadantīti{*6/498*}. nety ucyate, chidratvasya guṇasya paśor acoditatvāt. avyaṅgaṃ paśum ālabheteti hi codyate. tasmād acchidraḥ paśuḥ. na cāvayavaprasiddhyā samudāyaprasiddhir bādhyata ity uktam eva. tasmāc chāga evopādeyo nāśvādaya iti.
children.translated_text:
That [word <s>chāga</s>] is occasioned [by certain properties], [but] the quality of having a hole is not enjoined for the animal. // MS_6,8.41 //
This <s>sūtra</s> too follows upon [the previous thesis]. Now, why is the word <s>chāga</s> not occasioned by [the notion of] a hole (<s>chidra</s>)? For thus it is heard: 'The animal is indeed hollow (<s>śuṣira</s>) at that time — when they extract the <s>vapā</s> (omentum).' [We] reply: no — because the quality of having a hole (<s>chidratva</s>) is not enjoined for the animal. For it is enjoined: 'One should immolate an unblemished (<s>avyaṅga</s>) animal.' Therefore the animal [should be] without a hole. And it has already been stated that the well-known meaning of the composite is not overridden by the well-known meanings of the component parts. Therefore only a goat should be adopted, not a horse or others.

children.text:
jāter vā tatprāyavacanārthavattvābhyām // MS_6,8.42 //{*6/500*}
vāśabdo 'vadhāraṇāyām. yasmād avayavaprasiddhyā samudāyaprasiddhir na bādhyate. tasmāj jāter eva chāgaśabdo vācakaḥ. evaṃ samudāyasyārthavattānugṛhītā bhaviṣyatīti tatprāyavacanam{*6/501*} upapadyate. viśveṣāṃ devānām usrāṇāṃ chāgānāṃ meṣāṇāṃ vapānāṃ medaso 'nubrūhīti jātiprāye vacanam upapadyate. prāyeṇāpi hi niyamaḥ kriyate, yathā, agryaprāye likhitaṃ dṛṣṭvāgnyo 'yam iti buddhir bhavati. tasmāc chāga evopādātavya iti. kṛtvācintāyāṃ prayojanaṃ na vaktavyam.
children.translated_text:
Or rather, [the word is] of [the whole] class, because of [the composite's] meaningfulness and [its being used] predominantly for that. // MS_6,8.42 //
The word <s>vā</s> ('or') is for emphasis. Since the well-known meaning of the composite is not overridden by the well-known meanings of the parts, therefore the word <s>chāga</s> is expressive only of the class. Thus, the meaningfulness of the composite will be upheld, and the predominantly-for-that usage is also appropriate. 'Of the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, of cows, of goats, of rams — recite [the formulas] for the <s>vapās</s> and the fat' — the usage is appropriate when referring predominantly to the class. For restriction is made even by predominant usage — just as when something is written predominantly with fire-like [characters], upon seeing it, the cognition 'this is fire' arises. Therefore only a goat should be adopted. The purpose [of this inquiry] need not be stated when deliberation has been completed.

children.text: śrutipramāṇatvāc cheṣāṇāṃ mukhyabhede yathādhikāraṃ bhāvaḥ syāt // MS_7,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Because of the authority of <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text), when there is a division of the principal [rites], the subsidiaries (<s>śeṣa</s>) should belong according to [their] domain (<s>adhikāra</s>). // MS_7,1.1 //

children.text:
pūrveṇādhyāyaṣaṭkena pratyakṣavihitadharmaṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ darśapūrṇamāsādīnām itikartavyatā cintitā. uttareṇedānīm avihitetikartavyatākeṣv aindrāgnādiṣu cintayitum iṣyate. tatra yadi darśapūrṇamāsādīnāṃ prakaraṇe ye vihitā dharmāḥ, te sarvakarmasu vihitā bhavanti, tatas tair eva dharmair aindrāgnādayo 'pi dharmavanta uktāḥ, tathā kartavyāś ceti. nārtha uttareṇa ṣaṭkena. atha ye yasya prakaraṇa ucyante, te tatraivoktā bhavanti, tato 'dharmakāṇy aindrāgnīdīni. teṣu{*7/1*} cintā bhavati, kim eṣāṃ dharmāḥ santi, uta neti. yadā ca santi, tadā ke kiyanto vā kathaṃ cānuṣṭātavyā iti. tad artham uttaraḥ ṣaṭkaḥ pravartanīyaḥ{*7/2*}.
tatra saptamena tāvat santi dharmā ity ucyate. aṣṭamena ceme 'syeti. itthaṃ prayoktavyā iti navamena. daśam aikādaśadvādaśair etāvantaḥ prayoktavyāḥ, nāto 'dhikā iti.
tatredaṃ vicāryate, kiṃ yajiprayuktā ete dharmāḥ, kathaṃ yajir guṇavān syād ity evam artham āmnāyante, āhosvid apūrvaprayuktāḥ. katham apūrvaṃ syād iti. yadi yajiprayuktāḥ, [2]{*7/3*} tataḥ sarvārthāḥ. athāpūrvaprayuktāḥ, tato yathāprakaraṇaṃ vyavatiṣṭhante. kiṃ punar atra yuktam. apūrvaprayuktā iti. apūrvaṃ hi phalavat. aphalo yajiḥ. phalavati ca prayāso vidhīyamāno 'rthavān bhavati. tasmād apūrvaprayuktā dharmāḥ{*7/4*}. ataḥ paramācāryasya sūtropanyāsaḥ, śrutipramāṇatvāc cheṣāṇāṃ mukhyabhede yathādhikāraṃ bhāvaḥ syād iti. mukhyāny apūrvāṇi. tāni hi phalavattvāt pradhānāni, pradhāne ca mukhyaśabdaḥ. teṣāṃ bheda uktaḥ śabdāntarādibhir hetubhiḥ. tasmin mukhyabhede sati yathādhikāraṃ bhāvaḥ syāt, śeṣāṇām. ye yasyāpūrvasyādhikāre prakaraṇe{*7/5*} śiṣyante, te tasyaiva bhaveyuḥ. śrutipramāṇatvād ayam asyāpūrvasya śeṣaḥ, ayam asyety atra śrutir eva pramāṇaṃ kramate. na pratyakṣādīnām anyatamat. śrutyā ca ye yasya prakaraṇe śrūyante, te tasyaiva bhavitum arhanti. na cānyasyokto 'rtho 'nyasya bhavati. na hi yad devadattasya grāmāc chādanādikam, tad yajñadattasya bhavati. tasmād yathāprakaraṇaṃ vyavasthā dharmāṇām.
children.translated_text:
In the preceding six chapters (<s>adhyāyas</s>), the procedure for ritual acts such as the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and others, whose <s>dharmas</s> (ritual properties) are directly prescribed, has been investigated. Now, with the subsequent [chapters], it is desired to investigate the <s>Aindrāgna</s> and other [rites] whose procedural details are not [directly] prescribed. There, if the <s>dharmas</s> prescribed in the context of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and others are prescribed for all ritual acts, then by those very <s>dharmas</s> the <s>Aindrāgna</s> and others too have been declared to possess [ritual] properties and should be performed accordingly. [In that case,] there is no need for the subsequent six chapters. But if those that are stated in one [rite's] context belong only to that [rite], then the <s>Aindrāgna</s> and others are without [prescribed] properties. Regarding them, the inquiry arises: do they have <s>dharmas</s>, or not? And when they do have them, which ones, how many, and how are they to be performed? For this purpose, the subsequent six chapters are to be set forth.
In these, the seventh [chapter] first states that there are <s>dharmas</s>. The eighth [states] 'these are its [dharmas].' 'They should be employed in this manner' [is stated] by the ninth. The tenth, eleventh, and twelfth [state that] 'this many are to be employed — no more than this.'
Here, this is investigated: are these <s>dharmas</s> motivated by the sacrifice (<s>yaji</s>) — recorded for the purpose of making the sacrifice possessive of qualities — or are they motivated by the unprecedented [result] (<s>apūrva</s>) — [recorded] for the purpose of producing the <s>apūrva</s>? If motivated by the sacrifice, [2] then they serve all [rites]. But if motivated by the <s>apūrva</s>, then they are established according to [their] context. Now, what is proper here? [They are] motivated by the <s>apūrva</s>. For the <s>apūrva</s> is fruitful. The sacrifice [itself] is fruitless. And effort enjoined in connection with what is fruitful becomes meaningful. Therefore the <s>dharmas</s> are motivated by the <s>apūrva</s>. Hence the great teacher's formulation of the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Because of the authority of <s>śruti</s>, when there is a division of the principal [rites], the subsidiaries should belong according to [their] domain.' The 'principal' [rites] are the <s>apūrvas</s> — for they, being fruitful, are primary, and the word 'principal' (<s>mukhya</s>) [denotes] what is primary. Their division has been stated by reasons such as different words and the like. When there is such a division of the principal [rites], the subsidiaries should belong according to [their] domain — those that are taught in the domain (context) of a particular <s>apūrva</s> should belong to that [<s>apūrva</s>] alone. Because of the authority of <s>śruti</s> — that this subsidiary belongs to this <s>apūrva</s>, and that one to that — here <s>śruti</s> alone is the valid authority. Not any other [means of knowledge] such as direct perception and the like. And by <s>śruti</s>, those that are heard in the context of a particular [rite] should properly belong to that [rite] alone. And a meaning stated for one [rite] does not belong to another. For what belongs to <s>Devadatta</s> — village, garment, and the like — does not belong to <s>Yajñadatta</s>. Therefore the assignment of <s>dharmas</s> is according to [their] context.

children.translated_text: Or, because of non-distinction between origin and meaning, there would be uniformity of properties, like in beings (<s>sattvavat</s>). // MS_7,1.2 //

children.text:
atha vā, naitad evam, yathāprakaraṇaṃ dharmāṇāṃ vyavasthā iti. kiṃ tarhi. aikadharmyaṃ syād iti, samānadharmatā. sarve dharmāḥ sarvārthāḥ. kutaḥ. utpattyarthāvibhāgāt. utpattir iti yajiṃ brūmaḥ, apūrvasyotpādanāt. artha ity apūrvaṃ brūmaḥ, yajiprayojanatvāt. tayor avibhāgaḥ. sarvāṇy apūrvāṇi yajimanti. yajisaṃyogena dharmāḥ śiṣyante, yajetety uktvoktāḥ. te yajau na saṃbhavanti, tasyāphalatvāt. [3]{*7/7*} tatrāsaṃbhavantas tatsaṃbaddheṣv apūrveṣu vijñāyante. sa ca yajisaṃbandhaḥ sarveṣām apūrvāṇāṃ tulyaḥ. tasmāt sarvārthā bhavanti, satvadharmavat{*7/8*}. yathā satvadharmāḥ{*7/9*}, gaur na padā praṣṭavya{*7/10*} iti gotvasaṃbandhena śrūyamāṇās tatrāsaṃbhavantas tatsaṃbaddheṣu piṇḍeṣu vijñāyante, tasya ca gotvasaṃbandhasyāviśeṣāt sarvagavīṣu śuklanīlakapilakapotikāsu bhavanti. evam ihāpi.
ucyate, viṣama upanyāsaḥ. tatra gosāmānyasaṃbandhena dharmā vidhīyante. gaur na padā praṣṭavya{*7/11*} iti. iha punar yajiviśeṣasaṃbandhena dharmā vidhīyante. darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti{*7/12*}, jyotiṣṭomena yajeteti. viśiṣṭayajisaṃbaddha evāpūrve bhavitum arhanti, na sarvatreti. tatra brūmaḥ, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajetettham iti{*7/13*}. yadi yajir vidhīyeta, na dharmaiḥ saṃbadhyeta. na hi dvayor vidhīyamānayoḥ paraspareṇa saṃbandho bhavati. anuvādaś ca sann aviśeṣāt sarvayāgānuvādaḥ. tasmāt sarvathā dharmāḥ.
nanu darśapūrṇamāsaśabdo viśeṣako bhaviṣyati. na darśapūrṇamāsaśabdaḥ śaknoti yāgaṃ viśeṣṭum. ayaṃ hi vidhir vā syād anuvādo vā. yadānuvādaḥ, tadā dharmasaṃbandhārthaḥ. sa ca dharmasaṃbandho yāgānuvādenaiva tayoḥ siddhaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Or rather, this is not so — that the ritual rules (<s>dharma</s>) are distributed according to their respective contexts. What then? There should be uniformity of characteristics (<s>aikadharmya</s>) — sameness of attributes. All rules serve all purposes. Why? Because of the non-distinction between origination and purpose. By 'origination' we mean the sacrifice (<s>yaji</s>), since it produces the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>). By 'purpose' we mean the <s>apūrva</s>, since it is the object of the sacrifice. There is no distinction between these two — all <s>apūrva</s>s involve sacrifice. The rules are taught in connection with sacrifice — having stated 'one should sacrifice' (<s>yajeta</s>), they are stated. They are not possible in the sacrifice itself, because [the sacrifice] is without fruit [in itself]. Not being possible there, they are understood in the <s>apūrva</s>s connected with [the sacrifice]. And the connection with sacrifice is the same for all <s>apūrva</s>s. Therefore [the rules] serve all purposes — like properties of a class (<s>sattva</s>). Just as class-properties — 'a cow should not be kicked with the foot' — being heard in connection with the cow-class, and not being possible in [the class] itself, are understood in the individual [animals] connected with [the class]; and because the connection with the cow-class is undifferentiated, they apply to all individual cows — white, blue, brown, and grayish — so too here.
It is replied: the illustration is inapt. There, the rules are enjoined in connection with the general class 'cow' — 'a cow should not be kicked with the foot.' But here, the rules are enjoined in connection with a particular sacrifice — 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>,' 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' They properly belong only to the <s>apūrva</s> connected with the particular sacrifice, not universally. To this we reply: 'One should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — in this manner.' If the sacrifice (<s>yaji</s>) were being enjoined, it would not be connected with the rules. For two things both being enjoined do not have a mutual connection. And being a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), because of non-distinction, it is a restatement of all sacrifices. Therefore the rules [apply] universally.
[The objector says:] the word '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' will be the specifier. [We reply:] the word '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' cannot specify the sacrifice. For this [word] would be either an injunction or a restatement. When it is a restatement, it is for the purpose of connecting with the rules. And that connection with the rules is already accomplished by the restatement of sacrifice alone.

children.text:
nanu nivṛttikaro bhaviṣyati, darśapūrṇamāsāv evetthaṃ kuryān nānyān iti. naivaṃ śakyam. yat kāraṇam, na tasyānyanivṛttiḥ arthaḥ. nanu parisaṃkhyayā kariṣyati. nātra parisaṃkhyā yujyate. yady anyena vākyena yāgamātre dharmaprasaṅgaḥ kṛtaḥ{*7/14*} syāt, tata etat punarvacanaṃ parisaṃkhyāṃ kuryāt. atha punar asati prasaṅge 'nenaiva prasaṅgo 'nenaiva nivṛttir{*7/15*} ity atibhāra ekasyaiva vākyasya bhavati.
[4]{*7/16*} evaṃ tarhi, nātra yajeteti śabdo dharmavidhibhiḥ saṃbadhyate, yajetettham iti. kena tarhi. darśapūrṇamāsaśabdena. pratyakṣo hi tenāsya saṃyogaḥ, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti, parokṣo dharmavidhibhiḥ. kas tadā vākyārthaḥ. darśapūrṇamāsau kuryād iti. naivaṃ śakyam. evaṃ sati dharmā asaṃbaddhāḥ pāriplavā bhavanti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. yeyam ākhyātikī vibhaktiḥ yajeteti, sā darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ kartavyatāṃ vidadhāti. tatra kathaṃ yāgamātreṇa yāgaviśeṣeṇa vā dharmasaṃbandhaḥ syāt. vidhāyikā vibhaktir nāstīty asaṃbaddhā dharmā bhavanti.
naiṣa doṣaḥ. na vayaṃ vākyena dharmāṇāṃ saṃbandhaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ. kena tarhi. prakaraṇena. katham. kartavyatāyāṃ coditāyām itikartavyatākāṅkṣā bhavati, kathaṃ kuryād iti. prakaraṇena dharmāḥ saṃbadhyanta itthaṃ kuryād iti. naivaṃ śakyam. yadā hi darśapūrṇamāsau kartavyatayā codyate{*7/17*}, tadetikartavyatākāṅkṣaiva nāsti. prajñātetikartyavyatatvāt{*7/18*} tayoḥ. asatyāṃ cetikartavyatākāṅkṣāyāṃ prakaraṇam eva nāsti. evaṃ hy uktam, asaṃyuktaṃ prakaraṇād itikartavyatārthitvād{*7/19*} iti.
evaṃ tarhi, naivātra yāge dharmā vidhīyante. nāpi darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ kartavyatocyate. kiṃ tarhi. darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti padadvayena viśiṣṭaṃ yāgam anūdyātra dharmā vidhīyante, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajetettham iti. evam api darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ity anuvādo na yujyate. tṛtīyārthasyāsiddhatvāt. pūrvān anuvādo bhavati, apūrvaś ca tṛtīyārthaḥ. so 'vaśyaṃ vidhātavyaḥ. tasmiṃś ca vidhīyamāne 'nyad evāsaṃbaddham āpadyate, darśapūrṇamāsau yajeḥ karaṇam iti. tasmāt sa eva prathamaḥ pakṣo 'stu, yāgānuvādena dharmāṇāṃ vidhir iti.
nanu tatrāpi darśapūrṇamāsābhyām ity etan na saṃbadhyate.
[5]{*7/20*} nanu saṃbhantsyate. kālavacanaḥ san prāyiko nityānuvādo bhaviṣyati. prāyeṇa yāgānāṃ darśapūrṇamāsakālatvāt. tṛtīyā ca kālasyārthakṛtaṃ guṇabhāvam ālocyopapadyate. tathā cet sarve dharmāḥ sarvārthāḥ bhavanti.
children.translated_text:
[The objector says:] but [the word 'Darśapūrṇamāsa'] will serve as an exclusion — 'one should do it thus only in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, not in others.' This is not possible. The reason is: exclusion of others is not its purpose. [The objector:] but it will effect [exclusion] through enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>). Enumeration is not fitting here. If by another sentence the rules had been extended to sacrifice in general, then this repetition could effect an enumeration. But when, in the absence of such an extension, both the extension and the restriction [would come] from this same [sentence], there would be an excessive burden on a single sentence.
[The objector says:] then, the word '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice) does not connect with the rule-injunctions here — 'one should sacrifice in this manner.' Rather, [it connects] with the word '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' For its connection with that is direct — 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — while [the connection] with the rule-injunctions is indirect. What then is the sentence-meaning? 'One should perform the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' This is not possible. In that case, the rules would be unconnected, left floating. How so? This verbal inflection 'one should sacrifice' (<s>yajeta</s>) enjoins the obligation of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. There, how could there be a connection of rules with sacrifice in general or with a particular sacrifice? Since there is no enjoining inflection [remaining], the rules would be unconnected.
This is no defect. We shall not make the connection of rules by the sentence. By what then? By the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). How? When the obligation has been enjoined, there arises the expectation of procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) — 'how should one do it?' By the context, the rules are connected — 'one should do it in this manner.' This is not possible. For when the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is enjoined as the obligation, there is simply no expectation of procedure [at all], because the procedure of those two [rites] is already known. And in the absence of the expectation of procedure, there is no context at all. For thus it has been stated: 'What is not connected with context is for the purpose of procedure.'
Then, neither are rules enjoined here regarding sacrifice, nor is the obligation of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> stated. What then? By the two words 'with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' and 'one should sacrifice,' a specific sacrifice is restated, and the rules are enjoined regarding it — 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> in this manner.' Even so, 'with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' as a restatement is not fitting, because the instrumental meaning is not [yet] established. The restatement is of what is prior, while the instrumental meaning is unprecedented. That must necessarily be enjoined. And when it is being enjoined, something else [entirely] — unconnected — would result: 'the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is the instrument of sacrifice.' Therefore let the first position stand — the rules are enjoined through the restatement of sacrifice.
[The objector:] but even there, 'with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' does not connect.
[We reply:] it will connect. Being a statement of time, it will be a constant restatement based on common occurrence. For most sacrifices commonly take place at the time of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. And the instrumental case is explained by considering [it as indicating] the subordinate status of time, which is purposive. If so, all rules serve all purposes.

children.translated_text: Or, because of being a remainder of the injunction, they would be distributed according to the differentiation of that [injunction], since origination is subordinate. // MS_7,1.3 //

children.text:
karmacodanāyāḥ śeṣabhūto dharmasamāmnāya ekadeśabhūta ity arthaḥ{*7/21*}, darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta, anayāgnyavādhānādikayetikartavyatayeti. tasyāṃ codanāyāṃ yajer guṇabhāvaḥ śrūyate, darśapūrṇamāsaśabdo yajivacanaḥ{*7/22*}. karaṇabhāvo 'tra yajeḥ śrūyate. darśapūrṇamāsākhyena yāgasamudāyenānyat kuryād iti. yat tato 'nyat, tatkartavyatayā codyate, na yajiḥ. apūrvaṃ ca tat.
nanu phalam atra vākye śrūyate, svargakāmo yateta{*7/23*} iti. tatkartavyaṃ syāt. satyaṃ śrūyate, na tu tadyajinā kriyate. vinaṣṭe yajau tad bhavati. apūrvaṃ tu tena kriyate. tasmāt tasya kartavyatā ucyate. yasya kartavyatā, tad itikartavyatayā saṃbadhyate. tasmād apūrvārthā dharmāḥ. teṣāṃ cāpūrvāṇāṃ bhedaḥ{*7/24*}. atas tadbhedād yathāprakaraṇaṃ vyavatiṣṭhante dharmā iti.
athaitasmin pakṣe kathaṃ darśapūrṇamāsaśabdena yāgo viśeṣyate. ucyate, naivātra yāgo viśiṣyate. kiṃ tarhi. apūrvabhāvanaivobhayapadaviśiṣṭocyate{*7/25*}. yathāruṇayā piṅgākṣyaikahāyanyā somaṃ krīṇāti{*7/26*} iti. viṣama upanyāsaḥ. tatra hy anyad dravyam, anyo guṇaḥ. tena tatrobhayaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ yujyate{*7/27*}. iha punar yāgaḥ eva tau darśapūrṇamāsau. tenehobhayaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ{*7/28*} [6]{*7/29*} na yujyate. ucyate, ihāpi yajeteti sāmānyam, darśapūrṇamāsāv iti viśeṣaḥ, anyac ca sāmānyam anyo viśeṣaḥ.
evam api śrutyā sāmānyena{*7/30*} bhāvanā, vākyād viśeṣeṇa{*7/31*}. na caitad yugapad bhavatīti. evaṃ tarhi, naivātra śrutyarthe parigṛhyate. kiṃ tarhi. vākyārthaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam. śrutyarthe parigṛhyamāṇe darśapūrṇamāsaśabdo 'narthako bhavati. yajatiś cānuvādaḥ. yajaty ātmakatvād darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ. yajatisāmānādhikaraṇyāc ca darśapūrṇamāsaśabdasya.
children.translated_text:
The collection of rules is subsidiary to the injunction of ritual action — meaning, it is a component part [of the injunction]. 'One should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, with such-and-such procedure as the fire-establishment and so forth.' In that injunction, the subordinate status of sacrifice (<s>yaji</s>) is heard — the word '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' is a designation for sacrifice. The instrumental status of sacrifice is heard here. 'By the sacrificial aggregate (<s>yāgasamudāya</s>) named <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one should perform something else.' That which is other than [the sacrifice itself] — its obligation is what is enjoined, not [the obligation of] the sacrifice. And that [other thing] is the <s>apūrva</s> (unprecedented result).
[The objector:] but a fruit is heard in this sentence — 'one desiring heaven should strive' — that should be [what is] to be accomplished. True, it is heard; but that [fruit] is not produced by the sacrifice itself. When the sacrifice has perished, that [fruit] comes about. But the <s>apūrva</s> is produced by [the sacrifice]. Therefore the obligation of that [<s>apūrva</s>] is stated. That whose obligation [is stated] is connected with the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>). Therefore the rules are for the purpose of the <s>apūrva</s>. And the <s>apūrva</s>s are differentiated. Hence, because of their differentiation, the rules are distributed according to their respective contexts.
Now, in this view, how is the sacrifice specified by the word '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>'? We reply: sacrifice is not specified here. What then? The <s>apūrva</s>-<s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) itself is specified by both words together. Just as 'with a reddish, tawny-eyed, one-year-old [cow] one purchases <s>Soma</s>' — [the objector says:] the illustration is inapt. There, the substance is one thing and the quality another; therefore the dual specification is fitting. But here, the sacrifices themselves are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; therefore dual specification is not fitting. [We] reply: here too, 'one should sacrifice' is the general and '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' is the specific — and the general and specific are distinct.
Even so, by hearing (<s>śruti</s>) the productive force [is established] through the general; by the sentence, through the specific. And these two do not occur simultaneously. Then, the meaning of hearing (<s>śruti</s>) is not what is grasped here. What then? The sentence-meaning [is what is grasped]. Why? If the hearing-meaning were grasped, the word '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' would be purposeless. And the word '<s>yajati</s>' (one sacrifices) would be a restatement — because the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites] are by nature sacrificial. And the word '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' is co-referential with <s>yajati</s>.

children.text: satve{*7/32*} lakṣaṇasaṃyogāt sārvatrikaṃ pratīyeta // MS_7,1.4 //
children.translated_text: In [the analogy of] class-properties (<s>sattva</s>), because of the connection with a characterizing mark, [the rules] would be understood as universal. // MS_7,1.4 //

children.text: yat tu satvavad{*7/33*} iti. atra gavākṛtau dharmaḥ śrūyate. ākṛteḥ padārthatvāt. na ca tatra saṃbhavati. ato 'sāv ākṛtiḥ sahacāripiṇḍalakṣaṇārthā vijñāyate, yathā gaṅgāyāṃ gāva{*7/34*} iti. tac ca sāhacaryam, sarvapiṇḍānām aviśiṣṭam iti, sarvapiṇḍeṣu vihitaṃ bhavati. tasmāt tat sārvatrikaṃ pratīyeta. iha tu yajer guṇabhavena śravaṇān naiva yajau dharmāḥ śrūyante. kiṃ{*7/35*} tarhi. apūrva ity. evam apadiṣṭo hetuḥ. tasmād anupanyāsaḥ satvavad{*7/36*} iti.
children.translated_text: As to [the analogy] 'like class-properties' — there, the rule is heard regarding the cow-form (<s>ākṛti</s>), since the class-form is the referent of the word. And it is not possible [to apply the rule] there [in the abstract class]. Therefore that class-form is understood as a characterizing mark for the accompanying individual [animals] — just as 'cows on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' [means 'on the bank']. And that accompaniment is undifferentiated with respect to all individuals — hence [the rule] is enjoined regarding all individuals. Therefore it would be understood as universal. But here, because of the hearing of sacrifice as subordinate, the rules are simply not heard regarding sacrifice itself. Where then? Regarding the <s>apūrva</s>. Thus the reasoning has been indicated. Therefore the illustration 'like class-properties' is inapplicable.
