avibhāgāt tu naivaṃ syāt // MS_7,1.5 //
children.translated_text: But because of non-distinction, this should not be so. // MS_7,1.5 //

children.text:
atha tuśabdaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttau. naitad evam, apūrvaprayuktā dharmā [7]{*7/37*} iti. yajiprayuktā eva. kutaḥ. avibhāgāt. yajināvibhāgo dharmāṇām, pratyakṣaṃ kecid dravye śrūyante, kecid devatāyām, kecin mantreṣu. eṣa ca yajiḥ, yad dravyaṃ devatām uddiśya mantreṇa tyajyate. sa eṣa pratyakṣo yajinā saṃbandho dharmāṇām. apūrveṇa tv ānumānikaḥ. phale 'pi yajeḥ pratyakṣaśruto guṇabhāvaḥ, svargakāmo yajeteti. ānumāniko 'pūrveṇa. anumānāc ca pratyakṣaṃ balīyaḥ. tasmād yajyarthāḥ dharmāḥ.
nanu yajir bhaṅgitvāt kālāntare phalaṃ dātum asamarthaḥ. tatra kṛtā dharmā asamarthā eva bhavatīty uktam. atra sthitasya nyāyasyākṣepeṇa pratyavasthānaṃ kriyate. tailapānavad etad bhaviṣyati. yathā tailapānaṃ ghṛtapānaṃ vā bhaṅgitve 'pi sati kālāntare medhāsmṛtibalapuṣṭyādīni phalāni karoti. evaṃ yajir api kariṣyati, kiṃ no 'dṛṣṭāśrutenāpūrveṇa kalpiteneti.
children.translated_text:
Now the word <s>tu</s> ('but') [marks] a reversal of position. This is not so — that the <s>dharmas</s> (ritual properties) [7] are impelled by <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen potency). They are impelled by the <s>yaji</s> (sacrificial act) alone. Why? Because of non-separation (<s>avibhāga</s>). There is no separation of the <s>dharmas</s> from the <s>yaji</s> — some are directly perceived in connection with the substance, some with the deity, some in the mantras. And this is the <s>yaji</s>: that substance which is relinquished, directed toward a deity, by means of a mantra. This is the directly perceived connection of the <s>dharmas</s> with the <s>yaji</s>. But [a connection] with <s>apūrva</s> would be merely inferential. The subordinate status [of the <s>yaji</s>] with respect to the fruit is also directly heard — 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice.' [Whereas its subordinate status] with <s>apūrva</s> is [merely] inferential. And the directly perceived is stronger than inference. Therefore the <s>dharmas</s> are for the purpose of the <s>yaji</s>.
[The objector says:] but the <s>yaji</s>, being perishable (<s>bhaṅgitva</s>), is incapable of producing a fruit at a later time. The <s>dharmas</s> performed therein would be equally incapable — thus it was said. To this established position, a counter-argument is made by way of objection. This will be like the drinking of oil. Just as the drinking of oil or ghee, even though [the act is] perishable, at a later time produces fruits such as intelligence, memory, strength, nourishment and the like — so too the <s>yaji</s> will produce [fruit]. Why should we [bother] with a postulated <s>apūrva</s> that is unheard?

children.text: dvyarthatvaṃ ca vipratiṣiddham // MS_7,1.6 //
children.translated_text: And dual-purpose-ness is contradicted. // MS_7,1.6 //

children.text: evaṃ ca sati sarve dharmāḥ sarvārthā bhavanti. tathā caindrāgnādiṣu prayājādayaḥ santi. tatra saurye karmaṇi prayājānāṃ darśanam upapadyate. prayāje prayāje kṛṣṇalaṃ juhoti{*7/38*} iti. itarathā prayājāś ca vidhātavyāḥ. prayājeṣu ca kṛṣṇalahomaḥ. tathā ca dvyarthaṃ tat syāt{*7/39*}. dvyarthatvaṃ ca vipratiṣiddham. tasmād yajiprayuktā dharmā iti.
children.translated_text: And if it were so [that dharmas are impelled by apūrva], all <s>dharmas</s> would serve all purposes. Thus in the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (Indra-Agni) and other [rites], <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings) exist. There, the observation of <s>prayājas</s> in the solar rite (<s>saurya karman</s>) is appropriate — 'at each <s>prayāja</s> he offers a <s>kṛṣṇala</s> (gold grain).' Otherwise, <s>prayājas</s> would have to be prescribed [separately], and also the <s>kṛṣṇala</s>-oblation at the <s>prayājas</s>. And thus that would be dual-purpose. And dual-purpose-ness is contradicted [by the principle of parsimony]. Therefore the <s>dharmas</s> are impelled by the <s>yaji</s>.

[{7/39: E2: <s>tasyāt</s>}]

children.text: utpattau vidhyabhāvād vā codanāyāṃ pravṛttiḥ syāt tataś ca karmabhedaḥ syāt // MS_7,1.7 //
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of a prescription at [the time of] origination, or [because of] the activity being in the injunction (<s>codanā</s>), there would be a differentiation of rites. // MS_7,1.7 //

children.text: naitad evam, yajiprayuktā dharmā iti. codanāyāṃ pravṛttiḥ [8]{*7/40*} syāt. codanety apūrvaṃ brūmaḥ, codanārthatvād apūrvārthatvād apūrvaprayuktā dharmāḥ. phalavattvād ity ukto hetuḥ. yat tu prayakṣo yajisaṃbandho dharmāṇām iti. atra brūmaḥ, utpattau vidhyabhāvāt. utpattir iti yajiṃ brūmaḥ. utpattau yajau nāsti vidhiḥ. yajyarthā dharmā iti. kevalaṃ yajau śrūyante, kriyante ca. naitāvatā tadarthā bhavanti. yathā vāsasi rāgaḥ śrūyate, vāso rañjayatīti, vāsasi ca kriyate. na cāsau tadarthaḥ. stryarthaḥ puruṣārtho vā bhavati. evam ihāpi yajau śrūyamāṇāḥ kriyamāṇāś cāpūrvārthā bhaveyur arthavattvāya. tataś ca karmabhedaḥ syāt. yato 'pūrvārthā iti. yat tu yajeḥ pratyakṣam{*7/41*}, phale guṇabhāva iti. na kṛtvāpūrvaṃ{*7/42*} bhavatīti, prāṇāliko vijñāyate. praṇāḍyāpi ca yena kriyate, tat kāraṇaṃ bhavati. yathā gomayaiḥ pacati, tuṣapakvā bhavantīti. yat tu, tailapānavad yajitaḥ phalaṃ bhavatīti. atra brūmaḥ, tailapānasyāpi na kālāntare phalaṃ bhavati. dhātusāmyaṃ tasya phalam. tac ca tatkālam eva. yac ca phalaṃ balapuṣṭyādi, tat samyag āhārapariṇāmād bhavati. tasmād viṣama upanyāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that the <s>dharmas</s> are impelled by the <s>yaji</s>. The activity would be in the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) [8]. By 'injunction' we mean <s>apūrva</s> — because of being for the purpose of injunction, [i.e.,] for the purpose of <s>apūrva</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> are impelled by <s>apūrva</s>. The reason stated was 'because of producing fruit.' As for what was said — 'the connection of the <s>dharmas</s> with the <s>yaji</s> is directly perceived' — to this we say: because of the absence of a prescription at [the time of] origination. By 'origination' we mean the <s>yaji</s>. There is no prescription in the <s>yaji</s> [itself] — [the view that] the <s>dharmas</s> are for the purpose of the <s>yaji</s> [is refuted]. They are merely heard in the <s>yaji</s> and performed [in it]. That alone does not make them for its purpose. Just as dyeing is heard in connection with cloth — 'he dyes the cloth' — and is performed on cloth; yet it is not for the cloth's purpose — it is for a woman's purpose or a man's purpose. Similarly here too, [the dharmas], being heard and performed in the <s>yaji</s>, could be for the purpose of <s>apūrva</s>, in order to be meaningful. And thus there would be a differentiation of rites — because [the dharmas] are for the purpose of <s>apūrva</s>. As for what was said about the directly perceived subordinate status of the <s>yaji</s> in relation to the fruit — [the reply is:] without producing <s>apūrva</s>, [the yaji] does not [produce fruit]. This is understood as a vital channel (<s>prāṇālika</s>). And even a channel through which [something] is done becomes the cause. Just as 'he cooks with cow-dung' — [and the food] becomes 'cooked by husks.' As for what was said — 'the fruit [comes] from the <s>yaji</s> like the drinking of oil' — to this we say: even for the drinking of oil, the fruit is not at a later time. Its fruit is the balance of bodily constituents (<s>dhātusāmya</s>). And that is simultaneous [with the action]. And the fruit of strength, nourishment, etc. comes from the proper transformation of food. Therefore the illustration is dissimilar.

children.text: yadi vāpy abhidhānavat sāmānyāt sarvadharmaḥ syāt // MS_7,1.8 //
children.translated_text: Or even if [apūrva is the impeller], because of generality, like the designation, every <s>dharma</s> would [serve] all. // MS_7,1.8 //

children.text:
yady apy apūrvaṃ prayojakaṃ dharmāṇām, tathāpi sarvadharmaḥ syāt, sa sa padārthaḥ, abhidhānavat sāmānyāt. abhidhānaṃ tāvad eteṣāṃ samānam. apūrvam ity abhidhānavad dharmeṇāpy asya samānena bhavitavyam, vāhīkavat. yathā vāhīko 'tithir āgataḥ, yavānnam asmai prakriyatām ity ukte, yo yo vāhīkas tasya tasya yavānnaṃ kriyate. yathā vā, akṣyāmaye mudgaudano bhoktavyaḥ, udarāmaye payaḥ [9]{*7/43*} pātavyam iti. sarvatra ca hy akṣyāmaye mudgaudano bhujyate, udarāmaye 'pi payaḥ pīyate. evam ihāpy ekasyāpūrvasya ye dharmāḥ śrutās te sarvāpūrvāṇāṃ bhavitum arhanti.
api ca, aruṇaparāśarā nāma śākhinaḥ. teṣāṃ paricareṣu smṛtirūpaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati. ye darśapūrṇamāsayor dharmāḥ, te sarveṣṭīnām agnīṣomīyasya cety ārabhya, yāvat sarvāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayo 'nuktāntā iti. tac cānukramaṇam etam eva nyāyaṃ sūcayati. tasmād apūrvaprayuktatve 'pi sarve dharmāḥ sarvārthā iti.
children.translated_text:
Even if <s>apūrva</s> is the impeller of the <s>dharmas</s>, still every <s>dharma</s> would [belong to all rites] — [all <s>apūrvas</s> are] the same entity — because of generality, like the designation. First, the designation of these [<s>apūrvas</s>] is the same. Just as [the designation] '<s>apūrva</s>' [is the same], so too its <s>dharma</s> (property) should be the same — like a <s>Vāhīka</s> (foreigner). Just as 'a <s>Vāhīka</s> guest has arrived — let barley-food be prepared for him' — when this is said, for whoever is a <s>Vāhīka</s>, barley-food is prepared. Or just as 'in eye-disease, mung-bean porridge should be eaten; in stomach-ailment, milk [9] should be drunk' — everywhere, in eye-disease mung-bean porridge is eaten, and in stomach-ailment too milk is drunk. Similarly here, whatever <s>dharmas</s> are heard of one <s>apūrva</s>, they should belong to all <s>apūrvas</s>.
Moreover, there are [the Vedic scholars] called the <s>Aruṇa-Parāśaras</s>. In their auxiliary texts (<s>paricara</s>), there is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-text in the form of a <s>smṛti</s>. 'The <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — they belong to all <s>iṣṭis</s> and to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [rite]' — beginning from that, up to 'all archetypes and modifications, ending with the unstated.' And that enumeration points to this very principle. Therefore, even when impelled by <s>apūrva</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> serve all purposes.

children.text: arthasya tv avibhaktatvāt tathā syād abhidhāneṣu pūrvavattvāt prayogasya karmaṇaḥ śabdabhāvyatvād vibhāgāc cheṣāṇām apravṛttiḥ syāt // MS_7,1.9 //
children.translated_text: But because of the meaning being undivided, it should be so in the designations; because of the performance being precedented, because of the rite's character being [known] through language, because of the separation of the subsidiaries, there would be non-application [elsewhere]. // MS_7,1.9 //

children.text: upavarṇanāparihāras tāvad ucyate. yad uktam, vāhīkavad iti, atra brūmaḥ, arthasya tv avibhaktatvāt, tathā syād abhidhāneṣu. artho vāhīkatvam, taddeśasaṃbandhaḥ, so 'vibhaktaḥ. sarvavāhīkeṣv anugata ity arthaḥ. tannimittaś ca prītiviśeṣo na puruṣanimittaḥ. kathaṃ jñāyate. pūrvavattvāt prayogasya. pūrvavān atra prayogaḥ, bahuśo vāhīkāś cāvāhīkāś ca bhojitāḥ. tatrānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ jñatam etat, deśanimitteyaṃ yavānn apriyatā, na puruṣanimittatā. tasmāt tathā syād vāhīkādiṣv abhidhāneṣu. atheha karmaṇaḥ śabdabhāvyatvam. nānyataḥ{*7/44*} śakyam etaj jñātum. kasyāpūrvasya{*7/45*} dharmā iti. śabdena ca vyavasthitā vijñātā dharmāḥ. apūrvāṇāṃ ca vibhāgaḥ, ataḥ śeṣāṇām anyatra vihitānām anyatrāpravṛttiḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: First, the refutation of the illustration is stated. As to what was said — 'like the <s>Vāhīka</s>' — to this we say: but because of the meaning being undivided, it should be so in the designations. The meaning is '<s>Vāhīka</s>-ness' — the connection with that region — it is undivided, [i.e.,] it extends to all <s>Vāhīkas</s>. And the particular affection caused by that [connection] is not caused by the person [individually]. How is this known? Because of the performance being precedented (<s>pūrvavat</s>). Here the performance has precedent — many <s>Vāhīkas</s> and non-<s>Vāhīkas</s> have been fed. From that, through agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), this was known: this fondness for barley-food is caused by the region, not by the person. Therefore it should be so in designations such as '<s>Vāhīka</s>' etc. But here, the character of the rite is [known only] through language (<s>śabdabhāvya</s>). This cannot be known from any other [source] — which <s>dharmas</s> belong to which <s>apūrva</s>. And the <s>dharmas</s> known through language are established [in their respective places]. And the <s>apūrvas</s> are separate — therefore, the subsidiaries prescribed elsewhere would not apply (<s>apravṛtti</s>) elsewhere.

children.text: smṛtir iti cet // MS_7,1.10 //
children.translated_text: If [one cites] the <s>smṛti</s> [of the Aruṇa-Parāśaras] — // MS_7,1.10 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, smṛtir iti. tasya kaḥ parihāraḥ.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'the <s>smṛti</s>' [of the Aruṇa-Parāśaras shows all dharmas serve all]. What is the refutation of that?

children.text: na, pūrvavattvāt // MS_7,1.11 //
children.translated_text: No, because of being precedented. // MS_7,1.11 //

children.text: pūrvavatī hīyaṃ smṛtiḥ. codakaṃ dharmagrāhakaṃ vakyati, vidhyanto vā prakṛtivad iti. tena prāpitānāṃ dharmāṇām ayam anuvādaḥ. etan nyāyapūrvikā, nāprāptānāṃ vidhāyikā. yat kāraṇaṃ vyavasthā dharmāṇām etena nyāyena bhavati.
children.translated_text: For this <s>smṛti</s> is precedented. The injunctive principle (<s>codaka</s>) that comprehends <s>dharmas</s> will state: '[they are transferred] by a statement having the force of a prescription, or like the archetype.' Thus this [<s>smṛti</s>] is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of <s>dharmas</s> obtained through that [principle]. It presupposes that principle — it is not a prescription of what is not [yet] obtained. The reason being: the determination of the <s>dharmas</s> is through that principle.

children.text: arthasya śabdabhāvyatvāt prakaraṇanibandhanāc chabdād evānyatra bhāvaḥ syāt // MS_7,1.12 //
children.translated_text: Because of the meaning's character being [known] through language, and because of being based on context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), the existence [of dharmas] elsewhere would be from language alone. // MS_7,1.12 //

children.text:
idaṃ nigamanasūtram. nigamanaṃ ca pratijñāyā hetoś ca punarvacanam. tad idam ucyate, yasmād evam, tasmād arthasyāgnyanvādhānādeḥ śabdabhāvyatvāt, pratiprakaraṇaṃ ca nibandhanāc chabdād evānyatra bhāvaḥ syāt. yathā gandharvāpsaraso vā, etam unmādayanti, ya unmādyaty etā vai gandharvāpsaraso yadrāṣṭrabhṛtam. tasmai svāhā tābhyaḥ svāheti juhotīty agniprakaraṇe utpannānāṃ rāṣṭrabhṛtām udvāhe upadeśaḥ. eteṣāṃ rāṣṭrabhṛto juhoty abhyātānāṃ juhotīti. asty etasmin vacane yathādhikāraṃ vyavatiṣṭheran dharmā iti. evaṃ ca saty adharmakāṇy aindrāgnādīṇi. tadartham uttaro 'dhyāyaṣaṭkaḥ prārabdhavya iti.
tatra saptam ena tāvad aindrāgnādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ dharmāḥ santīty ucyate. te cātideśeneti. atideśo nāma ye paratra vihitā dharmās tam atītyānyatra teṣāṃ deśaḥ. yathā devadattasya bhojanavidhiṃ kṛtvā, śālisūpamāṃsāpūpair devadatto bhojayitavya [11]{*7/47*} iti. tam eva vidhiṃ yajñadatte 'tidiśati, devadattavad yajñadatto bhojayitavya iti. ślokam api udāharanti,
prakṛtāt karmaṇo yasmāt tatsamāneṣu karmasu/
dharmapradeśo yena syāt so 'tideśa iti sthitiḥ// iti.
sa ca nāmnā vacanena vā. tatra nāma trividham atideśakam, karmanām, saṃskāranām, yaugikam iti. vacanaṃ punar dvividham, pratyakṣaśrutam, ānumānikaṃ ca. tayor ānumānikam upariṣṭād vakṣyate. pratyakṣaśrutaṃ tv idānīm eva cintyate.
astīṣunām aikāhaḥ, aparaḥ śyenaḥ. tau dvāv apy ābhicārikau. tatreṣau kāṃścid dharmān vidhāyāha, samānam itarac chyeneneti. etac cintyate. kim ayam anuvādaḥ, vidhir iti. yadi vidhiḥ, tato 'tideśaḥ. śyenadhamān iṣāv atidiśati. athānuvādaḥ, tato neti. tatra kiṃ prāptam. tat sūtreṇaivopakramyate,
children.translated_text:
This is the concluding <s>sūtra</s>. And a conclusion is a restatement of the thesis and the reason. This is said: because it is thus, therefore — because of the meaning (of <s>agnyanvādhāna</s> and the like) having its character [known] through language, and because of being based in each individual context — the existence [of dharmas] elsewhere would be from language alone. Just as [in the case of] 'the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s> — they cause madness in him who goes mad; these are indeed the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, namely the <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛts</s> (kingdom-sustainers). To him <s>svāhā</s>, to them <s>svāhā</s>, he offers' — the <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛts</s> that arose in the fire-context are taught [as applicable] in marriage. 'Of these <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛts</s> he offers, of those assailed he offers.' In this statement there is [the principle] that the <s>dharmas</s> would be established according to their [respective] subject-matter (<s>adhikāra</s>). And if so, the <s>Aindrāgna</s> and other [rites] would be without <s>dharmas</s> [of their own]. For that purpose, the latter six books (<s>adhyāyas</s>) must be commenced.
In the seventh [book], first it is said that the <s>Aindrāgna</s> and other rites do have <s>dharmas</s>. And [that they obtain them] through extension (<s>atideśa</s>). Extension means: <s>dharmas</s> prescribed elsewhere, having passed beyond that [context], are placed (<s>deśa</s>) elsewhere. Just as, having made a food-prescription for <s>Devadatta</s> — 'Devadatta should be fed [11] with rice, lentil-soup, meat, and cakes' — that very prescription is extended to <s>Yajñadatta</s>: '<s>Yajñadatta</s> should be fed like <s>Devadatta</s>.' They also cite a verse:
'From which established rite, in rites similar to it,
there would be a placing of <s>dharmas</s> — that is called extension.'
And that [extension is] by name or by statement. There, names are of three kinds that effect extension: of rites, of consecrations, and etymological (<s>yaugika</s>). Statements again are of two kinds: directly heard, and inferential. Of those, the inferential will be discussed later. The directly heard is examined right now.
There is [a rite called] <s>Iṣu</s> ('Arrow') among the one-day rites, and another [called] <s>Śyena</s> ('Hawk'). Both are sorcery-rites (<s>ābhicārika</s>). There, having prescribed certain <s>dharmas</s> for the <s>Iṣu</s>, [the text] says: 'The other — the <s>Śyena</s> — is the same.' This is examined: is this a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) or a prescription (<s>vidhi</s>)? If a prescription, then [it is] an extension — it extends the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Śyena</s> to the <s>Iṣu</s>. But if a restatement, then not. In that regard, what is the prima facie view? That [question] is introduced by the <s>sūtra</s> itself:

children.text: samāne pūrvavattvād utpannādhikāraḥ syāt // MS_7,1.13 //
children.translated_text: In [the case of rites that are] the same, because of being precedented, there would be a domain of what has [already] arisen. // MS_7,1.13 //

children.text:
samānam itarac chyeneneti. atrotpannādhikāraḥ syāt. anuvāda ity arthaḥ. kutaḥ. pūrvavattvāt. ayam iṣuḥ pūrvavān, jyotiṣṭomapūrvakaḥ. jyautiṣṭomiko 'tra vidhyanta ity arthaḥ{*7/48*}. atra codakenotpannā jyautiṣṭomikā dharmāḥ santi. śyeno 'pi jyotiṣṭomapūrvakaḥ. tatrāpi te santi. ye iṣau śyene [12]{*7/49*} ca samānā bhanti, tān adhikṛtyāyaṃ vādo yujyate. tasmād utpannādhikāratvād anuvādaḥ.
kiṃ cetarad iti cābhāve nopapadyate. itaraśabdaś cāsannihite 'nupapannaḥ, sannihita eva bhavati. yathā, itara ādhāro{*7/50*} dīyatām. itaraḥ kambalo dīyatām iti sannihito dīyate, na prāvāramātraṃ kambalamātraṃ vā. jyautiṣṭomikāś ca sannihitāḥ. tasmāt teṣāṃ vādaḥ. teṣāṃ cedam anuvādaḥ.{*7/51*} vihitā hi te codakeneti.
children.translated_text:
'The other — the <s>Śyena</s> — is the same.' Here, there would be a domain of what has [already] arisen — [i.e.,] it is a restatement. Why? Because of being precedented. This <s>Iṣu</s> is precedented — preceded by the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-[derived properties] here are stated to have the force of a prescription. There, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-derived <s>dharmas</s> exist [in the <s>Iṣu</s>], having arisen through the injunctive principle. The <s>Śyena</s> too is preceded by the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; there too those [dharmas] exist. Those that are common [12] to both <s>Iṣu</s> and <s>Śyena</s> — with reference to them, this statement is appropriate. Therefore, because of being a domain of what has [already] arisen, it is a restatement.
[Moreover,] 'what is the other?' — this [question] is not appropriate in the absence [of something already present]. And the word 'other' (<s>itara</s>) is inappropriate for what is not proximate — it applies only to what is proximate. Just as 'let the other <s>ādhāra</s> (support-vessel) be given'; 'let the other blanket be given' — what is proximate is given, not any mere shawl or any mere blanket. And the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-[derived properties] are proximate. Therefore it is a statement about them. And this is their restatement — for they are prescribed by the injunctive principle.

children.text: śyenasyeti cet // MS_7,1.14 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues that it is] of the <s>Śyena</s> — // MS_7,1.14 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, jyautiṣṭomikānām anuvāda iti. naivam. śyenasya vaiśeṣikāṇāṃ lohitoṣṇīṣādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vidhiḥ{*7/52*}. kutaḥ. śyenagrahaṇasāmarthyāt. evaṃ śyenagrahaṇam arthavat bhaviṣyati, dharmān viśeṣayat. itarathānarthakaṃ syāt. sarveṣāṃ hy ekāhāhīnasatrāṇāṃ te samānāḥ. tatra yāvad uktaṃ syāt, samānam itarad iti, tāvad eva samānam itarac chyeneneti.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that it is a restatement of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-[derived properties] — not so. It is a prescription of the <s>dharmas</s> specific to the <s>Śyena</s>, such as the red turban (<s>lohitoṣṇīṣa</s>) and the like. Why? Because of the force of mentioning '<s>Śyena</s>.' Thus the mention of '<s>Śyena</s>' will be meaningful, as it distinguishes the <s>dharmas</s>. Otherwise it would be purposeless. For those [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-derived properties] are common to all one-day rites, <s>Ahīna</s> rites, and <s>Satras</s>. Therefore, as much as would be said by 'the other is the same,' that much [is also said by] 'the other — the <s>Śyena</s> — is the same.'

children.text: nāsannidhānāt // MS_7,1.15 //
children.translated_text: No, because of non-proximity. // MS_7,1.15 //

children.text: nāyaṃ śyenavaiśeṣikāṇāṃ vādo yujyate. kasmāt. asannidhānāt. ayam itaraśabdaḥ sannihite bhavati, na ca śyenaśabdena vaiśeṣikā iṣau sannihitāḥ{*7/53*}. yat tu śyenaśabdo vaiśeṣiko bhavatīti, vidhipakṣe 'vaiśeṣikatvaṃ doṣaḥ syāt. anuvādapakṣe tu naiva kaścid vidhīyate, kiṃ viśeṣyati. jyautiṣṭomikās tu sarvasādhāraṇāḥ santaḥ śyenasyāpi bhavantīty anuvādo yujyate. tasmāj jyautiṣṭomikānām evānuvādaḥ.
children.translated_text: This position of [the word '<s>itara</s>' referring to] the <s>Śyena</s>-specific [properties] is not appropriate. Why? Because of non-proximity (<s>asannidhāna</s>). This word '<s>itara</s>' (the other) refers to what is proximate, and the <s>Śyena</s>-specific [properties] are not proximate in [this] injunction by the word '<s>Śyena</s>.' As to [the argument] that the word '<s>Śyena</s>' is specific — in the injunction view, the non-specificity would be a defect. But in the restatement view, nothing at all is being enjoined — so what is being specified? However, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-[properties], being common to all, also belong to the <s>Śyena</s> — thus a restatement is appropriate. Therefore it is a restatement only of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-[properties].

children.text: api vā yady apūrvatvād itarad adhikārthe jyautiṣṭomikād vidhes tadvācakaṃ samānaṃ syāt // MS_7,1.16 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, if — because of unprecedentedness — '<s>itara</s>' [means what is] in addition, it would be an injunction [of what is] additional to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [properties]; the word denoting that would be 'the same.' // MS_7,1.16 //

children.text:
api veti pakṣāntaraparigrahe. vidhir ayaṃ śyenavaiśeṣikāṇām, jyautiṣṭomikānām{*7/55*} anuvādaḥ. kutaḥ. apūrvatvāt. evam apūrvam arthaṃ vidhāsyati. tathā pravṛttiviśeṣakaro bhaviṣyati. anuvādaḥ sann apravṛttiviśeṣakaro 'narthakaḥ syāt. nanv itaraśabdo 'yaṃ sannihite bhvati. ucyate, itarad adhikārthe, samānam itarat, samānam adhikam ity arthaḥ.
nanu sannihitavacano 'yaṃ nādhikārtha iti{*7/56*}. ucyate, na kevalam ayaṃ sannihitavacana eva. pūrvoktasadṛśam asannihitam api brūte. avaśiṣṭaṃ ca. yadā hi vastrāṇy anukramyetaraśabdaḥ prayujyate, devadattāya kambalo dīyatām, viṣṇumitrāya kauśeyam, yajñadattāya kṣaumam, itarac caitrāyeti, tadā vastram eva pradīyate, na hiraṇyaṃ rajataṃ vā. iha jyautiṣṭomikebhyo 'dhikān dharmān{*7/57*} anukramyetaraśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ. tenātrāpy adhikān eva vaktum arhati. tathādhikavacano bhvati.
atha jyautiṣṭomikān brūte, tathā sannihitavacanaḥ. tatrāvaśyam anyatarad dheyam. yady adhikārthatāṃ hitvā sannihitārthatāśrīyate, anuvādamātram anarthakaṃ bhavati. śyenaśabdaś cāvivakṣitārthaḥ. atha sannihitārthatāṃ hitvādhikārthatā gṛhyate, na kaścid doṣo bhavati. tasmāt sūtrakāra āha, itarad adhikārtha iti. ato jyautiṣṭomikād vidher adhikāḥ śyenavaiśeṣikā ye, ta ihātidiśyante. tadvācakaṃ [14]{*7/58*} samānaṃ syāt. samānaśabdaḥ syād ity arthaḥ. bhavati śyenaśabdaś ca vivakṣitaḥ.
cāturmāsyānāṃ vaiśvadeva āgneyādīni{*7/59*} havīṃṣi sārthavādavākyair vihitāni. dharmāś ca teṣām uktāḥ. varuṇapraghāseṣu kevalāni havīṃṣy āmnāya, yad vaiśvadevikānāṃ brāhmaṇam, tat teṣām atidiśyate, etad brāhmaṇāny eva pañca havīṃṣi, yad brāhmaṇānītarāṇi{*7/60*} iti. tatra{*7/61*} kim arthavādamātrasyāyam atideśaḥ, uta sārthavādakasya savidhikasya kāṇḍasyeti{*7/62*}. kathaṃ punar arthavādamātrasyātideśo bhavati. yathā pampākulāyapratimāś ca vṛkṣā iti. ke punar vidhayaḥ, ke arthavādāḥ. tredhā sannaddhaṃ barhir bhavati{*7/63*}, tredhā sannaddha idhmaḥ{*7/64*}, nava prayājā nava anuyājā ityevamādayo vidhayaḥ. vārtaghnāni vaitāni havīṃṣīty arthavādāḥ. tatredam ucyate,
children.translated_text:
The words '<s>api vā</s>' indicate the adoption of the other position. This is an injunction of the <s>Śyena</s>-specific [properties]; of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-[properties] it is a restatement. Why? Because of unprecedentedness — thus it will enjoin an unprecedented meaning. Accordingly, it will be a distinguisher of procedure. Being [merely] a restatement, it would be purposeless, not distinguishing procedure. [The objector says:] but this word '<s>itara</s>' refers to what is proximate. [We] reply: '<s>itara</s>' [means what is] in addition — '<s>samāna</s>' [means] 'additional'; 'the same [as those already mentioned, plus] additional' is the meaning.
[The objector says:] but this [word '<s>itara</s>'] denotes what is proximate, not what is additional. [We] reply: this [word] is not exclusively one that denotes what is proximate. It also denotes what is similar to what was previously stated [but] not proximate. And [it denotes] the remainder. For when, having enumerated garments, the word '<s>itara</s>' is used — 'let a blanket be given to <s>Devadatta</s>, silk to <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>, linen to <s>Yajñadatta</s>, and the other (<s>itara</s>) to <s>Caitra</s>' — then what is given [to Caitra] is indeed a garment, not gold or silver. Here [in our text], having enumerated the properties additional to those of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the word '<s>itara</s>' is used. Therefore here too it should denote only what is additional. Thus it is a statement of what is additional.
But [if it] denotes the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-[properties], then it is a statement of what is proximate. Of these two, one must necessarily be adopted. If, abandoning the additional-meaning, the proximate-meaning is adopted, it becomes a mere purposeless restatement. And the word '<s>Śyena</s>' would have unintended meaning. But if, abandoning the proximate-meaning, the additional-meaning is adopted, no fault arises. Therefore the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras) says: '<s>itara</s>' [means what is] in addition. Therefore those that are specific to the <s>Śyena</s>, being additional to the injunction of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — they are being extended here. The word denoting that [14] would be 'the same' — meaning the word '<s>samāna</s>' [is used]. And the word '<s>Śyena</s>' has intended meaning.
In the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> (seasonal sacrifices), in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [section], oblation substances such as the <s>Āgneya</s> and others are enjoined together with <s>arthavāda</s> sentences. And their <s>dharmas</s> (ritual properties) are stated. In the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [section], the oblation substances alone are recorded, and what is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (explanatory text) of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [section] is extended to them: 'This is indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the five oblations — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the others [i.e., the Vaiśvadeva oblations].' There [the question arises]: is this an extension of the <s>arthavāda</s> alone, or of the entire section (<s>kāṇḍa</s>) including both <s>arthavāda</s> and injunctions? Now, how could there be an extension of <s>arthavāda</s> alone? As in '<s>Pampā</s>-shoreline-like are the trees' [which is merely descriptive]. And which are the injunctions, which are the <s>arthavādas</s>? 'The <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) is bound in three ways,' 'the kindling wood is bound in three ways,' 'nine preliminary offerings, nine subsequent offerings' — these and the like are the injunctions. 'These oblations are destructive of disease' — these are the <s>arthavādas</s>. There this is stated:

children.text: pañcasaṃcareṣv arthavādātideśaḥ sannidhānāt // MS_7,1.17 //
children.translated_text: In the five recurring [oblations], the extension is of the <s>arthavāda</s> [alone], because of proximity. // MS_7,1.17 //

children.text:
pañcatāni havīṃṣi sarvaparvasu saṃcarantīti pañcasaṃcarāṇīty ucyante. teṣu pañcasaṃcareṣv arthavādamātrasyātideśa iti. kutaḥ. sannidhānād dhaviṣāṃ sannihitā arthavādāḥ. vidhibhir{*7/65*} ekavākyasaṃbaddhatvāt, na dharmavidhayaḥ. kim ataḥ. ata etad bhavati, yat pūrveṣāṃ brāhmaṇam iti vyapadeśo yujyate. [15]{*7/66*} tad dhi teṣāṃ brāhmaṇam, yena vidhīyante. ko 'nyo haviṣāṃ brāhmaṇasya ca saṃbandho 'nyatra vidheyavidhāyakabhāvāt. arthavādaiś caitāni vidhīyante, na dharmavidhibhiḥ. dharmavidhibhis tu yāni vidhīyante, na tāni havīṃṣi. tasmād arthavādānām atideśo na dharmavidhīnām.
api ca varuṇapraghāseṣv api kecid vaiśvadevikā dharmā vidhīyante. yathā, agniṃ mathnanti prasuvo bhavantīti. teṣām atideśena vihitānāṃ punar āmnānam anarthakaṃ syāt, yadi vidhayo 'tidiśyeran. tasmād arthavādātideśa iti.
children.translated_text:
The five oblation substances that recur in all <s>parvans</s> (ritual junctures) are called the 'five recurrents' (<s>pañcasaṃcara</s>). In those five recurrents, the extension is of the <s>arthavāda</s> alone. Why? Because of the proximity of the <s>arthavādas</s> to the oblation substances. Because of being syntactically connected with the injunctions [15], [the arthavādas are proximate to the oblations,] not the property-injunctions. What follows from this? From this it follows that the designation 'the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the previous [oblations]' is appropriate. For that is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of those [oblations] by which they are enjoined. What other connection could there be between oblations and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> than the relationship of enjoined-and-enjoiner? And these [oblations] are enjoined by the <s>arthavādas</s>, not by the property-injunctions. But those [items] that are enjoined by the property-injunctions — those are not oblation substances. Therefore the extension is of the <s>arthavādas</s>, not of the property-injunctions.
Moreover, in the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [section] too, some <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>-properties are [independently] enjoined — such as 'they churn the fire; they become progressive.' Re-stating those [already] enjoined by extension would be purposeless, if the injunctions [too] were being extended. Therefore the extension is of the <s>arthavāda</s> [alone].

children.text: sarvasya vaikaśabdyāt // MS_7,1.18 //
children.translated_text: Or [the extension is] of the whole [section], because of the uniformity of the word. // MS_7,1.18 //

children.text: naitad evam, arthavādamātrasyātideśa iti. savidhikasya sārthavādakasya kāṇḍasyātideśa{*7/67*} iti. kutaḥ. aikaśabdyāt. samānaśabdatvād ity arthaḥ. samāno 'yaṃ brāhmaṇam iti śabdo vidhīnām arthavādānāṃ ca. sa yathārthavādān gṛhṇāti, evaṃ{*7/68*} vidhīn api gṛhṇāti cet, tān apy atidiśati. yat tu vidhīnāṃ havirbhiḥ saṃbandho nāstīti. vidheyavidhāyakasaṃbandho nāsti, upakāralakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandho bhaviṣyati. ka upakāraḥ. yas eṣām aṅgāni vidadhāti. asti cet saṃbandhaḥ, brāhmaṇaśabdaśrutyā sarvātideśo nyāyya iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that the extension is of the <s>arthavāda</s> alone. [Rather,] the extension is of the entire section including both injunctions and <s>arthavādas</s>. Why? Because of the uniformity of the word — meaning, because of the sameness of the word. This word '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' is the same for both injunctions and <s>arthavādas</s>. Just as it grasps the <s>arthavādas</s>, if it also grasps the injunctions, then it extends those too. As to [the objection] that the injunctions have no connection with the oblation substances — there is no enjoined-enjoiner connection, [but] there will be a connection characterized by assistance. What assistance? That which prescribes their subsidiaries. If there is such a connection, then by hearing the word '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' the extension of all is proper.

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca vidhīnām atideśaṃ darśayati. kiṃ liṅgam. varuṇapraghāseṣu triṃśadāhutayo vājino{*7/69*} yajanty āhutīnāṃ saṃpattyai triṃśattvāya{*7/70*} iti varuṇapraghāse{*7/71*} triṃśatam āhutīr darśayati. yadi vidhayo nātidiśyeran, tā na syuḥ. tasmād atidiśyante.
children.translated_text: And an indicatory mark shows the extension of injunctions. What indicatory mark? 'In the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [section], thirty oblations — the strong ones sacrifice — for the attainment of the thirty-fold [number] of oblations' — it shows thirty oblations in the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s>. If the injunctions were not being extended, those [thirty oblations] would not exist. Therefore they are being extended.

children.text: vihitāmnānān neti cet // MS_7,1.20 //
children.translated_text: If [one objects] because of the re-recording of what is [already] enjoined — // MS_7,1.20 //

children.text: vihitāmnānād iti yad uktam, tasya kaḥ parihāraḥ. ābhāṣāntaṃ{*7/73*} sūtram{*7/74*}.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'because of the re-recording of what is [already] enjoined' — what is the rebuttal of that? This is an introductory (<s>ābhāṣā</s>) <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text:

children.text: atrocyate, vidhyatideśe 'pi sati nāgnimanthanādīnām āmnānam anarthakam. itarasya haviṣo 'rthena bhaviṣyati, dakṣiṇavaihārikasya mārutyāḥ{*7/75*}. tasmān naitaj jñāpakam, vidhīnām anatideśasya bhaviṣyati.
children.translated_text: To this we reply: even when there is extension of the injunctions, the re-recording of fire-churning and the like is not purposeless. It will be for the purpose of the other oblation substance — [namely] the southern <s>Vaihārika</s> [fire's oblation] for <s>Mārutī</s>. Therefore this is not an indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) — it will not [indicate] the non-extension of the injunctions.

children.translated_text: And [the same applies] in the case of the single-potsherd [cake] for <s>Indrāgni</s> — likewise. // MS_7,1.22 //

children.text: vaiśvadeve ekakapāla āmnātaḥ, dyāvāpṛthivīya ekakapāla iti, varuṇapraghāseṣv api kāya ekakapāla iti. tatrāparaḥ, aindrāgno dvādaśakapālo mārutyāmikṣā{*7/76*} iti. tathā sākamedheṣv apy ekakapālaindrāgnāv āmnātau, aindrāgna ekādaśakapāla indrāya vṛtraghne caruḥ vaiśvakarmaṇa ekakapāla iti. tatredam āmnātam. etad brāhmaṇa aindrāgnaḥ, etad brāhmaṇa ekakapālaḥ{*7/77*}, yad brāhmaṇa itara itaraś ceti. tatredam ucyate, ekakapālaindrāgnau ca tadvat, yadvat pañcasaṃcarāṇi. atrāpi savidhikasya sārthavādakasya kāṇḍasyātideśaḥ. tenaiva nyāyeneti. prāptisūtram etad uttaracintārtham.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [section], a single-potsherd [cake] is recorded: 'a single-potsherd [cake] for <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth).' And in the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [section] too: 'to whom [does] the single-potsherd [cake belong]?' Likewise [there is]: 'a twelve-potsherd [cake] for <s>Indrāgni</s>; a <s>mārutyāmikṣā</s> (curds for <s>Mārutī</s>).' Similarly in the <s>Sākamedha</s> [section] too, the single-potsherd [cake] and [the cake] for <s>Indrāgni</s> are recorded: 'an eleven-potsherd [cake] for <s>Indrāgni</s>; a <s>caru</s> (porridge) for <s>Indra Vṛtraghna</s> (Indra the Slayer of Vṛtra); a single-potsherd [cake] for <s>Viśvakarman</s>.' There this is recorded: 'this is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the [cake] for <s>Indrāgni</s>; this is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the single-potsherd [cake] — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the other and the other.' There this is stated: the single-potsherd [cake] and the [cake] for <s>Indrāgni</s> — likewise, just like the five recurrents. Here too the extension is of the entire section including both injunctions and <s>arthavādas</s>. By the very same reasoning. This is a <s>prāpti</s> (establishment) <s>sūtra</s> for the purpose of subsequent investigation.

children.text: ekakapālānāṃ vaiśvadevikaḥ prakṛtir āgrayaṇe sarvahomāparivṛttidarśanād avabhṛthe ca sakṛd dvyavadānasya vacanāt // MS_7,1.23 //
children.translated_text: Of the single-potsherd [cakes], the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [section] is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) — because of the observation of non-reversal of all oblations in the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>, and because of the statement of a single two-cutting [procedure] in the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>. // MS_7,1.23 //

children.text:
sākamedhe śrūyate, etad brāhmaṇa{*7/79*} ekakapāla iti. tatra cintyate, vaiśvadevikasyaikakapālasyedaṃ grahaṇam uta vāruṇaprāghāsikasyeti. kiṃ prāptam. vaiśvadevikasyeti brūmaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam. tasya vihitā dharmāḥ, alaṃkṛtyābhipūryopāṃśu yaṣṭavyaḥ, āviḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kārya{*7/80*} ityevamādayaḥ. vāruṇaprāghāsikas tv adharmakaḥ. yasya vihitā dharmāḥ, tatraitad yujyate vaktum, tadvad idaṃ kartavyam iti. tasmād vaiśvadevikasya grahaṇam.
nanv aindrāgnasamuccāraṇād ekakapālo 'pi vāruṇaprāghāsika eva syāt. na, avaśyam ekaparvaṇor eva samuccāraṇena bhavitavyam, nānāparvaṇor api samuccāraṇam aviruddham. tasmād vaiśvadevikasya grahaṇam.
iti prāpte ucyate, vāruṇaprāghāsikasyaikakapālasya grahaṇam iti. kutaḥ. tata{*7/81*} ekakapālānāṃ vaiśvadevikaḥ prakṛtiḥ. kathaṃ jñāyate. āgrayaṇe sarvahomāparivṛttidarśanāt. āgrayaṇe dyāvāpṛthivīyasyaikakapālasya sarvahomam aparyāvṛttiṃ{*7/82*} ca darśayati. yat sarvahutaṃ karoti, sā tv ekā paricakṣā, huto hutaḥ{*7/83*} paryāvartate, sā dvitīyā. ājyasyaiva dyāvāpṛthivyau yajeti{*7/84*} iti, ājyayāgavidhipare vākya ekakapālasya sarvahomam aparyāvṛttiṃ ca prāptāṃ darśayati. etasmād darśanād avabhṛthe ca sakṛd dvyavadānasya vacanāt. avabhṛte cāvadhāraṇaṃ bhavati, idam evaikakapālasya dvir avadyatīti. tena jñāyate, nūnam anyatra na dvir avadānam iti. tac caitat sarvaṃ vaiśvadevika ekakapāle vihitam. tasmād ekakapālānāṃ vaiśvadevikaḥ prakṛtiḥ. kim ataḥ. sākamedhike 'py ekakapāle vaiśvadevikā dharmāḥ prāptāḥ, teṣām atideśo 'narthakaḥ. vāruṇaprāghāsikasya ye dharmāḥ vaiśeṣikā aprāptāḥ, teṣām atideśo 'rthavān. tasmād vāruṇaprāghāsikasyaikakapālasyedaṃ grahaṇam iti. ucyate, liṅgam etat. kutaḥ prāptir iti. prāptim uttaratra vakṣyāmaḥ, svarasāmaikakapālāmikṣaṃ cety atra. ke punas te dharmāḥ. hiraṇyamayaḥ sruvaḥ śamīmayo{*7/85*} vetyevamādayaḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Sākamedha</s> rites it is heard: 'This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is a one-potsherd [cake].' There it is investigated: is this a reference to the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s> (offered to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>) one-potsherd [cake], or to the <s>Vāruṇaprāghāsika</s> (offered to <s>Varuṇa</s> in the <s>Prāghāsa</s> rite) [one-potsherd cake]? What is the prima facie view? We say it refers to the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s>. What is the reason? Its <s>dharmas</s> (ritual properties) are prescribed: 'having adorned, having filled, one should sacrifice silently; it should be performed openly when requested' — and so forth. But the <s>Vāruṇaprāghāsika</s> is without [prescribed] properties. It is fitting to say regarding the one whose properties are prescribed: 'this should be done in the same way.' Therefore [this is] a reference to the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s>.
[The objector says:] but since it is mentioned together with the <s>Aindrāgna</s>, the one-potsherd [cake] too should be the <s>Vāruṇaprāghāsika</s> alone. [We reply:] no — the co-mention necessarily pertains to those of the same [ritual] division alone; co-mention of those from different divisions is also not contradictory. Therefore [this is] a reference to the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s>.
Given this prima facie view, we say: this is a reference to the <s>Vāruṇaprāghāsika</s> one-potsherd [cake]. How so? Because the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s> is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the one-potsherd [cakes]. How is this known? From the observation of whole-oblation and non-reversal in the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> rite. In the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>, [the text] shows the whole-oblation and non-reversal of the <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s> one-potsherd [cake]. 'He makes it a whole-oblation' — that is the first specification; 'the offered [cake], having been offered, is reversed' — that is the second. 'He sacrifices to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> with ghee alone' — in a sentence whose purport is the prescription of the ghee-offering, it shows the whole-oblation and non-reversal as already obtained for the one-potsherd [cake]. From this observation, and from the statement of the two-cut portion being done once in the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), [we know this]. In the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> there is a determination: 'this alone is cut twice for the one-potsherd [cake].' From this it is known: 'surely elsewhere there is no double cutting.' And all this is prescribed for the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s> one-potsherd [cake]. Therefore the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s> is the archetype of one-potsherd [cakes]. What follows from this? In the <s>Sākamedha</s> one-potsherd [cake] too, the <s>Vaiśvadevika</s> properties are already obtained [by extension]; their transfer (<s>atideśa</s>) would be purposeless. The specific properties of the <s>Vāruṇaprāghāsika</s> that are not [already] obtained — their transfer would be meaningful. Therefore this is a reference to the <s>Vāruṇaprāghāsika</s> one-potsherd [cake]. [To this] we say: this is an indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>). [The question] 'how is [the archetype] obtained?' — we will state the obtainment later, in [the section] 'the <s>Svara</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, one-potsherd [cake], and <s>āmikṣā</s>.' And what are those properties? 'A golden ladle, [or one] made of <s>śamī</s> wood' — and so forth.

children.text: sāmno 'bhidhānaśabdena pravṛttiḥ syād yathāśiṣṭam // MS_7,2.1 //

children.text:
idaṃ śrūyate, rathantaram uttarayor gāyati{*7/87*}, kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyati{*7/88*} ityevamādīni samāmnāyante. tatra cintā, kim ihātidiśyate iti.
nanu yad rathantarādibhiḥ śabdair ucyate, tad atidiśyate. bāḍham. tad eva tu na jñāyate kim ebhiḥ śabdair ucyata iti.
nanu siddham etat, gīteṣu sāmākhyā{*7/89*} iti. tathā siddhasyākṣepaḥ kariṣyate. sa eva tu nirṇayo bhaviṣyati. yadio sa eva nirṇayaḥ, kim arthaḥ ākṣepaḥ. dārḍhyārthaḥ, sthūṇānikhananavat. tatra kiṃ prāptam. tad ucyate, sa stobhasvarakālābhyāsavikārāyāṃ hiṅkārapraṇavaprastāvodgīthapratihāropadravanidhanavatyām ṛci gītau{*7/90*} sāmaśabdo 'bhiyuktair upacaryate{*7/91*}. tasmāt saṃśayaḥ.
ucyate, nanu gītau satyāṃ bhāvād nānākhyasya saṃskārakarmaṇo vācakā ete śabdā ity uktam. tad evedam uktam ākṣipyate. neme saṃskārasya vācakāḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam. akarmakāle prayogāt. akarmakāle sāma prayujyate. na ca saṃskārakarmaṇi prokṣaṇāvakṣepaṇaparyagnikaraṇādīny akarmakāle prayujyante. prayojanābhāvāt. atha nu [20]{*7/92*} mantrā ete, tato 'nv ahaṃ svādhyo 'dhyetavya iti niyamād akarmakāle prayogo yujyate. tasmād ṛcāṃ nāmāni.
kiṃ ca, saṃjñābhedāt. saṃjñābhedaś ca bhavati, rathantaraṃ bṛhad ityevamādiḥ. sa ekatvāt saṃskārakarmaṇo anarthakaḥ. ekenaiva hi tadā paryāptam. yathā gītir iti. atharcāṃ nāmāni, tatas tāsāṃ bhedāt saṃjñāpṛthaktvaṃ yuktam.
api ca. yadi gānaṃ rathantaraṃ gānaṃ ca bṛhat, idaṃ rathantaram idaṃ bṛhad iti pṛthaktvena saṃjñāniveśo nopapadyate. ṛṅnāmatve tūpapadyate.
kiṃ ca, vikārapṛthaktvāt tu. pratisāma ca vikārapṛthaktvāt. pratisāma ca vikārapṛthaktvaṃ dṛśyate. tad ekatvād gānasya, anupapannam. saṃskārabhede hi vikārapṛthaktvaṃ dṛṣṭam. tad yathā, avahantes taṇḍulībhāvaḥ, piṣeś cūrṇam. na tv ekasya taṇḍulībhāvaś cūrṇanaṃ ca. atharṅnāmāny etāni. tata ṛcāṃ bhedād vikārapṛthaktvaṃ yujyate. tasmād ṛṅnāmānīti. tata uttaraṃ paṭhati, sāmno 'bhidhānaśabdena pravṛttiḥ syād yathāśiṣṭam iti. sāmno 'bhidhānaśabdena yathāśiṣṭam pravṛttiḥ syāt. yac chiṣṭaṃ pravaktṛbhiḥ śiṣyebhyaḥ. kiṃ ca śiṣṭam. stomādiviśiṣṭā ṛk sāma, sā pravarteta. kiṃ kāraṇam. tasyā rathantarādi nāmadheyam iti.
children.translated_text:
This is heard: 'He sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the latter [pressings]'; 'He sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]' — and such [statements] are recorded. There the inquiry is: what is being transferred (<s>atidiśyate</s>) here?
[The objector says:] surely, whatever is denoted by the words '<s>Rathantara</s>' and the like — that is being transferred. True. But the very thing that is denoted by these words is not known.
[The objector says:] but this is settled — '<s>Sāman</s>' is a designation for what is sung [as stated in MS 1.4.3]. [We reply:] that settled [position] will be challenged. But that very [challenge] will [lead to] the definitive conclusion. If it is the same conclusion, what is the purpose of the challenge? For the purpose of strengthening [the conclusion] — like the driving-in of a post.
There, what is the prima facie view? It is said: that word '<s>Sāman</s>' is used figuratively by the learned for an <s>ṛc</s> (Vedic verse) when it is sung — [that is,] when it possesses modifications of <s>stobha</s> (exclamatory syllables), <s>svara</s> (melodic accent), <s>kāla</s> (timing), and <s>abhyāsa</s> (repetition), and possesses the [parts called] <s>hiṅkāra</s>, <s>praṇava</s>, <s>prastāva</s>, <s>udgītha</s>, <s>pratihāra</s>, <s>upadrava</s>, and <s>nidhana</s>. Therefore there is doubt.
[We] reply: but when the singing [takes place], these words designate a transformative process (<s>saṃskārakarman</s>) with diverse names, as stated. This is what is now being said, and challenged. These [words] are not designations of the transformative process. What is the reason? Because of usage at non-ritual times. The <s>Sāman</s> is employed at non-ritual times. But the [operations of] transformative process — sprinkling, casting-in, circumambulation by fire, and the like — are not employed at non-ritual times, because of the absence of purpose. Now, [20] if these [words] are mantras, then because of the rule 'they should be studied by daily recitation,' employment at non-ritual times is fitting. Therefore they are names of <s>ṛc</s>s.
Moreover, because of differentiation of designations. There is differentiation of designations — '<s>Rathantara</s>,' '<s>Bṛhat</s>,' and so forth. That [differentiation], since the transformative process is one [and the same], would be purposeless. For in that case a single [name] would suffice — such as '<s>gīti</s>' (singing). But if they are names of <s>ṛc</s>s, then because of the differentiation of the <s>ṛc</s>s, the separateness of designations is fitting.
Furthermore, because even a child would [not accept this]. If the singing is the <s>Rathantara</s> and the singing is the <s>Bṛhat</s>, then placing designations separately as 'this is the <s>Rathantara</s>, this is the <s>Bṛhat</s>' is not fitting. But if they are names of <s>ṛc</s>s, it is fitting.
Moreover, because of the separateness of modifications. For each <s>Sāman</s>, the separateness of modifications is observed. That, since the singing [process] is one, is unfitting. For separateness of modifications is observed in [separate] transformative processes — as husking [results in] the grain-state, grinding [results in] flour. But a single [substance] does not have both the grain-state and grinding. But if these are names of <s>ṛc</s>s, then because of the differentiation of the <s>ṛc</s>s, the separateness of modifications is fitting. Therefore they are names of <s>ṛc</s>s.
Accordingly, [the teacher] reads the next [<s>sūtra</s>]: 'The application should be by the designating word of the <s>Sāman</s>, as instructed.' The application of the <s>Sāman</s> should be by the designating word, as instructed — as taught by teachers to students. And what is instructed? The <s>ṛc</s> characterized by specific <s>stoma</s> and the like is the <s>Sāman</s> — that should be applied. What is the reason? Its designation is '<s>Rathantara</s>' and the like.

children.text: śabdais tv arthavidhitvād arthāntare 'pravṛttiḥ syāt pṛthagbhāvāt kriyāyā hy abhisaṃbandhaḥ // MS_7,2.2 //
children.translated_text: But because of the words being for meaning-prescription, there would be no application to a different meaning, because of separateness; for the connection is with the action. // MS_7,2.2 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣanivṛttau. na tv evaṃ syāt, ṛcaḥ pravṛttir iti. katham. iha kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyatīti kavatīnāṃ vā kārye 'bhivatyo{*7/93*} 'tidiśyeran, kavatīnāṃ{*7/94*} vopary [21]{*7/95*} ādhāryādheyabhāvena{*7/96*}. tatra kārye tāvad atideśo na ghaṭate. kutaḥ. śabdair arthavidhitvāt. śabdānām arthavidhānaṃ kāryam. na ca, kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyatīti kavatībhir yo 'rtho 'bhidhīyate, tam abhivatyaḥ śaknuvanti vaktum. tasmān na karyātideśaḥ. ādheyatve 'pi na saṃbhavati, pṛthagbhāvāt. na hi śabdaḥ śabde samavaiti, pṛthag evāvatiṣṭhate. abhi tvā, kayā na iti{*7/97*}. kriyāyā hi gānakriyāyāḥ{*7/98*} śabdenābhisaṃbandho bhavet, na śabdasya. tasmād ādheyatvenāpi nātideśaḥ. ato nāyam ṛcaḥ pradeśa iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>tu</s> ('but') indicates the reversal of the position. But it should not be so — that the <s>ṛc</s> is what is to be applied. How so? Here, 'he sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]' — either the <s>Abhivati</s> [verses] would be transferred to the performance of the <s>Kavatīs</s>, or the <s>Abhivatis</s> [would be transferred] over the <s>Kavatīs</s> in a superimposition relation. Now, transfer to the performance is not fitting. Why? Because words are for meaning-prescription. The function of words is to prescribe a meaning. And the <s>Abhivati</s> [verses] cannot state the meaning that is denoted by the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] in 'he sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>Kavatīs</s>.' Therefore there is no transfer of performance. Superimposition too is not possible, because of separateness. For a word does not co-inhere in [another] word — [each] remains separate. '<s>abhi tvā</s>, <s>kayā naḥ</s>' [are separate verses]. For it is with the action — the action of singing — that a word would have a connection, not with [another] word. Therefore there is no transfer even by superimposition. Hence this is not a case of [applying] the <s>ṛc</s>.

children.text: svārthe vā syāt prayojanaṃ kriyāyās tadaṅgabhāvenopadiśyeran // MS_7,2.3 //
children.translated_text: Or they would be taught as subsidiaries of their own purpose and of the [other's] action. // MS_7,2.3 //

children.text:
svārtha vā pravartamānā abhivatyaḥ kavatīnām aṅgabhāvenopadiśyeran. kathaṃ punaḥ kavatīṣu gāyatīty aṅgabhāvaḥ śakya upadeṣṭum. śakyo yathā, yena karmaṇertset tatra jayān juhuyād{*7/99*} iti. kiṃ punaḥ prayojanaṃ kavatīnām abhivatyo nirvartayantīti. ucyate, prayojanam adṛṣṭaṃ kalpyam. kutaḥ. kriyāyāḥ. yasmāt kriyā śrūyate, kavatīṣu rathanataraṃ gāyatīti, yathā prayājādīnāṃ prayojanaṃ kriyāyāḥ.
ucyate, ayam evāsmin pakṣe doṣaḥ, yat prayojanaṃ kriyāyāḥ kalpayitavyam. tasmād ayam api pakṣo duḥśliṣṭaḥ.
children.translated_text:
Or, functioning for their own purpose, the <s>Abhivati</s> [verses] would be taught as subsidiaries of the <s>Kavatīs</s>. But how can the subsidiary relationship be taught in 'he sings [the Rathantara] in the <s>Kavatīs</s>'? It can be — just as 'in whatever ritual action one would [seek to] prosper, one should offer <s>jaya</s> oblations.' And what purpose do the <s>Abhivati</s> [verses] serve for the <s>Kavatīs</s>? We say: an unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) purpose should be postulated. Why? Because of the action — because an action is heard, 'he sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>Kavatīs</s>' — just as the purpose of the <s>prayājas</s> and other [preliminaries comes] from the action.
[We] reply: this is precisely the defect in this position — that a purpose must be postulated from the action. Therefore this position too is poorly constructed.

NOTES:
[{7/99: Cf. commentary on MS 3.4.25-27}]

children.text: śabdamātram iti cet // MS_7,2.4 //
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is the word alone [that is transferred] — // MS_7,2.4 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, kavatyaṅgabhāvenābhivatīnām upadeśo duḥśliṣṭa iti, tena tarhi śabdamātraṃ pradiśyatām. ratha[22]{*7/100*}ntaraśabdaṃ kavatīṣu prayuñjīta. kavatīḥ rathantaraśabdenābhilaped iti. kiṃ kāranam. śabda uccarite. tatra tāvan mukhyā pratipattiḥ. śabde kāryasyāsaṃbhavāt, arthe kāryaṃ vijñāyate, yathā gām ānayeti. iha tu śabda eva kāryaṃ saṃbhavati, nārthe. ato 'tra śabdaṃ vijñāsyāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that teaching the <s>Abhivatis</s> as subsidiaries of the <s>Kavatīs</s> is poorly constructed — then let the word alone be what is indicated. One should employ the <s>Rathantara</s>-word in the <s>Kavatīs</s>. One should call the <s>Kavatīs</s> by the <s>Rathantara</s>-word. What is the reason? The word is what is uttered. There, the primary understanding is first [sought]. Since an operation is not possible in the [mere] word, the operation is understood in the referent — just as 'bring a cow.' But here the operation is possible in the word itself, not in the referent. Therefore here we shall understand the word [as what is transferred].

children.text: nautpattikatvāt // MS_7,2.5 //
children.translated_text: Not so, because of [the word-referent relation] being innate (<s>autpattika</s>). // MS_7,2.5 //

children.text: pūrvasmād eṣa vādaḥ pāpīyān. kasmāt. autpattikatvāt. autpattiko hi nāmināmnoḥ saṃbandhaḥ. yaḥ śabdo yasmin artha autpattikena saṃbandhena prasiddhaḥ. na sa tato 'nyaṃ pratyāyayituṃ śaknoti. na hi gośabdenāśvo 'bhidhātuṃ śakyate.
children.translated_text: This position is worse than the previous one. Why? Because of [the word-referent relation] being innate. For the relation between name and named is innate. Whatever word is well known in whatever meaning by the innate relation — that [word] cannot make known something other than that [meaning]. For the meaning 'horse' cannot be denoted by the word 'cow.'

children.text: śāstraṃ caivam anarthakaṃ syāt // MS_7,2.6 //
children.translated_text: And the teaching (<s>śāstra</s>) would thus be purposeless. // MS_7,2.6 //

children.text: evaṃ ca saty atideśaśāstram anarthakaṃ syāt, aśakyārthatvāt. tasmān na śabdasyāpi pradeśo yuktaḥ. vṛttikāras tu mene, gānaśāstram aukthikyam anarthakaṃ syād iti. tasyābhiprāyaḥ, satyāṃ gatau naitāvān prayāsaḥ śiṣṭānām aphalo 'bhyupagantuṃ nyāyya iti.
children.translated_text: And this being so, the teaching of transfer (<s>atideśa</s>) would be purposeless, because of its purport being impossible. Therefore the indication of the word too is not fitting. But the commentator (<s>Vṛttikāra</s>) held that the <s>gānaśāstra</s> (teaching of singing) — the <s>Aukthikya</s> — would be purposeless. His intent is: given that this [understanding] is possible, it is not proper for the learned to accept so great an effort as fruitless.

children.text: svarasyeti cet // MS_7,2.7 //
children.translated_text: If [one says it is] of the melodic accent (<s>svara</s>) — // MS_7,2.7 //

children.text: iti cet paśyasi, nāmno 'tideśo 'yukta iti. tena [23]{*7/101*} tarhi svarasyātideśo bhavatu. svaraḥ sāmaśabdena loke 'bhidhīyate. susāmā devadatta iti. susvaro devadatta iti. svaro ghoṣo nāda{*7/102*} iti samānārthāḥ. sa sāmaśabdenocyate, sāma ca rathantaram. tasmāt tasyātideśaḥ.
children.translated_text: If you see it thus — that the transfer of the name is not fitting — then let the transfer be of the melodic accent. The word '<s>Sāman</s>' in ordinary usage denotes melodic accent. '<s>Devadatta</s> is <s>susāman</s> (melodious)' [means] '<s>Devadatta</s> has a good voice.' 'Voice,' 'sound,' '<s>nāda</s>' (tone) — these are synonymous. That is denoted by the word '<s>Sāman</s>,' and '<s>Sāman</s>' is the <s>Rathantara</s>. Therefore its transfer [is proposed].

children.text: nārthābhāvāc chruter asaṃbandhaḥ // MS_7,2.8 //
children.translated_text: Not so — because of the absence of the meaning, [there is] no connection with the [Vedic] text (<s>śruti</s>). // MS_7,2.8 //

children.text: naitad evam, svarasyātideśa iti. kutaḥ. arthābhāvād arthasyābhāvat. arthasyābhivatīsvarasya kavatīṣv abhāvāt. nanv asann evāsāv atideśena bhāvyate. ucyate, bhāvayitum api na śakyate. na hy abhivatyakṣarāṇām abhivyañjako nādaḥ kavatīṣu bhāvayituṃ śakyaḥ. yadi bhāvyeta, na kavatyo bhaveyuḥ. na ced bhāvyate, na bhūtaḥ. kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyatīty etasyāḥ śruteḥ padāntareṇābhisaṃbandho{*7/103*} na syāt. tasmān na svarasyātideśaḥ.
children.translated_text: This is not so — that the transfer is of the melodic accent. Why? Because of the absence of the meaning — because of the absence of the <s>Abhivati</s> melodic accent in the <s>Kavatīs</s>. [The objector says:] but that which does not exist is precisely what is brought into being by the transfer. [We] reply: it cannot be brought into being either. For the tone (<s>nāda</s>) that manifests the syllables of the <s>Abhivati</s> [verses] cannot be brought into being in the <s>Kavatīs</s>. If it were brought into being, they would not be <s>Kavatīs</s> [anymore]. And if it is not brought into being, it does not exist. [Then] there would be no connection of the words of this <s>śruti</s> — 'he sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>Kavatīs</s>' — with one another. Therefore the transfer is not of the melodic accent.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{7/103: E2: śruteḥ padānāṃ paraspareṇābhisaṃbandho}*
children.translated_text:
NOTES:
[{7/103: E2: <s>śruteḥ padānāṃ paraspareṇābhisaṃbandho</s>}]

children.text: svaras tūtpattiṣu syān mātrāvarṇāvibhaktatvāt // MS_7,2.9 //
children.translated_text: But the melodic accent would [apply] in [the production of] sound-origins, because of the non-distinction of <s>mātrā</s> (duration) and <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme). // MS_7,2.9 //

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣāntaraparigrahe. yady abhivatīsvarasya kavatīṣu pradeśo nopapadyate, anuvādo bhavatu, kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyatīti. katham. tad ucyate, iha kavatīṣu rathanatraṃ gāyatīty asya vākyasya dve vacanavyaktī bhavataḥ. kavatīṣu yad rathantaram, tad gāyatīty ekā. rathantaraṃ yat, tat kavatīṣu gāyatīty aparā. tayor yaiṣā dvitīyā, rathantaraṃ yat tat kavatīṣu gāyatīti. sā svarasya sāmatve na saṃbhavatīty uktam. na hy abhivatīsvaraḥ kavatīṣu samāveśayituṃ śakya iti. pūrvā tu saṃbhavati. kavatīṣu yad rathantaram, tad gāyatīti.
nanu sāpi na saṃbhavati. na hi kavatīṣu rathantaram asti. [24]{*7/104*} ataḥ param ucyate, svaras tūtpattiṣu syāt. svaras tv abhivatīsvaraḥ, kavatīnām utpattiṣūccāraṇeṣu syāt. katham. mātrāvarṇāvibhaktatvāt. bahavo mātrāvarṇāś cābhivatīnāṃ kavatīnāṃ cāvibhaktā abhibhavatīṣv api vidyante, kavatīṣv api. so 'sāv abhivatīsvaraḥ kavatīṣu sādhāraṇavarṇasamaveto vidyate, tasyānuvādo 'yaṃ ghaṭate, kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyatīti. tasmāt svarasyānuvādaḥ.
children.translated_text:
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) introduces the acceptance of another position. If the placement of the <s>Abhivatī</s> tone (<s>svara</s>) in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] is not possible, let [the sentence] be a restatement: 'In the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] one sings the <s>Rathantara</s>.' How? This is explained: here, the sentence 'In the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] one sings the <s>Rathantara</s>' has two possible construals. The first: 'That <s>Rathantara</s> which is in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] — one sings that.' The second: 'The <s>Rathantara</s>, whatever it is — one sings it in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses].' Of these two, the second — 'the <s>Rathantara</s>, whatever it is, one sings in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]' — has been said to be impossible when the tone [is taken as] the <s>Sāman</s>. For the <s>Abhivatī</s> tone cannot be fitted into the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]. But the first [construal] is possible: 'That <s>Rathantara</s> which is in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] — one sings that.'
[The objector says:] but even that is not possible — for there is no <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]. After this, it is stated: 'but the tone would be in the originary [recitations].' The tone — the <s>Abhivatī</s> tone — would be in the originary recitations (<s>utpatti</s>) of the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]. How? Because of the non-differentiation of syllable-measures (<s>mātrāvarṇa</s>). Many syllable-measures of the <s>Abhivatī</s> and <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] are undifferentiated — they are found both in the <s>Abhivatī</s> [verses] and in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]. That <s>Abhivatī</s> tone, being present in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] as conjoined with their common syllables, [makes possible] this restatement: 'In the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] one sings the <s>Rathantara</s>.' Therefore it is a restatement of the tone.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_7,2.10 //
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_7,2.10 //

children.text:
liṅgaṃ ca dṛśyata etasminn arthe. asti rathantaram uttarayor{*7/105*} iti. kiṃ talliṅgaṃ bhavati. evam āha, rathantaram uttarayor na paśyāmi{*7/106*} iti viśvāmitras tapas tepe, bṛhad uttarayor na paśyāmīti vasiṣṭha iti. yac ca vidyamānaṃ na dṛśyate, taddarśanāya yatnaḥ. kriyate, yathā ghaṭaṃ na paśyāmīti pradīpaṃ karoti, na śaśaviṣāṇaṃ na paśyāmīti. tasmād asty uttarayo rathantaraṃ bṛhac ca. tayor anuvāda iti.
NOTES:
*{7/105: SV 680, 681}*
*{7/106: SV 809-810}*
children.translated_text:
And an indicatory mark is observed for this meaning. 'There is a <s>Rathantara</s> in the latter two [days].' What is that indicatory mark? Thus it is stated: '<s>Viśvāmitra</s> performed austerities [saying] "I do not see the <s>Rathantara</s> in the latter two"; <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [said] "I do not see the <s>Bṛhat</s> in the latter two."' And what exists but is not seen — effort is made to see it; just as [one says] 'I do not see the pot' and lights a lamp — not 'I do not see a hare's horn.' Therefore the <s>Rathantara</s> and <s>Bṛhat</s> do exist in the latter two [days]. [The sentence] is a restatement of them.
NOTES:
[{7/105: SV 680, 681}]
[{7/106: SV 809-810}]

children.text: aśrutes tu vikārasyottarāsu yathāśruti // MS_7,2.11 //
children.translated_text: But because of the non-hearing [of any modification], the modification in the latter [verses should be applied] as per the [original] hearing. // MS_7,2.11 //

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati. naitad evam, svarasyānuvāda iti. kutaḥ. evaṃ saty uttarāsu vikāro na kaścic chruto bhavati. tadottarā yathāśrutāḥ prayoktavyāḥ. yathā svādhyāyakāle śrutāḥ. tatra rathantaram uttarayor gāyatīty etad anuvādamātram apravṛttiviśeṣakaram anarthakam evāpavadyate. ato na svarasyānuvādo yuktaḥ. [25]{*7/107*}
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [previous] position. This is not so — that it is a restatement of the tone. Why? If this were so, no modification would be heard in the latter [verses]. Then the latter [verses] should be employed as heard — as [they were] heard at the time of Vedic study (<s>svādhyāya</s>). There, 'one sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the latter two' would be dismissed as a mere restatement without effect on performance, [and thus] purposeless. Therefore a restatement of the tone is not fitting.

children.text: śabdānāṃ cāsāmañjasyam // MS_7,2.12 //
children.translated_text: And there would be inconsistency of the [<s>Sāman</s>-]words. // MS_7,2.12 //

children.text:
rathantarādīnāṃ ca sāmaśabdānām asāmañjasyaṃ syāt. rathantaram uttarayoḥ, bṛhad uttarayor iti. katham. tad ucyate, ayaṃ rathantaraśabdo bṛhacchabdo vā svarasya sāmaśabdatve svarasamudāya ānupūrvyā vyavasthite{*7/108*} svaraviśeṣe prayuktaḥ. sa ekadeśe bhinnānupūrvye vāsamañjaso{*7/109*} bhavati. tasmāt naitad yuktam. svarasya sāmaśabdaḥ, tasya cānuvāda iti.
atrāha, evaṃ bhavatā sarve pakṣā niruddhāḥ. tataḥ kim apravṛttir eveti. ucyate, ṛca eva pradeśo bhavatu. nanūktam, na śakyā ṛca ṛgantare pradeṣṭum iti. bāḍham, deśalakṣaṇā bhaviṣyati. kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyatīty ucyate. na ca śakyate kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gātum. tatra deśalakṣaṇā bhavati kavatīdeśa iti. yathā, agnau tiṣṭhati, kūpe tiṣṭhatīti. dharmalakṣaṇā vā syāt. rathantaradharmā vā kavatīṣu rathantaraśabdenātidiśyante. yathā, rathantare prastūyamāne pṛthivīṃ manasā dhyāyed{*7/110*} ityevamādayaḥ. yathācārye proṣite, ācāryānī bhavatām ācārya{*7/111*} ity ācāryaśuśruṣācāryānyām atidiśyate.
children.translated_text:
And there would be inconsistency of the <s>Sāman</s>-words such as <s>Rathantara</s> and others — 'the <s>Rathantara</s> in the latter two, the <s>Bṛhat</s> in the latter two.' How? This is explained: these words '<s>Rathantara</s>' and '<s>Bṛhat</s>' are used, on the view that the tone is the <s>Sāman</s>, for a specific tone established in a fixed sequence of the tonal aggregate. That [word] becomes inconsistent when [the sequence is] partially altered. Therefore this is not fitting — that the tone is [what is denoted by] the <s>Sāman</s>-word, and that [the sentence] is a restatement of it.
Here [the objector] says: thus you have refuted all positions. What then — should there be no performance at all? It is replied: let there be a placement of the <s>ṛc</s> (verse) [itself]. [The objector:] but it was said that an <s>ṛc</s> cannot be placed in another <s>ṛc</s>. True — [but] it will be a place-designation (<s>deśalakṣaṇā</s>). 'One sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]' is stated. And the <s>Rathantara</s> cannot be sung in the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses literally]. There, a place-designation occurs — 'at the location of the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]' — just as 'he stands in the fire,' 'he stands in the well.' Or it may be a property-designation (<s>dharmalakṣaṇā</s>). The properties of the <s>Rathantara</s> are extended to the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses] by the word '<s>Rathantara</s>.' Such as: 'When the <s>Rathantara</s> is being chanted, one should mentally meditate on the earth' — and similar [rules]. Just as 'when the teacher is absent, let the teacher's wife be the teacher for you' — the service due to the teacher is extended to the teacher's wife.

NOTES:
[{7/108: E2: <s>avasthite</s>}]
[{7/109: E2: <s>cāsamañjaso</s>}]
[{7/110: <s>Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa</s> 7.7.15}]
[{7/111: <s>Āpastamba Dharmasūtra</s> 1.2.7}]

children.text: api tu karmaśabdaḥ syād bhāvo 'rthaḥ prasiddhagrahaṇatvād vikāro hy aviśiṣṭo 'nyaiḥ // MS_7,2.13 //
children.translated_text: But rather, it would be an action-word (<s>karmaśabda</s>); the meaning is the [singing] process, because of being grasped through well-known [usage]; for the modification is undifferentiated from other [refinement-actions]. // MS_7,2.13 //

children.text:
api tu naivaṃ syāt, ṛcaḥ sāmaśabdaḥ. tasyāś ca pradeśa iti. tathā deśalakṣaṇā dharmalakṣaṇā vāśrayaṇīyā. agatiś caiṣā yallakṣaṇāparigrahaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. karmaśabdaḥ syāt. rathantarādir gānākhyasya saṃskārakarmaṇo vācakaḥ. kutaḥ. ukto nyāyo gītiṣu sāmākhyā{*7/112*} ity atra. tatra gīti[26]{*7/113*}viśiṣṭāyām ṛci, eṣa śabdo dṛṣṭaḥ. na cāgṛhītaviśeṣaṇā viśeṣye buddhir utpadyate. tasmād viśeṣaṇaṃ tāvad abhidhīyate. viśeṣaṇapratyayāc ca sahacarite viśiṣṭe pratyayaḥ. ato nāsty ṛcaḥ śabdena saṃsparśa iti. tenaiva nyāyena gītināmadheyam iti brūmaḥ.
kiṃ ca prasiddhagrahaṇatvāt. ayaṃ ca gāyatīti śabdo gānakriyāyāṃ prasiddhaḥ. kā punar asau śabdasyoccāraṇaviśeṣaḥ. gāyati gānaṃ karotīti, tadgrahaṇaś ca rathantarādiśabdaḥ. tadvacana ity arthaḥ. tena samuccāraṇād dvitīyāsāmarthyāc ca. yathā, āsāritakaṃ gāyatīti, vardhamānakaṃ gāyatīti.
nanu śabdavacanenāpi samuccāraṇaṃ bhavati, gāthāṃ gāyati, ṛcaṃ gāyati{*7/114*} iti.
satyam, vipariṇamya tu śabdam, gānena ṛcaṃ saṃskarotīti yathānipatitenārthena na saṃbadhyate gānaṃ karotīty ṛcam iti. tasmād gītivacanaḥ.
itaś ca gītivacanaḥ. kutaḥ. vikāro hy aviśiṣṭo 'nyaiḥ. vikāraś cātrargdravyasya dṛśyate. hrasvānām akṣarāṇāṃ dīrghatā, dīrghāṇāṃ ca hrasvatvam. vivṛtānāṃ saṃvṛtatvam, saṃvṛtānāṃ vivṛtatvam. so 'viśiṣṭo 'nyaiḥ saṃskārakarmabhiḥ. yathāvahantinā vrīhīṇāṃ taṇḍulībhāvaḥ, piṣiṇā taṇḍulānāṃ piṣṭībhāvaḥ. tasmāc chabdānāṃ saṃskāro gānākhyo rathantarādibhiḥ śabdair ucyate. tasyāyaṃ pradeśaḥ, rathantaram uttarayor gāyatītyevamādiḥ.
children.translated_text:
But rather, it should not be so — that the <s>Sāman</s>-word denotes the <s>ṛc</s> (verse), and that there is a placement of it. Or that a place-designation or property-designation should be resorted to — and resorting to a designation is a last resort. What then? It would be an action-word (<s>karmaśabda</s>). '<s>Rathantara</s>' and the like are designations for the refinement-action called singing (<s>gāna</s>). Why? The principle has been stated [at MS 1.4.3]: 'in the singings, the designation is <s>Sāman</s>.' There, this word is found in a <s>ṛc</s> qualified by a [specific] singing. And a cognition of the qualified does not arise without grasping the qualifier. Therefore the qualifier is what is first denoted. And from the cognition of the qualifier, there is cognition of the qualified that accompanies it. Hence there is no contact of the word with the <s>ṛc</s> [directly]. By this same principle, we say it is a name for the singing.
Moreover, because of being grasped through well-known [usage] — this word '<s>gāyati</s>' (he sings) is well known in the action of singing. What is that [action]? A special manner of uttering the sounds. 'He sings' means 'he performs a singing' — and the words '<s>Rathantara</s>' and the like grasp that [action]. The meaning is: they denote [the action]. [This is known] from co-utterance with [the verb] and from the force of the second [case ending, i.e., accusative]. Just as 'he sings the <s>Āsāritaka</s>,' 'he sings the <s>Vardhamānaka</s>.'
[The objector:] but co-utterance occurs even with sound-words — 'he sings a song (<s>gāthā</s>),' 'he sings a verse (<s>ṛc</s>).'
True, but by transforming the word — 'by singing, he refines the verse' — [the meaning is that] it does not connect with the literal meaning 'he performs a singing that is a verse.' Therefore it is a singing-word.
And for this further reason it is a singing-word. Why? For the modification is undifferentiated from other [refinement-actions]. A modification of the verse-substance is indeed observed here — the lengthening of short syllables, the shortening of long syllables, the opening of closed [vowels], the closing of open [vowels]. This is undifferentiated from other refinement-actions. Just as by husking, grains become rice; by grinding, rice becomes flour. Therefore the refinement of sounds called 'singing' is denoted by the words '<s>Rathantara</s>' and the like. [The sentence] 'one sings the <s>Rathantara</s> in the latter two' and similar [sentences] are the placement of this [singing-action].

children.text: adravyaṃ cāpi dṛśyate // MS_7,2.14 //
children.translated_text: And a non-material (<s>adravya</s>) [<s>Sāman</s>] is also observed. // MS_7,2.14 //

children.text:
api cādravyaṃ sāma dṛśyate. dravyaśabdaś chandogair ṛkṣv ācaritaḥ. adravyam anṛcam ity arthaḥ. anṛcaṃ sāma dṛśyate, prajāpater hṛdayam anṛcaṃ gāyati{*7/115*} iti. prajāpatihṛdayaṃ [27]{*7/116*} nāma sāma. tad anṛcy utpannam. yady ṛci sāmaśabdaḥ, kathaṃ prajāpatihṛdayam anṛcaṃ syāt. atha gīteḥ{*7/117*} sāmaśabdaḥ, tato vināpy ṛcā gītir bhavati. tatraitad upapadyate, prajāpater hṛdayam anṛcaṃ gāyatīti. tasmād api gītiḥ sāma.
nanūktam, saṃskārakarmatve 'narthako 'karmakāle prayoga iti.
tatra brūmaḥ,
children.translated_text:
And a non-material <s>Sāman</s> is observed. The word 'material' (<s>dravya</s>) is used by the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāmaveda followers) for the <s>ṛc</s>s (verses). 'Non-material' means 'without a verse' — a <s>Sāman</s> without a verse is observed: 'He sings the heart of <s>Prajāpati</s>, which is without a verse.' The [<s>Sāman</s>] called 'Heart of <s>Prajāpati</s>' originated without a verse. If the <s>Sāman</s>-word denoted the <s>ṛc</s>, how could the Heart of <s>Prajāpati</s> be 'without a verse'? But if the <s>Sāman</s>-word denotes the singing (<s>gīti</s>), then even without a verse, singing is possible. There this is accounted for: 'He sings the Heart of <s>Prajāpati</s>, which is without a verse.' Therefore singing is the <s>Sāman</s>.
[The objector says:] but it was said that if [the Sāman-word denotes] the refinement-action, then the usage outside of the ritual performance-time is purposeless.
To this we reply:

children.text: tasya ca kriyā grahaṇārthā nānārtheṣu virūpitvād artho hy āsāmalaukiko vidhānāt // MS_7,2.15 //
children.translated_text: And the [non-ritual-time] performance would be for the purpose of learning [the action]; in [instances] of different purposes, because of diversity of form — for the object of these [<s>Sāmans</s>] is non-worldly, because of [their being known only through] scriptural teaching. // MS_7,2.15 //

children.text: tasya kriyākarmakāle grahaṇārthā śikṣitum abhyasitum ca. nānārtheṣu nānābhūteṣv artheṣu bhinneṣv ity arthaḥ{*7/118*} virūpitvāt, āśrayabhedād vividharūpaṃ tadgānaṃ bhavati. tat praty ṛcaṃ śikṣitavyam abhyasitavyaṃ ca prayogaprāśubhāvāya. bhūmirathikavat, tad yathā, bhūmirathiko bhūmau ratham ālikhya yogyāṃ karoti. sā tasya yogyā{*7/119*} prayogakāle saukaryam utpādayati. artho hy āsāṃ rathantarādisaṃjñānāṃ na laukike vyavahāre siddhaḥ, yathāvahantyādīnām. kutaḥ. vidhānād. vidhīyate hy asau śiṣyopādhyāyasaṃbandhena, evaṃrūpaṃ rathantaraṃ bhavatīti. na laukiko vijñāyate. tasmān na paricodanaiṣā, akarmakāle prayogād iti.
children.translated_text: The performance of that [singing] outside the ritual-action time is for the purpose of learning — to learn and to practice. In [instances of] different purposes — in objects that are different, distinct — because of diversity of form: on account of the difference of substrate, the singing takes on manifold forms. That must be learned and practiced verse by verse, for the purpose of proficiency in performance. Like a chariot-trainee on land — just as a land-charioteer draws a chariot on the ground and practices maneuvers; that practice produces facility at the time of [actual] performance. For the object (<s>artha</s>) of these designations like '<s>Rathantara</s>' and the like is not established in worldly usage, as is [the case with words like] 'husking' and the like. Why? Because of [their being known only through] scriptural teaching. For [the <s>Rathantara</s>] is taught through the relationship of student and teacher — 'the <s>Rathantara</s> is of such a form.' It is not [something] known in the world. Therefore this is not a criticism — that there is [purposeless] usage outside the ritual-performance time.

children.text: atha yad uktam, saṃjñāpṛthaktvād iti. tatrocyate,
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'because of the distinctness of designations' — to that it is replied:

*{7/119: E2 om. yogyā}*

children.text: tasmin saṃjñāviśeṣāḥ syur vikārapṛthaktvāt // MS_7,2.16 //
children.translated_text: Regarding that [one singing-action], there would be distinctions of designation, because of the differentiation of modifications. // MS_7,2.16 //

children.text: tasminn ekasminn api gānākhye saṃskāre saṃjñāviśeṣā bhaveyuḥ. kutaḥ. vikārapṛthaktvāt. tulye 'pi gāne viśeṣo{*7/120*} [28]{*7/121*} bhavati. gānaviśeṣāc ca saṃjñāpṛthaktvam. yathā, āsāritakam, vardhamānakam iti{*7/122*}, anyathālakṣaṇāsāritakagītiḥ. anyathālakṣaṇā vardhamānakagītiḥ. evam ihāpy anyathālakṣaṇā rathantaragītiḥ, anyathālakṣaṇā bṛhadgītiḥ. tasmāt saṃjñāpṛthaktvam.
children.translated_text: Even regarding that one refinement-action called singing, there would be distinctions of designation. Why? Because of the differentiation of modifications. Even though the singing is the same [in kind], there are specific differences. And from the specific differences of singing, there is distinctness of designations. Just as '<s>Āsāritaka</s>' and '<s>Vardhamānaka</s>' — the <s>Āsāritaka</s> singing has one set of distinguishing characteristics; the <s>Vardhamānaka</s> singing has another set of distinguishing characteristics. So too here, the <s>Rathantara</s> singing has one set of distinguishing characteristics; the <s>Bṛhat</s> singing has another set. Therefore there is distinctness of designations.
