children.text: yoniśas yāś ca tulyavad itarābhirvidhīyante // MS_7,2.17 //
children.translated_text: And the source-verses (<s>yoni</s>) are similar [in that they are] enjoined equally with the other [non-source verses]. // MS_7,2.17 //

children.text: yoniś cāsau śasyā ca yoniśasyā. yoniśasyāś carcas tulyavad itarābhir ayoniśasyābhir vidhīyante. yāmyāḥ śaṃsati, śipiviṣṭavantīḥ śaṃsati{*7/123*}, rathantarasya yonim anuśaṃsati, bṛhato yonim anuśaṃsati{*7/124*} iti. kā tatra tulyatā. śaṃsatiśabdenābhidhānam{*7/125*}. ihaitau stautiśaṃsatiśabdau samāne 'pi stutyarthatve vyavasthitaviṣayau. pragīteṣu mantravākyeṣu stautiśabdaḥ, apragīteṣu śaṃsatiśabdaḥ, yathā, praügaṃ śaṃsati, niṣkevalyaṃ{*7/126*} śaṃsatīti. ājyaiḥ stuvate, pṛṣṭhaiḥ stuvanta iti. ataḥ śaṃsatiśabdena vidhānād apragītām ṛcaṃ rathantarasya yoniṃ darśayati. yadi ca gītiḥ rathantaram, tatas tasyāpragītā ṛgyoniḥ. anyathāyaṃ vyapadeśo nopapadyate, rathantarasya yonim iti. tasmād gītiṣu sāmākhyā.
children.translated_text: A <s>yoniśasyā</s> [is a verse that is both] a source (<s>yoni</s>) and praiseworthy (<s>śasyā</s>). The verses that are source-verses are enjoined equally with the other non-source verses. '[He] recites the <s>Yāmya</s> [verses]; [he] recites the <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>-containing [verses]; [he] recites the source of the <s>Rathantara</s>; [he] recites the source of the <s>Bṛhat</s>.' What is the equality there? The designation by the word '<s>śaṃsati</s>' (he recites). Here, these two words '<s>stauti</s>' (he chants) and '<s>śaṃsati</s>' (he recites), though both having the meaning of praising, have fixed domains. The word '<s>stauti</s>' [is used] for sung mantric passages; the word '<s>śaṃsati</s>' for unsung [passages]. As in: 'he recites the <s>Praüga</s>,' 'he recites the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.' And: 'they chant with the <s>Ājya</s> [chants],' 'they chant with the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants].' Therefore, by the prescription with the word '<s>śaṃsati</s>', [the text] shows the source of the <s>Rathantara</s> as an unsung verse. And if the singing (<s>gīti</s>) is the <s>Rathantara</s>, then its source — the unsung verse — is the <s>yoni</s>. Otherwise, the expression 'the source of the <s>Rathantara</s>' would not be accounted for. Therefore, the designation '<s>Sāman</s>' belongs to the singings.

children.text: ayonau cāpi dṛśyate 'tathāyoni // MS_7,2.18 //
children.translated_text: And [the <s>Sāman</s>-word] is observed even in what is not a source-verse — [in] what is other-than-a-source. // MS_7,2.18 //

children.text: ayonau ca sāma dṛśyate. sthālyāṃ saktv avadhīyata ity āhur yad bṛhad gāyatrīṣu kriyate 'pi caināṃ rujati. na cāsyāṃ saṃbhavatīti, bṛhato bṛhatī yoniḥ. tasya gāyatrīṣu prāptir nāsti, [29]{*7/127*} yady ṛcaḥ sāmaśabdaḥ. atha nu gīteḥ, tataḥ sā bṛhadgītir gāyatrīṣu vacanāt prāptā, tasyā ayam anuvādo ghaṭate, yad bṛhad gāyatrīṣu kriyata iti. atathāyoni ca sāma darśayati. yādṛśī yasya yoniḥ, tato 'nyādṛśe, yo vai vicchandasi sāmohati, sa ṛcaṃ saṃśṛṇāti, sāma vā viliśati, sāma saṃśṛṇāti, ṛcaṃ viliśatīti yatarad varṣīyaḥ, tasya saṃśaraḥ{*7/128*}, tac ca gītāv eva sāmni yujyate, narci. ūhatiśadaś ca gītāv eva samarthaḥ, narci. ṛk cet, saiva yathāmnāyaṃ padyate. tatra nāsty ūhaprasaṅgaḥ. tasmād api gītau sāmaśabdaḥ.
children.translated_text: And a <s>Sāman</s> is seen [applied] on a non-native [<s>ṛc</s>]. They say: 'It is like putting barley-groats in a pot' — that the <s>Bṛhat</s> [Sāman] is performed on <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses], and that it breaks them. It is not possible on them — the native [meter] of the <s>Bṛhat</s> is <s>Bṛhatī</s>. Its application to <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses] does not arise, [29] if the word '<s>Sāman</s>' refers to the <s>ṛc</s> (verse). But if [it refers] to the singing (<s>gīti</s>), then that <s>Bṛhat</s>-singing is applicable to <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses] by [Vedic] statement; and this restatement is fitting — 'the <s>Bṛhat</s> is performed on <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses].' And [the text] shows [that] a <s>Sāman</s> [is used] on a non-native [meter]. [The rule is:] 'Whatever is the native [meter] of each, [it is applied] on something different from that' — 'Whoever chants a <s>Sāman</s> on a verse of wrong meter, he tears the <s>ṛc</s>; or he tears the <s>Sāman</s> — he tears the <s>Sāman</s>, he tears the <s>ṛc</s>' — whichever is longer, its tearing [results]. And this is appropriate only in the <s>Sāman</s> as singing, not in the <s>ṛc</s>. And the word <s>ūhati</s> (adapts) is capable [of making sense] only in [the context of] singing, not in [the context of] the <s>ṛc</s>. If [it referred to] the <s>ṛc</s>, that very [ṛc] would be recited as handed down. There, there is no occasion for adaptation (<s>ūha</s>). Therefore the word '<s>Sāman</s>' [refers to] singing.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{7/127: E2: 5,401; E6: 3,19}*
*{7/128: E2: tasya vileśaḥ. yatarad varṣīyas tasya saṃśaraḥ}*

children.text: ekārthye nāsti vairūpyam iti cet // MS_7,2.19 //
children.translated_text: If [one objects that] in identity of meaning there is no diversity of form — // MS_7,2.19 //

children.text: yad uktam, tasya kriyā grahaṇārtheti. tatra paricodyate. aikārthye nāsti vairūpyam iti. rathantaragīter bṛhadgītir arthāntaram. tena rathantaragītau gṛhītāyāṃ bṛhadgītir agṛhītā bhavatīti yukto rathantare gṛhīte bṛhataḥ śikṣārtham akarmakāle prayogaḥ. rathantaragītes tv eka evārthaḥ. tasya yonyāṃ prayoge śikṣite punar uttarāsu na śikṣitavyam. tāsv akarmakāle prayogaḥ saṃskārakarmatve na yukto bhavati. tasmān na saṃskārasya sāmaśabda iti sthitāyāṃ pratijñāyāṃ sūtreṇa paricodayati.
children.translated_text: As to what was said — 'its performance is for the purpose of learning' — there the following objection is raised: in identity of meaning there is no diversity of form. The <s>Bṛhat</s>-singing is different in meaning from the <s>Rathantara</s>-singing. Therefore, when the <s>Rathantara</s>-singing is learned, the <s>Bṛhat</s>-singing remains unlearned — hence it is appropriate that when the <s>Rathantara</s> is learned, the <s>Bṛhat</s> should be practiced outside the ritual time for the purpose of learning. But the <s>Rathantara</s>-singing has one single meaning. When its performance in the native [meter] has been learned, it need not be learned again in the subsequent [meters]. For those [subsequent meters], practice outside the ritual time is not appropriate if [the performance] is a refinement-action (<s>saṃskārakarman</s>). Therefore, given the established thesis that the word '<s>Sāman</s>' does not [refer to] the refinement, the <s>sūtra</s> raises an objection.

children.text: syād arthāntareṣu aniṣpatter yathā pāke // MS_7,2.20 //
children.translated_text: There would be [diversity of form] in different objects, because of non-accomplishment [otherwise] — as in cooking. // MS_7,2.20 //

children.text: syād vairūpyam. kuta etat. arthānatreṣv aniṣpatteḥ. ṛgantareṣv āśrayabhedāt. yathā{*7/129*} pāke, yathaika evāyam arthaḥ [30]{*7/130*} pāko nāma. tasyārthāntare vairūpyaṃ bhavati. anyathālakṣaṇa odanasya pākaḥ, anyathālakṣaṇo guḍasya, yenaudanapāko gṛhītaḥ, nāsāv aśikṣitvā guḍaṃ paktuṃ jānāti. tasmāt tasyāpy akarmakāle prayoga upapadyate.
children.translated_text: There would be diversity of form. Why? Because of non-accomplishment in different objects — because of the difference of substrate in different <s>ṛcs</s>. As in cooking — [30] just as this single meaning called 'cooking' has diversity of form in different objects: the cooking of rice is of one kind, the cooking of sugar is of another kind — one who has learned the cooking of rice cannot, without learning [separately], cook sugar. Therefore for that [Rathantara-singing] too, practice outside the ritual time is appropriate.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{7/129: E2: āśrayabhedād bhidyate. yathā}*
*{7/130: E2: 5,402; E6: 3,20}*

children.text: śabdānāṃ ca sāmañjasyam // MS_7,2.21 //
children.translated_text: And [this view accounts for] the consistency of the words. // MS_7,2.21 //

children.text: evaṃ ca sāmaśabdānām ṛkśabdānāṃ ca sāmañjasyaṃ bhavati. kavatīṣu rathantaraṃ gāyati{*7/131*} iti kavatīśabda ṛca eva{*7/132*} vakṣati, rathantaraśabdaś ca sāma. itarathā kavatīśabde vā deśalakṣaṇā syāt. rathantaraśabde vā dharmalakṣaṇā. tasmād gītau sāmaśabda iti.
children.translated_text: And thus there is consistency of the <s>Sāman</s>-words and the <s>ṛc</s>-words. 'One sings the <s>Rathantara</s> on the <s>Kavatī</s> [verses]' — the word '<s>Kavatī</s>' refers precisely to the <s>ṛc</s>; the word '<s>Rathantara</s>' [refers to] the <s>Sāman</s>. Otherwise, the word '<s>Kavatī</s>' would require a locative figurative meaning (<s>deśalakṣaṇā</s>), or the word '<s>Rathantara</s>' would require a property-figurative meaning (<s>dharmalakṣaṇā</s>). Therefore the word '<s>Sāman</s>' [refers to] singing.

NOTES:
[{7/131: <s>Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa</s> 11.4.2}]
[{7/132: <s>Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa</s> 11.4.2}]

children.text: uktaṃ kriyābhidhānaṃ tacchrutāv anyatra dharmapradeśāḥ syāt // MS_7,3.1 //
children.translated_text: What is stated [elsewhere] is a designation of the action; when that [name] is heard [in another context], there should be an extension of properties (<s>dharmapradeśa</s>) to that other [rite]. // MS_7,3.1 //

children.text: nāmnā dharmapradeśaṃ vakṣyāma ity ādau pratijñātam, so 'yam ucyate. kuṇḍapāyināmayane śrūyate, māsam agnihotraṃ juhoti{*7/133*} iti. tatraitat samadhigatam, naiyamikād agnihotrāt karmāntaram etad iti. adhunāgnihotraśabaś cintyate, katham ayaṃ prayukta iti. tadartham ārabhyate, uktam kriyābhidhānaṃ tacchrutāv anyatra vidhipradeśaḥ syād iti. uktam ādau, kriyābhidhānaṃ karmanāmadheyam agnihotraśabda iti tatprakhyaṃ cānyaśāstram ity atra. tasyānyatra śrutau kauṇḍapāyinām ayanīye juhotau vidhipradeśaḥ syāt dharmapradeśaḥ{*7/134*}. naiyamikasyāgnihotrasya ye dharmās te 'sminn anena nāmnātidiśyeran. kiṃ kāraṇam. ucyate, paraśabdo 'yaṃ paratra vṛttaḥ, paraśabdasya paratra vṛttau tadvadbhāvo gamyate. sa yatra vijñāto bhavati tatrānūdyate. yathā siṃho devadatta iti. yatrāvijñātas tatra vidhīyate. yathā amī piṣṭapiṇḍāḥ siṃhāḥ kriyantām iti. iha cāvijñāto 'sya juhoter agnihotravadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt sa vidhīyate. māsam agnihotraṃ juhotīti, agnihotravaj juhotīti. kathaṃ punar asati vatipratyaye [32]{*7/135*} vatyarthaḥ śakyo 'vagantum iti. ucyate, sāhacaryāt, agnihotraśabdo 'yaṃ karmaṇā saṃbaddhaḥ, tatsahacaritadohanādidharmavattāṃ lakṣaṇayā śaknoti gamayitum. śaknoti ced gamayitum, pradeṣṭum api śaknoti{*7/136*}. evam anatreṇāpi vatim, vatyarthaḥ śakyo 'vagantum iti.
children.translated_text: It was promised at the beginning: 'We shall state the extension of properties by name.' That is now being stated. In the <s>Ku���ḍapāyins</s>' <s>Ayana</s> it is heard: 'For a month he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>.' There it has been determined that this is a ritual different from the regular (<s>naiyamika</s>) <s>Agnihotra</s>. Now the word '<s>Agnihotra</s>' is being investigated — how is it employed [here]? For that purpose this [sūtra] is begun: 'What is stated [elsewhere] is a designation of the action; when that [name] is heard [in another context], there should be an extension of properties to that other [rite].' 'What is stated' [means] stated at the beginning — 'the designation of the action is the name of the ritual' — the word '<s>Agnihotra</s>' — as [discussed] in [the passage about] 'another <s>śāstra</s> resembling it.' When that [name] is heard elsewhere — in the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s>' <s>Ayana</s> offering (<s>juhoti</s>) — there should be an extension of properties, a <s>dharmapradeśa</s>. Whatever properties belong to the regular <s>Agnihotra</s>, those should be extended to this [offering] by that name. What is the reason? We say: this is a word [that has its meaning established] elsewhere, employed in another context; when a word established elsewhere is employed in a different context, its having-the-character-of-that [original] is understood. Where it is [already] known, it is [merely] restated. Just as '<s>Devadatta</s> is a lion.' Where it is unknown, it is prescribed. Just as 'let those flour-balls be made into lions.' Here, the <s>Agnihotra</s>-character of this <s>juhoti</s> (offering) is unknown. Therefore that is prescribed: 'For a month he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>' — [means] he offers like the <s>Agnihotra</s>. But how, in the absence of the suffix <s>-vat</s> (like), [32] can the meaning 'like' be understood? We say: by association — this word '<s>Agnihotra</s>' is connected with the ritual action; by figurative extension it is able to convey the having-properties-such-as-milking-etc. associated with it. And if it is able to convey, it is also able to extend. Thus even without [the suffix] <s>-vat</s>, the meaning 'like' can be understood.

children.text: apūrve vāpi bhāgitvāt // MS_7,3.2 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, both would be unprecedented, because of equal sharing [of the name]. // MS_7,3.2 //

children.text:
vāpīti viparyāsena prayukte. api vety arthaḥ. api vāpūrve ete ubhe api karmaṇī syātām, na kauṇḍapāyinām ayanīyo juhotir naiyamikapūrvaḥ, sādhāraṇaṃ ca nāmadheyam ubhayoḥ. kutaḥ. bhāgitvāt. ayam api juhotir bhāgī etasya nāmadheyasya.
yathaiva tatrāgnihotraṃ juhotīti samuccāraṇam, evam ihāpi, tatra tulye samuccāraṇe tasyaivaitan nāmadheyam, nāsyety atra viśeṣahetur nāsti. tasmād ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇaṃ nāmeti, nāsti dharmapradeśaḥ.
naitad yuktam. kutaḥ.
children.translated_text:
The words '<s>vā</s>' and '<s>api</s>' are used in reverse [order] — the meaning is '<s>api vā</s>' (or rather). Or rather, both these rituals would be unprecedented — the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s>' <s>Ayana</s> offering is not preceded by [i.e., based on] the regular [<s>Agnihotra</s>]; and the name is common to both. Why? Because of equal sharing — this offering too is a sharer of this name.
Just as in that [regular Agnihotra] there is the utterance 'he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>,' so here too. When the utterance is the same in both, there is no distinguishing reason [to say] 'the name belongs to that one, not to this one.' Therefore the name is common to both — there is no extension of properties.
This is not correct. Why?

children.text: nāmnas tv autpattikatvāt // MS_7,3.3 //
children.translated_text: Because of the innate nature of the name. // MS_7,3.3 //

children.text: autpattiko hi nāmināmnoḥ sambandhaḥ. yan nāma yasminn artha autpattikena saṃbandhena prasiddham, tasminn eva sadā vijñeyam, nānyatra ca. tathāvyavasthāyāṃ śabdārthe viśvāso na syāt. uktam, anyāyaś cānekārthatvam iti. yadā ca nobhayārthaḥ, tadā naiyamikaṃ tāvad āha. tatsādṛśyavidhānārthaṃ cetaratrāpi prayoga upapadyata iti nāstītarābhidhānatve hetuḥ. tasmād vidhipradeśaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: For the relation between name and named is innate (<s>autpattika</s>). Whatever name is well-known in whatever meaning through an innate relation — in that [meaning] alone it is always to be understood, and not in another. Otherwise, there would be no confidence in word-meaning. It has been stated: 'Having multiple meanings is irregular.' And when [the word] does not have both meanings, it first refers to the regular [Agnihotra]. And the employment [of the name] in the other [context] too is justified for the purpose of prescribing the similarity with that. There is no reason for it to designate the other [rite independently]. Therefore there should be an extension of properties.

children.text: pratyakṣād guṇasaṃyogāt kriyābhidhānaṃ syāt tadabhāve 'prasiddhaṃ syāt // MS_7,3.4 //
children.translated_text: From the direct conjunction with qualities, [the name] would be a designation of the action; in the absence of that [conjunction, the name] would be unrecognized. // MS_7,3.4 //

children.text:
naiyamike 'gnihotre pratyakṣo guṇasaṃyogaḥ. pratyakṣavihitā dharmāḥ santi. itthaṃ dogdhītthaṃ śrapayati, catur unnayati{*7/138*}, khādiry agnihotrasamid bhavati{*7/139*}, itthaṃ juhoti, evaṃ pratyakṣād{*7/140*} guṇasaṃyogāt, naiyamikasya tan nāmadheyam iha prayujyamānam, dohanādi kriyābhidhānaṃ syāt, dharmapradeśakam ity arthaḥ. asya punar juhoter na kecid dharmāḥ santi. tadabhāve teṣāṃ dharmāṇām abhāve, aprasiddhaṃ syāt, na prajñāyeta, kim artham ayam agnihotraśabda iha prayukta iti.
evaṃ vā. pratyakṣo guṇāsaṃyogo, naiyamikasya dravyadevatāsaṃyogaḥ. dadhnā juhoti{*7/141*}, payasā juhoti{*7/142*}, agnaye ca prajāpataye ca sāyaṃ juhoti{*7/143*} iti. etasmāt pratyakṣād guṇasaṃyogāt kriyābhidhānaṃ syāt. karmanāmadheyam, itthaṃrūpo juhotir agnihotrākhya iti. athetarajuhoteḥ rūpaṃ nāsti. tadabhāve 'prasiddhaṃ syāt, na jñāyet, kīdṛśaṃ tadagnihotram iti.
nanu māso 'sya rūpaṃ bhaviṣyati. na, māsaḥ karmāṅgam, kartṛdharmaḥ saḥ. api ca, agnihotraṃ tu māse vidhīyate, na māsenāgnihotraṃ rūpyate. tasmān naiyamikasyaitan nāmadheyam, itaratra tadvad atideśa iti.
kim eṣa evotsargaḥ, sarvaṃ karmanāma, anyatra śrūyamāṇaṃ dharmāṇāṃ grāhakam iti. evaṃ khalu prāptam. evaṃ prāpta idam ārabhyate,
children.translated_text:
In the regular <s>Agnihotra</s>, the conjunction with qualities is direct. There are directly prescribed properties: 'one milks thus, one cooks thus, one draws up four [times], the <s>Agnihotra</s> kindling-wood is of <s>khadira</s>, one offers thus.' From this direct conjunction with qualities, of the regular [Agnihotra] that name — when employed here [in the Kuṇḍapāyins' context] — would be a designation of the action, [meaning it effects] an extension of properties. But this offering [of the Kuṇḍapāyins] has no [such] properties. In the absence of those — the absence of those properties — [the name] would be unrecognized: one would not understand for what purpose this word '<s>Agnihotra</s>' is employed here.
Or alternatively [read] thus: the direct conjunction with qualities — the conjunction of the regular [Agnihotra] with substance and deity — 'one offers with curds,' 'one offers with milk,' 'one offers in the evening to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>.' From this direct conjunction with qualities, [the name] would be a designation of the action — a ritual-name: 'the <s>juhoti</s> having such-and-such form is called <s>Agnihotra</s>.' But the form of this other <s>juhoti</s> does not exist [as defined]. In the absence of that, [the name] would be unrecognized — one would not know 'what is that <s>Agnihotra</s> like?'
[The objector says:] but the month will be its form. No — the month is a subsidiary of the ritual, a property of the agent. Moreover, the <s>Agnihotra</s> is prescribed within the month, not [that] the <s>Agnihotra</s> is characterized by the month. Therefore this is the name of the regular [Agnihotra]; in the other [context] there is an extension [of properties] like that — [this principle] having been established, the following is begun:

children.text: api vā satrakarmaṇi guṇārthaiṣā śrutiḥ syāt // MS_7,3.5 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, in the <s>Sattra</s> ritual, this <s>śruti</s> would be for the purpose of a quality. // MS_7,3.5 //

children.text:
gavāmayane śrūyate, vaiśvānaro jyotiṣṭomaḥ, prāyaṇīyam ahar bhavati{*7/145*} iti. asti tu dvādaśāhe prathamam ahaḥ prāyaṇīyam nāma, prāyaṇīyo 'tirātra{*7/146*} iti. tayor nānātvaṃ tenaiva nyāyena siddham, prakaraṇāntare prayojanānyatvam{*7/147*} iti.
tatrāyaṃ prāyaṇīyaśabdaḥ paratrāpi śrūyamāṇo na dharmāṇāṃ grāhakaḥ, kiṃ tarhi. guṇārthaiṣā śrutiḥ. katham. lakṣaṇayā nāmadheyaṃ dharmāṇāṃ grāhakam uktam. asati ca śrutyarthe lakṣaṇārtho grāhyaḥ. iha tu śrutyartha eva saṃbhavati. guṇārtha eṣa{*7/148*} śabdaḥ. guṇena kriyāyogena. tasmin karmaṇi śrutyaiva prayujyate. prayanty aneneti prāyaṇīyam, pravartate{*7/149*} 'nena satram iti. vākyaśeṣaś cāsyaitam evārtham āha, jyotir eva purastād dadhāti{*7/150*} iti. yena jyotiḥ prāyaṇīyaṃ bhavati, tena jyotiḥ purastāt kriyata ity arthaḥ, jyotir eva purastād dadhātīti. tasmān nāyam atideśaḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Gavāmayana</s> it is heard: 'The <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is the opening (<s>prāyaṇīya</s>) day.' But in the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> (twelve-day rite) there is a first day called '<s>prāyaṇīya</s>' — 'the opening <s>Atirātra</s>.' Their difference is established by that very principle — 'in a different context, a different purpose.' [i.e., MS 2.3.24]
There, this word '<s>prāyaṇīya</s>' — even when heard in another [context] — is not [meant as] an extender of properties. Rather, this <s>śruti</s> is for the purpose of [indicating] a quality. How? It was stated that the name conveys properties figuratively. But when the literal meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is possible, the figurative meaning should not be grasped. And here the literal meaning itself is possible — this word is for the purpose of a quality, [i.e., indicating] a connection with action. In that ritual, it is employed in its literal (<s>śruti</s>) sense. '<s>Prāyaṇīya</s>' [means] 'that by which one sets forth' — by this the <s>Sattra</s> commences. And the remainder of the sentence conveys this very meaning: 'He places light in front' — [meaning] that by which the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> is light, by that light is placed in front. Therefore this is not an extension [of properties].

children.text: viśvajiti sarvapṛṣṭhe tatpūrvakatvāj jyautiṣṭomikāni pṛṣṭhāny asti ca pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ // MS_7,3.6 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Viśvajit</s> with all <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], [the statement] would [indicate] the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], because of being preceded by that; and there is [indeed] a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>-word [applying to them]. // MS_7,3.6 //

children.text: viśvajit sarvapṛṣṭho bhavati{*7/151*} iti śrūyate. tatra vicāryate, kim ayam anuvādaḥ, vidhir iti{*7/152*}. kiṃ prāptam. anuvāda iti. kutaḥ. yo hy asarvapṛṣṭhaḥ, tasya sarvapṛṣṭhatā vidheyā. yas tu sarvapṛṣṭha eva, tasya tayā kiṃ vihitayā. ayaṃ ca [35]{*7/153*} sarvapṛṣṭha eva. katham. tatpūrvakatvāj jyotiṣṭomapūrvakatvāt{*7/154*}. jyautiṣṭomikāni stotrāṇy atra prāpyante. teṣu māhendrastotrādīni catvāri santi. tāni sarvāṇy asya, tair ayaṃ sarvapṛṣṭho bhavati. nanu na tāni pṛṣṭhāni. ucyate, asti ca pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ. teṣv asti pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ, saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhānīti. tasmād anuvādaḥ.
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'The <s>Viśvajit</s> has all <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants].' There it is investigated: is this a restatement, or an injunction? What is the prima facie view? It is a restatement. Why? For one that is not [already] 'with all <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>,' [having] all <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> would need to be enjoined. But one that is already 'with all <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>' — what would be [achieved] by enjoining that for it? And this [Viśvajit] [35] is already 'with all <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>.' How? Because of being preceded by that — because of being preceded by the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-<s>stotras</s> (chants) are applicable here. Among those, there are four such as the <s>Māhendra-stotra</s> etc. All of those belong to this [Viśvajit]; by them, this has all <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>. [The objector says:] but those are not [called] '<s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants].' [We] reply: there is indeed a '<s>Pṛṣṭha</s>'-word [for them] — in them there is the word '<s>Pṛṣṭha</s>': 'seventeen <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>.' Therefore it is a restatement.

children.text:

children.text: ṣaḍahād vā, tatra hi codanāḥ // MS_7,3.7 //
children.translated_text: Or from the six-day [rite], for there are injunctions [for it]. // MS_7,3.7 //

children.text: nāyam anuvādaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. vidhiḥ. anuvādo 'pravṛttiviśeṣakaro 'rthakaḥ{*7/155*} syāt. api ca jyotiṣṭome na pṛṣṭhabahutvam asti, yasyāyam anuvādaḥ syāt. ṣaḍahe tu tad asti. tatra hi codanāḥ, pṛṣṭhānāṃ rathantaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati{*7/156*} ityevamādyāḥ. tasmāt ṣāḍahikānām atideśako{*7/157*} vidhir iti.
children.translated_text: This is not a restatement. What then? A prescription. A restatement, not producing a distinction of application, would be purposeless. Moreover, in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> there is no multiplicity of <s>pṛṣṭha</s>-[chants], of which this could be a restatement. But in the six-day [rite], that [multiplicity] does exist. For there are injunctions — [such as] 'of the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [chant]' and so forth. Therefore [it is] a prescription that effects extension of the six-day [rite's properties].

children.text: liṅgāc ca // MS_7,3.8 //
children.translated_text: And because of an indicatory mark. // MS_7,3.8 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ caitam arthaṃ darśayati. pavamāne rathantaraṃ karoty ārbhāve bṛhat, madhya itarāṇi, vairūpaṃ hotuḥ sāma, vairājaṃ maitrāvaruṇasya, raivataṃ brāhmaṇāc chaṃsinaḥ, śākvaramac chāvākasyeti viniveśapare vākye ṣāḍahikāni pṛṣṭhāni{*7/158*} darśayati.
children.translated_text: And an indicatory mark shows this meaning. In a sentence that is concerned with the arrangement — 'In the <s>Pavamāna</s> [day] he uses <s>Rathantara</s>; in the <s>Ārbhava</s> [day], <s>Bṛhat</s>; in the middle [days], the others; <s>Vairūpa</s> is the <s>Sāman</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s>; <s>Vairāja</s> of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; <s>Raivata</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; <s>Śākvara</s> of the <s>Acchāvāka</s>' — it shows the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>-[chants] of the six-day [rite].

NOTES:
[{7/158: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.2.2.3}]

children.text: utpannādhikāro jyotiṣṭomaḥ // MS_7,3.9 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> has a domain of what has [already] arisen. // MS_7,3.9 //

children.text:
atha yad uktam, asti ca pṛṣṭhaśabda iti. tatra brūmaḥ, na tu eṣa autpattikaḥ pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ, utpannānāṃ stotrāṇām asāv adhikāraḥ, yāny etāni pṛṣṭhānīti. jñāte ca teṣāṃ pṛṣṭhatve tad upapadyate. na ca tatra jñātaṃ. kathaṃ tarhi ayam anuvādaḥ. [36]{*7/159*}
liṅgasamavāyāt. ekaṃ tatra pṛṣṭhaṃ{*7/160*} māhendrastotram iti. ṣāḍahikānāṃ punaḥ pṛṣṭhatvaṃ jñātam. katham. tatra hi codanety uktam. teṣāṃ vāde, śrautaḥ pṛṣṭhaśabdasyārthaḥ parigṛhīto bhavati. itarathā lākṣaṇikaḥ. tasmāt ṣāḍahikānāṃ pradeśa iti.
children.translated_text:
Now, as to what was said — 'there is the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s>' — to that we say: this word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> is not original (<s>autpattika</s>). It is a domain-designation (<s>adhikāra</s>) of <s>stotras</s> (praise-hymns) that have [already] arisen — 'these are the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>.' And when their <s>pṛṣṭha</s>-hood is known, it [i.e., the statement] is appropriate. But it is not known there [in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>]. How then is this a restatement? [36]
Because of the co-occurrence with an indicatory mark (<s>liṅgasamavāya</s>). There [in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], one <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [is known from] '<s>Māhendrastotra</s>' [being called a <s>pṛṣṭha</s>]. But the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>-hood of the six-day [rite's chants] is known. How? Because 'there are injunctions there' — as was stated. In their case [i.e., the six-day rite's chants], the meaning of the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> is grasped in its primary (<s>śrauta</s>) sense. Otherwise [it would be] figurative. Therefore [it is] an extension of the six-day [rite's properties].

children.text: dvayor vidhir iti cet // MS_7,3.10 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that it is a prescription for both — // MS_7,3.10 //

children.text:
iti cet paśyasi, ṣāḍahikānāṃ pṛṣṭhānāṃ vidhir iti. naitad yuktam. kiṃ kāraṇam. dvikara evaṃ sarvapṛṣṭhaśabdo 'bhyupagamyate{*7/161*}, pṛṣṭhāni ca vidadhāti. teṣāṃ ca sarvatvam. astu, ko doṣaḥ. asaṃbhava ity āha. yadi pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ pṛṣṭhāni vidadhāti, sarvaśabdena na śakyate viśeṣayitum. athānuvadati, tathā śakyate. pṛṣṭhāni tv avihitāni bhavanti. teṣv asatsu kasya idaṃ sarvatvaṃ vidhīyate. ubhayakriyāyāś cāsaṃbhavaḥ.
athātra bṛhadrathantarayor vikalpena prāptayoḥ sāmastyaṃ kevalaṃ vidhīyate, sarvapṛṣṭho bhavati{*7/162*} iti. ubhe api bṛhadrathantare bhavataḥ{*7/163*}, naikam iti. tato 'yaṃ doṣo na bhavati. tasmād dvayor adhikāraḥ.
children.translated_text:
If you see it thus — that it is a prescription of the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> of the six-day [rite] — this is not proper. What is the reason? Thus the word 'all-<s>pṛṣṭha</s>' is accepted as having dual function — it both prescribes the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> and [asserts] their totality. Let it be so — what is the fault? [We reply:] impossibility. If the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> prescribes the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, the word 'all' cannot specify them. But if it restates them, then it can. But the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> would be unprescribed; in their absence, whose totality is being prescribed? And there is impossibility of dual function.
But here, [one might argue:] when <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are obtained as alternatives, their totality alone is prescribed — 'it becomes all-<s>pṛṣṭha</s>.' Both <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> occur — not just one. Thus this fault does not arise. Therefore there is a domain for both.

children.text:
NOTES:
*{7/161: E2: 'bhyupagato bhavati}*
*{7/162: E1 hat sarvapṛṣṭho bhavati in Klammern}*
*{7/163: Tait. S. 3.7.1}*
children.translated_text:

children.text: na vyarthatvāt sarvaśabdasya // MS_7,3.11 //
children.translated_text: No, because of the purposelessness of the word 'all.' // MS_7,3.11 //

children.text: naivam etat. kutaḥ. vyarthatvāt sarvaśabdasya. evaṃ sati sarvaśabdo vyartho bhavaty arthaśūnyaḥ{*7/164*}. ayaṃ hi bahuviṣayo dvayor na yujyate. ṣāḍahikānāṃ tu vidhāne naiṣa doṣaḥ. nanu ca tatrāpi dvikaraḥ śabdo bhaviṣyati. ucyate, na bhaviṣyati. sarvatvaṃ kevalaṃ pṛṣṭhānāṃ vidhāsyati{*7/165*}, na pṛṣṭhāni. nanūktam, pṛṣṭheṣv asatsu kasyedaṃ srvatvaṃ vidhīyata iti. ucyate, pṛṣṭhānāṃ sarvatvaṃ hi vihitam, tat saṃpādayitavyam. na ca pṛṣṭhāny akurvatā, tat saṃpādayituṃ śakyate. tatrārthāt pṛṣṭhāni kariṣyati. evaṃ na [37]{*7/166*} dvyarthaḥ śabdo bhaviṣyati. sarvaśabdaś ca samarthitaḥ. tasmāt ṣāḍahikānām atideśa iti.
children.translated_text: This is not so. Why? Because of the purposelessness of the word 'all.' If it were so, the word 'all' would be purposeless — devoid of meaning. For this [word], being multi-referential, is not appropriate for just two. But in prescribing the six-day [rite's properties], this fault does not [arise]. [The objector says:] but there too the word would have dual function. We reply: it will not. 'All' will prescribe only the totality of the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, not the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> [themselves]. [The objector says:] but it was said, 'in the absence of the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, whose totality is being prescribed?' We reply: the totality of the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> has been prescribed; that must be accomplished. And without performing the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, that [totality] cannot be accomplished. Therefore, by implication, [37] the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> will be performed. Thus the word will not have dual function. And the word 'all' is vindicated. Therefore [it is] an extension of the six-day [rite's properties].

children.text: tathāvabhṛthaḥ somāt // MS_7,3.12 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (final bath) [is derived] from the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice]. // MS_7,3.12 //

children.text: varuṇapraghāseṣu śrūyate, vāruṇyā niṣkāsena tuṣaiś cāvabhṛthaṃ yanti{*7/167*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ, kiṃ dārśapūrṇamāsike 'pāṃ vyutseke tuṣaniṣkāsaṃ vidhīyate, uta saumikād avabhṛthād dharmātideśa iti. kiṃ yuktam. dārśapūrṇamāsike guṇavidhiḥ. evaṃ sannihitapratyayo 'nugṛhyate. sannihito hy asau codakena prāpitaḥ. nanu nāsāv avabhṛthaḥ. ucyate, asti tatrāvabhṛthaśabda iti. eṣa vai darśapūrṇamāsayor avabhṛtha{*7/168*} iti. evaṃ prāpta idam āha, tathāvabhṛthaḥ somāt, yathā ṣaḍahāt pṛṣṭhānām atideśaḥ. evaṃ saumikād avabhṛthād iha dharmātideśaḥ. kutaḥ. abhihito nyāyaḥ, uktaṃ kriyābhidhānaṃ tacchrutāv anyatra vidhipradeśaḥ syād{*7/169*} iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [rites] it is heard: 'With the <s>Vāruṇī</s> [formula], with a <s>niṣkāsa</s> (sifting), and with husks, they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (final bath).' There a doubt [arises]: is this prescribing a <s>niṣkāsa</s> and husks as subsidiary properties in the water-sprinkling (<s>apāṃ vyutseka</s>) of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, or is it an extension of properties from the <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice's <s>Avabhṛtha</s>? What is proper? A subsidiary-prescription in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [water-sprinkling]. Thus a proximate understanding is supported. For that [water-sprinkling] is proximate, having been obtained by the injunctive principle. [The objector says:] but that is not an <s>Avabhṛtha</s>. We reply: there is the word <s>avabhṛtha</s> there — 'This is indeed the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' Given this prima facie view, [the <s>sūtra</s>] says: similarly, the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> [is derived] from the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] — just as there is an extension of <s>pṛṣṭha</s>-properties from the six-day [rite], so here there is an extension of properties from the <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice's <s>Avabhṛtha</s>. Why? The principle has been stated: 'a stated action-designation, when heard [elsewhere], is a prescription-extension elsewhere.'

children.text: prakṛter iti cet // MS_7,3.13 //
children.translated_text: If [one argues that it derives] from the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) — // MS_7,3.13 //

children.text: atha yad uktam, dārśapaurṇamāsike 'vabhṛthe guṇavidhir bhavatv iti, tasya kaḥ parihāra ity ābhāṣāntaṃ sūtram.
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'let it be a subsidiary-prescription in the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — what is the refutation of that? This is an introductory <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: na bhaktitvāt // MS_7,3.14 //
children.translated_text: No, because of being [merely] a figurative expression (<s>bhakti</s>). // MS_7,3.14 //

children.text:
naitad yuktam. kutaḥ. yato nāsti darśapūrṇamāsayor avabhṛthaḥ. nanu, eṣa vai darśapūrṇamāsayor avabhṛtha{*7/170*} iti śrūyate. [38]{*7/171*} satyaṃ śrūyate, na tv evam avabhṛthatvam asya bhavati. katham. ucyate, eṣa vai darśapūrṇamāsayor avabhṛtha ity etasya vākyasya dvayī vacanavyaktiḥ. nirjñātāvabhṛthatvasya padārthasya vā darśapūrṇamāsasaṃbandha{*7/172*} ucyate, yathā devadatto yajñadattasya putra iti nirjñātaputratvasya devadattasya yajñadattasaṃbandhaḥ ucyate. nirjñātasaṃbandhasya vānirjñātāvabhṛthatvasyāvabhṛthatvam, yathā, ayam āmro yajñadattasya putra iti, nirjñātayajñadattasaṃbandhasyāmrasya putratvam ucyate. tad asyāpāṃ vyutsekasya darśapūrṇamānasaṃbandhaḥ prakaraṇān nirjñātaḥ, nāvabhṛthatvam. ato 'syāvabhṛthatvam ucyate. na cāyam avabhṛthaḥ.
nanv ayam apy avabhṛtho bhavatu. naitad yuktam. anyāyo hy anekārthatvam. kathaṃ tarhi śabdaprayogaḥ. sādṛśyāt. kiṃ sādṛśyam. apsu saṃbandhaḥ. sa eṣa bhaktyā praśaṃsāvādo 'pāṃ vyutsekasya, avabhṛtha ivāyam iti, yathāmre putravādaḥ. tasmān nāsti darśapūrṇamāsayor avabhṛthaḥ. ato nātra guṇavidhiḥ.
children.translated_text:
This is not proper. Why? Because there is no <s>Avabhṛtha</s> in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. [The objector says:] but it is heard — 'This is indeed the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>.' [38] True, it is heard; but it does not thereby become an <s>Avabhṛtha</s>. How? We reply: the sentence 'This is indeed the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' has two possible interpretations. Either the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-connection of an entity whose <s>Avabhṛtha</s>-hood is [already] known is being stated — just as 'Devadatta is the son of Yajñadatta' states the connection with Yajñadatta of Devadatta whose son-hood is [already] known. Or the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>-hood of [something] whose connection is [already] known but whose <s>Avabhṛtha</s>-hood is not [yet] known — just as 'this mango is the son of Yajñadatta' states the son-hood of the mango whose connection with Yajñadatta is [already] known. Now, this water-sprinkling's connection with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is known from context, but not its <s>Avabhṛtha</s>-hood. Therefore its <s>Avabhṛtha</s>-hood is being stated. But it is not [really] an <s>Avabhṛtha</s>.
[The objector says:] but let it be an <s>Avabhṛtha</s> too. This is not proper. For polysemy is irregular. How then [is] the use of the word [to be explained]? Because of similarity. What is the similarity? Connection with water. This is a praise-statement (<s>praśaṃsāvāda</s>) [based on] resemblance (<s>bhakti</s>) regarding the water-sprinkling — 'this is like an <s>Avabhṛtha</s>' — just as calling a mango a 'son' [is figurative]. Therefore there is no <s>Avabhṛtha</s> in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Hence no subsidiary-prescription applies here.

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca // MS_7,3.15 //
children.translated_text: And because of seeing an indicatory mark. // MS_7,3.15 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ caitam arthaṃ darśayati. kiṃ liṅgaṃ bhavati. evam āha, nāyurdāṃ juhoti, na sāma gāyati, na vā gamanamantraṃ japati{*7/173*} iti. saumikāvabhṛthadharmāṇāṃ pratiṣedhaṃ brūvaṃs taddharmaprāptiṃ darśayati. tasmāt saumikād avabhṛthād dharmapradeśa iti.
children.translated_text: And an indicatory mark shows this meaning. What is the indicatory mark? Thus it states: 'He does not offer the life-giving [oblation], he does not sing the <s>Sāman</s>, nor does he recite the going-mantra.' By stating the prohibition of <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice's <s>Avabhṛtha</s>, it shows that those <s>dharmas</s> are obtained [here through extension]. Therefore [it is] an extension of properties from the <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice's <s>Avabhṛtha</s>.

children.text: dravyādeśe taddravyaḥ śrutisaṃyogāt puroḍāśas tv anādeśe tatprakṛtitvāt // MS_7,3.16 //
children.translated_text: In a designation of substance, [the rite] takes that substance, because of the connection with <s>śruti</s>; but the cake [applies] when there is no designation, because of having that as its archetype. // MS_7,3.16 //

children.text:
vāruṇaprāghāsiko 'vabhṛthaḥ, saumikād avabhṛthād dharmāṇāṃ grāhaka ity yuktam. tatredaṃ cintyate, kiṃ puroḍāśadravyako 'sau, uta tuṣaniṣkāsadravyaka iti. kiṃ prāptam. puroḍāśadravyaka iti. kutaḥ. nāmnā puroḍāśaḥ prāpyate. nanu pratyakṣaśrutaṃ tuṣaniṣkāsam. satyaṃ pratyakṣaśrutam, na tu śakyate vidhātum. avabhṛtho 'tra vidhīyate, avabhṛthaṃ yantīti. yadi tuṣaniṣkāsam aparaṃ vidhīyeta, tato vākyaṃ bhidyeta. avabhṛthaṃ yanti, tac ca tuṣaniṣkāseneti. tuṣaniṣkāsaśravaṇam idānīṃ kim artham. anarthakam, saṃbandhābhāvāt.
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, dravyādeśe taddravyaḥ. dravyādeśa etasmin, tuṣaniṣkāsenāvabhṛtaṃ yantīti. taddravyaḥ syāt, tuṣaniṣkāsadravyaḥ. kutaḥ. śrutisaṃyogāt, tuṣaniṣkāsaṃ pratyakṣaśrutam, puroḍāśas tv ānumānikaḥ, atideśena prāpyate.
nanu puroḍāśo 'pi pratyakṣaśruto nāmnā. yady api pratyakṣaśrutaḥ, sāmānyena tu prāpyate, tuṣaniṣkāsaṃ tu viśeṣeṇa. bādhyate ca sāmānyaṃ viśeṣeṇa. api ca lakṣaṇayā puroḍāśo gamyate, śrutyā tuṣaniṣkāsam. śrutilakṣaṇayoś ca śrutir nyāyyā. tasmāt tuṣaniṣkāsadravyaka iti. atha yad uktam, na saṃbadhyate 'vabhṛthena tuṣaniṣkāsam, vākyabhedaprasaṅgād iti. tatra brūmaḥ, yady avabhṛthaṃ vihāya tuṣaniṣkāsaṃ vidhīyate, tato vākyabhedaḥ syāt. tuṣaniṣkāsadravyako 'pūrvo 'vabhṛthaś codyate. tathā saguṇakarmavidhānam aviruddham. avidhīyamāne ca tuṣaniṣkāse tadgrahaṇam anarthakam eva syāt. tasmāt tuṣaniṣkāsadravyakaḥ. puroḍāśas tv anādeśe [40]{*7/175*} tatprakṛtitvāt. yady atra pratyakṣaśrutaṃ na dravyaṃ syāt, tataḥ puroḍāśas tuṣaprakṛtitvāt syāt. atra tu pratyakṣaśrutaṃ tuṣaniṣkāsam, tasmān na puroḍāśaḥ.
ātithye śrūyate, vaiṣṇavo navakapālo bhavati{*7/176*} iti. tathā rājasūye, pūrvasmiṃs trisaṃyukte vaiṣṇvas trikapāla iti. tatra vicāraḥ, yo 'yaṃ trisaṃyukte vaiṣṇavas trikapāla iti vaiṣṇavaśabdaḥ, ayam ātithyadharmāṇāṃ grāhakaḥ, neti. kiṃ yuktam. grāhaka iti. kutaḥ. vihitadharmake karmaṇi dṛṣṭaḥ śabdo 'nyasminn avihite{*7/177*} śrūyamāṇo grāhaka{*7/178*} ity uktam, uktaṃ kriyābhidhānam{*7/179*} iti{*7/180*}. tatrāyam api vihitadharmaka ātithye dṛṣṭaḥ. idānīm avihitadharmake trisaṃyukte dṛśyate. tasmād dharmāṇāṃ grāhaka iti. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ,
children.translated_text:
The <s>Avabhṛtha</s> of the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [rites] takes its properties from the <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice's <s>Avabhṛtha</s> — this is proper. Now this is examined: does it take the cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) as its substance, or husks and sifting (<s>tuṣaniṣkāsa</s>)? What is the prima facie view? It takes the cake. Why? The cake is obtained by name [i.e., the word <s>avabhṛtha</s> brings the cake by extension]. [The objector says:] but husks and sifting are directly heard. True, they are directly heard, but they cannot be prescribed [separately]. The <s>Avabhṛtha</s> is being prescribed here — 'they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>.' If husks and sifting were prescribed separately, the sentence would be split: 'they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>' and 'that [is done] with husks and sifting.' What purpose does the mention of husks and sifting serve then? It is purposeless, because of the absence of connection.
Given this prima facie view, we say: in a designation of substance, [the rite] takes that substance. Here there is a substance-designation — 'with husks and sifting they go to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>.' It should take that substance — husks and sifting. Why? Because of the connection with <s>śruti</s> — husks and sifting are directly heard (<s>pratyakṣaśruta</s>), whereas the cake is [only] inferential, being obtained by extension.
[The objector says:] but the cake too is directly heard by name. Even though directly heard, it is obtained only through the general [principle of extension], while husks and sifting [are obtained] through the specific [statement]. And the general is overridden by the specific. Moreover, the cake is understood through figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), while husks and sifting through <s>śruti</s> (direct statement). And between <s>śruti</s> and figurative usage, <s>śruti</s> is proper. Therefore [it takes] husks and sifting as its substance. As for what was said — 'husks and sifting do not connect with the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> because of the danger of sentence-splitting' — to that we say: if the husks and sifting were prescribed apart from the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>, then there would be sentence-splitting. [But here,] an unprecedented <s>Avabhṛtha</s> with husks and sifting as its substance is being enjoined. Thus the prescription of a qualified rite is non-contradictory. And if the husks and sifting were not prescribed, their mention would be truly purposeless. Therefore [it takes] husks and sifting as substance. But the cake [applies] when there is no [substance-]designation, [40] because of having that [<s>Soma</s>-sacrifice's <s>Avabhṛtha</s>] as its archetype. If there were no directly heard substance here, then the cake [would apply], because of having husks as the archetype.
In the <s>Ātithya</s> (hospitality offering) it is heard: 'There is a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [cake] on nine potsherds.' Likewise in the <s>Rājasūya</s>: 'In the first <s>Trisaṃyukta</s> [rite], a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [cake] on three potsherds.' There the question [arises]: does the word <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> in 'the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> on three potsherds in the <s>Trisaṃyukta</s>' take the properties of the <s>Ātithya</s>, or not? What is proper? It does take them. Why? A word seen in a rite that has prescribed properties, when heard in another [rite] without prescribed properties, is a taker of properties — as stated: 'a stated action-designation.' There, this [word <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>] is seen in the <s>Ātithya</s>, which has prescribed properties. Now it is seen in the <s>Trisaṃyukta</s>, which has no [directly] prescribed properties. Therefore it takes the properties. Given this prima facie view, we say:

children.translated_text: But [it would be] a subsidiary-prescription, and [the word] would not take [properties], because of equality. // MS_7,3.17 //

children.text: guṇavidhir ayam. ātithyasya guṇaṃ viṣṇudevatāsaṃyogaṃ vidadhāti. sa eṣa dharmān grahītuṃ na śaknoti. kutaḥ. samatvāt. samo hy ayam ātithye trisaṃyukte ca. yathā tatra viṣṇuṃ devatāṃ{*7/181*} vidadhāti, evam atrāpi. śrutyarthāsaṃbhavāc ca lakṣaṇayā dharmāṇāṃ grāhakaḥ kalpyate. iha ca pratyakṣaśrutyartha eva saṃbhavati devatāvidhiḥ. tasmān nāyaṃ grāhaka iti.
children.translated_text: This is a quality-injunction. It enjoins the quality of the <s>Ātithya</s> (guest-rite) — the connection with <s>Viṣṇu</s> as deity. This [word] cannot grasp <s>dharmas</s> (ritual properties). Why? Because of sameness. For this [injunction] is the same in the <s>Ātithya</s> and in the <s>Trisaṃyukta</s> (threefold-connected [rite]). Just as there it enjoins <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the deity, so too here. And because the literal meaning of the hearing (<s>śruti</s>) is not possible [as a dharma-grasper], one is postulated as a grasper of <s>dharmas</s> by secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). But here, the directly perceptible literal meaning — the injunction of deity — is indeed possible. Therefore this is not a grasper [of dharmas].

children.text: nirmanthyādiṣu caivam // MS_7,3.18 //
children.translated_text: And [the same applies] in the case of the <s>nirmanthya</s> (freshly-churned fire) and the like — likewise. // MS_7,3.18 //

children.text: paśāv agnīṣomīye dharmavān nirmanthyo 'gnir āmnātaḥ. sādhyā [41]{*7/182*} vai devā{*7/183*} ity ārabhyāgnau śrūyate, nirmanthyeneṣṭakāḥ pacantīti. tathā, darśapūrṇamāsayor barhirājye dharmavatī{*7/184*}. paśau śrūyate, barhiṣā yūpāvaṭam avastṛṇātīti, ājyena yūpam anakti{*7/185*} iti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ nirmanthyādayaḥ śabdāḥ dharmāṇāṃ grāhakāḥ, neti. tatrādhikaraṇātideśaḥ kriyate. nirmanthyādiṣu caivam, yathā vaiṣṇavaśabde. atrāpy ayaṃ yaugiko nirmanthyaśabdaḥ sadyonirmathitam agnim āha. tathā barhir ājyam iti dravyaśabdau. te trayo 'pi svārthaṃ vidhāya kṛtārthā bhavanti, dharmān grahītuṃ na śaknuvanti. tasmān na grāhakāḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice], a <s>nirmanthya</s> fire endowed with <s>dharmas</s> is recorded. Beginning with 'the <s>Sādhya</s> gods indeed' [41], in [the passage about] fire it is heard: 'they bake the bricks with freshly-churned [fire].' Likewise, in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites], the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) and <s>ājya</s> (ghee) are endowed with <s>dharmas</s>. In the animal [sacrifice] it is heard: 'with <s>barhis</s> he strews the sacrificial-post pit'; 'with ghee he anoints the sacrificial post.' There a doubt [arises]: are the words '<s>nirmanthya</s>' and the like graspers of <s>dharmas</s>, or not? There an extension of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) is made: in the case of the <s>nirmanthya</s> and the like — likewise, just as with the word '<s>Vaiṣṇava</s>' (belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>). Here too, this etymological (<s>yaugika</s>) word '<s>nirmanthya</s>' denotes a fire freshly churned. Likewise, '<s>barhis</s>' and '<s>ājya</s>' are substance-words. All three, having enjoined their own [primary] meaning, are fulfilled [in their purpose] — they cannot grasp <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore they are not graspers [of dharmas].

children.text: cāturmāsyeṣu śrūyate, dvayoḥ praṇayanti, tasmād dvābhyām eti{*7/186*} iti. asti tu some praṇayanaṃ dharmavat, tathā darśapūrṇamāsayor adharmakam. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ saumikam etat praṇayam, uta dārśapaurṇamāsikam iti. tatra sūtreṇaivopakramaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> (seasonal sacrifices) it is heard: 'They lead forward (<s>praṇayanti</s>) with respect to two [parvans]; therefore he goes by means of two.' Now, in the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] there is a leading-forward (<s>praṇayana</s>) endowed with <s>dharmas</s>, and likewise in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites one] without <s>dharmas</s>. There a doubt [arises]: is this <s>praṇayana</s> the <s>Soma</s>-type, or the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-type? There, the introduction is by the <s>sūtra</s> itself:

NOTES:

[{7/183: <s>Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā</s> 3.9.5 (15)}]
[{7/184: <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.7.5.10}]
[{7/185: <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.3.3}]
[{7/186: <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 11.5.3.2,5,8}]

children.text: praṇayanaṃ tu saumikam avācyaṃ{*7/187*} hītarat // MS_7,3.19 //
children.translated_text: But the leading-forward (<s>praṇayana</s>) is the <s>Soma</s>-type; for the other [<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-type] cannot be expressed [by the word]. // MS_7,3.19 //

children.text: saumikam etat praṇayanam. kiṃ kāraṇam. avācyaṃ hītarad dārśapaurṇamāsikam{*7/188*}, codakena prāptatvāt. kathaṃ punar ayaṃ praṇayatiśabdaḥ, praṇayanamātravacanaḥ san saumikaṃ praṇayanaviśeṣaṃ śaknoti vaktum. lakṣaṇayeti brūmaḥ, tīrthaśabavat, tad yathā, tīrthaśabdaḥ, tīrthamātravacanaḥ san tīrthaviśeṣaṃ dharmasādhanaṃ kadācid brūte, tīrthayātrāṃ gata iti. [42]{*7/189*}
children.translated_text: This leading-forward is the <s>Soma</s>-type. What is the reason? For the other — the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-type — cannot be expressed [by the word '<s>praṇayana</s>'], because it is [already] obtained through the injunctive principle. Now, how can this word '<s>praṇayati</s>' (he leads forward), being a word denoting mere leading-forward, denote the specific <s>Soma</s>-type leading-forward? We say: by secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — like the word '<s>tīrtha</s>' (sacred ford). Just as the word '<s>tīrtha</s>,' being a word denoting mere ford, sometimes denotes a specific ford that is a means of <s>dharma</s> — as in 'he has gone on a pilgrimage (<s>tīrthayātrā</s>)' [42].

children.text: uttaravedipratiṣedhaś ca tadvat // MS_7,3.20 //
children.translated_text: And the prohibition of the <s>uttaravedi</s> (high altar) [confirms] likewise. // MS_7,3.20 //

children.text: na vaiśvadeva uttaravedim upavayanti na sunāsīrīya{*7/190*} iti, prāptipūrvako hi pratiṣedho bhavati. saumike ca praṇayana uttaravedir na dārśapaurṇamāsike.
children.translated_text: 'In the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [parvan] they do not construct the <s>uttaravedi</s>; nor in the <s>Sunāsīrīya</s>' — for a prohibition presupposes [prior] applicability. And the <s>uttaravedi</s> is [applicable] in the <s>Soma</s>-type leading-forward, not in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-type.

children.text: prākṛtaṃ vānāmatvāt // MS_7,3.21 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] the archetypal [<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-type], because of [the word] not being a name [of the Soma-type]. // MS_7,3.21 //

children.text:
prākṛtaṃ vaitat{*7/191*} praṇayanam, dārśapaurṇamāsikaṃ. kutaḥ. anāmatvat. praṇayanaśabdaḥ saumikasya praṇayanasya na nāmadheyam. naitat tasya vācakam ity arthaḥ. yady ayaṃ tasya vācakaḥ syāt, tatas tad iha brūyat. idaṃ tu padārthanāmadheyam, padārthasya prāṅnayanasya vācakam. yasya vācakaṃ tad iha śaknoty agneḥ prācīnaṃ nayanaṃ vaktum. tac cehāsty eva. tasmāt tasya vācakaḥ. evaṃ{*7/192*} sannihitapratyo na bādhito bhavati.
atha yad uktam, tīrthaśabavad bhaviṣyatīti. atra brūmaḥ, tīrthaśabdo 'pi tīrthamātram eva brūte. tīrthayātrāṃ gata iti tv uktvā kānicit tīrthāny anukrāntāni. yato 'sau tadviśiṣṭārtho vijñāyate. yatra tu kevalaḥ prayujyate, tatra tīrthamātram eva brūte. yathā, tīrthe snāti, tīrtham eva hi samānānāṃ bhavatīti. api ca saṃbhavati śrutyarthe, lakṣaṇārtho 'grāhyaḥ. saṃbhavati cātra śrutyarthaḥ. tasmān na lakṣaṇārtho grāhya iti.
children.translated_text:
Or this leading-forward is the archetypal [type] — the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>-type. Why? Because of not being a name [of the Soma-type]. The word '<s>praṇayana</s>' is not the proper name of the <s>Soma</s>-type leading-forward. This [word] is not its designator — that is the meaning. If this [word] were its designator, then it would denote that [Soma-type] here. But this is a word naming the action — it is a designator of the action of leading forward. That of which it is the designator — here it can denote the leading of the fire eastward. And that [type of leading] indeed exists here. Therefore it is its designator. Thus the proximate-meaning is not overridden.
Now, as to what was said — 'it will be like the word <s>tīrtha</s>' — to this we say: the word '<s>tīrtha</s>' too denotes merely a ford. But in '<s>tīrthayātrā</s>' (pilgrimage), having said [the word], some [specific] fords are enumerated — from which that [word] is understood in its specific meaning. But where it is used alone, there it denotes merely a ford — as in 'he bathes at a ford'; 'the ford indeed belongs to equals.' Moreover, when the literal meaning (<s>śrutyartha</s>) is possible, a secondary meaning should not be grasped. And the literal meaning is possible here. Therefore the secondary meaning should not be grasped.

children.text: parisaṅkhyārthaṃ śravaṇaṃ guṇārtham arthavādo vā // MS_7,3.22 //
children.translated_text: The hearing [of '<s>dvayoḥ praṇayanti</s>'] is for the purpose of enumeration, for a quality, or as an <s>arthavāda</s>. // MS_7,3.22 //

children.text: tatrāha, yad uktam avācyaṃ hītarad{*7/193*} iti, tasya kaḥ [43]{*7/194*} parihāraḥ. ucyate, parisaṅkhyārthaṃ vā syāt. dvayoḥ praṇayanti, na caturṣv iti. guṇārtham arthavādārthaṃ vā. tasmād dvābhyām etīti. tatra parisaṅkhyāyāṃ tāvat trayo doṣāḥ. guṇo 'pi na kaścid vidhīyate, pariśeṣād arthavādārtham. nanv arthavādo 'pi niṣprayojanaḥ, praṇayanasya prāptatvāt. arthavādasya prayojanam, uttarasminn adhikaraṇe vakṣyāmaḥ, madhyamayor vā gatyarthavādād iti.
children.translated_text: To this he says: as to what was said — 'for the other cannot be expressed' — what is the [43] rebuttal of that? [We] reply: [the hearing] may be for the purpose of enumeration: 'they lead forward with respect to two — not with respect to four.' Or it may be for the purpose of [enjoining] a quality, or for the purpose of an <s>arthavāda</s>: 'therefore he goes by means of two.' There, regarding the enumeration, there are three defects [making it untenable]. Nor is any quality being enjoined; by elimination, it is for the purpose of an <s>arthavāda</s>. [The objector says:] but even as an <s>arthavāda</s> it is purposeless, since the leading-forward is [already] obtained [from another source]. The purpose of the <s>arthavāda</s> — we shall state in the subsequent <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic): 'or [it applies to] the middle two [parvans], because of the <s>arthavāda</s> about going.'

children.text: prathamottamayoḥ praṇayanam uttaravedipratiṣedhāt // MS_7,3.23 //
children.translated_text: The leading-forward [applies to] the first and last [parvans], because of the prohibition of the <s>uttaravedi</s>. // MS_7,3.23 //

children.text: dvayoḥ praṇayantīti śrūyate. tatra saṃdehaḥ. katarayor dvayor iti. aniyame prāpte, ucyate, prathamottamayoḥ praṇayanam. kutaḥ. uttaravedipratiṣedhāt. tatrottaravediḥ pratiṣidhyate, na vaiśvadeva uttaravedim upavayantīti, na sunāsīrīya{*7/195*} iti. asmin praṇayane uttaravedyām agninidhānaṃ vihitam. ato yatra praṇayanam, tatrottaravediprāptiḥ. prāptau ca satyāṃ pratiṣedhaḥ, prathamottarayoś cāsau. tasmāt tayoḥ praṇayanam iti.
children.translated_text: 'They lead forward with respect to two' is heard. There a doubt [arises]: which two? When no determination is prima facie possible, we say: the leading-forward [applies to] the first and last [parvans]. Why? Because of the prohibition of the <s>uttaravedi</s>. There the <s>uttaravedi</s> is prohibited: 'In the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> they do not construct the <s>uttaravedi</s>; nor in the <s>Sunāsīrīya</s>.' In this leading-forward, the placing of fire on the <s>uttaravedi</s> is enjoined. Therefore, where there is leading-forward, there the <s>uttaravedi</s> is applicable. And when [the uttaravedi] is applicable, the prohibition [makes sense] — and that [prohibition is] for the first and last [parvans]. Therefore the leading-forward [applies] to those two.

children.text: madhyamayor vā gatyarthavādāt // MS_7,3.24 //
children.translated_text: Or [it applies to] the middle two [parvans], because of the <s>arthavāda</s> about going. // MS_7,3.24 //

children.text: madhyamayor vā parvaṇoḥ praṇayanam. kutaḥ. gatyarthavādāt. gatyarthavādenaitad dvayoḥ praṇayanam ucyate. tasmād dvābhyām etīti. ūrusaṃstute vaite{*7/196*} parvaṇī, ūru vaitau yajñasya, yad varuṇapraghāsāś ca{*7/197*} sākamedhāś ca{*7/198*} iti. ūru ca gamanasādhane, tatraivaṃ stutisaṃbandho vijñāyate. ūru yajñasya, varuṇapraghāsāś ca sāka[44]{*7/199*}medhāś ceti, tayor dvayoḥ praṇayanti. tasmād dvābhyām ūrubhyāṃ yajñaḥ samāptiṃ yānti. praṇayanena hi tau balavantau bhavataḥ, aṅgabhūyastvād iti. etat tadarthavādasya prayojanam.
children.translated_text: Or the leading-forward [applies to] the middle two <s>parvans</s>. Why? Because of the <s>arthavāda</s> about going — by the <s>arthavāda</s> about going, this 'leading-forward with respect to two' is stated: 'therefore he goes by means of two.' The two <s>parvans</s> praised [in terms of] thighs are these — 'these two are indeed the thighs of the sacrifice: the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> and the <s>Sākamedha</s>.' And thighs are the instruments of going — thus the connection with the praise is understood: 'the thighs of the sacrifice — the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> and the <s>Sākamedha</s>' — with respect to those two they lead forward. 'Therefore the sacrifice reaches its completion by means of two thighs.' For through the leading-forward those two become strengthened, because of [the leading-forward] becoming an additional subsidiary. This is the purpose of that <s>arthavāda</s>.

children.text: atha yad uktam, uttaravedipratiṣedhād iti. tatra brūmaḥ,
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'because of the prohibition of the <s>uttaravedi</s>' — to that we say:

children.text: auttaravediko nārabhyavādapratiṣedhaḥ{*7/200*} // MS_7,3.25 //
children.translated_text: The prohibition of the <s>uttaravedi</s> is a non-initiatory statement (<s>anārabhyavāda</s>). // MS_7,3.25 //

children.text:
anārabhya kiṃcit parvaviśeṣam, cāturmāsyeṣūttaravedir āmnātā, upātra vapanti{*7/201*} iti. tasyānārabhyavidher ayaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ.
nanu varuṇapraghāsānāṃ guṇavākyaprāptāv evāyaṃ teṣām eva, atreti vādaḥ syāt. naitad evam, prakaraṇāc cāturmāsyānām eva. yadi varuṇapraghāsānāṃ vādaḥ syāt, tatra pratiṣedhe trīṇy api parvāṇy utkīrtayet. athocyeta, dvayoḥ parvaṇor vādo bhavatv iti. atra brūmaḥ, na dvayoḥ parvaṇoḥ prakaraṇam, cāturbhāsyānāṃ vā prakaraṇam{*7/202*}, varuṇapraghāsānāṃ vā. varuṇapraghāsānāṃ dvayoḥ prakaraṇe parvaṇor utkīrtanaṃ pratiṣedhe na syāt. tasmāc cāturmāsyānām eva vādaḥ.
nanu evam apy arthavādenaitaj jñātam, madhyamayoḥ praṇayanam iti. kim arthaṃ prāptasya praṇayanasya punaḥśravaṇam iti. atra prayojanaṃ noktam. asati prayojane 'nyasmin parisaṅkhyārtham eva bhavati. tatra doṣā uktāḥ. tasmād guṇārtham evaitac chravaṇam.
nanu nāsti kaścid guṇaḥ. ucyate, guṇaḥ śrūyate, uttaravedyām agninidhānam. tasmāt tadarthā punaḥ śrutiḥ.
children.translated_text:
Without initiating any particular <s>parvan</s>, the <s>uttaravedi</s> is recorded in the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> [generally]: 'they construct [the <s>uttaravedi</s>] here.' This prohibition is of that non-initiatory injunction.
[The objector says:] but since the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [section] already has [the uttaravedi] obtained through the quality-sentence, this [prohibition] should be for those [Varuṇapraghāsa rites] alone — that is the position. This is not so — [it is for] the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> [in general], because of the context. If it were a statement about the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> [specifically], then in the prohibition it would enumerate all three <s>parvans</s>. And [if] it be said that the statement is about two <s>parvans</s> — to this we say: the context is not of two <s>parvans</s> — [either] it is the context of the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> [in general], or of the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s>. If the context were of the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> alone [as one of] two <s>parvans</s>, the enumeration of [individual] <s>parvans</s> in the prohibition would not occur. Therefore the statement is about the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> [in general].
[The objector says:] but even so, it is known from the <s>arthavāda</s> that the leading-forward [applies to] the middle two. What is the purpose of hearing again the leading-forward that is [already] obtained? To this [we say:] no purpose was stated [for it]. In the absence of another purpose, it would be for the purpose of enumeration alone. The defects of that [view] were stated. Therefore it is for the purpose of [enjoining] a quality.
[The objector says:] but there is no quality [being enjoined]. [We] reply: a quality is heard — the placing of fire on the <s>uttaravedi</s>. Therefore the re-hearing is for that purpose.

children.text: svarasāmaikakapālāmikṣaṃ ca liṅgadarśanāt // MS_7,3.26 //
children.translated_text: The <s>svara</s> (melody-note), the <s>sāman</s> (chant), the single-potsherd [cake], and the <s>āmikṣā</s> (curds) — [are extended] because of the observation of an indicatory mark. // MS_7,3.26 //

children.text:
gavāmayane śrūyate, abhito divākīrtyam ahastrayaḥ svarasāmāno bhavanti{*7/204*} iti. teṣāṃ viśeṣadharmā āmnātāḥ, yathā, saptadaśā bhavanti{*7/205*}, santatatayātigrāhyā gṛhyanta{*7/206*} ityevamādayaḥ. punar anyatra śrūyate, pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho dvau svarasāmānāv iti. tathā vaiśvadeve śrūyate, dyāvāpṛthivya ekakapāla iti. tatrāmnātā viśeṣadharmāḥ, sarvahutaṃ juhoty{*7/207*} aparyāvartayañ juhoti{*7/208*} iti. punar aparatra, kāya ekakapāla iti. tatraiva śrūyate, vaiśvadevyābhikṣeti. tatrāpi viśeṣadharmāḥ kecid āmnātāḥ. punar anyatra, maitrāvaruṇy āmikṣeti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kiṃ svarasāmaśabdo 'nyatra śrūyamāṇo gavāmayanikebhyaḥ svarasāmabhyo dharmāṇāṃ grāhakaḥ, uta neti. evam ekakapālāmikṣāśabdāv api. tatra guṇavidhis tu na gṛhṇīyāt samatvād{*7/209*} ity agrahaṇe prāpte. idam ucyate, svarasāmaikakapālāmikṣaṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ grāhakam. kiṃ kāraṇam. liṅgadarśanāt. liṅgaṃ tatra tādṛśaṃ dṛśyate. yena jñāyate, sarva ete dharmāṇāṃ grāhakā iti. svarasāmasu tāvat pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho dvau svarasamānāv{*7/210*} ity uktvāha. tatra yat tṛtīyaṃ saptadaśam ahas tat trayastriṃśasya sthānam abhiparyāharanti, sa uttarāṇāṃ stomānām avyavāyāya, trayāṇāṃ ca saptadaśānām anūcīnatāyāi{*7/211*} [46]{*7/212*} iti. yady etau svarasāmānau, gavāmāyanikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ grāhakau, tatraitāv api saptadaśau. tathātra trayaḥ saptadaśā anūcīnā bhavanti. tatraitad vacanaṃ yujyate, trayāṇāṃ saptadaśānām anūcīnatāyā iti.
tathāgrayaṇe, dyāv āpṛthivyam ekakapālaṃ vidhāyāha, yat sarvahutaṃ karoti, sā tv ekā paricakṣā, huto hutaḥ{*7/213*} paryāvartate, sā dvitīyā. ājyasyaiva dyāv āpṛthivyau yajeta{*7/214*} iti, ājyavidhipare vākye sarvahomam aparyāvṛttiṃ ca vaiśvadevikau dharmau prāptau darśayati.
tathā maitrāvaruṇyām āmikṣāyām, na vājinena pracaranti{*7/215*} iti vājinejyāṃ vaiśvadevikaṃ dharmaṃ pratiṣedhaṃs tato dharmaprāptiṃ darśayati. etebhyo liṅgebhyo etaj jñāyate, yathāsvaṃ dharmāṇāṃ grāhakā iti. pratipattyarthakarma vājinejyāṃ sviṣṭakṛttulyāṃ matvaitad uktam. āha, liṅgam apadiṣṭam, kutaḥ prāptir iti. ucyate, lakṣaṇayā prāptir, liṅgāt tu lakṣaṇāparigrahaḥ.
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Gavāmayana</s> it is heard: 'On either side of the <s>Divākīrtya</s> day, there are three days with <s>Svarasāman</s> [chants].' Their specific rules are recorded, such as: 'they have seventeen[-fold Stoma]'; 'by continuous [chanting] the <s>Atigrāhya</s> [cups] are taken' — and similar [rules]. Again, elsewhere it is heard: 'A <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day [rite has] two <s>Svarasāman</s> [days].' Likewise, in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [offering] it is heard: 'A single-potsherd [cake] for <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth).' There, specific rules are recorded: 'he offers as a <s>sarvahuta</s> (complete oblation)'; 'he offers without turning [the cake].' Again, elsewhere: 'a single-potsherd [cake] for <s>Kā</s> (Who?).' There too it is heard: 'with <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> <s>abhīkṣa</s> [curds].' There too certain specific rules are recorded. Again, elsewhere: 'the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> <s>āmikṣā</s> (coagulated milk).' There a doubt [arises]: does the word '<s>Svarasāman</s>' heard elsewhere draw the rules from the <s>Gavāmayana</s> <s>Svarasāmans</s>, or not? Likewise with the words '<s>Ekakapāla</s>' and '<s>Āmikṣā</s>' as well. There, when the prima facie view — 'a subsidiary-rule does not draw [rules from another context], because of equality' [MS 7.3.17] — leads to non-drawing, this is stated: '<s>Svarasāman</s>,' '<s>Ekakapāla</s>,' and '<s>Āmikṣā</s>' do draw rules [from their respective contexts]. What is the reason? Because of the observation of indicatory marks. Such indicatory marks are observed there, by which it is known that all of these draw rules [from their original contexts]. Regarding the <s>Svarasāmans</s>: having stated 'a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day [rite has] two <s>Svarasāman</s> [days],' [the text] says: 'There, the third day with seventeen[-fold Stoma] — they bring it around to the place of the thirty-three[-fold Stoma]; that is for the non-interruption of the subsequent <s>Stomas</s>, and for the continuity of the three seventeen[-fold days].' If these two <s>Svarasāman</s> [days] draw rules from the <s>Gavāmayana</s> <s>Svarasāmans</s>, then these two also have seventeen[-fold Stoma]. Thus, three seventeen[-fold Stoma days] are consecutive here. There, this statement is fitting: 'for the continuity of the three seventeen[-fold days].'
Likewise, in the <s>Agrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering), having prescribed a single-potsherd [cake] for <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>, [the text] says: 'That he makes it a <s>sarvahuta</s> — that is one designation; the offered [oblation] is turned around again — that is the second.' In a sentence aimed at prescribing ghee [as the offering substance]: 'One should sacrifice to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> with ghee alone' — [the text] shows that the <s>sarvahuta</s> [oblation] and the non-turning are <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> rules that have been drawn [from the original context].
Likewise, regarding the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> <s>āmikṣā</s>: 'They do not proceed with the <s>Vājina</s> [offering]' — by prohibiting the <s>Vājina</s> offering, [the text] shows that the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> rule [would otherwise have been] drawn from there, and thereby demonstrates the drawing of rules. From these indicatory marks, this is known: each of these draws rules from its respective [original context]. [The objection regarding] the <s>Vājina</s> offering as a concluding rite similar to the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> [offering] is addressed by saying: the indicatory mark has been pointed out; how then is the drawing [of rules] established? It is replied: the drawing is by secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), while from the indicatory mark, [we know] which secondary designation to adopt.

children.text: codanāsāmānyād vā // MS_7,3.27 //
children.translated_text: Or, because of the commonality of the injunction. // MS_7,3.27 //

children.text: svarasāmatvasāmāyāt, ekakapālatvasāmānyāt, āmikṣāsāmānyād vā. yasya liṅgam arthasaṃyogād{*7/216*} ity anena prāptir iti.
children.translated_text: Because of the commonality of being a <s>Svarasāman</s>, because of the commonality of being a single-potsherd [cake], or because of the commonality of being <s>āmikṣā</s>. [The drawing of rules is established] by the [principle]: 'of that which has an indicatory mark, [the drawing is] because of connection with the meaning' [MS 8.1.2].

children.text: kvacic chrūyate, vāso dadāti{*7/217*}, ano dadātīti. tatra vicāryate, kim, vāsasaḥ, anasaś ca kriyā prāpyate, uta neti. tatrāha, evaṃ tāvan naḥ parīkṣyam. kim karmanimittāv etau [47]{*7/218*} śabdau, utākṛtinimittāv iti. yadi karmanimittau, tataḥ prāpyate. athākṛtinimittau, tato neti. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. karmanimittāv iti. kutaḥ. karmāgame taddarśanāt. yadā tasmin dravye dāruṇi sūtre vā dārukāreṇa tantuvāyena vā karma kṛtaṃ bhavati, tadaitau śabdau pravartete, na prāk. ato vijñāyate, karmanimittāv iti. yadā karmanimittau, tad etad ārabhyate,
children.translated_text: Somewhere it is heard: 'he gives a garment (<s>vāsas</s>)'; 'he gives a cart (<s>anas</s>).' There it is investigated: is the [refinement-]action of the garment and the cart [also] drawn [from another context], or not? To this [the commentator] says: this much is to be examined first by us — are these two words (<s>vāsas</s> and <s>anas</s>) occasioned by action (<s>karmanimitta</s>), or by form (<s>ākṛtinimitta</s>)? If they are action-occasioned, then [rules] are drawn. But if form-occasioned, then not. What is the prima facie view first? They are action-occasioned. Why? Because of the observation of [the word's usage] when action has taken place. When in that substance — wood or thread — the action has been performed by a carpenter or weaver, then these words come into use, not before. Hence it is known that they are action-occasioned. When they are action-occasioned, this [inquiry] is commenced:

children.text: karmaje karma yūpavat // MS_7,3.28 //
children.translated_text: When [the word is] action-born, the action [is drawn], like in the case of the <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post). // MS_7,3.28 //

children.text: karmaja etasmin vāsa, ādau dravye śrūyaṃāṇe, karma prāpyate. katham. yūpavat, yathā yūpaśabdo joṣaṇādikriyānimittaḥ, sa yatra śrūyate, tatra joṣaṇādyāḥ kriyāḥ prāpyante, evam ihāpīti.
children.translated_text: When [the word is] action-born — when this garment [word], heard regarding a substance at the outset, [leads to] the action being drawn. How? Like the <s>yūpa</s> — just as the word '<s>yūpa</s>' is occasioned by the actions of shaping (<s>joṣaṇa</s>) and the like, and wherever that [word] is heard, the actions of shaping and the like are drawn; so too here.

children.text: rūpaṃ vāśeṣabhūtatvāt // MS_7,3.29 //
children.translated_text: Or [it is] the form [that is denoted], because [form is] the remainder-element. // MS_7,3.29 //

children.text: atrocyate, naitau karmanimittau. kiṃ kāraṇam. ye naimittikāḥ śabdāḥ, te nimittam upalabhya prayujyante, yathā daṇḍī chatrīti. imau tv anupalabhya kriyām, ākṛtimātre prayujyete. tasmān naitau kriyānimittāv iti. atrocyate{*7/219*}, ākṛtyā kriyām anumāya tataḥ śabdaṃ prayuṅkta iti. atra brūmaḥ, pratyakṣāṃ nimittatāṃ{*7/220*} gamyamānām utsṛjya, adṛṣṭāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ nimittatvakalpanāyāṃ hetur nāstīti. yat tūktam, kriyottarakālaṃ pravṛttidarśanād iti. atra brūmaḥ, prāk kriyāyā ākṛtir anabhivyaktā, sā kriyayābhivyajyate, yataḥ kriyottarakālaṃ śabdaprayogaḥ. tasmād ākṛtinimittau. yadaivam{*7/221*}, tadā siddhaṃ rūpaṃ deyam. kutaḥ. aśeṣabhūtatvāt, nātra kriyā [48]{*7/222*} śeṣabhūtā, kriyāvācinaḥ śabdasyābhāvāt. yūpe tu pratyakṣavihitā joṣaṇādyāḥ kriyāḥ. tasmād yūpavad ity atulyopanyāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: Here it is replied: these two [words] are not action-occasioned. What is the reason? Words that are occasioned [by something] are used upon perceiving the occasion — as '<s>daṇḍin</s>' (stick-bearer), '<s>chatrin</s>' (umbrella-bearer). But these two are used without perceiving the action, upon the mere form. Therefore they are not action-occasioned. Here it is said: having inferred the action from the form, one then employs the word. To this we reply: there is no reason to postulate the occasion in an unobserved action when the directly perceived occasion — [namely, the form] — is being abandoned. As to what was said — that usage is observed [only] after the action [has been performed] — to this we reply: before the action, the form is unmanifest; it is manifested by the action. That is why the word-usage [occurs] after the action. Therefore they are form-occasioned. This being so, the finished form alone should be given. Why? Because [form is] the remainder-element — there is no action here that is a remainder-element, because of the absence of a word denoting action. But in the <s>yūpa</s>, the actions of shaping and the like are directly prescribed. Therefore the [analogy] 'like the <s>yūpa</s>' is an inapt comparison.

viśaye laukikaḥ syāt sarvārthatvāt // MS_7,3.30 //
children.translated_text: In the [present] context, it should be the ordinary [fire], because [it] serves all purposes. // MS_7,3.30 //

children.text: gargatrirātra ājyadohāni sāmāni prakṛtya śrūyate, agnim upanidhāya stuvata{*7/223*} iti. tatra{*7/224*} viśayaḥ, kiṃ laukiko 'gnir upanidheyaḥ{*7/225*}, uta vaidika iti. kiṃ prāptam. vaidika iti. kutaḥ. sarvakarmārtha utpanno 'sau. yāny ahaṃ karmāṇi kariṣye yaiś cāsmy adhikṛta iti, ato vaidika upanidheya iti. evaṃ prāpte ucyate, viśaye laukikaḥ syāt sarvārthatvāt. etasmin viśaye laukikaṃ vaidikam iti, laukikaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Gargatrirātra</s> (three-night sacrifice of <s>Garga</s>), with reference to the <s>Ājyadoha</s> <s>Sāmans</s>, it is heard: 'Having placed fire nearby, they should chant.' There the question [arises]: should the ordinary (<s>laukika</s>) fire be placed nearby, or the Vedic (<s>vaidika</s>) [fire]? What is the prima facie view? The Vedic [fire]. Why? That [Vedic fire] was produced for all ritual purposes — 'whatever rituals I shall perform and for which I am eligible' — therefore the Vedic [fire] should be placed nearby. Given this prima facie view, it is stated: in this context, it should be the ordinary [fire], because [it] serves all purposes.

children.text: atha yad uktam{*7/226*}, vaidikaṃ sarvakarmārtham utpannam, tasmāt tadupanidheyam iti. atra brūmaḥ,
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was said — 'the Vedic [fire], produced for all ritual purposes, should be placed nearby' — to this we reply:

children.text:

*{7/224: E2,6: atra}*
*{7/225: E2: upavidheyaḥ}*
