children.text: na vaidikam arthanirdeśāt // MS_7,3.31 //
children.translated_text: Not the Vedic [fire], because of the specification of its purpose. // MS_7,3.31 //

children.text:
na vaidikam agnidravyaṃ śāstreṇotpāditam. tasya śāstreṇaiva kāryaṃ nirdiṣṭam, yadāhavanīye juhotītīy ārabhya. tasmin sarvārthe kalpyamāne nirdeśo 'narthakaḥ syāt. tasmāl laukiko 'gnir upanidheyaḥ. sarvārthatvaṃ caiṣāṃ sve sve kārye vartamānānāṃ bhaviṣyati. evam ubhayam aviruddham, sarvārthatvaṃ nirdeśaś ceti.
atha dhaiṣṇā agnayaḥ kasmān nopanidhīyante. atrocyate,
children.translated_text:
The Vedic fire-substance, produced by scripture, should not [be placed nearby]. Its purpose has been specified by scripture itself — beginning with 'one offers upon the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.' If [the Vedic fire] were postulated as serving all purposes, the [scripture's] specification would be purposeless. Therefore the ordinary fire should be placed nearby. And the 'serving-all-purposes' quality of these [fires] will apply while each operates in its own respective function. Thus both are non-contradictory — the serving-all-purposes quality and the specification.
Now, why are the <s>Dhaiṣṇya</s> (subsidiary hearth) fires not placed nearby? Here it is replied:

children.text: tathotpattir itareṣāṃ samatvāt // MS_7,3.32 //
children.translated_text: The origination of the others too is likewise, because of equality. // MS_7,3.32 //

children.text: itareṣām apy agnīnāṃ dhaiṣṇyānāṃ tathotpattiḥ, na sarvārtha [49]{*7/227*} ity arthaḥ. kutaḥ. samatvāt. ete 'pītarair agnibhiḥ samāḥ. eteṣām api nirdiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ, prāg āsīno dhiṣṇyān āghārayati{*7/228*} iti. atas te nopanidheyā iti.
children.translated_text: The origination of the other <s>Dhaiṣṇya</s> fires too is likewise — [meaning] not for all purposes. Why? Because of equality. These too are equal to the other [principal] fires. Their purpose too is specified: 'sitting to the east, he offers into the <s>Dhaiṣṇya</s> fires.' Therefore they should not be placed nearby.

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ syāt tacchabdatvāt // MS_7,3.33 //
children.translated_text: [The substance referred to as 'yūpa'] should be refined, because of [having] that word. // MS_7,3.33 //

children.text: ekādaśinyāṃ śrūyte, upaśayo yūpo bhavatīti. tatra saṃdehaḥ. kim etad upaśayadravyaṃ saṃskṛtam, joṣaṇādayaḥ saṃskārā atra kartavyāḥ, uta neti. kiṃ yuktam. saṃskṛtaṃ syat. kartavyā atra joṣaṇādayaḥ saṃskārāḥ. kutaḥ. tacchabdatvāt. ayaṃ yūpaśabdaḥ saṃskāranimittaḥ. sa eṣo 'satsu saṃskāreṣu nopapadyate. tasmāt te kāryā iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Ekādaśinī</s> (eleven-day rite) it is heard: 'The pillow (<s>upaśaya</s>) is a <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post).' There a doubt [arises]: should this pillow-substance be refined — should the refinement-actions of shaping (<s>joṣaṇa</s>) and the like be performed on it — or not? What is proper? It should be refined. The refinement-actions of shaping and the like should be performed on it. Why? Because of [having] that word — this word '<s>yūpa</s>' is occasioned by refinement-actions. That [word] is not applicable in the absence of refinement-actions. Therefore they should be performed.

children.text: bhaktyā vāyajñaśeṣatvād guṇānām abhidhānatvāt // MS_7,3.34 //
children.translated_text: Or [the word is] figurative, because of [the pillow] not being a remainder of the sacrifice, and because [the word] denotes qualities. // MS_7,3.34 //

children.text:
na vā kartavyāḥ. kutaḥ. ayajñaśeṣatvād. ete saṃskārā asmin kāṣṭhe kriyante. etena dvāreṇa yajatinā saṃbhatsyante. itthaṃ saṃskṛte kāṣṭhe niyuktena paśunā yajiḥ kriyamāṇo 'pūrvaṃ nirvartayati{*7/229*}. asmiṃś copaśaye na paśur niyujyate, tatra kṛtāḥ saṃskārā anarthakāḥ syuḥ.
nanu vacanasāmarthyād adṛṣṭārthā bhaviṣyanti. ucyate, nātra vacanam, yūpaḥ kartavya iti. vartamānāpadeśo 'yam.
nanu vartamānāpadeśo 'pi na ghaṭate, saṃskārāṇām abhāve. ucyate, bhaktyā bhaviṣyati. yathā, yaja[50]{*7/230*}māno vai yūpa iti. āha, tatra sādṛśyāt. iha punaḥ katham iti. ucyate, guṇānām abhidhānatvāt. yūpaguṇānāṃ yūpasaṃskārāṇām{*7/231*} abhidhānatvād yūpasaṃskārāḥ. tatra kecid arthaprāptāś chedanādayas tūṣṇīṃkṛtāḥ santi. tair ayam abhidhīyate, yūpa ity ayūpaḥ san. yathā snātā kanyānalaṃkṛtā mālāguṇenāpy alaṃkṛteti. evam ekadeśenāpi saṃskārāṇāṃ saṃskṛta iti stutyābhidhīyate.
children.translated_text:
Or they should not be performed. Why? Because of [the pillow] not being a remainder of the sacrifice. These refinement-actions are performed on this wood [i.e., the regular yūpa]. Through this [refinement], it will connect with the sacrifice (<s>yajati</s>). When the wood has been refined in this manner, the animal fastened to it [enables] the sacrifice to produce the <s>apūrva</s> (unprecedented result). But in this pillow (<s>upaśaya</s>), no animal is fastened; therefore the refinement-actions performed there would be purposeless.
[The objector says:] by the force of the [Vedic] statement, they will serve an unseen purpose. It is replied: there is no statement here 'a <s>yūpa</s> should be made.' This is a present-tense designation [i.e., descriptive, not prescriptive].
[The objector:] but even a present-tense designation is not fitting in the absence of refinement-actions. It is replied: it will be figurative (<s>bhakti</s>). Just as 'the sacrificer is indeed a <s>yūpa</s>.' [The objector] says: there, because of resemblance. But here, how? It is replied: because [the word] denotes qualities. Because of [the pillow] possessing the qualities of a <s>yūpa</s> — [namely,] the refinement-actions of the <s>yūpa</s> — [it is called a <s>yūpa</s>]. Some of these are established by implication — cutting and the like — which exist as silent [i.e., unprescribed] refinements. By means of those, this [pillow] is designated [as a '<s>yūpa</s>'], though it is not [actually] a <s>yūpa</s>. Just as a bathed maiden, adorned [with ornaments], is called 'adorned' even by the quality of wearing a garland alone. So too, even by a partial [set] of refinement-actions, [the pillow] is praised as 'refined' — [called] a '<s>yūpa</s>.'

children.text:
agnau śrūyate, pṛṣṭhair upatiṣṭhanta{*7/232*} iti. tatra cintyate, kiṃ pṛṣṭhadharmāḥ kartavyāḥ, uta neti. ke punas te. sāmānyadharmā hiṃkārādayaḥ, viśeṣadharmāḥ, rathantare prastūyamāne pṛthivīṃ manasā dhyāyed bṛhati samudram ityevamādayaḥ. kiṃ tāvat prāptam. tata āha, etat tāvan naḥ parīkṣyam. kim ayaṃ pṣṭhaśabdaḥ karmaṇo vācakaḥ, uta dravyasyeti.
nanu siddham etat karmanāmadheyaṃ pṛṣṭhaśabda iti, yasmin guṇopadeśaḥ pradhānato 'bhisaṃbandha ity atra. tāsv eva codanāsv etad uktam, saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni, vairūpaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ{*7/233*} vairājaṃ pṛṣṭham{*7/234*} iti. idānīm, pṛṣṭhair upatiṣṭhanta{*7/235*} ity asyāṃ cintyate. kiṃ punar atra yuktam. tata āha,
children.translated_text:
Regarding the fire[-altar], it is heard: 'They worship with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants].' There it is considered: should the rules of the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants] be performed, or not? What are those [rules]? General rules such as the <s>hiṅkāra</s> and the like; specific rules such as 'when the <s>Rathantara</s> is being chanted, one should mentally meditate on the earth; in the <s>Bṛhat</s>, on the ocean' — and similar [rules]. What is the prima facie view first? To this [the commentator] says: this much is first to be examined by us — is this word '<s>Pṛṣṭha</s>' a designation of the action, or of the substance?
[The objector says:] but it is settled that the word '<s>Pṛṣṭha</s>' is an action-designation — [as stated] in 'when a subsidiary-teaching relates to the principal as its primary connection.' In those very injunctions this was stated: 'the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> have seventeen[-fold Stoma]'; 'the <s>Vairūpa</s> is a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>'; 'the <s>Vairāja</s> is a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>.' Now, regarding 'they worship with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants],' [the question] is being considered. What is proper here? To this [the commentator] says:

children.translated_text: The word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> ('back') would be [a designation] of the action, because of instruction in that form. // MS_7,3.35 //

children.text: karmaṇaḥ pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ{*7/236*} syāt. kutaḥ. tathābhūtopadeśāt. [51]{*7/237*} tathābhūtaḥ{*7/238*} sann{*7/239*} upadeśaḥ, yatrāyaṃ pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ karmanāmādhigataḥ{*7/240*}. tathābhūto 'yam api. kim asya tathātvam. pṛṣṭhaśabdasāmānyam. pṛṣṭhaśabdas tatra karmavacano 'dhigataḥ. sa evāyam. tasmād ihāpi tadvacana evāvagantavyaḥ viśeṣābhāvāt. yady anyārthaḥ{*7/241*} kalpyate, ekaḥ śabdo 'nekārthaḥ syāt. tatra ko doṣaḥ. śabda uccarite saṃśayaḥ syāt, nārthapratyayaḥ. tatra vyavahāro na sidhyet. vyavahārārthaś ca śabdaprayogaḥ. kāraṇāntaraṃ ca prakaraṇādyapekṣyam. ekārthatve tu nirapekṣo 'rthapratyayaḥ. tasmād anekārthatvam anyāyyam. tasmāt karmanāma pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ. yadā karmanāma, tadā yadi tāvat tāni karmāṇīhopadiśyante, tatrotpattir eṣām anarthikā. atha mā bhūd eṣa doṣa ity etad upasthānaṃ tatra vijñāyate. tata idaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bādhyeta. tasmāt sādṛśyavidhir ayam. pṛṣṭher upatiṣṭhante{*7/242*}, pṛṣṭhasadṛśaiḥ karmabhir upatiṣṭhanta{*7/243*} iti, tatsādṛśyaṃ ca dharmair bhavati. tasmāt kartavyā dharmā iti.
children.translated_text: The word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> would be [a designation] of the action. Why? Because of instruction in that form. [51] Having that form as its instruction — [meaning] where this word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> is ascertained as a name of the ritual action. This too has that [same] form. What is its 'having that form'? The commonality of the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s>. The word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> was ascertained there as denoting the ritual action. This is the very same [word]. Therefore here too it should be understood as denoting the same [ritual action], because of the absence of distinction. If another meaning were postulated, a single word would have multiple meanings. What is the fault in that? Upon the utterance of the word, there would be doubt, not comprehension of the meaning. In that case, practical transactions would not succeed. And the purpose of word-usage is practical transaction. And an additional cause [such as] context and the like would have to be relied upon. But when [the word has] a single meaning, comprehension of the meaning is independent [of other factors]. Therefore having multiple meanings is improper. Therefore the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> is a ritual-name. When it is a ritual-name, then if those [<s>Pṛṣṭha</s>] ritual actions are being prescribed here, [the statement of] their origination would be purposeless. But lest there be this fault, the [sentence is understood as] 'an attendance' (<s>upasthāna</s>) upon them. Then this context would be overridden. Therefore this is a prescription of similarity: 'they attend with <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>' [means] 'they attend with ritual actions resembling the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>' — and that similarity is [achieved] through [sharing the same] properties. Therefore the properties should be performed.

children.text: abhidhānopadeśād vā vipratiṣedhād dravyeṣu pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ syāt // MS_7,3.36 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the instruction of denomination and because of conflict, the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> would [refer to] the materials (<s>dravya</s>, i.e., the <s>ṛc</s>s). // MS_7,3.36 //

children.text:
na caitad evam, karmaṇaḥ pṛṣṭhaśabda iti. kiṃ tarhi. dravyeṣu pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ syāt. ṛgdravyeṣv abhitvā śūra nonuma ityevamādīnām ṛcāṃ vācakaḥ. kutaḥ. abhidhānopadeśāt. abhidhānopadeśo 'yaṃ pṛṣṭhair upatiṣṭhanta{*7/244*} iti, pṛṣṭhair abhidadhātīty arthaḥ. katham punar ayam upasthānavacano 'bhidhānārthaḥ śakyo{*7/245*} vijñātum. ucyate, upagrahaviśeṣāt, mantrakaraṇa upatiṣṭhater ātmanepadaṃ bhavati. mantras tv abhidhānasya karaṇam, nopa[52]{*7/246*}sthānasya. upasthānaṃ śarīreṇa kriyate, manasā vā. tasmād abhidhānārthaḥ. sa eṣa vipratiṣedhaḥ. yadi pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ karmasu kalpyate, ātmanepadaṃ bādhyate. na hi tadā mantraḥ karaṇaṃ bhavati. athātmanepadam anurudhyate, upasthānavipratiṣedhaḥ, tadābhidhānārthatāpatati. tatrātmanepadānurodho nyāyyaḥ. pṛṣṭhaśabdo hi lakṣaṇayā pṛṣṭhasādhanaṃ mantraṃ bruvann arthavān bhavati{*7/247*}. ātmanepadaṃ tu mantrakaraṇenaivopapadyate. ataḥ pṛṣṭhasādhaneṣu mantreṣu pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ.
āha, naitad yuktam. upasthānārthatā hi śrutyopatiṣṭhateḥ. ātmanepadāl liṅgād abhidhātārthatā. na ca liṅgena śrutir bādhitavyā. ucyate, naivātra śrutir bādhyate. svārtham evopatiṣṭhatir āha samīpasthānam. tat tv abhidhānāya, abhidhānaṃ nirvartayitum agnisamīpe tiṣṭhed iti tiṣṭhatir āha, ātmanepadāt. tato 'virodhaḥ.
āha, evam apy abhidhānasya mantraḥ karaṇam, nopatiṣṭhateḥ. tatrāsaṃbandha evopasthānasya mantreṇa. tathā, pṛṣṭhair upatiṣṭhanta{*7/248*} iti samuccāraṇam anarthakaṃ syāt. ucyate, abhidhānam abhinirvartayan mantra upasthānasya karaṇaṃ bhavati. yato 'sya prayojanaṃ nirvartayati. na hi niṣprayojanam anuṣṭhīyate. tasmān mantreṣv eva pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ. mantreṣu cet, nāsti dharmāṇāṃ prāptiḥ. na hi mantrāṇāṃ dharmāḥ, adharmakās ta iti.
children.translated_text:
This is not so — that the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [refers to] the action. Rather, the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> would [refer to] the materials — it is a designation of the <s>ṛc</s>-materials such as '<s>abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ</s>' and the like. Why? Because of the instruction of denomination. This instruction is a denomination: 'they attend with <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>' — meaning 'they denominate with <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>.' But how can this attendance-statement be understood as meaning denomination? We say: because of the specific form of the [verbal] complement (<s>upagraha</s>) — when the instrument is a mantra, the middle voice (<s>ātmanepada</s>) of '<s>upatiṣṭhateḥ</s>' is used. And a mantra is the instrument of denomination, not of [physical] attendance. Attendance is done by the body or by the mind. Therefore [the sentence has the meaning of] denomination. This is the conflict: if the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> is applied to actions, the middle voice would be overridden — for then the mantra would not be the instrument. But if the middle voice is followed, there is a conflict with [the meaning of] attendance — then the meaning of denomination applies. There, following the middle voice is proper. For the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, by figurative extension denoting the mantra that is the instrument of the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>, becomes meaningful. But the middle voice is appropriate only with the mantra as instrument. Hence the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [refers to] the mantras that are the instruments of the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>.
He says: this is not proper. For the meaning of attendance belongs to '<s>upatiṣṭhateḥ</s>' by <s>śruti</s> (direct meaning). The meaning of denomination [comes] from the indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>) of the middle voice. And <s>śruti</s> should not be overridden by an indicatory sign. We reply: <s>śruti</s> is not overridden here. The verb '<s>upatiṣṭhateḥ</s>' expresses its own meaning — 'standing near.' But that [standing near] is for the purpose of denomination — 'one should stand near the fire in order to accomplish the denomination' — this is what the verb says, [as shown] by the middle voice. Therefore there is no conflict.
He says: even so, the mantra is the instrument of denomination, not of '<s>upatiṣṭhateḥ</s>.' There, there is simply no connection of attendance with the mantra. Likewise, [52] the co-utterance 'they attend with <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>' would be purposeless. We reply: while accomplishing the denomination, the mantra becomes the instrument of attendance, since it accomplishes its purpose. For nothing is performed without a purpose. Therefore the word <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [refers to] the mantras. And if [it refers to] the mantras, there is no obtainment of properties. For mantras do not have [ritual] properties — they are without properties.

children.text: itikartavyatāvidher yajateḥ pūrvavattvam // MS_7,4.1 //
children.translated_text: Because the injunction is of the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>), [the modification] would be like the earlier [archetype] (<s>pūrvavat</s>) with respect to the sacrifice (<s>yajati</s>). // MS_7,4.1 //

children.text:
anārabhya kiṃcic chrūyate, sauryaṃ caruṃ{*7/250*} nirvaped brahmavarcasakāma{*7/251*} iti. tatraiṣo 'rthaḥ samadhigataḥ, yāgo 'yaṃ codyata{*7/252*} iti, yajatis tu dravyaphalabhoktṛsaṃyogād eṣāṃ{*7/253*} karmasaṃbandhād{*7/254*} iti. tathedam apy uktam, karmaphalayoḥ saṃbandhe karma guṇataḥ, phalaṃ pradhānata iti, pratyarthaṃ cābhisaṃyogāt karmato hy abhisaṃbandhaḥ, tasmāt karmopadeśaḥ syād iti. idam api coktam, yajir apūrvaṃ sādhayati. tataś cāpūrvāt kālāntare phalaṃ bhavatīti, codanā punar ārambha ity atra. evam etasmin sati sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāma{*7/255*} ity atra sauryayāgenāpūrvaṃ kṛtvā brahmavarcasaṃ sādhayed brahmavarcasakāma ity evaṃ vijñāyate.
āha, yatra tṛtīyāyukto yajiḥ, tatra yukto guṇabhāvābhyupagamaḥ. yathā, jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeti{*7/256*} iti. iha tv asatyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ kathaṃ tṛtīyārtho gamyata iti. ucyate, kim atra tṛtīyānirdiṣṭena yajinā kāryam. yadā svabhāvasiddhaḥ karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ prati guṇabhāvaḥ. yatrāpy asau śrutaḥ, tatrāpy akiṃcitkara eva, gatārthatvāt. tathā, yatrāpi dvitīyā śrutiḥ, yathāgnihotraṃ juhuyād iti, tatrāpi vibhaktivyatyayo vā, īpsitatvasya{*7/257*} vāvivakṣā kāmaṃ vānarthakyaṃ syāt. na tu kathaṃcid api karmaṇaḥ prati guṇabhāvaḥ śakyo 'pahnotum. tasmād yāgenāpūrvasādhanam atrocyate. tatra yāgo vijñāyate. [54]{*7/258*} laukiko 'sau padārthaḥ. tena tu katham apūrvaṃ sādhyata ity etan na vijñāyate. iha tu yāgenāpūrvaṃ sādhayed ity etāvad evoktam. kathaṃ sādhayed itītikartavyatā noktā. yeṣāṃ cārthānāṃ jñāyata evetikartavyatā, teṣāṃ kartavyatvamātram upadiśyate, yathā, odanaṃ paced iti. yeṣāṃ tu na jñāyate, te sahetikartavyatayaivopadiśyante. yathā darśapūrṇamāsau. evaṃ cen nūnaṃ jñāyate, yāgenāpūrvanirvṛttāv itikartavyatā yasmād uktā{*7/259*} tasmān nūnam asāv astīti.
āha, yady asti loke, tato jñāyetaiva. atha nāsty eva, kathaṃ śakyā jñātum iti.
ucyate, bāḍham asti, laukikī vaidikī ca. laukikī tāvat pārvaṇasthālīpākādiṣu, vaidikī darśapūrṇamāsādiṣu. yadi tatpūrvā etāś codanās tadapekṣāḥ, sauryayāgenāpūrvaṃ sādhayet, yathājñātayetikartavyatayeti, tato yukta itikartavyatāyā avidhiḥ. na ca vidhīyate. ata itikartavyatāyā avidher yajateḥ pūrvavattvaṃ, vihitetikartavyatākatvam iti.
children.translated_text:
Without beginning [from an earlier context], it is heard: 'One should portion out a <s>caru</s> (porridge) for <s>Sūrya</s>, one desiring spiritual lustre.' There this meaning has been ascertained: it is a sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) that is being enjoined, and the sacrifice (<s>yajati</s>) is understood from the conjunction of substance, fruit, and enjoyer with the ritual action. And this too has been stated: in the connection of action and fruit, the action is subordinate and the fruit is primary. And: because of conjunction with each purpose, the connection is from the action; therefore there should be instruction of the action. And this too has been said: the sacrifice produces the unprecedented [result] (<s>apūrva</s>); from the <s>apūrva</s>, the fruit comes about at a later time — [as stated] in [the discussion of] 'injunction again is the commencement.'
This being so, in 'one should portion out a <s>caru</s> for <s>Sūrya</s>, one desiring spiritual lustre,' it is understood thus: 'one desiring spiritual lustre should accomplish spiritual lustre by producing the <s>apūrva</s> through the <s>Sūrya</s> sacrifice.'
He says: where the sacrifice (<s>yajati</s>) is connected with the instrumental case, there the acceptance of its subordinate status is fitting — as in 'one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.' But here, in the absence of the instrumental case, how is the instrumental meaning understood? We reply: what function does the sacrifice without an instrumental case-marker serve here? For the subordinate status of the ritual action with respect to the fruit is established by its own nature. Even where that [instrumental] is heard, it is of no effect, being redundant. Similarly, even where the accusative <s>śruti</s> is heard — as in 'one should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>' — there too, either there is an interchange of case-endings, or non-expression of the desired meaning, or it may just be purposeless. But in no way can the subordinate status of the action be denied. Therefore the production of the <s>apūrva</s> by the sacrifice is what is stated here. There, the sacrifice is understood. [54] That is a well-known worldly entity. But how the <s>apūrva</s> is to be produced by it — that is not understood. Now here, only this much is said: 'one should produce the <s>apūrva</s> by the sacrifice.' How one should produce it — the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) — is not stated. For those things whose procedure is [already] known, only the obligatoriness is taught — as in 'one should cook porridge.' But for those whose [procedure] is not known, they are taught together with the procedure — as the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites]. If this is so, then surely it is known — the procedure for producing the <s>apūrva</s> by the sacrifice — since [the procedure] is not stated, it must surely exist.
He says: if it exists in the world, then it would indeed be known. But if it does not exist at all, how could it be known?
We reply: indeed it exists — both worldly and Vedic. The worldly [procedure is found] in the <s>Pārvaṇa Sthālīpāka</s> and the like; the Vedic [procedure] in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like. If these injunctions are preceded by and dependent on those [known procedures], [the meaning is:] 'one should produce the <s>apūrva</s> by the <s>Sūrya</s> sacrifice, with whatever procedure is known' — then the non-injunction of the procedure is justified. And [the procedure] is not [separately] enjoined. Therefore, because the injunction is of the procedure, [the modification] is 'like the earlier [archetype]' with respect to the sacrifice — [meaning it] has a previously-prescribed procedure.

children.text: atha ya āhuḥ, yajeta yāgaṃ kuryād iti. juhuyād homaṃ kuryād iti. teṣāṃ kiṃ naiva dharmākāṅkṣā bhavati. bhavatīti brūmaḥ. yady api prajñātetikartavyato{*7/260*} yajir dravyaṃ devatāṃ pratyutsṛjyata iti. tathāpi yadā phalārthaḥ kriyate, tadā dharmān ākāṅkṣati. na hy adharmāt{*7/261*} phalaṃ bhavati. kathaṃ jñāyate. yo hy amedhyaṃ dravyam ucchiṣṭaḥ śayāno vā prauḍhapādo vāmena hastena vā pādena yathākathaṃcid{*7/262*} devatāyai{*7/263*} utsṛjati, tasya phalaṃ na bhavatīti śiṣṭāḥ smaranti. yas tu medhyaṃ dravyaṃ śucau deśe prayataḥ prāṅmukho dakṣiṇena hastena samāhitamanā [55]{*7/264*} mantravan niyamavac ca devatāyai{*7/265*} utsṛjati, tasya phalaṃ bhavatīti smaranti. tasmād yāvān yajatiḥ phalāyāmnāyate, sa sarvo dharmān ākāṅkṣati. atas teṣām apy asti dharmākāṅkṣā. satyām ākāṅkṣāyāṃ sannihitair dharmair avipratiṣiddhaḥ saṃbandhaḥ prakṛtau, vikṛtau{*7/266*} tv ānumānikaiḥ.
children.translated_text: Now, those who say: '<s>yajeta</s>' means 'one should perform a sacrifice'; '<s>juhuyāt</s>' means 'one should perform an offering' — for them, is there no expectation of [ritual] properties at all? We say: there is. Even though the sacrifice, whose procedure is [already] known, [involves] releasing a substance to a deity, nevertheless, when it is performed for the sake of fruit, it expects [ritual] properties. For from what lacks [proper] properties (<s>adharma</s>), fruit does not arise. How is this known? For the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) remember: one who [is] impure, reclining, with legs stretched out, with the left hand, or in whatever careless manner releases an unfit substance to a deity — for him fruit does not arise. But one who, [being] in a pure place, self-restrained, facing east, with the right hand, with concentrated mind, [55] with mantras, and with observances, releases a fit substance to a deity — for him fruit arises, so they remember. Therefore every sacrifice that is recorded [as producing] fruit expects [ritual] properties. Hence for them too there is an expectation of properties. When there is expectation, in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), the connection [of properties] is with those present in proximity, without conflict; in the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>), however, [it is] with those [obtained] by inference.

children.text: sa laukikaḥ syād dṛṣṭapravṛttitvāt // MS_7,4.2 //
children.translated_text: That [procedure] would be worldly, because of being observed in [worldly] practice. // MS_7,4.2 //

children.text:
adhunaivaṃ cintyate, kim aniyamo laukikī vaidikī vetikartavyatā, uta laukiky eva, āhosvid vaidikīti{*7/267*}. atra viśeṣābhāvād aniyame prāpte.
ucyate, sa laukikaḥ syāt. sa khalu kartavyatopāyo laukikaḥ syāt. kutaḥ. dṛṣṭapravṛttitvāt. dṛṣṭā hy asya tatra tatra pravṛttiḥ, yathā pārvaṇasthālīpāke, aṣṭakācarau, āgrahāyaṇīyakarmaṇi{*7/268*}, ity evaṃ yatra yatra yāgenāpūrvaṃ sādhyate, tatra tatrāsya pravṛttir dṛṣṭā. ato 'nvayād vijñāyate, yāgasyāpūrvaṃ sādhayato 'yam abhyupāya iti. ayaṃ cāpi yāgaḥ. tasmād asyāpi sa evābhyupāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Now it is thus investigated: is there no restriction — whether the procedure is worldly or Vedic — or is it worldly alone, or Vedic? Here, when non-restriction is obtained because of the absence of distinction, we say: that [procedure] would be worldly. That method of procedure would be worldly. Why? Because of being observed in [worldly] practice. For its practice is observed here and there — as in the <s>Pārvaṇa Sthālīpāka</s>, the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> ceremony, the <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s> rite — wherever the <s>apūrva</s> is to be produced by a sacrifice, there its practice is observed. Therefore, by positive correlation, it is understood: 'this is the method for the sacrifice that produces the <s>apūrva</s>.' And this too is a sacrifice. Therefore for this too, that very same method [applies].

children.text: vacanāt tu tato 'nyatvam // MS_7,4.3 //
children.translated_text: But because of the [Vedic] statement, [the procedure] would be different from that [worldly one]. // MS_7,4.3 //

children.text: āha, kim eṣa evotsargaḥ, sarvatra lokikītikartavyateti. evaṃ khalu prāptam. evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ, vacanāt tu tato 'nyatvam iti. yatra pratyakṣaṃ vacanaṃ vaidikyāḥ, tatra na laukikī syāt, vacanasāmarthyād vaidikī eva syāt, yathopasatsu gṛhamedhīye ca.
children.translated_text: [The objector] says: is this then the general rule — that everywhere the worldly procedure [applies]? This is indeed what has been arrived at. Given this, we say: because of [Vedic] statement, [the procedure would be] different from that. Where there is a direct [Vedic] statement of the Vedic [procedure], there the worldly [procedure] should not [apply] — by the force of the [Vedic] statement, only the Vedic [procedure] should [apply], as in the <s>Upasad</s> [rites] and in the <s>Gṛhamedha</s>.

children.text: liṅgena vā niyamyeta liṅgasya tadguṇatvāt // MS_7,4.4 //
children.translated_text: Or [the procedure] would be restricted by an indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>), because the indicatory sign is a quality of that [Vedic procedure]. // MS_7,4.4 //

children.text: liṅgena vetikartavyatā niyamyeta. katarā. yasyā liṅgam, vaidikyāś ca liṅgam. tasmād vaidikī. kiṃ punar liṅgam. saurye tāvac carau śrūyate, prayāje{*7/270*} kṛṣṇalaṃ juhoti{*7/271*} iti. tathā, aindrabārhaspatye, ardhaṃ barhiṣo lunāti, ardhaṃ na svayaṃ ditam ardhaṃ vedyāṃ karoty ardhaṃ na{*7/272*} iti. tathā pitṛyajñena hotāraṃ{*7/273*} vṛṇīte nārṣeyam iti. etair liṅgair jñāyate vaidikītikartavyateti. katham. tadguṇatvāt{*7/274*}. ete hi prayājādayo vaidikasyāpūrvasya guṇāḥ. yadi ca tadīyetikartavyatā pravartitā, tata eteṣu karmasv ete santi. tatraitāni vacanāny upapadyante, prayāje prayāje kṛṣṇalaṃ juhotītyevamādīni. tasmād vaidikītikartavyatā niyamyeta.
children.translated_text: Or the procedure would be restricted by an indicatory sign. Which one? That which has an indicatory sign — and it is the Vedic [procedure] that has the indicatory sign. Therefore the Vedic [procedure applies]. What then is the indicatory sign? In the <s>Saurya</s> <s>caru</s> (oblation to Sūrya) it is heard: 'At each <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering) he offers a <s>kṛṣṇala</s> (black seed).' Likewise, in the <s>Aindra-Bārhaspatya</s> [rite]: 'He cuts half the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass); [he does] not [cut the other] half — half is self-cut, half he places on the <s>vedi</s> (altar), half not.' Likewise: 'By the <s>Pitṛyajña</s> (ancestor-sacrifice), he chooses the <s>Hotṛ</s>, not an <s>Ārṣeya</s> [Sāman-singer].' By these indicatory signs it is known that the procedure is Vedic. How? Because the indicatory sign is a quality of that [Vedic procedure]. For these <s>prayājas</s> and such are qualities of the Vedic <s>apūrva</s>. And if its [i.e., the Vedic] procedure has been set in motion, then in those ritual acts these [elements] exist. And those statements are appropriate there — 'at each <s>prayāja</s> he offers a <s>kṛṣṇala</s>' and so forth. Therefore the Vedic procedure would be restricted [as the one to follow].

children.text: api vānyāyapūrvatvād yatra nityānuvādavacanāni syuḥ // MS_7,4.5 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of [the indicatory signs] not being preceded by a [valid] principle (<s>nyāya</s>), [these] would be constant-restatement statements wherever [they occur]. // MS_7,4.5 //

children.text:
api vā naivaṃ syāt, vaidikītikartavyateti. yat kāraṇam etair liṅgair na śakyate vaidikī niyantum. kutaḥ. anyāyapūrvatvāt. nyāyapūrvakaṃ hi vacanaṃ tatsādhakaṃ bhavati. na caitāni nyāyapūrvāṇi. na hi vaidikyāḥ pravṛttir yuktā, nibaddhā hi sā prakaraṇādibhiḥ kāraṇair darśapūrṇamāsādiṣu. kathaṃ tarhy etāni liṅgāni. ucyate, yatra nityānuvādavacanāni syuḥ. iha tāvad ardhaṃ barhiṣo lunāty ardhaṃ neti, barhir yatraiva{*7/275*} bhavaiṣyati. yat kāraṇam, sato barhiṣa ucyate{*7/276*}. na cehāsti barhiḥ. na hotāraṃ vṛṇīte nārṣeyam iti nityānuvādo bhaviṣyati. [57]{*7/277*}
nanu nityānuvādaḥ sann anarthako bhavati. kiṃ kriyatām, yasyārtho nāsti. prayāje prayāje kṛṣṇalaṃ juhotītivacanaṃ prayājānāṃ bhaviṣyati. kathaṃ punar atra prayājāś ca kṛṣṇalahomaś ca śakyo vaktum{*7/278*}. bhidyate hi tathā vākyam. evaṃ tarhi na prayājān vakṣyati. prayāje kṛṣṇalahomaṃ vidhāsyati. na cāsatsu prayājeṣu kṛṣṇalahomaḥ śakyate kartum ity arthāt prāyājān kariṣyati. tasmān na liṅgena vaidikyā niyamaḥ. yathoktena nyāyena laukikītikartavyateti.
children.translated_text:
Or rather, it should not be so — that the Vedic procedure [applies]. The reason is that by these indicatory signs the Vedic [procedure] cannot be restricted. Why? Because of not being preceded by a [valid] principle. For a statement preceded by a [valid] principle is what establishes [something]. And these are not preceded by a principle. For the operation of the Vedic [procedure] is not proper — for it is bound to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and other [rites] by causes such as context and the like. How then [are we to understand] these indicatory signs? We say: they would be constant-restatement statements. Here, 'he cuts half the <s>barhis</s>, not half' — the <s>barhis</s> will be wherever it is [already present by another rule]. The reason is: this is said of existing <s>barhis</s>. But here [in the modifications] there is no <s>barhis</s>. 'He does not choose a <s>Hotṛ</s>, not an <s>Ārṣeya</s>' — this will be a constant restatement. [57]
[The objector says:] but being a constant restatement, it becomes purposeless. What can be done — [the statement] has no purpose. 'At each <s>prayāja</s> he offers a <s>kṛṣṇala</s>' — this statement will be about the [pre-existing] <s>prayājas</s>. But how can both <s>prayājas</s> and the <s>kṛṣṇala</s>-offering be stated [by a single sentence] here? For thus the sentence would be split. Then [we say:] it will not be stating [the existence of] <s>prayājas</s>. It will prescribe the <s>kṛṣṇala</s>-offering at the <s>prayāja</s>. And since the <s>kṛṣṇala</s>-offering cannot be performed when <s>prayājas</s> do not exist, by implication it will [necessitate] the <s>prayājas</s>. Therefore the Vedic [procedure] is not restricted by the indicatory sign. By the previously stated principle, the worldly procedure [applies].

children.text: mitho vipratiṣedhāc ca guṇānāṃ yathārthakalpanā syāt // MS_7,4.6 //
children.translated_text: And because of mutual conflict, there should be a construction according to the purpose of the qualities [i.e., subsidiaries]. // MS_7,4.6 //

children.text: tatrāha, atha kasmān nobhe apītikartavyate saha pravartete iti. kim evaṃ bhaviṣyati. evaṃ tulyāpekṣā karmaṇām anyatarato na bādhitā bhavati. ucyate, sahapravṛttāv ekayā cet karma nirapekṣaṃ kṛtam, dvitīyasyāḥ pravṛttir vipratiṣiddhā. ato mithaḥ pravṛtter vipratiṣedhād yathārthakalpanā syāt. ekasyāḥ pravṛttiḥ syād iti arthaḥ. katham ekasyāḥ pravṛtter dharmāṇāṃ yathārthakalpanā bhavati. ye dharmā yeṣu kāryeṣu pravṛttāv utpannāḥ, ta ihāpi teṣv eva bhavanti. itarathā dvitīyasyā dharmā ayathārthā bhaveyuḥ pūrvair dharmaiḥ, teṣāṃ kāryāṇāṃ nirvartitatvāt. evam ekasyāḥ pravṛtter yathārthakalpanā bhavati. ato yathārthakalpanā syād ity anenaikasyāḥ pravṛttir ity uktaṃ bhavet. ekasyāḥ pravṛttau yathoktenaiva nyāyena laukikyāḥ pravṛttir iti.
children.translated_text: There [the objector] says: why should not both procedures operate together? What will [result from] this? Thus, the equal dependence of the ritual acts will not be overridden by either one. [We] reply: if in simultaneous operation the ritual act has been completed without remainder by one [procedure], the operation of the second is contradicted. Therefore, because of the mutual conflict in simultaneous operation, there should be a construction according to purpose — [meaning] only one should operate. How does a construction according to purpose of the properties [result from] the operation of one [procedure alone]? Whatever properties have arisen when [applied] to whatever ritual acts through [one] procedure — those exist here too in those same [acts]. Otherwise, the properties of the second [procedure] would be purposeless with respect to those ritual acts, since those acts have [already] been accomplished by the prior properties. Thus, from the operation of one [procedure], the construction according to purpose obtains. Therefore 'there should be a construction according to purpose' is saying that only one should operate. And upon the operation of one, by the previously stated principle, the worldly [procedure] operates.

children.text:
bhāgitvāt tu niyamyeta guṇānām abhidhānatvāt, saṃbandhād abhidhānavad yathā dhenuḥ kiśoreṇa // MS_7,4.7 //{*7/280*}
tuśabdaḥ pakṣanivṛttau. na tv evaṃ syāt, laukikītikartavyateti. kiṃ tarhi. vaidikī niyamyeta. kutaḥ. bhāgitvāt. vaidiky api bhāginī pravṛtteḥ. sāpi hy apūrvasyetikartavyatā. samāne ca bhāgitva ubhayor vaidiky eva syāt. guṇānām abhidhānatvāt. guṇā ete prayājādayaḥ sauryādiṣu dṛśyamānā abhidhāyakā bhavanty etasyārthasya. yathā vaidiky atretikartavyateti bodhakā bhavantīty arthaḥ.
kasmāt. saṃbandhāt. ete hi tayetikartavyatayā saṃbaddhāḥ. ataḥ sāhacaryāt tāṃ gamayanti. abhidhānavat. yathā kauṇḍapāyināmayana agnihotram ity abhidhānaṃ karmaṇo vācakam, tatkarmasahacaritān dharmān ānayati, teṣv asatsv etad abhidhānam iha na yujyata iti teṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tatra bhāvo vijñāyate. evam ihāpi prayājādīnāṃ darśanam asatyaṃ vaidikyāṃ na yujyata iti, tasyā apīha bhāvo vijñāsyate. nanv asati nyāye liṅgam akāraṇam. satyam evam, uktas tu nyāyo bhāgitvād iti.
yat tu dṛṣṭapravṛttir laukikīti. tatra brūmaḥ, yady api dṛṣṭapravṛttiḥ syāt, tathāpi vaidiky eva niyamyeta. katham. yathā dhenuḥ kiśoreṇa, tad yathā, kṛṣṇakiśorā dhenur{*7/281*} iti. yady api dhenuśabdo godhenvāṃ dṛṣṭapravṛttiḥ, tathāpy abhidhānasāmānyād aśvadhenvām api bhāgīti kiśoreṇa liṅgenāśvadhenvāṃ vijñāyate. evam ihāpi yady api laukikī dṛṣṭapravṛttiḥ, tathāpītikartavyatāsāmānyena bhāgitvāl liṅgena vaidikī vijñeyā.
children.translated_text:
But [the procedure] would be restricted because of [the Vedic procedure's] equal sharing, because the qualities [i.e., subsidiaries] are declarative [of it], because [their] connection is like a designation — just as [the word] 'cow' [is restricted to a mare] by [the qualifier] 'foal.' // MS_7,4.7 //
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [previous] position. It should not be so — that the worldly procedure [applies]. Rather, the Vedic [procedure] would be restricted. Why? Because of [its] equal sharing — the Vedic [procedure] too is a sharer of the operation. For it too is a procedure of the <s>apūrva</s>. And when both have equal sharing, only the Vedic [should apply]. Because the qualities are declarative — these qualities such as <s>prayājas</s> etc. that are seen in the <s>Saurya</s> and other [rites] are declarative of this meaning. [That is,] they are informants that the procedure here is Vedic.
Why? Because of the connection — for these are connected with that procedure. Therefore, by association, they convey it. Like a designation — just as in the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s>' <s>Ayana</s> the designation 'Agnihotra' is a name of the ritual act and brings the properties associated with that ritual, [and] in the absence of those [properties] that designation would not be appropriate here — thus the existence of those properties there is understood — so here too, the appearance of <s>prayājas</s> and such would be impossible without the Vedic [procedure] — thus the existence of that [Vedic procedure] here too will be understood. [The objector says:] but without a [valid] principle, the indicatory sign is not a cause. True, that is so; but the principle has been stated — 'because of equal sharing.'
As to [the argument that] the worldly [procedure] is the one with observed operation — to that we say: even if [the worldly procedure] has observed operation, still only the Vedic [procedure] would be restricted. How? Just as [the word] 'cow' [is restricted to a mare] by [the qualifier] 'foal' — as in [the expression] 'a cow with a dark foal.' Even though the word '<s>dhenu</s>' (cow) has its observed operation in [reference to] a milk-cow, still, because of the commonality of [the meaning] 'designation,' it shares [the meaning with] a mare, and by the indicatory sign of [the word] 'foal' [referring to a horse's young], it is understood [to mean] a mare. So here too, even though the worldly [procedure] has observed operation, still — because of the commonality of [being a] procedure and [its] equal sharing — by the indicatory sign, the Vedic [procedure] should be understood.

children.text: utpattīnāṃ samatvād vā yathādhikāraṃ bhāvaḥ syāt // MS_7,4.8 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, because of the equality of origins, [the properties] should belong according to [their respective] domains. // MS_7,4.8 //

children.text:
atha vā naiva liṅgena niyama iti. kutaḥ. utpattīnāṃ samatvāt. dharmāṇāṃ prayājādīnām utpattayaḥ samāḥ sarveṣām āgneyādyaṅgabhāvena, na parasparāṅgatvena. kim ataḥ. yadi prayājādīnām anuyājādayo 'ṅgāni syuḥ, tato yatra pradhānam, tatrāṅgānīti prayājadarśanenānuyājādayo 'numīyeran, yadā tu samapradhānā ete, tadā prayājadarśanena kāmaṃ prayājā anumīyeran, prayājadharmā vā. na tv anuyājādayaḥ. tasmāl liṅgam aniyāmakam. yat tv abhidhānavad iti. atra brūmaḥ, yuktaṃ tatra. tatra{*7/283*} hi paraśabdaḥ paratra prayuktaḥ san dharmān{*7/284*} atidiśatīty uktam.
api ca, vidhir asau. agnihotravad dhotavyam iti. ayaṃ punar anuvādaḥ. tenātra prayājādīnām eva nāsti prāptiḥ, kuto 'nuyājādīnām. tasmād viṣama upanyāsaḥ, abhidhānavad iti. ato yathādhikāraṃ bhāvaḥ syāt. ye dharmā yasyāpūrvasyādhikāra āmnātās te tatraiva bhaveyuḥ.
evaṃ tarhi, sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvaped{*7/285*} ity anenākhyātena pradhānasya vidhānotpattiḥ, śeṣāṇāṃ ca vacanaṃ bhavatu. kathaṃ kṛtvā. nānaṅgaṃ pradhānam ucyamānaṃ kasmaicit prayojanāya kalpata iti. tena ca prāpitānām aṅgānām etebhyo liṅgebhyo viśeṣāvadhāraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati. tatredam ucyate,
children.translated_text:
Or rather, there is simply no restriction by the indicatory sign. Why? Because of the equality of origins. The origins of the properties such as <s>prayājas</s> etc. are equal — all [have their origin] as subsidiaries of the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [rites], not as subsidiaries of one another. What [follows] from this? If the <s>anuyājas</s> (concluding offerings) etc. were subsidiaries of the <s>prayājas</s>, then where there is the principal, there [would be] the subsidiaries — and by seeing <s>prayājas</s>, the <s>anuyājas</s> etc. would be inferred. But when these are of equal principal-status, then by seeing <s>prayājas</s> one may well infer [the existence of] <s>prayājas</s>, or the properties of <s>prayājas</s>, but not <s>anuyājas</s> etc. Therefore the indicatory sign does not restrict. As to [the argument] 'like a designation' — to that we say: that is appropriate there. For there, a word established elsewhere, when employed in another [context], extends properties — that has been stated.
Moreover, that [Agnihotra case] is an injunction — 'one should offer like the <s>Agnihotra</s>.' But this [present case] is a restatement. Therefore here there is no applicability even of <s>prayājas</s> — how much less of <s>anuyājas</s> and such. Therefore the illustration 'like a designation' is inapt. Hence [the properties] should belong according to [their respective] domains — whatever properties are recorded in the domain of whatever <s>apūrva</s>, they should belong to that alone.
If so, then [consider:] 'one should offer the <s>Saurya</s> <s>caru</s>' — by this verbal inflection there is the origin-and-injunction of the principal, and there should [also] be a statement of the subsidiaries. How? Because without subsidiaries the principal being stated cannot be appropriate for any purpose. And the determination of specific [subsidiaries] for those [properties] thus obtained will be made from these indicatory signs. Here the following is said:

children.text: utpattiśeṣavacanaṃ ca vipratiṣiddham ekasmin // MS_7,4.9 //
children.translated_text: The statement of both origin [of the principal] and subsidiaries is contradictory in a single [verbal expression]. // MS_7,4.9 //

children.text: ekasmiñ śabde pradhānasyotpattir aṅgānāṃ ca vacanaṃ na [60]{*7/286*} saṃbhavati. kiṃ kāraṇam. utpannaṃ hi pradhānam aṅgān apekṣate. apekṣayā ca tāni gṛhyante. tasmān naitad api yuktam. yadi ca nirvaped ity anena śabdenāṅgāny api vidhīyeran, tatas teṣām api phalasaṃbandhaḥ syāt. tathāṅgatvam eva vyāhanyeta. tato 'yam api vādo na ghaṭate. tasmād yathokto laukika evābhyupāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: In a single word, the origin of the principal and the statement of subsidiaries is not [60] possible. What is the reason? For the principal, [once] originated, requires subsidiaries. And they are grasped through that requirement. Therefore this [view] too is not proper. And if by the word '<s>nirvaped</s>' (one should offer) the subsidiaries too were enjoined, then they too would have a connection with the fruit. And in that case, their very subsidiary-status would be contradicted. Therefore this argument too does not work. Hence, as previously stated, the worldly means alone [is] the [correct] approach.

children.text: vidhyanto vā prakṛtivac codanāyāṃ pravarteta, tathā hi liṅgadarśanam // MS_7,4.10 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, the injunction-ending [portion], like the archetype, should operate in the injunction; for thus the indicatory signs are observed. // MS_7,4.10 //

children.text:
vidhyanto vā sauryādikāyāṃ codanāyāṃ pravarteta, na dharmā laukikāḥ. kaḥ punar ayaṃ vidhyanto nāma. vidher anto vidhyantaḥ. atha vidhiḥ kaḥ. yad vākyam upalabhya puruṣaḥ kasmiṃścid arthe pravartate, kutaścid vā nivartate, sa vidhiḥ. vidhīyate hy anenārthaḥ. yathā loke devadatta gām abhyāja śuklām{*7/287*} iti, tasyābhyājetyādiḥ{*7/288*}. itaro 'ntaḥ. vede 'pi darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti vidhyādiḥ. vidhyanto 'pi pradhānavidhivarjitaṃ kṛtsnaṃ pauroḍāśikaṃ brāhmaṇam. tena sameto 'yaṃ vidhyādir viśiṣṭāpūrvanirvṛttiṃ prati puruṣaṃ pravartayati. tasmāt so 'syāntaḥ. tathā somena yajeta{*7/289*} iti vidhyādiḥ. saumikam api brāhmaṇaṃ vidhyantaḥ. eṣa vidhyanto nāma.
eteṣu ca sauryādiṣu vidhyādir asti, vidhyanto nāsti. eteṣv api sa vidhyantaḥ kalpyeta. kathaṃ kṛtvā. aparipūrṇaṃ yad vākyam, tad adhyāhāreṇa vā pūryeta, vyavahitakalpanayā vā. tatrādhyāhārād vyavahitakalpanā jyāyasī. adhyāhāre hy aśrutaḥ kalpyeta{*7/290*}. itaratra śrutena saṃbandhaḥ. tasmād vyavahito brāhmaṇāvayavo 'sya paripūrakaḥ kalpyate. yathā vasantāya kapiñjalān ālabhate{*7/291*}, grīṣmāya kalaviṅkān ālabhata{*7/292*} iti. tena vaidikītikartavyatā prāpyate.
yadi{*7/293*} tad brāhmaṇam asyāntaḥ kalpyate, tatra na bhavati. tad etanmayūranṛtyam āpadyate. tad yathā, mayūrasya nṛtyato 'nyadapāvriyate 'nyat saṃvriyate. evam ihāpīdaṃ saṃvriyate tadapāvriyate. naiṣa doṣaḥ. pratyakṣas tasya tatra bhāvaḥ. iha punar ānumānikaḥ. na cānumānikaṃ pratyakṣaṃ bādhate. iha tarhi na prāpnoti, pratyakṣavirodhāt. syād evam, yadi virodhaḥ syāt. na tv asti virodhaḥ. tatrāpi bhaviṣyati, ihāpi tad etad uktam, vidhyanto vā prakṛtivac codanāyāṃ pravarteteti.
ucyate, prakṛtivad iti kim. āha, aṣṭame prakṛtiniyamaṃ kariṣyati. iyam asya prakṛtir iti. tad ucyate, vidhyanto vā prakṛter iva pravarteta. yā yā tasya karmaṇaḥ{*7/294*} prakṛtir iti yasyāgneyaḥ prakṛtiḥ, tasyāgneyād eva. yasyāgnīṣomīyaḥ, tasyāgnīṣomīyād ity evaṃ sarvatra.
atha kasmān na laukiko vidhyantaḥ kalpyate. ucyate, laukikasya vidher abhāvād vidhyanta eva nāsti. kutas tat kalpaneti. āha, laukikītikartavyatā prāpyatām, kiṃ vidhyantakalpanayeti. ucyate, vaidikī hy atretikartavyatā na laukikī. kasmāt. tathā hi liṅgadarśanaṃ prayājādi samarthitaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text:
Or the 'remainder of the injunction' (<s>vidhyanta</s>) should operate in an injunction such as the <s>Saurya</s> and the like — not worldly <s>dharmas</s>. Now what is this 'remainder of the injunction'? The remainder (<s>anta</s>) of the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is the <s>vidhyanta</s>. And what is an injunction? That sentence, upon apprehending which a person engages in some object or desists from some [object] — that is an injunction. For by it a meaning is enjoined. Just as in the world — '<s>Devadatta</s>, drive up a white cow' — of that, 'drive up' and the like is the beginning of the injunction. The other [i.e., the object 'white cow'] is the remainder. In the <s>Veda</s> too — 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — [this] is the beginning of the injunction. And the 'remainder of the injunction' is the entire <s>Pauroḍāśika Brāhmaṇa</s> (the Brāhmaṇa text on the cake-offerings) excluding the principal injunction. Together with that [remainder], this beginning of the injunction impels the person toward the production of the specific <s>apūrva</s>. Therefore that is its remainder. Likewise, 'one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>' is the beginning of the injunction. The <s>Soma</s>-related <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is the 'remainder of the injunction.' This is what the 'remainder of the injunction' means.
Now in these <s>Saurya</s> and the like [rites], there is the beginning of the injunction, [but] no remainder. For these too, that remainder should be postulated. How? An incomplete sentence — that should be completed either by ellipsis (<s>adhyāhāra</s>) or by postulating a connection with [something] intervening. Of these, postulating a connection with something intervening is superior to ellipsis. For in ellipsis, something unheard is postulated. In the other [method], there is a connection with what is [actually] heard. Therefore an intervening portion of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is postulated as its completer — just as [in] 'for Spring one slaughters <s>kapiñjalas</s> (francolin partridges)'; 'for Summer one slaughters <s>kalaviṅkas</s> (sparrows).' By that, a Vedic procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) is obtained.
If that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is postulated as its remainder, it [the Brāhmaṇa] will not be present there [in its original context]. This amounts to a 'peacock-dance' situation. Just as when a peacock dances, one [part] is uncovered while another is covered — so here too, this is covered while that is uncovered. This is not a fault. Its presence there is directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>); here it is merely inferential. And what is inferential does not override what is directly perceived. [The objector says:] then it does not apply here, because of contradiction with what is directly perceived. [We reply:] it would be so if there were a contradiction. But there is no contradiction. It will exist there too and here also — that is what is stated: 'the remainder of the injunction, like the archetype, should operate in the injunction.'
[The question is:] what does 'like the archetype' mean? He says: in the eighth [book], the restriction of the archetype will be made — 'this is its archetype.' That is stated: the remainder of the injunction should operate as if from the archetype. Whatever is the archetype of a given ritual — for one whose archetype is the <s>Āgneya</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s>), [the procedure is derived] from the <s>Āgneya</s> alone. For one whose archetype is the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s>, from the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s>. And so on everywhere.
Now why is a worldly 'remainder' not postulated? [We] reply: because of the absence of a worldly injunction, there is simply no 'remainder of the injunction' [in the worldly domain]. How then could it be postulated? He says: let a worldly procedure be obtained — why postulate a 'remainder of the injunction'? [We] reply: for the procedure here is Vedic, not worldly. Why? For thus the observation of the indicatory mark — such as the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) and the like — is vindicated.

children.text: liṅgahetutvād aliṅge laukikaṃ syāt // MS_7,4.11 //
children.translated_text: Because of [the Vedic procedure] being caused by the indicatory mark, in [a rite] without an indicatory mark, the worldly [procedure] would apply. // MS_7,4.11 //

children.text: yadi liṅgād vaidiko 'bhyupāyo bhavati, tena tarhy aliṅge laukikaṃ syāt. yatra karmaṇi kiṃcil liṅgaṃ nāsti, tatra laukikaṃ syād vidhānam. yathā, aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet, yasya sajātāvīyur iti.
children.translated_text: If the Vedic approach arises because of the indicatory mark, then in [a rite] without an indicatory mark, the worldly procedure would apply. Where a ritual has no indicatory mark whatsoever, there the arrangement would be worldly. As in: 'one should offer an eleven-potsherd [cake] for <s>Indrāgni</s>, for one among whose kinsmen they live long.'

children.text: liṅgasya pūrvavattvāc codanāśabdasāmānyād ekenāpi nirūpyeta yathā sthālīpulokena // MS_7,4.12 //
children.translated_text: Because of the indicatory mark being precedented, [and] because of the commonality of the injunctive word, [the Vedic procedure] can be ascertained by even one [indicatory mark], like [judging rice by] a grain from the pot. // MS_7,4.12 //

children.text:
atrocyate, syād evam, yadi liṅgahetuko vaidika upāyaḥ syāt. na tv asau liṅgahetukaḥ. kiṃhetukas tu. vidhyantahetukaḥ. vidhyanto 'pi nyāyapūrvaḥ, sa ca nyāyas tulyaḥ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ vaikṛtānāṃ liṅgavatām{*7/296*} ca. kutaḥ. codanāśabdasāmānyāt. karmacodanāyāṃ śābdaḥ samānaḥ. sarvatra vidhyādir asti, na vidhyantaḥ. tulyaś cāpekṣayānyatra śrutena vidhyantena saṃbandhaḥ. tad etan nyāyapūrvakaṃ liṅgam ekatrāpi dṛśyamānam, tulyanyāyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dharmavattāṃ jñāpayati. yathā sthālyāṃ tulyapākānāṃ pulākānām ekam upamṛdyāny eṣām api siddhatāṃ jānāti, tulyo hetur asya cānyeṣāṃ ca siddhatvasyeti. tasmāt sarvatra vaidikītikartavyatā.
atha yad uktam, dṛṣṭapravṛttir laukikītikartavyateti. atra brūmaḥ, sāmānyatodṛṣṭam etad upadiśyate. sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ca yad avyabhicāri, tat pramāṇam. savyabhicāraṃ caitat. dṛṣṭā hi gaṇayāgādayo 'nevamitikartavyatākāḥ. tasmād dṛṣṭapravṛttitvād ity ahetuḥ.
yat tu vaidikyā bhāgitvāt tatpūrvakāṇi liṅgāni bhaviṣyantīti. atra brūmaḥ, bhāgitvasyāpūrvetikartavyatākatvaṃ{*7/297*} kila hetuḥ. tad bhāvaś ca tasyāḥ śabdapūrvaḥ. śabdena ca darśapūrṇamāsayor asau vijñāyate{*7/298*}, na sarvatreti. tasmān na bhāgitvam. ato vidhyantenaivetikartavyatā prāpyate, nānyathā. atha kasmād etāni vaikṛtāni vākyāni nyūnāny eva nānumanyante, kim ebhiḥ pūritaiḥ. nyūnāny anarthakāni bhavanti. bhavantu, ko [63]{*7/299*} doṣaḥ. śiṣṭair eṣāṃ saṃparigraho na yujyate. pramādād bhaviṣyatīti. nāsty akṣare mātrāyāṃ vā pramādaḥ. kuto etāvati granthe bhaviṣyati. katham. tulyaṃ ca sāṃpradāyikam{*7/300*} ity uktam. vyāmoho 'pi viduṣāṃ yugasahasrāṇi bahūni nānuvarteta. yujyate caiṣām apekṣayā pūraṇam. tasmād ūnāni nānumanyante. ato vaidikītikartavyateti siddham.
children.translated_text:
To this we reply: it would be so if the Vedic approach were caused by the indicatory mark. But it is not caused by the indicatory mark. By what then is it caused? By the 'remainder of the injunction.' And the 'remainder of the injunction' is preceded by [the general] principle, and that principle is the same for all modified rites (<s>vaikṛta</s>) — whether they have indicatory marks or not. Why? Because of the commonality of the injunctive word. In the injunction of the ritual action, the word [structure] is the same. Everywhere there is the beginning of the injunction, [but] no remainder. And the expectation for connection with a heard remainder elsewhere is the same [in all cases]. Therefore this principle-based indicatory mark, being observed even in one [place], indicates the possession of <s>dharmas</s> for all [rites] that share the same principle — just as, in a pot of [rice grains] cooked uniformly, pressing one grain, one knows the done-ness of the others too, because the cause of done-ness is the same for this one and the others. Therefore the Vedic procedure [applies] everywhere.
Now, as to what was said — 'the procedure based on observed [worldly] practice is the worldly procedure' — to this we say: this is [an inference based on] general observation (<s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s>). And a general observation that is non-deviant is a valid means of knowledge. But this one is deviant. For <s>gaṇa</s>-sacrifices and the like are observed to have procedures unlike this [worldly model]. Therefore 'because of procedure based on observed practice' is not a [valid] reason.
As for [the argument] that because of having a share in the Vedic [procedure], the indicatory marks will presuppose it — to this we say: the reason alleged is that having a share [implies] the prior existence of the <s>apūrva</s>-procedure. And the existence of that [prior procedure] is based on [Vedic] word. And by [Vedic] word, that is known [only] in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, not everywhere. Therefore there is no 'having a share [universally].' Hence the procedure is obtained only by the 'remainder of the injunction,' not otherwise. Now, why are these modified (<s>vaikṛta</s>) sentences not accepted as simply deficient — what [is gained] by completing them? [If] deficient, they would be meaningless. [The objector says:] let them be [meaningless] — what is the fault? [We reply:] their acceptance by the learned would not be appropriate. [The objector says:] it will be due to error. [We reply:] there is no error in [even] a syllable or a <s>mātrā</s> (metrical unit). How could [error] exist in a text of this extent? How? Because it was said: 'and what is traditional is equal [in authority]' [63]. Moreover, a delusion of the learned would not persist for many thousands of ages. And the completion of these by expectation is appropriate. Therefore they are not accepted as deficient. Hence [the conclusion] — the Vedic procedure — is established.

prajākāmā gavāmayanam upeyur{*7/301*} iti satraṃ vidhāyāmnāyate, jyotir gaur āyur{*7/302*} iti, gavāmayane dvādaśāhiko vidhyanta iti vakṣyati{*7/303*}, gaṇeṣu dvādaśāhasya{*7/304*} iti. tatra codakena dvādaśāhikā dharmāḥ prāpyante. ekāhānām api yathā svaṃ nāmabhiḥ prātisvikāḥ. ye tatra dvādaśāhikā aikāhikair aviruddhāḥ, te yathāprāptaṃ kriyante. viruddheṣu saṃśayaḥ. kiṃ dvādaśāhiko dharmaḥ kartavyaḥ, utaikāhika iti. kiṃ prāptam. tatra sūtreṇaivopakramaḥ. dvādaśāhikam ahargaṇe tatprakṛtitvāt. dvādaśāhaprakṛtitvād vidhyantenaiva prāpyante.
nanv evaṃ nāmadheyaṃ bādhyate. na bādhiṣyate nāmadheyaṃ jyotir ādi. adhikāgamād bhaviṣyati. ye jyautiṣṭaumikebhyo 'dhikāḥ stotraśastravikārāḥ, tadāgamāt, ekāhavat. yathā tasminn eva jyotiṣy ekāhe jyotiḥśabdo 'dhikāgamād bhavati. satsu jyautiṣṭaumikeṣu jyotiṣṭome 'bhāvāt. adhikadharmārtho 'yaṃ śabdaḥ, [64]{*7/305*} na cādhikānāṃ dvādaśāhikair virodho 'sti. tasmād dvādaśāhikaṃ dharmajātaṃ viruddhaṃ kartavyam iti.
adhikāgamāt tadākhyaṃ syād ekāhavad ity etasyāparā vyākhyā. ye dvādaśāhe 'dhikā aikāhikebhyaḥ kecid dharmā ucyante. abhiplavo 'nvahaṃ bhavati{*7/306*}, gorivītam{*7/307*} anvahaṃ bhavatīti. teṣām adhikānām āgamāt tadākhyaṃ syāt. etad dvādaśāhikam aharjyotirākhyam āyurākhyaṃ vā{*7/308*}. katham. ekāhavat. yathā tasminn evaikāhe 'yaṃ jyotirādiśabdo jyautiṣṭaumikebhyo 'dhikeṣu vaiśeṣikeṣu dharmeṣv āgateṣu bhavati, evam ihāpy adhikāgamasāmānyād gauṇo bhaviṣyati. yathā ṣāḍahikānāṃ pṛṣṭhānāṃ bhāvād ekāho viśvajit ṣaḍaha{*7/309*} ity uktam. tam ekāhaṃ ṣaḍaha ity ācakṣata{*7/310*} iti. evam ihāpi. gauṇaś cen na prāpakaḥ. tasmān nāsti nāmadheyād dharmaprāptir iti.
children.translated_text:
'Those desiring offspring should undertake the <s>Gavāmayana</s>' — having enjoined a <s>satra</s>, it is recorded: '<s>Jyotis</s> (Light), <s>Gaus</s> (Cow), <s>Āyus</s> (Life)' and the like. It will be stated: 'in the <s>Gavāmayana</s>, the remainder of the injunction is from the twelve-day [rite]'; 'in [day-]series, [the properties are] of the twelve-day [rite].' There, by the injunctive principle, the properties of the twelve-day [rite] are obtained. And those of one-day [rites come] according to their respective names. Those twelve-day [properties] that do not conflict with the one-day [rite properties] are performed as obtained. Regarding conflicting ones, a doubt [arises]: should the twelve-day property be [followed], or the one-day [rite property]? What is the prima facie view? The introduction is by the <s>sūtra</s> itself: '[the properties are] of the twelve-day [rite] in the day-series, because of that being the archetype.' Because of the twelve-day [rite] being the archetype, [the properties] are obtained by the 'remainder of the injunction' alone.
[The objector says:] but in that case, the name (<s>nāmadheya</s>) would be overridden. [We reply:] the name — <s>Jyotis</s> and the like — will not be overridden. It will apply because of the arrival of additional [elements]. Those modifications of <s>stotra</s> (chant) and <s>śastra</s> (recitation) that are additional to those of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — because of the arrival of those, [it is named] like a one-day [rite]. Just as in that very <s>Jyotis</s> one-day [rite], the word '<s>Jyotis</s>' applies because of the arrival of additional [elements] — since, while the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-properties exist [there too], there is no [separate] <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [identity]. This word [64] is for the purpose of the additional <s>dharmas</s>, and there is no conflict of the additional [elements] with the twelve-day [properties]. Therefore the twelve-day property-set [even where] conflicting must be performed.
'Because of the arrival of additional [elements], it would have that name, like a one-day [rite]' — this has another interpretation. Those <s>dharmas</s> that in the twelve-day [rite] are additional to the one-day [rite properties] — such as 'the <s>Abhiplava</s> occurs every day'; 'the <s>Gorivīta</s> occurs every day.' Because of the arrival of those additional [elements], it would have that name — this twelve-day [rite] named '<s>Jyotis</s>-day' or '<s>Āyus</s>-day.' How? Like a one-day [rite]. Just as in that very one-day [rite], this word '<s>Jyotis</s>' and the like applies when the specific properties additional to those of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> arrive — so here too, because of the commonality of the arrival of additional [elements], it would be figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>). Just as because of the presence of six-day <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], the one-day [rite] <s>Viśvajit</s> is called a 'six-day [rite]' — 'they call that one-day [rite] a six-day [rite].' So here too. And being figurative, it does not bring [properties]. Therefore there is no obtaining of <s>dharmas</s> from the name.

children.text: liṅgāc ca // MS_7,4.14 //
children.translated_text: And because of the indicatory mark. // MS_7,4.14 //

children.text: liṅgāc caitaj jñāyate, yathā dvādaśāhikaṃ kartavyam iti. kiṃ liṅgaṃ bhavati. dvābhyāṃ lomāvadyati dvābhyāṃ tvacaṃ dvābhyām asṛg dvābhyāṃ māṃsam{*7/311*} iti. evaṃ ṣaḍdvikān anukramyāha, yad dvādaśopasado bhavanti, ātmānam etan nirvadyata iti dvādaśāhikaṃ dharmaṃ dvādaśopasattvaṃ darśayati. tad upapadyate, yadi dvādaśāhikaṃ dharmajātaṃ virodhi kartavyam. itarathā caikāhikaṃ ṣaḍupasattvaṃ{*7/312*} syāt{*7/313*}. tasmāt paśyāmaḥ, dvādaśāhikaṃ kartavyam iti. tathedam aparaṃ liṅgam. yasyātiriktam ekādaśinyām ālabheran na priyaṃ{*7/314*} bhrātṛvyam atiricyeta. atha yad dvau paśū samasyeyuḥ, kanīya āyuḥ kurvīran{*7/315*}. yady ete brāhmaṇavantaḥ paśava ālambhante nāpriyaṃ bhrātṛvyam atyatiricyate [65]{*7/316*} na kanīya āyuḥ kurvīteti{*7/317*}, ekādaśinyāṃ vihāraṃ dvādaśāhikaṃ dharmaṃ darśayati. katham. vihāre saty atirekaḥ paśūnām āpadyate. atirekabhayāc ca dvayor dvayoḥ samāsaḥ. ekāhadharmaprāptau vihāro na syāt. tatraitaddarśanaṃ na yujyate. tasmād dvādaśāhikaṃ kāryam.
children.translated_text: And from the indicatory mark this is known — that the twelve-day [properties] should be performed. What is the indicatory mark? 'With two [days] he removes the hair, with two the skin, with two the blood, with two the flesh' — thus having enumerated six pairs, it says: 'that there are twelve <s>upasads</s> (preparatory rites) — thereby he removes [impurity from] himself' — it shows the twelve-day property of twelve <s>upasads</s>. That is appropriate if the twelve-day property-set [even where] conflicting is to be performed. Otherwise, the one-day [property of] six <s>upasads</s> would apply. Therefore we see that the twelve-day [properties] should be performed. And this is another indicatory mark: 'If for one there is a surplus on the eleventh [day], let them slaughter [the animal] — [otherwise] the hateful enemy would surpass [him]. And if they were to combine two animals, they would make [his] life-span shorter.' If these animals endowed with <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-texts are slaughtered, the hateful enemy will not surpass [him] [65], nor will they make the life-span shorter — it shows the twelve-day property of alternation (<s>vihāra</s>) on the eleventh [day]. How? When there is alternation, a surplus of animals results. And for fear of surplus, two by two are combined. If the one-day [rite] properties were to apply, there would be no alternation. Then this observation would not be appropriate. Therefore the twelve-day [properties] should be performed.

children.text: na vā kratvabhidhānād adhikānām aśabdatvam // MS_7,4.15 //
children.translated_text: Or not, because the designation of the ritual [overrides]; the additional [elements] would be without [Vedic] word. // MS_7,4.15 //

children.text:
na vā dvādaśāhikaṃ kāryam. kiṃ tarhi. ekāhikam. kiṃ kāraṇam. codakena dvādaśāhikaṃ prāpnoti, nāmadheyenaikāhikam. nāmadheyaṃ ca codakād balīyaḥ. kutaḥ. pratyakṣatvāt. pratyakṣaṃ nāmadheyam, codakaṃ tv ānumānikam.
nanu vidhyanto 'pi pratyakṣaḥ. satyaṃ prakṛtau pratyakṣo vidhyantaḥ, vikṛtau tv ānumānikaḥ, nāmadheyaṃ punar vikṛtāv api pratyakṣam, pratyakṣaṃ cānumānād balīyaḥ, tasmād aikāhikaṃ kāryam.
nanv adhikāryaṃ nāmadheyam ity uktam. atrocyate, adhikānām aśabdatvam. adhikānāṃ śabdo nāsti. ime jyotirādayaḥ śabdāḥ karmanāmadheyānīty uktam. api vā nāmadheyaṃ syād yad utpattāv apūrvam avidhāyakatvād{*7/318*} iti. yat tu, adhikāgamāt tadākhyaṃ syād iti. tatra brūmaḥ, vacanād adhikāgamo na nāmadheyena. yat tu, teṣv asatsu śabdasyābhāvād iti. naite kadācid āyurādiṣu na santi. kathaṃ teṣām abhāve śabdasyābhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ. yat tu, jyotiṣṭome nāsti jyotirādiḥ śabda iti. karmāntaratvāt. jyotiṣṭoma āyurādiḥ śabdo nāsti, na dharmābhāvāt. tasmād aikāhikaṃ viruddhaṃ dharmajātaṃ kartavyam iti. adhikāgamāt tadākhyaṃ syāt. ekāhavad ity etasya dvitīyavyākhyāparihāraḥ. gauṇaḥ sann anu[66]{*7/319*}vādamātram anarthakaṃ syāt. tasmāt pūrvoktena nyāyena nāmadheyaṃ dharmāṇāṃ prāpakam iti.
children.translated_text:
Or the twelve-day [rite's properties] should not be adopted. What then? The one-day [rite's properties]. What is the reason? Through the injunctive principle (<s>codaka</s>), [the <s>Gavāmayana</s>] obtains the twelve-day [rite's properties]; through the name, the one-day [rite's properties]. And the name is stronger than the injunctive principle. Why? Because of being directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). The name is directly perceived, while the injunctive principle is inferential.
[The objector says:] but the force of a prescription (<s>vidhyanta</s>) is also directly perceived. True — in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), the force of prescription is directly perceived; but in the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>), it is inferential. The name, however, is directly perceived even in the modification; and the directly perceived is stronger than the inferential. Therefore the one-day [rite's properties] should be adopted.
[The objector says:] but it was said that the name is excessive (<s>adhikārya</s>). To this we reply: the excessive [elements] have no [Vedic] word [support]. The excessive have no word — these words '<s>Jyotis</s>' and the like were said to be names of rites. Or rather, a name would be [that which] at its origination is unprecedented and non-prescriptive. As for what was said — 'because of the coming of the excessive, it would have that designation' — to that we say: by [Vedic] statement, the coming of the excessive [is established]; not by the name. As for what was said — 'in their absence, the word would not exist' — those [properties] are never absent in the <s>āyus</s>-rites and the like. How [then] has the absence of the word in their absence been observed? As for what was said — 'in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> the word <s>jyotis</s> and the like does not [appear]' — that is because of it being a different rite. In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the word <s>āyus</s> and the like does not occur — not because of the absence of properties [but because of being a different rite]. Therefore the one-day [rite's] contradicting set of properties should be adopted. 'Because of the coming of the excessive, it would have that designation' — this is the refutation of the second interpretation of '<s>ekāhavat</s>.' [The name,] being figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>), [66] would be merely a purposeless restatement. Therefore, by the previously stated principle, the name is a means of obtaining <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: liṅgaṃ saṃghātadharmaḥ syāt tadarthāpatter dravyavat // MS_7,4.16 //
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark is a property of the aggregate; because of the implication for that purpose, like a substance. // MS_7,4.16 //

children.text: atha yal liṅgam upadiṣṭam, dvādaśopasattvadarśanam, tasya parihāra ucyate. liṅgaṃ saṃghātadharmaḥ syāt. liṅgam etatsaṃghātadharmaḥ syāt. dvādaśāho 'haḥsaṃghātaḥ. sa phalāya codyate. dvādaśāham ṛddhikāmā upeyur iti. gavāmayanam api ahaḥsaṃghātāntaram. tasminn eva kārye phalasiddhau vidhīyate. tasya tatkāryāpattyā dvādaśāhadharmān gṛhṇāti, na codakena, dravyavat. yathā dravye vrīhau dharmāḥ śrutās te tatkāryāpanneṣu pratinidhibhūteṣu{*7/320*} prāpyante, na codakena tadvat.
children.translated_text: Now, as to the indicatory mark that was cited — the observation of twelve <s>upasattvas</s> (approach-days) — its refutation is stated. An indicatory mark is a property of the aggregate. The indicatory mark would be a property of this aggregate. The twelve-day [rite] is an aggregate of days. It is enjoined for the sake of a fruit — 'those desiring prosperity should approach [for] twelve days.' The <s>Gavāmayana</s> too is another aggregate of days. In that very [<s>Gavāmayana</s>], when the accomplishment of the fruit is prescribed, it takes the twelve-day [rite's] properties through the implication of sharing that purpose — not through the injunctive principle. [This is] like a substance. Just as the <s>dharmas</s> heard in connection with rice as a substance are obtained in substitutes (<s>pratinidhi</s>) such as [wild rice] that have come into [the place of] that purpose — not through the injunctive principle. Similarly [here].

children.text: na vārthadharmatvāt saṃghātasya guṇatvāt // MS_7,4.17 //
children.translated_text: Or not, because of being a property of the purpose [i.e., apūrva], because of the aggregate being subordinate. // MS_7,4.17 //

children.text: naitad yuktam. kutaḥ. arthadharmatvāt. apūrvadharmatvād ity arthaḥ. apūrvadharmo dvādaśopasattvaṃ na saṃghātadharmaḥ. kasmāt. saṃghātasya guṇatvāt. ahāny atra pradhānāni. dvādaśāheneti dvādaśatvaṃ{*7/321*} teṣāṃ guṇaḥ. viśeṣaṇam ity arthaḥ. viśiṣya eva kāryaṃ pratīyate, na viśeṣaṇe. yathā rājapuruṣa ānīyatām ity ukte puruṣa ānīyate, na rājā. yathā ca, mṛṣṭaṃ bhuṅkte devadatta ity ukte, na śākaṃ sūpo vā pratīyate. yad eva pradhānaṃ tat pratīyate. kim ataḥ. ato 'hāni phalavanti, na saṃghātaḥ. phalavataś ca dharmāḥ. tasmān na dvādaśopasattvaṃ saṃghātadharmaḥ. evaṃ [67]{*7/322*} cen na gavāmayane kāryāpattito dharmāḥ prāpyante. ato 'parihāro 'yam.
children.translated_text: This is not proper. Why? Because of being a property of the purpose (<s>artha</s>). The meaning is: because of being a property of the <s>apūrva</s>. The twelve <s>upasattvas</s> are a property of the <s>apūrva</s>, not of the aggregate. Why? Because the aggregate is subordinate. The days here are primary. 'By a twelve-day [rite]' — the twelve-ness is their quality, meaning: a qualifier. The thing to be done is understood only through what is qualified — not through the qualifier. Just as when 'let the king's man be brought' is said, the man is brought, not the king. And just as when 'Devadatta eats a delicacy' is said, neither vegetable nor soup is understood — only what is primary is understood. What follows from this? Therefore the days are fruitful, not the aggregate. And the <s>dharmas</s> belong to what is fruitful. Therefore the twelve <s>upasattvas</s> are not a property of the aggregate. [67] And if so, in the <s>Gavāmayana</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> are not obtained through purpose-implication (<s>kāryāpatti</s>). Therefore this is no refutation.

children.text: arthāpatter dravyeṣu dharmalābhaḥ syāt//6.4.18//
children.translated_text: Through [purpose-]implication, [there would be] obtainment of properties in substances. // MS_7,4.18 //

children.text:
yad uktam{*7/323*}, dravyavad iti. yuktaṃ dravyeṣu. tatra hi vrīhikāryāpannā nīvārāḥ kāryāpattitas taddharmāṃl labhante. iha punar dvādaśopasattvaṃ naiva saṃghātadharma ity apadiṣṭo hetuḥ. tasmād adṛṣṭānto dravyavad iti.
āha, kathaṃ tarhi idaṃ liṅgadarśanam. atrocyate,
children.translated_text:
As to what was said — 'like a substance' — that is appropriate for substances. For there, wild rice (<s>nīvāra</s>) that has come into the [role of fulfilling] the purpose of rice obtains its properties through purpose-implication. But here, it has been shown that the twelve <s>upasattvas</s> are simply not a property of the aggregate — [so] the reason is refuted. Therefore 'like a substance' is without an example.
He says: how then [is] this observation of an indicatory mark [to be explained]? To this we reply:

children.text: pravṛttyā niyatasya liṅgadarśanam // MS_7,4.19 //
children.translated_text: The observation of the indicatory mark is of [a rite that is] determined by [its own] operation. // MS_7,4.19 //

children.text:
gavāmayane dvādaśāhikaṃ prathamam ahaḥ, prāyaṇīyo 'tirātraḥ. tasya dharmo dvādaśopasattvam. tadupādāne mukhyasyānugrahaḥ. ṣaḍupasattvopādāne jaghanyānāṃ jyotirādīnām, mukhyasya prāptakālam anugraham atikramitum kiṃcit kāryaṃ{*7/324*} nāsti. atas tadanugrahārthaṃ dvādaśopasattvaṃ bhavati. tathā mukhyayā{*7/325*} pravṛttyā niyatasyaitaddarśanam, na codakaprāptyā. yasmāc codako nāmadheyād abalaḥ. vakṣyati ca, vipratiṣiddhadharmāṇāṃ samavāye bhūyasāṃ syāt sadharmatvam{*7/326*}. mukhyaṃ vāpūrvacodanāl lokavad{*7/327*} iti.
atha yad dvitīyaṃ liṅgadarśanam uktam, ekādaśinyāṃ vihāradarśanam. tatrocyate,
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Gavāmayana</s>, the first day is of the twelve-day type — the inaugural <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight) [rite]. Its property is the twelve <s>upasattvas</s>. When that [twelve-<s>upasattva</s>] is adopted, the primary [day] is favored. When [only] six <s>upasattvas</s> are adopted, the later [days such as] <s>Jyotis</s> and the like [are favored]; there is no purpose in going beyond the favor due to the primary [day] at its proper time. Therefore, for the sake of favoring it [the primary day], twelve <s>upasattvas</s> occur. Thus this observation [of the indicatory mark] is of [a rite] determined by the primary operation — not by the obtainment through the injunctive principle. For the injunctive principle is weaker than the name. And it will be stated [later]: 'In the conjunction of [rites with] contradicting properties, [the properties] of the majority should [prevail], being of the same character.' '[Or the] primary [should prevail], because of [the authority of] the injunction of the <s>apūrva</s>, as in worldly [usage].'
Now, as to the second indicatory mark that was cited — the observation of the <s>vihāra</s> (ritual wandering) on the eleventh [day] — to that we say:

children.text: vihāradarśanaṃ viśiṣṭasyānārabhyavādānāṃ prakṛtyarthatvāt // MS_7,4.20 //
children.translated_text: The observation of the <s>vihāra</s> (ritual wandering) is of what is specific; because of the non-initiatory statements (<s>anārabhyavāda</s>) being for the purpose of the archetype. // MS_7,4.20 //

children.text: anārabhyaikādaśinyāṃ vihāraḥ śiṣṭaḥ. tadādiprabhavāḥ paśavaḥ{*7/329*} syuḥ. tathā{*7/330*} tān evānūcīnān aharahar ālabheran, āgneyam eva prathame 'hany ālabheran, sārasvatīṃ meṣīṃ dvitīye, saumyaṃ babhruṃ tṛtīye, vāruṇam antataḥ. atha punaḥ paryāvarteṣv{*7/331*} āgneyam eva prathame 'hany ālabheran, sārasvatīṃ meṣīṃ dvitīye, saumyaṃ babhruṃ tṛtīye, vāruṇam antata iti. tad anārabhyavādānāṃ prakṛtyarthatvāj jyotiṣṭomaṃ praviṣṭam. tatrāhnāṃ bahutvasyābhāvād asaṃbhavād aparāṃ prakṛtiṃ dvādaśāham āgatam. tatrāpi punar jyotirādīnāṃ paryāvarteṣv ity etan na yujyata iti tṛtīyāṃ prakṛtiṃ gavāmayane praviṣṭam{*7/332*}. evam āgatasyaitad darśanam iti.
children.translated_text: Without initiating [any specific day], the <s>vihāra</s> on the eleventh [day] is taught [for the <s>Gavāmayana</s>]. The animals beginning with that [eleventh day] should [be offered in sequence]. Thus they should immolate those very [animals] in succession day after day — on the first day they should immolate an <s>Āgneya</s> (fire-deity [animal]), on the second a <s>Sārasvatī</s> ewe, on the third a brown <s>Saumya</s> (moon-deity [animal]), at the end a <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water-deity [animal]). Then again in the repetitions (<s>paryāvarta</s>): on the first day they should immolate an <s>Āgneya</s>, on the second a <s>Sārasvatī</s> ewe, on the third a brown <s>Saumya</s>, at the end a <s>Vāruṇa</s>. That [vihāra], because of the non-initiatory statements being for the purpose of the archetype, has entered the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [first]. There, because of the absence — impossibility — of multiplicity of days, it has come to another archetype: the twelve-day [rite]. There again, because of 'in the repetitions of the <s>Jyotis</s> and the like' not being appropriate, it has entered a third archetype: the <s>Gavāmayana</s>. Thus the observation [of the vihāra] is of [a rite] that has arrived [at the Gavāmayana] in this way.
